Ad-Dahhak and Al-Hasan said: That is, We bring them to life through faith after ignorance. The first is more apparent, that is, We bring them to life through resurrection for recompense. Then He threatened them with a mention in the books of hadith, which are: Second: Enumerating everything and everything that a person does. Qatada said: It means of deeds. Mujahid and Ibn Zayd also said this. Similar to this is His statement, A soul will know what it has put forward and left behind. (Al-Infitar 28:5), and His statement, On that Day man will be informed of what he put forward and left behind. (Al-Qiyamah 29:13), and His statement, Fear God, and let a soul look to what it has put forward for tomorrow. (Al-Hashr 59:18) So the traces of a person that remain and are remembered after the death of the person, whether good or evil, will be rewarded with a good trace, such as knowledge they taught, a book they compiled, an inheritance they kept, or a building they built such as a mosque, ribat, bridge, or the like. Or a bad trace, such as a job assigned to the Muslims by some oppressor, or a road they built to cause them to lose, or something they created to distract from the remembrance of God, such as tunes and music. Likewise, every good or bad tradition that is followed. It was said: It is the traces of those who walk to the mosques. And in this sense the verse was interpreted by Umar, Ibn Abbas, and Saeed bin Jubair. It was also narrated from Ibn Abbas that the meaning of and their footsteps was their steps to the mosques. An-Nahhas said: This is the most appropriate thing to say about it, because he said: The verse was revealed about that, because the Ansar lived far from the mosque. And in the hadith attributed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: For one foot, a good deed will be recorded for him, and for one foot, a bad deed will be erased from him, going and coming back, if he leaves the mosque. I said: In Al-Tirmidhi, it is narrated on the authority of Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri, who said: Banu Salamah were in the outskirts of Madinah, and they wanted to move closer to the mosque, so this verse was revealed: Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life, and We record what they have put forth and what they left behind. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Your footsteps are being recorded. But they did not move. He said: This is a good and rare hadith from the hadith of Al-Thawri. In Sahih Muslim, it is narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn `Abdullah, who said: Banu Salamah wanted to move closer to the mosque, and the area was empty. He said: report of that reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: O Banu Salamah, your dwellings record your footsteps; your dwellings record your footsteps. They said: It would not have pleased us if we had moved. Thabit Al-Bunani said: “I walked with Anas ibn Malik to the prayer and I hurried, but he stopped me. When the prayer ended, he said: ‘I walked with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and I hurried, but he stopped me. When the prayer ended, he said: ‘Didn’t you know that the marks are written?’” This is an argument based on the verse. Qatadah, Mujahid, and al-Hasan also said: The marks are in these steps. Al-Tha’labi narrated on the authority of Anas that he said: The marks are the steps taken to the Friday prayer. The singular of marks is athar, and it is also said athar. Third: In these hadiths explaining the meaning of the verse, there is evidence that being farther from the mosque is better. If it is next to a mosque, is it permissible for him to go beyond it to a farther one? There is a difference of opinion regarding this. It was narrated from Anas that he used to go beyond the newly built mosque to the old one. It was narrated from others: The further away from the mosque the greater the reward. Al-Hasan and others disliked this and said: He should not abandon a mosque near him and go to another one. This is the school of Malik. There are two opinions regarding going beyond his mosque to the Greater Mosque. Ibn Majah narrated from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: A man’s prayer in his house is equal to one prayer, and his prayer in the mosque of the tribes is equal to twenty-five prayers, and his prayer in the mosque in which he gathers is equal to five hundred prayers. Fourth: <your homes>is in the accusative case as an inducement, meaning stick to them, and <we write>is in the jussive mood as a response to that command. <and all>is in the accusative case as an implied verb indicated by <we counted it>as if he said: and we counted everything we counted. It is permissible to raise it as a subject, but its accusative case is more appropriate, to connect what the verb did to it with what the verb did to it? This is the opinion of Al-Khalil and Sibawayh. The imam is the book that is followed and is an evidence. Mujahid, Qatadah, and Ibn Zayd said: He meant the Preserved Tablet. A group said: He meant the scrolls of deeds.
36:13: The Almighty says: And present to them an example of the companions of the city, when there came messengers to it. This is addressed to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him. He was commanded to present to his people an example of the companions of the city. This city is Antioch according to all commentators, except for what Al-Mawardi mentioned. It was attributed to the people of Antiochus, which is the name of the one who built it, then it was changed when it was Arabized. As-Suhayli mentioned. It is also said: Antioch with a ta' instead of a ta'. There was a Pharaoh there called Antiochus who worshipped idols. As-Mahdawi mentioned, and Abu Ja'far An-Nahhas narrated it on the authority of Ka'b and Wahb. So God sent three to him: Sadiq and Saduq, and Shalom is the third. This is the opinion of At-Tabari. Others said: Simon and John. Al-Naqqash narrated: Simeon and John, but he did not mention Sadiq or Saduq. It is possible that <for example>and <the people of the village>are the objects of the verb to strike, or that <the people of the village>is a substitute for <for example>, meaning strike for them an example of the people of the village, so the complement is omitted. “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that these polytheists be warned that what happened to the infidels of the people of the village to whom three messengers were sent would happen to them.” It was said: Messengers from God as a beginning. It was also said: Jesus sent them to Antioch to call people to God.
36:14: And it is the saying of God Almighty: When We sent to them two, and the Lord attributed that to Himself, because Jesus sent them by the Lord's command, and that was when Jesus was raised to heaven. But they denied them, it was said that they beat them and imprisoned them. So We reinforced them with a third, meaning, We strengthened and intensified the message <with a third>. Abu Bakr read from Asim, So We reinforced them with a third, with a light pronunciation, and the rest stressed it. Al-Jawhari said: God Almighty's saying, So We reinforced them with a third, is lightened and stressed, meaning, We strengthened and intensified it. Al-Asma'i said: Abu Amr ibn al-Ala' recited to me about it by al-Mutalammis: I find that if she leaves, her flesh strengthens, but if she tightens her grip, she does not speak. That is, do not fret. Based on this, the two readings have the same meaning. It was said that the softening means we overcame and subdued, and from this: And He honored me in speech [p. 23] and the emphasis means we strengthened and multiplied. In the story: Jesus sent two messengers to them. They met an old man who was tending his sheep, and he was Habib the carpenter, the companion of <Ya Sin>. They called him to God and said: We are the messengers of Jesus. We invite you to the worship of God. He asked them for a miracle. They said: We heal the sick. He had a mad son. It was also said: He was sick in bed, so they stroked him. He got up, God willing, healthy. The man believed in God. It was also said: He is the one who came from the farthest part of the city, running. Their story spread, and they healed many sick people. The king - who used to worship idols - sent to them to inquire about them. They said: We are the messengers of Jesus. He said: What is your sign? They said: We heal the blind, the leper, and the sick by God’s permission, and we invite you to worship God alone. The king wanted to beat them. Wahb said: The king imprisoned them and flogged them a hundred lashes. The report reached Jesus, so he sent a third. It was said that Simon Peter, the chief of the disciples, supported them. He mingled with the king’s entourage until he was able to defeat them, and they became comfortable with him. They reported his story to the king, who was comfortable with him and showed agreement with him in his religion. The king was pleased with his approach. Then one day he said to the king: I have heard that you have imprisoned two men who called you to God, so why don’t you ask about them? Jesus replied: Anger prevented me from asking them. Jesus said: Why don’t you bring them? He ordered that to be done. Simon Peter said to them: What is your proof for what you claim? They said: We heal the blind and the leper. Then a boy with anointed eyes was brought to him, the place of his eyes was like a forehead. They called upon their Lord, and the place of sight split. They took two clay guns and placed them on his cheeks, and they became two eyeballs with which he could see. The king was amazed and said, "Here is a boy who died seven days ago, and I have not buried him until his father comes. Will your Lord revive him?" They called upon God openly, and Simeon called upon Him secretly. The dead man rose to life and said to the people, "If you died seven days ago and were found to be a polytheist, you will be thrown into seven valleys of Hell. I warn you of what you are in, so believe in God." Then the gates of heaven were opened, and I saw a young man with a handsome face interceding for these three, Simeon and his two companions, until God revived me. I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, with no partner, and that Jesus is the Spirit of God and His Word, and that these are the messengers of God. They said to him, Is Simeon also with them? He said, Yes, and he is the best of them. Then Simon informed them that he was the messenger of Christ to them. His words affected the king, so he called him to God. The king believed along with many people, while others disbelieved. Al-Qushayri narrated that the king believed but his people did not, and Gabriel cried out a cry that caused all the remaining disbelievers to die. It was narrated that when Jesus commanded them to go to that village, they said, O Prophet of God, we do not know how to speak their tongues and languages. So God prayed for them and they slept where they were. They woke up and found the angels carrying them and dropping them in the land of Antioch, so each one spoke to his companion in the language of the people. This is what He said: And We supported him with the Holy Spirit. They all said, Indeed, we are messengers to you.
36:15: "They said, 'You are only human beings like us. You eat food and walk in the markets. And the Most Merciful has not sent down anything that He commands or anything that He forbids. You are only lying in your claim to the message.'"
36:16: Then the messengers said: Our Lord knows that we are messengers to you, even if you deny us.
36:17: And our duty is only to convey the clear message that God is One.
36:18: They said to them, We see you as an ill omen meaning we consider you a bad omen. Muqatil said: The rain was withheld from them for three years, so they said, This is because of your bad luck. It is said that they continued to warn them for ten years. If you do not desist from our warning, we will surely stone you. Al-Farra' said: We will surely kill you. He said: Most of what is mentioned in the Qur'an about stoning means killing. Qatada said: It is similar to stoning with stones. It was also said: We will curse you, and all of it has been mentioned before. And a painful punishment will surely touch you from Us. It was said: It means killing. It was also said: It means painful torture. It was also said: It means painful torture before killing, such as flaying, cutting, and crucifixion.
36:19: Then the messengers said: Your omen is with you, meaning your bad luck is with you, meaning your share of good and evil is with you and is upon your necks, and it is not from our bad luck. Ad-Dahhak said its meaning. Qatada said: Your deeds are with you. Ibn Abbas said: It means that provisions and destinies follow you. Al-Farra' said: Your omen is with you means your provisions and deeds, and the meaning is the same. Al-Hasan read: My omen is your bad luck. "If you remember," Qatada said: "If you remember, you will be afflicted with bad luck." There are nine possible readings for this: The people of Madinah read: "If you remember" with a lightened second hamza. The people of Kufa read: "If" with both hamzas pronounced with emphasis. The third reading: <ُإن ذْفرتم>with two hamzas between them and an alif. The alif was inserted to dislike combining the two hamzas. The fourth reading: <ُإن>with a hamza followed by an alif, and after the alif a light hamza. The fifth reading: <ُاُن>with two open hamzas between them and an alif. The sixth reading: <ُُن>with two confirmed open hamzas. Al-Farra’ reported that this reading is the reading of Abu Razin. I said: Al-Tha'labi narrated it on the authority of Zur ibn Hubaish and Ibn al-Sumaiq. Isa ibn Umar and al-Hasan al-Basri read: "They said, 'Your omen is with you. If you remember,' meaning where. Yazid ibn al-Qa'qa', al-Hasan and Talhah read dhikrtum" with a light pronunciation. An-Nahhas mentioned all of them. Al-Mahdawi narrated on the authority of Talhah ibn Musarraf and Isa al-Hamadhani: "If you remember," with a long vowel, with the question hamza entering on a fatha hamza. Al-Majshun read: "If you remember," with one fatha hamza. So these are nine readings. Ibn Hurmuz read: "Your omen is with you, If you remember," meaning if you are admonished. This is a new statement, meaning if you are admonished, you will take ill omen. It was said that they only took ill omen because they heard that every prophet called his people and they did not respond, the result of which was destruction. "Rather, you are a people who transgress." Qatadah said: Transgressing in your omens. Yahya ibn Salam: Transgressing in your disbelief. Ibn Bahr said: Extravagance here means corruption, and its meaning is: You are a corrupt people. It was also said: Extravagant polytheists, and extravagance means exceeding the limit, and the polytheist exceeds the limit.
36:20: God the Almighty said: And there came from the farthest part of the city a man running. He was Habib ibn Murray, who was a carpenter. It was also said that he was a cobbler. It was also said that he was a plasterer. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Muqatil said that he was Habib ibn Isra'il the carpenter, and he used to carve idols. He was one of those who believed in the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and there were six hundred years between them, as did Tubba' al-Akbar, Waraqah ibn Nawfal, and others. He did not believe in any other prophet until after his appearance. Wahb said: Habib was a leper, and his home was at the farthest gate of the city. He devoted himself to worshipping idols for seventy years, calling upon them, hoping that they would have mercy on him and relieve his distress, but they did not respond to him. When he saw the messengers, they called him to the worship of God, so he said: Is there a sign? They said: Yes, we call upon our Lord, the Almighty, and He will relieve you of what is afflicting you. He said: This is truly amazing! I have been calling upon these gods for seventy years to relieve me, but they could not, so how can your Lord relieve it in one morning? They said: Yes, our Lord has power over whatever He wills. This can neither benefit nor harm. So he believed and supplicated to their Lord, and God removed what was ailing him, as if he had never been sick. Then he turned to earning a living. When evening came, he gave charity from what he earned, so he fed his family half and gave the other half in charity. When his people were about to kill the messengers, he came to them and said, O my people, follow the messengers. Qatada said: He used to worship God in a cave, and when he heard the report of the messengers, he came running and said to the messengers, Do you seek a reward for what you have brought? They said, No, our reward is only from God. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: So he believed in their truthfulness and had faith in them, and he turned to his people and said, O my people, follow the messengers.
36:21: Follow those who do not ask you for payment meaning if they were accused they would ask you for money and they are guided so be guided by them.
36:22: And why should I not worship He who created me? Qatada said: His people said to him, Are you of their religion?! He said, And why should I not worship He who created me? That is, created me. And to Him you will be returned. This is an argument from him against them, and he attributed the creation to himself, because it is a blessing upon him that requires gratitude, and the resurrection to them, because it is a threat that requires a deterrent. So, attributing the blessing to himself is more expressive of gratitude, and attributing the resurrection to the disbeliever is more effective.
36:23: Shall I take other gods besides Him? meaning idols. If the Most Merciful intends me harm, meaning what has befallen him of illness. Their intercession will not avail me at all, nor will they save me from the affliction I am in.
36:24: If I do that, I will be in clear error meaning clear loss.
36:25: Indeed, I have believed in your Lord, so listen. Ibn Mas'ud said: He addressed the messengers, stating that he believed in God, their Lord. The meaning of so listen is bear witness, meaning be my witnesses to my faith. Ka'b and Wahb said: He only said that to his people, I have believed in your Lord whom you disbelieved in. It was also said that when he said to his people, Follow the messengers * Follow those who do not ask of you any reward, they took him to the king and said, You have followed our enemy. He spoke to them at length to distract them from killing the messengers, until he said, Indeed, I have believed in your Lord. They then pounced on him and killed him. Ibn Mas'ud said, They trampled him underfoot until his reeds came out from his anus, and he was thrown into a well called Ar-Rass, and they are the people of Ar-Rass. In another narration, they killed the three messengers. As-Suddi said, They threw stones at him while he was saying, 'O God, guide my people,' until they killed him. Al-Kalbi said: They dug a hole and put him in it, then covered him with dirt, so he died. Al-Hasan said: They burned him and hung him from the city wall, and his grave is in the wall of Antioch, as narrated by Al-Tha’labi. Al-Qushayri said: Al-Hasan said: When the people wanted to kill him, God raised him to the sky, so he is in Paradise and will not die except with the destruction of the sky and the perishing of Paradise. When God restores Paradise, he will enter it. It was also said: They sawed him until he came out from between his legs. By God, his soul did not leave except to Paradise, so he entered it.
36:26: This is his saying: It was said, 'Enter Paradise.' So when he saw it, he said, Oh, would that my people knew * That my Lord has forgiven me. That is, that my Lord has forgiven me. So, ma with the verb is like a verbal noun. It was also said that it means who and the pronoun from the relative clause is omitted. It is also permissible for it to be an interrogative with a sense of astonishment, as if he said, Oh, would that my people knew that my Lord has forgiven me something. Al-Farra' said this. Al-Kisa'i objected and said, If this were correct, he would have said ma without an alif. Al-Farra' said, It is permissible to say ma with an alif, and it is an interrogative, and he recited verses about it. Al-Zamakhshari said, By what has been forgiven me is better, although keeping it is permissible. It is said, I know by what I have done this and by what I have done. Al-Mahdawi said, "Keeping the alif in interrogatives is rare. So, we should stop at "ya'lamoon." A group said: The meaning of enter Paradise is that Paradise is obligatory for you. It is report that he has deserved to enter Paradise, because entering it is deserved after the resurrection. I said: What appears from the verse is that when he was killed, he was told to enter Paradise. Qatada said: God admitted him to Paradise while he was alive and provided for. He meant the words of God Almighty: “And never think of those who are killed in the way of God as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision” (Al Imran 3:169) as explained previously in <Al Imran>. And God knows best. The Almighty’s saying: If only my people knew is based on the assumption that a questioner asked about what he found of his words at that great victory.
36:27: which is because my Lord has forgiven me and made me one of the honored ones and it was read <one of the honored ones>and there are two sayings about the meaning of his wish: One of them is that he wished that they knew about his condition so that they would know his good end and praiseworthy outcome. The second is that he wished that so that they would believe like his faith and become like his condition. Ibn Abbas said: He advised his people while alive and after death. Al-Qushayri traced it back to the Prophet and said: "And in the report that he, peace be upon him, said about this verse: It is valid for them during his life and after his death." Ibn Abi Layla said: Three nations did not disbelieve in God for the blink of an eye: Ali ibn Abi Talib, who was the best of them; the believer of the family of Pharaoh; and the companion of Yaseen. They are the truthful ones. Az-Zamakhshari mentioned this as a hadith from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. In this verse there is a great warning and evidence of the obligation to suppress anger, to be patient with the ignorant, to have compassion for the one who has entered into the midst of the wicked and the oppressors, to work hard to rescue him, to be gentle in ransoming him, and to be occupied with that instead of gloating over him and praying against him. Do you not see how he wished good for his killers and those who intended to harm him, even though they were disbelievers and idol worshippers? So when Habib was killed, God became angry on his behalf and hastened the vengeance on his people. He ordered Gabriel to shout at them and they all died.
36:28: So this is what He said: And We did not send down upon his people after him any soldiers from the heaven, nor would We have sent down meaning, We did not send down upon them any message or prophet after his murder. This was said by Qatada, Mujahid, and Al-Hasan. Al-Hasan said: The soldiers are the angels who descend with revelation to the prophets. It was also said: The soldiers are the armies, meaning, I did not need to send soldiers, armies, or troops to destroy them, rather, I destroyed them with a single blast. Ibn Mas'ud and others said the same meaning. So His statement, And We were not sending down is a diminutive of their matter, meaning, We destroyed them with a single blast after that man, or after he was raised to the heaven. It was also said: And We were not sending down upon those who came before them. Al-Zamakhshari: If you say, then why did He send down soldiers from the heaven on the day of Badr and the Trench? He said: So We sent upon them a wind and soldiers you did not see (al-Ahzab 33:9), and He said: With three thousand angels sent down “With five thousand angels marked” (Al Imran 3:124-125). I said: One king would have been enough, for the cities of the people of Lot were destroyed by a feather from Gabriel’s wing, and the lands of Thamud and the people of Salih by a shout. But God favored Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in everything over all the other prophets and messengers of resolve, let alone Habib the Carpenter. He granted him reasons for honor and respect that He granted to no one else. Among these is that He sent down to him soldiers from the sky. It is as if He indicated by His saying: And We did not send down and And We would not send down that sending down soldiers is one of the greatest matters that only someone like you would be qualified to do, and We would not do it for anyone other than you.
36:29: It was only a single shout. The general reading is <one>in the accusative case, assuming that their punishment was only a single shout. Abu Ja`far ibn al-Qa`qa`, Shaybah and al-A`raj read a blast in the nominative case. In His statement, It was only a single blast, and at once they were extinguished, they made being mean occurring or coming into being. It is as if he said, Nothing befell them except a single blast. Abu Hatim and many grammarians rejected this reading because of the feminine gender, so it is weak, just as Ma qamat illa Hind would be weak, since the meaning is No one stood up except Hind. Abu Hatim said, If it had been as Abu Ja`far read it, he would have said, “It was only a blast. An-Nahhas said, “None of this is impossible. It is said, ‘No woman or slave girl came to me except your slave girl,’ meaning, “No woman or slave girl came to me except your slave girl.” The interpretation of the nominative case reading is what Abu Ishaq said. He said, The meaning is that there was only a single blast upon them. Others estimated it as, No blast befell them except a single blast. “It has often had the meaning of ‘happened’ in Arabic speech.” `Abd ar-Rahman ibn al-Aswad read—and it is said that it is also in the same way as `Abdullah’s version—Indeed it was only a single wineskin. This is contrary to the Qur’an. Also, the well-known language is zaqqa yazqu if it shouts, and from it is the proverb: Heavier than the zawaqi. Therefore, it should have been zaqwa. This was mentioned by An-Nahhas. I said: Al-Jawhari said: Al-Zaqqu and Al-Zaqqi are sources, and the echo shouted, and every shouter shouted, and the shout is the shout. I said: Based on this, it is said: Zaqwa and Zaqiya are two dialects, so the reading is correct and there is no objection to it. And God knows best. Then they are extinguished means dead and inert, likening them to extinguished ashes. Qatada said: They perished. The meaning is the same.
36:30: The Almighty's saying: O regret for the servants is in the accusative case, because it is a vocative of an indefinite noun, and nothing but the accusative is permissible in it according to the Basrans. In the letter of Abi, <O regret for the servants>is in the genitive case. The true meaning of regret in the language is that a person is afflicted with remorse that makes him feel regretful. Al-Farra' claimed that the preferred choice is the accusative case, and that if the indefinite noun connected to the relative clause had been raised, it would have been correct. He cited as evidence things, including that he heard from the Arabs: O one concerned with our affair, do not worry. And he recited: * Oh house, the decay has changed it * An-Nahhas said: “This invalidates most of the vocative case, because it raises a pure indefinite noun, raises what is in the position of a noun with respect to length, and by deleting the tanween in the middle, and raises what is in the meaning of a direct object without a reason necessitating that. As for what he narrated from the Arabs, it does not resemble what he permitted, because the estimation of ‘O you who are concerned with our affair, do not be concerned with it’ is based on precedence and delay, and the meaning is: O you who are concerned, do not be concerned with our affair. The estimation of the verse is: O home, then he changed the addressee, meaning these are not this home of decay, as God the Almighty said: ‘Until, when you were in the ship and it sailed with them’ (Yunus 10:22). So ‘regret’ is in the accusative case as a vocative, as you would say ‘O man, come!’ The meaning of the vocative is: This is the place where regret is present.” At-Tabari said: The meaning is: O regret of the servants for themselves, and remorse and longing in mocking the Messengers of God, peace be upon them. Ibn Abbas said: ‘O regret upon the servants’ means: O woe upon the servants. And from him also: These people have taken the place of those who are grieving over them. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas narrated from Abu Al-Aaliyah that the servants here are the messengers. This is because when the disbelievers saw the punishment, they said: Alas for the servants! So they grieved over their killing and abandoning belief in them. They wished to believe when belief did not benefit them. This was also said by Mujahid. Ad-Dahhak said: It is a grief for the angels over the disbelievers when they denied the messengers. It was also said: Alas for the servants! is from the words of the man who came running from the farthest part of the city when the people rose up to kill him. It was also said: The three messengers are the ones who said when the people killed that man who came running from the farthest part of the city and the punishment descended upon the al-Nas 114:Alas for these people! It is as if they wished that they had believed. It was also said: This is from the words of the people who said when they killed the man and the messengers left them, or they killed the man along with the three messengers, according to the different narrations: Alas for these messengers and this man! Would that we had believed in them at a time when belief is beneficial. This was discussed, then he began with the statement: Whatever comes to them from a messenger. Ibn Hormuz, Muslim ibn Jundub, and Ikrimah read: O grief for the servants! with a sukoon on the ha’ out of concern for clarity and establishing the meaning in the mind, as it was a place for exhortation and warning, and the Arabs do that in similar cases, even if it is not a place for a pause. Among this is what was narrated from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that he would stop his recitation letter by letter, keen on clarity and understanding. It is possible that on the servants is related to grief. It is also possible that it is related to something omitted, not to grief, so it is as if he estimated the pause at grief and made the ha’ sukoon, then he said: on the servants! meaning, Do I grieve for the servants? Ibn Abbas, Ad-Dahhak, and others reported: O grief for the servants! is an addition without on. This is contrary to the Qur’an. It is also possible that it is from the category of addition to the subject, so the servants are the subject, as if when they witness the punishment they grieve, so it is like your saying, O rising of Zayd. It may also be an addition to the object, so the servants are the objects, as if the one who pities them feels sorry for the servants. The reading of the one who reads: <Oh, what a pity for the servants>strengthens this meaning.
36:31: God the Most High said: Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them? That to them they will not be returned? Sibawayh said: An is a substitute for kam, and the meaning of kam here is the predicate, therefore it is permissible to substitute for it what is not an interrogative. The meaning is: Have they not seen that the generations We destroyed will not be returned to them?" Al-Farra' said: "Kam" is in the accusative case for two reasons: One is by "yaruwa they see and he cited as evidence for this the fact that in Ibn Mas'ud's recitation it is did they not see those who destroyed us? The other reason is that kam is in the accusative case by ahlakkana" we destroyed. An-Nahhas said: The first statement is impossible because "kam" does not affect what precedes it, because it is an interrogative, and it is impossible for an interrogative to enter into the predicate of what precedes it. The same applies if it is a predicate, although Sibawayh hinted at some of this when he made "annahu a substitute for kam". Muhammad bin Yazid refuted this vehemently, saying, "How many is in the accusative case because of we destroyed and that they" is in the accusative case. The meaning according to him is "how many generations We destroyed before them" by extermination. He said: The evidence for this is that in the recitation of Abdullah, "Those generations We destroyed before them - to them they will not be returned. Al-Hasan read, Indeed, to them they will not be returned" with a kasra on the hamza as a new sentence. This verse is a refutation of those who claim that some of the creation will return before the Resurrection.
36:32: And indeed, every one of them will be brought before Us meaning on the Day of Resurrection for recompense. Ibn Amir, Asim, and Hamzah read: <And indeed, every one of them will be brought before Us" with a shaddah on <lama>, and the rest read it with a light shaddah. <In>is a light shaddah from the heavy shaddah, and what follows it is raised as a subject, and what follows it is the predicate. Its function is nullified when its pronunciation changes. The lam is required in the predicate to differentiate it from <inna>which means "ma". <ma>according to Abu Ubaidah is redundant. According to him, the interpretation is: And indeed, every one of them will be brought before Us" Al-Farra' said: And whoever makes it with a shaddah makes <lama>mean except and <inna>mean ma, meaning, every one of them is only for everyone, like His statement: He is only a man in whom is madness Al-Mu'minun 32:25. Sibawayh narrated in his statement: I ask you by God, why did you do that? Al-Kisa'i claimed that he did not know this. This meaning was previously mentioned in <Hud>. And in the letter of Abu Ubaidah: <And indeed, from them, all of them will be brought before Us>.
36:33: The Almighty said: And a sign for them is the dead land which We have given life to. With this, God the Almighty alerted them to the revival of the dead, and reminded them of His Oneness and the perfection of His power. It is the dead land which He has given life to with plants and the bringing forth of grain from it. From it meaning: from the grain they eat and are nourished by it. The people of Medina stressed the dead land and the rest lightened it, and this has been mentioned previously.
36:34: And We placed therein meaning on the earth, gardens meaning orchards of palm trees and grapevines and He mentioned them specifically because they are the highest fruits. And We caused springs to gush forth therein meaning in the orchards.
36:35: That they may eat of its fruit The ha' in <thamaruhu>refers to the water of the springs, because the fruit was included in it, as stated by al-Jurjani, al-Mahdawi, and others. It was also said that it means that they may eat of the fruit we mentioned, as He said: "And indeed, in the livestock is a lesson for you. We give you drink from what is in their bellies" (al-Nahl 16:66). Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read <min thamaruhu>with a damma on the th and the meem. The rest opened them both. Al-A'mash reported that the th was pronounced with a damma and the meem was pronounced with a sukoon. This has already been discussed in <al-An'am>. And what their hands have made <ma>is in the accusative case in apposition to <min thamaruhu>, meaning, and what their hands have made. The Kufians read <wa ma ammalathu>without a ha'. The rest read <amlathu>in the original form without any deletion. The deletion of the relative clause is also common in speech due to the length of the noun. <ma>may be a negative that has no position, so it does not need a relative clause or referent. That is, and their hands did not make it from the crops that God caused to grow for them. This is the saying of Ibn Abbas, Ad-Dahhak, and Muqatil. Others said: The meaning is, And from what their hands made, meaning from the fruits, and from the types of sweets and foods, and from what they made from grains as a treatment, such as bread and the oil extracted from sesame and olives. It was said: This goes back to what people plant. Its meaning was also narrated from Ibn Abbas: Will they not then be grateful for His blessings.
36:36: The Almighty's saying: Glory be to Him who created all pairs. He has declared Himself, glory be to Him, above what the disbelievers say, since they worshipped other than Him, despite what they saw of His blessings and the effects of His power. This contains an estimation of the matter, meaning glorify Him and declare Him pure from what is not befitting of Him. It was also said that it contains the meaning of amazement, meaning, how astonished these people are in their disbelief, despite what they witness of these signs. Whoever is amazed at something says, Glory be to God! The pairs are the types and kinds, so each pair is a kind, because they differ in color, taste, shape, smallness and largeness, so their difference is their pairing. Qatada said: It means male and female. From what the earth grows means from plants, because they are kinds. And from themselves means and He created from them children in pairs, males and females. And from that which they do not know meaning from the kinds of His creation on land, sea, sky and earth. Then it is possible that what He creates is not known to humans, but is known to the angels. It is possible that no creature knows Him. The evidence in this verse is that if He is the only One who creates, then no one should be associated with Him.
36:37: The Almighty says: "And a sign for them is the night. We strip thereof the day." That is, a sign indicating the Oneness of God, His power, and the necessity of His divinity. Stripping means scraping and pulling. It is said: God stripped him of his religion, then it is used to mean expulsion. The disappearance of light and the coming of darkness have been made like the stripping of something and the appearance of the stripped, so it is a metaphor. And dark means entering into darkness. It is said: We became dark meaning we entered into the darkness of the night, and we appeared means we entered at noon. Likewise, we became morning, we spent the morning, and we spent the evening. It was said: From it means about it, and the meaning is We strip it of the light of the day. So they are dark means in darkness, because the light of day penetrates the air and gives light, and when it exits from it, it becomes dark.
36:38: His Almighty saying: And the sun runs to its resting place may be interpreted as And a sign for them is the sun. It may be that the sun is in the nominative case with an implied verb that explains the second one. It may be that it is in the nominative case with the subject runs in the place of the predicate, meaning running. In Sahih Muslim, it is narrated on the authority of Abu Dharr who said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about His Almighty saying: And the sun runs to its resting place He said: Its resting place is under the Throne. “And in it, on the authority of Abu Dharr, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said one day: Do you know where this sun goes? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: It moves until it reaches its resting place under the Throne, then it falls down in prostration and remains like that until it is told: ‘Rise and go back from whence you came.’ So it goes back and rises in the morning from where it rose. Then it moves on, and people do not find anything strange about it until it reaches its resting place under the Throne, and it is told: ‘Rise and go back in the morning from where you set.’ So it rises in the morning from where it set. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you know when that will be? That is when “No soul will benefit from its faith if it did not believe before or earn any good through its faith” Al-An’am 6:158.” Al-Bukhari’s version: “On the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Abu Dharr when the sun set: Do you know where it goes? I said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: It goes until it prostrates beneath the Throne and asks permission, and permission is given to it. It is about to prostrate but it is not accepted from it. It asks permission, but it is not given permission. It is told, ‘Go back from where you came.’ Then it rises from the west. This is what God, the Most High, said: ‘And the sun runs to its resting place. That is the determination of the Almighty, the Knowing.’” Al-Tirmidhi’s version: “On the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: I entered the mosque when the sun set and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was sitting. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O Abu Dharr, do you know where it goes? I said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: It goes and asks permission to prostrate, and it is given permission, and it is as if it had been told, ‘Rise from where you came,’ and it rises from the west.” Then he recited: That is its resting place. He said: This is the recitation of Abdullah. Abu ‘Eesa said: This is a good and authentic hadith. Ikrimah said: When the sun sets, it enters a niche beneath the Throne, glorifying God until morning. When morning comes, it asks its Lord for permission to leave. The Lord says to it: Why is that? It says: When I leave, I will be worshipped instead of you. The Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, says: Come out, and you will have no problem with that. I will send Hell to them with seventy thousand angels who will lead them until they enter it. Al-Kalbi and others said: The meaning is that it runs to the furthest of its stations at sunset, then returns to the nearest of its stations. Its final destination is when it reaches a place which it does not exceed, but rather returns from it, just as a person travels a distance until he reaches his furthest destination, satisfies his desire, then returns to his original station from which he began his journey. And the sun reaches its furthest stations, which is its resting place when it rises at sunrise. That day is the longest day of the year, and that night is the shortest night. The day is fifteen hours and the night is nine hours. Then it begins to decrease and the sun returns. When the Pleiades rise, the night and day are equal, each one being twelve hours. Then it reaches its lowest stations and the luxuries appear. That day is the shortest of days, and the night is fifteen hours. When it rises, the Bucket and the Delayed are emptied, and the night and day are equal. So the night takes from the day every day a tenth of a third of an hour, and every ten days a third of an hour, and every month a full hour, until they are equal. The night takes from the day until it reaches fifteen hours, and the day takes from the night likewise. Al-Hasan said: The sun has three hundred and sixty risings in a year. It descends once every day, then it does not descend again for a year. So it moves through those stations, which are its resting place. This is the same meaning as the previous one. Ibn Abbas said: When it sets and reaches the place it does not exceed, it remains beneath the Throne until it rises. I said: What Ibn Abbas said reconciles the sayings, so ponder it. It was said: until the end of its term at the end of the world. Ibn Masoud and Ibn Abbas read: And the sun runs, with no resting place for it. That is, it runs night and day, without stopping or settling, until God rolls it up on the Day of Resurrection. Those who disagreed with the Mushaf argued and said: I recite according to the recitation of Ibn Masoud and Ibn Abbas. Abu Bakr al-Anbari said: This is false and should be rejected by those who transmitted it, because Abu Amr narrated from Mujahid from Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Kathir narrated from Mujahid from Ibn Abbas: And the sun runs to its resting place. These two chains of transmission from Ibn Abbas, whose authenticity is attested to by consensus, invalidate what was narrated with weak chains of transmission that contradict the school of thought and what the ummah has agreed upon. I said: The authentic hadiths that we mentioned refute his statement. He did not base it on the Book of God, may God kill him. His statement, to a place of rest for it means to its place of rest, and the place of rest is a place of settlement. That is the decree means that what was mentioned about the matter of the night, the day, and the sun is the decree of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.
36:39: God Almighty says: And the moon - We have determined for it phases until it returns [appearing] like an old dried date stalk. There are three issues: The first: The Almighty’s statement: And the moon could be interpreted as And a sign for them is the moon. It is permissible for And the moon to be in the nominative case as a subject. The Kufians read And the moon in the accusative case with an implied verb, and this is the preferred choice of Abu Ubaid. He said: Because before it is a verb and after it is a verb, before it is We strip and after it is We determined it. An-Nahhas said: “And all the Arab scholars, as far as I know, are against what he said, including Al-Farra’ who said: “The nominative case is more appropriate to me. Rather, the nominative case, according to them, is more appropriate because it is conjoined with what precedes it and its meaning is “And a sign for them is the moon.” His statement: Before it is “We strip then what is closer to it is It runs and before it is And the sun in the nominative case. And what he mentioned after it, We determined it has worked on the ha’.” Abu Hatim said: The nominative case is more appropriate because you occupied the verb with the pronoun, so you raised it as a subject. It is said: The moon is not the mansions, so how can he say: We have ordained for it mansions? There are two answers to this: One of them is: We have ordained for it mansions, like: And ask the town (Yusuf 12:82). The other interpretation is: We have ordained for it mansions, then the lam was deleted, and its deletion was good because the verb takes two objects, like: And Moses chose from his people seventy men (al-A’raf 7:155). The mansions are twenty-eight mansions, and the moon descends into one mansion every night, and they are: Ash-Shartaan, Al-Batin, Thuraya, Al-Debaran, Al-Haf’ah, Al-‘An’ah, Adh-Dhira’, Al-Nathra, Al-Taraf, Al-Kharataan, Al-Sarfah, Al-‘Awa’, Al-Samak, Al-Ghafr, Al-Rabbanayan, Al-Iklil, Al-Qalb, Al-Shula, Al-Na’aim, Al-Baldah, Sa’d Al-Dhabih, Sa’d Baligh, Sa’d Al-Su’ud, Sa’d Al-Akhbiya, Al-Fargh Al-Muqaddam, Al-Fargh Al-Mu’akhir, and Bel-Hout. When the moon reaches the end of the month, it returns to the beginning, and completes the celestial sphere in twenty-eight nights. Then it becomes hidden, then rises as a crescent, and returns to completing the celestial sphere through the mansions, which are divided among the zodiac signs, for each sign there are two mansions and a third. So Aries has the two halves and the batin and a third of the Pleiades, and Taurus has two-thirds of the Pleiades and the debaran and two-thirds of the Haf’ah, and so on for the rest of them. The naming of the zodiac signs has already been mentioned in Al-Hijr, and praise be to God. It was said that God Almighty created the sun and the moon from fire, then clothed them with light at rising. As for the light of the sun, it is from the light of the throne, and as for the light of the moon, it is from the light of the chair. That is the origin of creation and this covering. As for the sun, its covering was left as it was so that it might shine and rise. As for the moon, the Trustworthy Spirit commanded its wing over its face, so it erased its light with the power of the wing. That is because it is a spirit, and the spirit’s power is dominant over all things. Then that erasure remained as the creation saw it, then it was placed in a cover of water, then a course was made for it, so every night a moon appears to the creation from that cover in the amount of time it moons for them until its beginning is complete, and the creation sees it in its fullness and roundness. Then a part of it continues to return to the cover every night, so the vision and mooning decreases in the amount that it increased in the beginning. And it begins to decrease from the side that the sun does not see it, which is the direction of sunset, until it returns like an old dried cluster, which is a curved cluster due to its dryness and thinness. It is only called the moon because it moons, that is, it whitens the atmosphere with its whiteness until it becomes hidden. The second: Until it became like an old stalk. Al-Zajjaj said: It is the stem of the cluster on which the spikes are, and it is a verb from in’iraj which means to bend, meaning it moved from its places, and when it is at the end of it, it becomes thin, curved, and narrow until it becomes like a stalk. Based on this, the nun is extra. Qatada said: It is the dry, curved cluster of the palm tree. Tha’lab: <like an old stalk>He said: <the stalk>is that which remains of the elegance in the palm tree when it is cut, and <the old>is the worn out one. Al-Khalil: In the chapter on the quadrilateral verb <the stalk>is the base of the cluster, which is yellow and wide and resembles a crescent moon when it bends. Al-Jawhari: <the stalk>is the base of the cluster that is crooked and the spikes are cut from it, so it remains dry on the palm tree, and ‘arjan means hitting it with the stalk. So the nun according to these people is original, and from it is the poem of A’sha ibn Qays: The East is fragrant with musk and it is yellow like the crest of the moon. When the dried-up, matured, and curved arcs, it resembles the moon in its thinness and yellowness. It is also called ihan, kabasa, and qanu, and the people of Egypt call it isbatah. It is read: <al-Arjoon>with the same weight as farjoon, and they are two languages like al-baryoon and al-bazyoun. Al-Zamakhshari mentioned it and said: It is the branch of the cluster of dates between its spikes and its place of growth on the palm tree. Know that the year is divided into four seasons, each season seven mansions: The first of which is spring, and its beginning is fifteen days from March, and the number of its days is ninety-two days, in which the sun passes through three zodiac signs: Aries, Taurus, and Gemini, and seven mansions: Ash-Shartaan, Al-Batin, Al-Thuraya, Al-Debaran, Al-Haf’ah, Al-Hana’ah, and Al-Dhira’. Then summer begins on the fifteenth day of June, and its days are ninety-two days, during which the sun passes through three signs: Ash-Shartan, Leo, and Virgo, and seven mansions: An-Nathra, At-Taraf, Jabha, Kharatan, Sarfah, Awa, and Samak. Then autumn begins on the fifteenth day of September, and its days are ninety-one days, during which the sun passes through three signs: Libra, Scorpio, and Sagittarius, and seven mansions: Al-Ghafr, Al-Rabbanan, Al-Iklil, Al-Qalb, Al-Shulah, Al-Na’aim, and Al-Baldah. Then winter begins on the fifteenth day of December, and its days are ninety days, and it may be ninety-one days, during which the sun passes through three signs: Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces, and seven mansions: Sa’d Al-Dhabih, Sa’d Bal’a, Sa’d Al-Su’ud, Sa’d Al-Akhbiya, Al-Fargh Al-Muqaddam, Al-Fargh Al-Mu’akhir, and Batn Al-Hut. This is the Syriac division of the months: October, November, December, January, February, March, April, May, June, July, August, September. All of them are thirty-one days, except for November, April, June, and September, which are thirty, and February has twenty-eight and a quarter days. By this we only want you to consider the power of God Almighty, as He says: And the moon - We have determined for it phases. So if the sun is in the phase of the people of the crescent moon, then it will be in the phase after it, and dawn is two phases before it. So if the sun is in the phase of the people of the crescent moon, then it will be in the phase after it, and dawn is two phases before it. So if the sun is in the Pleiades on the twenty-five days of April, then dawn will be in the two conditions, and the people of the crescent moon will be in the Aldebaran. Then it will have a phase every night until it completes twenty-eight phases in twenty-eight nights. The sun has completed two phases, so it completes them, then it rises in the phase after the sun’s phase. So that is the decree of the Almighty, the Knowing. Third: The Almighty’s saying: The Ancient. Al-Zamakhshari said: The ancient is the transformed. When it is old, it becomes thin, bent, and yellow, so the moon is likened to it in three ways. It was said: The minimum waiting period for someone described as ancient is a year. So if a man said: Every slave of mine who is ancient is free, or wrote that in his will, he would free anyone who has had a year or more of his slave. I said: The rulings related to the new moon have already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah, and praise be to God.
36:40: The Almighty says: It is not for the sun to overtake the moon. <sun>is raised as a subject, and <la>cannot act as a definite noun. Scholars have discussed the meaning of this verse. Some of them said: It means that the sun cannot overtake the moon, thus nullifying its meaning. That is, each of them has authority over its own situation, so neither of them can interfere with the other and thus lose its authority, until God nullifies what He has planned for that, and the sun rises from its place of setting, as was explained at the end of Surat Al-An'am. It was also said: When the sun rises, the moon has no light, and when the moon rises, the sun has no light. This meaning was narrated from Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak. Mujahid said: That is, the light of one does not resemble the light of the other. Qatadah said: For each there is a limit and knowledge that they do not exceed or fall short of. When the authority of one comes, the authority of the other is lost. Al-Hasan said: They do not meet in the sky on the night of the new moon in particular. That is, the sun does not remain until the moon rises, but when the sun sets, the moon rises. Yahya ibn Salam said: The sun does not overtake the moon on the night of the full moon in particular, because it sets before the moon rises. It was also said that its meaning is that when they meet in the sky, one of them is in front of the other in stations that they do not share. Ibn Abbas also said this. It was also said that the moon is in the lowest heaven, and the sun is in the fourth heaven and does not overtake it. This was mentioned by An-Nahhas and Al-Mahdawi. An-Nahhas said: The best and most clear meaning that has been said about the moon, which cannot be denied, is that the moon’s movement is fast, and the sun does not overtake it in its movement. This was also mentioned by Al-Mahdawi. As for the statement of God, the Most High, And He joined together the sun and the moon Al-Qiyamah 6:9, this is when He prevented the sun from rising, as was explained previously at the end of Al-An’am and will also appear in Surah Al-Qiyamah. Their joining together is a sign of the end of this world and the establishment of the Hour. And each meaning the sun, moon, and stars floats in an orbit meaning they run. It was also said: they revolve. He did not say float because He described them with the actions of a rational being. Al-Hasan said: The sun, the moon, and the stars are an orbit between the heaven and the earth, not attached. If they were attached, they would not have moved. This was mentioned by Al-Tha'labi and Al-Mawardi. Some of them used as evidence the words of God, the Most High: Nor does the night outstrip the day, to mean that the day was created before the night, and that the night did not precede it in creation. It was also said: Each one of them comes at its time and does not outstrip the other until the sun and moon are joined together on the Day of Resurrection, as He said: And He will bring together the sun and the moon. This alternation now is to fulfill the interests of the servants. And that you may know the number of years and the account. (Al-Isra': 12). The night is for rest and relaxation, and the day is for action, as God, the Most High, said: And of His mercy He made for you the night and the day that you may rest therein and seek of His bounty. (al-Qasas 28:73) and He said: And We have made your sleep [for] rest. (An-Naba': 9), meaning that your bodies rest from the work of the day. So His words: Nor does the night outstrip the day, mean that it overcomes the day. It is said: So-and-so overtook so-and-so, meaning he overcame him. Al-Mubarrad said: I heard Amara reciting nor does the night outstrip the day so I said: What is this? He said: I meant outstrips the day so I deleted the tanween because it is lighter. An-Nahhas said: It is possible for the day to be in the accusative case without a tanween and for the tanween to be deleted due to the meeting of two quiescent letters.
36:41: The Almighty's saying: And a sign for them has three possible meanings: First, a lesson for them, because in the signs there is a consideration. Second, a blessing for them, because in the signs there is a blessing. Third, a warning for them, because in the signs there is a warning. Indeed, We carried their offspring in the laden ark is one of the most difficult things in the surah, because they are the ones who are carried. It was said that the meaning is: And a sign for the people of Mecca that We carried the offspring of past generations <in the laden ark>. So the two pronouns are different. This was mentioned by Al-Mahdawi. An-Nahhas narrated it on the authority of Ali bin Sulaiman that he heard him say it. It was also said that both pronouns refer to the people of Mecca, on the condition that their offspring are their children and the weak among them. So, according to the first opinion, the ark is Noah's ship. According to the second opinion, it is a generic noun, informing the Almighty of His kindness and grace that He created ships in which He carries those who find it difficult to walk and ride from among the offspring and the weak. So, on this basis, the two pronouns are in agreement. It was said: The offspring are the fathers and grandfathers, whom God the Almighty carried in Noah’s ark, peace be upon him. So the fathers are offspring and the sons are offspring, as evidenced by this verse, said Abu Uthman. And the fathers were called offspring, because the offspring of the sons were from them. A fourth saying: The offspring are the sperm that God the Almighty carried in the wombs of women, likening it to the laden ark, said Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, mentioned by Al-Mawardi. The derivation of offspring and the discussion of it has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. And the laden means the filled and the honored, and the ark can be singular and plural. And the discussion of it has already been mentioned in Surat Yunus.
36:42: The Almighty said: And We created for them from the like thereof that on which they ride. The original form is yakribbuhu but the ha' was dropped due to the length of the name and because it is the head of a verse. There are three opinions regarding its meaning: the school of thought of Mujahid, Qatadah and a group of the people of interpretation. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas that the meaning of from the like thereof for camels is that He created them for them to ride on land like the ships ridden in the sea, and the Arabs liken camels to ships. Tarafa said: As if the Malikis’ borders were the cells of a ship in the storms of Dd Plural of cell and in the great ship. The second opinion is that it refers to camels and beasts and everything that is ridden. The third opinion is that it refers to ships. An-Nahhas: This is the most correct because it has a continuous chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And We created for them from the like thereof that which they ride. He said: He created for them ships like them that they ride in. Abu Malik said: They are the small ships that He created like the big ships. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Al-Hasan. Ad-Dahhak and others said: They are the ships that were built after Noah’s Ark. Al-Mawardi said: A fifth opinion is based on the interpretation of Ali may God be pleased with him that the offspring in the laden ark are in the sperm in the wombs of women. In his statement, And We created for them from the like thereof that which they ride, that its interpretation is that women were created for the husbands to ride, but I have not seen it narrated.
36:43: The Almighty said: And if We will, We can drown them meaning in the sea, so the metaphor refers to the offspring or to all of them. This indicates the correctness of the statement of Ibn Abbas and those who said that what is meant by of his like are the ships, not the camels. So they will have no one to cry out to means they will have no helper. Narrated by Saeed from Qatadah. Shaiban narrated from him: They will have no protection, and their meanings are close. Crying means crying out and Fa'il means Fa'il. So they will have no one to cry to is permissible, because after it is what only allows for the nominative case, since it is definite, which is nor will they be saved. The grammarians prefer neither a man is in the house, nor Zaid. The meaning of they will be saved is that they will be saved from drowning. It was also said: from the torment.
36:44: Except for mercy from Us. Al-Kisa'i said: It is accusative of exception. Al-Zajjaj said: It is an accusative object for the sake of which, meaning for the mercy. And enjoyment is conjoined with it. Until a time means until death, as Qatadah said. Yahya ibn Salam said: Until the Resurrection, meaning unless We have mercy on them and provide for them until their appointed times. And that God hastened the punishment of the previous nations, and delayed the punishment of the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, even though they denied him, until death and the Resurrection.
36:45: God the Almighty says: And when it is said to them, Fear what is before you and what is behind you," Qatada said: "It means, 'Fear what is before you,' meaning, of the events that happened to the nations before you, and 'what is behind you' of the Hereafter." Ibn Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, and Mujahid said: "What is before you is what has passed of sins, and 'what is behind you' is what will come of sins." Al-Hasan said: "What is before you is what has passed of your life, and 'what is behind you' is what remains of it." It was also said: "What is before you is of this world, and 'what is behind you' is the punishment of the Hereafter," as Sufyan said. Al-Tha'labi narrated the opposite of this statement from Ibn Abbas. He said: "What is before you is of the matter of the Hereafter and what they did for it, and 'what is behind you' is of the matter of this world, so beware of it and do not be deceived by it." It was also said: "What is before you is what is apparent to you, and 'what is behind you' is what is hidden from you." The answer is omitted, and the meaning is: If they were told that, they would turn away. The evidence for this is his statement after that: And there does not come to them a sign from the signs of their Lord except that they turn away from it. So this is sufficient instead of that.
36:46: And there does not come to them a sign from the signs of their Lord except that they turn away from it. So this is sufficient for that.
36:47: God the Almighty says: And when it is said to them, 'Spend from what God has provided you,' meaning, give charity to the poor. Al-Hasan said: This means the Jews who were ordered to feed the poor. It was also said that they were the polytheists. The poor companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to them: Give us what you claim of your wealth is for God. This is due to God's statement: And they have assigned to God a share of what He has created of tilth and livestock. (Al-An'am 6:136) So they forbade them and said, If God had willed, He could have fed you, mockingly, but we will not feed you until you return to our religion. They said, Should we feed? meaning, Should we provide for someone whom God would feed if He willed? They had heard the Muslims say that God is the Provider. So they mockingly said, Should we provide for someone whom God would make rich if He willed? Ibn Abbas reported: There were heretics in Mecca, and when they were ordered to give charity to the poor, they said, No, by God! Would God make him poor while we feed him? They used to hear the believers linking the actions of God to the will of God, saying: If God had willed, He would have enriched so-and-so; if God had willed, He would have honored him; if God had willed, it would have been such-and-such. They gave this answer as a mockery of the believers and what they used to say about linking matters to the will of God. It was also said that they said this in connection with the words of the believers to them: Spend from that which God has provided for you (Ya-Sin 36:47). That is, if God has provided for us, He is able to provide for you, so why do you seek provision from us? This argument was invalid, because when God, the Most High, gives a servant wealth and then obligates him to take a right to it, it is as if He has taken that amount from him, so there is no point in objecting. They were truthful in their statement: If God had willed, He would have fed them, but they lied in their argument. And similar to this is His statement: Those who associate others with God will say, ‘If God had willed, we would not have associated others with Him.’ (Al-An’am 6:148), and His statement: They said, ‘We bear witness that you are the Messenger of God.’ And God knows that you are His Messenger, and God bears witness that the hypocrites are liars. (Al-Munafiqun 62:1) You are not but in manifest error. It was said that this is from what the disbelievers said to the believers, i.e., in asking for money and following Muhammad. Muqatil and others said its meaning. It was also said that this is from what the companions of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said to them. It was also said that this is from what God the Most High said to the disbelievers when they responded with this answer. It was also said that Abu Bakr As-Siddiq may God be pleased with him used to feed the poor Muslims when Abu Jahl met him and said, O Abu Bakr, do you claim that God is able to feed these people? He said, Yes. He said, Then why did he not feed them? He said, He tested some people with poverty and others with wealth, and He commanded the poor to be patient and commanded the rich to give. He said, By God, O Abu Bakr, you are not but in error! Do you claim that God is able to feed these people, but He does not feed them, and then you feed them?! Then this verse was revealed, and the words of God the Almighty were revealed: But as for him who gives and fears God * And believes in the best reward (al-Layl 92:5-6) and the verses. It was said that the verse was revealed about a group of heretics, and there were people among them who were heretics and did not believe in the Creator, and they mocked the Muslims with this and this saying. This was mentioned by Al-Qushayri and Al-Mawardi.
36:48: God Almighty says: And they say, ‘When will this promise come to pass?’ When it was said to them: Fear what is before you and what is behind you, they said: When will this promise come to pass? This was also a mockery from them, meaning that this threat will not be fulfilled.
36:49: God the Most High said: They are not awaiting meaning they are not waiting except for a single blast which is the blast of Israfil that will seize them while they are disputing meaning they are disputing about worldly matters and they will die on the spot, and this is the blast of the thunderbolt. There are five readings forيْشْنمفونthey are disputing: Abu Amr and Ibn Kathir read:ونونى يْشْنمفونthey are disputing with a fat-ha on the ya' and kha' and a shaddah on the sa'd. Warsh narrated this from Nafi' in the same way. As for the people of the readings and the companions of Nafi' apart from Warsh, they narrated from himونىْشْنمفونthey are disputing with a sukoon on the kha' and a shaddah on the sa'd, combining two sukoon letters. Yahya ibn Waththab, Al-A'mash and Hamzah read:ونى يْشْنمفون they are disputing with a sukoon on the kha' and a softened sa'd from ِْنِهمف. Asim and Al-Kisa'i readونى يْشْنمفونthey are disputing with a kasra on the kha' and a shaddah on the sa'd, and its meaning is that they are disputing with one another. It was said: It will take them while they are disputing with themselves about the argument that they will not be resurrected. Ibn Jubayr narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr on the authority of Asim, and Hammad on the authority of Asim, with the kasra on the ya and the kha and the shaddah. An-Nahhas said: The first reading is clearer, and the original is yachthasamoon, so the ta was assimilated into the sad and its vowel was transferred to the kha. In the letter of Abi < wa-hama yachthasamoon >- and the sukoon on the kha is not permissible, because it combines two sukoon letters, neither of which is a long vowel or a soft letter. It was said: They sukooned the kha as it was originally, and the meaning is they are disputing with each other, so the complement was deleted. It is possible that the meaning is they are disputing with their disputants about themselves, so the object was deleted. Al-Tha’labi said: It is the reading of Abi bin Ka’b. An-Nahhas said: As for < yakhṣamūn >, the original is also yachthasamoon, so the ta was assimilated into the sad and then the kha was kasra due to the meeting of two sukoon letters. Al-Farraa claimed that this reading is better and more numerous, so he left what is more appropriate, which is to put a vowel on the taa’ before the kha’ and brought a vowel for it and combined a yaa’ and a kasra, and he claimed that it is better and more numerous. How can it be more numerous when the people of Mecca, Basra and Medina read it with a fatha! What was narrated from ‘Aasim about the kasra on the yaa’ and the kha’ is for imitation. This has already been mentioned in Surah Al-Baqarah in He snatches away their sight (Al-Baqarah 2:2) and in Surah Yunus in He guides (Yunus 10:35). ‘Ikrimah said regarding the words of God, the Almighty, except for a single blast, that it is the first blast of the trumpet. Abu Hurairah said: The trumpet will be blown while the people are in their markets: whoever is milking will milk his camel, whoever is measuring a garment, and whoever is passing by for a need. Na`im narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Hour will come while two men have spread out their garments to sell, but they will not fold them until the Hour comes. A man will fill his trough to water his livestock, but he will not water them until the Hour comes. A man will lower his scales, but he will not raise them until the Hour comes. A man will raise his food to his mouth, but he will not swallow it until the Hour comes.” And in the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar: The first one to hear it will be a man filling his camels’ trough - he said - and he will faint, and the people will faint.
36:50: They cannot make a will meaning some of them cannot make a will to others regarding what is in their possession of a right. It was also said: Some of them cannot recommend to each other repentance and abstinence, rather they die in their markets and places. Nor will they return to their families means they die. It was also said: The meaning of Nor will they return to their families is they will not return to them with a word. Qatada said: Nor will they return to their families meaning to their homes, because they have hastened to do so.
36:51: The Almighty says: And the Trumpet will be blown. This is the second blast of creation. We explained in Surah An-Naml that there will be two blasts, not three. This verse is indicative of that. Al-Mubarak ibn Fadalah narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan that he said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Between the two blasts will be forty years: the first in which God will cause every living thing to die, and the second in which God will bring every dead thing to life. Qatada said: The word trumpet is the plural of sawrah, meaning the blown trumpet and the spirits. Sawrah and sawwar are like in Surah Al-Bina' and Surahs. Al-Ajjaj said: And there is a man with a closed canopy that I went to at the top of the wall It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he recited: And the Trumpet will be blown. An-Nahhas: The correct view is that the Trumpet with a sukoon on the waw means the horn. This was transmitted by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this is well-known in the speech of the Arabs. The linguists recited: We crushed them on the day of Al-Ghorin with hammers in the dust of Al-Naqain * A violent butt, not like the butt of two pictures * This has already been fully discussed in <Al-An'am>. And when they are from the graves meaning the tombs. It was read with a fa’ in <from the graves>, mentioned by Al-Zamakhshari. It is said: Jadath and Jadaf. The eloquent language is Al-Jadath with a tha’, and the plural is Ajdaath and Ajdaath. Al-Mutanahel Al-Hudhali said: I know the most recent, and I have learned the signs of the ink patterns. And he made an effort: that is, he took a grave. To their Lord they will hasten that is, they will go out, as Ibn Abbas and Qatada said. And from this is the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: *Take my clothes from your clothes and you will slip away* And from this comes the word nasil for the child, because he comes out of his mother’s womb. And it was said: they hasten. And nasilan and asalan: is to hasten in walking, and from this comes the gait of the wolf. He said: The wolf's lion became a boat, and the night became cold upon him, so he slipped away. It is said: the honey of the wolf and offspring, ya’sal and yansal, from the same root as daraba yadrubu. It is also said: yansal with dammah. It is to walk quickly, so the meaning is that they come out quickly. In the revelation: He did not create you and resurrect you except as a single soul (Luqman 31:28), and He said: They emerge from the graves as if they were locusts spreading out (al-Qamar 54:7) and in A questioner asked: On the Day they emerge from the graves quickly as if they were, toward an idol, dispersing (al-Ma’arij 70:43) meaning they hasten. And in the report: We complained to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about our weakness, and he said: Walk quickly, for it energizes you.
36:52: The Almighty said: They said, 'Woe to us!' Ibn al-Anbari said: <Woe to us!>is a good pause, then you can begin with Who has resurrected us?" It was narrated from some of the reciters: "<Woe to us! Who has resurrected us?> with a kasra on min and a tha' from ba'ath." This was narrated from Ali, may God be pleased with him. According to this school of thought, it is not appropriate to pause at the phrase "Woe to us! until one says from our sleeping place." In the recitation of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, it was: "Who has awakened us? with a connected from our sleeping place." This is evidence of the correctness of the school of thought of the common people. Al-Mahdawi said: Ibn Abi Layla read: "They said, 'Woe to us!' with an additional ta', which is the feminine of woe." Similar to it is: "Woe to me! Will I give birth when I am an old woman?" (Hud 11:72). And Ali may God be pleased with him recited: O woe to us who will afflict us! So from is related to the woe or a state of wealta so it is related to something omitted, as if he said: O woe to us, whoever afflicts us. And as it is possible for it to be a predicate of it, it is also possible for it to be a state of it. And from in His statement: from our sleeping place is related to the resurrection itself. Then it was said: How did they say this while they are among those being tormented in their graves? The answer is that Ubayy ibn Ka’b said: They sleep a sleep. And in another narration: They say: O woe to us who has afflicted us from our sleeping place. Abu Bakr al-Anbari said: This hadith should not be interpreted as meaning that ahbana is from the wording of the Qur’an as has been said by those who have attacked the Qur’an, but it is an explanation of ba’athana or an expression of some of its meanings. Abu Bakr said: And this is how I memorized it: from ahbana without an alif in ahbana and with a sukoon on the noon of min. The correct form of it, according to the language, is <min ahabna>with a fatha on the noon, given that the fatha on the hamza of ahab was placed on the noon of <min>and the hamza was dropped, as the Arabs said: Who informed you, who informed you? They mean who informed you. It is also said: I awoke the sleeper, so he awoke the sleeper. Ahmad bin Yahya al-Nahwi recited to us: A critic came at night to blame me, and no critic had ever lived before me. Abu Saleh said: When the first blast is blown, the torment will be lifted from the people of the graves, and they will sleep until the second blast, with forty years between them. This is what they will say: Who has raised us from our beds? Ibn Abbas and Qatada said the same. The scholars of semantics said: When the disbelievers see Hell and the types of torment in it, what they were tormented with in their graves will be compared to their torment, like sleep. Mujahid said: Then the believers will say to them: This is what the Most Gracious has promised. Qatada said: Then those whom God has guided will say to them: This is what the Most Gracious has promised. Al-Farra’ said: Then the angels will say to them: This is what the Most Gracious has promised. An-Nahhas said: These statements are in agreement, because the angels are among the believers and among those whom God has guided. And on this basis, the statement of God, the Almighty, is interpreted: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - those are the best of creation [Al-Bayyinah 7]. Likewise, the hadith, The believer in the sight of God is better than all that He has created. It is possible that the angels, peace be upon them, and other believers said to them: This is what the Most Gracious has promised. It was also said that when the disbelievers said to one another: Who has raised us from our beds? they believed the messengers when they witnessed what they had told them. Then they said: This is what the Most Gracious promised and the messengers spoke the truth, but we denied it. They acknowledged it when acknowledgment was of no use to them. Hafs would pause at from our beds and then begin by saying: This. Abu Bakr ibn al-Anbari said: Who has raised us from our beds is a good pause, then begin: This is what the Most Gracious has promised.
