It is permissible to pause at this of our beds, lowering this to follow bed, and begin with this is what the Most Gracious has promised, meaning that what the Most Gracious has promised has raised you, meaning what the Most Gracious has promised has raised you. An-Nahhas: The completion is on <from our resting place>and <this>in the nominative case as the subject and its predicate is <what the Most Gracious has promised>. It is also permissible for it to be in the accusative case as an adjective for <our resting place>, so the completion is <from this resting place>. <what the Most Gracious has promised>is in the nominative case in three ways. Abu Ishaq mentioned two of them. He said: It is by implying this. The second way is that it means the truth of what the Most Gracious has promised is that He has sent you. The third way is that it means that He has sent you what the Most Gracious has promised.
36:53: It will be but a single blast means that their resurrection and revival will be with a single blast, which is the saying of Israfil: O decayed bones, severed limbs, and torn hair! God commands you to gather for the passing of judgment. This is the meaning of His, the Truthful, saying: The Day they hear the blast in truth, that is the Day of Resurrection (Qaf: 42). And He said: Rushing to the Caller (al-Qamar 54:8), as will be mentioned later. And in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, if it is authentic from him, it is: It will be but a single wineskin, and the wineskin is the blast, and this has been mentioned previously. Then they will all be brought before Us <Then they will all be brought before Us <Then they will all be brought before Us <Then they will all be brought before Us" is the subject and its predicate is <all>indefinite, and <brought before>is from its description. The meaning of <brought before>is gathered and brought to the place of reckoning, which is like His saying: "And the matter of the Hour will not be but as the twinkling of an eye" (al-Nahl 16:77).
36:54: The Almighty says: So today no soul will be wronged at all meaning no reward for any action will be reduced. You will not be recompensed except for what you used to do <ma>is in the accusative case in two ways: The first is that it is a second object for something whose agent is not named. The second is by removing the adjective letter, meaning: except for what you used to do, meaning what you used to do, so it was deleted.
36:55: The Almighty said: Indeed, the companions of Paradise, that Day, will be occupied with amusement. Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and Mujahid said: Their occupation will be deflowering virgins. At-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim mentioned in his book Mushkil Al-Quran: Muhammad ibn Hamid Al-Razi told us, Ya'qub Al-Qummi told us, on the authority of Hafs ibn Hamid, on the authority of Shimr ibn Atiyyah, on the authority of Shaqiq ibn Salamah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, regarding His statement: Indeed, the companions of Paradise, that Day, will be occupied with amusement. He said: Their occupation will be deflowering virgins. Muhammad ibn Hamid told us, Harun ibn Al-Mughira told us, on the authority of Nahshal, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly. Abu Qilabah said: While a man from the people of Paradise is with his family, it will be said to him, Move back to your family, and he will say, I am busy with my family, and he will be told, Move back to your family as well. It was said: The people of Paradise will be too busy with their own pleasures and comforts to care about the sinners and their destination to the Fire, and the painful torment they will face, even if their relatives and family are among them. This was stated by Saeed ibn al-Musayyab and others. Waki' said: He means listening to music. Ibn Kaysan said: Busy means visiting one another. It was also said: As guests of God the Almighty. It was narrated that on the Day of Resurrection, a caller will call out: Where are My servants who obeyed Me and kept My covenant in secret? They will rise as if their faces were the full moon and the shining star, riding on mounts of light with reins of ruby, flying over the heads of creation, until they stand before the Throne. God the Almighty will say to them: Peace be upon My servants who obeyed Me and kept My covenant in secret. I have chosen you and selected you and selected you. Go and enter Paradise without being held to account, for there will be no fear concerning you, nor will you grieve. They will pass over the Sirat like a flash of lightning, and its gates will be opened for them. Then the creation will be stopped at the gathering place, and some of them will say to one another: O people, where is so-and-so and so-and-so?! That will be when they will ask one another, and a caller will call out, Indeed, the companions of Paradise, that Day, will be occupied and enjoying themselves. “Shaghal” and Shughl are two dialects that are recited in, like terror and terrorism, and saht and saht, as mentioned earlier. Fakihoon meaning delighted: Al-Hasan said: They are pleased. Ibn Abbas said: They are happy. Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak said: They are impressed. As-Suddi said: They are relaxed. The meanings are close. Humor is joking and pleasant speech. Abu Ja`far, Shaibah, and Al-A`raj read: Fakihoon without an alif, and they are two dialects like farah and farah, and haḍir and haḍir, as Al-Farra’ said. Al-Kisa’i and Abu Ubaidah said: Fakih means the one who has fruits, like sha’ham and wa la ham and tamar and wa la ban, and fakkah means the one who is amused and indulgent. <fakahun>without alif in Qatada’s saying: admirers. Abu Zaid said: a man is said to be funny if he is of a good nature and laughs. Talha bin Musarraf read <fakahin>in the accusative case as a state.
36:56: They and their spouses will be in shades, reclining on couches is a subject and predicate. It is possible that <they>is an emphasis, <and their spouses>is an appositive to the pronoun, and <reclining>is an adjective for <enjoying>. The general reading is: <in shades>with a kasra on the dhaal and the alif. Ibn Mas'ud, Ubayd ibn 'Umair, al-A'mash, Yahya, Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Khalaf read: in <shall>with a damma on the dhaal without an alif. So shade is the plural of shade, and shade is the plural of shade. On couches means beds in curtains, the singular of which is couch, like ship and ships. The poet said: As if the redness of the roses on its branches at noon in the laughing garden The cheeks of virgins, ashamed of modesty, are swaying with basil on the couches. In the hadith: “On the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whenever the people of Paradise have intercourse with their women, they will return as virgins.’” Ibn Abbas said: “A man from the people of Paradise will embrace a houri for seventy years, never tiring of her and she not tiring of him. Whenever he comes to her, he will find her a virgin, and whenever he returns to her, his desire returns to him. He will have intercourse with her with the strength of seventy men, and there will be no semen between them. He will ejaculate without semen from him or from her.”
36:57: For them therein is fruit is subject and predicate. And for them is whatever they call for The second dal is replaced by a ta' because yafta'ulun is derived from da'a, meaning that whoever calls for something will be given it. Abu Ubaidah said this, so the meaning of <yadhoo'un>is that they wish for something from the supplication. It was also said that the meaning is that whoever calls for something from it, it is his, because God has created them so that no one among them can call upon anything except what is appropriate and good to call upon. Yahya ibn Salam said: <yadhoo'un>means they desire. Ibn Abbas said: they ask. The meanings are close. Ibn al-Anbari said: <and for them is whatever they call upon>is a good pause, then you begin: <peace>meaning that for them is peace. It is permissible to raise peace to mean and for them is whatever they call upon, a pure Muslim. So according to this school of thought, it is not appropriate to stop at <ma d'ahoo'un>. Al-Zajjaj said: <peace>is raised as a substitute for <ma>meaning and for them is that God sends peace upon them, and this is the desire of the people of Paradise.
36:58: "It was narrated from the hadith of Jarir ibn Abdullah al-Bajali that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: While the people of Paradise were enjoying their bliss, a light shone for them. They raised their heads and behold, the Lord Almighty looked down upon them from above and said, 'Peace be upon you, O people of Paradise.' This is His saying: 'Peace, a word from a Merciful Lord.' He looked at them and they looked at Him, and they did not turn to any of the bliss as long as they were looking at Him until He was hidden from them, and His light and blessings remained upon them in their homes." This was mentioned by al-Tha'labi and al-Qushayri. Its meaning is established in Sahih Muslim, and we have already explained it in <Yunus>when God, the Most High, said: For those who have done good is the best [reward] and even more. (Yunus 10:26) It is permissible for <ma>to be indefinite and <salam>to be an attribute of it, meaning, And for them is what they call upon Muslim. It is also permissible for <ma>to be in the nominative case as a subject, and <salam>to be a predicate of it. Based on these aspects, one should not pause at <and for them is what they call upon>. In Ibn Mas'ud's reading, "Peace" can be a verbal noun, or in the accusative case if you wish, meaning, and for them is what they call for, meaning, and for them is what they call for, meaning, "peace" or safety, or a Muslim. According to this school of thought, it is not appropriate to stop at they call for. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi read "peace" as a new sentence, as if he said, "That is peace for them, over which they will not dispute". Thus, and for them is what they call for is complete. It is permissible for "peace" to be a substitute for and for them is what they call for, and the predicate of what they call for is for them. It is permissible for "peace" to be another predicate, and the meaning of the statement is that it is theirs alone and without dispute. A statement is a verbal noun meaning, God said that a statement, or by His saying a statement. The deleted verb is indicated by the wording of its verbal noun. It is permissible for the meaning to be, and for them is what they call for a statement, meaning, a promise from God. According to this second school of thought, it is not appropriate to stop at they call for. Al-Sijistani said, A stop at his saying, peace" is complete. This is a mistake because the statement is excluded from what precedes it.
36:59: God the Almighty said: And separate yourselves this Day, O criminals. It is said that they were separated, were set apart, and were distinguished with the same meaning. I distinguished him, so he was separated and was distinguished, and distinguished him, so he was distinguished. That is, this will be said to them when they stand for questioning when the people of Paradise are ordered to Paradise, meaning, leave their group. Qatada said: They will be isolated from all good. Ad-Dahhak said: The criminals will be separated from one another, so the Jews will be separated into a group, the Christians into a group, the Magians into a group, the Sabians into a group, and the idol worshippers into a group. It was also said: For every group in Hellfire, there is a house that they enter and close its door, so they will be in it forever, neither seeing nor being seen. Rawad ibn al-Jarrah said: The Muslims will be separated from the criminals, except for the people of desires, who will be with the criminals.
36:60: God Almighty says: Did I not enjoin upon you, O children of Adam? The covenant here means the commandment, that is, did I not command you and convey to you through the tongues of the messengers that you not worship Satan that is, do not obey him in disobeying Me.
36:61: Al-Kisa'i said: La is for prohibition. And worship Me with a kasra on the noon, as is the original, and whoever pronounces it with a damma dislikes a kasra followed by a damma. This is a straight path means My worship is a straight religion.
36:62: The Almighty said: And He has certainly led astray from among you meaning He has led astray a great multitude meaning a great many creations, as stated by Mujahid. Qatadah: Many multitudes. Al-Kalbi: Many nations, and the meaning is the same. The people of Medina and Asim read: <a mountain>with a kasra on the jim and the ba'. Abu Amr and Ibn Amir read <a mountain>with a damma on the jim and a sukoon on the ba'. The rest read <a mountain>with a damma on the jim and the ba' and a soft lam, and Al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Isa ibn Umar, Abdullah ibn Ubaid, and An-Nadr ibn Anas stressed it. Abu Yahya and Al-Ashhab Al-Uqaili read <a mountain>with a kasra on the jim, a sukoon on the ba', and a soft lam. So these are five readings. Al-Mahdawi and Al-Tha'labi said: All of them are dialects meaning creation. An-Nahhas: The first reading is clear, and the evidence for that is that they agreed that they read and the first generations (Ash-Shu’ara’: 184), so mountain is the plural of jabalah, and the derivation is all the same. It is from God created the creation, meaning He created them. A sixth reading has been mentioned, which is: And He has certainly led astray from among you a great generation, with the letter ya. It was narrated from Ad-Dahhak that one generation is ten thousand, and the many are what only God, the Almighty, can count. Al-Mawardi mentioned it, Did you not understand? His enmity and know that it is obligatory to obey God.
36:63: This is Hell, meaning the keepers of Hell will say to them, This is the Hell which you were promised but denied. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, God will gather mankind and the jinn, the first and the last, on one plain, then a neck of fire will rise over the creation and surround them. Then a crier will call out, "This is the Hell which you were promised. * Burn in it today for what you used to disbelieve." At that time, the nations will kneel, every pregnant woman will abort her pregnancy, and every nursing mother will forget what she was nursing, and you will see the people as if they were drunk, but they are not drunk, but the punishment of God is severe."
36:64: Perform it today for what you used to disbelieve.
36:65: The Almighty said: This Day We will seal up their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness about what they used to earn. And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he laughed. He said: Do you know why I laugh? We said: And God and His Messenger know best. He said: "From the servant addressing his Lord, saying: 'O Lord, did you not save me from injustice?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then I will not accept against myself except a witness from me.' He said: 'Then he said: 'Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a witness, and the noble scribes are witnesses.' He said: 'Then his mouth will be sealed and it will be said to his limbs: 'Speak.' He said: 'And they will speak of his deeds.' He said: 'Then he will be left alone to speak, and he will say: 'Away with you and away from you! I was struggling against you.'" [Also narrated by Muslim] on the authority of Abu Hurayrah. And in it: 'Then it will be said to him: 'Now We will send Our witness against you.' He will think to himself: 'Who is it that will bear witness against me?' So his mouth will be sealed and it will be said to his thigh, his flesh, and his bones: 'Speak.' So his thigh, his flesh, and his bones will speak.' By his work, so that he may excuse himself, and that is the hypocrite, and that is the one with whom God is angry. And Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Muawiyah bin Haidah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a hadith he mentioned, he said: And he pointed with his hand to Ash-Sham and said: From here to here you will be gathered, riding and walking, and you will be dragged on your faces on the Day of Resurrection. On your mouths will be seventy nations, you are the best of them and the most honored in the sight of God. And the first thing that will be expressed about any one of you will be his thigh. And in another narration: his thigh and his hand. The fadam is the strainer of the jug and the pitcher, as stated by Al-Layth. Abu Ubaid said: He means that they were prevented from speaking until their thighs spoke, so he likened that to the fadam that is placed on the pitcher. Then four aspects were said regarding the reason for the seal: The first is because they said: By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists (Al-An’am 6:23), so God sealed their mouths until their limbs spoke, as stated by Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari. The second is so that the people of the gathering would recognize them and distinguish them from them, as stated by Ibn Ziyad. The third is because the confession of a non-speaking person is more eloquent in proof than the confession of a speaking person, because it is presented in a miraculous manner, even though one day it will not need a miraculous nature. The fourth is so that it is known that his limbs that were They are helpers in his own right, and they have become witnesses against him in the right of his Lord. If it is said: Why did He say, And their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness, making what comes from the hand speech, and what comes from the foot testimony? It is said: The hand directly performs his action, and the foot is present, and the statement of one who is present against another is testimony, and the statement of the doer against himself is an admission of what he said or did. Therefore, what comes from the hands is expressed as speech, and what comes from the feet is expressed as testimony. It has been narrated from Uqbah ibn Amir that he heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say, The first bone of man to speak on the Day when mouths are sealed will be his left thigh. This was mentioned by al-Mawardi and al-Mahdawi. Abu Musa al-Ash’ari said, I believe that the first part to speak will be his right thigh. This was also mentioned by al-Mahdawi. Al-Mawardi said, “It is possible that the thigh comes before the other limbs in speaking, because he perceives the pleasure of his sins through his senses, which are in the lower part of them, the thigh. Therefore, due to its proximity to them, it is permissible for it to come before the other limbs in testifying against them.” He said: The left side is preferred because desire is stronger in the right side of the limbs than in the left side. Therefore, the left side is preferred over the right side due to its lower desire. I said: Or vice versa, due to the predominance of desire, or both of them together and abstinence, for the sum of that is the completion of desire and pleasure. And God knows best.
36:66: The Almighty says: "And if We willed, We could have obliterated their eyes, and they would race across the path. But how could they see?" Al-Kisa'i said: tamās, yatmaṣ, and yatmaṣ. According to the linguists, the one who is obliterated and tams is the blind man who has no slit in his eyes. Ibn Abbas said: The meaning is that We would have blinded them from guidance, so they would never be guided to the path of truth. Al-Hasan and Al-Suddi said: The meaning is that We would have left them blind, wandering about. So the meaning is that We would have blinded them, so they would not see a way to their homes or elsewhere. This is the preferred interpretation of Al-Tabari. His statement: And they would race across the path means they would race across the path to cross. <How could they see?>means from where can they see? Ata', Muqatil, Qatada, and it was narrated from Ibn Abbas: “And if We willed, We could have gouged out the eyes of their misguidance, blinded them to their error, and turned their sight from misguidance to guidance, so they would be guided and see their right path, and hastened to the path of the Hereafter.” Then He said: How then will they see? But You did not do that to them, meaning, how can they be guided while the eye of guidance is extinguished, remaining in misguidance? It was narrated from Abdullah ibn Salam in the interpretation of this verse other than what was mentioned, and he interpreted it as referring to the Day of Resurrection. He said: When the Day of Resurrection comes and the Bridge is extended, a caller will call out for Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his nation to arise, so the righteous among them will arise and the wicked among them will follow him to cross the Bridge. When they reach it, God will blind the eyes of their wicked, so they will race to the Bridge, so how can they see it until they cross it? Then a caller will call for Jesus (peace be upon him) and his nation to arise. He will arise and the righteous and the wicked among them will follow him, and that will be their path. And so will the rest of the prophets (peace be upon them). An-Nahhas mentioned it, and we have written it in At-Tadhkira with its meaning, as Ibn Al-Mubarak mentioned in his Raqa’iq. Al-Qushayri also mentioned it. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: Al-Aswad bin Al-Aswad took a stone with a group of Banu Makhzum to throw it at the Prophet (peace be upon him), but God blinded his sight and stuck the stone to his hand. He could not see it and could not find his way. And the verse was revealed about him. The one who is blurred is the one who has no slit between his eyelids. It is taken from the word to obliterate when the wind blurts the trace, as Al-Akhfash and Al-Qutbi said.
36:67: God the Almighty says: And if We willed, We could have transformed them in their places, so they would not have been able to proceed nor return. Transformation means changing the creation and turning it into stone, inanimate, or animal. Al-Hasan said: It means We would have made them sit down so they would not be able to proceed forward or return behind them. Similarly, inanimate objects do not advance or fall behind. Transformation may also mean changing the form of a human being into an animal, then that animal does not understand a place to aim for and is confused, so it does not accept or deviate. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: The meaning is, if We willed, We could have destroyed them in their dwellings. It was also said that the meaning is, if We willed, We could have transformed them in the place where they dared to commit the sin. Ibn Salam said: All of this will happen on the Day of Resurrection when God the Almighty will blind their eyes on the path. Al-Hasan, Al-Sulami, Zur ibn Hubaish, and Asim, and in the narration of Abu Bakr, read it: <their places>in the plural, the rest with the singular. Abu Haywah read: <they were not able to proceed>with a fat-ha on the meem. And the verb to go with a damma on the m is a verbal noun that means to go.
36:68: The Almighty said: And whomsoever We grant long life - We reverse him in creation. Asim and Hamza read <nankasahu>with a damma on the first noon and a shaddah on the kaf from tankees. The rest read <nankasahu>with a fatha on the first noon and a damma on the kaf from nakasatu al-shay' ankasahu nakas, meaning he turned something upside down and it was reversed. Qatada said: The meaning is that he becomes decrepit, similar to the state of youth. Sufyan said about the Almighty's saying: And whomsoever We grant long life - We reverse him in creation, when he reaches eighty years of age, his body changes and his strength weakens. The poet said: He who has lived, his days have worn him out and his two trusts, hearing and sight, have betrayed him. Long life turns youth into old age, strength into weakness, and increase into deficiency. This is what most often happens. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sought refuge from being sent back to the worst part of life. This has been explained in Surat An-Nahl. Do they not then understand? That the One Who did this to you is able to resurrect you. Nafi’ and Ibn Dhakwan read you understand with a ta’. The rest read it with a ya’.
36:69: The Almighty’s saying: And We have not taught him poetry, nor is it befitting for him. There are four issues in this: First: God Almighty informed us about the state of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and responded to the statement of those who said among the infidels that he was a poet, and that the Qur’an is poetry, by saying: And We have not taught him poetry, nor is it befitting for it. And likewise the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not recite poetry nor did he use its meter. And if he tried to recite an old verse in a simile, he would break its meter. He would only memorize the meanings, may God bless him and grant him peace. Among that is that he recited one day the words of Tarafa: Days will show you what you were ignorant of, and someone will come to you who you did not provide with report. One day, when he was asked who is the most poetic of people, he recited: Didn't you see that whenever I came knocking, I found her fragrant, even if she wasn't fragrant? And he recited one day: Do you make my loot and the loot of the slaves a hand between the bald and the bald? Peace be upon him, he would sometimes recite the straight verse in rare instances. It was narrated that he recited the verse of Abdullah bin Rawahah: He spends the night turning away from his bed when the polytheists make his beds heavy. Al-Hassan bin Abi Al-Hassan said: The Prophet, peace be upon him, recited: * Islam and gray hair are enough to deter a person * Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: O Messenger of God, the poet said: Kitten, if you are ready to go, gray hair is enough, and Islam is a prohibition for a person Abu Bakr or Umar said: I bear witness that you are the Messenger of God. God Almighty says: And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it befitting for him. And Al-Khalil bin Ahmad said: Poetry was more beloved to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, than much speech, but he could not master it. Second: His sometimes hitting the meter does not mean that he knows poetry, and likewise what sometimes comes from his prose speech that falls within his meter, like his saying on the day of Hunayn and others: Are you nothing but a finger that bled and suffered in the way of God? And his saying: I am the prophet, no lie, I am the son of Abdul Muttalib This may occur in verses of the Qur’an, and in every speech, but it is not poetry, nor does it have the same meaning, such as the saying of God the Almighty: By no means will you attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love (Al Imran 3:92) and His saying: Victory from God and an imminent conquest (As-Saff 67:13) and His saying: And basins like reservoirs and fixed cooking pots (Saba’ 34:13) and other verses. Ibn al-Arabi mentioned verses from them and discussed them and excluded them from the meter. However, Abu al-Hasan al-Akhfash said regarding His saying: I am the Prophet, there is no lie that it is not poetry. Al-Khalil said in Kitab al-‘Ayn that what comes from rhyme in two parts is not poetry. It was narrated from him that it is from the manhook of the rajaz. It was said: it is not from the manhook of the rajaz by stopping on the ba’ from his saying: There is no lie and from his saying Abd al-Muttalib but it is not known how the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said it. Ibn al-Arabi said: It is most apparent from his case that he said: No lie with the Ba' in the nominative case and with the Ba' in the genitive case from Abd al-Muttalib as an addition. An-Nahhas said: Some of them said: The narration is by i'rab, and if it is by i'rab, it is not poetry, because if the Ba' of the first verse is opened or closed or has a noon, and the Ba' of the second verse is broken, it is out of the meter of poetry. Some of them said: This meter is not poetry. This is stubbornness from the notables, because Arab poems on this basis have been narrated by Al-Khalil and others. As for his saying: Are you but a bloody finger? It was said that it is from the meter of sari', and that only happens if the Ta' of sama' is broken, because if it is sukun, it is not poetry at all, because these two words in this manner are fa'ul, and fa'ul has no place in the meter of sari'. Perhaps the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said with a sukun on the Ta' or a moving Ta' without saturation. The basis for the separation is that we assume that this is poetry, and the objection is dropped, and it does not necessarily mean that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was knowledgeable in poetry or a poet - that reciting a small verse and hitting the two rhymes of a rajaz or other poem does not necessarily mean that the one who recited it was knowledgeable in poetry, and he is not called a poet according to the consensus of scholars, just as someone who sews a thread is not a tailor. Abu Ishaq al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of And We did not teach him poetry is And We did not teach him to write meaning, We did not make him a poet. This does not prevent him from reciting some poetry. An-Nahhas said: This is one of the best things said on this subject. It has been said that God the Almighty only informed us that He did not teach him poetry, and He did not inform us that he would not recite poetry, and this is the apparent meaning of the statement. A clear statement was also made on this, and its author claimed that it is a consensus among the linguists, as they said: Whenever someone says something measuredly that is not intended as poetry, it is not poetry, but rather it is in accordance with poetry. This is a clear statement. They said: What God denied of his Prophet, peace be upon him, was the knowledge of poetry and its types, its meters and rhymes, and his being characterized by his speech. He was not described by consensus as such. Do you not see that the Quraysh debated over what to say to the Arabs about him when they came to them during the season? Some of them said: We say that he is a poet. The intelligent among them said: By God, the Arabs will surely lie to you, for they know all kinds of poetry, but by God, he does not resemble any of them, and his speech is not poetry. Anis, the brother of Abu Dharr, said: I attributed his speech to the recitations of poetry, but it did not agree that it is poetry. Narrated by Muslim. Anis was one of the most poetic Arabs. Likewise, when Utbah ibn Abi Rabi’ah spoke to him: By God, it is not poetry, nor soothsaying, nor magic, as will be explained in his story in Surah Fussilat, God willing. And others among the most eloquent of the Arabs and the most fluent of tongues said the same. Then, what comes out of the tongue in terms of measured speech is not considered poetry, but rather what is considered poetry is what is in the meter of poetry with the intention of it. For example, a speaker might say: Our sheikh told us and he calls out, ‘O companion of Al-Kisa’i!’ This is not considered poetry. A man would call out during his illness, and he was from the common, rational class: Take me to the doctor and say, ‘He has been cauterized.’ Third: Ibn al-Qasim narrated on the authority of Malik that he was asked about reciting poetry, so he said: Do not recite it too much, for one of its faults is that God says: And We have not taught him poetry, nor is it befitting for it. He said: It has reached me that Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him wrote to Abu Musa al-Ash’ari: Gather the poets who came before you and ask them about poetry and whether they still have any knowledge of it. So they brought Labid to him. He said: “So he gathered them and asked them, and they said: We know it and recite it.” So he asked Labid, and he said: “I have not recited poetry since I heard God the Almighty say: ‘Alif, Lam, Meem. This is the Book about which there is no doubt.’” (Al-Baqarah 2:2) Ibn al-Arabi said: This verse is not a fault in poetry, just as His statement: And you did not recite before it any book, nor did you inscribe it with your right hand (Al-Ankabut 29:48) is not a fault in writing. So illiteracy is not a fault in handwriting, and likewise denying the poetry of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) is not a fault in poetry.” It was narrated that Al-Ma'mun said to Abu Ali Al-Manqari: I have heard that you are illiterate, that you do not recite poetry, and that you make mistakes. He said: O Commander of the Faithful, as for the mistakes, perhaps I have slipped my tongue with something of them. As for illiteracy and broken poetry, the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, did not write or recite poetry. So he said to him, I asked you about three faults in yourself and you added a fourth, which is ignorance. O ignorant one! This was a virtue for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, but in you and your likes it is a shortcoming. The Prophet only forbade that to remove suspicion from him, not because of a fault in his poetry or writing. Fourth: The Almighty’s statement: And it is not befitting for him meaning it is not befitting for him to say it. God, the Exalted, the Majestic, made this a sign of His Prophet, peace be upon him, lest doubt enter into the mind of the one to whom he was sent, lest he think that he was strong in reciting the Quran due to his natural strength in poetry. An atheist cannot object to this because the meter of the Quran and the speech of the Messenger are in agreement, because whatever matches the meter of poetry and is not intended to be poetry is not poetry. If it were poetry, then every common person who spoke in a metered manner who does not know meter would be a poet, as was explained above. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of and it is not befitting for him is that it is not easy for him to say poetry, not composition. It meaning what he recites to you is nothing but a reminder and a clear Quran.
36:70: God the Almighty says: To warn whoever is alive meaning alive in heart, said Qatada. Ad-Dahhak: rational. It was also said that the meaning is: To warn whoever is a believer in God's knowledge. This is according to the reading of the ta', addressing the Prophet (peace be upon him), and it is the reading of Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir. The rest read it with the ya', meaning to warn God the Almighty or to warn Muhammad (peace be upon him), or to warn the Quran. It was narrated from Ibn As-Samiq' <liyanadhir>with the fatha on the ya' and the dhal. And the word will come into effect against the disbelievers meaning the argument based on the Quran will be made obligatory against the disbelievers.
36:71: The Almighty says: Have they not seen that We created for them This is the vision of the heart, meaning, have they not looked, considered, and contemplated. Of what Our hands have made Meaning, of what We have created and done without any intermediary, agency, or partnership. What means whom and the ha was deleted due to the length of the noun. If what was made a verbal noun, it would not have required the omission of the ha of the word. Cattle is the plural of na’am and na’am is masculine. So they are its owners Controlling and dominating.
36:72: And We have subjected it to them meaning We made it subservient to them so that the boy would lead the huge camel, beat it, and direct it as he wished, without disobeying it. From it is their riding The general reading is with a fatha on the ra', meaning their mount, as one says: a milking camel, meaning a milked camel. Al-A'mash, Al-Hasan, and Ibn Al-Sameeq read: <From it is their riding>with a damma on the ra' as a source. It was narrated from Aisha that she read: <From it is their riding>and this is how it is in her copy of the Qur'an. Riding and riding are one and the same, like milking and milking, and carrying and carrying. The Kufi grammarians reported that the Arabs say: a patient and thankful woman without a ha'. They also say: a milking sheep and a riding camel, because they wanted to differentiate between that which has the action and that which the action is performed upon, so they deleted the ha' from what was the subject and kept it in what was the object, as he said: It has forty-two black, milky ewes, as dark as a crow's tail. So it should be like this, their riding. As for the Basrans, they say: The ha’ was deleted for the sake of proportion. The evidence for the first opinion is what al-Jarmi narrated on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, who said: Riding can be for one person or a group, but riding can only be for a group. So on this basis, it is to remind the plural. Abu Hatim claimed that it is not permissible to say <Famhana rakubhum>with a damma on the ra’ because it is a verbal noun, and riding is that which is ridden. Al-Farra’ permitted <Famhana rakubhum>with a damma on the ra’, just as you say Famhana akalhum wa minha sharbakhum, and Wamhana yak’alu from its meat.
36:73: And they have benefits from them from their voices, fur, hair, fat, meat, and other things. And drinks means their milk. They were not declined because they are plurals that have no equivalent in one. Will they not then be grateful to God for His blessings.
36:74: The Almighty says: And they have taken besides God gods meaning they have seen these signs of Our power, then they have taken besides Us gods who have no power to act. Perhaps they will be aided because they hope for Our aid if a punishment befalls them. Some Arabs say: Perhaps he will do so.
36:75: They cannot help them meaning the gods. They used the plural with the waw and the nun because He spoke about them in the same way as humans. And they meaning the disbelievers, are an army present for them meaning the gods, a host present for them Al-Hasan said: They are prevented from them and repelled from them. Qatada said: They are angry on their behalf in this world. It was also said that the meaning is that they worship the gods and stand up for them, so they are like an army to them and they are unable to help them. These three sayings are close in meaning. It was also said that the gods are an army for the worshippers, present with them in the fire, so they cannot repel one another. It was also said that the meaning is that these idols are for these disbelievers God's army against them in hell, because they curse them and disavow worshipping them. It was also said that the gods are an army that will harm them on the Day of Resurrection because they aid them in their suspicions. In the report, it represents to every people what they used to worship in this world and follow it to the Fire, so they are a prepared army for them. I said: The meaning of this report is what was proven in Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, and in Al-Tirmidhi, from him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God will gather the people on the Day of Resurrection on one plain, then the Lord of the Worlds will look at them and say, Let every person follow what he used to worship. Then the one with the cross will have his cross, the one with the pictures will have his pictures, and the one with the fire will have his fire. Then they will follow what they used to worship, and the Muslims will remain.” He mentioned the hadith in full.
36:76: So do not let their statement grieve you. This is the eloquent language. Some Arabs say grieves you. The intention is to console their Prophet, peace be upon him, i.e., do not let their statement, that of a poet and magician, grieve you. The speech was completed, then he resumed, saying: Indeed, We know what they conceal and what they declare, of speech and action and what they show, so We will reward them accordingly.
36:77: The Almighty said: Has man not seen? Ibn Abbas said: Man is Abdullah bin Ubayy. Saeed bin Jubair said: He is Al-Aas bin Wa'il As-Sahmi. Al-Hasan said: He is Ubayy bin Khalaf Al-Jumahi. Ibn Ishaq said the same, and Ibn Wahb narrated it from Malik: We created him from a sperm-drop which is a small amount of water, sperm when it drips. Then he is a clear adversary meaning he argues in a dispute, explaining the argument. By that he means that he became a clear adversary after he was nothing worth mentioning. "That is because a decayed bone was brought to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: O Muhammad, do you think that God will revive this after it has rotted away? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes, and God will resurrect you and put you in Hell." Then this verse was revealed.
36:78: The Almighty said: “And he presented to Us an example and forgot his own creation. He said, ‘Who will give life to the bones when they have decayed?’” There are two issues in this: First: The Almighty’s statement: And he has presented to Us an example and has forgotten his creation. That is, he has forgotten that We created him from a dead sperm-drop and then put life into him. That is, his answer from himself is present. For this reason, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: Yes, and God will resurrect you and admit you to the Fire. This is evidence of the validity of analogy, because God, the Almighty and Majestic, provided evidence against those who deny the resurrection with the first creation. He said, ‘Who will give life to the bones when they are rotten?’ That is, worn out. The bone has rotted, so it is rotten and ashes. He said rumeem and not rameema because it is modified from its subject, and that which is modified from its proper form and weight is diverted from its i’rab, like His statement: And your mother was not unchaste. (Maryam 19:28) He dropped the ha because it is diverted from bagheeya. It was said that this disbeliever said to the Prophet (peace be upon him): Tell me, if I were to crush her and scatter her in the wind, would God bring her back? Then it was revealed: Say, ‘He will give it life who created it the first time.’ That is, from nothing, so He is able to bring it back to life in the second creation from something, which is the tailbone. It is also said that the tailbone is with the preposition ba. “And He is Knowing of all creation,” that is, how He begins and repeats. Second: In this verse is evidence that there is life in bones and that they become impure with death. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifa and some of the companions of Al-Shafi’i. Al-Shafi’i may God be pleased with him said: There is no life in them. This was previously mentioned in An-Nahl. If it is said that what he meant by His statement: Who gives life to the bones is the companions of the bones? The use of the complement in place of the complement to it is common in language and is found in the Shari’ah. We say that it only occurs when there is a necessity, and here there is no necessity that calls for this omission, nor is this estimation required, since the Creator, glory be to Him, has informed us of it and He is capable of it, and reality bears witness to it, since the sensation that is a sign of life is present in it, as Ibn Al-Arabi said.
36:80: The Almighty's saying: Who made for you fire from the green tree. God the Almighty pointed out His Oneness and indicated His perfect power in reviving the dead by what they witness of bringing the burnt dry thing out of the moist, fresh wood. This is because the unbeliever said: Semen is hot and moist by the nature of life, so life comes out of it. And the bone is cold and dry by the nature of death, so how can life come out of it?! So God the Almighty revealed: Who made for you fire from the green tree. That is, the green tree is made of water, and water is cold and moist, the opposite of fire, and these two do not mix. So God brought fire out of it. He is able to bring out opposites from opposites, and He is over all things competent. The verse refers to what is in the Markh and the A'far, which are the Arabs' flints. From this comes their saying: In every tree is fire. The Markh and the A'far solidify, so the A'far is the flint, which is the upper part, and the Markh is the flint, which is the lower part. Two branches are taken from them, like toothpicks, dripping water, and they are rubbed against each other, and fire comes out of them. He said: From the green tree, and he did not say al-khadra the green tree, which is a plural, because he referred it back to the word. Some Arabs say: The green tree, as God Almighty said: From a tree of Zaqqum, and therewith they will fill their bellies (al-Waqi’ah 56:52-53).
36:81: Then the Almighty said, arguing: Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them? That is, the likes of those who deny the resurrection. Salam Abu al-Mundhir and Ya`qub al-Hadrami read: is able to create the likes of them as a verb. Yes means that the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than their creation, so He who created the heavens and the earth is able to resurrect them. And He is the Creator, the Knowing. Al-Hasan read it differently from him: the Creator.
36:82: The Almighty said: His command is only when He intends a thing that He says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is. Al-Kisa’i read be in the accusative case in apposition to says, meaning that if He intends to create something, it does not require effort or preparation. This has been mentioned before in more than one place.
36:83: Glory be to Him in whose hand is the dominion over all things. He is far removed from weakness and polytheism. Malakut and Malakuti in Arabic language mean king. The Arabs say: My might is better than my mercy. Sa'id said on the authority of Qatadah: The dominion of all things are the keys to everything. Talhah ibn Musarraf, Ibrahim al-Taymi and al-A'mash read malakat which means kingdom, except that it is different from the Quran. And to Him you will be returned means you will be returned and go after your death. The general reading is with the ta' as an address. As-Sulami, Zur ibn Hubaish and the companions of Abdullah read they return with the ya' as a statement.
37:1: God the Almighty said: And those who line up in rows, * And those who drive away a driving * And those who recite the Reminder. This is the reading of most of the reciters. Hamzah recited with assimilation in both of them. This is the reading that Ahmad ibn Hanbal was repelled by when he heard it. An-Nahhas: It is far-fetched in Arabic for three reasons: First, that ta' is not from the point of articulation of sad, nor from the point of articulation of zay, nor from the point of articulation of dhal, nor from their sisters. Rather, its sisters are ta' and dal, and the sister of zay are sad and seen, and the sister of dhal are dha and tha. The second reason is that ta' is in one word and what follows it is in another word. The third reason is that when you assimilate, you combine two sukoon letters in two words. Combining two sukoon letters in such a situation is only permissible if they are in one word, such as dabah animal and shabah young woman. The figurative meaning of Hamzah's reading is that ta' has a close point of articulation compared to these letters. <By the assemblies>is an oath, the waw is a substitute for ba'. The meaning is Lord of those who rank up and those who repel in apposition to it.
37:2: God Almighty's saying: The rebukes are rebukes.
37:3: The Almighty said: And those who recite the Reminder.
37:4: Indeed, your God is One is the answer to the oath. Al-Kisa'i permitted opening the in in the oath. What is meant by As-Saffat and what follows it up to the saying those who recite the Reminder are the angels according to Ibn Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud, Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, and Qatadah. They line up in the sky like the rows of creation in this world for prayer. It was also said that they line up their wings in the air, standing in it until God commands them as He wills. This is like the way slaves stand in rows before their kings. Al-Hasan said: A row is for their rows before their Lord in prayer. It was also said that they refer to the birds, as evidenced by the saying of God the Almighty: Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading out their wings? (Al-Mulk 72:19). A row is the arrangement of a group in a line like the row in prayer. As-Saffat is the plural of a group. It is said: a group of people spread out, then it is pluralized as saffat. It was said: As-Saffat are the group of believers when they stand in rows in prayer or in jihad. This was mentioned by Al-Qushayri. <As-Zajirāt>are the angels according to Ibn Abbas, Ibn Mas`ud, Masruq and others, as we have mentioned. Either because they forbid and guide, according to As-Suddi. Or because they forbid from sins with sermons and advice. Qatadah said: They are the deterrents of the Qur’an. As-Saffāt Al-Dhikr are the angels who recite the Book of God Almighty. This was said by Ibn Mas`ud, Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ibn Jubayr and As-Suddi. It was also said that what is meant is Gabriel alone, so he was mentioned in the plural because he is the chief of the angels and therefore has soldiers and followers. Qatadah said: What is meant is everyone who recites the remembrance of God Almighty and His books. It was also said that they are the verses of the Qur’an, described by recitation, as God Almighty said: Indeed, this Qur’an relates to the Children of Israel (al-Naml 27:76). It is permissible to say that the verses of the Qur’an are As-Saffāt because some letters follow others. This was mentioned by Al-Qushayri. Al-Mawardi said: What is meant by recitals are the prophets who recite the Remembrance to their nations. If it is said: What is the ruling on the letter fa when it comes as a conjunction in attributes? It is said to him: Either it indicates the order of their meanings in existence, like his saying: What a shame for Al-Harith Al-Sabah, Al-Ghanim and Al-Aib As if he said: He who came in the morning and gained booty and then returned. Or according to their order in terms of difference in some aspects, like when you say: Take the best, then the most perfect, and do the best, then the most beautiful. Or according to the order of their descriptions in that, like his saying: May God have mercy on those who swore and those who fell short. So the matter of the conjunctive fa in the attributes is governed by these three rules, as Al-Zamakhshari said. <Your God is One>is the answer to the oath. Muqatil said: That is because the disbelievers in Mecca said: Make the gods one god, but how can this creation contain one god?! So God swore by these as an honor. And the verse was revealed. Ibn Al-Anbari said: It is a good pause.
37:5: Then it begins with Lord of the heavens and the earth meaning He is the Lord of the heavens. An-Nahhas: It is possible for <Lord of the heavens and the earth>to be a predicate after a predicate, and it is possible for it to be a substitute for <one>. I said: According to these two aspects, it is not stopped at <for one>. Al-Akhfash narrated: <Lord of the heavens - and Lord of the Easts>in the accusative case as an attribute of the noun in. The Almighty made clear the meaning of His Oneness, Divinity and perfect power, that He is <Lord of the heavens and the earth>, i.e., their Creator and Owner, and what is between them and Lord of the Easts, i.e., Owner of the places where the sun rises. Ibn Abbas: Every day the sun has a rising and a setting, and that is because God the Almighty created for the sun 365 windows at its rising place, and the same number at its setting, according to the number of days in the solar year. It rises every day in one of these windows, and sets in another. It does not rise in that window except on that day of the following year. It does not rise except unwillingly, so it says: My Lord, do not let me rise against Your servants, for I see that they disobey You. Abu Omar mentioned it in the book Al-Tamhid and Ibn Al-Anbari in the book Al-Radd on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: “I said to Ibn Abbas, ‘What do you think of what was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about Umayyah ibn Abi Al-Salt, whose poetry believed but whose heart disbelieved?’ He said, ‘It is true, so what do you reject of that?’ I said, ‘We reject his statement: And the sun rises every last night, red and its color turns rosy She does not send them her messengers except to punish or to flog. Why is the sun whipped? He said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, the sun never rises without being prodded by seventy thousand angels who say to it, “Rise, rise,” and it says, I will not rise upon a people who worship me instead of God. Then an angel comes to it and it shrinks from the light of the sons of Adam. Then a devil comes to it wanting to prevent it from rising, but it rises between his horns and God burns him beneath it. “Those are the words of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him): ‘It never rises except between the horns of a devil, and it never sets except that it falls down in prostration to God.’ Then a devil comes to it wanting to prevent it from prostrating, but it sets between his horns and God burns him beneath it.” Wording by Ibn al-Anbari. It was reported on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) spoke the truth in this poem: Saturn and Taurus under his right foot, and the eagle under the other, and Leith the observatory And the sun rises every last night, red, its color turning rosy She does not send them her messengers except to punish or to flog. Akrima said: “I said to Ibn Abbas: ‘O my master, does the sun flog?’ He said: ‘The narration compelled it to flog, but it fears punishment.’ He indicated by mentioning the rising places to the setting places, and that is why He did not mention the setting places. It is like His statement: ‘Garments to protect you from the heat’ (An-Nahl 16:81). He mentioned the easts specifically because the rising comes before the setting. And He said in Surah al-Rahman 55:‘Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests’ (Ar-Rahman 55:17). By the two easts He meant the farthest point from which the sun rises on long days, and the shortest day on short days, as mentioned previously in Ya-Sin. And God knows best.”
37:6: The Almighty said: Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment of stars. Qatada said: The stars were created three times: as missiles for the devils, a light by which to be guided, and an adornment for the nearest heaven. Masruq, Al-A'mash, An-Nakha'i, Asim, and Hamzah read: <bi adornment>is in the genitive case. <al-kawākim>is in the genitive case as a substitute for <al-zaynah>because it is it. Abu Bakr read it in the same way, except that he put <al-kawākim>in the accusative case with the verbal noun which is adornment. The meaning is that We adorned the stars in it. It is also permissible for it to be in the accusative case with an implied I mean, as if he said: Indeed, We adorned it <bi adornment>I mean <al-kawākim>. It was said: It is a substitute for adornment in the place. It is permissible for <bi adornment of the stars>to mean that the stars adorned it. Or it means that they are the stars. The rest said <bi adornment of the stars>as an addition. The meaning is We adorned the nearest heaven with the adornment of the stars, i.e. He made the stars beautiful. It may be like the reading of nun, except that the tanween was deleted for the sake of brevity.
37:7: And to protect is a verbal noun, meaning we have protected it completely. From every rebellious devil When He informed us that the angels descend with revelation from the heavens, He explained that He guarded the heavens from eavesdropping after He decorated them with planets. A rebel is a violent one from among the jinn and mankind, and the Arabs call him a devil.
37:8: The Almighty says: They do not listen to the highest assembly. Abu Hatim said: meaning, lest they hear. Then the word that was deleted, so the verb was raised. The highest assembly: the people of the lowest heaven and above it. Each one of them is called the highest in relation to the assembly of the earth. The pronoun in yasma'un refers to the devils. The majority of people read yasma'un with a silent seen and a soft mim. Hamzah and Asim, in the narration of Hafs, read lama yasma'un with a double seen and mim from tasmee'. According to the first reading, their hearing is negated, even though they listen, which is the correct meaning, and this is supported by the Almighty's statement: Indeed, they are removed from hearing Ash-Shu'ara' 26:212. According to the last reading, they neither listened nor heard. Mujahid said: They used to eavesdrop but did not hear. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas: lama yasma'un ila al-mila' they do not hear nor listen. The root of yasma'oon is yatasma'oon, so the ta was assimilated into the seen because of its proximity to it. Abu Ubaid chose this option because the Arabs hardly ever say I heard him but say I heard him to it. And they throw from every side means they throw meteors from every side.
37:9: Dahuran is a verbal noun, because the meaning of <yadhthifuna>is yadhthurunu. I drove him away, yadhthwan and dahuran means I expelled him. As-Salami and Yaqub al-Hadrami read <dahuran>with a fat-ha on the dal, making it a verbal noun on the pattern fa'ul. As for al-Farra', he estimated it as being the active participle. That is, they throw that which drives them away, i.e., with yadhthurun, then he deleted the ba'. The Kufians use this a lot, as they recited: You pass through the houses and you do not turn back There is disagreement as to whether this stoning occurred before the mission or after it for the sake of the mission. There are two opinions. The hadiths have mentioned this, as will be mentioned in Surah Al-Jinn on the authority of Ibn Abbas. It may be possible to reconcile the two by saying: Those who said that the devils were not pelted with stars before the mission of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and then they were pelted, that is, they were not pelted by stoning them to be cut off from hearing, but they were pelted at one time and not at another, and they were pelted from one side and not from the other. Perhaps the reference in the words of God, the Most High: And they are pelted from every side, driven away, and for them is a lasting punishment refers to this meaning, which is that they were not pelted except from some sides, so they became pelted constantly. Rather, before that, they were spies among humans, one of them would get what he needed while another did not, one would be safe while another did not, rather he would be arrested, punished and humiliated. When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was sent, the guarding of the heavens was increased, and meteors were prepared for them that had never existed before, so that they would be repelled from all sides of the heavens, and they would not remain in any of the seats they had in them. They were unable to hear anything that was going on in them, unless one of them was snatched away with his agility, followed by a piercing meteor before it descended to the earth, which threw it to his brothers and burned them. Thus, divination was abolished and the message and prophethood were achieved. If it is said: If this slinging was for the sake of prophethood, then why did it continue after the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him)? The answer is that it continued as long as prophethood lasted, because “the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) informed us of the nullity of divination, saying: ‘He is not one of us who practices divination.’” If it had not been guarded after his death, the jinn would have returned to hear it, and divination would have returned. This is not permissible after it has been invalidated. Because if the guardianship of the heavens was cut off for the sake of prophethood, then divination returned, doubt would enter the minds of the weak Muslims, and they would not believe that divination only returned because of the end of prophethood. So it is clear that wisdom dictates the continuation of the guardianship during the life of the Prophet (peace be upon him), and after God took him to His honor (peace be upon him and his family). And for them is a lasting punishment, meaning everlasting, according to Mujahid and Qatadah. Ibn Abbas said: Severe. Al-Kalbi, Al-Suddi, and Abu Salih: Painful, meaning the pain of which reaches the heart. It is taken from wasb, which means illness. Except for one who snatches a snatch, is an exception to His statement: And they are pelted from every side. It was said that the exception refers to something other than revelation, according to His statement: Indeed, they are removed from hearing, so one of them steals something of what the angels negotiate about, of what will happen in the world before the people of the earth know about it. This is due to the lightness of the bodies of the devils, so they are then pelted with meteors.:Sahih hadiths have been narrated on this subject, including: The devils used to ascend to the sky and sit one above the other to listen. The highest would advance towards the sky, then the one next to him, then the one next to him. Then God would decide a matter on earth, and the people of the sky would speak about it, and the lowest devil would hear it, then he would pass it on to the one below him. Perhaps a meteor would burn him up, and he might have spoken the words, or perhaps it would not burn him up, as we have explained. Then that word would descend to the soothsayers, who would tell a hundred lies along with it. Then that word would come true, and the ignorant would believe them all, as we have explained in Al-An'am. When God brought Islam, the sky was tightly guarded, so that not a single devil would escape who heard it. The shooting stars are the ones that people see collapsing. Al-Naqqash and Makki said: They are not the moving stars in the sky, because the movement of those cannot be seen, whereas the movement of these shooting stars can be seen, because they are close to us. Sufficient explanation has been given on this subject in Surat Al-Hijr. We mentioned in <Saba>“The hadith of Abu Hurairah. In it, the devils are on top of each other.” At-Tirmidhi said about it: A good and authentic hadith. In it: “On the authority of Ibn Abbas: The devils snatch the hearing and throw it to their allies. Whatever it brings is true, but they distort it and add.” He said: This is a good and authentic hadith. And snatching means taking something quickly. It is said: khataaf, khataaf, khataaf, khataaf, and khataaf. The original form of the doubled letters is ikhtafil, so the taa was assimilated into the taa because it is its sister, and the khaa was opened because the vowel of the taa was placed on it. And whoever breaks it, it is because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. And whoever breaks the taa, then the kasra follows the kasra.
37:10: The Almighty said, And a piercing meteor pursued him. That is, a shining one. This was said by Ad-Dahhak, Al-Hasan, and others. It was also said that what was meant were the stars of fire that followed them until they made them fall into the sea. Ibn Abbas said about shooting stars: They burn them without death. The shooting stars that people are pelted with are not fixed stars. This is indicated by seeing their movements. Fixed ones move, but their movements are not seen because of their distance. This has already been mentioned. The plural of shihab is shihab. The analogy in the small number is ashbah, even though it was not heard from the Arabs. Thaqib means shining. This was said by Al-Hasan, Mujahid, and Abu Majlaz. From this is His statement: Your flint is more piercing than its flints Any brighter. Al-Akhfash narrated in all of them: meteors, holes, holes, and holes. Al-Kisa’i narrated: the fire was pierced, holes, if it was kindled, and I pierced it. Zaid bin Aslam said in the hole that it is the kindling from their saying, Athqab Zandak, meaning, I lit your fire. Al-Akhfash said this and recited the poet’s saying: While man is a piercing meteor whose light has struck time and died down
37:11: The Almighty says: Ask them meaning ask them, meaning the people of Mecca. This is taken from the verb istifta' al-mufti. Are they more difficult to create, or those We have created? Mujahid said: Those We have created of the heavens, the earth, the mountains, and the seas. It was also said that this includes the angels and previous nations. The evidence for this is that He spoke about them as Yemen. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The angels. Another said: Of the previous nations, who perished while they were more difficult to create than them. This was revealed about Abu al-Ashd ibn Kalda, who was called Abu al-Ashd because of his great strength and power. He will be mentioned in al-Balad. Similar to this is: The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind (Ghafir 40:57) and His statement: Are you more difficult to create, or is the heaven? (an-Nazi'at: 27). We created them from sticky clay, meaning sticky, as Ibn Abbas said. And from this is the saying of Ali, may God be pleased with him: Learn, for God has given you more ease and good morals, all of which are necessary for you. Qatada and Ibn Zayd said: The meaning of < lazib > is sticky. Al-Mawardi: The difference between lazib and lazih is that lazih is that which sticks to each other, and lazih is that which adheres to whatever touches it. Ikrimah said: < lazib > sticky. Saeed ibn Jubayr: meaning good, free thing that sticks to the hand. Mujahid: < lazib > is necessary. The Arabs say: sticky clay and lazim, replacing the ba’ with the meem. Similar to it is their saying: latib and lazim, replacing the ba’ with the meem. And lazib is constant, you say: the thing became sticky due to its strike, and it is more eloquent than lazim. Al-Nabigha said: Do not think that there is no evil after good, and do not think that evil is a lasting blow. Al-Farra’ narrated on the authority of the Arabs: Tin latab means inseparable. Latab is the constant, so you say from it: Latab yaltabah labban and Latooban, like Lazb yalzib with the letter Damma “Lazuban”. Abu al-Jarrah recited about Latab: If this is from the wine I drank, then I repent from drinking wine. Headache, bone pain, period and sadness with bright light in the abdomen Al-Latib also means: sticky like lazib, on the authority of Al-Asma’i, as narrated by Al-Jawhari. Al-Suddi and Al-Kalbi said about lazib: it is pure. Mujahid and Al-Dahhak: it is stinking.
37:12: God's statement: Rather, I am amazed, and they ridicule. The reading of the people of Medina, Abu Amr, and Asim is with a fat-ha on the ta', addressing the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), meaning, Rather, I am amazed at what was sent down to you of the Qur'an, and they ridicule it. This is also the reading of Shuraih, who rejected the damma reading and said, God is not amazed by anything; rather, he who does not know is amazed. It was also said that the meaning is, Rather, I am amazed at their denial of the resurrection. The people of Kufa, except Asim, read it with a damma on the ta'. Abu Ubaid and Al-Farra' preferred this view, and it was narrated on the authority of Ali and Ibn Mas'ud. Shu'bah narrated on the authority of Al-A'mash on the authority of Abu Wa'il on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud that he read: <Rather, I am amazed> with a damma on the ta'. It was also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Al-Farra' said about God's statement, Rather, I am amazed, and they ridicule, the people read it with a nasb and a damma on the ta', but the nominative case is more preferable to me because it was narrated from Ali, Abdullah, and Ibn Abbas. Abu Zakariya Al-Farra’ said: “If wonder is attributed to God, the Almighty, then its meaning is not from God as it is from His servants. Similarly, His statement: “God mocks at them” (al-Baqarah 2:15) does not mean from God as it means from His servants. This explains the breaking of Shuraih’s statement as he rejected reading it with this word. Jarir and Al-A’mash narrated on the authority of Abu Wa’il Shaqiq bin Salamah who said: Abdullah, meaning Ibn Mas’ud, read it: Rather, I wonder and they mock. Shuraih said: God is not amazed by anything; He is only amazed by those who do not know.” Al-A’mash said: “I mentioned it to Ibrahim and he said: Shuraih was amazed by his own opinion. Abdullah was more knowledgeable than Shuraih, and Abdullah used to read it: “Rather, I wonder.” Al-Harawi said: Some of the Imams said: The meaning of his saying: Rather, I was amazed is rather I rewarded them for their amazement, because God Almighty informed about them in more than one place with amazement at the truth, so He said: And they were amazed that a warner had come to them from among themselves (Surah Sad: 4), and He said: This is indeed an amazing thing (Surah Sad: 6), Is it a wonder to the people that We have revealed to a man from among them (Surah Yunus 10:2), so God Almighty said: Rather, I was amazed rather I rewarded them for their amazement. I said: This is the complete meaning of Al-Farra’s statement, and Al-Bayhaqi chose it. Ali bin Sulayman said: The meaning of the two readings is the same, the meaning is: Say, O Muhammad, rather I am amazed, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is addressed by the Qur’an. An-Nahhas: This is a good statement, and the omission of the statement is common. Al-Bayhaqi: The first is more correct. Al-Mahdawi: It is possible that God’s statement about Himself with amazement may be interpreted as meaning that He has made clear of His command and His wrath upon those who disbelieve in Him what takes the place of amazement from created beings, just as His statement about Himself with laughter at those with whom He is pleased - according to what came in the report from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace - may be interpreted as meaning that He has made clear to them of His pleasure what takes the place of laughter from created beings, metaphorically and broadly. Al-Harawi said: It is said that the meaning of your Lord is amazed is that He is pleased and rewarded, so He called it amazement, although it is not amazement in reality, as God Almighty said: And God plans (al-Anfal 8:30) meaning: And God will reward them for their plan. And similarly, in the hadith: Your Lord is amazed at you and your despair. Amazement may mean that this action is considered great by God. In this case, the meaning of his statement, Rather, I am amazed is: Rather, their action is great in My sight. Al-Bayhaqi said: It is likely that this is the meaning of the hadith of Uqbah ibn Amir, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Al-Bayhaqi said: This hadith and others like it may be that His angels are amazed at His generosity and compassion for His servants, when He compelled them to believe in Him by fighting and being captured in chains, until when they believed, He admitted them to Paradise. It was said that the meaning of Rather, I am amazed is Rather, I denied. Al-Naqqash narrated it. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: Amazement at God means denying something and glorifying it, and it is the language of the Arabs. It was mentioned in the hadith Your Lord is amazed at your despair and despair “and they mock.” It was said that the waw is the waw of state, meaning I am amazed at them in their state of mockery. It was said that the speech ended at His saying Rather, I am amazed, then He resumed by saying and they mock, meaning at what you have brought when you recite it to them. It was said that they mock you when you call them.
37:13: God Almighty says: And when they are reminded, meaning when they are admonished by the Qur’an, according to Qatada. They do not remember, meaning they do not benefit from it. Saeed bin Jubayr said: meaning when they are reminded of what happened to the disbelievers before them, they turn away from it and do not reflect.
37:14: And when they see a sign meaning a miracle they mock meaning they ridicule, according to Qatada. And they say that it is magic. And istakhar and sakhar have the same meaning as istaqara and istaqara, and istajaba and ajaba. It was also said: they mock meaning they seek ridicule from others. Mujahid said: they mock. It was also said: meaning they think that the sign is a mockery.
37:15: And they said, 'This is nothing but obvious magic.' That is, if they were unable to counter the miracles with anything, they would say, This is magic, illusion, and deception.
37:16: If we die meaning, will we be resurrected if we die? This is a question of denial and mockery from them.
37:17: Or our forefathers of old meaning, or our forefathers are resurrected. The interrogative alif was added to the conjunction. Nafi' read: <or our forefathers>with a sukoon on the waw. This was previously mentioned in Surah <Al-A'raf>. In the words of God Almighty: Or the people of the towns (al-A’raf 7:98).
37:18: God Almighty says: “Say, 'Yes,' meaning, yes, you will be resurrected. 'And you will be humbled,' meaning, humiliated and degraded, because if they see what they denied happening, they will inevitably be humiliated. It was also said: meaning, the Resurrection will take place, even if you hate it. This is something that will happen despite you, even if you claim to deny it today.
37:19: It will be only one blast meaning one shout. Al-Hasan said: It is the second trumpet blast. The shout is called a blast because its purpose is to deter, that is, it is deterred like camels and horses are deterred at the market. Then they will be standing looking meaning they will be looking at one another. It was also said that the meaning is they will be waiting to see what will be done to them. It was also said that it is like His statement: Then the eyes of those who disbelieved will be staring (al-Anbiya 21:97). It was also said that it means they will be looking at the resurrection which they denied.
37:20: The Almighty said: And they will say, 'Woe to us! This is the Day of Judgment.' They cried out for woe upon themselves, because on that day they will know what has befallen them. It is in the accusative case as a verbal noun according to the Basrans. Al-Farra' claimed that it could be interpreted as: 'Woe to us!' and 'Woe' means 'grief.' Al-Nahhas said: If it were as he said, it would have been separate, but in the Qur'an it is connected, and we do not know of anyone who writes it except connected. <The Day of Judgment>is the Day of Reckoning. It was also said: the Day of Judgment.
37:21: This is the Day of Judgment which you used to deny. It was said that it is from what some of them said to each other, meaning this is the day which we denied. It was also said that it is from what God Almighty said to them. It was also said that it is from what the angels said, meaning this is the Day of Judgment between people, when the truth will be distinguished from falsehood. So A party will be in Paradise and a party will be in the Blaze. (al-Shura 42:7)
37:22: The Almighty's statement: Gather together those who did wrong and their spouses is from the statement of God to the angels: Gather together the polytheists and their spouses meaning their followers in polytheism, and polytheism is injustice. God the Almighty said: Indeed, polytheism is a great injustice [Luqman 13]. So the disbeliever will be gathered together with the disbeliever, as stated by Qatadah and Abu Al-Aaliyah. Umar ibn Al-Khattab said regarding the statement of God the Almighty: Gather together those who did wrong and their spouses he said: the adulterer with the adulterer, the drinker with the drinker, and the thief with the thief. Ibn Abbas said: and their spouses meaning their likes. This goes back to the statement of Umar. It was also said: and their spouses are their women who agree with disbelief, as stated by Mujahid and Al-Hasan, and it was narrated by An-Nu'man ibn Bashir from Umar ibn Al-Khattab. Ad-Dahhak said: and their spouses are their companions from among the devils. This is also what Muqatil said: Every infidel will be gathered with his devil in a chain.
37:23: And what they used to worship * other than God meaning idols, devils, and Satan. So guide them to the path of Hellfire meaning drive them to the Fire. It was also said: So guide them means show them the way. It is said: I showed him the way, or I showed him the way, meaning I showed him to it. I presented the gift and I presented the bride. It is also said: I presented her, meaning I made her like a gift.
37:24: God the Almighty says: Stop them, for they will be questioned. Isa bin Omar narrated <that they>with a fat-ha on the hamza. Al-Kisa'i said: meaning because they and because they, it is said: the animal stopped, I stop it stopping, so it stopped, transitive and intransitive, meaning detain them. This will happen before driving to Hellfire, and it has an intransitive and transitive construction, meaning stop them for the reckoning then drive them to the Fire. It was also said: They will be driven to the Fire first, then they will be gathered for questioning when they are close to the Fire. <that they will be questioned>about their deeds, words and actions, as stated by Al-Qurazi and Al-Kalbi. Ad-Dahhak: about their sins. Ibn Abbas: about there is no god but God. And also from him: about oppressing people. All of this is evidence that the disbeliever will be held accountable. This has been discussed previously in <Al-Hijr>. It was said: Their question is that it be said to them: Did there not come to you messengers from among you? (al-An’am 6:130), to establish the argument.
37:25: And it will be said to them: Why do you not support one another? as a rebuke and rebuke, meaning that some of you support one another and protect one another from God's punishment. It was also said that this is a reference to Abu Jahl's statement on the day of Badr: We are all victorious (al-Qamar 54:44). Its original form is tatanasuru you support one another, but one of the two ta's was dropped for ease. Al-Bazzi emphasized the ta' in the connection.
37:26: The Almighty says: Rather, today they are submissive. Qatada said: Submissive to the punishment of God the Almighty. Ibn Abbas: Submissive and humiliated. Al-Hasan: Obedient. Al-Akhfash: Throwing themselves into their hands. The meanings are close.
37:27: And some of them turned to others meaning the leaders and followers asking questions arguing. It is said that they do not ask questions, so no was omitted. An-Nahhas: The ignorant of the language made a mistake and thought that this is from His statement: There will be no kinship between them that Day, nor will they ask questions (al-Mu’minun 23:101). Rather, it means that they will not ask questions about the wombs, so one of them will say: I ask you by the kinship that is between me and you, for what has benefited me, or dropped a right that you have over me, or granted me a good deed. This is clear, because before it <there will be no kinship between them>.
