Al-Tirmidhi added: “And when he wakes up, let him say: ‘Praise be to God who has healed me in my body, restored my soul to me, and permitted me to remember Him.’” Al-Bukhari narrated from Hudhayfah who said: “When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went to bed at night, he would place his hand under his cheek and say: ‘O God, in Your name I die and live.’ When he woke up, he would say: ‘Praise be to God who has given us life after causing us to die, and to Him is the resurrection.’” God the Almighty says: {And He keeps those over whom He has decreed death} This is the reading of the common people that it is the named subject death in the accusative case, meaning God has decreed it. This is the preference of Abu Hatim and Abu Ubaid, because of His statement at the beginning of the verse: {God takes the souls}, so He decrees over them. Al-A’mash, Yahya ibn Waththab, Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read death has been decreed for them without naming the subject. An-Nahhas, and the meaning is the same, except that the first reading is clearer and more in line with the flow of speech, because they agreed on and sends and did not read it and sends. The verse draws attention to the greatness of His power and His uniqueness in divinity, and that He does what He wills, and He gives life and causes death, and no one else has the power to do that. Indeed in that are signs meaning in God’s taking the soul of the dead and the sleeping, and His sending back the soul of the sleeping and detaining the soul of the dead for a people who give thought. Al-Asma’i said: I heard Mu’tamir say: The soul of the human being is like a ball of yarn. The soul is sent out, then it goes, then it goes back, then it comes back and enters. So the meaning of the verse is that some of the soul is sent out during sleep, and most of it is in the body, connected to what comes out of it, a hidden connection. So when the person wakes up, most of his soul is drawn out and returns. Other than this has been said. In the Qur’an: “And they ask you, [O Muhammad], about the soul. Say, ‘The soul is of the affair of my Lord.’” (Al-Isra’ 17:85) meaning, none knows its true nature except God. This has been mentioned previously in Glory be to God.
39:43: The Almighty said: Or have they taken intercessors besides God? That is, rather, they have taken, meaning idols. The statement includes what implies lam, that is, Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought. They did not give thought, but they took their gods as intercessors. Say, ‘Even if they did not possess anything?’ That is, say to them, O Muhammad, Would you take them as intercessors even though they do not possess any power of intercession? “Nor do they reason?” because they are inanimate. This is a question of denial.
39:44: The Almighty’s saying: “Say: To God belongs all intercession.” This is a text that indicates that intercession belongs to God alone, as He says: Who is he that can intercede with Him except by His permission? (al-Baqarah 2:255) So there is no intercessor except through His intercession. And they do not intercede except for him with whom He is pleased. (Al-Anbiya’: 28) All together is an accusative of state. If it is said: All together only applies to two or more, and intercession is one. The answer is that intercession is a verbal noun, and the verbal noun refers to two and all. To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, then to Him you will be returned.
39:45: The Almighty’s saying: And when God is mentioned alone is in the accusative case as a verbal noun according to Al-Khalil and Sibawayh, and in the state according to Yunus. I felt disgusted Al-Mubarrad said: I felt withdrawn. This is the opinion of Ibn Abbas and Mujahid. Qatada said: I felt aversion, arrogance, disbelief, and disobedience. Al-Mu’arraj said: I felt disgusted. The root of Idhfaaz is aversion and turning away. Amr ibn Kulthum said: If the culture bites it, it will be disgusted and turn away from its customers. Abu Zaid said: The male ashmaaz is a male from fear, which means terrified. When the polytheists were told, There is no god but God, they would flee and disbelieve. And when those besides Him are mentioned, meaning the idols, when Satan cast into the Prophet’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) wish when reciting Surah An-Najm, those are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is hoped for. This was said by a group of commentators. When they rejoice, meaning joy and happiness appear on their faces.
39:46: The Almighty said: "Say: O God, Creator of the heavens and the earth" is in the accusative case because it is a vocative complement, and so is Knower of the unseen. According to Sibawayh, it is not permissible for it to be an adjective. You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they differ. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, he said: I asked Aisha may God be pleased with her how the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) used to begin his prayer when he got up at night. She said: When he got up at night and began his prayer, he said: "O God, Lord of Gabriel, Michael, and Israfil, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they differ. Guide me to the truth regarding that over which they differ, by Your permission. Indeed, You guide whom You will to a straight path." When al-Rabi' ibn Khaitham heard of the killing of al-Husayn ibn Ali may God be pleased with them, he recited: "Say: O God, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they differ." Saeed bin Jubair said: I know a verse that no one has ever read and asked God for something without Him giving it to him. It is the Almighty’s saying: “Say, ‘O God, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ.’”
39:47: The Almighty said: And if those who did wrong meaning, those who lied and associated others with God had all that is on the earth and the like thereof with it, they would offer it as ransom from the evil of the punishment meaning, from the evil of the punishment of that Day. This has already been mentioned in Surat Al Imran and Surat Ar Ra’d. And there will appear to them from God that which they had never reckoned with because of what was narrated in this regard, as narrated by Mansur on the authority of Mujahid, who said: They did deeds which they thought were good, but when they turned out to be bad, they turned out to be bad. As-Suddi said the same. It was also said: They did deeds which they thought they would repent from before death, but death overtook them before they repented, and they had thought that they would be saved by repenting. It is possible that they thought that they would be forgiven without repenting, so and there will appear to them from God that which they had never reckoned with of entering the Fire. Sufyan al-Thawri said about this verse: Woe to the hypocrites, woe to the hypocrites. This is their sign and their story. Ikrimah ibn Ammar said: Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir was extremely distressed by his death, so he was asked: What is this distress? He said: I fear a verse from the Book of God.
39:48: God Almighty says: And there will appear to them from God that which they had not reckoned with. So I fear that there will appear to me that which I had not reckoned with. And there will appear to them that is, will appear to them the evils of what they had earned that is, the punishment for what they had earned of disbelief and sins. And what they used to ridicule has encompassed them that is, will descend upon them that which they used to ridicule.
39:49: The Almighty says: And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us. It was said that it was revealed about Hudhayfah ibn al-Mughira. Then when We bestow upon him a favor from Us, he says, I have only been given it because of knowledge. Qatadah said, On knowledge" means I have knowledge of the means of earning. It was also reported from him, "On knowledge means on goodness with Me. It was also said, On knowledge" means knowledge from God of my favor. Al-Hasan said, "On knowledge" means knowledge that God taught me. It was also said that the meaning is that he said, "I know that if I am given this in this world, I will have a status with God. So God said, Rather, it is a trial." That is, rather, the blessings that I have been given are a trial by which you will be tested. Al-Farra' said, "The feminine form of it is used to denote the feminization of the trial. If it had been rather, it is a trial, it would have been permissible. An-Nahhas said, Rather, I gave it to him as a trial. "But most of them do not know." That is, you do not know that giving them money is a test.
39:50: The Almighty says: He has said it The feminine is the word those before them meaning the disbelievers before them like Qarun and others where he said: I have only been given it because of knowledge I have (al-Qasas 28:78) So what they used to earn did not avail them ma is for denial, meaning their wealth and children did not avail them at all against the punishment of God. It was said: What is it that enriched their wealth? So ma is an interrogative.
39:51: The Almighty says: So the evil consequences of what they earned will befall them meaning the recompense for their evil deeds. The recompense for an evil action is sometimes called an evil. And those who did wrong meaning they associated others with God among this nation, the evil consequences of what they earned will befall them meaning by returning and using the sword. And they will not escape meaning they will not be able to outsmart God or outpace Him. This has been mentioned previously.
39:52: The Almighty says: Do they not know that God expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe. He mentioned the believer specifically because he is the one who contemplates the verses and benefits from them. He knows that the abundance of provision may be a deception and a trap, while its restriction is a sign of elevation and glorification.
39:53: God Almighty says: Say, ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God.’ If you wish, you can delete the yaa, because the address is a place for deletion. An-Nahhas: Among the most important things that were narrated about it is what Muhammad bin Ishaq narrated on the authority of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar on the authority of Umar who said: When we agreed to emigrate, Hisham bin Al-Asi bin Wa’il As-Sahmi and I met with Ayyash bin Abi Rabia bin Utbah, and we said: The appointment is at the place of Banu Ghifar, and we said: Whoever among us is detained, so let his companion be punished. So I and Ayyash bin Utbah woke up and Hisham was detained from us, and he was tempted and we were tempted, so we used to say in Madinah: These people knew God, the Almighty, and believed in His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, then they were tempted by a calamity that befell them, and we do not see any repentance for them. And they also used to say this about themselves, so God, the Almighty, revealed the denial of His Book: Say, ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God,’ until His Most High’s saying: Is there not in Hell an abode for the arrogant? (al-Zumar 39:60). Umar said: So I wrote it with my own hand and then sent it to Hisham. Hisham said: When it came to me, I went out with it to Dhu Tuwa and said: O God, make it clear to me. I realized that it was revealed about us, so I returned and sat on my camel and caught up with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Saeed bin Jubair narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: There were some people from the polytheists who killed a lot and committed adultery a lot. They said to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) or sent to him: What you are calling to is good, if only you would tell us that we have the opportunity to repent. So God, the Almighty, revealed this verse: Say, ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves.’ Al-Bukhari mentioned it with a similar meaning. It has already been mentioned at the end of Al-Furqan. Ibn Abbas also narrated that it was revealed about the people of Mecca, and they said: Muhammad claimed that whoever worships idols and kisses the soul that God has forbidden will not be forgiven. How can we emigrate and become Muslim when we have worshipped another god along with God and killed the soul that God has forbidden? So God revealed this verse. It was said that it was revealed about a group of Muslims who were excessive in their worship and feared that God would not accept their repentance because of sins they had committed in the pre-Islamic era. Ibn Abbas and Ata’ also said: It was revealed about Wahshi, the killer of Hamza, because he thought that God would not accept his conversion to Islam. Ibn Jurayj narrated from Ata’ from Ibn Abbas that Wahshi came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Muhammad, I have come to you seeking protection, so delay me so that I may hear the words of God. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I would have liked to see you without protection, but if you have come to me seeking protection, then you are under my protection until you hear the words of God. I have associated partners with God, killed the soul that God has forbidden, and committed adultery. Will God accept my repentance? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was silent until the verse, And those who do not invoke with God another deity or kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse (Al-Furqan 25:68) to the end of the verse was revealed. He recited it to him and said, “I see a condition, so perhaps I will not do good. I am under your protection until I hear the word of God.” Then the verse, Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills (An-Nisa’ 4:48) was revealed. So he called for him and recited it to him and said, Perhaps I am one of those who do not wish to be under your protection until I hear the word of God. Then the verse, O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of mercy was revealed. He said, Yes, now I do not see a condition. So he became a Muslim. Hammad ibn Salamah narrated from Thabit from Shahr ibn Hawshab from Asma’ that she heard the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) reciting: “Say, ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God. Indeed, God forgives all sins and does not mind. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.’” In the copy of Ibn Mas’ud it is: Indeed, God forgives all sins for whomever He wills. Abu Ja’far al-Nahhas said: These two readings are based on the interpretation, meaning that God forgives whomever He wills. God has identified whomever He wills to forgive, namely the one who repents or the one who committed a minor sin and did not commit a major sin. What indicates that He means the one who repents is what comes after it: And turn to your Lord. So the one who repents will have all his sins forgiven. This is indicated by: And indeed, I am the Forgiving of whoever repents. (Ta-Ha: 82) So there is no problem with this. Ali ibn Abi Talib said: There is no verse in the Qur’an that is more comprehensive than this verse: Say, ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God.’ This has already been mentioned in Subhan Glory be to God. Abdullah bin Omar said: This is the most hopeful verse in the Quran. Ibn Abbas responded to them and said: The most hopeful verse in the Quran is the Almighty’s saying: And indeed, your Lord is the possessor of forgiveness for the people despite their wrongdoing. (Ar-Ra’d: 6) This has already been mentioned in Ar-Ra’d. It was also read: And do not despair with a kasra or a fatha on the noon. This has already been explained in Al-Hijr.
39:54: The Almighty said: And turn to your Lord in repentance meaning, return to Him in obedience. Since He explained that whoever repents from polytheism will be forgiven, He commanded repentance and returning to Him, and turning to Him means returning to God with sincerity. And submit to Him meaning, submit to Him and obey before the punishment comes to you in this world and then you will not be helped meaning you will not be protected from His punishment. It was narrated from the hadith of Jabir that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: It is from happiness that God prolongs a person's life in obedience and grants him repentance, and it is from misery that a person works and becomes proud of his work.
39:55: God the Almighty says: And follow the best of what was revealed to you from your Lord before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive. The best of what has been revealed is the Quran, and all of it is good. The meaning is what Al-Hasan said: Commit to obeying it and avoiding disobeying it. Al-Suddi said: The best is what God has commanded in His Book. Ibn Zayd said: It means the clear verses, and leave the knowledge of the ambiguous to its expert. He said: God sent down a book, the Torah, the Gospel, and the Psalms, then He sent down the Quran and commanded that it be followed, so it is the best and the miraculous. It was said: This is the best because it is an abrogator and judge over all other books, and all books have been abrogated. It was also said: It means forgiveness, because God the Almighty gave His Prophet the choice between forgiveness and retaliation. It was also said: Whatever God taught the Prophet that is not the Quran is good, and whatever was revealed to him from the Quran is the best. It was also said: The best of what has been revealed to you of the report of past nations.
39:56: The Almighty said: That a soul should say, 'Oh, how I regret it!' That is in the accusative case, meaning it is disliked. That a soul should say and according to the Kufians it means lest it should say, and according to the Basrans it means caution. That a soul should say and it was said: that is, before. That a soul should say because He said before this: Before the punishment comes to you (al-Zumar 39:54). Az-Zamakhshari: If you say, why is it repeated? I say: Because what is meant by it is some of the souls, and it is the soul of the disbeliever. It is possible that He means a soul distinct from the souls, either by severe obstinacy in disbelief, or by a great punishment. It is possible that what is meant is abundance, as Al-A'sha said: By the Lord of Baqi', if I shouted in its interior, a generous man would come to me shaking his head in anger. He wants groups of noble people to support him, not just one noble person. And similar to it is: Many a country has been cut off, and many a hero has been fought. He only means to multiply. Oh, my regret The original is Oh, my regret so the ya’ was replaced with an alif, because it is lighter and more possible in calling for help by extending the sound, and they may have added a ha’ to it. Al-Farra’ recited: Welcome to Najia's donkey. When he comes, I will bring him close to my tongue. And perhaps they added the letter ya after the letter alif to indicate addition. Abu Jaafar read it this way: O my regret, and regret is remorse. For what I neglected in the side of God Al-Hasan said: In obeying God. Ad-Dahhak said: That is, in the remembrance of God Almighty. He said: He means the Qur’an and acting upon it. Abu Ubaidah said: In the side of God That is, in the reward of God. Al-Farra’ said: The side is closeness and neighborhood. It is said: So-and-so lives in the side of so-and-so, meaning in his neighborhood. And from this comes and the companion by the side (An-Nisa’: 36), meaning, for what I neglected in seeking his neighborhood and closeness, which is Paradise. Az-Zajjaj said: That is, for what I neglected on the path, which is the path of God to which He called me. The Arabs call the cause and the path to something a side, they say: I swallowed my sorrows in your side, meaning for your sake and your reason and for the sake of pleasing you. It was said: On the side of God meaning on the side that leads to the pleasure of God Almighty and His reward, and the Arabs call the side a side. The poet said: Divide the effort for that heart, people are beside you and the prince is beside you Meaning the people on one side and the prince on the other. Ban Arafa said: meaning I left it to God’s command. It is said I did not do that because of my need. Kathir said: Do you not fear God while beside a lover who has a heart that is worthy of being cut off? Mujahid said the same, meaning you have wasted God’s command. It is narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: A man does not sit in a gathering, walk, or lie down without remembering God the Almighty in it, except that there will be regret upon him on the Day of Resurrection. That is, regret, regret. Abu Dawud narrated it with the same meaning. Ibrahim Al-Taymi said: Among the regrets on the Day of Resurrection will be that a man sees his wealth that God gave him in this world on the scale of someone else, although he inherited it and acted with it in accordance with what is right. He will have its reward, but the other will bear its burden. Among the regrets will be that a man sees his slave whom God gave him in this world in a position closer to God the Almighty, or he sees a man he knew who was blind in this world, but he himself will see on the Day of Resurrection while he is blind. And if you were among the mockers meaning, you were nothing but one of those who mocked the Qur’an and the Messenger in this world and the allies of God [the Most High]. Qatada said: It was not enough for him that he neglected the obedience of God until he mocked its people. The place of if you were is the accusative case as a state, as if he said: I was negligent while I was mocking, meaning I was negligent in my state of mockery. It was also said: I was nothing but mocking, playing, and falsehood, meaning my only effort was to worship other than God the Most High.
39:57: God the Almighty said: Or this soul should say, ‘If God had guided me,’ meaning if He had directed me to His religion, I would have been among the righteous, meaning against polytheism and sins. This statement, If God had guided me, I would have been guided, is a statement of truth. It is similar to the argument of the polytheists in what the Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, said about them in His statement: Those who associate others with God will say, ‘If God had willed, we would not have associated others with Him.’ (Al-An`am: 148) It is a statement of truth that is intended to mean falsehood, as Ali may God be pleased with him said when a Khawarij said, There is no rule but God’s.
39:58: God Almighty says: Or you say meaning this soul when you see the punishment, ‘If only I had another chance’ meaning a return. So I could be is in the accusative case as a response to the wish, and if you wish it is in apposition to another chance because its meaning is that I would return, as the poet said: Wearing an abaya and having my eyes comforted is more beloved to me than wearing something transparent. Al-Farra recited: You have no blessings from it except remembrance and fear, and you ask about its riders, where they headed. So the word ta'sal is in the accusative case, because the meaning of the speech is that you have no choice but to remember, and from it is to wear a cloak and be content, meaning to wear a cloak and be content. Abu Salih said: There was a knowledgeable man among the Children of Israel who found a note: “A servant may work a long time in obedience to God, and his work will end with the deeds of the people of Hell, so he enters Hell. And a man may work a long time in disobedience to God, and his work will end with the deeds of a man of the people of Paradise, so he enters Paradise.” He said: Why should I tire myself out? So he abandoned his work and took up immorality and disobedience. Satan said to him: You have a long life, so enjoy yourself in this world, then repent. So he took up immorality and spent his money at dawn, and the Angel of Death came to him when he was in the most delicious state he had ever been, and he said: “Oh, how I regret what I neglected in the side of God. My life wasted in obeying Satan.” So he regretted when regret would not benefit him, and God revealed his story in the Qur’an. Qatada said: These are of different types. One of them said: Oh, how I regret what I neglected in my duty to God (al-Zumar 39:56). Another of them said: If God had guided me, I would have been among the righteous (al-Zumar 39:57). Another said: If only I had another chance, I would be among the doers of good (al-Zumar 39:58). So God Almighty said in response to their words:
39:59: The Almighty says: Yes, My signs have come to you. Al-Zajjaj said: Yes is the answer to the negation, and there is no word of negation in the speech, but the meaning of If God had guided me is He would not have guided me. It is as if the speaker said I have not been guided, so it was said, Yes, He has made clear to you the path of guidance, so you were where if you wanted to believe you could believe. My signs meaning the Qur’an. It was said: By signs he meant miracles, i.e. the evidence was made clear, but you denied and belied it. And you were arrogant meaning you were too arrogant to believe. And you were among the disbelievers. He said: You were arrogant and you were and this is addressed to the male, because the soul can be applied to both males and females. It is said: three souls. Al-Mubarrad said: The Arabs say one soul, meaning one person. Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas narrated on the authority of Umm Salamah that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited: Indeed, there came to you My signs, but you denied them and were arrogant and were among the disbelievers. Al-A’mash recited: To me, My signs have come to him. This indicates that it is masculine. Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas did not follow Umm Salamah except that the reading is in the accusative case because nafs can be used for both masculine and feminine forms. Some have rejected this reading and said: If you break the ta’, you should say Wa kuntu min al-kawafir or Wa min al-kafir disbelieving women. An-Nahhas said: This is not necessary. Do you not see that before it is Wa kuntu min al-sakhirin that you say nafs, then He said: And if you were among the mockers, and He did not say Min al-sawakhirin or Min al-sakhirin the mockers. In Arabic, the interpretation of the ta’ with a broken ta’ is and you were arrogant and you were from the plural of magicians or from the mocking people or from the mocking people.
39:60: God the Almighty said: And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about God - their faces will be blackened. That is, because of the wrath and punishment that surrounded them. Al-Akhfash said: You will see tara is not a scholar in his statement: their faces will be blackened. Rather, it is a subject and predicate. Al-Zamakhshari said: A clause in the accusative case if you will see is from seeing with the eyes, and a second object if it is from seeing with the heart. Is there not in Hell an abode for the arrogant? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) explained the meaning of arrogance, saying: Fooling around the truth and looking down on people. That is, despising them. This has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah and other surahs. In the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr, the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: The arrogant will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection like ants, and smallness will overtake them until they are brought to the prison of Hell.
39:62: God Almighty says: “And God will save those who fear Him with their place of safety. No evil will touch them, nor will they grieve.” God is the Creator of all things, and He is, over all things, Disposer of affairs. That is, He is the Preserver and Guardian of them. This has been mentioned previously.
39:63: The Almighty said: To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. The singular is muqalid. It was also said: muqallad and it is mostly used for iqlaid. The keys are the keys according to Ibn Abbas and others. Al-Suddi said: The treasuries of the heavens and the earth. Another said: Like the treasuries of the heavens and the rain, and the treasuries of the earth are the plants. There is another language for it, aqalid and based on that, its singular is iqlaid. Al-Jawhari said: The iqlaid is the keys, and the muqallad is a key like the sickle, perhaps grass is tied with it as it is thrown when it is made into ropes, meaning it is twisted, and the plural is muqalid. And the sea drowned many people, meaning it closed them in. Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that Uthman ibn Affan may God be pleased with him asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about the interpretation of the words of God the Almighty: To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “No one has asked me about it. There is no god but God, and God is the Greatest, and glory be to God and His praise, I seek God’s forgiveness, and there is no power or strength except with God, the Most High, the Most Great. He is the First and the Last, and the apparent and the hidden. He gives life and causes death to come, and He is over all things competent.” Al-Tha’labi mentioned this in his interpretation, and added: “Whoever says it ten times in the morning or evening, God will give him six qualities: the first is that he will be protected from Satan, the second will be attended by twelve thousand angels, the third will give him a qintar of reward, the fourth will raise him in status, the fifth will marry him to the houris, and the sixth will have the reward of someone who recited the Qur’an, the Torah, the Gospel, and the Psalms, and he will also have the reward of someone who performed Hajj and Umrah and his Hajj and Umrah were accepted. If he died that night, he died a martyr.” Al-Harith narrated on the authority of Ali, who said: I asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about the interpretation of the verse: The keys, so he said: “O Ali, you have asked about the greatest of the keys, which is to say ten times in the morning and ten times in the evening: There is no god but God, and God is the Greatest, and Glory be to God, and praise be to God, and I seek forgiveness from God, and there is no power except with God, the First and the Last, and the Outward and the Inward. To Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs praise. God has six qualities: The first is that He protects him from Satan and his soldiers, and they will not have any power over him. The second is that he will be given a quintal in Paradise, which will be heavier in his scale than Mount Uhud. The third is that he will be raised in a degree that only the righteous will attain. The fourth is that God will marry him to the houris. The fifth is that twelve thousand angels will witness it and write it down for him on an open scroll, and they will bear witness to it for him on the Day of Resurrection. The sixth is that he will have a reward as if he had recited the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, and the Criterion, and as if he had performed Hajj and Umrah and God had accepted his Hajj and Umrah. And if he died that day, night, or month, he will be stamped with the stamps of the martyrs.” It was said that the keys are obedience. It is said that someone threw the keys to me, meaning he obeyed him in what he commanded. So the meaning of the verse is that he will be obeyed by In the heavens and the earth. God Almighty says: And those who disbelieve in the signs of God meaning the Qur’an, the arguments and the evidence. Those are the losers. This has been mentioned previously.
39:64: God the Almighty said: "Say: 'Is it other than God that you command me to worship?'" That was when they called the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to what they were doing of worshipping idols and said, It is the religion of your fathers. Ghayr is in the accusative case with a'būd on the basis that I worship other than God in what you command me. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case with ta'muruni by deleting the preposition, the meaning being: Do you command me to worship other than God because 'an' is understood and 'an' and the verb are a verbal noun, and it is a substitute for ghayr, the meaning being: Do you command me to worship other than God? Nafi' recited ta'muruni with one lightened 'nūn and a fathah over the 'ya'. Ibn 'Amir recited ta'muruni with two lightened 'nūns according to the original rule. The rest recited with one stressed 'nūn because of assimilation, and Abu 'Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose this because it occurred with one 'nūn in the copy of 'Uthman. Nafi` read it with the deletion of the second nun, and it was the second deleted letter because repetition and emphasis occur with it. Also, deleting the first letter is not permissible because it indicates the nominative case. Its explanation has already been mentioned in Al-An`am when God the Almighty says: Do you argue with me? (Al-An`am: 80). A`būd means that I worship, so when he deleted an, it was raised, as Al-Kisa`i said. And from it is the saying of the poet: Oh you who deter, prepare for war! The evidence for the correctness of this face is the reading of those who read I worship in the accusative case.
39:65: The Almighty said: And it has already been revealed to you, and to those before you, that if you should associate [anything] with God It was said: There is an inversion in the speech, and the meaning is: It has already been revealed to you, if you should associate [anything] with God, and it was also revealed to those before you. It was also said: And in its proper form, Muqatil said: That is, it has been revealed to you and to the prophets before you regarding monotheism, and there is no omitted monotheism. Then He said: If you should associate [anything] with God, O Muhammad, your work will surely become worthless and this is addressed specifically to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: The address is to him and what is meant is his nation, since God knows that he does not associate [anything] and that association will not occur from him. Frustration means nullification and corruption. Al-Qushayri said: “Whoever apostatizes, his previous acts of obedience will not benefit him, but the nullification of apostasy is conditional upon death as a disbeliever. For this reason, God said: “And whoever among you reverts from his religion and dies while he is a disbeliever - for those, their deeds have become worthless.” (al-Baqarah 2:217) So the general here is interpreted according to the restricted. For this reason we said: Whoever performs Hajj then apostatizes and returns to Islam, he is not required to repeat Hajj. I say: This is the view of Al-Shafi’i. According to Malik, he is required to repeat it. This has been fully explained in Al-Baqarah.
39:66: The Almighty's saying: Rather, worship God. An-Nahhas: In my book on the authority of Abu Ishaq, the wording of the name of God, the Almighty and Majestic, is accusative with worship. He said: There is no difference on this between the Basrans and Kufians. An-Nahhas said: Al-Farra' said: It can be accusative with an implied verb. Al-Mahdawi narrated it on the authority of Al-Kisa'i. As for the fa', Az-Zajjaj said: It is for recompense. Al-Akhfash said: It is redundant. Ibn Abbas said: worship means singular. Someone else said: Rather, God so obey and be among the grateful for His blessings, unlike the polytheists.
39:67: The Almighty said: And they have not appraised God with His true appraisal. Al-Mubarrad said: They did not magnify Him with His true greatness, like when you say so-and-so is of great esteem. An-Nahhas said: The meaning of this is: They did not appraise Him with His true greatness if they worshipped someone other than Him, although He is the Creator and Owner of all things. Then He spoke about His power and greatness, saying: And the earth entirely will be in His grasp on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be rolled up in His right hand. Then He declared Himself free from that being due to any limb, saying: Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him. In At-Tirmidhi, it is narrated on the authority of Abdullah, who said: A Jew came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Muhammad, God holds the heavens on one finger and the creation on one finger, then He says, 'I am the King.' The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) exposed him until his molars were visible, then he said: And they have not appraised God with His true appraisal. He said: This is a good and sound hadith. Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘God will take the earth on the Day of Resurrection and fold the heavens in His right hand, then say: ‘I am the King. Where are the kings of the earth?’” In At-Tirmidhi on the authority of Aisha that she asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about his statement: ‘And the entire earth will be in His grip on the Day of Resurrection and the heavens will be folded in His right hand.’ She said: ‘I said: Where will the people be on that day, O Messenger of God?’ He said: ‘On the Bridge of Hell.’ In another narration: ‘On the Bridge, O Aisha.’ He said: A hasan saheeh hadeeth. His statement: ‘And the entire earth will be in His grip’ and God will take the earth refers to His power and His encompassing of all His creation. It is said: ‘So-and-so is in My grip,’ meaning: ‘So-and-so is in My power.’ People say things are in His grip, meaning in His kingdom and power. The meaning of contraction and folding may be to annihilate and eliminate something. So His statement, And the earth entirely is in His grip may mean that the earth entirely will perish on the Day of Resurrection. What is meant by earth are the seven earths. Two witnesses testify to this: His statement, and the earth entirely because the context is one of emphasis and requires exaggeration. His statement, and the heavens are folded in His right hand does not mean folding or erecting, but rather what is meant by that is annihilation and disappearance. It is said, What we were in has been folded away from us and something else has come to us. And An age has been folded away from us means passing and going. The right hand in Arabic speech can mean power and possession. From this is His statement, Or what your right hands possess? (An-Nisa’ 4:3) meaning possession. And He said, We would have seized him by the right hand (Al-Haqqah 69:45) meaning by power and ability, meaning we would have taken his power and ability. Al-Farra’ and Al-Mubarrad said, The right hand means power and ability. They recited: If a banner is raised for glory, Araba will receive it with her right hand. Another said: When I saw the sun shining, I took what I needed from it with my right hand. He killed Sheneef, then Faran after him, and he was not trustworthy with the verses. And He specifically mentioned the Day of Resurrection, even though His power encompasses everything, because claims are cut off on that, as He said: And the command on that Day is God’s (al-Infitar 82:19) and He said: Owner of the Day of Judgment (al-Fatihah 1:4), as mentioned previously in al-Fatihah. And for that reason He said in the hadith: Then He says, ‘I am the King, where are the kings of the earth?’ We have added to this chapter in al-Tadhkirah an explanation, and we spoke about mentioning the left hand in the hadith of Ibn Umar, in which he said: Then He will fold the earth with His left hand.
39:68: The Almighty says: "And the Trumpet will be blown, and all who are in the heavens and the earth will fall unconscious except whom God wills. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on." He explained what will happen after the earth is seized and the heavens are folded, which is the blowing of the Trumpet. Here there will be two blasts: creation will die in the first and come to life in the second. This has been discussed previously in Surat An-Naml and Surat Al-An'am as well. The one who will blow the Trumpet will be Israfil, peace be upon him. It has been said that Gabriel will be with him, based on the hadith of Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri, who said that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: The two comrades of the Trumpet will have two horns in their hands, staring at each other, when they are commanded. Narrated by Ibn Majah in Sunan. In the book of Abu Dawud, it is narrated on the authority of Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) mentioned the comrade of the Trumpet and said: On his right is Gabriel and on his left is Michael. There is a difference of opinion as to who is excluded. It has been said that they are the martyrs wearing their swords around the Throne. It was narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, as mentioned by Al-Qushayri, and from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar, as mentioned by Al-Tha’labi. It was said: Gabriel, Michael, Israfil, and the Angel of Death, peace be upon them. It was narrated from the hadith of Anas: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited, And the Trumpet will be blown, and everyone in the heavens and the earth will fall unconscious except whom God wills. They said, O Prophet of God, who did God except? He said: (They are Gabriel, Michael, Israfil, and the Angel of Death. Then God the Almighty says to the Angel of Death, Who remains of My creation? And He knows best. He says, O Lord, Gabriel, Michael, Israfil, and Your weak servant, the Angel of Death, and God the Almighty says, Take the souls of Israfil and Michael, and they fall down dead like two great mountains. Then He says, Die, O Angel of Death, and he dies. Then God the Almighty says to Gabriel, O Gabriel, who remains? He says, Blessed and exalted are You, O Possessor of majesty and honor, Your face is everlasting and everlasting. And Gabriel is the dead, mortal. Then God the Almighty says, O Gabriel, your death is inevitable. So he falls down in prostration, flapping his wings, saying, Glory be to You, my Lord, blessed and exalted are You, O Possessor of majesty and honor.) Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, The superiority of His creation over the creation of Michael is like a great mountain over a mountain. Al-Tha’labi mentioned it. An-Nahhas also mentioned it from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) regarding the words of God the Almighty: Then everyone in the heavens and the earth will be stunned, except whom God wills. He said: Gabriel, Michael, the bearers of the Throne, the Angel of Death, and Israfil. In this hadith: “The last of them to die will be Gabriel, peace be upon him.” The hadith of Abu Hurairah about the martyrs is more authentic, based on what was mentioned previously in The Ants. Ad-Dahhak said: It is Ridwan, the Houris, Malik, and the Zabaniyyah. It was also said: The scorpions and snakes of the people of Hellfire. Al-Hasan said: It is God, the One, the Prevailing, and He will not leave anyone from the people of the heavens or the earth except that He will make him taste death. Qatada said: God knows best about His two front teeth. It was also said: The exception in His statement: Except whom God wills refers to whoever dies. It was said: The first blast, meaning everyone in the heavens and the earth will die, except for those who died before, because they had already died. In the two Sahihs and Ibn Majah, and this wording is his, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: A Jewish man in the marketplace of Madinah said: By Him Who chose Moses over all mankind. A man from the Ansar raised his hand and bit him. He said: “You say this while the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is among us.” I mentioned that to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he said: “God, the Almighty, says: ‘And the Trumpet will be blown, and all who are in the heavens and the earth will swoon except whom God wills. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on. ’ So I will be the first to raise his head, and suddenly I will see Moses taking hold of one of the pillars of the Throne. I do not know whether he raised his head before me or whether he was one of those whom God excepted. Whoever says, ‘I am better than Jonah, son of Matta,’ has lied.” At-Tirmidhi also recorded it and said, A good and sound hadith. Al-Qushayri said: “Whoever interprets the exception as referring to Moses and the martyrs, then they have died, but they are alive before God. It is possible that the stunned state is due to the loss of reason, not the loss of life. It is also possible that it is due to death, and it is not far-fetched that both death and life may be involved. All of that is permissible by reason, and the occurrence of the matter depends on the best of what is true.” I said: It was narrated in some of the chains of transmission of Abu Hurairah that he, peace be upon him, said: “Do not prefer me over Moses, for people will faint and I will be the first to regain consciousness. Then Moses will be holding on to the side of the Throne, and I will not know whether he was among those who fainted and regained consciousness before me, or whether he was among those whom God excepted.” Narrated by Muslim. A similar narration was narrated from Abu Sa’id al-Khudri. Recovering only occurs as a result of fainting and loss of reason, not as a result of death due to the coldness of life. And God knows best. God the Almighty said: And behold, they will be standing, looking. That is, when the dead of the earth and the heavens are alive, raised from their graves, and their bodies and souls are returned to them, and they will stand looking to see what they will be commanded. It was said: standing on their feet, looking to see what they were promised. It was also said: this looking means waiting, that is, they are waiting for what will be done for them. Al-Kisa’i permitted standing in the accusative case, as you say: I went out and behold, Zayd was sitting.
39:69: God the Almighty says: And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord. Shining is its illumination. It is said: the sun shone when it illuminated and rose when it rose. The meaning of with the light of its Lord is with the justice of its Lord, as stated by Al-Hasan and others. Ad-Dahhak said: with the judgment of its Lord, and the meaning is the same, that is, it illuminated and shone with the justice of God and His judgment of truth between His servants. Injustice is darkness, and justice is light. It was said: God will create a light on the Day of Resurrection that will cover the face of the earth, and the earth will shine with it. Ibn Abbas said: The light mentioned here is not from the light of the sun and the moon, but rather it is a light that God creates and with which He illuminates the earth. It was narrated that the earth on that day will be made of silver and will shine with the light of God the Almighty when He comes to pass judgment. The meaning is that it will shine with a light that God the Almighty created, so He attributed the light to Him in the same way that He attributes kingship to kingship. It was said: it is the day on which He will judge between His creation, because there will be day without night. Ibn Abbas and Ubaid bin Umair read: And the earth shone without naming its agent, and this is a reading based on explanation. Some people have gone astray here and thought that God, the Almighty, is of the same kind as the light and radiance of something perceptible, but He is exalted above any resemblance to things perceptible. Rather, He is the Illuminator of the heavens and the earth, and from Him comes all light, creation and establishment. Abu Ja`far al-Nahhas said: The Almighty’s statement: And the earth shone with the light of its Lord explains this hadith that has been transmitted through many authentic chains of transmission. You will look at God, the Almighty, and you will not be wronged in seeing Him It has been narrated in four ways: You will not be wronged, you will not be harmed, you will not be harmed, you will not be harmed, so the meaning of You will not be wronged is no harm will befall you as you are afflicted in this world by looking at kings. And You will not be harmed no harm will befall you. And You will not be wronged some of you will not gather together to ask him to show him. And You will not be harmed some of you will not oppose each other. It is said: he harmed him, harming him, meaning he opposed him. The Almighty said: And the Book was placed Ibn Abbas said: He means the Preserved Tablet. Qatada said: He means the Book and the scrolls in which are the deeds of the children of Adam, so I will take him by his right hand and I by his left. And the prophets will be brought means they will be brought and He will ask them about what their nations answered them. And the witnesses are those who testified against the nations from the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as God Almighty says: And thus We have made you a just community that you will be witnesses over mankind (2:143). It was said that what is meant by the martyrs are those who were martyred in the cause of God, so they will bear witness on the Day of Resurrection for those who defended the religion of God. Al-Suddi said: Ibn Zayd said: They are the guardians who bear witness against people regarding their deeds. God Almighty said: And every soul will be brought with it a driver and a witness (2:21). The driver drives it to the reckoning and the witness bears witness over it, and he is the angel assigned to the human being, as will be explained in Qaf. And it will be judged between them in truth meaning with honesty and justice. And they will not be wronged Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: Their good deeds will not be reduced nor will their bad deeds be increased.
39:70: God Almighty says: And every soul will be fully compensated for what it has done of good or evil. And He knows best what they do in this world. He, the Almighty, has no need for a book or a witness. Nevertheless, books and witnesses bear witness to the evidence.
39:71: The Almighty says: And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups. This is a statement that every soul will be fully rewarded for its deeds, so the disbeliever will be driven to Hell and the believer to Paradise. Groups means groups, the singular of which is zumrah, tahtmah, and gathering. Al-Akhfash and Abu Ubaidah said: Groups means scattered groups, one after the other. The poet said: You see people coming to his house in groups, one after the other. Another said: Until I saddened groups after groups It was said: A push and a rebuke with a voice like the sound of a flute. Until, when they come to it, its gates are opened is the answer to if, and it has seven gates. This has been mentioned in al-Hijr. And its keepers said to them one of them is a keeper like sadna and sadan, and they said to them, rebuking and reprimanding them, Did there not come to you messengers from among you reciting to you the verses of your Lord? meaning the books revealed to the prophets. And warning you meaning frightening you of the meeting of this Day of yours? They said, Yes meaning, it has come to us, and this is an admission from them that the proof has been established against them. “But the word of punishment has come true for the disbelievers: “I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together.” (Hud 11:119)
39:72: The Almighty says: It will be said, ‘Enter the gates of Hell.’ That is, it will be said to them, Enter Hell. Its gates have already been discussed. Wahb said: The guards will meet them with whips of fire and will push them with their whips, so that in one push they will fall into Hell as many as Rabi’ah and Mudar. Evil is the abode of the arrogant, this has already been explained.
39:73: The Almighty said: And those who feared their Lord will be driven to Paradise in groups. Meaning, from among the martyrs, ascetics, scholars, reciters of Quran, and others, who feared God Almighty and acted in obedience to Him. He said about both groups: And will be driven with the same wording. The people of Hell will be saved by being expelled to it with shame and disgrace, as is done with prisoners and those who rebel against the ruler when they are driven to prison or killed. The people of Paradise will be driven like their mounts to the abode of honor and contentment, because they will only go riding, as is done with those who are honored and respected among the visitors to some kings. How different the two drives are. Until, when they reach it and its gates are opened. It was said: The waw here is for conjunction, in conjunction with a sentence, and the roamer is omitted. Al-Mubarrad said: Meaning, they were made happy and it was opened. The omission of the answer is eloquent in the speech of the Arabs. He recited: Even if it is a soul that dies as a whole, it is a soul that sheds its souls. So the answer to law was deleted and the meaning would have been it would have been more beautiful. Al-Zajjaj said: Until when they came to it they entered it and this is close to the first. It was said: The waw is redundant. The Kufians said this and it is a mistake according to the Basrans. It was said: The addition of the waw is evidence that the gates were opened for them before they came due to their honor with God the Most High, and the meaning is until when they came to it its gates are open, as evidenced by His statement: Gardens of Eden, their gates open to them (p. 50). And the waw was deleted in the story of the people of Hell because they were granted a light and it was opened after they stood as a humiliation and intimidation for them. Al-Mahdawi mentioned it and Al-Nahhas narrated its meaning before him. Al-Nahhas said: As for the wisdom in proving the waw in the second verse and deleting it from the first, some of the people of knowledge have spoken about it with a statement that I do not know of anyone who spoke before him, which is that when God, the Almighty, said about the people of Hellfire: until, when they come to it and its gates are opened, this indicates that it was closed. And when He said about the people of Paradise: until, when they come to it and its gates are opened, this indicates that it was open before they came to it, and God knows best. It was said: It is the waw of eight, so when they reach seven they say and eight. Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash said this. God Almighty said: He subjected them to seven nights and eight days (al-Haqqah 69:7) and He said: Those who repent are the worshippers Then He said in the eighth: And those who forbid evil (al-Tawbah 9:112) and He said: And they say, ‘Seven and their eighth’ (al-Kahf 18:22) and He said: Wives and virgins (al-Tahrim 66:5) This has been discussed in full in Bara’ah and in Al-Kahf as well. I said: This was used as evidence by those who say that the gates of Paradise are eight. They mentioned the hadith of Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “There is none among you who performs ablution and completes it - or does it perfectly - then says, ‘I bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger,’ but the eight gates of Paradise will be opened for him, and he may enter through whichever of them he wishes.” Narrated by Muslim and others. At-Tirmidhi narrated this hadith of Umar and said in it: Eight gates of Paradise will be opened for him on the Day of Resurrection, with an addition of min, which indicates that the gates of Paradise are more than eight. We have already mentioned this in Kitab at-Tadhkir, and their number ended at thirteen. We have mentioned there the size and vastness of its gates according to what was reported in a related hadith. So whoever wants it can refer to it there. And its keepers will say to them, It was said: And its keepers will say to them, meaning, until they reach it and its gates are opened, “And its keepers will say to them,” “Peace be upon you. You have been well,” meaning in this world. Mujahid said: Through obedience to God. It was also said: Through righteous deeds. Al-Naqqash related it, and the meaning is the same. Muqatil said: When they cross the bridge of Hell, they will be detained on a bridge between Heaven and Hell, and some of them will be punished for the injustices that took place between them in this world. Then, when they are refined and made pure, Ridwan and his companions will say to them: “Peace be upon you” meaning greeting. You have become pure, so enter it to abide therein eternally. I said: Al-Bukhari included this hadith of Al-Qantara in his Jami’ from the hadith of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The believers will be saved from the Fire and detained on a bridge between Paradise and Hell, and some of them will be punished for wrongs committed between them in this world. Then, when they are refined and purified, they will be given permission to enter Paradise. By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, one of them will be better guided in his home in Paradise than in his home in this world.” Al-Naqqash narrated: “At the gate of Paradise is a tree from whose trunk two springs spring forth. The believers will drink from one of them and it will be purified. This is what God, the Most High, said: ‘And their Lord will give them to drink a pure drink.’” (al-Insan 76:21) Then they will wash from the other and their skin will be perfumed. Then its keepers will say to them: ‘Peace be upon you. You have become pure, so enter it to abide therein.’” This meaning is narrated from Ali, may God be pleased with him.
39:74: The Almighty said: And they will say, 'Praise be to God, Who has fulfilled His promise to us.' That is, when they enter, they will say this. And We have given inheritance to the earth. That is, the land of Paradise. It was said that they inherited the land that would have belonged to the people of Hell if they had been believers. This was stated by Abu Al-Aaliyah, Abu Salih, Qatada, Al-Suddi, and the commentators. It was also said that it refers to the land of this world, in both cases. The Almighty said: So excellent is the reward of the workers. It was said that it is from their saying, meaning, what an excellent reward this is. It was also said that it is from the words of God, meaning, what an excellent reward this is for the doers of good that You have given them.
39:75: God the Almighty said: And you will see the angels O Muhammad surrounding i.e. surrounding around the Throne on that Day glorifying with praise of their Lord enjoying that, not worshipping it, i.e. they will pray around the Throne in gratitude to their Lord. Surrendering is taken from the edges and sides of something. Al-Akhfash said: The singular of them is haaf. Al-Farra’ said: It has no singular since the name only applies to them together. Min precedes hawwal because it is a circumstance and a verb is transitive to a circumstance with or without a preposition. Al-Akhfash said: Min is redundant, i.e. surrounding the Throne. It is like saying: No one came to me. “Min” is for emphasis. Al-Tha'labi: The Arabs sometimes add the letter ba to glorification and sometimes leave it out, so they say: Subhanahu hamdulillah. God the Most High said: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High. (Al-A'la: 1) and He said: So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great. (Al-Waqi'ah: 74). And it will be judged between them in truth means between the people of Paradise and the Hellfire. It was also said that it will be judged between the prophets who were brought with the witnesses and their nations with truth and justice. And it will be said, 'Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.' That is, the believers will say, Praise be to God for the blessings and kindness He has rewarded us with and for giving us victory over those who wronged us. Qatada said about this verse: God began the first creation with praise to God, so He said, And it will be judged between them in truth, and it will be said, 'Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.' So it is necessary to follow his example and to begin and end every matter with praise of Him. It was said: The saying Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds is said by the angels, so based on this, their praise is to God Almighty for His justice and judgment. It was narrated in the hadith of Ibn Omar: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited Surat Az-Zumar on the pulpit, and the pulpit moved twice.”
40:1: It is Meccan according to Al-Hasan, Ata', Ikrimah, and Jabir. And from Al-Hasan except for the statement: And glorify the praises of your Lord (Ghafir 40:55) because the prayers were revealed in Medina. Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: Except for two verses of it that were revealed in Medina, which are: Indeed, those who dispute concerning the verses of God (Ghafir 40:56) and the one after it. They are eighty-five verses. And it was said eighty-two verses. In Musnad Al-Darimi, he said: Ja’far bin Awn told us, on the authority of Mis’ar, on the authority of Sa’id bin Ibrahim, who said: The Ha-Mim surahs were called brides. It was narrated from the hadith of Anas that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: The Ha-Mim surahs are the brocade of the Qur’an. A similar hadith was narrated from Ibn Mas’ud. Al-Jawhari and Abu Ubaidah said: Al-Ha-Mim are surahs in the Qur’an. Ibn Ma’ud said: Al-Ha-Mim is the brocade of the Qur’an. Al-Farra’ said: It is like saying Al-Fulani and Al-Fulani, as if he attributed the entire surah to Ha-Mim. Al-Kumait said: We found for you in Al-Ha-Mim a verse that was interpreted by a pious and honorable person from among us. Abu Ubaidah said: This is how Al-Umawi narrated it with a zay, and Abu Amr used to narrate it with a ra’. As for the common people’s saying Hawa Mim, it is not from the speech of the Arabs. Abu Ubaidah said: Hawa Mim are surahs in the Qur’an that are not analogical, and he recited: And with the seven Hawa Mims. He said: It is better to gather them with the letters Ha-Mim. It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “You have something as a fruit, and the fruit of the Qur’an is the letters Ha-Mim. They are beautiful, fertile, and neighboring gardens. So whoever wants to graze in the gardens of Paradise, let him recite the Ha-Mim.” And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The example of the Ha-Mim in the Qur’an is like the ink marks on the garments. Al-Tha’labi mentioned them both. Abu Ubaid said: Hajjaj bin Muhammad told me on the authority of Abu Ma’shar on the authority of Muhammad bin Qais who said: A man saw seven beautiful, adorned slave girls in a dream, so he said: Who are you, may God bless you? They said: We belong to those who recite the Ha-Mim. The meaning of the words of God the Almighty: Ha Meem is disputed. Ikrimah said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Ha Meem is one of the names of God the Almighty and they are the keys to the treasures of your Lord. Ibn Abbas said: Ha Meem is the greatest name of God. It was narrated from him: Alif-Lam-Raam, "Ha Meem, and Noon" are separate letters of the Most Gracious. It was also narrated from him: It is one of the names of God the Almighty by which He swears. Qatada said: It is one of the names of the Quran. Mujahid: The opening letters of the surahs. Ata' al-Khurasani said: The Ha' is the opening letter of His names Hamid, Hanaan, Ha-Hameem, and Ha-Hakeem, and the Meem is the opening letter of His names Malik, Majestic, Mannan, Mutakbir, and Musawwar. This is indicated by what Anas narrated that a Bedouin asked the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): "What is Ha Meem, for we do not know it in our language?" The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "The beginning of names and opening letters of surahs." Ad-Dahhak and Al-Kisa'i said: Its meaning is that what is to happen has been decreed. It is as if he wanted to point out the spelling of Ha Mim because it becomes Ha Mim with a damma on the Ha and a shaddah on the Meem, meaning it was decided and happened. Ka’b bin Malik said: When we met them, and the millstone turned around us, and there was no way to prevent the matter that God had protected. And also on his authority: The meaning of Ha Mim Amr God is that it is near, as the poet said: My day has been busy, some people are distracted and sleepy It was named Al-Ham’ because it brings one closer to death. The intended meaning is that His victory for His friends is near, and His vengeance on His enemies is like the day of Badr. It was said: letters of the alphabet. Al-Darami said: This is why the letters are read with a quiescent sound, so the spelling is excluded. If a surah is named with one of these letters, it is inflected, so you say I read Ha Mim, and it is inflected. The poet said: It reminds me of Hamim and the spear, so why don't you recite Hamim before advancing? Isa bin Omar Al-Thaqafi read it: Ha Mim with a fatha on the meem meaning read Ha Mim or because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Ibn Abi Ishaq and Abu Sammal read it with a kasra. The imala and kasra are for the meeting of two quiescent letters, or as an oath. Abu Jaafar read it with a severance from the ha’ of the meem. The rest read it with a connected pronunciation. Likewise in (Ha Mim. Ain Sin Qaf). Abu Amr, Abu Bakr, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, Khalaf, and Ibn Dhakwan read it with an imala on the ha’. It was narrated from Abu Amr between the two pronunciations, and it is the reading of Nafi’, Abu Jaafar, and Shaibah. The rest read it with a fatha and a full pronunciation.
40:2: The Almighty’s saying: The revelation of the Book is the subject and the predicate is from God, the Exalted in Might, the Knowing. It is possible that the revelation is the predicate of a deleted subject, meaning this the revelation of the Book. It is also possible that Ha Meem is the subject and the revelation is its predicate. The meaning is: God revealed the Qur’an and it is not transmitted nor is it something that can be denied.
40:3: The Almighty said: Forgiver of sin and Accepter of repentance, Severe in penalty. Al-Farra' said: He made it like an adjective for the definite noun although it is indefinite. Al-Zajjaj said: It is in the accusative case as a substitute. An-Nahhas: The investigation and summary of this discussion is that Forgiver of sin and Accepter of repentance may be definite but refer to the past, in which case they are adjectives. It is also permissible for them to refer to the future and the present, in which case they are indefinite. It is not permissible for them to be adjectives on this basis, but their accusative case is as a substitute. The accusative case is permissible as a present state. As for Severe in penalty, it is indefinite and its accusative case is as a substitute. Ibn Abbas said: Forgiver of sin for the one who says: There is no god but God and Accepter of repentance for the one who says: There is no god but God severe in punishment for the one who does not say: There is no god but God (Thabit Al-Bunani said: I was at the tent of Mus’ab bin Al-Rubair in a place where animals do not pass. He said: I recited “Ha Meem. The revelation of the Book is from God, the Exalted in Might, the Knowing” (Al-Baqarah 2:15). A man passed by me on a mount. When I said: Forgiver of sin, he said: Rather, O Forgiver of sin, forgive my sin. When I said: Accepter of repentance, he said: Say, O Accepter of repentance, accept my repentance. When I accepted: severe in punishment, he said: Say, O Severe in punishment, pardon me. When I said: Possessor of bounty, he said: Say, O Possessor of bounty, look upon me with goodness. So I stood up to him and he caught my sight, so I looked right and left but did not see anything. And the people of allusion said: Forgiver of sin is a bounty and Accepter of repentance is a promise severe in penalty is justice there is no god but He; to Him is the return is unique. It was narrated on the authority of Omar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, that he missed a very strong man from the people of Ash-Sham, and it was said to him: You keep drinking this drink, so Omar said to his secretary: Write from Omar to so-and-so, Peace be upon you, and I praise God to you, there is no god but He, in the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. “Ha Meem. The revelation of the Book is from God, the Exalted in Might, the Knowing. Forgiver of sin, Accepter of repentance, Severe in penalty. There is no god but He; to Him is the final destination.” Then he sealed the letter and said to his messenger: Do not give it to him until you find him awake, then he ordered those with him to pray for his repentance, so when the letter came to him, he began to read it and say: God has promised me that He will forgive me and warned me of His punishment, so he did not stop repeating it until he cried, then he died and his death was good and his repentance was good. When Omar heard of his command, he said: “This is what you should do if you see one of you slipping up. Correct him and ask God to forgive him, and do not be helpers of the devils against him.” Al-Tawbah may be the source of taba yatoob he repents and it is possible that it is the plural of tawbah repentance like dawmah dumah and azmah resolve and azm determination. From this, his saying: It fades for an hour and blows away for an hour. It is possible that repentance means repentance. Abu al-Abbas said: What comes to my heart first is that it is a verbal noun, meaning it accepts this verb, as you say he said a saying. If it is plural, then its meaning is it accepts repentance. Dhi al-Tawil is a substitute and an adjective, because it is definite. The root of tawil is to bestow favor and grace. It is said from it: O God, bestow favor and grace upon us. Ibn Abbas said: Dhi al-Tawil is the possessor of blessings. Mujahid said: the possessor of wealth and spaciousness, and from it is the saying of God the Almighty: {And whoever among you cannot afford it} (An-Nisa’: 25) meaning wealth and spaciousness. It is also narrated from Ibn Abbas: Dhi al-Tawil is the one who is independent of those who do not say La ilaha illa God. Ikrimah said: Dhi al-Tawil is the one who bestows favor. Al-Jawhar said: Tawil with the fat-ha is the mann, it is said from it he was tall upon him and he was tall upon him if he bestowed favor upon him. Muhammad bin Kaab said: The One of Generosity is the One of Bounty. Al-Mawardi said: The difference between generosity and generosity is that generosity is forgiveness for a sin, while generosity is an undeserved favor. Generosity is derived from length, as if He prolonged His bounty upon others. It was also said that it was because the duration of His bounty was prolonged. There is no god but He, to Him is the final destination, meaning the place of return.
40:4: God the Almighty says: None dispute concerning the verses of God except those who disbelieve. God the Almighty has recorded for those who dispute concerning the verses of God disbelieve, meaning disputing with falsehood, attacking them, and intending to refute the truth and extinguish the light of God the Almighty. This is indicated by His statement, the Almighty: And they dispute with falsehood to refute thereby the truth. (Ghafir 40:5). As for disputing concerning them to clarify its ambiguities, resolve its disputes, engage scholars in deducing its meanings, and repel those who deviate from it and from it, then it is the greatest jihad in the way of God. This meaning has already been fully explained in Surat Al-Baqarah, when God the Almighty says: Have you not seen him who disputed with Abraham concerning his Lord? (al-Baqarah 2:258). So let not their turning (also read: So let not their turning (i.e. their arrogance) in the lands deceive you, for even if I grant them respite, I will not neglect them, rather I will punish them. Ibn Abbas said: He means their trade from Mecca to Syria and to Yemen. It was said: Do not be deceived by the good and abundance of provision they have, for it is a short enjoyment in this world. Al-Zajjaj said: Do not be deceived by their safety after their disbelief, for their end is destruction. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: Two verses are very difficult for those who dispute about the Quran: His statement: None dispute about the verses of God except those who disbelieve and His statement: And indeed, those who differ over the Scripture are in extreme dissension Al-Baqarah 2:176.
40:5: The Almighty says: The people of Noah denied before them on the feminine form of the group, meaning they denied the messengers. And the parties after them meaning the nations who formed parties against their prophets by denying them, such as Aad and Thamud and those who came after them. And every nation intended to seize their messenger meaning to imprison him and torture him. Qatada and As-Suddi said: to kill him. Seizing is used to mean destroying, like His statement: Then I seized them, so how was My reproach! (al-Hajj 22:44). The Arabs call a prisoner al-Akhidh because he is captured for killing. Qutrub recited the words of the poet: If you take me, you will kill me. How many takers long for my immortality? And about the time when they took their Messenger, there are two sayings: One of them is when he called for them. The second is when the punishment descended upon them. And they argued with falsehood to refute thereby the truth meaning to remove. And from this comes the word dahdha meaning slippery slope, and falsehood is dahdh because it slips and slides and does not remain stable. Yahya bin Salam said: They argued with the prophets with polytheism to invalidate the faith with it. So I seized them or with the punishment. How was the punishment meaning the end of the nations who denied. Meaning, did they not find it to be true.
40:6: The Almighty said: And thus it has come to pass meaning it has become necessary and binding, taken from al-Haqq because it is the necessary. The Word of your Lord This is the reading of the general public on monotheism. Nafi’ and Ibn ‘Amir read: Words all together. Upon those who disbelieve they Al-Akhfash said: meaning because they and because they. Al-Zajjaj said: It is permissible that they are with a kasra on the hamza. The companions of the Fire meaning those who are tormented by it, and the speech is complete. Then he began and said:
40:7: God the Almighty said: Those who bear the Throne and those around it exalt [God] with praise of their Lord and believe in Him and ask forgiveness for those who have believed. It is narrated that the bearers of the Throne have their feet firmly planted on the ground and their heads have pierced the Throne, and they are in humility and do not know where they are going. They are the most noble and best of the angels. In the Hadeeth: “God the Blessed and Exalted commanded all the angels to go out in the morning and evening with peace to the bearers of the Throne, giving them preference over all the other angels.” It is said that God created the Throne from a green gem, and between its two legs is the flapping of a fast bird for eighty thousand years. It was said: Around the Throne are seventy thousand rows of angels, circling it, glorifying and praising God. Behind them are seventy thousand rows standing, placing their hands on their shoulders and raising their voices in glorifying and praising God. Behind them are one hundred thousand rows, placing their right hands on their left hands, and there is not one of them who does not glorify God in a way that no one else does. Ibn Abbas read: the Throne with a damma on the ‘ayn. Al-Zamakhshari may God have mercy on him mentioned all of it. It was said: This is connected to the mention of the disbelievers, because the meaning - and God knows best - those who bear the Throne and those around it declare God Almighty free from what the disbelievers say. And they ask forgiveness for those who believe meaning they ask God Almighty for forgiveness for them. The sayings of the commentators are that the Throne is the bed, and that it is a three-dimensional body created by God Almighty, and He commanded the angels to carry it and worship them by glorifying it and circumambulating around it, just as He created a house on earth and commanded the children of Adam to circumambulate it and face it in prayer. Ibn Tahman narrated on the authority of Musa ibn Uqbah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I have been given permission to speak about one of God’s angels who bears the Throne. The distance between his earlobe and his shoulder is a journey of seven hundred years.” Al-Bayhaqi mentioned that the Throne is mentioned in Ayat al-Kursi, and it is the greatest of all creation. Thawr ibn Yazid narrated on the authority of Khalid ibn Ma’dan, on the authority of Ka’b al-Ahbar, that he said: When God created the Throne, He said: God will never create a creation greater than me. So it withdrew, and God encircled it with a snake. The snake has seventy thousand wings, seventy thousand feathers on its wings, seventy thousand faces on each feather, seventy thousand mouths on each face, and seventy thousand tongues on each mouth. Every day, glorifications of God come out of its mouths, the number of raindrops, the number of leaves on trees, the number of pebbles and dust, the number of days in this world, and the number of all the angels. Then the snake coiled around the Throne, and the Throne reached halfway up the snake while it was coiled around it. Mujahid said: “Between the seventh heaven and the Throne are seventy thousand veils: a veil of light and a veil of darkness, a veil of light and a veil of darkness.” Our Lord, that is, they say, Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, that is, Your mercy and knowledge encompass all things. So when the verb afal was transferred from mercy and knowledge, it was placed in the accusative case as an explanation. So forgive those who have repented, that is, from polytheism and sins, and followed Your way, that is, the religion of Islam. And protect them from the punishment of Hellfire, that is, divert it from them so that it does not reach them.
