Ibrahim al-Nakha’i said: The companions of Abdullah used to say that the angels are better than Ibn al-Kawwa’; they seek forgiveness for those on earth, and Ibn al-Kawwa’ testifies against them of disbelief. Ibrahim said: And they used to say that they do not withhold forgiveness from anyone from the people of the Qiblah. Mutraf ibn Abdullah said: We found the most sincere servants of God to the servants of God to be the angels, and we found the most deceitful servants of God to the servants of God to be Satan, and he recited this verse. Yahya ibn Muadh al-Razi said to his companions about this verse: Understand it, for there is no paradise in the world more hopeful than it. If a single angel asked God to forgive all the believers, He would forgive them. How can that be when all the angels and the bearers of the Throne seek forgiveness for the believers? Khalaf ibn Hisham al-Bazzar, the reciter, said: I used to recite to Sulaym ibn ‘Eesa, and when I reached: And they seek forgiveness for those who have believed, he cried and then said: O Khalaf! How honorable is the believer in the sight of God when he is asleep on his bed while the angels seek forgiveness for him.
40:8: The Almighty says: Our Lord, and admit them to Gardens of Eden. It is narrated that Umar ibn al-Khattab said to Ka'b al-Ahbar: What are Gardens of Eden? He said: Palaces of gold in Paradise, which will be entered by the Prophets, the Truthful, the Martyrs, and the Just Leaders. Which You have promised them which is in the accusative case, describing the Gardens. And whoever is righteous whom is in the accusative case, in apposition to the ha' and the mim in His statement: And admit them. And whoever is righteous through faith, among their fathers, their spouses, and their descendants. A similar verse to this has already been mentioned in Ar-Ra'd. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: A man will enter Paradise and say: O Lord, where are my father, my grandfather, and my mother? Where are my children and my children's children? Where are my wives? It will be said: They did not know as much as You did. He will say: O Lord, I used to work for myself and for them. It will be said: Admit them to Paradise. Then he recited: Those who bear the Throne and those around it until His saying: And whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their offspring. He confirms from this verse His saying: And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith - We will join with them their offspring (al-Tur 52:21).
40:9: The Almighty says: And protect them from evil deeds. Qatada said: That is, protect them from what would harm them. It was also said that the meaning is: protect them from the punishment of evil deeds, and this is a command from whoever God protects, He protects him, with a kasra, meaning He preserves him. And whoever is protected from evil deeds on that Day - He has had mercy on him meaning by entering Paradise and that is the great attainment meaning the great salvation.
40:10: God the Almighty says: Indeed, those who disbelieve will be called, 'The hatred of God is greater than your hatred of yourselves.' Al-Akhfash said: The hatred of God is greater than your hatred of yourselves. This is the lam of initiation, which comes after the word they will be called, because its meaning is it will be said to them, and calling is a statement. Another said: The meaning is that it will be said to them: The hatred of God toward you in this world when you were called to faith and you disbelieved is greater than your hatred of one another on the Day of Resurrection, because some of them were hostile to one another and hated one another on the Day of Resurrection, so they submitted at that time, were submissive, and asked to be released from the Fire. Al-Kalbi said: Every person from the people of the Fire will say to himself, O soul, your hatred. So the angels will say to them while they are in the Fire: The hatred of God toward you when you are in this world and He sent messengers to you and you did not believe is greater than your hatred of yourselves today. Al-Hasan said: They will be given their book of deeds, and when they look at their sins, they will hate themselves, so they will call out, God’s hatred for you in this world, when you were called to faith and you disbelieved, is greater than your hatred for yourselves today. Mujahid said the same meaning. Qatadah said: The meaning is, God’s hatred for you, when you were called to faith and you disbelieved, is greater than your hatred for yourselves when you see the Fire. If it is said: How can they hate themselves? There are two views on this: One of them is that they made their sins the place of something hated. The second view is that when they reached a state where desires left them, and they knew that it was their souls that kept them in sin, they hated them. Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi said: When the people of the Fire despaired of what is with the keepers, and Malik said to them, You will remain (Az-Zukhruf 43:77), as will come, some of them will say to others, O those people! Indeed, what you see of torment and affliction has been sent down to you, so come, let us be patient, perhaps patience will benefit us, just as the people of obedience were patient in obeying God, and patience benefited them if they were patient. So they agreed on patience, so they were patient, and their patience was prolonged. Then they became impatient and cried out, “It is the same for us whether we impatient or patient. There is no escape for us.” (Ibrahim 14:21) That is, no refuge. Then Satan said at that time, “Indeed, God promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I broke my promise to you. And I had no authority over you.” (Ibrahim 14:22) until His saying, I am not your helper, nor are you my helpers. (Ibrahim 14:22) He said, “It will not avail you at all. Indeed, I disbelieved in what you associated with Him before.” (Ibrahim 14:22) So when they heard his words, they hated themselves. He said: So they were called out, God’s hatred is greater than your hatred of yourselves when you were called to faith and then disbelieved, until His saying, Is there any way out? He said: “Then he responded to them, ‘That is because when God alone is called upon, you disbelieve, but if partners are associated with Him, you believe. So the judgment belongs to God, the Most High, the Great.’” Ibn al-Mubarak mentioned it.
40:12: The Almighty said: That is because when God is called upon alone, you disbelieve. That is in the nominative case, meaning the matter That or That is the punishment you are in because of your disbelief. The speech is left unsaid, so respond that there is no way to refute. That is because when God is called upon meaning God is made One Alone, you disbelieve and you deny that divinity is exclusively for Him, and if a polytheist is associated with Him, you believe him and have faith in what He says. Al-Tha'labi said: I heard some of the scholars say: And if a partner is associated with Him after being returned to the world, if it were [in Him] you would believe you would give charity to the polytheist, similar to it, And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden. (Al-An'am: 28) So the judgment belongs to God, the Most High, the Grand regarding Him having a wife or a son.
40:13: The Almighty’s statement: It is He who shows you His signs meaning the proofs of His Oneness and His power and sends down to you provision from the sky He combined the manifestation of signs with the sending down of provision, because religions are based on signs, and bodies are based on provision. These signs are the heavens and the earth and what is in them and between them of the sun, the moon, the stars, the winds, the clouds, the steam, the rivers, the springs, the mountains, the trees, and the traces of garlic that have perished. And none will remember meaning none will take heed from these signs and proclaim the Oneness of God except he who turns back meaning he returns to obeying God.
40:14: God Almighty says: So call upon God meaning worship Him being sincere to Him in religion meaning worship. It was also said: obedience. Even though the disbelievers dislike the worship of God, so do not worship anyone other than Him.
40:15: The Almighty says: Exalted in degrees, Possessor of the Throne Possessor of the Throne is an implied subject. Al-Akhfash said: It is permissible to put it in the accusative case as a praise. The meaning of Exalted in degrees is Exalted in attributes. Ibn Abbas, Al-Kalbi and Saeed bin Jubair said: Exalted in the heavens and the seven heavens. Suhya bin Salam said: It is the elevation of His saints in Paradise. So Exalted according to this means Rafi', Fa'il means Fa'il. According to the first opinion, it is one of the attributes of the One Who is praised, and its meaning is that there is no one higher in rank than Him. He is the One who is deserving of degrees of praise and commendation, which are their types and categories, and none is deserving of them but Him, said Al-Hulaimi. We have already mentioned it in the Most Sublime Book in explanation of the Beautiful Names of God and the limit is for God. Possessor of the Throne means its Creator and Owner, not that He is in need of it. It was said: It is from their saying: The throne of so-and-so has been removed, meaning his kingdom and glory have been removed. He, glory be to Him, is Possessor of the Throne, meaning the permanence of His kingdom and authority. We have explained this in Al-Asna in explaining the beautiful names of God. He sends the Spirit, meaning revelation and prophethood, upon whomever He wills of His servants. It is called a spirit because people live by it, that is, they live from the death of disbelief, just as bodies live by spirits. Ibn Zayd said: The spirit is the Qur’an. God, the Most High, said: And thus We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], a spirit of Our command. (al-Shura 42:52) It was also said that the spirit is Gabriel. God, the Most High, said: The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down. “He brought it down.” (Ash-Shu’ara’: 193) And He said: Say, ‘The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord in truth.’ (al-Nahl 16:102) Of His command, meaning of His statement. It was also said: of His judgment. It was also said that of has the meaning of with, meaning by His command. To whomever He wills of His servants - meaning the prophets - He wills that they be prophets, and none of them has any free will. To warn of the Day of Meeting meaning that the Messenger was sent to warn of the Day of Resurrection. So His statement, To warn refers to the Messenger. It was also said that it means that God, by sending the Messengers to creation, will warn on the Day of Meeting. Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, and Ibn Al-Sameeq read To warn with a ta', addressing the Prophet, peace be upon him. On the Day of Meeting Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: The day when the people of the heavens and the people of the earth will meet. Qatada also said, as did Abu Al-Aaliyah and Muqatil: On it, creation and the Creator will meet. Qaybil: The worshippers and the worshipped. It was also said: The oppressor and the oppressed. It was also said: Every person will meet the reward for his deeds. It was also said: The first and the last will meet on one level. Its meaning was narrated from Ibn Abbas. All of them are correct in meaning.
40:16: The Almighty's saying: The Day they shall appear is a substitute for the first day. It was said that they is in the nominative case as a subject and appears is its predicate and the sentence is in the genitive case as an addition, therefore the tanween was deleted from day. This is according to Sibawayh as the circumstance has the meaning of when, as in I met you on the day of Zayd the Amir. If it had the meaning of when it would not be permissible, as in I will meet you on the day of Zayd the Amir. The meaning of appears is that they will emerge from their graves with nothing covering them, because the earth on that day will be a flat, smooth plain with no crookedness or unevenness, as was explained previously in Ta Ha. Nothing of them is hidden from God It was said that this is the world in The Day they shall appear meaning nothing of them or their deeds is hidden from Him The Day they shall appear. To whom belongs the kingdom today and that is when creation perishes. Al-Hasan said: It is the questioner, the Most High, and He is the Answerer, because He says that when no one answers Him, so He answers Himself, the Most High, and says: To God, the One, the Prevailing. An-Nahhas: The most authentic thing that has been said about it is what Abu Wa’il narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: The people will be gathered on a white land like silver, on which God, the Almighty and Majestic, was not disobeyed. Then a crier will be ordered to call out: To whom belongs the dominion today? The servants, believers and disbelievers alike, will say: To God, the One, the Prevailing. The believers will say this answer out of joy and delight, and the disbelievers will say it out of grief, submission and humility. As for this being the case while creation does not exist, then that is far-fetched, because there is no benefit in it. The statement is correct from Ibn Mas’ud, but it is not what can be taken by analogy or interpretation. I said: The first statement is clear because the intended meaning is to demonstrate His uniqueness in dominion when the claims of the claimants and the lineage of those who relate to Him have ceased, since every king and his kingdom and every arrogant person and his kingdom have vanished, and their lineage and claims have ceased. This is indicated by His words, the Truth, when the earth and souls are seized and the heavens are rolled up: I am the King; where are the kings of the earth? as mentioned previously in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah and in the hadith of Ibn Umar: “Then He will roll up the earth with His left hand and the heavens with His right, then He will say: I am the King; where are the tyrants, where are the arrogant ones?” And from him His words, the Most High: To whom belongs the dominion this day? refer to the cessation of the time of this world, after which there will be resurrection and spreading. Muhammad ibn Ka’b said: His words, the Most High: To whom belongs the dominion this day? will be between the two blasts when creation has perished and the Creator remains, and He will not see anyone other than Himself as a king or a slave, so He will say: To whom belongs the dominion this day? but no one will answer Him, because creation will be dead. Then He will come Himself and say: To God, the One, the Prevailing, because He remained alone and subdued His creation. It was said: A crier will call out and say: To whom belongs the kingdom today? The people of Paradise will respond: To God, the One, the Prevailing. And God knows best. Al-Zamakhshari mentioned this.
40:17: God the Almighty says: This Day every soul will be recompensed for what it has earned. That is, if they acknowledge that sovereignty belongs to God alone on that Day, it will be said to them, This Day every soul will be recompensed for what it has earned, of good or evil. No injustice will there be today. That is, nothing will be diminished from what he has done. Indeed, God is swift in account. That is, He does not require thought or clasping hands as accounting does, because He is the All-Knowing from whom nothing escapes His work, so He does not delay anyone's recompense for being occupied with something else. Just as He provides for them in a single hour, He will also call them to account in a single hour. This meaning was previously mentioned in Al-Baqarah. And in the hadith: And no, the day will not be midday until the people of Paradise have taken their naps in Paradise and the people of Hell have taken their naps in Hell.
40:18: The Almighty said: And warn them of the approaching Day meaning the Day of Resurrection. It is called this because it is near, as everything that is coming is near. So-and-so has approached means he is near, approaching. Al-Nabigha said: The departure has come, but our mounts have not yet begun to move, as if they had That is, it is near. A similar verse is: The Hour has drawn near (al-Najm 53:57), meaning the Hour has drawn near. Some of them used to recite verses like this: The man has come, and I have no provision but sins for my misery and distress When the hearts are at the throats, stifling is a case in which the meaning is understood. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is when the hearts of people are at the throats in a state of stifling. Al-Farra' permitted the estimation to be and warn them stifling. He permitted raising suppressing as predicate of the hearts. He said: The meaning is when they are stifling. Al-Kisa'i said: It is permissible to raise suppressing as a subject. It has been said that what is meant by the approaching day is the day of the approach of death, as said by Qatrub. Likewise, When the hearts are at the throats is when death is approaching. The first is more apparent. Qatadah said: It entered the throats from fear, so it does not come out nor return to its places. This will only happen on the Day of Resurrection, as He said: And their hearts are empty Ibrahim 14:43. It was said: This is a statement about the end of grief, as He said: And the hearts will reach the throats (al-Ahzab 33:10). And the day was added to the approaching on the basis of the imagining of the approaching Day of Resurrection or the approaching Day of Dispute. And according to the Kufians, it is from the category of adding something to itself, like the congregational mosque and the first prayer. The wrongdoers will have no close friend meaning no relative who will benefit nor an intercessor who will be obeyed so that he will intercede for them.
40:19: God the Almighty says: He knows the treachery of the eyes. Al-Mu'arraj said: There is an inversion in this, meaning He knows the treacherous eyes. Ibn Abbas said: It is a man who is sitting with people and a woman passes by, so he steals glances at her. And from him: It is a man who looks at a woman, and when his companions look at him, he lowers his gaze. But if he sees them being careless, he sneaks a glance. But when his companions look at him, he lowers his gaze, and God the Almighty knows from him that he wishes he could look at her private parts. Mujahid said: It is the stealth of the eyes at what God has forbidden. Qatadah said: It is the protrusion of the eye and closing it in a matter that God the Almighty does not like. Ad-Dahhak said: It is a person saying, I did not see, when he saw, or I saw, when he did not see. As-Suddi said: It is the symbol with the eye. Sufyan said: It is a glance after a glance. Al-Farra’ said: “The traitorous eyes is the second glance, and what the hearts conceal is the first glance. Ibn Abbas said: And what the hearts conceal meaning, would he commit adultery with her if he were alone with her or not? It was also said: And what the hearts conceal what they conceal and hide. When Abdullah ibn Surayh was brought to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) after the people of Mecca were reassured and Uthman may God be pleased with him had asked for his safety, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was silent for a long time, then he said: Yes. When he left, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to those around him: “I was only silent so that one of you might rise up and strike off his head.” A man from the Ansar said: Why didn’t you come to me, O Messenger of God? He said: A Prophet does not have traitorous eyes.
40:20: The Almighty says: And God judges with truth meaning He will punish whoever lowers his gaze from forbidden things, whoever looks at them, and whoever intends to commit immoral acts if he is able to. And those they invoke besides Him meaning idols do not judge at all because they do not know anything, nor are they able to do it, nor do they possess it. The general reading is with the letter ya as a predicate of the wrongdoers, and this is the preferred choice of Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim. Nafi', Shaibah, and Hisham read: You invoke with the letter ta, Indeed, God is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing Huwa as an extra separator. It is permissible for it to be in the nominative case as a subject, and what follows it is the predicate, and the sentence in.
40:21: His Almighty saying: Have they not traveled through the land and observed? is in the jussive mood in apposition to they travel. It is also permissible for it to be in the accusative mood as an answer, and the jussive and accusative moods in the dual and plural are the same. How was the outcome? is the subject of kana and the predicate is in kayfa. Waaq is in the genitive mood in apposition to the word. It is also permissible for it to be in the nominative mood in apposition to place, so its nominative and genitive cases are the same, because the ya is dropped and the kasra remains to indicate it. The meaning of this verse has been discussed in more than one place due to repetition.
40:22: God Almighty says: “That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved, so God seized them. Indeed, He is Powerful and Severe in penalty.”
40:23: The Almighty said: And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs and the end of the nine signs mentioned in the Almighty's saying: And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs and clear authority and their specification has already been mentioned. And clear authority means with a clear and evident argument, and it is masculine and feminine. It was said that what he meant by authority is the Torah.
40:24: The Almighty said: To Pharaoh, Haman, and Korah. He mentioned them specifically because the plotting behind Moses' enmity was against them. Pharaoh was the king, Haman was the minister, and Korah was the owner of wealth and treasures. So God included him with them because his actions in disbelief and denial were like their actions. They said, 'A lying magician.' When they were unable to oppose him, they attributed the miracles to magic.
40:25: The Almighty says: But when he brought them the truth from Us - which is the apparent miracle - they said, 'Kill the children of those who believed with him.' Qatada said: This was a killing different from the first killing, because Pharaoh had refrained from killing parents after the birth of Moses. When God sent Moses, he renewed the killing of the Prophet of Israel as a penalty for them, so that people would refrain from believing, and so that their numbers would not increase and they would be strengthened by the remembrance of their children. But God distracted them from that by sending down upon them various types of torment, such as frogs, lice, and the flood, until they left Egypt, and then God drowned them. This is the meaning of the Almighty's saying: And the plot of the disbelievers is only in error - meaning in loss and destruction. People will not refrain from believing, even if something similar is done to them, but their plot will go in vain.
40:26: God the Almighty says: And Pharaoh said, ‘Let me kill Moses, and let him call upon his Lord.’ “Kill” is in the subjunctive mood because it is the response to a command. And let him call upon is in the subjunctive mood because it is a command. Leave me is not in the subjunctive mood even though it is a command, but its wording is in the subjunctive mood and it is constructed. It was said: This indicates that it was said to Pharaoh: Indeed, we fear that they will call upon you and he will be answered. So he said: And let him call upon his Lord. That is, do not be alarmed by what he mentions about his Lord, for it has no reality, and I am your most high Lord. Indeed, I fear that he will change your religion, that is, your worship of me to the worship of his Lord. Or that corruption will appear on earth. If he does not change your religion, then corruption will appear on earth. That is, discord will occur among the people because of it. The reading of the Medinans, Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, Ibn Amir and Abu Amr is: and that corruption should appear on earth and the reading of the Kufians is or that corruption should appear with the opening of the ya’ with the nominative case and this is how it is in the Kufic copies of the Qur’an: or with an alif and Abu Ubaid agrees with this and said: Because it has an extra letter and a separation, and because or can have the meaning of and. An-Nahhas said: According to the most skilled grammarians, it is not permissible for it to have the meaning of and, because that would invalidate the meanings. If it were permissible for it to have the meaning of and, there would be no need for this here, because the meaning of and is that I fear both matters and the meaning of or for one of the two matters is I fear that your religion will be changed, so if that is not possible, corruption will appear on earth.
40:27: God Almighty said: And Moses said, ‘Indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord.’ When Pharaoh threatened to kill him, Moses sought refuge in God from every arrogant one, meaning one who is too proud to believe in God, and described him as not believing in the Day of Judgment.
40:28: It contains four issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And a believing man said, Some commentators mentioned that this man’s name was Habib. It was also said that he was Shimaan, with the letter sh. Al-Suhayli said: This is the most correct statement made about him. In the history of Al-Tabari, may God have mercy on him: His name is Khabrak. It was also said that he was Ezekiel. Al-Tha’labi mentioned this on the authority of Ibn Abbas and most scholars. Al-Zamakhshari said: His name was Simeon or Habib. It was also said that he was Kharbil or Hizbil. There was disagreement as to whether he was an Israelite or a Qutbite. Al-Hasan and others said that he was a Copt. It was also said that he was the cousin of Pharaoh, as Al-Suddi said. He said: He is the one who was saved with Moses, peace be upon him, and that is why He said: of the family of Pharaoh. This man is the one meant by the Almighty’s saying: “And a man came running from the farthest part of the city. He said, ‘O Moses!’” (al-Qasas 28:20) The verse. This is the statement of Muqatil. Ibn Abbas said: There was no believer from the family of Pharaoh other than him, Pharaoh’s wife, and the believer who warned Moses, saying, The eminent ones are plotting to kill you. It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The truthful ones are Habib al-Najjar, the believer from the family of Yasin; and the believer from the family of Pharaoh, who said, ‘Do you kill a man because he says, ‘My Lord is God?’ and the third is Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, and he is the best of them.” In this there is consolation for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, meaning, do not be amazed by the polytheists of your people. This man had standing with Pharaoh, and for this reason he did not harm him. It was also said that this man was from the Children of Israel who concealed his faith from the family of Pharaoh, also from al-Suddi. In the discussion of this there is an inversion, and the interpretation is: And a believing man said who concealed his faith from the family of Pharaoh. So whoever considers the man a Copt, then min is related to an omitted word as an attribute of the man, the interpretation is: And a believing man said, attributed to the family of Pharaoh, meaning from his family and relatives. And whoever considers him an Israelite, then min is related to yaktam in the position of the second object of yaktam Al-Qushayri: And whoever considers him an Israelite, then there is a discrepancy in that, because it is said that he concealed such and such a matter from him, but it is not said that he concealed it from him. God Almighty said: And they do not conceal from God a word (An-Nisa’: 42). Also, Pharaoh could not tolerate such a statement from the Children of Israel. The second: The Almighty’s saying: Would you kill a man because he says, ‘My Lord is God’? That is, because he says, and for the sake of because he says, ‘My Lord is God’, then that is in the accusative case, with the preposition removed. And he has come to you with clear proofs meaning the nine verses “from your Lord. But if he is a liar, upon him is his lie.” This was not because of doubt on his part in his message and truthfulness, but rather as a way of being gentle in asking for forgiveness and to avoid harm. If and if had been with the letter nun it would have been permissible, but the letter nun was deleted due to frequent usage according to Sibawayh, and because it is the letter nun of i’rab according to Abu al-Abbas. And if he is truthful, some of what he promises you will befall you, that is, if nothing befalls you except some of what he promises you, you will be destroyed. Abu Ubaidah’s school of thought is that the meaning of some of what he promises you is everything he promises you, and he recited the words of Labid: There are places where I don't like them, or some souls are attached to their bathrooms. So, some means all, because if some are afflicted, all will inevitably be afflicted, as they are included in the threat. This is a softening of speech in preaching. Al-Mawardi said: Some may be used in place of all to soften the speech and expand the speech, as the poet said: The patient may realize some of his need, while the hasty may make mistakes. It was also said: He said that because he warned them of different types of punishment, each of which is destructive. It was as if he warned them that one of the two punishments would befall them. Moses promised them the punishment of this world or the punishment of the Hereafter if they disbelieved, so the meaning is that one of the two punishments would befall you. It was also said: That is, this punishment that he spoke of would befall you in this world and is part of the threat, then the punishment would be repeated in the Hereafter as well. It was also said: He promised them punishment if they disbelieved and reward if they believed, so if they disbelieved, some of what they were promised would befall them. Indeed, God does not guide one who is transgressing against himself, a liar against his Lord, referring to Moses, and this would be from his saying, the believer. It was said: transgressing in his stubbornness, a liar in his claim, referring to Pharaoh, and this would be from the saying of God the Most High. Third: The Almighty’s saying: conceals his faith. Judge Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi said: Some of them thought that if a person who is accountable conceals his faith and does not utter it with his tongue, he is not a believer by virtue of his belief. Malik was inclined: If a man intends in his heart to divorce his wife, it is binding on him, just as he is a believer in his heart and a disbeliever in his heart. So he made the basis of faith on the heart, and that is the case, but not absolute. We have explained this in the Principles of Jurisprudence, the gist of which is that if a person who is accountable intends disbelief in his heart, he is a disbeliever even if he does not utter it with his tongue. However, if he intends faith in his heart, he is not a believer under any circumstances until he utters it with his tongue. Taqiyya and fear do not prevent him from uttering it with his tongue in what is between him and God Almighty. Rather, taqiyya prevents him from being heard by others. It is not a condition of faith that others hear it for it to be valid and accountable. Rather, it is a condition that others hear it for him to refrain from harming himself and his property. Fourth: Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: I said to Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As: Tell me about the worst thing the polytheists did to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: While the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in the courtyard of the Kaaba, Uqbah ibn Abi Mu’ayt took his place and seized the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, by the shoulder, twisted his garment around his neck and strangled him violently. Then Abu Bakr came forward and seized his shoulder and pushed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Do you kill a man because he says, ‘My Lord is God,’ when he has come to you with clear proofs from your Lord? Bukhari’s wording. Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim narrated in Nawader Al-Usul from the hadith of Ja’far bin Muhammad from his father from Ali may God be pleased with him who said: The Quraysh gathered after the death of Abu Talib with three men and wanted to kill the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). One of them came, attacking him and another, and the other tried to kill him. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called for help that day, but no one helped him except Abu Bakr, who had two braids. So he came, attacking this one and trying to kill that one, and saying at the top of his voice: Woe to you! Do you kill a man because he says, ‘My Lord is God?’ By God, he is the Messenger of God. So one of Abu Bakr’s braids was cut off that day. Ali said: “By God, the day of Abu Bakr is better than the believer of the people of Pharaoh. That was a man who concealed his faith, but God praised him in His Book. But this Abu Bakr showed his faith and sacrificed his wealth and blood for the sake of God, the Almighty and Majestic.” I said: The statement of Ali may God be pleased with him that this was a man who concealed his faith means that this was in the beginning, unlike Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him, who showed his faith and did not hide it. Otherwise, the Quran clearly states that the believer from the family of Pharaoh showed his faith when they wanted to kill Moses (peace be upon him), as will be explained. In Nawader Al-Usul also on the authority of Asma bint Abi Bakr may God be pleased with her, they said to her: What is the most difficult thing you saw the polytheists do with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him)? She said: The polytheists were sitting in the mosque, discussing with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) what he said about their gods. While they were like that, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would enter, and they would all stand up to him. When they asked him about something, he would tell them the truth. They said: Didn’t you say such and such about our gods? He said: Yes. They all clung to him until the cry came to Abu Bakr, who said to him: Save your companion. He left us and he had many tresses, and he entered the mosque saying: And for you, ‘Would you kill a man because he says, “My Lord is God, while he has come to you with clear proofs from your Lord?” So they turned away from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and turned to Abu Bakr. Abu Bakr returned to us and did not touch any of his hair except that it came with it, and he was saying: Blessed are You, O Possessor of majesty and honor, honor, honor.
40:29: The Almighty says: O my people, yours is the kingdom today. This is from the words of the believer from the family of Pharaoh. His saying: O my people is evidence that he was a Copt, and that is why He added them to himself and said: O my people so that they would be more likely to accept His advice. Yours is the kingdom, so thank God for that. Victorious in the land means prevailing. It is in the accusative case as a state, meaning in the state of your victory. What is meant by land is the land of Egypt according to Al-Suddi and others, like His saying: And thus We established Joseph in the land (Yusuf 12:56) meaning in the land of Egypt. Then who will protect us from the punishment of God if it comes to us? That is, from the punishment of God, warning them against His punishment if Moses was truthful. So he reminded and warned, and Pharaoh knew that his argument was clear, so he said: I do not show you except what I see. Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: I do not advise you except what I see for myself. And I do not guide you except to the path of right conduct in denying Moses and in believing in Me.
40:30: The Almighty said: And O my people, indeed I fear for you the Day of Calling. He increased the admonition and intimidation and revealed his faith, either submitting and preparing himself for the fight, or confident that they did not intend him harm, and God protected him from their evil with His true statement: So God protected him from the evil of their plotting. The common reading is the Calling with a light dal, and it is the Day of Resurrection. Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt said: And He spread out the creation, and when He spread it out, they understood its inhabitants until they called out. It was called thus because people call out to one another. The Companions of the Heights will call out to men they recognize by their mark, and the Companions of Paradise and the Companions of the Fire will call out, Indeed, we have found what our Lord promised us to be true. (Al-A’raf 7:44) The Companions of the Fire will call out to the Companions of Paradise, Pour on us some water. (Al-A’raf 7:50) The crier also calls out for misery and happiness: “Surely, so-and-so, son of so-and-so, has been wretched with a misery after which he will never be happy. Surely, so-and-so, son of so-and-so, has been blessed with a happiness after which he will never be miserable.” This is when deeds are weighed. The angels will call out to the Companions of Paradise, Indeed, this is Paradise which you have inherited for what you used to do. (Al-A’raf 7:43) And when death is slaughtered, it will call out, O People of Paradise, eternity without death! O People of the Fire, eternity without death! And every people will call out for their mothers, and so on. Al-Hasan ibn al-Samiq, Ya`qub, Ibn Kathir and Ibn Mujahid read: al-tanad with the addition of the ya’ in both connected and paused states, according to the original text. Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak and `Ikrimah read yawm al-tanad with a shaddah on the dal. Some Arabists said: This is a mistake, because it is from nada yanda, meaning to run away, as the poet said: And I am leaving, and my fear of her clubs has stirred up my spirits. I strive with naked anger. He said: This has no meaning on the Day of Resurrection. Abu Ja`far al-Nahhas said: This is a mistake, and reading it as such is good, as it means the Day of Discord. Ad-Dahhak said: That is when they hear the roaring of Hell, they will call out in flight, and they will not come to any region of the earth except that they will find rows of angels, so they will return to the place they were in. This is what He said: The Day of Calling and His saying: O company of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth (Ar-Rahman 55:33) and the verse. And His saying: And the angels are over its corners (Al-Haqqah 59:17) Ibn al-Mubarak mentioned this meaning. He said: Abdur-Rahman bin Yazid bin Jabir informed us: Abdur-Jabbar bin Ubaidullah bin Salman informed us regarding the words of God the Almighty: {Indeed, I fear for you the Day of Calling * The Day you will turn back in retreat} Then their eyes will respond to them with tears, so they will weep until the tears run out. Then their eyes will respond to them with blood, so they will weep until the blood runs out. Then their eyes will respond to them with pus. He said: A command from God will be sent upon them, so they will turn back in retreat. Then their eyes will respond to them with pus, so they will weep until the pus runs out and their eyes will be sunk like burning in mud. It was said: This will happen when Israfil, peace be upon him, blows the trumpet with the blast of terror. It was mentioned by Ali ibn Ma'bad, al-Tabari and others from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, which states: "Then the earth will be like a ship in the sea, battered by waves, so people will rock on its back, nursing mothers will be stunned, pregnant women will give birth to what is in their bellies, children will turn gray, and the devils will fly away, and the angels will meet them, striking their faces, and people will turn their backs, calling out to one another. This is the one about which God the Most High will say: "The Day of Calling * The Day you will turn your backs, having no protector from God. And whomever God sends astray, for him there is no guide." The hadith in full. We have already mentioned it in Kitab al-Tadhkirah and discussed it there. It was narrated from Ali ibn Nasr from Abu Amr that the sukoon on the dal in tanad is only in the wasl. Abu Ma'mar narrated from Abdul Warith that the ya' was added only in the wasl, and this is the view of Warsh. The well-known view from Abu Amr is to delete it in both cases. The rest of the seven recited this way, except for Warsh, according to what we mentioned from him, and except for Ibn Kathir, according to what was mentioned above. It was said: The Day of Resurrection was called the Day of Calling, because the unbeliever will be called out on it with woe, destruction, and regret. Ibn Jurayj said the same. It was also said: It contains an implied meaning, I fear for you the punishment of the Day of Calling. And God knows best.
40:31: The Almighty said: The Day you will turn back in retreat as a substitute for the Day of Calling And he whom God sends astray - for him there is no guide meaning, whoever God creates misguidance in his heart, there is no guide for him. There are two sayings about who said it: One of them is Moses. The second is the believer of the family of Pharaoh, and this is the more apparent. And God knows best.
40:32: God the Almighty says: And Joseph had already come to you before with clear proofs. It was said that this was from the words of Moses. It was also said that it was part of the sermon delivered to the believers from the family of Pharaoh. He mentioned their long-standing arrogance towards the prophets, and he meant that Joseph, son of Jacob, came to them with clear proofs. Are separate lords better or God, the One, the Prevailing? (Yusuf 12:39) Ibn Jurayj said: He is Joseph, son of Jacob. God the Almighty sent him as a messenger to the Copts after the death of the king before Moses with clear proofs, which are visions. Ibn Abbas said: He is Joseph, son of Ephraim, son of Joseph, son of Jacob. He stayed among them as a prophet for twenty years. Al-Naqqash narrated from Al-Dahhak that God the Almighty sent to them a messenger from the jinn called Joseph. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: The Pharaoh of Moses is the Pharaoh of Joseph, Omar. Others say: He is the last. An-Nahhas: There is nothing in the verse that indicates that it is him, because if a prophet brought clear proofs to those with him and those after him, then he brought them to all of them and it is upon them to believe him in them. So you did not cease to be in doubt about that which he brought you meaning your ancestors were in doubt. Until, when he perished, you said, ‘God will never send after him a messenger’ meaning one who claims to be a messenger. Thus does God mislead meaning like that misguidance God misleads whoever is a transgressor “polytheist” doubter “doubter of the Oneness of God Almighty.”
40:33: The Almighty said: "The Day you will turn back in retreat as a substitute for the Day of Calling And he whom God sends astray - for him there is no guide" meaning, whoever God creates misguidance in his heart, there is no guide for him. There are two sayings about who said it: One of them is Moses. The second is the believer of the family of Pharaoh, and this is the more apparent. And God knows best.
40:34: God the Almighty says: And Joseph had already come to you before with clear proofs. It was said: This is from the words of Joseph bin Yaqoub, he came to them with clear proofs. Are separate lords better or God, the One, the Prevailing? (Yusuf 12:39) Ibn Jurayj said: He is Joseph bin Ya'qub, God the Almighty sent him as a messenger to the Copts after the death of the king before Moses, with clear proofs, which are visions. Ibn Abbas said: He is Joseph bin Ephraim bin Joseph bin Ya'qub, he stayed among them as a prophet for twenty years. Al-Naqqash narrated from Al-Dahhak that God the Almighty sent to them a messenger from the jinn called Joseph. Wahb bin Munabbih said: The Pharaoh of Moses is the Pharaoh of Joseph, Umar. Others say: He is the last of Al-Nahhas. The verse does not indicate that it is him, because if a prophet comes with clear proofs for those who are with him and those who come after him, then he has brought them all with them and it is upon them to believe him in them. And you have not ceased to be in doubt about that which he has brought to you. That is, your ancestors were in doubt. Until, when he perishes, you say, ‘God will never send after him a messenger.’ That is, one who claims to be a messenger. Thus does God mislead. That is, like misguidance. God misleads one who is a transgressor, a polytheist, a doubter. “Doubters” who doubts the Oneness of God Almighty.
40:35: The Almighty says: Those who dispute concerning the verses of God meaning His apparent proofs without authority meaning without proof or evidence. And those is in the accusative case as a substitute for whom. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, God misguides those who dispute concerning the verses of God, so those is in the accusative case. He said: This is permissible from the words of the believer of the family of Pharaoh. It was also said: It is the beginning of an address from God the Almighty. with hatred is for clarification, meaning great is their dispute with hatred like His statement: and on the left (al-Kahf 18:18). And God the Almighty hates clarification, meaning He curses them and brings punishment upon them. Thus meaning, just as God has sealed the hearts of these disputants, so too God seals meaning He seals the heart of every arrogant, tyrannical person so that they do not understand what is right and do not accept the truth. The general reading is upon every arrogant heart by adding heart to the arrogant, and this was chosen by Abu Hatim and Abu Ubaid. There is an omission in the speech and the meaning is: Thus does God set a seal over every heart of every arrogant tyrant, so the second every was omitted because of the evidence for it. If the omission of every was not possible, the meaning would not be correct, because it would mean that He seals his entire heart and not the meaning is on him. Rather, the meaning is that He seals the hearts of the arrogant tyrants, heart by heart. What indicates the omission of every is the statement of Abu Dawud: A man you think is a man, but a fire lit at night is a fire. And every fire will return. And in the reading of Ibn Masoud upon the heart of every arrogant person, this is a reading based on explanation and addition. Abu Umur, Ibn Mahsin and Ibn Dhakwan, on the authority of the people of Ash-Sham, read heart with a tanween, based on the fact that arrogant is an adjective for the heart, so the heart is a metaphor for the whole, because the heart is the one that is arrogant and the rest of the organs follow it. For this reason, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Indeed, in the body there is a morsel of flesh which, if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. And that is the heart.” And it is permissible for the addition to be deleted, meaning upon every person with an arrogant heart, making the description for the owner of the heart.
40:36: God the Almighty said: And Pharaoh said, ‘O Haman, build for me a tower.’ When the believer from Pharaoh’s family said what he said, and Pharaoh feared that the words of this believer would take root in the hearts of the people, he thought that he was testing what Moses had brought of monotheism. If it became clear to him that it was correct, he would not hide it from them, but if it was not correct, he would make them steadfast in their religion. So he ordered his minister Haman to build the tower. This was mentioned previously in Al-Qasas. Perhaps I will reach the causes.
40:37: The Almighty said: The causes of the heavens The causes of the heavens is a substitute for the first. The causes of the heavens are its gates according to Qatada, Al-Zuhri, Al-Suddi, and Al-Akhfash. He recited: Whoever fears the causes of death will attain it, even if he seeks the causes of heaven with a ladder. Abu Saleh said: The paths of the heavens are their ways. It was also said: The things that the heavens hold onto. He repeated paths to emphasize the meaning, because when something is vague and then made clear, it emphasizes its importance. And God knows best. So he looked at the God of Moses So he looked at Him with a gaze that overlooked Him. He imagined that He was a body contained in places. Pharaoh claimed divinity and saw its realization in sitting in a prominent place. The common people read fa-tala’a in the nominative case, in agreement with his saying I reach. Al-A’raj, Al-Sulami, Issa, and Hafs read fa-tala’a in the accusative case. Abu Ubaidah said: It is in response to perhaps with the letter fa. An-Nahhas said: The meaning of the accusative is the opposite of the meaning of the nominative case, because the meaning of the accusative is that when you reach the paths, you look. The meaning of the nominative case is Perhaps I will reach the paths, then Perhaps I will look after that, except that then is more delayed than fa. “And I think he is a liar” means that I think Moses is a liar in his claim to be a god other than me, and I only do what I do to remove the reason. This caused Pharaoh to doubt God's command. It was said that suspicion means certainty, meaning that I am certain that he is lying, and I only say what I say to remove doubt from someone who is not certain of what I am certain of. God the Almighty said: And thus the evil of his deed was made attractive to Pharaoh meaning, just as he said this statement and doubted, Satan made his evil deed attractive to him, meaning polytheism and denial. And was averted from the path is the reading of the Kufians wasd without naming the agent, and this is the choice of Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim. It is permissible according to this reading wasd with a kasra on the sad and the kasra on the dal was transferred to the sad, and this is the reading of Yahya ibn Waththab and Alqamah. Ibn Abi Ishaq and Abdurrahman ibn Bakra read wasd from the sabi’il with the nominative case and tanween. The rest wasd with a fatha on the sad and the dal. Meaning, Pharaoh averted the people from the path. And the plot of Pharaoh was nothing but ruin meaning in loss and misguidance. From this is the saying: Perish the hands of Abu Lahab (al-Masad 111:1) and His saying: And they did not increase them except in ruin (Hud 11:101). And in a place except in loss (Hud 11:63), God destroyed his edifice and drowned him and his people as mentioned above.
40:38: God the Almighty said: And he who believed said, ‘O my people, follow me.’ This is part of what the believer of Pharaoh’s family said, meaning, follow my example in religion. I will guide you to the path of right conduct, meaning the path of guidance, which is Paradise. It was also said that it was from the words of Moses. Muadh ibn Jabal read ar-rashad with a shaddah on the shin, which is a mistake according to most Arab scholars, because it is said that it is irshad yurshed and it is not fa’al from af’al, rather it is from the triliteral, so if you want to multiply from the quadriliteral you say: mifa’al. An-Nahhas said: It is possible that rashad means yurshed, not that it is derived from it, but just as it is said la’al from pearls, so it has the same meaning and is not governed by it. It is also possible that rashad is from rashd, meaning the companion of rashd, as he said: Clean me up for them, O Umaima, you are a heretic Al-Zamakhshari: Al-Rashad is read as Fa’al from Rashd with a Kasra like ‘Alam or from Rashd with a Fatha like ‘Ibad. It was said: from Arshad like Jabbar from Ajbara but that is not the case because Fa’al from Af’al only occurs in a few letters: like Darak and Sar and Qasar Nujbar. Analogy is not valid based on this rare occurrence. It is possible that it is attributed to Rashd like ‘Awaj and Batat but not considered to be Fa’al. It appears in the Mus-haf as Atba’oon without a Ya’. Ya’qub and Ibn Kathir read it with the affirmation in both connected and paused pronunciation. Abu ‘Amr and Nafi’ deleted it when pausing and affirmed it when connected, except for Warsh who deleted it in both cases, and so did the rest because it occurred in the Mus-haf without a Ya’ and whoever affirmed it is according to the original.
40:39: God Almighty says: O my people, this worldly life is only a temporary enjoyment. That is, it is enjoyed for a little while, then it comes to an end and disappears. And indeed, the Hereafter is the home of settlement. That is, stability and eternity. What He means by the Hereafter is Heaven and Hell, because they do not perish. He explained this by saying:
40:40: The Almighty said: Whoever does evil meaning polytheism will not be recompensed except with the like thereof which is the punishment. And whoever does righteousness Ibn Abbas said: meaning there is no god but God while he is a believer believing in God and the prophets in his heart they will enter Paradise with a damma on the ya’ for what the doer is not named. This is the reading of Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaysin, Abu Amr, Ya’qub, and Abu Bakr on the authority of Asim, which indicates they will be provided for therein without account the rest enter with a fatha on the ya’.
40:41: God Almighty said: O my people, why do I invite you to salvation meaning to the path of faith that leads to Paradise and you invite me to the Fire? He explained that what Pharaoh said in his statement And I do not guide you except to the path of right conduct is the path of error whose consequence is the Fire, and they were inviting him to follow it, and for this reason he said.
40:42: God Almighty said: You call me to disbelieve in God and associate with Him that of which I have no knowledge - and he is Pharaoh - and I call you to the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving.
40:43: The Almighty's statement: There is no doubt. This has been discussed previously. Its meaning is true. That you call Me to ma means that which has no call. Al-Zajjaj said: No call will be answered that will benefit him. Another said: He has no call that will make him divinity in this world or in the Hereafter. Al-Kalbi said: He has no intercession in this world or in the Hereafter. Pharaoh first called people to worship idols, then he called them to worship cows. They were worshipped while they were young, but when they grew old, he ordered them to be slaughtered. Then he called for others to be worshipped. Then, when time passed, he said: I am your highest lord. "And that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire." Qatadah and Ibn Sirin said: He means the polytheists. Mujahid and Ash-Sha'bi said: They are the foolish and those who shed blood unjustly. Ikrimah said: The tyrants and the arrogant. It was also said: They are those who transgressed the limits set by God. This encompasses all that has been mentioned. And an in the places is in the accusative case by dropping the preposition. And according to what Sibawayh narrated on the authority of Al-Khalil, we know that la jram is a response to a statement that could be in the place of an in the nominative case, assuming that it is necessary that what you are calling me to is invalid, as if he said: It is necessary that what you are calling me to is invalid, and the return is to God, and that the transgressors are the people of the Fire.
40:44: The Almighty's saying: Then you will remember what I say to you. is a threat and a warning. The word what may mean who, meaning that I say to you. It may also be a source word, meaning you will remember what I say to you if the punishment befalls you. "And I entrust my affair to God" means I put my trust in Him and surrender my affair to Him. It was said: This indicates that they wanted to kill him. Muqatil said: This believer fled to the mountain but they could not catch him. It was also said: The one who said it was Moses. It appears more likely that he was the believer of the family of Pharaoh, and this is the saying of Ibn Abbas.
40:45: The Almighty said: And God saved him from the evil of their plotting. That is, from inflicting various types of punishment on him. So they sought Him but did not find Him, because he entrusted his affair to God. Qatada said: He was a Copt, so God saved him with the Children of Israel. The ha in this case refers to the believer in the family of Pharaoh. It was said that it refers to Moses, based on the previous disagreement. And the evil punishment befell the family of Pharaoh. Al-Kisa'i said: It is said that it descended upon, haqqa, hayqan, and hayuqan if it descended and stuck. Then he explained the punishment, saying:
40:47: The Almighty said: And when they dispute in the Fire meaning they quarrel therein. The weak will say to those who were arrogant about submitting to the prophets, Indeed, we were your followers in what you invited us to of polytheism in the world. So will you be relieved? meaning will you be burdened with a portion of the Fire from us? That is, a recompense of the torment. “Tabi’a” can be singular or plural according to the Basrans, its singular is tabi’. The people of Kufa said: It is a plural that has no singular like a verbal noun, and that is why it is not plural. If it were plural, it would have been said tabi’a.
40:48: God the Almighty said: Those who were arrogant said, ‘Indeed, we are all in it’ meaning in Hell. Al-Akhfash said: All is nominative as a subject. Al-Kisa’i and Al-Farra’ permitted Indeed, we are all in it in the accusative case as a description and to emphasize the pronoun in Indeed. Ibn Al-Sameeq and Isa bin Omar recited this in the same way. The Kufians call emphasis a description. Sibawayh forbade this, saying: “Because both do not describe, nor are they described by it. And substitution is not permissible in it, because the one who reports about himself cannot be substituted for anything else.” Al-Mubarrad said the same meaning, saying: “It is not permissible to substitute for the pronoun here, because it is addressed, and it is not substituted for the addressed or the addressed, because they are not ambiguous, so it cannot be substituted for them.” This is the text of his statement. Indeed, God has judged between the servants, meaning that He will not punish anyone for the sin of someone other than himself, so each of us is a disbeliever.
40:49: The Almighty said: And those in the Fire will say from the disbelieving nations. Some Arabs say alladhūn as a whole Muslim, and whoever says: alladhūna in the nominative case built it as it was built in the singular. Al-Akhfash said: The nun was added to alladhī so it resembles fifteen, so it was built on the fathah. The keepers of Hell Haznah is all khazīn and it is said: khazān and khazān Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment "Yakhfūf is a jussive answer even if it is with fa" and on this the Qur'an came in the most correct languages as it said: Your veil is a memory of a lover and a home Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi said: It was reported to me or mentioned to me that the people of Hell sought help from the guards, so God Almighty said: “And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell, ‘Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment.’” So they asked for one day in which the punishment would be lightened for them, and it was rejected.
40:50: God Almighty says: Did not your messengers come to you with clear proofs? They said, Yes. They said, Then call upon God, but the call of the disbelievers is only in error. The entire report. In the hadith on the authority of Abu Darda’, narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and others, he said: “Hunger will be afflicted upon the people of Hell until it equals the torment they are in. They will seek help from it and will be given thorny thorns that neither fatten nor relieve their hunger. They will eat it but it will not relieve them at all. Then they will seek help and will be given food that chokes them and they will choke on it. They will remember that in the world they used to overcome their choking with water. Then they will seek help for a drink and the boiling water will be lifted up for them with hooks. When it comes close to their faces, it roasts them. When it enters their stomachs, it will rip out their intestines and what is in their stomachs. Then they will seek help from the angels, saying, ‘Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the torment.’ They will answer them, ‘Did not your messengers come to you with clear proofs?’ They will say, ‘Yes.’ They will say, ‘Then call upon Him.’ But the call of the disbelievers is only in error.” That is, loss and destruction.
40:51: God the Almighty says: Indeed, We will support Our messengers. It is permissible to omit the damma because of its heaviness, and it is said: Our messengers, meaning Moses, peace be upon him. And those who believed in worldly life is in the accusative case in apposition to the messengers, and meaning the believer who was admonished. It was said: It is general for the messengers and believers, and their support is by raising the arguments and making them successful, according to Abu Al-Aliyah. It was also said: Taking revenge on their enemies. Al-Suddi said: No people killed a prophet or a group of Mormons who called to the truth, but God the Almighty sent someone to take revenge for them, so they were victorious in it, even if they were killed. God the Almighty says: And on the Day when the witnesses will stand, meaning the Day of Resurrection. Zayd ibn Aslam said: The witnesses are four: the angels, the prophets, the believers, and the bodies. Mujahid and Al-Suddi said: The witnesses and the angels testify for the prophets to convey the message and against the nations to deny it. Qatada said: The angels and the prophets. Then it was said: witnesses is the plural of martyr like sharif and ashraf. Al-Zajjaj said: witnesses is the plural of witness like sahib and companions. An-Nahhas said: The form of fa’il does not make it plural with af’al, nor does it say sa’lihi, but what came from it was heard, meaning it was performed as it was heard, and it was with the deletion of the extra letter. Al-Akhfash and Al-Farra’ permitted: And on the Day when the witnesses will stand with the ta’ as a feminine plural. In the hadith on the authority of Abu Darda’ and some of the hadith scholars, he said on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he said: Whoever defends the honour of his Muslim brother, it is a right upon God to defend him from the fire of Hell. Then he recited: Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe. And on his authority (peace be upon him), he said: Whoever protects a believer from a hypocrite who backbites him, God will send an angel on the Day of Resurrection to protect him and will reveal what he said.
40:52: The Almighty says: The Day instead of the first day. Their excuses will not benefit the wrongdoers. Nafi’ and the Kufians read yanfi’ with a ya’. The rest read it with a ta’. And for them is the curse and for them is the worst home. The curse is distance from God’s mercy and the worst home is Hell.
40:53: The Almighty says: And We had certainly given Moses guidance. This refers to supporting the messengers in this world and the hereafter, meaning We gave him the Torah and prophethood. The Torah was called guidance because of what it contained of guidance and light. In the Qur’an, it is said: Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. (al-Ma’idah 5:44) And We caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Scripture. Meaning, the Torah, We made it their inheritance.
40:54: The Almighty says: Guidance instead of the Book, and it is permissible to mean it is guidance, that is the Book. And a reminder for those of understanding meaning an admonition for those of reason.
40:55: God the Almighty says: "So be patient. Indeed, the promise of God is true." That is, be patient, O Muhammad, with the harm of the polytheists, as those before you were patient. Indeed, the promise of God is true by granting you victory and supplication, just as you granted victory to Moses and the Children of Israel. Al-Kalbi said: This was abrogated by the verse of the sword. And ask forgiveness for your sin. It was said: For the sin of your nation. The complement was deleted and the complement to it was replaced. It was also said: For your own sin, according to those who permit minor sins against the prophets. Whoever says it is not permissible said: This is an act of worship to the Prophet (peace be upon him) through supplication, as God the Almighty said: And give us what You promised us. (Al-Imran 3:194) The benefit is to increase degrees and for supplication to become a tradition for those who come after him. It was also said: So ask forgiveness of God for any sin you committed before your prophethood. And glorify the praises of your Lord in the evening and the morning. This means the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer, as stated by Al-Hasan and Qatada. It was said: It is a prayer that was in Mecca before the five daily prayers were made obligatory: two rak'ahs in the morning and two rak'ahs in the evening. Al-Mawardi also mentioned it from Al-Hasan. So this is one of the things that were abrogated, and God knows best. His statement: With the praise of your Lord is to thank and thank Him. It was said: And glorify the praises of your Lord meaning, continue glorifying Him in prayer and outside of it so that you will be occupied with that and not hastening victory.
40:56: God the Almighty said: Indeed, those who dispute dispute concerning the verses of God without any authority meaning proof that has come to them - there is in their hearts nothing but arrogance which they will never attain. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is there is nothing in their hearts except arrogance which they will never attain. Ability to omit. Another said: The meaning is they will never attain arrogance without omission, because these are people who saw that if they followed the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), their stature would diminish and their circumstances would diminish, and that they would rise if they did not follow him. So God the Almighty informed them that they would never attain the stature they had hoped for through denial. What is meant are the polytheists. It was also said that it means the Jews, so the verse is Madinan based on this, as mentioned at the beginning of the surah. The meaning is: If they are too arrogant to follow Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and say that the Antichrist will emerge soon and return the kingdom to us, and rivers will flow with him, and he is a sign from the signs of God, then that is arrogance which they will not attain, so the verse was revealed about them. Abu Al-Aaliyah and others said it. It was mentioned in Al-Imran that he will emerge and conquer all lands except Makkah and Madinah. We have already mentioned his full story in Kitab At-Tadhkirah. He is a Jew whose name is Saaf and his kunya is Abu Yusuf. It was also said: Everyone who disbelieved in the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). This is good because it is general. Mujahid said: It means that there is a greatness in their hearts that they will never attain, and the meaning is the same. It was also said that what is meant by arrogance is a great matter, i.e. they demand or demand a great matter that they can achieve with you, such as killing and the like, but they do not attain it, or they wish for your death before your religion is completed and they do not attain it. His statement, the Most High, {So seek refuge in God} It was said: From the trial of the Antichrist, according to the opinion of those who said that the verse was revealed about the Jews. And according to the other opinion, from the evil of the disbelievers. And it was said: From the like of what they were afflicted with of disbelief and arrogance. {Indeed, it is He who is the Hearing, the Seeing} He is a separator and it is the subject and what comes after it is its predicate, and the clause is the predicate of inna according to what was mentioned.
40:57: The Almighty says: The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind. Subject and predicate. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: That is, greater than the creation of the Antichrist when the Jews glorified him. Yahya bin Salam said: It is an argument against those who deny the resurrection, that is, they are greater than the re-creation of mankind, so why do they believe that I am incapable of it? But most people do not know that. God Almighty says: The blind and the seeing are not alike meaning the believer and the disbeliever, the astray and the guided. And those who believe and do righteous deeds meaning the one who does righteous deeds is not alike.
40:58: The Almighty said: Nor the evildoer who commits evil deeds. Little do you remember The general reading is with a ya’ as a predicate, and Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose it, because of what preceded it of the predicate and what followed it. The Kufians read it with a ta’ as a direct address.
40:59: His saying: The Hour is coming This is the lam of emphasis that entered into the predicate of in and its way is to be at the beginning of the sentence, because it emphasizes the sentence, except that it slips from its place, this is what Sibawayh said. You say: Indeed, Umar is outside, and it was only delayed from its place so that it would not be combined with in, because they convey the same meaning. And this is how in and an are not combined according to the Basrans. Hisham permitted in that Zaid is leaving, right, but if you delete right it is not permitted according to any of the grammarians, I knew it, this was said by An-Nahhas. There is no doubt about it means no suspicion or doubt. But most people do not believe meaning they do not believe in it, and then the difference between the obedient and the disobedient becomes clear.
40:61: The Almighty says: God is He who made the night for you that you may rest therein. “Ja`al” here means created, and the Arabs differentiate between Ja`al if it means created and Ja`al if it does not mean created. If it means created, then you only transit it to one object, and if it does not mean created, then you transit it to two objects, like His statement: Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur’an (Az-Zukhruf 43:3). This meaning has already been mentioned in more than one place. And the day giving sight means shining so that you may see your needs and manage your livelihood. Indeed, God is full of bounty to mankind, but most people do not give thanks for His bounty and blessings upon them.
40:62: The Almighty's saying: That is God, your Lord, the Creator of all things is evidence of His Oneness and Power. There is no god but Him, so how are you turned away? That is, how can you turn away and abandon the faith after its proofs have been made clear to you? Likewise, just as you were turned away from the truth despite the established proof for it, thus are those who used to deny the signs of God turned away.
40:63: God Almighty says: Thus are those who used to deny the signs of God deluded.
40:64: The Almighty said: It is God who made the earth a resting place for you. He added to the definition and evidence, meaning He made the earth a place of rest for you in your life and after death. And the sky is a structure was mentioned earlier. And He shaped you and perfected your shapes. Meaning He created you in the best form. Abu Razin and Al-Ashhab Al-Uqaili read Suwarkum with a kasra on the sad. Al-Jawhari said: Suwar with a kasra on the sad is a language for suwar which is the plural of suwar. This verse is recited in this language describing female slaves: Their eyes are more like purebred cows, and they are more beautiful than their appearance. And Saran is the plural of Sawar, which is a herd of cows, and Sawar is also a container of musk. The poet combined them in his saying: If the stars appear, I remember Layla, and I remember her when the stars blow And the word Siyar is used in this language. "And He has provided you with good things. That is God, your Lord. So blessed is God, Lord of the worlds." It was mentioned above.
40:65: God Almighty says: He is the Ever-Living meaning the Everlasting Who does not die. There is no god but Him, so call upon Him, making your religion sincere to Him meaning obedience and worship. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. Al-Farra’ said: It is a statement that contains an implied command, meaning call upon Him and be One with Him. All of this has already been mentioned in full in Surat Al-Baqarah and other surahs. Ibn Abbas said: Whoever says: There is no god but God should say: Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.
40:66: God Almighty said: “Say, ‘Indeed, I have been forbidden,’ meaning, say, O Muhammad: God, who is the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, and there is no god but Him, has forbidden me to worship anyone other than Him, when clear proofs have come to me from my Lord,’ meaning, the evidence of His Oneness, ‘and I have been commanded to submit,’ meaning, to humble myself and submit, ‘to the Lord of the Worlds.’ They had called him to the religion of his fathers, so he was commanded to say this.
40:67: The Almighty says: "It is He who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot. Then He brings you forth as a child." That is, children. This has already been mentioned. Then that you may reach your full strength. This is the state of full strength and perfect reason. This has already been explained in Al-An'am. Then that you may be elders. Nafi', Ibn Muhaisin, Hafs, Hisham, Ya'qub, and Abu Amr read it with a damma on the sheen, according to the original reading, because it is the plural of a verb, like qalb heart and quloob hearts and ra's head and ru'us heads. The rest read it with a kasra on the sheen to take into account the ya', and both are plurals of abundance. In a small number, it is ashyaakh old men, and the original is ashyaikh old women, like fals those and aflas those, except that the vowel on the ya' is heavy. It was also read a shaykh in the singular, like his saying a child, and the meaning is every one of you, and it was limited to the singular because the purpose is to clarify the genus. In As-Sahah: The plural of sheikh is shyuyukh, asheikhah, sheikha, sheikhan, mashayikhah, sheikhas, and mashyukhā, and the woman is sheikha. Ubaid said: As if she is a sheikha The man has grown old, he has grown old, he has called him shaykh as an expression of respect. The diminutive of shaykh is shaykh and shaykh also with a kasra on the sheen. Do not say shaykh an-nahhas. If a poet is forced to, it is permissible for him to say ash-shaykh like ayn and ayyān, except that it is better for ayn because it is feminine. The shaykh is the one who has passed forty years. And among you is he who dies before Mujahid said: meaning before he becomes an old man, or before these conditions if he comes out as a miscarriage. And that you may reach a specified term Mujahid said: Death is for everyone. The lam is the lam of consequence. And perhaps you will understand that and learn that there is no god but Him.
40:68: The Almighty said: It is He who gives life and causes death. He added in the warning, meaning, He is the One who has the power to give life and cause death. Then when He decrees a matter, meaning, He wants to do it, He says, To it, 'Be,' and it is. Ibn Amir put be in the accusative case as a response to the command. This has already been discussed in Surat Al-Baqarah.
40:69: God Almighty said: Have you not seen those who dispute concerning the verses of God? How are they diverted? Ibn Zayd said: They are the polytheists, as evidenced by His statement.
40:70: The Almighty said: Those who deny the Book and that with which We sent Our messengers. Most of the commentators said: It was revealed about the Qadarites. Ibn Sirin said: If this verse was not revealed about the Qadarites, then I do not know about whom it was revealed. Abu Qabil said: I do not think that those who deny predestination are anyone but those who dispute with those who have believed. Uqbah ibn Amir said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: This verse was revealed about the Qadarites. Al-Mahdawi mentioned this.
40:71: The Almighty says: When the shackles are on their necks meaning, they will soon come to know the invalidity of what they are in when they enter the Fire and their hands are chained to their necks. Al-Taymi said: If a shackle from the shackles of Hell were placed on a mountain, it would crush it until it reaches the black water. And the chains is in the nominative case, as is the general reading, in apposition to the shackles. Abu Hatim said: They are dragged is a new sentence based on this reading. Another one said: It is in the accusative case as a state, and the meaning is: When the shackles are on their necks and the chains are dragged. Ibn Abbas, Abu al-Jawza', Ikrimah and Ibn Mas'ud read And the chains in the accusative case, They are dragged with a fat-ha over the ya', and the meaning in this reading is And they drag him by the chains. Ibn Abbas said: If they drag them, then it is more difficult for them. Some of them reported And the chains in the genitive case, and the reason for that is that it is carried on the meaning, because the meaning is their necks in the shackles and chains, as al-Farra' said. Al-Zajjaj said: “Whoever reads and the chains are dragged in the accusative case, then the meaning is according to him: And in the chains are dragged, Ibn al-Anbari said: The accusative case in this meaning is not permissible, because if you say Zayd is in the house, it is not good to omit in and say Zayd the house, but the accusative case is permissible in the meaning of since their necks are in the shackles and chains, so you lower the chains in accordance with the interpretation of the shackles, because the shackles are in the accusative case, just as you say: ‘Abdullah disputed with Zayd the two chained ones,’ so you put the two rational ones in the accusative case. And it is permissible to raise them both, because if one of them disputes with his companion, then his companion has disputed with him. Al-Farra’ recited: Peace be upon the snakes, the ancient serpent, and the brave brave The snake is installed as a follower of snakes, if the foot makes peace with it, the foot makes peace with it. So whoever sets up chains or lowers them cannot stand on them. And the hot is the extreme heat. And it was said: boiling pus.
40:72: The Almighty said: Then into the Fire they will be blazing. That is, they will be thrown and will be its fuel, as stated by Mujahid. It is said: I lit the oven, meaning I lit it, and I lit it means I filled it. From this comes the phrase the blazing sea (al-Tur 52:6), meaning filled. So the meaning according to this is that the Fire will be filled with them.
