It was also said: The believers. It was also said: It is general, so the one who is thrown into the Fire is the disbeliever, and the one who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection is the believer. Ibn Bahr said: Do whatever you will is a threatening command, meaning after you know that they are not equal, you will inevitably be rewarded. Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do is a threat and a warning.
41:41: The Almighty says: Indeed, those who disbelieved in the message when it came to them The message here is the Qur'an according to everyone, because it contains the mention of what is needed of rulings. The good is omitted, meaning those who are doomed or punished. It was also said that the good is those who are called from a place far away (Fussilat 41:44). The statement what is said to you was an objection, then he returned to the message and said: And if We had made it a foreign Qur'an (Fussilat 41:44), then his statement: those who are called and the first is the preferred opinion. An-Nahhas said: According to all grammarians, as far as I know. And indeed, it is a precious Book meaning precious to God, as Ibn Abbas said, and from him: precious from God. It was also said: noble to God. It was also said: precious meaning God has made it precious so that falsehood cannot penetrate it. It was also said: It should be precious and respected and not be nullified in it. It was said: Aziz from Satan changing it, said Al-Suddi. Muqatil: He was protected from Satan and falsehood. Al-Suddi: He is not created, so there is no equal to Him. Ibn Abbas also said: Aziz means it is forbidden for people to say the same as Him.
41:42: The Almighty says: Falsehood cannot come to it from before it or from behind it. It is unable to change, add, or subtract. Saeed bin Jubair said: Denial cannot come to it from before it or from behind it. Ibn Jurayj said: Falsehood cannot come to it in what He reported about what happened in the past or what He reported about what will happen in the future. Ibn Abbas said: From before it from God Almighty nor from behind it meaning from Gabriel, peace be upon him, nor from Muhammad, peace be upon him. A revelation from One Who is Wise, Praiseworthy Ibn Abbas said: Wise in His creation, Praiseworthy to them. Qatada said: Wise in His command, Praiseworthy to His creation.
68:48: The Almighty says: What is said to you meaning of harm and denial except what was said to the messengers before you comforting and consoling His Prophet Indeed, your Lord is the Possessor of forgiveness to you and your companions and the Possessor of painful punishment meaning painful for your enemies. It was said: What is said to you of sincere worship of God except what was revealed to those before you, and there is no disagreement between the religious laws regarding monotheism, and it is like His statement: And it has already been revealed to you and to those before you that if you should associate [anything] with God, your work would surely become worthless (al-Zumar 39:65) meaning what is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you? It was said: Indeed, your Lord is a subject and what precedes it is a complete statement if the predicate is implied. It was said: It is connected to what is said to you. "Indeed, your Lord is the Possessor of forgiveness and the Possessor of painful punishment" meaning you were only commanded to warn and give good tidings. The Almighty says: So be patient for the decision of your Lord meaning for the decree of your Lord. The decree here is the decree. It was also said: So be patient for what your Lord has decreed for you regarding conveying the message. Ibn Bahr said: So be patient for the victory of your Lord. Qatada said: That is, do not be hasty and do not get angry, for your victory is inevitable. It was also said that it was abrogated by the verse of the sword. And do not be like the companion of the fish meaning Yunus, peace be upon him. That is, do not be like him in anger, annoyance and haste. Qatada said: It is God Almighty comforting His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and ordering him to be patient and not to be hasty as the companion of the fish was hasty. His story has already been mentioned in Surah Yunus, Al-Anbiya, and As-Saffat. The difference between adding dhi sahib in Surah Yunus is that there is no point in repeating it. When he called out meaning when he called out in the belly of the fish, saying: "There is no god but You; glory be to You. Indeed, I was of the wrongdoers." While he was filled with grief meaning filled with sorrow. It was said: Karaban. The first is the saying of Ibn Abbas and Mujahid. The second is the saying of Ata’ and Abu Malik. Al-Mawardi said: The difference between them is that grief is in the heart, and the cup is in the breath. It was also said: Makzoom is imprisoned. And the word kazm means confinement, and from it is their saying: So-and-so suppressed his anger, meaning he held back his rage. Abu Bahr said: It was also said: It is the one who is seized by his suppression, which is the course of the breath. Al-Mubarrad said this and others. This and others have already been mentioned in Yusuf.
41:44: The Almighty said: And if We had made it a foreign Qur’an, they would have said, ‘Why are its verses not explained in detail?’ [Is it] a foreign language and an Arabic one? There are three issues in this: First: The Almighty’s statement: And if We had made it a Qur’an in a foreign language, meaning in a language other than the Arabs, they would have said, ‘Why are its verses not explained in detail?’ Meaning, they were explained in our language, as we are Arabs and do not understand foreign languages. So He made it clear that He revealed it in their language so that the meaning of the miraculous nature would be established, as they are the most knowledgeable people about the various types of speech, both in prose and poetry. And if they were unable to oppose it, it would be the clearest proof that it is from God. If it had been in a foreign language, they would have said, We have no knowledge of this language. Second: If this is proven, then it is evidence that the Qur’an is Arabic, that it was revealed in the language of the Arabs, that it is not foreign, and that it was transferred from it to another language, so it was not the Qur’an. Third: The Almighty’s saying: A foreigner and an Arab? Abu Bakr, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa’i read A’jami and Arab with two light hamzas. The foreigner who is not from the Arabs can be eloquent or non-eloquent, and the foreigner who does not speak clearly can be from the Arabs or from the non-Arabs. The foreigner is the opposite of the eloquent, and he is the one who speaks clearly. The non-speaking animal is called a’jam, and from this the daytime prayer is a’jama’, meaning the recitation is not loudly recited during it. Therefore, the attribution to the foreigner is more emphatic, because the foreigner who is not from the Arabs can be eloquent in Arabic, and the Arab can be non-eloquent, so the attribution to the foreigner is more emphatic in clarity. The meaning is: A foreign Quran, and an Arab prophet? It is a question of denial. Al-Hasan, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Nasr bin Asim, Al-Mughirah, and Hisham from Ibn Amir read A’jami with one hamza as a statement. The meaning is Why were His verses not explained in detail? So some of them were Arabs whom Arabs understood, and non-Arabs whom non-Arabs understood. Saeed bin Jubair narrated that the Quraysh said: Why was the Qur’an not revealed in Arabic and foreign languages, so that some of its verses would be foreign and some Arabic? So this verse was revealed. And in the Qur’an, every language was revealed, including as-Sijjil, which is Persian and its root is sank-kil, meaning clay and stone. And al-Firdaws is Roman, as is al-Qistas. The people of Hijaz, Abu Amr, Ibn Dhakwan, and Hafs read it as a question, except that they softened the hamza according to their principles. The correct reading is the question reading. And God knows best. God the Almighty says: It is, for those who believe, a guidance and a healing. God knows that the Qur’an is a guidance and a healing from doubt, suspicion, and pain for whoever believes in it. And those who do not believe - in their ears is deafness. That is, a deafness to hearing the Qur’an. That is why they advise each other to engage in idle talk regarding it. Similar to this verse is: And We send down of the Qur’an that which is a healing and a mercy to the believers, but it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss. (al-Isra’ 17:82) This has already been fully discussed. The general reading of blindness is as a verbal noun. Ibn Abbas, Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, Amr ibn al-As, Mu’awiyah, and Sulayman ibn Qatah read and it is blind to them with a kasra on the meem, meaning it is not clear to them. Abu Ubaid chose the first reading, due to the consensus of the people on it, and because he said first: Guidance and healing. If it had been guide and healer, the kasra in blindness would have been better, so that it would be a description like them. The meaning is: And those who do not believe in not accepting it is like a whisper in their ears. “And it” meaning the Qur’an is a deafness upon them, because they do not understand, so the complement was deleted. It was also said that the meaning is and the deafness upon them is blindness. Those are being called from a distant place. This is said to someone who does not understand, as an example. Linguists have reported that it is said to someone who understands: You hear from nearby. And it is said to someone who does not understand: You are being called from afar. That is, as if he is being called from a distant place, so he does not hear the call nor understand it. Ad-Dahhak said: They are being called on the Day of Resurrection by their ugliest names from a distant place, so that will be more severe as a rebuke and disgrace to them. It was said: Whoever does not contemplate the Qur’an will be like a blind and deaf person, who is called from a far place, but the voice of the caller is cut off from him and he does not hear. Ali may God be pleased with him and Mujahid said: That is, far from their hearts. In the interpretation: As if they are being called from the sky but do not hear. Al-Naqqash narrated its meaning.
41:45: God the Almighty says: And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture meaning the Torah and there was disagreement over it meaning some people believed in it and some people disbelieved in it. The metaphor refers to the Scripture, and it is a consolation for the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), meaning do not be saddened by the disagreement of your people over your Scripture, for those before them differed over their Scripture. It was also said that the metaphor refers to Moses. Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord meaning in granting them respite. It would have been judged between them meaning by hastening the punishment. And indeed, they are in doubt about it of the Qur'an. Disturbing meaning extremely suspicious. This has been mentioned previously. Al-Kaabi said about this verse: Had God not delayed the punishment of this nation until the Day of Resurrection, the punishment would have come to them as He did to other nations. It was also said that the punishment is delayed until after the believers emerge from their loins.
41:46: His Almighty saying: Whoever does righteousness does so for the benefit of his own soul is a condition and its answer, and likewise and whoever does evil does so against it and God, the Almighty and Majestic, is independent of the obedience of His servants, so whoever obeys will be rewarded, and whoever does evil will be punished. And your Lord is not unjust to His servants He has denied injustice from Himself, the Almighty and Majestic, whether little or much. If exaggeration is denied, then anything else is denied. My proof is His true saying: Indeed, God does not wrong people at all (Yunus 10:44). And the trustworthy and just scholars and the steadfast imams have narrated from the just ascetic, from the trustworthy one on earth, from the trustworthy one in the heavens, from the Lord, the Almighty and Majestic: O My servants, indeed I have forbidden injustice for Myself and made it forbidden amongst you, so do not wrong one another [hadith]. Also, He is the Wise Owner, and whatever the Owner does with His kingdom is not to be objected to, since He has the right to dispose of His kingdom as He wishes.
41:47: God the Almighty says: To Him is returned the knowledge of the Hour meaning when it will be. That is because they said: O Muhammad, if you are a prophet, then tell us when the Hour will come. So this verse was revealed: And no fruits come forth from is redundant, meaning no fruit comes forth. from their cloaks meaning from their containers. The complete container is the fruit, the singular of which is kummah which is any container for money or other things. That is why the one who splits open from the fruit is called kummah. Ibn Abbas said: "Kummah is the disbeliever before it splits open. So when it splits open, it is not a kummah." Further explanation of this will come in Surah Ar-Rahman. Nafi', Ibn Umar, and Hafs read from the fruits in the plural. The rest read fruit in the singular, meaning the plural, because God says: and no female bears meaning the plural. He says: To Him is returned the knowledge of the Hour just as knowledge of fruits and offspring is returned to Him. And the Day He will call to them, meaning God will call to the polytheists, Where are My partners? Those whom you claimed in this world were gods who intercede. They will say, meaning the idols. It was also said: the polytheists. It is possible that He means all of them, the worshipper and the worshipped. We have given you permission, meaning we have made you hear and informed you. It is said: He gives permission, meaning he informs. He said: She let us know the names of a Lord who is constant and from whom constant repose is never tired. None of us is a witness meaning we inform you that none of us testifies that you have a partner. When they witness the Resurrection, they will disavow the idols, and the idols will disavow them, as mentioned previously in more than one place.
41:48: The Almighty says: And what they used to call upon before in this world has been nullified from them meaning, what they used to call upon before in this world has been nullified from them and they assumed meaning, they were certain and knew that there is no escape for them" meaning, escape from the Fire. "Ma here is a particle and not a noun, and therefore the verb ma" was not used in it and the verb was made nullified, meaning: And they assumed that they have no escape or way out. It is said: "haas yahyais haysaaan muhaysaan" if he flees. It was said: The assumption here, which is the most prevalent opinion, is that they do not doubt that they are the people of the Fire, but they hope to get out of it. It is not far-fetched that they have assumption and hope until they despair.
41:49: God the Almighty says: Man never tires of praying for good meaning he never tires of praying for good. Good here means money, health, power and honor. Al-Suddi said: Man here means the disbeliever. It was also said that it was Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira. It was also said that it was Utbah and Shaibah, the sons of Rabi'ah and Umayyah ibn Khalaf. In the recitation of Abdullah: Man never tires of praying for money. "But if evil touches him the poor or the sick, he despairs of the mercy of God, despairs" of His mercy. It was also said: "Despairs of the supplication being answered, Despairs" due to bad thoughts about his Lord. It was also said: "Despairs means he despairs of the removal of what is bad upon him, Despairs" means he thinks that it will be taken away, and the meanings are close.
41:50: God the Almighty says: And if We let him taste mercy from Us a good outcome, prosperity and wealth after adversity has befallen him harm, sickness, hardship and poverty. he will surely say, ‘This is for me’ meaning, this is something I deserve from God because of His pleasure with my deeds. So he sees the blessing as inevitably due from God the Almighty, and he does not know that He has tested him with blessings and hardship, so that his gratitude and patience may be clear. Ibn Abbas said: This is for me meaning, this is from Me. “And I do not think the Hour will occur. And if I should return to my Lord, I will have with Him the best” meaning Paradise. The lam is for emphasis. And he hopes for wishes for deeds. He said to Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Ali bin Abi Talib: The disbeliever has two wishes. As for this world, he says: If I were returned to my Lord, I would have with Him the best [reward]. As for the Hereafter, he says: Oh, would that we could be sent back and not deny the signs of our Lord and be among the believers. (al-An’am 6:27) and Oh, would that I were dust. (An-Naba’: 40) Then We will surely inform those who disbelieved of what they did. That is, We will recompense them. It is an oath that God has sworn. And We will make them taste a severe punishment.
41:51: The Almighty said: And when We bestow favor upon man meaning the disbeliever he turns away and distances himself. Ibn Abbas said: He means Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, Shaibah ibn Rabi'ah, and Umayyah ibn Khalaf, they turned away from Islam and distanced themselves from it. The meaning of turned away is that he refused to submit to the truth and was arrogant towards the prophets of God. It was said: turned away means he distanced himself. It is said: I distanced myself from him and I distanced myself from him, meaning I distanced myself from him and he distanced himself, so he distanced himself: I removed him, so he became distant. They distanced themselves means they became distant, and the remote place is the far place. An-Nabigha said: You are like the night that overtakes me, even if I think that the distance from you is vast. Yazid ibn al-Qaqa' readوخلین بنجهwith an alif before the hamza. It is possible that it is fromناخmeaning to rise. It is also possible that it is by changing the hamza to mean the first. And if evil touches him meaning something bad befalls him. Then he who supplicates extensively is abundant. The Arabs use length and breadth to mean abundance. It is said: So-and-so spoke at length and supplicated a lot. Ibn Abbas said: Then he who supplicates extensively is one who supplicates and cries for help. The disbeliever knows his Lord in times of affliction but does not know Him in times of ease.
41:52: God Almighty says: “Say: Have you considered?” That is, say to them, O Muhammad, Have you considered, O company of polytheists, if this Qur’an is from God and you disbelieved in it, who is more astray? That is, who among people is more astray? That is, no one is more astray than you due to your extreme dissension and enmity. It was said: If it is from God refers to the Book mentioned in His statement: We gave Moses the Scripture. The first is more apparent and is the statement of Ibn Abbas.
41:53: The Almighty says: We will show them Our signs in the horizons meaning the signs of Our Oneness and Power. And within themselves meaning the destruction of the dwellings of the former nations. And within themselves with plagues and diseases. Ibn Zayd said: In the horizons are the signs in the heavens. And within themselves are the events on earth. Mujahid said: In the horizons is the conquest of cities. Thus, God Almighty facilitated for His Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and for the caliphs after him and the supporters of his religion in the horizons of the world and the lands of the East and the Maghreb in general, and in the Maghreb in particular, conquests the likes of which were not possible for any of the caliphs on earth before them. They included victory over the tyrants and the Chosroes, the dominance of the few over the many, the empowerment of the weak over the strong, and His enabling them to accomplish unconventional and unusual matters through their hands. And within themselves is the conquest of Mecca. This is the preferred interpretation of al-Tabari. Al-Munhal bin Amr and Al-Suddi said it. Qatada and Al-Dahhak said: in the horizons God’s battles with the nations and in their souls on the day of Badr. Ata’ and Ibn Zayd also said: in the horizons meaning the regions of the heavens and the earth, from the sun, moon, mountains, stars, night, day, winds, rain, thunder, lightning, thunderbolts, plants, trees, mountains, seas and others. In As-Sahah: The horizons are the directions, the singular of which is a horizon and horizon like ‘Usr and ‘Usr, and a man who is horizontal with the opening of the hamza and the fa’: if he is from the horizons of the earth. Abu Nasr narrated it. Some of them say: horizontal with the closing of both of them, and this is the standard. And someone other than Al-Jawhari recited: We have taken the horizons of the sky to you, to its moon and the rising stars. And in their own selves is of the subtlest creation and wondrous wisdom, even the path of defecation and urination, for a man drinks and eats from one place and is distinguished from two places. The wonder of God’s creation and wisdom is in his eyes, which are like a drop of water, with which he sees the sky from the earth, a distance of five hundred years, and in his ears, with which he distinguishes between different sounds. And other wonders of God’s wisdom in it. It was said: And in their own selves from their being sperm to other changes in their states, as was explained previously in the believers. It was said: The meaning is they will see what the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) told them of the trials and report of the unseen until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth. There are four aspects to this: First, it is the Qur’an. Second, it is Islam that the Messenger brought to them and called them to. Third, that what God shows them and does of that is the truth. Fourth, it is that Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is the true Messenger. Did not your Lord suffice them? is in the nominative case as the subject of yakfi and that is a substitute for your Lord. So it is the nominative case of his power as a substitute for the place, and the genitive case of if as a substitute for the word. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case by estimating the deletion of the lām, and the meaning is Did not your Lord suffice them with what He guided them to of monotheism? Because He is a Witness over all things, and when He witnesses it, He will reward it. It was said that the meaning is Did not your Lord suffice them in punishing the disbelievers. It was said that the meaning is Did not your Lord suffice, O Muhammad, that He is a witness over the deeds of... that He is a witness over the deeds of the disbelievers. It was said that the meaning is Did not your Lord suffice, that He is a witness over the deeds of the disbelievers. It was said that the meaning is Did not your Lord suffice, that He is a witness over the deeds of the disbelievers.
41:54: The Almighty said: Unquestionably, they are in doubt in suspicion about the meeting with their Lord in the Hereafter. Al-Suddi said: meaning about the resurrection. Unquestionably, He encompasses all things meaning His knowledge encompasses all things. Al-Suddi said this. Al-Kalbi said: His power encompasses all things. Al-Khattabi said: He is the One whose power encompasses all of His creation, and He is the One who encompasses all things with knowledge, and has counted all things. This name is often used to describe threats, but its true meaning is to encompass all things and to eradicate all that is inflicted upon them. Its root is muhit encompassing, the vowel of the ya' was transferred to the ha' and made sukun quiet. It is said from this: ahata yahtihu ihataan to surround, and from this comes the wall of the house, and its people surround it. The horses surrounded someone: if they took hold of him from every side, and from this comes the Almighty's statement: and its fruit was encompassed Al-Kahf 18:42. And God knows best which is the correct interpretation of that.
42:1: Meccan according to Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata’, and Jabir. Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: Except for four verses of it that were revealed in Medina: Say, ‘I do not ask of you any reward for it except love for my relatives.’ to the end of it, and it is fifty-three verses. God Almighty says: Ha Meem.
42:2: The Almighty said, ‘Ain Qaf. Abdul-Mumin said: I asked Al-Hussein bin Al-Fadl: Why did you separate Ha Mim from ‘Ain Qaf and not separate Ka Ha Ya Ain Sad and Al-Ra and Al-Mas? He said: Because (Ha Meem, Ain Qaf) are among the surahs that begin with (Ha Meem), they are like their counterparts before and after them, so it is as if (Ha Meem) is the subject and (Ain Qaf) is its predicate. And because they are considered two verses, and their sisters that were written as a single verse are considered. And it was said that all the voiced letters are the same in meaning, in that they are the basis of expression and the foundation of speech, as mentioned by Al-Jurjani. And (Ha Meem, Ain Qaf) were written separately, and (Ka Ha Ya Ain Sad) connected because it was said: Ha Meem, meaning Ha Meem is what is to come, so they separated between what is estimated to be an action and what is not estimated, then if they had separated this and connected that, it would have been permissible, as narrated by Al-Qushayri. And in the reading of Ibn Masoud and Ibn Abbas (Ha Meem, Saq. Ibn Abbas said: And Ali, may God be pleased with him, knew the trials by them. And Arta’ah bin Al-Mundhir said, a man said to Ibn Abbas while Hudhayfah bin Al-Yaman was with him: Tell me about the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: (Ha Meem, Ain Qaf)? So he turned away from him until he repeated it to him three times, and he turned away from him. Then Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman said, "I will tell you about it. You already know why he left it. It was revealed about a man from his family called 'Abd al-Ilah or 'Abdullah. He will descend upon a river from the rivers of the East and build two cities on it. The river will split between them. When God wills their kingdom to vanish and their state to end, He will send a fire upon one of them at night, and it will become black and dark. It will all burn up as if it had never been in its place. Then its companion will wake up amazed at how it has been turned upside down! But it will be no more than the whiteness of its day until every obstinate tyrant gathers in it. Then God will cause the earth to swallow it and them all up. That is His saying, "Ha Meem, Ain Sin Qaf," meaning a decree of God's decrees, a trial and a judgment. Ha Meem (peace be upon him): justice from Him. "S": will be, "Qaf": will happen to these two cities. Similar to this interpretation is what Jarir ibn Abdullah al-Bajali narrated, saying: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: A city will be built between the Tigris and Dijla, Qutrabul and Sarat, in which the tyrants of the earth will gather, the treasuries will be brought to it, and it will be swallowed up by it, and in another narration by its people, for it will go away more quickly on the earth than a good child on soft soil. Ibn Abbas read: Ha Meem, Saq without Ain, and this is how it is in the copy of Abdullah ibn Masoud, as narrated by al-Tabari. Nafi’ narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “The Ha’ is His forbearance, the Meem is His glory, the Ain is His knowledge, the Seen is His brilliance, and the Qaf is His power. God swears by them.” Muhammad ibn Ka’b said: God swears by His forbearance, glory, loftiness, brilliance and power that He will not punish whoever seeks refuge in There is no god but God sincerely from his heart. Ja’far ibn Muhammad and Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: The Ha’ is from the Most Gracious, and the Meem is from the Glorious. And the letter ayn is from Al-Aleem, the letter seen is from Al-Quddus, and the letter qaf is from Al-Qahir. Mujahid said: The opening letters of the surahs. Abdullah ibn Buraydah said: It is the name of the mountain surrounding the world. Al-Qushayri mentioned, and the wording is from Al-Tha’labi: “When this verse was revealed, I could see the sadness in the face of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so it was said to him: O Messenger of God, what saddens you? He said: I have been informed of calamities that will befall my nation, such as subsidence, stoning, a fire that will gather them, a wind that will throw them into the sea, and successive signs connected to the descent of Jesus and the emergence of the Antichrist.” And God knows best. It was said: This is about the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The letter ha is his promised pool, and the letter mim is his extended kingdom, and his closeness in honor to the worshipped king. Ibn Abbas said: There is no prophet with a book except that it was revealed to him: Ha Meem, Ain Sin Qaf.
42:3: Thus does God, the Exalted in Might and Wise, inspire you and those before you. And for that reason He said: It is revealed to you and to those before you (al-Shura 42:3). Al-Mahdawi: It has been reported that (Ha Mim, Ain Sin Qaf) means it was revealed to the previous prophets. Ibn Muhaisin, Ibn Kathir, and Mujahid read (It is revealed) with a fat-ha on the ha’ for what is not named as its agent, and it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, so the preposition and noun are in the nominative case because they take the place of the agent. It is permissible for the name of what is not named as its agent to be implied, meaning the Qur’an that is included in this surah is revealed to you, and the name of God is raised by the implied verb, the estimate: God reveals it to you, like the reading of Ibn Amir and Abu Bakr: “In houses that God has permitted to be raised and that His name be mentioned therein. He is glorified therein in the mornings and the evenings” (al-Nur 24:36), meaning men glorify Him. And Sibawayh recited: May Yazid weep, humbled by his enmity and disheveled by those who have been tossed aside by calamities. He said: Let Yazid weep, then he explained who should weep for him. The meaning is that a supplicant weeps for him. It is permissible for it to be a subject and the predicate omitted, as if he said: God inspires him, or based on the assumption that a subject is omitted, meaning the inspirer is God, or the subject and predicate are (the Almighty, the Wise), and the rest read (inspires you) with a kasra on the ha’, and raising the noun as the subject.
42:4: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and He is the Most High, the Most Great. This has been mentioned in more than one place.
42:5: The Almighty’s saying: The heavens almost burst is the general reading with a ta’, and Nafi’, Ibn Waththab, and al-Kisa’i read with a ya’: they burst Nafi’ and others read it with a ya’, a ta’, and a shaddah on the ta’, which is the general reading. Abu Amr, Abu Bakr, al-Mufaddal, and Abu Ubaid read (they burst) from they burst, like the Almighty’s saying: When the heaven is burst [al-Infitar 82:Surah al-Baqarah, verse 200]. This has already been explained in Surah Maryam. Ibn Abbas said: (the heavens almost burst) means each one of them almost bursts above the one next to it, from the polytheists’ saying: God has taken a son (al-Kahf 18:4). Ad-Dahhak and As-Suddi said: (they burst) means they crack from the greatness and majesty of God above them. It was said: (above them) means above the earths from fear of God if they were of what has reason. God the Almighty says: And the angels exalt [God] with praise of their Lord, meaning they declare Him free from what is not permissible in describing Him and what is not befitting of His Majesty. It was also said: They are amazed by the audacity of the polytheists, so glorification is mentioned in the place of amazement. On the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him: Their glorification is amazement at what they see of their exposure to God’s wrath. Ibn Abbas said: Their glorification is humility at what they see of God’s greatness. The meaning of with praise of their Lord is by the command of their Lord. As-Suddi said: And they ask forgiveness for those on the earth. Ad-Dahhak said: For those on the earth of the believers. As-Suddi said: Its explanation is in Surat Al-Mu’min: And they ask forgiveness for those who believe. Based on this, the angels here are the bearers of the Throne. It was also said: All the angels of heaven, and this is the apparent meaning of Al-Kalbi’s statement. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: It is abrogated by His statement: And they ask forgiveness for those who believe. Al-Mahdawi said: The correct view is that it is not abrogated, because it is a statement, and it is specific to the believers. Abu Al-Hasan Al-Mawardi said on the authority of Al-Kalbi: When the angels saw the two angels who were tested and sent to Earth to judge between them, they were tempted by Venus and fled to Idris, the grandfather of Noah, peace be upon them, and asked him to pray for them. The angels glorified their Lord and asked forgiveness for the children of Adam. Abu al-Hasan ibn al-Hisar said: Some of the ignorant thought that this verse was revealed because of Harut and Marut, and that it was abrogated by the verse about the believer. They did not know that the bearers of the Throne are specifically assigned to ask forgiveness for the believers, and God has other angels who ask forgiveness for those on Earth. Al-Mawardi said: There are two opinions about their asking forgiveness for them: One of them is for sins and transgressions, and this is the apparent opinion of Muqatil. The second is that it is a request for provision and abundance for them, as al-Kalbi said. I said: This is more apparent, because the earth includes the disbeliever and others, and according to the opinion of Muqatil, the disbeliever is not included in it. A hadith has been narrated in this regard, narrated by Asim al-Ahwal on the authority of Abu Uthman on the authority of Salman, who said: If a servant remembers God in times of ease and then hardship befalls him, the angels say: This is a familiar voice from a weak human being who used to remember God in times of ease and then hardship befell him, so they seek forgiveness for him. But if he does not remember God in times of ease and then hardship befalls him, the angels say: This is an unfamiliar voice from a human being who did not remember God in times of ease and then hardship befell him, so they do not seek forgiveness for him from God. This indicates that the verse about the one who remembers God in times of ease and hardship is specific to some of the believers on earth, and God knows best. It is possible that by seeking forgiveness they mean seeking forbearance and forgiveness in the words of God the Most High: Indeed, God holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease to exist until He says: Indeed, He is Forbearing and Forgiving (Fatir 35:41), and the words of God the Most High: And indeed, your Lord is the possessor of forgiveness for the people despite their wrongdoing (al-Ra`d: 6). What is meant is to be patient with them and not to rush to take revenge on them, so it is general, as Al-Zamakhshari said. Mutraf said: We found that the most sincere servants of God to the servants of God are the angels, and we found that the most deceitful servants of God to the servants of God are the devils. It has been mentioned before: Indeed, God is the Forgiving, the Merciful. Some scholars said: He is awe-inspiring and great, glory be to Him, in the beginning, and gentle and good report of the end.
42:6: The Almighty says: And those who take protectors besides Him meaning idols that they worship, God is a Guardian over them meaning He preserves their deeds to reward them for them, and you are not a guardian over them This was abrogated by the verse of the sword, and in al-Naba 78:The heaven groaned and it is right for it to groan meaning it made a sound from the weight of its inhabitants due to their large number, for despite their large number they do not cease from worshipping God, and these disbelievers associate partners with Him.
42:7: The Almighty says: And thus We have revealed to you an Arabic Qur’an meaning, just as We revealed to you and to those before you these meanings, so too have We revealed to you a Qur’an that is close to God, which We explained in the language of the Arabs. It was said: That is, We sent down to you an Arabic Qur’an in the language of your people, just as We sent each messenger in the language of his people, and the meaning is the same, that you may warn the Mother of Cities meaning Mecca, and Mecca was called the Mother of Cities because the earth was spread out from beneath it, and from around it from all of creation, and warn of the Day of Assembly meaning the Day of Assembly, which is the Day of Resurrection, there is no doubt about it there is no doubt about it: A party in Paradise and a party in the Blaze subject and predicate, and Al-Kisa’i permitted the accusative case on the basis of: that you may warn a party in Paradise and a party in the Blaze.
42:8: The Almighty said: And if God had willed, He could have made them one community. Ad-Dahhak said: People of one religion, people of misguidance or people of guidance. But He admits whom He wills into His mercy. Anas bin Malik said, in Islam: And the wrongdoers is in the nominative case as a subject, and the predicate is They will have neither protector nor helper. It is in apposition to the word. It is permissible to say nor helper in the nominative case as a place, and from is redundant.
42:9: God Almighty says: Or have they taken meaning, rather, they have taken protectors besides Him meaning idols Then God is the Protector meaning your Protector, O Muhammad, and the Protector of those who follow you, there is no protector other than Him, and He gives life to the dead meaning at the resurrection and He is over all things competent, and other than Him among the protectors, they are not capable of anything.
42:10: The Almighty’s saying: And whatever you differ over is a narration of the saying of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the believers, meaning, and whatever the unbelievers from the People of the Book and the polytheists differed with you over regarding the matter of religion, then say to them, its ruling is up to God, not to you. And he ruled that the religion is Islam and nothing else, and the matters of the Shari’ah are only received from the statement of God. That is God, my Lord meaning, the One described by these attributes is my Lord alone, and in it is an implication: meaning, I said to them, O Muhammad, that is God who gives life to the dead and judges between those who differ. He is my Lord. Upon Him I have relied I depended, and to Him I turn I return.
42:11: The Almighty’s saying: Creator of the heavens and the earth is in the nominative case as an attribute of the name of God, or on the assumption that He is the Creator. The accusative case is permissible as a vocative, and the genitive case is a substitute for the ha’ in (upon Him) and the Creator is the Initiator and the Maker, and it has been mentioned before. He made for you mates from among yourselves It was said that its meaning is females, and that He only said: (from among yourselves) because He created Eve from Adam’s rib. Mujahid said: offspring after offspring. And of the livestock, mates means the eight that He mentioned in (the livestock), the male camels, cows, sheep, goats and their females. He multiplies you therein meaning He creates you and brings you up in it meaning in the womb. It was also said: in the belly. Al-Farra’ and Ibn Kaysan said: (in it) means by it. Al-Zajjaj also said: The meaning of (He multiplies you therein) is He multiplies you by it, meaning He multiplies you, He makes you mates, meaning wives, because they are the cause of offspring. It was said that the ha’ in (in it) For making, and it is indicated by (making), so it is as if he said: He creates you and multiplies you in making. Ibn Qutaybah: (He multiplies you therein) meaning in the pair, meaning He creates you in the wombs of females. And he said: And (therein) is in the womb, and there is a distance in it, because the womb is feminine and no male preceded it. There is nothing like Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing. It was said: The kaf is extra for emphasis, meaning there is nothing like Him. He said: Salaiyat Kama Yuthvin So he added a kaf to the kaf to emphasize the simile. It was said that the similitude is an additional form of emphasis, and this is the saying of Tha’lab, like what a thing is, like the saying of God Almighty: If they believe in the same as you believe in, then they are guided (al-Baqarah 2:137). And in the wording of Ibn Mas’ud: If they believe in what you believe in, then they are guided. Aws bin Hajar said: And the dead are like palm trunks covered by pouring rain Any trunks, and whoever believes in this matter that God, the Exalted, in His greatness, majesty, kingdom, and the beauty of His names and attributes, does not resemble any of His creations nor is He likened to them, but rather it came from what the Shari’ah has applied to the Creator and the creation, so there is no similarity between them in the true meaning, since the attributes of the Eternal, the Exalted and Majestic, are unlike the attributes of the creation, since their attributes are inseparable from purposes and accidents, and He, the Most High, is far removed from that, rather He has always been with His names and attributes as we have explained in the most sublime book in explanation of the beautiful names of God, and sufficient in this is His true statement: There is nothing like Him. Some of the established scholars have said: Establishing an essence that is not likened to essences nor is devoid of attributes. Al-Wasiti, may God have mercy on him, added further clarification and said: There is no essence like Him, nor a name like His name, nor an action like His action, nor an attribute like His attribute except from the aspect of agreement of the word, and the eternal essence was made to have a modern attribute, just as it is impossible for the modern essence to have an ancient attribute, and all of this is the doctrine of the people of truth, the Sunnah and the community, may God be pleased with them!.
42:12: The Almighty’s saying: To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. This was previously explained in Az-Zumar. An-Nahhas: And He who possesses the keys possesses the treasuries. The key is called iqlid, and its plural is not in accordance with the rules, like mahasin, and the singular is hasan. “He expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it. Indeed, He is Knowing of all things.” This was also previously mentioned in more than one place.
42:13: The Almighty’s saying: He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah. There are two issues in this: The first: The Most High’s saying: He has ordained for you of the religion meaning He who has the keys of the heavens and the earth has ordained for you of the religion what He ordained for the people of Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus. Then He explained that with His saying: That you establish the religion which is the monotheism of God and obedience to Him, and belief in His Messengers and Books and in the Day of Judgment, and in all the things by which a man establishes a Muslim. He did not mean the laws that are in the interests of nations in their good conditions, for they are different and varied. God Almighty said: To each of you We prescribed a law and a method (al-Ma’idah 5:48), and we have already discussed this. The meaning of He ordained is to guide, clarify, and explain the paths. He ordained for them He ordained a law, meaning He enacted a law. The legislator is the greatest road. The house is ordained if it is on a direct road. The camels are ordained if you allow them to have access to the law. The hide is ordained if you skin it. Jacob said: If you split what is between the two men. He said: And I heard it from Umm al-Hamaris al-Bakriyyah. And I began this matter with an initiation, meaning I entered into it: That you establish The word religion an is in the nominative case, based on the assumption that what He commanded Noah to do is to establish the religion. It is stopped on this basis at Jesus. It has also been said that it is accusative, meaning that He has prescribed for you the establishment of the religion. It has also been said that it is genitive in place of the ha in bih, as if he said: establish the religion with him. It is not stopped on Jesus on these two basis. It is permissible for an to be explanatory, like: walk, so it has no place in the parsing. Second: Judge Abu Bakr Ibn Al-Arabi said: It is proven in the authentic hadith that “the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in the famous great hadith of intercession: But go to Noah, for he is the first messenger whom God sent to the people of the earth. So they go to Noah and say to him: You are the first messenger whom God sent to the people of the earth...” This is correct and there is no problem with it, just as Adam was the first prophet without problem, because Adam had no one with him except his sons, and no obligations were imposed on him nor were prohibitions legislated for him. Rather, it was a warning about some matters and limited to the necessities of life, and taking into account the duties of life and survival. The period was established with Noah, so God sent him with the prohibition of mothers, daughters, and sisters, and imposed duties on him and clarified to him the etiquette in religions. This continued to be confirmed by the messengers and supported by the prophets, may God’s prayers be upon them, one after the other and one law after another, until God sealed it with the best of religions, our religion, on the tongue of the most honorable of messengers, our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. So the meaning was: We have enjoined upon you, O Muhammad, and Noah one religion, meaning in the fundamentals. The Sharia does not differ in it, and they are monotheism, prayer, zakat, fasting, Hajj, drawing closer to God through righteous deeds, and drawing near to Him through that which returns the heart and limbs to Him, and truthfulness and fulfilling the covenant, fulfilling the trust, and maintaining kinship ties, and forbidding disbelief, killing, adultery, and harming people however you do, and assaulting animals however you go, and intruding on baseness and that which leads to breaching honor, all of this is prescribed as one religion and a united nation, and it did not differ on the tongues of the prophets even if their numbers differed, and that is the saying of the Most High: Establish the religion and do not be divided therein meaning make it established, meaning always continuous, preserved, and stable without disagreement or disturbance in it, so among people there are those who fulfilled that and among them there are those who broke it, And whoever breaks it only breaks it to the detriment of his own soul (al-Fath 48:10). And the Sharia differed beyond this in meanings according to what God wanted, and what the interest required and wisdom required to be placed in the times for the nations, and God knows best. Mujahid said: God never sent a prophet except that He commanded him to establish prayer and give Zakat and acknowledging obedience to God, for that is the religion that He has prescribed for them. Al-Walibi said this on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and it is the opinion of Al-Kalbi. Qatada said: It means making permissible what is permissible and forbidding what is forbidden. Al-Hakam said: It makes mothers, sisters and daughters forbidden. What Al-Qadi mentioned includes these sayings and adds to them. He specifically mentioned Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus because they are the masters of the laws. God the Almighty said: That to which you invite them of monotheism and rejection of idols was difficult for them. Qatada said: The testimony that there is no god but God was difficult for the polytheists and they found it difficult, and Satan and his soldiers were fed up with it. But God the Almighty refused to do anything but support it, exalt it, and make it prevail over those who opposed it. Then He said: God chooses for Himself whom He wills meaning He selects, and choosing means choosing, meaning He chooses for monotheism whomever He wills. And guides to Himself whoever turns back meaning He appoints a successor for His religion whoever returns to Him.
42:14: And they did not become divided, Ibn Abbas said: meaning the Quraysh, except after knowledge had come to them Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him. They wished that a prophet would be sent to them. The evidence for this is the Almighty's statement in Surat Fatir 35:And they swore by God their most solemn oaths that if there came to them a warner (Fatir 35:42), a prophet. And He said in Surat al-Baqarah 2:But when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it (al-Baqarah 2:89), as was explained there. And it was said: the name of the previous prophets, for they differed among themselves when the period had been long, so some people believed and some people disbelieved. And Ibn Abbas also said: meaning the People of the Book. His evidence for this is in Surat Al-Munfikin: And those who were given the Scripture did not become divided except after there came to them clear proof (al-Bayyinah 98:4). So the polytheists said: Why was he singled out for prophethood? And the Jews envied him when he was sent, and so did the Christians, out of envy among themselves, meaning envy from some of them against others, seeking leadership. So their division was not due to a deficiency in eloquence and arguments, but rather to envy, injustice, and preoccupation with the world. And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, in delaying the punishment for these people, until a specified term, it was said: the Resurrection, because of the Most High’s statement: Rather, the Hour is their appointed time (al-Qamar 54:46). And it was said: until the term in which He decreed their punishment, it would have been decided between them, meaning between those who believed and those who disbelieved in the punishment’s descent. And indeed, those who were given the Scripture, meaning the Jews and Christians, after them, meaning after those who differed about the truth, are in disquieting doubt about it, about what the prophets recommended, and the Scripture here is the Torah and the Gospel. And it was said: Indeed, those who were given the Scripture, Quraysh, after them, after the Jews and Christians, are in doubt about the Qur’an or about Muhammad. Mujahid said: The meaning of after them is before them. It means by the polytheists of Mecca, namely the Jews and Christians.
42:15: The Almighty’s saying: Therefore, call and be steadfast. Since it is possible that the doubt was from the Jews and Christians, or from the Quraysh, it was said to him: Therefore, call, meaning that their doubt was clear, so call to God, that is, to that religion that God prescribed for the prophets and commanded them to follow. The lam has the meaning of to, like the Almighty’s saying: That your Lord has revealed to it (al-Zalzalah 99:5), that is, to it. That has the meaning of this, and the beginning of Al-Baqarah was mentioned previously. The meaning is Therefore, call to this Qur’an. It was said that there is an inversion in the speech, and the meaning is that what you are calling them to is difficult for the polytheists, so call. It was said that the lam is in its proper place, and the meaning is: Because of that which was mentioned previously, call and be steadfast. Ibn Abbas said: That is, to the Qur’an, so call the creation. And be steadfast is addressed to him, peace be upon him. Qatada said: That is, be steadfast upon the command of God. Sufyan said: That is, be steadfast upon the Qur’an. Ad-Dahhak said: Be steadfast upon conveying… The message, And do not follow their desires, meaning do not look at the disagreement of those who disagree with you, and say, ‘I have believed in what God has revealed of the Book, and I have been commanded to be just between you,’ meaning to be just, as God the Most High said: And I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds (Ghafir 40:66). It was said that it is the lam of ki, meaning in order to be just. Others said: to be just. Ibn Abbas and Abu al-Aaliyah said: to be just between you in religion, so I believe in every book and every messenger. Others said: to be just in all circumstances. It was said that this justice is justice in rulings. It was said in conveying the message: “God is our Lord and your Lord. For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. There is no argument between us and you.” Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: The address is to the Jews, meaning for us is our religion, and for you is your religion. He said: Then it was abrogated by His saying: Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day (al-Tawbah 9:29), the verse. Mujahid said: The meaning of there is no argument between us and you is no dispute between us and you. It was said that it is not abrogated, because The proofs have appeared, and the arguments have been established, so nothing remains but stubbornness, and after stubbornness there is no argument or argument. An-Nahhas said: It is possible that the meaning of (There is no argument between us and you) according to that statement is: He was not commanded to argue with you and fight you, then this was abrogated, just as if someone had said before the qiblah was changed: Do not reach the Kaaba, then the people changed after that, it would be possible to say that this was abrogated. God will gather us together means on the Day of Resurrection, and to Him is the final destination meaning He will judge between us when we turn to Him, and He will reward each one according to what he was upon. It was said: This verse was revealed about Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira and Shaibah bin Rabi’ah, and they asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to return from his call and religion to the religion of Quraysh, on the condition that Al-Walid give him half of his wealth and that Shaibah marry his daughter to him.
42:16: The Almighty’s statement: And those who dispute about God refers to the polytheists, after it has been answered. Mujahid said: After people have submitted to Islam. He said: And these people have imagined that ignorance will return. Qatada said: Those who dispute about God are the Jews and Christians, and their argument is that our Prophet came before your Prophet and our Book came before your Book. They saw for themselves the virtue of being People of the Book and that they were the children of the Prophets. The polytheists used to say: Which of the two parties is better in position and better in company? (Maryam 19:73), so God the Almighty said: And those who dispute about God after it has been answered, their argument is worthless before their Lord. That is, it has no stability, like something that slips from its place. The ha in lahu may refer to God the Almighty, that is, after they declared God’s Oneness and bore witness to His Oneness. It may also refer to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that is, after Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was answered in His call was from the people of Badr and God gave victory to the believers. It is said: His argument was refuted completely and became invalid, and God refuted it. Refutation means slipping, and the place of refutation and refutation also with movement means slipped, and his foot refuted, refutation means slipping, and the sun refuted from the middle of the sky, And upon them is wrath meaning in this world, and for them is a severe punishment meaning in the hereafter, an eternal punishment.
42:17: The Almighty says: God is He who sent down the Book meaning the Qur’an and all the revealed books, in truth meaning with honesty, and the Balance meaning justice, as Ibn Abbas and most of the commentators said. Justice is called a Balance because the Balance is the instrument of fairness and justice. It was said: The Balance is what is explained in the Books of what a person must act upon. Qatada said: The Balance is justice in what He commands and forbids. These sayings are close in meaning. It was said: It is the reward for obedience with reward and for disobedience with punishment. It was said: It is the Balance itself by which weighing is done. He sent it down from the sky and taught the servants to weigh by it, so that there would be no injustice or shortcoming between them. God the Almighty said: Indeed, We sent Our messengers with clear proofs and sent down with them the Scripture and the Balance that people may maintain justice (al-Hadid 57:25). Mujahid said: It is that by which weighing is done. The meaning of He sent down the Balance is His inspiration to the creation to act upon it and act upon it. It was said that the Balance is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, who judges between you. By the Book of God, And what do you know? Perhaps the Hour is near. So He did not inform him of it. He urges him to work according to the Book, justice, and equity, and to work according to the laws. It is rare that the Day will surprise you when there will be accountability and weighing of deeds, and He will fully repay whoever has fully repaid and will shortchange whoever has shortchanged. Perhaps the Hour is near, that is, from you, and you do not know. He said, Near, and did not say Near, because its feminine is not real because it is like time, as Al-Zajjaj said. The meaning is: Perhaps the Resurrection or perhaps the coming of the Hour is near. Al-Kisa’i said, Near is an adjective that describes the masculine and feminine plural with one meaning and wording. God the Most High said, Indeed, the mercy of God is near to the doers of good. (al-A’raf 7:56) The poet said: We were close, but the houses were far away. When we arrived, we disappeared right in front of their eyes.
42:18: The Almighty says: Those who do not believe in it urge it on meaning in a mocking way, thinking that it will not come, or to make the weak think that it will not happen. And those who believe are fearful of it meaning afraid and apprehensive because they themselves are insufficient despite the effort they put into obedience, as He says: And those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful because they will be returning to their Lord (al-Mu’minun 23:60), and they know that it is the truth meaning that there is no doubt about it. Unquestionably, those who dispute about the Hour meaning they doubt and dispute about the occurrence of the Hour, are in extreme error meaning from the truth and the path of consideration, because if they remembered, they would know that the One who created them from dust, then from a sperm-drop until they reached maturity, is able to resurrect them.
42:19: The Almighty said: God is Kind to His servants. Ibn Abbas said: He is kind to them. Ikrimah said: He is good to them. Al-Suddi said: He is gentle with them. Muqatil said: He is kind to the righteous and the wicked, as He does not starve them to death because of their sins. Al-Qurazi said: He is kind to them in presentation and accountability. He said: Tomorrow, the Master of creation will have a situation for creation in which the Majestic One will question them and be kind to them. Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn said: He is kind to them in provision in two ways: One is that He made your provision from good things, and the second is that He did not give it to you all at once and then you squander it. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: He is kind to them in the Qur’an, its details and its interpretation. Al-Junayd said: He is kind to His friends until they recognize Him, and if He were kind to His enemies, they would not have denied Him. Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kattani said: He is kind to those of His servants who seek refuge in Him when they despair of creation, and they put their trust in Him and return to Him. Then his heart will turn to Him. It was stated in the hadith of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “God Almighty looks at the ruined graves and says, ‘Their traces have been erased, their images have vanished, and the torment remains for them. I am the Kind, and I am the Most Merciful of the merciful. Lighten their torment,’ and He lightens their torment.” Abu Ali al-Thaqafi, may God be pleased with him, said: I pass by the graveyards as if I were the brother of Fatna, and the garment is thin Whoever splits his mouth, God will provide for him, and my Lord is kind to those who turn to Him. It was said: The Gracious One is He who spreads the virtues of His servants and conceals their faults. Based on this, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘O He who reveals the beautiful and conceals the ugly.’ It was also said: He is He who accepts little and gives abundantly. It was also said: He is He who mends the broken and makes the difficult easy. It was also said: He is He from whom nothing is feared except His justice and nothing is hoped for except His grace. It was also said: He is He who bestows blessings upon His servant beyond their capacity and orders them to obey beyond their ability. God Almighty said: “And if you should count the favors of God, you could not enumerate them” (al-Nahl 16:18), And He has bestowed upon you abundant favors, both apparent and hidden (Luqman 31:20), and He said: And He has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty (al-Hajj 22:78), God wants to lighten your burden (An-Nisa’: 28). It was also said: He is He who helps in service and increases praise. It was also said: He is He who does not hasten those who disobey Him nor disappoint those who hope in Him. It was also said: He is He who does not turn away those who ask Him nor make those who hope in Him despair. It was also said: He is He who…” He pardons those who err. It was said: He is the One who has mercy on those who do not have mercy on themselves. It was said: He is the One who lit a lamp in the secrets of the knowers of knowledge, from the vision, and made the straight path a path for them, and provided them with abundant water from the clouds of His righteousness. The words of Abu al-Aaliyah and al-Junayd also have been mentioned in al-An’am. We have mentioned all of this in the most sublime book in explaining the beautiful names of God under His name al-Lateef. Praise be to God, He provides for whom He wills and deprives whom He wills. There is wisdom in favoring a people with wealth, so that some may need others, as He said: So that they may take others in mockery Az-Zukhruf 43:32. This was a kindness to the servants, and also to test the rich with the poor and the poor with the rich, as He said: And We have made some of you a trial for others - will you have patience? Al-Furqan 25:20, as was explained previously: And He is the Strong, the Exalted in Might.
42:20: The Almighty says: Whoever desires the tillage of the Hereafter - We increase for him his tillage. Tillage is work and earnings. From this is the saying of Abdullah ibn Umar: Till for your worldly life as if you were to live forever, and work for your Hereafter as if you were to die tomorrow. From this is how a man is called a harith. The meaning is: Whoever seeks, with what We have provided him, tillage for his Hereafter, and fulfills the rights of God and spends in strengthening the religion, then We will only give him the reward for that, from ten to seven hundred or more. And whoever desires the tillage of this world, meaning whoever seeks, with the money that God has given him, leadership of this world and access to forbidden things, then We do not deprive him of provision at all, but he will have no share in the Hereafter from his money. God the Almighty says: "Whoever desires the immediate, We hasten for him therein what We will for whom We intend. Then We have made for him Hell, which he will burn, blamed and banished. But whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it with the necessary effort while he is a believer - for those, it is they whose effort is ever appreciated." (al-Isra’ 17:18-19) ], and it was said: (We will increase for him in his tillage) We will grant him success in worship and make it easy for him. It was said: The tillage of the Hereafter is obedience, meaning whoever obeys will have the reward. It was said: (We will increase for him in his tillage) meaning We will give him this world along with the Hereafter. It was said: The verse is about conquest, meaning whoever intends the Hereafter by his conquest will be given the reward, and whoever intends booty by his conquest will be given some of it. Al-Qushayri said: It appears that the verse is about the disbeliever, he will be given plenty in this world, meaning he should not be deceived by that because this world will not last. Qatada said: Indeed, God gives whatever He wills of this worldly matter based on the intention of the Hereafter, and He does not give anything based on the intention of this world except this world, what We have written for him. And whoever prefers this world over his Hereafter, We will not assign for him a share in the Hereafter except the Fire, and he will not obtain from this world anything except the provision We have allotted for him. It is inevitable that it will be given to him with or without preferring. Juwaybir narrated on the authority of Al-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: And the words of God, the Exalted, {Whoever desires the tillage of the Hereafter}, whoever is among the righteous. Whoever desires the reward of his righteous deeds for the Hereafter, We will increase for him in his tillage, meaning in his good deeds. And whoever desires the tillage of this world, meaning whoever is among the wicked desires the world through his good deeds, We will give him thereof. Then He abrogated that in the Glorious: Whoever desires the immediate, We hasten for him therein what We will for whom We intend. (al-Isra’ 17:18) The correct view is that this is not abrogated, because this is a report and all things are by the will of God Almighty. Do you not see that it has been authenticated: “On the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he said: ‘Let none of you say, ‘O God, forgive me if You will, O God, have mercy on me if You will.’” Qatadah said what was mentioned above, and it shows you that there is no abrogation. We mentioned in Hud that this is from the category of absolute and qualified, and that abrogation does not enter into reports. And God is the source of help. Question: This verse invalidates Abu Hanifa’s school of thought in his statement that whoever performs ablution to cool off, it suffices for him the obligatory ablution that he is required to perform. The obligatory ablution is from the cultivation of the Hereafter and cooling off is from the cultivation of this world, so one does not enter into the other, and his intention does not suffice for it according to the apparent meaning of this verse, as Ibn al-Arabi said.
42:21: The Almighty said: Or do they have partners? That is, do they have them? The meem and hamza are for rebuke, and this is connected to His statement: (He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah) The Almighty said: God is He who has sent down the Book in truth and the Balance (al-Shura 42:17). They did not believe in Him, so do they have gods who have ordained for them polytheism which God did not permit?! If this is impossible, then God did not legislate polytheism, so how can they adhere to it? And were it not for the decisive word on the Day of Resurrection, where He said: Rather, the Hour is their appointed time, “it would have been decided between them” in this world, so the wrongdoer would be punished quickly and the obedient would be rewarded. And indeed, the wrongdoers meaning the polytheists will have a painful punishment in this world: killing, capture, and subjugation, and in the Hereafter: the punishment of the Fire. Ibn Hurmuz read and with a fat-ha on the hamza in conjunction with and were it not for the word separating the conjoined and the conjoined to it with the answer to if only is permissible. It is also permissible for the position of that to be nominative, assuming: it is necessary that the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment, so it would be cut off from what preceded it, like the reading with a kasra, so be aware of it.
42:22: The Almighty says: You will see the wrongdoers fearful meaning afraid of what they have earned meaning of the recompense for what they have earned, and the wrongdoers here are the disbelievers, as evidenced by the division between the believer and the disbeliever and it will befall them meaning it will descend upon them and those who believe and do righteous deeds will be in the gardens of Paradise “garden” is the pleasant place with much greenery, and this has already been mentioned in ar-Rum “for them is whatever they wish with their Lord” meaning of bliss and abundant reward, that is the great bounty meaning it cannot be described and minds cannot be guided to the essence of its description, because if the Truth says something great, then who can estimate its value?
42:23: The Almighty says: That is the one with whom God gives good tidings to His servants who believe. It was read as yabshri from basharahu, “yabshri” from absharah, and yabshri from basharahu, and there is an omission in it, meaning that God gives good tidings to His believing servants so that they may hasten to the joy and increase their zeal in obedience. God Almighty says: “Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it except love for my relatives.” There are two issues in this: First: The Almighty’s saying: Say, ‘I do not ask of you for it any reward,’ meaning, say, O Muhammad, I do not ask of you for conveying the message any reward, except love for my kinship. Al-Zajjaj said: Except love is an exception not from the first, meaning, except that you love me for my kinship and protect me. The address is to the Quraysh specifically, as stated by Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Mujahid, Abu Malik, Al-Sha’bi and others. Al-Sha’bi said: Most people are against us in this verse, so we wrote to Ibn Abbas asking him about it, and he wrote that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the most middle-class of the Quraysh, and there was no clan among them that did not give birth to him. So God said to him: Say, ‘I do not ask of you for it any reward except love for my kinship,’ except that you love me for my kinship among you, meaning, you respect what is between me and you and believe me. Kinship here means kinship by blood, as if He said: Follow me for kinship if you do not follow me for prophethood. Ikrimah said: The Quraysh used to maintain kinship ties, “but when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, they severed that, and he said: Maintain kinship ties with me as you used to do.” So the meaning of this is, say, I do not ask you for any reward for it, but I remind you of my kinship, as an exception that is not from the first, mentioned by the fifth, and in Al-Bukhari on the authority of Tawus on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he was asked about the Almighty’s saying: Except for the love of kinship, so Saeed bin Jubair said: The kinship of the family of Muhammad, so Ibn Abbas said: You are hasty! There was no clan of the Quraysh except that he had a kinship with them, so he said: Unless you maintain the kinship ties between you. This is a statement. It was also said: Kinship is the kinship of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, meaning I do not ask you for a reward except that you love my kin and my family, as he commanded that they be respected by those who are near of kin. This is the statement of Ali ibn Husayn, Amr ibn Shu`ayb, and al-Suddi. In the narration of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, it is narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: When God Almighty revealed: “Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it except the love of my relatives,” they said: O Messenger of God, who are these whom we love? He said: Ali, Fatima, and their children. This is also indicated by what was narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: “I complained to the Prophet about the people’s envy of me, so he said: ‘Are you not satisfied that you will be the fourth of four, the first to enter Paradise: me, you, al-Hasan, al-Husayn, and our wives on our right and left, and our offspring behind our wives.” And on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Paradise has been forbidden to whoever wrongs my family and harms me in my progeny, and whoever does…” Whoever does a favor to one of the descendants of Abdul Muttalib and does not reward him for it, then I will reward him for it tomorrow when he meets me on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: The meaning is that they should be affectionate towards God the Almighty and draw near to Him by obeying Him. Qurb in this sense means nearness. It is said: qurbah and qurbah mean the same thing, like zulfa and zulfi. Qaza’ah bin Suwaid narrated on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ‘Say: I do not ask of you any reward for what I have given you except that you show affection to one another and draw near to Him through obedience.’” And Mansur and Auf narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan: “Say: I do not ask of you for it any reward except the love of my relatives.” He said: They seek to be close to God Almighty and draw near to Him by obeying Him. Some people said: The verse is abrogated and was revealed for His Prophet and his kinship ties. When he migrated, the Ansar sheltered him and supported him, and God wanted to join him with his brothers among the prophets when they said: “And I do not ask of you for it any reward. My reward is only from the Lord of the worlds.” (Ash-Shu’ara’: 109), so God Almighty revealed: “Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it; my reward is only from God.” (Saba’: 47), so it was abrogated by this verse and by His saying: “Say: I do not ask of you for it any reward, and I am not of the pretenders.” (Sad: 86), and His saying: Or do you ask them for a tribute? But the tribute of your Lord is better. (al-Mu’minun 23:72), and His saying: Or do you ask them for a reward, so they are burdened with debt? (al-Tur 52:40), as Ad-Dahhak said. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl, and it was narrated by Juwaybir on the authority of al-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Al-Tha’labi said: It is not strong. It is sufficient to say that whoever says that drawing closer to God through obedience to Him and loving His Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and his family has been abrogated. The Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: “Whoever dies loving the family of Muhammad dies a martyr. Whoever dies loving the family of Muhammad, God will make the angels and mercy visitors to his grave. Whoever dies hating the family of Muhammad will come on the Day of Resurrection with ‘despairing of God’s mercy today’ written between his eyes. Whoever dies hating the family of Muhammad will not smell the fragrance of Paradise. Whoever dies hating my family will have no share in my intercession.” I said: Al-Zamakhshari mentioned this hadith in his interpretation at a longer length than this, saying: “And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever dies loving the family of Muhammad dies a martyr. Whoever dies loving the family of Muhammad dies a believer with perfect faith. Whoever dies loving the family of Muhammad, the Angel of Death will give him good tidings of Paradise, then Munkar and Nakir. Whoever dies loving the family of Muhammad will be escorted to Paradise as a bride is escorted to her husband’s house. Whoever dies loving the family of Muhammad, two doors to Paradise will be opened for him in his grave. Whoever dies loving the family of Muhammad, God will make his grave a place of visitation for the angels of mercy. Whoever dies loving the family of Muhammad according to the Sunnah and the community. Whoever dies hating the family of Muhammad will come on the Day of Resurrection with it written between his eyes ‘despairing of God’s mercy. Whoever dies hating the family of Muhammad dies a disbeliever. Whoever dies hating the family of Muhammad will not smell the fragrance of Paradise.’” An-Nahhas said: The doctrine of Ikrimah is not abrogated. He said: “They used to maintain ties of kinship, but when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, they severed them. He said: ‘I do not ask you for any reward for it except that you love me and protect me for my kinship and not…’” You are lying to me. I said: This is the meaning of what Ibn Abbas said in Al-Bukhari and Al-Sha’bi on his authority himself, and based on that there is no abrogation. An-Nahhas said: The statement of Al-Hasan is good, and its authenticity is indicated by the hadith with a chain of transmission on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as Ahmad bin Muhammad Al-Azdi told us, he said: Al-Rabi’ bin Sulayman Al-Muradi told us, he said: Asad bin Musa told us, he said: Qaz’ah - who is Ibn Suwayd Al-Basri - he said: Abdullah bin Abi Nujayh told us, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, “That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘I do not ask of you any reward for what I inform you of of clear proofs and guidance except that you love God, the Almighty, and that you draw near to Him by obeying Him.’ So this one who clarifies on the authority of God, the Almighty, has said this, and the prophets, may God bless them and grant them peace, said the same before him: ‘My reward is only from God.’” Second: They differed about the reason for its revelation. Ibn Abbas said: When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to Medina, he was afflicted with calamities and rights that could not be contained in what he had in his hands. The Ansar said: This man, through whom God has guided you, is your nephew, and calamities and rights afflict him that cannot be contained in what he has in his hands. So we must gather for him. So they did, then they brought him to him and it was revealed. Al-Hasan said: It was revealed when the Ansar and the Muhajireen were boasting. The Ansar said: We did it, and the Muhajireen were proud of their kinship to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Muqsim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) heard something and gave a sermon, saying to the Ansar: Were you not humiliated and God honored you through me? Were you not astray and God guided you through me? Were you not afraid and God made you secure through me? Will you not respond to me? They said: How should we respond to you?
