He said: You say: Did not your people expel you and we sheltered you? Did not your people deny you and we believed you?... He enumerated before them. They said: They knelt on their knees and said: Ourselves. And our wealth is yours. Then this verse was revealed: Say, ‘I do not ask of you any reward for it except love for my relatives.’ Qatada said: The polytheists said, Perhaps Muhammad is seeking a reward for what he is given. So this verse was revealed to urge them to love him and his relatives. Al-Tha’labi said: This is more similar to the verse, because the surah is Meccan. God the Almighty said: And whoever does a good deed meaning earns. The root of qarf is earning. It is said: So-and-so does qarf for his family, meaning he earns. Qirfah is earning, and it is taken from their saying a man who is qirfa, if he is cunning. This has already been discussed in Al-An’am. Ibn Abbas said: And whoever does a good deed means affection for the family of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. We will increase for him therein good, meaning We will multiply the good deed by ten or more. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Appreciative. Qatada said: Forgiving is for sins, Appreciative is for good deeds. Al-Suddi said: Forgiving is for the sins of the family of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, Appreciative of their good deeds.
42:24: The Almighty’s saying: Or do they say, ‘He has invented a lie against God?’ The mim is a connective, and the meaning is, Do they say, ‘He has invented a lie?’ The statement is connected to what came before, because when God the Almighty said: And say, ‘I have believed in what God has revealed of the Book’ (al-Shura 42:15) and said: God is He who has sent down the Book with the truth (al-Shura 42:17), He said, completing the al-Sharh 94:Or do they say, ‘He has invented a lie against God?’ meaning the infidels of Quraysh said: Muhammad invented a lie against God. If God wills, He will seal is a condition and its answer, upon your heart. Qatadah said: He will seal your heart so that the Qur’an will be attributed to you. So God informed them that He had invented a lie against him so that he would do to Muhammad what He informed them of in this verse. Mujahid and Muqatil said: If God wills, He will strengthen your heart with patience in the face of their harm so that your heart will not be burdened by their words. It was said that the meaning is, If He wills, your discernment will slip. It was said that the meaning is, If God wills, He will seal the hearts of the infidels. And on their tongues and hasten their punishment, so the address is to him and what is meant is the disbelievers. Al-Qushayri mentioned: Then he began and said: And God erases falsehood. Ibn al-Anbari said: He seals your heart is complete. Al-Kisa’i said: There is an advancement and a delay in it, its meaning is: And God erases falsehood, so the waw was deleted from it in the Mushaf, and it is in the nominative case, just as it was deleted from His statement: We will call the guards (al-Alaq 96:18), and He will call man (al-Isra’ 17:11), and because it is in apposition to His statement: He will seal your heart (al-al-Shura 42:24), is complete. His statement: And God erases falsehood is an argument against those who deny what the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) brought, meaning if what he brought was falsehood, He would have erased it as is His custom with those who fabricate falsehoods. And He establishes the truth meaning Islam, so He confirms it with His words meaning what He revealed of the Qur’an, He is All-Knowing. “In the hearts of the servants” is general, meaning what is in the hearts of the servants, and it was said that it is specific, and the meaning is that if you were to tell a lie about God, He would know it and it would be imprinted in your heart.
42:25: The Almighty said: And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants. Ibn Abbas said: When the Almighty's saying, Say, 'I do not ask of you any reward for it except love for my relatives,' was revealed, some people said to themselves: He only wants to urge us to treat his relatives after him. Gabriel informed the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and that they had accused him, so He revealed: Or do they say, 'He has invented a lie against God?' The verse. The people said: O Messenger of God, we testify that you are truthful and we repent. So the verse was revealed: And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants. Ibn Abbas said: That is, from His friends and those who obey Him. The verse is general, and the discussion of the meaning of repentance and its rulings has already passed, and this wording has passed in Bara'ah. And He pardons misdeeds, that is, polytheism before Islam. And He knows what you do, that is, of good and evil. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, Hafs, and Khalaf read it with a ta' as an address, which is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud and his companions, and the rest with a ya' as a statement. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose it because it is between two pieces of report: the first: And He is the One who accepts repentance from His servants and the second: And He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds.
42:26: God Almighty says: “And He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds and increases them from His bounty. But for the disbelievers is a severe punishment.” (those) is in the accusative case, meaning that God will answer those who believe, that is, He will accept the worship of whoever is sincere to Him with his heart and obeys with his body. It was also said that He will give them what they ask for when they call upon Him. It was also said that He will answer the prayers of the believers, some of them to others. It is said that He answered and answered with the same meaning. This has already been mentioned in (Al-Baqarah), and Ibn Abbas said: And He will answer those who believe and do righteous deeds He will intercede for them on behalf of their brothers, and increase them from His bounty He said: He will intercede for them on behalf of their brothers’ brothers. Al-Mubarrad said: The meaning of (And He will answer those who believe) is that those who believe will call for an answer. This is the true meaning of istaf’ala. (those) is in the nominative case, and for the disbelievers is a severe punishment.
42:27: There are two issues: First: In its revelation. It was said that it was revealed about a group of people from the west bank who wished for abundant sustenance. Khabbab bin Al-Arat said: It was revealed about us. We looked at the wealth of Banu Nadir, Qurayzah and Banu Qaynuqa and we wished for it, so it was revealed: And if He had spread out means to expand. To spread something out means to spread it out. Also with the letter sad, they would have transgressed in the land in transgression and disobedience. Ibn Abbas said: Their transgression is their seeking of one status after another, one animal after another, one mount after another, and one garment after another. It was said: He meant if He had given them much, they would have sought more than that, because of His saying: If the son of Adam had two valleys full of gold, he would seek a third, which is transgression, and it is the meaning of Ibn Abbas’s saying. It was said: If We made them equal in the water, they would not have submitted to one another, and crafts would have been neglected. It was said: He meant by provision the rain, which is the cause of provision, meaning if He continued to rain, they would be distracted by it from supplication, so He would withhold it sometimes so that they would be humble and He would extend it at other times so that they would be grateful. It was said: When they were fertile, they would raid each other, so it is not far-fetched to interpret transgression as this. Al-Zamakhshari: (labaghaw) comes from bagh, which means injustice, meaning this one oppressed that one and that one oppressed this one, because wealth is a source of arrogance and greed, and Qarun is enough as a lesson, and from this is his saying, peace be upon him: What I fear most for my nation is the adornment of this world and its abundance, and some Arabs say: Al-Wasmi made a spring and a vine grow between us and the Banu Dudan. Meaning that they revived and spoke to themselves about transgression and arrogance, or from transgression, which is extravagance and pride, meaning that they would become arrogant on earth and do what follows arrogance of superiority and corruption in it, but He sends down according to what He wills meaning He sends down their provisions according to what He wills to suffice them. Muqatil said: He sends down according to what He wills He makes whomever He wills rich and whomever He wills poor. Second: Our scholars said: The actions of the Lord, glory be to Him, are not devoid of benefits, even if it is not obligatory upon God to reform. He may know from the condition of a servant that if He expanded it upon him, it would lead him to corruption, so He removes the world from him, as a benefit for him. So, a narrow livelihood is not humiliation, nor is ample livelihood a virtue. He gave to people, knowing that they would use it for corruption. If He had done to them something other than what He did, they would have been closer to reform. The matter is generally entrusted to His will, and it is not possible to adhere to the doctrine of reform in every action of God Almighty. Anas narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in what he narrated from his Lord, may He be blessed and exalted, that he said: “Whoever humiliates a friend of Mine has waged war against Me. I am the quickest thing to support My friends, and I become angry for them as a fierce lion becomes angry. I do not hesitate about anything I do as I hesitate about taking the soul of My believing servant. He hates death, and I hate to harm him, but it is inevitable for him. My believing servant does not draw near to Me by doing what I have made obligatory upon him. My believing servant continues to draw near to Me with voluntary acts until I love him, and when I love him, I am…” He has hearing, sight, a tongue, a hand, and a supporter. If he asks Me, I give to him, and if he calls upon Me, I answer him. And among My believing servants is he who asks Me for a door of worship, and I know that if I were to give it to him, torment would enter him and corrupt him. And among My believing servants is he who is not reformed except by wealth, and if I were to make him poor, poverty would corrupt him. And among My believing servants is he who is not reformed except by poverty, and if I were to make him rich, wealth would corrupt him. And I manage My servants because of My knowledge of their hearts, for I am All-Knowing, All-Aware. Then Anas said: O God, I am among Your believing servants who are not reformed except by wealth, so do not impoverish me by Your mercy.
42:28: God Almighty says: “And it is He who sends down rain after they have despaired and spreads His mercy. And He is the Protector, the Praiseworthy.” Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaisin, Hamid, Mujahid, Abu Amr, Yaqub, Ibn Wathab, Al-A’mash and others, and Al-Kisa’i read (yanzul) without a fat-ha, the rest with a shaddah. Ibn Wathab also, Al-A’mash and others read (qantu) with a kasra on the noon. All of this has been mentioned before. Al-Ghayth is the rain, and Al-Ghayth is called Ghayth because it provides relief to the creation. Al-Ghayth al-Ard means it befalls it. God provides the land with a ghayth, and the land receives a ghayth, so it is a land of ghayth and ghaythun. Al-Asma’i said: I passed by some Arab tribes and they had had rain, so I asked an old woman among them: Did the rain come to you? She said: We were given whatever we wanted with ghayth, meaning we were given rain. Dhu al-Rummah said: May God kill the nation of Banu so-and-so, how eloquent she is! I said to her: How was the rain with you? She said: Give us as much rain as we want. The first was mentioned by Al-Tha’labi and the second by Al-Jawhari. Sometimes he called the clouds and plants rain, and despair is called qanūt, as Qatada and others said. Qatada said: It was mentioned that a man said to Umar ibn Al-Khattab: O Commander of the Faithful, the rain has been scarce, the rain has become scarce and the people have despaired? He said, It will rain, God willing. Then he recited, And it is He who sends down rain after they have despaired. Rain is that which is beneficial in its time, and rain may be beneficial or harmful in its time or out of its time. Al-Mawardi said this. And spreads His mercy. It was said that it means rain, and this is what Al-Suddi said. It was also said that it means the sun after the rain, as Al-Mahdawi mentioned. Muqatil said: It was revealed regarding the withholding of rain from the people of Mecca for seven years until they despaired, then God sent down rain. It was also said that it was revealed regarding the Bedouin who asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about rain on Friday in the story of the prayer for rain, as Al-Qushayri mentioned. And God knows best. And He is the Protector, the Praiseworthy. “The Protector” is the one who supports His protectors, The Praiseworthy is the one praised in every tongue.
42:29: The Almighty’s statement: And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth meaning His signs indicating His power and what He has dispersed throughout them of living creatures Mujahid said: This includes the angels and people, and the Almighty has said: And He creates what you do not know (al-Nahl 16:8). Al-Farra’ said: He meant what He has dispersed throughout the earth, not the heavens, like His statement: From them come forth pearls and coral (al-Rahman 55:22). Rather, it comes forth from salt, not fresh water. Abu Ali said: Its meaning is what He has dispersed in one of them, so the complement was omitted. His statement: From them come forth meaning from one of them, And He is able to gather them meaning on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:If He wills.
42:30: The Almighty’s saying: And whatever strikes you of disaster - it is for what your hands have earned. Nafi’ and Ibn ‘Amir read (bima kasabtu) without fa’, the rest read (fabma) with fa’, and Abu ‘Ubaid and Abu ‘Ubaid chose it for the increase in the letter and the reward. Al-Mahdawi said: If you consider that (ma) is a relative, it is permissible to delete the fa’ or to keep it, and keeping it is better. If you consider it to be for the condition, deletion is not permissible according to Sibawayh, and al-Akhfash permitted it and provided evidence with the Almighty’s saying: And if you obey them, indeed, you would be polytheists (al-An’am 6:121). The disaster here is the limits for sins, said al-Hasan. Ad-Dahhak said: A man did not learn the Qur’an and then forget it except for a sin. God Almighty said: And whatever strikes you of disaster - it is for what your hands have earned. Then he said: What disaster is greater than forgetting the Qur’an? Ibn al-Mubarak mentioned it on the authority of ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Abi Rawad. Abu ‘Ubaid said: This is only for leaving it, but as for what…” He is persistent in reciting it and keen on memorizing it, but forgetfulness overcomes him, so that is not the case. What confirms that is that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would forget something from the Qur’an until he remembered it. An example of that is the hadith of Aisha, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: He heard a man reciting in the mosque and said: What is wrong with him, may God have mercy on him! He reminded me of verses I had forgotten from such-and-such Surah.” It was said that what means who, and the meaning is that which afflicted you in the past because of what your hands have earned. Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: This verse is the most hopeful verse in the Book of God Almighty. If He expiates for me calamities and pardons many, then what remains after His expiation and pardon! This meaning was narrated from him, may God be pleased with him, who said: Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said: Shall I not tell you of the best verse in the Book of God, which the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, told us: And whatever strikes you of disaster - it is for what your hands have earned. The verse: ((O Ali, whatever illness, punishment, or affliction befalls you in this world - it is for what your hands have earned. And God is too generous to punish you twice in the Hereafter. And whatever He pardons in this world - God is too forbearing to punish with it after His pardon.)) Al-Hasan said: When this verse was revealed, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no twitching of a vein, no scratch from a stick, and no blow from a stone except for a sin, and what God pardons is greater.)) Al-Hasan said: We entered upon Imran ibn Husayn and a man said: I must ask you about the pain I see in you. Imran said: O my brother, do not do that! By God, I love pain, and whoever loves pain is the most beloved of people to God. God the Almighty said: {And whatever strikes you of disaster - it is for what your hands have earned; but He pardons much.} This is what my hands have earned, and my Lord’s pardon of what remains is more. Al-Hamdani once said: I saw a sore on the back of Shureih’s palm, so I said: O Abu Umayyah, what is this? He said: This is for what your hands have earned, and He pardons much. Ibn Awn said: When Muhammad ibn Sirin was burdened with debt, he was distressed by it, so he said: I know this distress; it is for a sin I committed forty years ago. Ahmad ibn Abi Al-Hawari said: Abu Sulayman Al-Darani was asked: Why do wise people remove blame from those who wrong them? He said: Because they knew that God, the Most High, tested them for their sins. God, the Most High, said: “And whatever strikes you of disaster - it is for what your hands have earned. But He pardons much.” Ikrimah said: There is no calamity that befalls a servant or anything greater than it except for a sin that God would not have forgiven him except for it, or to attain a degree that He would not have reached except for it. It was narrated that a man said to Moses: O Moses, ask God for me about a need that He may fulfill for me, for He is most knowing of it. So Moses did so, and when he came down, he saw the man whose flesh had been torn apart by a wild animal and killed him. Moses said: What is wrong with this, O Lord? Then God, the Most High, said to him: O Moses, he asked Me for a degree that I knew he would not attain through his deeds, so I afflicted him with what you see in order to make it a means for him to attain that degree. When Abu Sulayman al-Darani mentioned this hadith, he would say: Glory be to He who was able to grant him that degree without trial! But He does what He wills. I said: Similar in meaning to this verse is the statement of God the Most High: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it (An-Nisa’ 4:123). This has already been discussed. Our scholars said: This is in the case of the believers. As for the disbeliever, his punishment is postponed until the Hereafter. It was also said that this is addressed to the disbelievers, and whenever evil befell them, they would say: This is due to the bad luck of Muhammad. He responded to them and said: Rather, it is due to the bad luck of your disbelief. The first is more common, more apparent, and more well-known. Thabit Al-Bunani said: It was said that the hours of harm eliminate the hours of sin. Then there are two opinions: One of them is that it is specific to adults, as a punishment for them, and in children, as a reward for them. The second is that it is a general punishment for adults in themselves and for children in others, such as parents. And He pardons many means that many sins are not subject to punishment, and this is what Al-Hasan said. It was also said that it means that He pardons many of the sinners and does not hasten to punish them. God Almighty says: So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it. There are three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it. Ibn Abbas used to say: Whoever among the disbelievers does an atom’s weight of good will see it in this world, but will not be rewarded for it in the Hereafter. Whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will be punished for it in the Hereafter, along with the punishment for polytheism. Whoever among the believers does an atom’s weight of evil will see it in this world, but will not be punished for it in the Hereafter if he dies, and he will be overlooked. If he does an atom’s weight of good, it will be accepted from him and multiplied for him in the Hereafter. In some hadiths: The atom has no weight. God Almighty used this to mean that He does not neglect any of the deeds of the son of Adam, whether small or large. It is similar to His saying: Indeed, God does not wrong, by as much as the weight of an atom. (An-Nisa’: 40). We have already discussed the atom there and that it has no weight. Some linguists have said that dhar is when a man strikes the ground with his hand, and whatever dirt sticks to it is dhar. Ibn Abbas also said: If you place your hand on the ground and raise it, then every piece of dirt that sticks to it is an atom. Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi said: Whoever does an atom’s weight of good as a disbeliever will see his reward in this world, in himself, his wealth, his family, and his children, until he departs this world with no good for him with God. Whoever does an atom’s weight of evil as a believer will see his punishment in this world, in himself, his wealth, his children, and his family, until he departs this world with no evil for him with God. The proof for this is what the trustworthy scholars have narrated from the hadith of Anas: This verse was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while Abu Bakr was eating. He stopped and said: O Messenger of God, do we see what we have done of good and evil? He said: Whatever you see of what you dislike is equal to the weight of an atom of evil, and the weight of an atom of good is saved up for you until you are given it on the Day of Resurrection. Abu Idris said: Its verification is in the Book of God: “Whatever strikes you of disaster - it is for what your hands have earned. But He pardons much.” (al-Shura 42:30) Muqatil said: It was revealed about two men, and that is because when it was revealed And they give food, in spite of the love for it. (al-Insan 76:8) One of them would beggars, and he would think it too little to give him a date, a piece of bread, or a walnut. Another would take minor sins lightly, such as lying, backbiting, or looking at someone, and would say, God has only threatened the Fire for major sins. So this verse was revealed to encourage them to give a little good, because it will soon become abundant. And to warn them against minor sins, such as lying, backbiting, or looking at someone. He said, God has only threatened the Fire for major sins. So this verse was revealed to encourage them to give a little good, because it will soon become abundant. And to warn them against minor sins, because it will soon become abundant. Saeed ibn Jubayr said the same. A minor sin will be greater in the eyes of its perpetrator on the Day of Resurrection than mountains, and all his good deeds will be less than anything else in his eyes. Second: The general reading is yarah with the fat-ha on the yaa in both. Al-Jahdary, Al-Sulami, Isa bin Omar, and Aban from Asim read: yarah with the damma on the yaa, meaning God will show it to him. The first and preferred option, due to the Almighty’s saying: The Day every soul will find present what it has done of good (Al Imran 3:30). Hisham made the haa sukoon in his saying yarah in both places. Likewise, Kisa’i narrated it from Abu Bakr, Abu Haywah, and Al-Mughira. Ya’qub, Al-Zuhri, Al-Jahdary, and Shaybah concealed it. The rest sufficed. It was said yarah means he will see his reward, because what he did has passed and is no longer seen. They recited: Whoever commits a transgression and commits an atom's weight of sin will see it. He will be rewarded for doing evil with evil, and he will be rewarded for doing good as well. Thus, His saying, Blessed be my Lord, in If the earthquake shakes and the earth shakes
42:31: And you will not escape on earth meaning you will not escape God, meaning you will not escape Him and you will not miss Him. And you have besides God no protector or helper has been mentioned in more than one place.
42:32: The Almighty said: And among His signs are the ships sailing in the sea like mountains. That is, among His signs indicating His power are the ships sailing in the sea as if they were mountains due to their size. The mountains are the mountains, and the singular of the ships is sail. God Almighty said: Indeed, when the water rose, We carried you in the ships. (al-Haqqah 69:11) It was called a ship because it sails in the water, and a ship is a young woman, called that because the water of youth runs through her. Mujahid said: The ships are palaces, and the singular of it is a flag. Al-Tha’labi mentioned it, and Al-Mawardi mentioned that they are mountains. Al-Khalil said that everything that is high among the Arabs is a flag. Al-Khansa’ said, mourning her brother Sakhr: And Sakhr is the one whom the guides follow, as if he were a flag with fire on its head. (If He wills, He can still the winds) This is how the people of Medina read it (the winds) in the plural.
42:33: And they will remain motionless on its back meaning the ships will remain motionless on the back of the sea, not moving. The water is motionless, and so is the wind and the ship, and the sun when it is at its zenith at noon, and everything that is fixed in a place is motionless, and the scale is motionless, and the people are motionless, and the motionless are the places where people and others are motionless. Qatada read (and they will remain motionless) with a kasra on the first lam as if it is a language, like taslidala adhal, and with a fatha on the lam, which is the well-known language: Indeed in that are signs meaning indications and indications, for every patient and grateful person meaning patient in the face of adversity and grateful for blessings. Qutrub said: What a patient and grateful servant is, who is grateful when given something and is patient when afflicted. Awn ibn Abdullah said: How many a person is blessed but is not grateful, and how many afflicted but are not patient.
42:34: The Almighty’s saying: Or destroy them for what they have earned. That is, if He wills, He can make the winds storms and destroy the ships, that is, He can drown them for the sins of their people. It was also said: He can destroy the people of the ships. And pardons many of their people, so He does not drown them with them. Al-Mawardi narrated it. It was also said: And pardons many, that is, He overlooks many sins, so God saves them from destruction. Al-Qushayri said: The common reading is and pardons in the jussive mood, and there is a problem with it, because the meaning is: if He wills, He can still the wind, so those ships remain stationary, and He destroys them for the sins of their people. It is not appropriate to connect and pardons to this, because the meaning becomes: if He wills, He pardons. This is not the meaning, rather the meaning is to inform about the pardon without the condition of will. So it is connected to the jussive mood in terms of wording, not in terms of meaning. Some people read and pardons in the nominative case, and it is good in meaning.
42:35: And those who dispute about Our verses know that they have no escape meaning the disbelievers, that is, if they are in the middle of the sea and the winds cover them from every direction or the ships remain stationary, they know that they have no refuge except God, and no one can protect them if God wants to destroy them, so they devote their worship to Him. This meaning has been mentioned in more than one place, and the discussion of seafaring has been mentioned in (Al-Baqarah) and other places in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it. Nafi` and Ibn `Amir read (and He knows) in the nominative case, while the rest read it in the accusative case. The nominative case is a resumption after the condition and consequence, like His statement in Surat At-Tawbah, And He will disgrace them and give you victory over them (al-Tawbah 9:14), then He said, And God turns in mercy to whom He wills (al-Tawbah 9:15), in the nominative case. Its equivalent in speech is, If you come to me, I will come to you and Abdullah departs, or that it is the report of a deleted subject, and the accusative case is for declension, like His statement, the Most High: "And God has not yet known those among you who strive and He has not yet known The patient ones (Al Imran 3:142) It was changed from the jussive mood to the accusative mood out of disdain for the successive jussive moods, like the saying of Al Nabigha: If Abu Qaboos perishes, the spring of the people and the sacred month will perish. And he holds on to the tail of a snake with a long back and no hump. This is the meaning of what Al-Farra’ said: If (and he knows) were made jussive, it would be permissible. Al-Zajjaj said: It is in the accusative case because (that) is omitted because before it is jussive. You say: What you do, I will do the same and I will honor you. If you wish, you can say: And I will honor you in the jussive case. In some copies of the Qur’an, (and he knows), this indicates that the accusative means: and he knows or because he knows. Abu Ali and Al-Mubarrad said: The accusative case with the omission of (that) is to make the first in the estimation of the source, meaning that it is from it that forgiveness and that he knows. So when he made it into a noun, he omitted that, just as you say: If you come to me and give me, I will honor you. So you put the word you give me in the accusative case, meaning if you come and that you give me. The meaning of from refuge is from flight and escape, as Qatrab said. Al-Suddi said: From refuge, and it is taken from their saying: The camel surrounded him with a haysa if it threw it, and from it is their saying: So-and-so deviates from the truth, meaning he turns away from it.
42:36: The Almighty says: Whatever you have been given of anything meaning of wealth and abundance in this world. It is but enjoyment meaning it is only enjoyment for a few days that will pass and go, so one should not boast about it. The address is to the polytheists. And what is with God is better and more lasting meaning of the reward for obedience for those who have believed "truthful and monotheistic and upon their Lord rely" was revealed about Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq when he spent all his wealth in obedience to God and the people blamed him. It was mentioned in the hadith that he spent eighty thousand.
42:37: There are two issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And those who avoid “those” is in the accusative case, in apposition to His saying: is better and more lasting for those who believe (al-Shura 42:36), meaning it is for those who avoid major sins. The discussion of major sins has already been mentioned in An-Nisa’. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read major sin. The singular may mean the plural when it is added, like the Almighty’s saying: And if you should count the favors of God, you could not enumerate them. (Ibrahim 14:34), and as came in the hadith: Iraq withheld its dirham and its bushel. The rest use the plural here and in An-Najm. “And immoralities” Al-Suddi said: He means adultery. Ibn Abbas said: He said: Major sin is polytheism. Some people said: Major sins are those that fall on minor sins that are forgiven when they are avoided. Immoralities are included in major sins, but they are more heinous and more heinous, like murder in relation to wounding, and adultery in relation to solicitation. It was said: Immoralities and major sins have one meaning, so it was repeated because of the multiplicity of the word. That is, they avoid sins because they are major and obscene. Muqatil said: Obscene acts are punishable by the prescribed punishments. The second: The Almighty’s saying: And when they become angry, they forgive. That is, they overlook and are patient with those who wrong them. It was said: It was revealed about Umar when he was insulted in Mecca. It was also said: It was revealed about Abu Bakr when people blamed him for spending all his money and when he was insulted, so he was patient. And on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, he said: Abu Bakr had accumulated wealth once, so he gave it all in charity for the sake of goodness, so the Muslims blamed him and the disbelievers blamed him, so the verse was revealed: “Whatever you have been given is but the enjoyment of worldly life. But what is with God is better and more lasting for those who have believed and upon their Lord rely.” until His saying: And when they become angry, they forgive. (al-Shura 42:37). Ibn Abbas said: A polytheist insulted Abu Bakr, but he did not respond to him, so the verse was revealed. This is from the good morals. They have compassion for their oppressor and pardon those who have wronged them. They seek thereby the reward and forgiveness of God, the Almighty, because God, the Almighty, said in Al Imran 3:And those who restrain anger and pardon the people. (AAl Imran 3:134), which is when a man attacks you. So suppress your anger towards him, and some of them recited: I forgave my oppressor for his oppression and gave him that right, knowingly. He still wrongs me and I feel sorry for him until I cry for him because of the injustice
42:38: There are three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And those who responded to their Lord and established prayer. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said that they are the Ansar in Medina. They responded to the belief in the Messenger when he sent twelve leaders from among them to them before the migration. And established prayer, meaning they performed it at its appointed times with its conditions and forms. The second: The Almighty’s saying: And their affair is by consultation among them. That is, they consult each other in matters. Shura is the source of shura consultation, like glad tidings, remembrance, and the like. So, before the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to them, if the Ansar wanted to do something, they would consult each other about it and then act upon it, so God praised them for it. Al-Naqqash said this. Al-Hasan said: That is, because they were obedient to the opinion in their affairs, they agreed and did not differ, so they were praised for their unanimous word. Al-Hasan said: No people ever consulted except that they were guided to the most correct of their matters. Al-Dahhak said: It is their consultation when they heard of the appearance of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the arrival of the leaders to them until their opinion was unanimous in the house of Abu Ayyub on belief in him and support for him. It was said: Their consultation regarding what was presented to them, so that some of them would not monopolize report without others. Ibn al-Arabi said: Shura is a bond for the group, a probe of the minds, and a cause of correctness. No people ever consulted except that they were guided. Al-Hakim said: If the opinion reaches the point of advice, then seek the opinion of a wise person or the advice of a firm person. Do not let consultation be a source of embarrassment to you, for the hidden things are a source of strength for the future. So God praised consultation in matters by praising the people who complied with that. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to consult his companions in opinions related to the interests of wars, and that is in many opinions. He did not consult them in rulings, because they are revealed from God on all sections of obligation, recommendation, disliked, permissible, and forbidden from the Qur’an and Sunnah. The first thing the companions consulted about was the caliphate, for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not specify it until what was previously explained between Abu Bakr and the Ansar happened. Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: “We are satisfied for our worldly life with whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was satisfied for our religion.” They consulted about the apostates, and Abu Bakr’s opinion settled on fighting. They consulted about the grandfather and his inheritance, and about the punishment for wine and its number. They consulted after the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in wars, until Umar consulted al-Hurmuzan when he came to him as a Muslim in the battles. Al-Hurmuzan said to him: “Its example and the example of the people in it from the enemies of the Muslims is like a bird with feathers and two wings and two legs. If one of the wings is broken, the two legs stand with a wing and the head. If the wing is broken, the two legs stand with a wing and the head.” The other: The two men and the head rose, and if the head is smashed, the two men and the two wings are lost, and the head is Khosrau, and one wing is Caesar and the other is a knight, so order the Muslims to march to Khosrau... And he mentioned the hadith, and some of the wise men said: I have never made a mistake! If a matter concerned me, I consult my people and do what they see fit. If I am right, they are the right ones, and if I am wrong, they are the wrong ones. Third: It has been mentioned in Al Imran what Shura included in terms of rulings when God the Almighty said: And consult them in the matter (Al Imran 3:159). Consultation is a blessing, and consultation is consultation, and so is consultation with a damma on the shin, you say from it: I consulted him in the matter and I consulted him with the same meaning. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If your leaders are the best of you and your rich are generous, and your affairs are decided by consultation among you, then the surface of the earth is better for you than its interior. But if your leaders are the worst of you and your rich are misers, and your affairs are in the hands of your women, then the interior of the earth is better for you than its surface.” He said: It is a strange hadith. And from what We have provided them they spend meaning, and from what We have given them they give in charity, and it has been mentioned in Al-Baqarah.
42:39: First: The Almighty’s saying: And those who, when they are wronged meaning, the polytheists’ wrongdoing afflicts them. Ibn Abbas said: This is because the polytheists wronged the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, and harmed them and expelled them from Mecca, so God gave them permission to leave and established them in the land and gave them victory over those who wronged them. This is His saying in Surat al-Hajj 22:“Permission is given to those who are being fought against because they were wronged. And indeed, God is competent to give them victory. * Those who were expelled” (al-Hajj 22:39-40) all the verses. It was said: It is general in the wrongdoing of every wrongdoer, whether a disbeliever or otherwise, meaning, if they are wronged by an oppressor, they do not surrender to his oppression. This is an allusion to enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong and implementing the prescribed punishments. Ibn Al-Arabi said: God mentioned victory in the case of wrongdoing in the context of praise, and He mentioned forgiveness for the crime in another place in the context of praise, so it is possible that one of them is a justification for the other, and it is possible that this is related to two situations, one of which is that The aggressor is openly immoral, rude to the public, and harmful to young and old, so taking revenge on him is better. In a similar case, Ibrahim al-Nakha’i said: They hated to humiliate themselves, so the immoral ones would punish them. The second: That it was a slip, or that it happened from someone who admits the slip and asks for forgiveness, so forgiveness here is better. In a similar case, the following was revealed: And to pardon is closer to righteousness (al-Baqarah 2:237), and His saying: But whoever gives charity therein, it is an expiation for him (al-Ma’idah 5:45), and His saying: “And let them pardon and overlook. Would you not like that God should forgive you?” (al-Nur: 22). I said, this is good, and this is what Al-Kaya Al-Tabari mentioned in his Ahkam, he said: The Almighty’s statement: And those who, when injustice befalls them, take revenge indicates on its surface that taking revenge in this context is better. Do you not see that he linked it to the mention of responding to God Almighty and establishing prayer? It is based on what Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i mentioned, that they hated for the believers to humiliate themselves, so that the wicked would dare to attack them. This is for those who transgressed and persisted in that, and the context in which forgiveness is commanded is if the offender is remorseful and desists. And he said after this verse: And whoever takes revenge after being wronged - against those there is no blame. This requires the permissibility of taking revenge, not the command to do so. And he followed it with his statement: And whoever is patient and forgives - indeed, that is of the matters [worthy] of determination. It is based on forgiveness for someone who is not persistent. As for someone who persists in aggression and injustice, it is better to take revenge on him, based on the indication of the one before it. And it was said: That is, if injustice befalls them, they help each other against it until they remove it from them and repel it. Ibn Bahr said this, and it goes back to Generally speaking, as we mentioned.
42:40: Second: The Almighty’s saying: And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it. The scholars said: God divided the believers into two categories: a category that pardons the oppressor, so He began by mentioning them in His saying: And when they become angry, they forgive. And a category that takes revenge on their oppressor, then He explained the limit of taking revenge by saying: And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it. So he takes revenge on the one who wronged him without transgressing. Muqatil and Hisham ibn Hujayr said: This is for the one who has been wounded, so he takes revenge on the one who wounded him by retaliation, not by other insults or cursing. Al-Shafi’i, Abu Hanifa, and Sufyan said this. Sufyan said: Ibn Shubramah used to say: There is no one in Mecca like Hisham. Al-Shafi’i interpreted this verse to mean that a person can take from the wealth of the one who betrayed him the same as he betrayed him without his knowledge, and he cited as evidence for that “the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Hind, the wife of Abu Sufyan: Take from his wealth what is sufficient for you and your children.” So he permitted her to take that without his permission, and it has been mentioned. The discussion of this is completed in Al-Baqarah. Ibn Abi Nujayh said: It is based on the response to wounds. If he says: May God disgrace him or May God curse him, he should not say the same. He should not respond to slander with slander or to a lie with a lie. Al-Suddi said: God only praised the one who took revenge on someone who wronged him without aggression exceeding the amount that was done to him, meaning as the Arabs used to do. The retribution was called evil because it is in response to it. The first was evil in money or body, and this retaliation makes him feel bad with the same as well. All of this has already been completed in Al-Baqarah. Third: The Almighty’s saying: But whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, Ibn Abbas said: Whoever abandons retaliation and reconciles between himself and the oppressor by forgiving, his reward is with God, meaning that God will reward him for that. Muqatil said: So forgiveness is one of the righteous deeds, and sufficient has been mentioned in Al Imran, and praise be to God. Abu Nu’aym al-Hafiz narrated on the authority of Ali ibn al-Husayn may God be pleased with them who said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, a caller will call out, Which of you is the best? Some people will stand and it will be said, Go to Paradise. The angels will meet them and say, Where are you going? They will say, To Paradise. They will say, Before the reckoning? They will say, Yes. They will say, Who are you? They will say, The best of you. They will say, And what was your best? They will say, When we were treated ignorantly, we were patient, when we were wronged, we pardoned. They will say, Enter Paradise, for excellent is the reward of the doers. He mentioned the hadith, Indeed, He does not like the wrongdoers, meaning the one who initiates the wrongdoing. This was said by Sa’id ibn Jubayr. It was also said that He does not like the one who transgresses in retaliation and oversteps the bounds. This was said by Ibn ‘Isa.
42:41: Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: And whoever retaliates after being wronged - against them there is no blame. This is evidence that he has the right to exact it himself. This is divided into three categories: One: That it be retaliation for a body that a human being deserves, so there is no blame on him if he exacts it without aggression and his right is proven before the judges, but the imam reprimands him for ignoring it by retaliation because of the boldness in shedding blood. If his right is not proven before the judge, then there is no blame on him between him and God, and he is apparently required to do so and is held accountable and punished for his action. The second category: That it be the punishment of God Almighty in which no human being has a right, such as the punishment for adultery and cutting off the hand for theft. If that is not proven before a judge, then it is taken and he is punished for it. If it is proven before a judge, then he is examined. If it is cutting off for theft, then the punishment is dropped because of the loss of the limb that deserves amputation, and he is not required to do so because the discretionary punishment is discipline. If it is flogging, then the punishment is not dropped because of his transgression while its location remains, so he is taken by its ruling. The third category: That it is a right. If he has money, it is permissible for its owner to prevail over his right until he reaches it if he is someone who is knowledgeable about it. If he is not knowledgeable, then he should look into it. If he is able to reach it when demanding it, then he does not have the right to take it secretly. If he cannot reach it when demanding it because the one who has it denies it and does not have evidence to testify for him, then there are two schools of thought regarding the permissibility of him taking it secretly. One of them is that it is permissible, which is the opinion of Malik and al-Shafi’i. The second is that it is prohibited, which is the opinion of Abu Hanifa.
42:42: Sixth: The Almighty’s statement: The way is only against those who wrong people meaning by their aggression against them, according to the majority of scholars. Ibn Jurayj said: meaning they wrong them by polytheism that is contrary to their religion, and transgress upon the earth without right meaning in lives and wealth, according to the majority. Muqatil said: Their transgression is their work of sins. Abu Malik said: It is what the infidels of Quraysh hope will be in Mecca a religion other than Islam. On this basis, Ibn Zayd said: All of this was abrogated by jihad, and this is specifically for the polytheists. Qatadah said: It is general, and this is what the apparent meaning of the statement indicates, and we have explained it, and praise be to God. Seventh: Ibn al-Arabi said: This verse is in contrast to the previous verse in Bara’ah, which is His statement, There is no way against the doers of good (al-Tawbah 9:91). Just as God denied the way for those who do good, so too He denied it for those who do wrong, and He has completed the explanation of the two sections. Eighth: Our scholars differed regarding the ruler who imposes a certain sum of money on the people of a country and takes it from them and they pay it according to their wealth. Is it permissible for someone who is able to free himself from that to do so, and if he is freed, then the rest of the people of the country are to take the full amount imposed on them? It was said: No, and this is the opinion of Sahnun, one of our scholars. It was also said: Yes, he is entitled to that if he is able to free himself, and this is what Abu Ja`far Ahmad ibn Nasr al-Dawudi and then al-Maliki held. He said: This is indicated by Malik’s statement regarding the one who collects a sheep from the sheep of one of his companions, and there is not a minimum amount in all of them, that it is an injustice to the one for whom it is taken and he has no claim against his companions for anything. He said: I do not accept what was narrated from Sahnun, because there is no example in injustice, and no one is obligated to involve himself in injustice for fear of doubling the injustice to others, and God Almighty says: The path is only against those who wrong people. Ninth, the scholars differed regarding the analysis. Ibn al-Musayyab did not permit anyone to take possession of his honor or wealth. Sulayman ibn Yasar and Muhammad ibn Sirin permitted possession of his honor and wealth. Malik saw the permissibility of wealth but not his honor. Ibn al-Qasim and Ibn Wahb narrated from Malik that he was asked about the statement of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, I do not permit anyone, and he said, That varies. So I said to him, O Abu Abdullah, what if a man gives another a loan and he perishes and cannot repay it? He said, I think he should permit it, and that is better in my opinion, because God the Most High says, ‘Those who listen to speech and follow the best of it.’ (al-Zumar 39:18) So it was said to him, Does a man wrong another? He said: I do not see that. In my opinion, it contradicts the first. God Almighty says: The way is only against those who wrong people (al-Tawbah 9:91), and He Almighty says: There is no way against the doers of good. So I do not see that He should absolve him of his injustice. Ibn al-Arabi said: So there are three opinions on the issue: One of them is that he does not make it permissible under any circumstances, said by Saeed bin al-Musayyab. The second is that he makes it permissible, said by Muhammad bin Sirin. The third is that if it is money, he makes it permissible, and if it is oppression, he does not make it permissible, and this is the opinion of Malik. The first view is that he does not make permissible what God has forbidden, so it is like changing the ruling of God. The second view is that it is his right, so he can drop it just as his blood and honor are dropped. The third view, which Malik chose, is that if a man is overcome by his refusal to pay your right, it is kind to him to release him, and if he is an oppressor, it is right not to leave him lest the oppressors be deceived and indulge in their ugly actions. In Sahih Muslim, the long hadith of Abu al-Yusr is in which he said to his creditor: Come out to me, for I know where you are. So he came out, and he said: What made you You hid from me? He said: By God, I will tell you something and not lie to you. I fear, by God, that I will tell you something and lie to you, and that I will make a promise and then break it. I was a companion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and by God, I was in financial difficulty. I said: By God? He said: God. He said: So a piece of paper was brought to me and he erased it and said: If you find something to pay, then pay it, otherwise you are absolved. He mentioned the hadith. Ibn al-Arabi said: This applies to a living person who is expected to pay due to the integrity of the pledge and the hope of being forgiven, so how about a dead person who has no absolution or pledge with him? Tenth: Some scholars said: If someone commits an injustice and his money is taken, he only gets the reward for what was withheld from him until his death, then the reward goes to his heirs, and so on to the last of them, because the money goes to the heir after him. Abu Ja`far al-Dawudi al-Maliki said: This is correct in terms of consideration. According to this statement, if the oppressor dies before the one he oppressed and does not leave anything, or leaves something in which his heirs do not know of any injustice, then the claim of the oppressed does not pass to the heirs of the oppressor, because the oppressor does not have anything left that the heirs of the oppressed are entitled to.
42:43: Eleventh: The Almighty’s saying: And for him who is patient and forgives, meaning is patient in the face of harm, and forgives means abandons seeking revenge for the sake of God Almighty. This is what Muslim was wronged about. It is narrated that a man insulted another man in the assembly of Al-Hassan, may God have mercy on him. The one who was insulted would hold back his anger and sweat, so he would wipe away the sweat. Then he stood up and recited this verse, and Al-Hassan said: By God, he understood it and understood it, for the ignorant have wasted it. In short, forgiveness is recommended, but the matter may be reversed in some cases, and abandoning forgiveness becomes recommended, as mentioned above, when there is a need to stop the increase of aggression and cut off the source of harm. “There is something from the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, which indicates this, which is that Zainab made Aisha, may God be pleased with them both, hear it in his presence, and he used to forbid her, but she would not stop. So he said to Aisha: “Go ahead and seek revenge.” Muslim included it in his Sahih with the same meaning. It was said: (Patience) from sins and concealing faults Indeed, that is of the matters of resolve meaning of the resolve of God that He commanded, and it was said of the resolve of the right that He was guided to. Al-Kalbi and Al-Farra’ mentioned that this verse was revealed about Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, along with three verses before it. Some of the Ansar had insulted him, so he responded to him and then stopped. These are the Medinan verses of this surah. It was said: These verses are about the polytheists, and this was at the beginning of Islam before the command to fight, then the verse of fighting abrogated it. This is the saying of Ibn Zayd, and it was mentioned before. In the interpretation of Ibn Abbas: (And whoever retaliates after being wronged) meaning Hamza bin Abdul Muttalib, Ubaidah, Ali, and all the Muhajireen, may God be pleased with them. For those there is no blame meaning Hamza bin Abdul Muttalib, Ubaidah, and Ali, may God be pleased with them all. The blame is only against those who wrong people meaning Utbah bin Rabi’ah, Shaibah bin Rabi’ah, Al-Walid bin Utbah, Abu Jahl, Al-Aswad, and all of the polytheists who fought on the day of Badr. And they seek… On the earth, meaning injustice and disbelief, “those will have a painful punishment,” and whoever is patient and forgives, meaning Abu Bakr, Umar, Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah, Mus’ab ibn Umair, and all the people of Badr, may God be pleased with them all, that is of the matters [worthy of] determination, as they accepted the ransom and were patient in the face of the harm.
42:44: God Almighty says, And he whom God leaves astray meaning, abandons him, will have no protector after Him. This is about the one who turned away from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in what he called him to of belief in God and love for the kin, and did not believe him in the resurrection and that the enjoyment of this world is little, meaning, whoever God leaves astray from these things, no guide will guide him. God Almighty says: And you will see the wrongdoers, meaning the disbelievers, when they see the punishment, meaning Hell. It was also said that they saw the punishment at death, saying, ‘Is there any way back?’ They ask to be returned to this world so that they may work in obedience to God, but they are not granted that.
42:45: The Almighty said: And you will see them exposed to it meaning to the Fire because it is their torment. So He referred to the torment mentioned with the feminine particle, because that torment is the Fire, or if you wish, Hell. And if he had taken into account the wording, he would have said upon it. Then it was said: They are all the polytheists exposed to Hell when they go to it. This was said by the majority. And it was said: The family of Pharaoh in particular, their souls are trapped in the bodies of birds that fly to Hell and come back, so it is their exposure to it. This was said by Ibn Mas`ud. And it was said: They are all the polytheists, their sins are exposed to them in their graves, and they are exposed to the torment in their graves. This is the meaning of what Abu al-Hajjaj said, Humbled from humiliation. Some of the reciters stopped at (humbled), and His saying (from humiliation) is connected to (they look), and it was said: It is connected to (humble), and humility is submission and humility, and the meaning of (they look from a hidden corner) is They will not raise their eyes to look completely, because they have lowered their heads. The Arabs describe the humiliated as lowering their gaze, just as they use the opposite of a sharp gaze if he is not accused of any suspicion, in which case it would be considered humiliation. Mujahid said: From a hidden eye means evidence. He said: They will look with their hearts because they will be gathered blind, and the eye of the heart is a hidden eye. Qatada, Al-Suddi, Al-Qurazi, and Saeed bin Jubayr said: They will steal glances from the intensity of fear. It was also said: The meaning is they will look from an eye with weak sight. Yunus said: From has the meaning of the preposition with, meaning they will look with a hidden eye, meaning weak from humiliation and fear. Al-Akhfash said something similar. Ibn Abbas said: With a withered, humiliated eye. It was also said: They will be terrified to look at it with all their eyes because of what they will see of the various types of torment. “And those who believed will say, ‘Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. ’” That is, the believers in Paradise will say, when they witnessed what happened to the disbelievers, that the loss in reality is what happened to these people. They have lost themselves because they are in eternal torment, and they have lost their families because if the family is in Hell, there is no benefit from them, and if they are in Paradise, then they will be prevented from reaching them. It was said that the loss of the family is that if they had believed, they would have had family in Paradise from among the houris. In Sunan Ibn Majah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘There is not one of you but has two homes, a home in Paradise and a home in Hell. When he dies and enters Hell, the people of Paradise inherit his home. This is what God says: ‘Those are the inheritors. ’” (al-Mu’minun 23:10), and it has been mentioned previously. In Al-Musnad Al-Darimi, on the authority of Abu Umamah, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘There is not one whom God admits to Paradise except that he has seventy-two wives from among the houris and seventy from his inheritance from the people of Hell. There is not one of them but has a wife before. ’” He is delicious and has a penis that does not sag. Hisham bin Khalid said about his inheritance from the people of Hellfire, meaning men who entered Hellfire and the people of Paradise inherited their women as Pharaoh’s wife inherited: Indeed, the wrongdoers will be in a lasting punishment, meaning permanent and never ending. Then it is possible that this is from the words of the believers, and it is possible that it was initiated by God Almighty.
42:46: God Almighty says: And they had no protectors meaning helpers and supporters to support them other than God meaning from His punishment and he whom God sends astray - for him there is no way meaning a path that would lead him to the truth in this world and Paradise in the Hereafter, because the path to salvation has been closed to him.
42:47: The Almighty says: Respond to your Lord meaning, respond to Him in what He has called you to of belief in Him and obedience. He responded and responded have the same meaning, and it has been mentioned before. Before there comes a Day from God that there is no repelling meaning the Day of Resurrection, meaning no one will repel it after God has decreed it and set a term and time for it. You will have no refuge meaning no refuge that will save you from the punishment. And you will have no denier meaning no helper that will support you. This was said by Mujahid. It was also said that nakeer means denier, just as alaim means painful, meaning that on that day you will not find anyone to deny the punishment that will befall you. This was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Kalbi Al-Zajjaj said this. Its meaning is that they will not be able to deny the sins that they are accused of. It was also said that of denier means denial of the one who will befall you of punishment, and nakeer and denier mean changing the reprehensible.
42:48: God Almighty says: But if they turn away meaning from faith then We have not sent you over them as a guardian meaning a guardian of their deeds so that you may hold them accountable for them. It was also said: entrusted with them so that you do not leave them until they believe, meaning you cannot compel them to believe. Your responsibility is only to convey [the message] It was also said that this was abrogated by the verse on fighting. And indeed, when We let man the disbeliever taste mercy from Us ease and health, he rejoices therein with its delight. And if evil befalls them affliction and hardship for what their hands have put forth, then indeed, man is ungrateful meaning for what came before of blessings, so he enumerates the misfortunes and forgets the blessings.
42:49: The Almighty’s saying: To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth is a beginning and a predicate. He creates what He wills of creation. He gives to whom He wills females and He gives to whom He wills males. Abu Ubaidah, Abu Malik, Mujahid, Al-Hasan, and Ad-Dahhak said: He gives to whom He wills females with no males alongside them, and He gives to whom He wills males with no females alongside them. He inserted the definite article for males but not for females because they are more honorable, so He distinguished them with the definite article. Wathilah ibn Al-Asqa’ said: One of the blessings of a woman is her giving birth to a female before a male. That is because God Almighty said: He gives to whom He wills females and He gives to whom He wills males, so He began with females. Or He pairs them [with] males and females. Mujahid said: It is for a woman to give birth to a boy, then to a girl, then to a boy, then to a girl. Muhammad ibn Al-Hanafiyyah said: It is for her to give birth to twins, a boy and a girl, or He pairs them with males and females. He said: Al-Qatabi: Marriage here means combining sons and daughters. The Arabs say: He has paired my camels if they combine the old and the young. And He makes whom He wills barren, meaning that he will not have children. It is said: a barren man, and a barren woman. The woman is barren, she is barren, barrenness, like Hamd praise and Aqmat sterility, like Azam greatness, and its root is cutting, and from it comes the barren king, meaning that the wombs are cut off by killing and disobedience for fear of the king, and a barren wind, meaning that it does not fertilize clouds or trees, and the Day of Resurrection is a barren day, because it fills the day after it. It is said: barren women and barrenness. The poet said: Women are barren, and they do not give birth to anything similar to it. Women are barren like it. Al-Naqqash narrated that this verse was revealed specifically about the prophets, although its ruling was general. He gave Lot female children, not a male, and gave Abraham male children, not a female, and gave Ishmael and Isaac males and females, and made Jesus and John barren. Something similar was narrated by Ibn Abbas and Ishaq ibn Bishr. Ishaq said: It was revealed about the prophets, then it became general. He gives to whom He wills female children means Lot, peace be upon him, no male was born to him, but he had two daughters. And He gives to whom He wills male children means Abraham, peace be upon him, no female was born to him, but he had eight male children.
42:50: Or He gives them both males and females means the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who had four sons and four daughters, and makes whom He wills barren means John, son of Zechariah, peace be upon them both. He did not mention Jesus. Ibn al-Arabi said: Our scholars said, He gives to whom He wills females means Lot, who had daughters but no son, and He gives to whom He wills males means Abraham, who had sons but no daughter. His statement, Or He gives them both males and females means Adam. Eve would give birth to twins for him in every pregnancy, a male and a female, and the male from this pregnancy would be married to the female from the other pregnancy, until God made the prohibition firm in the law of Noah, may God bless him and grant him peace. Likewise, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, had males and females among his children: al-Qasim, al-Tayyib, al-Tahir, Abdullah, Zaynab, Umm Kulthum, Ruqayyah, and Fatimah, all from Khadija, may God be pleased with her, and Ibrahim, who was from Mariyah. Coptic: And God divided creation from the time of Adam to our time, until the Hour comes, according to this limited estimation with His perfect wisdom and effective will, so that the offspring may remain, creation may continue, the promise may be fulfilled, the matter may be established, the world may be populated, and Heaven and Hell may each take what fills it and remain. So in the hadith: The Fire will not be filled until the tyrant places his foot in it, and it will say, ‘Enough, enough.’ As for Heaven, it will remain from it, and God will create another creation for it. Second: Ibn al-Arabi said: God Almighty, due to His all-encompassing power and immense strength, creates creation from nothing, and with His great kindness and perfect wisdom, He creates something from something, not out of need. He is Holy above needs and free from harm, as the Holy One said, “Peace.” So He created Adam from the earth and created Eve from Adam, and He created the creation from between them, from them, arranged according to intercourse, being from pregnancy, existing in the fetus by placement, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If the man’s semen precedes the woman’s semen, it is a male, and if the woman’s semen precedes the man’s semen, it is a female. And likewise in the Sahih also: If the man’s semen prevails over the woman’s semen, the child will resemble his paternal uncles, and if the woman’s semen prevails over the man’s semen, the child will resemble his maternal uncles. I said: This is the meaning of the hadith of Aisha, not its wording. Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr on her authority: “A woman said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Does a woman have to perform ghusl if she has a wet dream and sees water? He said: Yes. Aisha said to her: May your hands be covered with dust and she has sworn. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Leave her. Is there any resemblance except from before that? If her water prevails over the man’s water, the child will resemble his maternal uncles, and if the man’s water prevails over her water, he will resemble his paternal uncles.” Our scholars said: According to the implication of this hadith, the superiority requires resemblance. It came in the hadith of Thawban, also narrated by Muslim: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the Jew: The man’s water is white and the woman’s water is yellow. If they come together and the man’s water prevails over the woman’s water, a male will be born, God willing. If the woman’s water prevails over the man’s water, a female will be born, God willing…” The hadith. In this hadith, also, the superiority requires masculinity and femininity. According to the implication of the two hadiths, the resemblance between paternal uncles and males is required if the man’s water prevails, and likewise, if the woman’s water prevails, the resemblance is required if the woman’s water prevails.” The similarity between maternal uncles and females is because they are caused by one cause, and this is not the case, rather existence is different from that, because we find the similarity between maternal uncles and maleness and the similarity between paternal uncles and females, so it is necessary to interpret one of the two hadiths, and the one that is necessary to interpret is the one in the hadith of Thawban, and it is said that this superiority means that the water preceded the womb, and the reason for superiority is that since its meaning is victory from their saying So-and-so raced me, so I preceded him, meaning I defeated him, and from this is the saying of God Almighty: And we are not to be outdone (al-Ma’arij 70:41), meaning defeated, it is said of it: It rose, and this interpretation is supported by his saying in the hadith: If the man’s water precedes the woman’s water, they are male, and if the woman’s water precedes the man’s water, they are female. Judge Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi built on these hadiths and said: The two waters have four states: the first is that the man’s water comes out first, the second is that the woman’s water comes out first, the third is that the man’s water comes out first and is more, the fourth is that the woman’s water comes out first and is more, and the division is completed by the man’s water coming out first, then the woman’s water comes out after it and is more or vice versa, so if the man’s water comes out If the woman’s semen came out first and was more, the child was born male by virtue of precedence and the child resembled his paternal uncles by virtue of the majority. If the man’s semen came out first but when the woman’s semen came out was more, the child was male by virtue of the man’s semen being higher than the woman’s semen, the child was female by virtue of the woman’s semen coming out first and the child resembled his paternal uncles by virtue of the majority of the man’s semen. He said: By organizing these divisions, the speech is established and the contradiction is removed from the hadiths. So glory be to the Creator, the All-Knowing. Third: Our scholars said: The creation was continuous, male and female, until a hermaphrodite occurred in the first pre-Islamic period. The Arabs’ share of the inheritance and their long-lived man, Amir ibn al-Dharb, was brought to him, but he did not know what to say about him, and he postponed them from him. When night fell, he did not know where he was, and his bed was difficult for him, and he began to turn and toss, and thoughts came and went, until his maid did not know his condition and said: What is the matter with you? He said to her: I stayed up late for a matter I intended to do, and I did not know what to say about it. She said: What is it? He said to her: A man who has a penis and a vagina, what will be his condition with regard to inheritance? The slave girl said to him: He inherits it from where he urinates. So he paid her ransom and in the morning he presented it to them and they returned with it satisfied. Islam came on that basis and it was not revealed until the time of Ali may God be pleased with him so he ruled on it. The scholars of inheritance narrated on the authority of Al-Kalbi on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “On the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he was asked about a child born to him before and he mentioned where he inherits from? He said: From where he urinates.” It was narrated that a hermaphrodite from the Ansar was brought to him and he said: They inherit it from the first place he urinates. Muhammad ibn Al-Hanafiyyah narrated the same on the authority of Ali, and something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Al-Musayyab, Abu Hanifah, Abu Yusuf and Muhammad said the same. Al-Muzani narrated it on the authority of Al-Shafi’i. Some people said: There is no evidence in urine. If the urine comes out of both of them, Abu Yusuf said: He rules according to the majority. Abu Hanifah denied it and said: Do you rely on it? The followers of Al-Shafi’i did not make a rule for the large number. It was reported on the authority of Ali and Al-Hasan that they said: His ribs are counted, because a woman has one more rib than a man. What the scholars have said about this has already been mentioned in the verse of inheritance in Women with great emphasis, and praise be to God. Fourth: Judge Abu Bakr Ibn Al-Arabi said: “Some of the leaders of the common people denied the existence of the hermaphrodite, because God Almighty divided creation into male and female. We said: This is ignorance of the language, stupidity beyond the scope of eloquence, and a failure to know the breadth of power. As for the power of God Almighty, He is vast and all-knowing. As for the apparent meaning of the Qur’an, it does not deny the existence of the hermaphrodite, because God Almighty said: “To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He creates what He wills.” This is a general praise, so it is not permissible to make it specific, because power requires it. As for His statement: “He gives to whom He wills females, and He gives to whom He wills males. Or He pairs them [with] males and females, and He renders whom He wills barren,” this is a statement of what is common in existence, and He was silent about mentioning the rare because it falls under the generality of the first statement. Existence bears witness to it, and the sight belies its denier. A hermaphrodite who had no beard, had breasts, and had a slave girl was reading with us at the ribat of Abu Saeed on the martyred Imam from the lands of the Maghreb, and with us he read in the ribat of Abu Saeed on the martyred Imam from the lands of the Maghreb. He had no beard, had breasts, and had a slave girl. Your Lord knows best about him. Despite the length of my companionship, I was too shy to ask him, and today I wish I could confront him.” About his condition
42:51: There are two issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And it is not for a human being that God should speak to him except by revelation. The reason for that is that the Jews said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Why do you not speak to God and look at Him if you are a prophet, as Moses spoke to him and looked at him? We will not believe in you until you do that. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Moses did not look at him. Then the saying was revealed: And it is not for a human being that God should speak to him except by revelation. This was mentioned by al-Naqqash, al-Wahidi, and al-Tha’labi. Revelation. Mujahid said: It is a breath that is breathed into his heart, so it is inspiration. From this is his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: “The Holy Spirit breathed into my heart: ‘A soul will not die until it has completed its provision and its appointed time. So fear God and be fair in your request. Take what is permissible and leave what is forbidden.’” Or from behind a veil, as he spoke to Moses, Or He sends a messenger, like He sent Gabriel, peace be upon him. It was said: Except by revelation, a vision that he sees in his sleep. Muhammad ibn Zuhair said: Or from behind a veil. As He spoke to Moses, (or sends a messenger) Zuhair said: It is Gabriel, peace be upon him, and He reveals, by His permission, what He wills. This revelation from the messengers is a speech from them to the prophets, they hear it spoken and see it with their own eyes, and this was the state of Gabriel, peace be upon him, when he came down with the revelation to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abbas said: Gabriel, peace be upon him, came down to every prophet, and none of them saw him except Muhammad, Jesus, Moses, and Zechariah, peace be upon them. As for others, he was alive and inspired in a dream. And it was said: (except a revelation) by sending Gabriel (or from behind a veil) as He spoke to Moses, (or sends a messenger) to all people. Al-Zuhri, Shaybah, and Nafi’ read (or sends a messenger and reveals), raising both verbs, the rest in the accusative, so the raising is for resumption, meaning that He sends. And it was said (sends) in the nominative case in the place of the state, and the meaning is except inspiring or sending, and whoever places the accusative case attached it to the place of the revelation, because its meaning is that it is not for a human being that God should speak to him except that He inspires or sends. It is permissible for the accusative case to be based on the deletion of the preposition from the implied an, and for it to be in the position of a state, the estimation being or that he sends a messenger, and it is not permissible for or sends to be connected in the accusative case to that he speaks to him, because the meaning is corrupted, because it becomes: it is not for a human being to send him or for a messenger to be sent to him, and he has sent messengers from among the humans and sent to them. Second: This verse was used as evidence by those who saw that someone who swore not to speak to a man and then sent a messenger to him had broken his oath, because the sender was named in it as speaking to the recipient, unless the one who swore intended to address him directly. Ibn al-Mundhir said: They differed regarding a man who swore not to speak to someone and then wrote him a letter or sent him a messenger. Al-Thawri said: The messenger is not speaking. Al-Shafi’i said: It is not clear that he broke his oath. Al-Nakha’i said: The ruling regarding the letter is that he broke his oath. Malik said: He broke his oath regarding the letter and the messenger. He said once: The messenger is easier than the letter. Abu Ubaid said: Speech is other than writing and gestures. Abu Thawr said: He does not break his oath regarding the letter. Ibn al-Mundhir said: He does not break his oath regarding the letter and the messenger. I said: This is the opinion of Malik. Abu Omar said: Whoever swears not to speak to a man and then greets him intentionally or absentmindedly, or greets a group of people he is among, has broken his oath in all of that according to Malik.
