But if he sends a messenger to him or greets him during prayer, he has not broken his oath. I said: He breaks his oath regarding the Messenger unless he intends to speak to him directly, according to the verse. This is the opinion of Malik and Ibn al-Majishun. This meaning has been fully explained by our scholars at the beginning of Surah Maryam, and praise be to God.
42:52: It contains four issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And thus We have revealed to you, meaning, as We revealed to the prophets before you, We have revealed to you a spirit, meaning prophecy. Ibn Abbas said: Al-Hasan and Qatadah: From us. Al-Suddi: Revelation, Al-Kalbi: A book, Al-Rabi’: He is Gabriel, Ad-Dahhak: He is the Qur’an, and this is the saying of Malik ibn Dinar. He called it a spirit because it gives life from the death of ignorance, and He made it from His command, meaning He sent it down as He willed to whomever He willed, from the miraculous arrangement and amazing composition. It is possible to interpret His saying: And they ask you about the spirit (Al-Isra’ 17:85), to refer to the Qur’an as well, Say, ‘The spirit is from the command of my Lord’ (Al-Isra’ 17:85), meaning, they ask you from where you got this Qur’an. Say, “It is from the command of God. He sent it down to me as a miracle.” Al-Qushayri mentioned it. Malik ibn Dinar used to say: O people of the Qur’an, what has the Qur’an planted in your hearts? The Qur’an is the spring of the hearts, just as rain is the spring of the earth. The second: The Almighty’s saying: You did not know what the Book was, nor what faith was. That is, you did not know the path to faith. The apparent meaning of this indicates that he was not characterized by faith before the revelation. Al-Qushayri said: “It is one of the miracles of the mind. What most people have come to is that God did not send a prophet except that he believed in Him before the mission, and there is arbitrariness in it, unless it is proven by a definite revelation.” Judge Abu al-Fadl Iyad said: “As for their infallibility from this aspect before prophethood, people have a difference of opinion about it. The correct view is that they were infallible before prophethood from ignorance of God and His attributes and doubt about any of that. The reports and traces from the prophets have agreed to exonerate them from this deficiency, since they were born, and they were raised on monotheism and faith, indeed on the radiance of the lights of knowledge and the breaths of the kindness of happiness. Whoever studies their biographies from their childhood to their mission will realize this, as he knows from the state of Moses, Jesus, John, Solomon, and others, peace be upon them. God Almighty said: “And We gave him judgment while still a boy” (Maryam 19:12). He said: Commentators: Yahya was given knowledge of the Book of God when he was a child. Muammar said: He was two or three years old, and the boys said to him: Why don’t you play? He said: Was I created to play? It was said in His statement: Confirming a word from God (Al Imran 3:39), that Yahya believed in Jesus when he was three years old, so he testified to him that he was the word of God and His spirit. It was also said that he believed in him while he was in his mother’s womb, so Yahya’s mother used to say to Maryam 19:I find what is in my womb prostrating to what is in your womb as a greeting to it. And God stated the words of Jesus to his mother when she gave birth to him in His statement: Do not grieve (Maryam 19:24), according to the reading of those who read from beneath her and according to the statement of those who said that the caller was Jesus, and He stated his words in his cradle, so he said: “Indeed, I am the servant of God. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet” (Maryam 19:30). And He said: So We made Solomon understand it, and to each of them We gave judgment and knowledge (Al Anbiya: 79). And it was mentioned of the judgment of Solomon while he was a boy playing in the story of the stoned woman and in the story of the boy what his father David followed. Al Tabari narrated that his age when he was given the kingdom was twelve years, and likewise the story of Moses. And the commentators said about the words of God Almighty: And We had already given Abraham his soundness of mind before (Al-Anbiya’: 51), meaning We guided him when he was young, as Mujahid and others said. Ibn Ata’ said: He chose him before his creation began. Some of them said: When Abraham was born, God sent an angel to him, ordering him on behalf of God Almighty to make him know him in his heart and mention him with his tongue, so he said: I have done it, and he did not say I will do it, so that is his soundness of mind. And it was said: And it was said: That Abraham was thrown into the fire and his trial was when he was sixteen years old, and that Isaac was tested by slaughter when he was seven years old, and that Abraham’s reasoning with the planet, moon, and sun was when he was fifteen years old. And it was said: It was revealed to Joseph when he was a boy when his brothers were about to throw him into the well, with the words of God Almighty: “And We inspired him: You will surely inform them of this affair of theirs” (Yusuf 12:15), and other stories of theirs. And the people of the biography narrated that Amina bint Wahb informed that our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And peace be upon him, he was born when he was born with his hands stretched out to the ground and his head raised to the sky. And he said in his hadith, peace be upon him: When I grew up, I hated idols and I hated poetry, and I did not care about anything that the Jahiliyyah used to do except twice, and God protected me from them, and then I did not return to them. Then the matter was established for them, and the breaths of God Almighty followed one after the other upon them, and the lights of knowledge shone in their hearts until they reached the goal and attained, through God Almighty’s choosing them for prophethood, the attainment of the noble qualities, the ultimate without practice or exercise. God Almighty said: And when he reached his full strength and was well-established, We gave him wisdom and knowledge (al-Qasas 28:14). Al-Qadi said: And none of the people of report transmitted that anyone was prophesied and chosen who was known for disbelief and polytheism before that, and the basis for this matter is transmission. And some of them provided evidence that hearts are repelled from someone whose path was like this. Al-Qadi said: And I say that the Quraysh accused our Prophet, peace be upon him, of everything they fabricated, and the disbelievers of the nations reproached their prophets with everything they could and invented, from what God Almighty stated or what the narrators transmitted to us, and we did not find in any of that To reproach one of them for rejecting their gods and to rebuke him for abandoning what he had agreed upon with them. If this had been the case, they would have been the first to do so, and would have protested against him regarding his deity. And their rebuke of what was far-fetched before would have been more terrible and more conclusive in argument than their rebuke of him for forbidding them to abandon their gods and what their fathers had worshipped before. So in their insistence on turning away from it is evidence that they did not find a way to it, because if it had been, it would have been transmitted and they would not have remained silent about it, just as they did not remain silent about changing the direction of prayer and said: What has turned them away from their direction of prayer which they used to face? (al-Baqarah 2:142), as God related about them. Third: The scholars spoke about our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, whether he was a follower of a religion before the revelation or not. Some of them forbade that absolutely and rejected it rationally. They said: Because it is far-fetched that he would be followed by someone who is known to be a follower. They based this on good and bad. Another group said to stop regarding his matter, peace be upon him, and not to definitively rule on him in that, since the two aspects of them were not permitted by reason nor was the path of transmission clear to them in either of them. This is the school of Abu al-Ma’ali. A third group said: He was a follower of a law before him and acted upon it. Then these differed in the specification. A group went to the fact that he was on the religion of Jesus, for it abrogates all religions and sects before it, so it is not permissible for the Prophet to be on an abrogated religion. A group went to the fact that he was on the religion of Abraham because he is from his descendants and he is the father of the prophets. A group went to the fact that he was on the religion of Moses because it is the oldest religion. The Mu’tazila went to the fact that he must have been on a religion, but the specific religion is not known to us. He invalidated all of these statements. Our Imams, as they are contradictory statements and do not contain conclusive evidence, even though reason allows all of that, and what is decisive is that he, peace be upon him, was not related to one of the prophets in a way that would require him to be one of his nation and addressed with all of his law, rather his law is independent in itself, initiated by God, the Ruler, the Majestic and Almighty, and that he, peace be upon him, was a believer in God, the Majestic and Almighty, and did not prostrate to an idol, nor did he associate partners with God, nor did he commit adultery, nor did he drink alcohol, nor did he attend a night gathering, nor did he attend the rain oath, nor the oath of the perfumed ones, rather God exalted him and preserved him from that. If it is said: “Uthman bin Abi Shaybah narrated to us on the authority of Jabir: The Prophet, peace be upon him, used to witness the battles of the polytheists, and he heard two angels behind him, one of them saying to his companion: Go until you stand behind him, so the other said: How can I stand behind him when he has promised to touch the idols and he has not witnessed them yet?” “The answer is that this is a hadith that Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal strongly rejected and said: It is fabricated or similar to fabrication. Al-Daraqutni said: Uthman made a mistake in its chain of transmission and the hadith as a whole is fabricated and its chain of transmission is not agreed upon, so no attention should be paid to it. What is known about the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is that he disagrees with the people of knowledge, such as his saying: “I hate idols” and his saying in the story of Buhayra when he made the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, swear by al-Lat and al-Uzza when he met him in Syria on his journey with his uncle Abu Talib when he was a boy, and he saw in him the signs of prophethood and informed him of that. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Do not ask me about them, for by God I have never hated anything as much as I hate them. Buhayra said to him: By God, except that you tell me what I ask you about. He said: Ask whatever you want.” Likewise, what is known from his life, peace be upon him, and God’s guidance for him is that before his prophethood he used to differ with the polytheists in their standing at Muzdalifah during the Hajj, and he used to stand at Arafat, because it was the place where Abraham, peace be upon him, stood. If it is said: God Almighty said: “Say: Rather, the religion of Abraham” ( [al-Baqarah 2:135), and He said: To follow the religion of Abraham (al-Nahl 16:123), and He said: He has ordained for you a religion (al-Shura 42:13), and this requires that he be worshipping according to a religion. So the answer is that this is in what the religions do not differ in, such as monotheism and establishing the religion, as was explained in more than one place and in this surah when He said: He has ordained for you a religion and praise be to God. Fourth: If this is established, then know that scholars differed in the interpretation of the Almighty’s statement: You did not know what the Book was, nor what faith was. A group said: The meaning of faith in this verse is the laws of faith and its features, as mentioned by al-Tha’labi. It was said: The details of this law, meaning you were unaware of these details. It is permissible to use the word faith for the details of the law, as mentioned by al-Qushayri. It was said: You did not know before the revelation to recite the Qur’an, nor how to call people to faith, and something similar was said by Abu al-A’liyya. Bakr al-Qadi said: Nor faith, which is the obligatory duties and rulings. He said: Before that, he believed in His Oneness, then the obligatory duties were revealed, which he did not know before, so he increased his faith with the obligation. These four statements are close. Ibn Khuzaymah said: What is meant by faith is prayer, because the Almighty said: And God would not let your faith go to waste (al-Baqarah 2:143), meaning your prayers towards the Holy House, so the word is general and what is meant is specific. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fudayl said: Meaning you did not know what the Book was, nor what the people of faith were, and this is from the category of deleting the complement, meaning who… Do you believe? Abu Talib or Al-Abbas or others. It was said: You did not know anything while you were in the cradle and before reaching puberty. Al-Mawardi narrated something similar on the authority of Ali bin Isa who said: You would not have known what the Book was had it not been for the message, nor faith had it not been for reaching puberty. It was said: You would not have known what the Book was had it not been for Our favor upon you, nor faith had it not been for Our guidance to you. This is possible. There are two aspects to this belief: One of them is that it is belief in God, and he knows this after reaching puberty and before his prophethood. The second is that it is the religion of Islam, and he does not know it except after the prophethood. I said: The correct view is that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, was a believer in God Almighty from the time he grew up until he reached puberty, as mentioned above. It was said: (You did not know what the Book was, nor what faith was), meaning you were from an illiterate people who did not know the Book or faith, until you had taken what you brought them from someone who knew that among them. It is like the words of God Almighty: “And you did not recite before it any Book, nor did you inscribe it with your right hand. Then the falsifiers would have had doubts” (al-Ankabut 29:48). Its meaning was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. But We made it Ibn Abbas and Al-Dahhak said: meaning faith. Al-Suddi said: the Qur’an. It was also said: the revelation, meaning We made this revelation a light by which We guide whom We will meaning whom We choose for prophethood, like the words of God Almighty: He singles out for His mercy whom He wills (Al Imran 3:74). The pronoun is singular because the verb in the multiplicity of its names is like the verb in one noun. Do you not see that you say: Your coming forward and turning away pleases me, so you singularize it, while they are two. And indeed, you guide That is, you call and guide to a straight path, a straight religion in which there is no crookedness. Ali said: to a straight book. Asim Al-Jahdary and Hawshab read: (And indeed you guide) without the name of the agent, that is, you are called. The rest read (To guide) as the name of the agent. In Abu’s reading: (And indeed you call), Al-Nahhas said: This is not read as such, because it is contrary to the majority. Rather, what is like it is taken to be from its speaker by way of explanation, as he said: (And indeed you guide) meaning you call. Muammar narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding the words of God Almighty: {And indeed you guide to a straight path}, he said: And for every people there is a guide (al-Ra’d 13:7). The Almighty said: The Day the Spirit and the angels will stand in rows (Day) is an adverbial phrase, meaning the Day they will not have any power to speak to Him. The Day the Spirit will stand. There are eight different opinions about the Spirit: The first - that it is an angel from the angels. Ibn Abbas said: God did not create anything after the Throne greater than it, so when it is the Day of Resurrection, it will stand alone in a row, and all the angels will stand in a row, so the greatness of its creation will be like their rows. A similar report was narrated by Ibn Masoud, who said: The Spirit is an angel greater than the seven heavens, the seven earths, and the mountains. It is opposite the fourth heaven, glorifying God twelve thousand times every day, and God creates an angel from each glorification. So on the Day of Resurrection, it will come alone in a row, and the rest of the angels will stand in a row. The second - that it is Gabriel, peace be upon him. This was said by Al-Sha'bi, Al-Dahhak, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr. On the authority of Ibn Abbas: “To the right of the Throne is a river of light, like the seven heavens, the seven earths, and the seven seas. Gabriel enters every day and from every drop that falls from his feathers, God creates seventy thousand angels. Seventy thousand of them enter the Frequented House every day, and seventy thousand enter the Kaaba and do not return to them until the Day of Resurrection.” Wahb said: “Gabriel, peace be upon him, is standing before God, the Most High, trembling. God creates from every trembling one hundred thousand angels. So the angels are in rows before God, the Most High, with their heads bowed. When God permits them to speak, they say, ‘There is no god but You.’ This is what God, the Most High, says: ‘The Day the Spirit and the angels will stand in rows, they will not speak except for one whom the Most Merciful permits.’” In speech, and he will say what is right, meaning saying, There is no god but You. Third: Ibn Abbas narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: (The spirit in this verse is an army from among the soldiers of God Almighty, they are not angels, they have heads, hands and feet, they eat food). Then he recited: The Day the Spirit and the angels will stand in rows, for these are an army, and those are an army, and this is the opinion of Abu Salih and Mujahid. Based on this, they are created in the image of the sons of Adam, like people, but they are not people. Fourth: They are the noblest of the angels, said by Muqatil ibn Hayyan. Fifth: They are guardians over the angels, said by Ibn Abi Nujayj. Sixth: They are the sons of Adam, said by al-Hasan and Qatadah. So the meaning is those with a spirit. Al-Awfi and al-Qurazi said: This is something that Ibn Abbas concealed. He said: The spirit is a creation from among the creation of God in the image of the sons of Adam, and no angel descends from the heaven except that he has with him one of the spirit. Seventh: The spirits of the sons of Adam will stand in rows, so the angels will stand in rows, and that will be between the two blasts, before they are returned to the bodies, said by Atiyyah. Eighth - It is the Qur’an, said Zaid bin Aslam, and he recited: (And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command). And (Safa): a verbal noun meaning they stand in rows. The verbal noun indicates the singular and the plural, like justice and fasting. The day of Eid is called: the day of the rows. And he said in another place: (And your Lord will come with the angels, rank upon rank) (al-Fajr 89:22). This indicates the rows, this is when the presentation and the judgment will take place. Al-Qatabi and others said its meaning. And it was said: The spirit stands in a row, and the angels in a row, so they are two rows. And it was said: Everyone stands in a single row. They do not speak means they do not intercede except for he whom the Most Gracious has given permission in intercession. And he said ‘right’ meaning truly, said Ad-Dahhak and Mujahid. Abu Salih said: There is no god but God. Ad-Dahhak narrated from Ibn Abbas who said: They intercede for he who says there is no god but God. The root of right is correctness in speech and action, and it is from asaba meaning to hit as an answer from ajaba meaning to answer It was said: (They do not speak) meaning the angels and the spirit who stood in rows, they do not speak out of awe and reverence (except for he whom the Most Gracious has given permission) in intercession and they have spoken what is right, and they unify God Almighty and glorify Him. Al-Hasan said: The spirit will say on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:No one will enter Paradise except through mercy, and no one will enter Hell except through deeds. This is the meaning of the Almighty’s saying: {and he said what is right}.
42:53: The path of God is a substitute for the first, a substitute for a definite noun for an indefinite noun. Ali said: It is the Qur’an, and it was said: Islam. Al-Nawwas bin Sam’an narrated it on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, as kings, servants, and creation. To God do all matters return. A threat of resurrection and recompense. Sahl bin Abi al-Ja’d said: A copy of the Qur’an was burned, and nothing remained except His saying: To God do all matters return. And a copy of the Qur’an was drowned, and all of it was erased except His saying: To God do all matters return. And praise be to God alone.
43:1: It is Meccan by consensus. Muqatil said: Except for His saying: And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers, which is eighty-nine verses. The Almighty says: Ha Meem. This has been discussed previously, and it has been said that Ha Meem is an oath.
43:2: The Almighty’s saying: And the clear Book (And the clear Book) is a second oath, and God can swear by whatever He wills, and the answer is (Indeed, We made it) Ibn al-Anbari said: Whoever makes the answer to (And the Book) (Ha Meem) as you say God has revealed, then by God it is necessary to stop at (The clear Book), and whoever makes the answer to the oath (Indeed, We made it) does not stop at (The clear Book).
43:3: God Almighty says: Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur’an that you might understand. The meaning of We made it is that We named it and described it, and therefore it is transitive with two objects, like the saying of God Almighty: God has not made any lake (al-Ma’idah 5:103). Al-Suddi said: meaning We sent it down as a Qur’an. Mujahid said: We said it. Al-Zajjaj and Sufyan al-Thawri said: We explained it. In Arabic means We sent it down in the language of the Arabs, because every prophet sent down his book in the language of his people. Sufyan al-Thawri and others said this. Muqatil said this because the language of the people of the heavens is Arabic. It was said that what is meant by the book is all the books sent down to the prophets, because the book is a generic noun, so it is as if he swore by all the books that were sent down that he made the Qur’an in Arabic. The metaphor in his saying: We made it refers back to the Qur’an even though it is not mentioned in this surah, like the saying of God Almighty: Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree [al-Qadr 97:Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 200]. That you may understand means that you may understand its rulings and meanings. According to this statement, it is specific to the Arabs and not the non-Arabs. Ibn ‘Isa said this. Ibn Zayd said: The meaning is that you may reflect. Based on this, it is a general address to Arabs and non-Arabs. The book is described as clear because God has made clear His rulings and obligations in it, as mentioned previously in more than one place.
43:4: The Almighty’s saying: And indeed, it is in the Mother of the Book meaning the Qur’an in the Preserved Tablet with Us “high and wise” meaning exalted and perfected, in which there is no difference or contradiction. God the Almighty said: Indeed, it is a noble Qur’an * in a protected book (al-Waqi’ah 56:77-78), and He the Almighty said: Rather, it is a glorious Qur’an * in a Preserved Tablet (al-Buruj 85:21-22). Ibn Jurayj said: What is meant by the Almighty’s saying: (And indeed, it) meaning the deeds of creation of faith and disbelief, obedience and disobedience (high) means exalted from being reached or changed (wise) meaning preserved from deficiency or change. Ibn Abbas said: The first thing that God created was the pen, and He commanded it to write what He wanted to create, so the book is with it. Then he recited: And indeed, it is in the Mother of the Book with Us, high and wise. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i broke the hamzah in (the Mother of the Book), while the rest closed it, and this has been mentioned previously.
43:5: The Almighty’s saying: Should We turn away from you the Reminder utterly? meaning the Qur’an, according to Ad-Dahhak and others. It was said that what is meant by the Reminder is the punishment, i.e., should We turn away the punishment from you and not punish you for your extravagance and disbelief? This was said by Mujahid, Abu Salih, and As-Suddi. Al-Awfi narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Abbas said: The meaning is, Did you think that We would turn away the punishment from you while you did not do what you were commanded to do? And also from him that the meaning is, Do you deny the Qur’an and not be punished? As-Suddi also said: The meaning is, Should We leave you in vain and neither command you nor forbid you? Qatadah said: The meaning is, Should We destroy you and neither command you nor forbid you? And also from him: Should We withhold from sending down the Qur’an? It was lifted when the first of this nation rejected it and they were destroyed, but God returned it and repeated it to them with His mercy. Al-Kisa’i said: Should We turn away from you the Reminder utterly, so that you are not admonished nor commanded? And it was said that the Reminder is remembering, so it is as if he said: Should We leave…” Reminding you because you were a people who were extravagant, in the reading of those who opened it, and those who broke it made it for the condition and what preceded it an answer to it, because it did not work in the wording, and its equivalent is: And give up what remains of interest if you are believers (al-Baqarah 2:278). It was said: The answer is omitted and indicated by what came before, as you say: You are unjust if you did, and the meaning of the break according to Al-Zajjaj is the state, because in the speech there is a meaning of estimation and rebuke, and the meaning of to forgive is turning away, it is said: I forgave someone if I turned away from his sin, and you turned away from him turning away from him if you turned away from him and left him, and the origin of it is the side of the neck, it is said: I turned away from him meaning I made him the side of my neck, the poet said: Forgiving, but you will only be met with stinginess. Whoever gets bored of that connection will get bored of it. The word safhan is in the accusative case as a verbal noun because the meaning of shall we turn away is shall we forgive? It has also been said that the meaning is shall we turn away from you the remembrance while turning away, just as it is said: So-and-so came walking. The meaning of extravagant is polytheists. Abu Ubaidah chose the opening in an, which is the reading of Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Asim, and Ibn Amir. He said: Because God Almighty rebuked them for what they had done, and He knew of their actions before that.
43:6: The Almighty says: And how many prophets We sent among the former peoples. “How many” here is a declarative and what is meant by it is abundance. The meaning is how many prophets We sent, as He said: How many gardens and springs did they leave behind? (al-Dukhan 44:25), meaning how many did they leave behind.
43:7: And no prophet came to them meaning no prophet came to them but they used to mock him as your people mock you, consoling and comforting his prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
43:8: So We destroyed those stronger than them in strike meaning a people stronger than them in power. The metaphor in of them refers to the polytheists addressed in His statement: Shall We then turn away from you the Reminder? So He metaphorically referred to them after He addressed them. Stronger is in the accusative case as a state, and it was said that it is the object, meaning that We destroyed those stronger than these polytheists in their bodies and followers. And the example of the former peoples has passed meaning their punishment, according to Qatada. It was said: the example of the former peoples, so He informed them that they were destroyed for their disbelief, as narrated by al-Naqqash and al-Mahdawi. The metaphor is the description and the report.
43:9: God Almighty said: And if you ask them meaning the polytheists who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely say, “The Exalted in Might, the Knowing created them. So they acknowledged His creation and bringing into existence, then they worshipped others besides Him out of ignorance on their part, and this has been mentioned in more than one place.
43:10: The Almighty says: Who has made the earth a cradle for you. He described Himself, glory be to Him, with perfect power. This is the beginning of His informing us about Himself. If this was informing us about what the infidels said, He would have said, Who has made the earth a cradle for us, a bed and a carpet. This has already been mentioned. The Kufians read a cradle. "And He has made for you therein paths," meaning livelihoods. It was also said, roads, for you to take from them to wherever you want. "That you may be guided." So you may infer His power from His abilities. It was also said, "That you may be guided" in your travels. This was said by Ibn Isa. It was also said, "That you may know the favor of God upon you," this was said by Saeed bin Jubayr. It was also said, "That you may be guided to your livelihoods."
43:11: The Almighty said: And He who sent down from the sky water in due measure. Ibn Abbas said: That is, it was not sent down, according to Noah’s statement, without measure, until He drowned them. Rather, it is in due measure, neither a flood that would drown them nor one that would fall short of the need, so that it would be a livelihood for you and your livestock. Then We resurrected means We revived, with it meaning with water, a dead land meaning barren of vegetation. Thus you will emerge meaning from your graves, because He who is able to do this is able to do that. It has already been mentioned in Al-A’raf with a good pronunciation. Yahya ibn Waththab, Al-A’mash, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Ibn Dhakwan, on the authority of Ibn Amir, read they emerge with a fatha on the ba’ and a damma on the ra’, the rest with the passive verb.
43:12: First: The Almighty said: And He who created pairs meaning, God is the One who created pairs. Saeed bin Jubair said: meaning all kinds. Al-Hasan said: winter and summer, night and day, the heavens and the earth, the sun and the moon, Paradise and Hell. It was said: the pairs of animals, male and female, said Ibn Isa. It was also said: He meant the pairs of plants, as God Almighty said: And We caused to grow therein of every beautiful pair (Qaf: 7), and of every noble pair (Ash-Shu'ara': 7). It was also said: what a person experiences of good and evil, faith and disbelief, benefit and harm, poverty and wealth, health and sickness. I said: This statement includes all statements and brings them together in its generality: And He has made for you of the ships the ships, and the livestock the camels, that which you ride on the land and sea.
43:13: So that you may mount on their backs. He mentioned the metaphor because he referred it back to what is in His statement: (that which you ride), as Abu Ubaid said. Al-Farra’ said: He added the backs to one because what is meant by it is the genus, so the one became in the sense of the plural like the army and the soldiers, and for that reason he mentioned, and the backs are plural, meaning on the backs of this genus. Second: Saeed bin Jubair said: The livestock here are camels and cows. Abu Muadh said: The camels alone, and this is correct, based on the saying of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: “While a man was riding a cow, it said to him: ‘Are you created for this? You were only created for cultivation.’ The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘I believe in that, and so do Abu Bakr and Umar.’” They were not among the people, and this has already been fully explained at the beginning of Surat An-Nahl, and praise be to God. Third: The Almighty’s statement: So that you may mount on their backs means camels specifically, based on what we have mentioned, and because arks are ridden on their bellies. However, He mentioned both of them at the beginning of the verse and connected the end of it to one of them. It is possible that He made its exterior its interior, because the water covered it and concealed it, and its interior apparent, because it was revealed to those who were seen and appeared to those who saw. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: Then remember the favor of your Lord when you are mounted on it meaning you ride. The mention of the favor is the praise of God for making it subservient to us on land and sea. And say, ‘Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us’ meaning He made this mount subservient to us. In the reading of Ali ibn Abi Talib: Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us. “And we could not have subdued it” meaning able to bear it, according to the saying of Ibn Abbas and Al-Kalbi. Al-Akhfash and Abu Ubaidah said: Muqrinin means controlling it. It was said: similar in strength and power, from their saying, he is the horn of so-and-so if he is like him in strength. It is said: so-and-so is a horn for so-and-so, meaning he is controlling him. I qirnat such-and-such means I made it subservient and qirna lahu means he was able to do it and was strong over it, as if it became a horn for him. God Almighty said: And we could not have subdued it meaning able to bear it. Qatrib recited the saying of Amr ibn Ma’dikarib: The tribes knew what was said to us in the calamities of our two horns Another said: You have ridden my hardships with evil and injustice, but you are not able to face difficulties. Al-Muqrin is also: the one who is overcome by his farm, he has camels or sheep and has no helper with them, or he waters his camels and has no one to drive them away. Ibn Al-Sikkit said: There are two opinions about its origin: the first is that it is taken from the word iqran, it is said: aqran iqran if he was able, and aqrant ka-da-da if you made it able and controlled it, as if he put it in a qarn, which is a rope, so he tied it to it and tightened it. The second is that it is taken from the word muqarana, which is to link some of it to others in walking, it is said: qarant ka-da-da with ka-da if you tied it to it and made it its partner. Fifth, God Almighty taught us what to say when we ride beasts, and we know in another verse on the tongue of Noah, peace be upon him, what to say when we ride ships, which is the Almighty’s saying: “And he said, ‘Embark therein, in the name of God is its course and its anchorage. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.’” (Hud 11:41) How many a rider of an animal has stumbled, sunk, been thrust into, or fallen from its back and perished? How many a rider of a ship has been wrecked and drowned? Since riding is directly a forbidden matter and connected to causes of destruction, He commanded that one should not forget his day when connected to it, and that he will inevitably perish and will return to God Almighty, not escaping His judgment. He should not neglect to mention that in his heart and tongue until he is prepared to meet God by reforming himself, and being careful that his riding be one of the causes of his death in God’s knowledge while he is unaware of it. Even Sulayman ibn Yasar said that some people were on a journey and when they rode they would say, Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have subdued it. And among them was a man on his she-camel, which was razim, meaning it does not move due to emaciation. Razim is one of the camels that is fixed on the ground and does not get up from emaciation, or the she-camel had become razim, it got up from exhaustion and emaciation but did not move, so it is razim. Al-Jawhari said in As-Sahah. He said: As for me, I am this one, he said: So I jumped on it and broke its neck. It was narrated that a Bedouin rode his ra’ud and said: I am ra’ud, so the ra’ud drove it until it threw it down and broke its neck. The first was mentioned by Al-Mawardi and the second by Ibn Al-Arabi.
43:14: He said: It is not appropriate for a servant to abandon saying this, and it is not obligatory to mention it with the tongue. He should say whenever he rides, especially while traveling, if he remembers: ((Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have subdued it. And indeed, to our Lord we will return)) O God, You are the companion in travel, the successor over family and wealth. O God, I seek refuge in You from the hardships of travel, the gloom of returning, injustice after rest, and a bad sight in family and wealth. He means by (injustice after rest) the scattering of a man’s affairs after they have been gathered. Amr ibn Dinar said: I rode with Abu Ja`far to his land near a wall called Mudrikah, and he rode on a difficult camel, so I said to him: Abu Ja`far! Are you not afraid that it will throw you down? He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: On the hump of every camel is a devil. When you ride it, mention the name of God as He commanded you, then treat it with kindness, for only God bears the burden. And Ali said: Ibn Rabia: I witnessed Ali ibn Abi Talib riding an animal one day. When he put his foot in the stirrup, he said: In the name of God. When he was firmly on the animal, he said: Praise be to God. Then he said: Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have subdued it. And indeed, to our Lord we will return. Then he said: Praise be to God, and God is the Greatest three times. O God, there is no god but You. I have wronged myself, so forgive me, for no one forgives sins except You. Then he laughed, so I said to him: What makes you laugh? He said: I saw the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) do as I did and say as you said. Then he laughed, so I said to him: What makes you laugh, O Messenger of God? He said: The servant, or he said: It is strange for a servant to say: O God, there is no god but You, I have wronged myself, so forgive me, for no one forgives sins except You, knowing that no one forgives sins other than You. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi included it in his Musnad, and Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Khuwayzmandad included it in his Ahkam. Al-Tha’labi mentioned something similar in an abbreviated form on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, and his wording on his authority is: “When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would place his foot in the stirrup, he would say: In the name of God. When he was level, he would say: Praise be to God in every circumstance. Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have subdued it. And indeed, to our Lord we will return. And when you dismount from the ships and the livestock, say: O God, send us down at a blessed landing place, and You are the best of those who provide landing places.” Abu Nujayh narrated on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Whoever rides and does not say: Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have subdued it, Satan will say to him: Come, let us ride on horses or in some of the boats. So they ride, carrying with them vessels of wine and wine, and they do not stop drawing water until their clothes are full while they are on the backs of the animals.” Or in the bellies of ships while they sail with them, they remember nothing but Satan, and they obey nothing but his commands. Al-Zamakhshari said: It has reached me that some of the sultans rode while drinking wine from one country to another, between them a month’s journey, and he did not recover until the house was at peace, so he did not feel his journey nor did he sense it. How much difference is there between the actions of those riders and what God commanded regarding him in this verse?!
43:15: The Almighty said: And they have assigned to Him from among His servants a portion meaning equal, according to Qatada, meaning from those worshipped other than God Almighty. Al-Zajjaj and Al-Mubarrad: The portion here is the daughters. The believers were amazed at their ignorance when they acknowledged that the Creator of the heavens and the earth is God, then they assigned to Him a partner or a son, and they did not know that the One who has the power to create the heavens and the earth does not need anything to support him or to take comfort in him, because this is from the attributes of deficiency. Al-Mawardi said: The portion among the Arabs is the daughters. It is said: The woman has sufficed if she has given birth to daughters. The poet said: If a free woman is sufficient one day, it is no wonder that a free woman may be sufficient sometimes. Al-Zamakhshari: Among the innovations of interpretations is the interpretation of the part as females, and the claim that the part in the Arabic language is a name for females, and this is nothing but a lie against the Arabs and a newly invented and changed thing, and that did not convince them until they derived from it: the woman sufficed, then they made a house, and a house: If a free woman is satisfied one day, it is no wonder Her husband is from the daughters of the Aws tribe. Rather, His statement, And they have assigned to Him a portion of His servants is connected to His statement, And if you ask them, meaning, if you ask them about the Creator of the heavens and the earth, they will acknowledge Him. And they have assigned to Him, along with that acknowledgment, a portion of His servants, so they described Him with the attributes of created beings. The meaning of a portion of His servants is that they said the angels are the daughters of God, so they made them a portion of Him and a part of Him, just as a child is a part of his father and a part of him. A portion is read with two dammahs. Indeed, man meaning the disbeliever, is clearly ungrateful. Al-Hasan said: After the calamities and forgets the blessings, clear is the one who shows disbelief.
43:16: The Almighty says: Or has He taken from what He creates daughters? The mim is a connective, meaning He has taken from what He creates daughters, as you claimed that the angels are daughters of God. So the wording is a question but its meaning is confirmation. And He has chosen you for sons means He has singled you out for sons. It is said: I have chosen him with such-and-such, meaning I have favored him with it. I have chosen him with love, I mean I have made him sincere with him. I have made him sincere with him, I say: We have made him sincere with God. It is amazing that they attribute to God the choice of daughters while they have chosen sons for themselves, and He is too sacred to have a son. If an ignorant person imagined that He had taken a son for Himself, why did He not attribute both genders to Him? And why did these people make for themselves the most honorable of the two genders and for Him the lesser? This is like the Almighty's saying: Is it for you the male and for Him the female? That is, indeed, an unfair division. (An-Nahm: 21-22)
43:17: The Almighty said: And when one of them is given the good report of that which is presented to the Most Merciful as an example meaning that a daughter has been born to him, his face darkens meaning his face becomes blackened. It was said that the example he made is false, and it was said: because of the good report of a female, the proof for which is in Surat al-Nahl 16:And when one of them is given the good report of a female (al-Nahl 16:58). It is their condition that if one of them is told that a female has been born to him, he becomes distressed and his face turns red with rage and grief, and he is filled with distress. It was narrated from some of the Arabs that his wife gave birth to a female, so he deserted the house in which the woman was, and she said: Why doesn't Abu Hamza come to us? He stays in the house next to us. Angry that we do not give birth to sons, but rather take what we are given It was read as (blackened, blackened) and according to the reading of the group, his face is the subject of (shadow) and (blackened) is the predicate of (shadow), and it is permissible for (shadow) to have a pronoun referring back to someone and it is its subject, and (his face) is a substitute for the pronoun, and (blackened) is the predicate of (shadow), and it is permissible for (his face) to be raised as the subject, and (blackened) to be raised as its predicate, and in (shadow) it is its subject and the sentence is its predicate, and he is suppressing grief meaning sad, said Qatadah, and it was said distressed, said Ikrimah, and it was said silent, said Ibn Abi Hatim, and that is due to the corruption of his example and the invalidity of his argument, and whoever allows the angels to be daughters of God has made the angels a likeness of God, because the child is of the same kind as the father and resembles him, and whoever blackens his face with what is attributed to him that does not please him, is more deserving of blackening his face by attributing such a thing to someone who is more noble than him, so how about with God Almighty! The meaning of this verse has been sufficiently explained in Al-Nahl.
43:18: The Almighty’s saying: Or one who is brought up in adornment has two issues: The first is the saying of the Most High: Or one who grows up meaning he is raised and grows up. Nashu’ is education. It is said I grew up among the Banu so-and-so if I grew up among them. Nashu’ and nasha’ have the same meaning. Ibn Abbas, Ad-Dahhak, Ibn Waththab, Hafs, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i and Khalaf read yansha’ with a damma on the ya’, a fatha on the noon and a shaddah on the sheen, meaning he is raised and grows up in adornment. Abu Ubaid chose this because the chain of transmission in it is higher. The rest read yansha’ with a fatha on the ya’ and a sukoon on the noon. Abu Hatim chose this, meaning he is established and firm. Its root is from nasha’a, meaning he rose, as Al-Harawi said. Yansha’ is transitive, and yansha’ is intransitive. Second: The Almighty’s saying: in adornment meaning in decoration. Ibn Abbas and others said: They are female slaves whose attire is different from that of men. Mujahid said: Women were permitted to wear gold and silk, and he recited this verse. Al-Kaya said: It indicates that adornment is permissible for women, and there is consensus on it, and the reports on it are countless. I said: It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he used to say to his daughter: O my daughter, beware of adorning yourself with gold! For I fear for you the flames. God the Almighty said: And he is not clear in dispute. That is, in argument and presenting evidence. Qatada said: No woman spoke and had an argument except that she made it against herself. In the copy of Abdullah it is: And he is not clear in speech. The meaning of the verse: Ascribing to God one who is like this! That is, that is not permissible. It was said: The idols that originated in adornment were their idols, the smallest of which were made of gold and silver and their jewels. This was said by Ibn Zayd and Ad-Dahhak. The meaning of And he is not clear in dispute according to this statement is: that is, he is silent about the answer. From is in the accusative case, that is, they took for God one who originates in adornment. It is permissible for it to be nominative as a subject and the predicate is implied. Al-Farra’ said: Its meaning is: or whoever is in this state deserves worship. If you like, say it is in the genitive case, returning to the beginning of the statement, which is His statement: Because of what He struck, or according to what in His statement: From what He creates daughters. The fact that the substitute is in these two places is weak because the interrogative alif is a barrier between the substitute and that which is substituted.
43:19: And they made the angels, who are the servants of the Most Merciful, females. The Kufians read (servants) in the plural, and Abu Ubaid chose it, because the chain of transmission is higher in it, and because God Almighty only denied them when they said that they were the daughters of God, so He informed them that they were servants and that they were not His daughters. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he read (servants of the Most Merciful), and Saeed bin Jubayr said: In my copy of the Qur’an is (Abd al-Rahman), so he said: Erase it and write (servants of the Most Merciful), and the confirmation of this reading is the statement of God Almighty: Rather, they are honored servants (Al-Anbiya’: 26), and His statement God Almighty: Do those who disbelieve think that they can take My servants as protectors besides Me? (al-Kahf 18:102), and His statement God Almighty: Indeed, those you invoke besides God are servants like you (al-A’raf 7:194), and the rest read (with the Most Merciful) with a silent nun and Abu Hatim chose it. And the confirmation of this reading is the statement of God Almighty: Indeed, those who are with your Lord (al-A’raf 7:104) 206], and His saying: And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth and whoever is with Him (al-Anbiya 21:19). The intention is to clarify their lie and show their ignorance in attributing children to God Almighty, then in their control that the angels are females while they are the daughters of God, and the mention of the servants is to praise them, that is, how did they worship the One who is at the end of worship, then how did they rule that they are females without evidence, and making here means saying and ruling, you say: I made Zayd the most knowledgeable of people, that is, I ruled for him that witness their creation that is, bring them to the state of their creation until they ruled that they are females. And it was said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: How do you know that they are females?” They said: We heard that from our fathers and we testify that they did not lie about them being females. God Almighty said: Their testimony will be written down and they will be asked about it meaning they will be asked about it in the Hereafter. Nafi’ read awshahu with an interrogative hamza inside a damma hamza that is facilitated, and it is not extended except for what Al-Maseebi narrated from him that it is extended. Al-Mufaddal narrated from Asim something like that and the two hamzas were realized. The rest read ashhadu with one interrogative hamza. It was narrated from Al-Zuhri ashhadu khalqalihum as report. sattaktubu is the reading of the general public with a damma on the ta’ on the passive verb shahadahum in the nominative case. Al-Salami, Ibn Al-Sameeq and Hubayrah read from Hafs sankatub with a noon, shahadahum in the accusative case by naming the agent. From Abu Raja’ sattaktubu shahadatihum in the plural.
43:20: The Almighty said: And they said, ‘If the Most Gracious had willed,’ meaning the polytheists said, in mockery and ridicule: If the Most Gracious had willed, as you claim, we would not have worshipped these angels. This is a true statement from them, intended to be false. Everything is by the will of God, and His will is obligatory, as is His knowledge, so it is not possible to use it as evidence. Something contrary to what is known and intended is possible, even if it does not happen. If they had worshipped God instead of idols, we would have known that God wanted from them what they did. This meaning has already been mentioned in Al-An’am when He said: Those who associate others with God will say, ‘If God had willed, we would not have associated others with Him.’ (Al-An’am 6:148), and in Ya-Sin 36:Should we feed those whom, if God had willed, He would have fed them? [Ya-Sin 47]. His statement: They have no knowledge of that is attributed to His statement: And they have made the angels, who are the servants of the Most Gracious, females. That is, they have no knowledge of what they say: The angels are daughters of God. This was said by Qatada, Muqatil, and Al-Kalbi. Mujahid and Ibn Jurayj said: Meaning idols, that is, they have no knowledge of worshipping idols. From is a connection. They only guess, that is, they speculate and lie. They have no excuse for worshipping other than God Almighty. What was included in their words was that God commanded us to do this or was pleased with it from us, and for this reason He did not forbid us or hasten to punish us.
43:21: God Almighty says: Or have We given them a scripture before it to which they cling? This is equivalent to his saying: Witness their creation. The meaning is: Did they witness their creation or did We give them a book before it, that is, before the Qur’an, with what I call for, so they adhere to it and act according to what is in it.
43:22: There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: upon a nation meaning on a way and a school of thought. This was said by Omar bin Abdul Aziz. He, Mujahid, and Qatada used to read upon a nation with a kasra on the alif. Ummah is the way. Al-Jawhari said: And the nation with a kasra is the blessing. And the nation is also a language for the nation, and it is the way and religion. On the authority of Abu Ubaidah, Adi bin Zaid said about the blessing: Then after the peasant, the king and the slave, she showed them the graves there. On the authority of Ghair Al-Jawhari, Qatada and Atiyah said: On a nation means on a religion. From this is the saying of Qais bin Al-Khatim: We were following the nation of our fathers, and others follow the example of the first. Al-Jawhari said: The nation is the path and religion. It is said: So-and-so has no mother, meaning he has no religion or sect. The poet said: Are the people of a nation equal to the unbelievers? Mujahid and Qatrib said: On religion, on religion. In some copies of the Qur’an: They said, ‘Indeed, we found our fathers following a religion.’ These sayings are similar. It was reported from Al-Farra’: On religion, on a qiblah. Al-Akhfash: On straightness. He recited the words of Al-Nabigha: I swore and left no doubt for you. Can a slave be sinned if he is obedient? The second: And indeed, we are guided by their footsteps, meaning we are guided by them. In the other verse: following, meaning we imitate them, and the meaning is the same. Qatada said: following and following. This is evidence of the invalidation of imitation, because of their responsibility for imitating their fathers and their neglect of what the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, called them to. This has been fully discussed in Surat Al-Baqarah. Muqatil narrated that this verse was revealed about Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira, Abu Sufyan, Abu Jahl, Utbah, and Shaibah, the sons of Rabi’ah, from the Quraysh. That is, just as these said, those before them also said, consoling their Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Similar to it is: You are only told what was told to the messengers before you Fussilat 41:43. The pampered is the one who is spoiled, and what is meant here are kings and tyrants.
43:23: God Almighty says: And thus We did not send before you any warner to any city except that its affluent said, ‘Indeed, we found our fathers following a religion, and we will certainly follow in their footsteps.’
43:24: God the Almighty says: He said, ‘Even if I came to you with better guidance’ meaning, say, O Muhammad, to your al-Nas 114:Have I not come to you from God with better guidance than what you found your fathers following? They said, Indeed, we, in that with which you have been sent, are disbelievers. This means everything with which the messengers were sent. The address is to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and the wording is plural, because denying him is denying everyone else. It was also read as, Say, ‘And he said, “I have come to you and we have come to you” meaning, Would you follow your fathers, even if I came to you with a religion better guided than the religion of your fathers? They said, Indeed, we will remain steadfast in the religion of our fathers and will not abandon it, even if you bring to us something that is better guided. The discussion of imitation and its censure has already been discussed in Surat Al-Baqarah, so there is no point in repeating it.
43:25: The Almighty said: So We took vengeance upon them with famine, killing, and captivity. Then see how was the end of those who denied is the last command of the denial of the messengers. The general reading is (Say, Even if I come to you, and Ibn Amir and Hafez read (Say, Even if) as a report on the warner that he said this statement to them. Abu Ja`far read (Say, Even if we come to you with a noon and an alif, on the basis that the address from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is on behalf of all the messengers.
43:26: The Almighty said: And when he said meaning he mentioned to them when he said: Abraham to his father and his people, ‘Indeed, I am innocent of what you worship.’ Bara’ is used for singular and above, and it is dual, not plural, nor feminine, because it is a verbal noun used in place of an adjective. You do not say: al-Baraa’an and al-Baraa’un, because the meaning is the one who is innocent and those who are innocent. Al-Jawhari said: And I disavowed such-and-such, and I am innocent of it. Khala’ of it is not dual nor plural because it is a verbal noun in origin, like: sama’a sama’an. So if you say: I am innocent of it and khala’, you dualize, pluralize, and feminize. And you say in the plural: we are innocent of it, like faqih and faqha’, and bara’ also like kareem and karam, and bara’ like sharif and ashraf, and bara’ like naseeb and ansaba’, and bara’un, and a bara’ah woman, and they are bara’itan, and they are bara’at and bara’iyat, and a bara’ man and bara’ like ‘ajeeb and ajaab, and bara’ with the fat-ha is the first night of the month, and it was named thus because the moon is innocent of the sun..
43:27: God Almighty says: Except He who created me, and indeed, He will guide me. “Except He who created me” is a connected exception, because they worshipped God along with their gods. Qatada said: They used to say God is our Lord while worshipping idols. It is possible for it to be disconnected, meaning but He who created me guides me. He said that out of trust in God and to alert his people that guidance is from his Lord.
43:28: There are three issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And made it an enduring word. The pronoun in made it refers back to His saying: except He who created me. The subject pronoun in made it belongs to God Almighty, meaning that God made this word and statement enduring in his descendants, who are his children, meaning that they inherited the disavowal of worshipping other than God and they advised each other in that, and the descendants are those who come after him. Al-Suddi said: They are the family of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abbas said: His saying: in his descendants means in his successors, and there is an inversion in the speech, the meaning is that he will guide them so that they may return. And He made it an enduring word in his descendants, meaning that He said to them that so that they may repent from worshipping other than God. Mujahid and Qatadah said: The word is there is no god but God. Qatadah said: It will continue to be from the descendants of those who worship God until the Day of Resurrection. Ad-Dahhak said: The word is that you do not worship except God. Ikrimah: Islam, because God Almighty said: It is He who named you Muslims before (al-Hajj 22:78). Al-Qurazi said: And He made… The will of Abraham that he commanded his sons, which is his saying: O my sons, indeed God has chosen for you this religion (al-Baqarah 2:132), the verse mentioned in Al-Baqarah, is a word that remains in his offspring and sons. Ibn Zayd said: The word is his saying: I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds (al-Baqarah 2:131), and he read: And He named you Muslims before and it was said: The word is the prophecy. Ibn Al-Arabi said: And the prophecy remained in the offspring of Abraham, and monotheism is its origin and others follow them in it. Second: Ibn al-Arabi said: Abraham’s descendants were connected to Al-Ahqaf through his two answered supplications, one of them in his saying: Indeed, I will make you a leader for mankind. He said: And of my descendants? He said: My covenant does not include the wrongdoers. (al-Baqarah 2:124), so he said: Yes, except for those among them who wronged, for there is no covenant. Second: His saying: And keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols. (Ibrahim 14:35), and it was said: Rather, the first is his saying: And grant me a reputation of truth among later generations. (Ash-Shu’ara’: 84), so every nation venerates him, his sons and others who gather with him in Shem or Noah. Third: Ibn al-Arabi said: The mention of descendants here is connected in meaning, and this is one of the rulings and upon which life estate contracts and endowments are based. “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Any man who gives a life estate for himself and his descendants, it belongs to the one who gave it and does not return to the one who gave it, because he gave a gift in which inheritances fall.’” It is repeated in eleven expressions: The first expression: the child, and when it is used generally it refers to whoever is found from the man and his wife among the females and the males, and to the male children without the females linguistically and legally, and therefore the inheritance falls on the specified child and the male children of the specified without the female children because they are another people, and therefore they are not included in the confinement with this expression, Malik said this in the collection and others. I said: This is the doctrine of Malik and all his early companions, and their proof for that is the consensus that the children of daughters do not inherit, in accordance with the words of God Almighty: God instructs you concerning your children (An-Nisa’: 11). A group of scholars have held that the children of daughters, whether sons or offspring, are included in the endowments. The one who endows says: I have endowed them for my son or for my offspring. This is the choice of Abu ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-Barr and others. They have cited as evidence the words of God Almighty: Forbidden to you are your mothers and your daughters (An-Nisa’: 23). They said: When God forbade daughters, then the daughter’s daughter was thus forbidden by consensus, it was known that she was a daughter and it was obligatory for her to be included in the endowment for his son or his offspring. This meaning has already been fully discussed in Al-An’am. The second wording: sons. If he said: This is reserved for my son, then it does not extend beyond the specific son nor is it multiple. If he said: My son, then it extends to everyone he was born. If he said: On my sons, then it includes males and females. Malik said: Whoever gives charity to his sons and his sons’ sons, then his daughters and his daughters’ daughters’ daughters are included in that. Isa narrated on the authority of Ibn al-Qasim regarding whoever is reserved for his daughters, they are included in that with his daughters. What the group of his companions agreed upon is that the daughters’ children are not included in the sons. If it is said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said about al-Hasan, his daughter’s son: This son of mine is a master, and perhaps God will reconcile through him two great groups of Muslims. We say: This is a metaphor, and he only indicated by it his honor and his precedence. Do you not see that it is permissible to deny it from him, so a man says about his daughter’s son, He is not my son, even if it were true, it would not be permissible to deny it from him, because truths are not denied from those related to them. Do you not see that he is related to his father but not his mother? For this reason it was said about Abdullah ibn Abbas: He is Hashemite and not… Bahlali, even if his mother is Hilali. I said: This evidence is incorrect. Rather, he is a son in reality in the language because of the meaning of birth in it, and because the people of knowledge have agreed on the prohibition of the daughter’s daughter from the saying of God Almighty: Your mothers and your daughters are forbidden to you and God Almighty said: And among his descendants were David and Solomon until His saying: of the righteous (al-An’am 6:85). So Jesus was made from his descendants and he is the son of his daughter according to what was explained there. If it is said, the poet said: Our sons are our sons' sons, and our daughters are their sons, the sons of distant men. It was said to them: There is no evidence for this, because the meaning of his saying: It is only the sons of his male sons who have the ruling of his sons in inheritance and lineage, and the sons of his daughters do not have the ruling of his daughters in that, since they are attributed to someone other than him, so he informed of their separation in ruling while they are united in name, and he did not deny the name of son from the son of daughters because he is a son. A man may say about his son, he is not my son because he does not obey me and does not see any right for me, and he does not mean by that to deny the name of son from him, but rather he means to deny his ruling from him. And whoever uses this verse as evidence that the son of a daughter is not called a son has corrupted its meaning and nullified its benefit, and interpreted for its speaker what is not correct, since it is not possible for the son of a son to be called a son in the Arabic language, nor is the son of a daughter called a son, because the meaning of birth from which the name of son is derived is clearer and stronger in it, because the son of a daughter is her son by the reality of birth, and the son’s son is only his son by his wealth that was the cause of birth. And Malik, may God have mercy on him, did not exclude the sons of daughters from the confinement of his son because the name of son is not true. He has it in the language, but he excluded them from it by analogy to inheritance, and this has already been mentioned in Al-An’am, and praise be to God. The third word: offspring, which is taken from the word dhara’a meaning God created creation, so it includes daughters’ children, as He said: And among his offspring were David and Solomon, until He said: And Zachariah and John and Jesus. Rather, he was from his offspring from his mother’s side. The derivation of offspring has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah and in Al-An’am the discussion of and among his offspring the verse, so there is no point in repeating it. The fourth word: the heel, which in the language is an expression for something after something else, whether of the same kind or not. It is said: God followed with good, meaning He brought ease after hardship, and he followed the gray hair with blackness, and the heel is followed by a punishment and a heel if something comes after something, and for this reason it is said of a man’s child: his heel, and the woman who gives birth to a male after a female, thus forever, and the heel of a man: his child and his child’s child who remain after him, and the heel is the child, Ya’qub said: In the Qur’an: And made it a word remaining in his offspring (al-Zukhruf 43:28), and it was said: Rather, all the heirs are heel, and the heel is the child, and for this reason Mujahid explained it here, and Ibn Zayd said: Here they are the offspring, and Ibn Shihab said: They are the child and the child’s child, and others said it according to what was mentioned above from Al-Suddi, and in Al-Sahah, the heel with a kasra on the qaf is the back of the foot and it is feminine, and the heel of a man is also his child and his child’s child, and there are two languages for it: heel and heel with a sukoon, and it is also Feminine, on the authority of Al-Akhfash, and the offspring of someone in the place of his father is a consequence, meaning his successor, and it is a noun that means a source, like the Almighty’s saying: Its occurrence has no effect (al-Waqi’ah 56:2). And there is no difference according to any of the scholars between the word offspring and child in meaning, and there is a difference of opinion regarding offspring and progeny. It was said that they are in the position of the child and offspring, and the daughters’ children are not included in them according to the Maliki school of thought. And it was said that they are included in them, and the discussion of offspring has already passed here and in Al-An’am. The fifth expression: My offspring. According to our scholars, it is like saying, My son and My son’s son. For it includes the daughters’ children, and they must be included, because offspring means came out, and the daughters’ children came out of it in one way, and nothing specific to it was connected to it, as was the case with his saying, The consequence of what they had offspring. Some of our scholars said: Offspring is like the son and the offspring, and the daughters’ children are not included in it, unless the one who is detained says, “My offspring and Offspring of my offspring, as if he said, My offspring and My offspring of my offspring. But if he says, My son or My offspring on its own, then the daughters are not included in it. The sixth expression: Al-Aal, which is the family, and it is the seventh expression. Ibn Al-Qasim said: They are the same, and they are the agnates, brothers, daughters, and paternal aunts, and maternal aunts are not included in it. The origin of the people of the gathering is said: a place of people if it contains a group, and that is the agnates and whoever is included in the number of women, and the agnates are derived from it and are more specific to it. In the hadith of the slander, O Messenger of God, your family! We do not know anything but good, meaning Aisha. However, the wife is not included in it by consensus, even if she is the origin of the qualification, because her proof is not certain, as her bond may change and the divorce may be dissolved. Malik said: The family of Muhammad is all pious people, and it is not from this chapter. Rather, he meant that faith is more specific than kinship, so the call includes it, and he meant mercy. Abu Ishaq Al-Tunisi said: The family includes everyone from both parents, so the derivation has done its right and ignored the custom and the general usage. These meanings are based on the truth or on the custom used when it is general. So these are two expressions. The eighth expression: kinship. There are four opinions on this: The first is what Malik said in the book of Muhammad ibn Abdus: They are the closest, then the closest, according to ijtihad. Neither the daughters’ children nor the maternal aunts’ children are included in this. The second is what Ali ibn Ziyad said: His relatives from his father and mother are included in this. The third is what Ashab said: Every womb of men and women is included in this. The fourth is what Ibn Kinanah said: The paternal uncles, paternal aunts, maternal uncles, maternal aunts, and sister’s daughters are included in this. Ibn Abbas said in his interpretation of the verse: “Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it except love for the relatives” (al-Shura 42:23), he said: Except that you maintain the kinship between me and you. He said: There was no clan of Quraysh except that there was kinship between them and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is what he defines, and God knows best. The ninth expression: The clan, and it is defined by the authentic hadith: When God Almighty revealed: And warn your nearest relatives (Ash-Shu’ara’: 214), the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called the clans of Quraysh and named them as previously mentioned, and they are the nearest clan, and others are clan in general, and the expression is carried specifically to the closest by effort, as previously mentioned from the statement of our scholars. The tenth word: The people. This applies to men in particular from the clan, not women. The people include men and women, even though the poet said: I don't know, and I will think I know whether the Al-Husn family or the women are doing it. But he meant that if a man calls his people to victory, he means men, and if he calls them to sanctity, men and women are included among them, so the description is general and the context makes it specific. The eleventh word: The clients. Malik said: It includes the clients of his father and his son along with his clients. Ibn Wahb said: It includes the children of his clients. Ibn al-Arabi said: What is understood from it is that it includes those who inherit from him by loyalty. He said: These are the chapters of the discussion and its principles connected to the apparent meaning of the Qur’an and the Sunnah that explains it, and the branching and completion are in the Book of Questions, and God knows best.
43:29: The Almighty says: Rather, You gave enjoyment and it was also read (Rather, We gave enjoyment) these and their fathers meaning in this world with respite, until the truth came to them meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with monotheism and Islam, which is the foundation of the religion of Abraham, and it is the word that God left in his descendants, and a clear messenger meaning he explains to them what they need.
43:30: And when the truth came to them meaning the Qur'an, they said, 'This is magic, and indeed, we disbelieve in it' denying.
43:31: And they said, 'Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a man' meaning, Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a man It is also read upon a man with a silent jim, of the two cities, a great one meaning from one of the two cities, like the Almighty's saying: From them come forth pearls and coral (al-Rahman 55:22), meaning from one of them, or upon two men from the two cities, the two cities: Mecca and Ta'if, and the two men: Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira bin Abdullah bin Umar bin Makhzum, the uncle of Abu Jahl, and the one from Ta'if, Abu Mas'ud Urwah bin Mas'ud Al-Thaqafi, as Qatadah said. It was also said: Umair bin Abd Yalil Al-Thaqafi from Ta'if, and Utbah bin Rabi'ah from Mecca, and this is the saying of Mujahid. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas that the great one from Ta'if was Habib bin Amr Al-Thaqafi. Al-Suddi said: Kinanah bin Abd bin Amr. It was narrated that Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira, who was called the flower of Quraish, used to say: If what Muhammad says had come to pass, it would have been sent down upon me or upon Abu Mas'ud.
43:32: Do they distribute the mercy of your Lord? meaning prophethood, so they place it where they wish. We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world. That is, We made some people poor and others rich. So if the matter of this world is not in their hands, how can the matter of prophethood be entrusted to them? Qatada said: He will meet him weak in strength, lacking in resourcefulness, and with a weak tongue, although it is available to him. And he will meet him strong in resourcefulness, simple in tongue, although it is restricted to him. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Ibn Muhaisin, in a narration from him, read: their livelihoods. It was said: That is, We gave the great one of the two cities what We gave them, not because of their honor to Me, and I am able to take the blessing away from them. So what superiority and status do they have? And We raised some of them above others in degrees. That is, We distinguished between them, so some are superior and some are inferior, and some are leaders and some are followers. Muqatil said this. It was also said: By freedom and slavery, so some of them are owners and some are slaves. It was also said: By wealth and poverty, so some of them are rich and some are poor. It was also said: By enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, so that they may take... Some of them mock each other. Al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said: As slaves and servants, the rich mock the poor so that some of them are a means of livelihood for others. Qatada and Al-Dahhak said: It means so that some of them own each other. It was also said: It is mockery that means ridicule, i.e. the rich mock the poor. Al-Akhfash said: I mocked him and made fun of him, I laughed at him and laughed at him, I mocked him and with him. Each is said: The noun is mockery with the dammah, and sakhri and sakhri with the dammah and the kasrah. All people have damma on sakhriya except Ibn Muhaysin and Mujahid, as they read sakhriya. “And the mercy of your Lord is better than what they accumulate,” i.e. better than what they accumulate of this world. Then it was said: Mercy is prophethood, and it was said Paradise, and it was said: Completing the obligatory duties is better than many voluntary duties, and it was said: What He bestows upon them is better than what He rewards them for of their deeds.
43:33: It contains five issues: First: The scholars said: He mentioned the insignificance of this world and its small danger, and that it was so insignificant to him that he would make the houses and stairs of the infidels out of gold and silver. And were it not for the love of this world dominating hearts, which is interpreted as infidelity. Al-Hasan said: The meaning is that were it not for the fact that all people would disbelieve because of their inclination towards this world and their abandonment of the Hereafter, We would have given them in this world what we have described, because of the insignificance of this world before God, the Almighty. This is the view of most of the commentators, Ibn Abbas, Al-Suddi and others. Ibn Zayd said: And were it not for the fact that mankind would be one community in seeking this world and choosing it over the Hereafter, We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful roofs of silver for their houses. Al-Kisa’i said: The meaning is that were it not for the fact that there would be among the infidels the rich and the poor and among the Muslims the same, We would have given the infidels this part of this world because of its insignificance. Second: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read (Saqfan) with a fatha on the seen and a sukoon on the qaf, singular and plural, based on the Almighty’s saying: So the roof fell upon them from above them (al-Nahl 16:26). The rest read it with a damma on the seen and the qaf, plural, like rahn and rahn. Abu Ubaid said: There is no third for them. It was said: It is the plural of saqif, like kathib and kathib, and ragheef and raghaf, said Al-Farra’.
