It was said: It is the plural of saqf, so the plural of the plural becomes saqf and saqf, like fils and fulus. Then they made fa’ul as if it were a single noun, so they pluralized it as fa’l. It was narrated from Mujahid (Saqfan) with a sukoon on the qaf. It was said: The lam in (libaytuhim) means on, meaning on their houses. It was said: It is a substitute, as you say: I did this for Zayd to honor him. God Almighty said: And for his parents, to each one of them is a sixth (An-Nisa’: 11). Likewise, He said here: We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful their houses. " Third: The Almighty’s saying: And ascents meaning stairs, Ibn Abbas said this and it is the saying of the majority, its singular is mi’raj and mi’raj is as-salam, from which comes the Night of the Ascension, and the plural is ma’arij and ma’arij, like mafatih and mafatih, two dialects (and ma’arij) Abu Raja’ al-Attardi and Talha ibn Musraf read it, and it is the ascents and ladders, Al-Akhfash said: If you wish, you can make the singular mi’raj and ma’raj, like marqat and marqat, upon them they appear meaning on the ascents they ascend and climb. It is said: I appeared on the house, meaning I climbed its roof, and this is because whoever ascends something and is elevated on it appears to the onlookers, and it is said: I appeared on something, meaning I knew it, and I appeared on the enemy, meaning I defeated him, and “Nabigha Bani Ja’dah recited the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, his saying: We have risen to the sky in glory and majesty, and we hope for a manifestation above that. Any ascent, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became angry and said: To where? He said: To Paradise. He said: Yes, God willing. Al-Hasan said: By God, the world has inclined towards most of its people and he did not do that! So how would it be if he did?! Fourth: Some scholars have used this verse as evidence that the owner of the upper part has no right to the ceiling, because God Almighty made ceilings just as He made doors for them. This is the school of Malik, may God have mercy on him. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is because the house is a hall, a wall, a ceiling, and a door, and whoever owns the house owns its corners, and there is no dispute that the upper part to the sky belongs to him. They differed about the lower part. Some of them said it belongs to him, and some of them said he has nothing inside the earth. In our school of thought there are two opinions. The authentic hadith of al-Isra’i’ was explained above: A man sold a house to another man, and he built it, and found a golden jar in it. He brought it to the seller and said: I only bought the house without the jar. The seller said: I only sold the house for what is in it. They all exchanged it among themselves. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said that one of them should marry his son to the daughter of the other, and the money would be for them. The correct view is that the upper and lower parts belong to him unless he leaves them by selling them. If one of them sells one of the two places, he gets what he benefits from, and the rest is for the one who bought it from him. Fifth: Of the rulings on the upper and lower floors: If the upper and lower floors are between two men and the lower floor becomes damaged or its owner wants to demolish it, Sahnun reported on the authority of Ashhab that he said: If the owner of the lower floor wants to demolish, or the owner of the upper floor wants to build his upper floor, then the owner of the lower floor does not have the right to demolish it except out of necessity, and demolishing it is easier for the owner of the upper floor, lest the upper floor collapse with its collapse. And the owner of the upper floor does not have the right to build on his upper floor something that did not exist before except something light that does not harm the owner of the lower floor. And if a piece of wood from the ceiling of the upper floor breaks, then another piece of wood should be put in its place, unless it is heavier than it and there is fear that it will harm the people of the ceiling. Ashhab said: And the door of the house is on the owner of the lower floor. He said: If the lower floor collapses, its owner is forced to rebuild it, and the owner of the upper floor does not have to rebuild the lower floor. If the owner of the lower floor refuses to build, he is told to sell it to someone who will build it. Ibn al-Qasim narrated on the authority of Malik that the lower floor belongs to one man and the upper floor belongs to another and the lower floor becomes damaged, then its repair is on the owner of the lower floor and he is responsible for it. Suspending the upper floor until the lower floor is repaired, because he must either support it on a building or on a suspension. Similarly, if there is a height on the upper floor, then suspending the second floor is on the owner of the middle floor. It has been said that suspending the second floor is on the owner of the upper floor until the lower floor is built. The hadith of al-Nu’man ibn Bashir, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The example of the one who maintains God’s limits and the one who transgresses them is like people who drew lots for a ship, and some of them got the upper floor and some the lower floor. When those on the lower floor wanted to draw water, they passed by those above them and said, ‘If we make a hole in our share and do not harm those above us,’ if they leave them to do what they want, they will all perish, but if they take them by the hand, they will be saved and they will all be saved.” This is a principle in this matter, and it is an argument for Malik and Ashhab. It is evidence that the owner of the lower floor does not have the right to cause harm to the owner of the upper floor, and that if he causes harm to him, he is obligated to repair it, not the owner of the upper floor. The owner of the upper floor has the right to prevent him from harming him, because of the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: ‘If they take them by the hand, they will be saved and they will all be saved.’ It is not permissible to take…” Except at the hands of the oppressor or one who is forbidden from doing what is not permissible for him in the Sunnah. It contains evidence of deserving punishment for abandoning enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. It has been mentioned in Al-Anfal and it contains evidence of the permissibility of drawing lots and using it. It has been mentioned in Al Imran. So consider each in its place and you will find it explained. Praise be to God.
43:34: The Most High said: And for their houses, doors meaning, We made for their houses, and it was said: (for their houses) is a substitute for inclusion from His saying: for him who disbelieves in the Most Merciful (doors) meaning of silver, and couches likewise, and it is the whole of the bed, and it was said: the plural of the family, and the family is the plural of the bed, so it is the plural of the plural, they recline on it, reclining and leaning: leaning on something, and from it: I lean on it (Ta-Ha 20:18), and a man is a recliner, an example of a hamza of many leaning, and leaning is also what one leans on, and he leaned on the thing so he is leaning, and the place is a recliner, and he stabbed him until he leaned on him on af'aluh meaning he threw him in the position of someone who is reclining, and I leaned on the stick, and the ta' continued in all of that as a waw, so he did to him what he did with weighed and prepared.
43:35: And decorations here decoration is gold, according to Ibn Abbas and others, similar to it, or that you have a house of decorations (al-Isra’ 17:93), and it has been mentioned, and Ibn Zayd said: It is what people have in their homes of furnishings and furnishings, and Al-Hasan said: Engravings, and its origin is ornamentation, it is said: I decorated the house, meaning I adorned it, so-and-so decorated, he adorned, and the word decorations is in the accusative case to mean and We made for them with that decoration, and it was said: by removing the preposition, and the meaning is so We made for them a roof and doors and beds of silver and gold, so when he deleted of he said: and decorations so he made the accusative case: And indeed all of that is for the enjoyment of worldly life Asim, Hamza and Hisham read on the authority of Ibn Amir: And indeed all of that is for the enjoyment of worldly life with emphasis, the rest with emphasis, and this has been mentioned, and it was narrated on the authority of Abu Raja' to break the lam of when, what in his view is like the one who...and the pronoun is omitted, and the meaning is: And indeed, all of that is for the enjoyment of worldly life. The omission of the pronoun here is like its omission in the reading of those who read, An example of a mosquito or what is above it (al-Baqarah 2:26), and Completely for the one who does good (al-An’am 6:154). Abu al-Fath 48:All should be in the accusative case in this reading, because in is a lightened version of a heavy one, and if it is lightened and its function is invalidated, the lam is required for it at the end of the sentence to differentiate it from the negative in that has the meaning of what, such as Indeed, Zayd is standing. There is no lam here except the preposition. And the Hereafter is with your Lord for the righteous means Paradise for those who fear God and are conscious of God. Ka’b said: I find in some of God’s revealed books: Were it not that My believing servant would grieve, I would crown the head of My disbelieving servant with a crown, and it would not crack, nor would a vein throb with pain. In Sahih Al-Tirmidhi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The world is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the disbeliever. And on the authority of Sahl bin Sa’d, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If the world were worth as much as a mosquito’s wing in God’s sight, He would not have given a disbeliever a single sip of water from it. There is a hadith on this topic on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: A good and rare hadith. They recited: If the world was a reward for the doer of good, then there would be no livelihood in it for the oppressor. The prophets were hungry in it as an honor, and the stomachs of the animals were satisfied in it. Another said: Enjoy the days if you are firm, because you are between the one who forbids and the one who commands If the world keeps a person's religion, then what he misses from it is not harmful The world does not weigh the wing of a mosquito, nor the weight of a feather from the wing of a bird. He was not satisfied with this world as a reward for a good person, nor was he satisfied with this world as a punishment for an unbeliever.
43:36: The Almighty said: And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful - We appoint for him a devil, and he is to him a companion. Ibn Abbas and Ikrimah read and whoever is blind with the opening of the sheen, and its meaning is blind. It is said from it that someone is blind, and a man is blind and a woman is blind if he cannot see. From it is the saying of Al-A’sha: She saw a man who was absent from the delegation, of different appearance, blind and blind. And his saying: If she saw a blind man, harmed by the vicissitudes of fate and a dispelled and crazy time The rest with the dammah, and from ‘asha ya’sha if what befalls the blind afflicts him, and Al-Khalil said: ‘Ash-sha is looking with weak eyesight, and he recited: When you come to him and dine by the light of his fire, you will find the best fire with him and the best stove. Another said: What a fine young man he is, who sleeps by the light of his fire when the wind blows and the place is barren. Al-Jawhari: Al-Asha short is the source of Al-A’sha, which is the one who does not see at night and sees during the day. A woman is blind, and two women are blind. God made him blind, so Fa’sha in the broken form is Ya’sha ‘ashya. It was left in the dual as it is. He became blind if he saw himself as blind, and the nisba to A’sha is A’shawi, and to Al-Ashiyah is ‘ashwi. Al-Ashwa’ is the she-camel that does not see in front of it, so it strikes everything with its hands. So-and-so rode Al-Ashwa’ if he struck without insight, and so-and-so is a runner who struck blindly. This verse is connected to the words of the beginning of the surah: Shall We turn away from you the Reminder? (al-Zukhruf 43:5), meaning, We continue the Reminder to you, so whoever turns away from that Reminder by turning away from it to the sayings and falsehoods of the misguiders, We appoint for him a devil meaning, We attribute to him a devil as a reward for his disbelief, and he is to him a companion. It was said that in this world, he prevents him from what is lawful, and incites him to what is unlawful, and forbids him from obedience, and orders him to disobey, and this is the meaning of the words of Ibn Abbas. It was also said that in the Hereafter, when he rises from his grave, as said by Saeed Al-Jaziri. In al-Naba 78:When the disbeliever comes out of his grave, he intercedes with a devil who remains with him until they enter the Fire, and that the believer intercedes with an angel until God judges between His creation, as mentioned by Al-Mahdawi. Al-Qushayri said: The correct view is that he is to him a companion in this world and the Hereafter. Abu Al-Haytham and Al-Azhari said, I went to such-and-such means I intended it, and I went to such-and-such” means I turned away from it, so there is a difference between to and from. Such as: I turned towards him and turned away from him. Qatada said: He lives and turns away, and this is the opinion of Al-Farra’. An-Nahhas: It is not known in the language. Al-Qurazi said: He turns his back, and the meaning is the same. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Akhfash said: His eye becomes dark. Al-Atabi denied that ‘Ashwut’ means ‘I turned away’, and he said: The correct form is ‘Ta’ashitu’. This is the opinion of Abu Al-Haytham and Al-Azhari, and all the people of knowledge said the same. As-Salami, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Ya’qub and Asmah from Asim and from Al-A’mash read (Yaqidh) with a ya’ because of the mention of (Al-Rahman) first, meaning that Al-Rahman appoints a devil for him, the rest with a noon, and from Ibn Abbas (Yaqidh shaytan is appointed for him, so he is his companion) meaning constant and constant. It was said: (So he) is a metaphor for Satan, as mentioned above. It was said: About turning away from the Qur’an, meaning that he is a companion to Satan.
43:37: And indeed, they turn them away from the path meaning, indeed, the devils turn them away from the path of guidance. It was mentioned in the plural form because whoever in His statement, and whoever lives has the meaning of the plural. And they think meaning, and the disbelievers think that they are guided. It was said: And the disbelievers think that the devils are guided, so they obey them.
43:38: Until when He comes to us in the singular, Abu Amr, Hamza, Al-Kisa'i and Hafs read it, meaning the disbeliever on the Day of Resurrection. The rest read it (came to us) in the dual, meaning the disbeliever and his companion, and they were put in one chain, so the disbeliever says: Oh, would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts meaning the east of winter and the east of summer, as God Almighty said: Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests (Al-Rahman: 17), and something similar is the saying of Muqatil. The reading of the singular, even if it appears to be singular, the meaning is for both of them, because he has made that known by what comes after it, as he said: And she appointed a camel as her eye socket, and she split its two ends. Muqatil said: The unbeliever wishes that there was a distance between the east of the longest day of the year and the east of the shortest day of the year. That is why he said: The distance between the two easts. Al-Farra’ said: He meant the east and the west, so the name of one of them prevailed, just as it is said: the two moons for the sun and the moon, and the two occultations for Abu Bakr and Umar, and the two Basras for Kufa and Basra, and the two asras for tomorrow and afternoon. The poet said: We have taken the horizons of the sky upon you, for us are its two moons and the rising stars. Abu Ubaidah recited for Jarir: The Messenger of God would not have been pleased with their actions, nor with the two leaders, Abu Bakr and Umar. And Sibawayh recited: Lead me from the victory of the Khabibin Abdullah and Mus`ab, the sons of Al-Zubayr, are meant, but Abu Khabib is Abdullah. What an evil companion! That is, what an evil companion you are, because he will lead him to Hell. Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri said: When the unbeliever is sent, he will be paired with his companion from among the devils, and he will not leave him until he leads him to Hell.
43:39: The Almighty’s saying: And today it will not benefit you since you have wronged (when) is a substitute for today, meaning that God says to the disbeliever: Today it will not benefit you since you have associated partners in this world. This speech is the saying of the disbeliever: Oh, would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts. That is, regret will not benefit you today. (Indeed, you) with the kasra, in the punishment are partners. This is the reading of Ibn Amir, with a difference from the rest with the fatha, and it is in the nominative case, meaning: And today your sharing in the punishment will not benefit you, because each one has his greater share of it. God the Almighty knows that He prevented the people of Hell from seeking consolation as people who are afflicted in this world seek consolation, and that is because consolation is comforted by the people of this world, so one of them says: I have an example in the affliction and calamity, and that calms his sadness, as Al-Khansa’ said: If it weren't for the many people crying around me over their brothers, I would have killed myself. They do not cry like my brother, but I console myself by taking him as an example. If it is in the Hereafter, then taking them for granted will not benefit them at all, because they will be preoccupied with the torment. Muqatil said: Apologizing and regretting will not benefit you today, because your peers and you will share in the torment, just as you shared in disbelief.
43:40: The Almighty said: So can you make the deaf hear or guide the blind “O Muhammad” and whoever is in manifest error “meaning that is not for you, so do not be distressed if they disbelieve.” In it is consolation for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in it is a refutation of the Qadarites and others, and that guidance, right conduct, and failure in the heart are created by God Almighty. He misguides whomever He wills and guides whomever He wills.
43:41: God Almighty says: Then if We take you away meaning, if We expel you from Mecca because of the harm of the Quraysh, then We will take vengeance on them.
43:42: The Almighty said: Or We show you what We promised them, which is taking revenge on them during your lifetime, for indeed We have power over them. Ibn Abbas said: God showed him that on the day of Badr, and this is the opinion of most of the commentators. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: It is regarding the people of Islam, meaning the trials that occurred after the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. They will take you away, according to this, We will cause you to die. After the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, there was a severe punishment, so God honored His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and took him away, so he did not see it in his nation, which would please his eyes, and He left the punishment after him. There is no prophet who did not see the punishment in his nation. It was narrated: "The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was shown what his nation encountered after him, and he remained depressed, and he did not smile or relax until he met God Almighty." And on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud: "The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When God wants good for a nation, He takes away its prophet before it and makes him its predecessor and leader." If God wants to punish a nation, He punishes them while their Prophet is alive, so that his eyes may be comforted when they lied to him and disobeyed his command.
43:43: God Almighty says: So hold fast to what has been revealed to you meaning the Qur’an, even if someone denies it. Indeed, you are on a straight path that will lead you to God, His pleasure, and His reward.
43:44: The Almighty’s saying: And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people means the Qur’an is an honor for you and your people from Quraysh, as it was revealed in their language and to a man from them. Similar to it is: Indeed, We have sent down to you a Book in which is your remembrance (Al-Anbiya’: 10), meaning it honored you. The Qur’an was revealed in the language of Quraysh and addressed them. The people of all languages needed their language, everyone who believed in it, so they became dependent on them, because the people of each language needed to take it from their language in order to understand the meaning intended by it of commands and prohibitions and all the report of it. Thus, they were honored by that over all the people of languages, and that is why it was called Arabic. It was said: A clarification for you and your nation regarding what you need. It was said: A reminder by which you remember the matter of religion and act according to it. It was said: And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people meaning the caliphate, as it is in Quraysh and not in anyone else. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The people follow Quraysh in this matter. Their Muslim follows their Muslim and their disbeliever follows. To their disbelievers,” and Malik said: It is the saying of the man, My father told me, on the authority of his father, narrated by Ibn Abi Salamah on the authority of his father on the authority of Malik ibn Anas, as mentioned by al-Mawardi, al-Tha’labi, and others. Ibn al-Arabi said: I did not find this rank in Islam for anyone except in Baghdad, for the Banu Tamimi there say: My father told me, my father told me, to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And by that their status was honored, and the people held their position high, and the caliphate was sought through them. And I saw in the City of Peace the two sons of Abu Muhammad Rizq God ibn Abd al-Wahhab Abu al-Faraj ibn Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Harith ibn al-Asad ibn al-Layth ibn Sulayman ibn Aswad ibn Sufyan ibn Yazid ibn Akinah ibn Abdullah al-Tamimi, and they used to say: We heard our father Rizq God say, I heard my father... Ali ibn Abi Talib say, and he was asked about the compassionate and gracious one, so he said: The compassionate one is the one who turns away from him, and the gracious one is the one who begins with giving before asking, and the one who said: I heard Ali: Akinah ibn Abdullah is their highest ancestor, and it is stronger that what is meant by his saying: And He is… To remind you and your people” meaning the Qur’an. The speech is built upon it and to it the destination returns, and God knows best. Al-Mawardi said: And your people has two opinions: One of them is whoever follows you from your nation, as Qatada said and Al-Tha’labi mentioned it on the authority of Al-Hasan. The second is for your people from Quraysh. It is said: Who are this? It is said: From the Arabs. It is said: From which Arabs? It is said: From Quraysh. Mujahid said this. I said: The correct view is that it is an honor for whoever acts upon it, whether he is from Quraysh or not. Ibn Abbas narrated that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned from a military expedition or a campaign and called Fatimah and said: O Fatimah, buy yourself from God, for I cannot do anything for you before God. He said the same to his wives and said the same to his family, then the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Banu Hashim are not the most deserving of my nation, for the most deserving of my nation are the righteous. Nor are the Quraysh the most deserving of my nation, for the most deserving of my nation are the righteous. Nor are the Ansar the most deserving of my nation, for the most deserving of my nation are the righteous. Nor are the Mawali the most deserving of my nation, for the most deserving of my nation are the righteous. You are only a man and a woman, and you are like the bridle of a sa`. No one has superiority over anyone else except through piety. Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Let the people who boast about coals from the coals of Hell cease, or it will be worse in the sight of God than the dung beetles. She pushes away the stench with her nose. You are all children of Adam, and Adam was from dust. God has removed from you the shame of the Age of Ignorance and its boasting about fathers. People are believers who are pious and those who are wicked who are wretched. This was reported by Al-Tabari, and more clarification of this will come in Al-Hujurat, God willing. And you will be asked meaning about being thankful for it. This was said by Muqatil and Al-Farra’. Ibn Jurayj said: That is, you and those with you will be asked about what He has given you. It was also said: You will be asked about what you did with it, and the meanings are close.
43:45: God Almighty says: “And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers: Did We ever appoint gods to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful?” Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on the Night Journey from the Sacred Mosque to the Al-Aqsa Mosque, which is the Mosque of Jerusalem, God sent to him Adam and the Messengers he had been born to, and Gabriel was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Gabriel, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave permission and then established the prayer, then said: ‘O Muhammad, come forward and lead them in prayer.’ When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished, Gabriel said to him: ‘O Muhammad, ask those of Our Messengers We sent before you, did We appoint gods to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful?’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘I will not ask, I have had enough.’” Ibn Abbas said: “And they were seventy prophets, including Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, peace be upon them, but he did not ask them because he knew God better than them.” In a narration other than that of Ibn Abbas: They prayed behind the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in seven rows, the Messengers in three rows and the Prophets in four. Next to the Messenger of God’s back was Abraham, the friend of God, and on his right was Ishmael, and on his left was Isaac, then Moses, then the rest of the Messengers, so he led them in two rak’ahs. When he finished, he stood up and said: ‘My Lord has revealed to me. ’” “I asked you, ‘Was any of you sent to call to the worship of other than God? ’ They said, ‘O Muhammad, we bear witness that we were all sent with one message: that there is no god but God and that what they worship besides Him is false, and that you are the Seal of the Prophets and the Master of the Messengers. This has been made clear to us by your leadership over us, and that there is no prophet after you until the Day of Resurrection except Jesus, son of Mary, for he is commanded to follow in your footsteps. ’” Sa’id ibn Jubayr said regarding the verse, And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers, that he met the messengers on the night journey. Al-Walid ibn Muslim said regarding the verse, And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers, that he said: I asked Khalid ibn Du’laj about that, and he narrated to me on the authority of Qatadah, who said: He asked them on the night journey. He met the prophets, Adam, and Malik, the keeper of Hell. I said: This is the correct interpretation of this verse, and the min that comes before our messengers according to this statement is not redundant. Al-Mubarrad and a group of scholars said: The meaning is ask the nations whom We sent before you of Our messengers. It was narrated that in the reading of Ibn Mas`ud: And ask those to whom We sent before you Our messengers, and this is an explanatory reading. min according to this is redundant, and it is the saying of Mujahid, Al-Suddi, Al-Dahhak, Qatadah, Ata’, Al-Hasan, and Ibn Abbas also, meaning ask the believers of the People of the Two Books, the Torah and the Gospel. It was said: The meaning is ask us about Muhammad from the prophets whom We sent before you, so the min was deleted, and the pause at our messengers according to this is complete. Then he began with the question by way of denial. It was said that the meaning is ask whom We sent before you of Our messengers, so the complement was deleted, the address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant is his nation. Did We make gods to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful? He informed about the gods as he informed about those who have reason, so he said: worship and did not… Worship is less than worship, because the gods are treated by them as if they were rational, so the report about them is treated as if they were treated as if they were rational. The reason for this matter of asking is that the Jews and polytheists said to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): What you have brought is contrary to what came before you. So God commanded him to ask the prophets for confirmation and approval, not because he had any doubts about it. The people of interpretation differed regarding the Prophet’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) question to them, with two opinions: The first is that he asked them and the messengers said, We were sent with monotheism. This was said by Al-Wafidi. The second is that he did not ask them because of his certainty in God, the Almighty, until Ibn Zayd narrated that Michael said to Gabriel: Did Muhammad ask you about that? Gabriel said: He is stronger in faith and greater in certainty than to be asked about that. This meaning was presented in the two narrations as we mentioned.
43:46: The Almighty said: And We had certainly sent Moses with Our signs. When He informed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that He would take revenge on his enemy and established the proof with the testimony of the prophets and the agreement of all on monotheism, He confirmed for you the story of Moses and Pharaoh, and what Pharaoh did of denial, and what befell him and his people of drowning and denial, meaning We sent Moses with miracles, which are the nine signs, but he denied, so the beautiful outcome was made for him, and so it is for you.
43:47: God Almighty says: So when he brought them Our signs, at once they laughed at them. Meaning: They laugh: mocking and ridiculing, making their followers believe that these verses are magic and imagination, and that they are capable of doing them.
43:48: The Almighty said: And We did not show them a sign except that it was greater than its sister, meaning that the signs of Moses were among the greatest signs, and each one was greater than the one before it. It was said: except that it was greater than its sister, because the first requires knowledge and the second requires knowledge, so the second is added to the first and clarity increases. The meaning of brotherhood is similarity and suitability, as it is said: this is the companion of this, meaning they are close in meaning. And We seized them with punishment, meaning for their denial of those signs, and it is like the Almighty's saying: And We seized the people of Pharaoh with years of famine and loss of fruits (al-A’raf 7:130), and the flood, locusts, lice, and frogs. These last signs were a punishment for them and signs for Moses, that they might return from their disbelief.
43:49: The Almighty said: And they said, 'O magician!' When they witnessed the punishment, they said: O magician! They called him by what they used to call him before, according to their custom. It was said: They used to call scholars magicians, so they called him by that out of respect. Ibn Abbas said: O magician! "O scholar!" The magician was great among them, and they respected him. Magic was not a derogatory description. It was said: "O you who overcame us with your magic!" It is said: "I charmed him, so I charmed him!" meaning I overcame him with magic, like the Arabs say: "I argued with him, so I defeated him!" meaning I overcame him in argument. "I outdid him, so I outdid him!" and similar words. It is possible that they meant the magician in the true sense, in the sense of a question, so he did not blame them for that, hoping that they would believe. Ibn Amir, Abu Haywah, and Yahya ibn Waththab read: "O magician!" without an alif and with a damma on the ha'. The reason for that is that the ha' was mixed with what preceded it and attached to it. The addition of the letter ya that is required by the singular vocative, and Al-Farra’ recited: Oh stubborn heart, wake up from the beautiful, white, and ugly ones. The damma of the ha’ is based on the damma of the ya’. The meaning of this has already been mentioned in an-Nur. Abu Amr, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Yahya, and al-Kisa’i ayyuha stopped at the original, the rest without an alif, because it is thus found in the Qur’an. Call upon your Lord for us according to what He has covenanted with you meaning according to what He has informed us about His covenant with you. If we believe, He will reveal it to us, so ask Him and He will reveal it to us. Indeed, we are guided meaning in what is to come.
43:50: The Almighty says: So when We removed the punishment from them meaning, he called out and We removed it, at once they broke their covenant meaning, they broke the covenant that they had made for themselves and did not believe. It was said that their saying, Indeed, we are guided was a statement from them about themselves that they had believed, so when the punishment was removed from them, they turned back.
43:51: God Almighty says: And Pharaoh called out to his people. It was said: When he saw those signs, he feared that the people would turn against him, so he gathered his people and said, He called out in the sense of he said. Abu Malik said: It is possible that the Coptic leaders were with him, so he raised his voice among them, then it was spread among the Copts, as if it was called out among them. It was also said: He ordered someone to call out to his people. Ibn Jurayj said: He said, ‘O my people, is not mine the kingdom of Egypt?’ That is, no one disputes it with me: He ruled over forty farsakhs of it, similar to it. Al-Naqqash related it. It was also said: By the kingdom here he meant Alexandria. And these rivers flow beneath me, meaning the Nile rivers, and most of them are four: the King’s River, the Toulon River, the Damietta River, and the Tennis River. Qatada said: They were gardens and rivers flowing beneath his palaces. It was also said: From beneath his throne. It was also said: From beneath me means my control is effective in it without any maker. It was also said: If he held his reins, he held the Nile. Al-Qushayri said: It is permissible for the supernatural to appear on the one who claims divinity, since there is no need to distinguish between a god and someone other than a god through an extraordinary act. It was said: The meaning of and these rivers flow beneath me is that the leaders, chiefs, and tyrants march under my banner, as Ad-Dahhak said. It was said: By the rivers he meant money, and he expressed it as rivers because of its abundance and its appearance. His saying: flowing beneath me means I distribute it to those who follow me, because the encouragement and ability are in money without rivers. Do you not see? My greatness and strength and the weakness of Moses. It was said: My ability to defeat you and the inability of Moses. The waw in and these may be a conjunction of the rivers to the king of Egypt and flowing is an accusative of the state of it, and it is permissible for it to be a waw of the state, and the demonstrative pronoun is the subject, and the rivers is an attribute of the demonstrative pronoun, and flowing is the predicate of the subject, and the opening of the ya’ of under me is the people of Medina, Al-Bazzi, and Abu Amr, and the rest were silent. It was narrated from Al-Rashid that when he read it he said::I will appoint the best of my servants to it, so Al-Khasib was in charge of it, and he was in a state of ritual purity. On the authority of Abdullah bin Tahir, that he was appointed to it, so he went out to it, and when he approached it and saw it, he said: Is this the city that Pharaoh boasted about until he said: Is not the kingdom of Egypt mine??! By God, it is too small for me to enter it! So he turned his reins, then he stated his condition and said:
43:52: Or am I better? Abu Ubaidah and al-Suddi said: Umm means rather and is not a conjunction, according to the majority of commentators. The meaning is: Pharaoh said to his al-Nas 114:Rather, I am better "than this one who is humiliated" meaning he has no honor, so he humiliates himself in his needs due to his insignificance and weakness. "And he can hardly express" meaning what was in his tongue of the knot, as mentioned previously in Ta Ha. Al-Farra' said: There are two views regarding Umm: If you wish, you can make it part of the question that was made with "Umm" because of its connection to the speech before it, and if you wish, you can make it in conjunction with his saying: "Is not the kingdom of Egypt mine?" It was said: It is redundant. Abu Zaid narrated from the Arabs that they make Umm redundant, and the meaning is: I am better than this one who is humiliated. Al-Akhfash said: There is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: Do you not see or do you not see? As he said: O lizard of the vessel between Jalajil and the valleys, are you the mother of Umm Salem? Are you better than Umm Salim? Then he began and said: I am better. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said that the meaning is Do you not see? Or are you perceptive? So he connected Umm to Do you not see? because the meaning is I am better. That is because if they said to him, You are better than him, they were, in his view, perceptive. It was narrated on the authority of Isa al-Thaqafi and Yaqub al-Hadrami that they stopped at Umm so that the meaning would be, Do you not see or do you see? So he deleted the second Tabsee and it was said that whoever stopped at Umm made it redundant, and it is as if he stopped at Tabseerun from his statement, Do you not see? And the discussion on Tabseerun is not complete according to Al-Khalil and Sibawayh, because Umm requires connection to what precedes it. Some people said: The stop at his statement, Do you not see? Then he began Or am I better meaning, rather I am. Al-Farra’ recited: She looked like the sun's horn in the splendor of the morning, and her image, or are you more beautiful in the eye? Its meaning is: Rather, you are better. Al-Farra’ mentioned that some of the reciters read Ama Ana Khair, and the meaning of this is: Are you not better? It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid that he stopped at Am and began Ana Khair, and it was mentioned.
43:53: The Almighty said: Then why meaning why was not bracelets of gold placed on him? He only said that because it was the custom of the time and the attire of the honorable people. Hafs read aswarah as plural of sawar, like khimar and akhmara. Abu read asawir as plural of iswar, and Ibn Mas`ud read asawir aswairah. The rest read asawirah as plural of aswarah, so it is the plural of the plural. It is possible that asawirah is the plural of iswarah, and the ha’ was added to the plural instead of the ya’, so it is like zanadiq and zanadiqah, batariq and batariqa and the like. Abu `Amr ibn al-`Ala’ said: The singular of asawirah, asawir and asawir is iswar, and it is a dialect of sawar. Mujahid said: When they would surround a man, they would surround him with two bracelets and a gold necklace as a sign of his sovereignty. Pharaoh said: Why did not the Lord of Moses place bracelets of gold on him if he was truthful? Or the angels came with him in pairs means in succession, according to Qatada Mujahid: walking together, Ibn Abbas they help him against those who oppose him, and the meaning is: why didn't he add to him the angels whom he claims are with his Lord so that he may increase them and direct them to carry out his commands and prohibitions so that this would be more awe-inspiring in hearts, so he made his people think that the messengers of God should be like the messengers of kings in witness, and he did not know that the messengers of God were only supported by heavenly soldiers, and every rational person knows that God's protection of Moses despite his uniqueness and unity from Pharaoh despite his many followers, and providing Moses with the staff and the white hand was more eloquent than having him have bracelets or angels who would be with him as helpers according to Muqatil or evidence of his truthfulness according to Al-Kalbi, and this is not necessary because the miracle is sufficient, and it was possible that he lied with the coming of the angels just as he lied with the appearance of the signs, and Pharaoh mentioned the angels in the words of Moses because he who does not know their Creator does not believe in angels.
43:54: The Almighty said: So he made his people foolish. Ibn al-A'rabi said: The meaning is that he made his people ignorant, so they obeyed him, due to their lack of patience and limited intelligence. It is said: Joy made him foolish, meaning it disturbed him, and made him foolish, meaning it led him to ignorance. From this is the verse: And do not let those who have no certainty make you foolish. (al-Rum 30:60). It was also said: He provoked them with the people, so they obeyed him in disbelief. It was also said: He made his people foolish, meaning he found them to be weak-minded. This does not indicate that it is necessary for them to obey him, so there must be an implied meaning, He found them to be weak-minded, so he called them to misguidance, so they obeyed him. It was also said: He made his people foolish and subdued them until they followed him. It is said: He made him foolish, unlike he found him burdensome. He made him foolish, meaning he humiliated him. Indeed, they were a wicked people, meaning they had gone against the obedience of God.
43:55: The Almighty said: So when they angered Us, We took retribution from them. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: meaning they angered Us and enraged Us. Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated on his authority: meaning they angered Us. Al-Mawardi said: Their meanings differ, and the difference between them is that anger is the expression of dislike, and anger is the desire for revenge. Al-Qushayri said: Sorry here means anger, and anger from God is either the desire for punishment, in which case it is an attribute of the Self, or the punishment itself, in which case it is an attribute of the action. This is the meaning of what Al-Mawardi said. Umar ibn Dharr said: O people who disobey God, do not be deceived by God’s long patience with you, and beware of His anger, for He said: So when they angered Us, We took retribution from them. It was also said: They angered Us means they angered Our messengers and faithful friends, such as the magicians and the Children of Israel. It is like the Almighty’s saying: They harm God (al-Ahzab 33:57), and They fight God (al-Ma’idah 5:33), meaning His friends and messengers..
43:56: The Almighty said: So We made them a predecessor meaning We made the people of Pharaoh a predecessor. Abu Majlaz said: a predecessor for those who did their deeds, and an example for those who do their deeds. Mujahid said: a predecessor is information for the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and an example meaning a lesson for them. It was also narrated from him: a predecessor for the disbelievers of your people who precede them to the Fire. Qatada said: a predecessor to the Fire, and an example is a lesson for those who come after them. The predecessor is the one who preceded, it is said: salaf yaslaf salfan like talaban talaban meaning he advanced and went ahead, and a righteous deed preceded him, meaning he advanced. The people are the predecessors who preceded, and the predecessors of a man are his forefathers who preceded, and the plural is aslaf and salaf and the general reading is salfan with a fatha on the seen and the lam is the plural of salaf, like khadim and khuddam, and rasid and rasad, and haris and haris. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read salfan with a damma on the first letter. Al-Farra’ said: It is the plural of salif, like bedir and sirr. Abu Hatim said: It is the plural of salaf, like khashab and khashab, and thamar and thamar, and their meaning is the same. Ali, Ibn Mas’ud, Alqamah, Abu Wa’il, Al-Nakha’i, and Hamid bin Qais read salfan (with a damma on the seen and a fatha on the lam), the plural of salfa, meaning an advanced group. Al-Mu’arraj and Al-Nadr bin Shumayl said: salfan is the plural of salfa, like ghurfa and ghurfa, tarfa and tarf, and darkness and darkness.
43:57: The Almighty said: "And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers: 'Did We make gods to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful?'" The polytheists clung to the matter of Jesus and said: Muhammad only wants us to take him as a god, just as the Christians took Jesus, son of Mary, as a god. Qatada said this, and something similar was narrated by Mujahid, who said: The Quraysh said: Muhammad wants us to worship him as the people of Jesus worshipped Jesus. So God revealed this verse. Ibn Abbas said: What he meant by this was the debate of Abdullah ibn al-Zubayri with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the matter of Jesus, and that the one who made this example was Abdullah ibn al-Zubayri as-Sahmi, in his state of disbelief, when the Quraysh said to him: Muhammad recites: Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hellfire (al-Anbiya 21:98). He said: If I had been present, I would have responded to him. They said: And you would have said to him? He said: I used to tell him that the Christians worship this Messiah, and the Jews worship Ezra. Are they among the fuel of Hell? The Quraysh were amazed by his statement and saw that he had been deceived, and that is the meaning of His statement: they turn away, so God Almighty revealed: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it (Al-Anbiya’: 101). If Ibn Al-Zubayri had contemplated the verse, he would not have objected to it, because he said: And what you worship and did not say who you worship. Rather, he meant idols and the like of them that do not have reason, and he did not mean the Messiah or the angels, even though they were worshipped. This was mentioned at the end of Surat Al-Anbiya’. Ibn Abbas narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the Quraysh 106:O people of Quraysh, there is no good in anyone who is worshipped besides God. They said: Do you not claim that Jesus was a servant, a prophet, and a righteous servant? If he is as you claim, then he was worshipped besides God!” So God Almighty revealed: And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, at once your people turn away from him meaning they make a noise like the noise of camels when carrying heavy loads. Nafi’, Ibn ‘Amir, and Al-Kisa’i read they turn away ) with dammah on the sad and its meaning is they turn away, said Al-Nakha’i, and the others have kasrah. Al-Kisa’i said: They are two dialects: like ya’rshūn and ya’rshūn and yanmūn and yanmūn, and its meaning is they make noise, Al-Jawhari said: And sadda yasdudan, meaning he made noise, and it was said: with dammah it is from sadūd which is turning away, and with kasrah it is from dajjūj, said Qatrib. Abu Ubaid said: If it was from turning away from the truth it would have been: If your people turn away from it: Al-Farra’: They are the same, from it and from him Ibn Al-Musayyab: they turn away, they make noise, Ad-Dahhak ya’jūn, Ibn Abbas: they laugh Abu Ubaidah: from dammah its meaning is, so the meaning is: because of the inclination they are equal. yasdun is not transitive with min, and from kasrah its meaning is they make noise, min is connected to yasdun and the meaning is they make noise from it.
43:58: God Almighty said: And they said, ‘Are our gods better, or is he?’ That is, are our gods better, or is Jesus? Al-Suddi said: They argued with him and said: Everyone who is worshipped other than God is in Hell, so we are satisfied that our gods are with Jesus, the angels, and Ezra. So God Almighty revealed: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it. (Al-Anbiya’: 101), and Qatada said: Or is he they mean Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And in the reading of Ibn Mas’ud: Are our gods better or this and this strengthens the statement of Qatada, as it is a question of confirmation that their gods are better. The Kufians and Ya’qub read Are our gods with the two hamzas pronounced, and the rest read it softly. And it has been mentioned before: They did not set it forth to you except for argument Jidalan is a state, meaning two arguments, meaning they did not set forth this example to you except for the purpose of argument, because they knew that what was meant by the stones of Hell was what they had taken from the dead. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people arguing with falsehood. And in Sahih Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Abu Umamah, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No people went astray after they had been guided.” Except that they were given argument. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: “They did not present it to you except to argue. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people.”
43:59: The Almighty said: He is only a servant upon whom We bestowed favor. That is, Jesus is only a servant upon whom God bestowed prophethood, and made him an example for the Children of Israel, that is, a sign and a lesson from which to prove the power of God Almighty, for Jesus was without a father, then He bestowed upon him the ability to raise the dead, heal the blind, the leper, and all diseases, which was not bestowed upon anyone else at his time, even though the Children of Israel were at that time the most beloved of creation and the most beloved to God Almighty, and people were below them, and there was no one like them in the sight of God Almighty. It was said that what is meant by the servant upon whom We bestowed favor is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the first is more apparent.
43:60: The Almighty said: And if We willed, We could have made from among you meaning instead of you angels who would be your successors. Al-Suddi said: And something similar was narrated by Mujahid, who said: Angels who populate the earth instead of you. Al-Azhari said: From can be used for substitution, as evidenced by this verse. I said: This meaning has been mentioned previously in Bara’ah and elsewhere. It has been said: If We willed, We could have made angels from among mankind, even if this is not customary. The substances are of one kind, and the difference is in the descriptions. The meaning is: If We willed, We could have made the angels dwell on the earth, and there is no honor in Our dwelling them in the heavens, so that they would be worshipped, or they would be called daughters of God. The meaning of they succeed is that some of them succeed others, as Ibn Abbas said.
43:61: The Almighty said: And indeed, it is knowledge of the Hour, so have no doubt about it. Al-Hasan, Qatada, and Sa`id ibn Jubayr said: He means the Qur’an, because it indicates the nearness of the Hour, or through it you learn about the Hour, its horrors, and its conditions. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, As-Suddi, and Qatada also said: It is the emergence of Jesus, peace be upon him, and that is one of the signs of the Hour, because God sends him down from the sky before the Hour comes, just as the emergence of the Antichrist is one of the signs of the Hour. Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurairah, Qatada, Malik ibn Dinar, and Ad-Dahhak read: And indeed, it is knowledge of the Hour with a fat-ha on the `ayn and the lam, meaning a sign. It was narrated on the authority of `Ikrimah: And indeed, it is knowledge with two lams, and that is contrary to the copies of the Qur’an. On the authority of `Abdullah ibn Mas`ud, he said: When the night of the Prophet’s Night Journey came, he met Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, peace be upon them, and they discussed the Hour. They began with Abraham and asked him about it, but he had no knowledge. Then they asked Moses, but he had no knowledge. He had knowledge of it, so he attributed the hadith to Jesus, son of Mary, and said: I have been entrusted with what is less than its appointed time, but as for its appointed time, only God Almighty knows it. Then he mentioned the emergence of the Antichrist, and he said: Then come down and kill him. And he mentioned the hadith, which Ibn Majah included in his Sunan and in Sahih Muslim: “While he is referring to the Antichrist, God will send the Messiah, son of Mary, and he will come down at the white minaret east of Damascus between two Mahrouds, placing his hands on the wings of two angels. When he lowers his head, rain will drip, and when he raises it, pearls will flow from it. It is not permissible for a disbeliever to smell his breath except that he dies, and his breath will end wherever his gaze ends, and he will pursue him until he catches up with him at the gate of Ludd and kill him.”... The hadith. Al-Tha’labi, Al-Zamakhshari, and others mentioned from the hadith of Abu Hurairah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, will descend from the sky on a hill in the Holy Land called Afiq, between two cities, and his hair will be oily, and in his hand will be a spear with which he will kill the Antichrist. Then he will come to Jerusalem while the people are praying the afternoon prayer, and the imam will lead them in prayer. Then the imam will step back, and Jesus will put him forward and pray behind him.” “According to the Sharia of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, then he will kill the pigs, break the cross, destroy the churches and temples, and kill the Christians, except for those who believe in him.” Khalid narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The prophets are brothers because their mothers’ lineages are different, but their religion is one. I am the closest of people to Jesus, son of Mary, for there is no prophet between me and him. He will be the first to descend and break the cross, kill the pigs, and fight the people for the sake of Islam.’” Al-Mawardi said: Ibn Isa narrated on the authority of some people that they said that when Jesus descends, the obligation will be lifted so that he will not be a messenger until that time, commanding them from God Almighty and forbidding them. This is a rejected statement for three reasons, including the hadith, because the continuity of the world requires obligation in it, and because he descends commanding what is right and forbidding what is wrong. It is not strange that God Almighty’s command to him is limited to supporting Islam, commanding it, and calling people to it. I said: It is proven in Sahih Muslim and Ibn Majah on the authority of Abu Hurairah who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Jesus, son of Mary, will descend as a just judge. He will break the cross, kill the pigs, abolish the jizyah, leave the camels alone so that no one will run after them, and animosity, hatred, and envy will disappear. They will call for money but no one will accept it.’” And on his authority he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘How will you be when the son of Mary descends among you and your Imam is from among you?’” In another narration: And your mother is from among you. Ibn Abi Dhu’ayb said: Do you know what your mother is from among you? She said: Tell me. He said: “And your mother is from the Book of your Lord and the Sunnah of your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.” Our scholars, may God have mercy on them, said: This is a clear text that he will descend as a renewer of the religion of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, for what he learned, not with a new law, and the obligation will remain, as we have explained here and in the Book of Remembrance. It was also said: And indeed, it is knowledge of the Hour, meaning that Jesus’s revival of the dead is evidence of the Hour and the resurrection of the dead, as Ibn Ishaq said. I said: It is possible that the meaning is and that and that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is knowledge of the Hour, based on his saying, peace be upon him: I and the Hour have been sent like these two, and he joined his index and middle fingers. This was reported by Al-Bukhari and Muslim. Al-Hasan said: The first of its signs is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. So have no doubt about it means do not have any doubts about it: meaning about the Hour. Yahya bin Salam said this. Al-Suddi said: So do not deny it, and do not argue about it, for it will inevitably happen. “And follow” means in monotheism and in what has been conveyed to you from God. This is a straight path means a straight road to God, meaning to His Paradise. Ya’qub confirmed the ya’ in his saying: And follow in both cases, and likewise And obey and Abu Amr and Ismail from Nafi’ in the connection but not the pause, and the rest omitted it in both cases.
43:62: The Almighty says: And let not Satan turn you away meaning do not be deceived by his whisperings and the arguments of the disbelieving disbelievers, for the laws of the prophets did not differ in monotheism nor in what they informed of regarding knowledge of the Hour and other matters that they included of Paradise or Hell. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy was mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah and elsewhere.
43:63: The Almighty said: And when Jesus came with clear proofs, Ibn Abbas said: He means reviving the dead, curing illnesses, creating birds, the table and other things, and report of many of the unseen. Qatada said: The clear proofs here are the Gospel. He said, ‘I have come to you with wisdom,’ meaning prophethood, as al-Suddi said. Ibn Abbas knew what leads to beauty and refrains from the ugly. It was also said that it was the Gospel, as al-Qushayri and al-Mawardi mentioned. And that I may make clear to you some of that over which you differ, Mujahid said: Of the alteration of the Torah. Al-Zajjaj: The meaning is that I may make clear to you in the Gospel some of that over which you differ of the alteration of the Torah. Mujahid said: And he made clear to them in other than the Gospel what they needed. It was said: He made clear to them some of the rulings of the Torah over which they differed according to what they asked him. It is permissible that they differed over other things that they did not ask him about. It was said: The Children of Israel differed after the death of Moses over matters of their religion and matters of their worldly affairs, so he made clear to them their religion. The school of Abu Ubaidah says that some means All, including the Almighty’s saying: Some of what is promised to you will befall you (Ghafir 40:28). Al-Akhfash recited the words of Labid: There are places where I don't like them, or some souls cling to their doves. Death does not cling to some souls and not to others. Death is called clinging and relationship. Al-Mufaddal Al-Bakri said: And a questioner with Tha’laba bin Sir, who was attached to Tha’laba Al-Alooq Muqatil said: It is like His saying: And to make lawful to you some of what was forbidden to you (Al Imran 3:50), meaning what was made lawful in the Gospel of what was forbidden in the Torah, such as camel meat, the fat of every animal, and hunting fish on the Sabbath. So fear means fear polytheism and do not worship anyone but God alone. If this is what Jesus said, then how can it be possible for him to be a god or the son of a god. And obey in what I call you to of monotheism and other things.
43:64: The Almighty says: “Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.” That is, worshipping God is a straight path, and anything other than it is crooked and does not lead its follower to the truth.
43:65: The Almighty said: Then the parties differed among themselves. Qatada said: He means among themselves, and there are two opinions about them: One of them is that they are the People of the Book, the Jews and Christians, who differed with each other, as Mujahid and Al-Suddi said. The second: He is the Son of God, and the Jacobites said: He is God, and the Malikis said: He is the third of three, one of whom is God, as Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said. This has already been mentioned in Surah Maryam. So woe to those who have wronged, meaning they disbelieved and associated others with God, as in Surah Maryam, from the punishment of a painful Day, meaning the pain of His punishment. And similar to it: a sleeping night, meaning he sleeps in it.
43:66: The Almighty’s statement: Do they await meaning the parties are not awaiting anything but the Hour meaning the Resurrection, that it should come upon them suddenly meaning suddenly, while they do not perceive they are aware. This has been mentioned in more than one place. It has been said that the meaning is that the polytheists of Arabia are not awaiting anything but the Hour, and the parties according to this are those who formed parties against the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and denied him from the polytheists. This is connected to the Almighty’s statement: They did not present it to you except to argue.
43:67: The Almighty said: Friends on that Day meaning the Day of Resurrection, will be enemies to one another meaning enemies, they will be hostile to one another and curse one another except the righteous for they will be friends in this world and the Hereafter. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others said the same. Al-Naqqash narrated that this verse was revealed about Umayyah ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi and Uqbah ibn Abi Mu’ayt, who were two close friends. Uqbah used to sit with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Quraysh said: Uqbah ibn Abi Mu’ayt has become an apostate. Umayyah said to him: My face is forbidden to you if I meet Muhammad and do not spit in his face. Uqbah did that, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, vowed to kill him, so he killed him on the day of Badr patiently, and he killed Umayyah in the battle. This verse was revealed about them. Al-Tha’labi, may God be pleased with him, mentioned this verse and said: There were two believing friends and two disbelieving friends. Then one of the believers died and said: O Lord, so-and-so used to command me to obey You and obey Your Messenger. And he used to command me to do good and forbid me from evil, and tell me that I will meet You, O Lord, so do not lead him astray after me, and guide him as You have guided me, and honor him as You have honored me. So when his believing friend dies, God brings them together, and God the Most High says: Let each of you praise his companion. So he says: O Lord, he used to command me to obey You and obey Your Messenger, and command me to do good and forbid me from evil, and tell me that I will meet You. So God the Most High says: What an excellent friend, what an excellent brother, and what an excellent companion he was. So one of the disbelievers dies and he says: O Lord, so-and-so used to forbid me from obeying You and obeying Your Messenger, and command me to do evil and forbid me from good, and tell me that I will not meet You. So I ask You, O Lord, not to guide him and to lead him astray as You led me astray, and to humiliate him as You humiliated me. So when his disbelieving friend dies, God the Most High says to them: Let each of you praise his companion. So he says: O Lord, he used to command me to disobey You and to disobey Your Messenger, and he orders me to do evil and forbids me from good and tells me that I will not meet you, so I ask you to double the punishment for him, and God Almighty says: What a bad companion, brother and friend you were, and each one of them curses the other. I said: The verse is general for every believer, pious person, unbeliever, and misguided person.
43:68: God Almighty says: O My servants, there is no fear concerning you today, nor will you grieve. Muqatil said: Al-Mu'tamir bin Sulayman narrated it on the authority of his father: A caller will call out in the gathering places, O My servants, there is no fear for you today. The gathering will raise their heads and the caller will say, Those who believed in Our verses and were Muslims. (al-Zukhruf 43:69), so the people of other religions, other than the Muslims, will lower their heads. Al-Muhasibi mentioned in Al-Ri'ayah: It has been narrated in this hadith that the caller will call out on the Day of Resurrection, O My servants, I have no fear for you today, nor will you grieve. So the creation will raise their heads, saying, We are the servants of God. Then he will call out a second time, Those who believed in Our verses and were Muslims. So the disbelievers will lower their heads, and the monotheists will remain with their heads held high. Then he will call out a third time, Those who believed and were righteous. So the people who committed major sins will lower their heads, and the righteous will remain with their heads held high. He has removed fear and grief from them, as He promised them, for He is the Most Generous of the generous. He does not forsake His friend nor does He abandon him at the time of destruction. And it was read, O My servants.
43:69: Those who believed in Our verses and were Muslims. Al-Zajjaj said: Those who is an accusative adjective for My servants, a vocative noun with an added meaning. It was also said: Those who believed is the predicate of a deleted subject or a subject and its predicate are deleted, meaning they are the ones who believed or those who believed will be told, Enter Paradise.
43:70: God Almighty says: Enter Paradise, you and your spouses, in happiness. Abu Bakr and Zur ibn Hubaysh read O My servants with the fat-ha on the ya’ and with it confirmed in both instances. That is why Nafi’, Ibn ‘Amir and Ruways confirmed it with a sukoon in both instances, and the rest omitted it in both instances, because it was recorded confirmed in the copies of the people of Ash-Sham and Madinah and nothing else. Enter Paradise means it will be said to them, Enter Paradise, or O My servants who have believed, enter Paradise, “you and your spouses,” the Muslim women in this world. It was also said: your companions from among the believers, or it was also said: your spouses from among the houris. You will be delighted means you will be honored. This was said by Ibn ‘Abbas. And dignity in the good position means you rejoice, and joy is in the heart. Qatadah said: they enjoy, and bliss is in the body. Mujahid said: you will be pleased, and joy is in the eye. Ibn Abi Nujayh said: you will be amazed, and amazement here means attaining what is interesting. Yahya ibn Abi Katheer said: it is delight in listening, and this has already been mentioned in (Ar-Rum).
43:71: It contains four issues: First: The Almighty’s statement: They will be served with plates of gold and cups. That is, in Paradise they will have food and drinks served with them in plates of gold and cups. He did not mention the food and drinks because he knows there is no point in serving them with plates and cups without there being anything in them. He mentioned the gold in the plates and this dispensed with repeating the mention of cups, like the Almighty’s statement: And men who remember God much and women who remember (al-Ahzab 33:35). And in the two Sahihs: “On the authority of Hudhayfah that he heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘Do not wear silk or brocade, and do not drink from vessels of gold and silver, and do not eat from their plates, for they are for them in this world and for you in the Hereafter.’” And it was previously mentioned in Surat al-Hajj that whoever eats from them in this world or wears silk in this world and does not repent, that will be forbidden in the Hereafter, a permanent prohibition, and God knows best. The commentators said: Seventy thousand boys will be served with seventy thousand plates of gold to the lowest of them in Paradise, and they will be given them in the morning, each one of which will have a different color.” He will eat from the last part just as he eats from the first, and he will taste the last part just as he tastes the first. None of them will resemble each other. He will be given the same comfort and seven hundred thousand boys will circulate around the highest of them in degree every day, with each boy a plate of gold, in which there will be a type of food not found in the other. He will eat from the last part just as he eats from the first, and he will taste the last part just as he tastes the first. None of them will resemble each other. And cups means cups will be circulated around, as God Almighty said: There will be circulated around them vessels of silver and cups (al-Insan 76:15). Ibn al-Mubarak said: Muammar told us on the authority of a man on the authority of Abu Qilabah who said: They will be given food and drink, and when it is the last part of that, they will be given pure drink, and their stomachs will swell because of that, and a sweat will flow from their skins that is more fragrant than the scent of musk. Then he recited: A pure drink (al-Insan 76:21). In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The people of Paradise will eat They drink and do not urinate, defecate, or blow their noses. They said, What about the food? He said, “Belching and belching like the odor of musk. They are inspired to glorify God, praise Him, and extol God Almighty.” In another narration, Just as they are inspired to breathe. Second: The Imams narrated from the hadith of Umm Salamah, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: ‘Whoever drinks from vessels of gold and silver is only swallowing fire from Hell into his stomach.’” And he said: Do not drink from vessels of gold and silver, and do not eat from their plates. This indicates prohibition, and there is no disagreement about that. People differed about its use for other purposes. Ibn al-Arabi said: “The correct view is that it is not permissible for a man to use it for anything, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said about gold and silk: ‘These two are forbidden for the males of my nation, but permissible for its females.’ The prohibition of eating and drinking from it indicates the prohibition of its use, because it is a type of commodity, so eating and drinking are not permissible in principle. The reason for that is to hasten the matter of the Hereafter, and in that case eating, drinking, and all other forms of benefit are equal. And because he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘It is for them in this world and for us in the Hereafter.’ So he did not give us a share in it in this world.” Third: If the vessel is plated with them or has a ring of them, then Malik said: I do not like it to be drunk from, and likewise a mirror has a ring of silver, and I do not like it to be seen in it. Anas had a vessel plated with silver and he said: I gave the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) water to drink from it. Ibn Sirin said: It had an iron ring, so Anas wanted to put a silver ring in it, but Abu Talha said: I will not change anything that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did, so he left it. Fourth: If it is not permissible to use it, then it is not permissible to own it, because what is not permissible to use is not permissible to own, such as idols and tambourines. In the books of our scholars, it is obligatory to pay the value of whoever breaks it, but this is a corrupt meaning, because if it is broken, then there is no price for its value, and it is not permissible to evaluate it in zakat under any circumstances, and other than this is not to be paid attention to. God Almighty said: with plates. Al-Jawhari said: The plate is like the bowl, and the plural is plates. Al-Kisa’i said: The largest of the plates is the bowl, then the plate, which fills ten, then the plate, which fills five, then the queen, which fills two or three men, then the plate, which fills one man, and the plate is the book, and the plural is plates and plates. God Almighty says: And cups. Al-Jawhari said: A cup is a jug without a handle, and the plural is cups. Al-A’sha said, describing wine: A delicious, creamy dish with a hint of butter between its cup and ear Another said: Reclining, its doors slamming, the servant rushes towards it with a cup Qatada said: The round cup with a short neck and a short handle, and the pitcher: the rectangular neck and long handle. Al-Akhfash said: The cups are the pitchers without spouts. Qatrub said: They are the pitchers without handles. Mujahid said: They are the vessels with round mouths. Al-Suddi: They are the ones without ears. Ibn Aziz: Cups are pitchers without handles or spouts, and its singular is cup. I said: This is the meaning of what Mujahid and Al-Suddi said: It is the doctrine of the linguists that it is the one that has no ears or nakedness. God the Almighty says: And therein is whatever the souls desire and the eyes delight in. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Sulayman ibn Buraydah on the authority of his father that a man asked the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), O Messenger of God, are there horses in Paradise? He said: If God admits you to Paradise, you will not wish to be carried on a horse of red rubies that will fly with you wherever you wish in Paradise. A man asked him, O Messenger of God, are there camels in Paradise? He did not say to him the same as he said to his companion. He said: If God admits you to Paradise, you will have therein whatever your soul desires and your eyes delight in. The people of Madinah, Ibn ‘Amir, and the people of Ash-Sham read, And therein is whatever the souls desire. The rest read, The souls desire, meaning what the souls desire. You say, The one I struck Zayd, meaning those whom Zayd struck. And the eyes delight in, you say, The thing is delicious, and I found it delicious. And I enjoyed it and I took pleasure in it means, that is, in Paradise there is that which the eye takes pleasure in, so it was a beautiful sight. Saeed bin Jubair said: And the eyes take pleasure in looking at God Almighty, as in the hadith: I ask You for the pleasure of looking at Your face, “and you will abide therein” remaining permanently, because if it were to be cut off, it would be hated.
43:72: The Almighty said: And that Paradise meaning it will be said to them: This is that Paradise which was described to you in this world. Ibn Khalawayh said: The Almighty referred to Paradise with that and to Hell with this, to frighten with Hell and emphasize the warning against it, and He made it with the reference close like the present one which is seen, which you inherited because of what you used to do. Ibn Abbas said: God created for every soul a Paradise and a Hell, so the disbeliever inherits the Hellfire of Hell, and the Muslim inherits the Paradise of the disbeliever. This has been mentioned previously with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet in: The believers have succeeded [Surat Al-Baqarah, verse 200], from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, and also in Al-A’raf.
43:73: God Almighty says: Therein you will find abundant fruit, from which you will eat. Fruits are well-known, and their types are fruits, and the fruit seller is the one who sells them. Ibn Abbas said: They are all fruits, fresh and dry, meaning that in Paradise, in addition to food and drink, they will have many fruits from which they will make.
43:74: The Almighty says: Indeed, the criminals will abide eternally in the punishment of Hell. When He mentioned the conditions of the people of Paradise, He also mentioned the conditions of the people of Hell to demonstrate the superiority of the obedient over the disobedient.
43:75: The Almighty says: It will not be lightened for them meaning that the torment will not be lightened for them, and they will be in despair therein meaning that they will have lost hope in mercy. It was also said: They will be silent in a state of despair, and this has already been mentioned in Al-An’am.
43:76: God Almighty says: And We did not wrong them with punishment, but it was they who were the wrongdoers themselves with polytheism. It is permissible to say but it was they who were the wrongdoers in the nominative case as the subject and predicate, and the sentence is the predicate of was.
43:77: The Almighty said: And they will call out, 'O Malik!' He is the keeper of Hell, who created it for His wrath. When he rebukes the Fire with a rebuke, some parts of it will smite others. Ali and Ibn Mas`ud, may God be pleased with them, read And they will call out, 'O Mal!' This is contrary to the Mushaf. Abu al-Darda` and Ibn Mas`ud said: "The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, read: And they will call out, 'O Mal!'" with the lam specifically, meaning he softened the name and deleted the kaf. Tarkhīm is deletion, and from this is the tarkhīm of the name in calling out, which is to delete one or more letters from its end. So you say for Malik, 'O Mal!' and for Harith, 'O Har!' and for Fatimah, 'O Fatimah!' and for Aisha, 'O Aisha!' and for Marwan, 'O Marw!' And so he said: Oh Har, I will not let you throw me a disaster that no commoner or king has ever faced before me. Imru' al-Qais said: I see lightning, I will show you its flash, like the glitter of hands crowned with love for me He also said: Fatima, stop this pampering. If you have decided to break up with me, then be nice. Another said: Oh Marwa, my mount is imprisoned, hoping for blessings, but its Lord has not despaired. In the authentic hadith i.e., so, come, you have two options for the end of the shortened noun: One of them is to leave it as it was before the deletion, and the other is to build it with the damma, like: O Zaid, as if you put it in its place and did not pay attention to the deleted word.
