Abu Bakr al-Anbari said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Marwazi told us, he said: Muhammad, who is Ibn Sa’dan, told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of al-Hakam ibn ‘Uyaynah, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: We did not know what az-Zukhruf was until we found it in the recitation of ‘Abdullah a house of gold, and we did not know and they called out, O Malik or O Malik with the fatha or kasra of the lam until we found it in the recitation of ‘Abdullah and they called out, O Mal with the shortening. Abu Bakr said: This hadith should not be acted upon because it is disconnected and its like is not accepted in narration from the Messenger, peace be upon him, and the Book of God is more deserving of being taken into account and falsehood being denied from it. I said: In Sahih al-Bukhari, on the authority of Safwan ibn Ya`la, on the authority of his father, he said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, reciting on the pulpit: And they will cry out, ‘O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us!’ with the qaf, and Muhammad ibn Ka`b al-Qurazi said: It has reached me or been mentioned to me that the people of Hell sought help from the keepers, so God Almighty said: And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell, ‘Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment.’ (Ghafir 40:49), so they asked for one day to lighten their punishment, and it replied: Did not your messengers come to you with clear proofs? They said, Yes. They said, Then call upon Him, but the call of the disbelievers is not but in error. (Ghafir 40:50), he said: When they despaired of what the keepers had, they called upon Malik, who was over them and had a seat in the middle of it, and bridges over which the angels of punishment passed, so he could see its farthest point as he could see its nearest point, so they said: O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us! They asked for death. He said: So He remained silent about them and did not answer them for eighty years. He said: The year is three hundred and sixty days, the month is thirty days, and the day is like a thousand years of your reckoning. Then he looked at them after the eighty and said: You will remain. He mentioned the hadith, mentioned by Ibn al-Mubarak. In the hadith of Abu al-Darda’, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: They will say: Call upon Malik. They will say: O Malik, let your Lord finish us off. He said: You will remain.” Al-A’mash said: I was informed that between their call and Malik’s answering them is a thousand years. Narrated by al-Tirmidhi. Ibn Abbas said: They say that, but he does not answer them for a thousand years, then he says: You will remain. Mujahid and Nawf al-Bakali said: Between their call and his answering them is a hundred years. Abdullah ibn Amr said: Forty years. Ibn al-Mubarak mentioned it.
43:78: God Almighty says: We have certainly brought you the truth, but most of you hate the truth. It is possible that this is from what Malik said to them, meaning that you will remain in the Fire because We came to you with the truth in this world and you did not accept it. It is possible that it is from the speech of God to them today, meaning that We explained the evidence to you and sent messengers to you. But most of you Ibn Abbas said: But most of you means but all of you. It was said that by most he meant the leaders and commanders among them, and as for the followers, they had no effect. To the truth meaning to Islam and the religion of God are averse.
43:79: God Almighty says: Or have they decided upon a matter? Then We, too, have decided upon it. Muqatil said: It was revealed regarding their plot to deceive the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Dar al-Nadwa, when they had settled on what Abu Jahl had suggested to them, that a man from each tribe should come forward to participate in killing him, so that the demand for his blood would be weakened. So this verse was revealed, and God killed all of them at Badr. abramu they made perfect, and abram is the making of things. I abram something means I made it perfect, and abram the fighting if he made the killing perfect, and it is the second killing, and the first is Suhail, as he said:.....From Sahil and Mubram The meaning is: Or have they planned a plan, then We will plan a plan for them? Ibn Zayd, Mujahid, and Qatadah said: Or have they agreed to deny it, then We will agree to punish them with resurrection. Al-Kalbi said: Or have they decided a matter, then We will decide upon them with punishment. And or means rather. It was said: Or have they decided is in apposition to His statement: Have We appointed other than the Most Merciful gods to be worshipped? (al-Zukhruf 43:45). It was said: That is, We have brought you the truth, but you did not listen. Or have they listened, but turned away, because they decided in themselves a matter in which they believed in the punishment.
43:80: The Almighty says: Or do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private conversations? That is, what they keep secret within themselves and whisper among themselves. Yes, We hear and know. And Our messengers are with them, writing down. That is, the guardian angels are with them, writing down what they say. It was narrated that this was revealed about three men who were between the Kaaba and its curtains. One of them said: Do you think that God hears our speech? The second said: If you speak aloud, He hears, but if you speak in secret, He does not hear. The third said: If He hears when you speak out, then He hears when you speak in secret. This was stated by Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi. This meaning was previously mentioned from Ibn Mas’ud in Surat Fussilat.
43:81: The Almighty’s saying: “Say: If the Most Gracious had a son, then I would be the first of his worshippers.” There is a difference of opinion regarding its meaning. Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, and Al-Suddi said: The meaning is that the Most Gracious had no son. If means what, and the speech is complete on this basis. Then you begin: Then I would be the first of his worshippers, meaning the monotheists of the people of Mecca, on the basis that he had no son. The pause at the worshippers is complete. It was said: The meaning is: Say, O Muhammad, if it is proven that God had a son, then I would be the first to worship his son. However, it is impossible for him to have a son, and it is as you say to someone you are debating: If what you said is proven by evidence, then I would be the first to believe it. This is an exaggeration in the improbability, meaning there is no way to believe it. This is a softening of speech, like His saying: And either we or you are upon guidance or in manifest error. (Saba’: 24) The meaning on this basis is: Then I am the first of those who worship that son, because glorifying a son is glorifying a father. Mujahid said: The meaning is: If the Most Gracious had a son, then I would be the first to worship him. Alone, as he has no son, and Al-Suddi also said: The meaning is if he had a son I would have been the first to worship him as he had a son, but that is not appropriate, Al-Mahdawi said if according to these sayings is for the condition, and it is the best, and it is the choice of Al-Tabari, because its meaning is what is imagined with it that the meaning was not for him in the past, and it was said: The meaning of the worshippers is the two worshippers, and some scholars said, if it was like that it would be the two worshippers, and likewise Abu Abd Al-Rahman and Al-Yamani read so I am the first of the worshippers without an alif, it is said: a servant worships a servant with the movement if he is proud and angry then he is a servant, and the name is servanthood, like pride, on the authority of Abu Zaid Al-Farazdaq said: Those are my companions, so bring me someone like them, and I will hate to satirize Kulayb with a dram. He also chants: These are people who, if they satirize me, I will satirize them. I would rather not satirize Kulayb in Daram. Al-Jawhari said: Abu Amr said: The Almighty’s saying: So I am the first of the worshippers comes from the word anf annūf and angry. Al-Kisa’i and Al-Qutbi said the same, and Al-Mawardi narrated it from them. Al-Harawi said: The Almighty’s saying: So I am the first of the worshippers is said to be from ‘abd ya’budu, meaning from al-‘afinīn. Ibn ‘Arafa said: It is only said that ‘abd ya’budu a slave is a slave, and it is rarely said ‘ābīd. The Qur’an does not come with a little of the language or the unusual, but the meaning is: So I am the first of those who worship God Almighty, as He is One and has no children. It was narrated that a woman entered upon her husband and gave birth to a child from him after six months. This was mentioned to ‘Uthman, may God be pleased with him, so he ordered that she be stoned. ‘Ali said to him: God Almighty said: And his gestation and weaning is thirty months. (al-Ahqaf 46:15), and He said in another verse: And his weaning is in two years. (Luqman 31:14), so by God, he did not worship ‘Uthman until he sent for her to return. ‘Abdullah bin Wahb said: meaning he did not disdain or become accustomed. Ibn Al-A’rabi said: So I am the first of the worshippers means… The angry ones, and it was said: So I am the first of the worshippers meaning I am the first to worship Him in His Oneness, opposing you. Abu Ubaidah: Its meaning is the deniers, and it was said: He worshipped my right, meaning he denied me, and the people of Kufa, except for Asim, read son with a damma on the waw and a sukoon on the lam, the rest and Asim son and it was mentioned before.
43:82: Glory be to the Lord of the heavens and the earth meaning, in glorification and sanctification of Him, He has purified Himself from everything that requires occurrence, and He commanded the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to be purified, from what they describe meaning from what they say of lies.
43:83: The Almighty’s saying: So leave them to plunge into falsehood and play meaning the disbelievers of Mecca when they denied the punishment of the Hereafter, that is, leave them to plunge into their falsehood and play in their worldly life, until they meet their promised Day either the punishment in this world or in the Hereafter. It was said that this was abrogated by the verse of the sword. It was said that it is decisive, but it was presented as a threat. Ban Muhaisin, Mujahid, Hamid, Ibn al-Qa’qa’, and Ibn al-Samiq’ read until they meet with a fat-ha on the ya’ and a sukoon on the lam without an alif, and a fat-ha on the qaf here and in at-Tur and at-Ma’arij the rest read yilaqa. God Almighty says: And He is God in the heaven and God on the earth, and He is the Wise, the Knowing. This is a denial of their claim that God has a partner and a son, meaning that He is the One who deserves to be worshipped in the heavens and the earth. Umar may God be pleased with him and others said: The meaning is that He who is in the heavens is a god on the earth, and this is how he recited it. The meaning is that He is worshipped in them. It was narrated that he, Ibn Mas`ud, and others recited: And He who is in the heavens is God and on the earth is God. This is contrary to the Qur’an. God is raised as the predicate of a deleted subject, meaning that He who is in the heavens is a god. Abu `Ali said this, and its deletion is good due to the length of the speech. It was said: In means on, like the Most High’s statement: And I will surely crucify you on the trunks of palm trees (Ta-Ha: 71), meaning on the trunks of palm trees, meaning that He is able to dominate the heavens and the earth, And He is the Wise, the Knowing. It was mentioned above.
43:85: The Almighty said: And blessed is derived from barakah, and it has been mentioned before. And with Him is knowledge of the Hour meaning the time of its occurrence. And to Him you will be returned. Ibn Kathir, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa’i read and to Him they will be returned with a ya’, the rest with a ta’. Ibn Muhaisin, Hamid, Ya’qub, and Ibn Ishaq used to open the first letter according to their principles. The rest used a damma.
43:86: There are two issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: Except he who bears witness to the truth. “From” is in the accusative case, and what is meant by those they invoke besides Him are Jesus, Ezra, and the angels. The meaning is that these do not possess intercession except for he who bears witness to the truth and believes with knowledge and insight. This was said by Sa’id ibn Jubayr and others. He said: The testimony of truth is there is no god but God. It was also said that from is in the nominative case, meaning that those they invoke besides Him do not possess intercession, meaning the gods according to the statement of Qatadah, meaning that they do not intercede for their worshippers except he who bears witness to the truth, meaning Ezra, Jesus, and the angels, for they bear witness to the truth and the Oneness of God, and they know, the reality of what they bore witness to. It was said that it was revealed because Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith and a group of Quraysh said: If what Muhammad says is true, then we take the angels as our guardians, and they are more deserving of intercession for us than he. So God revealed: And those they invoke besides Him do not possess intercession except for he who bears witness to the truth. That is, they believed that the angels, idols, jinn, or devils intercede for them, and no one has intercession. On the Day of Resurrection, except for he who bears witness to the truth, meaning the believers if they are given permission. Ibn Abbas said: except for he who bears witness to the truth, meaning he bears witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. It was also said: These worshippers other than God do not have the power to have anyone intercede for them except for he who bears witness to the truth, for he who bears witness to the truth will be interceded for, but he who bears witness to the truth will not be interceded for. Except means but, meaning the polytheists will not attain intercession, but he who bears witness to the truth will attain intercession. So it is a disjunctive exception, and it is permissible for it to be connected, because in the phrase those they invoke other than Him are the angels. It is said: I interceded for him and I interceded for him, like I entrusted him and I entrusted him. The meaning of intercession and its derivation have already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah, so there is no point in repeating it. It was also said: except for he who bears witness to the truth, except for he for whom the angels bear witness that he was on the truth in this world, despite their knowledge of that from him, because God informed them of it, or because they witnessed him on the faith. Second: The Almighty’s statement: Except for those who bear witness to the truth while they know indicates two meanings: The first is that intercession for the truth is not beneficial except with knowledge, and that imitation is of no use without knowledge of the validity of the statement. The second: The condition of all testimonies in rights and other things is that the witness be knowledgeable about them, and similar to it is what was narrated “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: If you see something like the sun, then bear witness, otherwise leave it,” and this has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah.
43:87: The Almighty said: And if you ask them, ‘Who created them?’ they will surely say, ‘God.’ That is, they will acknowledge that God created them after they were nothing. Then how are they deluded? That is, how can they turn away from His worship and turn away from it until they associate others with Him, hoping for their intercession for him? It is said: afkahu ya’fuka afkān, meaning he turned him away and diverted him from something. From this is the Almighty’s saying: They said, ‘Have you come to us to turn us away from our gods?’ (al-Ahqaf 46:22). It was said: That is, if you ask the angels and Jesus who created them, they will say, God. “Then how are they deluded?” That is, how can these people be deluded in their claim that they are gods?
43:88: God Almighty said: And he said, ‘O my Lord, these are a people who do not believe.’ In qaylah there are three readings: accusative, genitive, and nominative. As for the genitive, it is the reading of Asim, Hamza, and the rest of the seven in the accusative. As for the nominative, it is the reading of al-A’raj, Qatadah, Ibn Hurmuz, and Muslim ibn Jundub. Whoever reads it in the genitive case takes it to mean: And with Him is knowledge of the Hour and knowledge of his qaylah. Whoever reads it in the accusative case takes it to mean: And with Him is knowledge of the Hour and He knows his qaylah. This is the preferred choice of al-Zajjaj. Al-Farra’ and al-Akhfash said: It is possible that wa qaylah is an exaggeration in His statement: We do not hear their secrets and their private conversations Az-Zukhruf 43:80. Ibn al-Anbari said: I asked Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Mubarrad: How do you put qaylah in the accusative case? So he said: He put it in the accusative case on And with Him is knowledge of the Hour and He knows what is said, so from this perspective it is not appropriate to stop at you will return nor at they know, and it is appropriate to stop at they write. Al-Farra’ and Al-Akhfash permitted putting the word qayl in the accusative case with the meaning: We do not hear their secrets, their whispers, and their words, as we mentioned from them. So from this perspective it is not appropriate to stop at they write. Al-Farra’ and Al-Akhfash also permitted putting it in the accusative case on the source, as if he said: And he said his words, and he complained his complaint to God Almighty as Ka’b bin Zuhair said: The informers walked by her side and said, O son of Abi Salma, you will be killed. He wanted: And they say their saying: And whoever raises his saying, then the estimation is: And with him is his saying, or his saying is heard, or his saying. This saying: Al-Zamakhshari: And what they said is not strong in meaning with the occurrence of a separation between the conjoined and the conjoined to it with what does not make an objection good and with the dissonance of the system, and stronger than that and more appropriate is that the accusative and genitive are based on the omission of the letter of the oath and its deletion, and the nominative is based on their saying: The oath of God and the trust of God and the oath of God and by your life, and his saying: Indeed, these are a people who do not believe is the answer to the oath, as if he said: And I swear by his saying, O Lord, or his saying, O Lord, my oath, that these are a people who do not believe, and Ibn Al-Anbari said: And it is permissible in Arabic and his saying in the nominative case, on the condition that you raise it with the fact that these are a people who do not believe, Al-Mahdawi: Or it is based on the estimation of his saying, his saying, O Lord, so the second saying, which is the predicate, was deleted, and the position of O Lord is accusative with the implied predicate, and that is not impossible because the deletion of some of the relative pronoun was impossible and some of it remained, because the deletion of the saying It has been used so often that it has become like the one mentioned, and the ha’ in qaylah refers to Jesus, and it was said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it was mentioned when he said: Say, ‘If the Most Gracious had a son’ (al-Zukhruf 43:81), and Abu Qilabah read O Lord with the opening of the ba’, and qayl is a source like qawl, and from it is al-Naba 78:He forbade qayl and qall, and it is said: I said a saying and qayl and qalan, and in An-Nisa’: And who is more truthful than God in statement? (An-Nisa’: 122).
43:89: God Almighty says: “So pardon them and say, ‘Peace.’ And they are going to know.” Qatada said: He ordered him to forgive them, then he ordered him to fight them, so forgiveness was abrogated by the sword. And similarly, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: So pardon them turn away from them, “and say, ‘Peace,’” meaning, kindly, meaning he said to the polytheists of Mecca ‘You will soon know.’ Then this was abrogated in Surat Bara’ah by the words of God Almighty: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9:5). It was said: It is a decisive verse that was not abrogated. The reading of the common people is ‘They will soon know’ (with the letter ‘ya’) as if it is a message from God Almighty to His Prophet threatening him. Nafi’ and Ibn ‘Amir read ‘You will know’ (with the letter ‘ta’) as if it is from the Prophet’s address to the polytheists threatening him. (‘Peace’) is raised with the omission of ‘upon you,’ as Al-Farra’ said. Its meaning is the command to bid them farewell with peace, and he did not make it a greeting to them, as Al-Naqqash related. Shu’ayb ibn Al-Habhab narrated that he informed him of that, how to greet them, and God knows best.
44:1: It is Meccan by consensus, except for the saying of God Almighty: Indeed, We will remove the punishment for a little (al-Dukhan 44:15), and it is fifty-seven verses, and it was said: nine. In Musnad Ad-Darami, on the authority of Abu Rafi’, he said: Whoever recites Ad-Dukhan on Friday night will wake up forgiven and will be married to the houris. Al-Tha’labi narrated it on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever recites Ad-Dukhan on Friday night will wake up forgiven. In another wording, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever recites Ad-Dukhan at night will wake up forgiven by seventy thousand angels. And on the authority of Abu Umamah, he said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever recites Ha Mim Ad-Dukhan on Friday night or on Friday, God will build for him a house in Paradise.” father-in-law
44:2: God Almighty says: And the clear Book. If you make Ha Mim the answer to the oath, the speech will be complete when he says: the clear one.
44:3: God Almighty says: “Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night. Indeed, We were to warn.” Then you begin Indeed, We sent it down. And if you make Indeed, We were warners the answer to the oath which is the Book, you stop at warners and begin in it is distinguished every matter of wisdom. It was said: The answer is Indeed, We sent it down, and some grammarians denied it in terms of it being a description of the one sworn by, and the description of the one sworn by is not a response to the oath, and the ha’ in We sent it down is for the Qur’an, and whoever says: He swore by all the books, then his saying: Indeed, We sent it down is a metaphor for other than the Qur’an, as was explained at the beginning of Az-Zukhruf, and the blessed night is the Night of Decree, and it is said: the night of the middle of Sha’ban, and it has four names: the blessed night, the Night of Bara’ah, the Night of the Deed, and the Night of Decree, and it was described as blessed because of what God sends down on His servants in it of blessings, goodness, and reward. Qatada narrated on the authority of Wathilah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The scrolls of Abraham were sent down on the first night of Ramadan, and the Torah was sent down six days before Ramadan, and the Psalms were sent down on the second of it. 10 of Ramadan, and the Gospel was sent down on the eighteenth of Ramadan, and the Qur’an was sent down on the twenty-fourth of Ramadan.” Then it was said that the entire Qur’an was sent down to the lowest heaven on this night, then it was sent down star by star on the rest of the days according to the agreement of causes. And it was said that what was sent down on every Night of Decree was sent down on the rest of the year. And it was said that the beginning of the sending down was on this night. And Ikrimah said: The night here is the night of the middle of Sha’ban. And the first is more correct, because of the saying of God Almighty: Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree [al-Qadr 97:Surah Al-Baqarah, verse two hundred]. Qatada and Ibn Zayd said: God sent down the entire Qur’an on the Night of Decree from the Mother of the Book to the House of Honour in the lowest heaven, then God sent it down to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the nights and days over twenty-three years. And this meaning has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah when God Almighty said: The month of Ramadan in which the Qur’an was sent down (al-Baqarah 2:185), and it will come later, God willing.
44:4: God Almighty says: Therein is distinguished every wise matter. Ibn Abbas said: God decides the affairs of this world for the next year on the Night of Decree, whether it be life, death, or provision. Qatadah, Mujahid, Al-Hasan, and others said the same. It was also said: Except for misery and happiness, for they do not change. Ibn Umar said this. Al-Mahdawi said: The meaning of this statement is that God, the Almighty, commands the angels regarding what will happen in that year, and that remains in His knowledge. Ikrimah said: “It is the night of the middle of Sha’ban, in which the affairs of the year are decided, the living are copied from the dead, and the pilgrims are recorded, so no one is added to them or subtracted from them.” Uthman bin Al-Mughira narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Deaths are cut off from one Sha’ban to the next, to the point that a man marries and has a child born to him, and his name has been recorded among the dead. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When it is the night of the middle of Sha’ban, then stand in prayer that night and fast that day, for God descends at sunset to the lowest heaven and says: ‘Is there anyone seeking forgiveness, so forgive him? Is there anyone afflicted, so heal him? Is there anyone seeking provision, so provide him? Is there such and such? Is there anyone seeking provision, so provide him? Is there such and such?’ until dawn comes.” Al-Tha’labi mentioned this. Al-Tirmidhi narrated with the same meaning on the authority of Aisha, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: ‘God Almighty descends on the night of the middle of Sha’ban to the lowest heaven and forgives more than the number of hairs on the sheep of Kalb.’” In this chapter, on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, Abu ‘Eesa said: We do not know of the hadith of Aisha as being traceable back to the Prophet except through the hadith of al-Hajjaj ibn Artah on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer on the authority of ‘Urwah on the authority of Aisha. I heard Muhammad classify this hadith as weak, and he said: Yahya ibn Abi Katheer did not hear from ‘Urwah, and al-Hajjaj ibn Artah did not hear from Yahya ibn Abi Katheer. I said: The author of Kitab Al-Aroos mentioned the hadith of Aisha at length, and he chose that the night in which every wise matter is distinguished is the night of the middle of Sha’ban, and that it is called the Night of Bara’ah. We have mentioned his statement and the response to it in other places, and that the correct view is that it is the Night of Decree as we have explained. Hammad bin Salamah narrated that Rabia bin Kulthum told us that a man asked Al-Hasan while I was with him, saying: O Abu Sa’eed, tell me about the Night of Decree. Is it in every Ramadan? He said: Yes, by God, besides whom there is no god, it is in every Ramadan. It is the night in which every wise matter is distinguished. In it, God decrees every creation, life span, provision and action until its like. Ibn Abbas said: It is written from the Mother of the Book on the Night of Decree what will happen in the year of death, life, provision and rain, even Hajj. It is said: So-and-so will perform Hajj and so-and-so will perform Hajj. And he said about this verse: Indeed, you see a man walking in the markets and his name has been included among the dead. This clarification of the rulings of the Sunnah is only for the angels who are entrusted with the causes of creation, and we have mentioned this meaning previously. Judge Abu Bakr Ibn al-Arabi said: “The majority of scholars are of the opinion that it is the Night of Decree, and among them are those who said: It is the night of the middle of Sha’ban, and this is false because God Almighty said in the Book of the Truthful and Decisive: “The month of Ramadan in which the Qur’an was revealed” (al-Baqarah 2:185). So he concluded that the time of its revelation is Ramadan, then he specified the night of its time here by saying: on a blessed night. So whoever claims that it is on any other night has made a great slander against God, and there is no reliable hadith about the night of the middle of Sha’ban, neither in its virtue nor in the abrogation of life spans in it, so do not pay attention to it. Al-Zamakhshari said: “And it was said that the copying of that from the Preserved Tablet begins on the Night of Bara’ah and the completion occurs on the Night of Decree, so the copy of provisions is given to Michael, and the copy of wars to Gabriel, and likewise earthquakes, lightning strikes, and landslides.” And the copy of the deeds is to Ismail, the master of the lowest heaven, who is a great king, and the copy of the calamities is to the Angel of Death. And from some of them, he gives every worker the blessings of his deeds, so he casts his praise on the tongues of creation, and his awe on their hearts. And it was read nafariq with emphasis, and yaqrq each according to its construction for the agent and the accusative of kull and the differentiator is God Almighty, and Zaid bin Ali, may God be pleased with him, read nafariq with the letter nun every wise matter every matter of wisdom, meaning it is done according to what wisdom requires.
44:5: The Almighty said: A command from Us. Al-Naqqash said: The command is the Qur’an that God revealed from Him. Ibn Issa said: It is what God decreed on the blessed night regarding the affairs of His servants, and it is a source in the place of a state.
44:6: God Almighty says: “A mercy from your Lord. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.” And also a mercy from your Lord and according to Al-Akhfash they are two states, their meaning is, We sent it down commanding it and being merciful. Al-Mubarrad: a command is in the place of the verbal noun, and the meaning is: We sent it down sending down. Al-Farra’ and Al-Zajjaj: a command is accusative with yufreeq like your saying yufreeq farqan so command means separation so it is a verbal noun, like your saying: he strikes a strike. And it was said: yufreeq indicates that he is commanded, so it is a verbal noun that what precedes it works on it. Indeed, We were messengers, a mercy from your Lord Al-Farra’ said: mercy is the object of messengers, and mercy is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Zajjaj said: mercy is an object for it, meaning We sent him for mercy. And it was said: it is a substitute for his saying a command and it was said: it is a verbal noun. Al-Zamakhshari: a command is accusative for specificity. He made every command abundant by describing it as wise, then he increased its abundance and earned it grandeur by saying: I mean by this command a command. Obtained from Us, being from Us, and as Our knowledge and management require. In the reading of Zayd bin Ali a matter from Us it is a matter, and it supports its being in the accusative case for specificity. Al-Hasan read mercy on that it is mercy, and it supports its being in the accusative case as it is an object for it.
44:7: The Almighty’s saying: Lord of the heavens and the earth. The Kufians read Lord in the accusative case, while the rest read it in the nominative case, in response to His saying: Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. If you wish, it is in the nominative case, and the predicate is There is no god but Him. Or it is the predicate of a deleted subject, meaning: He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, and the accusative case is in apposition to your Lord. Likewise, your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers of old in the accusative case in both of them. Al-Shayzari narrated it from Al-Kisa’i. The rest read it in the nominative case as a resumption. Then it is possible that this address is to the one who acknowledges that God created the heavens and the earth, meaning if you are certain of Him, then know that He has the power to send messengers and send down books. It is permissible for the address to be to the one who does not acknowledge that He is the Creator, meaning they should know that He is the Creator and that He is the One who gives life and causes death. It was said: The one who is certain here is the one who wants certainty and seeks it, as you say: So-and-so seeks help, meaning he wants help, and he accuses, meaning he wants… Tihama
44:8: The Almighty says: There is no god but He; He gives life and causes death. That is, He is the Creator of the world, so it is not permissible to associate anyone with Him who is not able to create anything. He gives life and causes death. That is, He gives life to the dead and causes the living to die. Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers of old. That is, your Master and the Master of those who came before you. Beware of denying Muhammad, lest the punishment befall you.
44:9: The Almighty says: Rather, they are in doubt, playing. That is, they are not certain about what they show of faith and acknowledgment in their saying that God is their Creator. Rather, they say it in imitation of their fathers without knowledge, so they are in doubt. Even if they think that they are believers, they are playing with their religion as they see fit without any proof. It was said: They are playing, they attribute slander to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in mockery. And it is said of someone who turns away from admonitions: He is not playing. He is like a child who plays and does what he does not know the consequences of.
44:10: The Almighty said: Then await the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke. Await means, O Muhammad, await these disbelievers on the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke. This was said by Qatada. It was also said that its meaning is to memorize their statement so that you may bear witness against them on the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke. That is why the Haaf is called a watcher. I say three things about al-Dukhan 44:The first is that it is one of the signs of the Hour that has not yet come, and that it will remain on earth for forty days, filling the space between heaven and earth. As for the believer, it will be afflicted with something like a cold. As for the disbeliever and the wicked, it will enter their noses, piercing their ears and constricting their breathing. It is one of the effects of Hell on the Day of Resurrection. Among those who said that the smoke has not yet come are Ali, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, Abu Hurairah, Zayd ibn Ali, al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Malekah, and others. Abu Saeed al-Khudri narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet that it is smoke that will stir up the people on the Day of Resurrection. The believer will be afflicted with something like a cold, and the disbeliever will puff until it comes out of every ear. Al-Mawardi mentioned it, and in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu al-Tufayl, “On the authority of Hudhayfah ibn Asid al-Ghifari, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked out while we were talking and said: What are you talking about? They said: We are talking about the Hour. He said: It will not come until you see ten signs before it. So he mentioned the smoke, the Antichrist, the Beast, the rising of the sun from the west, the descent of Jesus, son of Mary, the emergence of Gog and Magog, and three landslides: one in the east, one in the west, and one in the Arabian Peninsula. The last of these will be a fire that will emerge from Yemen and drive the people to their place of assembly.” In a narration on the authority of Hudhayfah: “The Hour will not come until there are ten signs: an landslide in the east, one in the west, one in the Arabian Peninsula, the smoke, the Antichrist, the Beast of the earth, Gog and Magog, the rising of the sun from the west, and a fire that will emerge from the depths of Aden and drive the people to the place of assembly.” Al-Tha’labi also narrated it on the authority of Hudhayfah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The first of the signs will be the emergence of the Antichrist, the descent of Jesus, son of Mary, and a fire that will emerge from the depths of Aden, driving the people to the place of assembly and spending the night with them wherever they spend the night.” And you take a nap with them when they say, and you wake up with them when they wake up, and you spend the evening with them when they spend the evening. I said, O Prophet of God, what is smoke? He said about this verse: Then await the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke that will fill the space between the east and the west and will remain for forty days and nights. As for the believer, he will be afflicted by it as if he had a cold, and as for the disbeliever, he will be like a drunkard, with smoke coming out of his mouth, nostrils, eyes, ears, and anus.” This is one opinion. The second opinion is that the smoke is what struck the Quraysh of hunger due to the supplication of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, until a man would see smoke between the sky and the earth. Ibn Mas’ud said: God removed it from them, and if it were the Day of Resurrection, He would not remove it from them. The hadith about him with this is in Sahih al-Bukhari, Muslim, and al-Tirmidhi. Al-Bukhari said: Yahya told me, he said: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Masruq, he said: Abdullah said: This only happened because when the Quraysh resisted the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he supplicated against them for years like the years of Joseph, and they were afflicted with drought and hardship until they ate bones. A man would look at the sky and see what was between him and it like smoke from the hardship, so God Almighty revealed: He said: So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was approached and it was said: O Messenger of God, ask God for rain for Mudar, for they have been destroyed. He said: For Mudar! You are indeed bold. Ask for rain and they were given rain. Then this verse was revealed: Indeed, you will return. Then when they were in prosperity, God, the Exalted, revealed: “The Day We shall strike with the greatest strike. Indeed, We will take retribution.” He said: It means the Day of Badr. Abu Ubaidah said: And the smoke and the drought. Al-Qatabi: It was called smoke because of the dryness of the earth when it rose from it like smoke. The third opinion is that it was on the day of the conquest of Mecca when the sky covered the dust, said Abd al-Rahman al-A’raj.
44:11: The Almighty’s saying: It covers the people is in the position of an attribute of the smoke. If it has happened as Ibn Mas’ud said, then it is specific to the polytheists of Mecca. If it is one of the signs of the Hour, then it is general based on what was mentioned previously. This is a painful torment means that God says to them: This is a painful torment. So whoever says that the smoke is a coming state, and it is said: This means painful is a narration of a past state, and whoever makes it future, then it is a narration of a coming state, and it is said: This means that, and it is said: that is, the people say to that al-Dukhan 44:This is a painful torment, and it is said: it is report of the approach of the matter, as you say: This is winter, so prepare for it.
44:12: God Almighty says: “Our Lord, remove the punishment from us. Indeed, we are believers.” That is, they say: Remove the torment from us we are believers, that is, we believe in You if You remove it from us. It was said that the Quraysh came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: If God removes this torment from us, we will submit. Then they preferred this statement. Qatada said: The torment here is smoke. It was also said: hunger, as narrated by al-Naqqash. She said: There is no contradiction, because the smoke was only from the hunger that afflicted them, as mentioned above. Hunger and famine may be called smoke, due to the dryness of the earth in a year of drought and the rise of dust due to the lack of rain. This is why a year of drought is called al-Ghubra’. It was also said that the torment here is snow. Al-Mawardi said: This has no basis, because this only happens in the Hereafter or among the people of Mecca, and Mecca was not from the lands of snow. However, it is said, so we narrated it.
44:13: God Almighty says: How can they be reminded? That is, how can they be reminded and admonished when the punishment comes, and there has come to them a clear Messenger, explaining to them the truth, and the reminder and the remembrance are one and the same, as Al-Bukhari said.
44:14: The Almighty said: Then they turned away from him meaning they turned away. Ibn Abbas said: That is, when will they learn a lesson, while God has kept them far from learning a lesson and remembering after they turned away from Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and denied him. It was also said: That is, how will their saying, We are believers benefit them after the punishment appears tomorrow or after the signs of the Hour appear? Knowledge has become necessary, and this is if you make the smoke an expected sign. And they said, 'A madman taught him' meaning, a human taught him or the priests and devils taught him, then he is mad and not a messenger.
44:15: The Almighty said: Indeed, We will remove the punishment for a little while. That is, for a short time. He promised to remove that punishment from them for a little while, that is, in a short time, so that it would be known that they would not fulfill their word, but would return to disbelief after it was removed. Ibn Mas`ud said this. So when it was removed from them by the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) praying for rain for them, they returned to denying it. And whoever said: The smoke is awaited, he said: By this he indicated what will be of the gap between one sign and another of the signs of the Hour, then whoever was decreed to be a disbeliever will continue in his disbelief. And whoever said this about the Day of Resurrection, he said: That is, if We removed the punishment from you, you would return to disbelief. And it was said: The meaning of Indeed, you will return is to Us, that is, you will be resurrected after death. And it was said: The meaning of Indeed, you will return is to the fire of Hell if you do not believe.
44:16: The Almighty’s saying: On the Day is based on what is indicated by Muntaqimoon, meaning We will take revenge on them on the Day We strike. Some grammarians have rejected this because what comes after in does not explain what comes before it. It has also been said that the one who acts on it is Muntaqimoon, which is also far-fetched, because what comes after in does not act on what comes before it, and it is not appropriate for it to be connected to His saying: Returning or His saying: Indeed, We will remove the punishment, since the meaning is not based on it. It is permissible to put it in the accusative case by implying a verb, as if he said: remind them or remember. It is also permissible for the meaning to be that you will return, so if you return, I will take revenge on you on the Day We strike with the greatest strike. For this reason, this was connected to the story of Pharaoh, for they promised Moses faith if He removed the punishment from them, then they did not believe until they drowned. It has been said: “Indeed, We will remove the punishment for a little while. Indeed, you will return.” This is a complete statement. Then He began: “On the Day We strike with the greatest strike. Indeed, We will remove the punishment for a little while. Indeed, you will return.” Muntaqimun meaning We take revenge on all the disbelievers. It was also said that the meaning is: Await the smoke and await the day We strike. So the conjunction waw was deleted, just as you say: Beware of the punishment. The great strike in the statement of Ibn Mas`ud means the day of Badr. This is the statement of Ibn `Abbas, Abu Ka`b, Mujahid, and Ad-Dahhak. It was also said that it means the punishment of Hell on the Day of Resurrection. This was stated by Al-Hasan, `Ikrimah, and Ibn `Abbas as well. Az-Zajjaj chose it. It was also said that it means smoke that falls in this world, or hunger or famine that falls, it was said, on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Mawardi said: It is possible that it means the Hour of Resurrection, because it is the end of his strikes in this world. It was also said that God took revenge on him, meaning He punished him. The noun for this is naqmah, and the plural is naqamaat. It was also said that there is a difference between naqmah and punishment. Punishment comes after the sin because it is part of the consequence, and naqmah may come before it. This was stated by Ibn `Abbas. It was also said that punishment is what is predetermined, and vengeance is not predetermined.
44:17: God Almighty says: And We had certainly tried before them the people of Pharaoh, and there came to them a noble messenger. That is, We tested them: The meaning of this trial and test is the command to obey, and the meaning is: We treated them as if they were being tested by sending Moses to them, but they denied and were destroyed. So this is what I will do to your enemies, O Muhammad, if they do not believe. It was also said: We tested them, that is, We tormented them by drowning. There is an inversion in the speech, and the meaning is: Indeed, a noble messenger came to the people of Pharaoh, and We tested them, that is, We drowned them, because the trial was after the coming of the messengers. The waw does not indicate order, and the meaning of noble is noble among his people. It was also said: noble in character by overlooking and forgiving. Al-Farra’ said: noble to his Lord, since He chose him for prophethood and to make him hear speech.
44:18: The Almighty said: That you deliver to me the servants of God. Ibn Abbas said: The meaning is that he came to them and said: Follow me. The servants of God is a vocative. Mujahid said: The meaning is send with me the servants of God and release them from the punishment. The servants of God in this case is the object. It was said: The meaning is that you listen to me so that I may deliver to you the message of my Lord: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger. That is, trustworthy with regard to the revelation, so accept my advice. It was said: Trustworthy with regard to what I demand from you, so I will not betray it.
44:19: The Almighty said: And do not exalt yourselves above God meaning do not be arrogant towards Him and do not rise above His obedience. Qatada said: Do not transgress against God. Ibn Abbas said: Do not fabricate lies against God. The difference between transgression and fabrication is that transgression is in action and fabrication is in words. Ibn Jurayj said: Do not magnify God. Yahya ibn Salam said: Do not be arrogant to the worship of God. The difference between glorification and arrogance is that glorification is the superiority of the powerful, and arrogance is the haughtiness of the despised. Al-Mawardi mentioned it: I come to you with clear authority. Qatada said: With an excuse of mine. Yahya ibn Salam said: With a clear argument, and the meaning is the same, meaning clear proof.
44:20: God Almighty said: And I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord, lest you stone me. As if they threatened to kill him, so he sought refuge in God. Qatada said: You stone with stones. Ibn Abbas said: You curse, and say, A lying magician. Nafi’, Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, Asim, and Ya’qub pronounced the dhal in ‘idhta and the rest assimilated it. The assimilating is for the sake of alleviation, and the pronunciation is according to the original. Then it was said: I sought refuge in God in what has passed, because God promised him and said: So that they will not reach you both (al-Qasas 28:35). It was said: I seek refuge, as you say I implore you by God, and I swear to you by God, meaning I swear.
44:21: The Almighty’s saying: And if you do not believe in me means if you do not believe me and do not believe in God for the sake of my proof, so the lam in li is a lam of ajal. It was also said: that is, if you do not believe in me, like His saying: So Lot believed in him (al-Ankabut 29:26), that is, in him. Then keep away from me means leave me alone, neither for me nor against me, as Muqatil said. It was also said: that is, be away from me and I will be away from you until God judges between us. It was also said: then leave me alone and refrain from harming me, and the meaning is close, and God knows best.
44:22: The Almighty’s saying: So he called upon his Lord is omitted, meaning they disbelieved, so he called upon his Lord, that these with the opening of an meaning that these, are a criminal people meaning polytheists, who refused to release the Children of Israel and to believe.
44:23: There are two issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: So travel by night with My servants, meaning, We answered his supplication and inspired him to travel by night with My servants, meaning those who believed in God from the Children of Israel, by night, meaning before morning, you will be pursued. The people of Hijaz read fasir with the alif connected, and so did Ibn Kathir, from sara. The rest read fasir with the sukoon, from asra, and it has been mentioned before, and the departure of Pharaoh behind Moses in Al-Baqarah, Al-A’raf, Taha, Ash-Shu’ara, and Yunus, and his drowning and the rescue of Moses, so there is no point in repeating it. Second: Moses, peace be upon him, was commanded to go out at night. Traveling at night is usually done out of fear, and fear can be of two types: either from the enemy, in which case the night is used as a curtain, so it is one of the curtains of God, the Most High; or out of fear of hardship for the animals and bodies, such as sea or drought, in which case travelling at night is an advantage. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would travel at night, at night, and be gentle and hasten, according to need and what the advantage dictates. In the Sahih, it is narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: If you travel in a time of fertility, then give the camels their share of the land, and if you travel during the year, then hasten to clean them. This has already been mentioned at the beginning of An-Nahl. Praise be to God.
44:24: God Almighty says: “And leave the sea in peace. Indeed, they are a drowned host.” Ibn Abbas said: Rahwan means a path. Ka’b and Al-Hasan said it, and from Ibn Abbas also: Samatan. Ad-Dahhak and Ar-Rabi’ said: Easy. Ikrimah said: Dry land, because of his saying: Then strike for them a dry path in the sea. (Ta-Ha 20:77) It was said: Parted. Mujahid said: Spread out. From him: Dry. From him: Staying. And it is well-known in the language. Qatada and Al-Harawi said it, and others said: Spread out. Ibn Arafa said: They both go back to one meaning, even though their wording differs, because if its flow stops, it opens up. And likewise, the sea would stop and open up for Moses, peace be upon him. Rahwan among the Arabs means still. It is said: The horses came Rahwan, meaning still. He said: And the horses tear at the reins like birds escaping from the hailstorm. Al-Jawhari: It is said: Do it at ease, meaning calmly, on your ease, and live comfortably, meaning calmly and at ease, and five raha, if it is easy, and the sea became calm, meaning it calmed down. Abu Ubaid said: He made the sea between his legs proud, meaning he opened it, and from this is the saying of the Most High: And leave the sea at ease. And pride is the easy walk. It is said: The camels came at ease, Ibn al-A’rabi said: He made the walk at ease, meaning he was gentle. Al-Qatami said in describing the riders: They walk slowly, neither the backs of their heads betray them nor do their hearts rely on them. Ar-Rahu and Ar-Rahwa: a high place, or a low place where water collects. They are opposites. Abu Ubaid said: Ar-Rahu is a hole in a straight area where rainwater and other water flows. And in a hadith that he ruled: There is no preemption in a courtyard, nor a road, nor a pass, nor a place of rest, nor a place of security, and all of them are raha’, and rahu is a woman with a wide waist, as narrated by Al-Nadr bin Shumayl, and rahu is a kind of bird and it is said: it is the crane, Al-Harawi said: It is possible that rahu is a description of Moses and Al-Qushayri said: meaning, walk quietly on your way, so rahu is a description of Moses and his people, not a description of the sea, and according to the first, it is a description of the sea, meaning leave it still as it is, it has separated, so do not order it to join until Pharaoh and his people enter, Qatada said: Moses wanted to strike the sea when he cut it with his staff until it was reunited, and he was afraid that Pharaoh would follow him, so this was said to him. And it was said: rahu is not from stillness, but rather it is the gap between two things, it is said: raha is between the two men, meaning a space, so his saying rahu means separated, and Al-Layth said: rahu is walking quietly, it is said: raha He calmly and quietly said: “He calmly and quietly said: ‘He calmly and quietly said: ‘He calmly and quietly said: ‘He calmly and quietly said: ‘He calmly and quietly said: ‘He calmly and quietly said: ‘He calmly and quietly said: ‘He calmly and quietly said: ‘He calmly and quietly said: ‘He calmly and quietly said: ‘He is a drowned army.’ He informed Moses of that to calm his heart.”
44:25: God Almighty says: How many gardens and springs did they leave behind? Kam is used to express abundance. The meaning of this verse has already been discussed in detail in Al-Shu'ara.
44:26: God Almighty says: And crops and a noble position.
44:27: The Almighty said: And a blessing in which they were reveling. Blessing with the fat-ha: enjoyment. It is also said: God’s blessing and His blessing, then you enjoy. A woman who is blessed and pampered has the same meaning. Blessing with the kasra is the hand, the favor, the favor, and what He bestowed upon you. Likewise, if you open the noon, you extend it and say: the blessings, and the blessings are the same. So-and-so is of abundant blessings, meaning abundant money. All of them are from al-Jawhari. Ibn Umar said: What is meant by blessing is the Nile of Egypt. Ibn Lahi’ah al-Fayyum: Ibn Ziyad: the land of Egypt due to its abundant goodness. It was said: what they were, so it is from spaciousness and ease. It is also said: blessing and blessing with the fat-ha and kasra of the noon, as narrated by al-Mawardi. He said: There are two aspects to the difference between them: One of them is that with the kasra of the noon it refers to kingship, and with the fat-ha it refers to the body and religion. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said. The second is that with the kasra it is from favor, which is favor and gift, and with the fat-ha it is from comfort, which is spacious living. Ibn Ziyad said it. I said: This is the difference that occurred in the Sahihs, and we have mentioned it. Abu Raja’, Al-Hasan, Abu Al-Ashhab, Al-A’raj, Abu Ja’far, and Shaiba read fakahin without an alif, and its meaning is ashreen batreen. Al-Jawhari said: A man fakaha in the kasra, so he is fakaha if he is in a good mood and jokes. Fakaha is also the arrogant one. It was read and comfort they were in it fakahin, meaning arrogant and ashreen, and fakahin means comfortable. Al-Qushayri: fakahin is carefree and joking. It is said: he is fakaha, meaning joking, and in it is jokes, meaning jokes. Al-Tha’labi: They are two dialects like al-haḍir and al-ḍarā, and al-farā and al-farah. It was said: a fakaha is one who enjoys various types of pleasure, just as an eater enjoys various types of fruit, and fruit is excess food that is indispensable.
44:28: God Almighty says: Likewise, We caused it to be inherited by another people. Al-Zajjaj said: “That is, the matter is thus, so it stops at thus. It was said that the kaf is in the accusative case, on the assumption that we do an action thus with those we want to destroy. Al-Kalbi said: thus I do with those who disobey me. It was said: thus was their affair, so they were destroyed. “And We gave it as an inheritance to another people” meaning the Children of Israel. God Almighty gave them the land of Egypt after they had been enslaved in it, so they became its inheritors, because that reached them like the arrival of inheritance. Similar to it is: And We gave inheritance to the people who had been oppressed the eastern and western parts of the earth (al-A’raf 7:137).
44:29: The Almighty said: So neither the heaven nor the earth wept for them meaning for their disbelief, nor were they reprieved meaning delayed from drowning. The Arabs used to say when a master died: The heavens and the earth wept for him, meaning his calamity spread throughout everything until the heavens and the earth wept for him, and the wind and lightning, and the winter nights wept for him. The poet said: The wind cries its sorrow and lightning flashes in the clouds Another said: The sun is rising, not eclipsed. The stars and the moon are crying for you. The Foreign Ministry said: Oh tree of Khabur, why are you still leafy as if you did not grieve for Ibn Tarif? This is by way of example and imagination, exaggerating the necessity of grieving and crying over him. The meaning is that they perished, so their calamity was not considered great and they did not feel any loss. It was said that there is an implied meaning in the speech, meaning that the people of heaven and earth from the angels did not cry over them, like the saying of God Almighty: And ask the town (Yusuf 12:82). Rather, they were pleased with their death. Al-Hasan said this. Yazid al-Raqashi narrated on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘There is no believer but that he has two doors in heaven from which his provision descends and a door from which his speech and deeds enter. When he dies, they miss him and cry over him.’ Then he recited: ‘And neither the heaven nor the earth wept for them,’ meaning that they did not do any righteous deed on earth for which they would cry, nor did any righteous deed ascend to heaven for which they would cry over that loss. Mujahid said: The heaven and the earth weep over the believer for forty mornings and they weep. Abu Yahya said: I was amazed by his statement, so he said: ‘Are you amazed! Why would the earth not weep over a servant who populates it with bowing and prostration?’” And why would the heavens not weep for a servant whose glorification and magnification therein make a buzz like the buzzing of bees?! Ali and Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them said that his place of prayer on earth and the place of ascent to heaven for his deeds weep for him. The meaning of the verse according to this is: So neither the places of ascent to heaven for his deeds nor the places of worship on earth wept for them. This is the meaning of the words of Sa`id ibn Jubayr: There are three aspects to the weeping of the heavens and the earth: First, it is like the well-known weeping of animals, and it is likely to be the words of Mujahid. Shuraih al-Hadrami said: “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Indeed, Islam began as something strange and will return to being strange as it began, so blessed are the strangers on the Day of Resurrection.’ It was said: ‘Who are they, O Messenger of God?’ He said: ‘They are those who, when people become corrupt, reform themselves.’ Then he said: ‘Beware, there is no estrangement for a believer. No believer dies in estrangement, absent from him, but the heavens and the earth weep for him.’ Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited: ‘So neither the heavens nor the earth wept for them.’ Then he said: ‘Beware, they do not weep for the disbeliever.’” I said: Abu Naim Al-Hafiz said: Muhammad bin Muammar told us: Shuaib Al-Harrani told us: Yahya bin Abdullah told us: Al-Awza’i told us: Ata’ Al-Khurasani told me: There is no servant who prostrates to God in any spot on earth except that it will bear witness for him on the Day of Resurrection and weep for him on the day he dies. It was said: Their weeping is the redness of their extremities. This was said by Ali bin Abi Talib may God be pleased with him, Ata’, Al-Suddi, Al-Tirmidhi, and Muhammad bin Ali. He narrated it from Al-Hasan. Al-Suddi said: When Al-Hussein bin Ali may God be pleased with them both was killed, the sky wept for him, and its weeping is its redness. Jarir narrated from Yazid bin Abi Ziyad, who said: When Al-Hussein bin Ali bin Abi Talib may God be pleased with them both was killed, the horizons of the sky turned red for him for four months. Yazid said: And its redness is its weeping. Muhammad bin Sirin said: They told us that the redness that occurs with twilight did not occur until Al-Hussein bin Ali may God be pleased with them both was killed. Sulayman Al-Qadi said: We were rained with blood on the day Al-Hussein was killed. I said: Al-Daraqutni narrated from the hadith of Malik bin Anas, from Nafi’, from Ibn Umar, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The twilight is the redness.’ And from Ubadah bin al-Samit and Shaddad bin Aws, they said: The twilight is the redness and the whiteness. So when the redness disappears, the prayer is permissible. And from Abu Hurayrah, he said: The twilight is the redness. This refutes what Ibn Sirin narrated, and it was mentioned previously in Subhan from Qurrah bin Khalid, who said: The sky did not weep for anyone except for Yahya bin Zakariya and al-Husayn bin Ali, and its redness is its weeping. And Muhammad bin Ali al-Tirmidhi said: Weeping is the flow of something, so when the eye flows with its water, it is said that it wept. And when the sky flows with its redness, it is said that it wept. And when the earth flows with its dust, it is said that it wept, because the believer is light and with him is the light of God, so the earth is illuminated by His light even if it is absent from your eyes. And if you lose the light of the believer, it becomes dusty and is covered with its dust, because it was dusty because of the sins of the polytheists. And it only becomes illuminated by the light of the believer, so when the believer is taken from it, it is covered with its dust. Anas said: When the day came that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) entered Medina, everything was illuminated. When the day came that he died, everything was darkened. We were burying him and we did not remove our hands from him until our hearts were filled with disbelief. As for the weeping of the sky, its redness is as Al-Hasan said. Nasr bin Asim said: The first signs are a redness that appears, and that is because of the nearness of the Hour, so it flows with weeping because of its emptiness of the lights of the believers. It was said: Its weeping is a sign that appears from it indicating grief and sorrow. I said: The first statement is more apparent, as there is no impossibility in that, if the heavens and the earth glorify, hear, and speak as we explained in Glory be to God, Mary, and Ha Mim Fussilat, then likewise they cry with what came in the report about that. God knows best the correctness of these statements.
44:30: God Almighty says: And We saved the Children of Israel from the humiliating punishment. Meaning what the Copts were doing to them by order of Pharaoh, such as killing their sons, using their women, enslaving them, and making them do hard labor.
44:31: The Almighty’s saying: From Pharaoh is a substitute for the humiliating torment. So from is not connected to His saying: from the torment, because it has been described, and it does not function after a description like a verb. It was said: That is, We saved them from the torment. And from Pharaoh: Indeed, he was exalted among the transgressors, that is, a tyrant among the polytheists. This is not a lofty position of praise, rather it is a lofty position in extravagance, like His saying: Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land (al-Qasas 28:4). It was said: This loftiness is the transgression of worshipping God.
44:32: The Almighty says: And We chose them meaning the Children of Israel. With knowledge meaning with Our knowledge of them due to the large number of prophets among them, over the worlds meaning the worldly people of their time, as evidenced by His statement to this nation, You are the best nation produced for mankind (Al Imran 3:110). This is the statement of Qatadah and others. It was also said: Over all the worlds because of the prophets He placed among them, and this is specific to them and not to others. This was narrated by Ibn ‘Isa, Al Zamakhshari and others. His statement: You are the best nation means after the Children of Israel, and God knows best. It was also said: This choice goes back to their deliverance from drowning and their inheritance of the land after Pharaoh.
44:33: The Almighty said: And We gave them of the signs meaning of the miracles of Moses, that which was a clear trial. Qatada said: The signs were their rescue from Pharaoh and the splitting of the sea for them, and the clouds shading them and the sending down of manna and quails. This address is directed to the Children of Israel. It was said that it was the staff and the hand. It is similar to what Al-Farra’ said: And the address is directed to the people of Pharaoh. A third statement is: It is the evil that he prevented them from and the good that he commanded them to do. This was said by Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid. The address is directed to both groups together, the people of Pharaoh and the Children of Israel. In His statement a clear trial there are four aspects: an apparent blessing, said Al-Hasan and Qatada, as God Almighty said: And that He may test the believers through Him with a good trial (al-Anfal 8:17). Zuhair said: So he gave them the best test that they could be given. The second: severe torment, said Al-Farra’. The third: a test that distinguishes the believer from the disbeliever, said Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid, and also from him: their trial with ease and hardship, then he recited: And We test you with evil and with good as trial (Al-Anbiya’: 35).
44:34: God Almighty says: These people say meaning the infidels of Quraysh.
44:35: God Almighty says: It is only our first death, and we will not be resurrected. “It is nothing but our first death” is the beginning of a statement, such as: It is nothing but your trial (al-A’raf 7:155), It is nothing but our worldly life (al-Mu’minun 23:37), And we will not be resurrected meaning we will not be resurrected.
44:36: Bring our fathers, if you should be truthful. God resurrected the dead, and they were resurrected. It has been mentioned previously. The resurrected are the ones who will be sent. It was said that the one who said this was from the infidels of Quraysh, Abu Jahl. He said: O Muhammad, if you are truthful in what you say, then send us two men from our fathers: one of them is Qusayy ibn Kilab, for he was a truthful man, so that we may ask him about what will happen after death. This statement by Abu Jahl is one of the weakest of doubts, because the return is for recompense, not for accountability. It is as if he said: If you are truthful in returning them for recompense, then return them for accountability. It is like the statement of someone: If he said that after us, a people will arise from among the sons, then why do not the fathers who have passed away return? Al-Mawardi related this. Then it was said: Bring our fathers is addressed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, alone, like His statement: My Lord, send us back (al-Mu’minun 23:99), as Al-Farra' said. It was also said that it is addressed to him and his followers.
44:37: The Almighty’s saying: Are they better or the people of Tubba’? This is a question of denial, meaning that they deserve, in this statement, the punishment, since they are not better than the people of Tubba’ and the destroyed nations. If We destroy those, then so will these. It was said: The meaning is, are they more abundant in blessings and wealth, or the people of Tubba’? It was said: Are they more honorable, stronger, and more secure, or the people of Tubba’? What is meant by Tubba’ is not a single man, but rather what is meant by it are the kings of Yemen. They used to call their kings Al-Taba’a, so Tubba’ is a title for their king, like the Caliph for the Muslims, Khosrau for the Persians, and Caesar for the Romans. Abu Ubaid said: Each one of them was called Tubba’ because he followed his companion. Al-Jawhari said: The Tubba’s are the kings of Yemen, and one of them is Tubba’, and Tubba’ is also a shadow. He said: The water returns to the enclosure and the sand dune. The sand dune returns to the quarry if it is thirsty. Al-Tubba' is also a type of bird. Al-Suhayli said: Tubba' is the name of every king who ruled Yemen, Ash-Shihr, and Hadhramaut. The king of Yemen alone was not called Tubba', as Al-Mas'udi said. Among the Tubba's are: Al-Harith Al-Ra'ish, who is the son of Hamal Dhu Saddad, Abraha Dhu Al-Manar, Amr Dhu Al-Adh'ar, Shimr bin Malik, to whom Samarkand is attributed, and Afriqis bin Qais, who drove the Berbers to Africa from the land of Canaan, and Africa was named after him. It is apparent from the verses that God, the Exalted, only intended one of these, and the Arabs knew him by this name more than they knew anyone else. Therefore, he, peace be upon him, said: I do not know whether Tubba’ is a specific person or not. Then it was narrated from him that he said: Do not curse Tubba’, for he was a believer. This indicates that he was a specific person, and God knows best, Abu Karb, who covered the Kaaba after he wanted to invade it, and after he invaded Medina and wanted to destroy it, then he turned away from it when he was informed that it was the place of emigration of a prophet named Ahmad. He said poetry that he entrusted to its people, and they inherited it from their ancestors until the Prophet, peace be upon him, emigrated, and they gave it to him. It is said that the book and poetry were with Abu Ayyub Khalid bin Zaid, and in it: I testify that Ahmad is a messenger from God, the Creator of all beings. If my life had been extended to his, I would have been his minister and cousin. Al-Zajjaj, Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, Al-Zamakhshari and others mentioned that a grave was dug for him in Sana’a, and it is said that it was in the Himyar region in Islam. Two healthy women were found in it, and at their heads was a silver tablet written in gold: This is the grave of Habibi and Lamis. It is also narrated: Habibi and Tamadhar. It is also narrated: “This is the grave of Radwa and the grave of Habibi, the daughters of Tubba’. They died while bearing witness that there is no god but God and they did not associate anything with Him, and the righteous died on that basis before them.” I said: Ibn Ishaq and others narrated that it was in the book he wrote: (As for what follows, I have believed in you and in your book that was revealed to you, and I am of your religion and your Sunnah, and I have believed in your Lord and the Lord of all things, and I have believed in all that came from your Lord of the laws of Islam. If I live to see you, then well and good, and if I do not live to see you, then intercede for me and do not forget me on the Day of Resurrection, for I am from your first nation and I pledged allegiance to you before your coming, and I am of your religion and the religion of Abraham, peace be upon him. Then he sealed the book and inscribed on it: To God belongs the command before and after.) And he wrote on its title: (To Muhammad ibn Abdullah, the Prophet of God and His Messenger, the Seal of the Prophets and the Messenger of the Lord of the Worlds, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the first Tubba.) We have mentioned the rest of his story and its beginning in Al-Lum’ Al-Lu’lu’iyyah, a commentary on the Ten Proofs of the Prophethood by Al-Farabi, may God have mercy on him. And from the day Tubba died until the day the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, a thousand years, no more and no less. There was a difference of opinion as to whether he was a prophet or a king. Ibn Abbas said: Tubba was a prophet. Ka’b said: Tubba was a king among the kings, and his people were soothsayers, and with them were people from the People of the Book. He ordered the two groups to bring a sacrifice, and they did so. The sacrifice of the People of the Book was accepted, and he converted to Islam. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: Do not curse Tubba, for he was a righteous man. Qatada narrated that Tubba was a man from Himyar. He marched with soldiers until he crossed Al-Hirah and came to Samarkand, which he destroyed. Al-Mawardi narrated it. Al-Tha’labi narrated from Qatada that he was Tubba Al-Himyari, and he marched in Janur until he crossed Al-Hirah, and he built Samarkand, and he killed and destroyed the country. Al-Kalbi said: Tubba is Abu Karb As’ad bin Maliki Karb, and he was only called Tubba because he was Tubba before him. Sa’id bin Jubayr said: He is the one who covered the Kaaba with ink. Ka’b said: God condemned his people, but He did not condemn him, and He used them as an example for the Quraysh because of their closeness to their home and their greatness in their souls. So when… God destroyed them and those before them because they were criminals. Whoever commits a crime with a weak hand and few numbers is more deserving of destruction. The people of Yemen were proud of this verse, as God made the people of Tubba better than Quraysh. It was said that the first of them was called Tubba because he followed the sun’s horn and traveled in the east with the armies. God the Almighty says: And those before them - We destroyed them. Those is in the nominative case in apposition to the people of Tubba’, We destroyed them is its relative clause, and those before them is related to it. It is also possible that those before them is the relative clause of those and that it is in the circumstance referring back to the relative pronoun. If that is the case, We destroyed them is in one of two cases: either already is estimated with it, in which case it is in the position of a circumstantial, or the deletion of a described word is estimated, as if he said: a people We destroyed, and the meaning is: Do you not consider that if We are able to destroy these mentioned, We are able to destroy the polytheists? It is possible that and those before them is the beginning of the predicate of We destroyed them, and it is possible that those is in the genitive case in apposition to Tubba’, as if he said: the people of Tubba’ who were destroyed before them. It is possible that those is in the accusative case with an implied verb indicated by We destroyed them, and God knows best.
44:38: The Almighty said: And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play. That is, heedless, as Muqatil said. It was also said: Heedless, which is what Al-Kalbi said.
44:39: The Almighty said: We did not create them except with the truth meaning except with the true command, as stated by Muqatil. It was also said: except for the truth, as stated by Al-Kalbi and Al-Hasan. It was also said: except to establish the truth and make it manifest through the Oneness of God and the commitment to obeying Him. This meaning has already been mentioned in the chapter on the prophets. But most of them meaning most people do not know that.
44:40: God Almighty says: The Day of Judgment is the appointed time for them all. The Day of Separation is the Day of Resurrection, and it was called thus because God Almighty will separate between His creation on it. The evidence for this is His statement, "Your wombs and your children will not benefit you on the Day of Resurrection. He will separate you." (al-Mumtahanah 60:3), and similar to this is His statement, And on the Day the Hour appears, that Day they will be separated. (Al-Rum: 14), The Day of Separation is the appointed time for all, as God Almighty said, Indeed, the Day of Separation is an appointed time. (al-Naba 78:17), meaning the time appointed to distinguish the wrongdoer from the good-doer, and to separate between them, one group in Paradise and one group in the Blaze. This is the ultimate warning and threat. There is no disagreement among Al-Farra' regarding raising their appointed time as the predicate of in and its subject is the Day of Separation. Al-Kisa'i and Al-Farra' permitted lowering their appointed time with in and the Day of Separation is an adverbial phrase in the position of the predicate of in, meaning that their appointed time is the Day of Separation.
44:41: The Almighty says: The Day when no protector will avail another at all. Day is a substitute for the first Day, and the protector is the cousin and the helper, meaning that Ibn Umar will not defend his cousin, nor a relative from his relative, nor a friend from his friend. Nor will they be aided, meaning that the believer will not aid the disbeliever because of his kinship. Similar to this verse is: And fear a Day when no soul will suffice for another soul at all. (al-Baqarah 2:48).
44:42: The Almighty’s saying: Except for he upon whom God has mercy. Mun is in the nominative case as a substitute for the pronoun in yasrunu, as if you said: No one rises except so-and-so, or as a subject and the predicate is implied, as if he said: Except for he upon whom God has mercy, then he is forgiven, or He suffices for him and intercedes and is aided, or as a substitute for the first mawla, as if he said: No one suffices except he upon whom God has mercy, and according to Al-Kisa’i and Al-Farra’ it is in the accusative case as a disjunctive exception, meaning, but for he upon whom God has mercy, what they need from among the created beings to suffice them will not be attained. It is permissible for it to be a connected exception, meaning, no one who is close can suffice for another except the believers, for they are permitted to intercede for one another. Indeed, it is He who is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful, meaning, the Avenger of His enemies, the Merciful to His friends, as He said: Severe in penalty, Lord of bounty (Ghafir 40:3). So He coupled the promise with the threat.
44:43: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum. Everything in the Book of God Almighty that mentions the tree is stopped with the letter ha’, except for one letter in Surat al-Dukhan 44:Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum.
