44:44: The food of the sinner, said Ibn al-Anbari. The sinner is the wicked, said Abu al-Darda'. He and Ibn Mas'ud read it this way. Hammam ibn al-Harith said, Abu al-Darda' used to make a man recite Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum is the food of the sinner, and the man would say: The food of the orphan. When he did not understand, he said to him: The food of the wicked. Abu Bakr al-Anbari said: My father told me, he said: Nasr told us, he said: Abu Ubaid told us, he said: Na'im ibn Hammad told us, on the authority of Abdul Aziz ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Ibn Ajlan, on the authority of Awn ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah ibn Mas'ud, he said: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud taught a man Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum is the food of the sinner, so the man said: The food of the orphan. Abdullah repeated the correct verse to him, and the man repeated the mistake. When Abdullah saw that the man's tongue was not straight, he said to him: Do you not know how to say: The food of the wicked? He said: Yes. He said: Then do it. There is no argument in this for the ignorant among the people of deviation, that it is permissible to replace a letter from the Qur’an with another, because that was only from Abdullah to bring the learner closer, and to prepare him for returning to the right path, and to use the truth and to speak with the letter according to the revelation of God and the narration of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Zamakhshari said: (And from this it is proven that replacing one word with another is permissible if it conveys its meaning, and from this Abu Hanifa permitted reading in Persian on the condition that the reader conveys the meanings in their entirety without missing anything from them. They said: This condition testifies that it is a permission, no permission, because in the speech of the Arabs, especially in the Qur’an, which is miraculous in its eloquence and the strangeness of its arrangement and styles, there are subtle meanings and purposes that no language of Persian or any other can convey independently. And Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, was good at Persian, so that was not from him with verification and insight. And Ali bin Al-Ja’d narrated from Abu Yusuf from Abu Hanifa something similar to what his two companions said in denying reading in Persian.) And the wound of Zaqqum: The tree that God created in Hell and called it the accursed tree. When the people of Hell are hungry, they take refuge in it and eat from it, so it boils in their stomachs as hot water boils. What reaches their stomachs from it is likened to molten copper. The common people read tagli with a ta’ as food, and it has the same meaning as a tree. It is not like mahl because it is mentioned for comparison. Al-athim is the sinner, from athama ya’thama, said by Al-Qushayri and Ibn ‘Isa. It was said that it is the polytheist who has acquired sin, said Yahya bin Salam. In Al-Sahah: A man has sinned with a kasra athman and ma’atham if he falls into sin, so he is athman, athman and athman also. The meaning of the food of the sinner is the sinful wicked one, and he is Abu Jahl. This is because he said: Muhammad promises us that in Hell there is Zaqqum, but it is tharid with butter and dates. So, by God, he is against what he said. Al-Naqqash narrated from Mujahid that the tree of Zaqqum is Abu Jahl.. I said: This is not authentic from Mujahid, and it is rejected by what we mentioned about this tree in Surat As-Saffat and Subhan as well.
44:45: Like boiling oil in the stomachs
44:47: The Almighty said: Take him meaning it will be said to the guards: Take him, meaning the sinner. So ride him meaning drag him and lead him. Atal means that you take hold of a man’s collar and ride him, meaning you drag him to you to take him to prison or a calamity. Atalat means you pull him violently. A man is Mu’tal in the broken form. He said, describing a horse: We branch it out, but we do not take it as a burden It contains two languages: ‘Atala and ‘Atana with both the ‘lam’ and the ‘nun’. This was said by Ibn al-Sikkit. The Kufians and Abu ‘Amr read ‘fa’ataluhu’ with the kasra, and the rest read it with the damma. To the midst of Hell is the middle of Hell.
44:48: The Almighty said: Then they poured over his head the torment of scalding water. Muqatil said: Malik, the keeper of Hell, strikes Abu Jahl’s head with an iron whip, and his head shatters from his brain, and his brain flows through his body. Then the angel pours over him scalding water, the heat of which has reached its peak, and it falls into his stomach. The angel says: Taste the torment. And similar to it is: He pours over their heads scalding water. (al-Hajj 22:19)
44:49: The Almighty said: Taste, for you are the mighty, the generous. Ibn al-Anbari said: The common people agreed on the kasra of in. It was narrated on the authority of al-Hasan on the authority of Ali, may God have mercy on him, Taste that you with the fatha of an, and al-Kisa’i read it this way. Whoever breaks in stops at thaq, and whoever opens it does not stop at thaq, because the meaning is taste because you and that you are the mighty, the generous. Qatada said: It was revealed about Abu Jahl, and he had said, There is no one in it who is more honored or generous than me, so it was said to him, Taste, for you are the mighty, the generous. Ikrimah said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Jahl met, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘God has commanded me to say to you, ‘It is more deserving of you,’ so he said, ‘With what are you threatening me! By God, neither you nor your Lord can do anything to me. I am one of the most honored and respected people in this valley.’ So God killed him on the day of Badr and humiliated him.” And this verse was revealed, meaning the angel says to him: Taste, you are the one who is honored and generous, as you claim. It was said: It means belittling, rebuking, mocking, humiliating and belittling, that is, he said to him: You are the one who is humiliated and disgraced. It is like what the people of Shu`ayb said to Shu`ayb: Indeed, you are the forbearing, the rightly guided (Hud 11:87), meaning the foolish, ignorant one in one of the interpretations, as mentioned above. This is the statement of Sa`id ibn Jubayr.
44:50: God Almighty says: This is what you were doubting. That is, the angels say to them: This is what you were doubting in the world.
44:51: The Almighty says: Indeed, the righteous will be in a secure position. When He mentioned the abode of the disbelievers and their punishment, He mentioned the dwelling place of the believers and their bliss. Nafi’ and Ibn ‘Amir read in the position with a damma on the meem, the rest with a fatha. Al-Kisa’i said: The position is the place of residence, as he said: The house has been destroyed, its place and its position have been destroyed Al-Jawhari said: As for the station and the place, each one of them may mean residence, and it may mean the place of standing, because if you make it from qama yaqum, then it is open, and if you make it from iqama yaqim, then it is closed, because if the verb exceeds three, then the place has a closed mim, because it is similar to the daughters of the four, like dahraja and this is mudharajana. And it was said: the station with the fatha is the scene and the council, and with the damma is the residence of Amin in which one is safe from harm.
44:52: The Almighty said: In gardens and springs instead of the station of a trustworthy one.
44:53: The Almighty says: They will wear fine silk and brocade, facing each other. They will not see each other’s backs, facing each other, and their seats will revolve around them wherever they go. Fine silk is the finer part of brocade, and heavy brocade is the coarse part. This was mentioned in the Cave.
44:54: The Almighty’s saying: Likewise means the matter is likewise that which we mentioned, so it is stopped at likewise. It was said: that is, just as We admitted them to Paradise and did to them what was mentioned previously, likewise We honored them by marrying them to houris with wide, blue eyes. The discussion of the eye has already passed in Al-Saffat. Houris are the whites, according to Qatada and the general public, the plural of houri. Houri is the white one whose leg can be seen through her clothes, and the viewer can see his face in her heel, like a mirror due to the fineness of the skin, the brightness of the complexion, and the purity of the color. The evidence for this interpretation is that in the letter of Ibn Masoud it is ba’eesa ‘ayn. Abu Bakr Al-Anbari mentioned that Ahmad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said that Hussein told us, he said that Ammar bin Muhammad told us, he said: I prayed behind Mansour bin Al-Mu’tamir, and he recited in Ha Meem Ad-Dukhan (Ba’eesa ‘ayn. They will not taste the taste of death except the first death). Al-‘Ays are the whites, and from this the white camels are called ‘Ays, the singular of which is a camel ‘Ays and a female camel ‘Ays. Imru’ Al-Qais said: They start to cry out to my voice when they hear it, just as I start to cry out to the voice of Aissa. The meaning of Hoor here: the piercingly beautiful women. Ibn Al-Mubarak mentioned that Muammar told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun Al-Awdi, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, who said: Indeed, a woman from the Hoor Al-Ayn is such that the marrow of her shin can be seen through the flesh and bone, and from under seventy garments, just as a red drink can be seen in a white bottle. Mujahid said: The Hoor are called Hoor because the eye is dazzled by their beauty, whiteness, and purity of their color. It was said that they were called Hoor because of the Hoor of their eyes. Hoor is the intense whiteness of the eye in its intense blackness. A Hoor woman is clearly Hoor. It is said: His eye is Hoor, and The squint of something is white. Al-Asma’i said: I do not know what is Hoor in the eye? Abu Amr said: Hoor is when the entire eye is black, like the eyes of gazelles and cows. He said: “There are no Hoor among the sons of Adam. Women are only called Hoor Al-Ayn because they resemble gazelles and cows.” Al-Ajjaj said: With the eyes of the houris Meaning pure, white eyes with intense black pupils. The plural of ‘aynā’ is ‘aynā’, which means wide, large eyes. On the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The dowries of the houris are handfuls of dates and pieces of bread.” And on the authority of Abu Qarṣafah, “I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Taking out the garbage from the mosque is the dowry of the houris.” And on the authority of Anas, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Sweeping the mosques is the dowry of the houris.” Al-Tha’labi, may God have mercy on him, mentioned this. We have devoted a separate chapter to this meaning in the book At-Tadhkirah. Praise be to God. There is a difference of opinion about which is better in Paradise, human women or houris. Ibn al-Mubarak said: Rashdin informed us on the authority of Ibn An’am on the authority of Hubban ibn Abi Jabalah who said: Those human women who enter Paradise will be preferred over houris by what they did in this world. It was narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that: Human women are seventy thousand times better than houris. It was also said that houris are better, based on the Prophet’s, may God bless him and grant him peace, supplication: And replace for him a wife better than his wife. And God knows best. Ikrimah read bahur ‘ayn as an adjective, and the adjective and tanween in bahur ‘ayn are the same.
44:55: God Almighty says: There they will call for every kind of fruit, safe and sound. Qatada said: Safe from death, illness, and Satan. It was also said: Safe from the interruption of the bliss they are in, or from being harmed or distressed by eating it.
44:56: The Almighty said: They will not taste death therein except the first death meaning they will not taste death therein at all because they will remain therein forever. Then He said: Except the first death as an interrupted exception, meaning but they have tasted the first death in this world. Sibawayh recited: Whoever is quicker to separate the paralysis, let him try it together and become Then he made an exception that was not from the first, saying: Except for the one who has been lost, like a branch in its uprooted fury. It was said that except means after, like when you say: I did not speak to a man today except a man with you, meaning after a man with you. It was also said that except means except, meaning except for the death that they died in this world, like the saying of God Almighty: And do not marry those women whom your fathers married, except what has already occurred (An-Nisa’: 22). It is like saying: I did not taste any food today except what I ate yesterday. Al-Qutbi said: Except for the first death means that when the believer is on the verge of death, the angels of mercy will meet him and he will find the spirit and basil, and his death will be in Paradise because of its characteristics, so it is a correct exception. Death is an accident that is not tasted, but it was made like food whose taste is hated, so the word taste was borrowed for it, And He saved them from the punishment of Hellfire.
44:57: A favor from your Lord meaning He did that to them as a favor from Him to them. A favor is a verbal noun that has an action on it. They call is also said to be the action on it. And He protected them is also said to be an implied verb. It is also said to mean the meaning of the statement before it, because it is a favor from Him to them, since He guided them in this world to deeds that would bring them into Paradise. That is the great attainment meaning happiness, great profit, and great salvation. It is also said that it is from your saying He won such-and-such, meaning he attained it and won it.
44:58: The Almighty said: We have only made it easy for your tongue meaning the Qur’an, meaning We have made it easy in your language for you and for whoever recites it: that they may remember meaning that they will be admonished and deterred. Similar to this is: And We have certainly made the Qur’an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember? (al-Qamar 54:17). So He concluded the Surah by urging people to follow the Qur’an even if it is not mentioned, as He said at the beginning of the Surah: Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night, “Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree” [al-Qadr 97:Surah Al-Baqarah, verse two hundred], as mentioned above.
44:59: The Almighty said: Then await, for they are awaiting. That is, await what I have promised you of victory over them, for they are awaiting your death. This was narrated by Al-Naqqash. It was also said: Await the victory from your Lord, for they are awaiting, according to your claim, your defeat. It was also said: Await that God judges between you and them, for they are awaiting the uncertainties of the event with you. The meanings are similar. It was also said: Await what I have promised you of reward, for they are like those awaiting what I have promised them of punishment. It was also said: Await the Day of Resurrection, for it is the Day of Judgment, and even if they do not believe in the occurrence of the Resurrection, they are considered like those awaiting it because that is what will be their outcome. And God Almighty knows best.
45:1: It is all Meccan according to Al-Hasan, Jabir and Ikrimah. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: except for one verse, which is: Say to those who believe to forgive those who do not expect the days of God (al-Jathiyah 45:14). It was revealed in Medina about Umar ibn Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him. Al-Mawardi mentioned this. Al-Mahdawi and Al-Nahhas said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It was revealed about Umar may God be pleased with him. A polytheist in Mecca insulted him before the migration, so he wanted to strike him, so God, the Almighty, revealed: Say to those who believe to forgive him who does not expect the days of God (al-Tawbah 9:5). Then it was abrogated by the words: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9:5). So the entire surah is Meccan according to this without dispute, and it is thirty-seven verses, and it was said six. God Almighty says: Ha Meem is the subject.
45:2: God Almighty says: The revelation of the Book is from God, the Exalted in Might, the Wise. “Tanzil” is its predicate. Some of them said: Ha Meem is the name of the surah, and Tanzil al-Kitab is its predicate, from God and the book is the Qur’an, and al-Maziz is the impregnable, al-Wise in His action. All of this has been mentioned before.
45:3: God Almighty says: Indeed, in the heavens and the earth meaning in their creation are signs for the believers.
45:4: God Almighty says: And in your creation and what He disperses of moving creatures are signs for a people who are certain.
45:5: God Almighty says: And the alternation of night and day and what God sends down from the sky of provision meaning rain. And He revives thereby the earth after its lifelessness, and the direction of the winds are signs for a people who understand. All of this has been presented in full in Al-Baqarah and other verses. The reading of the general public and what He disperses of living creatures at night and and the direction of the winds are signs is in the nominative case in both of them. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read the ta’ in both of them, and there is no disagreement about the first one being in the accusative case as the subject of in and its predicate in the heavens. The reason for the kasra in the second signs is in conjunction with what it worked on, the estimation is, in your creation and what He disperses of living creatures there are signs. As for the third, it has been said that the reason for the accusative case in it is the repetition of signs because the speech is long, as you say: I struck Zayd, Zayd. And it has been said that it is based on what in worked on, estimating the deletion of in, the estimation is: and in the alternation of night and day there are signs, so in was deleted because it was mentioned before. Sibawayh recited regarding the deletion: A man you think is a man, but a fire lit at night is a fire. So, the deletion of kull added to the noun naar majrur was made because it was mentioned before. It was said that it is a case of connecting two operators, and Sibawayh did not permit it, but al-Akhfash and a group of Kufians permitted it. So, he connected wa-ikhtilaf to his saying: And in your creation, then he said, And the turning of the winds are signs, so it needs to be connected, so it was not able to take the place of two different operators, because if it took the place of a nominative and a nasb, it would be a nominative and a nasb in one case. As for the reading of the nominative, then it is based on the position of in with what it worked on. The grammarians have also required in that the connection to two operators, because it is the connection of wa-ikhtilaf to and in your creation and the connection of ayat to the position of the first ayat, but it is possible to repeat fi, and it is permissible to raise it on the separation from what precedes it, so it is raised by the beginning, and what precedes it is its predicate, and it is the connection of a sentence to a sentence. Al-Farra’ reported the raising of wa-ikhtilaf and ayat together. The difference is the verses.
45:6: The Almighty said: These are the verses of God, meaning these are the verses of God, meaning His arguments and proofs that indicate His Oneness and Power. We recite them to you in truth, meaning with the truth in which there is no falsehood or lie. It was read yattaluhu with a ya’: Then in what statement after God? meaning after the statement of God, and it was said after His Qur’an. And His verses will they believe? The general reading is with a ya’ as a statement. Ibn Muhaisin and Abu Bakr on the authority of Asim, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read ta’minunu with a ta’ as an address.
45:7: The Almighty said: Woe to every slanderer and sinner. Woe is a valley in Hell, a threat to those who abandon the use of His verses for evidence. The slanderer is the liar, and slander is falsehood. Sinful means one who commits a sin. What is meant in what was narrated is: Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith, and according to Ibn Abbas, it is Al-Harith ibn Kalda, and Al-Tha’labi narrated that it is Abu Jahl and his companions.
45:8: He hears the verses of God recited to him meaning the verses of the Qur’an, "then he persists in his disbelief, feeling too proud to submit. It is taken from the verb sarra sarra, meaning to tighten it. Ibn Abbas and others said its meaning. It was said that its origin is from the donkey’s insistence on its pubis, meaning that it bends over it, bending its ears. "An is from ka'ana", a lightened form of the heavy form, as if he did not hear it. The pronoun is the pronoun of the matter, as in his saying: As if a gazelle gives to Nader Al-Salam The subject of the sentence is the accusative, meaning he insists like someone who does not listen. The meaning of this verse was mentioned in the beginning of Luqman, and the meaning of give him tidings of a painful punishment was mentioned in the cow.
45:9: The Almighty said: And when he learns something of Our signs, he takes it in ridicule. Similar to His statement about Zaqqum: It is the dates and the olives, and His statement about the keepers of Hell: If there are nineteen, then I will meet them alone. For those is a humiliating punishment. Humiliating and disgraceful.
45:10: The Almighty’s saying: Behind them is Hell meaning behind what they are in of arrogance in this world and haughtiness about the truth is Hell. Ibn Abbas said: Behind them is Hell meaning in front of them. Similar to this is: Behind him is Hell, and he will be given to drink from purulent water (Ibrahim 14:16), meaning in front of him. He said: Is there not behind me, if my death is delayed, a lesson with the children, crawling like an eagle? And what they have earned will not avail them at all meaning money and children. Similar to this is: Their wealth and children will not avail them at all against God (al-Mujadilah 58:17) meaning money and children, nor what they have taken as protectors besides God meaning idols, and for them is a great punishment meaning permanent and painful.
45:11: The Almighty’s saying: This is guidance is a subject and a predicate, meaning the Qur’an. Ibn Abbas said: It means everything that Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, brought. And those who disbelieve in the signs of their Lord meaning they denied His proofs, for them is a punishment of a painful torment. The torment is the torment, meaning for them is a punishment of a painful torment. The evidence for this is the Almighty’s saying: So We sent down upon those who did wrong a punishment from the sky (Al-Baqarah 2:59), meaning a torment. It was said: The filthy torment is like the unclean, it is like the Almighty’s saying: And he is given to drink of festering water (Ibrahim 14:16), meaning for them is a punishment from drinking the filthy drink. Ibn Muhaysin pronounced the damma on the ra’ of rajaz wherever it occurred. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaysin, and Hafs read ‘alim in the nominative case, meaning for them is a painful punishment from rajaz. The rest read it in the genitive case as a description of the torment.
45:12: The Almighty says: It is God who has subjected the sea to you so that ships may sail through it by His command and that you may seek of His bounty and that you may be grateful. He mentioned the perfection of His power and the completion of His blessings upon His servants, and explained that He created what He created for their benefit.
45:13: The Almighty’s saying: And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth - all from Him means that this is His doing, His creation, His kindness and His bounty. Ibn Abbas, Al-Jahdary and others read all of it as a favor with a kasra on the meem, a shaddah on the noon and a tanween on the ha’, in the accusative case as a source. Abu Amr said: And this is how I heard Muslimah read it manna meaning favor and generosity. And from Muslimah bin Muharib also all of it as a favor with the addition of the manna to the pronoun ha’, and according to Abu Hatim it is the predicate of a deleted subject, meaning that, or it is from Him. And the reading of the group is clear: Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.
45:15: The Almighty said: “Whoever does righteousness does so for [the benefit of] his own soul, and whoever does evil does so against it. Then to your Lord you will be returned.” It was presented.
45:16: The Almighty says: And We had certainly given the Children of Israel the Scripture meaning the Torah. And wisdom and prophethood Wisdom means understanding in the Scripture. It was also said that it means ruling and judging people. And prophethood means the prophets from the time of Joseph, peace be upon him, to the time of Jesus, peace be upon him. And We provided for them of the good things meaning the lawful foods, fruits, and foods that were in Syria. It was also said that it means the manna and quails in the wilderness. And We preferred them over the worlds meaning over the people of their time, as was explained previously in Ad-Dukhan.
45:17: The Almighty said: And We gave them clear proofs of the matter. Ibn Abbas said: He means the matter of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and the evidence of his prophethood, that he would migrate from Tihamah to Yathrib, and the people of Yathrib would support him. It was also said: The clear proofs of the matter are clear laws regarding what is permissible and what is forbidden, and miracles. They did not differ except after knowledge had come to them. He means Joshua bin Nun, so some of them believed and some of them disbelieved. This was narrated by Al-Naqqash. It was also said: Except after knowledge had come to them of the prophethood of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, so they differed about it out of envy among themselves, that is, out of envy of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. Ad-Dahhak said its meaning. It was said: The meaning of out of envy is that some of them transgressed against others, seeking superiority and leadership, and they killed the prophets. This is how the polytheists of your time, O Muhammad, had received clear proofs, but they turned away from them in order to compete for leadership. Indeed, your Lord will judge between them, that is, He will rule and decide. On the Day of Resurrection, concerning that over which they differed in this world.
45:18: There are two issues: English: The first: The Almighty’s saying: Then We placed you on a way of religion. Sharia in the language means: doctrine and religion. The watering place, which is the place where a drinker comes from, is called sharia, and from it comes the word shari’a because it is a path to the destination. Sharia is what God has prescribed for His servants of religion, and the plural is sharia’, and sharia’ in religion: the doctrines that God has prescribed for His creation. So the meaning of: We placed you on a way of religion is on guidance from the matter. Qatadah: Sharia is the command and prohibition, the limits and the obligations. Muqatil: the evidence, because it is a path to the truth. Al-Kalbi: the Sunnah, because it is prescribed in the manner of the prophets who came before him. Ibn Zayd: the religion, because it is the path to salvation. Ibn al-Arabi said: The command occurs in the language with two meanings: one of them is in the sense of the matter, like His saying: So they followed the command of Pharaoh, and Pharaoh’s command was not right. (Hud 11:97), and the second is one of the parts of speech that are opposite to the prohibition, and both can be intended here, and its interpretation is: Then We placed you on a way of religion, which is the religion of Islam, as God the Almighty said: Then We revealed to you, [O Muhammad], ‘Follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with God.’ (al-Nahl 16:123) There is no disagreement that God Almighty did not make any distinction between the laws in monotheism, virtues, and interests, but rather He made differences between them in the branches according to what He, glory be to Him, knew. Second: Ibn al-Arabi said: Some of those who speak about knowledge thought that this verse is evidence that the law of those before us is not our law, because God Almighty singled out the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his nation in this verse with a law. We do not deny that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his nation are singled out with a law. Rather, the dispute is over what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed us about regarding the law of those before us in the context of praise and commendation: is it necessary to follow it or not? The Almighty said: And do not follow the inclinations of those who do not know, meaning the polytheists. Ibn Abbas said: Qurayzah and Nadir. And on his authority: It was revealed when Quraysh called him to the religion of his fathers.
45:19: The Almighty says: Indeed, they will never avail you against God at all meaning if you follow their desires, they will not protect you from God’s punishment at all. Indeed, the wrongdoers are allies of one another meaning friends, supporters, and loved ones. Ibn Abbas said: He means that the hypocrites are allies of the Jews. And God is the ally of the righteous meaning their supporter and helper. The righteous here: avoid polytheism and sins.
45:20: The Almighty’s saying: These are insights for the people is a subject and predicate, meaning that what has been sent down to you is proofs, evidence, and landmarks for the people regarding the limits and rulings. It was read these are insights, meaning these verses. And guidance, meaning right conduct and a path that leads to Paradise for whoever takes it. And mercy in the Hereafter for a people who are certain.
45:21: The Almighty said: Or do those who commit evil deeds think that is, they acquired them. Acquisition is acquisition, and from it comes the limbs. It was mentioned in Al-Ma’idah, that We will make them like those who believed and did righteous deeds. Al-Kalbi said: Those who committed evil deeds are Utbah and Shaibah, the sons of Rabi’ah, and Al-Walid bin Utbah, and those who believed are Ali, Hamzah, and Ubaidah bin Al-Harith, may God be pleased with them, when they went out to them on the day of Badr and killed them. It was said that it was revealed about a group of polytheists who said: They will be given better in the Hereafter than what is given to the believer, as the Lord informed us about them in His saying: And if I should return to my Lord, indeed, I will have with Him the best (Fussilat 41:50). His saying: Or do they think is a question word in apposition, meaning denial. The Arabs pronounce it in the accusative without apposition if it is in the middle of the address, and some people say that it contains an omission, meaning, And God is the protector of the righteous. Do the polytheists know that, or do they think that We will make them equal? It was said that it is the mother of the disconnected letter, and the meaning of the hamza in it is the denial of the reckoning. The general reading of sawa’u is in the nominative case as the predicate of an advanced subject, meaning their life and death are the same, and the pronoun in muhyihim wa mutamatuhum refers to the disbelievers, meaning their life is the life of the evil of their death. Likewise, Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, and Al-A’mash read sawa’u in the accusative case, and Abu Ubaid chose it. He said: Its meaning is that We will make them equal. Al-A’mash also and Isa bin Umar read wa mutamatuhum in the accusative case, meaning that they are equal in their life and death. So when the preposition was dropped, it became accusative. It is permissible for muhyihim wa mutamatuhum to be a substitute for the ha’ and the mim in naj’alhum, and the meaning is that We will make their life and death the same like the life and death of those who believed. It is permissible for the pronoun in muhyihim wa mutamatuhum to refer to the disbelievers and the believers together. Mujahid said: The believer dies as a believer and is resurrected as a believer, and the disbeliever He will die as an unbeliever and will be resurrected as an unbeliever. Ibn al-Mubarak reported that Shu`bah told us on the authority of `Amr ibn Murrah on the authority of Abu al-Dahha on the authority of Masruq who said: A man from the people of Mecca said: This is the station of Tamim al-Dari. I saw him one night, until morning came, or almost morning came, reciting a verse from the Book of God, bowing and prostrating and weeping: Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds? - the whole verse. Bashir said: I spent the night with al-Rabi` ibn Khaitham one night, and he got up to pray. He passed by this verse, so he stayed the night until morning and did not return to it with intense weeping. Ibrahim ibn al-Ash`ath said: I often saw al-Fudayl ibn `Iyad repeating this verse and similar ones from the beginning of the night to the end, then he would say: I wonder which of the two groups are you from? This verse was called the Lament of the Worshippers because it was clear.
45:22: God Almighty says: God created the heavens and the earth in truth meaning with the true command. And that you may be recompensed meaning so that you may be recompensed. Every soul will have what it has earned meaning in the Hereafter. And they will not be wronged.
45:23: God Almighty says: “Have you seen he who has taken as his god his own desire and God has sent him astray due to knowledge and has set a seal upon his hearing and his heart and put over his vision a veil? Then who will guide him after God? Then will you not be reminded?” Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan and Qatada said: That is the disbeliever who has taken as his religion what he desires, and he does not desire anything except that he does it. Ikrimah said: Have you seen the one who makes the god of what he worships what he desires or approves of, so if he approves of something and likes it, he takes it as a god? Saeed bin Jubair said: One of them used to worship a stone, and if he saw something better than it, he would throw it away and worship another. Muqatil said: It was revealed about Al-Harith bin Qais Al-Sahmi, one of the mockers, because he used to worship what his soul desired. Sufyan bin Uyaynah said: They only worshipped stones because the House was made of stones. It was said: The meaning is: Have you seen the one who is led by his desires and his idol, astonishing the people of reason at this ignorance? Al-Hasan bin Al-Fadl said: In this verse there is an inversion, its meaning is: Have you seen the one who takes his desires as his god? Al-Sha’bi said: Desire is called desire because it throws its owner into the Fire. Ibn Abbas said: God did not mention desire in the Qur’an except that he condemned it. God Almighty said: And follow “His desires are like that of a dog (al-A’raf 7:176), and God Almighty said: And he followed his desires, and his affair was ever in neglect (al-Kahf 18:28), and God Almighty said: “Rather, those who do wrong follow their desires without knowledge. So who guides whom God has led astray?” (Al-Rum: 29), and God Almighty said: And who is more astray than he who follows his desires without guidance from God? (al-Qasas 28:50), and God Almighty said: And do not follow desires, for they will lead you astray from the path of God (Sad: 26), and Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Al-As said, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: ‘None of you truly believes until his desires are subservient to what you have brought.’” And Abu Umamah said, “I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, ‘No god is worshipped under the heavens more hateful to God than desires.’” And Shaddad ibn Aws said, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: ‘The intelligent person is he who judges himself and works for the hereafter, and the wicked person is he who follows his desires and hopes for God.’” And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, If you see greed being obeyed and desires being followed… And the world is influential and every person with an opinion admires his opinion, so you should pay attention to yourself and leave the affairs of the public. And the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “There are three things that lead to destruction and three that lead to salvation. The things that lead to destruction are obeyed greed, followed desires, and a person’s admiration of himself. The things that lead to salvation are: fear of God in secret and in public, moderation in wealth and poverty, and justice in pleasure and anger.” And Abu al-Darda’ may God be pleased with him said: When a man wakes up, his desires, deeds, and knowledge are combined. If his deeds are in accordance with his desires, then his day is a bad day, and if his deeds are in accordance with his knowledge, then his day is a good day. And al-Asma’i said: I heard a man say: Humiliation is love, the heart of its name. If you love, you will find humiliation. Ibn al-Muqaffa was asked about love, and he said: Hawaan is a word whose nun was stolen, so a poet took it and composed it, saying: The letter “nun of hawa is stolen from hawa. So if you love, you will find our love. Another said: Love is humiliation itself. If you love, you will gain humiliation. If you love, then love will enslave you, so submit to your love, whoever you are. And to Abdullah bin Mubarak: One of the signs of calamity is that you do not see any deviation from your desires. The slave is a slave to his soul and its desires, while the free man is satisfied sometimes and sips sometimes. And to Ibn Duraid: If the soul ever demands of you a desire and there is a way to conflict with it Leave it and go against what you like, because your like is an enemy and disagreement is a friend. And for Abu Ubaid al-Tusi: And the soul, if you give it what it desires, will open its mouth towards its desires. Ahmad ibn Abi Al-Hawari said: I passed by a monk and found him thin, so I said to him: Are you sick? He said: Yes. I said: Since when? He said: Since when did I know myself? I said: Will you seek treatment? He said: Medicine has exhausted me and I have decided to cauterize. I said: What is cauterization? He said: Going against your desires. Sahl ibn Abdullah Al-Sitri said: Your desires are your illness, if you go against them then it is your cure. Wahb said: If you are in doubt about two matters and you do not know which is better, then look for the one further from your desires and then do it. Scholars have written books and chapters on this subject, condemning desires and opposing them. We have pointed out what is sufficient of it. It is sufficient for you to read the words of God Almighty: But as for he who feared the position of his Lord and prevented the soul from desire, * then indeed, Paradise will be the refuge. (al-Nazi’at 79:40-41) God the Almighty said: And God led him astray, knowingly. That is, knowing that He knew him. It was also said: He led him astray from reward, knowing that he did not deserve it. Ibn Abbas said: That is, knowing that he would go astray. Muqatil: knowing that he was astray, and the meanings are close. It was also said: knowing that the idol worshipper neither benefits nor harms. Then it was said: knowingly may be a state of the subject, meaning: He led him astray, knowing that he was among the people of misguidance in his previous knowledge. It may also be a state of the object, so the meaning is: He led him astray while the disbeliever knew that he was astray. And He set a seal upon his hearing and his heart, that is, He sealed his hearing so that he would not hear the admonition, and He sealed his heart so that he would not understand the guidance. And He placed over his vision a covering, that is, a veil so that he would not see the right path. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read ghashwah with a fat-ha on the ghayn without an alif. This has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. The poet said: If you have clothed me in a veil, I have indeed purified you of my affection for a time. Who will guide him after God? That is, after He has led him astray. Will you not remember? Will you learn a lesson and know that He is capable of whatever He wills. This verse responds to the Qadarites and the Imamites and those who follow their path in belief, as it clearly states that they are prevented from guidance. Then it was said: And He has set a seal upon his hearing and his heart that it is outside the context of reporting about their conditions, and it was said: It is outside the context of supplicating against them, as mentioned in the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah. Ibn Jurayj narrated that it was revealed about Al-Harith ibn Qays from the Ghayatilah. Al-Naqqash narrated that it was revealed about Al-Harith ibn Nawfal ibn Abd Manaf. Muqatil said: It was revealed about Abu Jahl, because he circumambulated the Kaaba one night with Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira, and they talked about the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Abu Jahl said: By God, I know that he is truthful! He said to him: Stop! What made you say that?! He said: O Abu Abd Shams, in his youth we used to call him the truthful and trustworthy, but when his mind and maturity reached maturity, we called him the liar and traitor!! By God, I know that he is truthful! He said: So what prevents you from believing him and having faith in him? He said: The daughters of Quraysh are saying that I followed the orphan of Abu Talib because of a broken heart, and by Al-Lat and Al-Uzza I will never follow him. Then the verse was revealed: And He has set a seal upon his hearing and his heart.
45:24: The Almighty said: "And they say, 'There is only our worldly life. We die and we live.'" This is a denial on their part of the Hereafter, a lie about the Resurrection, and a nullification of the recompense. The meaning of we die and we live is that we die and our children live, as Al-Kalbi said. It was also read and we live with a damma on the noon. It was also said: some of us die and some of us live. It was also said: there is an inversion of the letter noon, meaning we live and we die, and this is the reading of Ibn Mas`ud. And nothing destroys us except time. Mujahid said: meaning the years and days. Qatada said: except life, and the meaning is the same. It was also read except an age that passes. Ibn `Uyaynah said: The people of the Jahiliyyah used to say: Time is what destroys us and it is what gives us life and causes us to die. So this verse was revealed. Qutrub said: And nothing destroys us except death. He recited the words of Abu Dhu`ayb: Death and its uncertainties are painful, and time does not forgive those who are impatient. Akrima said: That is, nothing destroys us except God. Abu Hurairah narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The people of ignorance used to say, Nothing destroys us except the night and the day, and it is what destroys us, causes us to die, and brings us back to life. They would curse time. God Almighty said: “The son of Adam harms me by cursing time, and I am time. In my hand is the command. I alternate night and day.” I said: His saying God said to the end is the text of Al-Bukhari and his wording, and Muslim also included it, as did Abu Dawud, and in Al-Muwatta’, “On the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Let none of you say, “Oh, the disappointment of time,” for God is time.” This hadith was used as evidence by those who said that time is one of the names of God, and they said: Those scholars who did not make it a name only did so in response to the Arabs in their pre-Islamic period, for they believed that time was the doer, as God informed us about them in this verse. So if harm, oppression, or misfortune befell them, they would attribute that to time. So it was said to them about that: Do not curse time, for God is time, meaning that God is the doer of these things that you attribute to time, so the curse is attributed to Him, glory be to Him. So they were forbidden from that, and the evidence for the correctness of this is what we mentioned from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God, the Blessed and Exalted, said: The son of Adam harms me…” The hadith. And the one who said it well, and he is Abu Ali Al-Thaqafi: Oh you who reproach time when it happens to you, do not blame time for its treachery Time is commanded by a commander, and time ends with his command. How many infidels have a lot of money that increases many times over their infidelity? A believer who has no dirham increases in faith despite his poverty. It was narrated that Salim bin Abdullah bin Omar used to often mention time, so his father rebuked him and said: Beware, my son, of mentioning time! And he recited: Time does not bring calamity or harm to anything in its time, so do not curse time. But whenever God sends a messenger to a group, He makes their easy things difficult. Abu Ubaid said: I debated with some atheists and he said: Don’t you see that he says God is time?! I said: Did anyone curse God during the Eternal Era? Rather, they used to say as Al-A’sha said: Whether in a place or on a journey, they will take their time. God has taken loyalty and justice for Himself, and has left the blame to men. Abu Ubaid said: It is the custom of the Arabs to criticize time during calamities and misfortunes, to the point that they mentioned it in their poetry and attributed events to it. Amr ibn Qami’ah said: The daughters of time threw me from where I did not see, so what about the one who is thrown but does not throw? If they were arrows, I would have avoided them, but I shoot without arrows. On the palms of my hands once, and on the temples three times, after which I stand up And there is much like it in poetry: they attribute that to time and attribute it to Him, while God Almighty is the doer, there is no lord other than Him. And they have no knowledge of that meaning knowledge. From is redundant, meaning they said what they said, doubting. They only conjecture meaning they only speak based on conjecture. The polytheists were of various types, including these, and those who affirmed the Creator and denied the Resurrection, and those who doubted the Resurrection and were not certain of denying it. In Islam, there occurred people who could not deny the Resurrection for fear of the Muslims, so they interpreted and saw the Resurrection as the death of the body, and they saw the reward and punishment as illusions that befall the souls, according to their claim. The evil of these people is more harmful than the evil of all the disbelievers, because these people confuse the truth, and one is deceived by their apparent deception. The Muslim is wary of the polytheist who openly declares his polytheism. It was said: We die and our traces live on, so this is the life of the male. It was also said: They pointed to reincarnation, meaning a man dies and his soul is placed in a state of death and lives on through him.
45:25: The Almighty said: And when Our clear verses are recited to them meaning, and when Our revealed verses are recited to these polytheists about the permissibility of resurrection, there is no refutation. Their argument is only that they say, 'Bring our fathers' Their argument is the predicate of was, and the noun except that they say, 'Bring our fathers' the dead ones. We will ask them about the truth of what they say. So God responded to them by saying: Say, 'God gives you life' meaning after you were dead sperm. Then He causes you to die, then He will gather you together for the Day of Resurrection just as He gave you life in this world. But most people do not know that God will bring them back as He began them. Az-Zamakhshari: If you say, why is their statement called an argument and not an argument? I say: Because they presented it as a proof presents his argument, and they presented it in its context, so it was called an argument by way of sarcasm, or because it was in their calculations and estimation an argument, or because it is in the style of His saying: Greetings between them are a painful blow It is as if it was said: Their argument was nothing but what is not an argument, and what is meant is the denial that they have any argument at all. If you say: How did His statement, Say, ‘God will give you life,’ occur as an answer to, Bring our fathers, if you should be truthful, I say: When they denied the resurrection and belied the messengers, and thought that what they said was a statement of rebuke, they committed what they acknowledged from God, the Almighty, the Majestic, who is the one who gives them life and then causes them to die, and added to the commitment of that the commitment of what is obligatory to acknowledge is that they were fair and listened to the caller of the truth, which is their gathering on the Day of Resurrection, and whoever was able to do that was able to bring their fathers, and it was the easiest thing for him.
45:26: God Almighty says: Say, ‘God gives you life, then causes you to die, then He will assemble you for the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt, but most people do not know.’
45:27: The Almighty says: And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, in creation and dominion. And on the Day the Hour appears, that Day the falsifiers will lose. The first Day is in the accusative case because of loses, and that Day is a repetition for emphasis or a substitute. It was said that the meaning is: And to Him belongs the dominion on the Day the Hour appears, and the agent in that Day is loses, and the object of loses is omitted, and the meaning is they will lose their homes in Paradise.
45:28: The Almighty’s saying: And you will see every nation kneeling meaning from the horror of that Day, and the nation here: the people of every religion, and there are five interpretations of al-Jathiyah 45:The first: Mujahid said: Mostawfiz, and Sufyan said: Mostawfiz is the one from whom nothing touches the ground except his knees and the tips of his fingers, Ad-Dahhak: that is at the time of reckoning, the second: gathered, said Ibn Abbas, Al-Farra’: the meaning is and you will see the people of every religion gathered, the third: distinct, said Ikrimah, the fourth: submissive in the language of Quraysh, said: He lowers his knees, he kneels and he kneels, he kneels and he kneels, on the pattern of fa’ul in them, and it has already been mentioned in Maryam, and the root of “al-Jathwa is a group of everything, Tarafa said describing two graves: You see two bodies of dirt covered with solid sheets of tin. Then it was said: It is specific to the infidels, said Yahya bin Salam, and it was said: It is general for the believer and the infidel awaiting the reckoning, and Sufyan bin Uyaynah narrated on the authority of Amr bin Abdullah bin Babaah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is as if I see you kneeling in a heap before Hell, mentioned by Al-Mawardi, Salman said: On the Day of Resurrection there is an hour that is ten years in which people will fall kneeling on their knees until Abraham, peace be upon him, calls out: I do not ask You today for anything but myself, Every nation will be called to its book, Yahya bin Salam said: To its reckoning, and it was said: To its book in which what it did of good and evil was transcribed, said Muqatil, and this is the meaning of Mujahid’s statement: It was said: its book is what the angels wrote upon it, and it was said: its book sent down upon it to see whether they acted upon what was in it, and it was said: The book here is the Preserved Tablet, and Yaqub Al-Hadrami read every nation in the accusative as a substitute for the first every because of the clarification in the second which Not in the first, because there is nothing in her kneeling from the state of explaining kneeling as in the second from mentioning the reason calling for it, which is her summoning to her book. And it was said: It was erected by the use of you see implied, and the raising is in the beginning, Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do of good or evil.
45:29: The Almighty’s saying: This is Our Book. It was said that it is from the words of God to them, and it was said that it is from the words of the angels, It speaks against you with the truth, meaning it bears witness, and it is a metaphor. It is said: The Book spoke of such-and-such, meaning it made clear. It was said that they read it and the Book reminds them of what they did, so it is as if it speaks against them. The evidence for this is His saying: And they say, ‘Woe to us! What is this Book that leaves out nothing small or great without enumerating it?’ (al-Kahf 18:49), and in al-Mu’minun 23:And with Us is a Book that speaks with the truth, and they will not be wronged. It was mentioned before, and speaks is in the place of a state of the Book, or from this, or a second predicate of this, or Our Book is a substitute for this and speaks is the predicate. Indeed, We were transcribing what you used to do. That is, We commanded that what you used to do be transcribed. Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: God has angels who descend every day with something in which they write down the deeds of the children of Adam. Abbas said: God and all the angels are purified, so they transcribe from the Mother of the Book in Ramadan everything that is of the children of Adam, and they check with God’s guardians over the servants every five days, and they find that what the guardians have brought of the servants’ deeds is in agreement with what is in their book from which they transcribed, with no increase or decrease in it. Ibn Abbas said: And does transcribing happen except from a book? Al-Hasan: We transcribe what the guardians wrote for the children of Adam, because the guardians raise the scrolls of deeds to the keepers. It was said: The guardians carry every day what they wrote for the servant, then when they return to their place, the good and bad deeds are transcribed from it, and the permissible deeds are not transferred to the second copy. It was said: When the angels raise the deeds of the servants to God Almighty, He commands that what contains reward and punishment be recorded with Him, and that what contains neither reward nor punishment is dropped from their total..
45:30: God Almighty says: But as for those who believe and do righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them to His mercy meaning Paradise. That is the clear attainment.
45:31: The Almighty says: And as for those who disbelieved, were not My verses recited to you? That is, were they not told that, and it is a question of rebuke, but you were arrogant about accepting them, and you were a criminal people, that is, polytheists who committed sins. It is said: So-and-so is the one who committed the sins of his family if he was their earner. The criminal is the one who committed sins himself. God Almighty said: Should We then treat the Muslims like the criminals? (al-Qalam 68:35), so the criminal is the opposite of the Muslim, so he is the one who is guilty of disbelief.
45:32: The Almighty said: And when it is said, ‘Indeed, the promise of God is true,’ meaning that the resurrection will happen. And the Hour, there is no doubt about it. Hamzah read and the Hour in the accusative case in apposition to promise, while the rest read it in the nominative case as a subject, or in apposition to the position of indeed, the promise of God. It is not good with the pronoun in the source, because it is not emphasized, and the raised pronoun is only attached to it without emphasis in poetry: You said, ‘We do not know what the Hour is,’ whether it is true or false. We only think a thought. Al-Mubarrad interpreted it as: We only think a thought. It was said that the interpretation is: We only think that you think a thought. It was said that you said, We only think a thought, “and we are not certain,” that the Hour is coming.
45:33: God Almighty says: And the evil consequences of what they did will become apparent to them. That is, the punishment for the evil consequences of what they did will become apparent to them. And what they used to ridicule will encompass them, that is, it will descend and surround them, of God’s punishment.
45:34: God Almighty says: And it will be said, ‘Today We will forget you.’ That is, We will leave you in the Fire just as you abandoned the meeting of this Day of yours, that is, you abandoned working for it. And your refuge is the Fire. That is, your dwelling and your final resting place. And you will have no helpers.
45:35: The Almighty said: That is because you took the verses of God meaning the Qur’an, in jest “and the worldly life deceived you” meaning it tricked you with its falsehoods and decorations, so you thought that there was nothing else and that there would be no resurrection, so today they will not come out of it meaning from the Fire, nor will they be asked to repent seeking to be appeased. This has been mentioned before. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read so today they will not come out with a fat-ha on the ya’ and a damma on the ra’, based on the Almighty’s statement: Whenever they want to come out of it, they will be returned to it (al-Sajdah 32:20). The rest read it with a damma on the ya’ and a fat-ha on the ra’, based on the Almighty’s statement: Our Lord, bring us out (al-Mu’minun 23:107), and similar to it.
45:36: The Almighty said: Then praise be to God, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds. Mujahid, Hamid, and Ibn Muhaisin read Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds in the nominative case in all of them, meaning He is Lord.
45:37: God Almighty says: And to Him belongs pride meaning greatness, majesty, permanence, authority, power, and perfection, “in the heavens and the earth. He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.” And God knows best.
46:1: Meccan according to all of them, and it is thirty-four verses, and it was said: five. The Almighty said: Ha Meem before.
46:2: The Almighty said: The revelation of the Book is from God, the Exalted in Might, the Wise. It was presented.
46:3: The Almighty’s saying: We did not create the heavens and the earth and all that is between them except in truth was previously mentioned. And a specified term means the Resurrection, according to Ibn Abbas and others, and it is the term at which the heavens and the earth will come to an end. It was also said that it is the term decreed for every creature. And those who disbelieve from that of which they were warned fear it. Turning away turning away, heedless, and not prepared for it. It is possible that ma is a source, meaning from their warning on that Day.
46:4: It contains five issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: Say, ‘Have you considered what you invoke besides God?’ That is, what you worship of idols and rivals besides God. Show me what they have created on the earth. That is, have they created anything on the earth? Or do they have a share? “in the heavens.” That is, in the creation of the heavens with God. Bring me a book before this. That is, before this Qur’an. Second: The Almighty’s saying: Or a trace of knowledge. The general reading is or a trace with an alif after the tha’. Ibn Abbas said: “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: It is a line that the Arabs used to draw on the ground.” Al-Mahdawi and Al-Tha’labi mentioned it, and Ibn Al-Arabi said: It is not authentic. In the famous hadith: “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: A prophet from among the prophets used to draw, so whoever matches his drawing, that is it.” It is also not authentic. I said: It is proven from the hadith of Muawiyah ibn al-Hakam al-Sulami, narrated by Muslim, and al-Nahhas narrated: Muhammad ibn Ahmad known as al-Juraiji told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Bandar told us, he said: Yahya ibn Sa`id told us, on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, on the authority of Safwan ibn Salim, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the words of God Almighty: or a trace of knowledge he said: handwriting. This is also correct. Ibn al-`Arabi said: They differed in its interpretation, some of them said: It came to permit striking, because some of the prophets used to do it, and some of them said: It came to forbid it, because “he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever agrees with his handwriting, that is it.’” There is no way to know the path of the Prophet mentioned earlier in this regard, so there is no way to act upon it. He said: By your life, neither the pebble-beaters nor the birds' warders know what God is doing. Its reality, according to its masters, goes back to the images of the planets. What emerges from them indicates what those planets indicate of good fortune or bad luck that will befall them. So it became an assumption based on assumption, and an attachment to an unseen matter whose path has been studied and whose verification has been lost. The Shariah has forbidden it, and informed that it is something that is exclusive to God and cut it off from creation. Even if they had before that means to which they could cling in order to attain unseen things, God has removed those means, obliterated those doors, and singled Himself out with knowledge of the unseen. It is not permissible to compete with Him in that, and it is not permissible for anyone to call upon Him, and seeking it is a burden if there is no prohibition on it. So, when the prohibition has been mentioned, seeking it is a sin or disbelief according to the intention of the seeker. I said: What he chose is the statement of Al-Khattabi. Al-Khattabi said: “His saying, peace be upon him: ‘Whoever agrees with his handwriting, that is it.’ This may be interpreted as a warning, since that was knowledge of his prophethood and it had ceased, so we were forbidden from engaging in that. Al-Qadi Iyad said: What is most apparent from the wording is the opposite of this, and the approval of the handwriting of whoever agrees with his handwriting. But how do you know the agreement when the Shari’ah forbade speculation and claiming the unseen in general? Rather, its meaning is that whoever agrees with his handwriting, that is the one they find to be correct, not that he intended to permit that for the one who does it, as some of them interpreted it. Makki narrated in his interpretation of his statement: ‘A prophet from among the prophets used to write,’ that he used to write with his index and middle fingers in the sand and then he was warned. Ibn Abbas said in his interpretation of his statement: ‘And among us are men who write,’ it is the line that the collector writes and is given a reward and says: Sit until I write for you, and in front of the collector is a boy with him a mile, then he comes to soft ground and the teacher writes lines quickly so that the number does not catch up with them, then he returns and erases. Draw two lines, two lines. If two lines remain, it is a sign of success, and if one line remains, it is a sign of disappointment. The Arabs call it “al-Asham,” and it is considered unlucky. Third: Ibn al-Arabi said: God Almighty did not leave any of the causes that indicate the unseen that He permitted to cling to and deduce from except visions, for He permitted them and informed that they are part of prophecy, as well as omens. As for superstitions and warnings, He forbade them. Omens are deduced from what is heard in speech what one wants from a matter if it is good. If one hears something bad, then it is superstition. The Shari’ah commands him to rejoice in the omen and to carry on with his matter happily. If one hears something bad, he should turn away from it and not return because of it. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, there is no omen except Your omen, and there is no good except Your good, and there is no god but You. Some of the men of letters narrated: Omens, warnings, and fortune-tellers are all misleading, and there are locks on the unseen. This is true, except for omens, which the Sharia has made an exception for and ordered. Therefore, what this poet has composed about it is not acceptable, for he has spoken out of ignorance, and the one who follows the Sharia is more truthful, more knowledgeable, and wiser. I said: Sufficient information has been given about superstitions and omens and the difference between them in Al-Ma’idah and elsewhere. And it was mentioned in Al-An’am that God, the Exalted, is the only One with knowledge of the unseen, and that no one knows that except what God has informed him of, or He makes a customary practice for that by which He knows what will happen according to custom, and it may differ. An example of this is if he sees a palm tree that has blossomed, then he knows that it will bear fruit, and if he sees that its blossoms have fallen, then he knows that it will not bear fruit. And it may be possible that a plague may come upon it that destroys its fruit, so that it does not bear fruit, just as it is also possible that his month will not be followed by his month, nor his day by his day, if God wants to destroy the world at that time, and other things that were explained in Al-An’am. Fourth: Ibn Khuwayjiz Mandad said: The Almighty’s statement: or a trace of knowledge means handwriting. Malik, may God have mercy on him, used to rule by handwriting if the witness recognized his handwriting, and if the judge recognized his handwriting or the handwriting of the one who wrote to him, he would rule by it. Then he changed his mind when what became apparent of tricks and forgery became apparent among the people. It was narrated from him that he said: People talk and become unjust, and they make judgments. But if the witnesses testify to the handwriting that is ruled by, such as if they testify that this is the judge’s handwriting and his book, we testify to what is in it even if they do not know what is in the book. Likewise, the will or the handwriting of a man in his admission of money to someone else, they testify that it is his handwriting and the like, so his school of thought does not differ that he rules by it. It was said: or a trace of knowledge or a remnant of knowledge, as said by Ibn Abbas, Al-Kalbi, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash and others. In Al-Sahah or a trace of knowledge a remnant of it, and likewise the trace with a fatha and it is said: the deer grew fat on trace, meaning the remnant of fat that was before that. Al-Mawardi and Al-Tha’labi recited the words of Al-Ra’i: And a woman who was excited about eating a plant in her thicket, and then she fled Al-Harawi said: “Al-Atharah and Al-Athar: the remainder.” It is said: There is neither an eye nor a trace. Maymun bin Mihran, Abu Salamah bin Abd Al-Rahman, and Qatada said: Or a trace of knowledge specifically from knowledge. Mujahid said: A narration that you inherit from those who came before you. Ikrimah and Muqatil said: A narration from the prophets. Al-Qurazi said: It is the chain of transmission. Al-Hasan: The meaning is something that is stirred up or extracted. Al-Zajjaj said: Or a trace means a sign. Atharah is a noun like generosity and bravery. The root of the word is from Athar, which is the narration. It is said: I transmitted the hadith, I transmitted it from someone other than you, and from this it is said: A transmitted hadith, meaning it was transmitted by generations after generations. Al-A’sha said: What you have argued about is clear to the listener and the follower. It is narrated between and it was read or athra with a damma on the hamza and a sukoon on the tha’, and it is possible that its meaning is a remnant of knowledge, and it is possible that its meaning is something transmitted from the books of the ancients, and the transmitted: what is spoken of from what its chain of transmission is authentic from the one who transmitted it from him, and Al-Salami, Al-Hasan and Abu Raja’ read it with a fatha on the hamza and the tha’ without an alif, meaning a special part of the knowledge that you were given or you were preferred by it over others, and it was narrated from Al-Hasan also and a group athra with a fatha on the alif and a sukoon on the tha’, the first was mentioned by Al-Tha’labi and the second by Al-Mawardi, and Al-Tha’labi narrated from Ikrimah: or an inheritance from knowledge if you are truthful. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: Bring me a book from before this or a trace of knowledge. This explains all the paths of evidence, the first of which is rational, which is the Almighty’s saying: “Say: Have you seen what you invoke besides God? Show me what they have created on the earth, or do they have a share in the heavens?” This is an argument with rational evidence that inanimate objects cannot be called upon besides God, for they neither harm nor benefit. Then He said: Bring me a book from before this, which explains the evidence of what has been heard or a trace of knowledge.
46:5: The Almighty said: And who is more astray meaning no one is more astray and ignorant, than he who calls upon besides God those who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection and they are the idols. And they are unaware of their call meaning they do not hear nor understand. So He brought them out, and they are inanimate, like the males of the children of Adam, since their worshippers had likened them to the kings and princes whom they serve.
46:6: The Almighty says: And when mankind is gathered together meaning on the Day of Resurrection. They will be enemies to them meaning these objects of worship will be enemies of the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection. So the angels are the enemies of the disbelievers, and the jinn and devils will immediately disown those who worshipped them and curse one another. It is possible that the idols were enemies of the disbelievers who worshipped them, assuming that life was created for them. The evidence for this is the Almighty's statement: We disavow to You that they used to worship us (al-Qasas 28:63). It was also said: They returned to their objects of worship because they were the cause of their destruction and the objects of worship denied their worship, which is His statement: and they were disbelievers in their worship.
46:7: God Almighty says: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, meaning the Qur’an. Those who disbelieve say of the truth when it has come to them, ‘This is obvious magic.’
46:8: God Almighty says: Or do they say, 'He invented it'? The meem is a connective, the meaning is: Do they say, 'He invented it', meaning, Muhammad says it, and it is a diversion from mentioning their calling the verses magic, and the meaning of the hamza in am is denial and astonishment, as if he said: Leave this and listen to their reprehensible saying from which astonishment is decided, and that is because Muhammad would not have been able to do it until he said it and invented it about God, and if he had been able to do it without the Arab nation, then his ability to do it would have been a miracle because it violated the norm, and if it was a miracle, then it would have been confirmation from God for him, and the judge does not believe the liar, so he is not a liar, and the pronoun refers to the truth, and what is meant by it are the verses, Say, 'If I invented it' by way of supposition, then you do not possess for me anything from God meaning, you are not able to repel God's punishment from me, so how can I invent it about God for your sake, He knows best what you indulge in meaning what you say, according to Mujahid, and it was said: You indulge in it of denial, and indulgence in something means engaging in it and rushing, They talked at length, i.e. they rushed into it. The camel pushed its water jug out of its stomach and brought it out. From this comes the poet’s saying: And they poured out their water after they had been choked with it And the people proceeded from Arafat to Mina, that is, they set out, and each set out is an exodus. Sufficient is He as a witness is an accusative of differentiation, between me and you meaning, He knows my truthfulness and that you are false, and He is the Forgiving of whoever repents, the Most Merciful to His believing servants.
46:9: The Almighty said: Say, ‘I am not an innovation among the messengers,’ meaning the first to be sent. There were messengers before me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas and others. Innovations means the first. Ikrimah and others read innovations with the opening of the dal, assuming the deletion of the complement, and the meaning is: I was not a person of innovations. It was said: innovations and innovations mean the same thing, like half and half. The poet innovated: he came with innovations, and something innovations with the kasra means innovative, and so-and-so is an innovator in this matter, meaning innovative and a people of innovations, on the authority of Al-Akhfash: And Qutrub recited the words of Adi bin Zaid: I am not an exception to the incidents that befall men who, after my misery, have become happier. And I do not know what will be done with me or with you, meaning on the Day of Resurrection. When this verse was revealed, the polytheists, Jews, and hypocrites rejoiced and said: How can we follow a prophet who does not know what will be done with him or with us, and that he has no superiority over us? Had he not innovated what he said of his own accord, the one who disobeyed him would have informed him of what will be done with him. So this verse was revealed: That God may forgive you what is past of your sin and what is to come (al-Fath 48:2). This verse was abrogated, and God humiliated the disbelievers. The Companions said: Congratulations, O Messenger of God. God has given you permission to do with you, O Messenger of God. Would that we knew what He will do with us? Then the verse was revealed: That He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow (al-Fath 48:5), and the verse was revealed: And give good tidings to the believers that they will have from God great bounty (al-Ahzab 33:47), as stated by Anas, Ibn Abbas, Qatadah, Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, and Ad-Dahhak. Umm Al-Ala, a woman from the Ansar, said: “We divided the Muhajirun emigrants and Uthman ibn Maz’un ibn Hudhafah ibn Jumah flew to us, so we recited our verses to him and he died. I said: ‘May God have mercy on you, Abu Al-Sa’ib! God has honored you.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘And how do you know that God has honored him?’ I said: ‘May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of God! Who else?’ He said: ‘As for him, certainty has come to him and we have seen nothing but good. By God, I hope for Paradise for him. By God, I am the Messenger of God, and I do not know what will happen to me or to you.’ She said: ‘By God, I will never see anyone after him.’” Al-Tha’labi mentioned this and said: He only said this when he did not know that his sin would be forgiven, and God only forgave his sin in the Battle of… Al-Hudaibiyah four years before his death. I said: The hadith of Umm al-Ala’ was included by al-Bukhari, and in it is the narration: And I do not know what will be done to him. It does not contain neither to me nor to you. This is the correct view, God willing, as will be explained. The verse is not abrogated, because it is a report. An-Nahhas said: It is impossible for there to be anything abrogating or abrogated in this for two reasons: one is that it is a report, and the other is that from the beginning of the surah to this point it is an address to the polytheists, an argument against them, and a rebuke to them. So it is necessary that this also be an address to the polytheists as it was before and after it. It is impossible for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say to the polytheists: And I do not know what will be done to me or to you, in the Hereafter, while the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the beginning of his mission until his death, continued to inform that whoever dies in disbelief will remain in Hellfire forever, and whoever dies in faith, follows him, and obeys him will be in Paradise. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw what will be done to him and to them in the Hereafter, and it is not permissible for him to say to them: I do not know what will be done to me or to you in the Hereafter, and they say: How can we follow you when you do not know whether you will be led to humiliation and ease or to torment? And punishment, and the correct statement in the verse is the statement of Al-Hasan, as Ali bin Muhammad bin Ja’far bin Hafs read on the authority of Yusuf bin Musa, who said: We were told by Wakee’, who said: We were told by Abu Bakr Al-Hudhali on the authority of Al-Hasan: And you do not know what will be done with me or with you in this world Abu Ja’far said: This is the most correct and best statement, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) does not know what will befall him and them of sickness, health, cheapness, high cost, wealth, poverty, and the like, “And if I knew the unseen, I would have increased in goodness, and no harm would have touched me. I am only a warner and a bringer of good tidings” (al-A’raf 7:188). Al-Wahidi and others mentioned on the authority of Al-Kalbi on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “When the affliction intensified for the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he saw in a dream that he was migrating to a land with palm trees, trees, and water, so he told his companions about it and they were happy with that, and they saw in it a relief from the harm they were in from the polytheists, then they remained for a while without seeing that, so they said: O Messenger of God, when will we migrate to the land that you saw?” The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) remained silent, so God the Most High revealed: And I do not know what will be done with me or with you, meaning I do not know whether I will go out to the place I saw in my dream or not. Then he said: “It is only something I saw in my dream. I do not follow except what is revealed to me,” meaning what I told you was not revealed to me. Al-Qushayri said: Based on this, there is no abrogation in the verse. It was said: The meaning is, ‘I do not know what obligations are imposed on me and you.’ Al-Tabari preferred that the meaning be: “I do not know what will happen to my situation and your situation in this world. Will you believe or disbelieve, or will you hasten the punishment or delay it.” I said: This is the meaning of Al-Hassan, Al-Suddi, and others.
