Al-Hassan said: I do not know what will happen to me or to you in this world, but as for the Hereafter, God forbid! He knew that he was in Paradise when he took his covenant with the messengers, but he said, “I do not know what will be done to me in this world. Will I be expelled as the prophets before me were expelled, or killed as the prophets before me were killed? And I do not know what will be done to you. Will I be my nation that believes or that denies, or my nation that will be pelted with stones from the sky, or that will be swallowed up by a landslide.” Then the verse was revealed: It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religions (al-Saff 61:9). He said: His religion will prevail over all religions. Then He said about his nation: And God would not punish them while you are among them (al-Anfal 8:33). So God informed him of what He would do to him and his nation, and there is no abrogation of all of this, praise be to God. Ad-Dahhak also said: I do not know what will be done to me or to you, meaning what you are commanded to do and forbidden from doing. It was said that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to say to the believers, I do not know what will be done to me or to you on the Day of Resurrection. Then God, the Most High, explained that in His saying, So that God may forgive you your past sins and what will come after. Delayed, "And with me, after that the state of the believers, then with me, the state of the unbelievers. I said: This is the meaning of the first statement, except that it includes abrogation in the sense of clarification, and that he is not to say that to the believers. What is correct is what we mentioned from Al-Hasan and others. The ma in ma yaf`al may be a relative pronoun, or an interrogative nominative, I only follow what is revealed to me, and I am only a clear warner. And it was read yahyu, meaning God Almighty, as mentioned in more than one place.
46:10: God Almighty said: Say, ‘Have you considered if it is from God?’ meaning the Qur’an. And you disbelieved in him. Al-Sha’bi said: What is meant is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And a witness from among the Children of Israel bore witness. Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Qatadah, and Mujahid said: He is Abdullah ibn Salam. He bore witness from among the Jews that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is mentioned in the Torah, and that he is a prophet from God. In Al-Tirmidhi, he said: It was revealed in verses from the Book of God, in which it was revealed: “And a witness from among the Children of Israel bore witness to the likes of him, so he believed, and you were arrogant. Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people.” It was mentioned at the end of Surat Al-Ra’d. Masruq said: It is Moses and the Torah, not Ibn Salam, because he converted to Islam in Medina, and the Surah is Meccan. He said: His statement: And you disbelieved in him is addressed to Quraysh. Al-Sha’bi said: It is whoever from among the Children of Israel believed in Moses and the Torah, because Ibn Salam only converted to Islam two years before the death of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Surah is Meccan. Al-Qushayri said: Whoever says the witness is Moses, says that the Surah is Meccan, and the name of Ibn Salam was two years before the death of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It is possible that the verse was revealed in Medina and was placed In a Meccan surah, the verse was revealed and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would say, Put it in such-and-such a surah. The verse is about arguing with the polytheists, and the evidence is that they used to consult the Jews about things, meaning that their testimony for them and the testimony of their Prophet for me are among the clearest evidence. It is not far-fetched that the surah is about arguing with the Jews. When Ibn Salam came as a Muslim before the Jews learned of his Islam, he said, O Messenger of God, make me a judge between you and the Jews. He asked them about him: What kind of man is he among you? They said, Our master and our scholar. He said, He has believed in me. They spoke ill of him... The hadith has been presented. Ibn Abbas said: The Jews were satisfied with the judgment of Ibn Salam and said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: If he testifies for you, we will believe. So he was asked, so he testified, and then he converted to Islam. On the like of it means on the like of what I have brought you. Moses testified to the Torah and Muhammad to the Qur’an. Al-Jurjani said: On the like is a connection, meaning that a witness testified against him that it is from God. So he believed meaning this witness. And you were arrogant you about belief. The answer If is omitted, its meaning is, then believe, will you believe? Al-Zajjaj said this. It was also said: Then he believed and you were arrogant Did you not wrong? This is explained by Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people. It was also said: Then he believed and you were arrogant Will you then feel secure from the punishment of God? And Have you seen is a word used for questioning and interrogation, and therefore it does not require an object. Al-Naqqash and others reported that in the verse there is an advancement and delay, and its meaning is, Say, Have you seen, if it is from God and a witness from the Children of Israel testifies, and he believes and you disbelieve, then God does not guide the wrongdoing people.
46:11: God Almighty said: And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, ‘If it had been good, they would not have preceded us to it.’ There are six different opinions about the reason for its revelation: First: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, invited Abu Dharr al-Ghifari to Islam in Mecca, and he responded. His people sought his protection, and their leader came to him and converted to Islam. Then the leader invited them, and they converted to Islam. report of this reached the Quraysh, and they said: “Ghifari is the allies. If this were good, they would not have preceded us to it.” So this verse was revealed, as Abu al-Mutawakkil said. Second: Zunayrah converted to Islam and her sight was damaged. They said to her: Al-Lat and Al-Uzza have damaged you. God restored her sight. The leaders of Quraysh said: If what Muhammad brought was good, Zunayrah would not have preceded us to it. Then God Almighty revealed this verse, as said by Urwah ibn Al-Zubayr. Third: Those who disbelieved were Banu Amir, Ghatafan, Tamim, Asad, Hanzala, and Ashja’. They said to those who had converted to Islam from Ghifar, Juhayna, Muzayna, and Khuza’a, If what Muhammad had brought had been any good, the shepherds of the camels would not have preceded us to it, for we are more powerful than them. This was said by Al-Kalbi and Al-Zajjaj, and Al-Qushayri narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Qatada said: It was revealed about the polytheists of Quraysh. They said, If what Muhammad was calling us to had been any good, Bilal, Suhayb, Ammar, so-and-so, and so-and-so would not have preceded us to it. This is the fourth statement. The fifth statement: The disbelieving Jews said to the believers, meaning Abdullah bin Salam and his companions: If the religion of Muhammad was true, they would not have preceded us to it. This was said by most of the commentators. Al-Tha’labi narrated it. Masruq said: The disbelievers said: If it was good, the Jews would not have preceded us to it. So this verse was revealed. This opposition from the infidels in their saying: If it had been good, they would not have preceded us in it is one of the greatest oppositions, as it turns against them for everyone who opposes them, so that it is said to them: If what you are upon was good, we would not have deviated from it, and if your denial of the Messenger was good, you would not have preceded us in it. Al-Mawardi mentioned this. Then it was said: His statement: They did not precede us in it may be from the words of the infidels to some of the believers, and it may be in reference to moving from addressing them to speaking in the third person, like the statement of God Almighty: Until, when you were in the ship and it sailed with them (Yunus 10:22), And when they were not guided by it meaning faith, and it was said the Qur’an, and it was said Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Then they will say, ‘This is an ancient falsehood’ meaning that when they did not attain guidance through the Qur’an or the one who brought it, they opposed it and accused it of lying, and they said this is an ancient falsehood, just as they said: Legends of the ancients. And it was said to some of them: Is there in the Qur’an: Whoever is ignorant of something, opposes it? He said, Yes. God Almighty said: And when they are not guided by it, they will say, ‘This is an ancient falsehood.’ And similar to it: Rather, they denied that of which they had no knowledge. (Yunus 10:39)
46:12: The Almighty said: And before it meaning before the Qur’an, the Book of Moses meaning the Torah as an imam to be followed in what is in it and a mercy from God. There is an omission in the speech, meaning you were not guided by it, because the Torah described the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and belief in him, so they abandoned that. Imam is in the accusative case as a state, because the meaning is: And the Book of Moses preceded him as an imam, and a mercy is conjoined with it. It was said: It is in the accusative case with an implied verb, meaning we sent it down as an imam and a mercy. Al-Akhfash said: It is definite, because the Book of Moses is definite by addition, because if an indefinite noun is repeated or added to or the definite article is added to it, it becomes definite. And this is a Book meaning the Qur’an confirming meaning the Torah and what came before it of the books. It was said: Confirming the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. An Arabic tongue is in the accusative case as a state, meaning confirming what came before it in Arabic. A tongue is an introduction to the state, meaning an emphasis. And as they say, Zaid came to me, a righteous man, and he mentioned a man for emphasis. And it was said: It is in the accusative case with an implied verb, meaning, and this is a confirming book, I mean an Arabic tongue. And it was said: It is in the accusative case with the omission of the preposition, meaning: in an Arabic tongue. And it was said: A tongue is the object, and what is meant by it is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, meaning this is a confirming book for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because it is his miracle. And the estimate is: confirming with an Arabic tongue, so the tongue is in the accusative case with confirming, which is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And it is far-fetched for the tongue to be the Qur’an, because the meaning is that it confirms itself. To warn those who have wronged is the reading of the general public linadhir with the ya’, report about the book, meaning to warn those who have wronged themselves with disbelief and disobedience. And it was said: It is report about the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. Nafi’, Ibn ‘Amir, and al-Bazzi read with the ta’, and Abu ‘Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose it, on the address of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. God Almighty said: You are only a warner (al-Ra’d 13:7), And good tidings for the doers of good bushra is in the nominative case, meaning it is good tidings. It was said: In apposition to the Book, meaning this is a book that confirms and gives good tidings. It is also permissible for it to be in the accusative case by dropping the preposition, meaning to warn those who have wronged and to give good tidings. So when the preposition was deleted, it was in the accusative case. It was said: On the source, meaning and give good tidings to the doers of good tidings. So when it was replaced by good tidings or glad tidings, it was in the accusative case, as you say: I came to visit you, and as an honor to you and to fulfill your right, meaning to visit you and honor you and fulfill your right. So, the honor was in the accusative case by an implied verb.
46:13: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, those who say, ‘Our Lord is God,’ and then remain steadfast… The meaning of the verse has already been presented. Ibn Abbas said, it was revealed regarding Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, and the verse is general: There will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
46:14: God Almighty says: Those are the companions of Paradise, abiding therein eternally as reward for what they used to do. Punishment is an accusative of the verbal noun.
46:15: It contains seven issues: First: The Almighty’s statement: And We have enjoined upon man, to his parents, good treatment. This indicates the difference in a person’s relationship with his parents. He may obey them or he may disobey them. That is, something like this is not far-fetched in the case of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his people, such that some may respond to him and some may disbelieve. This is the way the words connect to each other, as Al-Qushayri said. The second: The Almighty’s saying: goodly. The reading of the common people is goodly. This is how it is in the copies of the Qur’an of the people of the Two Holy Mosques, Basra, and Ash-Sham. Ibn Abbas and the Kufians read goodness. Their proof is the Almighty’s saying in Surat Al-An’am and Bani Israel, And to parents, goodness (al-Isra’ 17:23). This is how it is in the copies of the Qur’an of Kufa. The proof for the first reading is the Almighty’s saying in Surat al-Ankabut 29:And We have enjoined upon man, concerning his parents, goodness (al-Ankabut 29:8). They did not differ on it. Goodness is the opposite of ugliness, and goodness is the opposite of mistreatment. A recommendation is a command. We have already discussed this and on whom it was revealed. Third: The Almighty’s saying: His mother bore him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship, meaning with hatred and difficulty. The general reading is with the kaf open, and Abu Ubaid chose it. He said: Likewise, the word karah is with the fatha in all of the Qur’an except for the one in Surat al-Baqarah 2:Fighting has been prescribed for you, though it is hateful to you (Al-Baqarah 2:216), because that is a noun and all of these are verbal nouns. The Kufians read karhan with the damma. It was said: They are two dialects like weakness and weakness and witness and witness. Al-Kisa’i said this, and this is also the case with all of the Basrans. Al-Kisa’i also said, and Al-Farra’, regarding the difference between them, that karah with the damma is what a person forces upon himself, and with the fatha it is what he forces upon someone else, meaning by force and anger. For this reason, some of the Arabists said that karhan with the kaf open is a mistake. Fourth: The Almighty’s statement: And his gestation and weaning is thirty months. Ibn Abbas said: If she carries for nine months, she breastfeeds for twenty-one months, and if she carries for six months, she breastfeeds for twenty-four months. It was narrated that a woman was brought to Uthman who had given birth after six months, and he wanted to sentence her to the prescribed punishment. Ali, may God be pleased with him, said to him: “That is not required of her. God Almighty said: “And his gestation and weaning is thirty months.” And God Almighty said: Mothers shall nurse their children for two complete years. (al-Baqarah 2:233), so breastfeeding is twenty-four months and pregnancy is six months. Uthman retracted his statement and did not punish her. This has been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. It has been said that three months are not counted at the beginning of pregnancy, because the child in her is a sperm, a clot, and a lump of flesh, so it does not have a weight that can be felt. This is the meaning of the Almighty’s statement: And when he covered her, she conceived a light burden and passed through it. (al-A’raf 7:189) Weaning is weaning. This has been discussed previously in Luqman. Al-Hasan, Ya’qub, and others read: and his separation. With the opening of the fa and the sukoon of the sad, and it was narrated that the verse was revealed about Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, and his pregnancy and weaning lasted thirty months. His mother carried him for nine months and breastfed him for twenty-one months. There is an implied meaning in the speech, meaning the period of his pregnancy and the period of his weaning was thirty months. If it were not for this implied meaning, thirty would have been in the accusative case as an adverbial phrase and the meaning would have changed. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: Until he reached his full strength. Ibn Abbas said: Eighteen years. And he said in the narration of Ata’ from him: Abu Bakr accompanied the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he was eighteen years old and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was twenty years old, and they wanted to go to Syria for trade, so they stopped at a place where there was a lote tree, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat in its shade, and Abu Bakr went to a monk there and asked him about religion, so the monk said: Who is the man in the shade of the tree? He said: That is Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib. He said: By God, this is a prophet, and no one has taken shade under it after Jesus. So certainty and belief entered Abu Bakr’s heart, and he hardly ever left the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his travels and his presence. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was given the prophecy when he was forty years old, Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, believed in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he was thirty-eight years old. When he reached forty years of age, he said: My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents Al-An’am. Al-Sha’bi and Ibn Zayd said: The most severe is patience. Al-Hasan said: It is reaching the age of forty, and the proof against him was established from him. The discussion of the verse has already passed in Al-An’am. Al-Suddi and Al-Dahhak said: It was revealed about Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas, and it has been mentioned before. Al-Hasan said: It is a mursal hadith that was revealed in general terms, and God knows best. Sixth: The Almighty said: He said, ‘My Lord, inspire me.’ That is, inspire me. To be grateful is in the accusative case as a verbal noun, meaning to be grateful for Your blessings upon me meaning what You have bestowed upon me of guidance, and on my parents with compassion and mercy until they raised me when I was young, and it was said: You have bestowed upon me health and well-being and on my parents wealth and riches. Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: This verse was revealed about Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him. Both of his parents converted to Islam, and no one among the emigrants had both parents convert to Islam except him, so God enjoined them upon him and this was binding after him. His father is Abu Quhafah Uthman ibn Amir ibn Amr ibn Sa’d ibn Taym, and his mother is Umm al-Khair, and her name is Salma bint Sakhr ibn Amir ibn Ka’b ibn Sa’d, and the mother of his father Abu Quhafah is Qaylah (with a voiced ya’ with two dots below it) and the wife of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq is called Qatilah (with a voiced ta’ with two dots above it) bint Abd al-Uzza, and to do righteousness that pleases you. Ibn Abbas said: So God answered him and freed nine believers who were being punished. Among them were Bilal and Aamer bin Fuhaira, and he did not leave any good thing without God helping him in it. In the Sahih, it is narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Who among you is fasting today?’ Abu Bakr said: ‘I am.’ He said: ‘Who among you followed a funeral today?’ Abu Bakr said: ‘I am.’ He said: ‘Who among you fed a poor person today?’ Abu Bakr said: ‘I am.’ He said: ‘Who among you visited a sick person today?’ Abu Bakr said: ‘I am.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘If these things are combined in a person, he will enter Paradise.’” Seventh: The Almighty’s saying: And make righteous for me my offspring. That is, make my offspring righteous. Ibn Abbas said: So he did not have a son, father, or mother who did not believe in God alone. There was no one among the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he and his parents, sons, and daughters, all of them, except Abu Bakr. Sahl ibn Abdullah said: The meaning is: Make them true successors for me, and true slaves for you. Abu Uthman said: Make them pious to me and obedient to you. Ibn Ata’ said: Guide them to righteous deeds that will please you. Muhammad ibn Ali said: Do not give Satan, the self, and desires a way to them. Malik ibn Maqul said: Abu Ma’shar complained to Talha ibn Musarraf about his son, so he said: Seek help against him with this verse, and recite: “My Lord, inspire me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents and to do righteousness of which You approve. And make righteous for me my offspring. Indeed, I have repented to You, and indeed, I am of the Muslims.” Indeed, I have repented to You. Ibn Abbas said: I have returned from the matter that I was upon. And indeed, I am of the Muslims, that is, those sincere in monotheism.
46:16: The Almighty’s saying: Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did and overlook their misdeeds. The general reading is with a damma on the ya’ in both of them. It was also read yattaqubal and yatajidhu with a fatha on the ya’, and the pronoun in both of them refers to God Almighty. Hafs, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read nataqubal and nantajidhu with a noon in both of them, meaning We forgive them and pardon them. The origin of pardon is from jazat if you do not stop at it. This verse indicates that the verse before it, And We enjoined upon man to the end, is a mursal that was revealed in general terms. This is the saying of Al-Hasan. The meaning of nataqubal from them is that We accept their good deeds and overlook their misdeeds. Zayd ibn Aslam said, and he narrates it with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, that if they become Muslim, their good deeds are accepted and their misdeeds are forgiven. It was said: The best is that which requires reward from acts of obedience, and there is no reward or punishment in permissible good. Ibn ‘Isa narrated it. In the companions of Paradise. In means with, meaning from The people of Paradise, you say: May He honor you and be good to you among all the people of the city, meaning with all of them. The promise of truth is in the accusative case because it is a source that confirms what preceded it, meaning God promised the people of faith that He would accept from their good deeds and overlook their wrongdoers. The promise of truth, and it is a case of adding something to itself, because truth is that promise that God promised, it is like His Most High’s saying: The certainty of truth (al-Waqi’ah 56:95). This is according to the Kufians. As for the Basrans, its interpretation is: The promise of truthful speech or truthful book, so the description was deleted, and this has been mentioned in more than one place. That which they were promised in this world on the tongues of the messengers, and that is Paradise.
46:17: God Almighty said: And he who said to his parents, ‘Fie upon you! Do you promise me that I will come forth?’ That is, that I will be resurrected. And the generations before me have passed away. The reading of Nafi’, Hafs and others is af with a kasra and a tanween. Ibn Kathir read it without a tanween, and Ibn ‘Amir and al-Mufaddal from ‘Asim read it with a fatha without a tanween. The rest read it with a kasra without a tanween. All of these are dialects. It has already been mentioned in Bani Isra’il. The reading of the general public is ata’daanani with two light noons and the fatha of the ya’ of the people of Medina and Mecca. The rest kept it sukoon. Abu Haywah, al-Mughira and Hisham read ata’daanani with one double noon. This is also the case in the copies of the Qur’an of the people of Ash-Sham. The general public has a damma on the alif and a fatha on the ra’ of an khurooj. Al-Hasan, Nasr, Abu al-‘Aliyah, al-A’mash and Abu Mu’ammar read it with a fatha on the alif and a damma on the ra’. Ibn ‘Abbas, al-Suddi, Abu al-‘Aliyah and Mujahid said: It was revealed about ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, may God be pleased with them both, and his parents used to call him to Islam and he would respond to them with what God Almighty had informed them. Qatada and al-Suddi also said: He is ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr before his conversion to Islam, and his father and mother were…” Umm Ruman called him to Islam and promised him resurrection, so he responded to them with what God Almighty narrated about him, and this was from him before his conversion to Islam. It was narrated that Aisha, may God be pleased with her, denied that it was revealed about Abd al-Rahman. Al-Hasan and Qatada also said: It is a description of a disbelieving slave who was disobedient to his parents. Al-Zajjaj said: How can it be said that it was revealed about Abd al-Rahman before his conversion to Islam, while God Almighty says: Those are the ones against whom the word has come into effect among nations (al-Ahqaf 46:18), meaning the punishment, and one of its necessities is the lack of faith, and Abd al-Rahman is one of the best of the believers, so the correct thing is that it was revealed about a disbelieving slave who was disobedient to his parents. Muhammad bin Ziyad said: Muawiyah wrote to Marwan bin al-Hakam to have the people pledge allegiance to Yazid, so Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Bakr said: You have brought it like the Heraclians. Do you pledge allegiance to your sons?! Marwan said, “He is the one about whom God said: ‘And he who said to his parents, ‘Fie upon you both!’” 1:17. He said, “By God, that is not the case. If you had wanted, you could have named him, but God cursed your father while you were in his loins, so you are exempt from God’s curse.” Al-Mahdawi said, “Whoever attributed the verse to Abd al-Rahman, his statement after that, ‘Those are the ones upon whom the Word has come into effect,’ meant those who believed what was mentioned above. The beginning of the verse is specific and the end of it is general. It was said that when Abd al-Rahman said, ‘And generations before me have passed away,’ he said, ‘In addition to that, where are Abdullah ibn Jud’an, Ibn Uthman ibn Amr, Ibn Amir ibn Ka’b, and the elders of Quraysh so that I may ask them about what they say? His statement, ‘Those are the ones upon whom the Word has come into effect,’ refers to those people.” I said: The story of Abdur-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr in Surat Al-An'am, when he said, He has companions who call him to guidance (Al-An'am 6:71), has already passed, which indicates that this verse was revealed about him, since he was a disbeliever, and when he became a Muslim and achieved excellence, it was determined that what is meant by his saying, Those are the ones against whom the Word has come into effect, "and they meaning his parents, seek aid from God" is that they call upon God for guidance for him, or they seek aid from God for his disbelief. So when the preposition was omitted, the verb was connected and made accusative. It was said that seeking aid is supplication, so there is no need for the preposition "with". Al-Farra' said: God answered his supplication and helped him. "Woe to you! He believed" meaning he believed in the resurrection. "Indeed, the promise of God is truth" meaning it is true and there is no breach in it. "Then he says, This meaning what his parents say, is nothing but legends of the ancients meaning their stories and what they wrote that have no basis.
46:18: The Almighty’s statement: Those are the ones upon whom the Word has come into effect means those referred to by Ibn Abi Bakr in his statement: Bring to life for me the elders of Quraysh, and they are the ones meant by his statement: And generations before me have passed away. As for Ibn Abi Bakr, Abdullah or Abd al-Rahman, God answered his father’s supplication in his statement: And make righteous for me my offspring, as mentioned above. The meaning of: The Word has come into effect upon them is that the punishment is obligatory upon them, and it is the word of God: These are in Paradise, and I do not care, and these are in the Fire, and I do not care, “among nations” means with nations, that have passed away, has come before and passed, before them of the jinn and mankind the disbelievers, that they meaning those disbelieving nations, were losers for their deeds, meaning their efforts were wasted and they lost Paradise.
46:19: The Almighty said: “And for all are degrees” meaning, for each of the two groups, the believers and the disbelievers, from among the jinn and mankind, there are ranks with God on the Day of Resurrection according to their deeds. Ibn Zayd said: The degrees of the people of Hell in this verse go downwards, and the degrees of the people of Paradise are upwards. And that He may fully recompense them for their deeds Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaisin, Asim, Abu Amr, and Ya’qub read it with the letter ya because of the mention of God before it, which is the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, the promise of God is true (Yunus 10:55). Abu Hatim chose it, and the rest read it with the letter nun in response to the Almighty’s saying: And We have enjoined upon man, concerning his parents (Al-‘Ankabut: 8). This is the choice of Abu ‘Ubaid: And they will not be wronged meaning, the wrongdoer will not be increased nor will the good-doer be diminished. I know
46:20: God Almighty said: And on the Day when those who disbelieved are exposed to the Fire meaning, the cover is removed and they are brought close to the Fire and look at it, You have taken away your good things meaning it is said to them, You have taken away, so the statement is implied. Al-Hasan, Nasr, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Ya’qub, and Ibn Kathir read A’zahabtum with two light hamzas, and Abu Hatim chose it. Abu Haywah and Hisham read A’zahabtum with one long hamza as a question, the rest with one hamza without a long vowel as a statement, and all of them are eloquent languages and their meaning is rebuke. The Arabs rebuke with questions and without questions, and this has been mentioned previously. Abu Ubaid chose to leave out the question because it is the reading of the seven imams: Nafi’, Asim, Abu Amr, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa’i, along with those who agreed with them: Shaibah, Al-Zuhri, Ibn Muhaisin, Al-Mughirah ibn Abi Shihab, Yahya ibn Al-Harith, Al-A’mash, and Yahya ibn And Thaab and others, this is what most people are doing, and leaving the question is better, because proving it gives the impression that they did not do that, as you say: I wronged you? You mean I did not wrong you, and proving it is also good. The speaker says: I went and did such and such, he rebukes and says: I went and did that! All of that is permissible, and the meaning of you went away with your good things is that you enjoyed the good things in this world and followed desires and pleasures, meaning sins. So today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation, meaning the punishment of disgrace and disgrace. Mujahid said: Humiliation is humiliation, Qatadah: in the language of the Quraysh. Because you were arrogant upon the earth without right meaning you acted superior to its people without justification, and because you were wicked in your actions through transgression and injustice. It was also said: You spent your good things meaning you wasted your youth in disbelief and sins. Ibn Bahr said: The good things are youth and strength, taken from their saying his best things are gone, meaning his youth and strength. Al-Mawardi said: I found Ad-Dahhak also said this. I said: The first statement is more apparent. Al-Hasan narrated on the authority of Al-Ahnaf bin Qais that he heard Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, say: I know better about the hardship of life. If I wanted, I could have made livers, sala’, sanab, and salaiq, but I keep my good deeds, for God Almighty described people and said: You have spent your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them. Abu Ubaid said in the hadith of Omar: If I wanted, I could have called for salaiq and sanab, karakir and humps, and in some of the hadith: and afladh. Abu Amr and others said: Al-Sala’ with long and broken vowels is the barbecue, and it was named thus because it is roasted in the fire. Al-Sala’ is also: the roasting of the fire. If you open the sad, you shorten it and say: he roasted the fire. Al-Sanab is the dyes made from mustard and raisins. Abu Amr said: For this reason, the mule is called sanabi, and its color was likened to that. He said: Al-Sala’iq with seen is what is boiled from legumes and others. Another said: It is Al-Sala’iq with sad. Jarir said: The cost of living for the Zayd family is on me, but who will provide me with the gifts and the hookahs? And salaiq: wide thin bread, and this meaning has already been mentioned in Al-A’raf. As for karakir, they are karakir of camels, its singular is karkara and it is well-known. This is the saying of Abu Ubaid. And in As-Sahah: And karkara is the millstone of the camel’s throat, and it is one of the five blows, and karkara is also a group of people, and Abu Malik Amr bin Karkara is a man from the scholars of language. Abu Ubaid said: As for aflaadh, its singular is faladh, and it is a piece of the liver. A’sha Bahla said: It is enough for him to have a hard time if he is afflicted by a roasting, and his thirst is satisfied by drinking a lot of water. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that Omar, may God be pleased with him, said: If I wished, I would be the best of you in food and the softest in clothing, but I save my good things for the Hereafter. When Omar came to Ash-Sham, he had food prepared for him, the likes of which he had never seen before. He said: This is for us, but what about the poor Muslims who died without having their fill of barley bread? Khalid ibn al-Walid said: Paradise is for them. Omar’s eyes filled with tears, and he said: If our share of this world is this rubbish, and they have gone with their share of Paradise, then they have been far removed from us. In Sahih Muslim and others: “Omar, may God be pleased with him, entered upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in his drinking place when he was abandoning his wives. He said: I turned around and did not see anything that would distract the eye except a pair of folded leather garments whose fragrance was spreading. I said: O Messenger of God, you are the Messenger of God and His chosen one, while this is Khosrow and Caesar in brocade and silk?” He said: So he sat up and said: Are you in doubt, O Ibn al-Khattab? Those are people for whom their good things were hastened in their lives. The world, so I said: Ask forgiveness for me! He said: O God, forgive him. Hafs ibn Abi Al-Aas said: I used to eat lunch at Umar ibn Al-Khattab’s house, may God be pleased with him, bread and oil, bread with vinegar, bread with milk, bread with dried meat, and the least of that was fresh meat. He used to say: Do not sift the flour, for it is all food. Then, thick, cracked bread was brought to him, and he started eating and saying: Eat. But we did not eat. He said: Why are you not eating? We said: By God, O Commander of the Faithful, we will return to softer food than this food of yours. He said: O son of Abi Al-Aas, do you not see that I know that if I were to order a fat goat, its hair would be removed and it would come out praying as if it were such and such? Do you not see that I know that if I were to order a sa’ or two sa’s of raisins, and I put it in a water skin, then I would pour water over it, it would cry out as if it were the blood of a gazelle? I said: O Commander of the Faithful, yes! How do you describe life? He said: Yes! By God, there is no god but Him, were it not that I fear that my good deeds will be diminished on the Day of Resurrection, I would have shared your life! But I heard God the Most High say to a al-Nas 114:You squandered your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them, “So today you are recompensed with the punishment of humiliation” meaning humiliation because you were arrogant upon the earth without right meaning you acted too proudly to obey God and His servants, and because you were wicked you disobeyed God. Jabir said: My family craved meat, so I bought it for them. Then I passed by Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him and he said: What is this, Jabir? So I told him and he said: Whenever one of you craved something, he puts it in his stomach! Isn’t he afraid that he might be one of the people of this verse: You have spent your good things, Ibn al-Arabi said: This is a rebuke from him to him for his excessive buying of meat and his abandoning the roughness of bread and water. If one consumes good things from what is permissible, his nature seeks them out and habit makes him enjoy them. If he loses them, he finds it easy to obtain them through doubtful means until he falls into what is purely forbidden due to the prevalence of habit and the prevalence of desire over the soul that commands evil. So, ‘Umar took the matter into account from the beginning and protected it from its beginning, as his peers do. The one who regulates this matter and preserves its law is that a person should eat whatever he finds, whether good or barren, and not make an effort to eat good things and make them a habit. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would eat his fill if he found them, and be patient if he did not have them. He would eat sweets if he could, and drink honey if he could, and eat meat if it was available, and he would not rely on it at all, nor make it a habit. The livelihood of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is well-known, and the way of the Companions is transmitted. So, today, when what is forbidden has taken hold and the spoils of life are corrupted, salvation is difficult, and God He grants sincerity and helps in salvation through His mercy. It has been said that the rebuke is for abandoning gratitude, not for consuming permissible good things. This is good, for consuming permissible good things is permitted. If he abandons gratitude for it and uses it to help him in what is not permissible for him, then he has lost it. And God knows best.
46:21: The Almighty said: And remember the brother of ‘Aad he is Hud bin Abdullah bin Rabah, peace be upon him, he was their brother in lineage not in religion when he warned his people in Al-Ahqaf meaning remind these polytheists of the story of ‘Aad so that they may take heed from it, and it was said: He ordered him to remember in himself the story of Hud so that he may follow his example, and his people’s denial of him would be easy for him, and Al-Ahqaf is the land of ‘Aad, and they are the great sands, according to Al-Khalil and others, and they had conquered the people of the earth with their strength, and Al-Ahqaf is the plural of Haqf, which is the long and crooked part of the great sand that did not reach a mountain, and the plural is Haqaf, Ahqaf, Huquf, and Ahqaf, the sand and the crescent, meaning crooked, and it was said: Al-Haqf is the plural of Haqaf, and Al-Ahqaf is the plural of plural, and it is said: Haqf Ahqaf, Al-A’sha said: He went to Artah, Haqf Ahqfa Any rectangular sand dune, and the verb is ahqf. Al-Ajjaj said: The nights are folding, one by one, like the crescent moon, until I close it That is, he bent and turned around, and Imru’ al-Qais said: Like the sand dunes, the two newborns walk on it, expecting it to be soft and easy to touch. And what is meant by Al-Ahqaf here is disputed. Ibn Zayd said: They are elevated, oblong sands like mountains, but they are not yet mountains. The evidence for that is what we have mentioned. Qatada said: They are elevated mountains in Ash-Shihr, and Ash-Shihr is close to Aden. It is said: Ash-Shihr Oman and Ash-Shihr Oman, and it is the sea coast between Oman and Aden. And from him also, it was mentioned to us that Ad were living in Yemen, people of sands overlooking the sea in a land called Ash-Shihr. And Mujahid said: It is a land of Hisma called Al-Ahqaf. Hisma with a kasra on the ha is the name of a land in the desert in which there are towering mountains with smooth surfaces that the darkness hardly leaves. Al-Nabigha said: So he became wise in the mountains of Hasma, the dust-dusted, the darkness-covered Al-Jawhari said: Ibn Abbas and Al-Dahhak said: Al-Ahqaf is a mountain in the Levant. Ibn Abbas also said: It is a valley between Oman and Mahra. Muqatil said: The homes of Ad were in Yemen in Hadhramaut in a valley called Mahra, and the Mahri camels are named after it, so they say: Mahri and Mahari camels. They were people of pillars that moved in the spring, and when the rains increased, they returned to their homes. They were from the tribe of Iram. Al-Kalbi said: Al-Ahqaf is a mountain from which the water dried up during the time of flooding. The water would drain from the earth, but its trace would remain. Al-Tufayl narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that he said: The best of two valleys among people is a valley in Mecca and a valley in which Adam descended in the land of India. The worst of two valleys among people are a valley in Al-Ahqaf and a valley in Hadhramaut called Barhut, into which the souls of the unbelievers are cast. The best well among people is the well of Zamzam, and the worst well among people is the well of Barhut, and it is in that valley in Hadhramaut. And the warners have passed away means the messengers have passed away. Before him means before Hud. And behind him means and after him. Al-Farra’ said: And in Ibn Mas’ud’s reading before him and after him, that you worship none but God. This is from the words of the sender, so it is an interjectional statement. Then Hud said: Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a terrible Day. And it was said: that you worship none but God is from the words of Hud, and God knows best.
46:22: The Almighty’s saying: They said, ‘Have you come to us to turn us away from our gods?’ There are two interpretations of this: One of them is to turn us away from worshipping them through slander. The second is to turn us away from our gods through prevention. Ad-Dahhak said: Urwah ibn Udaynah said: If you are not good at what you do, then others have already done it. He says: If you are not successful in doing good, then you are among a people who have been turned away: Then bring us what you promise us. This indicates that a promise can be used as a threat, if you should be among the truthful. That you are a prophet.
46:23: God Almighty said: “He said, ‘The knowledge’ of the time of the coming of the punishment is only with God, not with me. ‘And I convey to you what I have been sent with’ from your Lord, ‘but I see that you are a people who are ignorant’ in your question of hastening the punishment.
46:24: When they saw it as a cloud, Al-Mubarrad said: The pronoun in saw it refers to something unmentioned, and this is shown by His statement: a cloud, so the pronoun refers to the clouds, meaning when they saw the clouds as a cloud, a cloud is in the accusative case for repetition, it was called that because it appears in the sky, and it was said: it is in the accusative case for the state, and it was said: the pronoun refers to His statement: Then bring us what you promise us. So when they saw it, they thought it was a cloud that would rain on them, but the rain had been slow to come to them, and when they saw it facing their valleys, they were happy, and it had come to them from a valley from which it was customary that what came from it was rain, as Ibn Abbas and others said. Al-Jawhari said: The cloud that appears on the horizon, from this is the statement of God Almighty: This is a cloud that will bring us rain, meaning that it will bring us rain, because it is definite and cannot be an attribute of a cloud, which is indefinite, and the Arabs only do such things with difficult nouns from verbs and not others. Jarir said: Oh God, if he wanted you, he would have found you distancing him and depriving him. It is not permissible to say: This is our young man. An Arab said after breaking the fast: There is a fasting woman who will not fast, and a standing woman who will not stand. So he made it an adjective for the indefinite noun and an addition to the definite noun. I said: His saying: It is not permissible for it to be an attribute of an accident is contrary to the saying of the grammarians, and the addition in the estimation of separation, so it is a verbal addition, not a real one, for it did not give the first definition, but rather the noun is indefinite in its state, so therefore it became an attribute of the indefinite, this is the saying of the grammarians in the verse and the verse, and the attribute of the indefinite is indefinite, and Lord does not enter except with the indefinite, Rather it is meaning Hud said to them, and the evidence for that is the reading of the one who read Hud said, Rather it is and the one who read Say, Rather, what you have hastened is a wind meaning God said: He said, Rather, it is what you have hastened, meaning their saying, Then bring us what you promise us then he explained what it is and said: A wind in which is a painful torment and the wind with which they were tormented arose from that cloud that they saw, and Hud came out from among them, so it began to carry the tents and carry the women and raise them as if they were locusts, then they struck the rocks with them. Ibn Abbas said: The first thing that they saw was that they stood up and stretched out their hands, The first thing they knew was that it was a torment was that they saw men and livestock coming out of their homes, blown away by the wind between the sky and the earth like feathers. They entered their homes and closed their doors, but the wind tore the doors open and threw them down. Then God commanded the wind, and it blew the sands away from them, and they were under the sand for seven nights and eight days, groaning. Then God commanded the wind, and it removed the sands from them and carried them away, throwing them into the sea.
46:25: It is the one about which God Almighty said: It destroyed everything by the command of its Lord, meaning everything it passed through of the men of Ad and their wealth. Ibn Abbas said: Meaning everything it was sent to. Destruction means destruction, as well as devastation. It was read it destroys everything from the root word dammaru damman, it is said: he destroyed it with destruction and devastation and it was destroyed upon it with the same meaning, and dammar yadmur damur means he entered without permission. In the hadith: Whoever asks permission before his eyes has destroyed, with the mim pronounced with a lightened mim, and Tadmur is a city in the Levant, and a Tadmurian jerboa is a small, short person. By the command of her Lord with the permission of her Lord. In Bukhari, “On the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, she said: I never saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, laughing so much that I could see his uvula. He would only smile.” She said: And whenever he saw a cloud or a wind, it would be evident on his face. She said: O Messenger of God, when people see a cloud, they rejoice, hoping that it will rain, but when you see it, I see dislike on your face. He said: O Aisha, what assures me that there will be no torment in it? Some people were tormented by a wind, but some people saw a storm and said, ‘This is a cloud that will bring us rain.’ Narrated by Muslim and al-Tirmidhi, who said: A good hadith. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: ‘I was aided by the north wind, and I destroyed the ‘Ad people by the south wind.’” Al-Mawardi mentioned that the one who said: This is a cloud that will bring us rain was from the people of ‘Ad: Bakr ibn Mu’awiyah. When he saw the clouds, he said: I see a cloudy sky that will not leave anyone from ‘Ad. ‘Amr ibn Maymun mentioned that it was…” Ibn Ishaq said: Hud and those who were with him from the believers secluded themselves in a pen, nothing of it affected him or those with him except what softened the tops of their garments, and the souls enjoyed it, and it would pass by those of Ad in the desert between the sky and the earth and crush them with stones until they perished. Al-Kalbi narrated that their poet said about that: Then Hud invoked against them a curse, and they became listless. A wind blew upon them, leaving Ad in a state of extinction. She spent seven nights without leaving a single stick on earth. And Hud lived among his people for one hundred and fifty years after them. So they became such that nothing could be seen except their dwellings. Asim and Hamza read nothing could be seen except their dwellings with a ya’, not the subject. Hammad bin Salamah narrated the same on the authority of Ibn Kathir, except that he read you see with a ta’. This was narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr on the authority of Asim. The rest you see with an open taa, their dwellings in the accusative, meaning you do not see, O Muhammad, except their dwellings. Al-Mahdawi said: And whoever reads with a taa without the agent being named, then according to the apparent word it is the feminine dwellings, and it is rare and is only used in poetry. Abu Hatim said: This is not correct in the language unless it is omitted, as you say in speech, Do you not see the women except Zainab? And it is not permissible to say, Do you not see except Zainab? And Sibawayh said: Its meaning is you do not see their persons except their dwellings. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose the reading of Asim and Hamza. Al-Kisa’i said: Its meaning is nothing is seen except their dwellings, so it is based on the meaning, as you say, No one stood up except Hind, and the meaning is, No one stood up except Hind. Al-Farra’ said: The people are not seen because they were under the sand, and their dwellings are only seen because they are standing. Thus do We recompense the criminal people. That is, with this punishment We punish the polytheists.
46:26: The Almighty said: And We have certainly empowered them in that in which We have empowered you. It was said: Indeed, We have empowered you in that in which We have empowered you. This is what Al-Qutbi said: Al-Akhfash recited: One hopes for what one does not see and is exposed to the slightest danger Another said: As soon as we became cowardly, our fates and the state of others will be destroyed. It was said: Ma means who, and in means what, and the meaning is: And We have empowered them in that in which We have not empowered you, Al-Mubarrad said. It was said: It is a conditional and its answer is an omitted pronoun, and the meaning is: And We have empowered them in that in which, if We had empowered you, your transgression would have been greater and your obstinacy more intense, and the speech was completed, then he began, saying: And We gave them hearing, sight, and hearts, meaning hearts with which they understand, so their hearing, sight, and hearts availed them nothing from the punishment of God, because they were denying disbelieving in the verses of God, and that which they were mocking encompassed them” encompassed them, that which they were mocking.
46:27: The Almighty says: And We destroyed the towns around you meaning the stone of Thamud, the towns of Lot, and similar towns that were adjacent to the land of Hijaz, and their stories were well-known to them, And We diversified the signs meaning the arguments, evidence, various types of proofs, and sermons, meaning We explained them to the people of those towns, that they might return but they did not return. It was said: meaning We diversified the verses of the Qur’an in promise and threat, stories, and miracles, so that perhaps these polytheists would return.
46:28: The Almighty said: Then why did He not aid them? Lawla means why, that is, why did not their gods, by whom they claimed to draw near to God, aid them so that they might intercede for them when they said: These are our intercessors with God (Yunus 10:18), and prevent them from the destruction that befell them? Al-Kisa'i said: The sacrifice is everything by which one draws near to God Almighty, from obedience and ritual sacrifice, and the plural is sacrifices, like monks and monks, and one of the two objects of the verb takhada refers back to those who were deleted, and the second is gods and sacrifice is a state, and it is not correct for sacrifice to be a second object, and gods to be a substitute for it because the meaning is corrupted, as Al-Zamakhshari said: And it was read sacrifice with a damma on the ra', rather they went astray from them meaning they perished from them. And it was said: rather they went astray from them meaning their gods went astray from him because they were not afflicted with what It was said: They went astray from them meaning they abandoned the idols and disavowed them. And that is their lie meaning the gods that went astray from them in their lie in their saying that they bring them closer to God. The general reading is ifkahum with a kasra on the hamza and a sukoon on the fa’, meaning their lie. Al-ifk is a lie, and so is ifikah, and the plural is afaka’ik, and a man is an afak meaning a liar. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Ibn al-Zubayr read and that is afkahum with a fatha on the hamza, the fa’, and the kaf, based on the verb, meaning that saying turned them away from monotheism. Al-afk with a fatha is the source of your saying: afkahu ya’fukahu afkan, meaning he turned him away and diverted him from something. Ikrimah read afkahum with a shaddah on the fa’ for emphasis and emphasis. Abu Hatim said: It means he turned them away from the bliss they were upon. Al-Mahdawi also mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas afkahum with a long vowel and a kasra on the fa’, meaning he turned them away. On the authority of Abdullah Ibn Al-Zubayr, with a difference of opinion, said: afkahum with a long vowel, so it is permissible for it to be af’alhum, meaning he led them to slander, and it is permissible for it to be fa’ilhum like khadhihum, and the evidence for the general reading afkahum is his statement: And they were not inventing meaning they were lying, and it was said: afkahum is like afkahum slander and slander are like caution and caution, Al-Mahdawi said.
46:29: The Almighty says: And when We directed to you a company of the jinn This is a rebuke to the polytheists of Quraysh, meaning that the jinn heard the Qur'an and believed in it and knew that it was from God, but you turned away and persisted in disbelief. The meaning of We directed is We directed you and sent you, and that is because they were turned away from eavesdropping from the sky by shooting stars, as will be mentioned later. They were not turned away from it after Jesus except when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was sent. The commentators Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Jubayr, Mujahid and others said: When Abu Talib died, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out alone to Taif seeking support from Thaqeef. He headed towards Abd al-Yalil, Mas`ud and Habib, who were brothers, Banu Amr bin `Umair, and with them was a woman from Quraysh from Banu Jumah. He called them to faith and asked them to support him against his people. One of them said: He would tear off the cloths of the Ka`bah if God sent you! Another said: God did not find anyone to send but you! The third said: By God, I will never speak to you again. If God has sent you as you are, then you are too dangerous for me to respond to you. If you are lying, then it is not appropriate for me to speak to you. Then they incited their fools and slaves against him, cursing him and laughing at him, until the people gathered around him and forced him to take refuge in the wall of Utba and Shaiba, the sons of Rabi’ah. He said to the Jumhaiyah: What have we encountered at the hands of your in-laws? Then he said: O God, I complain to You about my weakness, the paucity of my resources, and my insignificance among people. O Most Merciful of the merciful, You are the Lord of the weak and You are my Lord. To whom will You entrust me? To a slave who treats me harshly, or to an enemy to whom You have given authority over me! If You are not angry with me, then I do not care, but Your well-being is more spacious for me. I seek refuge in the light of Your face from Your anger descending upon me, or Your wrath befalling me. You are to be blamed until You are satisfied, and there is no power or strength except with You. So the two sons of Rabi’ah took pity on him and said to their Christian servant called Addas, Take a bunch of grapes and put them on this plate, then put them in front of this man. When he put them in front of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, In the name of God, and then he ate. Addas looked at his face and said, By God, these are not the words that the people of this town say! The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, From which country are you, Addas, and what is your religion? He said, I am a Christian from Nineveh. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him, Are you from the town of the righteous man Yunus ibn Matta? He said, And how do you know who Yunus ibn Matta was? He said, That was my brother; he was a prophet, and I am a prophet. Then Addas knelt down until he kissed the head, hands, and feet of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The two sons of Rabi’ah said to him, Why did you do that?! He said: O my master, there is nothing on earth better than this. Tell me of something that only a prophet would know. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, departed when he had despaired of any good for Thaqeef, until he was in Batn Nakhl. He got up at night to pray, and a group of jinn from Nasibin passed by him. The reason for that was that the jinn used to eavesdrop. When the sky was guarded and meteors were thrown, Satan said: What you have seen in the sky is something that happened on earth. So he sent his squadrons to find out. Satan said: What happened in the sky is something that happened on earth. So he sent his squadrons to find out the report. The first of them were the riders of Nasibin, who were the nobles of the jinn, to Tihamah. When they reached Batn Nakhl, they heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, praying the dawn prayer in Batn Nakhl and reciting the Qur’an. They listened to him and said: Be silent. A group said: Rather, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was ordered to warn the jinn and call them to God Almighty and recite the Qur’an to them. So God Almighty sent to him a group of jinn from Nineveh and gathered them for him. The Prophet said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: I want to recite the Qur’an to the jinn tonight, so which of you will follow me? They lowered their heads. Then he said it a second time and they lowered their heads. Then he said it a third time and they lowered their heads. Ibn Mas’ud said: I will, O Messenger of God. Ibn Mas’ud said: And no one was with him except me. So we set off until we were at the top of Mecca. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) entered a valley called the Valley of Al-Hujun. He drew a line for me and ordered me to sit in it and said: Do not leave it until I return to you. Then he set off and recited the Qur’an. I began to see things like eagles soaring and walking in their wings, and I heard a noise and a murmuring until I feared for the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him). Many black lions covered him and came between me and him until I could not hear his voice. Then they began to scatter like pieces of clouds, going away. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) finished at dawn and said: Have you slept? I said: “No, by God. I thought many times of seeking help from the people until I heard you hitting them with your staff, saying: “Sit.” He said: If you went out, I would not be safe from being snatched by one of them. Then he said: Did you see anything? I said: Yes, O Messenger of God, I saw black men wearing white clothes. He said: Those are the jinn of Nasibin who asked me for provisions and food, so I gave them every loose bone, dung and excrement. They said: O Messenger of God, people find it disgusting to us. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade using bones and dung for istinja’ cleaning oneself after cleansing oneself and I said: O Prophet of God, what good will that do them? He said: They do not find a bone without finding meat on it on the day it was eaten, and they do not find dung without finding a living creature in it on the day it was eaten. I said: O Messenger of God, I heard a great uproar. He said: The jinn argued among themselves about a murdered person, so they brought a dispute, and I judged between them justly. Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) defecate and then came to me and said: Do you have water? I said: O Prophet of God, I have with me a vessel containing some date wine. I poured it over his hands and performed ablution. He said: Good dates and pure water. A similar meaning was narrated by Muammar from Qatadah and Shu’bah also from Ibn Mas’ud. There is no mention of date wine in the hadith of Muammar. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi that Ibn Masoud saw a group of Zutt and said: Who are these? He said: These are the Zutt. He said: I have only seen their likeness to the jinn on the night of the jinn, so they were incited, following one another. Ad-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Lahi’ah, who told me that Qais bin Al-Hajjaj told me on the authority of Hanash on the authority of Ibn Abbas on the authority of Ibn Masoud that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) performed ablution with wine on the night of the jinn, so he performed ablution with it and said: It is a pure drink. Ibn Lahi’ah does not need it. And with this chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Masoud: that he went out with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the night of the jinn, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: Do you have any water with you, O Ibn Masoud? He said: I have wine in a jug. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Pour some of it over me. He performed ablution and said: It is a drink and purification. This is narrated by Ibn Lahi’ah alone and his hadith is weak. Ad-Daraqutni said: It was said that Ibn Mas’ud did not witness the Night of the Jinn with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Abu Muhammad ibn Sa’id narrated to us, Abu al-Ash’ath narrated to us, Bishr ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, Dawud ibn Abi Hind narrated to us, on the authority of ‘Amir, on the authority of ‘Alqamah ibn Qays, who said: I said to ‘Abdullah ibn Mas’ud: Did any of you witness the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the night when a caller from the jinn came to him? He said: No. Ad-Daraqutni said: This is a sound chain of transmission and there is no disagreement about the trustworthiness of its narrator. ‘Amr ibn Murrah said: I said to Abu ‘Ubaid: Was ‘Abdullah ibn Mas’ud present on the Night of the Jinn? He said: No. Ibn Abbas said: The jinn were seven men from the jinn of Nasibin, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made them messengers to their people. Zur ibn Hubaysh said: They were nine, one of them was Zuba’ah. Qatadah said: They were from the people of Nineveh. Mujahid said: From the people of Harran. Ikrimah said: From the island of Mosul. It was also said: They were seven, three from the people of Najran and four from the people of Nasibin. Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in this hadith, and he mentioned Nasibin in it, saying: It was raised to me until I saw it, so I asked God to increase its rain, make its trees flourish, and make its river abundant. Al-Suhayli said: It is said that they were seven, and they were Jews who converted to Islam, and that is why they said: It was sent down after Moses. It was said that their names were: Shasir, Masir, Manshi, Mashi, and Al-Ahqab. Ibn Duraid mentioned these five, and among them was Amr ibn Jabir. Ibn Salam mentioned it on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Subai’i on the authority of his sheikhs on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he was with a group of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, walking. Then a hurricane was raised for them, then a bigger hurricane came, and behold, a snake was killed. One of us took his cloak, tore it, shrouded the snake in part and buried it. When night fell, two women asked, Which of you buried Amr ibn Jabir? We said, We do not know who Amr ibn Jabir was! They said, “If you were seeking reward, then you have found it. The wicked jinn fought with the believers, and Amr was killed!” He was the snake you saw, and he was one of the people who listened to the Qur’an from Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him), then they returned to their people as warners. Ibn Salam mentioned in another narration that the one who shrouded him was Safwan ibn al-Mu’attal. I said: Al-Tha'labi mentioned this report in a similar manner, saying: Thabit bin Qataba said: Some people came to Ibn Mas'ud and said: We were on a journey and saw a snake writhing in its blood, so one of us took it and hid it. Then some people came and said: Which of you buried Amr? We said: And who is Amr? They said: The snake that you buried in such and such a place. As for him, he was one of the people who heard the Qur’an from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and there was a fight between two tribes of jinn, Muslims and unbelievers, and he was killed. In this report, Ibn Mas’ud was not traveling nor was he present at the burial, and God knows best. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya mentioned on the authority of a man from the Tabi’in whom he named: A snake entered his tent, panting with thirst, so he gave it water to drink, then it died, so he buried it. Then someone came at night and greeted him and thanked him, and he said that the snake was killed by a man from the jinn of Nasibin named Zawba’ah. Al-Suhayli said: We have been informed about the virtues of ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd Al-‘Aziz, may God be pleased with him, from what Abu Bakr ibn Tahir Al-Ashbili narrated to us, that ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd Al-‘Aziz was walking in a desert land, and if he saw a dead snake, he shrouded it with the remainder of his cloak and buried it. Then someone said: O Sarq, I bear witness that I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: You will die in a desert land, and a righteous man will suffice you. He said: Who are you, may God have mercy on you? He said: A man from the jinn who listened to the Qur’an from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and none of them remained except me and Siraq, and Siraq is dead. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, was killed by a snake that she saw in her room listening and Aisha reading. She was brought to me in a dream and it was said to her: You have killed a believing man from the jinn who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. She said: If he had been a believer, he would not have entered the sanctuary of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. She was told: He did not enter upon you except while you were veiled, and he only came to listen to the remembrance. Aisha was startled and bought slaves and freed them. Al-Suhayli said: We have mentioned the names of these jinn that we had in our possession. If there were seven, then Al-Ahqab among them is a description of one of them, and it is not a proper name. The names that we mentioned earlier are eight, and God knows best. I said: Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir mentioned in his history: Hamah bin Al-Haim bin Laqis bin Iblis. It was said that he was a believer among the jinn and one of those who met the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and taught him Surah When the Inevitable Comes [Surah al-Waqi’ah 56:Surah Al-Baqarah, verse two hundred], Al-Mursalat and Amma Yatas’aloon [Surah Al-Naba’: Surah Al-Baqarah, verse two hundred], When the Sun is Wrapped Up and Al-Hamd and Al-Mu’awwidhatayn. He mentioned that he was present at the killing of Abel and participated in his blood when he was a boy of one year, and that he met Noah and repented at his hands, and Hud and Salih and Jacob and Joseph and Elias and Moses bin Imran and Jesus bin Maryam, peace be upon them. Al-Mawardi mentioned their names, Mujahid, saying: Hasi and Masi and Mansha and Shasir and Masir and Al-Ard and Anyan and Al-Ahqam. Abu Amr Uthman bin Ahmad, known as Ibn Al-Sammak, mentioned them. He said: Muhammad bin Al-Baraa told us. He said: Al-Zubayr bin Bakkar told us. He said: Hamza bin Utbah bin Abi Lahab was called a jinn. Nasibin who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he says: Hasi, Masi, Shasir, Masir, Al-Afkhar, Al-Ard, and Aniyal. God the Almighty said: So when they attended it meaning they attended the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is a type of speech. It was also said: When they attended the Qur’an and listened to it, they said, ‘Listen’ meaning some of them said to each other, ‘Be quiet to listen to the Qur’an.’ Ibn Mas’ud said, they came down to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was reciting the Qur’an in Batn Nakhl. When they heard him, they said, ‘Listen’ they said, Shh. They were seven, one of them was Zuba’ah. So God the Almighty revealed: “And when We directed to you a company of the jinn, listening to the Qur’an. When they attended it, they said, ‘Listen’” until His saying, in clear error. It was also said: Listen to hear the words of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the meaning is close. So when it was decreed Lahiq ibn Humayd and Khubayb ibn ‘Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr read So when it was decreed with a fat-ha on the qaf and the dad, meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, before the prayer. This is because they went out when the sky was guarded against eavesdropping to find out what had necessitated that? They came to Wadi Nakhal while the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was reciting the dawn prayer. They were seven, and they heard him and went back to their people as warners. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not know about them. Rather, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was commanded to warn the jinn and recite the Qur’an to them. So God sent a group of jinn to him so that they would listen to him and warn their people. When he recited the Qur’an to them and finished, they went back at his command, intending to target those of their people from the jinn behind them, warning them against disobeying the Qur’an and warning them of the punishment of God if they did not believe. This indicates that they believed in the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and that he sent them. This is indicated by their saying, O our people, respond to the caller of God and believe in him. Had it not been for that, they would not have warned their people. It was previously reported from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) made them messengers to their people. Based on this, the Night of the Jinn is two nights. This meaning has been fully presented. In Sahih Muslim, there is evidence of this, as will be explained in Say, ‘It has been revealed to me.’ (al-Jinn 72:2) Verse two hundred], and in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Ma’n, he said: I heard my father say: I asked Masruq, who informed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the jinn on the night they listened to the Qur’an? He said: Your father, meaning Ibn Mas’ud, told me that a tree informed him about them.
46:30: God Almighty said: They said, ‘O our people, indeed we have heard a Book revealed after Moses,’ meaning the Qur’an, and they were believers in Moses. Ata’ said: They were Jews, then they converted to Islam, and that is why they said: It was revealed after Moses. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The jinn had not heard about Jesus, and that is why they said: It was revealed after Moses, “confirming what was before it,” meaning what came before it of the Torah, guiding to the truth, meaning the religion of truth, and to a straight path, the straight religion of God.
46:31: The Almighty’s saying: O our people, respond to the caller of God means Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. This indicates that he was sent to the jinn and mankind. Muqatil said: God did not send a prophet to the jinn and mankind before Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. I said: What indicates his statement is what is in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘I have been given five things that were not given to anyone before me. Every prophet was sent specifically to his own people, and I have been sent to every red and black person. Spoils of war were made lawful for me, but they were not made lawful for anyone before me. The earth was made pure and good for me, and a place of prostration, so whenever the time for prayer comes, I pray wherever I am. I have been aided by terror from a distance of a month’s journey. I have been given intercession.’” Mujahid said: The red and black people are the jinn and mankind. In a narration from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah: And I have been sent to all of creation, and the prophets were sealed with me. “And believe in him,” meaning in the caller, who is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was also said: in him, meaning in God, because of His saying: He will forgive you some of your sins. Ibn Abbas said: Seventy men from their people responded to them, so they returned to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and met him in al-Batha’. He recited the Qur’an to them and commanded and forbade them. Question: This verse indicates that the jinn are like humans in terms of commands and prohibitions, reward and punishment. Al-Hasan said: The believing jinn have no reward other than their salvation from the Fire. This is indicated by the words of God the Almighty: He will forgive you some of your sins and save you from a painful punishment. Abu Hanifa said the same. He said: The jinn have no reward except that they will be saved from the Fire, then it will be said to them: Become dust like the animals. Others said that just as they are punished for their wrongdoing, they will be rewarded for their good deeds like humans. This is the view of Malik, Al-Shafi’i and Ibn Abi Layla. Ad-Dahhak said: The jinn will enter Paradise and eat and drink. Al-Qushayri said: The correct view is that this is something about which there is no definitive proof, and knowledge is with God. I said: The Almighty’s statement: And for all are degrees according to what they have done (al-Ahqaf 46:19) indicates that they will be rewarded and will enter Paradise, because He said at the beginning of the verse: O company of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you, relating to you My verses? until He said: And for all are degrees according to what they have done (al-An’am 6:132). And God knows best, and further clarification of this will come in Surat Ar-Rahman, God willing.
46:32: God Almighty says: And whoever does not respond to the Caller of God will not escape Him on earth meaning God will not escape Him nor will He overtake Him. And he will have no protectors besides Him meaning no supporters to prevent him from God’s punishment. Those are in manifest error.
46:33: The Almighty’s saying: Have they not seen that it is God who created the heavens and the earth? “Seeing” here means knowledge, and that and its noun and predicate replace the objects of seeing. “And He is not weary of creating them, able to give life to the dead.” This is an argument against those who deny resurrection. The meaning of is not weary is that He is unable and weak to create them. It is said: He was weary of His command, and was if he was not guided to His path. Assimilation is more common, and you say in the plural was with a light wa, and was also with a shaddah. He said: They are tired of their order as the dove is tired of its egg I became exhausted by my situation if you did not find guidance for it, and he exhausted me. Al-Hasan read wa lam a’i with a kasra on the ‘ayn and a sukoon on the ya’, and this is rare and irregular. The weakening of the ‘ayn and the correction of the lam did not occur except in a few names such as ghayyah and verse, and it did not occur in the verb except for a verse recited by Al-Farra’, which is the saying of the poet: She is like a barrage of women walking in the shade of her house, but she is tired. Qadir Abu Ubaidah and Al-Akhfash said: The letter ba is an additional letter for emphasis, like the letter ba in His statement: And sufficient is God as a witness and His statement: It produces oil (Al-Mu'minun 23:20). Al-Kisa'i, Al-Farra' and Al-Zajjaj said: The letter ba in it is behind the question and the denial at the beginning of the speech. Al-Zajjaj said: The Arabs insert it with the denial, saying: I did not think that Zaid was standing, and they do not say: I thought that Zaid was standing. This is because of the insertion of ma and the insertion of an for emphasis, and the meaning is: Is not God capable, like the statement of the Most High: Is not He who created the heavens and the earth capable? (Yasin 36:81). Ibn Mas'ud, Al-A'raj, Al-Jahdary, Ibn Abi Ishaq and Ya'qub read yaqdir is capable, and Abu Hatim chose this, because the insertion of ba in the predicate of an is ugly. Abu Ubaid chose this as the reading of the common people, because in the reading of Abdullah He created the heavens and the earth is capable without a ba, and God knows best.
46:34: God Almighty says: And the Day those who disbelieved will be exposed to the Fire. That is, He will remind them on the Day they are exposed and it will be said to them, Is this not the truth? They will say, Yes, by our Lord. Then the declarant will say to them, Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve. That is, you disbelieved.
