46:35: The Almighty said: So be patient, as were patient the messengers of strong will. Ibn Abbas said: Those of determination and patience. Mujahid said: They are five: Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad, peace be upon them. They are the people of the laws. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: Those of strong will are Noah, Hud, and Abraham. God Almighty commanded His Prophet, peace be upon him, to be the fourth of them. Al-Suddi said: They are six: Abraham, Moses, Solomon, Jesus, and Muhammad, peace be upon them all. It was said: Noah, Hud, Salih, Shuaib, Lot, and Moses, and they are the ones mentioned in order in Surat Al-A'raf and Surat Al-Shu'ara. Muqatil said: They are six: Noah was patient with the harm of his people for a period, Abraham was patient with the fire, Isaac was patient with the slaughter, Jacob was patient with the loss of his child and the loss of his sight, Joseph was patient with the well and the prison, and Job was patient with the hardship. Ibn Jurayj said: Among them are Ishmael, Jacob, and Job, but not Jonah, Solomon, or Adam. Al-Sha’bi, Al-Kalbi, and Mujahid also said: They are those who were ordered to fight, so they revealed their faith and fought the infidels. It was also said: They are the noble messengers mentioned in Surat Al-An’am, and they are eighteen: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Noah, David, Solomon, Job, Joseph, Moses, Aaron, Zachariah, John, Jesus, Elias, Ishmael, Elisha, Jonah, and Lot. Al-Hasan bin Al-Fadl chose it because of his saying after it: Those are the ones whom God has guided, so follow their guidance (al-An’am 6:90). Ibn Abbas also said: All the messengers were people of resolve. Ali bin Mahdi Al-Tabari chose it. He said: The word min was used for the sake of alliteration, not for the sake of partiality, as you say: I bought robes of fine linen and cloaks of silk, meaning be patient as the messengers were patient. It was also said: All the prophets were people of resolve except Jonah bin Matta. Do you not see that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade anyone to be like him, due to the lightness of… And haste appeared from him when he took over, angry with his people, so God tested him with three things: He sent the giants against him until they raided his family and his money, He sent a wolf against his son and ate him, and He sent a whale against him and swallowed him, said Abu al-Qasim al-Hakim. Some scholars said, the people of resolve are twelve prophets sent to the Children of Israel in the Levant, but they disobeyed them, so God revealed to the prophets that I am sending my punishment to the disobedient Children of Israel. This was difficult for the messengers, so God revealed to them, choose for yourselves, if you wish, I will bring down the punishment upon you and save the Children of Israel, and if you wish, I will save you and bring down the punishment upon the Children of Israel. So they consulted among themselves and their opinion agreed that the punishment should be brought down upon them and God should save the Children of Israel, so God saved the Children of Israel and brought down the punishment upon those people, and that is because He sent the kings of the earth against them, so some of them were sawed with saws, some of them had their heads and faces flayed, some of them were crucified on wood until they died, and some of them were burned with fire, and God knows best. Al-Hasan said, the people of resolve are four: Abraham And Moses, David, and Jesus. As for Abraham, it was said to him, Submit, and he said, I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds. (al-Baqarah 2:131), then he was tested in his wealth, his children, his country, and himself, and he was found to be truthful and faithful in all that he was tested with. As for Moses, his resolve when his people said to him, Indeed, we are to be overtaken. He said, No indeed, my Lord is with me; He will guide me. (Ash-Shu’ara’: 61-62). As for David, he made a mistake, so it was pointed out to him, so he wept for forty years until a tree grew from his tears, and he sat under its shade. As for Jesus, his resolve was that he did not place brick upon brick and said, It is a passage, so pass it, but do not build on it. So God Almighty was saying to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace: Be patient, meaning be truthful in what you have been tested with like the truthfulness of Abraham, confident in the support of your Lord like the trust of Moses, concerned about your past mistakes like the concern of David, ascetic in the world like the asceticism of Jesus. Then it was said, “It is: It was abrogated by the verse of the sword. It was also said that it was a decisive verse, but it appears to be abrogated because the Surah was Meccan. Muqatil said that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) on the day of Uhud, so God the Almighty commanded him to be patient with what befell him as the messengers of strong will were patient, to make things easier for him and strengthen him. And God knows best. “And do not hasten them.” Muqatil said: By supplicating against them. It was also said: In bringing punishment upon them, for their most distant goal is the Day of Resurrection. The object of hastening is omitted, which is the punishment. It will be as if, on the Day they see what they are promised. Yahya said: Of the punishment. Al-Naqqash: Of the Hereafter. They did not remain meaning in this world until the punishment came to them, and this is what Yahya said. Al-Naqqash said: In their graves until they are resurrected for the reckoning, except for an hour of a day, meaning on the Day of Resurrection. It was said: He made them forget the horror of the torment they witnessed during their long stay in this world. Then he said: A message, meaning this Qur’an is a message. Al-Hasan said: A message is in the nominative case with an implied subject, the evidence for which is the Almighty’s statement: This is a message for mankind and that they may be warned thereby Ibrahim 14:52, and His statement: Indeed in this is a message for a people who worship Al-Anbiya’ 21:106. A message means conveying. It was said: That is, that stay is a message, said Ibn Isa. So, one stops at this on a message and on a day. Abu Hatim mentioned that some of them stopped at and do not be hasty, then began for them with the meaning of a message for them. Ibn al-Anbari said: This is a mistake, because you separated the message from the lam, which is a nominative with something that is not from them. It is permissible in Arabic to say balaghan and balaghan with the meaning of except for an hour as a message, on the source or On the description of the hour, and the preservation of the meaning of from the day as a notification, and in the accusative Isa bin Omar and Al-Hasan read, and it was narrated from some of the readers balagh as a command, so on this reading the pause is on from the day then he begins balagh So are none destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people meaning those who go against the command of God, said Ibn Abbas and others, and Ibn Muhaisin read So are none destroyed except the people attributing the action to the people, and Ibn Abbas said: If a woman has difficulty giving birth, she should write these two verses and two words on a page, then wash her and give her to drink from it, and say: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no god but God, the Great, the Forbearing, the Generous. Glory be to God, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth and Lord of the Mighty Throne, It will be as if on the Day they see it that they had not remained except an afternoon or a morning thereof (al-Nazi’at 79:46), It will be as if on the Day they see what they are promised that they had not remained except an hour of a day, a notification, so are none destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people? God’s words are true. On the authority of Qatada: God does not destroy anyone except a polytheist. It was said: This is the strongest verse about hope, and God knows best.
47:1: Medinan according to Ibn Abbas, mentioned by Al-Nahhas, and Al-Mawardi said: According to everyone except Ibn Abbas and Qatada, who said: Except for one verse that was revealed to him after the Farewell Pilgrimage when he left Mecca, and he kept looking at the House while he was crying out of grief over it, and the verse And how many a city was mightier than your city (Muhammad 47:13) was revealed to him, and Al-Tha’labi said: It is Meccan, and Ibn Hibat God narrated it on the authority of Al-Dahhak and Sa’id bin Jubayr, and it is thirty-nine verses, and it was said eight. God Almighty says: Those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of God - He will render worthless their deeds. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: They are the people of Mecca who disbelieved in the Oneness of God, and they prevented themselves and the believers from the religion of God, which is Islam, by forbidding them from entering it. Al-Suddi said: Ad-Dahhak said: from the path of God from the House of God by preventing those who visit it. The meaning of He rendered their deeds worthless is: He nullified their plot and deceit against the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and turned the tables on them. Ad-Dahhak said: It was said: He nullified what they did in their disbelief with what they called good deeds, such as maintaining family ties, freeing captives, hosting guests, and preserving neighbors. Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed about those who were fed at Badr, and they were twelve men: Abu Jahl, Al-Harith ibn Hisham, Utbah and Shaibah, sons of Rabi’ah, Abu Umayyah, sons of Khalaf, Munabbih and Nabih, sons of Al-Hajjaj, Abu Al-Bukhtari ibn Hisham, Zam’ah ibn Al-Aswad, Hakim ibn Hizam, and Al-Harith ibn Amir ibn Nawfal.
47:2: The Almighty said: And those who have believed and done righteous deeds and believed in what was revealed to Muhammad, Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: They are the Ansar. Muqatil said: It was revealed specifically about people from Quraysh. It was said: They are general, including those who disbelieved and believed. The meaning of He rendered their deeds worthless is: He invalidated them. It was said: He led them astray from guidance by diverting them from success. And did righteous deeds, whoever said that they are the Ansar, it means helping in their homes and wealth. Whoever said that they are from Quraysh, it means emigration. Whoever said it is general, then righteous deeds are all the deeds that please God Almighty. And believed in what was revealed to Muhammad, they did not contradict him in anything. Sufyan al-Thawri said this. It was said that they believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in what he brought. And it is the truth from their Lord, meaning that their faith is the truth from their Lord. It was said: That is, the Qur’an is the truth from their Lord, with which it abrogated what came before it. He removed from them their misdeeds, meaning what had passed of their misdeeds before belief. And He set right… Their condition, that is, their affair, according to Mujahid and others. Qatada said: Their condition, according to Ibn Abbas, is their affairs. The three are similar and are interpreted as correcting what is related to their worldly affairs. Al-Naqqash related that the meaning is correcting their intentions, and from this is the saying of the poet: If you accept my kindness, I will accept the same, but if you turn away, I will go to a bad state. And on this interpretation it is attributed to the righteousness of their religion, and mind is like a source, and no action is known from it, and the Arabs do not collect it except in poetic necessity, so they say in it: balat, Al-Mubarrad: The mind may be in another place with the meaning of the heart, it is said: what occurs to so-and-so on my mind, meaning on my heart, Al-Jawhari: And mind is the ease of the soul, it is said so-and-so is easy-going, and mind: the state, it is said what is wrong with you, and their saying: this is not from my mind, meaning from what I care about, and mind: the great whale from the whales of the sea, and it is not Arabic, and the balla is the container of perfume, Persian Arabized, and its origin in Persian is bilah, Abu Dhu’ayb said: As if she had a bale of lamentation on her, with a fragrance through the two palms
47:3: The Almighty says: That is because those who disbelieve follow falsehood, and those who believe follow the truth from their Lord. That is in the nominative case, meaning that is the matter, or that misguidance and guidance previously mentioned, are caused by this. So the disbeliever follows falsehood, and the believer follows the truth. Falsehood is polytheism, and the truth is monotheism and faith. Thus does God set forth examples for the people. That is, like this explanation that God made clear to the people about good and bad deeds, and the pronoun in their examples refers to those who disbelieve and those who believe.
47:4: It contains four issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: So when you meet those who disbelieve, strike [their] necks. When He distinguished between the two groups, He commanded jihad against the disbelievers. Ibn Abbas said: The disbelievers are the idolaters who worship idols. It was also said: Everyone who opposes the religion of Islam, whether a polytheist or a People of the Book, if he is not bound by a covenant or protection. Al-Mawardi mentioned this, and Ibn Al-Arabi chose this, and said: This is correct due to the generality of the verse in it. Then strike [their] necks is a verbal noun. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, strike [their] necks, and He mentioned specifically the necks because killing is most often caused by them. It was also said that it is in the accusative case to encourage. Abu Ubaidah said: It is like you saying, O soul, be patient. It was also said that the meaning is: Aim to strike [their] necks. He said: Then strike [their] necks, and He did not say, Kill them, because the phrase strike [their] necks contains harshness and severity that is not in the word killing, because it depicts killing in the most hideous way, which is slitting the neck and cutting off the limb that is the head of the body, its top, and the most prominent of its limbs. The second: The Almighty’s saying: Until you have slaughtered them meaning you have increased the killing. It has already been mentioned in Al-Anfal when the Almighty said: Until he has made slaughter in the land (al-Anfal 8:67). Then secure the bonds meaning if you have captured them. The bond is a noun from the word itthaq, and it may be a verbal noun, as it is said: I bound him with a bond and ithaqan. As for the bond with a kasra, it is the name of the thing that is tied with, like a ribat, as Al-Qushayri said. Al-Jawhari said: And secure him in the bonds, meaning he tightened them. The Almighty said: Then secure the bonds and the bonds with a kasra on the waw is a dialectal term for it. Rather, he ordered the tightening of the bonds so that they would not escape. Either a favor from Us upon them in general terms without ransom, or a ransom. He did not mention killing here, being satisfied with what preceded from killing at the beginning of the speech. From Us and ransom are accusative with an implied verb, and fada is read in the shortened form with a fatha on the fa’, meaning either that… They wished them from us, or ransom them. It was narrated from one of them that he said: I was standing at the head of Al-Hajjaj when the prisoners of the companions of Abd Al-Rahman bin Al-Ash’ath were brought to him, and they were four thousand eight hundred. About three thousand of them were killed until a man from Kinda came to him and said: O Hajjjaj, may God not reward you well for the Sunnah and generosity! He said: Why is that? He said: Because God the Most High said: “So when you meet those who disbelieve, strike [their] necks until, when you have inflicted slaughter on them, then secure their bonds. Then either [take] a favor from us afterward or ransom them.” (Surah Al-Baqara: 10) regarding those who disbelieved. By God! I did not offer a favor nor ransom. And your poet said in describing his people’s noble traits: We do not kill prisoners, but we release them if the burden of debts becomes too heavy for them. Al-Hajjaj said: Shame on these corpses! Was there no one among them who could speak like this? Let those who remain go. So the remaining prisoners, about two thousand in number, were released that day, based on the words of that man. Third: Scholars differed in their interpretation of this verse, with five opinions: The first: that it was abrogated: and it is about the people of idols, it is not permissible for them to be ransomed nor to be granted a favor, and what abrogated it according to them is the saying of the Most High: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9:50), and His saying: But if you overtake them in war, scatter with them those behind them (al-Anfal 8:57), and His saying: And fight the polytheists altogether (al-Tawbah 9:36), the verse, said by Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, As-Suddi, Ibn Jurayj, and Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas, said by many of the Kufians, and Abd Al-Rahman Al-Jawzi said: He wrote to Abu Bakr regarding a prisoner who had been taken prisoner, and they mentioned that they sought him for a ransom of such and such, so he said: Kill him, because killing a man from the polytheists is more beloved to me than such and such. The second: It applies to all the infidels, and it has been abrogated according to the opinion of a group of scholars and people of insight, including Qatadah and Mujahid. They said: If a polytheist is taken prisoner, it is not permissible to show him favor, nor to ransom him so that he is returned to the polytheists. According to them, ransom is not permissible except with a woman, because she is not to be killed. The abrogating verse is: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them, as Surah Bara’ah was the last verse to be revealed by divine revelation. Therefore, it is obligatory to kill every polytheist except for those who can be spared from among the women and children and those from whom the jizyah is taken, and this is the well-known opinion of the school of Abu Hanifa, for fear that they will return to fight the Muslims. Abd al-Razzaq mentioned that Muammar informed us on the authority of Qatadah: Then either a favor afterward or a ransom He said: It was abrogated by Then scatter with them those behind them Mujahid said: It was abrogated by Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them and this is the opinion of al-Hakam. Third: It is abrogating. This was stated by Ad-Dahhak and others. Ath-Thawri narrated on the authority of Juwaybir on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them. He said: It was abrogated by Then either a favor from us later or a ransom. Ibn Al-Mubarak said on the authority of Ibn Jurayj on the authority of Ata’: Then either a favor from us later or a ransom. The polytheist is not to be killed, but he is to be shown favor and ransom, as God, the Almighty, said. Ash’ath said: Al-Hasan disliked killing the captive, and he would recite, Then either a favor from us later or a ransom. Al-Hasan also said: There is an inversion in the verse, as if he said, Then strike the necks until the war lays down its burdens. Then he said, Until, when you have inflicted slaughter on them, then secure the bonds. He claimed that if the imam has a captive in his hands, he does not have the right to kill him, but he has the choice in three situations: either to show favor, to ransom, or to enslave him. Fourth: The statement of Saeed bin Jubair: There is no ransom or captivity except after slaughter and killing by the sword, based on the Almighty’s saying: It is not for a prophet to have captives until he has inflicted a great slaughter in the land (al-Anfal 8:67). So if he is captured after that, then the imam has the right to rule according to what he sees of killing or other things. Fifth: The verse is decisive, and the imam has a choice in every situation. It was narrated by Ali bin Abi Talha on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and many scholars said the same, including Ibn Omar, Al-Hasan, and Ata’. It is the school of Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Al-Awza’i, Abu Ubaid, and others. It is the choice because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Rightly-Guided Caliphs did all of that. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, killed Uqbah bin Abi Mu’ayt and Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith on the day of Badr, and he ransomed all the other prisoners of Badr. He spared Thamamah bin Aththal Al-Hanafi while he was a prisoner in his hand. He took a slave girl from Salamah bin Al-Akwa’ and ransomed some Muslims with her. Some people from Mecca came down to him, peace be upon him, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took them and spared them. He spared the captives of Hawazin. All of this is proven in the Sahih, and all of it has been mentioned in Al-Anfal and other books. Al-Nahhas said: This is based on the fact that the two verses are decisive and are acted upon. This is a good statement, because abrogation only occurs for something decisive. So, if it is possible to act upon the two verses, there is no point in saying that they are abrogated, if it is permissible for worship to occur if… We met those who disbelieved and killed them. If captivity is permissible, then killing, enslavement, ransom, and favor are permissible, as long as it is in the best interest of the Muslims. This statement is narrated from the people of Medina, Al-Shafi’i, and Abu Ubaid. Al-Tahawi narrated it as a doctrine from Abu Hanifa, and the well-known opinion from him is what we have presented. And success comes from God Almighty. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: Until the war lays down its burdens. Mujahid and Ibn Jubayr said: It is the emergence of Jesus, peace be upon him. Mujahid also said: The meaning is until there is no religion but the religion of Islam, so every Jew, Christian, and follower of a religion submits, and the sheep is safe from the wolf. Something similar was narrated by Al-Hasan, Al-Kalbi, Al-Farra’, and Al-Kisa’i. Al-Kisa’i said: Until the creation submits. Al-Farra’ said: Until they believe and disbelief disappears. Al-Kalbi said: Until Islam prevails over all religions. Al-Hasan said: Until they worship none but God. It was said: The meaning of burdens is weapons, so the meaning is: Tighten the bonds until you are safe and lay down your weapons. It was said: Its meaning is until the war, meaning the fighting enemies lay down their burdens, and it is their weapon in defeat or farewell. The forelegs are called burdens. Al-A’sha said: I prepared for war its equipment: long spears and male horses. And from the woven fabric of David, he follows it in the footsteps of the tribe, one donkey after another. It was said: until the war lays down its burdens meaning its burdens, and the burden is the weight, and from it the king’s minister because he bears the burdens on his behalf, and its burdens are the weapons because of the weight of carrying them. Ibn al-Arabi said: Al-Hasan and Ata’ said in the verse there is an inversion, the meaning is so strike the necks until the war lays down its burdens, and when you have inflicted slaughter on them then tighten the bonds, and the imam does not have the right to kill the prisoner, and it was narrated on the authority of al-Hajjaj that he handed a prisoner to Abdullah ibn Umar to kill him but he refused and said: This is not what God has commanded us to do, and he recited: until when you have inflicted slaughter on them then tighten the bonds We said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said it and did it, and in God’s interpretation of the gift and ransom there is no prohibition of anything other than it, for God has made it clear to me regarding adultery that he ruled on flogging, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made clear the ruling on stoning, and perhaps Ibn Umar disliked that at the hands of al-Hajjaj so he apologized for what he said, and your Lord knows best. God the Almighty said: “That is so. And if God had willed, He could have taken revenge on them.” That is in the nominative case as mentioned above, meaning the matter is that which you mentioned and explained. It was said: It is accusative with the meaning of do that. It is permissible for it to be a subject, meaning that is the ruling on the disbelievers. It is a word that the eloquent person uses when moving from one statement to another, and it is as God the Almighty said: This, and indeed for the transgressors is an evil destination. (Surah Sad: 55), meaning this is true, and I know that the wrongdoers have such and such. The meaning of He would have taken revenge on them is that He destroyed them without fighting. Ibn Abbas said: He would have destroyed them with an army of angels. But that He may test some of you by others, meaning He commanded you to war so that you may be tested and tried by others, so that He may know the patient mujahideen, as in the same surah. And those who are killed in the way of God, meaning those killed among the believers, He will not let their deeds go to waste. The reading of the general public is they fought, and this is the choice of Abu Ubaid. Abu Amr and Hafdh read they killed with a damma on the qaf and a kasra on the ta’. Al-Hasan read it like that, except that The letter taa is emphasized to indicate abundance. Al-Jahdary, Isa bin Omar, and Abu Haywah read qaltu with the qaf and the taa open without an alif, meaning those who killed the polytheists. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that this verse was revealed on the day of Uhud, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was in the valley, and the wounds and killing had spread. The polytheists shouted: Hubal is exalted, and the Muslims shouted: God is Most High and Most Majestic, and the polytheists said: A day for the day of Badr, and war is a back-and-forth. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Say, they are not the same. Our dead are alive with their Lord, receiving provision, and your dead are being tortured in the Fire. The polytheists said: We have al-Uzza, and you have no Uzza. The Muslims said: God is our protector, and you have no protector. This has been mentioned previously in Al Imran.
47:5: God Almighty says: He will guide them and set right their condition. Al-Qushayri said: Abu Amr’s reading of killed is far-fetched, because of the Almighty’s statement: He will guide them and set their condition right. The one who is killed is not described with this. Someone else said that the meaning could be that He will guide them to Paradise, or He will guide whoever remains of them, meaning He will ensure guidance for them. Ibn Ziyad said: He will guide them to argue with Munkar and Nakir in the grave. Abu al-Ma’ali said: Guidance may also be used to mean guiding the believers to the paths of Paradise and the roads leading to it. From this is the Almighty’s statement describing the mujahideen: “And He will not let their deeds go to waste. He will guide them.” And from this is His statement, the Almighty: So guide them to the path of Hellfire. (al-Saffat 37:234) meaning, then take them to it.
47:6: God Almighty says: And He will admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them. That is, when they enter it, they are told to go back to their homes. They know their homes better than the people of Friday when they go back to their homes. Mujahid and most of the commentators said that its meaning is clear. In Al-Bukhari, there is evidence that this statement is correct, on the authority of Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The believers will be saved from the Fire and detained on a bridge between Paradise and Hell. Some of them will be punished for wrongs committed between them in this world until they are refined and purified, and permission will be given to them to enter Paradise. By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, one of them will be guided to his home in Paradise better than his home in this world.’” It was said: He made it known to them means He explained it to them until they recognized it without proof. Al-Hasan said: God, the Most High, described Paradise to them in this world, and when they entered it, they recognized it in its description. It was said: There is an omission in it, meaning He made its paths, dwellings, and houses known to them, so the complement was omitted. It was said: This definition is supported by evidence, and it is the angel assigned to the servant’s work. He walks and the servant follows him until the servant reaches his home, and the angel informs him of everything that has been made for him in Paradise. The hadith of Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri rejects it. Ibn Abbas said: He made it known to them means He made it pleasant for them with various pleasures. It is taken from ‘arf, which is a pleasant scent. And seasoned food means flavoured. The Arabs say: The pot is seasoned if you season it with salt and spices. And the poet said, addressing a man and praising him: I knew a writer who knew the calamities He says: As the itb is known, which is the cow and the cow, and it is a shirt without sleeves that women wear, and it is said: It is from placing food some on top of some due to its abundance, it is said that it is known silk, meaning some on top of some, and it is from the continuous mane like the mane of the horse, and it is said: He made it known to them meaning He guided them to obedience until they deserved Paradise, and it is said: The people of Heaven knew that it was for them as a manifestation of their honor in it, and it is said: The obedient knew that it was for them.
47:7: The Almighty’s statement: O you who have believed, if you support God, He will support you. That is, if you support the religion of God, He will support you against the disbelievers. Similar to this is, And God will surely support those who support Him. (al-Hajj 22:40), which has already been mentioned. Qutrub said: If you support the Prophet of God, God will support you, and the meaning is the same. And will make firm your feet, that is, when fighting. It has been said that it is against Islam, and it has been said that it is against the path. It has been said that what is meant is making hearts firm with security, so making firm the feet is an expression of victory and assistance in a place of war. This meaning has already been mentioned in Al-Anfal, and He said there: When your Lord revealed to the angels, ‘I am with you, so strengthen those who have believed.’ (al-Anfal 8:12), so He established an intermediary there and negated it here, like the Almighty’s statement: Say, ‘The Angel of Death will take you.’ (Al-Sajdah: 11), then He negated it by saying: God is He who created you, then provided for you, then causes you to die. (Al-Rum: 40), He who created death and life. (al-Mulk 67:2) And there are many like it, for there is no doer but God alone.
47:8: The Almighty’s saying: And those who disbelieved may be in the nominative case as a subject, or in the accusative case as explained by so woe to them as if he said: woe to those who disbelieved, and woe to them is in the accusative case as a source by way of supplication, as Al-Farra’ said, like watering for him and grazing for him, and it is the opposite of curse for him. Al-A’sha said: It is better for her to be miserable than for me to say to her There are ten sayings about it: The first: Far from them, said Ibn Abbas and Ibn Jurayj. The second: Sadness for them, said Al-Suddi. The third: Misery for them, said Ibn Zayd. The fourth: Cursing them from God, said Al-Hasan. The fifth: Destruction for them, said Tha’lab. The sixth: Disappointment for them, said Al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd. The seventh: Ugly for them, narrated by Al-Naqqash. The eighth: In spite of them, said Al-Dahhak also. The ninth: Evil for them, said Tha’lab also. The tenth: Misery for them, said Abu Al-Aaliyah. It was said: Al-Ta’s is degradation and stumbling. Ibn Al-Sikkit said: Al-Ta’s is to fall on his face, and Al-Naks is to fall on his head. He said: Al-Ta’s is also destruction. Al-Jawhari said: Its origin is the fall, and it is the opposite of recovery. And Ta’s with the opening of the ‘ayn means to be miserable, and God made him miserable. Majma’ bin Hilal said: She says, after separating her from her friend, I am miserable, just as you made me miserable, O Majma’. It is said: May God damn someone, meaning may God cause his destruction. Al-Qushayri said: Some people permit may God damn him with a kasra on the ‘ayn. I said: And from it is the hadith of Abu Hurairah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Cursed is the slave of the dinar, the dirham, the velvet, and the cloak. If he is given something, he is satisfied, and if he is not given something, he is not satisfied.’” Narrated by Al-Bukhari. In some versions of this hadith, it says: Cursed and upside down, and if he is struck, I do not puff myself up. Narrated by Ibn Majah. The Almighty said: And He rendered their deeds worthless meaning He nullified them because they were in obedience to Satan. The letter fa was included in His statement: So wretched is he because of the ambiguity in those who and and He rendered their deeds worthless came in the good sense based on the word those who because it is a predicate in the wording, so the letter fa was included based on the wording.
47:9: God Almighty says: That is because they hated what God revealed, so He rendered worthless their deeds. That is, misguidance and misery, because they hated what God revealed of books and laws, so He rendered worthless their deeds, meaning their good deeds, such as building the mosque, hosting guests, and various acts of worship. God does not accept deeds except from a believer. It was said: He rendered worthless their deeds, meaning the worship of idols.
47:10: God Almighty says: Have they not traveled through the land and observed what was the end of those before them? God destroyed them and there is the like of it for the disbelievers. He explained the conditions of the believer and the disbeliever, as a reminder of the necessity of faith. Then he connected this to contemplation, meaning, did not these people travel through the land of Aad and Thamud and the people of Lot and others, so that they might take a lesson from them and look with their hearts at how was the last affair of the disbelievers before them? God destroyed them meaning He destroyed you and uprooted them. It is said: He destroyed him completely, and destructed has the same meaning. Then He threatened the polytheists of Mecca, saying: And for the disbelievers is the like thereof meaning the likes of this action, meaning destruction. Al-Zajjaj and Al-Tabari said: The ha refers to the consequence, meaning, and for the disbelievers of Quraysh is the likes of the consequence of the denial of the previous nations if they do not believe.
47:11: God Almighty says: That is because God is the protector of those who believe, and because the disbelievers have no protector. That is, their guardian and supporter. In the wording of Ibn Masoud that is because God is the guardian of those who believe, so the guardian here is the supporter. This was said by Ibn Abbas and others. He said: So both vaginas began to think that he was the master of fear behind and in front of them. Qatada said: It was revealed on the Day of Uhud while the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in the valley, when the polytheists shouted: “One day for another. We have al-Uzza, and you have no Uzza.” The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Say: God is our protector, and you have no protector.” It has already been mentioned, and that the disbelievers have no protector, meaning that no one will support them from God.
47:12: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, God will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. This has been mentioned in more than one place, and those who disbelieve will enjoy themselves in this world as if they were livestock, with no concern except their bellies and their private parts, heedless of what is in their future. It has been said: The believer provisions himself in this world, the hypocrite adorns himself, and the disbeliever enjoys himself. And the Fire will be their abode, meaning a place and home.
47:13: The Almighty said: And how many a town. We have already discussed how many in Al Imran, and here it means how many, that is, how many a town. Al Akhfash recited the words of Labid: We saw kings, commoners, and the key to the shackles of the captive. Its meaning is: How many people of a town, more powerful than your town which expelled you meaning its people expelled you, We destroyed them, and they had no helper. Qatada and Ibn Abbas said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, left Mecca for the cave, he turned to Mecca and said: O God, you are the most beloved of lands to God and you are the most beloved of lands to me, and had it not been for the polytheists who expelled me, I would not have left you. So the verse was revealed. Al-Tha’labi mentioned it, and it is a sound hadith.
47:14: The Almighty’s saying: Is he who is upon clear evidence from his Lord? The alif is an alif of confirmation, and the meaning of on clear evidence is on firmness and certainty, as Ibn Abbas, Abu Al-Aaliyah, said: he is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and clear evidence is the revelation, like he to whom the evil of his deed has been made attractive meaning the worship of idols, and he is Abu Jahl and the disbelievers, and they followed their desires meaning what they desired, this beautification is from God in creation, and it is possible that it is from Satan in the form of a supplication and whispering, and it is possible that it is from the disbeliever, meaning he made the evil of his deed attractive to himself and he persisted in disbelief, and he said: evil is on the wording of from and and they followed is on its meaning.
47:15: He said: The example of Paradise which the righteous have been promised When the Almighty said: Indeed, God will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens, He described those gardens, meaning the description of Paradise for the righteous. We have already discussed this in Al-Ra’d, and Ali bin Abi Talib read, The example of Paradise which the righteous have been promised, in it are rivers of water not stagnant, meaning not old-smelling, and stagnant is like stagnant, and water has become stagnant, stagnant, and stagnant if its smell changes, and likewise ajanat ya’junan ajanan and ajunan, and it is said with a kasra in them: ajan and asna ya’junan and ya’junan asnan and ajanan, said Al-Yazidi, and a man also becomes stagnant with a kasra only if he enters a well and a foul odor from the well’s odor or something else hits him and he faints or the house of the young man, Zuhair said: I may leave the horn with yellow fingers, swaying in the spear with the stench of a foul smell. It is narrated al-wasn and the water became stagnant. Abu Zaid: It became stagnant on me, meaning it became ill and slow. Abu Amr: The man became stagnant on his father, taking his morals. Al-Laythani said: If he inclined to him in a resemblance, and the general reading is asan with a long vowel, and Ibn Kathir and Hamid read asan with a short vowel, and they are two languages, like hadith and hara. Al-Akhfash said: asan is for the state, and asan, like fa’il means to receive, and rivers of milk not “rivers of wine delicious for the drinkers” meaning the feet did not approach it and the speaker did not polish it like the wine of this world, so it is delicious and pleasant to drink and the drinkers do not hate it. So: a drink of deliciousness and deliciousness mean the same thing, and deliciousness is several times delicious, rivers of purified honey honey is what flows from the saliva of bees, purified) meaning from wax and dirt, God left it like that, it was not cooked over a fire nor was it defiled by the bees, and in al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Atiq al-Hakim bin Mu’awiyah on the authority of his father on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace God’s Messenger (may God’s prayers and peace be upon him) said: In Paradise there is a sea of water, a sea of mountain, a sea of milk, and a sea of Kharm, then the rivers will split after that. He said: A good and authentic hadith. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him, he said: “The Messenger of God (may God’s prayers and peace be upon him) said: ‘Massiha, Ceyhan, the Nile, and the Euphrates are all rivers of Paradise.’” Ka’b said: The Tigris River is the river of the water of the people of Paradise, the Euphrates River is their river of milk, the River of Egypt is their river, and the Seyhan River is their river of honey. Three of the four rivers flow from the River of Kauthar. Honey is an excuse and is feminine. Abbas said: From purified honey means that it does not come from the bellies of bees. And for them therein are all kinds of fruits “from” is redundant for emphasis. And forgiveness from their Lord means for their sins. Like one who is eternally in a fiery fur He said: Is one who is in this bliss like one who is born in? Al-Zajjaj said: That is, is one who has clear evidence from his Lord and is given these things like one whose deeds are made attractive to him while he is eternally in the Fire? So his saying: Like one is a substitute for Poem: Is he who has been made to look good in his evil deeds? Ibn Khaisan said: The example of this Paradise in which there are fruits and rivers is like the example of the Fire in which there is scalding water and Zaqqum. The example of the people of Paradise in eternal bliss is like the example of the people of Hell in eternal torment. And they will be given a drink of [another] appointment meaning, very boiling, when it is brought near, it will roast their faces and their juices will fall out. Instead of drinking it, he will cut up their intestines and extract them from their anuses. Intestines is the plural of ma’i, and the dual is ma’yan, which is all of the contents in the stomach.
47:16: Taste: And among them are those who enjoy themselves with you meaning, among those who boast and eat as livestock eat, and their evil deeds have been made attractive to them. There are people who enjoy themselves with you, and they are the hypocrites, Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, Rifa’ah bin al-Tabut, Zayd bin al-Salit, al-Harith bin Amr, and Malik bin Dakhshum. They will deliver the sermon on Friday for a short period. Tell the hypocrites to turn away from him, so that they may go out and ask about him. He and Muqatil said: It was said that they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the believers, and they listen to what he says, and the believer will understand it but the disbeliever will not. Until when they leave you meaning, when they leave your gathering, they will say to those who have been given knowledge. Ikrimah said: He is Abdullah bin Abbas. Ibn Abbas said: You were experiencing, meaning you were among those who have been given knowledge. In a narration from Ibn Abbas: He means Abdullah bin Mas’ud. Abdullah bin Mas’ud said: He is Abdullah bin Mas’ud. Al-Qasim bin Abd al-Rahman said: He is Abu Al-Darda’, and Zaid said: He taught the companions what did he say just now meaning now, in a mocking manner, meaning I did not touch upon an explanation, and just now means the hour is the closest time to you, from your saying, did you learn the first thing if you started with it and from it a matter of nose, and a garden of nose, meaning no one took care of it, and a cup of nose: if nothing was drunk from it, like her son was asked to drink from it like a garden of nose, the poet said: Their neighbor's secret is forbidden to them, and their neighbor eats the tip of the bowl. Another said: The grilled meat, the pickle, the loaf of bread, the beautiful nosed slave girl, and the cup For the stabbed horses and horses picking Imru' al-Qais said: He squeezed my nose That is, at its beginning, and the beginning of everything is its beginning. Qatada said about these hypocrites: People are of two types: one who understands about God and benefits from what he hears, and a man who does not understand and does not benefit from what he hears. It was said: People are of three types: a listener who acts, a wise listener, and a heedless listener who abandons. He said: Those whose hearts God has sealed so they did not believe. And followed their desires in disbelief.
47:17: The Almighty says: And those who are guided meaning to faith, God increases them in guidance. It was also said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, increased them in guidance. It was also said: What they hear of the Qur'an is guidance, meaning their certainty is doubled. Al-Farra' said: The hypocrites and their mockery increased them in guidance. It was also said: The revelation of the abrogating verse increased them in guidance. There are four sayings about the guidance that increased them: The first: It increased them in knowledge, said by Al-Rabi' bin Anas. The second: That they knew what they heard and acted upon what they knew, said by Al-Dahhak. The third: It increased their insight into their religion and belief in their Prophet, said by Al-Kalbi. The fourth: It opened their hearts to what they are upon of faith. And gave them their piety meaning He inspired it in them. It was also said: There are five aspects to it: The first: He gave them fear, said by Al-Rabi'. The second: The reward of their piety in the Hereafter, said by Al-Suddi. The third: He guided them to the work that was imposed upon them, said by Muqatil. Fourth: He explained to them what they should avoid. This was said by Ibn Ziyad and al-Suddi as well. Fifth: He abandoned the abrogated verses and acted upon the abrogating verses. This was said by Atiyya and al-Mawardi. It is possible. Sixth: He abandoned the concessions and taking the obligatory verses. It was read and gave them instead of and gave them. Ikrimah said: This was revealed regarding those who believed among the People of the Book.
47:18: ْوض،ُْاَْنًََعثت ََا واََا: ْا صلى ا َلَه وَلْرَوْقا ، ًَوخََه اََخاري و اَََمَي و اَن ما، ْمَلَُف،واَوَُىًَاَََا لََاَُاًَاََاََُْا: َْوق،"ْفََي رُانًَوََوى َعثت واََا َعَي: َْوق،اَفَن:َلْون من اََاسََومَه،اََي ُي ْون معُمُا ما:ْويْوَما،قاَه اَحََى،واَْخانَاََْاق اََمًََلمات اََا َََْا َلى َُا، ْوْثَة اَلئاَْْوًوقل، ْوُْاْة اَزور واَرحاََْص اَما وَصله،َُْيُالَْاْوواح،لْاََاب في َْاب اََََْة مات واَحم ومَه، َُْعَفًَلمَُْلَه ََْوا لَف، ََْومَه روََت اَْوَو، ْالَل: ََْو الَوْقا،اََُْي في غََه َوَه َْْوُصَعت ََْاََََْا وقََْزمعت َاَصَْْت ق َوس َنْقا،َْا ََعلمُا وحََُا َهْفلن َفَه في اَعمَََُْ: ْوََا:مَُا قوَاةَََُعُا َََخًَِى ََعََْمن رَسَََْصف َملَاة ََْى وَََى َأََاب َه وْوْلَْفَه فَُا وُو معصَُْفأ َن: " ََْحو ََاًَمن اََاْاَْماََْْن" ًََْ ََُْْن َأ" ،: 25 ) ََاََص" (مامَون وََاء مامَاتْرَا: " ْمن قا" ُُْْئو وُي،َخَُاَُفي َوُْخَلَْ ًَََوُي غ، ًََََوزنًََْورئ وما َخاف َن ْْون خُأ من اََاوي:اَزمخَْي،َن ََي َمَوًَمَو ََْاءة، َْْْْ ََاََْن من غََْْ ًََْوَن َْون اَحق،َن ََي َمَو ًََْ َُِْْن َأًْمَُْاََااَي وغََه منَوروي ََو َعف،اَحَن ْثًَْان اَوقف َلى اََاًََْ َُِْْن ْأََومن ق:اَمُْويْقا: ْوَُه قا،َِى اَخلقْمن اَْك مَْوْوما َحَمله اَْل، ًَاحَق اََُا.َاء ََْاُُاَِْن ْْوا في مََئُا ف ََواَضم، ََاَخَُْاََْاء و َنََُْْا" ََُْْاَُِْاَُْفاَى" َُِْا صاَحََََْاَُْفمن:اََََاف، ًََلَاَُْاَمَفوع في وْوص ََْاَحجَُْاَََاة َِا وصلَُْلن: َْوق،معَاه قَاْة غََهْقا، ًَاََا َما:وفي الخُار وَُان، َْوفَه اَن ز، َْقاَه اَن ز، ًَمَيء اََا َََْْاةَُْأَمُُْو َْاا:اَثاَي، ََْوَََما َملوه من خَََُْْْ: ْقاَْن اَََي صلى ا َلَه وَل"روى ََان َن ََس،وْخوَفاة َِْى َورك َا فلن قَْا فلن قًاَََامَْْْون َُا َوَْْفإَْْحََوا ََماء.ََْه اَماورْي،َور َكَ
47:19: The Almighty said: Know that there is no god but God. Al-Mawardi said: There are three aspects to this, even though the Messenger knew God: The first is to know that God taught you that there is no god but God. The second is that whatever you know by inference, know it with certainty. The third is to remember that there is no god but God. He expressed the remembrance with knowledge because it came from him. And on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah that he was asked about the virtue of knowledge, he said: Did you not hear His statement when He began with it: Know that there is no god but God and ask forgiveness for your sin. Then He ordered action after knowledge and said: Know that the life of this world is but play and amusement until His statement: Race one another to forgiveness from your Lord (al-Hadid 57:20-21). And He said: And know that your wealth and your children are but a trial (al-Anfal 8:28). Then He said after that: So beware of them (Al-Taghabun: 14). And the Almighty said: And know that whatever you gain of anything, a fifth of it is for God (al-Anfal 8:10). 41], then he ordered the work to be done. His saying, the Most High: And seek forgiveness for your sin has two possible meanings: First: It means seek forgiveness from God that you have committed a sin. Second: Seek forgiveness from God so that He may protect you from sins. It was said: When He mentioned to him the condition of the disbelievers and the believers, He commanded him to remain steadfast in faith, meaning, remain steadfast in what you are upon of monotheism, sincerity, and caution regarding what requires seeking forgiveness for it. It was also said: The address is to him and what is meant by it is the nation. According to this saying, the verse requires a person to seek forgiveness for all Muslims. It was also said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was distressed by the disbelief of the disbelievers and hypocrites, so the verse was revealed, meaning, know that there is no one who can remove what is in you except God, so do not attach your heart to anyone other than Him. It was also said: He commanded seeking forgiveness so that the nation would follow his example, and for the believing men and believing women, meaning for their sins. This is a command for intercession. Muslim narrated on the authority of Asim al-Ahwal, “On the authority of Abdullah ibn Sarjis al-Makhzumi, who said: I came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and ate from his food, so I said: O Messenger of God, may God forgive you! My companion said to him: Did the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, seek forgiveness for you?” May God bless him and grant him peace? He said: Yes, and for you. Then he recited this verse: And ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women. Then she turned and looked at the Seal of Prophethood between his shoulders, with two moles on it that looked like warts. And God knows your movements and your resting place. There are five opinions on this: First, He knows your deeds in your movements and your resting place. Second: Your movements in your deeds during the day and your resting place in your nights while sleeping. It was also said: Your movements in this world, and your resting place in this world and the Hereafter. This was said by Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak. Ikrimah said: Your movements in the loins of the fathers to the wombs of the mothers, and your resting place your standing on the earth. Ibn Kaysan said: Your movements from back to belly to this world, and your resting place in the graves. I said: The general applies to all of this, so nothing of the movements or stillness of the children of Adam is hidden from Him, glory be to Him, and so is all of His creation. He knows all of that before it is a whole and a detail, first and last. Glory be to Him! There is no god but Him.
47:20: God Almighty says: And those who believe say, meaning the sincere believers, Why was a surah not sent down? longing for revelation and eagerness for jihad and its reward. The meaning of Why is it not is Why not? “But when a decisive surah is sent down” means there is no abrogation in it. Qatadah said: Every surah in which jihad is mentioned is decisive, and it is the most severe of the Qur’an against the hypocrites. In Abdullah’s reading, When a newly revealed surah is sent down means a newly revealed surah. And fighting is mentioned therein means jihad is enjoined therein. It is read as When a surah is sent down and fighting is mentioned therein in the active form and fighting is mentioned therein. You will see those in whose hearts is disease meaning doubt and hypocrisy. They will look at you with the look of one fainting from death meaning they will look downcast and angry with staring and staring, like someone who stares at death. This is because they avoid fighting out of panic and fear, and because they secretly incline toward the disbelievers. God Almighty says: It is more appropriate for them. It is more appropriate for them Al-Jawhari said: Their saying: It is more appropriate for you, is a threat and a warning. The poet said: First, then first, then first. Is there milk for the milk of a mule? Al-Asma’i said: Its meaning is that something that would destroy him approached him, i.e., it befell him. He recited: He was divided between two of them, and it is better to exceed three. Any one who is close to increasing, Tha’lab said: No one has said anything better about awla than what Al-Asma’i said, and Al-Mubarrad said: It is said to someone who is about to be destroyed and then escapes: Awla lak, meaning you are close to being destroyed, as it was narrated that an Arab used to shoot prey continuously and it would escape from him, so he would say: Awla lak, then he shot prey and was close to it and then it escaped from him, so he said: If it were better to feed the people, it would have stopped them, but it would be better to leave the people hungry. It was said: It is like a man saying to his friend: O deprived one, what have you missed! Al-Jurjani said: It is taken from woe, so it is more af’al, but there is an inversion in it, which is that the ‘ayn of the verb takes the place of the lam. We have already discussed His statement: So it is more fitting for them, Qatada said: It is as if he said punishment is more fitting for them. It was said: That is, the hated one is their ally.
47:21: The Almighty’s saying: Obedience and a kind word obedience and a kind word meaning obedience and a kind word are better and more excellent, and this is the view of Sibawayh and Al-Khalil. It was said that the meaning is that our command is obedience and a kind word, so the subject was deleted and the pause is at so it is more appropriate for them, and likewise for the one who estimated they say obedience from us. It was said that the second verse is connected to the first, and the lam in his saying: for them has the meaning of the ba’, meaning obedience is more appropriate and more fitting for them and more deserving of them than abandoning compliance with God’s command, and this is the reading of Abu they say obedience. It was said that obedience is an attribute of a surah on the basis of: So if a surah of obedience is revealed, then one does not pause at so it is more appropriate for them. Ibn Abbas said: Their saying obedience is information from God Almighty about the hypocrites and the meaning is that they have obedience and a kind word. It was said: The obligation of the duties upon them, so if the The obligatory duties were difficult for them to obtain, so it is stopped at the more appropriate. The Almighty said: So when the matter is decided meaning the fighting is serious, or the obligation of fighting becomes obligatory, they dislike it, so they dislike it. The answer to if is omitted. It was said that the meaning is: So when the people of the matter decide, “If they were true to God meaning in faith and jihad, it would be better for them than disobedience and opposition.
47:22: First: The Almighty’s saying: Then would you, if you were given authority? There is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of if you were given authority. It was said that it is from the word wilayah. Abu al-‘Aliyah said: The meaning is, Then would you, if you were given authority and made rulers, spread corruption on the earth by taking bribes? Al-Kalbi said: That is, would you, if you were given authority over the nation, spread corruption on the earth by injustice? Ibn Jurayj said: The meaning is, Then would you, if you were given authority, spread corruption on the earth by committing sins and severing family ties? Ka’b said: The meaning is, Then would you, if you were given authority, kill one another? It was said: It is from turning away from something. Qatadah said: That is, would you, if you were given authority, spread corruption on the earth by shedding unlawful blood and severing family ties? It was said: Then would you, if you were given authority, spread corruption on the earth by shed- ing unlawful blood and severing family ties. It was said: “Then would you, if you were given authority, spread corruption on the earth by shed-... He went on to say in Surat Al-Baqarah in full, and Bakr Al-Muzani said: It was revealed about the Kharijites and the Khawarij, and there is some distance in it, and it is more apparent that it was only meant for the hypocrites, and Ibn Hayyan said: Quraysh, and similarly Al-Musayyab bin Sharik and Al-Farra’ said: It was revealed about the Umayyads and the Hashimites, and the evidence for this interpretation is what “Abdullah bin Mughaffal narrated, he said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘Would you, if you were given authority, spread corruption on the earth? ’ Then he said: They are this tribe of Quraysh, God has taken upon them, if they were given authority, that they would not spread corruption on the earth or sever their ties of kinship.” Ali bin Abi Talib read if you were given authority that you would not spread corruption on the earth with a damma on the ta’ and the waw and a kasra on the lam, and this is the reading of Ibn Abi Ishaq, and Ruways narrated it on the authority of Ya’qub, saying: If you were given authority over unjust rulers, you would go out with them in the sedition and fight them, and sever your ties of kinship with oppression and killing, and Ya’qub, Salam, Isa, and Abu Hatim read and sever your ties of kinship with a fatha on the ta’. And the lightening of the qaf, from the cutting, in consideration of the Almighty’s saying: And they sever that which God has commanded to be joined (Ar-Ra’d: 25). This reading was narrated by Harun from Abu Amr, and Al-Hasan read wa-taqatāwu with the open letters and stressed, in consideration of the Almighty’s saying: And they cut off their affair among themselves (Al-Anbiya’: 93). The rest read wa-ta-taqatāwu with the damma of the ta’ and the stressed ta’, from cutting off for emphasis, this is the choice of Abu Ubaid. The mention of ‘asaytum in Al-Baqarah was mentioned before, and Al-Zajjaj said in the reading of Nafi’: If this were permissible, then ‘asay with the kasra would be permissible. Al-Jawhari said: And it is said ‘asaytu an af’al lahi, and ‘asaytu with the kasra, and it is read fa-ha-‘asaytum with the kasra. I said: His statement indicates that they are two languages, and the discussion of Al-Baqarah has already been completed.
47:23: The Almighty said: Those are the ones whom God has cursed meaning He has expelled them and kept them far from His mercy and made them deaf to the truth, and blinded their sight meaning their hearts to goodness. So He followed the report that whoever does that, His curse is due upon him, and he is deprived of the benefit of his hearing and sight so that he does not submit to the truth even if he hears it, so He made him like an animal that does not reason. And He said: Then will you perhaps then He said: Those are the ones whom God has cursed so He returned from addressing to the third person, as is the custom of the Arabs in that.
47:24: The second is the Almighty’s saying: Do they not then consider the Qur’an meaning do they understand it and know what God has prepared for those who have not turned away from Islam, Or are there locks upon their hearts? meaning rather there are locks upon their hearts that God the Almighty has locked upon them so they do not understand. This refutes the doctrine of the Qadarites and the Imamites, and in a hadith with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, “The Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: ‘There are locks upon them like locks of iron until God opens them.’” The root of qaf is dryness and hardness, and what dries from a tree is called a lock, and qafeel is similar to it, and qafeel is also a plant and qafeel is the sound. The rajaz poet said: When he came to you dry and crisp, you struck him with the lock How did you read your Sheikh Al-Azba? Al-Qurashib with a kasra on the qaf is the elderly man, according to Al-Asma’i. Fasting has made it dry, as stated by Al-Qushayri and Al-Jawhari. So the locks here refer to the heart being agitated and devoid of faith, meaning faith does not enter their hearts nor does disbelief leave them, because God Almighty has sealed their hearts and said: on hearts, because if He had said on their hearts, the heart of others would not have entered into this sentence. What is meant is, are there locks on the hearts of these people and the hearts of those who have this characteristic? Third: In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God created the creation, and when He finished with them, the womb stood up and said: ‘This is the place of one seeking refuge from being severed.’ He said: ‘Yes. Are you not pleased that I connect with those who connect with you and sever with those who sever with you?’ She said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘Then that is for you.’ Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Recite if you wish: “Would you perhaps, if you were given authority, cause corruption in the land and sever your ties of kinship? Those are the ones whom God has cursed and made deaf and blinded their sight. Do they not then reflect upon the Qur’an, or are there locks upon their hearts?”’” The apparent meaning of the verse is that it is addressed to all disbelievers. Qatada and others said that the meaning of the verse is: Perhaps you, or it is feared for you, if you turn away from faith, will return to corruption in the land and shed blood. Qatada said: How did you see the people when they turned away from the Book of God, the Most High? Did they not shed unlawful blood, sever the ties of kinship, and disobey the Most Gracious? So, according to this, the womb is the womb of the religion of Islam and faith, which God has called brotherhood in His saying, The believers are but brothers (al-Hujurat 49:10). According to Al-Farra’, the verse was revealed about Banu Hashim and Banu Umayyah, and what is meant is those among them who concealed hypocrisy. So, by severing the womb, He referred to the kinship that existed between them and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, by denying the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that necessitates fighting. In short, womb is of two types: general and specific. The general womb is the womb of religion, and it is necessary to maintain it by adhering to faith, loving its people, supporting them, advising them, not harming them, being just between them, being fair in dealing with them, and fulfilling their obligatory rights, such as caring for the sick and the rights of the dead, such as washing them, praying over them, and burying them, and other rights due to them. As for the specific womb, which is the womb of kinship on both sides of a man, his father and mother, then specific rights and more are obligatory for them, such as spending, checking on their conditions, and not neglecting them. They should be looked after in times of need, and the general rights of kinship are confirmed in their right, so that if rights conflict, the closest should be started first. Some of the people of knowledge said: The kinship that must be maintained is every forbidden kinship, and accordingly, it is not obligatory for paternal uncles and maternal uncles. It was said: Rather, this applies to every kinship that is included in this of the kin with regard to inheritance, whether they are forbidden or not. From this, it is concluded that it is not obligatory to maintain ties with the mother’s kin from whom one does not inherit, and it is not forbidden to sever ties with them. This is not correct. What is correct is that everything that is included and encompassed by kinship must be maintained in every case, as an act of worship and religiously, based on what we mentioned first, and God knows best. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated in his Musnad, he said: Shu’bah told us, he said: Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar told me, he said: I heard Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi narrating, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The womb will have a tongue under the Throne on the Day of Resurrection that will say: O Lord, I have severed ties, O Lord, I have been wronged, O Lord, I have been wronged. Then its Lord will respond to it: Are you not pleased? That I maintain ties with those who maintain ties with you and sever ties with those who sever ties with you. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Jubayr ibn Mut’im, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: ‘One who severs ties of kinship will not enter Paradise.’” Ibn Abi Umar said: Sufyan said: He means one who severs ties of kinship. Narrated by Al-Bukhari. Fourth: His peace be upon him saying: God Almighty created the creation until He finished with them. Created means invented, and its origin is estimation, as mentioned above. Creation here means the created, and from it is His Almighty saying: This is the creation of God (Luqman 31:11), meaning His creation. The meaning of finished with them is that He completed their creation, not that He occupied Himself with them and then finished His occupation with them, since His action is not through direct action or handing over, nor is His creation through an instrument or attempt, exalted be He above that. His saying: The womb stood up and said can be interpreted in one of two ways: One of them is that God Almighty appointed someone from the angels to speak about the womb and say that, and it is as if He entrusted this worship with someone who struggles for it and writes down the reward of whoever connects it and the sin of whoever severs it, just as God entrusted the rest of the deeds with honorable scribes, and with observing the times of the prayers angels who follow one another. The second is that it is by way of estimation and representation that conveys exhaustion and great care, so it is as if He said: If the womb were among those who reason and speak, it would say this, as God Almighty said:: If We had sent down this Qur’an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and coming apart from fear of God. Then He said: And these examples We present to the people that perhaps they will give thought. (al-Hashr 59:21), and His statement: And she said, ‘This is the station of one who seeks refuge in You from being severing ties.’ The purpose of these words is to inform of the importance of maintaining kinship ties, and that God, the Exalted, has placed them in the position of someone who seeks refuge with Him, so He grants him refuge and includes him in His protection and care. If this is the case, then God’s kin will not be let down and His covenant will not be broken. Therefore, He said, addressing the womb, Are you not satisfied that I connect with those who connect with you and sever ties with those who sever ties with you? This is like the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: “Whoever prays the dawn prayer is under the protection of God, the Exalted, so do not let God seek you out regarding His protection, for whoever seeks Him out regarding His protection, He will seize him and then throw him on his face into the Fire.”
47:25: God Almighty says: Indeed, those who turned back after guidance had become clear to them - Satan enticed them and prolonged hope for them. Qatada said: They are the disbelievers of the People of the Book. They disbelieved in the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, after they knew his description among them. This was said by Ibn Jurayj. Ibn Abbas, Ad-Dahhak, and As-Suddi said: They are the hypocrites. They sat back from fighting after they learned about him in the Qur’an. Satan enticed them means he made their sins seem fair to them. This was said by Al-Hasan. And I gave them respite means Satan extended their hope and promised them long work. This was also narrated by Al-Hasan. He said: The One Who gave them respite and extended their lives is God Almighty. This was said by Al-Farra’ and Al-Mufaddal. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: The meaning of I gave them respite is He gave them respite. Based on this, God Almighty gave them respite in their punishment. Abu Amr, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Isa bin Umar, Abu Ja`far, and Shaybah read And I gave them respite with a damma on the hamza, a kasra on the lam, and a fatha on the ya’, without naming the agent. This is also what Ibn Hurmuz, Mujahid, Al-Jahdary, and Ya`qub read, except that they made the ya’ sukun as a statement from God Almighty: on the authority of He himself does that to them, as if he said: And I dictate to them, and Abu Hatim chose it. He said: Because the opening of the hamza suggests that the devil dictates to them, and that is not the case, so that is why he changed to the damma. Al-Mahdawi said: And whoever reads and dictates to them, then the subject is the name of God Almighty, and it was said the devil, and Abu Ubaid chose the reading of the common people. He said: Because the meaning is known, for His statement: That you may believe in God and His Messenger and support him and honor him and glorify Him (al-Fath 48:9), returning glorification to the name of God, and honor and honor to the name of the Messenger.
47:26: The Almighty said: That is because they said meaning that this was a dictation to them so that they would persist in disbelief because they said: meaning the hypocrites and the Jews, to those who hated what God revealed meaning the polytheists, We will obey you in some of the matter meaning in opposing Muhammad and showing hostility towards him, and refraining from jihad with him and weakening his command in secret, and they only said that secretly so God informed His Prophet, and the reading of the common people is asrarruhum with a fat-ha on the hamza as a plural of secret, and this is the choice of Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim, and the Kufians, Ibn Waththab, Al-A’mash, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i and Hafs from Asim read israrruhum with a kasra on the hamza as a source, like the Almighty’s saying: And I confided in them secrets (Nuh 71:9), a plural for the different types of secret.
47:27: The Almighty said: How then meaning how will their condition be, when the angels take their souls while they strike meaning striking, so it is in the position of a state, and the meaning of the speech is to frighten and threaten, meaning if the punishment is delayed for them then it will be until the end of life, and this has been mentioned in Al-Anfal and An-Nahl, and Ibn Abbas said, no one will die while committing a sin except by a severe beating of his face and back, and it was said: that is during fighting in support of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, by the angels striking their faces when they are pursued and their backs when they flee, and it was said: that is on the Day of Resurrection when they are driven to the Fire.
47:28: God Almighty says: That meaning that is their recompense because they followed that which angered God. Ibn Abbas said: It is their concealment of what was in the Torah of the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. If it is applied to the hypocrites, then it is a reference to what they concealed of disbelief, and they hated His pleasure meaning faith, so He rendered worthless their deeds meaning what they did of charity, maintaining family ties, and other things, as mentioned above.
47:29: God Almighty says: Or do those in whose hearts is disease hypocrisy and doubt, meaning the hypocrites, think that God will not bring to light their hidden hatred “Hatred is what is concealed of hatred, and there is disagreement about its meaning. Al-Suddi said: Their deception. Ibn Abbas said: Their envy. Qatrib said: Their hostility. He recited the words of the poet: Tell Ibn Hind what you want with the logic of a friend who has become bad and has built grudges. It was said: Their grudges, the singular of which is grudge. He said: And the one who has a grudge, I refrain from it It was mentioned earlier, and Amr ibn Kulthum said: And grudge after grudge spreads among you and brings out the hidden disease Al-Jawhari said: “Grudge and grudge: hatred. He held a grudge against him in the broken form and the people held grudges and grudges: they concealed their grudges. You took the boy under your lap. Al-Ahmar recited: He looks like a naughty boy Any carrier in his lap. Ibn Muqbil said: If I were to sever my weapon when it was intended, and my elbow would be like the head of a sword when it was sharpened. A stubborn horse: it does not give what it has of running except by hitting, and the meaning is: Or do they think that God will not reveal their enmity and hatred towards the people of Islam?
47:30: The Almighty said: And if We willed, We could have shown them to you meaning, We could have made them known to you. Ibn Abbas said: He made them known to you in Surat Bara’ah. The Arabs say: I will show you what I do, meaning I will make you do it. And from this is the Almighty’s saying: By what God has shown you (An-Nisa’: 105), meaning by what He has taught you. And you would have known them by their mark meaning by their signs. Anas said: After this verse, none of the hypocrites were hidden from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He knew them by their mark. We were on a campaign in which there were seven hypocrites whom people doubted. One night they woke up and on the forehead of each one of them was written: This is a hypocrite, and that was their mark. Ibn Zayd said: God decreed that they should be made known and ordered that they should leave the mosque, but they refused except to cling to There is no god but God, so their blood was spared, and they married and were married by it. And you will surely know them by the tone of their speech meaning by its content and meaning. And from this is The poet said: The report of the speech was not a tune Anything that is known by meaning but is not stated explicitly is taken from the word lahn in grammar, which is to deviate from the truth. From this is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: You bring your disputes to me, and perhaps some of you are more eloquent in their argument than others, meaning I will deviate from it in the answer due to his ability to conjugate speech. Abu Zayd: I pronounced a lahn for him with the fat-ha I pronounced a lahn if I said to him a statement that he would understand from you and that would be hidden from others. And he pronounced it from me with the kasra he pronounced it a lahn meaning he understood it. And I pronounced it to him, and I pronounced it to people, making them understand. Al-Fazari said: The hadith of Aldha is one of the things that the describers describe and weigh. Wonderful logic, sometimes a little melody, but the best speech is that which is melody He wants her to say something while she means something else, and she presents herself in her speech, removing it from its context with her cleverness and intelligence. God Almighty said: And you will surely recognize them by the tone of their speech. Al-Qital Al-Kalabi said: And I have revealed to you so that you may understand, and I have composed a tune that is not doubtful. Marrar Al-Asadi said: I composed a deceitful tune, and your rejection disturbed me, so you satisfy the hostile slanderers. Al-Kalbi said: After this verse was revealed, no hypocrite spoke to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) without him recognizing him. It was said: The hypocrites would address the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with words they spoke to one another, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would hear that and take the usual outward meaning, so God, the Most High, alerted him to it, so after this he would recognize the hypocrites when he heard their speech. Anas said: After this verse, no hypocrite was hidden from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). God made that known to him through revelation or a sign that he recognized by God’s informing him of it. And God knows your deeds, meaning nothing of it is hidden from Him.
47:31: The Almighty’s saying: And We will surely test you means that We will worship you with the laws, even though We know the consequences of matters. It has been said: We will treat you as those who are tested, until We know those among you who strive and are patient upon it. Ibn Abbas said: until We know until we distinguish. Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: until we bless until we see. This has been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. The general reading is with the letter nun in nablukum and ya’lam and nablu and Abu Bakr read from Asim with the letter ya in them. Ruways narrated from Ya’qub that the waw in nablu is sukoon on the basis of what came before. The rest put the letter waw in response to His saying: until We know. This knowledge is the knowledge by which recompense occurs, because He only recompenses them for their deeds, not for His eternal knowledge of them. So its interpretation is: until We know those who strive with knowledge of testimony, because if they are ordered to work, what they did will be witnessed from them. So recompense with reward and punishment occurs based on knowledge of testimony. And We will test your report We will test it and reveal it. Ibrahim bin Al-Ash'ath said: When Al-Fudayl bin Ayyadh read this verse, he would cry and say: O God, do not test us, for if you test us, you will disgrace us and tear off our veils.
47:32: God Almighty says: “Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of God and oppose the Messenger after guidance has become clear to them - never will they harm God at all, and He will render their deeds worthless.” It refers to the hypocrites or the Jews. Ibn Abbas said: They are the ones who were fed on the day of Badr. Its counterpart is, Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of God (al-Anfal 8:36). He is a prophet with proofs and signs: They will not harm God at all with their disbelief and He will render their deeds worthless meaning the reward for what they did.
47:33: There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, obey God and obey the Messenger.
