When He explained the state of the disbelievers, He commanded the believers to adhere to obedience in His commands and to obedience in the Messenger’s Sunnah. And do not invalidate your deeds, meaning your good deeds, with sins. Al-Hasan said this. Al-Zuhri said: with major sins. Ibn Jurayj: with showing off and seeking fame. Muqatil and Al-Thamali said: with showing off. It is addressed to whoever was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, through his Islam. They are all similar, and the statement of Al-Hasan includes them. It indicates that major sins nullify acts of obedience and sins take one out of faith. Second: Our scholars and others have used this verse as evidence that ending a voluntary act, whether it be prayer or fasting, after having begun it is not permissible because it nullifies the deed, and God has forbidden it. Those who permitted it, namely Imam al-Shafi’i and others, said that what is meant by it is nullifying the reward for an obligatory deed, so he forbade a man from nullifying its reward. As for what was voluntary, no, because it is not obligatory upon him. If they claim that the wording is general, then it is permissible to make a general specific, and the reason for making it specific is that voluntary is voluntary, and voluntary requires choice. On the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah: They used to think that no sin would harm one who is a Muslim, until this verse was revealed. They feared that major sins would invalidate their deeds. Muqatil said: God Almighty says: If you disobey the Messenger, then you have invalidated your deeds.
47:34: God Almighty says: Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of God and then die while they are disbelievers - never will God forgive them. By God, considering death as a disbeliever necessitates eternal damnation to Hell. This has already been discussed in Surat Al-Baqarah. It has also been said that what is meant by the verse are the people of the well, and its ruling is general.
47:35: There are three issues: The first is the Almighty’s saying: So do not weaken, meaning become weak in fighting. Weakness means weakness, and a person has weakened and others have weakened him. It is transitive and intransitive. He said: I am not weak from poverty And also, it was weakened with a kasra and wahan, meaning weakness. It was also read fa ma wahanu with a damma and a kasra on the ha’, and this was mentioned in Al Imran. Second: The Almighty’s saying: “And you call to peace” meaning reconciliation while you are superior meaning and you know God better than them. It was said: The meaning is and you are the victors because you are believers even if they outwardly defeat you in some circumstances. Qatada said: Do not be the first of the two groups to supplicate to the other. Third: The scholars differed regarding its ruling. It was said that it abrogates the statement of God the Almighty: “And if they incline to peace, then incline to it” (al-Anfal 8:61), because God the Almighty has the tendency to incline to peace if the Muslims do not need peace. It was said that it was abrogated by the statement of God the Almighty: “And if they incline to peace, then incline to it” (al-Anfal 8:61). It was said that it is decisive, and the two verses were revealed at two different times. It was said that His statement: “And if they incline to peace, then incline to it” is specific in one opinion to their individuals and the other is general. It is not permissible to make peace with the infidels except in case of necessity, and that is if we are unable to resist them due to the weakness of the Muslims. This meaning has already been fully explained. And God is with you means with victory and assistance, like And indeed, God is with the doers of good (al-Ankabut 29:69). And He will not deprive you of your deeds means He will not diminish you, according to Ibn Abbas and others. And from this is the one who has been killed and his blood was not recovered. You say from him, And his wound will be wound. And Witr, from his saying, peace be upon him: Whoever misses the Asr prayer, it is as if he has lost his family and his wealth, meaning he has taken them, and likewise Witr is his right, meaning he has diminished it. And the Most High said: And He will not deprive you of your deeds, meaning He will not diminish you in your deeds, as you say: I entered the house, and you mean in the house. Al-Jawhari said: Al-Farra’: And He will not deprive you is derived from witr, which means singular, so the meaning was, and He will not single you out without reward.
47:36: The Almighty’s saying: The life of this world is only play and amusement. This was mentioned in Al-An’am. And if you believe and fear God, He will give you your reward. This is a condition and its answer. And He does not ask you for your wealth. That is, He does not command you to give all of it in zakat, but rather He commanded you to give some of it. This was said by Ibn ‘Uyaynah and others. It was also said: He does not ask you for your wealth for Himself or because of a need for it. He only commands you to spend in His cause so that His reward may return to you. It was also said: He does not ask you for your wealth He only asks you for His wealth, because He is the owner of it and He is the One who bestows it. It was also said: Muhammad does not ask you for your wealth as a reward for conveying the message, similar to this: Say, ‘I do not ask you for it any reward.’ (al-Furqan 25:57).
47:37: The Almighty said: If they ask you about it, he will insist on you. It is said: He is insistent in asking, "he is persistent, and he insists" have the same meaning. Al-Hafi is the one who asks thoroughly, and likewise, Ihfaa is the thoroughness in speech and dispute. From this comes the word "ahfa sharibih," meaning he is thorough in taking it. "Be miserly and your grudges will come out," meaning miserliness will bring out your grudges. Qatada said: God knows that asking for money brings out grudges. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ibn Muhaisin, and Hamid read wa-takharuj with an open taa and a closed raa, wa-takharuj with a nominative case because it is the subject. Al-Walid narrated on the authority of Ya`qub Al-Hadrami wa-nakhruj with a noon, and Abu Mu`mar on the authority of Abd Al-Warith on the authority of Abu `Amr wa-ya-kharuj with a nominative case in the jim as a break and a new beginning. The well-known view from him is wa-ya-kharuj like the rest of the reciters, in apposition to what came before.
47:38: The Almighty says: Here you are, you are being called upon meaning, here you are, O believers, being called upon to spend in the cause of God meaning in jihad and the path of goodness. But among you is he who is stingy, and whoever is stingy is only stingy from himself meaning, from himself, meaning, he prevents himself from the reward and recompense. And God is the Rich meaning, He has no need of your wealth, and you are the needy of it. And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people meaning, more obedient to God than you. At-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people; Then they will not be the likes of you. They said: Who will replace us? He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, struck Salman on the shoulder and then said: (This one and his people. He said: A strange hadith in its chain of transmission is questionable. Abdullah bin Ja`far bin Nujayh, the father of Ali bin al-Madini, also narrated this hadith on the authority of al-`Ala` bin `Abd al-Rahman on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: Some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Messenger of God, who are these people about whom God mentioned that if we turn away, they will be replaced and they will not be like us? He said: Salman was beside the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace thigh and said: This one and his companions By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if faith were suspended from the Pleiades, men from Persia would attain it. Al-Hasan said: They are the non-Arabs. `Ikrimah said: They are the Persians and the Romans. Al-Muhasibi said: There is no one after the Arabs from all the non-Arab races who have better religion and scholars than them except the Persians. It was said: They are the Yemenis, and they are the Ansar. Shuraih bin Ubayd said this. Ibn `Abbas said the same: They are the Ansar. It was narrated from him that they are the angels. It was narrated from him that they are the Tabi`un. Mujahid said: They are whomever He will. From all other people, Then they will not be like you. Al-Tabari said: That is, in being stingy with spending in the way of God. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari that when this verse was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was pleased with it and said: It is more beloved to me than the world, and God knows best.
48:1: Medinan by consensus, and it consists of twenty-nine verses, and it was revealed at night between Mecca and Medina regarding Al-Hudaybiyyah. Muhammad bin Ishaq narrated on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Al-Miswar bin Makhramah and Marwan bin Al-Hakam, who said: Surat Al-Fath was revealed between Mecca and Medina regarding Al-Hudaybiyyah from beginning to end. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of his father: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was traveling on one of his journeys, and Umar bin Al-Khattab was traveling with him at night. Umar asked him about something, but the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not answer him. Then he asked him, but he did not answer him. Then he asked him, but he did not answer him. Umar bin Al-Khattab said: May Umar’s mother be bereaved. I called upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, three times, and he did not answer you. Umar said: So I moved my camel and went ahead of the people, and I was afraid that something had been revealed regarding the Qur’an. I had not waited long before I heard someone shouting at me, so I said: I was afraid that something had been revealed regarding the Qur’an, so I came.” The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “I greeted him and he said: ‘A surah has been revealed to me tonight which is dearer to me than all that the sun rises upon. Get up and recite: “Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest.”’ This is the wording of al-Bukhari. At-Tirmidhi said: A good, rare and authentic hadith. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Qatadah, that Anas ibn Malik told them: When the verse: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, that God may forgive you what is past of your sin and what is to come and complete His favor upon you and guide you to a straight path up to the words a great victory was revealed, he returned from al-Hudaybiyyah while they were in a state of grief and depression, and the sacrificial animals had been slaughtered at al-Hudaybiyyah. He said: A verse has been revealed to me which is dearer to me than the entire world.’ ‘Ata’ said on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas: The Jews cursed the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the Muslims when the verse: I do not know what will be done with me or with you (al-Ahqaf 24:9) was revealed. They said: How can we follow a man who does not know what will be done with him? This was very difficult for the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so God revealed: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, * That God may forgive you your sins, past and future. Muqatil ibn Sulayman said something similar: When the verse And I do not know what will be done with me or with you was revealed, the polytheists and hypocrites rejoiced and said: How can we follow a man who does not know what will be done with him or his companions? Then, after he returned from al-Hudaybah, the verse was revealed: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, meaning, We have decreed a decree for you. This verse abrogated that one, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: A surah has been revealed to me that would not please me with red camels. Al-Mas’udi said: I have been informed that whoever recites Surat al-Fath on the first night of Ramadan in voluntary prayer, God will protect him that year. God Almighty says: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest. There is disagreement about what this conquest is. In Bukhari, Muhammad bin Bashar told me, he said: Ghandar told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, he said: I heard Qatadah from Anas, Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, he said: Al-Hudaybiyah. Jabir said: We did not count the conquest of Mecca except on the day of Al-Hudaybiyah. Al-Bara’ said: You count the conquest as the conquest of Mecca, and the conquest of Mecca was a conquest, and we count the conquest as the Pledge of Ridwan on the day of Al-Hudaybiyah. We used to count with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, fourteen hundred, and Al-Hudaybiyah is a well. Ad-Dahhak said: Indeed, We have granted a clear conquest without fighting, and the peace treaty was part of the conquest. Mujahid said: He slaughtered him at Al-Hudaybiyah and shaved his head. He said: The conquest of Al-Hudaybiyah was a great sign, its water was emptied into it and flowed with water until all who were with him drank. Musa bin Uqbah said: A man said when they were returning from Al-Hudaybiyah, “This is not a conquest. They prevented us from the House.” The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Rather, it is the greatest of conquests. The polytheists have agreed to repel you from their country with wine and ask you for the matter.” And they desire safety from you, and they have seen from you what they disliked.” Al-Sha’bi said: Regarding the words of God Almighty: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, he said: It is the conquest of Hudaybiyyah. He achieved therein what he had not achieved in any other battle. God forgave him his past and future sins. The Pledge of Ridwan was given, and they were fed with the date palms of Khaybar. The sacrificial offerings reached the place, and the Romans were victorious over the Persians. The believers rejoiced at the victory of the People of the Book over the imprisoned. Al-Zuhri said: Hudaybiyyah was the greatest of the conquests, and that is because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to it with one thousand and four hundred. When the peace treaty was concluded, the people walked among themselves and learned and heard from God. No one wanted Islam except that he was able to do so. Those two years had not passed except that the Muslims had come to Mecca with ten thousand. Mujahid and Al-Awfi said: It is the conquest of Khaybar, and the first is more, and Khaybar was only a promise and an enemy, as will be explained in the words of God Almighty: Those who stayed behind will say when you set out (al-Fath 48:15), and His saying: God has promised you many spoils which you will take, so He has hastened this for you. (al-Fath 48:20), and Mujammi’ ibn Jariyah, who was one of the reciters of the Qur’an, said: We witnessed Al-Hudaybiyyah with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and when we left it, we saw the people shaking their camels. Some of the people said to one another: What is the matter with the people? They said: God has revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: So we went out, hurrying, and we found the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at the foreleg of Al-Ghamim. When the people had gathered, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: {Indeed, We have granted you, [O Muhammad], a clear conquest.} Umar ibn Al-Khattab said: Is this a conquest, O Messenger of God? He said: Yes, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, it was a conquest. Khaybar was divided among the people of Hudaybiyyah. No one entered except those who witnessed Hudaybiyyah. It was said that the words of God Almighty: a conquest indicate that Mecca was conquered by force, because the word conquest does not apply in any way except to what was conquered by force. This is the true meaning of the word. It may be said: The city was conquered by peace, so peace is not understood except by linking it to conquest. Thus, the conquest in peace became a metaphor, and the reports indicate that it was conquered by force. This has been said before and will come.
48:2: God Almighty says: That God may forgive you your past and future sins and complete His favor upon you and guide you to a straight path. Ibn al-Anbari said: A clear victory is not complete, because his statement, So that God may forgive you what has passed is connected to the victory, as if he said: “Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory so that God may combine forgiveness for you with the victory, so that God may combine for you with it that which will please your eye in this world and the hereafter.” Abu Hatim al-Sijistani said: It is the lam of the oath, and this is a mistake, because the lam of the oath is not broken or accusative, and if this was permissible, it would have been permissible: So that Zayd may stand, meaning So that Zayd may stand. Al-Zamakhshari said: If you say, how was the conquest of Mecca made a reason for forgiveness? I said: He did not make a reason for forgiveness, but rather for the combination of a number of four things, which are: forgiveness, completion of the blessing, guidance to the straight path, and the glorious victory. It is as if he said: We facilitated for you the conquest of Mecca and granted you victory over your enemy so that you might gather for yourself the glory of both worlds and the honor of this world and the hereafter. It is permissible that the conquest of Mecca, in that it was a struggle against the enemy, was a reason for forgiveness and reward. In Al-Tirmidhi: On the authority of Anas, he said: So that God may forgive you your past and future sins was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, upon his return from Al-Hudaybiyyah. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A verse has been revealed to me that is dearer to me than anything on the face of the earth. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it to them, and they said: Congratulations and well-pleased, O Messenger of God. God has revealed to you what He will do with you, so what will He do with us? And the verse was revealed to him: That He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow, until he reached a great attainment. He said: A good and authentic hadith. In it, on the authority of Majma’ ibn Jariyah, the people of interpretation differed about the meaning of that God may forgive you what is past of your sin and what is to come so it was said: what is past of your sin before the message, and what is to come after it, said Mujahid, and something similar was said by al-Tabari and Sufyan al-Thawri. al-Tabari said: It goes back to the words of God the Most High: When there comes the help of God and the conquest to His words: repentant, “that God may forgive you what is past of your sin” before the message, and what is to come until the time of the revelation of this verse. Sufyan al-Thawri said: that God may forgive you what is past of your sin what you did in the Jahiliyyah before revelation was sent to you and what is to come everything you did not do, and al-Wahidi said this. The discussion of the occurrence of minor sins upon the prophets has already passed in Surat al-Baqarah, so this is one saying: And it was said: and what is past before the conquest, and what (It was delayed after the conquest. It was said: What preceded before the revelation of this verse, and what was delayed after it. Ata’ al-Khurasani said: What preceded of your sin meaning the sin of your parents Adam and Eve, and what was delayed of the sins of your nation, and it was said: of the sin of your father Abraham, and what was delayed of the sins of the prophets, and it was said: And what preceded of the sin of the Day of Badr, and what was delayed of the sin of the Day of Hunayn. That is because the sin that preceded on the Day of Badr was that he began to supplicate and say: O God, if you destroy this group, you will never be worshipped on earth again. And he began to repeat this statement at intervals, so God revealed to him: How do you know that if you destroy this group, I will never be worshipped again? So this was the previous sin. As for the sin and the delayed one, it was on the Day of Hunayn. When the people were defeated, he said to his uncle Abbas and his cousin Ibn Sufyan: Give me a handful of pebbles from the valley. So he gave it to them, and he took it in his hand and threw it in the faces of the polytheists and said::I saw the faces, Ha Mim, they will not be victorious. So the people were defeated, one and all, and no one remained but his eyes were filled with sand and gravel. Then he called out to his companions and they returned. He said to them upon their return: If I had not shot at them, they would not have been defeated. So God Almighty revealed: And you did not throw when you threw, but it was God who threw (al-Anfal 8:17). So this was the later sin. Abu Ali Al-Rudhbari said: He says, if you had an old or new sin, we would have forgiven you for it. God Almighty says: And He completes His favor upon you. Ibn Abbas said: In Paradise. It was also said: With prophecy and wisdom. It was also said: With the conquest of Mecca, Taif, and Khaybar. It was also said: With the submission of those who were arrogant and the obedience of those who were tyrannical. And guides you to a straight path. That is, He keeps you on the right path until He takes you to Him.
48:3: The Almighty says: And God will grant you a mighty victory, meaning a victorious and powerful victory that is not followed by humiliation.
48:4: God Almighty says: “It is He who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers that they would increase in faith along with their [present] faith. And to God belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth. And ever is God Knowing and Wise.” As-Sakinah: Serenity and tranquility. Ibn Abbas said: Every serenity in the Qur’an is tranquility except that in Surat Al-Baqarah. The meaning of increasing faith was mentioned earlier in Surat Al-Imran. Ibn Abbas said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent with the testimony that there is no god but God. When they believed him in it, he increased their prayer. When they believed him, he increased their zakat. When they believed him, he increased their fasting. When they believed him, he increased their Hajj. Then he completed their religion for them. This is what He said: That they may increase in faith along with their faith, meaning belief in the laws of faith along with their belief in faith. Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: Fear along with their fear. Ad-Dahhak said: Certainty along with their certainty. And to God belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth, Ibn Abbas said: He means the angels, jinn, devils, and mankind. And God is Knowing of the conditions of His creation, Wise in what He wills.
48:5: God Almighty says: “That He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally, and that He may remove from them their misdeeds. And that is, in the sight of God, a great attainment.” That is, He sent down tranquility so that their faith would increase, and that increase would be due to their entering Paradise. It was said that the lam in li-dikhul relates to what the lam relates to in His statement: that God may forgive you. And that that is, that promise of entering Mecca and forgiveness of sins, was with God a great success that is, salvation from every sorrow and attainment of every desired thing. It was said that when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited to his companions, that God may forgive you what has passed of your sin and what will come after, they said: Congratulations to you, O Messenger of God, so what is for us? Then it was revealed: That He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens. And when he recited: And complete His favor upon you, they said: Congratulations to you. Then it was revealed: And I have completed My favor upon you (al-Ma’idah 5:3). Then when he recited: And guide you to a straight path, it was revealed regarding the Ummah: And guide you to a straight path. And when he said: And God will support you with a mighty victory, it was revealed: And it has been incumbent upon Us to support the believers (Al-Rum: 47). It is like the saying of the Most High: “Indeed, God and His angels send blessings on the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings on him and salute him with a worthy salutation.” (al-Ahzab 33:56), then He said: It is He who sends blessings upon you (al-Ahzab 33:43). Al-Qushayri mentioned this.
48:6: The Almighty said: And He punishes the hypocritical men and hypocritical women, and the polytheistic men and polytheistic women meaning by causing them to suffer because of the superiority of the Muslims’ word, and by giving the Prophet, peace be upon him, power to kill, capture, and enslave them. Those who think evil of God means their thought that the Prophet, peace be upon him, would not return to Medina, nor any of his companions when he went out to Hudaybiyyah, and that the polytheists would eradicate them, as He said: Rather, you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: Evil here means corruption, upon them is the circle of evil in this world through killing, captivity, and capture, and in the Hereafter in Hell. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read circle of evil with the dammah, and the rest read it with the fathah. Al-Jawhari said: It distressed him, it distressed him with evil al-Fath, and mis’a’ah and masaya, the opposite of masaya, the opposite of his secret, and the noun is evil with the dammah, and it was read upon them The circle of evil means defeat and evil. Whoever opens it will be harmed. And God became angry with them and cursed them and prepared Hell for them, and evil it is as a destination.
48:7: The Almighty's saying: "And to God belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth. And God is Exalted in Might and Wise." This has all been mentioned before in more than one place, and praise be to God. It was said that when the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah took place, Ibn Abi Talib said: Does Muhammad think that if he makes peace with the people of Mecca or conquers it, he will not have any enemies? So where are the Persians and the Romans?! God the Almighty made it clear that the soldiers of the heavens and the earth are more numerous than the Persians and the Romans. It was said that this includes all of creation. Ibn Abbas said: And to God belong the soldiers of the heavens are the angels, and the soldiers of the earth are the believers. He repeated it because what came before came after mentioning the polytheists of Quraysh, and this comes after mentioning the hypocrites and all the other polytheists. The intention in both places is to frighten and intimidate. If He wanted to destroy the hypocrites and polytheists, that would not be beyond His power, but He delays them until an appointed term.
48:8: The Almighty says: Indeed, We have sent you as a witness. Qatada said: Over your nation to convey the message. It was also said: A witness over them regarding their deeds of obedience or disobedience. It was also said: Explaining to them what We sent you with. It was also said: A witness over them on the Day of Resurrection. So he is a witness to their actions today, and a witness over them on the Day of Resurrection. This meaning has already been mentioned in An-Nisa’, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr: Explaining. And a bearer of good tidings for those who obey him of Paradise, and a warner of the Fire for those who disobey. Qatada and others said this. The derivation of good tidings and their meanings has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. Witness, bearer of good tidings, and warner are in the accusative case. Sibawayh said: I passed by a man with a falcon hunting with it tomorrow. So the meaning is: We have sent you as a witness over them on the Day of Resurrection. Based on this, you say: I saw Umar standing tomorrow.
48:9: The Almighty’s saying: That you may believe in God and His Messenger. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaisin, and Abu Umar read liyyi’minu with a ya’, and likewise ya’ziruhu wa yuqruhu wa yusbihihu all with a ya’ as a predicate, and Abu Ubaid chose it because of the mention of the believers before and after it. As for before it, it is His saying liyadakhu and as for after it, it is His saying: Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, the rest with a ta’ as a direct address, and Abu Hatim chose it: And you honor him, meaning you glorify him and magnify him, as Al-Hasan and Al-Kalbi said. Ta’zir is glorification and respect, and Qatada said: You support him and prevent him, and from this comes ta’zir in the hadd, because it is a deterrent, Al-Qatami said: Why don't you come to me early without being foolish and reproaching me? The one who is loved is not helped by reproach. Ibn Abbas and Ikrimah said: You fight with him with the sword. Some linguists said: You obey him and respect him meaning you rule him. As-Suddi said: It was said: You glorify him. Reverence is also glorification and respect, and the ha in both of them refers to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Here, there is a complete pause. Then you begin and glorify Him, meaning you glorify God morning and evening, meaning in the evening. It was said: All the pronouns refer to God Almighty, so based on this, the interpretation of you honor and respect Him is that you affirm for Him the validity of His Lordship and deny that He has a son or partner. Al-Qushayri chose this statement, and the first is the statement of Ad-Dahhak. Based on this, some of the speech refers to God Almighty, which is and you glorify Him, without disagreement, and some of it refers to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, which is and you honor and respect Him, meaning you call upon him by the message and prophethood, not by name and nickname. In you glorify Him, there are two aspects: One of them is glorifying Him by declaring Him, glory be to Him, free from all Ugly, and the second is the act of prayer in which there is glorification in the morning and in the evening, meaning in the morning and evening, and the statement has been made in it and the poet said: By my life, you are the house whose people are most honored, and I sit in its shade in the evenings.
48:10: The Almighty’s statement: Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you at Al-Hudaybiyyah, O Muhammad, are only pledging allegiance to God. He made it clear that their pledge to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is only a pledge to God, as He, the Almighty, said: Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed God (An-Nisa’: 80). This pledge is the Pledge of Ridwan, as will be explained in this surah, God willing. The Hand of God is above their hands. It was said: His hand in reward is above their hands in fulfillment, and His hand in favor of them with guidance is above their hands in obedience. Al-Kalbi said: Its meaning is that God’s favor upon them is above what they did in the pledge. Ibn Kaysan said: God’s power and victory are above their power and victory. But whoever breaks his pledge after the pledge, breaks only to the detriment of himself, meaning that the harm of breaking his pledge will come back to him, because he has deprived himself of reward and incurred punishment. And whoever fulfills what he has pledged to God, it was said about the pledge, and it was said about his faith, then He will give him a great reward. Meaning in Paradise. Hafs and Al-Zuhri read upon him with a damma on the ha’, and the rest read it with a genitive. Nafi’, Ibn Kathir, and Ibn Amir read fasna’tuhi with a noon, and Al-Farra’ and Abu Mu’adh chose it. The rest read it with a ya’, and it is the choice of Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim, because of the proximity of the name of God to it.
48:11: The Almighty said: The bedouins who stayed behind will say to you. Mujahid and Ibn Abbas said: He means the bedouins of Ghifar, Muzaynah, Aslam, Ashja` and Ad-Dail, and they are the bedouins who were around Madinah. They stayed behind with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he wanted to travel to Mecca in the year of the conquest, after he had provoked them to go out with him out of fear of the Quraysh. He entered ihram for Umrah and led the sacrificial animals with him, so that the people would know that he did not want war, but they were reluctant to go and claimed to be busy, so it was revealed. He only said: those who stayed behind because God left them behind from the company of His Prophet. The one who stayed behind is the one who is abandoned, and this has already been mentioned in Bara’ah. Our wealth and our families have occupied us means that we have no one to take care of them. So ask forgiveness for us they came asking for forgiveness and their belief was contrary to their outward appearance, so God exposed them with His saying: They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts and this is pure hypocrisy. "Say: Who can control for you anything against God if He intends to harm you?" He read Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i Dharan with the damma of the dad here only, meaning something that will harm you. Ibn Abbas said: Defeat. Al-Baqih with the fatha, and it is the source of dharahtu dharan, and with the damma the name of what befalls a person from emaciation and bad condition, and the source leads from time and more, and Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose it, they said: because he contrasted it with benefit which is the opposite of harm, and it was said: they are two languages with the same meaning, like poverty and poverty and weakness and weakness, or he wanted benefit for you meaning victory and booty, and this is a response to them when they thought that staying behind the Messenger would ward off harm from them and hasten benefit for them.
48:12: The Almighty said: Rather, you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families, that is, they said: Muhammad and his companions are head-eaters who will never return, and that was made attractive meaning hypocrisy, in your hearts and this attractiveness is from Satan, or God creates that in their hearts, and you thought an evil thought that God would not support His Messenger, and you were a people who were ruined, meaning destroyed, as Mujahid said. Qatadah said: corrupt and not fit for any good. Al-Jawhari said: Bur is the corrupt, destroyed man in whom there is no good. Abdullah bin Al-Zubayri Al-Sahmi said: O Messenger of God, the King, my tongue is mended. It has not been torn since I was in a coma. A woman who is also a perisher, as Abu Ubaid narrated, and a perishing people, God Almighty said: And you were a perishing people, which is the plural of ba’ir, like ha’il and hawl, and so-and-so has perished, meaning he has perished, and God has made him perish, meaning He has destroyed him. It was said: Purished are evil, as Ibn Bahr said. Hassan bin Thabit said: Height is of no use to men, but God may guide the path of the barren people. Any dead person.
48:13: The Almighty says: And whoever does not believe in God and His Messenger - then indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers a Blaze. This is a threat to them, and a statement that they disbelieved through hypocrisy.
48:14: God Almighty says: “To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And ever is God Forgiving and Merciful.” That is, He is independent of His servants, but He only tested them with the task to confirm those who believe and punish those who disbelieve and disobey.
48:15: The Almighty said: Those who stayed behind will say, when you set out to take the spoils, meaning the spoils of Khaybar, because God Almighty promised the people of Hudaybiyyah the conquest of Khaybar, and that it would be theirs exclusively, whether they were absent or present. None of them was absent from it except Jabir ibn Abdullah, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided it for him like the share of those who were present. Ibn Ishaq said: The one in charge of the division of the spoils in Khaybar was Jabbar ibn Sakhr al-Ansari from Banu Salamah, and Zayd ibn Thabit from Banu al-Najjar. They were both accountants and distributors. Leave us to follow you, meaning leave us. You say: Dharhu, meaning leave him, and he leaves him, meaning he abandons him. Its root is Wadharuhu yadharhu, like Wasaahu yasaahu, and his chest has been made blind. It is not said: Wadharuhu or Wadharuhu, but he left him while he was leaving. Mujahid said: They stayed behind from going out to Mecca, so when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out and took some people and sent them out, they said: Leave us to follow you and fight. With you, they want to alter the word of God, that is, to change it. Ibn Zayd said: It is the saying of God the Almighty: And they asked your permission to go out, so say, ‘You will never go out with me, nor will you fight with me an enemy,’ the verse. At-Tabari and others rejected this statement, because the Battle of Tabuk took place after the conquest of Khaybar and after the conquest of Mecca. It was said: The meaning is that they want to change the promise of God that He promised to the people of Hudaybiyyah, and that is because God the Almighty gave them the spoils of Khaybar in exchange for the conquest of Mecca, as they returned from Hudaybiyyah with a peace treaty, as Mujahid and Qatadah said, and At-Tabari chose it, and most of the people of interpretation agreed with it. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read kalam without the alif and the kasra of the lam, the plural of word, like Salamah and Salam. The rest read kalam as a source. And Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose it, considering his saying: Indeed, I have chosen you over mankind with My messages and My speech (al-A’raf 7:144). Speech is what is independent of sentences. Al-Jawhari said: Speech is a generic noun that applies to little and much, and the word is not less than three words because it is the plural of a word, like nabqah and nabq. For this reason, Sibawayh said: This is the chapter on knowing what words are in Arabic. He did not say what speech is, because he meant three things themselves: the noun, the verb, and the particle. So he came with what can only be a plural, and left out what can apply to one and a group. Tamim says: It is a word, with a kasra on the kaf. And it has been mentioned in Bara’ah that it says: Thus said God before meaning before our return from Al-Hudaybiyyah that the spoils of Khaybar are for those who witnessed Al-Hudaybiyyah specifically. Then they will say, ‘Rather, you envy us’ that we share with you from the spoils. And it was said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you go out, I will not prevent you except that you have no share. So they said: This is envy. So the Muslims said: God told us in Al-Hudaybiyyah what they would say, and He said: And they will say, ‘Rather, you envy us.’ God Almighty said: Rather, they did not understand except a little, meaning they did not know anything except worldly matters. It was also said: They did not understand anything of the religious matters except a little, which is abandoning fighting.
48:16: It contains four issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Say to those of the bedouins who stayed behind meaning say to those who stayed behind from Al-Hudaybiyyah You will be called to fight a people of great strength Ibn Abbas, Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah, Mujahid, Ibn Abi Layla, and Ata’ al-Khurasani said: They are the Persians. Ka’b, Al-Hasan, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla said: The Romans. And from Al-Hasan also: The Persians and the Romans. Ibn Jubayr said: Hawazin and Thaqif. Ikrimah said: Hawazin. Qatadah said: Hawazin and Ghatafan on the day of Hunayn. Al-Zuhri and Muqatil said: Banu Hanifah, the people of Al-Yamamah, the companions of Musaylimah. Rafi’ ibn Khadij said: By God, we used to recite this verse in the past: You will be called to fight a people of great strength but we did not know who they were until Abu Bakr called us to fight Banu Hanifah, so we knew that it was them. Abu Hurayrah said: This verse has not yet come, and the apparent meaning of the verse refutes it. Second: In this verse there is evidence of the validity of the Imamate of Abu Bakr and Umar may God be pleased with them, because Abu Bakr called them to fight Banu Hanifa, and Umar called them to fight Persia and Rome. As for the statement of Ikrimah and Qatadah that it was in Hawazin and Ghatafan on the day of Hunayn, no, because it is impossible for the one calling them to be the Messenger (peace be upon him), because he said: You will never go out with me, nor will you fight an enemy with me (al-Tawbah 9:83). This indicates that the one meant by the one calling is other than the Prophet (peace be upon him), and it is known that no one called these people after the Prophet (peace be upon him) except Abu Bakr and Umar may God be pleased with them. Al-Zamakhshari: If that is authentic from Qatadah, then the meaning is you will never go out with me as long as you are in the state of sickness of heart and confusion in religion, or according to the statement of Mujahid, the promise was that they would not follow the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) except as volunteers with no share in the spoils, and God knows best. The second: The Almighty’s saying: Either you fight them or they submit. This is the ruling on those from whom the jizyah is not imposed. It is connected to you fight them, meaning it will be one of two things: either fighting or Islam. There is no third option. In the letter of Abi, or they submit, it means until they submit, just as you say: Eat or you are satisfied, meaning until you are satisfied. He said: I told him, "Don't cry. We are only trying to become king or die and be unable to do so." Al-Zajjaj said: He said or they submit because the meaning is or they submit without fighting, and this is in fighting the polytheists, not the People of the Book. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: If you obey, God will give you a good reward - booty and abundance in this world, and Paradise in the Hereafter. But if you turn away as you turned away before - the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah, He will punish you with a painful punishment - which is the punishment of the Fire.
48:17: God Almighty says: “There is no blame upon the blind or upon the lame or upon the ill. And whoever obeys God and His Messenger - He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow. And whoever turns away - He will punish him with a painful punishment.” Ibn Abbas said: When the verse: And if you turn away as you turned away before, He will punish you with a painful punishment was revealed, the people of that time said: What about us, O Messenger of God? Then the verse: There is no blame upon the blind or upon the lame or upon the ill was revealed, meaning there is no sin on them for staying away from jihad because of their blindness, old age, and weakness. This has been discussed clearly in Bara’ah and elsewhere. Lameness is a defect that befalls one leg, and if that has an effect, then the weakness of two legs is more likely to have an effect. Muqatil said: They are the people of that time who stayed away from Hudaybiyyah, and he has excused them, meaning whoever among them wants to go with you to Khaybar, let him do so. And whoever obeys God and His Messenger in what he commanded him, He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow. Nafi’ and Ibn ‘Amir readََُْهwith a nun for emphasis, while the rest read it with a ya. Abu ‘Ubaid and Abu Hatim preferred this because the name of God came first. And whoever turns away, He will punish him with a painful punishment.
48:18: The Almighty said: God was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree. This was the Pledge of Ridwan, and it was Al-Hudaybiyyah. This is the story of Al-Hudaybiyyah in brief: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stayed on his way back from the Battle of Banu Al-Mustaliq in Shawwal, and went out in Dhul-Qa'dah to perform Umrah. He called upon the Bedouins who were around Madinah, but most of them were slow to come back. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out with those who were with him from the Muhajireen and Ansar and those who followed him from the Arabs, and all of them were around one thousand four hundred, and it was said: one thousand five hundred, and other things were said, as will come. And he led the sacrificial animals with me, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) entered ihram so that the people would know that he had not set out to fight. When the report of his departure reached the Quraysh, they all went out to prevent the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from entering the Sacred Mosque and Mecca, and if he fought them, they would fight him without that. They sent Khalid ibn al-Walid with cavalry to Kar’ al-Ghamim. The report of that reached the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) while he was in Usfan. The one who informed him was Bishr ibn Sufyan al-Ka’bi, so he took a route to go out behind them, and he went out to al-Hudaybiyyah from the lower part of Mecca. His guide among them was a man from the tribe of Aslam. When the report of that reached the cavalry of the Quraysh that were with Khalid, they ran to the Quraysh to inform them of that. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) arrived at al-Hudaybiyyah, his she-camel (peace and blessings of God be upon him) knelt down and the people said: Leave! Leave! The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It was not hidden and it was not in its nature, but it was He who held back the elephant from Mecca. If the Quraysh invite me today to a plan in which they ask me to maintain kinship ties, you will give it to them. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, descended there, and it was said: O Messenger of God, there is no water in this valley! Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) took out an arrow from his quiver and gave it to one of his companions. He lowered it into one of those wells and plunged it into its belly, causing fresh water to suffice for the entire army. It was said that the one who lowered the arrow into the well was Najiyah ibn Jundub ibn Umair al-Aslami, who was the driver of the Prophet’s (peace and blessings be upon him) camel at that time. It was also said that al-Bara’ ibn Azib lowered the arrow into the well. Then the ambassadors took place between the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and the infidels of Quraysh, and the back-and-forth and dispute lasted until Suhayl ibn Amr al-Amri came and agreed with him that he (peace and blessings be upon him) would leave for most of that period. Then the next year he would come to perform the minor pilgrimage and enter Mecca with his companions unarmed, keeping their swords in their scabbards. He would stay there for three days and then leave. There would be a peace treaty between him and them for ten years, during which people would intermingle and feel safe with one another. Whoever came from the infidels to the Muslims as a Muslim, whether man or woman, would be returned to the infidel, and whoever came from the Muslims to the infidels as an apostate, they would not return him to the Muslims. This was very difficult for the Muslims. Some of them had a discussion about it, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was more knowledgeable about what God had taught him, that He would grant relief to the Muslims. So he said to his companions: Be patient, for God will make this peace treaty a cause for the emergence of His religion. The people became accustomed to saying this after some of them had been estranged from him, and Abu Suhayl ibn Amr wrote at the beginning of the treaty document: From Muhammad, the Messenger of God. They said to him: If we had believed you in that, we would not have prevented you from what you want! So it is necessary to write in your name, O God. So he said to Ali, who was writing the treaty document: Erase, O Ali, and write in your name, O God. Ali refused to erase with his hand, Muhammad, the Messenger of God. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Show it to me. So he pointed to him, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, erased it with his hand and ordered him to write from Muhammad bin Abdullah. On that day, Abu Jandal bin Suhayl came with the trace of the treaty document while he was chained, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned it to his father. This was very difficult for the Muslims, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed them and informed Abu Jandal that God would make a way out and relief for him. Before the treaty, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had sent Uthman bin Affan to Mecca as a messenger. Then report came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that the people of Mecca had killed him. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called for allegiance to him to fight and fight for the people of Mecca. It was narrated that he pledged allegiance to them to die, and it was narrated that he pledged allegiance to them not to flee. It was the Pledge of Ridwan under the tree, in which God, the Most High, informed us that He was pleased. On the authority of those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, under it, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed us that they would not enter the Fire, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, struck his right hand on his left for Uthman, so he is as if he had witnessed it. And Wakee’ mentioned on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: The first to pledge allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Al-Hudaybiyah was Abu Sufyan Al-Asadi. And in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Al-Zubayr on the authority of Jabir, who said: We were four hundred on the day of Al-Hudaybiyah, so we pledged allegiance to him and Umar was holding his hand under the tree, which was a tamarisk tree, and he said: We pledged allegiance to him that we would not flee, and we did not pledge allegiance to him to die. And on his authority that he heard a neighbor asking: How many were there on the day of Al-Hudaybiyah? He said: We were fourteen hundred, so we pledged allegiance to him and Umar was holding his hand under the tree, which was a tamarisk tree, so we pledged allegiance to him, except for Jad ibn Qays al-Ansari, who hid under the belly of his camel. And on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja`d, he said: I asked Jabir ibn Abdullah about the people of the tree, so he said: If we were one hundred thousand, it would be enough for us. We were one thousand five hundred, and in another narration we were fifteen hundred. And on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa, he said: The people of the tree were one thousand three hundred, and Aslam was one-eighth of the emigrants. And on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ubayd, he said: I said to Salamah: On what did you pledge allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah? He said: On death. On the authority of Al-Bara’ ibn Azib, he said: Ali may God be pleased with him wrote the peace treaty between the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the polytheists on the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah. He wrote: This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) agreed upon. They said: Do not write ‘Messenger of God,’ for if it were true that you are the Messenger of God, we would not fight you. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Ali: Erase it. He said: I am not one to erase it. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) erased it with his own hand. Among the conditions they stipulated was that they should enter Mecca and stay there for three days, and not enter it with any weapon except a weapon sheath. I said to Abu Ishaq: What is a weapon sheath? He said: A skin and what is in it. Anas reported: The Quraysh made peace with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) among them was Suhayl ibn Amr. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Ali: Write ‘In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.’ Suhayl ibn Amr said: As for ‘In the name of God,’ we do not know what ‘In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful’ means! But write what we know: In Your name, O God. He said: Write ‘From Muhammad, the Messenger of God.’ They said: If we knew that you were His Messenger, we would follow you! But write your name and your father's name. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Write from Muhammad ibn Abdullah. They stipulated to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Whoever comes from you, we will not return him to you, and whoever comes to you from us, you will return him to us. They said: O Messenger of God, should we write this? He said: Yes, whoever goes from us to them, God will distance him, and whoever comes to us from them, God will make for him relief and a way out. Abu Wa'il said: Sahl ibn Hunaif said on the day of Siffin: O people, accuse yourselves. We were with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and among the polytheists. Then Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him came and went to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, are we not in the right and they in the wrong? He said: Yes. He said: Are not our dead in Paradise and their dead in Hell? He said: Yes. He said: Then why should we give up our religion and go back before God has yet to judge between us and them? He said: O Ibn Al-Khattab, I am the Messenger of God, and God will never humiliate me. So Umar left, but he could not stay angry, so he went to Abu Bakr and said: O Abu Bakr, are we not on the right and they on falsehood? He said: Yes. He said: Are not our dead in Paradise and theirs in Hell? He said: Yes. He said: Then why should we give up our religion and go back before God has judged between us and them? He said: O Ibn Al-Khattab, he is the Messenger of God, and God will never humiliate him. So the Quran was revealed to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about the victory, so he sent to Umar and read it to him. He said: O Messenger of God, was he the victory? He said: Yes, and his heart was at ease and he went back. God the Almighty said: Then He knew what was in their hearts of truthfulness and loyalty. Al-Farra’ said: Ibn Jurayj and Qatadah said: From the satisfaction with the matter of the pledge of allegiance on the condition that they would not flee. Muqatil said: From the dislike of the pledge of allegiance on the condition that they would fight with him to the death. Then He sent down tranquility upon them until they pledged allegiance. It was also said: Then He knew what was in their hearts of depression at the polytheists’ repulsion of them and the Prophet’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) vision of them not being seen, when he saw that he was entering the Kaaba, until the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: That was only a vision in a dream. Al-Siddiq said: There was no entry in it this year. Tranquility is reassurance and peace of mind regarding the truth of the promise. It was also said: Patience. And He rewarded them with an imminent conquest. Qatadah and Ibn Abi Layla said: The conquest of Khaybar. It was also said: The conquest of Mecca. It was read: And He gave them.
48:19: The Almighty’s saying: And much spoils they will take meaning the wealth of Khaybar. Khaybar had real estate and wealth, and was located between Al-Hudaybiyyah and Mecca. spoils according to this is a substitute for an imminent conquest and the waw is inserted. It was also said that and spoils of Persia and Rome.
48:20: The Almighty said: God has promised you many spoils that you will take. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: They are the spoils that will last until the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Zayd said: They are the spoils of Khaybar. And He hastened this for you meaning Khaybar, said Mujahid. Ibn Abbas said: He hastened the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah for you. And He withheld the hands of the people from you meaning the people of Mecca. He withheld them from you through the treaty. Qatada said: How were the hands of the Jews from Medina after the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out to Hudaybiyyah and Khaybar? This is the preferred choice of At-Tabari, because withholding the hands of the polytheists at Hudaybiyyah is mentioned in His statement: And it is He who withheld their hands from you. Ibn Abbas said: In withholding the hands of the people from you he means Uyaynah ibn Hisn Al-Fazari, Awf ibn Malik An-Nadri, and those who were with them, when they came to aid Khaybar while the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was besieging them. So God, the Almighty, cast the Lord into their hearts and withheld them from the Muslims. And that it may be a sign for the believers meaning and that it may be Their defeat and your safety is a sign for the believers, so they know that God protects them when they are present and when they are absent. It was also said: And that their hands being restrained from you will be a sign for the believers. It was also said: That is, and that this which He hastened for you will be a sign for the believers of your truthfulness when you promised them that they would attain it. The waw in and that it will be is inserted according to the Kufians. The Basrans said: It is a conjunction to an implied word, that is, and that He restrains the hands of the people from you so that you may thank Him and so that it will be a sign for the believers. And guide you to a straight path meaning that He increases your guidance, or makes you steadfast on guidance.
48:21: The Almighty said: And another another is connected to this, meaning He hastened for you these spoils and other spoils that you were not able to obtain, God has encompassed them. Ibn Abbas said: They are the conquests that were opened to the Muslims, such as the lands of Persia and Rome, and everything that the Muslims conquered, and this is the saying of Al-Hasan, Muqatil, and Ibn Abi Layla. Also from Ibn Abbas, Ad-Dahhak, Ibn Zayd, and Ibn Ishaq: It is Khaybar, which God promised to His Prophet before he conquered it, and they did not hope for it until God informed them of it. Also from Al-Hasan and Qatada: It is the conquest of Mecca. Ikrimah said: Hunayn, because he said: you were not able to obtain it. This indicates that an attempt was made for it and the attainment of the desired goal was missed immediately, as was the case in Mecca. Al-Qushayri said this. Mujahid said: It is what will be until the Day of Resurrection. The meaning of God has encompassed them is that if you are not able to obtain them immediately, then they are withheld from you and will not be missed. It was said: God has encompassed them He knew that it would happen. For you, as He said: And that God has encompassed all things in knowledge (al-Talaq 65:12), and it was said: God has preserved it for you, so that He may open it for you and God is over all things competent.
48:22: The Almighty said: And if those who disbelieve fight you, they will turn their backs. Qatada said: He means the disbelievers of Quraysh at Al-Hudaybiyyah. It was said: And if those who disbelieve fight you Ghatafan and Asad and those who wanted to support the people of Khaybar, the tables would have turned against them. Then they will find neither protector nor helper.
48:23: The Almighty’s saying: The way of God which has already been in effect means God’s way and His past customs, the victory of His friends over His enemies. Sunnah is in the accusative case as a source, and it was said: The way of God means like the way of God, and the way is the method and conduct. He said: Do not be dismayed by the way you have led, for the first to be satisfied is the one who leads it. Sunnah is also a type of date from Medina. And you will not find any change in the way of God.
48:24: The Almighty said: And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Mecca - that is, Al-Hudaybiyyah, after He had given you victory over them. Yazid bin Harun narrated: Hammad bin Salamah told us on the authority of Thabit on the authority of Anas: Eighty men from the people of Mecca descended upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Mount At-Tan'im, armed, intending to surprise the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions. We captured them peacefully and spared them. Then God Almighty revealed: And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Mecca after He had given you victory over them. Abdullah bin Mughaffal Al-Muzani said: We were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, at Al-Hudaybiyyah at the base of the tree that God mentioned in the Qur'an. While we were like that, thirty young men armed came out to us and rose up in our faces. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, invoked God against them, and God took away their sight. He said: Come, Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Have you come under the covenant of anyone, or has anyone given you security? They said: No, by God. So he released them, and God, the Most High, revealed: And it is He who has restrained their hands from you. Ibn Hisham reported on the authority of Wakee’: “There had come from the Quraysh about seventy or eighty men to attack the Muslims and seize the opportunity to attack them. The Muslims became aware of them and took them as prisoners. This was while the ambassadors were walking among them in the peace treaty, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, released them. They are the ones called Al-Anqa’, and among them were Mu’awiyah and his father. Mujahid said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was excused from performing Umrah, when his companions took some people from the Sacred Sanctuary by surprise. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent them out, and that was the victory in the valley of Mecca.” Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that a man from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Zunaym, climbed the pass of Al-Hudaybiyyah, and the polytheists shot him with an arrow and killed him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent cavalry, and they brought twelve horsemen from the infidels. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Do you have a covenant with me? They said: No. So he sent them, and it was revealed. Ibn Abza and Al-Kalbi said: They are the people of Al-Hudaybiyyah. God held their hands back from the Muslims until the peace treaty was concluded. They had all gone out and headed towards the Muslims, and the Muslims’ hands were held back from them. It was mentioned previously that Khalid bin Al-Walid was in the cavalry of the polytheists. Al-Qushayri said: This is a narration, and the correct version is that he was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, at that time. Salamah bin Al-Akwa’ said: They were in the matter of the peace treaty when Abu Sufyan came, and the valley was moving with men and weapons. He said: So I came with six of the polytheists, driving them armed, and they did not possess any power to benefit or harm themselves. I brought them to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Umar had said on the way: O Messenger of God, we come to a people in a party and we do not have any weapons or a trotter? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent to Medina by way of the road, and they brought him every weapon and mount that was in it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was informed that Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl had come out to you with five hundred horsemen. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Khalid ibn al-Walid, This is your cousin who has come to you with five hundred. Khalid said, I am the sword of God and the sword of His Messenger. On that day, he was called the Sword of God. He went out with horses and defeated the infidels and pushed them back to the walls of Mecca. This narration is more authentic. There was fighting between them with stones, and it was said with arrows and nails. It was said that what was meant by withholding the hand was that it was stipulated in the letter that whoever came to us from them would be returned to them. Some people from Mecca came out as Muslims and feared that the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, would return them to the polytheists, so they went to the coast, including Abu Basir. They began to raid the infidels and seize their caravans, until the leaders of Quraysh came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said, Get them with you so that we may be safe. He did so. It was said that Ghatafan and Asad intended to prevent the Muslims from the Jews of Khaybar because they were their allies. So God prevented them from that, so it is the cessation of the hand in the valley of Mecca There are two opinions on this: One of them means Mecca, the second: Al-Hudaybiyyah, because some of it is added to the sanctuary. Al-Mawardi said: And in His statement: after He had given you victory over them with the conquest of Mecca, and this was revealed after the conquest of Mecca, and in it is evidence that Mecca was conquered by peace, because the Almighty said: He restrained their hands from you and your hands from them. I said: The correct view is that this verse was revealed at Al-Hudaybiyyah before the conquest of Mecca, according to what we have presented from the people of interpretation from the Companions and the Followers. Al-Tirmidhi narrated: Abd bin Hamid told us, Sulayman bin Harb told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas: Eighty men descended upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions from Mount At-Tan’im at the time of the dawn prayer, intending to kill him. They seized them, but the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, freed them, and God Almighty revealed: And it is He who has restrained their hands from you and your hands from them. Abu ‘Eesa said: This is a good and authentic hadith, and it has been mentioned previously. As for the conquest of Mecca, what the reports indicate is that it was conquered by force, and we have already discussed this in Hajj and elsewhere: And God is Seeing of what you do.
48:25: The Almighty said: They are the ones who disbelieved and prevented you from the Sacred Mosque and the offering, withheld from reaching its destination. There are three issues in this: First: The Almighty’s statement: They are the ones who disbelieved meaning the Quraysh. They prevented you from entering the Sacred Mosque in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) entered into ihram with his companions for Umrah, and they prevented the sacrificial animals and prevented them from reaching their destination. This is what they did not believe in, but their previous pride and the fanaticism of the Age of Ignorance led them to do what they did not believe to be religious, so God rebuked them for that and threatened them with it, and He brought comfort to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with His explanation and His promise. The second: The Almighty’s saying: And the sacrificial offering is withheld, meaning imprisoned, and it was said that it was stopped. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ said: Al-Jawhari collected it: Akkafahu means to detain and stop it, he keeps it and keeps it, ikfahu and ikfahu is from it. And from it is the saying of the Almighty: And the sacrificial offering is withheld, it is said: What kept you from such and such? And from it is the seclusion in the mosque, which is confinement. That it reaches its place, meaning they granted it to it. Al-Farra’ said: Al-Shafi’i, may God be pleased with him, said: The sanctuary, and Abu Hanifa, may God be pleased with him, said the same. The place of the one who is prevented is the sanctuary, and the place with a kasra on the ha’: the limit of the thing, and with a fatha: it is the place where people stop. The sacrificial offering was seventy camels, but God, by His grace, has a place for it. The scholars differed on this, as was explained previously in Al-Baqarah, when God Almighty said: And if you are prevented (al-Baqarah 2:196). And what we mentioned is correct. And in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, he said: We slaughtered with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the year Al-Hudaibiyah: The camel was sacrificed by seven, and the cow was sacrificed by seven. On his authority, he said: We participated with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Hajj and Umrah, each seven in a camel. A man said to Jabir: Is there a share in the camel as is shared in the camel? He said: It is nothing but a camel. Jabir was present at Al-Hudaibiyah and said: We slaughtered seventy camels on that day, seven of us sharing in a camel. In Al-Bukhari, it is narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: We went out with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to perform Umrah, and the infidels of Quraysh prevented us from reaching the House, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) slaughtered a camel and shaved his head. It was said: The one who shaved his head on that day was Khurash ibn Umayyah ibn Abi Al-Ays Al-Khuza’i. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered the Muslims to slaughter and then to become halal. They did so after some hesitation, and one of them angered the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Umm Salamah said to him: If you slaughter, they will slaughter. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) slaughtered a gift and they slaughtered with his slaughter. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) shaved his head and prayed for those who shaved and those who cut their hair. Once, Ka’b ibn Ujrah saw lice falling on his face, so he said: Do your lice bother you? He said: Yes. So he ordered him to shave while he was at Al-Hudaibiyah. Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Al-Daraqutni, and it has been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And the guidance. Guidance and guidance are two dialects. It was read until the guidance reaches its place with a light stress and a heavy stress. The singular is hadiya a gift. This has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah as well. It is connected to the kaf and the mim of saddukum and ma’kufan is a state. The position of an in His saying: that it reaches its place is accusative based on the assumption that it is based on saddukum, meaning they prevented you and prevented the guidance from reaching it. It is permissible for it to be an object for it, as if he said: And they prevented the guidance out of dislike for it to reach its place. Abu Ali: It is not correct to carry it on ‘akf, because we do not know that ’akf came transitive. The coming of ma’kufan in the verse may be carried on the meaning, as if since it was confinement, the meaning was carried on that, just as the obscenity was carried on the meaning of confinement, so it was transitive with ‘ila. If it is carried on that, its position is accusative based on the analogy of what Sibawayh said, and genitive based on the analogy of what Al-Khalil said, or it is an object for it, as if he said: Imprisoned for fear that it would reach its destination, and it is permissible to estimate the accusative in that because about came before, so it is as if he said: And they prevented you from the Sacred Mosque, and they prevented the sacrificial offering from reaching its destination. Similar to it is what Sibawayh narrated on the authority of Yunus 10:I passed by a man, Zaid and Amr, so he omitted the accusative because he mentioned it before. The Almighty said: And had it not been for believing men and believing women whom you did not know, lest you trample them and there befall you on their part a disgrace without knowledge. There are three issues in this: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And had it not been for believing men meaning the weak believers in Mecca among the unbelievers, such as Salamah ibn Hisham, Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi’ah, Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl, and their likes, you did not know them meaning you did not recognize them, and it was said you did not know that they were believers, that you would trample them by killing and striking them. It is said: I trampled the people, meaning I struck them. That may be in the nominative case as a substitute for men and women, as if he said, And had it not been for your trampling believing men and believing women, and it may be in the accusative case as a substitute for the ha’ and the mim in you learned them, so the meaning would be: you did not know their trampling, which is in both cases a substitute for inclusion, and you did not know them is an attribute of men and women, and the answer to had it not been is omitted, and the meaning is: And had you trampled believing men and believing women whom you did not know, God would have given you permission to enter Mecca, and He would have given you power over them. But We protected whoever concealed his faith in it. Ad-Dahhak said: Were it not for the believing men and believing women in the loins of the infidels and the wombs of their women, you would not have known that you would trample their fathers and destroy their children. The second: The Almighty’s saying: And a disgrace befalls you on their part without your knowledge. Disgrace is a defect and is derived from arr, which means scabies. That is, the polytheists say: They have killed the people of their religion. It was said: The meaning is that you will be afflicted by their killing with something for which you are required to pay the expiation for accidental killing, because God Almighty only made it obligatory for the killer of a believer in the land of war if he had not emigrated from it and his faith was not known to him to pay the expiation without the blood money in His saying: He was from a people hostile to you and he was a believer, then the freeing of a believing slave (An-Nisa’: 92). This was said by Al-Kalbi, Muqatil, and others. The discussion of it has already been mentioned in An-Nisa’. Ibn Zayd said: Disgrace is a sin. Al-Jawhari and Ibn Ishaq said: The penalty of blood money. Qatrab: severity. It was also said: general. Third: The Almighty’s statement: without knowledge is a preference for the Companions and a statement about their noble characteristic of being chaste from sin and infallible from transgression, even if they had harmed someone in this way it would have been unintentional. This is like the ant’s description of the soldiers of Solomon, peace be upon him, in its statement: Solomon and his soldiers will crush you while they perceive not (al-Naml 27:18). The Almighty’s saying: That God may admit into His mercy whom He wills, even if they were to separate. There are four issues in this: The first: The Almighty’s saying: That God may admit into His mercy whom He wills, if you were to separate. The lām in li-dkhul is connected to something omitted, meaning that if you killed them, God would admit them into His mercy. It is permissible for it to be connected to faith and not apply to believing men without believing women, nor to believing women without believing men, because all enter into mercy. It was said: The meaning is that God did not permit you to fight the polytheists so that whoever among the people of Mecca had decided to become Muslim would become Muslim after the peace treaty would become Muslim. And likewise, many of them became Muslim and their Islam was good, and they entered into His mercy, meaning His Paradise. Second: The Almighty’s saying: If you were to separate means if they were to be distinguished, as stated by Al-Qutbi. It was also said: If they were to disperse, as stated by Al-Kalbi. It was also said: If the believers were to separate from the unbelievers, the unbelievers would be punished by the sword, as stated by Ad-Dahhak. But God defends the unbelievers by means of the believers. Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: I asked the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, about this verse: If you were to separate, We would punish those who disbelieved, so he said: They are the polytheists from the ancestors of the Prophet of God and those who came after them and during their time who were in their loins a people of believers, so if the believers were to separate from the loins of the unbelievers, God, the Almighty, would punish the unbelievers with a painful punishment. Third: This verse is evidence of the disbeliever’s respect for the believer’s sanctity, as it is not possible to harm a disbeliever except by harming a believer. Abu Zayd said: I said to Ibn al-Qasim: Tell me, if a group of polytheists were in one of their fortresses, and the Muslims besieged them and among them were some Muslim prisoners in their hands, should this fortress be burned or not? He said: I heard Malik when he was asked about a group of polytheists in their mounts: Should we throw fire at the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) while they had prisoners in their mounts? He said: Malik said: I do not see that, because God Almighty said to the people of Mecca: If they had moved away, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment. Likewise, if a disbeliever shields himself with a Muslim, it is not permissible to shoot him. If someone does that and kills a Muslim, then he must pay blood money and expiation. If they did not know, then there is no blood money or expiation. This is because if they knew, then they do not have the right to shoot.
