If they did it, then they become accidental killers, and their blood money is due from their relatives. If they did not know, then they are allowed to shoot. If the action is permitted, it is not permissible for them to remain in it as a consequence. Ibn al-Arabi said: A group said that its meaning is if they moved away from the wombs of women and the loins of men. This is weak, because one who is in the loins or in the abdomen cannot be penetrated and no shame is inflicted on him. God Almighty has stated clearly, saying: And were it not for believing men and believing women whom you did not know, that you might trample them. This does not apply to one who is in the womb of a woman and the loins of men, but rather applies to the likes of al-Walid ibn al-Walid, Salamah ibn Hisham, and Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi’ah. And Abu Jandal bin Suhayl, and Malik also said: We besieged the city of the Romans and their water was withheld, so they would bring down the prisoners to draw water for them, and no one would be able to shoot arrows at them, so the water would be obtained for them without our consent. Abu Hanifa and his companions and al-Thawri permitted shooting at the fortresses of the polytheists even if there were Muslim prisoners and their children among them, and if the infidels used a Muslim child as a shield, they would shoot at the polytheist, and if one of the Muslims was injured, there is no blood money or expiation for that. Al-Thawri said: There is no expiation or blood money for that. Al-Shafi’i said with our statement: This is clear, because access to what is permissible when forbidden is not permissible, especially with the soul of a Muslim, so there is no statement except what Malik, may God be pleased with him, said, and God knows best. I said: The shield may be permissible, and there is no difference in it, God willing, if the benefit is absolutely necessary and definitive. The meaning of it being necessary is that the infidels cannot be reached except by killing the shield. The meaning of it being definitive is that it is definitive for the entire nation, so that killing the shield will benefit all Muslims. If that is not done, the infidels will kill the shield and seize control of the entire nation. The meaning of it being definitive is that that benefit is definitely achieved by killing the shield. Our scholars said: There should be no difference in considering this benefit with these restrictions, because the assumption is that the shield is definitely killed, either by the hands of the enemy, in which case the great corruption will occur, which is the enemy seizing control of all Muslims, or by the hands of the Muslims, in which case the enemy will perish and all Muslims will be saved. It is not possible for a rational person to say: The shield should not be killed in this situation in any way, because it would entail the loss of the shield, Islam, and the Muslims. However, since this benefit is not free of corruption, the soul of anyone who does not consider it deeply is repelled by it, because that corruption, in relation to what results from it, is nothing or almost nothing, and God knows best. Fourth: The reading of the general public is law taza’ilu except for Abu Haywah, who read taza’ilu which is like taza’ilu in meaning, and taza’il means to be different, and taza’ilu is tafa’ilu, from zalat, and it was said: it is tafa’ilu We would have punished those who disbelieved It was said: the lam is an answer to two statements, one of them is lawla rijal and the second is law taza’ilu It was said that the answer to lawla is deleted, and it was mentioned before, law taza’ilu is the beginning of a statement.
48:26: God Almighty says: “When those who disbelieved put into their hearts arrogance - the arrogance of the times of ignorance - then God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers and imposed upon them the word of righteousness. And they were most worthy of it and most deserving of it. And God is Knowing of all things.” The agent in idh is the Almighty’s saying: We would have punished them meaning We would have punished them because they did this, or an implied verb, the meaning of which is: And remember al-ha’iyah protection which is arrogance. It is said: I was protected from such-and-such with arrogance with emphasis and mahmiyah if you were averse to it and it was inside you and arrogant to do it, from it the saying of al-Mutalammiss: I am one of them, and my honor is their honor, just as the one with the nose protects his nose from being scratched. That is, to prevent. Al-Zuhri said: Their pride in acknowledging the Prophet’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) message and in opening with In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful protected them, and they were prevented from entering Mecca. The one who refused to write In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, and Muhammad is the Messenger of God was Suhayl ibn Amr, as mentioned above. Ibn Bahr said: Their pride was driven by their fanaticism for their gods that they worshipped besides God, and their pride in worshipping anything other than them. It was said: The pride of the Age of Ignorance because they said: They killed our sons and brothers, then they enter our homes, and Al-Lat and Al-Uzza will never enter them. So God sent down His tranquility meaning reassurance and dignity upon His Messenger and upon the believers. It was said: He made them steadfast in contentment and submission, and did not enter their hearts what entered the hearts of those of pride. And He made them adhere to the word of piety. It was said: There is no god but God. It was narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka’b, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It is the saying of Ali, Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, Amr ibn Maymun, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ikrimah, Ad-Dahhak, Salamah ibn Kuhayl, Ubayd ibn Umair, Talhah ibn Musarrif, Ar-Rabi’, As-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd. It was also said by Ata’ Al-Khurasani, who added, Muhammad is the Messenger of God. It was also narrated by Ali and Ibn Umar: It is There is no god but God, and God is Greatest. Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah and Mujahid also said: It is “There is no god but God alone, with no partner. His is the kingdom and His is the praise, and He is over all things omnipotent.” Az-Zuhri said: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful,” meaning that the polytheists did not acknowledge this statement, so God singled it out for the believers. The word of piety is that by which one protects oneself from polytheism. It was also narrated by Mujahid that the word of piety is sincerity, and they were more deserving of it and more worthy of it, meaning more deserving of it than the disbelievers of Mecca, because God Almighty chose them for His religion and the company of His Prophet. And God was with all… Something knowledgeable.
48:27: Qatada said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw in a dream that he would enter Mecca in this manner. When he made peace with the Quraysh at Hudaybiyyah, the hypocrites doubted until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said that he would enter Mecca. Then God Almighty revealed: God has truly fulfilled the vision of His Messenger, so He informed them that they would enter in a year other than that, and that his vision, may God bless him and grant him peace, was true. It was said that Abu Bakr was the one who said that the dream was not specified by a time, and that he would enter. It was narrated that the vision was at Hudaybiyyah, and that the vision of the prophets is true, and the vision is one of the aspects of revelation to the prophets. You will enter Abu Bakr in the next year the Sacred Mosque, God willing. Ibn Kaysan said: It is a narration of what was said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his dream. He was addressed in his dream with what was customary, so God informed about His Messenger that he said, and for this reason he made an exception. He was disciplined with the discipline of God Almighty where He said: And never say of anything, ‘I will do that tomorrow,’ * except that “God wills (al-Kahf 18:23). It was said: God addressed His servants with what He loves them to say, as He said: And never say of anything, ‘Indeed, I will do that tomorrow,’ except, ‘If God wills.’ It was said: He made an exception in what He knows so that the creation may be excepted in what they do not know, as Tha’lab said. It was said that God knew that He would kill some of those who were with Him at Al-Hudaibiyah, so the exception was made for this meaning, as Al-Husayn ibn Al-Fadl said. It was said: The exception from safe refers to addressing the servants according to what is customary. It was said: The meaning of God willing is if God commands you to enter. It was said: That is, if God makes it easy. It was said: God willing means as God wills. Abu Ubaidah said: If has the meaning of when, that is, if God wills, as God Almighty says: Fear God and give up what remains of interest, if you are believers. (al-Baqarah 2:278), that is, if you were. There is some distance in it, because when is in the past tense of the verb, and when is in the future, and this entry In the future, he promised them entry into the Sacred Mosque and made it conditional upon their will, and that was in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah. He informed his companions of that and they were happy. Then that was delayed from the year in which they had eaten, and that upset them and was difficult for them, so he made peace with them and returned. Then God gave permission in the following year, so God revealed: God has truly fulfilled the vision of His Messenger in truth. And it was said to him in a dream: You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, God willing. So he narrated in the revelation what was said to him in the dream. So there is no doubt here, as some of them claimed that the exception indicates doubt, and God Almighty does not doubt, and you will surely enter is confirmation, so how can doubt if be in the sense of if “safe” that is, from the enemy, shaving your heads and cutting your hair. Shaving and cutting are both for men, and that is why the masculine is more prevalent than the feminine, and shaving is better, and women have only cutting their hair. This has been said in Al-Baqarah, and in the Sahih that Muawiyah took from the hair of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, at Al-Marwah, and this was during the Umrah, not the Hajj, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, during his Hajj does not… You fear the one who shaves and trims his hair, and the meaning is: not afraid). So he knew what you did not know meaning he knew what good and righteousness there was in delaying the entry that you did not know, and that is because when he, peace be upon him, returned, he went from there to Khaybar and conquered it, and returned with the wealth of Khaybar and took from the equipment and strength many times what he had in that year, and he came to Mecca with preparation, strength, and equipment many times that. Al-Kalbi said: That is, He knew that they had entered it a year ago, and you did not know about it. It was said: He knew that there were believing men and believing women in Mecca, whom you did not know. So He made a near victory before that, that is, before the vision of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the conquest of Khaybar. This was said by Ibn Zayd and Al-Dahhak. It was also said: The conquest of Mecca. Mujahid said: It is the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, and most of the commentators disagreed. Al-Zuhri said: What God opened in Islam was greater than the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, because fighting only took place when people met. When there was a truce, the war laid down its burdens and people felt safe with each other. They met and negotiated, talked, and debated. No one spoke about Islam like what had been in Islam before that, and more. Evidence of that is that they were 1,400 on the day of Hudaybiyyah in the year 6, and after the year of Hudaybiyyah they were 10,000 in the year 8.
48:28: The Almighty says: It is He who has sent His Messenger meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religions meaning to make it superior to all religions. So, religion is a noun meaning a source, and the singular and plural forms are the same in it. It was said: meaning to make His Messenger prevail over all religions, meaning over the religion that He legislated with proof, then with the hand and the sword, and abrogated everything else. And sufficient is God as a witness witness is in the accusative case for explanation, and the ba’ is redundant, meaning God is sufficient as a witness for His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his testimony does not demonstrate the validity of his prophethood through miracles. It was said: witness for what he was sent with, because the infidels refused to write: This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of God, has agreed upon.
48:29: It contains five issues: The first: The Most High said: Muhammad is the Messenger of God. Muhammad and Messenger are its predicate. It was said that Muhammad is the subject and Messenger of God is his description. And those with him are in apposition to the subject and predicate in what follows it. So, in this estimation, one does not stop at Messenger of God. In the first, one stops at Messenger of God because his attributes, peace be upon him, are more than what his companions were described with. So Muhammad is the subject and Messenger of God is the predicate. And those with him is a second subject, and strong is its predicate and merciful is a second predicate. The attributes being in the group of the Prophet’s companions, peace and blessings be upon him, is more likely. Ibn Abbas said: The people of Al-Hudaybiyyah were harsh on the disbelievers, meaning harsh on them like a lion on its prey. It was said: What is meant by those with him are all the believers. Compassionate among themselves, meaning they have mercy on one another. It was said that they are sympathetic and affectionate. Al-Hasan read: Strong against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves in the accusative case as a state, as if he said: And those with him in their state of harshness against the disbelievers. And their compassion among themselves, And whoever does not believe in God and His Messenger - then indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers a Blaze. This is information about their frequent prayers, they seek bounty from God and approval. That is, they seek Paradise and the approval of God Almighty. The second: The Almighty’s saying: Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration. The mark is the sign, and there are two pronunciations for it: lengthening and shortening, meaning that the signs of praying at night and the signs of staying up late appear. In Sunan Ibn Majah, he said: Ismail bin Muhammad al-Talkhi told us, Thabit bin Musa Abu Yazid told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever prays a lot at night, his face will be beautiful during the day.’” Ibn al-Arabi said: Some people inserted it into the hadith of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, by mistake, and there is no mention of it from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, even a single letter. Ibn Wahb narrated from Malik, Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration, which is related to their foreheads being covered with earth when prostrating, and Saeed bin Jubayr said the same. In the authentic hadith, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he prayed on the morning of the twenty-first of Ramadan, and the mosque was covered and was on a trellis, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, left his prayer and on his forehead and nose were traces of water and mud.” Al-Hasan said: It is A whiteness that will be on the face on the Day of Resurrection. Saeed bin Jubair also said this. Al-Awfi narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Al-Zuhri also said this. In Sahih, it is narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, in which it says: “Until when God has finished judging between His servants and wants to bring out by His mercy whomever He wants from the people of Hell, He commands the angels to bring out from the Hellfire whoever did not associate anything with God, whom God wants to have mercy on, who says, ‘La ilaha illa God.’ They will recognize them in the Hellfire by the mark of their prostration. The Fire will consume the sons of Adam except the mark of prostration. God has forbidden the Fire to consume the mark of prostration.” Shahr bin Hawshab said: The place of prostration on their faces will be like the moon on a full moon. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: The mark in this world is a good appearance. Mujahid also said: It refers to humility and modesty. Mansour said: I asked Mujahid about the statement of God, Their mark is on their faces. Is it a mark between the eyes of a man? He said: No, perhaps there is between the eyes of a man the size of a goat’s knee, yet his heart is harder than stone! Rather, it is a light in their faces from humility. Ibn Jurayj said: It is dignity and splendor. Shamr ibn Atiyyah said: It is the yellowness of the face from standing in prayer at night. Al-Hasan said: If you saw them, you would think they were sick, but they are not sick. Ad-Dahhak said: It is not a mark on their faces, but it is the yellowness. Sufyan Ath-Thawri said: They pray at night, and when they wake up, that is seen in their faces. Its explanation is the statement of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever prays a lot at night, his face will be beautiful during the day. This has already been said previously. Ata’ Al-Khurasani said: This verse includes everyone who maintains the five daily prayers. Third: The Almighty’s saying: That is their example in the Torah and their example in the Gospel. Al-Farra’ said: There are two interpretations. If you wish, you can say that the meaning is that is their example in the Torah and in the Gospel also, like their example in the Qur’an, so the pause would be at the Gospel. If you wish, you can say: The rest of the statement is that is their example in the Torah. Then he began and said: And their example in the Gospel. Ibn Abbas and others said the same: They are two examples, one in the Torah and the other in the Gospel, so he pauses on this at the Torah. Mujahid said: It is one example, meaning that this is their description in the Torah and the Gospel, so he does not pause at the Torah on this, but pauses at the Gospel and begins: Like a plant that sends forth its shoot, meaning they are like a plant and its shoot means its young and offspring. Ibn Zayd and others said this. Muqatil said: It is a single plant, so if what comes after it comes forth, then it has sprung. Al-Jawhari said: The shoot of the plant and the plant is its young, and the plural is ashta’. And the plant has sprung, meaning it came out. Its edge. Al-Akhfash said in his statement its edge came out meaning its end. Al-Tha’labi narrated it on the authority of Al-Kisa’i. Al-Farra’ said: The crop has become branched, so it is branched if it comes out. The poet said: He brought forth the shore on the face of the earth and the branches of fruit from the trees. Glass: He brought forth its plant, meaning its vegetation. It was said that the plant is the thorn of the ear of corn, and the Arabs also call it: the safa, which is the thorn of the animal, said Qatrib. It was said that it is the ear of corn, so ten, nine, and eight ears of corn come out of the grain, said Al-Farra’, narrated by Al-Mawardi. Ibn Kathir and Ibn Dhakwan read shata’a with the ta’ open, and the rest made it quiescent. Anas, Nasr bin Asim, and Ibn Waththab read shata’a like his stick, and Al-Jahdary and Ibn Abi Ishaq read shata’a without a hamza, and all of them have dialects in them. This is a parable that God Almighty gave to the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, meaning that they would be few in number then increase and multiply. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, began to supplicate, he was weak, but he was answered one by one until his matter became strong, like a seed that appears weak after sowing, then becomes stronger one by one until its plants and offspring become thick. This was one of the most correct parables and most powerful statements. Qatada said: The parable of the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is that it is written in the Gospel that there will emerge from a people who will produce the growth of plants, who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. He supported him means he strengthened him, aided him, and strengthened him, meaning he strengthened the plant’s root. It was said the opposite, meaning he strengthened the plant’s root. The general reading is He supported him with a long vowel. Ibn Dhakwan, Abu Haywah, and Hamid ibn Qays read He supported him with a short vowel, like his verb. What is right is long. Imru’ al-Qays said: In a curve, the lost one has been supported by its plants, which have brought about victorious armies and have disappointed. And it stood firm on its stem on the branch on which it stands, so it becomes its stem. Stem is the plural of stalk. The farmers delight means that this crop delights its farmers. It is an example, as we have explained. The crop is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the shore is his companions. They were few and then became many, and weak and then became strong. This was said by Ad-Dahhak and others. To enrage the disbelievers through them. The lam is related to something omitted, meaning that God did this to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions to enrage the disbelievers through them. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: God has promised those who believe meaning God has promised those who are with Muhammad, and they are the believers whose deeds are righteous from them forgiveness and a great reward meaning an unending reward, which is Paradise. The word min in His saying from them is not a specification for some of the Companions without others, but rather it is a general and generic word, like the Almighty’s saying: So avoid the uncleanness of idols (al-Hajj 22:30). It is not intended to be specific, but rather it refers to the type, meaning avoid the uncleanness of the type of idols, since uncleanness occurs from various types, including adultery, usury, drinking alcohol, and lying. So He included min to indicate the type, and likewise minhum meaning from this type. The companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, may be singled out with the promise of forgiveness as a preference for them, and God promised forgiveness to all of the believers. In the verse there is another answer, which is that min emphasizes the statement, and the meaning is that God promised them all forgiveness and a great reward, so it follows the example of the Arab saying: I cut a shirt from the garment, meaning I cut the entire garment into a shirt. And min did not divide anything, and this is witnessed in the Qur’an: And We send down from the Qur’an that which is a healing (al-Isra’ 17:82). Its meaning is, We send down the Qur’an as a healing, because every letter of it heals, and healing is not specific to some of it without others. However, some of the linguists say: min is a generic term, meaning We send down healing from the same type as the Qur’an, and from the side of the Qur’an, and from the side of the Qur’an. Zuhair said: Is it true that Damna did not speak? He wanted to know from the side of Umm Awfa Damna, or from its houses Damna, and the other said: Brother Raghib gives her and asks her, but he refuses to be wronged by Al-Nawfal Al-Zafar From did not divide anything, as the goal was to reject injustice because he is Nawfal Zafar, and Nawfal is the one who gives a lot, and Zafar is: the one who carries burdens and believes in people. Fifth: Abu Urwah Al-Zubayr, from the descendants of Al-Zubayr, narrated: We were with Malik bin Anas, and they mentioned a man who was criticizing the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Malik recited this verse: Muhammad is the Messenger of God and those with him, until he reached: He delights the farmers in order to enrage the disbelievers with them. Malik said: Whoever among the people wakes up in the morning with anger in his heart against one of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then this verse has affected him. Al-Khatib Abu Bakr mentioned this. I said: Malik did well in his statement and was correct in his interpretation. Whoever denies one of them or criticizes him in his narration has rejected God, Lord of the Worlds, and has invalidated the laws of the Muslims. God Almighty said: Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and those with him are strong against the disbelievers (48:18), and He said: God was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree (48:18), and other verses that included praise for them and testifying to their truthfulness and success. God Almighty said: Men who have been true to what they pledged to God (33:23), and He said: To the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their properties, seeking bounty from God and approval (59:8), and then the Almighty said: And those who were established in the home and in faith before them (59:9), and all of this is from His knowledge, Blessed and Exalted be He, of their condition and the outcome of their affair, and “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the best of people.” My generation and those who follow them, and he said: Do not revile my companions, for if one of you were to spend gold equivalent to Mount Uhud, he would not attain the level of one of them, nor even half of it, both of them were narrated by al-Bukhari. In another hadith: If one of you were to spend what is on the earth, he would not attain the level of one of them, nor even half of it, Abu Ubaid said: Its meaning is that he would not attain the level of one of them if he gave charity, nor even half of it. So half is the half here, and likewise a tenth is called a tenth, a fifth a fifth, a ninth a ninth, an eighth a precious, a seventh a seventh, a sixth a sixth, a quarter a quarter, and the Arabs did not say a third a third. In al-Bazzar, on the authority of Jabir, with a sound chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Indeed, God chose my companions over all the worlds, except for the prophets and messengers, and He chose for me four of my companions, meaning Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman, and made them my companions,” and he said: Among my companions there is goodness, and Uwaim ibn Sa’idah narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Indeed, God Almighty chose me and chose my companions, and made for me from among them ministers, brothers, and in-laws. So whoever reviles them “Upon him is the curse of God, the angels, and all of mankind, and God will not accept from him on the Day of Resurrection any ransom or compensation.” There are many hadiths with this meaning, so beware of falling into the trap of any of them, as did the one who attacked the religion and said: The two Mu’awwidhat are not from the Qur’an. There is no authentic hadith from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) confirming them and including them in the revelation except from ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir. ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir is weak and no one else agreed with him on it, so his narration is rejected. This is a refutation of what we mentioned from the Qur’an and Sunnah, and a nullification of what the Companions transmitted to us from the religion. ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir ibn ‘Isa al-Juhani is among those who narrated to us the Shari’ah in the two Sahihs of al-Bukhari and Muslim and others. God praised them, described them, commended them, and promised them forgiveness and a great reward. Whoever attributes a lie to him or to one of the Companions is outside the Shari’ah, invalidating the Qur’an, and attacking the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Whenever one of them attributes a lie, he has insulted him, because there is no shame or defect greater than lying after disbelief in God. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cursed whoever insulted his companions. The one who belies the youngest of them, and there is no young one among them, is included in the curse of God, which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, bore witness to, and which was imposed on everyone who insulted one of his companions or slandered him. On the authority of Umar ibn Habib, he said: I attended the assembly of Harun al-Rashid, and an issue arose that was disputed among those present, and their voices were raised. Some of them used as evidence a hadith narrated by Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Some of them raised the hadith, and the defense and argument increased until some of them said: This hadith is not acceptable on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, because Abu Hurayrah is one of them in what he narrates. They declared his denial, and I saw that al-Rashid had taken their side and supported their statement, so I said: The hadith is authentic on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Hurayrah is authentic in his transmission and truthful in what he narrates on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and others. Al-Rashid looked at me angrily, and I got up from the assembly and went back to my house. I did not stay long until it was said: The postmaster is at the door. He entered and said to me: Answer the emir. The believers answer the questioner, and embalm and shroud! So I said: O God, You know that I defended the companion of Your Prophet, and I respected Your Prophet so that his companions would not be slandered, so save me from him. So I was brought to Rashid while he was sitting on a golden chair, his arms uncovered, with a sword in his hand and a mat in his hands. When he saw me, he said to me: O Omar bin Habib, no one has ever responded to and rebuffed my words with the same response you gave me! So I said: O Commander of the Faithful, what I said and argued about contains contempt for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and what he brought. If his companions are like those who slander him, then the Shariah is invalid, and the obligations and rulings on fasting, prayer, divorce, marriage, and the prescribed punishments are all rejected and not accepted! So he came to his senses and said: You have revived me, O Omar bin Habib, may God revive you. And he ordered that I be given ten thousand dirhams. I said: The Companions are all just, the saints of God Almighty and His chosen ones, and the best of His creation after His prophets and messengers. This is the doctrine of the people of the Sunnah, and what the group of imams of this nation are upon. A group who do not care about them have gone so far as to say that the state of the Companions is like the state of others, so it is necessary to investigate their justice. Some of them differentiated between their state at the beginning of the matter and said: They were just at that time, then conditions changed for them and wars and bloodshed appeared among them, so it is necessary to investigate. This is rejected, because the best of the Companions and their virtuous ones, such as Ali, Talhah, Al-Zubayr and others, may God be pleased with them, are among those whom God praised, purified, was pleased with, and satisfied with, and promised them Paradise with His Almighty saying: Forgiveness and a great reward. And especially the ten who were certain of Paradise by the Messenger’s informing them, they are the role models, despite their knowledge of many of the tribulations and matters that befell them after their Prophet by informing them of that. This does not diminish their status and virtue, because those matters were based on ijtihad, and every ijtihadist is correct, and it will come. The discussion of these matters will be explained in Surat Al-Hujurat, God willing.
49:1: Meccan by consensus and it has eighteen verses There are three issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, do not put yourselves forward before God and His Messenger. The scholars said: There was rudeness and bad manners among the Arabs in addressing the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and in calling people by nicknames, so the surah is about commanding good morals and observing good manners. Ad-Dahhak and Ya’qub Al-Hadrami read: Do not put yourselves forward with a fat-ha on the ta’ and the dal from to advance. The rest read: Do not put yourselves forward with a damma on the ta’ and a kasra on the dal from to correct. Their meanings are clear, that is, do not put your words or actions forward before God and the words and actions of His Messenger in matters of religion and worldly affairs. Whoever puts his words or actions forward before the Messenger, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, has put them forward before God, the Almighty, because the Messenger, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, only commands on the orders of God, the Almighty and Majestic. Second: There are six opinions regarding the reason for its revelation: First: What Al-Wahidi mentioned from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abi Malekah told me that Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told him: A group of Banu Tamim came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr said: The matter of Al-Qa’qa’ bin Ma’bad, and Umar said: The matter of Al-Aqra’ bin Habis, so Abu Bakr said: You only wanted to contradict me, and Umar said: You did not want to contradict you, so they argued until their voices rose, and the following was revealed regarding that: O you who have believed, do not precede God and His Messenger until His saying: And if they had been patient until you came out to them. Narrated by Al-Bukhari on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Al-Sabah, also mentioned by Al-Mahdawi. Second: What was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to appoint a man as his successor in Medina when he went to Khaybar, so Umar suggested another man to him, so the following was revealed: O you who have believed, do not put yourselves forward before God and His Messenger. Al-Mahdawi also mentioned it. Third: What Al-Mawardi mentioned on the authority of Al-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: That the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent twenty-four men from his companions to Banu Amir, and they killed them except for three who stayed behind and surrendered and returned to Madinah. They met two men from Banu Sulaym and asked them about their lineage. They said: We are from Banu Amir, because they are from Banu A’zz of Banu Sulaym, so they killed them. Then a group of Banu Sulaym came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: There is a treaty between us, and two men from among us have been killed. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, paid blood money for them with one hundred camels, and this verse was revealed to him regarding their killing of the two men. Qatada said: Some people used to say: If only it had been revealed about such-and-such, if only it had been revealed about such-and-such? This verse was revealed. Ibn Abbas: They were forbidden to speak before his speech. Mujahid: Do not slander God and His Messenger until God decides through the tongues of His Messenger. Al-Bukhari also mentioned it. Al-Hasan: It was revealed about a people who slaughtered before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed, so he ordered them to repeat the slaughter. Ibn Jurayj: Do not perform acts of obedience before their time, which God the Most High and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded. I said: These five later sayings were mentioned by Judge Abu Bakr Ibn Al-Arabi, and Al-Mawardi had listed them before him. The judge said: They are all correct and fall under the generality. God knows best what the reason for the verse was, and perhaps it was revealed without a reason, and God knows best. The judge said: If we say that it was revealed regarding the advancement of acts of worship beyond their times, then it is correct, because every act of worship that is timed by a time cannot be advanced beyond it, such as prayer, fasting, and Hajj, and that is by me. However, the scholars differed regarding zakat, because it was a financial act of worship and was required for an understood meaning, which is to fill the need of the poor, and because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, hastened the alms-tax of two years from Al-Abbas, and because it came from collecting the alms-tax on the day of Eid Al-Fitr so that it would be given to those entitled to it on the day of obligation, which is the day of Eid Al-Fitr. All of this necessitated the permissibility of advancing it for the year and for two days. If the beginning of the year comes and the nisab is in its state, then it takes its place, and if the beginning of the year comes and the nisab has changed, then it becomes clear that it is a voluntary alms-tax. Ashhab said: It is not permissible to advance it for a moment beyond the year, like prayer. It is as if he extended the origin of acts of worship and saw that it is one of the pillars of Islam, so he gave it its due. In the system and good arrangement, and the rest of our scholars saw that a slight precedence in it is permissible because it is excused in the Sharia, unlike a lot, and what Ashhab said is more correct, because the separation of a little from a lot in the principles of the Sharia is correct, but it has meanings that are specific to a little and not a lot, as in our issue, the day is like a month in it, and the month is like a year, so it is either a complete precedence as Abu Hanifa and Al-Shafi’i said, or preserving the worship at its appointed time as Ashhab said. Second: The Almighty’s saying: Do not put yourselves forward before God. This is a principle for not exposing oneself to the sayings of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and for obligating one to follow and emulate him. Likewise, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said during his illness: ‘Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.’ Aisha said to Hafsa, may God be pleased with them both: ‘Tell him that Abu Bakr is a man who is emotional, and when he takes your place, the people will not hear him because of his crying. So, tell Umar to lead the people in prayer.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘You are like the companions of Joseph. Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.’” The meaning of His saying the companions of Joseph is the temptation of turning away from what is permissible to what is impermissible. Perhaps those who use analogy might have used this verse as evidence, but this is false on their part, because what its evidence has been established does not mean that he should put himself forward. The evidence of the Qur’an and Sunnah has been established on the obligation to use analogy in the branches of Islamic law, so there is no putting himself forward. And fear God, meaning in the prohibited precedence. Indeed, God is Hearing of your words and Knowing of your actions. O you.
49:2: It contains six issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet. Al-Bukhari and Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: “Abdullah ibn Al-Zubayr told me that Al-Aqra’ ibn Habis came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr said: ‘O Messenger of God, appoint him over his people.’ Umar said: ‘Do not appoint him, O Messenger of God.’ They spoke in the presence of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, until their voices rose. Abu Bakr said to Umar: ‘You only wanted to contradict me.’ Umar said: ‘I did not want to contradict you.’ Then this verse was revealed: “O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet.” He said: After that, whenever Umar spoke in the presence of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would not listen to his words until he had asked him questions. He said: And Ibn Al-Zubayr did not mention his grandfather, meaning Abu Bakr. He said: This is a strange and hasan hadith. Some have narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abi Mulaykah as a mursal hadith, but it does not mention Abdullah ibn Al-Zubayr in it. I said: It is Al-Bukhari. He said: On the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah: The two good men were almost destroyed: Abu Bakr and Umar. They raised their voices in the presence of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when the caravan of Banu Tamim came to him. One of them pointed to Al-Aqra’ ibn Habis, the brother of Banu Majashi’, and the other pointed to another man. Nafi’ said: I do not remember his name. Abu Bakr said to Umar: You only wanted to contradict me. He said: I did not want to contradict you. So their voices were raised in that regard, and God Almighty revealed: O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet. Ibn Al-Zubayr said: After this verse, Umar did not hear the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until he asked him about it. He did not mention that from his father, meaning Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq. Al-Mahdawi mentioned on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him: His statement: Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet was revealed about us when I, Ja’far, and Zayd ibn Haritha raised our voices, disputing over the daughter of Hamza when Zayd brought her from Mecca. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled in favor of Ja’far because her maternal aunt was with him. This hadith has already been mentioned. In Al Imran and in the two Sahihs, “On the authority of Anas bin Malik: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, missed Thabit bin Qais, so a man said: O Messenger of God, I know for you his knowledge. So he went to him and found him sitting in his house with his head bowed. So he said to him: What is the matter with you? He said: Evil!” He raised his voice above the voice of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so his work was in vain and he was one of the people of Hellfire. So the man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him that he had said such and such. Moses said: So he returned to him a last time with great glad tidings, and he said: Go to him and tell him that you are not one of the people of Hellfire but one of the people of Paradise. This Thabit is Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas al-Khazraji, and his nickname is Abu Muhammad because of his son Muhammad, and it was said: Abu Abd al-Rahman. Three of his sons were killed on the day of al-Harrah: Muhammad, Yahya, and Abdullah. He was an eloquent orator and was known for that. He was called the orator of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, just as Hassan was called the poet of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When the delegation of Tamim came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they asked to boast, their orator stood up and boasted. Then Thabit ibn Qays stood up and gave an eloquent and powerful sermon and defeated them. Their poet, al-Aqra’ ibn Habis, stood up and recited: We have come to you so that people may know our virtue if they differ with us when mentioning noble deeds. We are the leaders of all people, and there is nothing in the land of Hijaz like Darim. We have the square in every raid that takes place in Najd or in the land of Tihamah. Hassan stood up and said: Bani Darm, do not be proud, for your pride will backfire when good deeds are mentioned. You are crazy about us, you are proud of us, while you are our servants and wet-nurse. In their verses. They said: Their orator is more eloquent than our orator, and their poet is more poetic than our poet. Their voices rose, so God revealed: Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet, nor be loud to him in speech. Ata’ al-Khurasani said: The daughter of Thabit ibn Qays told me: When the verse O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet was revealed, her father entered his house and closed the door. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, missed him, so he sent to him asking about him. He said: I am a man with a loud voice, and I fear that my deeds have been wasted. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You are not one of them, but you will live well and die well. He said: Then God revealed: Indeed, God does not love every arrogant boaster (Luqman 31:18). He closed his door and began to cry, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, missed him, so he sent to him and informed him. He said: O Messenger of God, I love beauty and I love to be the leader of my people. He said: You are not one of them, but you will live with praise, be killed as a martyr, and enter Paradise. She said: When the day of Yamamah came, he went out with Khalid ibn al-Walid to… Muslimah. When they met, they withdrew. Thabit and Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah, said: This is not how we fought with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then each of them dug a hole for himself, and they stood firm and fought until they were killed. Thabit was wearing a valuable shield that day. A Muslim man passed by and took it. While a Muslim man was asleep, Thabit came to him in his sleep and said: I give you a will, so beware of saying this is a dream and you will lose it. When I was killed yesterday, a Muslim man passed by me and took my shield. His house was at the farthest point of the people, and next to his tent was a horse, which was stretched out in length. A basket was placed over the shield, and on top of the basket was a saddle. Go to Khalid and tell him to send for my shield and take it. When you come to Medina to the Caliph of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, meaning Abu Bakr, tell him: I owe such and such a debt, and so-and-so, one of my slaves, is freed, and so-and-so is freed. The man went to Khalid and told him. He sent for the shield and brought it and told Abu Bakr about his dream, and he approved his will. He said: We do not know. It is not proven that anyone’s will was approved after his death. May God have mercy on him. Abu Omar mentioned it in Al-Isti’ab. The second: The Almighty’s saying: And do not speak to him aloud, meaning do not address him as O Muhammad or O Ahmad, but rather as O Prophet of God or O Messenger of God, out of respect for him. It was said that the hypocrites used to raise their voices in the presence of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so that the weak Muslims would follow their example, so the Muslims were forbidden from doing that. It was also said: Do not speak aloud to him, meaning do not speak aloud to him, as one says, He fell into his mouth, meaning, like the loudness of some of you to others, the kaf is the kaf of comparison in the accusative case, meaning do not speak aloud to him aloud like the loudness of some of you to others. This is evidence that they did not forbid speaking aloud in general so that it would be permissible for them to speak to him only in a whisper and in a low voice. Rather, they forbade a specific loudness restricted by a description, I mean the loudness described by resembling what they were accustomed to among themselves, which is the absence of consideration for the majesty of prophethood and the greatness of its status and the degradation of all other ranks, even if they are higher than its rank, lest your deeds be rendered worthless while you do not… You feel, that is, in order to frustrate, that is, to nullify. This is what the Basrans say. The Kufians say: That is, so that your deeds are not nullified. Third: The meaning of the verse is the command to honor and respect the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to lower your voices in his presence and when addressing him. That is, if you speak, you should not raise your voices beyond the level that his voice can reach, and you should lower your voices so that his speech is predominant over their speech, and his loudness is dazzling compared to your loudness, so that his superiority over you is clear, his precedence is obvious, and his distinction from your majority is like that of a piebald. Do not drown out his voice with your chatter and dazzle his speech with your uproar. In the reading of Ibn Mas`ud: Do not raise your voices. Some scholars disliked raising one’s voice at his grave, peace be upon him, and some scholars disliked raising one’s voice in the gatherings of scholars as an honor to them, since they are the inheritors of the prophets. Fourth: Judge Abu Bakr Ibn Al-Arabi said: The sanctity of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he was dead is like his sanctity when he was alive, and his words that are transmitted after his death are as exalted as his words heard from his own mouth. So when his words are recited, it is obligatory for everyone present not to raise their voices at them, nor to turn away from them, just as it was obligatory for him to do so in his assembly when he recited them. God Almighty has drawn attention to the permanence of the aforementioned sanctity over time in His saying: And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent (al-A’raf 7:204). His words, may God bless him and grant him peace, are from revelation, and they have the same wisdom as the Qur’an, except for some exceptional meanings that are explained in books of jurisprudence. Fifth: The purpose of raising the voice, nor speaking loudly, is not to be intended as contempt or disdain, because that is disbelief, and those being addressed are believers. Rather, the purpose is a voice that, in itself and what is heard from its tone, is not appropriate for what is feared by the great and respected by the great. One must lower it and return it to a level that inclines it to what is clearly commanded of honor and respect. The prohibition also did not include raising the voice in a way that would offend the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), which is what they did in war, or arguing with a stubborn person, or terrorizing an enemy, or something similar. In the hadith, it is narrated that he (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said to Al-Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib when the people were defeated on the day of Hunayn: Call out to the people. Al-Abbas had the loudest voice among people. It is narrated that a raid came to them one day, and Al-Abbas shouted: Oh, morning! So pregnant women miscarried because of the loudness of his voice. And in it, the Nabigha of Banu Ja’dah said: Abu Urwa's reprimand of wild animals if he feared they would mix with the sheep The narrators claimed that he used to drive away wild beasts from the sheep, and the beasts' bile would seep into his stomach. Sixth: Al-Zajjaj said: That your deeds may be rendered worthless. The meaning is that they may be rendered worthless, meaning that your deeds may be rendered worthless. The lam that is implied is the lam of becoming. His statement, That your deeds may be rendered worthless while you are not aware, does not require that a person disbelieve without knowing. Just as a disbeliever is not a believer except by choosing belief over disbelief, likewise a believer is not a disbeliever without intending disbelief or choosing it, by consensus. Likewise a disbeliever is not a disbeliever without knowing.
49:3: The Almighty said: Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of God meaning they lower their voices in his presence when they speak out of reverence for him, or when they speak to someone else in his presence out of reverence for him. Abu Hurairah said: When the verse Do not raise your voices was revealed, Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: By God, I will not raise my voice except like a secret brother. Sunayd mentioned that Abbad ibn al-Awwam told us on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr on the authority of Abu Salamah, who said: When the verse Do not put yourselves forward before God and His Messenger was revealed, Abu Bakr said: By Him who sent you with the truth, I will not speak to you after this except like a secret brother. Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr said: When the verse Do not raise your voices was revealed, Umar did not speak to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, after that and heard his speech until he asked him why he lowered his voices. Then the verse Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of God - those are the ones whose hearts God has tested for piety was revealed. Al-Farra’ said: meaning, he has made them pure for piety. Al-Akhfash said: meaning, he has singled them out. For piety, Ibn Abbas said: God tested their hearts with piety He purified them from every ugly thing, and put in their hearts the fear of God and piety. Omar, may God be pleased with him, said: He removed desires from their hearts, and the test is an active participle from the verb to test the leather until it expanded, so the meaning of God tested their hearts for piety is to expand and expand it for piety. According to the previous sayings: He tested their hearts and purified them, like your saying: I tested the silver, meaning I examined it until it was pure, so in the speech there is an omission that the speech indicates, which is sincerity. Abu Amr said: I have tested everything I have striven for, and he recited: The afflictions have come, their fatigue is evident. They have been tested and disturbed. They have prolonged their suffering. For them is forgiveness and a great reward.
49:4: God Almighty says: Indeed, those who call to you from behind the chambers, most of them do not reason. Mujahid and others said: It was revealed about the Bedouins of Banu Tamim. A delegation from them came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they entered the mosque and called out to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from behind his room: Come out to us, for praising us is an adornment and criticizing us is a disgrace. They were seventy men who offered their children as ransom, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had gone to bed for the afternoon. It was narrated that the one who called out was Al-Aqra’ ibn Habis, and that he was the one who said: My praise is an adornment, and my blame is a disgrace. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: That is God. Al-Tirmidhi mentioned it on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib as well. Zaid bin Arqam narrated that some people came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and some of them said to each other: Let us go to this man. If he is a prophet, we are the luckiest people to follow him, and if he is a king, we will live in his chamber. So they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they began to call out to him while he was in his room: O Muhammad, O Muhammad. Then God Almighty revealed this verse. It was said that they were from Banu Tamim. Muqatil said: They were nineteen: Qasim bin Asim, Al-Zubayr bin Badr, Al-Aqra’ bin Habis, Suwaid bin Hashim, Khalid bin Malik, Ata’ bin Habis, Al-Qa’qa’ bin Ma’bad, Waki’ bin Waki’, and Uyaynah bin Hisn, who was the obeyed fool. He was one of the pullers who pulled ten thousand qanats, meaning he followed him. His name was Hudhayfah, and he was called Uyaynah because of the blemish in his eyes. Abd Al-Razzaq mentioned this about Uyaynah: that he was the one about whom the verse was revealed: And do not obey one who has made us heedless. “And his heart turned away from our remembrance” (al-Kahf 18:28). And it has been mentioned at the end of Al-A’raf, from his saying to Omar, may God be pleased with him, what is sufficient, Al-Bukhari mentioned it, and it was narrated that they came at noon and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asleep, so they began to call out to him: O Muhammad, O Muhammad, come out to us, so he woke up and came out, and it was revealed, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked and he said: They are the rude ones of Banu Tamim, were it not that they are among the most vehement of people in fighting the one-eyed Antichrist, I would have called upon God to destroy them, and the rooms are the plural of room, like the rooms are the plural of room, and the darkness is the plural of darkness, and it was said: the rooms are the plural of stone, and the stone is the plural of room, so it is the plural of the plural, and there are two languages in it: the damma and the fatha of the jim. He said: When they saw us, our knees were clearly visible on the ground, not mixing seriousness with jest. Al-Hujra: a patch of land enclosed by a wall. A camel pen is called al-Hujra, and it is a verb meaning a passive participle. Abu Ja`far ibn al-Qa`qa` read al-Hujraat with a fat-ha on the jim because of the difficulty of the two dhammahs. Al-Hujraat was read with a sukoon on the jim to make it easier. The root of the word is prevention, and whatever you prevent someone from reaching, you have blocked it. Then it is possible that the one being called is part of the sentence, so he said: Most of them do not reason, meaning that those who call you are from a group of people who are mostly ignorant.
49:5: God Almighty says: “And if they had been patient until you came out to them, it would have been better for them. And God is Forgiving and Merciful.” That is, if they had waited for your departure, it would have been better for them in their religion and their worldly life. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not hide himself from the people except at times when he was busy with his own affairs, so disturbing him in that situation was bad manners. It was said: They came as intercessors for the captives of Banu Anbar, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, freed half of them and ransomed the other half. If they had been patient, he would have freed all of them without ransom. And God is Forgiving and Merciful.
49:6: It contains seven issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, if there comes to you a disobedient one with information… It was said that this verse was revealed about Al-Walid bin Uqbah bin Abi Mu’ayt, and the reason for that is what Saeed narrated on the authority of Qatada. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Al-Walid ibn Uqbah as a tax collector to Banu Al-Mustaliq. When they saw him, they approached him, and he was afraid of them, according to one narration: because of the grudge that had existed between him and them. He returned to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him that they had apostatized from Islam. The Prophet of Islam, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Khalid ibn Al-Walid and ordered him to verify and not to rush. Khalid set out until he reached them at night. He sent his spies, and when they arrived, they informed Khalid that they were adhering to Islam, and they heard their call to prayer and their prayers. When morning came, Khalid came to them and saw the truth of what they had said. He returned to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him. This verse was revealed. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: Deliberateness is from God, and haste is from Satan. In another narration: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him to Banu Al-Mustaliq after they had converted to Islam. When they heard of him, they rode to him. When he heard of them, he was afraid of them, so he returned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him that the people had intended to kill him and had withheld their tax. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, understood that they were about to attack him. While they were like that, their delegation came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, we heard about your Messenger, so we went out to him to honor him and pay him the charity we had been given. He kept returning, and we were informed that he was claiming to the Messenger of God that we went out to fight him, but by God, we did not go out for that. So God, the Most High, revealed this verse, and Al-Walid was called a fasiq, meaning a liar. Ibn Zayd, Muqatil, and Sahl ibn Abdullah said: The fasiq is the liar. Abu Al-Hasan Al-Warraq said: He is the one who announces the report. Ibn Tahir said: He who is not ashamed of God. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read fat-habatu from at-tattabah. The rest read fat-habitu from at-tabyeen, that you may strike meaning so that you may not strike. that is in the accusative case by dropping the preposition, a people with ignorance meaning with a mistake, so that you may become regretful of what you did for haste and lack of deliberation. Second: In this verse there is evidence for accepting the report of a single person if he is just, because it only commands verification when transmitting the report of a sinner. If someone’s sin is proven, his statement regarding the report is invalid by consensus, because the report is a trust and sin is an indication that invalidates it. The consensus has excluded from this what is related to claims and denial, and establishing a deliberate right over another, such as if he says: This is my slave, then his statement is accepted. And if he says: So-and-so has sent this as a sacrifice for you, then that is accepted. Likewise, the report of a disbeliever is accepted in such a case. Likewise, if he acknowledges a right over himself to another, then it is not invalid by consensus. As for establishing a right over another, Al-Shafi’i and others said: He is not a guardian in marriage. Abu Hanifa and Malik said: He is a guardian, because he is in charge of her property and is responsible for her private parts, like the just person. Even if he is sinful in his religion, his jealousy is abundant and with it he protects the harem and may spend money and preserve the sanctity. And if he is in charge of money, then marriage is more appropriate. Third: Ibn al-Arabi said: It is strange that al-Shafi’i and his peers permitted the leadership of a sinner, and how can someone who cannot be trusted with even a grain of money be trusted with a quintal of religion? The origin of this is that the rulers who used to lead the people in prayer, when their religions became corrupt and it was not possible to abandon the prayer behind them, and it was not possible to remove them, prayed with them behind them, as Uthman said: Prayer is the best thing that people do, so if they do well, then do well, and if they do wrong, then avoid their wrongdoing. Then there were those among the people who, if they prayed with them out of caution, would repeat the prayer to God, and among them were those who would make it their prayer, and I say that it is obligatory to repeat it, so no one should abandon the prayer with those imams whom he does not approve of, but he repeats it secretly to himself, and that does not affect anyone else. Fourth: As for his rulings, if he is a governor, he shall implement what is in accordance with the truth and reject what is contrary to it, and his ruling that he has approved shall not be overturned under any circumstances. Do not pay attention to any statement other than this, whether it is an influential narration or a statement that is told, for there is much talk and the truth is clear. Fifth: There is no disagreement that it is valid for a person to be a messenger on behalf of someone else in a statement he conveys or something he communicates, or permission he informs, if it does not go beyond the rights of the sender and the conveyor. If a right of someone other than them is attached to it, his statement is not accepted. This is permissible due to the necessity calling for it, because if no one acted among people in these meanings except the just, nothing would come of it due to their lack of that, and God knows best. Sixth: The verse is evidence of the corruption of the statement of those who say: All Muslims are just until the injury is proven, because God Almighty commanded verification before acceptance, and there is no meaning to verification after the execution of the ruling, because if the judge’s ruling is made before verification, then the one against whom the ruling is made has been wronged out of ignorance. Seventh: If he rules based on what is most likely, then this is not acting based on ignorance, such as ruling based on two just witnesses and accepting the opinion of a knowledgeable and diligent scholar. Rather, acting based on ignorance is accepting the opinion of someone whose acceptance is not based on a most likely opinion. This issue was mentioned by Al-Qushayri, and the one before it was Al-Mahdawi.
49:7: The Almighty says: And know that among you is the Messenger of God, so do not lie, for God will teach him your report and you will be disgraced. If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would be cursed, meaning if he were to rush to what you wanted before the matter became clear to us, it would be hardship and sin for you, because if he had killed the people that Al-Walid bin Uqbah sought to kill, it would have been a mistake, and cursed is he who wanted to bring about the destruction of those people because of the enmity that existed between him and them. The meaning of obeying the Messenger to them is to follow what he orders regarding what they say about people and to listen to them. Cursed is sin. It is said: a man was cursed. Cursed is also immorality and adultery, as in Surat An-Nisa. Cursed is also falling into a difficult matter. The statement about you were cursed has already been made at the end of Bara'ah with more than this. But God has endeared faith to you, this is addressed to the sincere believers who do not lie about the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor do they tell falsehood, meaning He made faith the most beloved of religions to you. And He adorned it with His guidance. In your hearts meaning He made it good to you until you chose Him. This is a refutation of the Qadarites, the Imamites, and others, as mentioned previously in more than one place. He, glory be to Him, is the One Who is unique in creating the essence of creation, their actions, their attributes, the diversity of their languages, and their colors. He has no partner. And He has made hateful to you disbelief, immorality, and disobedience Ibn Abbas said: He means lying specifically. Ibn Zayd said the same. It was said: Everything that deviates from obedience is derived from the word fasqat meaning the date came out of its husk, and the mouse from its hole. This has already been discussed in detail in Al-Baqarah. Disobedience is the plural of disobedience. Then he moved from addressing to reporting, saying: Those meaning they are the ones whom God guided, so He made faith beloved to them and made disbelief hateful to them, meaning He deemed it ugly in their eyes. They are the rightly guided like the saying of God, the Most High: And whatever you give in zakat, desiring the countenance of God - it is those who will receive double (ar-Rum 30:39). An-Nabigha said: Oh, house of Mayya in the highlands, the Sind is strong and the past has been long upon it Righteousness is staying on the path of truth while remaining firm in it, from the word rashad, which means rock. Abu Al-Wazea said: Every rock is a guide. And he recited: Uncopied and tattooed, pray the light of the deaf, the guidance
49:8: The Almighty says: As a favor and blessing from God meaning God did that to you as a favor, meaning as a favor and blessing, so it is the object for which it is done. And God is Knowing and Wise Knowing of what is good for you Wise in managing you.
49:9: It contains ten issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And if two parties among the believers should fight, then make settlement between them. Al-Mu’tamir bin Sulaiman narrated on the authority of Anas bin Malik who said: It was said: O Prophet of God, why don’t you go to Abdullah bin Ubayy? So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went to him. He rode a donkey and the Muslims set off walking, and it was marshy land. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to him, he said: Go away from me! By God, the stench of your donkey has hurt me. A man from the Ansar said, “By God, the smell of the donkey of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is better than yours.” A man from his people became angry on behalf of Abdullah, and each of their companions became angry. There was a war between them with palm branches, hands, and sandals. We were informed that this verse was revealed about it. Mujahid said: It was revealed about the Aws and the Khazraj. Mujahid said: Two tribes of the Ansar fought with sticks and sandals, so this verse was revealed. A similar verse was narrated by Sa`id ibn Jubayr: There was fighting between the Aws and the Khazraj during the time of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with palm leaves, sandals, and the like, so God revealed this verse about them. Qatada said: It was revealed about two men from the Ansar who were arguing about a right between them. One of them said, I will take my right by force, because of the large number of his tribe. The other called on him to take him to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) for judgment, but he refused to follow him. The matter continued between them until they fell to each other and attacked each other with hands, sandals, and swords. So this verse was revealed. Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed about the war between Sameer and Hatib. Sameer had killed Hatib, so the Aws and Khazraj fought until the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them. Then it was revealed, and God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers to reconcile between them. Al-Suddi said: There was a woman from the Ansar called Umm Zaid, who was married to a man from outside the Ansar. She quarreled with her husband and wanted to visit her people, so her husband imprisoned her and put her in an upper room where no one from her family could enter. The woman sent word to her people, and her people came and brought her down to take her out. The man went out and called for help from his family, so his workers came out to prevent the woman from her family. They pushed each other and fought with sandals, so the verse was revealed. The group includes one man, a group, or two people. It is one of the things that was interpreted in meaning rather than in wording, because the two groups are in the meaning of the people. In Abdullah’s reading: (until they return to the command of God. Then if they return, then take justice between them). Ibn Abi Ubla read: We fought on the basis of… The wording of the two groups, and it was mentioned at the end of Bara’ah, and Ibn Abbas said about the words of God Almighty: And let a party of the believers witness their punishment (al-Nur 24:2), he said: One or more, and a group of something is a part of it. “Then make peace between them” by calling to the Book of God for them or against them. But if one of them transgresses against the other she transgresses and does not respond to the judgment of God and His Book. Transgression means arrogance and corruption. Then fight against the one who transgresses until she returns to the command of God that is, returns to His Book. And if she returns she returns. “Then make peace between them with justice” that is, force them to be fair. And act justly O people, do not fight. It was said: Be just that is, act equitably. Indeed, God loves those who act justly that is, the just and righteous. Second: The scholars said: The two groups of Muslims will not be free from fighting, either they fight out of transgression from both of them or not. If it is the former, then it is obligatory to walk between them in a way that will reconcile them and produce recompense and truce. If they do not separate and do not reconcile and they persist in transgression, then it is up to them to fight. But if it is the latter, which is that one of them transgresses against the other, then it is obligatory to fight the transgressing group until it desists and repents. If it does, then it is obligatory to reconcile it with the transgressor in a just and fair manner. If fighting broke out between them due to a doubt that entered between them and both of them are right in their own eyes, then it is obligatory to remove the doubt with clear proof and conclusive evidence on the paths of truth. If they ride the back of obstinacy and do not act in the manner to which they were guided and advised by following the truth after it became clear to them, then they have joined the two transgressing groups, and God knows best. Third: This verse proves the obligation of fighting the rebellious group whose rebellion against the Imam or any of the Muslims is known, and it proves the invalidity of the statement of those who forbid fighting the believers and argue with the words of the Prophet (peace be upon him): Fighting a believer is disbelief. If fighting a rebellious believer were disbelief, then God would have commanded disbelief, exalted be God above that! Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him fought those who adhered to Islam but refused to pay zakat, and he ordered that no one who was loyal to a slave should be pursued, nor should any wounded be killed, and their wealth was not permissible, unlike what is obligatory regarding the disbelievers. At-Tabari said: “If it were obligatory in every disagreement between the two groups to flee from it and stay at home, then no punishment would be carried out, no falsehood would be abolished, and the hypocrites and immoral people would find a way to consider permissible everything God has forbidden them from the wealth of the Muslims, the captivity of their women, and the shedding of their blood, by forming parties against them, and the Muslims would refrain from attacking them. This contradicts the words of the Prophet (peace be upon him): “Take control of your fools.” Fourth: Judge Abu Bakr Ibn Al-Arabi said: This verse is the basis for fighting Muslims, and the mainstay in the war against those who interpret it. The Companions relied on it, and the notables of the people of the religion resorted to it. It is what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, meant when he said: Ammar will be killed by the rebellious group, and “His, peace be upon him, saying regarding the Khawarij: They will emerge with good, one group at a time of division,” and the first narration is more correct, because he, peace be upon him, said: They will be killed by the first of the two groups to the truth, and the one who killed them was Ali Ibn Abi Talib and those who were with him. It was established among the scholars of the Muslims and proven by the evidence of the religion that Ali, may God be pleased with him, was an imam, and that everyone who revolted against him was a rebel, and that fighting him is obligatory until he returns to the truth and submits to peace, because Uthman, may God be pleased with him, was killed and the Companions were innocent of his blood, because he forbade fighting those who revolted against him and said: I will not be the first to succeed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his nation by killing, so he was patient in the face of the affliction, submitted to the ordeal and sacrificed himself for the nation, then the people were not able to do anything in vain, so it was presented to The rest of the companions whom Omar mentioned in the Shura, and they fought over it, and Ali, may God be pleased with him, was more deserving of it and its people, so he accepted it as a precaution for the nation, lest its blood be shed in sectarianism and falsehood, or its order be breached to an unattainable extent, for perhaps the religion would change and the pillar of Islam would be destroyed. So when he was pledged allegiance to, he asked the people of Ash-Sham, in the condition of the pledge of allegiance, and seek the truth and you will reach it, and they said: You do not deserve the pledge of allegiance while the killers of Uthman are with you, you see them morning and evening. So Ali had a sounder opinion and more correct statement in that, because if Ali had taken retaliation from them, tribes would have become fanatical towards them and it would have become a third war, so he waited for them until the matter was secured and the pledge of allegiance was concluded, and the request was made by the guardians in the ruling council, so that the judgment would be carried out with justice. There is no disagreement among the nation that it is permissible for the imam to delay retribution if that leads to the incitement of strife or the dispersion of the word. This is what happened to Talha and al-Zubayr, as they did not remove Ali from his position nor did they object to him in terms of religion. Rather, they saw that it was more appropriate to begin by killing Uthman’s companions. I said: This is a statement about the reason for the war that occurred between them. A group of scholars said: The incident in Basra between them was not because they had decided to fight, but rather suddenly, and as a way for each of the two groups to defend themselves, thinking that the other group had betrayed them, because the situation had been settled between them, and a peace and separation had been made with satisfaction. The killers of Uthman, may God be pleased with him, feared that they would be empowered and surrounded, so they met and consulted and differed, then their opinions agreed that they should separate into two groups, and start the war as magicians in the two armies, and the arrows would differ between them, and the group in Ali’s army would cry out: Treachery of Talha and al-Zubayr, and the group in Talha and al-Zubayr’s army: Treachery of Ali. So they succeeded in what they had planned, and the war broke out, so each group was defending its treachery within itself, and preventing the shedding of its blood.
