This is correct from both groups and obedience to God Almighty, because the fighting and refraining from it occurred in this way, and this is the correct and well-known, and God knows best. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: Then fight against those who rebel until they return to the command of God. This is a command to fight, and it is a communal obligation. If some people carry it out, the rest are exempted from it. For this reason, some of the Companions may God be pleased with them refrained from these duties, such as Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas, `Abdullah ibn `Umar, Muhammad ibn Maslama, and others. `Ali ibn Abi Talib approved of this for them, and each one of them apologized to him with an excuse that he accepted from them. It is narrated that when the matter was entrusted to Mu`awiyah may God be pleased with him, he rebuked Sa`d for what he did and said to him: You were not among those who reconciled between the two groups when they fought, nor among those who fought the rebellious group. Sa`d said to him: I regret not fighting the rebellious group. It is clear that not everyone is to be blamed for what he did, but rather it was an action based on ijtihad and an implementation of the requirements of the Shari`ah. And God knows best. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: “But if they return, then make peace between them with justice.” Part of justice in their peace treaty is that they do not demand what happened between them of blood or money, because that would be lost based on interpretation, and their demand would alienate them from the peace treaty and increase their transgression, and this is a fundamental principle of interest. The tongue of the nation said: The wisdom of God Almighty in the war against the Companions was to make them aware of the rulings on fighting the people of interpretation, since the rulings on fighting the polytheists were known through the tongue and actions of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. Seventh: If a rebellious, aggressor revolts against the just imam, without any proof, the imam shall fight them with all the Muslims or with those who are sufficient, and he shall call them before that to obedience and entry into the community. If they refuse to return and make peace, they shall be fought, and their prisoners shall not be killed, nor shall their fugitives be pursued, nor shall their wounded be slaughtered, nor shall their children or property be taken captive. If the just person kills the rebel, or the rebel kills the just person who is his guardian, they shall not inherit from each other, and a deliberate killer shall not inherit under any circumstances. It has been said that the just person inherits from the rebel, by analogy with retaliation. Eighth: The blood or property that the rebels and the Khawarij consumed and then repented are not to be held accountable for. Abu Hanifa said: They are liable. Al-Shafi’i has two opinions. The basis of Abu Hanifa’s opinion is that it is destruction by aggression, so liability is required. The basis for this, according to us, is that the Companions, may God be pleased with them, in their wars did not pursue a fleeing person, nor did they attack a wounded person, nor did they kill a prisoner, nor did they guarantee a life or property. This is the example. Ibn ‘Umar said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘O servant of God, do you know how God rules regarding those who rebel from this nation?’ He said: ‘God and His Messenger know best.’ He said: ‘Their wounded are not to be finished off, their prisoners are not to be killed, their fugitives are not to be pursued, and their spoils are not to be divided.’ As for what was in place, it is returned in kind. All of this applies to those who rebelled based on an interpretation that is permissible for them. Al-Zamakhshari mentioned in his interpretation that if the rebellious group was small in number such that it had no protection, it is liable for what it had gained after the group, but if it was large and had protection and strength, it is not liable, except according to Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, may God have mercy on him.” God, for he was issuing a fatwa that the guarantee is binding upon her if she returns, and as for before the assembly and recruitment or when she disperses when the war lays down its burdens, then whatever she has gained she is liable for with everyone, so carrying the reconciliation with justice in His saying “Then make peace between them with justice” (al-Hujurat 49:9), according to the doctrine of Muhammad is clear and consistent with the wording of the revelation, and according to the saying of others, its direction is that it is carried on the fact that the rebellious group is small in number, and what they mentioned that the purpose is to kill grudges and remove hatred without guaranteeing crimes, is not a good contrast to what is commanded from the works of justice and observing equity, Al-Zamakhshari said: If you say: Why is justice linked to the second reconciliation and not the first? I said: Because what is meant by fighting in the beginning of the verse is that they fight as transgressors or two women who are riding on suspicion, and whichever of them it is, what the Muslims must do regarding them is to reconcile them and calm the mob by showing the truth and sound sermons and removing suspicion, unless they persist, in which case fighting is obligatory. As for the guarantee, it is not applicable, and it is not like that if one of them is transgressing, because the guarantee is applicable in both of the mentioned ways. Ninth: If they take over a country, take the alms, implement the prescribed punishments, and rule over them with legal rulings, neither the alms nor the prescribed punishments will be sufficient for them, and their rulings will not be overturned except what is contrary to the Qur’an, the Sunnah, or consensus, just as the rulings of the people of justice and the Sunnah are overturned. This was stated by Mutraf and Ibn al-Majishun. Ibn al-Qasim said: It is not permissible under any circumstances. It was narrated from Asbagh that it is permissible. It was also narrated from him that it is not permissible, as Ibn al-Qasim said. Abu Hanifa said the same, because he acted unjustly by someone whose appointment it is not permissible, so it is not permissible, as if they were not rebels. The main support for us is what we mentioned before, that when the turmoil was resolved and the dispute was resolved by a truce and peace treaty, the Companions may God be pleased with them did not object to any of them in a ruling. Ibn al-Arabi said: What I think is that this is not permissible, because when the turmoil was resolved, the imam was the rebel, and there was no one to object to him, and God knows best. Tenth: It is not permissible to attribute to any of the Companions a definite error, since they all exerted effort in what they did and wanted God Almighty, and they are all our leaders. We have been commanded to refrain from what their descendants did, and not to mention them except with the best mention, due to the sanctity of the Companions and the prohibition of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from cursing them, and that God forgave them, and informed of His satisfaction with them. This is in addition to what has been reported from the report through various chains of transmission from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Talha is a martyr walking on the face of the earth. So if what he went out to in war was disobedience, then he would not have been a martyr because of being killed in it. Likewise, if what he went out to was an error in interpretation and a shortcoming in what was required of him, because martyrdom does not occur except through killing in obedience, then it is necessary to interpret their matter according to what we have explained. Among the evidence for that is what has been authenticated and spread from the report of Ali that the killer of al-Zubayr is in Hell, and his saying: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Give glad tidings to the killer of Ibn Safiyyah of Hell. And if that is the case, then it has been proven that Talha and al-Zubayr were not disobedient or sinful. By fighting, because if that were the case, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not have said about Talhah, a martyr, nor would he have said that the killer of al-Zubayr is in Hell. Likewise, whoever sat there and was not mistaken in interpretation, but rather correct, God showed them the effort. If that was the case, that would not require cursing them, disavowing them, declaring them immoral, and nullifying their virtues and their jihad, and their great wealth in religion, may God be pleased with them. Some of them were asked about the blood that was shed between them, and he said: “That was a nation that has passed on. It shall have what it earned, and you shall have what you have earned. And you will not be asked about what they used to do.” (al-Baqarah 2:134), and some of them were asked about it as well, and he said: That is blood from which God has purified my hands, so I will not stain my tongue with it, meaning in order to avoid falling into error and judging some of them with what he was not correct in. Ibn Furak said: Some of our companions said: The way in which the disputes that occurred between the Companions were like the way in which the brothers of Joseph with Joseph, then they did not go beyond the limits of guardianship and prophethood, so the same is the case with what occurred. Among the Companions, Al-Muhasibi said: As for the blood, we are confused about it due to their differences. Al-Hasan Al-Basri was asked about their fighting, and he said: It was a fighting that the Companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, witnessed, and we were absent. They knew, and we were ignorant. They gathered, so we followed. They differed, so we stopped. Al-Muhasibi said: We say as Al-Hasan said, and we know that the people were more knowledgeable about what they entered into than us. We follow what they agreed upon, and we stop at what they differed upon, and we do not innovate an opinion from us. We know that they exerted themselves and wanted God Almighty, since they were not accused of religion, and we ask God for success.
49:10: There are three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: The believers are but brothers, meaning in religion and sanctity, not in lineage. For this reason it was said: Brotherhood in religion is more steadfast than brotherhood in lineage, because brotherhood in lineage is severed by opposing religion, but brotherhood in religion is not severed by opposing lineage. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him, he said: “The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: ‘Do not envy one another, do not hate one another, do not spy, do not seek out faults in one another, do not outbid one another, and be, O servants of God, brothers.’” In another narration: “Do not envy one another, do not outbid one another, do not hate one another, do not turn your backs on one another, and do not undercut one another, and be, O servants of God, brothers. A Muslim is a brother to a Muslim; he does not wrong him, does not forsake him, and does not look down on him. Piety is here,” and he pointed to his chest three times. “It is enough evil for a man to look down on his Muslim brother. The whole of a Muslim is sacred to another Muslim: his blood, his wealth, and his honor.” This is the wording of Muslim. In other than the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, “The Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: A Muslim is a brother to a Muslim; he does not wrong him, does not criticize him, does not forsake him, and does not act arrogantly.” He should not build a house to cover the wind except with his permission, nor should he harm him with the drops of his pot unless he scoops a scoop for him, nor should he buy fruit for his children to take out to his neighbor’s children, nor should he feed them from it.” Then, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Be careful, and only a few of you will be careful.” The second: The Almighty’s saying: “So make peace between your two brothers,” meaning between every two Muslims who are quarreling. It was said: between the Aws and the Khazraj, as mentioned above. Abu Ali said: He meant by the two brothers the two groups, because the dual form is used and what is meant by it is the majority, like the Almighty’s saying: Rather, both His hands are spread out (al-Ma’idah 5:64). Abu Ubaidah said: Meaning, make peace between every two brothers, so it applies to everyone. Ibn Sirin, Nasr bin Asim, Abu Al-Aliyah, Al-Jahdary, and Ya’qub read between your brothers with a ta’ for the plural, and Al-Hasan read your brothers and the rest, your brothers with a ya’ for the dual form. Third: In this verse and the one before it there is evidence that transgression does not remove the name of faith, because God the Most High called them brothers believers even though they were transgressors. Al-Harith Al-A’war said: Ali bin Abi Talib may God be pleased with him, who is the role model, was asked about fighting the transgressors among the people of the Camel and Siffin: Are they polytheists? He said: No, because they fled from polytheism. It was said: Are they hypocrites? He said: No, because the hypocrites do not remember God except a little. It was said to him: What is their condition? He said: Our brothers transgressed against us.
49:11: The Almighty says: O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people; perhaps they may be better than them; nor let women ridicule [other] women; perhaps they may be better than them. There are four issues in this: First: The Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people; perhaps they may be better than them. It was said that it is with God and it was said better than them meaning believing and submitting inwardly, and mockery is ridicule, I mocked him, I mocked him, mocking with the movement and mockery and mocking with the dammah, and Abu Zaid narrated I mocked him, and it is the worse of the two languages, and Al-Akhfash said: I mocked him and I mocked him, and I laughed at him and I laughed at him, and I mocked him and I mocked him, each is said: and the noun is mockery and mockery, and it was read with them in His Almighty’s saying so that some of them may take others as a mockery (al-Zukhruf 43:32), and it was mentioned before and so-and-so is mockery, he mocks in work, it is said: a mockery servant, and a mockery man also, he mocks him, and mockery with the opening of the kha mocks people. Second: There is a difference of opinion about the reason for its revelation. Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed about Thabit bin Qais bin Shammas, who had a deafness in his ear. If they preceded him to the gathering of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), they would make room for him so that he could sit next to him to hear what he said. One day he came and had missed one rak’ah of the dawn prayer with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) finished, his companions took their seats from him, and each man crouched in his seat, and they stuck to it. Hardly anyone would make room until a man could not find a place to sit and remain standing. When Thabit finished the prayer, he stepped over people’s necks and said: Make room, make room. So they made room for him until he reached the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and there was a man between him and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The man said to him: I have found a place to sit, so sit down! Thabit sat behind him angrily, then he said: Who is this? They said: So-and-so. Thabit said: The son of so-and-so! He mocked him with it, meaning his mother in the pre-Islamic era, so the man felt ashamed, so it was revealed. Ad-Dahhak said: It was revealed about the delegation of Banu Tamim who were mentioned earlier in the surah. They mocked the poor companions, such as Ammar, Khabbab, Ibn Fuhayrah, Bilal, Suhayb, Salman, Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhaifah, and others, when they saw their poor condition, so it was revealed about those among them who believed. Mujahid said: It is the mockery of the rich of the poor. Ibn Zayd said: One whose sins God has concealed should not mock the one whom God has exposed, for perhaps revealing his sins in this world is better for him in the hereafter. It was said: It was revealed about Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, when he came to Madinah as a Muslim, and whenever the Muslims saw him they would say, The son of the Pharaoh of this nation. So he complained about that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so it was revealed. In short, no one should dare to mock someone who attacks him with his own eyes if he sees him in poor condition, or with a physical defect, or not eloquent in his conversation. Perhaps he is more sincere in conscience and purer of heart than someone who is the opposite of his quality, so he wrongs himself by belittling the one whom God has honored, and mocking the one whom God has glorified. The Salaf were so extreme in their caution and protection from that that Amr ibn Shurahbil said: If I saw a man suckling a goat and laughed at him, I would fear that I would do the same as he did. And on the authority of Abdullah ibn Masoud: The calamity is entrusted to speech. If I mocked a dog, I would fear that I would turn into a dog. And speech in the language is for those mentioned specifically. Zuhair said: I don't know, and I will think I know whether the Al-Husn family or the women are doing it. They were called a people because they stand with their caller in times of hardship. It was said that it is the plural of standing, then it was used for every group even if they are not standing. Women may be included in the people metaphorically, and this was explained in Surat Al-Baqarah. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And not women from among women, perhaps they may be better than them. He mentioned women alone because they are more often mocked. God Almighty said: Indeed, We sent Noah to his people [Nuh 71:Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 200], so it included everyone. The commentators said: It was revealed about two women from the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who mocked Umm Salamah, because she tied her waist with a sabibah, which is a white garment, similar to a sabibah, and let its ends hang down behind her so that she would drag it. Aisha said to Hafsa, may God be pleased with them both, Look! What she drags behind her is like a dog’s tongue, this was their mockery, and Anas and Ibn Zayd said: It was revealed about the wives of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, they insulted Umm Salamah for being short, and it was said: It was revealed about Aisha, she pointed with her hand to Umm Salamah, O Prophet of God, she is short, and Ikrimah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Safiyyah bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab came to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: O Messenger of God, the women insult me and say to me, O Jewess, daughter of two Jewesses! The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Why did you not say that my father is Aaron, my uncle is Moses, and my husband is Muhammad? So God revealed this verse. Fourth: In Sahih al-Tirmidhi, it is narrated on the authority of Aisha who said: “I told the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about a man, and he said: ‘I would not be pleased to tell about a man even though I have such and such.’ I said: ‘O Messenger of God, Safiyyah is a woman,’ and she gestured with her hand like this, meaning that she is short. He said: ‘You have mixed up a word which, if mixed with the sea, would mix it.’” In al-Bukhari, it is narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Zam’ah who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade a man from laughing at what comes out of the soul, and he said: ‘None of you should beat his wife like a stallion, then perhaps he will embrace her.’” In Sahih Muslim, it is narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘God does not look at your outward appearance or wealth, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds.’” This is a great hadith which requires that one should not be certain of someone’s fault because of what he sees in him of acts of obedience or disobedience. Perhaps whoever maintains outward deeds, God will know in his heart a reprehensible characteristic that would make those deeds invalid, and perhaps whoever we see committing negligence or sin, God will know in his heart a praiseworthy characteristic that will cause him to be forgiven because of it. Actions are conjectural signs, not definitive proof. This means that we should not exaggerate in glorifying someone who we see doing good deeds, and we should not look down on a Muslim who we see doing bad deeds. Rather, we should look down on and condemn that bad state, not the offending person. So ponder this, for it is a careful examination, and success comes from God. The Almighty’s saying: And do not insult one another has three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And do not find fault with one another. Finding fault means faulting. This was mentioned in Bara’ah when he said: And among them is he who finds fault with you concerning charities. (al-Tawbah 9:58), and At-Tabari said: Finding fault is with the hand, the eye, the tongue, and a gesture, and backbiting can only be done with the tongue. This verse is like the Almighty’s saying: And do not kill yourselves. (An-Nisa’: 29), meaning do not kill one another, because the believers are like one soul, so it is as if he killed his brother, killing himself. And like the Almighty’s saying: So greet yourselves. (al-Nur 24:61), meaning greet one another, and the meaning is: do not find fault with one another. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, and Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: Do not slander one another. Ad-Dahhak said: Do not curse one another. It was read: And do not find fault with one another with the dammah. In His saying: yourselves, there is an indication that the wise person does not find fault with himself, so he should not find fault with others because… Like himself, “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The believers are like one body; if one part of it is ill, the rest of the body feels pain with sleeplessness and fever.” Bakr bin Abdullah Al-Muzni said: If you want to see many faults, then look at a faultfinder, because he only finds fault with people because of the fault he has. “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: One of you sees the speck in his brother’s eye and leaves the log in his own eye.” It was said: Part of a person’s happiness is to be preoccupied with his own faults rather than the faults of others. The poet said: If a person is wise and pious, his piety will distract him from his faults. As the sick person is distracted from the pain of all people, his pain is his pain Another said: Do not reveal people's faults that you have covered, lest God expose your faults. And mention their good qualities when they are mentioned, and do not burden any of them with what is in you. The second: The Almighty’s saying: And do not insult one another by nicknames. Nabz with a fat-ha is the title, and the plural is anbaaz. Nabz with a sukoon is the verbal noun. You say, nabazahu yanbazu nabzan, meaning he called him by nicknames. So-and-so insults the children, meaning he calls them by nicknames. The word is doubled for abundance. It is also said that nabz and nazb are bad nicknames. Tanabazu bi al-alaqab means they called each other by nicknames. In al-Tirmidhi, on the authority of Abu Jubayrah ibn al-Dahhak, he said: A man among us would have two or three names, and he would be called by one of them, and perhaps he would dislike it. So this verse was revealed: And do not insult one another by nicknames. He said: This is a good hadith. This Abu Jubayrah is the brother of Thabit ibn al-Dahhak ibn Khalifa al-Ansari, and Abu Zayd ibn al-Rabi’, the companion of al-Harawi, is trustworthy. In the Musannaf of Abu Dawud, on his authority, he said: This verse was revealed about us, in Banu Samlah: “And do not insult one another by nicknames. Evil is the name of immorality after faith.” He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and there was not a man among us who did not have two or three names, so he made…” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would say, O so-and-so, and they would say, Easy, O Messenger of God, for he would get angry at this name. So the verse was revealed: And do not insult one another by nicknames. This is one opinion, and there is a second opinion. Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: A man would be taunted after his conversion to Islam for his disbelief, O Jew, O Christian, so this was revealed. It was narrated from Qatada, Abu al-Aaliyah, and Ikrimah. Qatada said: It is a man saying to another, O immoral man, O hypocrite. Mujahid and al-Hasan also said this. How evil is the name of immorality after faith, meaning it is evil for a man to be called an infidel or a fornicator after his conversion to Islam and repentance. This was said by Ibn Zayd. It was said that the meaning is that whoever calls his brother an infidel or mocks him is an immoral person. In the Sahih: Whoever says to his brother, ‘O infidel,’ then one of them has incurred it if it is as he said, otherwise it will come back upon him. So whoever does what God has forbidden of mockery, backbiting, and insulting, then that is immorality, and that is not permissible. It was narrated that Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a man disputed with him, so Abu Dharr said to him: Leave, O son of the Jewess! The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What do you see here, red and black? You are not better than him, meaning in piety. Then the verse was revealed: And do not insult one another by nicknames. Ibn Abbas said: Insulting one another by nicknames means that a man has committed evil deeds and then repented, so God forbade insulting oneself for what happened in the past. This is indicated by what was narrated: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever insults a believer for a sin from which he has repented, it is right for God to test him with it and disgrace him for it in this world and the hereafter.” Third: An exception was made for someone who was predominantly used, such as the lame or the hunchback, and he did not earn a living from it, so the nation permitted it and the people of the religion agreed upon his statement. Ibn al-Arabi said: By God, there is something mentioned in their books that I do not approve of regarding Salih Jazarah, because he copied the word Kharza and was given the name by it. Likewise, their statement regarding Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Hadrami: Mutin, because he fell into the category of mud and similar things that were predominant among the later people, and I do not see it as permissible in the religion. Musa ibn Ali ibn Rabah al-Misri used to say: I do not absolve anyone who uses the diminutive form of the name of my father. The majority of his name was the diminutive form with a damma on the ‘ayn. What controls all of this is that everything that a person dislikes when called by it is not permissible because of the harm, and God knows best. I said: And based on this meaning, Al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him, translated in the Book of Etiquette of Sahih Al-Bukhari in the chapter on what is permissible in mentioning people, such as their saying tall or short without intending to disgrace a man. He said: And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What does Dhu al-Yadayn say? Abu Abdullah bin Khuwaiz Mandad said: The verse includes the prohibition of calling a person by what he dislikes, and it is permissible to call him by what he likes. Do you not see that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Umar al-Faruq, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, Uthman Dhu al-Nurayn, Khuzaymah Dhu al-Shahadatayn, Abu Hurayrah Dhu al-Shamalayn and Dhu al-Yadayn, and similar things? Al-Zamakhshari said: It was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: It is the right of the believer over the believer that he calls him by the name he loves most. For this reason, using a kunya is from the Sunnah and good etiquette. Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: Spread kunyas, for they are a source of inspiration. Abu Bakr was given the title al-Ateeq and al-Siddiq, Umar al-Faruq, Hamza the Lion of God, and Khalid the Sword of God. He said: Among the famous people in the pre-Islamic era and Islam were those who did not have a title, and these titles have not ceased. Goodness is common among all nations, Arabs and non-Arabs, in their conversations and correspondence without any objection. Al-Mawardi said: As for the desirable and good titles, they are not disliked. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, described a number of his companions with descriptions that became for them the most important titles. I said: As for what appears to be dislike if what is meant by it is the description and not the defect, then that is common. Abdullah bin Mubarak was asked about a man who says: Hamid al-Tawil, Sulayman al-A’mash, Hamid al-A’raj, and Marwan al-Asghar, so he said: If you mean his description and not his defect, then there is nothing wrong with it. And in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abdullah bin Sarjis, he said: I saw the bald man - meaning Umar - kissing the stone, and in another narration: the bald man. God Almighty says: And whoever does not repent meaning from these titles that offend the listeners, then it is those who are the wrongdoers to themselves by committing these prohibitions.
49:12: It contains ten issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, avoid much suspicion. It was said that it was revealed about two men from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who backbited their companion. This was because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he traveled, would bring a needy man with two wealthy men to serve them. So he brought Salman with two men. Salman went to the house and his eyes overcame him, so he slept and did not prepare anything for them. Then they came and did not find food or condiments, so they said to him: Go and ask the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, for food and condiments for us. So he went and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Go to Usamah ibn Zayd and tell him if you have any leftover food, let him give it to you. Usamah was the treasurer of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. So he went to him and Usamah said: I do not have anything. So he returned to them and informed them. They said: He had some, but he was stingy. Then they sent Salman to a group of the companions, but he did not find anything with them. They said: If we send Salman to the well of Samiha, its water will boil away. Then they set out to spy, is there… Usama had something, so the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw them and said: Why do I see the greenness of the meat in your mouths? They said: O Prophet of God, by God we have not eaten meat or anything else today. He said: But you have continued to eat the meat of Salman and Usama Then the verse was revealed: “O you who have believed, avoid much [negative] assumption. Indeed, some assumption is sin.” Al-Tha’labi mentioned it, meaning do not think the same of good people if you know that they appear to be good. The second is proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the falsest of speech. Do not look for the faults of one another, do not spy, do not outbid one another, do not envy one another, do not hate one another, and do not turn away from one another. O servants of God, be brothers.’” Bukhari. Our scholars said: Suspicion here and in the verse refers to accusation, and the subject of warning and prohibition is an accusation that has no reason to warrant it, such as someone who is accused of immorality or drinking alcohol, for example, and nothing appears to warrant that. The evidence that suspicion here means accusation is the statement of God Almighty: And do not spy. This is because the thought of suspicion may occur to him initially, and he wants to spy on the report of that and search for it, and to examine and listen to the truth of what happened to him of that accusation, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade that. If you like, you can say: What distinguishes the suspicions that must be avoided from others is that everyone who is suspected is someone who is seen to be modest and righteous, and trustworthy on the surface, so corruption and betrayal are suspected of him. It is forbidden, unlike someone who is known to be suspicious and openly commit evil deeds. “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: God has forbidden a Muslim’s blood and honor, and that he should be suspected of evil.” And on the authority of Al-Hasan: We were in a time when suspicion of people was forbidden, and today you are in a time when you should work and be silent, and think whatever you want of people. Third: Suspicion has two cases: a case that is known and strengthened by some form of evidence, so it is permissible to rule on it. Most of the rulings of the Shari’ah are based on the preponderance of suspicion, such as analogy, the single report, and other matters of value of lost property and blood money for crimes. The second case is when something occurs to the mind without evidence, so that it is not more deserving than its opposite. This is doubt, so it is not permissible to rule on it. It is what is prohibited, as we have stated above. A group of innovators have denied worshipping God based on suspicion and the permissibility of acting upon it, out of control over religion and a claim to reason. There is no basis for that to be relied upon, for the Creator, Most High, did not condemn all of it, but rather condemned some of it. Perhaps they relied on the hadith of Abu Hurayrah Beware of suspicion, for this is not an argument, because suspicion in the Shari’ah is of two types: praiseworthy and blameworthy. The praiseworthy type is that which safeguards the religion of the one who suspects and the one suspected when they reach maturity, and the blameworthy type is its opposite, as indicated by the words of God, Most High: Indeed, some suspicion is sin, and His words: Why, when you heard it, did not the believing men and believing women think good of one another? (al-Nur 24:12), and His statement, And you thought evil thoughts and you were a people of ruin (al-Fath 48:12), and “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If one of you praises his brother, let him say, ‘I think so and so,’ and I do not vouch for anyone before God,” and he said, If you have a suspicion, then do not verify it, and if you envy, then do not seek it, and if you have a bad omen, then move on. Narrated by Abu Dawud, and most scholars agree that bad thoughts about someone who appears to be good are not permissible, and that there is no harm in bad thoughts about someone who appears to be ugly, as Al-Mawardi said. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: And do not spy. Abu Raja’ and Al-Hasan, with some differences, and others, read and do not seek out with a ha, and there is a difference of opinion as to whether they have one meaning or two. Al-Akhfash said: One of them is not far from the other, because spying is searching for what is concealed from you, and seeking out report and searching for it. It was said that spying with a jeem is searching, and from this it was said: A man is a spy if he searches for matters, and with a ha: it is what a person has perceived with some of his senses. A second opinion about the difference: that with a ha you seek it for yourself, and with a jeem that he is a messenger for others, said Tha’lab, and the first is better known. I spied on the report and sought it out, and from this is the word spy. The meaning of the verse is: Take what is apparent and do not follow the faults of the Muslims, meaning that none of you should search for the faults of his brother until he speaks against him after God has covered it. In the book of Abu Dawud, it is narrated on the authority of Mu’awiyah who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: If you follow the faults of people, you will corrupt them or almost corrupt them. It corrupts them, Abu Darda’ said: “A word that Mu’awiyah heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, by which God Almighty benefited him.” On the authority of Al-Miqdam bin Ma’di Karib, on the authority of Abu Umamah, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: ‘If a ruler seeks suspicion among people, he corrupts them.’” On the authority of Zayd bin Wahb, who said: “Ibn Mas’ud was visited and it was said: ‘This is so-and-so whose beard is dripping with wine.’ Abdullah said: ‘We have been forbidden from spying, but if something appears to us, we will take it.’” On the authority of Abu Barzah Al-Aslami, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘O group of people who have believed with their tongues, but faith has not entered their hearts, do not backbite the Muslims and do not pursue their faults, for whoever pursues their faults, God will pursue his faults, and whoever God pursues his faults, He will disgrace him in his own home.’” Abd Al-Rahman bin Awf said: “I was guarding a night with Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, in Madinah, when we saw a lamp in a house whose door was closed to people who were making loud noises and chattering. Umar said: ‘This is the house of Rabi’ah bin Umayyah bin Khalaf, and they are now drinking. What do you think!?’” I said: I see that we have done what God has forbidden. God the Almighty said: And do not spy, and we have spied. So Omar turned away and left them. Abu Qilabah said: Omar ibn al-Khattab was told that Abu Mihjan al-Thaqafi was drinking wine with his companions in his house. Omar went until he entered upon him, and there was no one with him except a man. Abu Mihjan said: This is not permissible for you! God has forbidden you from spying. So Omar went out and left him. Zayd ibn Aslam said: Omar and Abd al-Rahman went out to eat, and a fire appeared to them. They asked permission, and the door was opened. There was a man and a woman singing, and in the man’s hand was a cup. Omar said: And you are doing this, so-and-so? He said: And you are doing this, O Commander of the Faithful! Omar said: Who is this from you? He said: My wife. He said: What is in this cup? He said: Clear water. He said to the woman: Who are you singing? She said: This night has become long and dark, and I am kept awake by the absence of a friend to play with. By God, if it weren't for God, I would have shaken the sides of this bed. But my mind and modesty are enough for me, and my husband is too generous to be given his ships Then the man said: This is not what we are ordered to do, O Commander of the Faithful! God Almighty said: And do not spy He said: You have spoken the truth. I said: It is not understood from this report that the woman was not the man’s wife, because Omar did not approve of adultery. Rather, she sang those verses in remembrance of her husband, and that she said them in his absence, and God knows best. Amr ibn Dinar said: There was a man from the people of Medina who had a sister who complained, so he used to visit her and she died, so he buried her. He was the one who went down into her grave, and a bag containing dinars fell from his sleeve. He sought help from some of his family, so they dug up her grave. He took the bag and said: I will go inside to see what has become of my sister. So he uncovered her and behold, the grave was burning with fire. He came to his mother and said: Tell me, what did my sister do? He said: Your sister has died, so why do you ask about her actions? He kept on at her until she said to him: One of her actions was that she used to delay the prayers beyond their appointed times, and when the neighbors slept, she would go to their homes and stick her ear to their doors, spying on them and finding out their secrets. He said: This is how she perished! Fifth: The Almighty said: And let not some of you backbite others. God, the Almighty, forbade backbiting, which is to mention a man’s faults. If you mention him with something he does not have, then it is slander. Its meaning is established in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Hurayrah: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Do you know what backbiting is?’ They said: ‘God and His Messenger know best.’ He said: ‘It is mentioning your brother with something he dislikes.’ It was said: ‘What if what I say is true in my brother?’ He said: ‘If what you say is true in him, then you have backbitten him, and if it is not true in him, then you have slandered him.’” It is said: He backbitten someone if he fell into it. The noun is ghaybah, which is mentioning a fault in his absence. Al-Hasan said: Backbiting has three aspects, all of which are in the Book of God, the Almighty: backbiting, slander, and slander. As for backbiting, it is to say about your brother what he is in. As for slander, it is to say about him what you have heard about him. As for slander, it is to say about him what is not true. Shu’bah said: Mu’awiyah, meaning Ibn Qurrah, said to me: ‘If a man with his hand cut off passes by you, and you say, This one has his hand cut off, then it is backbiting.’ Shu’bah said::So I mentioned it to Abu Ishaq and he said he was truthful. Abu Hurairah narrated that Ma’iz al-Aslami came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and testified that he had committed adultery. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) stoned him. Then the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) heard two of his companions saying, one of them to the other: Look at this man whom God concealed, but his soul would not let him until he was stoned like a dog. So he remained silent about them. Then he walked for a while until he passed by the carcass of a donkey carrying its leg. He said: Where are so-and-so and so-and-so? They said: Here we are, O Messenger of God. He said: Go down and eat from the carcass of this donkey. They said: O Prophet of God, who will eat from this? He said: You have not harmed your brother’s honor more severely than eating from it. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, he is now in the rivers of Paradise, immersed in them. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? God likened backbiting to eating carrion, because the dead does not know that his flesh is being eaten, just as the living does not know that the one who backbites him is backbiting. Ibn Abbas said: God gave this example for backbiting because eating the flesh of the dead is forbidden and abhorrent, and likewise backbiting is forbidden in religion and ugly in people’s hearts. Qatada said: Just as one of you would refrain from eating the flesh of his dead brother, he should also refrain from backbiting him when he is alive. He used eating meat instead of backbiting because the Arabs had this custom. The poet said: If they eat my flesh, I will provide for their flesh, and if they destroy my glory, I will build glory for them. And the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: He who continues to eat the flesh of people has not fasted. So he likened backbiting people to eating their flesh. Whoever disparages or slanders a Muslim is like someone who eats his flesh while he is alive, and whoever backbites him is like someone who eats his flesh while he is dead. In the book of Abu Dawud, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, he said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: When I was taken up to heaven, I passed by people who had nails of copper with which they were scratching their faces and chests. I said: Who are these, O Gabriel? He said: These are the ones who eat the flesh of people and backbite them.” And on the authority of Al-Mustawrid, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Whoever eats a morsel of food because of a Muslim, God will feed him the like of it from Hellfire. And whoever clothes a Muslim with a garment, God will clothe him with the like of it from Hellfire. And whoever places a man in a position of reputation and hypocrisy, God will place him in a position of reputation and hypocrisy on the Day of Resurrection.” And the statement of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) has already been mentioned: O group of people who have believed with their tongues but faith has not entered their hearts, do not backbite the Muslims. And his statement to the two men: Why do I see greenness? The meat is in your mouths.” Abu Qilabah al-Raqashi said: I heard Abu Asim say: I have not backbitten anyone since I knew what backbiting entails. Maymun ibn Siyah did not backbite anyone, nor did he allow anyone to backbite anyone in his presence. He would forbid him, and if he stopped, then he would stand up. Al-Tha’labi mentioned from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah that he said: “A man stood up from the presence of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they saw weakness in his standing, so they said: O Messenger of God, how weak is so-and-so!” He said: You ate your brother’s flesh and backbite him. On the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, he said: The least form of backbiting is to say that so-and-so has curly hair, except that he dislikes it. Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him said: Beware of mentioning people, for it is a disease. Instead, remember God, for it is a cure. Ali ibn al-Husayn may God be pleased with him heard a man backbiting another, so he said: Beware of backbiting, for it is the food of people’s dogs. Amr ibn Ubayd was told: So-and-so spoke ill of you until we pitied you. He said: Be merciful to him. A man said to al-Hasan: I have heard that you backbite me! He said: Your standing with me is not such that I judge you by my good deeds. Seventh: Some people have said that backbiting only applies to religion and not to physical appearance and lineage. They said: That is what God did to him. Others have said the opposite of this and said: Backbiting only applies to physical appearance, character, and lineage. Backbiting about physical appearance is more serious, because whoever finds fault with a craftsmanship finds fault with its maker. All of this is rejected. As for the first, it is rejected by the hadith of Aisha when she said about Safiyya: She is a short woman. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to her: You have said a word that if the sea were mixed with it, it would mix it. Narrated by Abu Dawud. Al-Tirmidhi said about it: A sound hadith. What is similar to it is according to what was mentioned above. The consensus of scholars in the past is that it is backbiting if it is intended to mean a fault. As for the second, it is also rejected by all scholars, because scholars from the beginning of time from the Companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the followers after them, did not consider backbiting to be greater than backbiting about religion, because a fault in religion is the greatest fault. Every believer hates to be mentioned in his religion more than he hates in his body. It is sufficient to refute whoever said this statement by his, peace be upon him, saying: If you say about your brother what… He hates it, for he has backbitten him, the hadith, so whoever claims that this is not backbiting has rejected what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said explicitly, and the generality of the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Your bloods, your wealth and your honour are sacred to you is sufficient, and this is general for religion and the world, and the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever has wronged his brother in his honour or wealth, let him seek his forgiveness from him, so it includes all honour, so whoever singles out one thing from that and not the other has contradicted what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said. Eighth: There is no disagreement that backbiting is a major sin, and that whoever backbites someone must repent to God Almighty. Does the backbiter consider it permissible? There is a difference of opinion about it. A group said: He does not have to ask for his forgiveness, but it is a sin between him and his Lord. They argued that he did not take from his money nor did he harm his body in a way that would diminish it, so that is not an injustice that he should ask for forgiveness from him. Rather, injustice is that from which there is a replacement and compensation in money or body. A group said: It is an injustice, and its expiation is to seek forgiveness for the one who backbit him. They argued that it is a hadith narrated on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: The expiation for backbiting is to ask forgiveness for the one you backbited. A group said: It is an injustice, and he must ask for its forgiveness. They argued that it is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Whoever has wronged his brother in his honor or wealth, let him ask for forgiveness from him before a day comes when there will be no dinar or dirham to be taken from his good deeds. If he has no good deeds, some of his companion’s bad deeds will be taken and added to his bad deeds.” Al-Bukhari narrated it from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever has wronged his brother in his honor or anything else, let him ask for forgiveness from him today before he will have no dinar or dirham, if he has any.” A good deed will be taken from him in proportion to his wrongdoing, and if he has no good deeds, some of his companion’s bad deeds will be taken and placed on him.” This meaning was presented in Surat Al Imran when God Almighty said: “And never think of those who are killed in the way of God as dead. Rather, they are alive.” (Al Imran 3:169) It was narrated from the hadith of Aisha that a woman entered upon her, and when she stood up, a woman said: How long her dress is! Aisha said to her: You have backbitten her, so consider it permissible. The narrations from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, indicate that it is an injustice for which the backbiter must seek forgiveness. As for the statement of those who say: Backbiting is only in money and body, the scholars have agreed that the slanderer has an injustice against the slandered, and he should take him to the prescribed punishment until he carries it out against him. This is not in body or money. This is evidence that the injustice is in honor, body and money. God Almighty said about the slanderer: But if they do not produce witnesses, then it is they who are liars in the sight of God (al-Nur 24:13). The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever slanders a believer with something that is not in him, God will imprison him in the mud of destruction. All of this is not in money or body. As for those who say: It is an injustice, and the expiation for an injustice is to seek forgiveness for its perpetrator, they contradicted themselves by calling it an injustice, then saying: Its expiation is to seek forgiveness for its perpetrator, because his saying ‘an injustice’ confirms the injustice of the oppressed, and if the injustice is proven, it does not remove it. Regarding the oppressor, there is nothing wrong except for the oppressed to forgive him. As for the statement of Al-Hasan, it is not an argument, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever has wronged his brother in his honor or wealth, let him forgive him. Some of them went so far as to leave forgiveness for the one who asked him, and they saw that what God has forbidden is not permissible for him. Among them is Sa’id ibn Al-Musayyab, who said: I do not forgive the one who wronged me. It was said to Ibn Sirin: “O Abu Bakr, this is a man who asked you to forgive him for a wrong he has committed against you, so he said: “I did not forbid it to him, so forgive it. God has forbidden backbiting to him, and I would never forgive what God has forbidden to him.” The hadith of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) indicates forgiveness, which is the argument and the clarification, and forgiveness indicates mercy and is from the aspect of forgiveness, and God the Almighty said: But whoever pardons and makes reconciliation - his reward is due from God (al-Shura 42:40). Ninth: Backbiting a sinner who is openly and openly evil does not fall under this category. In the hadith: Whoever throws off the cloak of modesty, there is no backbiting for him, and “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Mention the sinner for what he is like so that people may beware of him.’” So backbiting is for the person who conceals himself. It was narrated from Al-Hasan that he said: “There are three who have no respect: the one who follows his passions, the openly sinful person, and the imam who is permissive.” Al-Hasan said when Al-Hajjaj died: O God, You are his nation, so cut off his way from us. In another narration: “His disgrace, for he came to us, timid and bleak, extending a short-fingered hand, and by God, no dust had sweated on it in the cause of God. He combs his hair and walks slowly, and ascends the pulpit and roars until he misses the prayer. He does not fear God nor is he ashamed of people. Above him is God and below him are a hundred thousand or more. No one says to him: ‘Prayer, O man.’ Then Al-Hasan says: ‘Never!’” The sword and the whip prevented that. Al-Rabi’ bin Subaih narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: There is no backbiting for the people of innovation. Similarly, if you say to a judge, seeking his help to take your right from someone who wronged you, and you say, ‘So-and-so wronged me, or made me angry, or betrayed me, or hit me, or slandered me,’ this is not backbiting. The scholars of this ummah are unanimous on this. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The one who has a right has a say. He said: The delay of a rich person is injustice. He said: The one who has money is permitted to show off and punish. This includes asking for a fatwa, such as Hind’s statement to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Abu Sufyan is a stingy man who does not give me or my children what is sufficient for me and my children, so should I take from him without his knowledge? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Yes, take it. So she reminded him of his stinginess and injustice to her and her children. He did not see it as backbiting, because he did not change his mind about her. Rather, he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) answered her by giving her a fatwa. Similarly, if there is a benefit in mentioning him badly, such as his (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saying: As for Mu’awiyah, he is a vagabond with no money. As for Abu Jahm, he does not put his stick down from his shoulder. This is permissible, and his intention was that the daughter of Qais would not be deceived by them. All of them were said by Al-Muhasibi, may God have mercy on him. Tenth: The Most High said: dead. It was also read as dead and it is in the accusative case as a state of the meat, and it is permissible to make it in the accusative case as referring to the brother. And when the Most High decided that none of them would like to eat the carcass of his brother, He followed that with His Most High saying: Then you hated it. There are two interpretations: One of them is that you hated eating dead meat, so likewise hate backbiting. It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid. The second is that you hated that people would backbite you, so hate backbiting people. Al-Farra’ said: That is, you hated it, so do not do it. It was said: Its wording is report and its meaning is a command, that is, hate it. And fear God is in apposition to it. It was said: It is in apposition to His saying: Avoid it, “And do not spy.” Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.
49:13: It contains seven issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: O mankind, indeed We have created you from a male and a female, meaning Adam and Eve. The verse was revealed about Abu Hind. Abu Dawud mentioned it in Al-Marasil. Amr bin Othman and Katheer bin Ubaid told us, they said: Baqiyah bin Al-Waleed told us, he said: Al-Zuhri told me, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered the Banu Bayada to marry Abu Hind to a woman from among them. So he said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Should we marry our daughters to our clients? Then God, the Almighty, revealed: {Indeed, We created you from a male and a female and made you peoples}. Al-Zuhri said: It was revealed about Abu Hind specifically. It was said: “It was revealed about Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, and his statement about the man who did not make room for him: the son of so-and-so. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Who is the one who mentioned so-and-so? Thabit said: I am, O Messenger of God. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Look at the faces of the people. He looked and said: What did you see? He said: I saw white, black, and red. He said: You will not excel them except in piety.” So this verse was revealed about Thabit, and it was revealed about the man who did not make room for him: {O you who have believed, when you are told, Make room in assemblies} (Al-Mujadilah: 11). Ibn Abbas said: When it was the day of the conquest of Mecca, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered Bilal to climb onto the roof of the Kaaba and call to prayer. Atab ibn Asid ibn Abi Al-Ays said: Praise be to God who took my father so that he would not see this day. Al-Harith ibn Hisham said: Muhammad did not find anything other than this black crow. And Suhayl ibn Amr said: If God wills something, He changes it. And Abu Sufyan said: I do not say anything that I fear that the Lord of the heavens will inform me of. So Gabriel came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and informed him of what they had said. So he called them and asked them about what they had said, and they confessed. So God, the Most High, revealed this verse, forbidding them from boasting about lineage and piling up wealth, and from disdaining the poor, for the basis is piety, that is, everyone from Adam and Eve. Excellence is in piety. And in Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Ibn Umar: “The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, delivered a sermon in Mecca and said: O people, God has removed from you the arrogance of ignorance and its pride in their fathers. People are of two types: a pious man who is honored by God, and a wicked, wretched man who is insignificant to God. People are the children of Adam, and God created Adam from dust. God, the Most High, said: ‘O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of God is the most righteous of you. Indeed, God is Knowing and Acquainted.’” Narrated by Abdullah ibn Ja`far, the father of Ali bin Al-Madini, and he is weak. Yahya bin Ma’in and others deemed him weak. At-Tabari included in his book, Adab Al-Nufus, and Ya’qub bin Ibrahim told me, saying, “Ismail told us, saying, ‘Saeed Al-Jariri told us, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, who said: ‘I was told, or someone who witnessed the sermon of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, in Mina in the middle of the days of Tashreeq while he was on a camel told me, and he said, “O people, your Lord is one, and your father is one. There is no superiority of an Arab over a non-Arab, nor of a non-Arab over an Arab, nor of a black person over a red person, nor of a red person over a black person, except by piety. Have I conveyed the message?’ They said, ‘Yes.’ He said, ‘So that the witness may convey to the absent one.’” And in it, on the authority of Abu Malik Al-Ash’ar, he said, “The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said, ‘God does not look at your lineage, nor your lineage, nor your bodies, nor your wealth, but He looks at your hearts. So whoever has a righteous heart, God will be merciful to him. You are the children of Adam, and the most beloved of you to Him is the most righteous of you.’” And Ali, may God be pleased with him, has this meaning in his poetry, and it is well-known: People are competent in terms of representation, their father is Adam and their mother is Eve Soul to soul and similar spirits and the greatest created in them and members If they have a lineage of their own, they will boast about the clay and water. The credit goes only to the people of knowledge, for they are the guides to those who seek guidance. Every person is judged by what he does well, and men have a mark on their actions. And against every man is what he is ignorant of, and the ignorant are enemies to the people of knowledge. Second: God Almighty made clear in this verse that He created creation from male and female, and likewise in the beginning of Surat An-Nisa. If He had willed, He would have created it without them, as He created Adam, or without a male, as He created Jesus, peace be upon him, or without a female, as He created Eve from one of the two sides. This permissible ability does not mean existence, and it has been reported that God created Eve from Adam from a rib that He extracted from his ribs, so perhaps this is the division, as Ibn Al-Arabi said. Third: God created lineages, marriages, tribes, and peoples between males and females, and created for them the means of knowing each other, and made communication through them for the wisdom that He has determined and He knows best. So each person has his lineage, so if a man denies him, he deserves the punishment for slandering him, such as if he denies him from his relatives and lineage, by saying to an Arab: O foreigner, or to a foreigner: O Arab, and the like of that by which denial occurs in reality. End quote. Fourth: Some of the early scholars held that the fetus is only created from the man’s semen, and is nurtured in the mother’s womb, and is derived from the blood in it. They cited as evidence the words of God Almighty: Did We not create you from a despised water? Then We placed him in a secure lodging. (al-Mursalat 77:20-21), and His words: Then He made his offspring from an extract of despised water. (Al-Sajdah: 8), and His words: Was he not a drop of ejaculated semen? (al-Qiyamah 75:37). This indicates that creation is from one water. The correct view is that creation is only from the semen of the man and the woman, based on this verse, as it is a text that does not allow for interpretation. God Almighty’s words: He was created from a gushing fluid, emerging from between the backbone and the ribs. (Al-Tariq: 6-7), what is meant by this is the loins of men and the ribs of women, as will be explained. As for what they cited as evidence, it does not contain more than that God Almighty mentioned the creation of man from water, lineage, and sperm, and did not attribute it to one of the parents without the other. So it is proven that the water and the lineage belong to them and the sperm is from them, based on what we have mentioned, and that the woman ejaculates as the man ejaculates, and from that comes the resemblance, according to what was explained at the end of Ash-Shura. And He said in the story of Nuh 71:Then the waters met by a matter already decreed (al-Qamar 54:12), and He only meant the water of the sky and the water of the earth, because the meeting can only be between two, so it is not denied that it is Then He made his offspring from a lineage of despised water and the Most High’s saying: Did We not create you from a despised water? He meant two waters, and God knows best. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: And We have made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. The peoples are the heads of the tribes, such as Rabi’ah, Mudar, Aws, and Khazraj. The singular is sha’b with a fat-ha on the shin. They were named thus because of their branching out and gathering together like the branches of a tree. The people are from opposites. It is said that he gathered them together, and from this comes the word mush’ab with a kasra on the m, which is the most famous, because it gathers and branches together. He said: He was leaning on his forehead and his hands were covered with a scythe, as if it were smooth and forked. And its branch if it disperses it, and from it death was named peoples because it is dispersing, as for the people with the kasra, it is the road in the mountain, and the plural is ravines, Al-Jawhari said: The al-Nas 114:what branched out from the tribes of the Arabs and the Persians, and the plural is people, and the al-Nas 114:a group that does not prefer the Arabs over the Persians, and as for what is in the hadith: that a man from the people converted to Islam, he means from the Persians, and the al-Nas 114:the great tribe, and he is the father of the tribes to whom they are attributed, that is, he gathers them and includes them, Ibn Abbas said: The people are the majority like Mudar, and the tribes are the thighs, and Mujahid said: The people are the distant lineage, and the tribes are below that, and from him also that the people are the closest lineage, and Qatada said it, the first mentioned from him Al-Mahdawi, and the second Al-Mawardi, the poet said: I have seen Saud from many peoples, but I have never seen anyone as happy as Saad bin Malik. Another said: Tribes of peoples who do not have a generous or noble person among them It was said: The peoples are the Arabs of Yemen from Qahtan, and the tribes are from Rabi’ah, Mudar and the rest of Adnan, and it was said: The peoples are the clans of the Persians, and the tribes are the clans of the Arabs, and Ibn Abbas said in a narration: The peoples are the clients, and the tribes are the Arabs, Al-Qushayri said: Based on this, the peoples are those for whom no lineage is known, such as India, the mountains and the Turks, and the tribes are from the Arabs, Al-Mawardi, and it is possible that the peoples are those added to the regions and valleys, and the tribes are those who share lineages, the poet said: They dispersed into tribes, and every island had a Commander of the Faithful and a pulpit. Abu Ubaid narrated on the authority of Ibn al-Kalbi on the authority of his father: The people are larger than the tribe, then the faction, then the building, then the stomach, then the thigh. It was also said: The people, then the tribe, then the building, then the stomach, then the thigh, then the faction, then the clan. Some writers composed it and said: I mean the people, they are the most numerous tribe in the world, then the tribe. Then the architecture follows, then the abdomen and thigh after that and the faction Then after that comes the clan, but it is small compared to what we mentioned. Another said: A tribe before it is a people, after them is a building, then a clan after it is a thigh A young man is sheltered only by his own clan, and no share of his wealth is worthless. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, the most honorable of you in the sight of God is the most righteous of you. This was mentioned previously in Surat Az-Zukhruf, when God Almighty said: And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people. (al-Zukhruf 43:44), and in this verse there is what indicates to you that righteousness is what is taken into consideration by God Almighty and by His Messenger, not lineage and ancestry. An was read with the fat-ha, as if it was said: Why does he boast about lineages? It was said: Because the most honorable of you in the sight of God is the most righteous of you, not the most related. In Al-Tirmidhi, on the authority of Samurah, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Lineage is wealth, and generosity is piety.” He said: A good, strange, and authentic hadith. This goes back to the words of God Almighty: The most honorable of you in the sight of God is the most righteous of you. It was stated in a text from him, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever wants to be the most honorable of people, let him fear God. And fearing means observing the limits of God Almighty, both commands and prohibitions, and being characterized by what He has commanded you to be characterized by, and abstaining from what He has forbidden you. This has been mentioned in more than one place. In the hadith from the narration of Abu Hurairah, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, God Almighty will say on the Day of Resurrection, ‘I made lineage and you made lineage, so I made the most honorable of you the most righteous, and you refused except to say so-and-so, son of so-and-so. Today I raise my lineage and lower your lineage. Where are the righteous? Where are the righteous?’” Al-Tabari narrated from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘My friends are the righteous on the Day of Resurrection, even if their lineage is closer than their lineage. People come with deeds and you come with…’” In this world you carry it on your necks, you say, O Muhammad, and I say, This is how it is, and I turn away from both sides. In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Abdullah bin Amr, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say openly, not secretly: “The family of my father are not my guardians. My guardians are God and the righteous believers.” And from Abu Hurairah: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked: Who is the most honorable of people? He said: Joseph, son of Jacob, son of Ishaq, son of Abraham. They said: We are not asking you about this. He said: The most honorable of them in the sight of God is the most righteous of them. They said: We are not asking you about this. He said: About the origins of the Arabs? Their best in the pre-Islamic period are their best in Islam if they understand.” And they recited in that regard: What does a servant do with the glory of wealth? All glory belongs to the pious. He who knows God but is not satisfied by knowing God is the wretched one. Seventh: Al-Tabari mentioned that Umar ibn Muhammad told me that Ubayd ibn Ishaq al-Attar told us that Mandil ibn Ali told us on the authority of Thawr ibn Zayd, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja`d, who said: A man from the Ansar married a woman and he criticized her lineage. The man said: I did not marry her for her lineage, I married her for her religion and character. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It does not matter if you are not from the family of Hajib ibn Zararah. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God, the Blessed and Exalted, brought Islam and with it removed the base, completed the deficient, and removed blame. There is no blame on a Muslim. The blame is only the blame of the Age of Ignorance. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I hope that I am the most fearful of God among you and the most knowledgeable of what I fear. Therefore, he was the most honorable of people in the sight of God Almighty. Ibn al-`Arabi said: This is what Malik noted regarding compatibility in marriage. Abdullah ibn Malik narrated: A freed slave marries an Arab woman, and he used this verse as evidence. Abu Hanifa and al-Shafi`i said: Lineage and wealth should be taken into consideration. In the Sahih, on the authority of Aisha, that Abu Hudhayfah ibn Utbah ibn Rabi’ah, who was among those who witnessed Badr with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, adopted Salim and married him to Hind, the daughter of his brother Al-Walid ibn Utbah ibn Rabi’ah. He was a freed slave of a woman from the Ansar, and Duba’ah bint Al-Zubayr was married to Al-Miqdad ibn Al-Aswad. I said: The sister of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf was married to Bilal, and Zaynab bint Jahsh was married to Zayd ibn Haritha, so this indicates the permissibility of marrying Arab slave women, and that compatibility in religion is taken into consideration. The evidence for this is also what Sahl ibn Sa`d narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari: “A man passed by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: What do you say about this? They said: If he proposes marriage, he should be married, and if he intercedes, his intercession should be accepted, and if he speaks, his intercession should be listened to.” He then remained silent. Then a poor Muslim man passed by and he said: What do you say about this? They said: If he proposes marriage, he should not be married, and if he intercedes, his intercession should not be accepted, and if he speaks, his intercession should not be listened to. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This man is better than filling the earth with the likes of this one.” And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A woman is married for her wealth, her beauty, and her religion. In another narration: And for her lineage, so choose the one with religion, may your hands be rubbed with dust. Salman proposed to Abu Bakr for his daughter, and he accepted him, and he proposed to Umar for his daughter, but he deviated from him, then he asked him to marry her, but Salman did not do so. Bilal proposed to Al-Bukair's daughter, but her brothers refused. Bilal said: O Messenger of God, what have I suffered from Banu Al-Bukair? I proposed to them for their sister, but they refused and harmed me. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) became angry on behalf of Bilal. When the report reached them, they went to their sister and said: What have we suffered because of you? Their sister said: My affair is in the hands of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so they married her. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said about Abu Hind when he cupped him: Marry Abu Hind and give others in marriage to him. He was a freed slave of Banu Bayada. Ad-Daraqutni narrated from the hadith of Az-Zuhri from Urwah from Aisha that Abu Hind, the freed slave of Banu Bayada, was a cupper and cupped the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever is pleased to look at the one in whose heart God has pictured faith, let him look at Abu Hind. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Marry others and give others in marriage to him. Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr said: Lineage may be considered in compatibility in marriage, and it is connection to the tree of prophethood or to scholars who are the heirs of the prophets or to those who are distinguished in asceticism and righteousness. A pious believer is better than a wicked relative. If they are both pious, then the relative should be preferred, just as a young man is preferred over an old man in prayer if they are equal in piety.
49:14: God Almighty said: The desert Arabs say, ‘We have believed.’ Say, ‘You have not believed; but say, “We have submitted, for faith has not yet entered your hearts. And if you obey God and His Messenger, He will not deprive you of anything of your deeds. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.’” It was revealed about some Bedouins from Banu Asad ibn Khuzaymah who came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in a year of drought and declared the two testimonies of faith, but they were not believers in secret. They spoiled the roads of Madinah with their waste and raised prices. They used to say to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him): We have come to you with our luggage and children, and we did not fight you as Banu so-and-so fought you, so give us some of the charity. They began to show him favors, so God, the Most High, revealed this verse about them. Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed about some Bedouins who wanted to be called by the name of the emigrants before they emigrated, so God informed them that they had the names of Bedouins, not the names of the emigrants. Al-Suddi said: It was revealed about the Bedouins mentioned in Surat al-Fath 48:the Bedouins of Muzaynah, Juhaynah, Aslam, Ghifar, Al-Dil, and Ashja’. They said, We have believed, so that they would feel safe about themselves and their wealth. But when they were called to Madinah, they stayed behind, so it was revealed. In short, the verse is specific to some Bedouins, because among them are those who believe in God and the Last Day, as God, the Most High, described. The meaning of but say, ‘We have submitted,’ is that we have surrendered for fear of being killed. And the captivity, and this is a characteristic of the hypocrites, because they submitted in the outward form of their faith but their hearts did not believe, and the reality of faith is belief in the heart, and as for Islam, it is accepting what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought in the outward form, and that spares the blood. And if you obey God and His Messenger means if you are sincere in faith, He will not deprive you meaning He will not diminish any of your deeds “La ya’lituhu wa yilituhu, decrease it.” Abu Amr read La ya’lituhum with a hamza, from alta ya’litu alta, and this is the choice of Abu Hatim, considering the words of God Almighty: And We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds (al-Tur 52:21). The poet said: Tell Bani Tha'al about me, conveying the message with all due diligence and without lying. Abu Ubaid chose the first. Ru’bah said: A night of dew flowed and did not turn me away from its secret. I wish That is, nothing prevented me from seeing her secret, and likewise he prevented him from seeing her. The verb and the verb have the same meaning. It is also said: He did not prevent him from doing anything, meaning he did not decrease it, like he prevented him. Al-Farra’ said: And he recited: And they eat what I mean the guardian did not turn as if on the edges of the end of the farms His saying: It did not decrease anything from it, and made it grow, means made it grow. It is said: The earth did not decrease anything, meaning it did not grow. And the guardian is the rain after the wasmi. It was called guardian because it follows the wasmi.
