He did not say: It does not decrease you, because obedience to God Almighty is obedience to the Messenger.
49:15: God Almighty says: The believers are only those who have believed in God and His Messenger and then have not doubted meaning they have believed and have not doubted and have proven that through jihad and righteous deeds. Those are the truthful in their faith, not those who have submitted out of fear of being killed or in the hope of gain. So when this verse was revealed, the Bedouins swore that they were believers in secret and in public, but they lied.
49:16: God Almighty says: “Say: Do you teach God about your religion?” which you are following? And God knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and God is Knowing of all things.
49:17: The Almighty’s saying: They do you a favor by becoming Muslims, referring to their saying: We have come to you with our burdens and our children, and that is in the accusative case, assuming that they became Muslims. “Say: ‘Do not do me a favor by your Islam,’ meaning by your Islam. ‘Rather, God does you a favor by guiding you to faith.’” That is in the accusative case, assuming that it is because, and it was said: because. In the copy of Abdullah’s copy, when He guided you, “if you were truthful,” that you were believers. Asim read if He guided you with the kasra, and there is some discrepancy in it, because of His saying, if you were truthful, and it is not said that He does you a favor by guiding you if you were truthful. The apparent reading is that He guided you. This does not indicate that they were believers, because the meaning of the statement is: If you believe, then that is God’s favor upon you.
49:18: The Almighty said: Indeed, God knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and God is Seeing of what you do. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaisin, and Abu Amr read it with the letter ya as a statement, in response to his statement, The Bedouins said. The rest read it with the letter ta as an address.
50:1: All of it is Meccan according to Al-Hasan, Ata’, Ikrimah, and Jabir. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said, except for one verse, which is the saying of God Almighty: And We created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six days, and We were not touched by any weariness. And in Sahih Muslim: “On the authority of Umm Hisham bint Al-Harith ibn An-Nu’man, she said: Our oven and the oven of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were the same for two years or a year and part of a year, and I did not take “Qaf, by the Glorious Qur’an” except from the tongue of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would recite it every Friday from the pulpit when he addressed the people.” And “On the authority of ‘Umar, may God be pleased with him, he asked Abu Waqid Al-Laithi: What did the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recite on the days of Sacrifice and Fitr? He said: He would recite in them “Qaf, by the Glorious Qur’an” and The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split. And “On the authority of Jabir ibn Samurah: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to recite “Qaf, by the Glorious Qur’an” in Fajr, and his prayer after that was shortened.” God the Almighty says: “Qaf. By the Glorious Qur’an.” The common people read Qaf with Jazm, while Al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq, and Nasr Ibn Asim read it with Kasra on the Fa’ because Kasra is a brother of Jazm, so when the last letter is quiescent, they give it a Khafd vowel. Isa Al-Thaqafi read it with Fatha on the Fa’, giving it the lightest vowel. Harun and Muhammad Ibn Al-Sameeq read Qaf with Dammah because it is usually a construction vowel like Mundhu, Waqt, Qabl, and Ba’d. There is a difference of opinion as to the meaning of Qaf: What is it? Ibn Zayd, Ikrimah, and Al-Dahhak said: It is a mountain surrounding the earth of green emerald, the sky from it and above it are the two ends of the sky, and the sky above it is domed. And whatever emerald befalls people was because of what fell from that mountain. Abu Al-Jawza’ narrated it from Abdullah Ibn Abbas. Al-Farra’ said: According to this, the i’rab of Qaf should have been made clear because it is a noun and not a spelling. He said: Perhaps Qaf alone was mentioned as part of its name, like the saying of the poet: I told her to be patient and she said: Qaf That is, I am standing. This is a good interpretation. The beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah has been mentioned, and it says: Dhul-Qarnayn ascended Mount Qaf and saw small mountains beneath it. He said to him: Who are you? He said: I am Qaf. He said: What are these mountains around you? He said: They are my veins. There is no city except that there is a vein of my veins in it. So when God wants to shake a city, He commands me, so I move that vein of mine and the earth shakes. He said to him: O Qaf, tell me something of the greatness of God. He said: The affair of our Lord is great, and behind me is a land a distance of five hundred years’ journey by five hundred years of mountains of snow, some of which crush others. Were it not for them, they would have been burned by the heat of Hell. This indicates that Hell is on the face of the Earth, and God knows best its location and where it is on the Earth. He said: Tell me more. He said: Gabriel, peace be upon him, will stand before God with their heads bowed. When God permits them to speak, they will say: There is no god but God. This is the saying of God the Most High: {The Day the Spirit and the angels will stand in rows, they will not speak except for one whom the Most Merciful permits and he will say what is right.} meaning the saying: There is no god but God. Al-Zajjaj said: His statement Qaf means the matter has been decided, as it was said about Ha Meem, meaning, Ha Meem is the matter. Ibn Abbas said: Qaf is one of the names of God the Most High, by which He swore. It was also narrated from him: that it is one of the names of the Quran, and this is the saying of Qatada. Al-Qurazi said: The opening of the names of God the Most High is: Qadir, Qahir, Qahir, Qadir, Qaddi, and Qabid. Al-Sha’bi said: It is the opening of the surah. Abu Bakr Al-Warraq said: Its meaning is: Stop at Our command and prohibition and do not transgress them. Muhammad ibn Asim Al-Antaki said: It is the closeness of God to His servants. Its explanation is: {And We are nearer to him than his jugular vein.} Ibn Ata’ said: God swore by the strength of the heart of His beloved Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, as he carried the message, but that did not affect him due to his lofty state. By the Glorious Qur'an meaning of high status. It was also said: generous, said Al-Hasan. It was also said that Kathir is taken from high status and high rank, not from high number, from their saying So-and-so has high status, and from this is the saying of the Arabs in the popular proverb In every tree there is fire, and Markh and Afār were considered abundant, meaning these two types of fire were considered abundant and exceeded all other trees", said Ibn Bahr. The answer to the oath was said to be: "We know what the earth takes away from them, meaning We know, and it was also said that it is Indeed in that is a reminder", and this is the choice of Al-Tirmidhi. Muhammad bin Ali said: "Qaf" is an oath by a name that is the greatest of names that have been given to the servants, which is power. And he also swore by the Glorious Qur'an. Then he related what came out of the power of the creation of the heavens and the earths, the provisions of the servants, the creation of mankind, the description of the Day of Resurrection, Paradise and Hell. Then he said: Indeed in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart. So the oath fell on this surah: A reminder for whoever has a heart or listens while he is present. Ibn Kaysan said: Its answer is: What he utters of a word. The people of Kufa said: The answer to this oath is: Rather, they were amazed. Al-Akhfash said: Its answer is omitted, as if he said: “Qaf. By the Glorious Qur’an,” You will be resurrected, is indicated by: When we have died and become dust.
50:2: The Almighty said, Rather, they were amazed that a warner had come to them from among themselves. “An” is in the accusative case, assuming that a warner had come to them from among themselves, meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The pronoun refers to the disbelievers, and it was said to refer to the believers and the disbelievers together. Then He distinguished between them by saying, the Most High: Then the disbelievers said, and He did not say they said, but rather He described their state and their actions as ugly and described them as disbelievers, as you say: So-and-so came to me and made me hear something unpleasant, and the wicked man said to me, You are such-and-such. “This is an amazing thing.” Amazing is the thing that is astonished by, and likewise, wonder with the damma and wonder with the shaddah are more than it, and likewise, the marvel. Qatada said, They were astonished that they called to one God. And it was said: From warning them of the resurrection and the revival, which the Qur’an has stated is more appropriate.
50:3: The Almighty's saying: When we have died and become dust will we be resurrected? This implies that is a far-fetched return. Return means return, meaning it is a far-fetched return, i.e. impossible. It is said: I returned him, I returned him, a return, and he returned, he returns, a return. And there is another implied meaning, i.e., they said, Shall we be resurrected when we die? The mention of resurrection, even though it is not mentioned here, has been mentioned in other places, and the Quran is like a single surah. Also, the mention of resurrection is included in His saying: Rather, they wonder that a warner has come to them from among themselves, because he only warns of punishment and accountability in the hereafter.
50:4: The Almighty says: We already know what the earth takes away from them meaning what it consumes of their bodies, so nothing is lost to Us to the point that it would be impossible for Us to restore them. And in the Qur'an: "He said, 'Then what about the former generations?' He said, 'Their knowledge is with my Lord, in a Register. My Lord does not err, nor does He forget.'" And in the Sahih: Every son of Adam will be eaten by the dust, except the coccyx; from it he was created and on it he will be rebuilt. It has been previously established that the earth does not consume the bodies of the prophets, saints, and martyrs. God has forbidden the earth to consume their bodies. We have explained this in Kitab al-Tadhkirah, and it has also been previously mentioned in this book. Al-Suddi said: "Decrease here means death. We know who among them will die and who will remain, because whoever dies is buried, as if the earth is decreasing people." And from Ibn Abbas: It is those of the polytheists who enter Islam. And with Us is a record that preserves meaning their number and names, so it is a fa'il with the meaning of fa'il. It was said that the Preserved Tablet means that it is preserved from the devils, or that everything is preserved in it. It was also said that the Book is an expression for knowledge and statistics, as you say: I have written this for you, meaning I have preserved it. This left out the apparent meaning without necessity. It was also said that it means that we have a book that preserves the deeds of the children of Adam so that we may hold them accountable for them.
50:5: The Almighty said: Rather, they denied the truth meaning the Qur'an according to everyone's opinion. Al-Mawardi narrated it. Al-Tha'labi said: The truth is the Qur'an. It was also said: Islam. It was also said: Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him. So they are in a confused state meaning: mixed. They say sometimes he is a magician, sometimes a poet, and sometimes a soothsayer. This was said by Ad-Dahhak, Ibn Zaydouq, and Al-Qatadah. Different in goodness, ambiguous, but the meaning is close. Abu Hurairah said: corrupt. From this, the trusts of people became corrupted, and the religion became confused and the matter became mixed. Abu Dawud said: Marj al-Din, so I prepared for him the supervisor of the Harak, the knitted Al-Katd Ibn Abbas said: Al-Marij is the reprehensible matter. Imran bin Abi Ata’ said about it: Marij is mixed and he recited: She wandered around and sought out its interior, and it fell like a thread of silk. The thread branch. Al-Awfi said about it in the matter of misguidance, which is their saying a magician, a poet, a madman, a soothsayer. It was said that it is variable, and the origin of Marj is disturbance and anxiety. It is said that the matter of people was confused, and the matter of religion was confused, and the ring was confused on my finger if he was anxious from emaciation. And in the hadith: How will you be, O servant of God, if you were among a people whose covenants and trusts were confused and they differed and they were like this and like this, and he interlocked his fingers. Narrated by Abu Dawud, and we mentioned it in the Book of Remembrance.
50:6: The Almighty says: Have they not looked at the sky above them? A look of consideration and contemplation, and that the One who is able to create it is able to restore it. How We constructed it and raised it without pillars. And adorned it with stars. And it has no rifts. The plural of farj is a crack. And from the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: She closes her vagina from behind Al-Kisa’i said: There is no difference, no discrepancy, and no gap in it.
50:7: And the earth We have spread out and placed firm mountains therein. This was explained in Ar-Ra'd. And We caused to grow therein of every kind meaning every kind of plant. Delightful meaning beautiful and pleasing to the observers. This was explained in Al-Hajj.
50:8: Insight means that We made that an insight to indicate the perfection of Our power. Abu Hatim said that it is in the accusative case as a source, meaning that We made that an insight and a warning of Our power. And a reminder is in apposition to it. For every servant who turns back refers to God Almighty, who thinks about His power.
50:9: The Almighty said, And We sent down from the sky meaning from the clouds blessed water meaning abundant in blessing. And We caused to grow thereby gardens and grain for harvest The meaning is: And the grain for plants is the harvest, which is everything that is harvested. This is the opinion of the Basrans. The Kufians said that it is a case of adding something to itself, as one says: the mosque of the congregation, Rabi' al-Awwal, the truth of certainty, the jugular vein, and the like. This was said by al-Farra'. The original form is the harvested grain, so the alif and lam were deleted and the described thing was added to the description. Ad-Dahhak said the harvested grain is wheat and barley. It was also said: Every grain that is harvested, stored, and eaten.
50:10: And tall palm trees is an accusative case of state in response to his statement: And the grain of the harvest and tall is a state of state. And the tall and tall ones were said by Mujahid and Ikrimah. Qatadah and Abdullah ibn Shaddad said: By their stems, they are straight in length. Saeed ibn Jubayr said: Levels. Al-Hasan and Ikrimah also said, and Al-Farraa: Pregnant women who are well-fed. It is said of a sheep that it has given birth. The poet said: When we left the house, it remained tall and proud, with tall, towering oxen. The first is more common and more popular in the language. It is said that the palm tree has become long and has become tall. He said: We have wine, not vineyard wine, but the fruit of the tall trees. Generous ones in the sky have gone too far, and their fruits have been lost to the hands of the criminals. It is said that someone was above his companions, meaning he was above them. A she-camel is also known as a basaqat if milk enters her udder before giving birth, so she is mubsiq and the camels are mubasiq. Qutbah ibn Malik said: I heard the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recite basaqat with a sad. Al-Tha’labi mentioned this. I said: What is in Sahih Muslim. On the authority of Qutbah ibn Malik, he said: I prayed and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) led us in prayer. He recited “Qaf. By the Glorious Qur’an” until he recited And the tall palm trees. I kept repeating it and I do not know what he said. However, it is not permissible to replace the sad with the seen because of the qaf. For it is a date palm in layers. The date palm in layers is the first part of the date palm to emerge. It is said: The date palm in layers emerged and the date palm in layers, and its date palm in layers before it splits. Nadeed means overlapping, some of it arranged on top of others. In Al-Bukhari, nadeed al-kafiri is as long as it is in its sleeves, and its meaning is arranged some of it on top of others. But if it emerges from its sleeves, it is not nadeed.
50:11: Provision for the servants meaning We provided them with provision, or it means We caused it to grow as provision because growing has the same meaning as provision, or it means that it is an object for it, meaning We caused it to grow for their provision, and provision is that which is prepared to be benefited from. This has been discussed previously. "And We revived thereby a dead land. Thus is the emergence" meaning from the graves, meaning just as God revived this dead land, so He will bring you out alive after your death. So the kaf is in the nominative case as a subject, and this meaning has been mentioned in more than one place. He said dead because the intended meaning is the place, and if he had said dead, it would have been permissible.
50:12: The Almighty said, The people of Noah denied before them. That is, just as these people denied, so did those people deny, and so the punishment befell them. He mentioned to them the report of those who denied before them and frightened them with what seized them. We have mentioned their stories in more than one place when mentioning them.
50:13: God Almighty said: And Aad, Pharaoh, and the brothers of Lot.
50:14: Every messenger denied from these nations of disbelievers so My threat came true meaning My threat and punishment came true upon them.
50:15: The Almighty says, Are We weary of the first creation? That is, are We weary of it, so are We weary of the resurrection? This is a rebuke to those who deny the resurrection and an answer to their saying, That is a far-fetched return. It is said, You are weary of the matter if you do not know its meaning. Rather, they are in confusion about a new creation. That is, in bewilderment about the resurrection. Some of them believe it and some of them deny it. It is said that the matter became confusing to them, meaning that they were confused.
50:16: The Almighty said, And We have certainly created man meaning people, and it was said Adam, and We know what his soul whispers to him meaning what is in his secret, heart, and conscience. In this is a warning against the sins that he conceals. And whoever said that what is meant by man is Adam, then what his soul whispered to him was eating from the tree, and then it is general for his children, and whispering is the speech of the soul, like hidden speech. Al-A’sha said: You hear the whispers of the jewelry when you turn away, as if you were helped by the scent of the thorns of the zajal. It was mentioned in Al-A'raf, And We are nearer to him than his jugular vein. It is the jugular vein that extends from the throat to his shoulder. They are two veins on the right and left. Its meaning was narrated from Ibn Abbas and others, and it is well-known in the language. The rope is the vein, so it was attributed to itself due to the difference in the two words. Al-Hasan said: The jugular vein is the aorta, which is a vein attached to the heart. This is a metaphor for nearness, meaning We are nearer to him than his jugular vein, which is from him, and not in the sense of a short distance. It was said: It is more in control of him than his jugular vein, which is from himself, because it is a vein that mixes with the heart, so the knowledge of the Lord is nearer to him than the knowledge of the heart. Its meaning was narrated from Muqatil, who said: The jugular vein is a vein that mixes with the heart, and this nearness is the nearness of knowledge and power. The parts of a human being block others, but nothing blocks the knowledge of God.
50:17: God the Almighty said: When the two receivers receive, sitting on the right and on the left. Meaning, We are closer to him than his jugular vein when the two receivers receive, and they are the two angels assigned to him. Meaning, We are more knowledgeable about his condition, so we do not need an angel to inform him, but they were assigned to him to enforce the argument and confirm the matter upon him. Al-Hasan, Mujahid and Qatadah said, The two receivers are two angels who receive your deeds, one on your right, writing down your good deeds, and the other on your left, writing down your bad deeds. Al-Hasan said, "Until when you die, your record of deeds will be folded up and it will be said to you on the Day of Resurrection, 'Read your record. Sufficient for you is yourself this Day as a reckoner against you.'" God is just towards you, who made you your own reckoner. Mujahid said, God, with His knowledge of your condition, assigns to man two angels by night and two angels by day, who record his deeds and write down his traces, to enforce the argument. One of them is on his right, writing down the good deeds, and the other is on his left, writing down the bad deeds. This is the meaning of the Almighty’s statement: On the right and on the left, seated. Sufyan said: I have been informed that the writer of good deeds is trustworthy over the writer of bad deeds. So when a servant sins, he says, Do not hasten, perhaps he will seek forgiveness from God. Its meaning was narrated from the hadith of Abu Umamah, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The writer of good deeds is on a man’s right and the writer of bad deeds is on his left. The writer of good deeds is trustworthy over the writer of bad deeds. So when he does a good deed, the one on his right writes it down as ten, and when he does a bad deed, the one on his right says to the one on his left, “Leave him for seven hours, perhaps he will glorify God or seek forgiveness.” It was narrated from the hadith of Ali, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The seat of your two angels is on your front teeth; your tongue is their pen, and your saliva is their ink. You run about that which does not concern you, so have no shame before God or before them.” Ad-Dahhak said: Their seat is under the mouth on the chin. Aouf narrated it from Al-Hasan, who said: Al-Hasan liked to clean his chin. He only said seated, and he did not say two seated, although they are two, because what was meant was one on the right, one seated, and one on the left, so the first was omitted because the second indicated it. Sibawayh said it, and the poet said it too We are satisfied with what we have and you are satisfied with what you have, but the opinion differs Al-Farazdaq said: I guarantee to whoever comes to me what he has earned and he refuses, and I am not treacherous. He did not say raḍīyan nor ghadūr treacherous. Al-Mubarrad's school of thought is that what is in the recitation comes first and last due to expansion, and the second was deleted because the first indicates it. Al-Akhfash and Al-Farra''s school of thought is that what is in the recitation represents the two and the plural, and there is no deletion in the speech. Qa'id means sitter like the All-Hearing and the All-Knowing and the All-Powerful and the Witness. It was said that Qa'id means seated like akeel and nadīm meaning eater and companion. Al-Jawhari said that Fa`il and Fa`ul are among the forms that can be used in singular, dual, or plural forms, such as the Almighty’s saying, Indeed, we are the Messengers of the Lord of the Worlds, and His saying, And the angels after that will be our support. And the poet said about the plural form, recited by Al-Tha`labi: I am heading to it, and the best messenger is the one who knows the details of the report What is meant by Qa'id here is the one who is constantly present and constant, not the opposite of Qa'im.
50:18: The Almighty said: Not a word does he utter but by him is an observer ready to record. That is, he does not speak anything but that it is written down over it. It is taken from the word food, which means expelling it from the mouth. There are three interpretations of the observer: One is that it is the one who follows up on matters. The second is that it is the guardian, as stated by Al-Suddi. The third is that it is the witness, as stated by Ad-Dahhak. There are two interpretations of the atid: One is that it is the present one who never disappears. The second is that it is the guardian who is prepared either for preservation or for testimony. Al-Jawhari said: atid is the thing that is present and prepared. He prepared it taktudu and he prepared it ittiyudun meaning he prepared it for a day. From this is the Almighty’s saying: And I prepared for them a place to recline. A horse ‘ittada and ‘ittada with a fatha or kasra on the ta’ means prepared for running. I said, and it all goes back to the meaning of presence, including the poet’s saying: Even if you are absent from my sight, your memory is always present in my heart. Abu al-Juza’ and Mujahid said: Everything is recorded for a person, even groaning during his illness. Ikrimah said: Only that for which he will be rewarded or punished is recorded. It was also said: “Everything that he says is recorded for him, and when the end of the day comes, what was permissible is erased from him, such as ‘go,’ ‘sit,’ and everything that does not involve reward or blame. And God knows best.” It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah and Anas that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “There are no two guardians who raise to God what they have memorized, and God sees good at the beginning of the document and good at the end of it, except that God says to His angels: ‘Bear witness that I have forgiven My servant for what is between the two ends of the document.’” Ali may God be pleased with him said: God has angels with white documents, so hope for good in the beginning and end of it, and He will forgive you for what is in between. Abu Naim Al-Hafiz narrated that Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Al-Fadl ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Khuzaymah narrated to us that my grandfather Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us that Muhammad ibn Musa Al-Harashi narrated to us that Suhayl ibn Abdullah narrated to us that he heard Al-A’mash narrating on the authority of Zayd ibn Wahb on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: When the two guardians descend upon a male or female slave, they have a sealed book with them and they write down whatever the male or female slave utters. Then when they want to leave, one of them says to the other, ‘Unlock the sealed book that you have with you,’ so he unlocks it for him and in it is whatever was written, just as in the statement of God the Most High: ‘Not a word does he utter but there is a watcher by him ready to record.’” This is strange from the hadith of Al-A’mash on the authority of Zayd. No one narrated it on his authority except Suhayl. It was narrated on the authority of Anas that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God has appointed two angels to His servant who write down his deeds. When he dies, they say, ‘Our Lord, so-and-so has died, so give us permission to ascend to the heavens.’ God Almighty says, ‘My heavens are filled with My angels glorifying Me.’ They say, ‘Our Lord, may we reside on Earth.’ God Almighty says, ‘My Earth is filled with My creation glorifying Me.’ They say, ‘O Lord, where shall we be?’ God Almighty says, ‘Be at the grave of My servant, glorify Me, praise Me, and exalt Me, and write that down for My servant until the Day of Resurrection.’”
50:19: The Almighty said, And the intoxication of death will come with the truth. That is, it overwhelmed him and overwhelmed him. As long as a person is alive, his words and deeds are recorded for him to be held accountable for, then death will come to him, which is what he sees when he witnesses the manifestation of the truth in what God Almighty promised and threatened him with. It was said that the truth is death, and it was called the truth either because it is deserved or because it will move to the abode of truth. Based on this, there is an inversion in the speech, and its meaning is, The intoxication of truth came with death. This is also the case in the readings of Abu Bakr and Ibn Masoud may God be pleased with them. Because the intoxication is the truth, it was attributed to itself due to the difference in the two words. It was said that the truth, according to this reading, may be God Almighty, that is, the intoxication of God Almighty’s command came with death. It was said that the truth is death, and the meaning is the intoxication of death with death. This was mentioned by Al-Mahdawi. Someone who criticized the Quran claimed, saying: Do you contradict the Quran just as Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq contradicted it and read, The intoxication of truth came with death. He argued against him that two narrations were narrated from Abu Bakr: one of them is in agreement with the Qur’an, so it should be acted upon, and the other is rejected and falls under the category of forgetfulness on his part, if he said it, or a mistake on the part of some of those who transmitted the hadith. Abu Bakr al-Anbari said: Ismail bin Ishaq al-Qadi told us, Ali bin Abdullah told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Masruq, who said: When Abu Bakr was dying, he sent for Aisha, and when she entered upon him, she said: This is as the poet said. If you ever choke and feel constricted in your chest Abu Bakr said: Why did you not say as God said: “And the stupor of death will come in truth. That is what you were avoiding.” He mentioned the hadith and the stupor is one of the stupors. In the Sahih: On the authority of Aisha: That the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, had a bowl or a container of water in front of him, so he would put his hands in the water and wipe his face with it, saying: “There is no god but God. Indeed, death has stupors.” Then he raised his hand and said: In the highest company until he died and his hand deviated. Narrated by Al-Bukhari. It was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that he said: “The righteous servant experiences death and its stupors, and his joints greet one another, saying: ‘Peace be upon you. You leave me and I leave you until the Day of Resurrection.’” And Jesus, son of Mary, said: O company of disciples, supplicate to God to make this stupor easy for you, meaning the stupor of death. It was narrated: Indeed, death is more severe than being struck with swords, sawed through with saws, and cut with scissors. “That is what you were avoiding,” meaning it is said to the one who is overcome by the stupor of death: That is what you were fleeing from and turning away from. It is said: He deviated from something means he deviated from it and turned away from it. Its root is haydudah with a fat-ha on the ya’, then it was sukun because there is no fa’lul in speech other than sa’fuq. And you say when reporting something about yourself, ‘I deviated from something’, ‘ahid haydan muhidun’ if you turned away from it. Tarafa said: Abu Munther, you sought loyalty, but you gave it up and you were stubborn as a camel strays from the edge.
50:20: The Almighty says, And the Trumpet will be blown. This is the blast for resurrection. That is the Day of Threat, which God promised to the disbelievers that He would punish them on it. We have already discussed the blowing of the Trumpet in full, and praise be to God.
50:21: The Almighty says: And every soul will come with it a driver and a witness. There is a difference of opinion about the driver and the witness. Ibn Abbas said: The driver is from the angels and the witness from themselves are their hands and feet. Narrated by Al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. Abu Hurairah said: The driver is the angel and the witness is their deeds. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: The meaning is a driver who drives it and a witness who testifies to its deeds. Ibn Muslim said: The driver is its companion from the devils. He is called a driver because he follows it even if he does not urge it on. Mujahid said: The driver and the witness are two angels. Uthman ibn Affan may God be pleased with him said while he was on the pulpit: And every soul will come with it a driver and a witness. A driver is an angel who drives it to the command of God and a witness who testifies to its deeds. I said: This is more authentic, for the hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The son of Adam is heedless of what God, the Almighty, has created for him. God, there is no god but Him. When He wants to create him, He says to the angel, ‘Write down his provision, his legacy, and his lifespan, and write him as miserable or happy.’ Then that angel rises and God sends another angel to guard him until he reaches maturity. Then God sends two angels to write down his good and bad deeds. Then, when death comes to him, those two angels rise. Then the Angel of Death, peace be upon him, comes and takes his soul. When he enters his grave, He returns the soul to his body. Then, the Angel of Death rises. Then, the two angels of the grave come to him and test him. Then, they rise. When the Hour comes, the Angel of Good and the Angel of Bad deeds descend upon him and produce a book tied around his neck. Then, they appear with him, one as a driver and the other as a witness. Then God, the Almighty, said: ‘Indeed, you were heedless of this, but We have removed your covering, and your sight today is sharp.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘You will surely ascend from one level to another.’ He said: ‘State after state.’ Then, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Indeed, a great matter awaits you.’ So seek help from God, the Almighty. It was narrated by Abu Naim al-Hafiz from the hadith of Ja`far ibn Muhammad ibn `Ali on the authority of Jabir, and he said in it: This is a strange hadith from the hadith of Ja`far, and the hadith of Jabir was narrated only by Jabir al-Ju`fi from him, and from him al-Mufaddal. Then there are two opinions about the verse: One of them is that it is general for Muslims and disbelievers, and this is the opinion of the majority. The second is that it is specific to disbelievers, as was said by al-Dahhak.
50:22: The Almighty's saying, Indeed, you were heedless of this, so We removed your covering from you. Ibn Zayd said that what is meant by it is the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), meaning, you, O Muhammad, were heedless of the message among the Quraysh during their ignorance. Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak said that what is meant by it are the polytheists, meaning they were heedless of the consequences of their actions. Most of the commentators said that what is meant by it is the righteous and the wicked. This is the preferred view of At-Tabari. It was said that it means, O human, you were heedless of the fact that every soul has a driver and a witness, because this can only be known through the divine texts. So We removed your covering from you, meaning your blindness. There are four interpretations of this: One of them is that he was in his mother's womb and was born, as As-Suddi said. The second is that he was in the grave and was resurrected. This is the meaning of Ibn Abbas’s statement: The third: The time of presentation on the Day of Resurrection. Mujahid said that it is the descent of the revelation and the carrying of the message. This is the meaning of Ibn Zayd’s statement: So your sight today is sharp. It was said that it means the sight of the heart, just as it is said that he is perceptive in jurisprudence. So the sight and insight of the heart is its perception of the evidence of thoughts and the results of consideration, just as the eye sees what is opposite it of people and objects. It was also said that it means the sight of the eye, which is the apparent meaning, that is, the sight of your eye today is sharp, that is, strong and penetrating, it sees what was hidden from you. Mujahid said: So your sight today is sharp, meaning your sight on the tongue of your scale when your bad and good deeds are weighed. Ad-Dahhak said the same. It was also said: He will see what he will end up with of reward and punishment. This is the meaning of Ibn Abbas’ statement. It was also said that it means that the disbeliever will be gathered and his sight will be sharp, then he will turn blue and go blind. It was also read: I was about you, so your sight with a kasra, addressing the self.
50:23: The Almighty said, And his companion said, meaning the angel assigned to him, according to Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Ad-Dahhak, This is what I have ready, meaning, this is what I have of his deeds recorded and preserved. Mujahid said, “He says, ‘This is what you have assigned to me from among the sons of Adam, I have brought it and brought the register of his deeds.’ It was also said that the meaning is, ‘This is what I have of punishment, present.’ Also from Mujahid: His companion who was assigned to him from among the devils. Ibn Zayd said in the narration of Ibn Wahb from him that it is his companion from among mankind.
50:24: So God the Almighty says to his companion: Throw both into Hellfire. Al-Khalili and Al-Akhfash said: This is the eloquent speech of the Arabs, to address one person using the dual form, so you say: Woe to you, saddle her and drive her away, take him and release him to one person. Al-Farraa said: You say to one person: Get away from us. The origin of that is that the minimum number of helpers of a man in his camels and sheep and his companions in his travels are two, so the speech of a man to his two companions is derived from it, and from that they say to one person in poetry: My two friends, then he says: O friend. Imru’ al-Qais said: My friend, I passed by Umm Jundub, and the tears fell on my tormented heart. He also said: Stop and let us weep over the memory of a beloved and a home in the valley between Dakhul and Hawmal. Another said: If you rebuke me, O son of Affan, I will rebuke, and if you invite me, I will be an unapproachable offer. It was said that it came thus because the companion is for the group and the two. Al-Mazini said: His saying: Alqayyā indicates Alqayyā Alqayyā. Al-Mubarrad said: It is a dual form for emphasis, the meaning is Alqayyā Alqayyā, so Alqayyā replaces repetition. It is possible that Alqayyā is a dual form for addressing the truth from the saying of God the Most High, addressing the two angels. It was said that it is addressing the driver and the guardian. It was said that the original is Alqayyān with a light noon that changes to an alif in the pause, so the connection is based on the pause. Al-Hasan read Alqayyān with a light noon like His saying: And that they will be among the debased and His saying: We will surely sweep us away “Every disbeliever is stubborn” meaning obstinate. Mujahid and Ikrimah said this. Some of them said: The stubborn one is the one who turns away from the truth. It is said when Ya’nad with a kasra, Anūdān, meaning he contradicted and rejected the truth while he knows it, so he is obstinate and ‘ānad, and the plural of ‘āneed is like raghaif and raghf.
50:25: Preventer of good meaning the obligatory zakat and every obligatory right. Transgressor in his speech, conduct and command. Suspicious doubter of monotheism. This was said by Al-Hasan and Qatadah. It is said that a man is arab, so he is suspicious if he comes with doubt, and he is the polytheist it indicates.
50:26: God Almighty said: Who has set up with God another god. It was said that it was revealed about Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira, and what he meant by his saying a preventer of good was that he was preventing his brother's sons from converting to Islam. So cast him into the severe punishment is an emphasis on the first command.
50:27: His companion said, 'Our Lord, I did not make him transgress.' Meaning, the devil who was appointed for this stubborn disbeliever disowned him and denied him. But he was in far error from the truth and was a transgressor by his own choice. I only called him and he responded to me. His companion here is his devil without any difference. Al-Mahdawi narrated it, and Al-Tha'labi narrated that Ibn Abbas and Muqatil said, His companion is the king. That is because Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira says to the king who was writing down his sins, Our Lord, he hastened me. The king says, Our Lord, I did not make him transgress, meaning, I did not make him hasten. Sa'id bin Jubair said, The disbeliever says, 'Our Lord, he added to what I wrote.' The king says, Our Lord, I did not make him transgress, meaning, I did not add to what I wrote." Then...
50:28: God the Almighty says, Do not dispute before Me, meaning the disbelievers and their companions from among the devils. Al-Qushayri said: This indicates that the companion is the devil. And I have already brought you the threat, meaning I have sent the messengers. It was said that this is addressed to everyone who disputes. It was also said that it is for two people and it was used in the plural.
50:29: What is not changed in My Word It was said that it is His saying, Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof, and whoever brings an evil deed will not be recompensed except with the like thereof. It was also said that it is His saying, I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together. Al-Farra' said: What is not false in My Word means that what is said is not added to it nor subtracted from My knowledge of the unseen. And I am not unjust to the servants Meaning, I will not punish those who have not committed a crime. This was said by Ibn Abbas. The meaning of this had been discussed in Hajj and elsewhere.
50:30: The Almighty said, On the Day We will say to Hell, 'Are you filled?' and it will say, 'Are there any more?' Nafi' and Abu Bakr read On the Day He says with a ya' in consideration of His statement, Do not dispute before Me. The rest read it with a noon as a direct address from God, the Most High, and it is the noon of majesty. Al-Hasan read On the Day I say. Ibn Mas'ud and others also read On the Day it is said. The word On the Day it is said was in the accusative case meaning what is changed by saying before Me, On the Day. It was also said that it was with an implied verb meaning, And warn them. "On the Day We will say to Hell, 'Are you filled?'" based on what preceded from His promise to it that He would fill it. This question is for the purpose of confirming His report, fulfilling His promise, rebuking His enemies, and warning all of His servants. Hell will say, "Are there any more?" meaning there is nothing left in place for increase. Such as his saying, peace be upon him: Did Aqeel leave us a quarter or a house? That is, what did he leave? The meaning of this statement is denial. It is possible that it is a question meaning more, that is, is there more? So I will increase. This is suitable for both aspects because in the question there is a kind of denial. It was said that there is no statement, but rather it is by way of a proverb, that is, in what appears from her condition she is in the position of someone who speaks about that, as the poet said: The basin was filled and my cotton said, "Slow down, I have filled my stomach." This is the interpretation of Mujahid and others. That is, is there a path that has been filled? And it was said that God will make the Fire speak until it says this as the limbs speak. This is more correct based on what we have explained in Surat Al-Furqan and in Sahih Muslim, Al-Bukhari and Al-Tirmidhi. On the authority of Anas bin Malik: On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Hell will continue to throw people into it and it will say, Is there more? until the Lord of Glory places His foot therein, and then some parts will fold up on top of others and it will say, Enough, enough, by Your glory and generosity. And there will continue to be surplus in Paradise until God creates for it a creation and inhabits them with the surplus of Paradise.” Wording by Muslim. And in another narration from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah: As for the Fire, it will not be filled until God places His foot upon it and says to it, Enough, enough. Then it will be filled and some parts will fold up on top of others, and God will not wrong any of His creation. As for Paradise, God will create for it a creation. Our scholars, may God have mercy on them, said: As for the meaning of foot here, they are people whom God will bring forward to the Fire, and He has previously known that they are among the people of the Fire. Likewise, the man, which is a large number of people, and others. It is said: I saw a man from the people and a man from the locusts. The poet said: A man passed by us and a man from the right-hand tribe withdrew to them. The tribes of Lakhm, Ukl and Himyar are hostile to the two sons of Nizar. This meaning is explained by what was narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, who said: “In Hellfire there is no house, no chain, no whip, and no coffin except that it has the name of its owner on it. Each of the guards awaits his companion whose name and description he knows. When each one of them has completed what he was ordered to do and what he is awaiting, and none of them remains, the guards will say, ‘Enough, enough. We have had enough.’ That is, we are satisfied, we are satisfied. At that time, Hellfire will withdraw upon those in it and close in, since no one remains waiting. So that waiting group is referred to as a man and a foot. This interpretation is supported by his statement in the same hadith: ‘And there will continue to be surplus in Paradise until God creates for it a creation and inhabits them in the surplus of Paradise.’ We have expanded this meaning and prepared the ground for it in the Book of Names and Attributes of the Most Sublime Book. Praise be to God. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said regarding the meaning of his statement, ‘until the Almighty places his foot in it,’ meaning whoever knew in advance that he would be among the people of Hellfire.
50:31: The Almighty says, And Paradise will be brought near to the righteous, not far away. That is, it will be brought near to them. It was said that this was before entering this world, that is, it will be brought near to their hearts when they were told to avoid sins. It was also said that after entering, their places in it will be brought near to them, so they will not be far away. Not far away that is, from them. This is an emphasis.
50:32: This is what you are promised. That is, it will be said to them: This is the reward that you were promised in this world through the tongues of the messengers. The general reading is you are promised with the ta' indicating address. Ibn Kathir read it with the ya' indicating the report because it came after mentioning the righteous. For every frequently turning back to God and preserver. Repeating al-worship means turning to God from sins, then he goes back and sins again. O mountains, echo with him. Al-Hakam ibn Utaybah said: It is the one who remembers God in solitude. Ash-Sha'bi and Mujahid said: It is the one who remembers his sins in solitude and seeks God's forgiveness for them. This is the view of Ibn Mas'ud. Ubayd ibn Umair said: It is the one who does not sit in a gathering until he seeks God's forgiveness in it. It was narrated from him that he said: We were told that the frequently turning back is the preserver who, when he gets up from his gathering, says: "Glory be to God and praise be to Him. O God, I seek Your forgiveness for what I did in this gathering of mine." And in the hadith: “Whoever says when he stands up from a gathering, ‘Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You, there is no god but You, I seek Your forgiveness and I repent to You,’ God will forgive him for what happened in that gathering.” And this is how the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say, and some scholars said, I like to say I seek Your forgiveness and ask You for repentance, but I do not like to say I repent to You except in its true form. I said this is preferable, but following the hadith is more appropriate. Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: He is the one who relies on God in good times and bad. Al-Qasim said: He is the one who is not occupied with anything except God, the Almighty and Majestic. Hafiz: Ibn Abbas said: He is the one who preserves his sins until he turns away from them. Qatada said: Hafiz is the one who preserves what God has entrusted to him of His right and His blessings and entrusted him with them. Ibn Abbas also said: He is the one who preserves God’s command. Mujahid: He is the one who preserves God’s right by acknowledging and His blessings by thanking. Ad-Dahhak said: He is the one who preserves God’s commandment by accepting it. Makhul narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Whoever maintains four rak’ahs from the beginning of the day will be one who frequently turns back and preserves. Al-Mawardi mentioned this.
50:33: His saying, the Most High, Whoever fears the Most Merciful in secret "Min is in the accusative case as a substitute for His saying, For every frequently turning [to God] is a Guardian" or as an attribute of frequently turning [to God]. It is permissible to put it in the nominative case as a resumption and the predicate is "Enter it as if the answer to the condition was omitted and the estimation is It will be said to them, Enter it" and fear in secret means that you fear Him without seeing Him. Ad-Dahhak and As-Suddi said it means in seclusion when no one can see him. Al-Hasan said: When he lowers the curtain and closes the door. "And comes with a heart turning [to God]" turning to obedience. It was also said: sincere. Abu Bakr Al-Warraq said: The sign of the one who turns [to God] is that he is aware of His mercy and loyal to Him, humble before His majesty, and abandoning his own desires. I said: It is possible that the repentant heart is the sound heart, as God Almighty said: Except for he who comes to God with a sound heart, as mentioned above, and God knows best.
50:34: َيْاَخلوَْوَْْخلوُا ََلًََََََُه اُْلََْخلوُا َي مخَص َْْو. َُْمن ا وملئَْه َلََْلَْوق.ََك من اَعَابًََلم من خْي لن منْاَْلَْْخلوُا وفي َوْوقا. ْاََعْمن زواًََلم.ْْون اََمع

50:39: َمَهْخُاب َلََي صلى ا َلَه وَلَْلى ما ََوَََاءت فاص َالمَْوَزَت ق.َلَكََُْلى ما ََوَه اَمَْْون َي ُون َمَََاَص َلى ماََمعَا فاصَْْو.وَمَهُْو ثاَت َلََي صلى ا َلَه وَلَْْو.اَََتِْن ا اَََاح َو: َُْمن قوََْوَه اََُو راغب َه اَصلواتُْلوع اَْمس اََْوب قاَْرَك قْوََح َحم اََْوب صلةًََُلوع اَْمس اَصَح اَثاَََْو صاَح قْاَخمس قا اَََي صلىَََْْا َاََا: ْا مَفوَا قاَََْنََََرواه" َاَعص ْماََََْْون رََِْْما: ْاََْر فَاًََلََِى اََمََُ َِ ْا َلَه وَل َْْْلَوا َلى صلة قََ َََْصلة فماًَْضامون في حاَ ََْون َُا اََم رَكْوََح َحم" ََََقَاءةْثَََعَي واَفًََُلوع اَْمس اَحص َْاَن وقْوقاَْـمَلُمَفق َلَه واَلفًَُلوع اَْمس اَََمَعَْق َََْفََحه َعَي صلة اَعْاءَن وَْومن اَل. َواَعصََُُغَوَُا ا َُاءُْلوع اَْمس اََْوب قاَْْزَُا قْاَمعَى َََْحه َاََو ُْلوع اَْمس قاََْعض اَعلماء في قْاَخَاَاَي وََو الحوص وقا اَََْنًثمامْوقا،اََْوبَْاََْوب اََْعََن قَْوقََرْعَي اَف َصلونْصلى ا َلَه وَلْْان َوو الََاب من َصحاب محم:َن ََس ًَََْْا َاَم: َْن ََس َن ماَك قا" ْاَمَْب وفي صحَح مَلَْرْعََن ق قَاْة ما َْرك َحْا َصليْوقا" "" "" """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""..َََا وََا ََزت اََلميَِاََْعََن
50:40: Third: The Almighty’s saying: And during part of the night glorify Him, and at the ends of prostration. There are four opinions on this: The first is the glorification of God Almighty at night. Abu Al-Ahwas said: The second: It is the prayer of the entire night. Mujahid said: The third: It is the two rak’ahs of Fajr. Ibn Abbas said: The fourth: It is the last ‘Isha’ prayer. Ibn Zayd said: Ibn Al-Arabi said: Whoever says that it is the glorification at night is supported by the authentic hadith: “Whoever gets up at night and says: There is no god but God alone, with no partner or associate. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is over all things omnipotent. Glory be to God and praise be to God. There is no god but God, and God is Greatest. There is no power or strength except with God, the Most High, the Almighty.” As for the one who says that it is the night prayer, then the prayer is called glorification because of what it contains of glorifying God, and from this is the glorification of the Duha prayer. As for the one who says that it is the Fajr or ‘Isha’ prayer, it is because they are from the night prayers, and ‘Isha’ is clearer. Fourth: The Almighty said: And after prostration. Umar, Ali, Abu Hurairah, Al-Hasan bin Ali, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Al-Nakha’i, Al-Sha’bi, Al-Awza’i, and Al-Zuhri said: After prostration are the two rak’ahs after Maghrib, and after the stars are the two rak’ahs before Fajr. Al-Awfi narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Abbas narrated it on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Two rak’ahs after Maghrib, after prostration.’” Al-Tha’labi mentioned it with the wording of Al-Mawardi. “It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: I spent a night with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he prayed two rak’ahs before Fajr, then he went out to pray and said: O Ibn Abbas, two rak’ahs before Fajr, after the stars, and two rak’ahs after Maghrib, after prostration.” Anas said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever prays two rak’ahs after Maghrib before speaking, his prayer will be recorded in ‘Illiyyin. Anas said: “He recited in the first rak’ah: ‘Say: O you disbelievers,’ and in the second: ‘Say: He is God, the One.’” Muqatil said: Its time is before the red twilight has set. Ibn Abbas also said: It is Witr. Ibn Zayd said: It is the voluntary prayers after the obligatory prayers, two rak'ahs after every obligatory prayer. An-Nahhas said: The apparent meaning indicates this, but it is better to follow the majority, and this is authentically reported on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him. Abu Al-Ahwas said: It is the glorification after prostration. Ibn Al-Arabi said: It is the strongest opinion in terms of its view. In the authentic hadith: “The Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) used to say after the obligatory prayer: There is no god but God alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is over all things omnipotent. O God, there is no one who can prevent what You have given, nor give what You have prevented, and wealth does not benefit one who is wealthy from You.” It was said that it was abrogated by the obligatory prayers, so no one is obligated to pray except five prayers. This was reported by the congregation. Fifth: Nafi`, Ibn Katheer and Hamza read it with a kasra on the hamza as a verbal noun from the verb adbara ish idbaran if it turned away. The rest read it with a fatha on the plural of dabar, which is the reading of Ali and Ibn Abbas. An example of it is tanab and atnaab or dabar like qifl and aqfal. They used it as an adverbial phrase like I came to you at the end of the prayer and at the end of the prayer. There is no disagreement at the end of By the Mount and and the turning away of the stars that it is with a kasra as a verbal noun and it is the disappearance of their light when the second dawn appears, which is the whiteness splitting from the blackness of the night.
50:41: His Almighty saying, And listen on the Day when the Crier will call from a place nearby. The object of listening is omitted, meaning listen to the call and the sound or the shout, which is the shout of the Resurrection and it is the second trumpet blast, and the caller is Gabriel, and it was said Israfil. Al-Zamakhshari: It was said Israfil blows and Gabriel calls, so he calls for the gathering and says, Come to the accounting. So the call, according to this, will be at the place of assembly. It was also said that he listened to the call of the disbelievers with woe and destruction from a place nearby, meaning everyone hears and no one will be far from that call. Ikrimah said: The caller of the Most Gracious calls, and it is as if he is calling in their ears. It was also said that the nearby place is the rock of Jerusalem. It is said: It is the middle of the earth and the closest earth to the sky by twelve miles. Kaab said: Eighteen miles. The first was mentioned by Al-Qushayri and Al-Zamakhshari and the second by Al-Mawardi. Gabriel or Israfil will stand on the rock and call out for the gathering: O decayed bones and severed joints, O rotten bones and perishing palms and empty hearts and corrupt bodies and flowing eyes, rise to present themselves to the Lord of the Worlds. Qatada said: He is Israfil, the owner of the Trumpet.
50:42: The Day they hear the Shout in truth meaning the Shout of Resurrection. The meaning of coming out is the gathering for the reckoning. That is the Day of Coming Out meaning the Day of Coming Out from the graves.
50:43: Indeed, it is We who bring to life and cause to die. We cause the living to die and bring the dead to life. Prove the truth here.
50:44: The Day the earth will split open from them, scurrying to the crier who will call out the trumpet to Jerusalem That will be an easy gathering for Us meaning easy and simple. The Kufians read tashaqqu with a light shin, deleting the first ta', the rest by assimilating the ta' into the shin. Ibn Muhaisin, Ibn Kathir, and Yaqubiya confirmed the crier in both cases based on the original, and Nafi' and Abu Amr confirmed it in the connection only, and the rest deleted it in both cases. I said: The Sunnah has made this verse more clear. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Muawiyah bin Haidah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a hadith he mentioned, and he pointed with his hand to Ash-Sham and said: From here to here you will be gathered, riding and walking, and you will be dragged on your faces on the Day of Resurrection, with your mouths covered with blood. You will be seventy nations, and you are the best of them and the most honored by God. The first thing that will be revealed about one of you will be his thigh. And in another narration: His thigh and his hand. And Ali bin Ma’bad narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a hadith he mentioned: Then God Almighty will say to Israfil: Blow the blast of resurrection. So he will blow, and the spirits will come out like bees, filling the space between heaven and earth. Then God Almighty will say: By My glory and majesty, every soul will return to its body. So the spirits will enter the earth into the bodies, then they will enter the nostrils and will walk in the bodies as poison walks in the bodies of one who has been bitten. Then the earth will split open and reveal you, and I am the first from whom the earth will split open, and you will come out of it as young men, all of you thirty-three years old. And the language on that day will be Syriac. And he mentioned the hadith, and we have mentioned All of this and more is covered in the ticket, praise be to God.
50:45: The Almighty said, We know best what they say meaning your denial and insults. And you are not a tyrant over them meaning a person who can force them to Islam. Thus the verse was abrogated by the command to fight. The word jabbār comes from jabrīyah and taslālt because jabbār does not mean mugbār just as kharaj does not mean mukhār as narrated by al-Qushayri al-Nahhas. It was also said that the meaning of jabbār is you do not force them but this is wrong because it does not come from af'al and al-Tha'labi narrated and Tha'lab said that the letters fa'āl have come with the meaning of mufā'il and they are irregular. jabbār means mugbār and drāk means mudrik and sara' means musarī and bīka' means mubkā'. 'ādā means ma'd and it was read And I guide you only to the path of right guidance with a shaddah on the shin meaning the guide, which is Moses. And it was said that it is God and likewise it was read As for the ship, it belonged to poor people meaning poor. And Abu Hamid Al-Kharzanji said: The Arabs say: A falling sword means a falling one. And it was said that it is a tyrant and a musaytir as in Al-Ghashiyah You have no control over them. And Al-Farra’ said: I heard from the Arabs who say: He forced him to do something, meaning he subdued him. So the tyrant from this language means subduing, correct. And it was said that the tyrant is from their saying: I forced him to do something, meaning I compelled him, and it is a Kinanite language and they are two languages. Al-Jawhari: And I compelled him to do something, meaning I forced him to do it. And I compelled him also, referring it to compulsion, just as you say: I disbelieved him if you refer it to disbelief. So remind with the Qur’an whoever fears My threat. Ibn Abbas said: They said: O Messenger of God, if you had frightened us, then the verse was revealed: So remind with the Qur’an whoever fears My threat meaning what I have prepared for whoever disobeys Me of punishment. So the threat is the punishment and the promise is the reward. The poet said: Even if I threatened him or promised him, I will break my promise and fulfill my promise. Qatada used to say: O God, make us among those who fear Your threat and hope for Your appointment. The yaa’ was included in My threat to Jacob in both instances, and Warsh included it in the connection but not in the pause. The rest were omitted in both instances. And God knows best. Surah Qaf has been interpreted. Praise be to God.
51:1: The Almighty said: And the scatterers scatter. Abu Bakr Al-Anbari said: Abdullah bin Najiyah narrated to us, Yaqub bin Ibrahim narrated to us, Makki bin Ibrahim narrated to us, Al-Ja`id bin Abd Al-Rahman narrated to us, on the authority of Yazid bin Khusayfah, on the authority of Al-Sa’ib bin Yazid, that a man said to Umar, may God be pleased with him: I passed by a man asking about the interpretation of the difficult parts of the Qur’an, so Umar said: O God, give me power over him. So the man entered upon Umar one day while he was wearing clothes and a turban, and Umar was reciting the Qur’an. When he finished, the man stood up and said: O Commander of the Faithful, what is And the scatterers scatter? So Umar stood up, rolled up his sleeves, and began to flog him, then said: Dress him in his clothes, carry him on a saddlebag, and carry him to his neighborhood. Then let him stand up and give a sermon and say: Subaygh sought knowledge but made a mistake, so he continued to be lowly among his people after having been a master among them. On the authority of Amir bin Wathilah that Ibn Al-Kawwa asked Ali may God be pleased with him and said: O Commander of the Faithful, what is And the scatterers scatter? He said: Woe to you! Ask to understand and do not ask to be stubborn. And the scatterers scatter are the winds. And those carrying heavy loads are the clouds. And those running smoothly are the ships. And those who divide a matter are the angels. Al-Harith narrated on the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him: And the scatterers scatter he said: The winds. And those carrying heavy loads he said: The clouds carry water as the four-legged beasts carry the burden. And those running smoothly he said: The ships are heavy. And those who divide a matter he said: The angels come with different commands, Gabriel with harshness, Michael with mercy, and the Angel of Death comes with death. Al-Farra’ said: It was said that it comes with different commands of fertility, drought, rain, death, and accidents. It is said that the wind scatters the dust, it scatters it, and it scatters it. Then it was said: By the scatterers and what follows are oaths. And when the Lord swears by something, He confirms its honor. It was said that the meaning is By the Lord of the scatterers. The answer is Indeed, what you are promised meaning that which you are promised of good and evil, reward and punishment is true there is no lie in it. The meaning of truthful is truthful. The noun is in the position of a verbal noun. And indeed, the judgment will come to pass meaning the recompense will descend upon you. Then He began another oath and said: By the heaven full of woven paths, you are indeed in a different statement. It was said that the scatterers are the women who give birth because in their offspring are the seeds of creation because they sow children, so they became scatterers. And He swore by them because in their ribs are the best of His righteous servants. And He specified women with that without men, even though each one of them is a scatterer for two reasons: One of them is because they are vessels without men, so because the two seeds meet in them, they were specifically mentioned. Second: That the climax in them takes longer and they are closer to intercourse. The pregnant ones are burdened means clouds. It was said that pregnant women are if they are heavily pregnant. Waqr, with a kasra on the waw, is the weight of the load on the back or in the stomach. It is said: he came carrying his burden and he loaded his camel. Waqr is most often used to carry a mule or a donkey, and the wasq is used to load a camel. This woman is muwaqqar, with a fatha on the qaf, if she carries a heavy load. The palm tree is burdened, its load is heavy. It is said a palm tree is muwaqqar, muwaqqar, and muwaqqarra. It was said muwaqqar, which is not according to analogy because the verb is for the palm tree. It was said: muwaqqar, with a kasra on the qaf, according to the analogy of saying a pregnant woman, because the load of the tree is similar to the load of women. As for muwaqqar, with a fatha, it is unusual. It was narrated in the saying of Labid describing a palm tree: The nerve of the trotters in the Gulf of Mahlam carried from it a respected and gagged one The plural is muwaqir. As for waqar with the fatha, it is the heaviness of the ear. His ear was heavier, waqar means silence. The source of the word is the movement, except that it came with the sukoon. The statement about it was presented in Al-An’am. And the ships that sail with ease means the ships sail with the winds with ease to wherever they are directed. It was said that it is the clouds. And regarding its sailing with ease according to this statement, there are two aspects: One of them is to wherever God Almighty directs it from the lands and regions. The second is the ease of its sailing, and that is well-known among the Arabs, as Al-A’sha said. Her walk from her neighbor's house was like the walk of a cloud, neither slowing down nor hurrying up.
51:2: God Almighty's saying: The pregnant women are a coffin
51:3: The Almighty said: And the flowing ones with ease.
51:4: The Almighty said: And the divisions are a matter.
51:5: God Almighty says: You are only promised something true.
51:6: God Almighty says: And indeed, the judgment will come to pass.
51:7: The Almighty says: And the heaven of interwoven fabrics. It was said that what is meant by the heaven here are the clouds that shade the earth, and it was also said that it is the raised heaven. Ibn Umar said: It is the seventh heaven. This was mentioned by Al-Mahdawi, Al-Tha'labi, Al-Mawardi, and others. There are seven opinions about interwoven fabrics: The first said by Ibn Abbas, Qatadah, Mujahid, and Al-Rabi': It is of good and even character. And Ikrimah said: Have you not seen the weaver when he weaves a garment and does it well? It is said from this that he interwoven the garment, he interwoven it with the broken word habkan, meaning he wove it well. Ibn Al-A'rabi said: Everything that you perfect and do well, you have interwoven it. The second: Of adornment, this was said by Al-Hasan and Saeed bin Jubayr. And from Al-Hasan also: Of stars, which is the third. The fourth said the opinion of Al-Farra': Interwoven fabric breaks everything, like sand when a still wind passes over it, and standing water when a wind passes over it. An iron shield has interwoven fabrics, and curly hair is broken by interwoven fabrics. In the hadith of the Antichrist, his hair is interwoven. Zuhair said: Crowned with the roots of the star, woven by the wind of Kharij, the one who sacrifices his water for you But it is far from the servants so they do not see it. The fifth: The one with intensity. Ibn Zayd said it and he read: And We built above you seven strong ones. The strong-built one is the one with intense creation from the Persians and others. Imru’ al-Qais said: He may carry me in his nose, following the two views, woven into a corridor Another said: Marj al-Din, so I prepared for him the supervisor of the Harak, the knitted Al-Katd In the Hadith: That Aisha, may God be pleased with her, used to tuck herself in under her garment during prayer, meaning she would tighten and secure her garment. Sixth: The one with the impudence, said Khasif, and from it is an impudence garment and an impudence face between the impudence. Seventh: What is meant by the paths is the stream that is in the sky, and it was named thus because it is like the traces of a stream. And the tuck is the plural of tuck. The rajaz poet said: As if the weaver had covered her with a rug, and woven it with silk Al-Habbak and Al-Habikah are the methods of dealing with sand and the like. The plural of Al-Habbak is Habak and the plural of Al-Habikah is Habayik and Al-Habikah is like Al-Abka, which is a grain of gruel, according to Al-Jawhari. It was narrated from Al-Hasan regarding his saying the one who loves: Al-Habbak, Al-Habbak, Al-Habbak, Al-Habbak, Al-Habbak, and Al-Habbak. Al-Habbak was also read like the group. It was narrated from Ikrimah and Abu Majlaz Al-Habbak and Al-Habbak, its singular is Habiqa, and Al-Habbak is a shortened form of it. Al-Habbak, its singular is Habka. Whoever reads Al-Habbak, the singular is Habka like Barqah and Barq or Habka like Dhulmah and Dhulmah. Whoever reads Al-Habbak, it is like Ibil and Ital, and Al-Habbak is a shortened form of it. Whoever reads Al-Habbak, it is anomalous, as there is no verb in the speech of the Arabs, and it is based on the intermingling of languages, as if he broke the Ha’ to break the Ba’, then he imagined Al-Habbak and made the Ba’ a Damma. Al-Mahdawi said all of them.
51:8: The Almighty’s saying, Indeed, you are in a different statement. This is the answer to the oath that is, and the heaven, meaning that you, O people of Mecca, are in a different statement regarding Muhammad and the Qur’an. Some believe and some deny. It was said that it was revealed regarding those who divided. It was said that their disagreement was their saying, He is a magician, rather, He is a poet, rather, He invented it, rather, He is insane, rather, He is a soothsayer, rather, He is a legend of the ancients. It was said that their disagreement was that some of them denied the resurrection and some of them doubted it. It was said that what is meant are the worshippers of idols and statues who acknowledge that God is their Creator and worship other than Him.
51:9: The Almighty says, He who turns away from it will be turned away from it meaning he who turns away from believing in Muhammad and the Quran will be turned away from Al-Hasan and others. It was said that the meaning is from belief from what they meant by their saying is magic, divination, and legends of the ancients. It was said that the meaning is that he will be turned away from that difference from God has protected him afkahu ya'fuquhu afkan, meaning he turned him away and turned him away from something. From this is the saying of the Almighty, Have you come to us to turn us away? Mujahid said that the meaning of Indeed, it is We who sent down the Qur'an and indeed, We will be its guardian is yu'fanunu from afan, and afan is the corruption of the mind. Al-Zamakhshari said: It was read yu'fanunu from afan, meaning he forbids him from haraam from afan al-dar' if he exhausts him from milking the udder. Qutrab said: yukhadu'unu from khada'. Al-Yazidi said: he repels from him from dafa' and the meaning is the same and all of them go back to the meaning of diversion
51:10: The Almighty said, The liars are killed in the interpretation: Cursed are the liars. Ibn Abbas said: meaning, the doubters are killed. He means the priests. Al-Hasan said, they are those who say, We will not be resurrected. The meaning of killed is that these are those who should be called to death by the believers. Al-Farra' said, The meaning of killed is cursed. He said, The liars are the liars who fabricate things they do not know, saying, 'Muhammad is a madman, a liar, a magician, and a poet.' This is a curse upon them, because whoever is cursed by God is like someone who has been killed and destroyed. Ibn Al-Anbari said, We were taught to supplicate against them, meaning, say, 'The liars are killed.' It is the plural of kharis. Kharas means lying, and Kharas means lying. Kharas is also used, meaning, a lie. It is said, Kharas, ikhtras, khalaq, ikhtilaq, bishk, ibtishk, sarj, istarj, and man, meaning a lie. An-Nahhas related this. Kharas is also an estimate of the amount of fresh dates on the palm tree. The palm trees have been harvested. The noun is kharas with a kasra. It is said, How many palm trees have you harvested? and kharas is the one who harvests them. It is common. The origin of kharas is cutting off, as explained previously in Al-An’am. From this comes kharis for the gulf because the water is cut off to it. kharas is the bead of the carrot if it is isolated, because it is cut off from its sisters. And kharas is the wood because it is cut off from its counterparts due to its pleasant scent. And kharas is the one who has hunger and cold because it is cut off from it. It is said: the man is kharas with a kasra, so he is kharas, meaning hungry and chilled. Hunger without cold is not said kharas. Cold without hunger is said kharas. And kharas with a damma and a kasra is a ring of gold or silver, and the plural is kharasan. Included in kharas are the sayings of astrologers and everyone who claims to be conjectural and estimating. Ibn Abbas said: They are the dividers who divided the lands of Mecca and divided the saying about the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to turn people away from believing in him.
51:11: The Almighty says, Those who are in a state of heedlessness. Ghumrah is what covers and conceals something. From this comes the word Ghamr a river that covers meaning it immerses whoever enters it. Among the depths of death. Sahun heedless means distracted and oblivious to the matter of the Hereafter.
51:12: God Almighty says, They ask, ‘When is the Day of Judgment?’ That is, when is the Day of Reckoning? They say that in mockery and doubt about the Resurrection.
51:13: On the Day when they are tested by the Fire means they are burned. This is from their saying You have tested the gold meaning you burned it to test it. The root of test is testing. It was said that it is built on the basis of its addition to something that is not established, and its position is accusative based on the previous estimation, or nominative based on the Day of Judgment. Al-Zajjaj said: He says, I like the day when you are standing and the day when you rise. If you wish, you can open it. It is in the nominative position, so this is in the accusative case, and in the meaning it is nominative. Ibn Abbas said: They are tested means they are tormented. And from this is the saying of the poet: Every man of God's servants is oppressed in the valley of Mecca, subdued and tempted.
51:14: The Almighty said, Taste your trial, meaning it will be said to them, Taste your punishment. Ibn Zayd Mujahid said, Your burning. Ibn Abbas said, Your denial, meaning your recompense. Al-Farra' said, Your punishment, "which you were hastening," in this world. He said this and did not say this because trial here means punishment.
51:15: God Almighty says, Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and springs. When He mentioned the destination of the unbelievers, He mentioned the destination of the believers, meaning that they will be in gardens with flowing springs that are perfect for recreation.
51:16: The Almighty's saying, taking is in the accusative case as a state. What their Lord has given them means what He has given them of reward and various types of honor. This was stated by Ad-Dahhak. Ibn Abbas and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, taking what their Lord has given them means performing the obligatory duties. Indeed, they were before that meaning before they entered Paradise in this world. doers of good with regard to the obligatory duties. Ibn Abbas said, The meaning is that before the obligatory duties were imposed upon them, they were doing good in their deeds.
51:17: It contains five issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: They used to sleep but little of the night. The meaning of they used to sleep is that they sleep. Sleeping at night is sleeping, and naja’a is a light sleep. Abu Qais bin Al-Aslat said: The egg has been laid on my head, so I do not eat sleep except for sleeplessness Amr bin Ma'dikarib said that he was longing for his sister, and that her captivity was Al-Samma Abu Duraid bin Al-Samma. The security of Rayhana, the All-Hearing Caller, keeps me and my companions awake It is said that someone slept, slept, and that someone slept, with the voiced ghayn. This was said by al-Jawhari. There is a difference of opinion as to what was said: an extra conjunction. This was said by Ibrahim al-Nakha’i. The meaning is that they slept a little at night and prayed most of it. Ata’ said: This was when they were commanded to stand in prayer at night. Abu Dharr used to hold back and take a stick to lean on until the permission was revealed: Stand in prayer at night except for a little. So ma is for negation, which is the complete negation of sleep from them. Al-Hasan said: They did not sleep except for a short time at night, and sometimes they became active and worked hard until dawn. It was narrated on the authority of Ya`qub Al-Hadrami that he said: They differed in the interpretation of this verse. Some of them said: They were few means their number was small. Then he began by saying: At some point they slept meaning at some point they slept at night. Ibn Al-Anbari said: This is invalid because the verse only indicates their little sleep, not their small number.
