And if we began with at some point they slept meaning at some point they slept at night, there would not be any praise for them in this because all people slept at night, unless it was something that was denied. I said: According to what some people have interpreted - which is the statement of Ad-Dahhak, that their number was few - the speech is connected to what came before it, from his statement, Indeed, they were before that doers of good, meaning that the doers of good were few. Then he resumed and said, of the night they slept. According to the first and second interpretations, they were but a little of the night would be a renewed address after the completion of what came before it, and the pause would be at they slept. Likewise, if you make little the predicate of was and raise what with little as if he said, they slept a little of the night, then what may be a negative, or it may be with the verb as a verbal noun, or it may be a nominative in place of the name of was, meaning their slept was a little of the night. And the accusative of little if you estimate what as an additional confirmation with they slept on the assumption that they were a little time or a little slept, they slept. If you do not estimate what as an additional word, then his statement little is the predicate of was, and it is not permissible to make it accusative with they slept because if you estimate its accusative with they slept with the assumption of what as a verbal noun, the relative clause is placed before the relative pronoun. Anas and Qatada said in interpreting the verse: It means they used to pray between the two evening prayers, Maghrib and Isha. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: They did not sleep between the two evening prayers. Ibn Wahb said the same. Mujahid said: “It was revealed about the Ansar. They used to pray the two evening prayers in the Prophet’s mosque, peace and blessings be upon him, then they would go to Quba.” Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Al-Hussein said: They did not sleep until they prayed the Isha prayer. Al-Hasan said: It is as if he considered their sleep to be a little compared to their waking up for prayer. Ibn Abbas and Mutraf said: “Say: ‘Not a night will come upon them except that they pray to God in it, either from the beginning or from the middle.’” Second: It was narrated on the authority of one of the worshippers that someone came to him in his sleep and recited to him: How can you sleep at night with a peaceful eye, while you do not know which gathering to attend? It was narrated on the authority of a man from Azd that he said: I used to not sleep at night, so I slept towards the end of the night and behold, I saw two young men who were the most handsome I had ever seen, and they were wearing cloaks. They stopped at each worshipper and gave him a cloak, then they went to the sleeping people and did not give them any cloaks, so I said to them: Give me some of your cloaks, but they said to me: It is not a cloak for clothing, rather it is the pleasure of God that descends upon every worshipper. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Khallad that he said: A friend of mine told me: While I was sleeping one night, the Day of Resurrection was presented to me and I looked at some of my brothers whose faces were radiant and their colors were shining, and they were wearing cloaks unlike other people. I said: Why are these covered while others are naked and their faces are bright while others are covered in dust? Someone said to me: Those whom you saw covered are the ones who pray between the call to prayer and the iqamah, and those whose faces were bright are the ones who stay up late and pray at night. He said: I saw people on camels and I said: Why are these riding while others are walking barefoot? He said to me: These are the ones who stood up to draw closer to God Almighty, and God gave them the best reward for that. He said: I woke up in my dream, Alas for the worshippers, how noble is their standing. Then I woke up from my dream, afraid. Third: The Almighty’s statement, And in the hours before dawn they would seek forgiveness. This is a second form of praise, meaning they would seek forgiveness for their sins. This was stated by Al-Hasan. The hours before dawn are a time when it is hoped that supplications are answered. This has already been discussed in Al-Imran. Ibn Umar and Mujahid said, They would pray at the hours of dawn, so they called the prayer seeking forgiveness. Al-Hasan said, regarding the Almighty’s statement, They used to sleep but little of the night, they extended the prayer from the beginning of the night until the hours of dawn, then they sought forgiveness at the hours of dawn. Ibn Wahb said, “It was about the Ansar, meaning that they would go out from Quba and pray in the mosque of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Ibn Wahb narrated from Ibn Lahi’ah from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, who said, “They used to sprinkle water on the fruits for some of the Ansar, then they would sleep for a little, then they would pray at the end of the night.” Ad-Dahhak: Fajr Prayer Al-Ahnaf bin Qais said: I showed my deeds to the deeds of the people of Paradise, and there were people who had separated from us by a distance whose deeds we could not reach. They slept but little of the night. And I showed my deeds to the deeds of the people of Hell, and there were people in whom there was no good, who denied the Book of God, His Messenger, and the resurrection after death. So we found that the best of us were the people who mixed good deeds with bad ones.
51:19: Fourth: The Almighty’s saying, And in their wealth is a right for the beggar and the deprived. A third form of praise. Muhammad ibn Sirin and Qatadah said that the right here is the obligatory zakat. It was also said that it is a right other than zakat, by which one can maintain family ties, provide for a guest, carry a load, or enrich the deprived. Ibn Abbas said the same because the surah was revealed in Mecca and zakat was made obligatory in Medina. Ibn al-Arabi: The strongest opinion regarding this verse is that it is zakat, because the Almighty said in Surah A beggar asked, “And those in whose wealth is a recognized right * for the beggar and the deprived.” The recognized right is the zakat whose amount, type, and time have been specified by the Lawgiver. As for other than that, for those who believe in it, it is not known because it is not measured, typed, or timed. Fifth: The Almighty says: For the beggar and the deprived. The beggar is the one who asks people because of his poverty. This was stated by Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and others. And the deprived is the one who is deprived of money. There is disagreement about its definition. Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and others said: The deprived is the one who has no share in Islam. Aisha may God be pleased with her said: The deprived is the one who is not able to earn his living. It is said: A man who is deprived, with the letter ra pronounced as fat-ha, meaning he is limited and deprived. This is contrary to the saying: blessed. The earnings of someone are distorted if his livelihood is made difficult for him, as if his provision has been diverted from him. Qatada and Al-Zuhri said: The deprived is the one who is self-sufficient and does not ask people for anything and is not aware of his need. Al-Hasan and Muhammad bin Al-Hanafiyyah said: The deprived is the one who comes after the spoils and has no share in them. It was narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent out an expedition and they captured spoils, then some people came after they had finished, so this verse was revealed: and in their wealth. Ikrimah said: The deprived is the one who has no money left. Zayd ibn Aslam said: It is the one whose fruit, crops, or offspring are destroyed. Al-Qurazi said: The deprived one is the one who is afflicted by a plague. Then he recited: “Indeed, we are losers. Rather, we are deprived.” Similar to it is in the story of the companions of the garden where they said: Rather, we are deprived. Abu Qilabah said: There was a man from the people of Yamamah who had wealth, then a flood came and took his wealth. One of his companions said: This is the deprived one, so they divided it in his favor. It was also said: It is the one who seeks the worldly life and then turns away from it. This is also narrated from Ibn Abbas. Abdurrahman ibn Humayd said: The deprived one is the slave. It was also said: It is the dog. It was narrated that Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz was on the road to Makkah when a dog came, so Umar may God have mercy on him snatched a sheep’s shoulder and threw it to him, saying: They say he is the deprived one. It was also said: It is the one whose maintenance is obligatory due to poverty among the lineage, because he has been deprived of his own earnings until his maintenance is obligatory from the wealth of others. Ibn Wahb narrated from Malik: It is the one who is deprived of provision. This is a good statement because it includes all statements. Al-Sha’bi said to me: Today, seventy years have passed since I had a wet dream. I ask about the deprived. I am no more knowledgeable about it today than I was that day. It was narrated by Shu’bah on the authority of Asim al-Ahwal on the authority of al-Sha’bi. Its root in the language is al-mumnu’, from al-haram, which means prevention. Alqamah said: The sheep are fed on the day of the sheep, wherever you go, and the deprived are deprived Anas reported that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Woe to the rich on the Day of Resurrection from the poor. They will say, Our Lord, they have wronged us in our rights which You have imposed upon us. God Almighty will say, By My glory and majesty, I will bring you near and keep you far away. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited, And in their wealth is a right for the needy and the deprived. Al-Tha’labi mentioned this.
51:20: The Almighty says, And on the earth are signs for those of certain faith. When He mentioned the matter of the two groups, He explained that there are signs on the earth that indicate His ability to resurrect and bring about revival. Among these signs is the resurgence of plants after they had become dry, and among them is that He has determined sustenance for the animals in it, and among them is their travels in the lands where they witness the effects of the destruction that befell the nations that denied. Those of certain faith are those who know and confirm the Oneness of their Lord and the truth of the prophethood of their Prophet. He singled them out for mention because they are the ones who benefit from those signs and contemplating them. God
51:21: God Almighty says, And in yourselves - will you not see? It was said that the meaning is, And on the earth and in yourselves are signs for those of certain faith. Qatadah said, The meaning is, whoever travels on the earth will see signs and lessons, and whoever reflects within himself will know that he was created to worship God. Ibn al-Zubayr and Mujahid said, It means the path of defecation and urination. As-Sa'ib ibn Sharik said, "He eats and drinks from one place and excretes from two places. If he drank pure milk, water and feces would come out of it, so that is the sign within the soul." Ibn Zayd said, "The meaning is that He created you from dust and gave you hearing, sight and hearts. Then, suddenly, you are human beings dispersing." As-Suddi said, And within yourselves means, in your life and death and in what enters and exits of your food. Al-Hasan said, And in old age after youth, and weakness after strength, and gray hair after blackness. It was said, The meaning is, in the creation of yourselves from a sperm-drop, a clot, a lump of flesh, flesh and bone until the soul is breathed in, and in the differences in languages, colors and forms. And other verses, both internal and external. It is enough for you with the hearts and what is established in them of minds and what they are distinguished with of types of meanings and arts and with the tongues and speech and the articulations of letters and sight and limbs and all the limbs and what they come to for what they were created and what is made up in the limbs of the joints for bending and flexing and that if something of them touches, the impotence comes and if it relaxes, humiliation comes down So blessed be God, the best of creators “Do you not see?” meaning the sight of the heart so that they may know the perfection of His power. And it was said that He makes the impotent successful and the decisive one deprived. I said that everything mentioned is intended to be considered. We have already mentioned in the verse of monotheism in Surat Al-Baqarah that there is nothing in the human body, which is the small world, that does not have a counterpart in the large world. We mentioned there the consideration that is sufficient and enriching for whoever ponders.
51:22: The Almighty said, And in the sky is your provision and that which you are promised. Saeed bin Jubair and Ad-Dahhak said, provision here is what comes down from the sky of rain and snow, by which crops grow and creation lives. Saeed bin Jubair said, Every spring that stands is made of snow. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan that whenever he saw a cloud, he would say to his companions, By God, it is your provision, but you are depriving it because of your sins. The scholars of semantics said, And in the sky is your provision means, And in the rain is your provision. Rain is called sky because it descends from the sky. The poet said: If the sky falls on the land of a people, we will take care of it, even if they are angry. Ibn Kaysan said: It means upon the Lord of the heaven is your provision. Similar to it is: And there is no creature on earth but that upon God is its provision. Sufyan al-Thawri said: And in the heaven is your provision. That is, with God in the heaven is your provision. It was said that the meaning is: And in the heaven is the decree of your provision, and what is in it for you is written in the Mother of the Book. Sufyan said: Wasil al-Ahadab read: And in the heaven is your provision, and he said: “Do I not see my provision for the third time in a date palm? He had a brother who had better intentions than him, so he entered with him, and they became two dates. This remained their habit until God separated them by death.” Ibn Muhaisin and Mujahid read: And in the heaven is your provider with an alif, and likewise at the end of it: Indeed, it is God who is the Provider. “And what you are promised.” Mujahid said: It means of good and evil. Someone else said: Of good in particular, and it was said evil in particular, and it was said Paradise. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah al-Dahhak said: And what you are promised of Paradise and Hell. Ibn Sirin said: And what you are promised of the Hour. Al-Rabi’ said the same.
51:23: His Almighty saying, By the Lord of the heaven and the earth, it is the truth. He confirmed what He informed them of regarding the resurrection and the provision He created in the heaven, and He swore by it that it was the truth. Then He confirmed it by saying, Likewise, you speak. He singled out speech from among the other senses, because other senses are susceptible to likening, such as what is seen in a mirror, the impossibility of taste when bile and the like are prevalent, and the ringing and buzzing in the ear. Speech is free from that and is not hindered by echo, because it only occurs after speech has occurred from the speaker, untainted by anything that would confuse it. Some of the wise men said: Just as every person speaks by himself and cannot speak with the tongue of another, so too every person eats his own sustenance and cannot eat the sustenance of another. Al-Hasan said: It has reached me that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God curse the people to whom their Lord swore by Himself, but they did not believe Him. God Almighty said: By the Lord of the heaven and the earth, it is the truth. Al-Asma’i said: I was once coming from the mosque in Basra when a rough, coarse Bedouin appeared on his camel, with his sword slung over his head and his bow in his hand. He approached and greeted him and said: From whom is this man? I said: From the tribe of Asma’. He said: Are you from Asma’? I said: Yes. He said: And from where have you come? I said: From a place where the words of the Most Gracious are recited. He said: And the Most Gracious has words that are recited by humans? I said: Yes. He said: Recite to me some of it. I recited: By the scatterers scatter until His saying: And in the heaven is your provision. He said: O Asma’i, that is enough! Then he went to his camel, slaughtered it, and cut its hide into pieces. He said, Help me to distribute it. So we distributed it to those who came and those who turned away. Then he took his sword and bow, broke them, and placed them under the saddlebags. He turned towards the desert, saying, And in the heaven is your provision and that which you are promised. I hated myself and blamed myself. Then I performed Hajj with Rashid. While I was circumambulating, I heard a soft voice. I turned around and saw a Bedouin, thin and yellow. He greeted me and took my hand and said, Recite to me the words of the Most Gracious. He made me sit behind the Maqam. I recited By the adversaries until I reached the words of God Almighty, And in the heaven is your provision and that which you are promised. The Bedouin said, We have found what the Most Gracious promised us to be true. He said, And is there anything else besides this? I said, Yes, God Almighty says, ‘By the Lord of the heaven and the earth, it is the truth, just as you speak.’ The Bedouin shouted and said, Glory be to God! Who is it that angered the Majestic One so that he swore? Did they not believe him in what he said, until they forced him to swear an oath? He said it three times and his soul left him. Yazid bin Marthad said that a man became hungry in a place where there was nothing, so he said: O God, the provision that You promised me, so bring it to me. So he was satisfied and quenched his thirst without food or drink. Abu Saeed Al-Khudri said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: If one of you were to flee from his provision, it would follow him as death follows him. Al-Tha’labi narrated it in his chain of transmission. In Sunan Ibn Majah, on the authority of Hubbah and Sawa’ bin Khalid, they said: We entered upon the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, while he was working on something, so we helped him with it. Do not despair of provision as long as your heads are shaking, for a person is born red without a husk, then God provides for him. It was narrated that a group of Bedouins planted a crop, and a disaster struck it, so they were sad because of it. A Bedouin woman came out to them and said: What is the matter with you that you have lowered your heads and your hearts are constricted? He is our Lord and He knows us. Our provision is upon Him. He brings it to us wherever He wills. Then she began to say: If there was a rock in the sea, solid, gathered, and smooth A provision for a soul that God has created, that will not split until it delivers to itself everything in it. Or if there was a path between the seven layers, God would have made its ascent easy for the ascender. Until you get what is written on the tablet for you, if you do not get it, it will come to you. I said, and in this meaning is the story of the Ash'aris when they sent their messenger to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he heard the saying of God the Most High: And there is no creature on earth but that upon God is its provision, so he returned without speaking to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he said: The Ash'aris are not more insignificant to God than the creatures, and we have mentioned that in Surat Hud. And Luqman said: O my son, indeed, if it be the weight of a mustard seed and be within a rock, and this has already been mentioned in Luqman, and we have discussed this topic in detail in the book Quanning Greed through Asceticism and Contentment, and praise be to God. This is the true trust that is not tainted by anything, and it is the emptiness of the heart with the Lord, which God has provided for us and has not referred us to anyone other than Him, by His grace and generosity. The Almighty said: Like what you speak The general reading is like in the accusative case, meaning like what you, so it is accusative based on the deletion of the kaf, meaning like your speaking, and ma is redundant, as some of the Kufians said. Al-Zajjaj and Al-Farraa said that it is permissible for it to be accusative for emphasis, meaning a truth has occurred like your speaking, so it is as if it is an adjective for a deleted verbal noun. Sibawayh said that it is constructed when it is added to something that is not established, and ma is redundant for emphasis. Al-Mazini said: Like with ma" is like one thing, so it is constructed with the fatha for that reason. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose it. He said: Because some Arabs always make mithl in the accusative case, so you say, A man like you said to me, and I passed by a man like you, with mithl in the accusative case, meaning like. Abu Bakr, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Al-A’mash read mithl in the nominative case, as an attribute of haqq because it is indefinite, even if it is added to a definite noun, as it is not specific to addition due to the abundance of things that come after them, similarity between similar things occurs. mithl is added to ankum, and ma is redundant, and it is not with what comes after it in the position of a verbal noun, since there is no verb with it to be a verbal noun with. It is permissible for it to be a substitute for haqq.
51:24: The Almighty’s saying, Has there come to you the story of the honored guests of Abraham? He mentioned the story of Abraham, peace be upon him, to show that he destroyed those who denied his signs, just as he did with the people of Lot. Has there come to you? means has it not come to you? It was said that Hall means has like the Almighty’s saying, Has there not come upon man a period of time? The discussion of Abraham’s guests in Hud and Al-Hijr has already been discussed. The honored ones means in the sight of God. Its evidence is the Almighty’s statement: Rather, they are honored servants. Ibn Abbas said: He means Gabriel, Michael, and Israfil. Uthman bin Husayn added: And Raphael, peace be upon him. Muhammad bin Ka’b said: Gabriel was with nine people. Ata’ and a group said: They were three: Gabriel, Michael, and another angel with them. Ibn Abbas said: He called them honored because they were not frightened. Mujahid said: He called them honored because Abraham served them himself. Abdul Wahhab said: Ali bin Ayyad said to me: I have some harissa, what do you think of it? I said: What a good opinion I have of it. He said: Go with us. So I entered the house and the boy called out to find him absent. I was startled by him with the jug and basin and a handkerchief on his shoulder. I said: To God we belong and to Him we shall return. If you had known, O Abu Al-Hasan, that the matter would be like this, he said: Take it easy, for you are honored in our sight, and the honored are served with the soul. Look at the Almighty’s statement: Has there come to you the report of Abraham’s honored guests?
51:25: The Almighty’s saying, “When they entered upon him and said, ‘Peace,’” It was mentioned in Al-Hijr. “He said, ‘Peace,’” meaning, “Peace be upon you.” It is also possible to say, “My matter is peace,” or “My return is peace to you.” The people of Kufa, except for Asim, read it with a kasra on the seen. An unknown people, meaning, You are an unknown people, meaning, strangers we do not know you. It was said that this is because he saw them in a form other than that of humans and not like the angels whom he knew, so he recognized them, so he said, An unknown people. It was also said that he recognized them because they entered upon him without permission. Abu Al-Aaliyah said that he recognized their greeting at that time and in that land. It was also said that he feared them. It is said that he recognized him if he feared him. The poet said: You denied me, but the only thing you denied of the events was gray hair and baldness.
51:26: The Almighty says, He returned to his family. Az-Zajjaj said, meaning he returned to his family. This has already been mentioned in Al-Saffat. It is also said, aragh and artagh meaning to seek. And what do you want? meaning you want and request. aragh ila. "Woe to me! Will I give birth while I am an old woman? They said, 'Thus,'" meaning as we have told you and informed you. "Your Lord said," so do not doubt it. There was a year between the good report and the birth. Sarah had not given birth before that, so she gave birth when she was ninety-nine years old, and Abraham at that time was one hundred years old. This has already been mentioned. "Indeed, it is He who is the Wise, the Knowing." Wise in what He does, Knowing of the interests of His creation.
51:27: The Almighty said, And he brought it near to them, meaning the calf. He said, ‘Will you not eat?’ Qatada said, Most of Ibrahim’s wealth was cows, and he chose them fat for them as an extra measure of honor to them. It was also said that in some languages, the calf is a sheep. Al-Qushayri mentioned it. In As-Sahah: The calf is the offspring of a cow, and calves are the same, and the plural is ‘ajajil, and the female is ‘ajila, according to Abu Al-Jarrah. A cow with a calf is Mu’ajjil, and ‘Ajil is a tribe from Rabi’ah.
51:28: The Almighty said, So he felt fear of them meaning he sensed fear in himself from them. It was also said that he concealed it because they did not enter ihram with his food. It is one of the human morals that whoever enters ihram with someone's food feels safe from him. Amr ibn Dinar said, "The angels said, 'We will not eat except for a price.' He said, 'Eat and pay its price.' They said, 'What is its price?' He said, 'You mention God when you eat and praise Him when you finish.' They looked at each other and said, 'This is why God has taken you as a friend.'" This was mentioned previously in Hud. When they saw the fear in Abraham, they said, 'Do not fear.' They informed him that they were God's angels and messengers. And they gave him good tidings of a learned boy, meaning a son who would be born to him from his wife Sarah. It was also said that when they informed him that they were angels, he did not believe them, so they called upon God, and He revived the calf that he had brought near to them. Awn ibn Abi Shaddad narrated: Gabriel stroked the calf with his wing, so it started running until it joined its mother and the mother of the calf in the house. The meaning of knowledgeable is that after reaching maturity, it will be among those with knowledge of God and His religion. The majority are of the opinion that the one given good tidings was Isaac, while Mujahid alone said: It is Ishmael, and he is nothing, because God the Most High says, And We gave him good tidings of Isaac, and this is the explicit text.
51:29: The Almighty said: Then his wife came in a shriek meaning in a shout and uproar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas and others. From this comes the creaking of the door, which is its sound. Ikrimah and Qatadah said: It is the moaning and groaning. This coming from one place to another was not. Al-Farra' said: It is rather like your saying He came to insult me meaning he began to insult me. It was said: She came in a shriek, meaning a group of women hearing the words of the angels. Al-Jawhari said: A shriek is a shout and a shout, a shriek is a group, and a shriek is intensity from distress and other things. Imru' al-Qais said: So he joined him to the guides and placed their holes in a bundle that did not leave. This verse has three possible meanings. The scorching heat of summer is intense heat. When Sarah heard the good report, she slapped her face, meaning she hit her face with her hand, as women do when they are surprised. This was said by Sufyan al-Thawri and others. Ibn Abbas said: She slapped her face, meaning she slapped it. The root of sakk is striking, sakahu means he hit him. The rajaz poet said: Oh nightingale, come and hit us Al-Amawi said: When a gazelle trots on the ground and crouches, it contracts. And a barren old woman said, meaning, Should I give birth to a barren old woman? Al-Zajjaj said: And she said, ‘I am a barren old woman, so how can I give birth?’ As she said: Woe is me! Shall I give birth when I am an old woman and this?
51:30: "They said, 'Likewise,' meaning as we told you and informed you. 'Your Lord said,' so do not doubt it. There was a year between the good report and the birth, and Sarah had not given birth before that. She gave birth when she was ninety-nine years old, and Abraham was at that time one hundred years old. This has already happened. 'Indeed, He is the Wise, the Knowing.' Wise in what He does, and Knowing of the interests of His creation.
51:31: God Almighty said, He said, ‘What is the matter with you, O messengers?’ When Abraham, peace be upon him, was certain that they were angels by bringing the calf back to life and giving the good report, he said to them, What is the matter with you? meaning, what is your affair and your story, O messengers?
51:32: They said, 'We have been sent to a people of criminals.' He means the people of Lot.
51:33: Let us send down upon them stones of clay, meaning let us throw them at them.
51:34: Marked means marked. It was said: it was striped in black and white, and it was said: black and red. It was also said: Marked means known to be stones of torment. It was also said: on each stone was the name of the one who would perish by it. It was also said: on them were things like rings. All of this was mentioned in Hud. So the stones followed their travelers and their stragglers, and no one escaped them. With your Lord means with God, and He had prepared them to stone whoever He had decreed should be stoned. Then it was said that they were cooked like bricks. Ibn Zayd said this, and this is the meaning of the Almighty's saying: stones of baked clay as explained previously in Hud. It was also said that they are the stones that we see and their origin is clay, and they only become stones by the sun burning them over the ages. He only said of clay to indicate that they are not stones of water, which is hail. This was narrated by Al-Qushayri.
51:35: The Almighty says, So We brought out whoever was in it of the believers. That is, when We wanted to destroy the people of Lot, We brought out whoever was in his people of the believers so that the believers would not perish. This is what the Almighty says, So set out with your family.
51:36: And We found therein none but a house of Muslims meaning Lot and his two daughters, and another omission is meaning We found therein none but the people of a house. It may be said that a noble house refers to the people. His statement therein is a metaphor for the village, but it was not mentioned before because the meaning is understood. Also, His statement, Indeed, We have been sent to a people of criminals indicates the village because the people only live in a village. It was said that the pronoun therein refers to the group, and the believers and the Muslims here are the same, so the wording is the same so as not to be repeated, as He said, I only complain of my suffering and my grief to God, and it was said that faith is the belief of the heart and Islam is submission with the outward appearance, so every believer is a Muslim, but not every Muslim is a believer. He called them believers in the first verse because there is no believer who is not a Muslim. This meaning has been discussed in Surat Al-Baqarah and elsewhere. His statement, The Bedouins said, ‘We have believed.’ Say, ‘You have not believed.’ indicates the difference between faith and Islam, which is what is required by the hadith of Gabriel, peace be upon him, in Sahih Muslim and elsewhere, and we have explained it in more than one place.
51:37: The Almighty says, And We left therein a sign meaning a lesson for the people of that time and those who came after them, similar to it, And We have certainly left therein a clear sign for a people who understand. Then it was said: The sign that was left is the ruined village itself. And it was said that the stacked stones that they were stoned with are the sign. For those who fear because they are the ones who will benefit.
51:38: The Almighty says, And in Moses meaning, We also left in the story of Moses a sign. Al-Farra’ said, It is connected to His statement, “And on the earth are signs and And in Moses “When We sent him to Pharaoh with clear authority” meaning with a clear argument, which is the staff. It was also said that it means with miracles from the staff and other things.
51:39: The Almighty said, Then he turned away with his support, meaning Pharaoh turned away from faith. With his support, meaning with his armies and soldiers. Ibn Zayd said this, and it is the meaning of Mujahid’s strength. From this is his saying, Or he took refuge in a strong support, meaning the strength and the clan. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said, With his strength, and from this is the saying of Antarah: How weak is my support of war, but how old is my time It was said: By himself. Al-Akhfash said: By his side, like the Almighty’s saying: He turned away and distanced himself by his side. Al-Muraij Al-Jawhari said this. The corner of something is its stronger side, and it takes refuge in a strong corner, meaning honor and protection. Al-Qushayri: The corner is the side of the body. This is an expression of exaggeration in turning away from something: And a magician or a madman said, or in the meaning of and because they all said it. Al-Muraij and Al-Farra’ said this. He recited the verse of Jarir: Ath'alaba of the knights or winds that made them equal to Tahya and Al-Khashab Or it may be used in the sense of waw, as in the Almighty’s saying: And do not obey among them a sinner or an ingrate. And waw has the meaning of then marry such women as seem good to you, two, three, or four. All of this has been mentioned before.
51:40: So We seized him and his soldiers for their disbelief and turning away from the faith. Then We cast them i.e., We threw them into the sea, and he was blameworthy meaning Pharaoh because he did something for which he was blameworthy.
51:41: The Almighty said, And among the 'Aad meaning, We left a sign in the 'Aad for whoever reflects. When We sent upon them the barren wind which is the one that does not fertilize clouds or trees and in which there is no mercy, blessing, or benefit. And from this, a barren woman who does not conceive or give birth. Then it was said: It is the south wind. Ibn Abi Dhi'b narrated on the authority of Al-Harith bin Abd Al-Rahman on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: The barren wind is the south wind. Muqatil said it is the south wind as in the Sahih on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: I was aided by the north wind and the 'Aad were destroyed by the south wind. Ibn Abbas said it is the calamities. Ubaid bin 'Umair said its dwelling place was the fourth land, and nothing opened up to the 'Aad from it except the distance between the nostrils of a bull. Ibn Abi Nujayh narrated on the authority of Mujahid also that it is the south wind, and God knows best.
51:42: The Almighty says, It leaves nothing it comes upon but that it makes it like chaff. That is, like something dry and shattered. When a plant dries up and disintegrates, it is called chaff and shatter. Ibn Abbas said, Like something that has perished and decayed. Mujahid said the same. From this comes the poet’s saying: You left me when time had taken away my sight, and I remained like the decayed bone of a palm tree. Qatada said that it is the dry plant that has been trampled on. Abu Al-Aaliyah and Al-Suddi said that it is like crushed dirt, tartar, and ashes. Yaman said that it is the grass that the livestock throw away with their dung. The lip is called rimmah, and the lip is called maqama with a kasra, and the lip with a fatha is a language for it. The origin of the word is from ramah al-azm if it is worn out. You say from it ramah al-azm, yarmu with a kasra, ramah, so it is ramīm. The poet said: He saw the consequences behind that, a disgrace, and I remained like the rotten bone of a palm tree. The word rama in the broken form means worn-out bones. The plural is ramam and ramam. Similar to this verse is destroys everything, as mentioned above.
51:43: The Almighty says, And in Thamud meaning, there is also a lesson and a sign in them when it was said to them, Live enjoying the world for a time meaning until the time of destruction, which is three days, as in Hud 11:Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days. It was said that the meaning of enjoy yourselves is, submit to God and enjoy yourselves until the time of your appointed time.
51:44: They transgressed the command of their Lord meaning they disobeyed the command of God and hamstrung the she-camel. So the thunderbolt seized them meaning death. It was said that it refers to every devastating punishment. Al-Husayn ibn Waqid said: Every thunderbolt in the Qur’an refers to punishment. Umar ibn al-Khattab, Hamid, Ibn Muhaysin, Mujahid, and al-Kisa’i read the word the thunderbolt. It is said that a man was struck by a thunderbolt or a stunned person, meaning he fainted. The sky struck them, meaning it cast a thunderbolt upon them. The thunderbolt also refers to the cry of punishment, as has been mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah and others. And they were looking at it during the day.
51:45: So they were not able to stand up It was said that it means to get up. And it was said that they were not able to bear the punishment of God independently, or to endure it, or to rise up to it, or to repel it from themselves. You say, I will not rise up to this matter meaning, I cannot bear it. Ibn Abbas said: That is, their bodies were gone, but their souls remained in the punishment. And they were not able to defend themselves meaning, to protect themselves from the punishment when they were destroyed, that is, they had no helper.
51:46: The Almighty’s saying, And the people of Noah before. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, and Abu Amr read and the people of Noah in the accusative case, meaning, and in the people of Noah there is also a verse. The rest read it in the accusative case, meaning, And We destroyed the people of Noah. Or it could be in apposition to the ha’ and the mim in took them away or the ha’ in took us away, meaning, so the thunderbolt took them and took the people of Noah. Or We cast them into the sea, and We cast the people of Noah away. Or it could mean, Remember.
51:47: His Almighty saying, And the heaven We constructed with power. When he mentioned these verses, he said: And in the heaven are signs and lessons that indicate that the Creator is capable of perfection. So he connected the matter of the heaven to the story of the people of Noah because they are two signs. The meaning of with power is with strength and ability, according to Ibn Abbas and others. And indeed, We are expanding it. Ibn Abbas said: Able. It was also said that it means, And indeed, We are Possessor of vastness, and by creating it and other things, nothing we desire is restricted to Us. It was also said that it means, And indeed, We are expanding provision for Our creation, according to Ibn Abbas as well. Al-Hasan: And indeed, We are able. It was also narrated from him: And indeed, We are expanding provision with rain. Ad-Dahhak said, We enriched you. His evidence is for the one who is expanded according to his ability. Al-Qutbi said, Possessor of vastness for Our creation. The meanings are close. It was also said, We made spacious between them and the earth. Al-Jawhari said, And a man expanded means he became spacious and wealthy. From this is His Almighty saying, And the heaven We constructed with power, and indeed, We are expanding it. That is, We are wealthy and able, so it includes all the sayings.
51:48: And the earth We have spread out meaning We spread it out like a bed on the surface of the water and extended it. Then excellent are the spreaders meaning we are the best spreaders for them. The meaning of the plural is to glorify. We spread out the bed means we smoothed it out and made it firm. The preparation of matters means making them level and right.
51:49: The Almighty says, And of everything We have created pairs, meaning two different types and kinds. Ibn Zayd said, That is, male and female, sweet and sour, and the like. Mujahid said, "He means male and female, sky and earth, sun and moon, night and day, light and darkness, plain and mountain, jinn and mankind, good and evil, morning and evening, and things of different colors of tastes, smells, and sounds." That is, We made this like that, indicating Our power, and He who is able to do this should be able to repeat it. It was also said, And of everything We have created pairs, so that you may know that the Creator of pairs is One, so that in His description there is no movement or stillness, light or darkness, sitting or standing, beginning or end, since He, the Almighty, is One. There is nothing like Him, "that you may remember."
51:50: The Almighty's saying, "So flee to God. Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner." After what had happened previously of their nations denying their prophets and destroying them, God the Almighty said to His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Say to them, O Muhammad, that is, say to your people, "So flee to God. Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner." That is, flee from disobeying Him to obeying Him. Ibn Abbas said: Flee to God by repenting from your sins and from Him, flee from Him to Him and work in obedience to Him. Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Uthman ibn Affan said: So flee to God means leave Makkah. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: Beware of everything other than God, for whoever flees to anything other than Him cannot protect himself from it. Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: Flee from obeying Satan to obeying the Most Merciful. Al-Junayd said: Satan calls to falsehood, so flee to God and He will protect you from him. Dhu al-Nun al-Misri said: Flee from ignorance to knowledge and from disbelief to gratitude. Amr ibn Uthman said: Flee from yourselves to your Lord. He also said: Flee to what God has already given you and do not depend on your own movements. Sahl ibn Abdullah said: Flee from everything other than God to God. Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner, meaning I warn you of His punishment for disbelief and disobedience.
51:51: The Almighty said, And do not make with God another deity. He ordered Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say this to the people, and he is the warner. It was also said that it is an address from God to the creation. I am to you from Him, meaning from Muhammad and his swords, a warner, meaning I warn you of His punishment and His sword if you associate partners with Me. This was said by Ibn Abbas.
51:52: The Almighty’s saying, Likewise, no messenger came to those before them. This is a consolation for the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, meaning, just as your people denied you and said, He is a magician or a madman, so did those before them deny and say the same. The kaf in Likewise can be accusative, assuming I warn you with a warning like the warning of the messengers who came before me who warned their people, or nominative, assuming the matter is likewise, meaning like the first. The first is to frighten those who disobeyed Him from among the monotheists, and the second is to frighten those who associated partners with Him from among the atheists. The completion is based on his saying, Likewise, as reported by Ya’qub and others.
51:53: The Almighty says, They enjoined it upon one another. That is, the first of them enjoined upon the last of them to deny it, and they conspired against it. The alif is for rebuke and amazement. Rather, they are a transgressing people. That is, they did not enjoin one another, but rather transgression brought them together, which is exceeding the limit in disbelief.
51:54: The Almighty says, Then turn away from them, meaning, turn away from them and forgive them. You will not be blamed before God, because you have done what was required of you in conveying the message.
51:55: Then this was abrogated by the saying of the Most High: And remind, for indeed, the reminder benefits the believers. It was said that it was abrogated by the verse of the sword. The first is the saying of Ad-Dahhak, because he was commanded to turn to them with admonition. Mujahid said: Then turn away from them, so turn away from them. For you are not to be blamed, meaning your Lord will not blame you for any shortcomings on your part. And remind, meaning with admonition, for admonition benefits the believers. Qatadah said: And remind with the Qur’an, for the reminder with it benefits the believers. It was said that he reminded them of the punishment and the days of God. He specified the believers because they are the ones who will benefit from them.
51:56: His statement, the Most High, And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me. It was said that this is specific to those who were previously known by God to worship Him, so He came with the general wording, meaning specificity, and the meaning is, And I did not create the people of happiness from among the jinn and mankind except to worship Me. Al-Qushayri said, "The verse has been specifically made specific, because the insane and the children were not commanded to worship Me, so it could be said that He intended worship from them. And God, the Most High, said, "And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind. And whoever was created for Hell is not among those created for worship, so the verse is applied to the believers among them, and it is like His statement, the Most High, The desert Arabs said, 'We believe.'" But a group of them said, as mentioned by Ad-Dahhak, Al-Kalbi, Al-Farra', and Al-Qutbi. And in the reading of Abdullah, "And I did not create the jinn and mankind from the believers except to worship Me." And Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: That is, I did not create the jinn and mankind except to command them to worship Me. Al-Zajjaj relied on this statement and it is indicated by the statement of God the Almighty: And they were commanded only to worship one God. If it is said, how could they disbelieve when He created them to acknowledge His Lordship and to humble themselves before His command and will? It is said that they humbled themselves before His decree upon them, because His decree is binding upon them and they are not able to resist it. Only those who disbelieved opposed them by doing what He commanded them to do. As for humbleness before His decree, then it is not impossible. And it is said, Except that they should worship means except that they should acknowledge Me in worship willingly or unwillingly. Narrated by Ali ibn Abi Talha from Ibn Abbas. So, the unwillingness is what is seen in them from the traces of the craftsmanship of Mujahid except that they should know Me. Al-Tha’labi: This is a good statement, because if He had not created them, then His existence and Oneness would not have been known. The evidence for this interpretation is the statement of the Most High: And if you ask them, ‘Who created them?’ they will surely say, ‘God.’ “And if you ask them, ‘Who created the heavens and the earth?’ they will surely say, ‘The Exalted in Might, the Knowing.’” Verses similar to this are also reported by Mujahid. Zayd ibn Aslam also said: Except to command and forbid them. This is what they were created with of misery and happiness. He created the happy ones among the jinn and mankind for worship, and He created the wretched ones among them for disobedience. Al-Kalbi also said: Except to make them One. As for the believer, he makes Him One in times of hardship and ease. As for the disbeliever, he makes Him One in times of hardship and affliction, but not in times of blessing and ease. This is indicated by the statement of the Most High: And when waves cover them like canopies, they supplicate God, sincere to Him in religion. And Ikrimah said: Except to worship and obey Him, so I reward the worshipper and punish the denier. It was said that the meaning is: Except to enslave them. The meanings are close. You say, Abd is between Ubuddah and Ubuddah. The root of Ubudh is submission and humiliation, and enslavement is humiliation. It is said: A paved path. He said: Functional function above the temple And servitude means enslavement, which is to take him as a slave. Likewise, servitude and worship mean obedience and devotion means asceticism. So the meaning of to worship is to be humbled, submissive and worshipped.
51:57: I do not want from them any provision from the connection of meaning provision, rather I am the Provider and the Giver. Ibn Abbas and Abu al-Juza' said: It means I do not want them to provide for themselves nor to feed themselves. It was also said that the meaning is I do not want My servants to provide for themselves nor to feed them.
51:58: Indeed, it is God who is the Provider. Ibn Muhaisin and others read the Provider "the Possessor of strength" meaning the severe and powerful. Al-A'mash, Yahya ibn Waththab and Al-Nakha'i read "the strong" in the accusative case as an adjective for strength. The rest read it in the nominative case as an adjective for "the Provider or the Possessor from His saying the Possessor of strength or it could be the predicate of a deleted subject or it could be an adjective for the noun of in" in the position or a predicate after a predicate. Al-Farra' said that his right was "the strong" so he mentioned it because he used it to mean something twisted and tightly woven. It is said: a strong rope. Al-Farra' recited: For every age I have worn a garment until my head is covered with a gray mask From Rita and Al-Yamna Al-Ma'saba He mentioned the mu'asab because the right hand is a type of clothing. From this chapter is the Almighty's saying: "But whoever receives an admonition meaning admonition, and the wrongdoers will be seized by the shriek" meaning the shouting and the sound.
51:59: The Almighty said, Then for those who did wrong meaning those who disbelieved from among the people of Mecca will be punished with sins like the sins of their companions meaning a share of punishment like the share of the disbelievers from the previous nations. Ibn al-A'rabi said, A day of sins means a long, never-ending evil. The root of sins in the language is a large bucket. They used to draw water and divide it into shares, so it was said that sins have a share. From this, the rajaz poet said: We have sins and you have sins. If you refuse, then we have the heart. Alqamah said: Every day I have been blessed with a blessing, so a portion of your blessings are due to sins. Another said: By your life, death knocks on every son of a father, and among them are sins. Al-Jawhari and the sins of the long-tailed horse, and the sins are the portion and the sins are the meat of the lower back, and the sins are the bucket full of water. Ibn Al-Sikkit said in it water close to being full, it is feminine and masculine and it is not called it when it is empty sins, and the plural in the smallest number is adhanba and the many are dhanayib like camels and female camels. So they do not hasten meaning they do not hasten the punishment to descend upon them, because they said, O Muhammad, Then bring us what you promise us, if you should be of the truthful. So what descended upon them on the day of Badr was what He fulfilled His promise with and hastened His vengeance upon them, then for them in the hereafter is the eternal punishment and the everlasting disgrace that has no end, no end, no limit and no perishing.
51:60: The Almighty said, So woe to those who disbelieve from the Day they are promised. Surah Adh-Dhariyat has been interpreted, and praise be to God.
52:1: The Almighty said, And the Mount. Mount is the name of the mountain upon which God spoke to Moses. God swore by it to honor and glorify it and to remind us of the signs it contains. It is one of the mountains of Paradise. Ismail bin Ishaq narrated: Ismail bin Abi Uways told us, Kathir bin Abdullah bin Amr bin Auf told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, that he said: "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Four mountains are among the mountains of Paradise, and four rivers are among the rivers of Paradise, and four great battles are among the great battles of Paradise. It was said, 'What is the greatest mountain?' He said, 'Mount Uhud loves us and we love it, and Mount Tur is a mountain among the mountains of Paradise, and Lebanon is a mountain among the mountains of Paradise, and al-Judi is a mountain among the mountains of Paradise.'" He mentioned the hadith, and we have already discussed it in the book, At-Tadhkirah. Mujahid said, The Mount is the mountain in Syriac, and what is meant by it is Mount Sinai. As-Suddi said the same. Muqatil bin Hayyan said, They are two mountains, one of them is called Mount Sinai and the other Mount Zayta because figs and olives grow on them. It was said that it is a mountain in Madyan and its name is Zubayr. Al-Jawhari said that Zubayr is the mountain on which God spoke to Moses, peace be upon him. I said: Madyan is in the Holy Land, and it is the village of Shuaib, peace be upon him. It was said that every mountain that produces vegetation is a mountain, and that which does not produce vegetation is not a mountain. Ibn Abbas said: It has already been fully discussed in Surat Al-Baqarah.
52:2: His Almighty saying, And a Book inscribed meaning written, meaning the Qur'an, which the believers read from the copies of the Qur'an, and the angels read it from the Preserved Tablet, as God Almighty said, Indeed, it is a noble Qur'an, in a protected book. It was also said that it means all the books revealed to the prophets, and each book was on parchment, which its people would spread out to read. Al-Kalbi said, It is what God wrote for Moses with his own hand from the Torah, and Moses would hear the scratching of the pen. Al-Farra' said, "It is the scrolls of deeds, so whoever takes their scroll in their right hand and whoever takes their scroll in their left, its counterpart is: "And We will produce for him on the Day of Resurrection a scroll which he will find spread out. And His saying, And when the scrolls are spread out," it was also said that it is the scroll that God Almighty wrote for His angels in heaven, so that they may read in it what was and what will be. It was also said that what is meant is what God wrote in the hearts of the faithful believers, its explanation is, "Those are the ones in whose hearts He has decreed faith." I said: This statement is permissible because he used the word hearts to refer to parchment. Al-Mubarrad said that parchment is what is thinned from the skin for writing on, and manshur is the extended one. Al-Jawhari said the same in Al-Sahah and said that parchment with the fat-ha is what is written on, and it is thin leather.
52:3: And from this is the saying of God Almighty, On spread parchment. And parchment is also the great one of the turtles. Abu Ubaidah said, and its plural is parchments. The intended meaning is what Al-Farra’ said, and God knows best. And every page is parchment because of the thinness of its edges. And from this is the saying of Al-Mutalammis: It is as if she is from the past, and her book is written As for slavery with a kasra, it is the property. It is said that a slave is a slave. Al-Mawardi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that slavery with a fatha is what is between the east and the west.
52:4: God the Almighty says: And the Frequented House Ali, Ibn Abbas and others said that it is a house in the heaven opposite the Kaaba. Seventy thousand angels enter it every day and then exit it, never returning to it. Ali may God be pleased with him said: It is a house in the sixth heaven. It was also said that it is in the fourth heaven. Anas ibn Malik ibn Sa'sa'ah narrated that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I was brought to the fourth heaven and the Frequented House was raised for us. It is opposite the Kaaba. If it were to fall on it, seventy thousand angels enter it every day. If they exit it, they would never return to it. Al-Mawardi mentioned this. Al-Qushayri narrated from Ibn Abbas that it is in the lowest heaven. Abu Bakr Al-Anbari said that Ibn Al-Kawwa' asked Ali may God be pleased with him: What is the Frequented House? He said: It is a house above the seven heavens under the Throne, called Ad-Dhirah. This is also in As-Sahah. Ad-Dhirah with a dammah is a house in the heaven, and it is the Frequented House, according to Ibn Abbas. Its population is due to the large number of angels who visit it. Al-Mahdawi said about it: It is parallel to the Throne. And in Sahih Muslim, “On the authority of Malik bin Sa’sa’ah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the hadith of the Night Journey: Then he was taken up to the Frequented House, and I said, ‘O Gabriel, what is this?’ He said, ‘This is the Frequented House, which is entered every day by seventy thousand angels. If they leave it, they will never return to it.’” And he mentioned the hadith. And in a hadith confirmed on the authority of Anas bin Malik that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I came to Al-Buraq.” The hadith includes: Then he ascended with us to the seventh gate, and Gabriel, peace be upon him, asked for permission. It was said, Who is this? He said, Gabriel. It was said, And who is with you? He said, Muhammad. It was said, And has he been sent to him? He said, He has been sent to him. So it was opened for us, and there I saw Abraham, peace be upon him, leaning his back against the Frequented House, and there are seventy thousand angels entering it every day, and they will never return to it.” And on the authority of Ibn Abbas also, he said: God has fifteen houses in the heavens and the earths, seven in the heavens and seven on the earths, and the Kaaba, and all of them are opposite the Kaaba. Al-Hasan said: The Frequented House is the Kaaba, the Sacred House, which is frequented by people. God populates it every year with six hundred thousand. If people are unable to do that, God will complete it. By the angels, and it is the first house that God established for worship on earth. Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: The Frequented House was on earth in the place of the Kaaba in the time of Adam, peace be upon him. When the time of Noah, peace be upon him, came, he ordered them to perform Hajj, but they refused and disobeyed him. When the water overflowed, it was raised and placed parallel to it in the lowest heaven. Seventy thousand angels visit it every day, and they do not return to it until the Trumpet is blown. He said: So God, the Almighty, the Majestic, designated for Abraham the site of the House where it had been. God, the Almighty, said: “And when We designated for Abraham the site of the House, [saying], ‘Do not associate anything with Me and purify My House for those who perform Tawaf and those who stand [in prayer] and those who bow and prostrate.’”
52:5: And the raised ceiling means the sky. He called it a ceiling, because it is to the earth as the ceiling is to the house. Its explanation is: And We made the sky a protected ceiling. Ibn Abbas said: It is the Throne and it is the ceiling of Paradise.
52:6: And the sea that is set ablaze. Mujahid said: The one that is kindled. It was mentioned in the hadith: The sea will be set ablaze on the Day of Resurrection and will be fire. Qatada said: The filled one. The grammarians recited for An-Namir ibn Talib: If he wanted to go up to the fire place, he would see the spring of sesame around it. He wants to see a lit and filled spring. It is possible that the filled one is fire, and it would be like the previous statement. Ad-Dahhak, Shimr ibn Atiyyah, Muhammad ibn Ka’b and Al-Akhfash also said that it is the lit and heated one, like the lit oven. From this it is said: the one who is lit is lit. The evidence for this interpretation is the statement of God the Almighty: And when the seas are lit. That is, the oven is lit. I lit it with a lit fire, meaning I heat it up. Sa’id ibn Al-Musayyab said: Ali may God be pleased with him said to a Jewish man: Where is Hell? He said: The sea. He said: I see you as none but truthful, and he recited: And the sea is lit. “And when the seas are lit” is lightened. Abdullah ibn Amr said: One should not perform ablution with sea water because it is the layer of Hell. Ka’b said: The sea will be lit tomorrow and will increase in the fire of Hell. This is one statement. Ibn Abbas said: The lit one whose water has gone. Abu Al-Aaliyah said the same. Atiyyah and the poet Dhu al-Rummah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: A nation went out to draw water and said: The Cistern is emptied, meaning empty. Ibn Abi Dawud said: Dhu al-Rummah has no hadith except this one. It was also said that emptied means empty, the proof for which is: And when the seas are made to gush forth meaning the earth dries them up so that no water remains in them. A third statement was made by Ali may God be pleased with him and Ikrimah. Abu Makin said: I asked Ikrimah about the emptied sea and he said: It is a sea below the Throne. Ali said: Under the Throne there is thick water. It is called the Sea of Life, and it rains on its servants for forty mornings after the first Trumpet blast, and they grow in their graves. Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: The emptied is the one that mixes fresh water with salt. I said: The meaning of fajarat in one of the two interpretations goes back to this, meaning that its fresh water flowed into its salt water. And God knows best. And it will come. Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The imprisoned is the one who is confined.
52:7: Indeed, the punishment of your Lord will surely come to pass. This is the answer to the oath, meaning it will come to pass upon the polytheists. Jubayr ibn Mut'im said: I came to Medina to ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the prisoners of Badr. I came upon him while he was reciting in the sunset prayer, By the Mount, up to His saying, "Indeed, the punishment of your Lord will surely come to pass. There is none to avert it." It was as if my heart had split open. I submitted out of fear of the punishment descending, and I did not think that I would get up from my place until the punishment had befallen me. Hisham bin Hassan said: Malik bin Dinar and I went to Al-Hasan and there was a man with him reciting By the Mount until he reached “Indeed, the punishment of your Lord will surely come to pass. There is none to avert it.” So Al-Hasan wept and his companions wept, and Malik began to tremble until he fainted. When Bakkar was appointed as a judge, two men came to him disputing, and one of them was accused of swearing an oath. He wanted to reconcile between them and give his opponent something from his own pocket in exchange for his oath, but he refused except the oath, so he made him swear by the beginning of By the Mount until he said to him, Say, ‘Indeed, the punishment of your Lord will surely come to pass,’ if you are lying. So he said it and went out and was broken immediately.
52:8: God Almighty says: There is none to repel it.
52:9: The Almighty’s saying, On the Day when the sky will sway violently. The agent in On the Day is to occur, meaning the punishment will befall them on the Day of Resurrection, which is the day when the sky will sway. Linguists said: Mara means that something moved, came, and went, just as the tall palm tree is overtaken by a wave, and the dates are the same. Ad-Dahhak said, They surge into one another. Mujahid said, They surge into one another. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Akhfash said, They are overturned. And he recited to Al-A’sha: As if her walk from her neighbor's house was like a cloud, neither slowing down nor hurrying up. It was said that it runs, and from this is the saying of Jarir: The blood of the dead is still flowing in the Tigris until the water of the Tigris becomes cloudy. Ibn Abbas said: The sky will be in turmoil on that day with everything in it and will be disturbed. It was also said: Its people will revolve in it and some of them will surge into others. The path is also called the turmoil, and from this is the saying of Tarafa: The wave is the wave, and a she-camel is swift. The camel’s forearms sway when they waver on its side. The poet said: On the back of a mortar horse The mortar is the side and their saying: I do not know if he went to Ghare or Mar, meaning he went to Ghare or Dar and then returned to Najd. And the dust in the wind is called Al-Murr. It was said that the sky here is the universe and its Murr is the disorder of its system and the difference in its path, said Ibn Bahr.
52:10: And the mountains will move Muqatil said: They will move from their places until they are level with the ground. It was also said: They will move like the moving clouds in this world today. Its explanation is: And you will see the mountains and think them rigid, while they will pass like the passing of clouds. This meaning was previously mentioned in Al-Kahf.
52:11: So woe on that Day to the deniers. Woe is a word said to someone who is doomed, and the letter fa was added because the statement implies retribution.
52:12: Those who are engaged in idle talk meaning in hesitating about falsehood, which is their engagement in the matter of Muhammad by denying it. It was also said: in engaging in worldly matters, they are playing, not remembering an account or a reward. This was mentioned in Bara'ah.
52:13: The Almighty’s saying, The Day they are called is a substitute for That Day and They are called means they are pushed into Hell with force and violence. It is said: I pushed him away means I pushed him away. And from this is the Almighty’s saying, Then that is he who drives away the orphan. And in the interpretation: The keepers of Hell will chain their hands to their necks and gather their forelocks to their feet, then they will push them into the Fire, pushing them on their faces and squeezing them around their necks until they return to the Fire. Abu Raja’ al-Attardi and Ibn al-Sameeq read The Day they are called to the Fire of Hell as a softening of the call, so when they come close to the Fire the keepers will say to them.
52:14: This is the fire which you used to deny in this world.
52:15: The Almighty’s saying, Is this bewitched? is a question that means rebuke and reprimand. That is, it will be said to them, Is this bewitched that you see now with your eyes, or do you not see? It was said that or means rather, that is, rather, you did not see in the world and did not understand.
52:16: The Almighty says, Enter it, meaning the keepers will say to them, Taste its heat by entering it. "Whether you are patient or not, it is all the same for you, meaning whether you have patience in it or not, so it is all the same is its predicate, meaning whether you are impatient or patient, nothing will benefit you, as He informed us that they will say, It is all the same for us whether we are impatient or patient. You will only be recompensed for what you used to do."
52:17: God Almighty says, Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and pleasure. When He mentioned the state of the unbelievers, He also mentioned the state of the believers.
52:18: Fakihin means those with many fruits. It is said: A man is Fakih meaning he has fruits, just as it is said of Ibn wa Tamer, meaning he has milk and dates. He said: You deceived me and claimed that you are the son of a summer warrior Meaning: One with milk and dates. Al-Hasan and others read it as fakahin without an alif, and its meaning is admiring and soft, according to Ibn Abbas and others. It is said: a man fakahu with a kasra, so he is faka if he is of a good nature and joking. Fakkah is also the arrogant and haughty person. This has been discussed in Ad-Dukhan with what He gave them, meaning what He gave them, and their Lord protected them from the punishment of Hellfire.
52:19: Eat and drink that is, they will be told that at ease. Enjoyment is that which is not marred by bitterness, distress, or turbidity. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, may you be blessed with what you have attained at ease. It was also said: That is, may you enjoy the delights of Paradise at ease. It was also said: That is, eat and drink at ease, so it is an adjective in the place of a verbal noun. It was also said: At ease, that is, lawful. It was also said: There is no harm in it or misfortune. It was also said: At ease, that is, you will not die, for that which does not remain, or that which a person does not remain with, is marred but not at ease.
52:20: The Almighty says, Reclining on couches. Couch is the plural of bed. There is an omission in the speech, the meaning being: Reclining on cushions of couches lined up. Ibn al-A'rabi said, meaning connected to each other until they become a row. And in the narrations, it is described as being arranged in the sky at such and such a length, so when the servant wants to sit on it, it humbles itself before him, but when he sits on it, it returns to its state. Ibn Abbas said, it is couches of gold crowned with emeralds, pearls, and rubies, and the couch is between Mecca and Aila. And We married them to fair maidens with large, beautiful eyes means We coupled them with them. Yunus ibn Habib said, The Arabs say, 'He married him to a woman' and 'He married a woman', and it is not from the speech of the Arabs to marry a woman. He said, and the statement of God, the Almighty, And We married them to fair maidens with large, beautiful eyes means We coupled them with them, from the statement of God, the Almighty, Gather together those who did wrong and their spouses meaning and their companions. Al-Farra' said, I married a woman is a language for Azd Shanu'a, and the meaning of the wide-eyed houris has been discussed previously.
52:21: His Almighty saying, And those who have believed and whose offspring have followed them, the general reading has been wata'abatahum with a connected alif, a shaddah on the ta', a fathah on the 'ayn, and a sukoon on the ta'. Abu 'Amr read wata'abnahum with a sukoon on the ta' and the 'ayn, and a noon, taking into consideration His saying, We joined them so that the speech would be consistent. As for His saying, their offspring, the first one was read by Ibn 'Amir, Abu 'Amr, and Ya'qub in the plural form. It was narrated from Nafi' except that Abu 'Amr broke the ta' as the object and made the rest of them damma. The rest read dharihituhum with a singular pronoun and a damma on the ta', which is the well-known reading from Nafi'. As for the second one, Nafi', Ibn 'Amir, Abu 'Amr, and Ya'qub read it with a kasrah on the ta' as a plural. The rest of them dharihituhum with a singular pronoun and a fathah on the ta'. There are different interpretations regarding its meaning. Four narrations have been narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, the first of which is that he said: God will raise the offspring of the believer with him in his rank in Paradise, even if they are below him in deeds, so that his eye may be comforted by them, and he recited this verse. It was narrated by An-Nahhas in An-Nasikh wa-l-Mansukh, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God, the Almighty, will raise the offspring of the believer with him in his degree in Paradise, even if he did not reach it through his deeds, so that his eyes may be comforted by them. Then he recited: And those who believe and whose offspring follow them in faith, the verse. Abu Ja’far said: So the hadith became attributed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this is how it should be, because Ibn Abbas would not say this except on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, because it is a statement on the authority of God, the Almighty, of what He does, meaning that He, may His praise be exalted, revealed it. Az-Zamakhshari: So God will gather for them all kinds of happiness through their happiness in themselves, and through marrying the houris, and through the company of believing brothers, and through the gathering of their children and offspring with them. It was also narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: Indeed, God joins the believer’s young offspring who have not yet reached faith. Al-Mahdawi said that offspring applies to both young and old. If offspring here is meant to be for young people, then His statement, through faith, would be in the position of a state of the two objects, and the meaning would be through faith from the fathers. If offspring is meant to be for adults, then His statement, through faith, would be a state of the subjects. The third statement from Ibn Abbas is that what is meant by those who believed are the Muhajireen and Ansar, and offspring are the followers. In another narration from him: If the fathers are of a higher rank, God raises the children to the fathers, and if the children are of a higher rank, God raises the fathers to the sons, so the fathers are included in the name of offspring, as in His statement, And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship. It was also narrated from Ibn Abbas that it goes back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, one of them will ask about his parents, his wife, and his children. It will be said to them that they did not reach what you reached. He will say, “O Lord, I worked for myself and for them.” Then he will be commanded to join them with him. Khadija may God be pleased with her said: I asked the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about two of my sons who died during the pre-Islamic era. He said to me: They are in Hell. When he saw the hatred on my face, he said: If you saw where they were, you would hate them. She said: O Messenger of God, are my children from you? He said: In Paradise. Then he said: The believers and their children are in Paradise, and the polytheists and their children are in Hell. Then he recited: And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith 2:170. And We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds 2:170. That is, We did not deprive the children of the reward for their deeds because of their short lives, nor did We deprive the fathers of anything of the reward for their deeds by including their offspring in them. The ha’ and the mim refer to the verse: And those who believed 2:170. Ibn Zayd said: The meaning is: And whose offspring followed them in faith 2:170. We included with the offspring their young children who had not yet reached the age of action. So the ha’ and the mim, according to this statement, refer to the offspring. Ibn Kathir recited and We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds 2:170. And the rest opened and on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said, Alatanahum with a long vowel, Ibn al-A’rabi said, Alatah ya’alitahu alta and Alatah yu’alitahu ilata “Walatu yalituhu lita” all of them if it reduces it. In the Sahih, Walatuhu ‘an wajihah yaltuhu and Walatuhu yalituhu means it prevented him from his face and diverted him. Likewise, Alatah ‘an wajih is a verb and af’al with one meaning. It is also said, He did not diminish anything from his work, meaning he did not diminish it, like Alatah. It has already been mentioned in Al-Hujurat. Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned. It was said that it refers to the people of Hell. Ibn Abbas said, The people of Hell are held in pledge for their deeds, and the people of Paradise are destined for their bliss. For this reason, he said, Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned, except the companions of the right hand. It was said that it is general and every person is held in pledge for his deeds, so no one will be deprived of the reward for his deeds. As for the increase in the reward for the deeds, it is a favor from God. It is possible that this is in the offspring who did not believe, so they will not join their believing fathers, but will be held in pledge for their disbelief.
52:22: God Almighty says, And We provided them with fruits and meat of whatever they desired. That is, We provided them with more of that from God, in addition to what they had before.
52:23: The Almighty says, They will compete over a cup therein meaning they will take it from one another, meaning the believer, his wives, and his servants in Paradise. The cup is the vessel of wine and any vessel filled with a drink or other thing. When it is empty, it is no longer called a cup. Evidence of the competition and the cup in the language is the statement of Al-Akhtal: And a drinker who profits from the cup, make me regret neither the presence nor the bracelet I quarreled with him for the sweet scent of the comprehensive wine, and the chickens crowed and the time came for the journey Imru' al-Qais said: When we argued and I allowed it, I grabbed a leaning branch with its branches. This has already been mentioned in Surah al-Saffat 37:There is no idle talk in it meaning in the cup, meaning no idle talk will take place between them. Nor sin nor anything in which there is sin. Nor sin is the root word for sin. That cup will not make them sinful because it is permissible for them. It was also said: Nor sin means in Paradise. Ibn Ata’ said: Any idle talk will take place in a gathering located in the Garden of Eden, and their drinkers will be angels, and their drink will be in remembrance of God, and their basil and greetings will be from God, and the people are the guests of God. Nor sin means no lying. Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak said: meaning they will not lie to one another. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaisin and Abu Amr read: Nor sin with a fat-ha at the end, while the rest read it with a dhammah and tanween. This has already been mentioned in Surah Al-Baqarah when God says: “Neither friendship nor intercession, nor [any] intercession. And the disbelievers.” All praise is due to God.
52:24: The Almighty's saying, And there will circulate among them young boys of theirs, meaning with fruits, gifts, food and drink. The evidence for this is, They will be circulated among them with trays of gold, "They will be circulated among them with a cup of pure wine." Then it was said that they are the children of their children who preceded them, so God, the Most High, comforted their eyes with them. And it was said that they are those whom God, the Most High, served from the children of others. And it was said that they are young boys created in Paradise. Al-Kalbi said that they will never grow up. "As if in beauty and whiteness, they were pearls hidden" in shells, and the hidden is the protected.
