And the Almighty’s saying, And there will circulate among them immortal boys. It was said that they are the children of the polytheists and they are the servants of the people of Paradise, and there is no fatigue in Paradise nor any need for service, but He informed that they are at the ultimate level of bliss. “On the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her that the Prophet of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: The lowest status of the people of Paradise is he who calls out to one of his servants, and a thousand answer him, all of them, ‘At your service, at your service.’” And on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar that the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: There is no one from the people of Paradise except that a thousand servants will strive for him, each servant doing a job that his master is not doing.” And on the authority of Al-Hasan that they said: O Messenger of God, if the servant is like a pearl, then what will be the one who is served? He said: The distance between them is like the distance between the moon on a full moon and the smallest of the stars.” Al-Kisa’i said: I concealed something means I covered it and protected it from the sun, and I concealed it in my soul means I kept it secret. Abu Zaid said: Kannanatuhu and Kannanatuhu mean in the shelter and in the soul together. You say: I concealed knowledge and I concealed it, so it is mukanun and makana, and I concealed the girl and “I concealed her, so she is mukanun and makana.
52:25: The Almighty said, And some of them will turn to others, asking one another. Ibn Abbas said: When they are raised from their graves, they will ask one another. It was also said: In Paradise, they will ask one another, meaning they will remember the fatigue and fear of the consequences they faced in this world. And they will praise God for removing their fear. It was also said that some of them will say to one another, How did you reach this exalted station?
52:26: They said, 'Indeed, we were before, among our families, fearful.' That is, each of the people responsible said to his questioner, Indeed, we were before, that is, in this world, fearful and apprehensive of God's punishment.
52:27: So God bestowed His favor upon us with Paradise and forgiveness, and it was said with success and guidance. And saved us from the punishment of the poisonous winds. Al-Hasan said: Samoom is a name for Hellfire and a layer of the layers of Hellfire. It was said that it is the fire as you say Hellfire. It was also said that it is the fire of the punishment of the poisonous winds. Samoom is a hot wind, and it is feminine. It is said from it that he poisoned our day, so it is poisonous, and the plural is sama'im. Abu Ubaidah said that Samoom is used during the day and it may be at night, and heat is used during the night and it may be during the day. Samoom is used for the scorching cold, and it is more for the scorching heat and sun. The rajaz poet said: Today is a cold day, its poisons are from the panic of the day, so I do not blame him
52:28: The Almighty said, Indeed, we used to call upon Him before meaning in this world to bestow forgiveness upon us for our shortcomings. It was also said that we used to call upon Him meaning we used to worship Him Indeed, it is He who is the Most Kind, the Most Merciful. Nafi' and Al-Kisa'i read it with a fat-ha on the hamza meaning because the rest read it with a kasra on the beginning and Al-Barr Al-Kateef as Ibn Abbas said and also from him that it means that He is the Truthful in what He promised and Ibn Jurayj said it.
52:29: The Almighty said, Then remind, meaning, O Muhammad, remind your people of the Qur'an. For you are not, by the grace of your Lord, meaning by the message of your Lord, a soothsayer, inventing statements and reporting what will happen tomorrow without revelation. Nor a madman. This is a refutation of what they said about the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him. Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt said that he was mad, Shaibah ibn Rabi'ah said that he was a magician, and others said that he was a soothsayer. So God, the Almighty, denied them and refuted them. Then it was said that the meaning of Then you are not, by the grace of your Lord, is an oath, meaning, by the grace of God, you are neither a soothsayer nor a madman. It was said that it is not an oath, but rather it is like what you say: You are not, by the grace of God, ignorant, meaning God has cleared you of that.
52:30: The Almighty said, Or do they say, ‘He is a poet?’ That is, rather, they say, Muhammad is a poet. Sibawayh said, The servants were addressed with what happened in their speech. Abu Ja`far al-Nahhas said, This is a good statement, except that it is not clear or explained. Sibawayh meant that umm in the speech of the Arabs is for moving from one hadith to another, as he said: Should I leave a prostitute or a girl? Then the conversation was over and he went on to something else and said: Mother of the rope, and there is a leper in it What came in the Book of God the Most High of this, its meaning is confirmation, rebuke and moving from one hadith to another. The grammarians represent it with bal. “We are waiting for him to be struck by the vicissitudes of fate.” Qatada said: A group of the infidels were waiting for Muhammad’s death. It will suffice you as it sufficed the poet of Banu so-and-so. Ad-Dahhak said: These are Banu Abd al-Dar. They attributed to him that he was a poet, meaning that he would perish soon as the poets before him perished, and that his father died young, so he might die as his father died. Al-Akhfash said: We are waiting for him to be struck by the vicissitudes of fate. He deleted the preposition, as you say: I intended for Zayd and I intended for Zayd. Death is death according to Ibn Abbas. Abu al-Ghoul at-Tahawi said: They prevented the fever of the valley with a strike that unites the scattered parts of death Which of the fates says that the strike brings together people who are scattered in places. If their deaths came to them in their places, they would come to them separately. So they gathered in one place, and the deaths came to them together. Al-Suddi said on the authority of Abu Malik on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Doubt in the Qur’an is doubt except for one place in the mountain. Doubt of the fates means the events of matters. And the poet said: Death is waiting for her, perhaps she will divorce him one day or her husband will die Mujahed said: The vicissitudes of fate are the events of time, and fate is time. Abu Dhu’ayb said: Death and its uncertainties are painful, and time does not forgive those who are impatient. Al-A'sha said: If she saw a blind man, harmed by the vicissitudes of fate and a time that is bewildered and crazy Al-Asma'i said: Al-Manun is the night and the day, and they were called thus because they shorten lifespans and cut short deadlines. It was narrated from him that time was called Manun because it takes away the animal's manna, i.e. its strength. Similarly, Al-Manun is Abu Ubaidah. Time was called Manun because it is a weak derivative of the word manin, meaning a weak rope, and Al-Manun is the weak dust. Al-Farra' said: Al-Manun is feminine and can be singular or plural. Al-Asma'i: Al-Manun is singular and has no plural. Al-Akhfash: It is a plural and Al-Manun is masculine and feminine, so whoever makes it masculine makes it time or death, and whoever makes it feminine, so based on the meaning it is as if he meant Al-Manun.
52:31: God Almighty said, “Say, ‘Wait,’ meaning, say to them, O Muhammad, ‘Wait, for I am with you among those who wait,’ meaning among those awaiting the punishment for you. So they were punished with the sword on the day of Badr.
52:32: The Almighty said, Or do their dreams command them to do this meaning to lie to you Or are they a transgressing people meaning or have they transgressed without reason. It was also said that or means rather meaning rather, rather they disbelieved out of transgression even though the truth was made clear to them. It was said to Amr ibn al-'As: Why did your people not believe even though God described them as having reason? He said: Those are reason that God deceived them, meaning He did not guide them to success. It was also said that their dreams means their minds, because reason is not given to the disbeliever, and if he had a reason he would have believed. Rather, the disbeliever is given the mind, so it became an argument against him. The mind accepts knowledge in general. The mind distinguishes knowledge and estimates the limits of commands and prohibitions. It was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that a man said: O Messenger of God, how sane is so-and-so the Christian? He said: No, the unbeliever has no mind. Haven’t you heard the words of God Almighty: And they said, ‘If only we had listened or reasoned, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze.’ And in the hadith of Ibn Umar, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, rebuked him and then said: No, for the sane person is the one who acts in obedience to God. Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Hakim Abu Abdullah, mentioned it with his chain of transmission.
52:33: Or do they say, 'You fabricated it'? That is, he made it up and invented it, meaning the Qur’an. 'Tafaqul' means forcing something to say, and it is usually used to denote lying. It is said, 'You made me say something I did not say!' and 'You made me say something I did not say,' meaning, you claimed it against me. 'He said a lie about him,' meaning, he lied about him. 'He fought against him,' meaning, he made him arbitrate. He said: And a position in the house of truth and happiness, and he did not fight from the judgment of a doctor The first is for denial and the second is for affirmation, meaning it is not as they say: Rather, they do not believe, out of denial and arrogance.
52:34: Then let them produce a hadith like it meaning a Qur'an that resembles it of their own accord if they are truthful in that Muhammad fabricated it. Al-Jahdary read Then let them produce a hadith like it with the addition and the ha' in like it refers to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the hadith that is meant to refer to the Qur'an is attributed to him because he was the one sent with it and the ha' refers to the group's reading of the Qur'an.
52:35: The Almighty says, Or were they created from nothing? "Or is an additional conjunction, meaning, Were they created from nothing? Ibn Abbas said, From a Lord who created them and determined them. It was also said, Without a mother or father, so they are like inanimate objects, they do not reason, and God's proof cannot be established against them. They are not like that. Were they not created from a sperm-drop, a clot, and a lump of flesh?" This was said by Ibn Ata'. Ibn Kaysan said, "Or were they created in vain and left aimlessly? From nothing means for nothing, so from has the meaning of lam. Or are they the creators?" That is, do they say that they created themselves? They do not obey God's command, and they do not say that. If they acknowledge that there is a Creator other than them, then what prevents them from acknowledging that He is to be worshipped, not idols, and from acknowledging that He is able to resurrect.
52:36: Or did they create the heavens and the earth? That is, the matter is not like that, for they did not create anything. Rather, they are not certain of the truth.
52:37: Or do they have the treasures of your Lord? Or do they have them, so they do not need God and turn away from His command. Ibn Abbas said: The treasures of your Lord are rain and provision. It was also said that they are the keys to mercy. Ikrimah said: They are the prophecy. That is, are the keys of your Lord with the message in their hands, so they place them wherever they want? He gave an example of the treasures that contain all kinds, so they have no end. Or are they the ones who control? Ibn Abbas said: The ones who control are the tyrants. Also from him are the falsifiers. Ad-Dahhak said and from Ibn Abbas also: Or are they the ones who are in charge? Ata' said: It is said, You controlled me, meaning, you took me as your servant. Abu Ubaidah said in As-Sahah: The one who controls and has power over something is the one who supervises it, looks after its affairs, and records its actions. Its origin is from the word satra line, because the writer writes and the one who does it is the one who controls and controls it. It is said, You controlled us. Ibn Bahr: Or are they the ones who control? That is, they are the guardians. It is taken from tasreen (the writing that preserves what is written in it. So musatter here means the one who keeps what God has written in the Preserved Tablet. It has three pronunciations: sad which is how the general public reads it, and this is the reading of Ibn Muhaisin, Hamid, Mujahid, Qunqub, Hisham, and Abu Haywah. And by issuing a shadda on the sad with a zay which is the reading of Hamzah, as mentioned previously in as-Sirat.
52:38: The Almighty said, Or have they a ladder? That is, do they claim that they have a way to ascend to the heavens, an ascent, and a means by which they can listen to report and attain knowledge of the unseen, just as Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, attained it through revelation? Then let their listener produce clear authority. That is, a clear argument that what they are following is true. A ladder is one of the stairs that one ascends. Perhaps the word al-Gharz was given this name. Abu al-Rabis al-Tha'labi said, describing his she-camel: A heart attack: If a man praises his Lord with peace, he will be planted in a climate that will hasten him. Zuhair said: Whoever fears the causes of death will encounter them, even if he seeks the causes of heaven with a ladder. Another said: You committed a sin against me, and as soon as you committed it, you used an excuse to leave me peacefully. Ibn Muqbil said in the collection: A person does not acquire the most beautiful lands, nor does he build ladders to the heavens. Ahajaa is the areas like arjaa, its singular is haja and rajaa is maqsur. It is also narrated as a’na al-bilad and a’naa’, meaning sides and regions, its singular is anw in kasra. Ibn al-A’rabi said: its singular is ‘anna’ in maqsur. And a’naa’ from the people came to us, its singular is ‘anw in kasra. They are people from different tribes. They listen to it means on it, like the saying of God the Almighty: In the trunks of the palm trees meaning on them. Al-Akhfash said this. Abu Ubaid said they listen to it. Al-Zajjaj said: It means He inspired, like Gabriel who comes to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, with revelation.
52:39: The Almighty’s saying, Or does He have daughters and you have sons? He belittled their dreams as a rebuke and a rebuke to them. That is, do you attribute daughters to God while you are proud of them? And whoever has such a mind, it is not unlikely that he will deny the resurrection.
52:40: Or do you ask them for a reward? That is, for conveying the message. So they are burdened by the debt. That is, they are burdened by the debt that you are asking them to pay, and are exhausted by what you have charged them with.
52:41: Or do they have knowledge of the unseen, so they write down meaning, they write down for people what they want of knowledge of the unseen. It was also said, Do they have knowledge of what is hidden from people, so that they know what the Messenger informed them of regarding the Day of Resurrection, Paradise, and Hellfire? The resurrection is false. Qatadah said, When they said, 'We are waiting for him to experience a misfortune,' God said, 'Or do they have knowledge of the unseen?' so that they know when Muhammad will die or what his fate will lead to. Ibn Abbas said, Or do they have the Preserved Tablet, so they write down what is in it and inform people of what is in it? Al-Qutbi said, They write down and judge, and the book is judgment. From this is the saying of God, Your Lord has decreed upon Himself mercy, meaning judgment. And the saying of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I will surely judge between you by the Book of God, meaning by the judgment of God.
52:42: God Almighty says, Or do they intend a plot against you? That is, a scheme against you in the House of Assembly. Then those who disbelieve are the ones who will be plotted against. That is, the ones who will be plotted against. And the evil plot does not encompass except its own people. That is because they were killed at Badr.
52:43: Or do they have a god other than God? Who creates, provides, and prevents? Glory be to God from what they associate with Him. He has declared Himself far above having a partner. Al-Khalil said: Everything in Surat At-Tur that mentions or is an interrogative word and not a conjunction.
52:44: The Almighty said, And if they see a fragment of the sky falling, He said that in response to their saying, Then let a fragment of the sky fall upon us, and their saying, Or let the sky fall upon us, as you claim, in fragments, so know that if He had done that, they would have said, Heaped clouds, meaning some of them above others, fell upon us, and it is not the sky. This is the action of the obstinate one, or the action of one who is overcome by imitation, and among the polytheists there are two types. The plural of kasfa is kasfa, which is a piece of something. It is said, Give me a fragment of your garment, and its plural is also kasfa. It is also said that kasfa and kasfa are one and the same. Al-Akhfash said, Whoever reads kasfa makes it singular, and whoever reads kasfa makes it plural. This has been discussed previously in Subhan and others, and Al-Hamdulillah.
52:45: The Almighty’s saying So leave them is abrogated by the verse of the sword until they meet their Day on which they will be struck dead with a fatha on the ya’ as read by the general public, and Ibn ‘Amir and ‘Aasim read it with a damma. Al-Farra’ said: They are two dialects:َقَقَقandَقَقَقlikeَقأدandَقأد. Qatadah said: The day they die. It was also said: It is the day of Badr. It was also said: The day of the first trumpet blast. It was also said: The day of resurrection, on which a punishment will come to them that will strip them of their minds. It was also said: They will be struck dead with a damma on the ya’ from ‘َقَقَقُه ا.
52:46: The Almighty says, The Day their plot will not avail them at all, meaning what they plotted against the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in this world. Nor will they be aided by God. The Day is in the accusative case as a substitute for Their Day on which they will be struck dead.
52:47: The Almighty said, And indeed, for those who do wrong meaning disbelieve is a punishment less than that. It was said, Before their death, where are the calamities of this world, such as pains, illnesses, plagues, and the loss of wealth and children? Mujahid said, It is hunger and exhaustion for seven years. Ibn Abbas said, It is killing. And from him, It is the punishment of the grave. Al-Bara' ibn Azib and Ali, may God be pleased with them, said, It is less than that. And it was said, It is a punishment lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter. "But most of them do not know," that the punishment will descend upon them. And it was said, "But most of them do not know," what they will become.
52:48: The Almighty’s saying, And be patient over the decision of your Lord, for indeed, you are before Our eyes. There are two issues in this: The first: And be patient for the decision of your Lord. It was said that it refers to the decision of your Lord regarding the message He entrusted you with, and it was said that it refers to His trial in what He tested you with from your people. Then it was abrogated by the verse of the sword. The second: The Almighty’s saying, For you are before Our eyes, meaning under Our sight and view. We see and hear what you say and do. It was also said that We see you, protect you, surround you, guard you, and watch over you. The meaning is the same. From this is the Almighty’s saying to Moses, peace be upon him, And you shall do it under My eyes, meaning under My protection and guard. This has been mentioned previously. There are two issues: First: The statement of God the Almighty: And glorify the praises of your Lord when you rise. There is a difference of opinion regarding the interpretation of His statement: when you rise. Awn ibn Malik, Ibn Mas`ud, `Ata`, Sa`id ibn Jubayr, Sufyan al-Thawri, and Abu al-Ahwas said that one should glorify God when he rises from his seat, saying: Glory be to God and His praise or Glory be to You, O God, and Your praise. If the gathering was good, then your praise will increase, but if it was not, then it will be an expiation for it. The evidence for this interpretation is what was narrated by al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Whoever sits in a gathering and engages in much idle talk, and says before rising from his seat: ‘Glory be to You, O God, and with Your praise. I bear witness that there is no god but You. I seek Your forgiveness and I repent to You,’ then whatever happened in that gathering will be forgiven.” He said: A good, sound, rare hadith. And in: “It was narrated on the authority of Ibn `Umar: We used to count for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) one hundred times in a single gathering before he stood up: ‘O my Lord, forgive me and spend the night with me, for You are the Accepter of Repentance, the Forgiving.’” He said: A good, sound, rare hadith. Muhammad ibn Ka'b, Ad-Dahhak and Ar-Rabi' said: The meaning is when you stand up for prayer. Ad-Dahhak said: Say: Allahu Akbar, the Greatest, and Al-Hamdulillah a lot, and Glory be to God morning and evening. Al-Kaya At-Tabari said: This is far-fetched, because his statement, When you stand up does not indicate glorification after the takbir, because the takbir is what comes after standing up, and glorification comes after that. This indicates that what is meant is when you stand up from every place, as Ibn Mas'ud may God be pleased with him said. Abu Al-Jawza' and Hassan ibn Atiyah said: The meaning is when you get up from your sleep. Hassan said: So that he begins his work with the remembrance of God. Al-Kalbi said: Remember God with the tongue when you get up from your bed until the prayer begins, which is the dawn prayer. There are various authentic narrations on this, including the hadith of Ubadah, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: ‘Whoever wakes up at night and says: ‘There is no god but God alone, with no partner for Him. His is the dominion and His is the praise. He is over all things omnipotent.’ ‘Praise be to God,’ ‘Glory be to God, and God is greatest.’ Or he says: ‘O God, forgive me.’ Or he makes supplication, his prayer will be answered. If he performs ablution and prays, his prayer will be accepted.’” Narrated by Al-Bukhari. A man wakes up at night: if he wakes up from his sleep with a sound. This is the same as the roaring of an ostrich, which is its sound. Some of them say: ‘The mighty ostrich roars loudly, as they say: ‘The ostrich buzzes loudly.’” On the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say when he got up to pray in the middle of al-Layl 92:‘O God, to You be praise. You are the Light of the heavens and the earth and of those in them. To You be praise. You are the Sustainer of the heavens and the earth and of those in them. To You be praise. You are the Lord of the heavens and the earth and of those in them. You are the Truth, and Your promise is the Truth, and Your word is the Truth, and meeting You is the Truth, and Paradise is the Truth, and Hell is the Truth, and the Hour is the Truth, and the prophets are the Truth, and Muhammad is the Truth. O God, to You I have submitted, and upon You I have relied, and in You I have believed, and to You I turn.’” I have repented and I have disputed with You and I have turned to You for judgment, so forgive me for what I have done in the past and what I will do in the future, what I have kept secret and what I have declared. You are the First and the Last. There is no god except You and there is no god other than You. Agreed upon. And Ibn Abbas also reported that whenever the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) woke up at night, he would wipe the sleep from his face and then recite the last ten verses of Surat Al Imran. Zayd ibn Aslam said: The meaning is when you get up from the midday nap for the noon prayer. Ibn al-Arabi said: As for the midday nap, there is no evidence for it and it is included in the night sleep. Ad-Dahhak said: It is the tasbih in prayer when one gets up for it. Al-Mawardi said: There are two opinions regarding this tasbih. One of them is saying: Glory be to my Lord, the Almighty, in bowing and Glory be to my Lord, the Most High, in the second prostration. It is turning one’s face in prayer, saying: Glory be to You, O God, and with Your praise, and blessed is Your name, and exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god other than You. Ibn al-Arabi said: Whoever says that it is the tasbih for prayer, then this is the best of it, and the narrations for that are many, the greatest of which is what is proven. On the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that when he got up for prayer, he would say: I have turned my face. We have mentioned it and others at the end of Surat Al-An’am and in Al-Bukhari, “On the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, that he said: I said, O Messenger of God, teach me a supplication that I may say in my prayer. He said, ‘Say, O God, I have wronged myself greatly, and no one forgives sins except You, so forgive me with forgiveness from You and have mercy on me, for You are the Forgiving, the Merciful.’”
52:49: Second: The Almighty’s saying, And during part of the night, glorify Him and at the decline of the stars. This was previously mentioned in full in Qaf when discussing the Almighty’s saying, And during part of the night, glorify Him and at the decline of the stars. As for and at the decline of the stars, Ali, Ibn Abbas, Jabir, and Anas said: It means the two rak’ahs of Fajr. Some scholars interpreted the verse according to this statement as a recommendation and considered it abrogated by the five daily prayers. Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said that his saying, and at the decline of the stars, means the Fajr prayer, and this is the preferred opinion of At-Tabari. According to Ibn Abbas, it means the glorification at the end of the prayers. With a kasra on the hamza in and at the decline of the stars, the seven recited it as a verbal noun, as we explained in Qaf. Salim ibn Abi Al-Ja’d and Muhammad ibn As-Sameeq read adbar with a fatha, and something similar was narrated from Ya’qub, Salam, and Ayoub, and it is the plural of dabar and dabar. And manage the matter and manage it in its finality. At-Tirmidhi narrated from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Fadil from Rashdin ibn Kurayb from his father, “from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: The setting of the stars is the two rak’ahs before dawn, and the setting of prostration is the two rak’ahs after sunset.” He said: This is a strange hadith that we do not know of as being traceable back to the Prophet except from this chain of narration from Muhammad ibn Fadil from Rashdin ibn Kurayb. I asked Muhammad ibn Isma’il about Muhammad ibn Fadil and Rashdin ibn Kurayb, which of them is more trustworthy? He said: The closest of them is, and Muhammad is more trustworthy in my opinion. I asked Abdullah ibn Abdur-Rahman about this, and he said: The closest of them is, and Rashdin ibn Kurayb is more trustworthy in my opinion. At-Tirmidhi said: What Abu Muhammad said, and Rashdin ibn Kurayb is more trustworthy and older in my opinion than Muhammad. Rashdin met Ibn Abbas and saw him. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, she said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was not more committed to any voluntary prayer than to two rak’ahs before dawn. And on her authority, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: Two rak’ahs before dawn are better than the world and everything in it. The interpretation of Surat At-Tur has been completed. Praise be to God.
53:1: All of it is Meccan according to Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata' and Jabir. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said that it is Meccan, except for one verse, which is the verse in which God the Almighty says: Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities (al-Najm 53:32). It was also said that it is sixty-two verses. It was also said that the entire Surah is Medinan. The correct view is that it is Meccan, as Ibn Mas'ud narrated that he said: It is the first Surah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) announced in Mecca. And in Al-Bukhari, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prostrated at the star, and the Muslims, polytheists, jinn, and humans prostrated with him.” And “On the authority of Abdullah: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited Surat An-Najm and prostrated at it, and no one among the people remained who did not prostrate. Then a man among the people took a handful of pebbles or dirt and raised it to his face and said: This is sufficient for me. Abdullah said: I saw him after he was killed as a disbeliever.” Agreed upon. The man is said to be Umayyah ibn Khalaf. In the two Sahihs: On the authority of Zayd ibn Thabit, may God be pleased with him: He recited to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Surah By the star when it goes down, but he did not prostrate. This has been discussed at the end of Al-A’raf, and praise be to God. God the Almighty said: {And the star when it goes down.} Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: The meaning of And the star when it goes down is the Pleiades when they set with the dawn. The Arabs call the Pleiades a star even though they are stars in number. It is said that they are seven stars, six of which are visible and one is hidden, with which people test their sight. In Ash-Shifa by Al-Qadi Iyadh: “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to see eleven stars in the Pleiades.” Mujahid also said that the meaning is And the Qur’an when it descends, because it descends as stars. Al-Farra’ said the same. Al-Farra’ also said: It means all the stars of the sky when they set. This is the saying of Al-Hasan, who said: God swears by the stars when they set. It is not impossible to express them with one word while meaning plural, like the saying of Al-Ra’i: So she became a star in a quick puzzle in the hands of those who eat her frozen Omar bin Abi Rabia said: The best star in the sky is the Pleiades, and the Pleiades on earth are the most beautiful of women. Al-Hasan also said: What is meant by the star are the stars when they fall on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Suddi said: The star here is Venus because some Arabs used to worship it. It was also said that what is meant by it are the stars that the devils were used to interpret, and the reason for that is that when God Almighty wanted to send Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, as a messenger, the falling of the stars increased before his birth, so most of the Arabs were terrified by them and sought help from a blind soothsayer of theirs, who used to inform them of events, so they asked him about them and he said: Look at the twelve constellations. If one of them falls, then the world will be gone, and if nothing of them falls, then something great will happen in the world, so they felt that, and when the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, was sent, it was the great event that they felt that way, so God Almighty revealed: {And the star when it goes down} meaning that the star that fell is for this prophecy that happened. It was also said that the star here is the plant that has no stem, and it fell to the ground. Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn, may God be pleased with them, said: And the star meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, when it falls means when it descends from the sky on the night of the Ascension. And on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, may God be pleased with them both: Utbah ibn Abi Lahab, who had the daughter of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) married to him, wanted to go to Ash-Sham. He said, I will go to Muhammad and harm him. So he went to him and said, O Muhammad, he is a disbeliever in the star when it sets and in the One who draws near and hangs down. Then he spat in the face of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), returned his daughter to him, and divorced her. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, O God, send upon him one of Your dogs. Abu Talib was present and was shocked at her and said, O my nephew, you did not need this call. So Utbah returned to his father and informed him. Then they went to Ash-Sham and stopped at a place. A monk from the monastery looked down upon them and said, This is a lush land. Abu Lahab said to his companions, O people of Quraysh, help us tonight! For I fear for my son from the call of Muhammad. So they gathered their camels and made them kneel around them, and surrounded Utbah. Then a lion came, sniffing at their faces until it struck Utbah and killed him.” Hassan said: Whoever returns the year to his family, the lion will not eat the one who returns The root of the word star is rising. It is said: star of the sun or star of so-and-so in such-and-such country meaning he rebelled against the sultan. And hawa is the descent and fall. It is said: hawa yahwi hawayan like mada yamdi mazdan. Zuhair said: He made the goats fall with the bucket's weight, and handed them the bribe. Another said: While we were in the black hole, the camels were falling fast A thought crossed my heart from the memory of you and here I could not move on Al-Asma’i: Hawa with the fat-ha means he fell to the bottom. He said: Likewise, anhawa in walking means he continued in it. Hawa and anhawa in it are two languages with the same meaning, and the poet combined them in his saying: How many homes, if it weren't for me, would have fallen, just as they fell due to their own sins, from lack of wisdom. It is said about love: Hawa, with a kasra, yahwi hawa, meaning love.
53:2: The Almighty says: Your companion has not gone astray. This is the answer to the oath, meaning Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, has not gone astray from the truth nor has he deviated from it. And he has not gone astray. Going astray is the opposite of right guidance, meaning he has not gone astray. It has also been said that it means he did not speak falsehood. It has also been said that it means he did not fail in what he sought, and going astray means failure. The poet said: Whoever finds good, people praise him for his actions, and whoever goes astray will not lack someone to blame him for his error. Whoever is disappointed in his quest, people will blame him. Then it is possible that this is a statement about what happened after the revelation. It is also possible that it is a statement about his condition in general terms, meaning that he was always a monotheist of God. This is correct, as we explained in Ash-Shura when He said: You did not know what the Book was, nor what faith was (al-Shura 42:52).
53:3: God Almighty says: Nor does he speak from [his own] inclination.
53:4: God Almighty says: It is only a revelation revealed. There are two issues: First: The Most High’s statement: Nor does he speak from [his own] inclination. Qatada said: Nor does he speak the Qur’an from his own inclination. “It is only a revelation revealed” to him. It was said: From inclination means by inclination, as Abu Ubaidah said, like the Most High’s statement: So ask about it one who is informed. An-Nahhas: The statement of Qatada is more appropriate, and from is in its proper context, meaning his speech does not go beyond his own opinion, it is only by revelation from God the Almighty, because after it: It is only a revelation revealed. Second: This verse may be used as evidence by those who do not allow the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to exercise independent reasoning in matters of incidents. It also indicates that the Sunnah is like the revealed revelation in actions. The hadith of Al-Miqdam bin Ma’di Karib on this matter was presented in the introduction to the book, and praise be to God. Al-Sijistani said: If you wish, you can replace It is only a revelation revealed with Your companion has not gone astray. Ibn Al-Anbari said: This is a mistake, because the light in cannot be replaced with ma. The evidence for this is that you do not say, “By God, I did not stand up. Indeed, I am sitting.”
53:5: The Almighty's statement: He was taught by one of intense strength means Gabriel, peace be upon him, according to the opinion of all the commentators, except for Al-Hasan, who said: It is God, the Almighty. The Almighty's statement: of great strength according to Al-Hasan completes the statement, and its meaning is possessor of strength, and strength is one of the attributes of God, the Almighty. Its origin is from the intensity of twisting a rope, as if he continued twisting it until it reached a limit that made it difficult to unravel. Then He said: And He rose above the Throne meaning God, the Almighty, that is, He rose above the Throne. Its meaning was narrated from Al-Hasan. Al-Rabi' bin Anas and Al-Farra' said: And He rose above the highest horizon meaning Gabriel and Muhammad rose above it, peace be upon them. This is in conjunction with the implied nominative with -He. When most Arabs want to use conjunction in such a situation, they make the thing conjoined to appear as a metaphor, so they say: He and so-and-so rose above it, and they rarely say He and so-and-so rose above it. Al-Farra' recited: Have you not seen that the spring hardens and becomes uneven? And the castor oil that is split That is, he and castor oil are not equal. Similar to this is: If we and our fathers are dust, meaning: If we are dust, like and our opinions. The meaning of the verse: Gabriel and Muhammad, peace be upon them, were established on the Night of the Isra’ Journey to Heaven with the highest horizon. He permitted the conjunction of the pronoun so that it would not be repeated. Al-Zajjaj denied that except in poetic necessity. It was said: The meaning is: Gabriel was established with the highest horizon, and this is better. If the one established is Gabriel, then the meaning of of good character in his description is of good speech, as Ibn Abbas said. Qatada said: of tall, good character. It was said: Its meaning is of good health and free from ailments, and from this is the saying of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: Charity is not permissible for a rich person or one of good character. Imru’ al-Qais said: I was always among them, resourceful, wise, and trustworthy. It has been said: (Dhu Marra) is of strength. Al-Kalbi said: And among the strength of Gabriel, peace be upon him, was that he uprooted the cities of the people of Lot from the lower earth, and carried them on his wing until he raised them to the sky, until the people of the sky heard the barking of their dogs and the crowing of their roosters, then he turned them over. And among his strength was also that he saw Satan speaking to Jesus, peace be upon him, over some eagles in the holy land, so he blew him with his wing a blast that threw him to the furthest mountain in India. And among his strength was his shout to the Thamud in their number and great number, so they became kneeling and motionless. And among his strength was his descent from the sky upon the prophets and his ascent to them faster than the blink of an eye. And Qatrib said: The Arabs say to every wise and wise man: Dhu Marra. The poet said: Before I met you, I had a balance for every opponent. His sound judgment and wise mind were evident in the fact that God entrusted him with His revelation to all His messengers. Al-Jawhari said: Bitterness is one of the four natures, and bitterness also means strength and sharpness of mind. A bitter man means strong and bitter. He said: You see a thin man and despise him, but the stuffing of his clothes is a bitter lion. Laqit said: Until she continued to squint at his bitterness, the bitterness of determination, neither comforting nor comforting Mujahid and Qatada said: Dhu Marra means strong. From this is the saying of Khafaf bin Nadba: I am a man of old, so keep me safe in times of calamity Power is an attribute of God Almighty, and an attribute of the creation.
53:6: Fastawa means Gabriel, as we have explained, that is, he rose and ascended to a place in the sky after he taught Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. This was said by Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Ibn Jubayr. It was also said that Fastawa means he stood in the form in which God Almighty created him. Because he used to come to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the form of a human being, just as he used to come to the prophets, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked him to show him the self that God created him with, so he showed him himself twice: once on earth and once in heaven. As for on earth, it was in the highest horizon. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in Hira, so Gabriel came out to him from the east, covering the earth to the west. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, fell unconscious, so he came down to him in the form of a human being, hugged him to his chest, and began to wipe the dust from his face. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regained consciousness, he said: O Gabriel, I did not think that God created anyone in such a form. He said: O Muhammad, I have only spread two of my wings, and I have six hundred wings between the east and the west. He said: This is indeed great. He said: I am only a little compared to what God created. God created Israfil, who has six hundred wings, each one of which is the size of all my wings. Sometimes he becomes small out of fear of God Almighty until he is as small as a person can carry. Meaning the little bird, its evidence is the Almighty’s saying: And he had certainly seen him on the clear horizon. As for in the sky, it was at the Lote Tree of the Limit, and none of the prophets saw it in that form except Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. A third opinion is that the meaning of then rose straight is that the Qur’an rose straight in his chest. According to this view, there are two interpretations: One is in the chest of Gabriel when it was revealed to him. The second is in the chest of Muhammad when it was revealed to him. A fourth opinion is that the meaning of then rose straight is that he became balanced, meaning Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. According to this view, there are two interpretations: One is that he became balanced in his strength, the second in his message. Al-Mawardi mentioned them both. I said: According to the first opinion, the complete statement would be of great strength. According to the second opinion, it would be of strong strength. A fifth opinion is that it means then he ascended. There are two views on this: one is that Gabriel, peace be upon him, ascended to his place, as we mentioned earlier. The second is that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ascended by way of the Night Journey. A sixth opinion is then he rose meaning God Almighty, that is, he rose above the Throne, according to al-Hasan, and this has been discussed previously in al-A’raf.
53:7: The Almighty’s saying And He is on the highest horizon is a phrase in the accusative case, and the meaning is So He rose high up i.e. Gabriel rose high up in his image and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had not seen him in that image before that until he asked him about it as we mentioned. The horizon is the side of the sky and its plural is horizons. Qatada said it is the place from which the sun comes. Sufyan said the same, it is the place from which the sun rises. Something similar was said by Mujahid. It is said a horizon and a horizon like asr and asr and it has been mentioned in Ha Meem As-Sajdah and the horse a horizon with the dammah means wonderful and so is the female. The poet said: My legs are my lap, my tail is my tail, and my complaint is my horizon is my chestnut It was said that he (the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace) was on the highest horizon, meaning on the Night of the Isra’. This is weak because it is said that he and so-and-so were established, but it is not said that he and so-and-so were established except in poetic necessity. The correct view is that Gabriel, peace be upon him, and Gabriel were established on the highest horizon in his original form, because he would appear to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he came down with revelation in the form of a man. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, loved to see him in his true form, so he was established on the horizon of the East and filled the horizon.
53:8: The Almighty’s statement, Then he drew near and came down means that Gabriel drew near after he had been established at the highest horizon of the earth. He came down and descended to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the revelation. The meaning is that when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw what he saw of his majesty and was awed by it, God returned him to the form of a human being when he drew near to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the revelation. This is the Almighty’s statement, Then He revealed to His Servant meaning God revealed to Gabriel, and Gabriel was two bow lengths away or nearer. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Rabi’, and others. Ibn Abbas also reported regarding the Almighty’s statement, Then he drew near and came down that its meaning is that God, the Blessed and Exalted, drew near to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and came down and something similar was narrated by Anas bin Malik from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The meaning is that his command and his judgment drew near to him. The root of taddaal is to descend to something until one is close to it, so he was placed in a position of nearness. Labid said: I hung down on him, returning, and on the ground were the child’s absences Al-Farra’ said that the fa’ in fatadala has the meaning of waw and the interpretation is then Gabriel, peace be upon him, descended and drew near. However, it is permissible if the meaning of the two verbs is the same or almost the same, you can put whichever you want first, so you say fadana fa qarabah he drew near and qarabah fa qarabah he drew near and shatmaani fa nasaa’ he cursed me and did evil and shatmaani fa nasaa’ he cursed me and did evil because cursing and doing evil are one and the same. Similarly, the Almighty said, The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split, meaning – and God knows best – the moon has split and the Hour has drawn near. Al-Jurjani said in speech that there is an inversion of precedence and delay, meaning he descended and drew near, because descending is the cause of drawing near. Ibn al-Anbari said, then Gabriel descended, meaning he descended from the sky and drew near to Muhammad, peace be upon him. Ibn Abbas said, the roof was lowered for Muhammad, peace be upon him, on the night of the Ascension, so he sat on it, then it was raised and drew near to his Lord. This will come later. Whoever says the meaning is then Gabriel and Muhammad were on the highest horizon may say, then Muhammad drew near to his Lord, a drawing near of honor, then he drew near, meaning he prostrated. This is what Al-Dahhak said. Al-Qushayri said: It was said on this basis that he dangled, meaning he pampered himself, like you say you think, meaning you think. This is far-fetched because pampering is not acceptable in the description of servitude.
53:9: The Almighty’s saying, Then he was two bow lengths away or nearer means Muhammad was from his Lord or from Gabriel. Then he was two bow lengths away means the distance of two Arabic bow lengths. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Ata’, Al-Farra’, and Al-Zamakhshari. If you ask, how is the interpretation of His saying, Then he was two bow lengths away? I say that its interpretation is that the distance of his closeness was like the distance of two bow lengths. So these additional words were deleted, as Abu Ali said in His saying: You made me a finger from the defeat That is, the distance of a finger, or less, according to your estimation, like the Almighty’s saying, or they increase. In As-Sahah: And you say between them is a bow’s length, and qayb of a bow, and qad of a bow, and qayd of a bow, meaning the length of an bow. Zayd ibn Ali read it as qad, and it was also read as qayd and qadr. Az-Zamakhshari mentioned it. Qaab is what is between the handle and the handle, and for every bow there are two qabas. Some of them said regarding the Almighty’s saying, two bow lengths, he meant the two qabas of a bow, so he changed it. And in the Hadeeth: And the distance of the bow of one of you in Paradise, and the place of his whip is better than the world and everything in it. And the qad is the whip. In As-Sahah, it is narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: And the distance of the bow of one of you in Paradise is better than the world and everything in it. And the example was given by the bow because they do not differ in qabs, and God knows best. Al-Qadi ‘Iyad said: Know that what is mentioned of the attribution of closeness and nearness to God or to God is not closeness of place nor closeness of distance. Rather, the closeness of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to his Lord and his closeness to Him is a demonstration of his great status, the honor of his rank, the radiance of the lights of his knowledge, and witnessing the secrets of His unseen and power. And from God the Most High: benevolence, comfort, expansion and honor. And in his saying, peace be upon him: Our Lord descends to the lowest heaven, it is interpreted in one way as a general descent, acceptance and benevolence. Al-Qadi said: And his saying, Then he was two bow lengths away or nearer, whoever makes the pronoun refer to God the Most High and not to Gabriel, it is an expression of the utmost closeness, gentleness of place, clarification of knowledge and supervision of the truth from Muhammad, peace be upon him, and an expression of the answer to desires, the fulfillment of demands, the manifestation of generosity, the loftiness of position and closeness to God. And in it is interpreted what is interpreted in his saying, peace be upon him: Whoever draws near to Me a handspan, I will draw near to him an arm’s length, and whoever comes to Me walking, I will come to him running. Closeness through answering and acceptance, bringing benevolence and hastening what is hoped for. And it has been said, Then Gabriel drew near to his Lord, Then he was two bow lengths away or nearer, said Mujahid. And what is indicated by what is narrated in the hadith: “The closest of the angels to God is Gabriel, peace be upon him.” And it has been said: or in the sense of and, meaning two bow lengths away and nearer. And it has been said: in the sense of rather, meaning even closer. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: Al-Qab is the front of the Arab bow, where the strap is tied to it that its owner takes off his shoulder, and each bow has one qab. So he said that Gabriel came close to Muhammad, peace be upon him, as close as two bow lengths. Saeed bin Jubair, Ata’, Abu Ishaq Al-Hamadani, Abu Wa’il Shaqiq bin Salamah said: So he was two bow lengths means the length of two cubits, and the bow is the cubit by which everything is measured. It is the language of some of the Hijazis, and it was said that it is also the language of Azd Shanu’ah. Al-Kisa’i said: His statement So he was two bow lengths or even nearer means one bow length, like the poet’s saying: And the two men threw it twice, and I cut it off with the right direction, not with the left direction. He wanted to make a single mission, and the bow is masculine and feminine. When it is feminine, he said in its diminutive form, qawīsah, and when it is masculine, he said qawīs. In the proverb, he said, From the best arrows, qawīs, and the plural is qāṣī, qaṣī, aqwās, and qiyas. Abu Ubaidah recited: Bracelet chord measurement The bow is also the remainder of the date in the vessel, and the bow is a tower in the sky. As for the bow with the dammah, it is the monk’s cell. The poet said, mentioning a woman: To tempt me, and this is the one who wipes the bow
53:10: His Almighty saying: Then He revealed to His servant what He revealed is an emphasis on the revelation that was revealed to him. The meaning of revelation was presented, which is to throw something quickly, and from this comes the word waha revelation, and the meaning is: So God revealed to His servant Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, what He revealed. It was said that the meaning is: So He revealed to His servant Gabriel, peace be upon him, what He revealed. It was also said that the meaning is: So Gabriel revealed to the servant of God Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, what his Lord revealed to him. This was said by Al-Rabi', Al-Hasan, Ibn Zayd, and Qatadah. Qatadah said: God revealed to Gabriel, and Gabriel revealed to Muhammad. Then it was said: Is this revelation ambiguous? We are not aware of it, and we worship by believing in it in general, or is it known and explained? Two opinions: And with the second, Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: God revealed to Muhammad: Did I not find you an orphan and give you shelter? Did I not find you lost and guide you? Did I not find you poor and make you rich? Have We not expanded your breast for you, and removed from you your burden which weighed upon your back, and raised high for you your repute? It was said that God revealed to him that Paradise is forbidden to the prophets until you enter it, O Muhammad, and to the nations until your nation enters it.
53:11: God the Almighty said, The heart did not deny what it saw. That is, the heart of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not lie on the Night of Ascension, because God the Almighty placed his sight in his heart until he saw his Lord, and God made that a vision. It was also said: It was a true vision with the sight. The first is narrated from Ibn Abbas. In Sahih Muslim, it says that he saw Him with his heart, and this is the opinion of Abu Dharr and a group of the Companions. The second is the opinion of Anas and a group. It was also narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: Do you wonder that the friendship was for Abraham, the speech was for Moses, and the vision was for Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him). It was also narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: As for us, Banu Hashim, we say that Muhammad saw his Lord twice. This has already been discussed in Al-An’am, when it says: No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision. Muhammad ibn Ka’b narrated on the authority of some of the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: We said: O Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon you), have you seen your Lord? He said: I saw Him with my heart twice. Then he recited: The heart did not deny what it saw. A third statement is that it saw His majesty and greatness, as stated by Al-Hasan. Abu Al-Aaliyah narrated: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asked: Did you see your Lord? He said: I saw a river, and I saw behind the river a veil, and I saw behind the veil a light. I saw nothing else. And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: I asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), Did you see your Lord? He said: Light, that is, I saw Him. The meaning is: The light overwhelmed me and dazzled me, preventing me from seeing Him. This is indicated by the other narration: I saw a light. Ibn Mas’ud said: He saw Gabriel in his true form twice. Hisham recited on the authority of Ibn ‘Amir and the people of Ash-Sham: He did not deny with emphasis, meaning: Muhammad’s heart did not deny what he saw with his eyes that night, but rather he believed it. So (ma) is an object without a preposition, because it is transitive and doubled without a preposition. It is possible for ma to mean who and the antecedent is omitted, and it is possible for it to be with the verb a verbal noun, the rest of which are light, meaning that the heart of Muhammad did not lie in what he saw, so he omitted the adjective letter. Hassan, may God be pleased with him, said: If you were truthful in what you told me, I would have been saved, as Al-Harith bin Hisham said. That is, in what you told me. It is possible that it is with the verb as a source, and it is possible that it is in the meaning of that, that is, the heart of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not lie about what he saw.
53:12: The Almighty said, Do you then dispute with him about what he sees? Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read aftamaruhu with a fat-ha on the ta’ without an alif, meaning do you deny him? Abu Ubaid chose it because he said they did not dispute with him, but rather they denied him. It is said, He showed him his right, meaning he denied it, and I showed him. The poet said: If you abandon a brother of truth and honor, you will have experienced a brother who was not experienced. Meaning, you denied it. Al-Mubarrad said: It is said, Mara’a ‘an haqqi he denied his right or ala haqqi he prevented him from it and pushed him away from it. He said: And ‘ala is used as an example with the meaning of about in the words of Banu Ka’b ibn Rabi’ah, may God be pleased with you, meaning, be pleased with you. Al-A’raj and Mujahid read aftamaroohu with a damma on the ta’ without an alif from amraytu meaning, you make him doubt and doubt it. The rest read aftamaroohu with an alif meaning, do you argue with him and push him away that he saw God? The two meanings are intertwined because their argument is denial. It was said that denial was always from them, and this is a new argument. They said: Describe Jerusalem to us and tell us about our caravan that is on the way to Syria. As mentioned above.
53:13: The Almighty said, And indeed, he saw him descending another time. “Descent” is a verbal noun in the place of a circumstance, as if he said: And indeed, he saw him descending another time. Ibn Abbas said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw his Lord once again with his heart. Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, on his authority, who said: The heart did not lie about what it saw. “And he saw him on another descent.” He said that he saw him with his heart twice. So his saying on another descent refers to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for he had many ascents and descents according to the number of obligatory prayers, so for each ascent there was a descent. Based on this, the Almighty said: At the Lote Tree of the Limit, meaning that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was at the Lote Tree of the Limit, and in some of those descents. Ibn Mas’ud and Abu Hurairah said in their interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And he saw him on another descent, that it was Gabriel. This is also proven in Sahih Muslim. Ibn Mas’ud said that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I saw Gabriel on the highest horizon, with six hundred wings, from whose feathers pearls and rubies were scattered. Al-Mahdawi mentioned this.
53:14: The Almighty’s saying, at the Lote Tree of the Limit, is at the point where he saw it, as we have explained. The Lote Tree is the Nabq tree, and it is in the sixth heaven. It was mentioned in the seventh heaven, and the hadith with this in Sahih Muslim, the first, is what was narrated once, “On the authority of Abdullah, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on the Night Journey, he reached the Lote Tree of the Limit, and it is in the sixth heaven. What ascends from the earth ends at it, and what descends from above it ends at it, and what descends from above it ends at it, and it is taken from it. He said, “When that which covers the Lote Tree covers it,” he said, A carpet of gold. He said, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was given three things: he was given the five daily prayers, he was given the final verses of Surat al-Baqarah, and he who from his nation did not associate anything with God was forgiven for the intrusive sins.” The second hadith was narrated by Qatada, on the authority of Anas, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When I was raised to the Lote Tree of the Limit in the seventh heaven, its Nabq is like the jars of Hajar, and its leaves are like the ears of elephants. Two rivers emerge from its trunk, apparent and two rivers, hidden. I said, O Gabriel: What is this? He said: As for the two hidden ones, they are in Paradise, and as for the two apparent ones, they are the Nile and the Euphrates. The wording of Ad-Daraqutni: Nabq, with a kasra on the ba, is the fruit of the lote tree, one of which is nabqah. It is also said nabq with a fatha on the noon and a sukoon on the ba. Both were mentioned by Yaqub in Al-Islah, and it is the language of the Egyptians, but the first is more eloquent and is what was proven from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. At-Tirmidhi narrated: On the authority of Asma’ bint Abi Bakr, may God be pleased with them both, she said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say - and the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary was mentioned to him - he said: A rider can travel in the shade of its branch for a hundred years, or a hundred riders can take shelter in its shade - Yahya was uncertain - in it are beds of gold, as if its fruit were jugs. Abu ‘Eesa said: This is a good hadith. I said: “And this is the wording of Muslim from a hadith narrated on the authority of Thabit on the authority of Anas: ‘Then he took me to the Lote Tree of the Limit, and behold, its leaves were like the ears of elephants, and behold, its fruit was like jugs. But when that which covered it by the command of God, the Mighty and Majestic, covered it, it changed, and none of God’s creation can describe its beauty.’” There are nine different opinions as to why it was called Sidrat al-Muntaha. The first is what was mentioned previously on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, that everything that descends from above it and ascends from below ends there. The second is that the knowledge of the prophets ends there, and their knowledge of what is beyond it is hidden. This was said by Ibn Abbas. The third is that deeds end there and are taken from there. This was said by Ad-Dahhak. The fourth is that the angels and prophets end there and stop at it. This was said by Ka’b. The fifth is that it was called Sidrat al-Muntaha because the souls of the martyrs end there. This was said by Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas. The sixth is that the souls of the believers end there. This was said by Qatadah. The seventh is that everyone who follows the Sunnah and method of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ends there. This was said by Ali may God be pleased with him and Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas as well. Eighth: It is a tree on the heads of the bearers of the Throne, to which the knowledge of creation ends. Kaab also said this. I said, he means, and God knows best, that its height and the heights of its branches have exceeded the heads of the bearers of the Throne, and the evidence for this is what was mentioned previously, that its origin is in the sixth heaven and its highest point is in the seventh heaven, then it rose above that until it exceeded the heads of the bearers of the Throne, and God knows best. The ninth was named thus because whoever is raised to it has reached the highest level of honor. And on the authority of Abu Hurairah: When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was taken on the Night Journey, he reached the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary. It was said to him, This is the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary, to which everyone, except your nation, will reach according to your way. Then he saw that it was a tree from whose root flowed rivers of water unpolluted, and rivers of milk whose taste never changed, and rivers of wine delicious to those who drink, and rivers of pure honey. Then he saw that it was a tree in whose shade a fast rider could travel for a hundred years without crossing it, and its leaf would cover the entire nation.
53:15: The Almighty's saying, Near it is the Garden of Refuge. This identifies the location of the Garden of Refuge, which is at the Lote Tree of the Limit. Ali, Abu Hurairah, Anas, Abu Sabra Al-Juhani, Abdullah ibn Az-Zubayr, and Mujahid read, Near it is the Garden of Refuge, meaning the Garden of the Night. Mujahid said, He means gardens, and the ha refers to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Al-Akhfash said, It overtook him, as you say the Garden of the Night, meaning it concealed him and overtook him. The reading of the common people is, The Garden of Refuge. Al-Hasan said, It is the one to which the righteous go. It was also said that it is the Garden to which the souls of the martyrs go. Ibn Abbas said, It is to the right of the Throne. It was also said that it is the Garden to which Adam (peace be upon him) took refuge until he was expelled from it, and it is in the seventh heaven. It was also said that the spouses of the believers are all in the Garden of Refuge, and it is called the Garden of Refuge because the souls of the believers take refuge in it, and it is under the Throne, so they enjoy its blessings and breathe its pleasant fragrance. It was said that Gabriel and Michael, peace be upon them, take refuge there, and God knows best.
53:16: The Almighty said, When that which covers the lote tree covers itself, Ibn Abbas, Ad-Dahhak, Ibn Mas'ud and his companions said, It was a moth of gold. Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas narrated it with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). It was mentioned earlier in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Al-Hasan said: The light of the Lord of the Worlds covered it, so it shone." Al-Qushayri said: "The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asked, 'What covered it?' He said, 'A moth of gold.'" In another report, A light from God covered it, so that no one could look at it. Ar-Rabi' ibn Anas said: The light of the Lord covered it, and the angels landed on it as crows land on a tree. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "I saw the lote tree covered with a moth of gold, and I saw on every leaf an angel standing, glorifying God Almighty. This is His saying, "When that which covers the lote tree covers itself," Al-Mahdawi and Ath-Tha'labi mentioned it. Anas ibn Malik said: "When that which covers the lote tree covers itself," he said: "Locusts of gold." This was narrated with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Mujahed said: It is a green flutter. And on his authority, peace be upon him: A flutter of green birds covers it. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The Lord of Glory covers it, meaning His command, as in Sahih Muslim, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet: So when what covered it was covered by the command of God It was said that it is to glorify the command, as if he said: When the lote tree was covered by what God knew of the signs of His kingdom. And likewise His statement, the Most High: Then He revealed to His servant what He revealed “And the overturned tree, He inclined * So what covered it covered it” And similar to it is: The Inevitable * What is the Inevitable? Al-Mawardi said in his book, The Meanings of the Qur’an: If it is said, why was the lote tree chosen for this matter and not other trees? It is said that the lote tree is distinguished by three characteristics: an extended shade, a delicious taste, and a pleasant scent, so it resembles faith, which combines words, deeds, and intention. So its shade is to faith like deeds because it transcends, its taste is like intention because it is latent, and its scent is like words because it is apparent. Abu Dawud narrated in his Sunan, saying: Nasr bin Ali told us, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Uthman bin Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Saeed bin Muhammad bin Jubair bin Mut’im, on the authority of Abdullah bin Habashi, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever cuts down a lote tree, God will throw his head into the Fire.’” Abu Dawud was asked about the meaning of this hadith, so he said: This hadith is brief, meaning: whoever cuts down a lote tree in the open desert, where travelers and animals seek shade, in vain and unjustly, without any right to it, God will throw his head into the Fire.
53:17: The Almighty says, His sight did not swerve, nor did it go astray. Ibn Abbas said: That is, he did not deviate to the right or to the left, nor did he exceed the limit he saw. It was also said, he did not go beyond what he was commanded to do. It was also said, he did not extend his sight to any signs other than what he saw. This is a polite description of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in that situation, as he did not turn to the right or to the left.
53:18: The Almighty said, He has certainly seen of the greatest signs of his Lord. Ibn Abbas said: He saw a flying carpet that filled the horizon. Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abdullah, who said: He saw of the greatest signs of his Lord. Ibn Abbas said: He saw a green flying carpet that filled the horizon of the sky. And on his authority, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Gabriel, peace be upon him, in a green flying robe. It filled the space between the sky and the earth. Al-Bayhaqi said: His statement in the hadith, He saw a flying carpet, means Gabriel, peace be upon him, in his image on a flying carpet. A flying carpet is a rug, and it is also said to be a mattress, and it is also said that it was a garment that was his clothing, as it was narrated that he saw him in a flying carpet. I said: Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The heart did not lie about what it saw. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Gabriel, peace be upon him, in a garment of fine linen, filling the space between heaven and earth. He said: This is a good and authentic hadith. I said: It has been narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse of God the Almighty, He drew near and came close, that it is in the form of precedence and delay, meaning that the flap was lowered for Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the night of the Ascension, so he sat on it, then it was raised and came close to his Lord. He said, “Gabriel left me and all sounds ceased to reach me, and I heard the speech of my Lord. So on this flap there is what one sits on, like a rug or something else.” In the first meaning, it is Gabriel. Abdur-Rahman ibn Zayd and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: He saw Gabriel (peace be upon him) in the form he is in in the heavens. Likewise in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abdullah, who said, He has seen some of the greatest signs of his Lord. He said, “He saw Gabriel (peace be upon him) in his form with six hundred wings.” It is not far-fetched with this that he was in a garment of flap and on a flap, and God knows best. Ad-Dahhak said: He saw the Lote Tree of the Limit, and from Ibn Masoud he saw the golden furnishings that covered the Lote Tree. Al-Mawardi narrated it and it was said that he saw the Ascension and it was said that it is what he saw that night during his journey in his return and beginning, and this is the best evidence for it to show him some of Our signs. It is permissible for it to be for partiality and for the major particle to be the object of saw and it is originally an attribute of the signs and it was also used alone for the heads of the signs. It is permissible to describe a group with a female attribute like the saying of the Most High and I have therein other interests. It was said that the major particle is an attribute of something omitted, meaning he saw some of the major signs of his Lord. It is permissible for it to be from an extra letter, meaning he saw some of the major signs of his Lord. It was said that there is an advancement and delay in it, meaning he saw some of the major signs of his Lord.
53:19: The Almighty's saying, Have you considered Al-Lat and Al-Uzza? When He mentioned the revelation to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and mentioned the effects of His power as he mentioned, He argued with the polytheists because they worshipped things without reason and said, Have you considered these gods which you worship? Has anything been revealed to you as was revealed to Muhammad? Al-Lat belonged to Thaqeef, Al-Uzza belonged to Quraysh and Banu Kinanah, and Manat belonged to Banu Hilal. Hisham said: Manat belonged to Hudhayl and Khuza'ah, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent Ali may God be pleased with him to destroy it in the year of the conquest. Then they took Al-Lat in Taif. It is newer than Manat and was a square rock. Its custodians were from Thaqeef and they had built a structure around it, so the Quraysh and all the Arabs venerated it. Because of this, the Arabs were called Zayd Al-Lat and Taym Al-Lat. It was in the place of the left minaret of the Taif mosque and remained like that until Thaqif converted to Islam. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah, who demolished it and burned it with fire. Then they took Al-Uzza, which was newer than Al-Lat. It was taken by Zalim ibn As’ad, and it was in the valley of Nakhal al-Sham, above Dhat ‘Irq. They built a house on it and they could hear the sound from it. Ibn Hisham said: And he told me on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Al-Uzza was a devil who would come to three tamarisk trees in Batn Nakhal. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, conquered Mecca, he sent Khalid ibn al-Walid, may God be pleased with him, and said: Go to Batn Nakhal, and you will find three tamarisk trees. Cut down the first one. So he went to it and cut it down. When he came to him, he said: Did you see anything? He said: No. He said: Then cut down the second one. So he went to it and cut it down. Then he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Did you see anything? He said: No. He said: Then cut down the third one. So he came to it and saw an Abyssinian woman with her hair fluffed up and her hands on her shoulders, waving her fangs. Behind her was Dubayyah al-Sulami, who was its custodian. He said: Oh glory to your ingratitude, no glory to you, I saw that God has humiliated you Then he struck it and split its head and behold it was a hot coal. Then he cut down the tree and killed the guardian Dibya. Then he came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and informed him. He said: That was al-‘Uzza, and it will never be worshipped again. Ibn Jubayr said: al-‘Uzza is a white stone that they used to worship. Qatadah: A house that was in Batn Nakhal. Manat was an idol of Khuza’ah. It was said that al-Lat, as some commentators mentioned, was taken by the polytheists from the word God. Al-‘Uzza is from al-‘Aziz, and Manat is from Manna of God when He decreed something. Ibn ‘Abbas, Ibn al-Zubayr, Mujahid, Hamid, and Abu Salih read al-Lat with a shaddah on the ta’. They said: He was a man who used to mix gruel for the pilgrims. Al-Bukhari mentioned it on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas. When he died, they devoted themselves to his grave and worshipped him. Ibn ‘Abbas: He used to sell gruel and ghee near a rock and pour it on it. When that man died, Thaqeef worshipped that rock out of respect for the one who mixed gruel. Abu Salih: He was only a man in Ta’if. He used to stand over their gods and mix gruel for them. When he died, they worshipped him. Mujahid: There was a man on the top of a mountain of his. A spoil from which he would make ghee, take curd from it, and gather its messengers. Then he would make hais from it and feed the pilgrims. It was in Batn Nakhl, and when it died, they worshipped it, which was Al-Lat. Al-Kalbi said that there was a man from Thaqeef called Sarmah ibn Ghanm, and it was said that he was Amir ibn Dharb Al-Adwani. The poet said: Do not support Al-Lat, for God will destroy her. How can he support you who does not support himself? The correct reading is Al-Lat with a light pronunciation is the name of an idol, and stopping on it with a ta’ is the choice of Al-Farra’. Al-Farra’ said: I saw Al-Kisa’i ask Abu Faq’as Al-Asadi and he said: Dhaha for Dhat and Lah for Al-Lat, and he read: Af-Ra’ytum Al-Lah. And this is how Al-Duri reads from Al-Kisa’i and Al-Bazzi from Ibn Kathir: Lah with a ha’ in stopping. And whoever says that Al-Lat is from God stopped with a ha’ as well. It was said that its origin is Lahiyya like Sha’at, its origin is Shahah, and it is from Lahit, meaning to disappear. The poet said: She was distracted and never knew of any outsider. I wish she had left so we could have seen her. In As-Sahah, Al-Lat was the name of an idol belonging to Thaqeef in Taif. Some Arabs stop on it with a ta’ and some with a ha’. Al-Akhfash said, “We heard some Arabs say Al-Lat and Al-Uzza, and say, ‘It is Al-Lat,’ making it a ta’ for silence, and ‘It is Al-Lat. So know that it is a genitive in the nominative case.” This is like ‘Ams’ with a kasra in any case, and it is better than it, because the alif and lam in Al-Lat are not dropped even if they are extra. As for what we heard from most of them regarding Al-Lat and Al-Uzza with a kasra, it is ‘God’ because it is a ha’, so it became a ta’ for connection, and in that language it is like ‘kan’ from ‘al-amr’ ‘kayt and kayt’. Likewise, ‘hayyat’ is in the language of those who break it, except that it is permissible for ‘hayyat’ to be a plural, but that is not permissible for Al-Lat because the ta’ is not added in the plural except with an alif. If you make the alif and ta’ extra, the name remains with one letter.
53:20: The Almighty said: And Manat, the third, the other. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaisin, Hamid, Mujahid, As-Sulami, and Al-A'sha read from Abu Bakr and Manat with a long vowel and a hamza.
