The rest omitted the hamza, two dialects. It was said that it was called that because they used to shed blood there to get closer to it. Thus, Mina was called that because of the large amount of blood shed there. Al-Kisa'i, Ibn Kathir, and Ibn Muhaisin stopped with the ha' according to the original. The rest stopped with the ta' following the script of the Mushaf. In As-Sahah: Manat was the name of an idol belonging to Hudhayl and Khuza'ah between Mecca and Medina. The ha' is for the feminine, and it is paused with the ta', which is a dialect, and the nisba to it is Manawi. Abd Manat ibn Udd ibn Tabikha and Zayd Manat ibn Tamim ibn Murr, it is long and short. Hawbar Al-Harithi said: Did Tamim ibn Abd Mana’ah come to us because of the hatred between us? God the Almighty says: The other. The Arabs do not say other for the third, but rather other is an adjective for the second. They differed on its meaning. Al-Khalil said that he said that to fit the beginnings of the verses, like his saying other aims and he did not say other. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: In the verse there is an inversion of the meaning of which is: Have you seen the other al-Lat and al-Uzza and the third Manat? It was said that he said and the third other Manat because it was ranked after al-Lat and al-Uzza in the polytheists' veneration, so the discussion is in accordance with it. We have mentioned from Ibn Hisham that Manat was first in the inversion, therefore it was given priority to them in veneration, and God knows best. There is an omission in the verse indicated by the context, meaning: Have you seen these gods? Have they benefited or harmed such that they can be partners with God?
53:21: Then he said, in a rebuke and rebuke manner, Do you have males and He has females? in response to their saying that the angels are daughters of God and the idols are daughters of God.
53:22: The Almighty’s saying, That meaning this division is an unfair division meaning unjust, deviant from the right and deviating from the truth. It is said, Daaz in the ruling, meaning he was unjust. And Daaz is his right, Yadhizuhu Dhaizan on the authority of Al-Akhfash, meaning he diminished it and shortchanged it. He said: And it is sometimes pronounced with a hamzah, so it is said, Daa’zahu, Yada’zuhu Dhaa’zan and he recited: If you distance yourself from us, we will disparage you, but if you stand, your share will be cut off and your nose will be in humiliation. Al-Kisa’i said: It is said dhaz yadhiz dayzan and dhaz yadhuz dawzan and dha’az yadha’az dha’azan if he wronged, transgressed, cheated, or diminished. The poet said: Banu Asad have gone astray with their rule, as they make the head like the tail. God the Almighty said: An unfair division meaning unjust, and it is fa'lī like Ṭuba and Ḥablā. They only broke the Ḍād to preserve the ya' because it is not in speech, so fa'lī is an adjective, but it is from the construction of nouns like sha'rī and oleander. Al-Farra' said: Some Arabs say dawzā and ḍayzā with a hamzah. Abu Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Zayd that he heard the Arabs pronounce the hamzah on Ḍayzā. Another one said: Ibn Kathir read it that way, making it a verbal noun like ḍikrā and not an adjective since there is no fa'lī among the adjectives, and its root is not fa'lī, since it does not contain what necessitates changing. It is from their saying da'azatuh, meaning I wronged him. So the meaning is an unfair division. It has been said that they are two expressions with the same meaning. Others have also narrated Ḍayzī and Ḍaḍāzi and Ḍawzī. Al-Mūraj said: They disliked the ḍād in Ḍayzā. They feared the ya' would change to a waw, which is from the daughters of waw. They broke the letter Ḍād for this reason, as they said in the plural of abīḥ“baydh” white, and the root is būdh like hamr red, saffar yesfar, and khidr green. As for the one who said: Ḍāz yadhūz, the noun is derived from it, dawzā like shūrā.
53:23: The Almighty says, They are only names you have named meaning, these idols are only names you have named meaning, you carved them and named them gods. You and your fathers meaning, you imitated them in that. God has not sent down any authority for them meaning, God has not sent down any proof or evidence for them. They follow nothing but conjecture He returned from addressing to the report, meaning, these people follow nothing but conjecture. And what their souls desire meaning, they incline toward it. The reading of the common people is yataba’un with a ya. Isa bin Umar, Ayyub, and Ibn al-Sameeq read yataba’un with a ta indicating the address, and this is the reading of Ibn Mas’ud and Ibn Abbas. And there has already come to them guidance from their Lord meaning, clarification from the Messenger that they are not gods
53:24: Or shall man have what he desires? That is, what he longs for, that is, it is not for him. It was also said, Or shall man have what he desires of sons, that is, he will have them but not daughters. It was also said, Or shall man have what he desires without a reward, that is not the case. It was also said, Or shall man have what he desires of prophethood, that it will be for him but not for others. It was also said, Or shall man have what he desires of the intercession of idols, this was revealed about Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith. It was also said about Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughirah, and it was also said about all the disbelievers.
53:25: . To God belongs the Hereafter and the first life. He gives to whomever He wills and withholds from whomever He wills, not what anyone desires.
53:26: The Almighty said, And how many an angel is there in the heavens whose intercession will avail nothing except after God has given permission for whom He wills and is pleased with. This is a rebuke from God the Most High to those who worship angels and idols and claim that this brings them closer to God the Most High. So know that the angels, despite their frequent worship and their honor with God, do not intercede except for those for whom He has given permission to intercede. Al-Akhfash said: The angel is one and its meaning is plural, and it is like the Almighty’s saying, There is not one of you who can prevent Him from interceding. It was said that He mentioned only one angel because the word how many indicates plural.
53:27: The Almighty says, Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are the disbelievers who say that the angels are daughters of God and the idols are daughters of God. They call the angels by female names meaning like a female name. That is, they believe that the angels are female and that they are the daughters of God.
53:28: And they have no knowledge of it meaning that they did not see the angels creating it, nor did they hear what they said from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor did they see it in a book. They follow meaning that they follow nothing but conjecture that the angels are females, and conjecture is of no avail against the truth.
53:29: The Almighty said, So turn away from whoever turns away from Our remembrance, meaning the Qur’an and faith. This was abrogated by the verse of the sword, and he intended nothing but the life of this world. It was revealed about Al-Nadr, and it was said: about Al-Walid.
53:30: That is the extent of their knowledge meaning, they only see the affairs of their worldly life and are ignorant of their religious affairs. Al-Farra' said, He belittled them and looked down on them meaning, that is the extent of their minds and the extent of their knowledge, that they preferred this world over the Hereafter. It was also said that they made the angels and idols daughters of God. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way meaning, who has deviated from His religion. And He is most knowing of who is guided so He will reward each one according to their deeds.
53:31: His Almighty saying, And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, that He may reward those who do evil for what they have done and reward those who do good with good. The lam is related to the meaning indicated by And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, as if He said, "He is the Owner of that. He guides whom He wills and misguides whom He wills, that He may reward the doer of good for his good and the doer of evil for his evil." It was also said, And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth is an interruption in the speech, and the meaning is that your Lord knows best who has strayed from His path, and He knows best who has been guided, that He may reward." It was also said that it is the lam of consequence, meaning, to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, meaning, the consequence of the matter of creation is that there will be among them evildoers and good-doers, so for the evildoer there is evil, which is Hell, and for the doer of good there is good, which is Paradise.
53:32: His Almighty saying, Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, except minor ones. There are three issues in this. The first: His Almighty saying, Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities. This is a description of the doers of good, meaning they do not commit the major sins, which is polytheism, because it is the greatest of sins. Al-A'mash, Yahya ibn Waththab, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa'i read it as major for monotheism. Ibn Abbas interpreted it as polytheism. And immoralities means adultery. Muqatil said, Major sins means every sin sealed with Hellfire, and and immoralities means every sin for which there is a prescribed punishment. We have already discussed this in An-Nisa', then he made an exception, which is: The second issue: He said, Except for the minor sins, which are minor sins that no one is safe from falling into except those whom God protects and preserves. There is a difference of opinion regarding its meaning. Abu Hurairah, Ibn Abbas, and Ash-Sha’bi said that the minor sins are everything less than fornication. Muqatil ibn Sulayman mentioned that this verse was revealed about a man called Nabhan At-Tammar who had a shop where he sold dates. A woman came to him to buy dates from him, so he said to her, There is something better than this inside your shop. When she entered, he tried to seduce her, but she refused and left. Nabhan regretted it and came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said, O Messenger of God, there is nothing that a man does but I have done it except intercourse. He said, Perhaps her husband is a transgressor. So this verse was revealed, and it was mentioned at the end of Hud. Ibn Mas’ud, Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, Hudhayfah, and Masruq also said that the minor sins are everything less than intercourse, such as kissing, winking, looking, and lying together. Masruq narrated from Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, who said, “The fornication of the eyes is looking, the fornication of the hands is touching, and the fornication of the feet is walking. It is only the private parts that confirm or deny it.” If it happens beforehand, then it is zina, and if it happens later, then it is a minor sin. In Sahih Al-Bukhari and Muslim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: I have not seen anything more like minor sins than “Abu Hurairah said that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: God has decreed for the son of Adam his share of zina, which he will inevitably attain. The zina of the eyes is looking, the zina of the tongue is speaking, the soul desires and longs, and the private parts confirm that or deny it.” The meaning is that the great immorality and complete zina that warrants the prescribed punishment in this world and the punishment in the hereafter is in the private parts, and anything else has a share of the sin, and God knows best. In the narration of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: “The share of fornication has been written for the son of Adam, which he will inevitably catch up to. The fornication of the eyes is looking, the fornication of the ears is listening, the fornication of the tongue is speaking, the fornication of the hand is touching, the fornication of the foot is walking, the heart desires and longs, and the private parts confirm that and deny it.” Narrated by Muslim. Al-Tha’labi mentioned the hadith of Tawus on the authority of Ibn Abbas, in which he mentioned the ear, hand, and foot, and he added after the eyes and tongue: And the fornication of the lips is kissing. This is a statement. Ibn Abbas also said: It is a man who commits a sin and then repents. He said: Didn’t you hear the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: If God forgives, He forgives a lot. What servant of yours is there who does not have pain? Narrated by Amr ibn Dinar on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Ibn Abbas. An-Nahhas said: This is the most authentic of what has been said about it and the most noble of its chains of transmission. Shu’bah narrated on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God the Almighty except for a touch, he said: It is for the servant to touch the sin and then not repeat it. The poet said: If you forgive, O God, you forgive a lot, and which servant of yours is there without pain? And this is what Mujahid and Al-Hasan said: It is the one who commits a sin and does not repeat it. A similar hadith was narrated from Az-Zuhri who said: Al-Lammah is when a person commits adultery then repents and does not do it again, or when he steals or drinks alcohol then repents and does not do it again. The evidence for this interpretation is the verse in which God the Almighty says: {And those who, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins} (Al-Anfal 11:20). Then He said: {For those, their reward is forgiveness from their Lord} (Al-Anfal 11:20). So He guaranteed them forgiveness, as He said after Al-Lammah: {Indeed, your Lord is Vast in forgiveness} (Al-Anfal 11:20). Based on this interpretation, except for Al-Lammah is a connected exception. Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Al-Aas said: O God, whatever is less than shirk. It was said: Al-Lammah is a sin between the two limits, meaning that for which no punishment was imposed in this world and for which no punishment was threatened in the Hereafter, and for which the five daily prayers can expiate. This was stated by Ibn Zayd, Ikrimah, Ad-Dahhak, and Qatadah. Al-Awfi and Al-Hakam ibn Utaybah narrated it from Ibn Abbas. Al-Kalbi said: Lammam has two meanings: Every sin for which God has not mentioned a prescribed punishment in this world or a punishment in the Hereafter. Therefore, the five daily prayers expiate it, as long as it does not reach the major sins and immoralities. The other meaning is the great sin that a person commits time and time again and then repents from it. Also from Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurairah, and Zaid bin Thabit: It is what happened in the pre-Islamic period, so they will not be held accountable for it. This is because the polytheists said to the Muslims: You were only working with us yesterday, so this verse was revealed. Zaid bin Aslam and his son said the same, and it is like the saying of God: And that you marry two sisters together, except for what has already occurred. It was said: Lamam is to commit a sin that is not usually done. This was said by Naftawayh. He said: The Arabs say It only comes to us occasionally, meaning from time to time. He said: It is not to be touched but not done, because the Arabs do not say It has come to us except when a person does it, not when he intends to do it but does not. In As-Sahih: A man’s lamam is from lamm and it is minor sins. It is said: It is approaching a sin without committing it. And he recited, other than Al-Jawhari: Come to Zainab before the caravan departs and say, If we get tired, then what does the heart own? Any closer. Ata’ bin Abi Rabah said: Lammam is the habit of the soul from time to time. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: It is what comes to mind, i.e., it occurs to the heart. Muhammad bin Al-Hanafiyyah said: Everything you think of, good or evil, is lamm. The evidence for this interpretation is the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him): The devil has a touch and the angel has a touch. The hadith has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah when God Almighty says: The devil threatens you with poverty. Abu Ishaq Al-Zajjaj said: The origin of lamm and ilmaam is what a person does time after time, but he does not delve into it or persist in it. It is said: I visited it if you visited it and left it. It is said: I did it only lamma or ilmaman, meaning time after time. Your visit is only lamma and ilmaman, and from it is the lamm of the imagination. Al-A’sha said: The pain of a phantom murdered after her rope was loosened from our rope and we were cut off It was said that except means and, but Al-Farra’ denied this and said: The meaning is except for the minor sins that are close together. It was also said that lamm is a sudden glance. I said: This is far-fetched, as it is excused from the outset and no one is held accountable for it, because it occurs without intention or choice, and its explanation has already been presented in An-Nur. Lamam is also a form of madness, and a man is laamum, meaning he has a jinn. It is also said that someone was afflicted with a touch of the jinn, which is possession and a small thing. The poet said: So, Kabisha, that was nothing but the words of a dreamer in his imagination. Third: The Almighty’s saying, Indeed, your Lord is Vast in forgiveness for whoever repents from his sin and seeks forgiveness. This was said by Ibn Abbas. Abu Maisarah Amr ibn Shurahbil, who was one of the best companions of Ibn Masoud, said, “I saw in a dream that I entered Paradise and there were tents pitched. I said, ‘To whom do these belong?’ They said, ‘To Dhu al-Kila’ and Hawshab, who were among those who killed one another.’ I said, ‘How is that?’ They said, ‘They met God and found Him Vast in forgiveness.’” Abu Khalid said, I have been informed that Dhu al-Kila’ freed twelve thousand girls. God the Almighty says, He knows you better than yourselves "when He created you from the earth" meaning your father Adam from clay. The wording is plural. At-Tirmidhi Abu Abdullah said: It is not like this with us, rather the creation occurred on the soil that was lifted from the earth and we were all in that soil and that clay. Then the waters came out of the clay to the loins with the scattered souls in their different forms. Then He extracted them from their loins in their different forms, some of them shining like pearls, some more luminous than others, some black like hot black, and some blacker than others. So the creation occurred on us and on him. Isa bin Hammad Al-Asqalani told us: Bishr bin Bakr told us: Al-Awza’i told us: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: The first and the last were presented to me in front of my room tonight. Someone said: O Messenger of God, and who of creation has passed on? He said: Yes, Adam and those after him were presented to me. Was anyone created? They said: And who are in the loins of men and the wombs of their mothers? He said: Yes, they were represented in the clay and I knew them just as He taught Adam all the names. I said, and it was mentioned in the beginning of Al-An’am that every human being is created from the clay of the spot in which he is buried. And when you were fetuses, the plural of fetus, which is the child as long as it is in the womb. It is called a fetus because of its concealment and hiding. Amr ibn Kulthum said: Hybrid color did not read fetus Makhool said, “We were fetuses in our mothers’ wombs, then some of us miscarried, and we were among those who remained. Then we became sucklings, then some of us perished, and we were among those who remained. Then we became adolescents, then some of us perished, and we were among those who remained. Then we became young men, then some of us perished, and we were among those who remained. Then we became old men, may you have no father. So what do we expect after this?” Ibn Lahi’ah narrated on the authority of Al-Harith bin Yazid, on the authority of Thabit bin Al-Harith Al-Ansari, who said: The Jews used to say, whenever a young boy of theirs died, he was a friend. report of that reached the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so he said, “The Jews have lied. There is no soul that God creates in its mother’s womb except that it is either wretched or blessed.” Then God, the Most High, revealed this verse: He is most knowing of you when He produced you from the earth to the end of it. A similar verse was narrated on the authority of Aisha: The Jews used to say, ‘So do not praise yourselves,’ meaning, do not praise yourselves or speak ill of yourself, for that is further from showing off and closer to humility. He knows best who fears Him meaning who is sincere in his actions and fears God’s punishment. Al-Hasan and others said: God knows every soul’s actions, what it will do, and what it will become. The meaning of this verse has already been discussed in Surat An-Nisa’, when God the Almighty says: Have you not seen those who claim themselves to be pure? Ponder its meaning there. Ibn Abbas said: “There is no one from this nation whom I claim to be pure except the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him). And God knows best.”
53:33: The Almighty's saying, Have you seen him who turned away? The verses, when explaining the ignorance of the polytheists in worshipping idols, mentioned one of them specifically for his evil deeds. Mujahid, Ibn Zayd, and Muqatil said that it was revealed about Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira, who had followed the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in his religion, but some of the polytheists reviled him and said, Why have you abandoned the religion of the elders and led them astray and claimed that they are in the Fire? He said, If you fear the punishment of God, so he guaranteed to him that if he gave him something from his wealth and returned to his polytheism, he would bear the punishment of God on his behalf. So he gave the one who rebuked him some of what he had guaranteed him, then he was stingy and prevented him, so God revealed this verse. Muqatil said, Al-Walid praised the Qur'an then refrained from it, so the verse was revealed, And gave a little, meaning of goodness with his tongue, and emphasized that, meaning he cut that off and refrained from it. It was also reported from him that he gave the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) the pledge of faith then turned away, so the verse, Have you seen him who turned away? was revealed. Ibn Abbas, Al-Suddi, Al-Kalbi, and Al-Musayyab bin Sharik said: This was revealed about Uthman bin Affan may God be pleased with him. He used to give charity and spend it on charitable purposes. His foster brother, Abdullah bin Abi Sarh, said to him: What are you doing? Soon you will have nothing left. Uthman said: I have sins and wrongdoings, and by what I do I seek the pleasure of God Almighty and hope for His forgiveness. Abdullah said to him: Give me your camel and its saddle and I will bear all your sins. So he gave it to him and had witnesses testify against him, and he refrained from some of what he used to give in charity. Then God Almighty revealed: {Have you seen him who turns away * And gives little and is stingy?} So Uthman returned to the best and most beautiful of that. Al-Wahidi and Al-Tha’labi mentioned this. Al-Suddi also said: It was revealed about Al-Aas bin Wa’il Al-Sahmi, because he sometimes agreed with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi said: It was revealed about Abu Jahl bin Hisham, who said: By God, Muhammad only orders good morals. This is the meaning of the Almighty’s saying: And he gave little and was straitened. Ad-Dahhak said: It is Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith, who gave five she-camels to a poor man from the Muhajireen when he apostatized from his religion, and he guaranteed to bear the sin of his return. The root of akadda is from beggary. It is said about someone who dug a well and then reached a rock that is not easy for him in digging: he has stagnated. Then the Arabs used it to mean someone who gave but did not complete it, and someone who asked for something but did not reach the end of it. Al-Hutay’ah said: He gave a little, then he was less generous in giving. And whoever does good to people will be praised. Al-Kisa’i and others said: The hoof becomes akdā and ajbāl if it reaches a mound or a mountain in its hole and is unable to dig. And he dug, so he became akdā if he reached the backbone. And it is said: kadayt his fingers became tired if they became exhausted from digging. And kadayt his hand became tired if it did not do anything. And the plant becomes akdā little if its yield decreases. And the land becomes kadayt almost and kadayt almost and it is kadayt little if its growth is slow. From Abu Zaid. And akdayt I turned a man away from something means I turned him back from it. And the man becomes akdā little if his goodness decreases.
53:34: The Almighty said, And he gave a little and was deprived. That is, he cut off a little.
53:35: The Almighty says, Does he have knowledge of the unseen, so he sees? That is, does this beggar have knowledge of what is hidden from him regarding the punishment? So he sees That is, he knows what is hidden from him regarding the Hereafter and what will happen to him, such that he can guarantee bearing the punishment for someone else. This is sufficient as ignorance and foolishness. This seeing is transitive with two objects, and the two objects are omitted, as if he said, So he sees the unseen like he sees.
53:36: The Almighty’s saying, Or has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Moses? meaning the scriptures of and Abraham who fulfilled as in Surat Al-A’la the scriptures of Abraham and Moses, meaning that no soul will be taken in place of another, as He said, No bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. He mentioned the scriptures of Abraham and Moses specifically because between Noah and Abraham, a man would be taken for the sin of his brother, son, and father. Al-Hudhayl ibn Shurahbil said that this is a lightened version of the heavy one, and its position is in the genitive case in place of what, or it could be in the nominative case with the omission of he. Sa’id ibn Jubayr and Qatadah read it in a light form, and its meaning is truthful in his words and deeds, and it returns to the meaning of the reading of the group. And fulfilled with emphasis, meaning he fulfilled all that was imposed on him, so he did not omit anything from it. This has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah when God Almighty said, And when his Lord tested Abraham with commands, and he fulfilled them. And fulfillment is completion. Abu Bakr Al-Warraq said that he fulfilled the condition of what he claimed, so He tested him in his wealth, his children, and himself, and found him fulfilling that, so that is that. His saying, And Abraham who fulfilled, meaning he claimed Islam and then confirmed his claim. It was also said: And in his work every day with four rak’ahs in the early part of the day. Al-Haytham narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Sahl ibn Sa’d al-Sa’idi narrated on the authority of his father: Shall I not tell you why God Almighty called His friend Abraham who fulfilled? Because he used to say every morning and evening, Glory be to God when you go to bed and when you wake up verse. Sahl ibn Mu’adh narrated it on the authority of Anas on the authority of his father on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was also said: And in, meaning fulfilled what he was sent with, which is His saying, No bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another. Ibn Abbas said: Before Abraham, peace be upon him, they would punish a man for the sin of another, and they would punish a guardian for a guardian in killing and wounding, so a man would be killed for his father, son, brother, paternal uncle, maternal uncle, cousin, relative, wife, husband, and slave. Abraham, peace be upon him, conveyed to them on the authority of God Almighty, No bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another. Al-Hasan, Qatada, and Sa’id ibn Jubayr said regarding God Almighty’s saying, and fulfilled, he acted according to what he was commanded. And he conveyed the messages of his Lord. This is better because it is general, and Mujahid said the same, and he fulfilled what was imposed upon him. Abu Malik Al-Ghifari said that the Almighty’s statement, And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another to His statement, Then which of the favors of your Lord do you dispute? is in the scriptures of Abraham and Moses. The discussion of And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another has already been completed at the end of Al-An’am.
53:37: God Almighty said, And Abraham who fulfilled
53:38: The Almighty says: No soul shall bear the burden of another.
53:39: The Almighty's saying, And that man can have nothing but what he strives for. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that it was abrogated by the Almighty's saying, And those who have believed and whose offspring follow them in faith - We will join with them their offspring. Thus, the child will be on the Day of Resurrection in the scale of his father. God the Almighty will intercede for fathers for their children and children for their fathers. This is indicated by the Almighty's saying, Your fathers and your sons - you do not know which of them is nearest to you in benefit. Most of the commentators said: It is definitive and no one's work will benefit anyone. They unanimously agreed that no one can pray on behalf of another. Malik did not permit fasting, Hajj, or charity on behalf of a dead person, but he said that if he left a will for Hajj and died, it is permissible to perform Hajj on his behalf. Al-Shafi'i and others permitted voluntary Hajj on behalf of a dead person. It was narrated on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her that she performed I'tikaf on behalf of her brother Abd al-Rahman and freed a slave woman on his behalf. It was narrated that Sa`d ibn `Ubadah said to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): My mother has died, so should I give charity on her behalf? He said: Yes. Which charity is best? He said: Giving water to drink. All of this has already been mentioned in detail in Surat Al-Baqarah, Surat Al-`Imran, and Surat Al-A`raf. It has also been said that God, the Almighty, said: And that man will have nothing but what he strives for. The lam of the genitive in Arabic means ownership and obligation, so man will have nothing but what he strives for. So if someone else gives charity on his behalf, then nothing is due to him, except that God, the Almighty, bestows upon him what he is not entitled to, just as He bestows upon children by admitting them into Paradise without their doing any work. Al-Rabi` ibn Anas said: And that man will have nothing but what he strives for, meaning the disbeliever. As for the believer, he will have what he strives for and what someone else strives for. I said: Many hadiths indicate this statement, and that the believer receives the reward of righteous deeds from others. Many of them have been presented before for those who reflect on them, and there is no disagreement regarding charity, as in the introduction to the book of Muslim on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mubarak, and in the Sahih: “When a person dies, his deeds come to an end except for three: a righteous child who prays for him.” All of this is a favor from God, the Almighty, just as the increase in multiplication is a favor from Him, and He writes for them for one good deed ten to seven hundred times to a million good deeds, as “It was said to Abu Hurairah, ‘Did you hear the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, say: God rewards for one good deed a million times. ’ He said, ‘I heard him say: God rewards for one good deed two million good deeds. ’” This is a favor and the path of justice. And that man shall have nothing but what he strives for. I said: It is possible that his statement, And that man shall have nothing but what he strives for, is specific to the bad deed, as evidenced by what is in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: God, the Almighty, said: If My servant intends to do a good deed but does not do it, I write it down as a good deed for him. If he does it, I write it down as ten good deeds to seven hundred times over. But if he intends to do a bad deed but does not do it, I do not write it down for him. If he does it, I write it down as one bad deed.” Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: Except what he strives for means except what he intended. His statement, may God bless him and grant him peace: People will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection according to their intentions.
53:40: The Almighty says, And that his effort will soon be seen, meaning that God Almighty will show him his reward on the Day of Resurrection. Then He will reward him, meaning He will reward him for it, with the fullest reward. Al-Akhfash said, It is said, ‘I rewarded him with the reward,’ and ‘I rewarded him with the reward,’ the same, there is no difference between them. The poet said: If Alqamah bin Saad rewarded his efforts, I would not reward him with a single day’s affliction. He combined the two languages.
53:41: God Almighty says: Then He will reward him with the fullest reward.
53:42: The Almighty’s saying, And indeed, to your Lord is the final destination, meaning the return, the outcome, and the destination. He punishes and rewards. It was also said that the blessing begins from Him and that security is to Him. And on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka’b, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding His saying, And indeed, to your Lord is the final destination, he said: There is no thought about the Lord. And on the authority of Anas, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When God Almighty is mentioned, then he stops. I said: And from this meaning is his saying, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him: The devil comes to one of you and says, ‘Who created such and such?’ until he says to him, ‘Who created your Lord?’ When he reaches that point, let him seek refuge in God and stop. It was mentioned at the end of Al-A’raf. And the one who said it did well: Do not think about the Most High, the Almighty, for if you do, you will perish and be let down. Here are his creations, so consider them and say what the venerable Khalil said:
53:43: The Almighty’s saying, And that it is He who makes people laugh and cry. The intermediaries have disappeared and the truths remain with God Almighty, for there is no doer but Him. In Sahih Muslim, “On the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, she said: No, by God, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, never said that the dead is tormented by the crying of his family, but he said: God increases the torment of the unbeliever by the crying of his family, and God is He who makes people laugh and cry, and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another.” And on her authority, she said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by some of his companions who were laughing, so he said: If you knew what I know, you would laugh little and cry much. Then Gabriel came down to him and said: O Muhammad, God says to you, And that it is He who makes people laugh and cry. So he returned to them and said: I had not taken forty steps until Gabriel came to me and said: Go to these people and tell them that God Almighty is He who makes people laugh and cry, meaning He decreed the causes of laughter and crying. Ata’ ibn Abi Muslim said: He means He makes me happy and sad, because happiness brings about laughter. Sadness brings crying. It was said to Umar: Did the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) laugh? He said: Yes, faith is more firmly rooted in their hearts than the firmest mountains. This meaning has been mentioned previously in An-Naml and Bara’ah. Al-Hasan said: God makes the people of Paradise laugh in Paradise. And He makes the people of Hell cry in Hell. It was also said that He makes whomever He wills laugh in this world by making them happy and makes whomever He wills cry by making them sad. Ad-Dahhak: He made the plants on the earth laugh and the sky cry with rain. It was also said that He made the trees laugh with their flowers and the clouds cry with rain. Dhu An-Nun said: He makes the hearts of the believers and the knowers laugh with the sun of His knowledge and makes the hearts of the disbelievers and the sinners cry with the darkness of His denial and disobedience. Sahl ibn Abdullah said: God makes the obedient laugh with mercy and makes the sinners cry with wrath. Muhammad ibn Ali At-Tirmidhi said: He makes the believer laugh in the Hereafter and makes him cry in this world. Bassam ibn Abdullah said: God makes their teeth laugh and their hearts cry, and he recited: The teeth laugh and the insides burn, but their laughter is a fabrication and a lie. Oh God, there is a man crying with eyes that have no tears, and there is a man laughing with teeth that have no breath It was said: God Almighty has distinguished man from all other animals with laughter and crying, and there is no other animal that laughs and cries except man. It was also said: Only monkeys laugh and do not cry, and only camels cry and do not laugh. Youssef bin Al-Hussein said: Tahir Al-Maqdisi was asked: Do the angels laugh? He said: They did not laugh, nor did anyone below the throne, since Hell was created.
53:44: And that it is He who causes death and brings to life meaning He decreed the causes of death and life. It was said that He created death and life as He said: Or he who was dead and We gave him life (al-An'am 2:17). And He said: Only those who listen respond, and God will raise the dead (al-An'am 2:18) based on what was mentioned above. This is what is referred to by the statement of Ata': He caused death by His justice and brought to life by His grace. And the statement of those who said: He caused death by withholding and miserliness and brought to life by generosity and giving. It was said: He caused death of the sperm and brought life to the soul. It was said: He caused death of the fathers and brought life to the sons. It was said: By life He means fertility and by death, barrenness. It was said: He put me to sleep and awakened. It was said: He caused death in this world and brought life to life for the resurrection.
53:45: And that He created the two mates, the male and the female meaning from the children of Adam. He did not mean that Adam and Eve were created from a drop of sperm. A drop of sperm is water, derived from the word nataaf when it drips.
53:46: Tamaana means pouring into the womb and ejaculating, as said by Al Kalbi, Ad-Dahhak, and Ata' ibn Abi Rabah. It is said that a man ejaculates and he ejaculates from semen, and it was called Mina by this name because of the blood that is ejaculated in it, i.e. shed. It was also said that Tamaana means to estimate, as said by Abu Ubaidah. It is said that he ejaculated something if he estimated it, and he ejaculated it for him, as the poet said: Until you find what you want, German Whatever the Almighty can do for you
53:47: The Almighty says: And that upon Him is the other creation meaning, He will return the souls to their ghostly forms for the resurrection. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read the creation with a fat-ha on the sheen and a long vowel, meaning He promised that and His promise was true.
53:48: And that it is He who enriches and makes sufficient. Ibn Zayd said: He enriches whom He wills and makes poor whom He wills, then he recited: He expands provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for him. And he recited: He contracts and expands. This was chosen by Al-Tabari. Also from Ibn Zayd, Mujahid, Qatada, and Al-Hasan: Enriched means to be in charge, and Aqna means to serve. It was said: Aqna means to give you possessions that you acquire, and this is also the meaning of Aqna. It was said: Its meaning is that He is pleased with what He has given, i.e., He enriched him, then He was pleased with what He gave him, as Ibn Abbas said. Al-Jawhari said: A man was made sufficient, like rich, he is rich, and God made him sufficient, i.e., God gave him what he acquires of possessions and wealth. God also made him sufficient, meaning He is pleased with him. Al-Qana means contentment, on the authority of Abu Zaid, who said: The Arabs say: Whoever is given one hundred goats has been given qana, and whoever is given one hundred sheep has been given wealth, and whoever is given one hundred camels has been given desire. It is said: God enriched him and made him content, meaning He gave him what he finds comfort in. It was also said: He enriched himself and made his creation poorer than him, meaning He enriched himself and made His creation poorer than him. This was said by Sulayman al-Taymi. Sufyan said: He enriched himself with contentment and made him content. Al-Akhfash said: He made him poorer. Ibn Kaysan said: He gave birth. This goes back to what was mentioned above.
53:49: And that He is the Lord of Sirius Sirius is the bright planet that rises after Gemini, and its rising occurs during intense heat. They are the two Sirius, the transiting Sirius in Gemini, and Sirius the obscure Sirius in the forearm. The Arabs claim that they are the sisters of Canopus. He was mentioned as the Lord of Sirius, even though he was the Lord of someone else, because the Arabs used to worship him. Then God informed them that Sirius was a creature and not a Lord. There was disagreement about who worshipped him. Al-Suddi said: Himyar and Khuza'a used to worship him. Another said: The first to worship him was Abu Kabsha, one of the Prophet's grandfathers on his mother's side. That is why the polytheists of Quraysh used to call the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) Ibn Abi Kabsha when he called to God and opposed their religions. They said: What we have encountered from Ibn Abi Kabsha! Abu Sufyan said on the day of the conquest, while he was standing in some narrow straits and the armies of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) were passing by him: The matter of Ibn Abi Kabsha has been decided. Those Arabs who did not worship Sirius used to venerate it and believe in its influence on the world. The poet said: September has passed, the heat has risen, and the fire of Sirius has subsided. It was said: The Arabs say in their fables: Suhayl and Sirius were a pair, then Suhayl descended and became Yemeni, then Sirius followed it and crossed the galaxy and was called Al-Obour, and Al-Ghamisaa stayed and cried for the loss of Suhayl until his eyes closed, so it was called Ghamisaa because it was more hidden than the other.
53:50: And that He destroyed the first 'Aad He called them the first because they were before Thamud. It was also said that Thamud were before 'Aad. Ibn Zayd said: They were called the first 'Aad because they were the first nation to be destroyed after Noah, peace be upon him. Ibn Ishaq said: They are two 'Aad. The first was destroyed by the furious wind, then there was the other which was destroyed by the blast. It was also said that the first 'Aad is 'Aad bin Iram bin Aws bin Sam bin Noah, and the second 'Aad are from the descendants of the first 'Aad, and the meanings are close. It was also said that the latter 'Aad are the tyrants and they are the people of Hud. The general reading is (the first 'Aad) with the tanween and hamza. Nafi', Ibn Muhaisin and Abu 'Amr read (the first 'Aad) by moving the vowel of the hamza to the lam and assimilating the tanween into it, except that Qalun and Al-Soussi pronounce the silent hamza. The rest changed it to a waw as it is originally, and the Arabs change this change and say: Stand now from us and add the two together, meaning: Stand now and add the two together.
53:51: And Thamud - what He left behind. Thamud are the people of Salih who were destroyed according to the Sahih. It was read (Thamudan) and (Thamud) as mentioned before. It is in the accusative case in apposition to ‘Aad.
53:52: And the people of Noah before meaning, and the people of Noah before him were destroyed, Ad and Thamud Indeed, they were more unjust and more rebellious because of the length of time Noah was among them, to the point that a man among them would take his son by the hand and go to Noah, peace be upon him, and say: Beware of this man, for he is a liar. My father walked with me to this man and said to me as I said to you. So the older one would die in disbelief, and the younger one would grow up following his father's advice. It was said that the metaphor refers to everyone mentioned from Ad, Thamud, and the people of Noah, meaning that they were more disbelieving and more rebellious than the polytheists of the Arabs. So there is consolation and comfort in it for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, as if he was saying to him: Be patient too, for the good outcome is for you.
53:53: And the overturned city fell down meaning the cities of the people of Lot, peace be upon him, were overturned with them, i.e. they were turned upside down and their top became their bottom. It is said: afkatuhu meaning he turned them upside down and diverted them. Ahwa means he swallowed them up after they were raised to the sky. Gabriel raised them up then he threw them down to the earth. Al-Mubarrad said: he made them fall down. It is also said: hawa with the fat-ha, yahwi hawya, meaning it fell, and ahwa means he caused them to fall.
53:54: And that which covered it covered it meaning that it was covered with what it was covered with of stones. God the Most High said: And We turned it upside down and rained down upon it stones of baked clay. It was said that the metaphor refers to all of these nations, meaning that what covered them of punishment covered them, and it was not clear because each of them was destroyed by a blow different from that by which the other was destroyed. It was also said that this is to magnify the matter.
53:55: Then which of the favors of your Lord do you doubt? That is, which of the favors of your Lord do you doubt? The addressee is the disbelieving person. The favors are blessings, the singular of which is alay, ila, and ila. Jacob read it as tamara by assimilating one of the two ta's into the other and emphasizing the letter.
53:56: The Almighty says: This is a warner among the first warnings. Ibn Jurayj and Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: He means that Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, is a warner of the truth with which the prophets before him were warned. If you obey him, you will succeed, otherwise what happened to those who denied the previous messengers will happen to you. Qatadah said: He means the Qur'an, and that he is a warner of what the previous scriptures warned with. It was also said: What He has informed us of of the report of the past nations who perished is to frighten this nation lest what happened to those people of warnings befall them, i.e. like a warning. In the speech of the Arabs, a warning means warning, just as denier means denial, i.e. this is a warning to you. Abu Malik said: What I have warned you of of the events of the past nations is in the scriptures of Abraham and Moses. Al-Suddi said: Abu Saleh told me: These letters that God Almighty mentioned in His saying: Or has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Moses * and Abraham who fulfilled to His saying: This is a warner among the first warners are all in the scriptures of Abraham and Moses.
53:57: The Almighty said: The Hour has drawn near meaning the Hour has drawn near and the Resurrection is near. He called it the Hour because it is close to Him, as He said: They see it far off, but We see it near. It was also said that He called it the Hour because it is close to the people and near them so that they may prepare for it, because everything that is coming is near. He said: The departure time has come, but our passengers have not yet left our saddlebags, as if they had In As-Sahah: Azfa At-Tarhul Ya’zuf Azfan means it drew near and came close. From this is the saying of God the Almighty: The Day of Resurrection has drawn near, meaning the Day of Resurrection. A man is azfa meaning he is imposing, so he is azf on the doer. Al-Mutaazef is the short one who is close. Abu Zaid said: I asked an Arab, What is Al-Muhannati’? He said, Al-Mutaka’ki. I replied, What is Al-Mutaka’ki? He said, Al-Mutaazef. I said, What is Al-Mutaazef? He said, You are an idiot, and he left me and passed by.
53:58: There is no one to uncover it besides God meaning there is no one besides God who can delay or bring it forward. It was said: Uncovering means uncovering, meaning that none can uncover or reveal it except God. So, Kashifah is a noun meaning a source and the ha in it is like the ha in al-'aqabah end result, al-'afiyah healthy well-being, dahiyah calamity and al-baqiah remaining, like their saying: So-and-so has no remainder ma bayyih meaning any permanence. It was also said: It means no one can repel that, meaning that when the Resurrection comes, none of their gods will uncover it and none will save them except God. The Resurrection has been called al-Ghashiyah the Overwhelming, so if it is al-Ghashiyah the Overwhelming, then its rejection is kashf. So, al-Kashifah according to this is a deleted feminine adjective, meaning a uncovering soul, a uncovering group or a uncovering state. It was said that Kashifah means revealer and the ha is for emphasis like rawiyah narrator and dahiyah catastrophe.
53:59: The Almighty says, Do you then marvel at this statement? meaning the Qur’an. This is a question of rebuke. Do you then marvel at it? is a denial of it. And you laugh in mockery and do not cry in aversion and fear of the threat. "It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was never seen laughing after the revelation of this verse except with a smile." "Abu Hurairah said: When the verse "Is it at this statement that you marvel?" was revealed, the people of the Suffa said: "Indeed we belong to God and indeed to Him we shall return." Then they wept until their tears ran down their cheeks. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard their weeping, he wept with them, and we wept because of his weeping. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "He who weeps out of fear of God will not enter Hellfire, and he who persists in disobeying God will not enter Paradise. And if you did not sin, God would replace you with people who would sin, and He would forgive them and have mercy on them. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. Abu Hazim said: Gabriel descended upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a man was with him who was weeping. He said to him: Who is this? He said: This is so-and-so. Gabriel said: We weigh all the deeds of the children of Adam except weeping, for God Almighty extinguishes seas of Hellfire with a single tear.
53:60: God Almighty said: And you laugh and do not cry.
53:61: The Almighty said, And you are heedless meaning distracted and turning away. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, it was narrated by Al-Walibi and Al-Awfi from him. Ikrimah said on his authority: It is singing in the language of Himyar. It is said, Samad lana meaning to talk to us. So when they heard the Quran being recited, they would sing and play so that they would not hear. Ad-Dahhak said, Samidon meaning, high and proud. In As-Sahah: Samad, samud and raised his head in arrogance. Every one who raises his head is samd. He said: The stillness of the night is light and the clouds are blue He says: There is no fodder in their stomachs. Ibn al-A'rabi said: Samada Samood is high. And camels samada in their gait are hurried. Samud is amusement and Samid is the playful. It is said for a female singer: Asmadina, meaning they distracted us with singing. And fertilizing the earth is to put manure in it, which is saddlery and ashes. And fertilizing the head is to remove its hair, a language for tasbeed. And the man is Asmaad with the Hamza is Asma'idad meaning he swelled with anger. It was narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, that the meaning of Samidun is to sit, not praying or waiting for the prayer. Al-Hasan said: They stand for prayer before the Imam stands. From this is what was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he went out and the people were waiting for him, so he said: Why do I see you standing? Al-Mawardi narrated it and Al-Mahdawi mentioned it: On the authority of Ali, that he went out to prayer and saw the people standing waiting for him, so he said: Why are you standing? Al-Mahdawi said it. What is known in the language is Samad, Yasmeed, Samoud, if he is busy and turns away. Al-Mubarrad said: Samidun, Khamidun. The poet said: The two events brought the women of Al Harb the power to support him. Saleh Abu Al-Khalil said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited, “Is it at this statement that you marvel? And laugh and do not cry, while you are heedless. So prostrate to God and worship Him,” he was never seen laughing except smiling until he died, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Nahhas mentioned this.
53:62: The Almighty's saying, So prostrate to God and worship Him. It was said that what is meant by it is the prostration of reciting the Quran, and this is the opinion of Ibn Mas'ud. Abu Hanifa and Ash-Shafi'i also said the same. The beginning of the Surah was mentioned earlier from the hadith of Ibn Abbas, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prostrated in it and the polytheists prostrated with him. It was said that the polytheists prostrated with him because they heard the voices of the devils during the recitation of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he said, Have you considered Al-Lat and Al-'Uzza? And Manat, the third, the other? And that he said, Those are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is hoped for. This is how it is narrated by Sa'id ibn Jubayr, It is hoped for. And in the narration of Abu Al-'Aliyah, And their intercession is accepted, and the likes of them are not forgotten. So the polytheists rejoiced and thought that it was from the words of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as was explained above in the Hajj. When the report reached Abyssinia, the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) who were there, they returned, thinking that the people of Mecca had believed. The people of Mecca were harsher on them and began to torture them until God relieved them. It was said that what is meant is the obligatory prostration in prayer, and this is the opinion of Ibn Umar, who did not consider it one of the obligatory prostrations. Malik also said the same. Ubayy ibn Ka`b may God be pleased with him narrated: The last action of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was to omit prostration in the Mufassal. The first is more correct, and the statement about it has been explained at the end of Al-A`raf. Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds. The interpretation of Surat An-Najm has been completed.
54:1: All of it was revealed in Mecca according to the majority of scholars. Muqatil said: Except for three verses from the words of God Almighty: Or do they say, 'We are all victorious?' to the words: And the Hour is more grievous and bitter. This is not correct based on what follows. They are fifty-five verses. God the Almighty said: The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split. “Draw near” means it has drawn near, just as the approaching hour has drawn near as we have explained. So, in relation to what has passed, it is near, because most of the world has passed, as Qatada narrated on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) delivered a sermon when the sun was about to set, and he said: Nothing remains of your world in comparison to what has passed except what remains of this day in comparison to what has passed. And we do not see of the sun except a little. Ka’b and Wahb said: The world is six thousand years. Wahb said: Five thousand six hundred years have passed. An-Nahhas mentioned this. Then the Almighty said: And the moon has split meaning, the moon has split. Hudhayfah also recited it: (The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split) with the addition of (already). The majority of scholars agreed with this, and it was proven in Sahih al-Bukhari and others from the hadith of Ibn Mas`ud, Ibn `Umar, Anas, Jubair ibn Mut`im, and Ibn `Abbas may God be pleased with them. Anas said: The people of Makkah asked the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) for a sign, and the moon split in Makkah twice, so the verse: (The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split) was revealed until His saying: Continuing magic Dhahabi says. Abu `Eisa al-Tirmidhi said: This is a good and authentic hadith. Al-Bukhari’s wording on the authority of Anas said: The moon split into two parts. Some people said: The splitting of the moon has not yet occurred and it is awaited, meaning that the Hour has drawn near and the moon has split, and that when the Hour comes, the sky will split with everything in it of the moon and other things. Al-Qushayri said the same. Al-Marudi mentioned that this is the view of the majority, and he said: Because when it splits, no one will remain who will not see it, because it is a sign and people are equal with regard to signs. Al-Hasan said: The Hour has drawn near, and when it comes, the moon will split after the second blast. It was also said: And the moon will split meaning the matter will become clear and apparent, and the Arabs use the moon as an example of what is clear. He said: Stand up, O my mother's sons, on the breasts of your mounts, for I am inclined towards a tribe other than yours. She protected the needs and the night was full of moons, and she tightened the folds of the mounts and saddles. It was said: The splitting of the moon is the splitting of the darkness from it by its rising during it, just as the dawn is called a breaking because of the splitting of the darkness from it. Its splitting may be expressed by its splitting, as Al-Nabigha said: When they turned back, and they had a great noise, a caller called us at the break of dawn. I said: It has been proven by the transmission of trustworthy individuals that the moon split in Mecca, and this is the apparent meaning of the revelation. It is not necessary that people be equal in that, because it was a night sign, and that it was by the Prophet’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) supplication to God Almighty in response to a challenge. It is narrated that when Hamzah ibn Abdul Muttalib converted to Islam out of anger at Abu Jahl’s insulting of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he asked God to show him a sign that would increase his certainty in his faith. It was previously mentioned in the Sahih that the people of Mecca were the ones who asked and requested God to show them a sign, so he showed them the moon splitting into two halves, as in the hadith of Ibn Mas’ud and others. It was also narrated from Hudhayfah that he delivered a sermon in Mada’in and then said: “Behold, the Hour has drawn near, and the moon split during the time of your Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him).” It was also said that this is a case of advancing and delaying, and its meaning is that the moon split and the Hour drew near, as Ibn Kaysan said. Al-Farra’ mentioned that if two verbs are close in meaning, then you may advance or delay them when God Almighty says: Then He drew near and descended.
54:2: The Almighty said: And if they see a sign, they turn away. This indicates that they saw the splitting of the moon. Ibn Abbas said: A group of people gathered around the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: If you are truthful, then split the moon for us into two parts, one half over Abu Qubays and the other half over Quaiqaan. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to them: If you do that, will you believe? They said: Yes? And it was the night of Badr, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) asked his Lord to grant him what they had said, so the moon split into two parts, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was calling out to the polytheists: O so-and-so, O so-and-so, bear witness. In the hadith of Ibn Mas`ud: The moon split during the time of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Quraysh said: This is from the magic of Ibn Abi Kabshah. He has bewitched you, so ask the travelers. So they asked them and they said: We have seen the moon split. Then this verse was revealed: “The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split. And if they see a sign, they turn away.” That is, if they see a sign that proves the truthfulness of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him), they turn away from faith. And they say, ‘Persistent magic,’ meaning, it is going away, from their saying: The thing passed and continued if it went away. This was said by An, Qatadah, Mujahid, Al-Farra’, Al-Kisa’i, and Abu Ubaidah, and Al-Nahhas chose it. Abu Al-`Aliyah and Al-Dahhak said: It is a firm, strong, and intense verse, and it is from mara, which means strength, as Laqit said: Until she continued on her bitterness, the bitterness of determination, neither by force nor by force Al-Akhfash said: It is taken from passing the rope and weakening the strength of its twisting. It was said: Its meaning is bitterness. It is said: The matter of the thing became bitter, and likewise the thing passed, it passes with the fat-ha, bitterness, so it is bitter, and his matter changed it and passed it. Al-Rabi’ said: Continuous and effective. Yaman: past. Abu Ubaidah: void. It was said: permanent. He said: And there is nothing that is straight and continuous That is, permanent. It was said: Some of it resembles others, meaning that Muhammad’s actions continued in this manner, so he did not produce anything that had a reality, but rather all of it was imagination. It was said: Its meaning is that he passed from the earth to the heavens.
54:3: And they denied our Prophet and followed their desires meaning their misguidance and choices. And every matter is settled meaning that it is settled for every worker whose work he does. So goodness is settled for its people in Paradise, and evil is settled for its people in Paradise. With his family in hell. Shaiba read it with a fat-ha on the qaf, meaning that everything has a time when it occurs, without precedence. It was delayed and it was narrated on the authority of Abu Jaafar bin Al-Qaqa’a: Every matter is settled with the kasra of the qaf and the ra’. He made it an adjective for a matter, and on this basis it is permissible for it to be raised by the subject and the predicate is omitted, as if he said: Every matter established in the Mother of the Book will come to pass. It is permissible for it to be raised by being connected to the Hour. Meaning: The Hour has drawn near and every matter is settled, meaning that matters are settling near on the Day of Resurrection. And whoever raises it makes it report for everything.
54:4: His Almighty saying, And there has certainly come to them from the report meaning some of the report, so the Almighty mentioned from that what He knew they needed and that there was healing for them in it, and there were matters more than that, but He only related to us what He knew we needed and was silent about what was beyond that, and that is His Almighty saying, And there has certainly come to them from the report meaning these unbelievers have come from the report of the past nations that in which is a deterrent meaning that which would deter them from unbelief if they had accepted it. Its original form is muztajar, but the ta' was changed to a dal because the ta' is a voiceless letter and the zay is a voiced letter, so the ta' was replaced with a dal, agreeing with them in the place of articulation and agreeing with the zay in the voiced pronunciation. Muztajar is from zajr, which means to stop. It is said zajarhu wa izdajarhu fanazjara wa izdajar, and zajartu ana fanazjara, meaning I restrained him, so he restrained, as He said: So what the prostitute asks for is a refusal to accept his desires. It was read as muzjar by replacing the ta’ of the word ifti’al with a zay and assimilating the zay into it, as narrated by Al-Zamakhshari.
54:5: Profound wisdom means the Qur'an and it is a substitute for what from His saying what is not a deterrent and it is possible that it is the predicate of a deleted subject, meaning it is his ruling So what are the warnings of no avail if they lied and disobeyed as God Almighty said And what are the signs and warnings of a people who do not believe So what is a negation, meaning the warnings are of no avail to them. It is possible that it is an interrogative in the sense of rebuke, meaning what are the warnings of anything to them when they turn away from them? The warning may mean a warning, and it may be the plural of warner.
54:6: The Almighty’s saying, Then turn away from them, meaning, turn away from them. It was said that this was abrogated by the verse of the sword, and it was also said that it is the rest of the statement. Then He said, The Day the Caller calls, the agent in the Day they will emerge from the graves, or in humility, or an implied verb, meaning, Then turn away from them, for they will have a Day when the Caller will call. It was also said, Turn away from them, O Muhammad, for you have established the proof and will see them on the Day when the Caller will call. It was also said, meaning, turn away from them on the Day of Resurrection and do not ask about them and their conditions, for they will be called to something terrible, and a severe punishment will befall them. It is like saying, Do not ask about what happened to so-and-so if you inform him of a great matter. It was also said, That is, every matter will be settled on the Day when the Caller will call. Ibn Kathir read it with a sukoon on the kaf, while the others read it with a damma. They are two dialects like ‘asr and ‘asr, and shaghal and shaghal. Its meaning is the terrible and great matter, which is the Day of Resurrection, and the caller is Israfil, peace be upon him. It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid and Qatadah that they read it with a kasra on the kaf and a fatha on the ra’, indicating a passive verb.
54:7: With their eyes humbled Humility in the eyes means submission and humiliation. Humility was added to the eyes because the effect of glory and humiliation is clear in the person’s viewer. God the Most High said, Their eyes humbled and He the Most High said, Humbled from humiliation, looking from the corner of one’s eye. It is said that someone was humbled or submissive if he was humiliated. And he lowered his gaze, meaning he lowered it. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, and Abu Omar read it with an alif. It is permissible in active participles if they precede the plural, such as khashi’an absarhum, and feminine, such as khashi’an absarhum. It is permissible to pluralize, such as khashi’an absarhum. He said: And young men of good face from Iyad bin Nizar bin Ma'ad And humbly, the plural of khashi’, and the accusative in it is in the state of the ha’ and the mim in ‘anhum’, so it is ugly to stop on this estimation on ‘anhum’. And it is permissible for it to be in the state of the pronoun in ‘yakhrujun’, so it is stopped on ‘anhum’. And it was read khasha’ absarhum as the subject and the predicate, and the location of the sentence is the accusative in the state like his saying: I found him very generous and kind They will emerge from the graves meaning the tombs, the singular of which is jadth “as if they were locusts scattered, rushing to the caller.” And in another place he said: On the Day when people will be like scattered moths. So these are two descriptions at two different times. One of them is when they emerge from the graves, they will emerge terrified, not knowing where to go, so some of them will enter into others. Then they will be like scattered moths, one into the other, with no direction for the other to head towards. Then when they hear the caller, they will head towards him, and they will become like scattered locusts, because locusts have a direction to head towards. And rushing means hurrying, as Abu Ubaidah said. And from this is the saying of the poet: Their home is in the Tigris. I saw them rushing to listen to the Tigris. Ad-Dahhak: Approaching deliberately. Ibn Abbas: Looking. Ikrimah: Opening their ears to the sound. The meaning is close. It is said that a man hataa directly looks at something and does not stop looking at it. And ahta’a directly means stretching his neck and raising his head. The poet said: Nimr ibn Saad worships me, and I see Nimr ibn Saad obedient and devoted to me. A camel with a straight neck, meaning it is fast in its running. The disbelievers will say, ‘This is a difficult day,’ meaning the Day of Resurrection, because of the hardship that will befall them on it.
54:8: God Almighty says: Rushing toward the caller, the disbelievers say, ‘This is a difficult day.’
54:9: The Almighty says, The people of Noah denied before them, He mentioned a number of incidents from past nations to comfort and console the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Before them, meaning before your people. So they denied Our servant, meaning Noah. Az-Zamakhshari: If you ask, what is the meaning of his statement, So they denied after his statement, You have denied, I say that it means they lied, so they denied Our servant, meaning they lied to him, one lie after another, every time a generation of deniers passed among them, another generation of deniers followed, or the people of Noah denied the messengers, so they denied Our servant, meaning when they were denying the messengers and rejecting prophethood completely, they denied Noah because he was one of the messengers. And they said, 'He is mad,' meaning he is mad. And he was deterred, meaning he was deterred from denying prophethood by cursing and threatening to kill him. It was said that He said, And he was deterred in the form of an unspecified agent because it is the beginning of a verse.
54:10: So he called upon his Lord, meaning Noah called upon them at that time and said: My Lord, I am overcome, meaning they overcame me with their rebellion. So grant me victory, meaning grant me victory. It was said that the prophets would not call upon their people to perish except with God Almighty's permission for them to do so.
54:11: So We opened the gates of heaven meaning We answered his prayer and ordered him to build the ship and We opened the gates of heaven with pouring water meaning abundant. This was said by Al-Suddi. The poet said: My eyes are filled with tears of joy for the sake of the good of those who came before and after them. It was said that it is the flowing position, and from it is the saying of Imru’ al-Qais describing a downpour: The morning passed by, then a torrential downpour of rain descended upon it. Al-Hamar is pouring. The water and tears pour down. He also pours out a lot of water and is quick. He pours water from his money to him, meaning he gave it to him. Ibn Abbas said: So We opened the sky with pouring water without clouds that did not stop for forty days. Ibn Amir and Jacob read: So We opened with a shaddah for emphasis. The rest read: So We opened with a light So We opened with a light So We opened with a shaddah for emphasis. Then it was said: It is the opening of its curtains and the breadth of its paths. It was also said that it is the galaxy, which is the extension of the sky, and from it it was opened with pouring water. Ali, may God be pleased with him, said this.
54:12: Then the water met meaning the water from the sky and the water from the earth according to a matter already decreed meaning according to an amount such that one did not exceed the other, as related by Ibn Qutaybah, meaning the water from the sky and the earth were equal. It was also said that measured means predestined for them. Qatadah said that it was decreed for them if they disbelieved that they would drown. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: Sustenance came before bodies and decree came before calamity. He recited this verse and said: The water met. The meeting only occurs between two or more because water can be plural or singular. It was also said that when they meet they become one water. Al-Jahdary recited The two waters met and Al-Hasan recited The two springs met. These are contrary to the decree. Al-Qushayri says in some copies of the Qur'an: The two springs met which is the language of Tayy. It was also said: The water from the sky was cold like snow and the water from the earth was hot like scalding water.
54:13: And We carried him on planks meaning on a ship with planks. And nails Qatada said that it means the nails with which the ship was nailed, i.e., made firm. Al-Qurazi, Ibn Zayd, and Ibn Jubayr said the same. Al-Walibi narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Al-Hasan, Shahr ibn Hawshab, and Ikrimah said that it is the prow of the ship that strikes the waves. It was called that because it pushes the water, i.e., it repels it. And nails mean pushing and shoving. Al-Awfi narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas. He said that nails mean the whole of the ship. Al-Layth said: Dasar is a thread made of palm fiber used to tie down the planks of a ship. In As-Sahah, Dasar is the singular of Dasr, which are threads used to tie down the planks of a ship. It is also said: They are nails. God Almighty said: On planks and nails. Dasar is also like Usar and Usar, and Dasr means pushing. Ibn Abbas said about ambergris: It is something that he pushes into the sea, Dasran, meaning he pushes it. He pushed it with a spear. A man is Mudasser.
54:14: It runs under Our eyes meaning under Our sight. It was also said that it was by Our command, or it was said that it was by Our protection and guardianship, as was mentioned in Hud. And from this is the saying of people to someone who is entrusted with a deposit, The eye of God is upon you, meaning that He protected and protected it. And it was also said that it was by Our revelation, or it was said that it means by the eyes springing from the earth. And it was also said that it was by the eyes of Our guardians from the angels who are entrusted with guarding it, and everything that God created can be attributed to it. And it was also said that it means it runs under Our guardians, as in the report, A disease of one of Our eyes did not occur to him. "A recompense for him who disbelieved" meaning that We made that a reward and recompense for Noah for his patience in the face of the harm of his people, and he was the one who was disbelieved in. So the lam in "for him" is the lam of the object. And it was said that "disbelieved means denied. So from" is a metaphor for Noah, and it was also said that it is a metaphor for God, and the recompense means punishment, meaning a punishment for their disbelief in God Almighty. Yazid bin Ruman, Qatada, Mujahid and Hamid read reward for he who disbelieved with the opening of the kaf and the fa, meaning: the drowning was a reward and punishment for he who disbelieved in God. No one was saved from drowning except Awj bin Anq, as the water reached his throat. The reason for his salvation was that Noah needed teak wood to build the ship, but he could not carry it, so Awj carried that wood to him from Syria, and God thanked him for that and saved him from drowning.
54:15: And We have certainly left it as a sign meaning this action is a lesson. It was also said that he meant that the ship was left as a sign for those after the people of Noah to take heed from it and not deny the messengers. Qatada said that God left it in Baqardi on the land of the peninsula as a lesson and a sign until the first of this nation looked at it. How many ships came after it that turned to ashes. Is there anyone who will remember? One who will be admonished and fearful. Its root is muzdakkar derived from dhikr remembrance, but it became difficult for the tongues, so the ta was changed to a dal to agree with the dhal in sound, and the dhal was assimilated into it.
54:16: How was My punishment and My warning? That is, My warning. Al-Farra' said that warning and warning are two sources. It was said that warning is the plural of warner and warner means warning, while nakir means denial.
54:17: And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy to remember meaning, We have made it easy to memorize and have helped whoever wants to memorize it. Is there anyone who seeks to memorize it who can be helped to do so? It is possible that the meaning is, And We have certainly prepared it for remembrance, taken from the verb yasar to saddle his camel for travel, if he saddled it, and yasar to saddle his horse for war, if he saddled and bridled it. He said: And I went to him with the bridle, and he said to me, There I will be rewarded for what I did. Saeed bin Jubair said: There is no book from God’s books that is read in its entirety outwardly except the Qur’an. Someone else said: This was not for the Children of Israel, and they did not read the Torah except by looking at it, except for Moses, Aaron, Joshua bin Nun, and Ezra, peace be upon them. Because of that, they were tempted by Ezra when he wrote the Torah for them from memory when it was burned, as was explained earlier in Surat Bara’ah. So God, the Most High, made it easy for this nation to memorize His book so that they would remember what is in it, i.e., they would make up the remembrance. Making up means that it would be effective in them until it becomes like a self or a composition for them. Is there anyone who will remember? A reader who will read it. Abu Bakr Al-Warraq and Ibn Shawdhab said: Is there anyone who seeks good and knowledge who will be helped in it? It was repeated in this Surah for the purpose of alerting and understanding. It was said that God, the Most High, related to this nation in this Surah the report of the nations and the stories of the messengers, and how the nations dealt with them, and what was the outcome of their affairs and the affairs of the messengers. So in every story and report, there is a reminder for the listener that if he remembered. This verse was repeated when mentioning each story by saying, Is there anyone who will remember? because hal is an interrogative word that requires them to understand what is in their hearts and to make it an argument against them. The lam in hal is for display and the ha is for extraction.
