54:18: The Almighty said, `Aad denied they are the people of Hud so how was My punishment and My warnings "Nadhr occurred in this surah in six places with the ya' omitted in all copies of the Qur'an. Ya`qub read it as confirmed in both instances and Warsh in the connected version only and the rest omitted it and there is no disagreement about the omission of the ya' from his saying: Then the warnings do not avail and the waw from his saying yadhu as for the ya' of the first da'i, Ibn Muhays, Ya`qub, and Hamid Fatabzi confirmed it in both instances and Warsh and Abu `Amr confirmed it in the connected version and the rest omitted it. As for the second da'i, Ya`qub, Ibn Muhays, and Ibn Kathir confirmed it in both instances and Abu `Amr and Nafi` confirmed it in the connected version and the rest omitted it.
54:19: The Almighty said, Indeed, We sent upon them a furious wind meaning very cold. This was said by Qatada and Ad-Dahhak. It was also said that it was very loud. It has already been mentioned in Ha Mim As-Sajdah. On a continuous ill-omened day meaning on a day that was unlucky for them. Ibn Abbas said: It was a day that they considered unlucky. Az-Zajjaj said: It was on a Wednesday. Ibn Abbas said: It was the last Wednesday of the month. It destroyed their young and old. Harun Al-A'war read it as Nahas with a kasra on the ha. It has already been mentioned in Ha Mim As-Sajdah. On days of ill-omened days meaning that it was always unlucky. It continued with its bad luck upon them and the torment continued with them until they perished. It was also said that it continued with them to the fire of Hell. Ad-Dahhak said: It was bitter to them. Al-Kisa’i also narrated that some people said that it is from bitterness. It is said that something is bitter and a matter, meaning it is like a bitter thing that people hate. He also said: So taste it. What is tasted may be bitter. It has also been said that it is from mara meaning strength, meaning on a day of continuous bad luck, with a strong omen like something tightly twisted that cannot be undone. If it is said: If Wednesday is a day of continuous bad luck, how will supplications be answered on it? It has been reported that the supplication of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was answered between noon and afternoon. The hadith of Jabir regarding that has been mentioned in Al-Baqarah, then the answer, and God knows best, is what is reported in a report narrated by Masruq: “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Gabriel came to me and said: God commands you to judge by oath with a witness. He said: Wednesday is a day of continuous bad luck.” It is known that he did not mean by that that it is bad luck for the righteous, but rather he meant that it is bad luck for the wicked and corrupt, just as the bad luck days mentioned in the Qur’an were bad luck for the disbelievers of the people of ‘Ad, not for their Prophet and the believers in him among them. If that is the case, it is not far-fetched that the oppressor would be given respite from the first of Wednesday until…” That the sun sets, and when the day has passed and there is no return, the supplication of the oppressed person against him is answered, so the day is unlucky for the oppressor. The supplication of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was only against the infidels. Jabir’s statement in his hadith, No serious matter has befallen me, is an indication of this, and God knows best.
54:20: The Almighty's saying It uproots people is in the position of an attribute of the wind, meaning it uproots them from their places. It was said that it uprooted them from under their feet as a palm tree is uprooted from its roots. Mujahid said that it would uproot them from the ground and throw them on their heads, breaking their necks and separating their heads from their bodies. It was also said that it uprooted people from their homes. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said on the authority of his father that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The wind uprooted people from their graves. It was also said that they dug holes and entered them, and the wind would uproot them from them and break them, and those holes would remain as if they were the roots of palm trees whose contents had perished, so their places would remain hollowed out. It is narrated that seven of them dug holes and stood in them to repel the wind. Ibn Ishaq said: When the wind blew, seven men from Aad stood up. He named six of them for us, the strongest and most powerful of Aad, including Amr ibn al-Hilli, al-Harith ibn Shaddad, al-Hilqam, the two sons of Taqan, and Khaljan ibn Saad. They forced their families into a gorge between two mountains, then they lined up at the entrance of the gorge to repel the wind from the families in the gorge. The wind started to blow them away, man by man. Then a woman from Aad said: Time has taken Amr ibn Hali and the congratulations Then, with plowing and tillage, the tops of the hills rise. And he who blocked the wind during the days of calamities Al-Tabari has deleted the word in Al-Kalam, and the meaning is: You will pull people out and leave them as if they were hollowed-out palm trunks. So the Kaf is in the accusative case because of the deleted word. Al-Zajjaj: The Kaf is in the accusative case as a state, and the meaning is: You will pull people out, likened to the trunks of palm trees. The simile is said to be for the holes they were in, and the Aajaz is the plural of Aajz, which is the back of something. The Aad people were described as being tall, so they were likened to palm trees that have fallen on their faces. He said: The trunks of hollowed-out palm trees because of the word palm tree, which is a plural that can be masculine or feminine. The hollowed-out is the one that has been uprooted from its root. You hollowed out the tree, you pulled it out from its root, so it became hollow. Al-Kisa’i: You hollowed out the well, meaning you descended until you reached its bottom. Similarly, the vessel, if you drink what is in it until you reach its bottom, and you hollowed out the well, you make it have a bottom. Abu Bakr bin Al-Anbari said: Al-Mubarrad was asked in the presence of Ismail Al-Qadi about a thousand issues, this being one of them. He was asked: What is the difference between the words of God Almighty: And to Solomon We subjected a violent wind and A violent wind came upon it and His words: As if they were hollow trunks of palm trees and Trunks of palm trees hollowed out? He said: Whenever you are presented with something from this chapter, if you wish, you can return it to the wording as masculine or to the meaning as feminine. It was said that palm trees and date palms have the meaning of masculine and feminine, as we mentioned.
54:21: God Almighty said: How then was My punishment and My warnings?
54:22: God Almighty said: And We have certainly made the Qur’an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?
54:23: God Almighty says, Thamud denied the warnings. They are the people of Salih who denied the messengers and their prophet, or they denied the signs that were warnings.
54:24: The Almighty said, And they said, 'Shall we follow a single human being from among us?' And we leave a group? Abu al-Ashab, Ibn al-Sameeq, and Abu al-Samal al-Adawi read Absher in the nominative case, one." Likewise, it is nominative as the subject and predicate. We follow him. The rest read it in the accusative case, meaning, shall we follow a single human being from among us? We follow him. Abu al-Samal read "Absher in the nominative case, one from among us, in the accusative case, raising Absher" with an implied verb indicating it. "Shall I cast as if he said, Shall we inform a human being from among us? His saying one may be a state of the implied in from among us and the circumstance that raises it, and the interpretation is Shall we inform a human being from among us, alone? It may be a state of the pronoun in We follow him" alone, with no supporter for him. "Indeed, then we are in error" meaning, going astray from the right path. "And madness" meaning, madness, from their saying, a rabid she-camel, meaning, as if she is mad from the intensity of her activity. Ibn Abbas mentioned it. The poet said, describing his she-camel: You think it is a price if the journey shakes it and the rhythm of walking is tiring Al-Dhamil is a type of camel’s gait. Abu Ubaid said: If the gait rises a little above the neck, then it is the tazdid. If it rises above that, then it is the dhamil. Then it is said dhamal yadhamlu and dhamil dhameel. Al-Asma’i said: A camel does not gait for a day and a night except that it is my dowry. J said: Ibn Abbas also said: Al-Sa’r is the torment. Al-Farra’ Mujahid said: After the truth, Al-Suddi said in Ithiraq, he said: Did you wake up today or did a cat miss you and you are madly in love? Any burning and blazing. Abu Ubaidah is the plural of Sa’ir, which is the flame of fire. The mad camel goes so-and-so because of the intensity with which it is blazing. The meaning of the verse is that we are then in misery and hardship because of what is required of us.
54:25: The Almighty says, Was the message cast down upon him from among us? That is, he was singled out for the message from among the people of Thamud, among whom were those who were richer and better off. It is a question that means denial. Rather, he is a wicked liar. That is, he is not as he claims, but rather wants to appear arrogant and seek to be haughty towards us without any justification. Ashr means playful, haughty, and active. It is said: A horse is ashr if it is playful and active. Imru' al-Qais said, describing a dog: And He overtakes us, for He is the tame, all-hearing, all-see...knowing. Stick the molars, bend the ribs, follow the wise, active, pointy It was said that Ashr is arrogant and Ashr is arrogant. The poet said: And I left and howled, pointing at it, and the stabbing has killed its heroes It was said: It is the one who transgresses to a position he does not deserve, and the meaning is the same. Ibn Zayd and Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad said: The evil one who does not care what he says. Abu Ja`far and Abu Qilabah read ashr with a fatha on the shin and a shaddah on the ra’, meaning by it we are the most evil and the most wicked.
54:26: The Almighty's saying They will know tomorrow meaning they will see the punishment on the Day of Resurrection or when the punishment descends upon them in this world. Ibn Amir and Hamzah read it with a ta' as if it were from Salih's statement to them, addressing them. The rest read it with a ya' as God's informing Salih about them. His saying tomorrow is for approximation, as people usually say about consequences that tomorrow is with today. He said: Death has arrows that never miss. He who is not dead today will die tomorrow. Al-Tarmah said: O heal me before the wailing of the mourners and before the soul’s turmoil within its sides And the day before tomorrow, how I long for a tomorrow when my friends leave and I am not. Rather, he meant the time of death, not the specific tomorrow. From the most evil liar. Abu Qilabah read the most evil with a fatha on the shin and a shaddah on the ra’, in keeping with the original principle. Abu Hatim said, The Arabs hardly ever speak with “the most evil and the last except in the form of poetry, like the saying of Ru’bah: Bilal is the best of people and the son of the last Rather, they say that he is the best of his people, but he is the worst of people. God Almighty said, You are the best nation produced for mankind, and He said, And they will know who is in worst position. And it was narrated on the authority of Abu Haywah with the opening of the sheen and the softening of the ra’, and on the authority of Mujahid and Sa’id ibn Jubayr with the damma of the sheen and the ra’ and the softening. An-Nahhas said: It is the meaning of the worst, and similar to it is a cautious and wary man.
54:27: The Almighty said, Indeed, We will send the she-camel out meaning We will take her out from the plateau they asked about. It was narrated that Salah prayed two rak'ahs and supplicated, and the rock they had appointed split open, revealing her hump, and a she-camel emerged. A trial for them meaning a test, and it is the object of the verb. So watch for them meaning wait for what they will do. And be patient meaning be patient with their harm. The root of the letter ta in istabbar is a ta, but the letter ta was changed to agree with the letter sad in emphasis.
54:28: The Almighty said, And inform them meaning, inform them that the water is to be divided between them meaning, between the people of Thamud and the she-camel. She has a day and they have a day, as the Almighty said, She has a drink and you have a drink - a known day. Ibn Abbas said: On the day of their drinking, the she-camel would not drink any of the water and would give them milk to drink, and they would be in comfort. But when it was the she-camel’s day, she would drink all of the water and leave nothing for them. He only said, between them because when the Arabs spoke about the children of Adam with the animals, they would defeat the children of Adam. Abu Al-Zubayr narrated on the authority of Jabir who said: When we came to Al-Hijr during the expedition of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to Tabuk, he said: O people, do not ask about these verses. These are the people of Salih who asked their prophet to send them a she-camel. So God, the Almighty, sent them the she-camel. She used to come back from that pass and drink their water on the day she came, and they would milk from it the same as they used to drink on the day after. This is the meaning of the Almighty’s saying: And inform them that the water is to be divided between them. Every drink is to be divided. Drinking in the broken form is a portion of water, and in the proverb the last of it is the one that is drunk the least. Its origin is in watering camels because the last of them comes and the trough has run dry. The meaning of drinking is that it is brought by the one who owns it. So the she-camel would bring water on the day she came back and would disappear from them on the day they came back. This was said by Muqatil. Mujahid said that the Thamud would bring water on the day after she came back and drink, and they would bring milk on the day she came back and milk it.
54:29: The Almighty’s saying, So they called upon their companion, meaning to urge them to hamstring her. So he took it upon himself to hamstring her, “so he hamstrung” her. The meaning of to take is to take the action, from their saying atawwat, meaning I took it. And from this is the saying of Hassan: They both milked the juice, so he gave me a bottle and loosened it for the joint. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: He ambushed her at the base of a tree on her way, shot her with an arrow that pierced her leg muscle, then attacked her with the sword and exposed her Achilles tendon. She fell down and let out a single roar, her udder flowing from her belly. Then he slaughtered her, and her udder flowed until it reached a rock at the top of a mountain. Then he took refuge with her. Salih, peace be upon him, came to them, and when he saw that the she-camel had been hamstrung, he cried and said: You have violated the sanctity of God, so be glad of the punishment of God. This meaning has been explained in Al-A’raf. Ibn Abbas said: The one who hamstrung her was red, blue, blond, and had a bare back. It is said that his name was Qidar ibn Salaf, and Al-Afwah Al-Awdi said: Or before him, like Qaddar, when people followed him in his misguidance, they perished. The Arabs call the butcher Qadar, in imitation of Qadar, a former ill-fated man from the Thamud tribe. Muhalhil said: We strike their heads with swords, the strike of fate is the strike of the ancients. Zuhair mentioned it and said: Then she will produce for you boys of the most unfortunate nature, all of them like the red ones of Ad. Then she will suckle and be weaned. He wanted war, so he referred to Thamud as Aad.
54:30: God Almighty said: How then was My punishment and My warnings?
54:31: The Almighty said, Indeed, We sent upon them a single blast meaning the blast of Gabriel, peace be upon him, and this has already been mentioned in Hud. And they were like chaff in a pen Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Abu Al-Aaliyah read it with a fatha on the dhal, meaning the enclosure. It was also read as kahashima al-muhtadhir. Whoever reads it with a kasra makes it the subject, and whoever reads it with a fatha makes it the object. It is said of a man of little good: He is a poor enclosure. Abu Ubaid said, I think he called his wealth a pen because he kept it with him and prevented it. It is a verbal noun with the meaning of a passive participle. Al-Mahdawi, with a fatha on the dhal from al-muhtadhir, is a verbal noun, and the meaning is like the chaff of enclosure. It is possible that al-muhtadhir is the tree from which the enclosure is made. Ibn Abbas said: Al-Muhtadhir is the man who makes a pen for his sheep with trees and thorns, and whatever falls from that and is trampled by the sheep is the chaff. He said: They stirred up a fuss like the smoke of a fire that ignites a scorched dry stubble. And on his authority: Like grass that sheep eat. And on his authority also: Like rotten, burnt bones. This is the saying of Qatada. Saeed bin Jubair said: It is the dust scattered from the walls on a windy day. Sufyan al-Thawri said: It is what is scattered from the enclosure if you hit it with a stick. It is fa’il with the meaning of maf’ul. Ibn Zayd said: The Arabs call everything that was wet and then dried up hashīm. And the prohibition is prevention. And the muhtazir is the active participle. It is said from it: he prohibited himself from his camels. And ḥaḍar means he gathered the trees and placed some of them on top of each other to prevent the cold wind and wild beasts from his camels. The poet said: He saw the carcasses of the camels lying beside him, as if their bones were dry wood. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, they were like wheat that was trampled and crushed. The crushed wheat is the one who takes a pen for his crops, and the crushed wheat is the crumbs of the ear of corn and the straw.
54:32: God Almighty says: And We have certainly made the Qur’an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?
54:33: The Almighty said, The people of Lot denied the warning. He also informed about the people of Lot when they denied Lot.
54:34: The Almighty said, Indeed, We sent upon them a hailstorm, meaning a wind that pelted them with pebbles, which are gravel. Al-Nadr said: Hasib is the pebbles in the wind. Abu Ubaidah said: Hasib is stones. In the Sahih, Hasib is a strong wind that stirs up pebbles, and so is Hasaba. Labid said: It happened to her that her people lost their tails, and every straw was a pebble. The wind blew, meaning it became very strong, so it is a very strong and violent wind. Al-Farazdaq said: We are receiving the northern Levant, which is striking us with hailstones like scattered cotton. Except the family of Lot meaning those who followed him in his religion and none but his two daughters. We saved them by magic. Al-Akhfash said: He made it in the accusative case because it is an indefinite noun. If he had intended the magic of a specific day, he would not have made it in the accusative case. Its counterpart is Go down to Egypt because it is indefinite. So when he made it definite in his statement, Enter Egypt, if God wills, he did not make it in the accusative case. Al-Zajjaj said the same about magic: if it is an indefinite noun intended to mean magic from the magic spells, it is declined. You say, I came to him at magic, oh this one. But if you mean the magic of your day, you do not decline it. You say, I came to him at magic, oh this one, and I came to him by magic. Magic is what is between the end of the night and the break of dawn, and in Arabic it is the mixing of the blackness of the night with the whiteness of the beginning of the day because at this time are the signs of night and the signs of day.
54:35: A favor from Us a favor from Us upon Lot and his two daughters, so it is in the accusative case because it is the object. Thus do We reward the grateful meaning the one who believed in God and obeyed Him. And he had warned them meaning Lot, frightening them of Our punishment our punishment and our seizing them with torment. Then they disputed about the warning meaning they doubted what the Messenger had warned them about and did not believe him. It is a verbal noun from mariyah.
54:36: The Almighty said, And they certainly sought to seduce him from his guest. That is, they wanted him to enable them to have access to those angels who had come to him in the guise of guests, seeking to commit an immoral act, as mentioned above. It is said, I seduce him to such-and-such, meaning I sought him out. He sought the pasture, meaning he sought it out. In the hadith: If any one of you urinates, let him go back to urinate meaning, let him look for a soft or sloping place. So We blinded their eyes It is narrated that Gabriel, peace be upon him, struck them with his wing and they became blind. It is also said: Their eyes became like the rest of the face, so that no slit could be seen, just as the wind obliterates landmarks with the dust it blows over them. It is also said: Rather, God blinded them despite their healthy eyesight, so they did not see them. Ad-Dahhak said: God blinded their eyesight, so they did not see the messengers. They said: We saw them when they entered the House, so where did they go? So they returned and did not see them.
54:37: The Almighty said, So taste My punishment and My warning. That is, We said to them, Taste. What is meant by this command is the report, that is, I made them taste My punishment that Lot warned them of.
54:38: The Almighty says, And indeed, early in the morning, a lasting torment overtook them. That is, a permanent, general torment that will remain with them until it leads them to the torment of the Hereafter. And that torment will turn their city upside down upon them and make its highest part its lowest part. Early in here is an indefinite noun, and that is why it was declined.
54:39: The Almighty’s saying, So taste My punishment and warning. The punishment that befell them in the form of blinding their eyes is not the punishment by which they were destroyed, so the repetition is good.
54:40: The Almighty said, And We have certainly made the Qur’an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember? It was presented.
54:41: The Almighty says, And indeed, there came to the people of Pharaoh a vow. He means the Copts, and the vow was Moses and Aaron. The plural form may be used for both.
54:42: They denied Our signs Our miracles that prove Our Oneness and the prophecy of Our prophets, which are the staff, the hand, the years, the clouds, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and the blood. It was said that the warners are the messengers, for Joseph and his sons came to them until Moses came to them. It was also said that the warners are the warnings. So We seized them with the seizure of the Mighty meaning the Victorious in His vengeance, the Powerful meaning the One capable of doing whatever He willed.
54:43: The Almighty said, Your disbelievers are better than those. He addressed the Arabs, and it was said that he meant the disbelievers of the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was also said that it is a question. It is a question of denial and its meaning is negation, meaning that your disbelievers are not better than the disbelievers of the nations that came before them who were destroyed because of their disbelief. Or have you immunity in the scriptures? That is, in the books revealed to the prophets, stating safety from punishment. Ibn Abbas said, Or have you immunity from punishment in the Preserved Tablet?
54:44: God Almighty said, Or do they say, ‘We are all victorious?’ That is, a group that is unbearable due to their large numbers and strength. He did not say victorious in accordance with the beginnings of the verses. So God responded to them and said:
54:45: The assembly will be defeated meaning the assembly of the infidels of Mecca, and that happened on the day of Badr and others. The general reading is sehzemmu with a ya' for what does not have a named agent, the plural in the nominative case. Rawis read on the authority of Ya'qub sanzahem with a noon and a kasra on the zay, the plural in the accusative case. And they will turn their backs is the general reading with a ya' as a report on them. Isa, Ibn Ishaq and Rawis read on the authority of Ya'qub wa-tulawun with a ta' as a direct address. Al-daber is a generic noun like dirham and dinar, so it was singular and the intended meaning is plural because of the openings of the verses. And Muqatil said: Abu Jahl struck his horse on the day of Badr, then he advanced from the ranks and said: Today we will be victorious over Muhammad and his companions. Then God revealed: “We are all victorious. The host will be put to flight and they will turn their backs.” And Sa`id ibn Jubayr said: Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas said: When the verse The host will be put to flight and they will turn their backs was revealed, I did not know which host would be defeated. Then on the day of Badr, I saw the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) jumping up in his armor and saying: O God, the Quraysh have come to challenge you and challenge your Messenger with their pride and arrogance, so betray them this morning. Then he said: The host will be put to flight and they will turn their backs. So I understood its interpretation. This is one of the miracles of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), because he informed of the unseen and it happened as he informed. Time defeated him: that is, it came upon him and destroyed him. From this is the saying of Al-Nabigha: He who has wronged Labed has wronged him And I betrayed him: I corrupted. Ibn Abbas said: There were seven years between the revelation of this verse and Badr, so according to this the verse is Meccan. In Bukhari: “On the authority of Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, may God be pleased with her, she said: “The revelation was sent down to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Mecca while I was a girl playing: ‘Rather, the Hour is their appointed time, and the Hour is more grievous and more bitter.’” And on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said while he was in his tent on the day of Badr: I ask You by Your covenant and Your promise, O God, if You will, You will never be worshipped today. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, took his hand and said: It is enough, O Messenger of God, for you insisted on your Lord while He was in his armor. He went out saying: “The hosts will be routed and they will turn their backs. Rather, the Hour is their appointed time,” meaning the Resurrection.
54:46: The Almighty said, And the Hour is more grievous and bitter. That is, more grievous and bitter than what befell them on the Day of Badr. And more grievous is from the word dahyah, which means a great matter. It is said, such-and-such a matter befell him, meaning, a calamity befell him, and Ibn al-Sikkit said, A calamity befell him, a calamity, which is an emphasis on it.
54:47: The Almighty’s saying, Indeed, the criminals are in error and madness. There are four issues in this: First: The Almighty’s saying, Indeed, the criminals are in error and madness. That is, in deviation from the truth and madness, meaning burning. It has also been said that it is madness, as mentioned previously in this surah.
54:48: The Almighty said, The Day they are dragged into the Fire on their faces, 'Taste the touch of Hellfire.' In Sahih Muslim: On the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The polytheists of Quraysh came to argue with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) concerning predestination, so the verse was revealed, "The Day they are dragged into the Fire on their faces, 'Taste the touch of Hellfire. Indeed, We have created all things with predestination.'" At-Tirmidhi also included it, who said: A hasan sahih hadith. Muslim narrated on the authority of Tawus, who said: I met some of the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saying, Everything is by predestination. He said: I heard Abdullah ibn Umar say: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, Everything is by predestination, even incapacity and intelligence, or intelligence and incapacity. This refutes the doctrine of the Qadarites. Taste, meaning they will be told to taste, and its touch is the pain they will feel when they fall into it. Saqar is one of the names of Hellfire that is not declined, because it is a definite feminine noun, and so are Laza' and Jahannam. Ata' said: Saqar is the sixth layer of Hell. Qatrib said: Saqar is from the sun's saqaratuhu and its lahathu saqaratuhu. It is a very hot day.
54:49: The second: The Almighty’s saying, Indeed, We are everything. The general reading is every in the accusative case. Abu al-Samal read every in the nominative case as the subject. Whoever places the accusative case on the subject, then it is by implying a verb, which is the choice of the Kufians because if the verb is required, then it is more appropriate for it. The accusative case is more indicative of the generality of the creations of God Almighty, because if you delete the explanatory We created it and reveal the first, then it would become We created everything in measure. It is not correct for We created it to be an attribute of something, because the attribute does not work on what precedes the described, nor is it an explanation of what works on what precedes it. Third: The Sunnis believe that God Almighty has determined all things, i.e., He knew their quantities, conditions, and times before creating them. Then He created from them what He previously knew, that He would create it in the manner that He previously knew. So no event occurs in the upper or lower world except that it comes from His Almighty knowledge, power, and will, not from His creation. And that the creation has nothing in it except a type of acquisition, attempt, relation, and addition. And all of that only happened to them through the facilitation of God Almighty, His power, success, and inspiration. Glory be to Him, there is no god but Him, and no creator other than Him, as the Qur’an and Sunnah have stated, not as the Qadarites and others have said, that deeds are up to Us and the lives are in the hands of others. Abu Dharr may God be pleased with him said: A delegation from Najran came to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and they said: Deeds are up to Us and the lives are in the hands of others. So these verses were revealed up to His saying: Indeed, We created all things by measure. They said: O Muhammad, sin is written against us and we are punished. He said: You are the opponents of God on the Day of Resurrection. Fourth: Abu Al-Zubayr narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah may God be pleased with him who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: The Magians of this nation who deny the decree of God: if they fall ill, do not visit them; if they die, do not attend their funeral; and if you meet them, do not greet them. This was narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan. It was also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Jabir who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: There are two groups of my nation who have no share in Islam: the people of Irja’ and the people of Qadar. Al-Nahhas narrated on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Sharik Al-Kufi who said: Uqbah ibn Mukram Al-Dhabi narrated on the authority of Yunus ibn Bakir on the authority of Saeed ibn Maysarah who said: Anas said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: The Qadarites who say: Good and evil are in our hands have no share in my intercession, and I am not one of them, and they are not one of me. In Sahih Muslim it is narrated that Ibn Umar disavowed them, as he does not disavow anyone except a disbeliever. Then he confirmed this by saying: By Him by whom Abdullah ibn Umar swears, if one of them had gold the size of Mount Uhud and spent it, God would not accept it from him until he believed in Qadar. This is similar to what God Almighty said about al-Munafiqun 63:And nothing prevented their expenditures from being accepted from them except that they disbelieved in God and in His Messenger. This is clear. “Abu Hurairah said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Belief in predestination removes worry and sadness.”
54:50: The Almighty said, And Our command is but one, like the blink of an eye. That is, except once. Like the blink of an eye. That is, My judgment of creation is faster than the blink of an eye. A blink is a look with haste. It is said: He blinked the lightning with his sight. In As-Sahah, it is said that he glanced at it with a quick look. The noun is a glance, and the lightning and the star flashed, meaning they flashed.
54:51: God Almighty says: And We have certainly destroyed your followers meaning those similar to you in disbelief from among the past nations. It was also said that they were your followers and supporters. So is there any who will remember? meaning anyone who will remember.
54:52: The Almighty says, And everything they did is in the scriptures. That is, everything that the nations before them did, good or evil, was written down for them. This is an explanation of His statement, Indeed, We created all things with measure. “In the scriptures,” that is, in the Preserved Tablet. It was also said that it is in the books of the guardian angels, and it was also said that it is in the Mother of the Book.
54:53: And every small and great sin is recorded meaning every sin, big and small, is recorded for its doer before he commits it so that he will be punished for it, and it is recorded if he commits it, it is recorded, it is recorded, it is written, it is recorded, it is recorded like it.
54:54: The Almighty’s saying, Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and rivers. When He described the unbelievers, He also described the believers. River means rivers of water, wine, honey, and milk. Ibn Jurayj said this, and He used the singular because it is the beginning of the verse. Then the singular may refer to all of them. It was said: In a river in light and spaciousness, and from this comes the day because of its light, and from it the wound flowed. The poet said: I held it in my hand and its rupture was evident. What is behind it can be seen. Abu Majlaz, Abu Nahik, Al-Araj, Talha bin Masraf, Qatadah, and Nahr read it with two dammahs, as if it were the plural of day, not night, for them, like clouds and clouds. Al-Farra’ said: Some Arabs recited to me: If you are Layla, then I am a river. When I see the morning, I do not wait. The owner of the day. Another said: If it weren't for Tharidan, we would have perished from starvation. Tharid at night and Tharid by the river.
54:55: In a seat of truth meaning a seat of truth in which there is no idle talk or sin, and that is Paradise. With a Sovereign, All-Powerful meaning He has power over whatever He wills. With Him here is nearness, closeness, status, rank, dignity, and position. Al-Sadiq said: God praised the seat of truth, so none sit in it except the people of truth. Uthman al-Batti recited in the seats of truth in the plural. Seats are the places where people sit in the markets and elsewhere. Abdullah ibn Buraydah said: The people of Paradise enter every day upon the Compeller, Blessed and Exalted, and they recite the Qur'an to their Lord, Blessed and Exalted, and each person has sat in his seat, which is his seat, on pulpits of pearls, rubies, emeralds, gold, and silver, according to their deeds. Their eyes will never be satisfied with anything as they are satisfied with that, and they will never hear anything greater or more beautiful than it. Then they return to their homes, their eyes content, until the same thing the next day. Thawr ibn Yazid said on the authority of Khalid ibn Ma'dan: It has reached us that the angels will come to the believers on the Day of Resurrection and say: O friends of God, go. They will say: Where to? They will say: To Paradise. The believers will say: You are taking us to a place other than our desire. They will say: What is your desire? They will say: A seat of truth with an All-Powerful King. This hadith has been narrated specifically with this meaning. In the hadith, it says that a group of wise men will be escorted by the angels to Paradise. They will say: You are taking us to a place other than our desire. They will say: What is your desire? They will say: The seat of truth with the Beloved, as He has said: In a seat of truth with an All-Powerful King. And God knows best.
55:1: It is all Meccan according to Al-Hasan, Urwah ibn Al-Zubayr, Ikrimah, Ata’ and Jabir. Ibn Abbas said: Except for one verse, which is the saying of God Almighty: He is asked by whoever is in the heavens and the earth 76 verses. Ibn Mas’ud and Muqatil said: It is all Medinan. The first statement is more correct, because Urwah ibn Al-Zubayr narrated: The first to recite the Qur’an aloud in Mecca after the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was Ibn Mas’ud. This was because the Companions said: The Quraysh have never heard this Qur’an recited aloud, so who will make them hear it? Ibn Mas’ud said: I will. They said: We fear for you. We only want a man with a clan to protect him. But he refused, then he stood at the station and said: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The Most Gracious * has taught the Qur’an. Then he continued raising his voice while the Quraysh were in their gatherings. They pondered and said: What is Ibn Umm Abd saying? They said: He is saying what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, claims was revealed to him. Then they beat him until they left marks on his face. It is authentic that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up to pray. In the morning, he went to a palm tree and recited Surah Ar-Rahman. A group of jinn passed by and believed in him. In At-Tirmidhi, it is narrated on the authority of Jabir that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out to his companions and recited to them Surah Ar-Rahman from beginning to end, and they remained silent. He said: I recited it to the jinn on the night of the jinn, and they responded better than you. Whenever I came to the verse: Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny? they said: “No, our Lord, do we deny any of Your favors. To You is praise.” He said: A strange hadith. This is evidence that it was revealed in Mecca, and God knows best. It was narrated that Qays ibn Asim Al-Minqari said to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Recite to me some of what was revealed to you. So he recited Surah Ar-Rahman to him. He said: Repeat it. So he repeated it three times, and he said: “By God, it has a freshness and it has sweetness, its lower part is abundant and its upper part is fruitful. No human being can say this, and I bear witness that there is no god but God and that you are the Messenger of God.” It was narrated on the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Everything has a bride, and the bride of the Qur’an is Surah Ar-Rahman. The Almighty said: The Most Gracious * He taught the Qur’an. Saeed bin Jubair and Amer Al-Shaabi said: The Most Gracious is the opening of three surahs. If they are combined, they become one of the names of God Almighty: Alif, Lam, Meem (Nun). Thus, the sum of these is The Most Gracious.
55:2: The Almighty says, He taught the Qur’an meaning He taught it to His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) until he conveyed it to all of the people. It was revealed when they said, Who is the Most Gracious? It was also said that it was revealed in response to the people of Mecca when they said, It is only a human being who teaches it, and he is the Most Gracious of Yamamah, meaning Musaylimah the Liar. So God, the Almighty, revealed, The Most Gracious * He taught the Qur’an. Al-Zajjaj said that the meaning of He taught the Qur’an is that He made it easy to remember and recite, as He said, And We have certainly made the Qur’an easy for remembrance. It was also said that He made it a sign for the people to worship with.
55:3: He created man. Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and Al-Hasan said that it means Adam, peace be upon him.
55:4: He taught him eloquence the names of everything. It was also said that He taught him all languages. Ibn Abbas and Ibn Kaysan also said that man here refers to Muhammad, peace be upon him, and eloquence is the explanation of what is lawful and what is unlawful, and guidance from misguidance. It was also said that it refers to what was and what will be, because it explains the first and the last and the Day of Judgment. Ad-Dahhak said that eloquence is good and evil. Ar-Rabi' ibn Anas said that it is what benefits him and what harms him, and so did Qatada. It was said that man refers to all people, so it is a name for the species, and eloquence, according to this, is speech and understanding, and it is one of the things that man was given preference over all other animals. As-Suddi said that He taught every speech, their language that they speak, and Yaman said that writing and calligraphy are with the pen. Similar to it is He taught by the pen * He taught man that which he knew not.
55:5: The sun and the moon move according to precise calculations meaning they move according to a known calculation, so the predicate was omitted. Ibn Abbas, Qatadah, and Abu Malik said: It means they move according to calculations in stations that they do not exceed or deviate from. Ibn Zayd and Ibn Kaysan said: It means that times, terms, and ages are calculated by them. Were it not for the night and the day, and the sun and the moon, no one would know how to calculate anything if the entire universe were night or day. Al-Suddi said: By calculation is the estimation of their terms, meaning they move according to terms like the terms of people, so when their term comes, they perish. Similar to it is: Each moves according to a specified term. Ad-Dahhak said: By measure. Mujahid: By calculation is like the calculation of the millstone, meaning its pole rotates in something like a pole. And calculation can be a verbal noun of hasabatuhu, with the letter damma, hasab and hasaban, like al-ghufran, kufr, and al-rajhan. And hasaba also means I counted it. Al-Akhfash said: And the plural of hasab is like shihab and shahban. And also, with the dammah, is the torment and the arrows are limited. It was mentioned in Al-Kahf, the singular form is hisbanah, and the hasbanah is also the small pillow. You say from it, hasabatuhu, if you put him on a pillow. He said: Unaccounted for Not honored or shrouded.
55:6: And the star and the tree prostrate. Ibn Abbas and others said: The star is that which has no stem and the tree is that which has a stem. Ibn Abbas recited the words of Safwan ibn Asad al-Tamimi: The great bottom has become a star and its members have been destroyed, and Tamim and Wael have been brought alive. Zuhair bin Abi Salma said: Crowned with the roots of the star, woven by the south wind for the sake of the one who loves you The derivation of the star is from the star of something, meaning it appears and rises. Their prostration is with the prostration of their gods. Ad-Dahhak said that Al-Farraa said that their prostration is that they face the sun when it rises, then they incline with it until the shade is lost. Az-Zajjaj said that their prostration is the rotation of the shadow with them, as God the Almighty said, and seeks the shade of its shadows. Al-Hasan and Mujahid said that the star is the star of the sky, and its prostration, according to Mujahid, is the rotation of its shadow, and this is the choice of At-Tabari, narrated by Al-Mahdawi. It was said that the prostration of the star is its setting, and the prostration of the tree is the possibility of picking its fruit, narrated by Al-Mawardi. It was said that the combination of that is subject to God, so do not worship the star as a group of Sabians worshipped the stars, and many of the Persians worshipped the tree. Prostration is submission, and the meaning is the effects of occurrence, narrated by Al-Qushayri An-Nahhas. The origin of prostration in the language is submission and obedience to God the Almighty. It is from all dead things, their submission to the command of God the Almighty and their obedience to Him, and from animals likewise, and it is from the prostration in prayer. Muhammad bin Yazid recited about the star in the meaning of the stars, he said: So she became a star in a quick puzzle in the hands of those who eat her frozen
55:7: And the sky He raised. Abu Samal read and the sky in the nominative case as the subject, and he chose that because it was conjoined to the sentence And the star and the tree prostrate, so the conjoined word was made composed of a subject and a predicate like the word it is conjoined to. The rest read it in the accusative case because of an implied verb indicated by what follows. And He placed the balance means justice, according to Mujahid, Qatadah, and As-Suddi. That is, He placed justice on the earth which He commanded. It is said that God placed the law. And so-and-so placed such-and-such, meaning he cast it. And it was said that the Qur'an is based on this balance because it explains what is needed, and this is the saying of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Fadl. Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Ad-Dahhak also said that it is the balance with the tongue by which people are weighed so that they may be just with one another. It is a predicate meaning the command to be just, indicated by the statement of God the Almighty: And establish weight in justice. Justice is fairness. It was also said that it is judgment. And it was said that He meant placing the balance in the hereafter to weigh deeds. The root of the word balance is scales. This was discussed in Al-A'raf.
55:8: That you do not transgress in the balance The position of an may be accusative, assuming the preposition is omitted, as if he said: lest you transgress, like the saying of the Most High: God makes clear to you, lest you go astray. It is also possible that an has no position in the syntax, so it would mean that you transgress, according to this estimation, in the jussive mood, like the saying of the Most High: And the eminent among them set out, saying, Walk."" That is, walk. Transgression is exceeding the limit. So whoever says that the balance is justice, said that its transgression is tyranny. And whoever says that it is the balance by which weighing is done, said that its transgression is cheating. Ibn Abbas said: That is, do not betray the one for whom you weigh. And it was narrated that he said: O group of clients, let two matters be fulfilled by which people are destroyed: the measure and the balance. And whoever says that it is the judgment, said that its transgression is the distortion. And it was said that it contains an omission, that is, He set the balance and commanded you not to transgress therein.
55:9: And establish weight in justice meaning, do it uprightly and justly. Abu Darda' may God be pleased with him said: Establish the scale with justice and fairness. Ibn Uyaynah said: Establishing is with the hand and justice is with the heart. Mujahid said: Justice means equity in Roman. It was also said that it is like saying: He established the prayer, meaning he performed it on time. And the people established their markets, meaning they came to them on time. That is, do not abandon dealing in weight and justice. And do not make deficient the balance and do not reduce the balance and do not cheat in measure and weight. This is like His statement: And do not reduce the measure and weight. Qatadah said about this verse: Be just, O son of Adam, as you would like to be treated justly, and give in full as you would like or be given in full, for justice is the goodness of people. It was also said that the meaning is: Do not make deficient the scale of your good deeds on the Day of Resurrection, lest that be a regret for you. The word scale is repeated at the beginnings of verses. It is said that the repetition is for the command to give full weight and observe justice therein. The common reading is takhsaraw with a damma on the ta’ and a kasra on the seen. Bilal ibn Abi Burda and Aban ibn Uthman read it with a fatha on the ta’ and the seen, and they are two dialects. It is said akhsartu al-mizan and khasrattuhu like ajbartuhu and jabbartuhu. It is said that takhsaraw with a fatha on the ta’ and the seen is based on the estimation of the deletion of the preposition, and the meaning is do not lose on the scale.
55:10: And the earth He has placed for all creatures. All creatures are people, according to Ibn Abbas. Al-Hassan is the jinn and mankind. Al-Dahhak is everything that creeps on the face of the earth, and this is general. In it is fruit, meaning everything that people enjoy from the various types of fruits.
55:11: And the palm trees with sleeves Sleeves is the plural of kam in the broken form. Al-Jawhari said: Kammah in the broken form and kammah are the container of pollen and the covering of light, and the plural is kammam, akmah, and akmaam, and the akameem are also. And kam is the young camel if he feels pity for it and covers it until it grows strong. Al-Ajjaj said: But if you had witnessed people when they were in grief, would you not have relieved their grief? And they fainted and covered themselves. And the palm tree became covered and covered itself, meaning it took out its sleeves. And the sleeve with the kasra and the muzzle also is what the camel’s mouth is covered with so that it does not bite. You say from it a muzzled camel, meaning cupped. And kammat something means you covered it. And the sleeve is what conceals something and covers it. And from it comes the sleeve of the shirt with the damma and the plural is sleeves and kummah, like hab and habbah and the sleeve is the round cap because it covers the head. He said: I told them, A kilo is the same as some of your dirhams, and I eat the same. Al-Hasan said: The one with sleeves means the one with fibers, because the palm tree is covered with fibers, and its sleeve is the fibers in its necks. Ibn Zayd: The one with the date palm before it bursts open. Ikrimah said: The one with the loads.
55:12: And the grain with husks and basil Grain is wheat, barley and the like, and husk is straw, according to Al-Hasan and others. Mujahid is the leaves of trees and crops. Ibn Abbas: The straw and leaves of the crop that are blown away by the winds. Saeed bin Jubair: The first part of the crop to grow, meaning the first part to grow from it, Al-Farra' said it. The Arabs say: We went out to husk the crops, if they cut some of it before it ripens. And likewise in Al-Sahah: And I husk the crops, meaning I cut them before it ripens. And from Ibn Abbas also, husk is the green leaves of the crop, if its tops are cut off and its counterpart dries up. And He made them like eaten-up straws Al-Jawhari: And the crops were husk, meaning they had a lot of crops. Abu Qais bin Al-Aslat Al-Ansari said: If Jumada withholds its rain, my sides will be covered with a heavy rain. And the storm also means gain, and from it the rajaz poet said: Without any storm or disturbance Likewise, the leaves of the ears of corn are called ‘a’tisaf and ‘aseefa. Al-Harawi said: ‘A’saf and ‘aseefa are the leaves of the ears of corn.’ Al-Tha’labi narrated and Ibn Al-Sikkit said: The Arabs say for the leaves of the crop ‘a’saf and ‘aseefa and ‘jal’ with a kasra on the jim. Alqamah ibn ‘Abdah said: Watering the sins whose summer rain has bent down, whose slopes are covered with rain. In As-Sahah: “Al-Jal with a kasra is the reed of the crop when it was harvested. And basil is provision, from Ibn Abbas and Mujahid. Ad-Dahhak is the language of Himyar and from Ibn Abbas also and Ad-Dahhak and Qatadah that it is the basil that is smelled and Ibn Zaid said it and from Ibn Abbas also that it is the greenery of the crop and Saeed bin Jubair said it is what stands on a stalk. Al-Farra’ said the edible stalks of the crops and basil is what is not eaten. Al-Kalbi said that the stalks are the leaves that are not eaten and basil is the edible seed and it was said that basil is every herb with a pleasant smell and it was called basil because a person smells its pleasant smell. That is, he smells so it is a verb of Ruhan from the smell and the root of the ya in the word is waw changed to ya to differentiate it from the spiritual which is everything that has a soul. Ibn al-A'rabi said: It is said that something is spiritual and rayhani, meaning it has a spirit. It is also possible that it has the pattern fa'ilan, so its origin is rayuhan, then the waw was replaced with a ya', and the kahin was assimilated and softened, then the softening was required due to its length and the addition of the two extra letters alif and nun. The origin of what is composed of ra', waw and ha' is shaking and movement. In as-Sahah, rayhan is a well-known plant and rayhan is sustenance. You say: I went out seeking the basil of God. An-Nimr ibn Talib said: God's peace, basil, mercy, and a sky of pearls In the hadith: “The child is from the basil of God.” And their saying: Glory be to God and His basil, they put them in the accusative case as a verbal noun, meaning to glorify Him and to seek provision. As for His saying: And the grain with husks and basil, the husk is the stalk of the crop and the basil is its leaves, according to al-Farra’. The reading of the common people is: And the grain with husks and basil, with the nominative case in all of them in apposition to the fruit. Ibn ‘Amir, Abu Haywah, and al-Mughira put them in the accusative case in apposition to the earth. And it was said that a verb was implied, meaning, He created the grain with husks and basil. From this perspective, it is appropriate to stop at with sleeves. Hamzah and al-Kisa’i put basil in the genitive case in apposition to the husk, meaning, in it is the grain with husks and basil. This is not impossible according to the opinion of those who make basil provision, so it is as if he said: And the grain with provision. Provision, from where the husks are provision, is provision, because the husks are provision for animals and basil is provision for people. There is no doubt about that according to those who say it is the fragrant basil.
55:13: His statement, the Most High, Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny? is addressed to mankind and the jinn because mankind will be subject to them. This is the opinion of the majority, as indicated by the hadith of Jabir mentioned at the beginning of the surah, and it was narrated by al-Tirmidhi, in which it says, The jinn have a better response than you. It was said that when He said, He created man and He created the jinn, this indicates that what preceded and what followed were for them. Also, He said, We will attend to you, O two heavy burdens, which is addressed to mankind and jinn. He said in this surah, O company of jinn and mankind. Al-Jurjaan said: He addressed the jinn along with mankind, even though the jinn were not mentioned first, as in His statement, the Most High, until they are hidden behind the veil. The jinn were mentioned previously in what was previously revealed in the Qur’an, and the Qur’an is like a single surah. So, if it is proven that they are accountable like mankind, both genders are addressed in these verses. It was said that the address is to mankind, in accordance with the Arab custom of addressing one person in the dual form, as previously stated in throw them both into Hell. Likewise, His statement, Stop and let's cry My friend passed by me As for what comes after the creation of man and the creation of the jinn, it is addressed to mankind and the jinn, and the correct opinion is that of the majority, based on the Almighty’s saying, And the earth He laid out for all creatures. The blessings are the favors, and the opinion of all the commentators is that its singular is ila and ila like ma’i and ‘asa and ila and ali are four languages, as narrated by Al-Nahhas. He said, And in one, ‘ana’i al-layl there are three in which the open alif and the silent lam are dropped, and this has already been mentioned in Al-A’raf and An-Najm. Ibn Zayd said that it is the power and the estimation of speech, so which of the power of your Lord would you deny? Al-Kalbi said this, and Muhammad ibn Ali chose it at-Tirmidhi, who said: This surah is among the surahs of the knowledge of the Qur’an, and knowledge is the leader of the army, and the army follows it. It only became a science because it is a surah of the description of sovereignty and power, so He said: The Most Gracious * Taught the Qur’an. So He began the surah with the name of the Most Gracious from among the names so that the servants would know that everything He describes after this of His actions, His kingdom, and His power came out to them from the great mercy of His mercy, so He said: The Most Gracious * Taught the Qur’an. Then He mentioned man, so He said: He created man. Then He mentioned what He did with him and what He bestowed upon him. Then He mentioned the reckoning of the sun and the moon, and the prostration of things from what stars and trees do, and He mentioned the raising of the heaven and the setting of the balance, which is justice, and the setting of the earth for mankind. So He addressed these two heavy burdens, the jinn and mankind, when they saw what came out of the power and sovereignty with His mercy with which He had mercy on them, without any benefit or need for that, so they associated idols with Him and every worshipped thing they took besides Him, and they denied the mercy with which these things came out to them, so He said, asking them: Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny? That is, By what power do you deny your Lord? Their denial was only that they attributed to Him, in these things that came from His dominion and power, a partner who owns with Him and has power with Him. That is their denial. Then He mentioned the creation of man from clay, and the creation of the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire. Then He asked them, saying: Then which of the favors of your Lord will you deny? That is, by what power do you deny your Lord? For He has power after power in every creation. The repetition in these verses is for emphasis, exaggeration in the statement, and to take as an argument against them what He stopped them from creating a creation. Al-Qutbi said: God the Most High enumerated His blessings in this Surah and mentioned His creation with His favors. Then He followed each characteristic and described it and each blessing He placed with this one and made it a separator between every two blessings to alert them to the blessings and to make them acknowledge them, just as you say to someone whom you continue to bestow your goodness upon and he disbelieves and denies it: Weren’t you poor, so I enriched you; would you deny this? Weren’t you weak, so I honored you; would you deny this? Weren’t you a necessity, so I used you as an argument; would you deny this? Weren't you a man, so I carried you? Do you deny this? Repetition is good in such a case. He said: How many blessings you had, how many, how many He said Do not kill a Muslim if you are a Muslim woman. Beware of his blood. Beware. Another said: Do not cut off a friend while you blink an evil word at him. Do not tire of visiting him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him Al-Hussein bin Al-Fadl said: Repetition is to repel negligence and confirm the argument.
55:14: His Almighty saying He created man When He, glory be to Him, mentioned the creation of the greater world of the heavens and the earth and what they contain of evidence of His Oneness and Power, He mentioned the creation of the smaller world and said He created man - by agreement of the people of interpretation - meaning Adam from clay like pottery. Clay is the dry mud that makes a clinking sound. He likened it to pottery that has been baked. It was said that it is clay mixed with sand. It was also said that it is the putrid mud from the clinking of meat. The root is when it stinks. It has already been mentioned in Al-Hijr and He said here from clay like pottery and He said there: from clay from black mud that has been aged. He said: Indeed, We created them from sticky clay and He said: Like the example of Adam - He created him from dust. This is in agreement with the meaning, and that is that He took from the dust of the earth and kneaded it until it became clay, then it moved and became like black mud, then it moved and became clay like pottery.
55:15: And He created the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire. Al-Hasan said: The jinn is Iblis, who is the father of the jinn. It was also said that the jinn is one of the jinn, and the smoke is the flame, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God created the jinn from pure fire. It was also narrated from him that it is from its tongue which is at its end when it is ignited. Al-Layth said: The smoke is the bright flame with an intense flame. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas that it is the flame that rises above the fire, mixing some of it with others, red, yellow, green, and similarly on the authority of Mujahid, and all of them are close in meaning. It was said that the smoke is every matter that is sent forth and not forbidden. A similar saying of Al-Mubarrad is that Al-Mubarrad said: The smoke is the sent forth fire that is not forbidden. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Hasan said: The smoke is the mixing of fire, and its root is from the word marj which means to be disturbed and mixed. It is narrated that God the Most High created two fires, then He stirred one of them with the other, and one of them consumed the other, which is the fire of poison, so He created Iblis from it. Al-Qushayri said: Marj in the language means sent or mixed. It is an active participle with the meaning of passive, like his saying, flowing water and a pleasant life. The meaning is a meadow. Al-Jawhari said in Al-Sahah: Marj min Nar means a fire with no smoke from which the jinn were created.
55:16: God Almighty says: Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:17: The Almighty says, Lord of the two Easts and Lord of the two Wests, meaning He is the Lord of the two Easts. In Surah As-Saffat, it says, And Lord of the Easts, and we have already discussed this there.
55:18: God Almighty says: Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:19: The Almighty said, He has released the two seas meeting together. Marj means to leave, send away, and neglect. It is said that the sultan has let the people meet together if he has neglected them. Marj continues to mean neglect, as an animal meets together in the pasture. It is also said that Marj khlat mixed. Al-Akhfash said, and some people say that Marj al-Bahrain is like Marj fa’al meaning to mix and af’al have the same meaning. Bahrain Ibn Abbas said, it is the sea of the sky and the sea of the earth. Mujahid and Sa’id ibn Jubayr said this. They meet every year. It is also said that their two ends meet. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said, it is the sea of Persia and Rome. Ibn Jurayj said that it is the salty sea and freshwater rivers. It is also said that it is the sea of the east and the west that meet together. It is also said that it is the sea of pearls and coral.
55:20: The Almighty said, Between them is a barrier meaning a barrier. The first statement is what is between the heaven and the earth. This was said by Ad-Dahhak. According to the second statement, the earth between them is the space, as was said by Al-Hasan and Qatadah. According to other statements, it is the divine power, as mentioned in Al-Furqan. In the hadith, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: God Almighty spoke to the western side and said: "I am going to make within you servants of Mine who will glorify Me, magnify Me, declare My greatness and magnify Me. How will You deal with them?" It said: I will drown them, O Lord. He said: I will carry them in my hands and place Your might in your regions. Then He spoke to the eastern side and said: "I am going to make within you servants of Mine who will glorify Me, magnify Me, declare My greatness and magnify Me. How will You deal with them?" It said: "I will glorify You with them when they glorify You, and I will magnify You with them when they glorify You, and I will praise You with them when they glorify You, and I will glorify You with them when they glorify You." So God rewarded it by making a barrier between them. One of them turned into salty and bitter, while the other remained fresh. Furat: This hadith was mentioned by Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim Abu Abdullah, who said: Salih bin Muhammad told us, Al-Qasim Al-Amri told us, on the authority of Sahl, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah: They do not transgress. Qatadah said: They do not transgress against the people and drown them. He made a dry land between them and the people. And from him and Mujahid also: Neither of them transgresses against the other and overcomes him. Ibn Zayd: The meaning of they do not transgress is that they meet, and the meaning of the statement is the merging of the two seas that meet. If it were not for the isthmus between them, they would not transgress to meet. It was said: The isthmus is between this world and the hereafter, meaning there is a period of time between them that God has decreed, which is the period of this world, so they do not transgress. So when God permits the end of this world, the two seas become one thing, and it is like His statement: And when the seas overflow. Sahl bin Abdullah said: The two seas are the path of good and evil, and the isthmus between them is success and protection.
55:21: God Almighty says: Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:22: The Almighty says, From them come forth pearls and coral. That is, He brings forth for you from the water pearls and coral just as He brings forth grain, straw, and basil from the dust. Nafi' and Abu Amr read it with a damma on the ya' and a fatha on the ra', indicating a passive verb. The rest read it with a fatha on the ya' and a damma on the ra', indicating that the pearl is the subject. He said: From them, it only comes out of salt, not fresh water, because the Arabs put the two genders together and then describe one of them, like the saying of God Almighty: O company of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you? The messengers are from mankind, not the jinn, as Al-Kalbi and others said. Al-Zajjaj said: God mentioned them both, so if something comes out of one of them, then it has come out of them, and it is like the saying of God Almighty: Have you not seen how God created seven heavens in layers? And made the moon within them a light and made the sun a lamp? The moon is in the lowest heaven, but He made the mention of the seven more beautiful, so it is as if what is in one of them is in them. Abu Ali Al-Farsi said: This is from the category of deleting the complement, meaning from one of them, like his saying: Upon a great man from the two cities, meaning from one of the two cities. Al-Akhfash Saeed said: Some people claimed that pearls come out of fresh water, and it was said that they are two seas, from one of them comes pearls and from the other coral. Ibn Abbas said: They are the two seas, the sky and the earth. When the water of the sky falls into the shell of the sea, it forms pearls and emerges from them. At-Tabari said the same. Al-Tha’labi said: It was mentioned to me that a stone was in the interior of a shell, and a drop hit part of the stone and did not hit the rest, so where the drop of the stone hit was a pearl and the rest was a stone. It was said that freshwater and salty things may meet, so the freshwater is like pollen for the salty thing, so it was attributed to them just as a child is attributed to the male and female, even if the female gives birth to it. For this reason it was said that pearls do not come out except from a place where the freshwater and salty things meet. It was said: Coral is the large and large pearls. This was said by Ali and Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them. Pearls are its small ones. It was also narrated from them the opposite. Pearls are the large pearls and coral is its small ones. This was said by Ad-Dahhak and Qatadah. Ibn Mas’ud and Abu Malik said: Coral is the red beads.
55:23: God Almighty says: Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:24: His Almighty saying And to Him belong the ships meaning the ships The well-established The general reading is the well-established with a fatha on the sheen. Qatadah said that it means the creatures that run, taken from the verb to create. Mujahid said it is the ships whose sails have been lifted. He said: And if their sails have not been lifted then they are not well-established. Al-Akhfash said it is the ships that run. In the hadith: Ali, may God be pleased with him, saw ships that had been sailed and said: By the Lord of these well-established ships, they did not kill Uthman nor did they help in his killing. Hamza and Abu Bakr read it on the authority of Asim with a difference of opinion on his authority: the well-established with a kasra on the sheen meaning the well-established, the journey. The verb was added to it as a metaphor and expansion. It was said: the lifters are the law, meaning the uprooting. And whoever opens the sheen said the raised ones are the law like the flags meaning like the mountains. And the flag is the tall mountain. He said If they cut off knowledge, knowledge will appear Ships at sea are like mountains on land, and this was explained in Shura. Yaqub read al-Jawari with a ya’ when pausing, and the others omitted it.
55:25: God Almighty says: Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:26: The Almighty's saying, Everything on it will perish. The pronoun in on it refers to the earth, which was mentioned at the beginning of the surah in His saying, And the earth He spread out for all creatures. It could also be said that He is the most honorable of all that is on it, meaning the earth even if it is not mentioned. Ibn Abbas said that when this verse was revealed, the angels said, The people of the earth have perished. So the verse, Everything will perish except His Face, was revealed, and the angels were certain of perishing. Muqatil said this: The aspect of the blessing in the perishing of creation is equality between them in death, and with death feet become equal. It was said that the aspect of the blessing is that death is the reason for transfer to the abode of recompense and reward.
55:27: And the Face of your Lord will remain meaning God will remain. The Face is an expression of His existence and His essence, glory be to Him. The poet said: Fate has decreed that His creation be destroyed, so everything other than Him is perishable. This is what was accepted by our scholars, Ibn Fawrak, Abu Al-Ma'ali, and others. Ibn Abbas said: The face is an expression for it, as God said: And there will remain the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor. Abu Al-Ma'ali said: As for the face, what is meant by it according to most of our Imams is the existence of the Creator, the Most High, and this is what our Sheikh accepted. And the evidence for that is the saying of God the Most High: And the Face of your Lord will remain. And what is described as remaining when creation is exposed to annihilation is the existence of the Creator, the Most High. We have already discussed this in Surat Al-Baqarah, when God the Most High said: So wherever you turn, there is the Face of God. We have already mentioned it in full in Al-Kitab Al-Asna. Al-Qushayri said: Some people said: It is an attribute additional to the essence, not a description by which one turns to whomever God wishes to honor. What is correct to say: His face is His existence and His essence. It is said: This is the face of the command, the face of correctness, and the very essence of correctness. It has also been said: That is, what is apparent with its evidence remains, like the appearance of a person with his face. And it has been said: The direction by which one draws near to God remains. Dhul-Jalal Jalal is the greatness of God, His pride and His deservingness of praise. It is said: Jal ash-shay' is great and I made it great meaning I made it great. Jalal is a noun from jalla which means I honor. And ikram means He is worthy of being honored for what is not befitting of Him, such as associating partners with God with Him, as you say: I honor you for this. And from this is the honoring of the prophets and saints. We have already discussed these two names in terms of language and meaning in the Most Sublime Book. Anas narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Stick to me, O Dhul-Jalal and ikram. It was narrated that it was said by Ibn Mas'ud and its meaning is: stick to that in supplication. Abu Ubaid said: Ilzaath means sticking to something and persevering in it. It is also said: Ilzaath means insisting. Sa'id al-Maqburi reported that a man was insistent and kept saying: "O God, O Dhul-Jalal and ikram. O God, O Dhul-Jalal and ikram?" Then he was called: I have heard, so what is your need?
55:28: God Almighty says: Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:29: The Almighty says, Whoever is in the heavens and the earth asks Him. It was said that the meaning is that whoever is in the heavens asks Him for mercy and whoever is on the earth asks Him for provision. Ibn Abbas and Abu Salih said that the people of the heavens ask Him for forgiveness and they do not ask Him for provision, and the people of the earth ask for both of them. Ibn Jurayj said that the angels ask for provision for the people of the earth, so both requests are from the people of the heavens and the people of the earth for the people of the earth. In the hadith: Among the angels is an angel with four faces: one face like a human’s face and he asks God for provision for the children of Adam; one face like a lion’s face and he asks God for provision for the wild beasts; one face like a bull’s face and he asks God for provision for the cattle; and one face like an eagle’s face and he asks God for provision for the birds. Ibn Ata’ said: They asked him for the strength to worship Him. Every day He is concerned with a matter. This is a new statement, and every day is an adverbial phrase because of His saying in a matter or an adverbial phrase for asking. Then He begins, He is concerned with a matter. Abu al-Darda’ may God be pleased with him narrated that the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Every day He is in a matter. He said: It is His business to forgive a sin, relieve distress, raise up a people and lower others. And “On the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the statement of God Almighty: “Every day He is in a matter” He forgives a sin, removes distress, and answers the supplicant.” And it was said: It is His business to give life and cause death, to honor and humiliate, to provide for and withhold. And it was said: He meant His business in the two days of this world and the Hereafter. Ibn Bahr said: All of time is two days, one of them is the duration of the days of this world and the other is the Day of Resurrection. So His business, glory be to Him, in the days of this world is trial and testing by commanding and forbidding, giving life and causing death, giving and withholding. And His business on the Day of Resurrection is recompense and accounting, reward and punishment. And it was said that what is meant by that is telling about His business in every day of the days of this world, and this is the apparent meaning. In the language, business means a great matter, and the plural is businesses. What is meant by business here is the plural, like the statement of God Almighty: Then He brings you forth as a child. And Al-Kalbi said: It is His business to drive destinies to their appointed times. And Amr ibn Maymun said regarding the statement of God Almighty: Every day He is in a matter: “It is His business to He causes the living to die, and settles in the wombs whom He wills, and He honors the lowly and humiliates the honorable. One of the princes asked his minister about the verse: Every day He is concerned with a matter, but he did not understand its meaning, so he asked him to wait until the next day. He went home sadly, and a black slave of his said to him: What is the matter with you? So he told him. The minister said to him: Go back to the prince, and I will interpret it for him. So he called him and said: "O prince, His affair is that He merges night into day and merges day into night. He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living. He heals the sick and makes the healthy sick. He tests the healthy and heals the afflicted. He honors the lowly and humiliates the honorable. He impoverishes the rich and enriches the poor." The minister said to him: You have relieved me, so may God relieve you. Then he ordered the minister's clothes to be taken off and the slave dressed in them. The youth said: O my master, this is from the affair of God Almighty. On the authority of Abdullah bin Tahir: that he called Al-Hussein bin Al-Fadl and said to him: Three verses are unclear to me, so I have asked you to explain them to me: The Almighty’s saying, “So he became among the regretful,” and it is authentically stated that regret is repentance. His saying, Every day he is concerned with a matter, and it is authentically stated that the pen has dried up regarding what will happen until the Day of Resurrection. His saying, And that man can have nothing but what he strives for, so what about the multiples? He said: Al-Hussein said: It is possible that regret does not constitute repentance in that nation and that it constitutes repentance in this nation because God, the Almighty, has given this nation special characteristics that no other nation shares with them. It was said that Cain’s regret was not for killing Abel, but for carrying his child.
