Then he recited the words of God the Most High: A group of the first and a group of the latter. Mujahid said: All of them are from this nation. Sufyan narrated from Abaan from Sa`id ibn Jubayr from Ibn `Abbas, “From the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): ‘Two-thirds together from my nation,’ meaning, ‘A group of the first and a group of the latter.’” This statement was narrated from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq may God be pleased with him. Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him said: Both thirds are from the nation of Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him). Some of them are at the beginning of his nation, and some of them are at the end. It is like the saying of God the Almighty: And among them are he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds by God’s permission. It was also said: A group from the first meaning from the beginning of this nation. And a few from the last who hasten to do acts of obedience until they reach the level of the first. For this reason, the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: The best of you are my generation. Then he is placed among the companions of the right hand between the first and the last. The word thalth comes from the word thallat which means to divide something, so the meaning of thalth is the same as the meaning of sect, as Al-Zajjaj said.
56:15: The Almighty said: On lined couches meaning the foremost in Paradise. (On couches) meaning their seats are on couches, the plural of sirr. Mowdoon Ibn Abbas said: Woven with gold. Ikrimah said: Encrusted with pearls and rubies. Ibn Abbas also said: (Mowdoon) is arranged in rows, as he said in another place: On lined couches. He also said and from Mujahid: Overlaid with gold. In the commentaries: (Mowdoon) means woven with gold bars, encrusted with pearls, rubies, and emeralds. And wadhun means doubled weaving and arrangement. It is said: So-and-so wove the stones and bricks, separating them, so they are mowdoon. And a coat of mail mowdoon means tightly woven like arranged. Al-A'sha said: And of the woven fabric of David, they are driven with the tribe, one by one. He also said: And white like the end, decorated with a bow above the body’s pocket The woven bed: the one whose surface is like a woven one. From this comes the word wadeen: a lining of woven threads, some of which are inserted into others. From this comes his saying: She runs to you, worried and distressed
56:16: Reclining on them meaning on the couches facing each other meaning they do not see each other's backs, rather the beds revolve around them. This applies to the believer, his wife and his family, meaning they recline facing each other. This was stated by Mujahid and others. Al-Kalbi said: The length of each couch is three hundred cubits, so when the servant wants to sit on it, it humbles itself, but when he sits on it, it rises up.
56:17: The Almighty says: There will circulate among them immortal boys meaning young men who will never die, as Mujahid said. Al-Hasan and Al-Kalbi said: They will never grow old or change, and from this is the saying of Imru’ Al-Qais: And who enjoys nothing but the eternally happy, the carefree, the one who does not go to bed in distress? Saeed bin Jubair said: Mukhalladun Maqartun means immortal, and a group of jewelry is called immortal. It was also said: Masroon and something similar, according to Al-Farra’. The poet said: And immortalized in silver, as if their buttocks were the highest of the dunes. It was said: Muqarratoon means girdled with belts. Ikrimah said: Immortal is blessed. It was said: At one age, God created them for the people of Paradise, to go around them as He wishes, without a mother. Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him and Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: The children here are the children of the Muslims who die young, and they have no good or bad deeds. Salman Al-Farsi said: The children of the polytheists are the servants of the people of Paradise. Al-Hasan said: They had no good deeds to be rewarded for, nor bad deeds to be punished for. So they were placed in this position. The meaning is that the people of Paradise are in the utmost joy and bliss, and bliss is only completed by the servants and children surrounding the person. With cups and ewers “cookies” is the plural of cup. This has been mentioned in az-Zukhruf, which is the vessel that has no handles or spouts. The ewers that have handles and spouts, the singular of which is ibreek, are called this because their color shines from their clarity.
56:18: And a cup from a flowing spring This was discussed in (By the ranks). The flowing spring is water or wine, but what is meant here is wine flowing from springs. It was said: it is apparent to the springs, so (flowing) is a passive participle of seeing. It was also said: it is a passive participle of meaning, which means abundance. And it was explained that it is not like the wine of this world, which is extracted by pressing, effort, and processing.
56:19: The Almighty said: They will not have a headache from it meaning their heads will not be split from drinking it, meaning it is a pleasure without harm, unlike the drinks of this world. Nor will they be intoxicated was mentioned earlier in (Al-Saffat) meaning they will not become intoxicated and lose their minds. Mujahid read: They will not have a headache meaning they will not have a headache, meaning they will not be scattered, like the Almighty's saying: On that Day they will be headaches. The people of Kufa read They will have a headache with a kasra on the zay, meaning their drink will not run out and their wine will not be exhausted. From this is the saying of the poet: By my life, whether you bleed or wake up, you, the family of Abjara, will be bad companions. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Wine has four characteristics: intoxication, headache, vomiting, and urine. God Almighty mentioned the wine of Paradise and cleared it of these characteristics.
56:20: The Almighty says: And fruits of whatever they choose. That is, they choose whatever they wish because of its abundance. It was also said: And selected and pleasing fruit, and choosing means selecting.
56:21: And the meat of birds of whatever they desire. Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi: Anas ibn Malik said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked, What is Al-Kawthar? He said, "That is a river that God, the Most High, has given me - meaning in Paradise - whiter than milk, sweeter than honey. In it are birds with necks like the necks of camels." Umar said, This is very soft. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, I have eaten it, but it is better than that. He said, A good hadith. Al-Tha’labi narrated it from the hadith of Abu al-Darda’ that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “In Paradise there are birds like the necks of camels, lined up before the friend of God. One of them will say, ‘O friend of God, I have grazed in meadows beneath the Throne and drunk from the springs of submission, so eat from me.’ They will continue to boast before him until one of them comes to his mind and falls before him in different colours. He will eat from it whatever he wants. When he is full, the bones of the bird will be gathered together and he will fly away to graze in Paradise wherever he wants.” Umar said, O Prophet of God, it is soft. He said, I can eat from it softer than it. It was narrated from Abu Sa’id al-Khudri that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “In Paradise there are birds, each of which has seventy thousand feathers. It will land on the face of a man from the people of Paradise, then it will shake itself off and from each feather will come out a colour of food whiter than snow, cooler and softer than butter, and sweeter than honey, with no colour resembling its companion. It will eat from it whatever it wants and then go and fly away.”
56:22: The Almighty's saying: And wide-eyed maidens has been read in the nominative, accusative, and genitive cases. Whoever uses the genitive case, namely Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, and others, may have it conjoined with cups and it is based on the meaning, because the meaning is that they enjoy cups, fruits, meat, and wide-eyed maidens, as Al-Zajjaj said. It may have been conjoined with Gardens, meaning they are in Gardens of Delight and among wide-eyed maidens, assuming the complement is deleted, as if he said: and in the company of wide-eyed maidens. Al-Farra': The genitive case is based on the same wording, even though they differ in meaning, because the wide-eyed maidens are not to be walked around with. The poet said: If the prostitutes appear one day and move their eyebrows and eyes The eye is not glazed, but it is lined with kohl. Another said: I saw your husband in the battlefield, wearing a sword and a spear. Qatrab said: It is connected to the cups and pitchers without being based on the meaning. He said: It is not denied that they will be served with wide-eyed maidens and that they will enjoy that. The most likely accusative is that of Al-Ashab Al-Uqaili, Al-Nakha’i, and Isa bin Umar Al-Thaqafi, and it is also in the copy of Abi, so it is based on the assumption of an implied verb, as if he said: And they will marry wide-eyed houris. It is also good to carry the accusative case based on the meaning, because the meaning of it will be served to them is that they will give it. Whoever raises it, and this is the opinion of the majority - and this is the choice of Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim - then it is based on the meaning of and they have wide-eyed houris, because the wide-eyed houris will not be served to them. Al-Kisa’i said: Whoever says and wide-eyed houris in the nominative case and explains it by saying that they will not be served with them, then this is required of them in the case of fruit and meat, because that is not served with and one does not serve except with wine alone. Al-Akhfash said: It is permissible for it to be based on the meaning, because the meaning is for them are cups and for them are wide-eyed houris. It is possible that it is connected to a group and a group as a subject and its predicate is on lined couches and likewise and wide-eyed houris. It began with the indefinite noun to specify it with the description.
56:23: Like means like hidden pearls meaning that which has not been touched by hands and dust has not fallen on it, so it is the purest and most sparkling, meaning they are in the similarity of their bodies in beauty from all sides as the poet said: As if you were created in the shell of a pearl, and all its corners are faces of ambush.
56:24: A reward for what they used to do meaning a recompense, and the word is in the accusative case as a direct object. It is also permissible for it to be in the verbal noun, because the meaning of Immortal youths will circulate among them is that they will be rewarded. We have already discussed the houris in (By the Mount) and elsewhere. Anas said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘God created the houris from saffron.’” Khalid ibn al-Walid said: “I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘A man from the people of Paradise will hold an apple from the apples of Paradise and it will split in his hand, and from it will emerge a houri who, if she looked at the sun, would be ashamed of her beauty, without that detracting from the apple.” A man said to him: ‘O Abu Sulayman, this is amazing, and it does not detract from the apple?’ He said: ‘Yes, like a lamp from which another lamp is lit, and it does not detract, and God is able to do whatever He wills.’” It was narrated on the authority of Ibn ‘Utbas, may God be pleased with them both, that he said: God created the houris from her toes to her knees from saffron, from her knees to her breasts from the most fragrant musk, from her breasts to her neck from the most ash-grey amber, and from her neck to her head from white camphor. She will be dressed in seventy thousand garments like anemones. When she approaches, her face will shine with a brilliant light, just as the sun shines for the people of Paradise.” The world, and when it turns away, her liver can be seen from the softness of her clothes and skin. On her head are seventy thousand tufts of fragrant musk, each tuft of which has a maidservant who raises its train and calls out: This is the reward of the saints, a reward for what they used to do.
56:25: God the Almighty says: Therein they will hear no idle talk or sinful speech. Ibn Abbas said: Falsehood or lies. Idle talk is what is nullified in speech, and sinful speech is the source of athamatuhu meaning I told him I sinned. Muhammad ibn Ka’b: nor sinful speech meaning they will not blame one another. Mujahid: Therein they will hear no idle talk or sinful speech cursing or sinful speech.
56:26: "Except for a word of peace, peace" (Qilaan) is in the accusative case because of (-yasma'oon) or an interrupted exception, meaning but they say a word or they hear. And "Peace, peace" are in the accusative case because of the saying, meaning except that they say good things. Or it is in the source, meaning except that some of them say peace to one another. Or it is a description of (-qailaan), and the second peace is a substitute for the first, and the meaning is except for a word in which one is safe from idle talk. And it is permissible to raise it on the assumption of peace be upon you. Ibn Abbas said: meaning they greet one another. And it was said: the angels greet them or their Lord, the Almighty, greets them.
56:27: The Almighty’s saying: And the companions of the right - what are the companions of the right? refers back to mentioning the stations of the companions of the right, who are the first to what was mentioned previously, and the repetition is to magnify the status of the bliss in which they are.
56:28: In thornless lote trees means in jujubes whose thorns have been pruned, i.e. cut off, as stated by Ibn Abbas and others. Ibn al-Mubarak said: "Sufwan narrated to us on the authority of Salim ibn Amir who said: The companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to say: 'The bedouins and their questions benefit us.' He said: One day a bedouin came and said: 'O Messenger of God! God has mentioned in the Qur'an a harmful tree, but I have never seen a tree in Paradise that would harm its inhabitant?' The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: 'What is it?' He said: The lote tree, for it is harmful.' He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: 'Does He not say, "In thornless lote trees? God has pruned its thorns and replaced each thorn with a fruit, and it produces fruit from which seventy-two types of food are produced, none of which resembles the other.' Abu Al-Aaliyah and Al-Dahhak said: The Muslims looked at Waj which is a fertile valley in Taif and were impressed by its lote trees, so they said: If only we had something like this. So this verse was revealed. Umayyah bin Abi Al-Salt said, describing Paradise: The gardens in Paradise are shady, with young maidens, whose lote trees are adorned with green leaves. Ad-Dahhak, Mujahid and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: At Sidr Makhdud meaning one that is laden with fruit. This is close to what we mentioned in the hadith. Saeed ibn Jubayr: Its fruit is larger than pots. This was mentioned previously in Surat An-Najm when God Almighty said: At Sidrat al-Muntaha and that its fruit is like the pots of Hajar, from the hadith of Anas on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
56:29: The Almighty said: And banana trees in layers. Talh is the banana tree, its singular is talha. This was said by most of the commentators, Ali, Ibn Abbas and others. Al-Hasan said: It is not a banana, but a tree that provides cool, moist shade. Al-Farra and Abu Ubaidah said: It is a large tree with thorns. Some of the storytellers, namely Al-Ja'di, said: Her guide gave her good report and said, Tomorrow you will see the acacia trees and the ropes. Talh is any large tree with many thorns. Az-Zajjaj: It is possible that it is in Paradise and its thorns have been removed. Az-Zajjaj also said: Like the tree of Umm Ghailan, it has very fragrant light, so they were addressed and promised what they would love like it, except that its superiority over everything in this world is like the superiority of everything else in Paradise over everything in this world. As-Suddi said: The Talh of Paradise is similar to the Talh of this world, but its fruit is sweeter than honey. Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him read: (and arranged fruit clusters) with the letter ‘ayn and recited this verse: (and palm trees with dense clusters of dates) and said: What is the matter with Talh? It is (and arranged fruit clusters) then he said: (with clusters of dates) It was said to him: Should we not change it? He said: The Qur’an should not be attacked or changed. He chose this reading and did not see it proven in the scriptures because it contradicts its agreed-upon script. This was said by Al-Qushayri. Abu Bakr al-Anbari narrated it, saying: My father told me, al-Hasan ibn Arfa told us, Isa ibn Yunus told us, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Sa’d, on the authority of Qais ibn Ibad, who said: I read in the presence of Ali, or it was read in the presence of Ali - Mujalid was unsure - And bananas in layers. Ali, may God be pleased with them both, said: What is with the bananas? Don’t you read And a date palm in layers. Then he said: For it are layered date palms. So he said to him: O Commander of the Faithful, should I remove it from the Mushaf? He said: No, lest the Qur’an be disturbed today. Abu Bakr said: The meaning of this is that he went back to what was in the Mushaf and knew that it was correct, and he nullified what he had said. The layered and stacked fruit that has been arranged beginning and end with a load does not have a prominent stem, rather it is arranged, and the arrangement is the arrangement, and the arranged fruit is arranged. An-Nabigha said: I freed the one who was imprisoning him and lifted him to the prison and the table Masruq said: The trees of Paradise, from their roots to their branches, are full of fruit like a whole. Every time a person eats a fruit, it returns to its place better than before.
56:30: The Almighty's saying: And an extended shade is permanent and everlasting, it does not disappear and the sun does not nullify it, as in His saying: Have you not seen how your Lord extended the shade? And if He had willed, He could have made it stationary. That is in the morning, which is the period between dawn and sunrise, as was explained above. And all of Paradise is shade with no sun with it. Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: It means the shade of the Throne. Amr ibn Maymun said: A journey of seventy thousand years. Abu Ubaidah said: The Arabs say for a long time, a long life, and something that does not end, extended. Labid said: Consolation prevailed, and I was not defeated, a long, eternal, extended age In Sahih al-Tirmidhi and others, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider would travel for a hundred years without crossing it. And read, if you wish, ‘and an extended shade.’”
56:31: And poured water means flowing continuously. The root of pouring is pouring. It is said: he poured it sakban. The word sakub is its pouring. It is said: he poured sakban and he poured insakban. That is, poured water flows day and night without a groove, never stopping from them. The Arabs were nomads and people of hot lands. Rivers in their lands were scarce and they could not reach water except with a bucket and a rope. So they were promised the opposite of that in Paradise. The well-known reasons for recreation in this world were described to them, which are the trees and their shade, the waters and rivers and their regularity.
56:32: The Almighty says, And abundant fruit, meaning it is not few and precious as it was in their country.
56:33: The Almighty says, Nor cut off meaning at any given time, such as the cutting off of summer fruits in winter. Nor forbidden meaning it is not prohibited like the fruits of this world. It was also said, Nor forbidden meaning it is not prevented by thorns, distance, or a wall. Rather, if the servant desires it, it will come near to him until he takes it. God the Almighty says, And its fruits will be made accessible to him. It was also said that it is not cut off by time nor forbidden by prices. And God knows best.
56:34: The Almighty’s saying, And raised couches. “Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the Almighty’s saying, And raised couches, he said, Their height is like the distance between the heaven and the earth, a journey of five hundred years. He said: A strange hadith that we do not know of except from the hadith of Rushdin bin Saad. Some of the people of knowledge said in their interpretation of this hadith, The couches in the levels and what is between the levels is like the distance between the heaven and the earth. It was said that the couches here are a metaphor for the women in Paradise, and they were not mentioned before, but the Almighty’s saying, And raised couches, indicates that they are the place of women, so the meaning is, And women of high status in their beauty and perfection.
56:35: His evidence is the statement of God the Almighty: Indeed, We created them a new creation meaning, We created them a creation and perfected them a creation. The Arabs call a woman a bed, a garment, and a loincloth. God the Almighty said: They are your clothing. Then it was said: According to this, they are the houris, meaning, We created them without giving birth. It was also said: What is meant are the women of the children of Adam, meaning, We created them a new creation, which is the restoration, meaning, We restored them to a state of youth and perfect beauty. The meaning is, We created the old woman and the young girl as one creation, and they were implied and not mentioned previously, because they have already been included among the companions of the right hand, and because the bed is a metaphor for women, as mentioned above. "It was narrated from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) regarding the statement of God the Almighty: "Indeed, We created them a new creation," he said: (Among them are the virgins and the previously married)." Umm Salamah may God be pleased with her said: I asked the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about the verse: “Indeed, We created them a special creation. And made them virgins, * Arab and equal in age.” He said: “O Umm Salamah, they are those who were taken in this world as old women, black-eyed, blind, and dry-eyed. God made them, after old age, equal in age, having one birth in being equal in being.” An-Nahhas narrated it on the authority of Anas, who said: Ahmad ibn Amr told us, who said: Amr ibn Ali told us, who said: Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Musa ibn Ubaydah, on the authority of Yazid al-Raqashi, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who traced it back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Indeed, We created them a special creation. He said: They are the old women, black-eyed and dry-eyed, who were blind and dry-eyed in this world. Al-Musayyab bin Sharik said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding His statement, ‘Indeed, We created them a new creation’ verse, ‘They are the old women of this world. God created them a new creation. Whenever their husbands came to them, they found them virgins.’ When Aisha heard that, she said, ‘How painful!’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to her, ‘There is no pain there.’”
56:37: Araba is the plural of Aroob. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others said: The Arabs are those who are in love with their husbands. And also from Ibn Abbas: It is the seductive Aroob. Ikrimah: The coquettish. Ibn Zayd: In the language of the people of Medina. And from it is the saying of Labid: In the tent is a pure, not obscene bride, with beautiful rumps that blind the eyes. It is the word shakla in the language of the people of Mecca. Also on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam: The beautiful-speaking one. Also on the authority of Ikrimah and Qatada: The Arab women who are endeared to their husbands. Its derivation is from araba if it is clear. So, the Arab woman shows her love for her husband through her appearance, coquettishness, and beautiful speech. It is said that it is the beautiful woman who is conjugal in order to be more enjoyable. Ja’far bin Muhammad narrated on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, who said: “The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘Araba.’ He said: ‘Their speech is Arabic.’” Hamza and Abu Bakr read on the authority of Asim: Araba with a sukoon on the ra. The rest used to pronounce it with a damma, and they are both permissible in the plural of fa’ool. “Atraba” means those born at the same time in equality and at the same age, thirty-three years. It is said of women atraab and of men aqran. The Arabs used to be drawn to women who had passed the age of youth and had descended from old age. It was said: Atraba means examples and similarities, as said by Mujahid. Al-Suddi: They are equal in morals, there is no hatred or envy between them.
56:38: For the companions of the right hand. It was said: The houris are for the forerunners, and the Arab women of equal age are for the companions of the right hand.
56:39: His statement, the Most High: A group from the former peoples * And a group from the latter ones. The discussion goes back to His statement, the Most High: And the companions of the right hand - what are the companions of the right hand? That is, they are A group from the former peoples * And a group from the latter ones. The discussion of its meaning has already passed. Abu Al-Aaliyah, Mujahid, Ata bin Abi Rabah, and Ad-Dahhak said: A group from the former peoples means from the predecessors of this nation. And a group from the latter ones from this nation from its last, indicated by what was narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding this verse: A group from the former peoples * And a group from the latter ones. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They are all from my nation. Al-Wahidi said: The companions of Paradise are of two halves, one half from the previous nations and one half from this nation. This is refuted by what was narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan and by Al-Tirmidhi in his Jami’ on the authority of Buraydah ibn Khasib may God be pleased with him who said: “The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: ‘The people of Paradise are one hundred and twenty rows, eighty of which are from this nation and forty from all other nations.’” Abu ‘Eesa said: This is a hasan hadith. The word three is in the nominative case as a subject, or as a predicate of the descriptive particle is omitted. Its meaning is: The companions of the right are two thirds: a group from these and a group from those. The first are the past nations, and the last are this nation according to the second opinion.
56:41: The Almighty said: And the companions of the left - what are the companions of the left? He mentioned the dwellings of the people of Hell and called them the companions of the left, because they take their books with their left hands. Then He magnified their mention in affliction and torment, saying: What are the companions of the left? * In scorching winds. The scorching winds are the hot winds that enter the pores of the body. What is meant here is the heat and scorching of Hell.
56:42: And scalding water means scalding hot water that is extremely hot. When the fire burns their livers and bodies, they resort to scalding water, like someone who resorts to water to quench his heat from a fire, but finds it scalding hot, extremely hot and boiling. It was previously mentioned in Al-Qital "And they were given to drink scalding water, so it tore their intestines apart."
56:43: And a shade of scorching heat meaning they are terrified by the intense smoke of Hellfire and seek the shade just as the people of this world are terrified and find it a shade of scorching heat, meaning from the smoke of Hellfire, very black. Narrated by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others. Similarly, yahmuum in the language means: very black, and it is derived from ham, which is the fat blackened by the burning of fire. It was also said that it is derived from hammah, which is charcoal. Ad-Dahhak said: The Fire is black and its people are black and everything in it is black. Ibn Abbas also said: The Fire is black. Ibn Zayd said: Al-Yahmuum is a mountain in Hellfire, and the people of Hellfire seek help under its shade.
56:44: Not cold but rather hot because it is from the smoke of the edge of Hell. Nor generous sweet, according to Ad-Dahhak. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: Nor is its appearance good, and everything that has no good in it is not generous. It was said: And shade of scorching heat meaning from the Fire in which they will be tormented, like the Almighty's statement: For them are shades of Fire above them and shades beneath them.
56:45: They were before that in luxury meaning they only deserved this punishment because they were in luxury in this world with what is forbidden. The one who is in luxury is the one who is pampered, according to Ibn Abbas and others. Al-Suddi said: (in luxury) means polytheists.
56:46: And they persisted in the great oath meaning they persisted in polytheism, narrated by Al-Hasan, Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Yazid. Qatada and Mujahid said: The great sin from which they did not repent. Al-Sha'bi: It is the false oath, and it is one of the major sins. It is said: He broke his oath, and that was their breaking of the oath. God the Most High said, informing us about them: And they swore by God their most solemn oaths that God would not raise up anyone who died. In al-Naba 78:He used to perform the great oath of polytheism in Hira', meaning he did what would absolve himself of the sin of breaking the oath, which is the sin.
56:47: And they used to say, 'When we die, will we die?' This is a rejection and denial of the matter of resurrection on their part.
56:49: Then God Almighty said: Say to them, O Muhammad, Indeed, the first ones of your fathers and the last ones of you will be gathered together for a time of a known day meaning the Day of Resurrection. The meaning of the statement is an oath, and the inclusion of the lam in God Almighty’s saying: will be gathered together is evidence of the oath in the meaning, meaning that you will be gathered together in a true oath, unlike your false oath.
56:50: They will be gathered together at a appointed time on a known day.
56:51: Then you, O you who have gone astray from guidance are the deniers of the resurrection.
56:52: They will eat from the tree of Zaqqum, which is a tree with an unpleasant appearance and an unpleasant taste, and it is mentioned in Surat Al-Saffat.
56:53: And they will fill their bellies with it meaning from the tree, because what is meant by the tree is the tree. It is possible that the first from is redundant, or the object is omitted, as if he said: We will eat from the tree of Zaqqum food. And his saying: from Zaqqum is an attribute of the tree, and if the attribute is considered redundant, it is in the accusative case according to the meaning, or in the genitive case according to the wording. If you assume the object is omitted, the attribute is only in the genitive case.
56:54: The Almighty said: And they will drink from it meaning from Zaqqum, or from the food, or from the tree, because it is masculine and feminine. From scalding water which is boiling water that has boiled intensely and is the pus of the people of Hell. That is, the heat of what they eat from Zaqqum, along with the intense hunger, will cause them to become thirsty, so they will drink water that they think will quench their thirst, but they will find it to be boiling water.
56:55: The Almighty said: And they will drink the drink of burning camels. Nafi', Asim and Hamzah read sharb with a damma on the sheen. The rest read it with a fatha. These are two good dialects. The Arabs say: Sharbat sharban sharban and sharban sharban and sharban sharban with two dhammah. Abu Zaid said: I heard the Arabs say with a damma, fatha and kasra on the sheen. The fatha is the correct verbal noun, because every verbal noun with three letters has a fa'l fa'l. Don't you see that you can refer it to the single letter, so you say fa'lah tanha sharbah sharbah and with a damma the noun is used. It was said: The fatha and the noun are two verbal nouns, so sharb is like akmal eating, shadhr sharban is like dhikr remembrance, and sharb sharb with a kasra is a drink like ground flour. Al-haim are the thirsty camels that are not quenched due to an illness that afflicts them, according to Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Qatadah, al-Suddi and others. Ikrimah also said: They are the sick camels. Ad-Dahhak: Al-Haim is a disease that afflicts camels that causes them to become extremely thirsty. The singular form is ahim and the female is haima. This disease is also called hayam. Qais ibn al-Mulawwah said: It is said that he has been afflicted with the disease of infatuation, and I have learned the place of its cure. A people who are thirsty are also called haim, meaning thirsty. Some Arabs say about camels: haim and haima, and the plural is haim. Labid said: I passed to her acquaintances, and she was ugly and ruined from the Eid Ad-Dahhak, Al-Akhfash, Ibn Uyaynah and Ibn Kaysan said: Al-Haym is the flat, sandy land. It was also narrated from Ibn Abbas: They drink the drink of sand that is not quenched by water. Al-Mahdawi: All camels and sand that cannot be quenched are called Ahaym and Haymaa. In As-Sahah: Al-Hiyam with the Dammah is the most severe thirst. Al-Hiyam is like madness from love. Al-Hiyam is a disease that afflicts camels, so they wander aimlessly in the land, not grazing. It is said: a Haymaa camel. Al-Hiyama is also a desert with no water. Al-Hiyam with the Tafaha: the sand that does not hold together so that it does not flow from the hand because of its softness. The plural is Haym like Qadhal and Qadhal. Al-Hiyam with the Kasra is the thirsty camel, singular Hayman. A Haymaa camel is like Atshan and Atsha.
56:56: The Almighty’s saying: This is their lodging on the Day of Judgment meaning their provision that is prepared for them, like the lodging that is prepared for guests as an honor to them, and there is sarcasm in it, as in the Almighty’s saying: Then give them tidings of a painful punishment and as in the saying of Abu al-Sa’d al-Dhabi: When the tyrant with the army visited us, we made spears and sharp blades his refuge. Yunus bin Habib and Abbas read on the authority of Abu Amr, This is their place of residence, with a sukoon on the zay. This has already been discussed at the end of Al Imran. “The Day of Judgment” is the Day of Recompense, meaning in Hell.
56:57: The Almighty says: We created you, so why do you not believe? That is, why do you not believe in the futility? Because repetition is like the beginning. It was also said that the meaning is that we created your provision, so why do you not believe that this is your food if you do not believe?
56:58: God Almighty says: Have you seen what you desire? That is, what you pour of semen into the wombs of women.
56:59: Do you create it? That is, do you fashion it from a human being? Or are We the Creators? The Determiners, the Fashioners. This is their argument and an explanation of the first verse, that is, if you acknowledge that We are its creators and no one else, then you are admitting to fooling around. Abu al-Samal, Muhammad ibn al-Samiq' and Ashhab al-'Uqayli read it as (َتمنوُن) with a fat-ha on the ta'. They are two languages: amaani and munna, amdha and madhhi, yammni and yammhi and yamdha. Al-Mawardi said: I think their meanings may differ, so amani is when it is ejaculated from sexual intercourse, and munna is when it is ejaculated from a wet dream. There are two views on naming semen as maniyyah: One of them is due to its shedding, which is its estimation. The second is due to its estimation, and from it comes the manna that is weighed because it is a measure for that, and likewise semen is a correct measure for the depiction of creation.
56:60: His statement, the Most High: We have decreed death among you is also an argument, meaning that the One who has the power to cause death has the power to overcome all creation, and if He has the power to resurrect, then He will be glorified. Mujahid, Hamid, Ibn Muhaisin, and Ibn Kathir read it with a soft dal. The rest read it with a shaddah. Ad-Dahhak said: meaning, We made the inhabitants of the heavens and the inhabitants of the earth equal. It was also said: We decreed. It was also said: We wrote, and the meanings are close, as no one will remain except Him, the Almighty. And We will not be outdone * In replacing the likes of you meaning, if We wanted to replace the likes of you, no one would be able to bring us forth, meaning, no one could overcome us. And We means, we will not be overcome. At-Tabari said: The meaning is, We have decreed death among you so that We will replace the likes of you after your death with others of your kind, and We will not be outdone in your appointed times, meaning, no one will come later and no one will come later.
56:61: And We will create you in that which you do not know of images and forms. Al-Hasan said: That is, We will make you apes and pigs as We did with peoples before you. It was also said that the meaning is that We will create you in the resurrection in a form other than your worldly form, so the believer will be beautiful with the whiteness of his face, and the disbeliever will be ugly with the blackness of his face. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The words of God, In that which you do not know mean in the crops of black birds that are in Barhout like swallows, and Barhout is a valley in Yemen. Mujahid said: In that which you do not know in whatever creation We will. It was also said that the meaning is that We will create you in a world you do not know, and in a place you do not know.
56:62: The Almighty said: And you have certainly known the first creation meaning when you were created from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh, and you were nothing, according to Mujahid and others. Qatadah and Ad-Dahhak: meaning the creation of Adam, peace be upon him. Then why do you not remember? meaning why do you not remember? And in al-Naba 78:It is truly amazing for someone to deny the other creation while he sees the first creation, and amazing for someone to believe in the hereafter while he does not strive for the eternal home. The general reading is the creation with a short vowel. Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr read the creation with a long vowel, and this has already been explained in Al-Ankaboot.
56:63: The Almighty said: Have you seen what you till? This is another argument, meaning tell me about what you till from your land, sowing seeds in it. Do you grow it and produce it as a crop, so you make the ear and the grain in it, or do we do that? The sowing and the splitting of the earth are from you. If you admit that the bringing out of the ear of grain is not from you, then how do you deny bringing out the dead from the earth and bringing them back?! And He attributed the tillage to them and the planting to Him, because the tillage is their action and occurs according to their choice, while the planting is from the action of God and grows according to His choice. Likewise, what Abu Hurairah narrated from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that he said: (Let none of you say I sowed, but rather say I plowed, for the Sower is God.)
56:64: Abu Hurairah said: Have you not heard the statement of God the Almighty: Is it you who sow it, or are We the sower? It is recommended for anyone who sows seeds in the ground, after seeking refuge, to recite: Have you seen that which you till? Al-An'am 2:17, and then say: "Rather, God is the Sower, the Causer, and the Destroyer. O God, send blessings upon Muhammad, and provide us with its fruits, and protect us from its harm, and make us among those who are grateful for Your blessings, and among those who remember Your favors, and bless it for us, O Lord of the Worlds." It is said that this statement protects that crop from all pests: worms, locusts, and others. We heard it from a trustworthy person and he tested it and found it to be so. The meaning of Do you sow it is that you make it a crop. It is also said: So-and-so is a sower, just as one says a tiller, meaning he does what will turn into a crop that pleases the sower. The word sowage is sometimes used metaphorically to refer to sowing the soil and tilling it. I said: It is a prohibition of guidance and etiquette, not a prohibition of prohibition and obligation. From this is his saying, peace be upon him: (Let not any of you say, My slave or My female slave, but rather say, My boy and My female slave and My young man and My young woman. This has already been discussed in Yusuf. Some scholars have exaggerated and said: Do not say, I plowed and obtained, but rather, say, God helped me so I plowed, and He gave me by His grace what I obtained. Al-Mawardi said: This verse includes two matters, the first of which is gratitude to them for causing their crops to grow so that they could live by it so that they would thank Him for His blessings upon them. The second is the proof that requires consideration, because when He caused their crops to grow after their seeds had perished and had reached a state of maturity from rot and dust until they became green crops, then He made them strong and robust many times what they were, so by returning them from what they killed, it is easier for them and more capable. This proof is convincing to those with sound natures. Then He said, If We willed, We could have made them debris meaning broken, meaning the crops. And the broken, perishable debris that is of no use as food or nourishment. Thus, He also draws attention to two matters: The first is the blessings He bestowed upon them in their crops, since He did not make them broken so that they would thank Him. The second is that they would consider this in themselves, just as He makes crops broken when He wills, and likewise He destroys them when He wills, so that they may learn a lesson and be deterred.
56:65: And you remained in amazement meaning you were amazed by its passing and regretted what had happened to you. This was said by Al-Hasan, Qatada and others. In As-Sahah: And you remained in amazement means you were amazed and it is also said: you regret, God the Most High said: And you remained in amazement meaning you were regretting. And you enjoyed something means you enjoyed it. Yaman said: you regret your spending, the evidence for this is: So he began to wring his hands over what he had spent on it. Ikrimah said: you blame and regret what you did in the past of disobeying God which necessitated your punishment until it reached you in your crops. Ibn Kaysan: you grieve, and the meanings are close. There are two pronunciations for it: you are in amazement and you are regretting. Al-Farra' said: the letter nun is the language of Ikl. In As-Sahah: Tafakkan means regretting what has passed. It was said: Joking is talking about what does not concern you, and from this joking is called joke with damma. As for joke with fatha, it is the source of the man’s joke with kasra, so he is joker if he is of a good nature and jokes. The reading of the common people is fadhaltum with fatha on the dhaal. Abdullah read (fadhaltum) with kasra on the dhaal and Harun narrated it from Hussein from Abu Bakr. So whoever opens it is on the original, and the original is dhaltum so he deleted the first lam for ease, and whoever breaks it moves the kasra of the first lam to the dhaal then deletes it. That is, you regret it
56:66: Inna lamghramoon Abu Bakr and al-Mufaddal read (a'ina) with two hamzas as a question, and Asim narrated it on the authority of Zur ibn Hubaysh. The rest of them with one hamza as a report, meaning they say Inna lamghramoon meaning tormented, on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Qatadah who said: And gharam is torment, and from this is the saying of Ibn al-Muhallam: I trust that memorization is my nature and that my heart is infatuated with you Mujahid and Ikrimah said: He is fond of us. From this is the saying of Al-Nimr bin Talib: He kept it a secret and was obsessed with it. It is said: So-and-so is infatuated with so-and-so, meaning he is obsessed with her. From this comes the word gharamak, which means necessary evil. Mujahid also said: We will surely encounter evil. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: We will surely perish. An-Nahhas said: We are indeed infatuated is taken from gharam, which means destruction, as he said: The Day of the Eagle and the Day of the Jafar were torment and they were a loss Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Kaysan: It is from the word gharam, and al-Maghram is the one whose money was lost without compensation, meaning we lost the love we squandered. Al-Hamdani once said: We will be held accountable.
56:67: Rather, we are deprived meaning we were deprived of the income we sought. Deprived is the one who is prevented from provision. Deprived is the opposite of provided for, and it is the one who is distorted according to Qatada. Anas reported that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) passed by the land of the Ansar and said: What prevents you from tilling the land? They said: The drought. He said: "Do not do that, for God, the Most High, says: 'I am the Sower. If you wish, I sow by water, and if you wish, I sow by the wind, and if you wish, I sow by seeds.'" Then he recited: Have you seen that which you till? Is it you who sow it, or are We the Sower? I said: In this report and the hadith before it, there is what confirms the statement of those who include the farmer among the names of God Almighty, and the majority of scholars rejected it, and we have mentioned that in the book Al-Asna fi Sharh Asma God Al-Husna.
56:68: The Almighty said: Have you seen the water which you drink? To revive yourselves with it, and quench your thirst, because drinking is a consequence of food, and for this reason food came before in the verse, don't you see that you give your guest to drink after you feed him? Al-Zamakhshari: If you reversed it, you would fall under the words of Abu Al-Ala: If you give people pure water to drink, they will give their guests pure water to drink. Some Arabs were given water to drink and he said: I will not drink except from a drink of water.
56:69: Did you bring it down from the clouds? meaning the clouds, the singular is muznah, so the poet said: We are like rainwater, there is no one who can provide for us, and no one who is stingy with us. This is the statement of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others that zan is the cloud. Also on the authority of Ibn Abbas and al-Thawri: Mazn is the sky and the clouds. In al-Sahah: Abu Zayd: Maznah is the white cloud and the plural is Mazn, and Maznah is the rain. He said: Have you not seen that God sent down rain and the gazelles dusted themselves in the dugouts? Or are We the One who sends it down? That is, if you know that I sent it down, why do you not thank Me by sincerely worshipping Me? And why do you deny My ability to bring it back?
56:70: If We willed, We could have made it bitter. That is, very salty, as Ibn Abbas said. Al-Hasan: It is bitter and bitter, and you do not benefit from it in drinking, farming, or anything else. Then why do you not thank the One who did this to you?
56:71: God Almighty says: Have you seen the fire that you kindle? That is, tell me about the fire that you kindle with a spark from a fresh tree.
56:72: Did you create its tree? meaning that from which the flint is made, which is the Markh and the Afar. From this comes their saying: In every tree there is fire. The Markh and the Afar were praised, meaning they were plentiful, as if they had taken from the fire what was sufficient for them. It is also said: because they burn quickly. It is said: I kindled the fire if you ignite it. And the flint is kindled if the fire is sparked from them. And there is another language for it: The flint is kindled with a kasra in both of them. Or are We the originators? meaning the inventors and creators. So if you know My power, then thank Me and do not deny My power to resurrect.
56:73: The Almighty said: We have made it a reminder meaning the fire of this world is a lesson for the greater fire, said Qatada. And Mujahid: insight for the people from the darkness. It is authentically reported that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: (This fire of yours that the children of Adam kindle is a part of seventy parts of the fire of Hell) They said: O Messenger of God, if it is sufficient? He said: (Then it is exceeded by sixty-nine parts, all of them like its heat) And provision for the strengthened Ad-Dahhak said: meaning benefit for the travelers, they are called thus because they stop in Al-Qawy, which is the desert. Al-Farraa' said: Travelers are only called Muqawi if they stop in Al-Qayy, which is the barren land in which there is nothing. The same is true for Al-Qawy and Al-Qawwaa with a long and short vowel, and a place of quwaa has no companion in it. It is said: The house is quwat and quwayt also meaning it is empty of its inhabitants. An-Nabigha said: Oh, house of Mayya in the highlands, the Sind is strong and the past has been long upon it Antara said: I came back from the ruins of an ancient time, stronger and more desolate after Umm Al-Haytham It is said: Aqwa means he was strong and his companions were strong, and Aqwa if he traveled, meaning he settled in the qawa and the qaf. Mujahid said: For the strengthened are those who enjoy it from all people in cooking, baking, warming themselves and lighting themselves, and by it they remember the fire of Hell and seek refuge with God from it. Ibn Zayd said: For the hungry in preparing their food. It is said: I have been strengthened since such and such, meaning I did not eat anything, and so-and-so spent the night in the qawa and the desert if he spent the night hungry without any taste. The poet said: I choose the strong, full of heart, to avoid being called mean. Al-Rabi' and Al-Suddi said: For the strengthened are those who have no flint with them, meaning a fire to kindle and bake with? Al-Awfi narrated it from Ibn Abbas. Qatrib said: The strengthened is from the opposites, it can mean the poor and it can mean the rich. It is said: A man is strong if he does not have provisions, and strong if his animals are strong and his wealth is abundant. Al-Mahdawi: The verse applies to all, because fire is needed by the traveler and the resident, the rich and the poor. Al-Tha'labi narrated that most of the commentators agreed on the first opinion. Al-Qushayri said: He specified the traveler to benefit from it because his benefit from it is greater than the benefit of the resident, because the people of the desert need a fire which they light at night to ward off wild beasts and for many of their needs.
56:74: God Almighty says: So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great. That is, God is far removed from what the polytheists attributed to Him of rivals and inability to resurrect.
56:75: It contains seven issues: First: The Almighty’s statement: So I swear not. “No” is a connective according to most of the commentators, and the meaning is So I swear, as evidenced by His statement: And indeed, it is an oath. Al-Farra’ said: It is a negation, and the meaning is that the matter is not as you say. Then he started with I swear. A man may say: No, by God, it was not like this, but he does not mean by that a negation of the oath, rather he means by it a negation of what came before. That is, the matter is not as you mentioned, rather it is like this. It was said: No means except to draw attention, as He said: Good morning, old ruins He drew attention to the virtue of the Qur’an so that they might ponder it, and that it is neither poetry, nor magic, nor divination as they claimed. Al-Hasan, Hamid, and Isa bin Omar read (fal-aqsam) without an alif after the lam, as a correct reading. It is a verb in the state of things, and it is understood as a deleted subject, the estimation: fal-ana aqsam bi-kha. If it was intended to be in the future tense, the nun would have been required. The nun was deleted with a verb that was intended to be in the future tense, and it is an anomaly. Second: The Almighty’s saying: By the positions of the stars. The positions of the stars are their risings and setting, according to Qatada and others. Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah: Their dwellings. Al-Hasan: Their setting and scattering on the Day of Resurrection. Ad-Dahhak: They are the stars that the people of the Age of Ignorance used to say when they were rained upon, We were rained upon by such-and-such a star. Al-Mawardi: And the Almighty’s saying: So I swear is used in its true sense of negating an oath. Al-Qushayri: It is an oath, and God the Almighty may swear by whatever He wants, and we do not have the right to swear by anyone other than God the Almighty and His eternal attributes. I said: This is indicated by Al-Hasan’s recitation of So I swear and what God, the Almighty, has sworn by of His creation in more than one place in His Book. Ibn Abbas said: What is meant by the positions of the stars is the revelation of the Qur’an in stages. God, the Almighty, sent it down from the Preserved Tablet in the highest heaven to the recording scribes. The scribes sent it down to Gabriel over twenty nights, and Gabriel sent it down to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon them both, over twenty years. So He sent it down to the younger generation of his nation. This was narrated by Al-Mawardi from Ibn Abbas and Al-Suddi. Abu Bakr Al-Anbari said: Ismail bin Ishaq Al-Qadi narrated to us, Hajjaj bin Al-Minhal narrated to us, Hammam narrated to us, from Al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Qur’an was revealed to the lowest heaven all at once, then it was revealed to earth in stages. After that, it was divided into five verses, five by five, or more and fewer. This is the statement of God, the Almighty: “So I swear by the positions of the stars. And indeed, it is a tremendous oath, if you only knew. Indeed, it is a noble Qur’an.” Al-Farra’ narrated from Ibn Mas’ud that the positions of the stars are the definitive parts of the Qur’an. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read bi-mawqāf with the singular form, which is the reading of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, Al-Nakha’i, Al-A’mash, Ibn Muhaisin, and Ruways on the authority of Ya’qub. The rest read it with the plural form. Whoever read it with the singular form did so because it is a generic noun that replaces the plural in one word, and whoever read it with the plural form did so because of the difference in its types.
56:76: And indeed, it is a great oath, if you only knew.
56:77: Third: The Almighty's saying: Indeed, it is a noble Qur'an. It was said that the ha refers to the Qur'an, meaning that the Qur'an is a great oath, as stated by Ibn Abbas and others. It was also said that what God swore by is great. Indeed, it is a noble Qur'an. He mentioned what he swore by, meaning that He swore by the positions of the stars that this Qur'an is a noble Qur'an, not magic or divination, and not a fabrication, rather it is a noble and praiseworthy Qur'an, which God the Almighty made a miracle for His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It is noble for the believers, because it is the speech of their Lord and a cure for their hearts. It is noble for the people of the heavens, because it is the revelation and inspiration of their Lord. It was also said that noble means uncreated. It was also said that it is noble because of the noble morals and meanings it contains. It was also said that it is because it honors the one who memorizes it and magnifies the one who recites it.
56:78: Fourth: The Almighty said: In a protected book Safeguarded by God Almighty. It was also said: Protected and preserved from falsehood. The book here is a book in the heavens, as stated by Ibn Abbas. Jabir bin Zaid and Ibn Abbas also said: It is the Preserved Tablet. Ikrimah: The Torah and the Gospel, in them is mentioned the Qur’an and who it was revealed to. As-Suddi: The Psalms. Mujahid and Qatada: It is the Qur’an that is in our hands.
56:79: Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: None shall touch it except the purified. There is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of none shall touch it. Is it literal in touching with the limb or merely in meaning? Likewise, there is a difference of opinion regarding the purified - who are they? Anas and Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: None shall touch that Book except those purified from sins, and they are the angels. Abu al-Aaliyah and Ibn Zayd said the same: “They are those who have been purified from sins, like the messengers from the angels and the messengers from the children of Adam. So Gabriel, who brought it down, was purified, and the messengers to whom he brought it were purified.” Al-Kalbi said: They are the noble and righteous scribes. All of this is one statement, and it is similar to what Malik chose when he said: The best thing I have heard about His statement, None shall touch it except the purified, is that it is similar to the verse in ‘Abasa wa tawalla He frowned and turned away: “So whoever wills may remember it. * In honored scrolls, * Exalted and purified, * By the hands of scribes, * Noble and virtuous.” He means that the purified are the angels who were described as pure in Surah ‘Abasa. It was said that the meaning of None shall touch it is that None shall bring it down except the purified, meaning the messengers from the angels to the messengers from the prophets. It was said that none shall touch the Preserved Tablet, which is the hidden book, except the purified angels. It was said that Israfil is the one entrusted with that, as narrated by al-Qushayri. Ibn al-‘Arabi said: This is false because the angels do not reach it at any time or in any way. If that were what was meant by it, there would be no room for an exception in it. As for the one who said that it is what is in the hands of the angels in the scrolls, this is an ambiguous statement, and it is the choice of Malik. It was said: What is meant by the Book is the Mushaf in our hands, and this is the most apparent. Malik and others narrated that in the letter of Amr ibn Hazm that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) wrote to him and copied it (From Muhammad the Prophet to Shurahbil ibn Abd Kulal, Al-Harith ibn Abd Kulal, Nu`aym ibn Abd Kulal, Qil Dhi Ra`in, Ma`afir and Hamdan. As for what follows), and in his letter it was: Only the pure shall touch the Qur’an. Ibn Umar said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Do not touch the Qur’an except when you are pure. Umar’s sister said to him when he embraced Islam and he had entered upon her and called for the scroll: None shall touch it except the purified. So he stood up, washed himself and converted to Islam. This has already been mentioned at the beginning of Surah Taha. Qatada and others said on this meaning: None shall touch it except the purified from ritual impurities and impurities. Al-Kalbi: from polytheism. Al-Rabi` ibn Anas: from sins and transgressions. It was said: The meaning of None shall touch it is None shall read it except the purified ones except the monotheists, as stated by Muhammad ibn Fadil and Abdah. Ikrimah said: Ibn Abbas used to forbid allowing any of the Jews and Christians to read the Qur'an. Al-Farra' said: None shall find its taste, benefit, and blessing except the purified ones, meaning those who believe in the Qur'an. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is the preferred opinion of al-Bukhari. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "He has tasted the taste of faith who is content with God as his Lord, Islam as his religion, and Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) as his Prophet." Al-Husayn ibn Fadl said: Its interpretation and explanation are only known to those whom God has purified from polytheism and hypocrisy. Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: None will be granted the success to act upon it except the fortunate ones. It was also said: The meaning is: None shall touch its reward except the believers. Mu'adh narrated it from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Then it was said: The apparent meaning of the verse is a statement of the Sharia, meaning that none may touch it except those purified by the Sharia. If something other than that is found, then it is not in accordance with the Sharia. This is the preferred opinion of Judge Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi. He rejected the notion that its wording is a statement but its meaning is a command. This meaning has already been mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah. Al-Mahdawi: It is permissible for it to be a command and for the damma of the seen to be a damma of i'rab. It may be a prohibition, and the damma of the seen may be a damma of construction, and the verb may be in the jussive mood. Sixth: The scholars differed regarding touching the Qur’an without ablution. The majority of scholars forbid touching it, based on the hadith of Amr ibn Hazm. This is the view of Ali, Ibn Mas’ud, Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas, Sa’id ibn Zayd, Ata’, Az-Zuhri, An-Nakha’i, Al-Hakam, Hammad, and a group of jurists, including Malik and Ash-Shafi’i. There are different narrations from Abu Hanifah. It was narrated from him that one who is in a state of minor ritual impurity may touch it. This was also narrated from a group of the early Muslims, including Ibn Abbas, Ash-Sha’bi, and others. It was narrated from him that he may touch its outer surface, its margins, and anything that does not contain any writing. As for the book, only one who is pure may touch it. Ibn Al-Arabi said: If this is accepted, it strengthens the argument against him, because the forbidden is forbidden. What the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) wrote to Amr ibn Hazm is the strongest evidence for this. Malik said: It may not be carried by one who is not pure, by a strap or on a pillow. Abu Hanifah said: There is nothing wrong with that. He did not forbid carrying it by a strap or touching it with a barrier. It was narrated from Al-Hakam, Hammad, and Dawud ibn Ali that there is no harm in carrying it or touching it, whether it is pure or impure, for a Muslim or a non-Muslim. However, Dawud said: It is not permissible for a polytheist to carry it. They cited as evidence for its permissibility the letter of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to Caesar, which is a case of necessity, so there is no proof in it. There are two views regarding children touching it: One of them is that it is forbidden, taking into consideration the adult. The second is that it is permissible, because if it is forbidden, the Qur’an will not be memorized, because learning it is in a younger state, and because even if the child is pure, it is not complete, because the intention is not valid from him. So if it is permissible to carry it when not completely pure, then it is permissible to carry it when in a state of minor impurity.
56:80: Seventh: The Almighty’s statement: A revelation from the Lord of the worlds, meaning revealed, like their saying: The prince struck and the Yemenite wove. It was also said: Revealed is an adjective for the Almighty’s statement: Indeed, it is a noble Qur’an. It was also said: meaning it is a revelation.
56:81: The Almighty’s saying: Is it this narration meaning the Qur’an that you are disbelieving? That is, you are lying. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Ata’ and others. The one who is disbelieving is the one whose appearance is different from his inner self, as if he is likened to oil in his apparent ease. Muqatil ibn Sulayman and Qatadah said: Disbelieving are disbelievers. Similar to this is: They wish that you would be disbelieving so that they would be disbelieving. The historian said: “The disbelieving one is the hypocrite or the disbeliever who softens his side to hide his disbelief. Compromising and softening are denial, disbelief and hypocrisy. Its root is softness and to keep secret what is different from what is apparent. Abu Qais ibn al-Aslat said: Firmness and strength are better than oil, understanding and fear Adhan and dahan are one and the same. Some people said: dahant means to cover up and adhant means to deceive. Ad-Dahhak said: “madhanoon” are turning away. Mujahid: They are collaborating with the infidels in their disbelief in it. Ibn Kaysan: The mudhan is the one who does not understand what God has given him and repels it with excuses. Some linguists said: Madhanoon are those who abandon certainty in accepting the Quran.
56:82: God the Almighty says: And you make your provision that you deny. Ibn Abbas said: You make your gratitude denial. Al-Haytham bin Adi mentioned that one of the languages of Azd Shanu'ah is: What provision has so-and-so received? meaning, He did not thank him. It is appropriate to replace the noun provision with thank him, because thanking provision requires an increase in it, so thankfulness is provision in this sense. So it was said: And you make your provision meaning you are thankful for your provision, which if it had come from you would have become your provision. That you deny provision, meaning you replace thankfulness with falsehood, like God the Almighty's saying: And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping. Meaning, they did not pray, but they would whistle and clap instead of prayer. It explains that whatever good befalls the servants should not be seen as coming from intermediaries that are usually causes, but rather they should see it as coming from God Almighty, then they should meet it with gratitude if it is a blessing, or patience if it is something unpleasant, out of worship and humility towards Him. It was narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: And you make your gratitude that you deny the truth. It was also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that what was meant by it was seeking rain by means of stars, which is the Arab saying: It rained because of such-and-such a star. Narrated by Ali ibn Abi Talib on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. In Sahih Muslim, it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: It rained during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Among the people were grateful and among them were disbelievers. They said: ‘This is the mercy of God.’ Some of them said: ‘The occurrence of such-and-such a star has come true.’ So this verse was revealed: ‘So I swear by the positions of the stars’ - until he reached - ‘And you make your provision that you deny.’” It was also narrated on his authority: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out on a journey and they felt thirsty. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘What do you think if I invoke God for you and you are given rain, perhaps you will say: ‘This rain is because of such-and-such a star?’” They said: O Messenger of God, this is not because of the timing of the stars. So he prayed two rak’ahs and supplicated to his Lord, and a wind blew, then a cloud blew and they had rain. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a group of his companions passed by a man scooping water from a cup and saying: ‘We were given rain because of such-and-such a star,’ but he did not say: ‘This is from God’s provision.’ So the verse was revealed: ‘And you make your provision that you deny.’” That is, your gratitude to God for His provision to you, that you deny. By grace and you say, We were given rain by such-and-such a star, like you saying, I considered My kindness to you to be a bad deed from you to me, and I considered My favor to you to be that you took me as an enemy. In Al-Muwatta’, it is narrated on the authority of Zaid bin Khalid Al-Juhani that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, led us in the dawn prayer at Al-Hudaibiyah following a rain that had fallen during the night. When he finished, he faced the people and said, Do you know what your Lord has said? They said, God and His Messenger know best. He said, “Among My servants there has become one who believes in Me and one who disbelieves in the star. As for he who says, “We were given rain by the grace and mercy of God,” he is a believer in Me and a disbeliever in the star. As for he who says, We were given rain by such-and-such a star, he is a believer in the star and a disbeliever in Me.” Al-Shafi’i may God have mercy on him said: “I do not like anyone to say, ‘Our rain was due to such-and-such a star,’ even though the star in our view is a created time that neither harms nor benefits, neither brings rain nor withholds any rain. Whoever says, ‘Our rain was due to such-and-such a star,’ as some of the polytheists of the Jahiliyyah meant by that statement, is a disbeliever, and his blood is permissible if he does not repent.” Abu ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-Barr said: “As for his statement, peace and blessings be upon him, narrating from God, the Most High: ‘Some of My servants have become believers in Me and some have disbelieved,’ I believe its meaning is of two types: As for the first, whoever believes that the star is the one who brings down rain and creates the clouds, rather than God, the Most High, is a disbeliever with a clear kufr that must be made to repent and he must be killed. If he refuses, Islam will be rejected and the Qur’an will reject him.” Another interpretation is to believe that God sends down water through the star, and that it is the cause of water according to what God has decreed and foreordained in His knowledge. Although this interpretation is permissible, it also constitutes disbelief in the blessings of God Almighty and ignorance of His subtle wisdom in that He sends down water whenever He wills, sometimes with such-and-such a star, and sometimes with such-and-such a star. Often a star rises but no water comes down with it, and that is from God, not from the star. Similarly, Abu Hurairah would say when it had rained in the morning: We have been rained by the star of victory, then he would recite: Whatever mercy God opens for mankind, none can withhold. Abu Umar said: “In my opinion, this is similar to the statement of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him): “We have been rained by the grace and mercy of God.” Similar to this is the statement of Umar ibn al-Khattab to al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib when he prayed for rain through him: “O uncle of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), is there any part of the star of Thuraya left?” Al-Abbas said: The scholars claim that it appears on the horizon seven days after its setting. But not even a seventh day had passed before they had rain.” Umar said: Praise be to God, this is by the grace and mercy of God. It seems that Omar, may God have mercy on him, knew that the Pleiades were a time when rain was expected and hoped for, so he asked him about it: Has it come out or is there some left of it? Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated on the authority of Ismail ibn Umayyah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard a man on one of his travels saying: We received rain from some of the lion’s tusks. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You have lied, rather it is the rain of God, the Almighty and Majestic. Sufyan said: The lion’s tusks are the arm and the forehead. The common reading is takdhibun from takdhib. Al-Mufaddal read on the authority of Asim and Yahya ibn Waththab takdhibun with the taa’ open and lightened. Its meaning is what we mentioned before from the saying of the one who said: We received rain from such-and-such a star. It was proven from the hadith of Anas bin Malik, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘There are three things that will always exist in my nation: boasting about lineage, wailing, and the stars.’” Muslim’s wording on this is: “There are four things from the days of ignorance that my nation will never abandon: boasting about lineage, criticizing lineage, seeking rain by the stars, and wailing.”
56:83: The Almighty said: Then why, when it reaches the throat meaning why, when the soul or spirit reaches the throat. It was not mentioned before because the meaning is well-known. Hatim said: Amawi, wealth is of no use to a young man if he chokes one day and his chest feels tight. In a hadith: The Angel of Death has helpers who sever the veins and collect the soul little by little until it reaches the neck, where the Angel of Death takes it.
56:84: And you at that time will be awaiting My command and authority. It was also said: You will be awaiting the House, having no power over it. Ibn Abbas said: He means those of the deceased's family who are present, waiting for his soul to depart. Then it was said: This is a refutation of their statement to their brothers, If they had been with us, they would not have died or been killed. That is, did they return the soul of one of them when it reached the throat? It was also said: The meaning is, why don't you, when the soul of one of you reaches the throat at the time of death and you are present, hold onto his soul in his body, despite your eagerness to prolong his life and your love for its survival? This is a refutation of their statement, We die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time. It was also said: This is addressed to the one who is in the death throes, that is, if what you have is not from God, why don't you preserve your soul for yourself?
56:85: And We are nearer to him than you meaning in power, knowledge, and vision. Amir ibn Abd al-Qays said: I did not look at anything except that I saw God Almighty closer to me than it. It was also said: He meant Our messengers who are in charge of taking his soul are nearer to him than you "but you do not see" meaning you do not see them.
56:86: The Almighty said: Then why, if you are not to be held accountable meaning, why, if you are not to be held accountable or rewarded for your deeds, and from this is the Almighty's saying: Will we indeed be held accountable? meaning rewarded and held accountable. This has been mentioned before. It was also said: Not owned nor subjugated. Al-Farra' and others said: I brought him close and owned him. And he recited for Al-Hutay'ah: You have judged your sons until you have left them finer than flour. It means he owned him. And he subjugated him, meaning he humiliated him and enslaved him. It is said: he subjugated him, he subdued him. This has already been discussed in Al-Fatihah when God Almighty says: The Day of Judgment.
56:87: You return it You return the soul to the body. If you are truthful meaning, you will not return it, so your claim that you are not owned or accountable is invalid. You return it is an answer to the Almighty's saying: Then why, when it reaches the throat and His saying: Then why, if you are not to be held accountable, both were answered with one answer, said Al-Farra'. The Arabs sometimes repeat two letters, but their meaning is the same, and from this is the saying of the Almighty: Then if there comes to you guidance from Me - whoever follows My guidance - there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve, both were answered with one answer, and they are two conditions. It was said that one of them was omitted because the other indicated it. It was said that there is an inversion in it, its metaphor: Then why, if you are not to be held accountable, you return it, returning the soul of this dead person to his body when it reaches the throat.
56:88: The Almighty said: But if he was among those brought near, He mentioned the classes of creation at death and at the resurrection, and explained their degrees, saying: But if he this deceased was among those brought near, which are the foremost.
56:89: Spirit, basil, and a garden of delight. The general reading is (Farooh) with a fat-ha on the ra', and its meaning according to Ibn Abbas and others is: a respite from the world. Al-Hasan said: The spirit is mercy. Ad-Dahhak said: The spirit is rest. Al-Qutbi said: The meaning for him in the grave is a pleasant breeze. Abu Al-Abbas Ibn Ata' said: The spirit is looking at the face of God, and basil is listening to His words and revelation. And a garden of delight means that he will not be veiled from God the Almighty therein. Al-Hasan, Qatada, Nasr bin Asim, Al-Jahdary, Ruways, and Zaid from Ya'qub read (Farooh) with a damma on the ra', and it was narrated from Ibn Abbas. Al-Hasan said: The spirit is mercy, because it is like life for the deceased. Aisha may God be pleased with her said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) read (Farooh) with a damma on the ra', and its meaning is that he will remain and have life in Paradise, and this is mercy. (And basil) Mujahid and Saeed bin Jubair said: meaning provision. Muqatil said: it is provision in the language of Himyar. It is said I went out seeking the basil of God, meaning His provision. An-Nimr bin Talib said: God's peace, basil, mercy, and a sky of pearls Qatada said: It is Paradise. Ad-Dahhak: Mercy. It was said that it is the well-known basil that is smelled. Al-Hasan and Qatada also said this. Ar-Rabi’ ibn Khaitham: This is at death and Paradise is hidden for him until he is resurrected. Abu Al-Jawza’: This is when his soul is taken and he is met with bundles of basil. Abu Al-Aliyah: The soul of none of those brought near in this world will leave him until he is brought two branches of basil and he smells them, then his soul is taken in them. The origin of basil and its derivation were mentioned at the beginning of Surah Ar-Rahman, so ponder it. Al-Tha’labi cited many sayings about the soul and basil other than what we have mentioned. Whoever seeks them will find them there.
56:90: God Almighty says: But if he was among the companions of the right hand, meaning, if this deceased person was among the companions of the right hand.
56:91: "So peace be upon you from the companions of the right" meaning, you will only see what you like of safety from them, so do not worry about them, for they will be safe from God's punishment. It was also said that the meaning is, "Peace be upon you from them," meaning, you will be safe from worrying about them. The meaning is the same. It was also said that the companions of the right will supplicate for you, O Muhammad, that God sends blessings and peace upon you. It was also said that the meaning is that they greet you, O Muhammad. It was also said that the meaning is, You, O servant, are safe from what you dislike, for you are among the companions of the right, so the word you was omitted. It was also said that he will live with peace out of honor.
