Based on this, there are three opinions regarding the place of peace: One of them is when his soul is taken in this world, the Angel of Death greets him, as stated by Ad-Dahhak. Ibn Mas'ud said, "When the Angel of Death comes to take the soul of a believer, he says, 'Your Lord sends you peace.'" This was previously mentioned in Surah An-Nahl when God says, Those whom the angels take in death while they are good. The second is when he is questioned in the grave, Munkar and Nakir greet him. The third: When he is resurrected on the Day of Resurrection, the angels will greet him before he reaches it. I said: It may be possible that you greet him in the three situations, and that would be an act of honor after honor. And God knows best. The answer to (if) according to Al-Mubarrad is omitted, the meaning being: whatever it is, “Then peace be upon you from the companions of the right,” if he is from the companions of the right, “Then peace be upon you from the companions of the right,” so the answer to the condition was omitted because of the indication of what preceded it, just as the answer was omitted in something like your saying you are unjust if you do, because of the indication of what preceded it. Al-Akhfash is of the view that the fa’ is the answer to (amma) and (in), and the meaning of that is that the fa’ is the answer to (amma) and it has filled the place of the answer to (in) according to the previous estimation, and the fa’ is the answer to them in this way. The meaning of (amma) according to Al-Zajjaj is: to move from one thing to another, i.e. leave what we were in and take up something else.
56:92: God Almighty says: But if he is among those who deny the frivolity and are astray from guidance and the path of truth.
56:93: Then there will come down boiling water meaning they will have a provision of boiling water, as He said: Then indeed, you, O astray deniers, will eat it and as He said: Then indeed, they will have a mixture of boiling water on top of it.
56:94: And a burning in Hellfire means entering into the Fire. It was said: a stay in Hellfire and enduring its various types of torment. It is said: He made him burn in Hellfire and made him burn in it. The verbal noun here is added to the object, just as it is said: someone was given money, meaning he is given money. It was read: (and a burning in Hellfire) with a kasra on the ta', meaning he was sent down from a burning in Hellfire. Then Abu Amr assimilated the ta' into the jim, which is far-fetched.
56:95: Indeed, this is the absolute truth meaning, what we have narrated is the purest and most sincere of certainty. It is permissible to attribute truth to certainty although they are one and the same due to the difference in their wording. Al-Mubarrad said: It is like saying the essence of certainty or pure certainty; it is a case of attributing something to itself according to the Kufians. According to the Basrans, it is the absolute truth of a matter or the certain report. It was also said that it is an emphasis. It was also said that the origin of certainty is to be an attribute of truth, so the described is added to the attribute by extension and metaphor, like His statement: and for the home of the Hereafter. Qatadah said about this verse: "Indeed, God will not leave anyone until He has made him certain of the certainty of this Quran. As for the believer, he has certainty in this world, so that will benefit him on the Day of Resurrection. As for the disbeliever, he has certainty on the Day of Resurrection when certainty will not benefit him."
56:96: So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great, meaning glorify God, the Most High, from evil. The ba is redundant, meaning glorify the name of your Lord, and the name that is named. It was also said: So glorify means begin by mentioning your Lord and His command. It was also said: So mention the name of your Lord, the Most Great, and glorify Him. "On the authority of Uqbah ibn Amir, who said: When "So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great," was revealed, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: (Include it in your bowing), and when "Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High," was revealed, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: (Include it in your prostration)" Narrated by Abu Dawud. And God knows best.
57:1: "On the authority of Al-Arbadh bin Sariyah: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to recite the Tasbihat before going to sleep and would say: 'In them is a verse better than a thousand verses.'" He meant Surat Al-Hadid, Al-Hashr, Al-Saff, Al-Jumu'ah, and Al-Taghabun. God the Almighty says: Whatever is in the heavens and the earth exalts God meaning, glorifies God and declares Him free from evil. Ibn Abbas said: Whatever is in the heavens of those He created from the angels and the earth of anything with a soul or without a soul, has prayed to God. It was also said: It is a glorification of indication. Al-Zajjaj denied this and said: If this were a glorification of indication and the appearance of the effects of creation, it would have been understood. So why did He say: But you do not understand their glorification (Al-Isra’ 17:44)? Rather, it is a glorification of speech. He provided evidence with the words of God the Almighty: And We subjected the mountains to glorify God with David (Al-Anbiya’ 21:79). So if this was a glorification of indication, then what specificity was there for David? I said: What he mentioned is correct, and its explanation and the statement about it have already been mentioned in Subhan in the words of God Almighty: And there is not a thing but glorifies Him with praise (al-Isra’ 17:44) And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
57:2: The Almighty says: To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth meaning He is unique in that. Dominion refers to the possession and the implementation of a command, for He, glory be to Him, is the King, the Able, the Subduer. It was said: He meant the treasuries of rain, plants, and all other sustenance. He gives life and causes death means He causes the living to die in this world and He gives life to the dead for the resurrection. It was said: He gives life to the sperm, which is dead, and He causes the living to die. The position of He gives life and causes death is in the nominative case, meaning He gives life and causes death. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case, meaning To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, giving life and causing death, as a state of the genitive in to Him and the preposition is the agent in it. And He has power over all things meaning nothing is impossible for God.
57:3: The Almighty said: He is the First and the Last, the Evident and the Hidden. There are different meanings of these names, and we have explained them in the book Asna. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, explained them in an explanation that suffices for anyone who says anything. "He said in Sahih Muslim from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah: O God, You are the First, and there is nothing before You, and You are the Last, and there is nothing beyond You. You are the Evident, and there is nothing above You. You are the Hidden, and there is nothing beneath You. Pay off our debt and enrich us from poverty." The Most Prevailing is apparent, and the Hidden is the All-Knowing, and God knows best. And He is All-Knowing of all things of what was or will be, and nothing is hidden from Him.
57:4: The Almighty says: He knows what goes into the earth meaning what enters it of rain and other things and what comes out of it of plants and other things and what comes down from the sky of provision, rain, and angels and what ascends therein of angels and the deeds of the servants And He is with you meaning with His power, authority, and knowledge “wherever you are. And God is Seeing of what you do” He sees your deeds and observes them, and nothing of them is hidden from Him. In this verse, He combines He rose over the Throne with And He is with you. Accepting the apparent meanings of both is a contradiction, so it indicates that interpretation is necessary, and ignoring interpretation is an admission of contradiction. Imam Abu al-Ma’ali said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the Night Journey was not closer to God Almighty than Jonah, son of Matta, when he was in the belly of the whale. This has been mentioned previously.
57:5: The Almighty says: To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. This repetition is for emphasis, meaning He is the true worshipper. And to God all matters will return, meaning the matters of creation in the Hereafter. Al-Hasan, Al-A’raj, Ya’qub, Ibn ‘Amir, Abu Haywah, Ibn Muhaisin, Hamid, Al-A’mash, Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, and Khalaf read it with a fat-ha on the ta’ and a kasra on the jim. The rest read it with a fat-ha on the jim.
57:6: The Almighty’s saying, He merges the night into the day and merges the day into the night was mentioned in Al Imran. And He is Knowing of that within the breasts meaning, nothing is hidden from Him, and whoever has this characteristic, it is not permissible to worship anyone other than Him.
57:7: The Almighty's saying: Believe in God and His Messenger meaning, believe that God is One and that Muhammad is His Messenger. And spend give charity. It was also said that they spent in the way of God. It was also said that what is meant is the obligatory zakat. It was also said that what is meant is other forms of obedience and what is close to it. Of that over which He has made you successors is evidence that the origin of the kingdom belongs to God, the Most High, and that the servant has no power except to dispose of it in a way that pleases God, for which He will reward him with Paradise. So whoever spends from it in the rights of God and finds it easy to spend from it, just as it is easy for a man to spend from someone else's money if he is given permission to do so, then he will have a great reward and a tremendous recompense. Al-Hasan said: Successors over it by inheriting it from those who were before you. This indicates that it is not your money in reality, and you are only in it as representatives and trustees, so seize the opportunity to establish the truth before it is removed from you to those after you. Those of you who have believed and done righteous deeds and spent in the cause of God will have a great reward, which is Paradise.
57:8: The Almighty's saying: And what is the matter with you that you do not believe in God? is a question that is intended as a rebuke. That is, what excuse do you have for not believing when all the causes have been removed?! And the Messenger invites you This shows that there is no judgment before the revelation of the Shari'ah. Abu Omar read: And He has taken your covenant without the name of the subject. The rest read it with the name of the subject, that is, God took your covenant. Mujahid said: It is the first covenant that was while they were in the back of Adam that God is your Lord, you have no god but Him. It was also said: He took your covenant by implanting in you minds and establishing for you the proofs and arguments that call to following the Messenger. If you are believers means if you are. It was also said: If you are believers in the arguments and evidence. It was also said: If you are believers in the truth of a certain day, then now is the last time for you to believe due to the establishment of the arguments and signs with the mission of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for his proofs have been proven. It was said: If you believe in God, your Creator. And they were known for this. And it was said: This is addressed to a people who believed and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took their covenant, but they apostatized. And His statement: If you are believers means if you acknowledge the conditions of belief.
57:9: The Almighty says: It is He who sends down to His Servant clear verses meaning the Qur’an. It was also said: the miracles, that you must believe in Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, because of the miracles he has, and the Qur’an is the greatest and most important of them. That He may bring you out meaning with the Qur’an. It was also said: with the Messenger. It was also said: with the call. From darkness meaning polytheism and disbelief to the light meaning faith. And indeed, God is to you Kind and Merciful.
57:10: It contains five issues: First: The Almighty’s statement: And what is [the matter] with you that you do not spend in the cause of God? Meaning: What is preventing you from spending in the cause of God and in that which brings you closer to your Lord, while you die and leave behind your wealth which will go to God? So the meaning of this statement is a rebuke for not spending. And to God belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth. Meaning: They will return to Him upon the passing of those in them, just as an inheritance returns to its rightful owner. Second: The Almighty’s statement: Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought. Most commentators agree that what is meant by conquest is the conquest of Mecca. Al-Sha’bi and Al-Zuhri said: The conquest of Al-Hudaybiyyah. Qatada said: There were two fights, one better than the other, and two expenditures, one better than the other. Fighting and spending before the conquest of Mecca were better than fighting and spending after that. And in the statement there is an omission, meaning Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought and those who spent and fought after the conquest. So it was omitted because the statement indicates it. Spending before the conquest was greater because people’s need was greater due to the weakness of Islam, and doing that was more difficult for the spenders at that time, and the reward was commensurate with the effort. And God knows best. Third: Ashhab narrated on the authority of Malik who said: The people of virtue and determination should be given precedence, and God the Almighty said: Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought. Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed about Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, so it is clear evidence of the distinction between Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, and the precedence, because he was the first to convert to Islam. And on the authority of Ibn Masoud: The first to display Islam with his sword were the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr, because he was the first to spend on the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And on the authority of Ibn Umar he said: “I was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr was with him, and he was wearing a cloak that he had tucked around his chest with a hook. Gabriel came down and said, ‘O Prophet of God! Why do I see Abu Bakr wearing a cloak that he has tucked around his chest with a hook?’ He said, ‘He spent his money on me before the conquest.’ He said, ‘God says to you, convey my greetings to Abu Bakr and say to him, ‘Are you satisfied in this poverty of yours or are you dissatisfied?’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘O Abu Bakr, God, the Mighty and Sublime, conveys his greetings to you and says, ‘Are you satisfied in this poverty of yours or are you dissatisfied?’ Abu Bakr said, ‘Would I be dissatisfied with my Lord? I am satisfied with my Lord! I am satisfied with my Lord! I am satisfied with my Lord!’ He said, ‘God says to you, I am satisfied with you as you are satisfied with Me.’ Abu Bakr wept. Gabriel, peace be upon him, said, ‘By Him who sent you, O Muhammad, with the truth, the bearers of the Throne have been tucked around with cloaks since your companion tucked around with his cloak.’ For this reason, the Companions put him before themselves and acknowledged his precedence and leadership. Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) preceded Abu Bakr in prayer, and I prayed a third of Umar’s life. Whenever a man comes to me who prefers me over Abu Bakr, I flog him with the punishment of a slanderer, eighty lashes, and he rejects his testimony. Those who came before them endured more hardship than those who came after them, and their insight was also more penetrating. Fourth: Progress and backwardness may be in worldly rulings, but in religious rulings, Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded us to treat people with the highest status. “The highest status is prayer.” And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said during his illness: They told Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer. He said: The one who leads the people in prayer is the one who knows the Book of God best. He said: And let the older of you lead you in prayer. This is from the hadith of Malik ibn al-Huwayrith, which was mentioned earlier. Al-Bukhari and some scholars understood from it that he meant older status, and as the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Loyalty is due to older age. He did not mean older age. Malik and others said: Age has a right. Al-Shafi’i and Abu Hanifa took this into consideration, and it is more deserving of consideration, because if knowledge and age are combined in two good things, knowledge takes precedence. As for the rulings of this world, they are based on the rulings of religion. So whoever takes precedence in religion takes precedence in this world. And in the narrations: He is not one of us who does not respect our elders, protect our young, and acknowledge the rights of our scholars. Among the authentic hadiths about individuals is: If a young man honors an old man because of his age, God will provide for him someone who will honor him when he grows old. And they chanted Oh, you who criticize the elderly, who acted wickedly in their youth and were extravagant. Mention, if you wish, your grandfather, and mention your father, my nephew. Know that youth is leaving you and its burden is not lost He who does not respect the elderly will never be overtaken by the age of old age. Fifth: Say to Him, the Most High: And to both God has promised the best. That is, the ones who came before, the ones who preceded, and the ones who came after, the ones who came after. God has promised them all Paradise with varying degrees. Ibn Amir read and both in the nominative case, and it is also in the nominative case in the copies of the Sham’an. The rest read and both in the accusative case as is in their copies of the Qur’an. So whoever puts it in the accusative case, it is because the verb has been applied to both, meaning God has promised the best. And whoever puts it in the nominative case, it is because when the object comes before the verb, its function is weakened, and the ha’ is omitted from promise.
57:11: The Almighty's saying: Who is it that would loan God a goodly loan? is an encouragement to spend in the way of God. This has already been discussed in Surat Al-Baqarah. The Arabs say about anyone who does a good deed: he has loaned, as He said: If you give a loan, give it back, for only God can give it back. A boy is not a camel It is called a loan because the loan is given for the purpose of recovering something in return. That is, who is he that spends in the way of God that God should replace it with many times over? Al-Kalbi said: A loan means a good charity, that is, one that is accepted as a reward from him, without any favor or harm. He will multiply it for him between seven and seven hundred times as much as God wills. It was said: A good loan is to say: Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is Greatest. Narrated by Sufyan from Ibn Hayyan. Zayd ibn Aslam said: It is spending on one’s family. Good is voluntary worship. It was said: It is a good deed. The Arabs say: I have with so-and-so a loan of truth and a loan of evil. Al-Qushayri said: A good loan is for the one who gives charity to be sincere in intention and of good character, seeking thereby the face of God without showing off or seeking reputation, and for it to be lawful. And from the good loan is not to aim for the bad one and spend it, because God the Almighty says: And do not aim towards the bad thereof, spending [in charity] (Al-Baqarah 2:267), and to give charity while hoping to live, “because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asked about the best charity, and he said: ‘That you give it while you are healthy and stingy, hoping to live, and do not delay until it reaches your collarbones and you say to so-and-so such-and-such, and to so-and-so such-and-such.’” And to conceal one’s charity, because God the Almighty says: But if you conceal it and give it to the poor, it is better for you (Al-Baqarah 2:271), and not to show off, because God the Almighty says: Do not invalidate your charities by reminders or injury (Al-Baqarah 2:264), and to belittle much of what one gives, because the whole world is little, and to make it from the most beloved of his wealth, because God the Almighty says: By no means will you attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love (Al-Imran 3:92), and to make it abundant, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The best of slaves are those with the highest price and the most precious to their families. He will multiply it for him. Ibn Kathir and Ibn Amir read He will multiply it for him by dropping the alif, except for Ibn Amir and Ya'qub, who put the fa' in the accusative case. Nafi' and the people of Kufa and Basra read He will multiply it for him by the alif and softening the 'ayn, except for Asim, who put the fa' in the accusative case. The rest raised it in apposition to He lends. The accusative case is an answer to the question. This has been discussed in detail in al-Baqarah 2:And for him is a noble reward meaning Paradise.
57:12: The Almighty said: {On the Day you see the believing men and believing women} who work on a Day {and will have a noble reward} and there is an omission in the speech, meaning {and will have a noble reward} and on the {Day you see} therein the {believing men and believing women, their light will run} i.e. it will go on the Sirat according to Al-Hasan, and it is the light that they will pass through {before them} i.e. in front of them. {And on their right} Al-Farra’ said: The preposition ba has the meaning of in, i.e. in their right. Or it has the meaning of about, i.e. about their right. Ad-Dahhak said: Their light is its destroyer, and on their right is their books, and At-Tabari chose this. i.e. their faith and righteous deeds will run before them, and on their right are the books of their deeds. So the preposition ba in this case has the meaning of in. And it is permissible on this basis to stop at before them and not stop if it has the meaning of about. Suhayl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi and Abu Haywah read it with a kasra on the alif, meaning faith, which is the opposite of disbelief. He connected a non-adverbial phrase to a noun phrase because the meaning of an adverbial phrase is a state of affairs and it is connected to something omitted. The meaning is that he strives, being in front of them or on their right, and the phrase in front of them is not connected to the word strives itself. It was said that he meant the Qur'an by the light. Ibn Mas'ud said: They will be given their light according to their deeds. Some of them will be given their light like a palm tree, and some of them will be given their light like a standing man, and the light of the one who has the shortest span of his foot will be on his big toe, so it will be extinguished at one time and ignited at another. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Among the believers will be those whose light will shine like the distance between Madinah and Aden, or between Madinah and Sana'a, or even less than that, until there will be those whose light will not shine except where their feet are. Al-Hasan said: So that they may be illuminated by it on the Sirat, as mentioned above. Muqatil said: To be a guide for them to Paradise. And God knows best. God the Almighty says: Good tidings to you today are gardens beneath which rivers flow. The meaning is, it will be said to them: Good tidings to you today is entering gardens. The omission of the complement is necessary because the good tidings have already occurred, and Paradise is a spring, so it cannot be the same. Beneath them flow rivers of milk, water, wine, and honey beneath their dwellings. Abiding therein is a state of the omitted entry. The meaning is, Good tidings to you today is entering gardens beneath which rivers flow. Abiding therein is understood, and it is not a state of your good tidings, because there is a separation between the relative clause and the relative pronoun. It is possible that it is among what the good tidings indicate, as if he said, You are given good tidings of abiding. It is possible that the adverbial phrase, which is today, is a predicate of your good tidings, gardens, instead of the good tidings, based on the omission of the complement, as previously mentioned. Abiding therein is a state, based on what previously mentioned. Al-Farra’ permitted the accusative case of gardens as a state, based on today being a predicate of your good tidings, which is unlikely, because gardens does not have the meaning of a verb. He allowed that your good report be in the accusative case, meaning that they give them good report, and that gardens be in the accusative case with the good report, and in this there is a distinction between the relative clause and the relative pronoun.
57:13: The Almighty said, On the Day the hypocrites will say, the agent in the Day, That is the great triumph. It was said: It is a substitute for the first day. Wait for us, we will learn. The general reading is by connecting the alif with a damma on the dhaal from nazeer, and waiting is waiting, meaning wait for us. Al-A'mash, Hamzah, and Yahya bin Waththab read Anzuruna with a severing of the alif and a kasra on the dhaal from inzaar. That is, give us time and delay us. Anzarahtu means I delayed him, and istazaartu means I asked him to wait. Al-Farra' said: The Arabs say: Give me time, I wait for me. And he recited for Amr bin Kulthum: Abu Hind, do not rush us and wait for us to tell you for sure. That is, we waited. We draw from your light meaning we are illuminated by your light. Ibn Abbas and Abu Umamah said: “On the Day of Resurrection, people will be covered in darkness - Al-Mawardi said: I think it will be after the judgment has been passed - then they will be given a light in which they will walk.” The commentators said: “God will give the believers a light on the Day of Resurrection according to their deeds by which they will walk on the path, and He will also give the hypocrites a light to deceive them, as evidenced by the statement of God the Almighty: ‘And it is He who will deceive them’” An-Nisa’ 4:142. It was said that they are only given the light because all of them are people of the call, except for the disbeliever. Then the hypocrite will have his light taken away because of his hypocrisy, as Ibn Abbas said. Abu Umamah said: The believer will be given the light and the disbeliever and the hypocrites will be left without light. Al-Kalbi said: “Rather, the hypocrites seek light from the light of the believers, but they are not given light. So while they are walking, God sends among them a wind and darkness, thereby extinguishing the light of the hypocrites. This is what God the Almighty says: {Our Lord, perfect for us our light} (At-Tahrim 66:8). The believers say this, fearing that it will be taken away from them as the hypocrites took it away. So when the hypocrites remain in the darkness, unable to see where they set foot, they say to the believers: “Wait for us, that we may borrow from your light.” Your light was said: Go back means the angels said to them: Go back. It was also said: Rather, it is the believers saying to them: Go back behind you to the place from which we took the light, and seek light for yourselves there, for you will not be able to borrow from our light. So when they returned and were isolated in seeking light, A wall was placed between them. It was also said: Why did you not seek light from this world by believing? By a wall means a wall; the by is a connecting link. Al-Kisa’i said: A wall is a barrier between Paradise and Hell. It was narrated that this wall is in Jerusalem at a place called the Gate of Mercy. Abdullah ibn Amr said: It is the eastern wall of Jerusalem, its interior contains the mosque, and its exterior is the torment, meaning Hell. Ibn Abbas narrated something similar. Ziyad ibn Abi Sawada said: Ubadah ibn as-Samit stood on the eastern wall of Jerusalem and cried and said: From here the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) told us that he saw Hell. Qatada said: It is a wall between Paradise and Hell. Its interior contains mercy, meaning Paradise, and its exterior is the torment, meaning Hell. Mujahid said: It is a veil, as in Al-A’raf, and we have already discussed this. It has also been said that the mercy inside it is the light of the believers, and the torment outside it is the darkness of the hypocrites.
57:14: God the Almighty says: They will call out to them, meaning the hypocrites will call out to the believers, Were we not with you? in this world, meaning we prayed as you pray, fought as you fight, and did we do as you do? They will say, Yes, meaning the believers will say, Yes, you were with us outwardly, but you tempted yourselves, meaning you used yourselves for temptation. Mujahid said, You destroyed yourselves with hypocrisy. It was also said, With sins, as Abu Sinan said. It was also said, With desires and pleasures, as Abu Numayr al-Hamadani narrated. And you waited and doubted, meaning, And you waited for death for the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and for the believers to go through misfortune. It was also said, And you waited for repentance, and you doubted, meaning you doubted the Divine Unity and Prophethood, and the wishful thinking deceived you, meaning falsehoods. It was also said, Long hope. It was also said, It was what they hoped for from the weakness of the believers and the misfortunes that would befall them. Qatada said: Wishes here are the devil’s deceptions. It was also said: the world, as Abdullah ibn Abbas said. Abu Sinan said: It is their saying that he seeks forgiveness for us. Bilal ibn Sa'd said: "Your remembrance brings good things and your forgetting brings bad things to you. It is a deception." Until the command of God comes meaning death. It was also said: the victory of His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Qatada said: their being thrown into the fire. And the Deceiver deceived you meaning he tricked you with God meaning Satan, said by Ikrimah. It was also said: the world, said by Ad-Dahhak. Some scholars said: The eternal is considered by the past, and the end is deterred by the first, and the happy one is he who is not deceived by greed, and does not rely on deception. Whoever remembers fate forgets his wishes, and whoever prolongs hope, his deeds become bad, and he is heedless of the appointed time. The word al-Ghurur is used in the exaggerated form for abundance. Abu Haywah, Muhammad ibn As-Samiq' and Simak ibn Harb read al-Ghurur with a damma on the ghayn, meaning falsehoods, and it is a verbal noun. On the authority of Ibn Abbas: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, drew lines for us, and drew a line from them to one side and said: Do you know what this is? This is a parable of the son of Adam and a parable of wishing, and those lines are hopes while he wishes when death comes to him. And on the authority of Ibn Masoud, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, drew a square line for us, and drew a line in the middle of it and made it extend from it, and drew small lines to its right and left, and said: This is the son of Adam, and this is his appointed time surrounding him, and this is his hope that has passed his appointed time, and these small lines are the accidents. If one of them errs, this one will crush him, and if this one misses, this one will bite him.
57:15: God the Almighty says: So today no ransom will be taken from you O hypocrites nor from those who disbelieved "Have they despaired of salvation. The common reading is yu'akhudhu" with a ya', because the feminine is not real, and because a separation has been made between them and the verb. Ibn 'Amir and Ya'qub read "yu'akhudhu" with a ta', and Abu Hatim chose it to indicate the feminization of the ransom. The first is the choice of Abu 'Ubayd, meaning no substitute or compensation will be accepted from you, nor from another soul. "Your refuge is the Fire" meaning your place and abode. "It is your Master" meaning more deserving of you, and a master is someone who looks after a person's interests. Then it was used to refer to someone who is constantly involved in something. It was said: meaning the Fire controls their affairs, meaning that God the Blessed and Exalted creates life and reason in it, so it is distinguished by wrath against the disbelievers. For this reason, it is followed in God's saying: "The Day We will say to Hell, 'Are you filled?' and it will say, 'Are there any more?'" (Qaf: 30). "And evil is the destination." It is a bad reference and destination.
57:16: God Almighty says: Has not the time come for those who believe? That is, it is approaching and coming. The poet said: Isn't it time, O heart, for me to leave ignorance and for the gray hair that is evident to us to bring about reason? Its past tense is ani in al-Qasi. It is said: It is time for you - with a long vowel - that he did such-and-such. It is time for us, like ani lak which is a reversed form of it. Ibn al-Sikkit recited: Is it not time for my blindness to be revealed and for me to fall short of Layla? Yes, it is time for me So he combined the two languages, and Al-Hasan read al-ma yan the groaning sound, and its root is alam the pain, and ma was added, so it is a negation of the speaker’s saying: It was such and such, and lam is a negation of his saying: It was such and such. And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, he said: There was only four years between our conversion to Islam and when God rebuked us with this verse, Has not the time come for those who have believed that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of God? Al-Khalil said: Rebuke means addressing someone with arrogance and reminding them of their grudges. You say, I rebuked him “that their hearts should become humbly submissive” means that they should be humble and soften at the remembrance of God and what has come down of the truth. It was narrated that joking and laughter increased among the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) when they lived in luxury in Madinah, so the verse was revealed. And when this verse was revealed, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: God is impatient for you to be humble. Then they said: We are humble. Ibn Abbas said: “God felt the hearts of the believers were slow to respond, so He rebuked them thirteen years after the revelation of the Qur’an. It was said that it was revealed about the hypocrites one year after the Hijra. This is because they asked Solomon to tell them about the wonders of the Torah, so the following verse was revealed: ‘Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the clear Book’ (Yusuf 12:1) until His saying: ‘We relate to you the best of stories’ (Yusuf 12:3). So he informed them that this story was better than others and more beneficial for them, so they stopped talking to Solomon. Then they asked him like the first, so the following verse was revealed: ‘Has not the time come for those who have believed that their hearts should humble themselves at the remembrance of God and what has come down of the truth?’” (Yusuf 12:3). According to this interpretation, those who believed openly spoke with their tongues. Al-Suddi and others said: ‘Has not the time come for those who have believed’ - both outwardly and secretly - ‘that their hearts should humble themselves at the remembrance of God?’ It was said that it was revealed about the believers. Sa’d said: It was said, ‘O Messenger of God, why don’t you tell us stories?’ So the following verse was revealed: ‘We relate to you’ (Yusuf 12:3). So they said after that… Time: If you had told us, then this verse was revealed: God has sent down the best statement (al-Zumar 39:23). They said after a while: If you had reminded us. So God revealed: Has not the time come for those who have believed that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of God and what has come down of the truth? And something similar was narrated by Al-Nawawi, Masoud, who said: There were only four years between our conversion to Islam and when we were reprimanded with this verse. So some of us would look at one another and say: What have we innovated? Al-Hasan said: He was the slowest of them, and they were the most beloved of his creation to him. It was said: This address was to those who believed in Moses and Jesus, not Muhammad, peace be upon him, because after this he said: And those who have believed in God and His messengers, meaning: Has not the time come for those who believed in the Torah and the Gospel for their hearts to soften toward the Qur’an, and for them not to be like those who came before Moses and Jesus, when a long period passed between them and their prophet and their hearts hardened. God the Almighty said: And do not be meaning and that they are not, so it is accusative in apposition to that you humble yourself. It was said: It is apocopated as a prohibition, its meaning is and do not be. The evidence for this interpretation is the narration of Rawis on the authority of Ya’qub: Do not be with the letter ta’, which is the reading of Isa and Ibn Ishaq. He says: Do not follow the path of the Jews and the Ansar. They were given the Torah and the Gospel, but time passed them by. Ibn Mas’ud said: When time passed for the Children of Israel, their hearts hardened, so they invented a book from themselves which they considered permissible, and the truth stood between them and many of their desires, until they threw the Book of God behind their backs as if they did not know. Then they said: Present this book to the Children of Israel, and if they follow you, then leave them, but if they do not follow you, then kill them. Then they agreed to send him to one of their scholars, and they said: If he follows us, no one will oppose us, and if he refuses, we will kill him, and no one will oppose us after him. So they sent for him, and he wrote the Book of God on a piece of paper, put it back in a horn, and hung it around his neck. Then he put on his clothes and came to them, and they showed them their book and said: Do you believe in this? He struck his chest with his hand and said: I believe in this, meaning the one hung on his chest. So the Children of Israel split into seventy-two sects, and the best of their sects were the companions of Dhul-Qarn. Abdullah said: And whoever among you lives will see an evil, and it is enough for one of you, when he sees an evil and is unable to change it, that God knows in his heart that he hates it. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: He means the believers among the People of the Book, for whom time was long and they were impatient for the coming of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). So their hearts hardened, and many of them are wicked. He also meant those who innovated monasticism and the monastic dwellers. It was also said: The learned man is the one who does not know what he is practicing among the scholars and opposes those who do know. It was said: They are those who do not believe in the knowledge of God Almighty. A group of them remained steadfast in the religion of Jesus until the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was sent, and they believed in him. A group of them turned away from the religion of Jesus, and they are the ones whom God declared corrupt. Muhammad bin Kaab said: The Companions were in Mecca during a drought, but when they migrated, they found comfort and luxury, so they stopped doing what they were doing, and their hearts hardened. God admonished them, and they regained consciousness. Ibn al-Mubarak said: Malik bin Anas told us: It reached me that Jesus (peace be upon him) said to his al-Nas 114:Do not speak too much without mentioning God Almighty, lest your hearts harden. The hard heart is far from God, but you do not know. Do not look at the sins of people as if they were masters, but look at them - or he said at your sins - as if you were slaves, for people are of two types: the healthy and the afflicted, so have mercy on the afflicted, and thank God for the well-being. This verse, Has not the time come for those who have believed that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of God? was the reason for the repentance of Al-Fadl ibn Ayyad and Ibn Al-Mubarak, may God have mercy on them both: as Abu Al-Mutraf Abdul-Rahman ibn Marwan Al-Qalanisi said: Abu Muhammad Al-Hasan ibn Rasheeq told us, and he said: Ali ibn Ya’qub Al-Zayyat told us, he said: Ibrahim ibn Hisham told us, he said: Zakariya ibn Abi Abaan told us, he said: Al-Layth ibn Al-Harith told us, he said: Al-Hasan ibn Daher told us, he said: Abdullah ibn Al-Mubarak was asked about the beginning of his asceticism, he said: I was one day with my brothers in an orchard of ours, and that was when the fruits of various kinds were bearing fruit, so we ate and drank until nightfall and then slept, and I was fond of playing the oud and the tambourine, so I got up during some of the night and played a sound called Rasheen Al-Sahar, and he meant Sinan Singing, and a bird was hoot above my head on a tree, and the oud in my hand was not answering me as I wanted, and then it spoke as a human speaks - meaning the oud in his hand - and said: Has not the time come for those who have believed that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of God and what has come down of the truth? I said: Yes, by God! And the oud broke, and I sent away those who were with me, and this was the beginning of my asceticism and my turning back. We were told about the poem that Ibn al-Mubarak wanted to play on the oud: Isn't it time for you to have mercy and disobey the critics and blamers? I mourn for a young man who is infatuated with you and mourns your absence. He spends the night observing the planets and stars. What would happen to the gazelle if it made permissible what was forbidden to be joined? As for Ad-Dhayl ibn Ayyad, the reason for their repentance was that he fell in love with a neighbor, so she made a date with him at night. While he was climbing the wall to meet her, he heard a reciter reciting: Has not the time come for those who have believed that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of God? So he retreated saying: Yes, by God, the time has come! Then the night took him to a ruined area in which there was a group of passersby, some of them saying to one another: Hey, Fudayl is blocking the road! Al-Fudayl said: Oh! I see myself at night striving to disobey God, while some Muslims fear me! O God, I have repented to You, and I have made my repentance to You the neighboring of Your Sacred House.
57:17: The Almighty said: Know that God revives the earth after its death meaning, He revives the barren land after its death with rain. Salih Al-Mari Al-Ani said: He softens the hearts after their hardness. Ja'far bin Muhammad said: He revives them with justice after injustice. It was also said: The meaning is: Likewise, He revives the disbeliever with guidance to faith after his death in disbelief and misguidance. It was also said: Likewise, God revives the dead among the nations, and distinguishes between the one whose heart is humble and the one whose heart is hard. We have made clear to you the signs that you may understand meaning, God's revival of the earth after its death is evidence of God's power, and that He is the One Who revives the dead.
57:18: God the Almighty says: Indeed, the men and women who give charity Ibn Kathir and Abu Bakr read it on the authority of Asim with a soft sad in both of them from believing in what God the Almighty has revealed. The rest read it with a shaddah, meaning the men and women who give charity, so the a was assimilated into the sad, and this is also in the copy of Abu. It is on the charity, and that is why he said: And loan God a goodly loan, and charity and spending in the way of God. Al-Hasan said: Everything in the Qur'an about a goodly loan is voluntary. It was said: It is a righteous deed, such as charity and other deeds done sincerely and for the sake of God. The verb was conjoined with the noun because the noun is in confirmation of the verb, meaning that those who give charity and borrow, will have their reward multiplied for them the like thereof. The general reading is with a fathah on the ayn for what the agent is not named. Al-A'mash read yadhi'afuhu with a kasrah on the ayn and added a ha. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, and Ya'qub read yadhi'afu with a fathah on the ayn and a shaddah on it. And they will have a generous reward meaning Paradise.
57:19: God Almighty says: “And those who believe in God and His messengers - those are the truthful and the martyrs with their Lord. They will have their reward and their light.” There is a difference of opinion about and the martyrs as to whether it is separated from what came before it or connected to it. Mujahid and Zaid bin Aslam said: The martyrs and the truthful are the believers, and it is connected. Its meaning was narrated from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, so we do not stop at this with his saying: the truthful. This is the saying of Ibn Masoud in interpreting the verse. Al-Qushayri said: God the Most High said: Then those will be with those upon whom God has bestowed favor of the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous. The truthful are the prophets, and the martyrs are those who follow the truthful, and the righteous follow the martyrs. It is possible that this verse is about those who believed in the messengers, I mean: And those who believed in God and His messengers - those are the truthful and the martyrs. The meaning of the martyrs is those who testified to God’s Oneness, so a truthful person is above a truthful person in degrees, as the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: The people of the highest gardens will be seen by those below them as one of you sees a star in the horizon of the sky, and Abu Bakr and Umar are among them, and they were blessed. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas and Masruq that the martyrs are not the truthful. So the martyrs in this case are separate from what preceded it, and stopping at His statement: the truthful ones is good. The meaning is and the martyrs are with their Lord; they will have their reward and their light meaning they will have their own reward and their own light. There are two opinions about them: One of them is that they are the messengers who will testify against their nations regarding their belief and disbelief. This was said by Al-Kalbi, and his evidence is the statement of God the Almighty: And We have brought you, [O Muhammad], as a witness over these (An-Nisa’: 41). The second is that they are the nations of the messengers who will testify on the Day of Resurrection. There are two opinions about what they will testify to: One of them is that they will testify against themselves regarding what they did of obedience and disobedience. This is the meaning of the statement of Mujahid. The second is that they will testify for their prophets regarding their conveying the message to their nations. Al-Kabbi said: Muqatil said a third opinion: that they are those killed in the cause of God the Almighty. A similar statement was narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said that he meant the martyrs of the believers. The and is the and of initiation. According to this opinion, the truthful ones are separated from the martyrs. There is a difference of opinion about identifying them. Ad-Dahhak said that they were eight men: Abu Bakr, Ali, Zaid, Uthman, Talhah, Az-Zubayr, Saad, and Hamza. Umar ibn Al-Khattab may God be pleased with them followed them, and God included him among them because he confirmed the truth of his Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: The truthful ones are those who believed in the Messenger and did not deny him for an instant, such as the believer from the family of Pharaoh, the companion of the family of Yasin, Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, and the People of the Trench. God Almighty says: And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs Where are the messengers and miracles? Those are the companions of Hellfire So they will have no reward or light.
57:20: The Almighty’s saying: Know that the life of this world is only play and amusement. The connection is that a person may abandon jihad for fear of being killed, and for fear of inevitable death. So He made it clear that the life of this world is fleeting, so God’s command should not be to preserve what does not last. What is the connection between His estimation: Know that the life of this world is only vain play and joyful amusement, then it will end? Qatada said: Play and amusement means eating and drinking. It was said that it is as is known from its name. Mujahid said: All play is amusement. This meaning has already been mentioned in Al-An’am. It was said: Play is what brings desire for this world, and amusement is what distracts from the Hereafter, i.e., occupies oneself from it. It was also said: Play is acquisition, and amusement is women. Adornment is what one adorns oneself with. The disbeliever adorns himself with this world and does not work for the Hereafter, and the same is true for those who adorn themselves in disobedience to God. And boast among yourselves means that some of you boast to others about it. It was also said: about creation and strength. It was also said: about lineage, as was the custom of the Arabs in boasting about their fathers. In Sahih Muslim, it was narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: God revealed to me that you should be humble so that no one transgresses against another or boasts over another. It was also authentically narrated that he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Four things in my ummah are from the matters of the Jahiliyyah: boasting about lineage,” the hadith. All of this has been mentioned previously. And increasing in wealth and children, because the custom of the Jahiliyyah was to increase in children and wealth, and the believers increased in faith and obedience. Some of the later scholars said: Playing like children’s games, having fun like young men’s games, adornment like women’s adornment, boasting like one’s peers, and multiplying like a farmer’s multiplying. It was said: The meaning is that the world is like these things in its transience and passing away. On the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him, he said to Ammar: Do not grieve over the world, for the world is six things: food, drink, clothing, smelling, riding, and fornication. The best of its food is honey, which is the spit of a fly. The most common of its drink is water, and all animals are equal in it. The best of its clothing is brocade, which is woven from a worm. The best of its smelling is musk, which is the blood of a mouse. The best of its riding is the horse, and men are killed on it. As for fornication, it is women, which is a mount. By God, you see the most beautiful of women, meaning the ugliest of them. Then God gave an example of a crop in a downpour, saying: Like a downpour meaning rain, The growth of which pleases the disbelievers. The disbelievers here are the farmers because they cover the seeds. The meaning is that the life of this world is like a crop, its greenery pleases those who look at it because of the abundance of rain, but it soon becomes dry, as if it had never existed. When the farmers are pleased, then it is the ultimate in what is desirable. The meaning of this parable has already been mentioned in Yunus and the Cave. It has been said that the disbelievers here are the disbelievers in God, the Almighty, because they are more impressed by the adornments of this world than the believers. This is a good statement, because the root of admiration is for them and among them, and it is evident from them, which is the glorification of this world and what is in it. And among the monotheists, there are branches of this that arise from their desires, and they become diminished and insignificant when they remember the Hereafter. The position of the kaf is in the nominative case as an adjective. Then it becomes violent means that it dries up after its greenness, then you see it yellow meaning changed from its previous freshness. Then it becomes debris meaning crumbs and straw, and its beauty is gone after it has been adorned. This is also the case with the disbeliever. And in the Hereafter is a severe punishment meaning for the disbelievers. It is good to pause on this, and begin with and forgiveness from God and approval meaning for the believers. Al-Farra' said: And in the Hereafter is severe punishment and forgiveness. Its meaning is either severe punishment or forgiveness, so do not stop at severe. And the life of this world is only the enjoyment of delusion. This is an emphasis on what came before, meaning it deceives the disbelievers, but as for the believer, this world is his enjoyment of transport to Paradise. It was said: Working for this worldly life is the enjoyment of delusion, as a way to discourage working for this world and to encourage working for the Hereafter.
57:21: The Almighty said: Race one another to forgiveness from your Lord. That is, hasten to do righteous deeds that will bring about forgiveness from your Lord. It was said: Hasten to repent, because it leads to forgiveness. This was said by Al-Kalbi. It was also said: The first Takbir with the Imam. This was said by Makhul. It was also said: The first summer. And a Garden as wide as the heaven and the earth. If you joined some of them to each other. Al-Hasan said: It means all of the heavens and the earth spread out, each one over the other. It was also said: He means for one man, that is, for each one a Garden of this vastness. Ibn Kaysan said: He meant by it one Garden from the Gardens. Width is derived from length, and it is the custom of the Arabs to express the vastness of something by its width rather than its length. He said: As if the lands of God are wide and wide for the fearful and wanted, like a heavy load. All of this has already been mentioned in Al Imran. Tariq bin Shihab said that some people from Al Hirah said to Omar may God be pleased with him: “Have you seen the statement of God the Almighty: “And a Paradise whose width is like the width of the heaven and the earth”? So where is Hell? Omar said to them: Have you seen the night when it has passed and the day comes? Where is the night? They said: You have taken something similar to what is in the Torah. “Prepared for those who believe in God and His messengers” is only a condition of faith, and it strengthens hope. It has been said that the condition of faith here is added to it in Al Imran, saying: Prepared for the righteous * Who spend during ease and hardship and who restrain anger and pardon the people “That is the bounty of God which He bestows on whom He wills” meaning that Paradise cannot be attained or entered except by the mercy and grace of God the Almighty. This has already been mentioned in Al Iraq and other verses. And God is the possessor of great bounty.
57:22: The Almighty says: Whatever disaster strikes upon the earth Muqatil said: drought and scarcity of plants and fruits. It was also said: catastrophes in crops. nor within yourselves with afflictions and diseases, said Qatadah. It was also said: the implementation of the prescribed punishments, said Ibn Hayyan. It was also said: narrowness of livelihood, and this is the meaning narrated by Ibn Jurayj. except in a Book meaning in the Preserved Tablet. before We bring it into being The pronoun in we bring it into being refers to the souls or the earth or the disasters or all of them. Ibn Abbas said: Who was before He created the disaster. Saeed bin Jubair said: before He created the earth and the soul. Indeed, that is easy for God meaning He created that and preserved it all. Easy for God is easy. Al-Rabi' bin Salih said: When Saeed bin Hubayr may God be pleased with him was taken, I cried, so he said: What makes you cry? I said: I cry because of what I see in you and what you are going to. He said: Do not cry, for it was in God’s knowledge that it would happen. Have you not heard the words of God the Almighty: No disaster strikes upon the earth or among yourselves except that it is in a register before We bring it into being (al-Baqarah 2:170). Ibn Abbas said: When God created the pen, He said to it, Write, and it wrote down everything that would happen until the Day of Resurrection. A group of virtuous people left behind this verse as a cure for their illnesses, but they did not use it out of trust in their Lord and reliance on Him. They said, God’s knowledge counts the days of sickness and the days of health. If people had been eager to reduce or increase that, they would not have been able to do so. God the Almighty said: No disaster strikes upon the earth or among yourselves except that it is in a register before We bring it into being (al-Baqarah 2:170). It has been said that this verse is connected to what came before it, which is that God the Almighty is responsible for whatever befalls them in jihad, such as killing and wounding. He explained that what keeps them from jihad, such as preserving wealth and the loss that befalls it, for everything is decreed and cannot be averted. Rather, a person is required to obey the command.
57:23: Then he disciplined them and said this: So that you will not grieve over what has passed you by, meaning so that you will not be sad over what has passed you by of sustenance, and that is because if they knew that sustenance had been lost, they would not grieve over what they had missed of it. And on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: None of you will taste the sweetness of faith until he knows that what has befallen him was not going to miss him and what missed him was not going to befall him. Then he recited, So that you may not grieve over what has escaped you, meaning, so that you may not be sad over what has escaped you of this world, for it was not destined for you, and had it been destined for you, it would not have escaped you. And do not rejoice in what He has given you, meaning of this world, Ibn Abbas said. Sa’d ibn Jubayr said: of well-being and fertility. Ikrimah narrated: meaning of this world. Ibn Abbas said: There is no one who does not grieve, and the two forbidden joys are those in which one goes beyond what is permissible. God the Most High said: And God does not like everyone self-deluded and boastful, meaning, regarding what he has been given of this world, boasting about it to people. The common reading of ataakum with a long alif means, He gave you of this world. Abu Hatim preferred this. Abu Al-Aliyah, Nasr ibn Asim, and Abu Amr read ataakum with a short alif, and Abu Ubaid preferred this meaning, He came to you. It is equivalent to missed you, and that is why he did not say missed you. Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq said: O son of Adam, why do you grieve over something lost that death cannot restore to you, or rejoice over something you have that death cannot leave in your hand? It was said to Buzurgmihr: O wise man! Why do you not grieve over what has passed, and rejoice over what is to come? He said: Because what is lost cannot be made up for by a lesson, and what is to come cannot be sustained by ink. Al-Fudayl ibn Iyadh said in this regard: The world is both destroyer and beneficiary; that which is destroyed has no return, and that which is beneficial heralds departure. It was also said: The arrogant one is the one who looks at himself with an eye of pride, and the boastful one is the one who looks at people with eyes of contempt; both are hidden polytheism. The boastful one is like a milkmaid whose two strings are tied together so that milk can be collected inside them, so the buyer thinks that this is normal, but it is not. Similarly, the one who sees himself in a good state and adornment while pretending to be so, is the boastful one.
57:24: The Almighty says: Those who are miserly meaning He does not like the arrogant. Those who are miserly "Those who are miserly" is in the accusative case as an attribute of the arrogant. It was also said that it is in the nominative case as a predicate of "those who are miserly" so God has protected me from them. It was also said that he meant the Jewish leaders who were miserly in explaining the description of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in their books, lest people believe in him and their livelihood would be lost. This was said by Al-Suddi and Al-Kalbi. Saeed bin Jubair said: "Those who are miserly" means with knowledge. "And enjoin miserliness on people" meaning not to teach people anything. Zayd bin Aslam said: It is miserliness in fulfilling the duty of God the Almighty. It was also said that it is miserliness with charity and rights. This was said by Amir bin Abdullah Al-Ash'ari. Tus said that it is miserliness with what is in one's hands. These three sayings are close in meaning. The scholars differentiated between miserliness and generosity into two categories: One is that which takes pleasure in withholding; and the generous is that which takes pleasure in giving. The second is that the miser is the one who gives when asked, and the generous is the one who gives without being asked. And whoever turns away from faith, then indeed, God has no need of him. It is possible that when He encouraged charity, He informed them that those who are miserly with it and order people to be miserly with it, then indeed, God has no need of them. The common reading is al-Bukhl with a damma on the ba’ and a sukoon on the kha’. Anas, Ubayd ibn Umair, Yahya ibn Ya’mar, Mujahid, Hamid, Ibn Muhaisin, Hamzah, and al-Kisa’i read ab-Khal with two fathahs, which is the dialect of the Ansar. Abu al-Aaliyah and Ibn al-Sumaiqa’ read al-Bukhl with a fatha on the ba’ and a sukoon on the kha’. Nasr ibn Asim reported that al-Bukhl with two dhammahs, and all of these are well-known dialects. The difference between miserliness and stinginess was mentioned at the end of Al-Imran. Nafi` and Ibn `Amir read For God is the Rich, the Praiseworthy without He. The rest read He is the Rich, as a disjunction. It is also permissible for it to be the subject and the Rich to be its predicate, and the sentence to be the predicate of in. Whoever deletes it, it is better for it to be a disjunction, because deleting it is better for it to be a disjunction, because deleting the disjunction is easier than deleting the subject.
57:25: The Almighty says: Indeed, We sent Our messengers with clear proofs, meaning with clear miracles and manifest laws. It was said: sincerity to God Almighty in worship, establishing prayer, and giving zakat. This is what the messengers called for: Noah and those after him to Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him. And We sent down with them the Scripture, meaning the Scriptures, meaning We revealed to them the report of what came before them. And the balance, Ibn Zayd said: It is what is weighed and dealt with, that people may conduct themselves with justice, meaning with fairness in their dealings. His statement, with justice, indicates that he meant the well-known balance. So the meaning is that We sent down the Scripture and set up the balance, so it is from the category of: I fed her straw and cold water. This is indicated by the words of God Almighty: And the heaven He raised and set up the balance (al-Rahman 55:7). Then He said: And establish weight in justice (al-Rahman 55:9). This has already been discussed. And We sent down iron, in which is great force. Umar, may God be pleased with him, narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God sent down four blessings from the sky to the earth: iron, fire, water, and salt.” Ikrimah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Three things came down with Adam, peace be upon him: the Black Stone, which was whiter than snow; the staff of Moses, which was made of myrtle from Paradise, and its length was ten cubits the length of Moses; and iron. Three things came down with him: the anvil, the two hooks, and the miqa’ah, which is the hammer. This was mentioned by Al-Mawardi. Al-Tha’labi said: Ibn Abbas said: Adam came down from Paradise with five iron tools from the blacksmiths: the anvil, the two hooks, the miqa’ah, the hammer, and the needle. Al-Qushayri narrated it, saying: The miqa’ah is what is sharpened with. It is said that the iron fell, meaning it was sharpened. In As-Sahah: The miqa’ah is the place where the falcon lands, the short piece of wood on which it is pounded, the hammer, and the long whetstone. It was narrated that iron was sent down on a Tuesday. In it is great force, meaning to exhaust the blood. Therefore, he forbade cupping and cutting on Tuesdays, because it is a day when blood flows. It was narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: On Tuesday there is an hour when the blood does not stop. It was also said: And We sent down iron, meaning We created it and fashioned it, as God the Almighty said: And He has sent down for you from the grazing livestock eight mates. This is the statement of Al-Hasan. So it is from the earth and not sent down from the sky. The scholars of semantics said: That is, He brought out iron from the minerals and taught them how to make it through His revelation. In it is great might means weapons, legs, and Paradise. It was also said: That is, there is great fear in it from the fear of being killed. And benefits for people. Mujahid said: It means Paradise. It was also said: It means people’s benefit from iron tools, such as knives, axes, needles, and the like. And that God may know who supports Him means He sent down iron to know who supports Him. It was also said that it is an apostrophe for the statement of God, the Most High: That people may uphold justice meaning We sent Our messengers and sent down with them the Book and these things, so that people may deal with truth. And that God may know who supports Him and that God may see who supports His religion and supports. And His messengers unseen Ibn Abbas said: They support them, they do not deny them, and they believe in them unseen, meaning even though they do not see them. Indeed, God is Powerful and Exalted in Might. Powerful in taking, Exalted in Might, meaning impregnable and victorious. It has been mentioned before. It has also been said: in the unseen with sincerity.
57:26: The Almighty says: And We had certainly sent Noah and Abraham. He explained how beautiful it is to send messengers with the Book. He informed us that He sent Noah and Abraham and made prophethood among their offspring. And We placed among their offspring prophethood and the Book. That is, We made some of their offspring prophets, and some of them nations who recite the books sent down from the heaven: the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, and the Criterion. Ibn Abbas said: The Book is written with a pen. And among them that is, those who followed Abraham and Noah, are guided. It was also said: And among them are guided that is, among their offspring are those who are guided. And many of them are wicked that is, disbelievers who have disobeyed God.
57:27: It contains four issues: God the Almighty says: Then We followed up meaning We followed in their footsteps meaning the descendants. It was said: after Noah and Abraham. With Our messengers Moses, Elias, David, Solomon, Jonah, and others. And We followed up with Jesus, the son of Mary so he is from the descendants of Abraham through his mother. And We gave him the Gospel which is the book revealed to him. Its derivation was mentioned previously at the beginning of Surah Al Imran. Second: The Almighty’s statement: And We placed in the hearts of those who followed him in his religion, meaning the disciples and their followers, compassion and mercy, meaning affection, so they would love one another. It was said: This is an indication that they were commanded in the Gospel to make peace and refrain from harming people, and God softened their hearts for that reason, unlike the Jews whose hearts hardened and who distorted words from their proper meanings. Compassion is gentleness, and mercy is compassion. It was said: Compassion is the alleviation of all, and mercy means carrying a burden. It was said: Compassion is the most intense mercy. The statement is complete. Then He said: And monasticism which they innovated, meaning on their own. It is better for monasticism to be in the accusative case with an implied verb. Abu Ali said: And they innovated it as monasticism, they innovated it. Al-Zajjaj said: Meaning, they innovated it as monasticism, just as you say, I saw Zaid and Amr, I spoke. It was said: It is connected to compassion and mercy, and the meaning according to this is that God Almighty gave it to them, but they changed and innovated in it. Al-Mawardi said: There are two readings for it, one of them with a fat-ha on the ra’, which refers to the fear of monasticism. The second is with a damma on the ra’, and it is attributed to the monks, like the Radwaniyyah from Ridwan, because they forced themselves to endure hardships by abstaining from food, drink, and marriage, and clinging to caves and monasteries. This is because their kings changed and altered, and a few remained who became monastic and ascetic. Ad-Dahhak said: Kings after Jesus, peace be upon him, committed forbidden acts for three hundred years, but those who remained on the path of Jesus denounced them, so they killed them. Then some people who remained after them said: If we forbid them, they will kill us, as it is not appropriate for us to remain among them. So they isolated themselves from people and took monasteries. Qatadah said: The monasticism that they innovated is the rejection of women and the taking of monasteries. In a hadith with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, it means their clinging to the wilderness and mountains. We did not prescribe it for them means we did not impose it on them nor did we command them to do it. This was said by Ibn Zayd. And the statement of God, except seeking the pleasure of God means we did not command them except with what pleases God. Ibn Muslim said: Al-Zajjaj said: We did not prescribe it for them means we did not prescribe anything for them at all. Seeking the pleasure of God can be used as a substitute for the ha’ and the alif in We wrote it and the meaning is: We did not prescribe it for them except seeking the pleasure of God. It was said: Except seeking is an interrupted exception and the meaning is: We did not prescribe it for them, but they innovated it seeking the pleasure of God. They did not observe it as it should be observed meaning they did not perform it as it should be performed. This is particular, because some people did not observe it, but rather, through monasticism, they sought leadership over the people and consumed their wealth, as God the Almighty said: {O you who have believed, indeed many of the scholars and the monks devour the wealth of people unjustly and avert [people] from the way of God.} (al-Tawbah 9:34) This is about a people whose monasticism led them to seek leadership in the end. Sufyan Ath-Thawri narrated from Ata’ ibn As-Sa’ib from Sa’id ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of God the Almighty: {And monasticism, which they innovated}, he said: There were kings after Jesus who changed the Torah and the Gospel, and among them were believers who read the Torah and the Gospel and called to the religion of God the Almighty. So some people said to their king: Why don’t you kill this group? The believers said: We will suffice you against ourselves. A group said, Build for us a pillar and raise us up on it, and give us something to raise our food and drink with, and we will not be turned back to you. A group said, Let us wander through the land and drink as wild beasts drink, and when you get the better of us, kill us. A group said, Build for us houses in the deserts and we will dig wells and cultivate vegetables so that you will not see us. There was not one of these who did not have a close friend among them. So they did, and those people followed the way of Jesus, and after them came a people who changed the Book and said, We will wander and worship as you worship. Those people were still polytheists and had no knowledge of the faith of those who came before them, whom they followed. This is what God the Most High said, “And monasticism, which they invented for themselves. We did not prescribe it for them except seeking the pleasure of God.” He says that these righteous people invented it, but they did not observe it the later ones with the observance it should be observed “so We gave those among them who believed their reward” meaning those who invented it first and observed it and many of them are wicked meaning the later ones, when God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and only a few of them remained, they came from the caves, monasteries and caverns and believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Third: This verse indicates that every innovation is an innovation, so whoever innovates something good should persist in it and not deviate from it to its opposite, lest he be included in the verse. On the authority of Abu Umamah al-Baahili - whose name was Sadi ibn Jillan - who said: You innovated the night prayer of Ramadan, but it was not prescribed for you. Rather, fasting was prescribed for you, so persist in performing the night prayer if you do it and do not abandon it, because some people from the Children of Israel innovated innovations that God had not prescribed for them, seeking thereby the pleasure of God, but they did not observe them as they should have been observed. So God rebuked them for abandoning them, saying: “And monasticism, which they innovated for them. We did not prescribe it for them except seeking the pleasure of God, but they did not observe it as it should have been observed.” Fourth: The verse indicates that people should not slip up in monasteries and houses, and this is recommended when times become corrupt and friends and brothers change. A promise has been made that is fully explained in Surat Al-Kahf, and praise be to God. In the Musnad of Ahmad ibn Hanbal, on the authority of Abu Umamah Al-Baahili may God be pleased with him, he said: “We set out with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) on one of his expeditions. A man passed by a cave in which there was some water. He thought to himself that he would stay in that cave, so that the water in it would sustain him and he would eat the plants around it and give up the world. He said: I came to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and mentioned that to him. If he gives me permission, I will do so, otherwise I will not. So he came to him and said: O Prophet of God, I passed by a cave in which there was water and plants that would sustain me, and I thought to myself that I would stay in it and give up the world. The Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: I was not sent with Judaism or Christianity, but I was sent with the easy-going, tolerant faith. By the One in Whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, a morning or afternoon in the cause of God is better than the world and whatever is in it, and the standing of one of them in the first row is better than his prayer of sixty years.” The Kufians narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: Do you know which people are most ignorant? I said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: The most knowledgeable of people are those who are most aware of the truth when people differ about it, even if he is limited in action and even if he crawls on his backside. Do you know from where the Children of Israel adopted monasticism? The tyrants appeared among them after Jesus, and they committed sins against God. The people of faith became angry and fought them, and the people of faith were defeated three times, and only a few of them remained. They said: If they annihilate us and no one remains for the religion to call to it, then let us disperse throughout the earth until God sends the unlettered Prophet whom Jesus promised us - meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace - so they dispersed among the mountains and created monasticism, some of them held fast to their religion and some of them disbelieved - and he recited: And monasticism the verse - Do you know what the monasticism of my nation is? Migration, jihad, fasting, prayer, Hajj, Umrah, and glorifying God on the hills. O Ibn Masoud, those Christians who came before you differed into seventy-two sects, and three of them were saved. And the rest of them perished, a group that competed with the kings and fought them for the religion of God and the religion of Jesus - peace be upon him - until they were killed, and another group that was not able to compete with the kings stayed among their people, calling them to the religion of God and the religion of Jesus, son of Mary. So they wandered in the mountains and practiced monasticism therein, which is what God the Most High said about them: And monasticism which they invented - the verse - “And among them is he who believed in Me, followed Me, and confirmed Me - he has observed it with its right observance. And whoever does not believe in Me - then those are the defiantly disobedient.” He means those who became Jews and Christians. And it was said: These are the ones who lived at the time of Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him, but did not believe in him, so those are the defiantly disobedient. And in the verse there is consolation for the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, meaning that the first ones persisted in disbelief as well, so do not be surprised at the people of your time if they persist in disbelief. And God knows best.
57:28: The Almighty's saying: O you who have believed Where did you believe in Moses and Jesus Fear God and believe in His Messenger in Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him He will give you a double portion of His mercy meaning twofold reward for your belief in Jesus and Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him.
