This is similar to the Almighty's saying: Those will be given their reward twice over for what they patiently endured and this has already been discussed. The portion is the share and the portion and this has already been discussed in the chapter on women and it is in the chapter on a cloak that a rider wraps himself in to protect him from falling, as Ibn Jurayj said. Az-Zuhri said something similar. He said: Its derivation is from the cloak that a camel rider covers his hump with, so that he does not fall. Its interpretation is that He will give you two shares that will protect you from the destruction of sins, just as a cloak protects the rider. Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari said: Two shares means double in the dialect of Abyssinia. From Zaid: From the reward of this world and the hereafter. It was said: When the verse Those will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured was revealed, the believing People of the Book boasted to the Companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so this verse was revealed. Some scholars have used this verse as evidence that a good deed only has one reward. He said: A good deed is a general term that applies to every type of faith, and we apply it generally. So if a good deed is applied to one type, then it does not have more than one reward for it. If it is based on a good deed that includes two types, then the reward for it is double, as evidenced by this verse, for He said: double portions of His mercy. A portion is a share, like a likeness. So He made for the one who feared God and believed in His Messenger two shares: a share for fearing God and a share for his belief in His Messenger. This indicates that the good deed for which He made ten is the one that combines ten types of good deeds, which is faith in which God the Most High combines ten types, as He the Most High says: Indeed, the Muslim men and the Muslim women (Al-Ahzab 33:35), the entire verse. So these ten types, which are their rewards, are their likes, so each type of them is like. This is a corrupt interpretation, and its justification is from the general apparent meaning, in His statement: Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof (Al-An`am 6:16), in a way that does not permit a specific generality, because what combines ten good deeds, then only the like of them will be recompensed for each good deed. If it were as mentioned, then there would be no difference between a good deed and a bad deed. And He will make for you a light meaning clarification and guidance, according to Mujahid. Ibn Abbas said: It is the Qur’an. It was also said: It is a light by which you will walk in the Hereafter on the Bridge, and on the Day of Resurrection to Paradise. He said: You will walk with them among the people, calling them to Islam, so you will be leaders in the religion of Islam, and the leadership you held will not be removed from you. This is because they feared that their leadership would be removed if they believed in Muhammad, peace be upon him. What they would miss out on was taking bribes from the weak by distorting the rulings of God, not true leadership in the religion. And He will forgive you your sins, and God is Forgiving and Merciful.
57:29: The Almighty’s statement: So that the People of the Scripture may not know means to know, and that there is no is an additional, emphatic conjunction, as stated by Al-Akhfash. Al-Farra’ said: Its meaning is so that he may know, and there is no additional conjunction in every statement that contains denial. Qatadah said: The People of the Scripture envied the Muslims, so the verse: So that the People of the Scripture may not know was revealed, meaning so that the People of the Scripture may know that they have no power over anything of God’s bounty, and that bounty is in God’s hand. Mujahid said: The Jews said, Soon there will come forth from among us a prophet who will cut off hands and feet. But when he came forth from among the Arabs, they disbelieved, so the verse: So that he may not know was revealed, meaning so that the People of the Scripture may know, that they have no power, meaning that they are not able, like the Almighty’s statement: So that no word will return to them (Ta-Ha: 89). And on the authority of Al-Hasan: So that the People of the Scripture may not know. This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Mujahid. And it was narrated Qatrab with a kasra on the lam and a sukoon on the yaa. The fatha on the lam of jar is a well-known language. The reason for the sukoon on the yaa is that the hamza of an was deleted, so it became lan, then the nun was assimilated into the lam, so it became lala. When the two lams met, the middle one was replaced with a yaa, as they said in amma: ayma. The same applies to the reading of those who read laila with a kasra on the lam, except that they kept the lam according to the well-known language in it, so it is stronger in this respect. And from Ibn Masoud: so that he may not know, and from Hattan bin Abdullah: because he knows. And from Ikrimah: so that he may know, and this is contrary to the written law. From the bounty of God It was said: Islam. And it was said: the reward. Al-Kalbi said: From the provision of God. And it was said: the countless blessings of God. And that the bounty is in the hand of God It is not in their hands, so they can divert the prophethood from Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, to whomever they love. And it was said: And that the bounty is in the hand of God meaning it belongs to Him. He gives it to whomever He wills. In Al-Khari: Al-Hakam bin Nafi’ narrated to us, he said: Shu’aib narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, he said: Salim bin Abdullah informed me, and that Abdullah bin Omar said: I heard the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, say while he was standing on the pulpit: Your survival in comparison to the nations that came before you is like the period between the afternoon prayer and sunset. The People of the Torah were given the Torah and they acted upon it until midday. They were unable to do so, so they were given one qirat each. Then the People of the Gospel were given the Gospel and they acted upon it until the afternoon prayer. Then they were unable to do so, so they were given one qirat each. They were given the Qur’an and you acted upon it until the sun set. So you were given two qirats each. The People of the Torah said: Our Lord, these do less work and have more reward. He said: Have I wronged you in any respect in your reward? They said: No. He said: Then that is My bounty which I give to whom I will. In another narration: “The Jews and Christians became angry and said: Our Lord” the hadith and God is the possessor of great bounty. The interpretation of Surat Al-Hadid is complete, and praise be to God.
58:1: All of them are Medinan. Except for a narration from Ata' that the first ten of them are Medinan and the rest are Meccan. Al-Kalbi said: All of them were revealed in Medina except for the statement of God Almighty: "There are not three who confer privately but He is the fourth of them," which was revealed in Mecca. There are two issues: God the Almighty said: "God has certainly heard the statement of the one who argues with you O Muhammad concerning her husband and directs a complaint to God." The one who complained to God was Khawlah bint Tha'labah. It was also said that she was bint Hakeem. It was also said that her name was Jamila. Khawlah was a brother, and her husband was Aws ibn as-Samit, the brother of Ubadah ibn as-Samit. Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him passed by her during his caliphate and the people were with him on a donkey. She stopped him for a long time and admonished him saying: "Omar, you used to be called Umayr, then you were called Omar, then you were called Commander of the Faithful. So fear God, O Omar, for whoever is certain of death fears missing out, and whoever is certain of the reckoning avoids the punishment." He stood listening to her words and it was said to him: "O Commander of the Faithful, do you stand like this for this old woman?" He said: "By God, you would have detained me from the beginning of the day to the end of it, except for the obligatory prayer. Do you know who this old woman is?" She is Khawlah bint Tha’labah, God heard his words from above the seven heavens. Does the Lord of the Worlds hear her words, O Umar? Aisha may God be pleased with her said: Blessed is He who encompasses all things. I hear the words of Khawlah bint Tha’labah, and some of them are hidden from me. She is going to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) to uncover her husband and she is saying: O Messenger of God! He has consumed my youth and made my belly swell for him. Now that I am old and my children are cut off, he has become apparent to me. O God, I complain to You! I did not stop until Gabriel came down with this verse: God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband and directs a complaint to God. Narrated by Ibn Majah in Sunan. And in Bukhari from this: “On the authority of Aisha, she said: Praise be to God, whose hearing encompasses all sounds. A woman came to complain to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I was in a corner of the house, unable to hear what she was saying. Then God, the Almighty, revealed: {God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband.} Al-Mawardi said: She is Khawlah bint Tha’labah. It was also said: Tantah Khuwaylid. This is not different, because one of them is her father and the other is her grandfather, so she was named after each of them. Her husband is Aws ibn al-Samit, the brother of Ubadah ibn al-Samit. Al-Tha’labi said: Ibn Abbas said: She is Khawlah bint Khuwaylik al-Khazrajiyah. She was married to Aws ibn al-Samit, the brother of ‘Atada ibn al-Samit. She had a beautiful body, and her husband saw her prostrating and looked at her buttocks, and he was pleased with her. When she turned away, he wanted her, but she refused, so he became angry with her. - ‘Urwah said: There was a man who had a defect, and some of his defects affected him, so he said to her: You are to me like the back of my mother. And ila’ and zihar were forms of divorce in the pre-Islamic period, so she asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said to her: She is forbidden.” She said: By God, he did not mention divorce. Then she said: I complain to God of my poverty, loneliness, and desolation, and separation from my husband and cousin, and I have expressed my displeasure to him. He said: I am forbidden to him. She kept asking him and he asked her until the verse was revealed to him. Al-Hasan narrated that she said: O Messenger of God! God has abrogated the traditions of the Age of Ignorance, and my husband has divorced me. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Nothing has been revealed to me about this. She said: O Messenger of God, has everything been revealed to you and this has been hidden from you?! He said: It is what I told you. She said: I complain to God, not to His Messenger. Then God revealed: God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband and directs a complaint to God verse. Ad-Daraqutni narrated from the hadith of Qatada that Anas ibn Malik told him that Aws ibn as-Samit declared zihar a false declaration from his wife Khuwaylah, and Tha’labah complained about that to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). She said: I have grown old and my bones have become thin. So God revealed the verse of zihar. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Aws: Free a slave; I have no means of doing that. He said: Then fast for two consecutive months. He said: If I make the mistake of eating three times in one day, my sight fails. He said: Then feed sixty poor people. He said: I cannot find anything except that you help me and maintain ties of kinship. He said: So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) helped him with fifteen sa’s until God collected for him, and God is Forgiving and Merciful. Indeed, God is Hearing and Seeing. He said: They thought that he had the same amount, and that was for sixty poor people. In at-Tirmidhi and Sunan Ibn Majah: “That Salamah ibn Sakhr al-Bayadhi divorced his wife, and that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: ‘Free a slave.’ He said: ‘So I struck the side of my neck with my hand. I said: ‘No, by the One who made you stumble with the truth, I do not own anything else.’ He said: ‘Then fast for two months.’ I said: ‘O Messenger of God! Did what happened to me happen only because of fasting?’ He said: ‘Then feed sixty poor people.’” And Ibn al-Arabi mentioned it in his Ahkam: “It was narrated: Khawlah bint Dulaihj was divorced by her husband, so she came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and asked him about that. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, “She has become forbidden to him.” She said, I am complaining to God of my need. Then she returned and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, She has become forbidden to him. She said, I am complaining to God of my need for him. Aisha was washing the right side of his head. Then she moved to the other side and the revelation had come down to him. She was about to repeat it, but Aisha said, Be quiet, for the revelation has come down. When the Qur’an was revealed, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to her husband, Free a slave. He said, I do not have the means. He said, Fast for two consecutive months. He said, If I do not eat three times a day, I fear that my sight will become impaired. He said, Then feed sixty poor people. He said: He helped me. So he helped him with something. Abu Ja`far al-Nahhas said: The people of interpretation say that she was Khawlah and her husband was Aws ibn al-Samit, and they differed about her lineage. Some of them said: She was an Ansari woman and she was a Tha`laite woman. Some of them said: She was the daughter of Dulaij. It was said: She was the daughter of Khuwaylid. Some of them said: She was the daughter of al-Samit. Some of them said that she was a slave girl who belonged to Abdullah ibn Ubayy, and she was the one about whom God revealed: And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution if they desire chastity (al-Nur 24:33) because he forced her to commit adultery. It was said that she was the daughter of Hakim. Al-Nahhas said: This is not contradictory. It is possible that she was attributed once to her father, once to her mother, and once to her grandfather. It is possible that she was a slave girl who belonged to Abdullah ibn Ubayy, so she was called Ansar and Al-Wala’, because he was among the Ansar even though he was one of the hypocrites. [Third] It was read "Qad sama'a God with idgham and Qad sama'a God" with izhar. The basic meaning of hearing is to perceive what is heard, and this is the choice of Sheikh Abu al-Hasan. Ibn Fawrak said that it is correct to say that it is seeing what is heard. Al-Hakim Abdullah said about the meaning of hearing: It is the perception of sounds that creatures perceive with their ears without having ears. This is because sounds are not hidden from Him, even if He is not described by the sense compound in the ear. This is because sounds are not hidden from Him, even if He is not described by the sense compound in the ear, like the deaf among people who do not have this sense, are not qualified to perceive sound. Hearing and sight are two attributes like knowledge, power, life and will. They contain attributes of the Self that the Creator, glory be to Him, has always been described by. "Shaka and ashtaqa" have the same meaning. It was read "tawawaraka meaning that He debates with you, and tajadika" means that He questions you.
58:2: It contains twenty-three issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: Those who swear off their wives Ibn Amir, Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i and Khalaf read yadharoon with a fatha on the ya’, a shaddah on the tha’ and an alif. Nafi’, Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr and Ya’qub read yadharoon with a dhammah on the ya’, a shaddah on the tha’ and a fathah on the ya’. Abu Al-Aaliyah, Asim and Zur ibn Hubaish read yadharoon with a damma on the ya’, a softened tha’, an alif and a kasrah on the ha’. This has been mentioned previously in Al-Ahzab. In Abu’s reading it is yadharoon and it has the same meaning as the reading of Ibn Amir and Hamzah. The mention of the back is a metaphor for the meaning of riding, and the belly of a human being is ridden, but the back is used as a metaphor because what is ridden from non-human beings is only ridden on its back, so the back is used as a metaphor for riding. It is said: Nal ‘an ‘ar’atu means he divorced her as if he got off a mount. The meaning of you are forbidden to me like the back of my mother is: you are forbidden to me and it is not permissible for me to ride you. Second: The reality of zihar is likening one back to another, and what requires the ruling is likening the purity of a permissible divorce to the back of a forbidden divorce. For this reason, the jurists agreed that whoever says to his wife, You are to me like the back of my mother, is performing zihar. Most of them say that if he says to her, You are to me like the back of my daughter or sister or any other mahram, then he is performing zihar. This is the school of Malik, because he, Abu Hanifa, and others said. There is a difference of opinion regarding this from al-Shafi’i may God be pleased with him. Something similar to what Malik said was narrated from him, because he likened his wife to the back of someone who is permanently forbidden to him, like the mother. Abu Thawr narrated from him that zihar can only be performed by the mother alone. This is the school of Qatadah and al-Sha’bi. The first is the opinion of al-Hasan, al-Nakha’i, al-Zuhri, al-Awza’i, and al-Thawri. Third: The origin of zihar is that the man says to his wife, You are to me like my mother’s back. He only mentioned the back as a euphemism for the back and to conceal it. If he said, You are to me like my mother, but did not mention the back, or he said, You are to me like my mother, then if he intended zihar, then his intention is valid. If he intended divorce, then it is absolute and irrevocable according to Malik. If he did not intend divorce or zihar, then he has committed zihar. The explicit zihar does not refer to divorce, just as the explicit divorce and its known euphemism do not refer to zihar. The euphemism for zihar specifically refers to an irrevocable divorce by intention. Fourth: The words of zihar are of two types: explicit and implicit. The explicit form is: You are to me like my mother’s back, and You are with me, and You are from me, and With me like My mother’s back. Similarly, You are to me like my mother’s stomach, head, vulva, or the like. Similarly, Your vulva, head, back, stomach, or leg are to me like my mother’s back is an act of zihar. For example, if someone says: Your hand, leg, head, or vulva are divorced, she is divorced. Al-Shafi’i said in one of his two opinions: It is not zihar. This is weak on his part, because he agreed with us that it is valid to attribute divorce to it specifically in reality, unlike Abu Hanifa, who said that it is valid to attribute zihar to it. Whenever he compares her to his mother or one of his paternal grandmothers or his maternal aunts, then this is zihar without dispute. If he compares her to other mahrams who are not permissible for him under any circumstances, such as a daughter, sister, aunt, or maternal aunt, then this is an act of zihar according to most of the jurists, and according to Imam al-Shafi’i may God be pleased with him according to the correct opinion of the school, as we have mentioned. A metaphor is to say: You, you are to me like my mother or like my mother, as the intention is considered in this. If he intended zihar, then it is an apparent zihar. If he did not intend zihar, then it is not an zihar according to Al-Shafi’i and Abu Hanifa. The view of Malik may God be pleased with him on this matter has been presented previously, and the evidence for that is that he stated the comparison of his wife to his mother, so it was an zihar. The ruling of zihar is not binding because of the wording, but rather it is binding because of its meaning, which is prohibition, as stated by Ibn Al-Arabi. Fifth: If he compares all of his family members to one of his mother’s limbs, then he has committed zihar, contrary to Abu Hanifa’s statement that if he compares her to a limb that is permissible for him to look at, then he has not committed zihar. This is not correct, because looking at it with limited enjoyment is not permissible for him, and in this comparison he intends zihar. Imam Al-Shafi’i said in one opinion: It is not zihar except in the back alone. This is invalid, because every limb of hers is forbidden, so likening it to it is zihar like purity, and because the one who makes zihar only intends to liken the permissible to the forbidden, so it is binding on him according to the meaning. Sixth: If he likens his wife to a foreign woman, and mentions the back, it is considered zihar based on the first principle. But if he does not mention the back, our scholars differed concerning it. Some of them said: It is considered zihar. Some of them said: It is considered divorce. Abu Hanifa and Al-Shafi’i said: It is nothing. Ibn Al-Arabi said: This is invalid, because he likened a woman’s permissible husband to a mahram, so he was restricted by his ruling like the back. Names are based on their meanings according to us, and according to their words, and this is a contradiction of the principle on their part. I said: The disagreement regarding zihar with a foreign woman is strong according to Malik. Some of his companions do not consider zihar except with mahrams specifically and do not consider zihar with anyone else. Some of them do not consider it anything. Some of them consider it a divorce with a foreign woman. According to Malik, if he says: Like the back of my son or my slave or Like the back of Zayd or Like the back of a foreign woman, it is zihar and it is not permissible for him to have intercourse with her while he is swearing an oath. It has also been narrated from him that zihar with anyone other than a mahram is nothing, as al-Kufi and al-Shafi’i said. Al-Awza’i said: If he says to her, You are to me like the back of so-and-so, then it is an oath for which he must make expiation. And God knows best. Seventh: If he says: You are forbidden to me like my mother’s back, then it is a zihar and not a divorce, because his saying: You are forbidden to me may mean that it is forbidden by divorce, so she is divorced, and it may mean that it is forbidden by zihar, so when he stated it clearly, it was an explanation of one of the two possibilities and he ruled accordingly. Eighth: Zihar is obligatory for every wife, whether consummated or not, regardless of the circumstances, by a husband who is permitted to divorce. Similarly, according to Malik, if a man has sexual intercourse with his female slaves, if he declares Zihar regarding them, then Zihar is obligatory for them. Abu Hanifa and Al-Shafi’i said: It is not obligatory. Judge Abu Bakr ibn Al-Arabi said: This is a very difficult issue for us, because Malik says: If he says to his female slave, You are forbidden to me, then it is not obligatory. So how can the explicit prohibition be nullified in this case and his implicit pronouncement be valid? However, the female slave is included in the generality of his statement: of their women, because he meant of their permissible women. The meaning here is that the word relates to weakness, not to annulling the contract, so it is valid for the female slave. Its origin is an oath by God Almighty. Ninth: The zihar is binding before marriage if the husband marries the woman from whom he has zihar, according to Malik. However, it is not binding according to Al-Shafi’i and Abu Hanifa, because God the Almighty says: of their women, and this woman is not one of his women. The origin of this issue has already been discussed in Surat Al-Bara’ah, when God the Almighty says: And among them are those who made a covenant with God (At-Tutah: 75). Tenth: A dhimmi is not required to pronounce zihar pronouncement of zihar on his wife. Abu Hanifa said the same. Al-Shafi’i said: A dhimmi’s zihar is valid, and our evidence is the statement of God, the Most High: from among you, meaning from among the Muslims. This excludes the dhimmi from the address. Marriages of non-Muslims are invalid and deserve to be annulled, so no ruling of divorce or zihar applies to them. This is like the statement of God, the Most High: And bring to witness two just men from among you (al-Talaq 65:2). If the marriages do not meet the conditions of validity, then they are invalid, and there is no zihar in an invalid marriage under any circumstances. Eleventh: The Almighty’s statement, from among you, requires the validity of the slave’s zihar, contrary to those who forbade it. Al-Tha’labi narrated it from Malik, because he is among the Muslims and the rulings of marriage are valid for him, even if he is unable to free a slave or feed the poor, he is able to fast. Twelfth: Malik may God be pleased with him said: Women are not required to perform zihar. Rather, God the Almighty said: Those of you who swear an oath of divorce from their wives He did not say those of you who swear an oath of divorce from their husbands. Rather, zihar is only required of men. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is how it was narrated from Ibn al-Qasim, Salim, Yahya ibn Sa’id, Rabi’ah, and Abu al-Zinad, and it is correct in meaning, because the permissibility, contract, permission, and prohibition in marriage are in the man’s hand, not the woman’s. This is a consensus. Abu ‘Umar said: Women are not required to perform zihar according to the majority of scholars. Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad said: It is zihar. Al-Thawri, Abu Hanifah, and Muhammad said: A woman’s zihar from a man is not valid, whether before or after marriage. Ash-Shafi’i said: A woman is not to be considered a zihar apostate from a man. Al-Awza’i said: If a woman says to her husband: You are to me like the back of my mother so-and-so, then this is an oath for which she must expiate. Ishaq said the same: A woman cannot be considered a zihar apostate from a man, but she must expiate an oath for which she must expiate. Az-Zuhri said: I think she should expiate for zihar, and her words should not prevent her from having intercourse with her husband. This was narrated by Muammar. Ibn Jurayj narrated from Ata’ who said: She has forbidden what God has made permissible, so she must expiate for an oath. This is the opinion of Abu Yusuf. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: She does not have to do anything. Thirteenth: If someone has a blemish and his words become regular at some times, and he pronounces a zihar divorce, then his zihar is binding, as was narrated in the hadith: That Khawlah bint Tha’laba, whose husband was Aws ibn al-Samit, had a blemish and some of his words affected him, so he pronounces a zihar divorce from his wife. Fourteenth: If a man becomes angry and declares divorce from his wife or divorces her, his anger does not remove the legal ruling from him. In some versions of this hadith, Yusuf bin Abdullah bin Salam said: Hawlah, the wife of Aws bin As-Samit, told me: There was something between me and him, and he said: You are to me like my mother’s back. Then he went out to the gathering of his people. Her saying: There was something between me and him, is evidence of a dispute that embarrassed him, so he declared divorce from her. Anger is futile and does not remove a legal ruling or justify it according to Islamic law, and the same applies to a drunkard. It is: Fifteenth: He is bound by the ruling of zihar and divorce while intoxicated if he is sane and understands what he says, based on the words of God Almighty: Until you know what you are saying (An-Nisa’: 43), as explained previously in An-Nisa’. And God knows best. Sixteenth: The one who has committed li’anal promiscuity should not approach his wife, nor should he have sexual intercourse with her, nor should he enjoy anything from her until he makes atonement, contrary to one of Al-Shafi’i’s two opinions, because his saying, You are to me like the back of my mother, requires the prohibition of all enjoyment in its wording and meaning. If he has sexual intercourse with her before making atonement, and she is: Seventeenth: He should seek forgiveness from God and refrain from her until he offers one expiation. Mujahid and others said: He must offer two expiations. Sa`d narrated from Qatadah, and Mutraf from Raja` ibn Haywah from Qubaysah ibn Dhu`ayb from `Amr ibn al-`As regarding the one who pronounces li’l-Zihar: If he has intercourse before offering expiation, he must offer two expiations. Mu`ammar narrated from Qatadah that Qubayd ibn Dhu`ayb said: He must offer two expiations. A group of imams narrated, including Ibn Majah and al-Nasa`i, from Ibn Abbas: A man committed slander against his wife and had intercourse with her before making atonement. He came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and mentioned that to him. The man said: What made you do that? He said: O Messenger of God! I saw the whiteness of her anklet in the moonlight and I could not control myself from having intercourse with her. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) laughed and ordered him not to go near her until he made atonement. Ibn Majah and Ad-Daraqutni narrated from Sulayman ibn Yasar from Salamah ibn Sakhr that he committed slander during the time of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), then he had intercourse with his wife before making atonement. He came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and mentioned that to him. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered him to make atonement and not to commit stoning. Eighteenth: If a man pronounces zihar absolution with four wives in one statement, such as saying, You are to me like my mother’s back, then he has pronounces zihar with each one of them, and it is not permissible for him to have intercourse with any of them, but one expiation is sufficient for him. Ash-Shafi’i said, He must offer four expiations. There is no evidence for any of this in the verse, because the plural wording applies to all believers, and reliance is on Al-Mughni. Ad-Daraqutni narrated from Ibn Abbas that ‘Umar ibn Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him used to say, “If a man has four wives and he pronounces zihar with one of them, one expiation is sufficient for him. If he pronounces zihar with one after the other, then he must offer one expiation for each one of them.” This is a consensus. Nineteenth: If he says to four women: If I marry you, you will be as high as my mother’s back, and he marries one of them, he is not to approach her until he makes atonement. Then the oath is dropped from him regarding the rest of them. It has been said: He is not to have intercourse with the rest of them until he makes atonement. The first is the correct school of thought. Al-Muwafiyah twentieth: If he says to his wife: You are to me like my mother’s back and you are divorced irrevocably, then the divorce and the zihar are binding on him together, and he does not atone until he marries her again after another husband, and he does not have intercourse with her if he marries her until he atones. If he says to her: You are divorced irrevocably and you are to me like my mother’s back, then the divorce is binding on him and he is not bound by the zihar, because a divorce does not apply to a divorced woman. Twenty-first: Some scholars said that a divorce pronounced by a woman who has not been consummated with is not valid. Al-Muzani said: A divorce pronounced by a woman who has been divorced in full is not valid. This is meaningless, because the rulings of marriage are established in both cases, and just as divorce applies to her, so too does a divorce pronounced by her, by analogy and consideration. And God knows best. Twenty-second: The Almighty’s statement: They are not their mothers meaning, They are not their wives with their mothers. The general reading of their mothers is with the ta in the genitive case, in the dialect of the people of Hijaz, like the Almighty’s statement: This is not a human being (Yusuf 12:31). Abu Ma’mar, As-Sulami, and others read their mothers with the fa in the dialect of Tamim. Al-Farra’ said: The people of Najd and Banu Tamim say Ma hada bi-shara’, and Ma hunna ammathi with the genitive case. Their mothers are none but those who gave birth to them means that their mothers are none but the mothers. And in the proverb: Your offspring are from my blood. The ‘ul has already been mentioned in those who in Al-Ahzab. Twenty-third: The Almighty says: And indeed, they say an abominable statement and a lie. That is, a terrible statement that is not known in Islamic law. Falsehood is lying. And indeed, God is Forgiving. If He makes expiation for them, it will free them from this abominable statement.
58:3: It contains twelve issues. First: The Almighty’s statement: And those who swear to divorce their wives This is the subject and the predicate is the freeing of a slave. The word upon them was omitted because the statement indicates it, meaning, they must free a slave. It was also said: meaning, your expiation is to free a slave. The apparent consensus among scholars is that a man says to his wife, You are to me as the back of my mother. This is the reprehensible and false statement that God meant by His statement, And indeed, they say a reprehensible statement and a lie. So whoever says this statement, it is forbidden for him to have intercourse with his wife. So whoever repeats what he said must pay the expiation for zihar, because God the Almighty said: And those who swear to divorce their wives and then go back on what they said must free a slave. This indicates that the expiation for zihar is not due to words in particular until they are repeated. This is a problematic word that people have differed about, with seven opinions: The first: It is the intention to have intercourse, and this is the well-known opinion of the two scholars of ‘Iraq, Abu Hanifa and his companions. It was narrated from Malik: If he intends to have intercourse with her, then it is a repetition, but if he does not intend to, then it is not a repetition. Second: To intend to abstain from fasting, after purifying oneself from it, as Malik said. Third: To intend to do both. This is the opinion of Malik in his Muwatta. Malik said regarding the statement of God the Almighty: And those who swear an oath of divorce against their wives and then go back on what they said, he said: I heard that the interpretation of that is that a man swears an oath of divorce against his wife and then decides to have sexual intercourse with her and keep her. If he decides to do that, then expiation is required of him. But if he divorces her and has not decided after declaring his divorce to keep her and have sexual intercourse with her, then expiation is required of him. Malik said: If he marries her after that, he should not have sexual intercourse with her until he pays the expiation for declaring divorce. The fourth opinion: It is intercourse itself. If he does not have sexual intercourse, then it is not a return. This is according to al-Hasan and Malik as well. The fifth opinion: Imam al-Shafi’i may God be pleased with him said: It is that he keeps her as a wife who is considered dhihar while being able to divorce her. This is because when he pronounced dhihar, he intended to forbid her. If he leads to divorce, then he has gone against what he began by forbidding her, and there is no expiation required of him. But if he refrains from divorcing her, then he has returned to what he was doing and expiation is required of him. The sixth opinion: Dhihar creates a prohibition that can only be removed by expiation. The meaning of repetition according to those who say this is that he does not permit himself to have intercourse with her except with an expiation that he offers both of them. This was stated by Abu Hanifa and his companions and Al-Layth ibn Sa'd. The seventh is repeating the wording of zihar. This is the opinion of the proponents of zihar who deny analogy. They said: If the wording of zihar is repeated, then it is a repetition, but if it is not repeated, then it is not a repetition. This is attributed to Bakir ibn Al-Ashbah, Abu Al-Ashbah, Abu Al-'Aliyah and Abu Hanifa as well. It is also the opinion of Al-Farra'. Abu Al-'Aliyah said: The apparent meaning of the verse supports this, because He says: Then they go back to what they said meaning to what they said. Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the words of God the Almighty: And those who swear an oath of divorce against their wives and then go back to what they said, that it is for him to say to her, You are to me like the back of my mother. So if he says that to her, then she is not lawful for him until he expiates the guarantee of zihar. Ibn Al-'Arabi said: As for the claim that it is a return to the wording of zihar, it is definitely invalid and is not authentically reported from Bakir. It is more likely that we are from the ignorance of David and his followers. Stories of demonstrators have been narrated, and there is no mention of the expiation for them, because they repeated the statement. Also, the meaning contradicts it, because God Almighty described it as an abomination of injustice and falsehood. So how can it be said to him, if you repeat the forbidden statement and the reason for the forbidden, then expiation is obligatory upon you? This is not reasonable. Do you not see that every reason that necessitates expiation does not require repetition, such as murder, intercourse during fasting, or other things? I said: His statement, Shibah, may be due to Dawud’s ignorance and his spreading it, which led him to accuse him of it. Those we have mentioned have said the same as Dawud. As for the statement of Al-Shafi’i, that he left divorce when he was able to do so, it is invalidated by three main matters: First: He said: Then - which appears to indicate that it requires delay. Second: His statement, the Most High, Then they return requires the existence of an action on the part of the husband, and the passage of time is not due to their action. Third: A revocable divorce does not contradict remaining in possession, so the ruling of zihar is not dropped like ila’. If it is said: If he saw her talking, he did not hold on to her, so holding on to the mother by marriage is not valid. This is the main opinion of the people of Transoxiana. We say: If he intends to do something contrary to what he said and sees it contrary to the mother, he has disbelieved and returned to his family. The realization of this statement is that the intention is a statement that invalidates it. This is a man who said a statement that required the analysis, which is marriage, and he said a statement that required the prohibition, which is the zihar, then he went back to what he said, which is the analysis. It is not correct that it was the beginning of a contract from him, because the contract remains and remains, except that he said a determination that contradicts what he believed and said in himself regarding the zihar that he informed about by his saying, You are to me like my mother’s back. If that was the case, he disbelieved and returned to his family, because of his saying, before they touch each other. This is an explanation that is very sophisticated in its art. Second: Some of the people of interpretation said: The verse has an inversion, and the meaning is And those who swear off their wives and then return to what they were doing of sexual intercourse the freeing of a slave for what they said, meaning it is upon them. Freeing a slave for what they said: So the preposition in His statement: for what they said is connected to the omitted word which is the predicate of the subject, which is upon them, as Al-Akhfash said. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: Then they return to wanting intercourse because of what they said. It was said: The meaning is what they used to show off to their women in the pre-Islamic era, then they return to what they said in the pre-Islamic era in Islam, so the expiation for returning is to free a slave. Al-Farra’: The lam means about and the meaning is: Then they return to what they said, wanting intercourse. Al-Akhfash recited: When they said and to what they said is one, and the lam and to alternate. He said: Praise be to God, who has guided us to this (al-A’raf 7:43) and He said: So guide them to the path of Hellfire (al-Saffat 37:23) and He said: Because your Lord inspired her (al-Zalzalah 99:5) and He said: And it was inspired to Noah (Hud 11:36). Third: The Almighty’s saying: Then the freeing of a slave means that he must free a slave. It is said: I freed him meaning I made him free. Then this slave must be complete and free from every defect, and part of its perfection is her conversion to Islam according to Malik and Al-Shafi’i, like the slave in the case of murder. According to Abu Hanifa and his companions, a non-Muslim woman and someone with a trace of slavery, such as a freed slave and others, are sufficient. Fourth: If he frees half of two slaves, it does not suffice for us, nor according to Abu Hanifa. Al-Shafi’i said it suffices, because half of two slaves means one slave, and because the expiation for emancipation is through money, so it is permissible for it to be divided or fragmented, like feeding. Our evidence is the saying of God the Almighty: Then the freeing of a slave. This term refers to one person, and part of a slave is not a slave, and this is not something that can be combined, because the worship related to a slave is that half of two slaves cannot take their place. The basic principle is that if two men share in two sacrifices, and because if he orders two men to perform Hajj on his behalf, it is not permissible for one of them to perform half of it, and likewise this. And because if he instructs that a slave be purchased and emancipated on his behalf, it is not permissible for half of two slaves to be emancipated on his behalf, and likewise in our case, and thus their evidence is invalidated. Feeding and other things do not suffice for expiation according to us. Fifth: The Almighty’s statement: before they touch each other meaning that he has intercourse with her. It is not permissible for the one who has pronounced zihar to have intercourse before offering expiation. If he has intercourse with her before offering expiation, he has sinned and disobeyed, but the expiation is not waived for him. It was narrated from Mujahid that if he has intercourse before starting to offer expiation, he must offer another expiation. It was narrated from others that the expiation and obligation of zihar are waived and he is not required to do anything at all, because God Almighty has made expiation obligatory and commanded it before intercourse. So if he delays it until he touches her, then its time has passed. The correct view is that the expiation is obligatory, because by his intercourse he committed a sin and that does not waive the expiation. He must make it up as if he delayed a prayer past its proper time. In the hadith of Aws ibn as-Samit, when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) informed him that he had intercourse with his wife, he ordered him to offer expiation. This is a clear text, regardless of whether the expiation is by freeing a slave, fasting, or feeding the poor. Abu Hanifa said: If his expiation is feeding the poor, then it is permissible for him to have intercourse and then feed the poor. However, other than intercourse, such as kissing, touching, or pleasure, it is not forbidden according to the majority of scholars. Al-Hasan and Sufyan said this, and it is the correct opinion of the Shafi’i school. It was also said: All of that is forbidden, as are all types of touching. This is the opinion of Malik and one of the two opinions of Al-Shafi’i. It has been mentioned previously. Sixth: The Most High said: This is what you are admonished with, meaning they are commanded to do it. And God is All-Aware of what you do, of declaring others to be infidels and other things.
58:4: Seventh: If someone does not have a dome or its price, or he owns it but is in dire need of it for his service, or he owns its price but needs it for his expenses, or he has a home and nothing else and he does not have anything else, then he may fast according to Al-Shafi’i. Abu Hanifa said: He does not fast and he must free a slave even if he is in need of that. Malik said: If he has a house and a servant, he must free a slave. But if he is unable to free a slave, it is: Eighth: He must fast for two consecutive months. If he breaks his fast during them without an excuse, he must start them again. If he breaks his fast due to an excuse such as travel or illness, it is said that he must continue. This was stated by Ibn al-Musayyab, al-Hasan, Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah, Amr ibn Dinar, and al-Sha’bi. It is one of the two opinions of al-Shafi’i and is the correct one according to his school of thought. Malik said that if he falls ill while fasting as expiation for zihar, he must continue if he becomes healthy. The school of thought of Abu Hanifa may God be pleased with him is that it is… It begins. This is one of the two opinions of Al-Shafi’i. Ninth: If a person begins fasting and then finds a slave, he must complete the fast and it is sufficient for him according to Malik and Ash-Shafi’i, because this is what he was commanded to do when he started fasting. The fast is invalidated and a slave is freed according to Abu Hanifa and his companions, by analogy to a young girl who is observing her waiting period for months and sees blood before the end of the period, as she begins her menses again according to the consensus of the scholars. If a person begins his fast on a journey and breaks his fast, he must begin fasting according to Malik, Ash-Shafi’i and Abu Hanifa, and his statement is consecutive. He must continue fasting according to Al-Hasan Al-Basri, because this is an excuse and by analogy to Ramadan, even if there is a period in between when fasting is not permissible as an expiation, such as the two Eids, and the month of Ramadan has been interrupted. Tenth: If the one who is performing the ritual prayer has intercourse during the two months during the day, the continuity is invalidated according to Al-Shafi’i, but at night it is not invalidated because it is not a place for fasting. Malik and Abu Hanifa said: It is invalidated in all cases and he must begin the expiation, because God the Almighty says: before they touch each other. This condition applies to the two months as a whole and to parts of them. If he has intercourse before they have expired, then it is not the fast that was commanded, so he must start it again, just as if he said, Pray before you speak to Zaid, so he spoke to Zaid during the prayer, or he said, Pray before you see Zaid, so he saw him during the prayer, so he must start it again because this prayer is not the prayer that was commanded. Likewise, this is the case, and God knows best. Eleventh: If a person’s illness is prolonged and there is no hope of recovery, then he is like someone who is unable to fast due to old age. It is permissible for him to change his fasting to feeding the poor. If his illness is one from which recovery is hoped, and he is in dire need of intercourse with his wife, then it is his choice to wait until he is recovered until he is able to fast. If he makes atonement by feeding the poor and does not consider whether he will be able to fast, it is sufficient for him. Twelfth: Whoever pretends to be a slave while he is financially able and then becomes better off, his fast is not valid. Whoever pretends to be a slave while he is financially able and then becomes better off before making expiation, he must fast. However, his condition on the day he makes expiation should be considered. If he had intercourse with her while he was not able and financially able and did not fast until he became better off, he must free her. If he began fasting and then became better off, if a valid portion of his fast has passed, such as Friday or similar fasts, he should continue. But if it is today or two days or similar, he should leave the day and return to freeing her, and this is not obligatory upon him. Do you not see that it is not obligatory upon someone who has performed tayammum during prayer to do so and begin purification, according to Malik. Thirteenth: If he frees two slaves as expiation for zihar, murder, or breaking the fast in Ramadan, and combines both of them in each expiation, it is not valid. He is in the same position as one who frees one slave as expiation for two. Similarly, if he fasts for them for four months, he must fast for each of them for two months. It has been said that this is valid. If he pronounces zihar on two wives, and frees a slave for one of them without specifying her, he is not permitted to have intercourse with either of them until he expiates for another expiation. If he specifies the expiation for one of them, it is permissible for him to have intercourse with her before expiating for the other. If he pronounces zihar on four wives, and frees three slaves for them and fasts for two months, neither the freeing nor the fasting is valid, because he only fasted for fifteen days for each one. If he expiates for them by feeding them, it is permissible for him to feed two hundred poor people on their behalf, but if he is unable to do so, then there is a difference, unlike the freeing and fasting, because fasting for two months is not different, while feeding is different. A chapter containing six issues: First: God the Almighty mentioned the expiation here in order. There is no way to fast except to free a slave, and likewise there is no way to feed except when one is unable to fast. So whoever is not able to fast must feed sixty poor people, giving each one a mudd according to the mudd of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). If he feeds a mudd according to the mudd of Hisham, which is two mudds less a third, or he feeds a mudd and a half according to the mudd of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), that is sufficient for him. Abu Omar ibn Abdul Barr said: The best of that is two mudds according to the mudd of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), because God the Almighty did not say in the expiation for zihar, from the average of what you feed (al-Ma’idah 5:89), so it is obligatory to intend satiety. Ibn Al-Arabi said: Malik said in the narration of Ibn Al-Qasim and Ibn Abdul-Hakim: A mudd according to the mudd of Hisham, which means satiety here, because God the Almighty mentioned food in general terms and did not mention the average. And he said in the narration of Ashhab: Two mudds according to the mudds of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). It was said to him: Didn’t you say the mudd of Hisham? He said: Yes, I prefer a debt of the Prophet’s (peace and blessings be upon him) debt. Ibn Al-Qasim also said the same about him. I said: This is the narration of Ibn Wahb and Mutraf from Malik: that he gives one mudd to each poor person according to the mudd of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). This is the view of Abu Hanifa and his companions. The view of al-Shafi’i and others is that he gives one mudd to each poor person, and he is not required to spend more than that, because he expiates with food and is not required to spend more than the mudd. Its basis is the expiation for breaking the fast and breaking an oath. Our evidence is the statement of God: Then feed sixty poor persons. The general term feeding includes satiety, and that is not usually achieved with one mudd except by adding to it. Likewise, Ashhab said: I said to Malik: Is satiety different for us and for you? He said: Yes! Satisfaction for us is one mudd according to the mudd of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and satiety for you is more, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prayed for us to be blessed but not for you, so you eat more than we eat. Abu al-Hasan al-Qabisi said: The people of Madinah only took the mudd of Hisham as expiation for zihar as a punishment for those who zihar, against whom God has testified that they say reprehensible and false words. Ibn al-Arabi said: The speech here was about the mudd of Hisham, as you see, and I wish that time would destroy its mention and erase its trace from the books, because the city in which the revelation came down and the Messenger settled and among them the zihar took place, and it was said about it: Then feed sixty poor people, they understood it and knew what was meant by it and that it was satiety, and its amount was known to them and established among them, and that satiety was mentioned in the reports many times, and the situation continued like that during the days of the Rightly-Guided Caliphs until Satan blew into Hisham’s ear, and he saw that the mudd of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not satisfy him, nor would anyone like him or his peers. So he suggested to him to make a mudd that would be enough to satisfy him, so he made it two ratls and forced the people to do it, but when it got wet, it returned to being about three ratls, so he changed the Sunnah and removed the place of blessing. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said when he supplicated to his Lord for the people of Madinah that blessings be maintained for them in their mudd and sa’, just as He blessed Abraham in Makkah, so blessings were flowing through the supplication of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in his mudd. Satan sought to change this tradition and remove this blessing, but no one responded to him in that regard except Hisham. It was the right of the scholars to abolish his mention and erase his trace if they did not change his command. But to refer to his mention in the rulings and make it an explanation of what God and His Messenger mentioned after it had been explained by the companions to whom it was revealed is a serious matter. Therefore, the narration of Ashhab in mentioning Madinah with the mudd of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in the expiation for zihar is more beloved to us than the narration that it is with the mudd of Hisham. Do you not see how Malik drew attention to this knowledge by saying to Ashhab: Satiety for us is with the mudd of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and satiety for you is more important because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) supplicated for us to be blessed. And with this I say, if worship is performed according to the Sunnah, if it is done with the body it will be accepted more quickly, and if it is done with money then a small amount of it will be heavier on the scale, more blessed in the hand of the one who takes it, more pleasant on his cheek, less harmful to his stomach, and more strengthening for his back. And God knows best. Second: According to Malik and Al-Shafi’i, feeding less than sixty poor people is not sufficient. Abu Hanifa and his companions said: If he feeds one poor person every day with half a sa’ until the number is complete, it is sufficient. Third: Judge Abu Bakr Ibn Al-Arabi said: It is strange that Abu Hanifa said that the guardianship of a free man is invalid. He argued with the words of God Almighty: Then the freeing of a slave and he did not differentiate between the sane and the foolish. This is a weak understanding that does not suit his status, because this verse is general, and the ruling of guardianship among the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was widespread and reasoning dictates it. And whoever was subject to guardianship due to his youth or guardianship and the foolish reached puberty, it was forbidden to give him money, so how can his action be implemented in his case when the specific ruling applies to the general. Fourth: The ruling of zihar, according to some scholars, abrogates what they held regarding zihar as a divorce. The meaning of this has been narrated from Ibn Abbas, Abu Qilabah, and others. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: That is so that you may believe in God and His Messenger, meaning that which we have described of the severity of the expiation. That you may believe, meaning that you may believe that God has commanded it. Some scholars have argued that this expiation is belief in God, the Most High, since when He mentioned it and made it obligatory, He said: That is so that you may believe in God and His Messenger, meaning that this is so that you may be obedient to God, the Most High, and abide by His limits and not transgress them. So expiation is called faith because obedience and observance of the limits is faith. So it is proven that everything similar to it is faith. If it is said: The meaning of His saying: That is so that you may believe in God and His Messenger, is so that you do not return to zihar, which is reprehensible speech and falsehood. It is said to him: It is possible that this is intended and the first is intended, so the meaning is that so that you do not return to reprehensible speech and falsehood, but rather you abandon them in obedience to God, the Most High, since He has forbidden them, and so that those who perform zihar avoid them until you disbelieve, since God has forbidden touching them, and you disbelieve since God, the Most High, has commanded expiation and made it obligatory for you to pay it. So with all of this you are believers in God and His Messenger, because these are limits that you observe and acts of obedience that you perform, and obedience is to God. And to his Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, we believe. And success comes from God. Sixth: The Almighty says: And these are the limits set by God, meaning between disobeying Him and obeying Him. So disobeying Him is Zihar, and obeying Him is expiation. And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment, meaning for those who do not believe in the rulings of God Almighty, there is the punishment of Hell.
58:5: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, those who oppose God and His Messenger When He mentioned the believers who abide by His limits, He mentioned those who oppose and contravene them. Opposition means enmity and contravention of the limits, and it is similar to His saying: That is because they opposed God and His Messenger (al-Anfal 8:13). It was said: They oppose God meaning the allies of God, as in the hadith: Whoever humiliates my friend has declared war on me. Al-Zajjaj said: Muhadah is to be in a manner that contradicts the manner of your companion. Its root is muman'ah, and from it comes the word al-hadid, and its meaning is al-haddad for the gatekeeper. Kabtawa they were subdued. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Akhfash said: They were destroyed. Qatada said: They were disgraced as those before them were disgraced. Ibn Zayd said: They were tormented. Al-Suddi said: They were cursed. Al-Farra' said: They were enraged on the Day of the Trench. It was also said: The Day of Badr. The intended meaning is the polytheists. It was also said: They were subdued means it will be. It is good report from God to the believers of victory. The past tense was used to approximate the one being described. It was also said: It is in the language of Madhhij. And We have sent down clear verses concerning those who opposed God and His Messenger among those before them in what We did to them. And for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment.
58:6: The Almighty said: The Day is in the accusative case with - a humiliating punishment or with a verb that is understood and mentioned to magnify the Day. God will resurrect them all meaning men and women. He will resurrect them from their graves in one state. Then He will inform them meaning He will tell them what they did in the world. God has counted it All-Knowing in their books of deeds. And they forgot it until He reminded them of it in their books so that the argument against them would be more effective. And God is Witness over all things All-Knowing and All-Seeing. Nothing is hidden from Him.
58:7: God the Almighty says: Have you not seen that God knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth? Nothing secret or public is hidden from Him. Whatever secrets take place is the general reading with the letter ya because of the barrier between them. Abu Ja`far ibn al-Qa`qa`, al-A`raj, Abu Haywah, and Isa read ma-takun with the feminine form of the verb. Najwa means secrets, and it is a verbal noun, and a verbal noun may be described by it. It is said: People of Najwa meaning people of Najwa. From this is the saying of God the Almighty: And when they whisper (al-Isra`: 47). God the Almighty says: Three in the accusative case by adding Najwa to it. Al-Farra` said: Three is an adjective for Najwa, so it was lowered, and if you wish, you may double Najwa to it. If it is accusative with the omission of a verb, it is permissible. This is the reading of Ibn Abi `Ubla: three and five in the accusative case as a state with the omission of yatanawun, because Najwa indicates it, as al-Zamakhshari said. It is permissible to raise three as a substitute for a secret whisper. Then it was said: Every secret is a secret whisper. It was also said: A secret whisper is when three people are alone together, whispering something to each other. A secret is when something happens between two people. But He is their fourth. He knows and hears their secret whispering, as indicated by the opening of the verse with knowledge and then its conclusion with knowledge. It was also said: A secret whisper is from a high place on the ground, so the two whispering people whisper and are alone with their secret, just as a high place on the ground is free of anything that connects to it. The meaning is that God’s hearing encompasses all speech, and God heard the argument of the woman from whom her husband divorced her. And not less than that or more. Salam, Ya’qub, Abu Al-Aliyah, Nasr, and Isa read it in the nominative case in the place of from a secret whisper before entering from because its meaning is what is a secret whisper. Three can be raised in the place of not less with less, like your saying: There is no power nor saying except with God with the opening of al-hawl and the raising of quwwa. It is permissible for them to be raised as the beginning, like your saying: There is no power nor strength except with God. This has been fully explained in Surah Al-Baqarah. Al-Zuhri and Ikrimah read it with a ba’, but the majority read it with a tha’ and a fatha on the ra’ in the wording, and its position is in the genitive case. Al-Farra’ said about the verse: There are not three who confer privately but that He is their fourth, nor five but that He is their sixth, he said: The meaning is not clear and the number is not intended because God only intended, and He knows best, that He is with every number, whether small or large. He knows what they say secretly and openly, and nothing is hidden from Him. For that reason, He was satisfied with mentioning some of the number and not others. It was said that the meaning of this is that God is with them with His knowledge wherever they are, without disappearing or moving. This was revealed about a group of hypocrites who did something secretly, so God knew that nothing was hidden from Him. This was said by Ibn Abbas. Qatadah and Mujahid said: It was revealed about the Jews. Then He will inform them “will tell them” what they did “of good and bad” “on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, God is Knowing of all things.”
58:8: There are three issues: God the Almighty said: Have you not considered those who were forbidden from secret conversation? It was said that this was regarding the Jews and the hypocrites, as we mentioned earlier. It was also said that it was regarding the Muslims. Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed regarding the Jews and the hypocrites. They used to whisper among themselves, look at the believers and wink at each other. The believers would say: Perhaps they have heard about our brothers and relatives among the Muhajireen and Ansar being killed, or a calamity, or a defeat. This would upset them, so they frequently complained to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), so he forbade them from secret conversation, but they did not desist, so this verse was revealed. Muqatil said: There was a truce between the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Jews. When a believer passed by them, they would whisper among themselves until the believers would think evil of him and would turn away from his path. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade them from doing so, but they did not desist, so this verse was revealed. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: A man would come to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and ask him for a need and whisper to him, while the land at that time was at war. They would imagine that he was whispering to him about a war, a calamity, or an important matter, so they would be alarmed by that, so this verse was revealed. The second: Abu Saeed Al-Khudri narrated that he said: One night we were talking when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came out to us and said: What is this whispering? Didn’t you forbid whispering? We said: We repent to God, O Messenger of God. We used to mention the Messiah meaning the Antichrist out of fear of him. He said: Shall I not tell you of something that I fear most? We said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: Hidden polytheism, that a man should work in place of another. Al-Mawardi mentioned this. Hamzah, Khalaf, and Ruways read it on the authority of Ya’qub and they produce it in the weight of yafta’alun, which is the reading of Abu Abdullah and Abu Hatim, because of the saying of God the Most High: When you whisper and you whisper. An-Nahhas said: Sibawayh narrated that yaf’a’alu, ifta’alu, and ifta’alu come with one meaning, like takhasamau and ikhtisamau, and taqatala and atalla. Based on this, yafta’alu and ifta’alu are one. The meaning of with sin and aggression is lying and injustice. And disobeying the Messenger, meaning opposing him. Ad-Dahhak, Mujahid, and Hamid read disobeying the Messenger in the plural. Third: The statement of God the Almighty: {And when they come to you, they greet you with that with which God has not greeted you.} There is no disagreement among the transmitters that what is meant by this is the Jews. They would come to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and say, As-samu ‘alayka, meaning outwardly “peace” but inwardly they meant death. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would say, upon you in one narration, and in another narration, upon you. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is problematic. They used to say, If Muhammad were a prophet, God would not have given us respite for our insulting and belittling him. They did not know that God the Almighty is Forbearing and does not hasten to punish one who insults Him, so how about one who insults His Prophet? It has been proven that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, “No one is more patient with harm than God. They call upon Him to have a wife and children, yet He cures them and provides for them.” So God the Almighty revealed this to uncover their secrets and disgrace their inner selves, as a miracle for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). It was proven on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas: A Jew came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions and said: Death be upon you. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, responded to him and said: Do you know what this Jew said? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: He said such and such, so return it to me. They returned it. He said: I said: As-Samu ‘Alaykum Death be upon you. He said: Yes. Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: When the People of the Book greet you, then say to you what you said. Then God the Most High revealed: And when they come to you with that with which God has not greeted you. I said: It was included by Al-Tirmidhi and he said: This is a good and authentic hadith. It was proven that Aisha said: Some Jews came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: Death be upon you, O Abu al-Qasim. I said: Death be upon you, and may God do and do to you. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Easy, O Aisha, for God does not like vulgarity or obscenity. I said: O Messenger of God, do you not see what they are saying?! He said: “Don’t you see that I respond to them with what they say by saying: ‘And upon you.’” Then this verse was revealed: With what God has not revealed to you, meaning that God has greeted you and they are saying Death be upon you, and Death is death. Narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim with the same meaning. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If the People of the Book greet you, say, ‘And upon you.’ This is how it is narrated: And upon you with the letter waw. Scholars have spoken about it because the conjunction waw implies a partner, and it is necessary that he be included with them in what they have prayed for us of death, or of the weariness of our religion, which is boredom. It is said: He is bored, “he is bored,” weariness, and wasama. Some of them said: And is redundant, just as it was added in the words of the poet: When we reached the neighborhood square and he turned away That is, when we passed, he turned away and the waw was removed. Some of them said: It is for resumption, as if he said: And death be upon you. Some of them said: It is in its proper form of conjunction, and that does not harm us, because we are answered by them and they are not answered by us, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said. [Abu] al-Zubayr narrated that he heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say: Some Jews greeted the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Death be upon you, O Abu al-Qasim. He said: And upon you as well. Aisha said angrily: Did you not hear what they said? He said: “Yes, I heard and responded to them. We respond to them but they do not respond to us.” Narrated by Muslim. The waw narration has the best meaning, and its confirmation is the most correct and well-known narration. There is a difference of opinion as to whether returning the greeting of a non-Muslim is obligatory like returning the greeting of a Muslim. This is the view of Ibn Abbas, al-Sha'bi, and Qatadah, as it was commanded. Malik, as narrated by Ashhab and Ibn Wahb, held that it is not obligatory. If you return the greeting, then say, Upon you. Ibn Tawus preferred to say when returning the greeting: "Upon you be peace," meaning, It has been lifted from you. Some of our companions chose: As-Salam with a kasra on the seen, meaning stones. What Malik said is more appropriate in following the Sunnah, and by God, Masruq narrated on the authority of Aisha, who said: Some Jews came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: As-Samu ‘Alayka, O Abu al-Qasim. He said: And upon you. Aisha said: I said: As-Samu ‘Alayka and Al-Dhamm. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Aisha, do not be obscene. She said: Did you not hear what they said? He said: Did you not respond to them as they said, saying: And upon you. In another narration, he said: Aisha became aware of them and cursed them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Enough, O Aisha, for God does not like obscenity and obscenity. He added, so God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed: And when they come to you, they greet you with that with which God has not greeted you to the end of the verse. The word dhamm with a light mim is a defect. In the proverb Never lack a good person who is blameworthy meaning a defect. It is pronounced with a hamza and without a hamza. It is said: dhamahu yadhamuhu like dhab yadhib and the passive participle is blameworthy with a hamza. From this, madhuman madhhuran (al-A’raf 7:18). It is also said: dhamah yadhimhu with a light karama yarumihu God the Almighty says: And they say among themselves, ‘Why does God not punish us for what we say?’ They said, “If Muhammad were a prophet, God would punish us for what we say. So why would God not punish us?” It was also said, They said, ‘If he responds to us and says, “And upon you is death, and death is death, had he been a prophet, his call would have been answered concerning us and we would have died.” This is a source of astonishment from them, for they were People of the Book and they knew that prophets may get angry, but punishment is not hastened for those who anger them. Hell is sufficient for them, meaning Hell is sufficient as punishment for them tomorrow. So wretched is the destination. Where is the reference?
58:9: The Almighty said: O you who have believed, when you confer privately He forbade the believers from conferring privately among themselves as the hypocrites and the Jews did, so He said: O you who have believed, when you confer privately meaning whisper to each other. Do not confer privately This is the reading of the majority. Yahya ibn Waththab, Asim, and Ruways read on the authority of Ya'qub, Do not confer privately with sin, aggression, and disobedience to the Messenger, and confer privately with righteousness meaning obedience and piety" with abstaining from what God has forbidden. It was said that the address is to the hypocrites, meaning O you who believed, according to their claim. It was also said that it means O you who believed in Moses. "And fear God, to whom you will be gathered" meaning you will be gathered in the Hereafter.
58:10: There are two issues: First: The Most High said: Indeed, the confidential conversation is only from Satan meaning from the devils’ embellishments that those who believe may grieve if they imagine that the Muslims have been harmed in the raids, or if they gather to plot against the Muslims, and perhaps they would whisper to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the Muslims would think that they were humiliating them in front of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). And it will not harm them meaning the whispering at all except by God’s permission meaning by His will. It was also said: by His knowledge. And from Ibn Abbas: by His command. And in God let the believers put their trust meaning they should entrust their affair to Him, and delegate all their matters to His help, and seek refuge in Him from Satan and from all evil, for it is He who has given power to Satan with whisperings as a trial and test for the servant, and if He had willed, He could have diverted him from him. Third: In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Ibn Omar, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If there are three, then two should not whisper to each other without one. And Abdullah bin Masoud said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you are three, then two of you should not whisper close to the other until you mix with the people, lest it sadden him. This hadith explains the ultimate prohibition, which is that the third should not find someone to talk to, as Ibn ‘Umar did. He was talking with a man, and another came wanting to talk to him privately, but he did not talk to him until he called a fourth. He and the first said to him, Stand back, and he whispered to the man who wanted to announce it. Narrated by al-Muwatta’. It also indicates the reason for his statement, In order to sadden him, meaning that something happens to him that saddens him. This is by thinking in his heart that talking about him is something he dislikes, or that they do not consider him worthy of including him in their conversation, or other such whisperings of Satan and inner conversations. All of this happens because he is alone. If someone else is with him, he is safe from that. Based on this, all numbers are equal in this regard, so four should not whisper to one, nor ten, nor a thousand, for example, because that meaning exists in his case. Rather, its existence in a large number is more possible and more likely, so the meaning is more appropriate. And three were specifically mentioned because they are the first. A number in which that meaning is achieved. The apparent meaning of the hadith includes all situations and times, and Ibn Umar, Malik and the majority held this view. Whether the whispering is about something recommended, permissible or obligatory, sadness is caused by it. Some people have said that this was in the early days of Islam, because that was the case with the hypocrites, and the hypocrites would whisper to each other, but not the believers. So when Islam spread, this was dropped. Some of them said: This is specific to traveling in places where a man does not feel safe from his companion. But in cities and among buildings, no, because he will find someone to help him, unlike traveling, which is a place where one is likely to be assassinated and without help. And God knows best.
58:11: There are seven evenings: First: The statement of God the Almighty: {O you who have believed, when you are told, Make room in assemblies,} After explaining that the Jews greeted Him in a way God did not greet Him with, and condemning them for that, He went so far as to improve etiquette in the company of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), so that they would not cramp his gathering. He ordered the Muslims to be kind and affectionate, so that they would make room for one another, so that they could listen to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and look at him. Qatadah and Mujahid said: They were competing to be in the company of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), so they were ordered to make room for one another. Ad-Dahhak said the same. Ibn Abbas said: What is meant by this is the battlefields when they lined up for war. Al-Hasan and Zayd ibn Habib said: When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) fought the polytheists, his companions would quarrel over who would be in the first row, and they would not make room for one another, out of a desire to fight and be martyred. So this verse was revealed, and it is like His saying: seats for fighting (Al Imran 3:121). Muqatil said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was in the Suffah, and the place was narrow on a Friday. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to honor the people of Badr from among the Muhajireen and Ansar. Some people from the people of Badr came, among them Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, who had been ahead in the assembly.
