They stood in front of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on their feet, waiting for space to be made for them, but they were not made room for them. This upset the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so he said to those around him who were not from Badr: Stand up, so-and-so, and you, so-and-so, equal in number to the number of people who stood up from the people of Badr. This upset those who stood up, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw the hatred in their faces. The hypocrites winked and spoke, saying: How unfair these people are! They loved to be close to their Prophet, so they were ahead in the place. So this verse was revealed. God the Almighty said this verse. Tafashu means make room for each other. “So-and-so made room for his brother in his sitting place, meaning he made room for him. From this comes the saying: A spacious city and you have space in such-and-such. “Fasa yasfaha” is like mana’a means he made room in the sitting place. Fasa yasfaha is like karama means he became spacious. From this comes the word a spacious place. Second: As-Salami, Zur ibn Hubaysh and Asim read it in al-majalis. Qatada, Dawud ibn Abi Hind and Al-Hasan read it differently from him: If it is said to you, ‘Space out,’ the rest [of the people] make space in the assemblies. So whoever uses the plural, it is because his statement, Space out in the assemblies indicates that each one has a seat. The same applies if what is meant by it is war. Likewise, it is permissible for what is meant by the Prophet’s Mosque (peace and blessings be upon him) to be plural because each one sitting has a seat. Likewise, it is permissible for what is meant by the singular assemblies is the Prophet’s Mosque (peace and blessings be upon him), and it is permissible for what is meant by the plural according to the general principle, like their saying: The dinar and dirham have multiplied. I said that the correct interpretation of the verse is that it is general in every gathering in which Muslims gather for good and reward, whether it is a gathering of war, remembrance, or a gathering on Friday, then each one has more right to the place he reached first. “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Whoever reaches something that no one else has reached has more right to it.’ But one should make room for his brother so long as that does not cause him harm and make him leave his place because of the narrowness. Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: A man should not get up from his seat and then sit in it. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade a man from getting up from his seat in another, but rather make room and spread out. Ibn Umar disliked a man getting up from his seat and then sitting in his place. Wording by Al-Bukhari. Third: If one of the people sits in a place in the mosque, it is not permissible for someone else to make him stand until he sits in his place, because Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr on the authority of Jabir on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “None of you should make his brother stand on Friday and then go back to his seat and sit in it, but rather say, ‘Make room.’” Branch: The rule regarding a place: If someone stands up so that someone else can sit in his place, his place is his place. If the place he stood up to is like the first one in hearing the imam’s words, then that is not disliked for him. But if it is further away from the imam, then that is disliked for him, because it means missing out on his share. Fourth: If a person orders another person to go early to the mosque and he finds a place for him to sit in, it is not disliked. Then when the order comes, he gets up from the place, because it was narrated that Ibn Sirin used to send a boy to his gathering on Friday and he would sit for him in it, and when he came, he would get up from it for him. Branch: Based on this, whoever sends a rug or prayer rug and it is spread out for him in a place in the mosque. Fifth: Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If one of you stands up - and in the hadith of Abu ‘Uwanah, he stands up from his seat - then returns to it, he has more right to it. Our scholars said: This indicates the correctness of the statement that the one sitting should have his place reserved for him until he stands up from it, because if he has more right to it after he stands up, then the one sitting down is more entitled to it and more deserving. It has been said that this is recommended, because it is a place that no one owns before or after sitting down, and this is questionable, which is to say: We accept that it is not his property, but he has it reserved for him until he has fulfilled his purpose from it, so it is as if he owns its benefit, if he has prevented someone else from competing with him for it. And God knows best. Sixth: The Almighty’s statement: God will make room for you meaning in your graves. It was also said: in your hearts. It was also said: He will make room for you in this world and the Hereafter. And when it is said, ‘Rise,’ then rise. Nafi’, Ibn ‘Amir, and ‘Aasim read it with a damma on the sheen in both of them. The rest read it with a kasra, and they are two dialects like they dedicate themselves (Al-A’raf 7:138) and they erect (Al-A’raf 7:137). The meaning is rise for prayer, jihad, and doing good deeds, as stated by most of the commentators. Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak said: When the call to prayer is made, then rise for it. This is because some men were reluctant to pray, so it was revealed. Al-Hasan and Mujahid also said: Meaning, rise for war. Ibn Zayd said: This was in the house of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Every man among them would like his last meeting with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to be that. So God, the Almighty, said: And when it is said, ‘Rise,’ then rise, about the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Then rise, because he has needs, so do not delay. Qatada said: The meaning is: respond if you are called to a good command. This is the correct view because it is general. Nashz is rising, taken from the earth’s nashz, which means its elevation. It is said nashaz yanshiz or yanshiz if he moves away from his place, meaning he rose from it. A woman is nashiz who has abandoned her husband. The origin of this is from nashz, and nashz is what rose from the earth and moved away, mentioned by An-Nahhas. Seventh: The Almighty’s statement: God will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, by degrees. That is, in reward in the Hereafter and in honor in this world. He will raise the believer above the non-believer and the scholar above the non-scholar. Ibn Mas’ud said that God praised the scholars in this verse. The meaning is that God will raise those who have been given knowledge above those who have believed but not been given knowledge, by degrees, that is, degrees in their religion, if they do what they are commanded to do. It was said that the wealthy disliked being crowded by those wearing wool, so they would race to the Prophet’s (blessings and peace of God be upon him) assembly, so the addressee was them. “The Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) saw a wealthy man clutching his garment in anger at some poor man who wanted to sit with him, so he said: O so-and-so, I feared that your misfortune or his poverty would reach him. This verse shows that elevation with God Almighty is through knowledge and faith, not by being the first to reach the head of gatherings. It was said that by those who have been given knowledge, He meant those who have recited the Qur’an. Yahya ibn Yahya said on the authority of Malik: “God will raise those who have believed among you” meaning the Companions and those who have been given knowledge by degrees by which God will raise the scholar and the seeker of truth. I said: The general meaning is more likely to apply to this issue and more deserving of the meaning of the verse. The believer is raised by his faith first, then by his learning. In Sahih it is narrated that Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him used to place Abdullah ibn Abbas before the Companions, so they spoke to him about that. He called them and invited him, and asked them about the interpretation of {When there comes the help of God and the conquest} (al-Nasr 110:1), but they remained silent. Ibn Abbas said: It is the term of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) that God has informed him of. Umar said: I do not know of it except what you learn. In Bukhari it is narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abbas that he said: Uyaynah ibn Hisn ibn Hudhayf ibn Badr came and stayed with his nephew, Al-Hur ibn Qays ibn Hisn. He was one of the men whom Umar brought close to him, and the reciters of Quran were the companions of Umar’s gatherings and consultations, whether they were old or young. The hadith has already been mentioned at the end of Surat Al-A’raf. In Sahih Muslim it is narrated that Nafi’ ibn Abd al-Rith met Umar in Usfan, and Umar had appointed him over Mecca. He said: Whom have you appointed over the people of the valley? He said: Ibn Abza. Umar said: Who is Ibn Abza? He said: One of our clients. He said: So you appointed a client over them! He said: He is a reciter of the Book of God and he is knowledgeable about the inheritance laws. Omar said: Your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God raises some people with this book and lowers others with it. The beginning of the book has already passed, and praise be to God. It was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Between the scholar and the worshipper are one hundred degrees. Between every two degrees, a well-prepared horse is present for seventy years. “And it was narrated from him, may God bless him and grant him peace: The superiority of the scholar over the worshipper is like the superiority of the moon on the night of the full moon over all the other planets. “And on his authority, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him: Three will intercede on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:the prophets, then the martyrs. “Their status is greater because they are an intermediary between prophethood and martyrdom, as is the testimony of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. On the authority of Ibn Abbas: Solomon, peace be upon him, was given the choice between knowledge, wealth, and kingship, and he chose knowledge, so he was given wealth and kingship with it.
58:12: There are three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, when you speak privately to the Messenger, “conferring” means you whisper. Ibn Abbas said: This was revealed because the Muslims kept asking the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) questions to the point that they became difficult for him. God Almighty wanted to make things easier for His Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), but when he said that, many people stopped. Then God expanded upon them with the verse that follows it. Al-Hasan said: This was revealed because some Muslims used to confide in the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and converse with him. Some Muslims thought that they were belittling them in their private conversations, so this was difficult for them, so God commanded them to give charity when they conferred privately to stop them from seeking his private conversations. Zayd ibn Aslam said: This was revealed because the hypocrites and the Jews used to confide in the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and say that he was an ear who heard everything that was said to him, yet he did not prevent anyone from confiding in him. This was difficult for the Muslims because Satan was making them believe that they were confiding in him by saying that groups had gathered to fight him. He said: Then God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed: O you who have believed, when you confer privately, do not confer privately about sin and aggression and disobedience to the Messenger (al-An’am 2:17). But they did not desist, so God revealed this verse. The people of falsehood desisted from private conversation, because they did not offer charity before their private conversation. This was difficult for the people of faith, and they refrained from private conversation, because many of them were unable to give charity. So God made things easier for them with what follows the verse. Second: Ibn al-Arabi said: “This report from Zayd indicates that rulings are not based on public interest, as God the Almighty said: ‘That is better for you and purer,’ then He abrogated it even though it was better and purer.” This is a great refutation of the Mu’tazila regarding its commitment to public interest, but the narrator of the hadith from Zayd was his son Abd al-Rahman, and scholars have declared him weak. The matter in God the Almighty’s statement: ‘That is better for you and purer,’ is a well-known refutation of the Mu’tazila. And God knows best.” Third: Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ali bin Alqamah Al-Anmari, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, who said: When the verse, O you who have believed, when you confer privately with the Messenger, present before your private conversation an amount of charity, was revealed, I asked him. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to me, What do you think of a dinar? I said, They cannot afford it. He said, Then half a dinar. I said, They cannot afford it. He said, Then how much? I said, A barley grain. He said, You are indeed insignificant. He said, Then the verse, Did you fear to present before your private conversation an amount of charity?" was revealed. He said, "Through me God lightened the burden on this nation." Abu 'Eisa said: This is a good and strange hadith. We only know it from this source. The meaning of his saying, "a barley grain" means the weight of a barley grain of gold. Ibn al-'Arabi said: This indicates two good issues of the principles of jurisprudence: the first - invalidating an act of worship before performing it. The second - considering the amounts by analogy, contrary to Abu Hanifa. I said: It appears that the abrogation occurred after the charity was done. It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid that the first one to give charity in this regard was the son of Abu Talib, may God be pleased with him, who spoke privately with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was narrated that he gave a ring in charity. Al-Qushayri and others mentioned on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib that he said: In the Book of God there are verses that no one before me did, and no one after me will do, and they are: O you who have believed, when you confer privately with the Messenger, present before your private conversation an amount of charity. I had a dinar which I sold, and whenever I conferred privately with the Messenger, I would give a dirham in charity until it ran out. Then it was abrogated by the other verse: Do you fear to present before your private conversation an amount of charity? Ibn Abbas said the same thing: God abrogated it with the verse that comes after it. Ibn Umar said: “Ali may God be pleased with him had three things, if I had just one of them, it would have been dearer to me than red camels: his marriage to Fatimah, his being given the banner on the day of Khaybar, and the verse of private conversation. “That is better for you” meaning than withholding it, and purer for your hearts from sins. But if you cannot find anything” meaning the poor, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.
58:13: There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Did you fear? The meaning of estimation is to be apprehensive. Ibn Abbas said: Did you fear? That is, you were stingy with charity. It was also said: you feared. Fear is the fear of something unpleasant. That is, you feared and were stingy with charity. It was also said: you feared. Fear is the fear of something unpleasant. That is, you feared and were stingy with charity, and it was difficult for you. To present alms before your private conversation. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: This was only for ten nights, then it was abrogated. Al-Kalbi said: This was only for one night. Ibn Abbas said: There remained only an hour of the day until it was abrogated. Qatada said the same. And God knows best. The second is the saying of God the Almighty: {But if you do not, and God has forgiven you} meaning, God abrogated that ruling. This is addressed to whoever finds something to give in charity. {Then establish prayer and give zakat} so the obligation of zakat abrogated this charity. This indicates the permissibility of abrogation before action. What was narrated from Ali may God be pleased with him is weak, because God the Almighty said: {But if you do not,} this indicates that no one gave anything in charity. And God knows best. {And obey God} in His obligations, {and His Messenger} in His Sunnah, {and God is Acquainted with what you do}.
58:14: The Almighty said: Have you not considered those who took as allies a people with whom God has become angry? Qatadah said: They are the hypocrites who took as allies the Jews. They are not of you, nor of them. He says: The hypocrites are not of the Jews, nor are the Muslims of their time with them. Al-Sudri and Muqatil said: This was revealed regarding Abdullah ibn Ubayy and Abdullah ibn Nabtal, the hypocrites. One of them used to sit with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and then relay his conversation to the Jews. While the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was in one of his rooms, he said: A man with a heavy heart and a tyrant will enter upon you just now, looking with the eyes of a devil. Abdullah ibn Nabtal entered - and he was short, dark-skinned, and had a light beard. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Why do you and your companions revile me? He swore by God that he had not done that. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: I have done it. He left and brought his companions, and they swore by God that they had not reviled him. This was then revealed. Ibn Abbas said the same meaning. Narrated by Ikrimah on his authority: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting in the shade of a tree, the shade almost shrinking from him, when he said: “A blue-eyed man will come to you this hour, looking at you with the gaze of Satan.” We were like that when a blue-eyed man approached, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called for him and said: Why do you and your companions curse me? He said: Let me bring them to you. So he passed by and brought them, and they all swore that none of that had happened. Then God Almighty revealed: The Day God will resurrect them all, except for His saying: They are the losers. The Jews are mentioned in the Qur’an with the wrath of God upon them.
58:15: God has prepared for them meaning for these hypocrites a severe punishment in Hell, which is the lowest level. Evil indeed is what they used to do meaning evil are their deeds.
58:16: They took their oaths as a shield to protect themselves from being killed. Al-Hasan and Abu Al-Aaliyah read their oaths with a kasra over the hamza here and in Al-Munafiqun. That is, they took their confession as a shield, so their tongues believed out of fear of being killed and their hearts disbelieved. So for them is a humiliating punishment in this world by being killed and in the Hereafter by the Fire. And turning away means preventing from the path of God meaning from Islam. It was said: And in killing them for disbelief because of what they displayed of hypocrisy. It was also said: That is, by spreading rumors and discouraging Muslims from jihad and frightening them.
58:17: God the Almighty says: Neither their wealth nor their children will avail them at all against God meaning against His punishment at all. Muqatil said: The hypocrites said: Muhammad claims that he will be victorious on the Day of Resurrection. Then we will be doomed! By God, we will surely be victorious on the Day of Resurrection with ourselves, our children and our wealth, if there is to be a Resurrection. So the verse: The Day God will resurrect them all was revealed, meaning, a humiliating punishment will be theirs on the Day He resurrects them. And they will swear to Him as they swear to you today. This is an amazing matter, which is their deception with oaths tomorrow, and definite knowledge has become essential. Ibn Abbas said: It is their saying: By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists (Al-An'am 6:23). And they think that they are on something with their denial and their oaths. Ibn Zayd said: They thought that it would benefit them in the Hereafter. It was said: And they think in this world that they are on something because in the Hereafter they will know the truth by compulsion. The first is more apparent. And “on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: On the Day of Resurrection, a crier will call out, “Where are the opponents of God?” Then the Qadarites will stand up with black faces and blue eyes, slanting jaws, and their saliva dripping. They will say, By God, we have not worshipped any sun or moon besides You, nor have we taken any god besides You. Ibn Abbas said, By God, they have spoken the truth! Polytheism came to them from where they did not know. Then he recited, “And they think that they are upon something. Unquestionably, it is they who are the liars.” They are, by God, the Qadarites. Three times.
58:19: The Almighty says: Satan has overcome them meaning he has prevailed and become powerful, meaning with his whisperings in this world. It was also said: Strong and All-Knowing. Al-Munfadil said: He surrounded them. A fourth possibility is that he has gathered them and brought them together. It is said: He gathered something meaning he gathered it and brought some of it together. If someone gathers them, then he has overcome them, become powerful over them, and surrounded them. And made them forget the remembrance of God meaning His commands to act in obedience to Him. It was also said: His prohibitions and the prohibition against disobeying Him. Forgetting may mean heedlessness, or it may mean abandonment, and both interpretations are valid here. Those are the party of Satan meaning his group and his clan. Unquestionably, the party of Satan - they are the losers in their transaction, because they sold Paradise for Hell, and sold guidance for misguidance.
58:20: The Almighty said: Indeed, those who oppose God and His Messenger is mentioned at the beginning of the Surah. Those are among the most humiliated meaning among the humiliated, none is more humiliated than them. God has decreed, I will surely prevail" meaning God has decreed that. It was also said: It was written in the Preserved Tablet, on the authority of Qatada. Al-Farraa' said: "wrote" means said. "I" is an emphasis. "And My messengers" will be sent from them with war, for they will be victorious by war, and whoever is sent from them with proof, then he will be victorious by proof. Muqatil said: The believers said: If God opens for us Makkah, Dhaif, Khaybar and what is around them, we hope that God will purify us against the Persians and the Romans. Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul said: Do you think that the Romans and Persians are like the towns that you defeated?! By God, they are more numerous and more powerful than you think of them. So the verse, I will surely prevail, I and My messengers, was revealed. Similar to it is: “And Our word has already gone forth for Our servants, the messengers. Indeed, they will be the victorious. And indeed, Our soldiers will be the predominant.” (al-Saffat 37:172)
58:22: There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: You will not find a people who believe in God and the Last Day loving “Where do they love and befriend” whoever opposes God and His Messenger “even if they were their fathers” “Al-Suddi said: It was revealed about Abdullah ibn Abdullah ibn Ubayy. He sat with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the man, may God bless him and grant him peace, drank some water. He said to him: By God, O Messenger of God, what left of your drink so that I may save it for my father, perhaps God will purify his heart with it? So he brought it to him. Abdullah said to him: What is this? He said: It is the leftover drink of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. I have brought it to you so that you may drink it, perhaps God will purify your heart with it. His father said to him: Why don’t you bring me your mother’s urine, for it is purer than her? He became angry and came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God! Did you not give me permission to kill my father? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Rather, be gentle with him and treat him well.” Ibn Jurayj said: I was told that Abu Quhafah cursed the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and his son Abu Bakr slapped him so hard that he fell on his face. Then he came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and mentioned that to him. He said: Or did you do it? Do not do it again. He said: By Him who tells you the truth, if the slap was close to me, I would have killed him. Ibn Mas`ud said: This was revealed about Abu `Ubaydah and Abu `Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah. He killed his father, `Abdullah ibn al-Jarrah, on the day of Uhud, and it was said, on the day of Badr. Al-Jarrah would stand up to Abu `Ubaydah, but Abu `Ubaydah would avoid him. When he increased his attacks, Abu `Ubaydah went after him and killed him. Then God revealed when he killed his father: You will not find a people who believe in God and the Last Day (al-Baqarah 2:17). Al-Waqidi said: This is what the people of Ash-Sham say. I asked a man from Banu al-Harith ibn Qahr, and they said: His father died before Islam. Or their sons means: Abu Bakr called his son `Abdullah to duel on the day of Badr, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Enjoy yourself, O Abu Bakr. Do you not know that you are to me like my hearing and sight?” Or their brothers meaning Mus’ab ibn Umair who killed his brother Ubayd ibn Umair on the day of Badr. Or their clan meaning Umar ibn al-Khattab who killed his maternal uncle al-Aas ibn Hisham ibn al-Mughira on the day of Badr, and Ali and Hamza who killed Utbah, Shaiba and al-Walid on the day of Badr. It was said that the verse was revealed about Hatib ibn Abi Balta’ah, when he wrote to the people of Mecca about a march. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the master of the conquest, as will be explained at the beginning of Surat Al-Mumtahanah, God willing. He explained that faith is corrupted by befriending infidels, even if they are relatives. Second: Malik, may God have mercy on him, used this verse as evidence of hostility toward the Qadarites and avoiding sitting with them. Ashhab said on the authority of Malik: “Do not sit with the Qadarites and be hostile to them for the sake of God, because God Almighty says: ‘You will not find a people who believe in God and the Last Day having affection for those who oppose God and His Messenger.’” I said: The meaning of the people of destiny includes all the people of injustice and aggression. It was narrated on the authority of al-Thawri that he said: They used to think that it was revealed about those who accompanied the sultan. It was narrated on the authority of Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Dawud that he met al-Mansur during the circumambulation and when he recognized him, he ran away from him and recited it. “And it was narrated on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he used to say: O God, do not grant a sinner any favor with me, for I have found in it that it was revealed, ‘You will not find a people who believe in God and the Last Day’ - to His saying - ‘Those are the ones in whose hearts He has inscribed faith’” meaning, He has created in their hearts belief, meaning those who do not befriend those who oppose God. It was said: He wrote down, as al-Rabi’ ibn Anas said. It was also said: He made, like the saying of God the Almighty, ‘So register us among the witnesses’ (Al Imran 3:53) meaning, make us. And His statement: So I will prescribe it for those who fear God (al-A’raf 7:156). It was said: He wrote means to gather, and from this comes he wrote and the nun of iman was placed in the accusative case with the meaning God wrote, and this is the best opinion, due to the statement of God the Most High: And supported them with a spirit from Him. Abu Al-A’li, Zaid bin Habash, and Al-Mufaddal from Asim read kataba for what the agent is not named, iman, by raising the nun. Raz bin Habash and their ashirahim read it with an alif and a kasra on the ta for the plural, and Al-A’mash narrated it from Abu Bakr from Asim. It was said: He wrote in their hearts, meaning on their hearts, as in his verse: in the trunks of palm trees (Ta-Ha 20:71). He mentioned the hearts specifically because they are the seat of faith. And He supported them, strengthened them, and aided them with a spirit from Him. Al-Hasan said: and with victory from Him. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: with the Qur’an and its proofs. Ibn Jurayj said: with light, faith, proof, and guidance. It was also said: with mercy from God. Some of them said: He supported them with Gabriel, peace be upon him, “And will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. God is pleased with them,” meaning before their deeds. And they are pleased with Him, “rejoiced in what He gave them.” “Those are the party of God. Unquestionably, the party of God - they are the successful ones.” Saad bin Abi Saeed Al-Jurjani said on the authority of some of his sheikhs: David, peace be upon him, said: My God! Who are your party and around your throne? So God revealed to him: “O David, their eyes are angry, their hearts are pure, their hands are sound. Those are my party and around my forest.”
59:1: "Ibn Abbas narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever recites Surat Al-Hashr, nothing will remain of Paradise, Hell, the Throne, the Footstool, the heavens, the earth, the insects, the wind, the clouds, the birds, the beasts, the trees, the mountains, the sun, the moon, and the angels, but that they will pray for him and seek forgiveness for him. If he dies that day or night, he will die a martyr." Narrated by Al-Tha'labi. Al-Tha'labi narrated on the authority of Yazid Al-Raqashi on the authority of Anas: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘From the end of Surat al-Hashr, “If We had sent down this Qur’an upon a mountain” (al-Hashr 59:21) - to the end - and he died that night, he would have died a martyr.” Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ma’qil ibn Yasar who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever says three times in the morning, I seek refuge in God, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from Satan the accursed, and recites three verses from the end of Surat al-Hashr, God will assign seventy thousand angels to pray for him until the evening, and he will die during that day as a martyr. And whoever recites it in the evening, the same applies.’” He said: A good, uncomplicated hadith. God Almighty says: “Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth exalts God. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.”
59:2: The Almighty’s saying: It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes. There are three issues in this: First: The Almighty’s saying: It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes. Saeed bin Jubair said: I said to Ibn Abbas: What is Surah Al-Hashra? He said: “Say: Surah An-Nadir.” They were a group of Jews from the descendants of Aaron, peace be upon him, who settled in Medina during the persecutions of the Children of Israel, awaiting Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Their affair was as God has clearly stated. The second: The Almighty’s saying: For the first gathering. The gathering is the plural, and it has four aspects: two evils in this world and two gatherings in the Hereafter. As for the one in this world, the Almighty’s saying: It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes for the first gathering. Al-Zuhri said: They were from a tribe that had not been exiled, and God Almighty had decreed exile for them, and if it were not for that, He would have punished them in this world, and the first gathering they were gathered to in this world would have been to Ash-Sham. Ibn Abbas and Ikrimah said: Whoever doubts that the place of gathering will be in Ash-Sham, let him read this verse: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Go out. They said: Where to? He said: To the place of gathering. Qatada said: This is the first gathering. Ibn Abbas said: They are the first of the People of the Book to be gathered and expelled from their homes. It was said: They were expelled to Khaybar, and that the meaning of the first gathering is their expulsion from their fortresses to Khaybar, and the last of it is Umar may God be pleased with him expelling them from Khaybar to Najd and Adhraat. It was also said: Tayma and Jericho, and that was because of their disbelief and breaking their covenant. As for the second gathering, it will be their gathering close to the Resurrection. Qatada said: A fire will come and gather the people from the east to the west, spending the night with them where they spent the night, and resting with them where they rested, and eating from them whoever stayed behind. This is confirmed in Sahih, and we have mentioned it in The Book of Remembrance. Ibn Wahb narrated something similar from Malik, who said: I said to Malik: Will they be expelled from their homes? He said to me: The gathering on the Day of Resurrection will be the gathering of the Jews. He said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) expelled the Jews to Khaybar when they were asked about wealth and they concealed it, so he made it permissible for them to do so. Ibn al-Arabi said: The gathering has a beginning, a middle, and an end. The first is the expulsion of Banu al-Nadir, the middle is the expulsion of Khaybar, and the end is the gathering on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Hasan said: They are Banu Qurayzah. The rest of the commentators disagreed with him and said: Banu Qurayzah were not gathered together, but they were killed. Narrated by al-Tha’labi. Third: Al-Kaya al-Tabari said: “Reconciling with the people of war on the basis of evacuation from their homes without anything is not permissible now. Rather, that was in the beginning of Islam and then it was abrogated. Now, it is necessary to fight them, take them captive, or impose the jizya on them.” God the Almighty says: {You did not think that they would come out} meaning the greatness of the matter of the Jews and their strength and power in the hearts of the Muslims, and their unity of word. {And they thought that their fortresses would protect them} It was said: They are Al-Watih, Antah, As-Salam, and Al-Katibah. {From God} meaning from His command. They were people of many weapons - meaning many weapons - and their fortresses were impregnable, so nothing could protect them from them. {So God came to them} meaning His command and His punishment. {From where they did not expect} meaning they did not suspect. It was also said: From where they did not know. It was also said: {From where they did not expect} by killing Ka`b ibn Al-Ashraf, as stated by Ibn Jurayj, As-Suddi, and Abu Salih. God the Almighty said: And He cast terror into their hearts by killing their master Ka’b bin al-Ashraf. The one who killed him was Muhammad bin Maslama, and Abu Nailah Salkan bin Salamah bin Waqash - who was Ka’b bin al-Ashraf’s foster brother - and Ibad bin Bishr bin Waqash, and al-Harith bin Aws bin Muadh, and Abu Isa bin Jabr. His story is well-known in the biography. In the Sahih: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was aided by terror within a distance of a month’s journey. So how could he not be aided by terror within a distance of a mile’s journey from Medina to the Banu Nadir area? This is specific to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and not to anyone else. God the Almighty said: They destroy their homes. The general reading is with a light pronunciation of akhrab, meaning they demolish. As-Salami, Al-Hasan, Nasr ibn Asim, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Qatada and Abu Amr read yukharibun with a shaddah from takhreeb. Abu Amr said: I chose the shaddah because ikhrab means leaving something in ruins without a static pronunciation. Banu Nadir did not leave it in ruins, but rather they destroyed it by demolishing it. This is supported by God the Almighty's statement: with their own hands and the hands of the believers. Others said: Destruction and Ikhrab have the same meaning, and emphasis has the meaning of multiplying. Sibawayh narrated that the meanings of Fa`ala and Af`alat alternate, like Akhrabtuhu I destroyed it and Kharabtuhu I ruined it and Afrahtuhu I made it happy and Farahtuhu I made it happy. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim preferred the former. Qatada and Ad-Dahhak said: The believers were destroying from the outside in order to enter, and the Jews were destroying from the inside in order to rebuild what had been destroyed of their fortress. It was reported that they made peace with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that they would not be against him or for him. When he appeared on the day of Badr, they said: He is the prophet described in the Torah, so do not return his banner. When the Muslims were defeated on the day of Uhud, they doubted and broke their promise. Ka`b ibn al-Ashraf went out to Mecca with forty riders, and the Quraysh formed an alliance against him at the Ka`ba. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered Muhammad ibn Maslama al-Ansari to kill Ka`b by treachery, then attacked them with battalions at dawn. He said to them: Get out of Medina. They said: Death is more beloved to us than that, so they called for war. It was said that they asked God's Messenger (peace be upon him) for ten days to prepare to leave, so Abdullah bin Abi Al-Munafiq and his companions sent word to them: Do not leave the fortress, for if they fight you, we are with you and will not abandon you, and if you leave, we will leave with you. So they trained in the alleys and fortified them for twenty-one nights. When God cast terror into their hearts and they despaired of the victory of the hypocrites, they asked for peace, but he refused them anything except evacuation, as will be explained. Al-Zuhri, Ibn Zayd, and Urwah bin Al-Zubayr said: When the Prophet (peace be upon him) made peace with them on the condition that they would have what the camels could carry, they preferred the wood and columns, so they would demolish their houses and load them on their camels, and the believers would destroy the rest. Zayd also said: They would destroy them so that the Muslims would not inhabit them after them. Ibn Abbas said: Whenever the Muslims gained control of one of their houses, they would demolish it to expand the area of fighting. They would dig through their houses from one end to the next to fortify themselves in them, and they would throw stones at those from which they had expelled the Muslims. It was also said: To fill their livelihoods. Ikrimah said: With their own hands, they would destroy their interiors and what was inside them so that the Muslims would not take them. And with the hands of the believers, they would destroy their exterior so that they could gain access to them. Ikrimah said: Their houses were decorated, so they envied the Muslims for living in them. So they destroyed them from within, and the Muslims destroyed them from without. It was also said: They would destroy their houses by breaking the promise, and with the hands of the believers in expelling them from them. Ibn al-Arabi said: If corruption is done by hand, it is literal, and if it is done by breaking the covenant, it is a metaphor. However, al-Zuhri’s statement about the metaphor is more appropriate than the statement of Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’. God the Almighty said: So take heed, you who have vision. That is, take heed, you who have intellects and minds. It was also said: O you who witnessed that with your own eyes, so it is the plural of sight. Among the considerations here is that they took refuge in the fortresses of God’s wealth so that God would bring them down from them. Among the aspects of this is that He sent over them someone who had their sight. Among the aspects also is that they destroyed their wealth with their own hands. Whoever does not take heed from others will take heed within himself. In the correct proverbs: Happy is he who takes heed from others.
59:3: The Almighty said: And had it not been that God decreed upon them exile meaning, were it not that He would exile them from their home, and that they would remain for a period, some of them believing and some of them would have children who would believe. He would have punished them in this world meaning, by killing and captivity, as He did with Banu Qurayzah. Exile is leaving one's homeland. It is said: He expelled himself, exiling, and his exiling someone else, exiling. The difference between exiling and leaving, even though their meanings in terms of banishment are the same, is in two aspects: First, that exiling is when one is with one's family and children, while expulsion may be while one's family and children remain. Second, that exiling is only for a group, while exiling can be for one person or a group, as Al-Mawardi said.
59:4: The Almighty said: That meaning that is the clarification is because they opposed God meaning they opposed Him and disobeyed His command. And whoever opposes God Talha bin Masraf and Muhammad bin Al-Sameeq read and whoever opposes God with the doubling apparent as in Al-Anfal, and the rest assimilated it.
59:5: It contains five issues: First: The Almighty’s statement: What you cut down of palm trees is in the accusative case with cut down, as if he said: What did you cut down? That is because when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) descended upon the fortresses of Banu Nadir - which was Al-Buwayrah - when they broke the covenant with Quraysh to aid him on the Day of Uhud, he ordered their palm trees to be cut down and burned. They differed on the number of those. Qatadah and Ad-Dahhak said that they cut down six of their palm trees and burned one. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said that they cut down one palm tree and burned another. That was with the approval of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) or by his order, either because it weakened them or because the place was spacious enough to cut them down. That upset them, so they - the Jews of the People of the Book - said: O Muhammad, don’t you claim that you are a prophet seeking reform? Is cutting down palm trees and burning trees considered reform? And have you found in what God revealed to you permission to spread corruption on earth?! That upset the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The believers found themselves in such a state that they differed. Some of them said, Do not sever what God has bestowed upon us. Some of them said, Sever it so that we may enrage them thereby. So the verse was revealed confirming those who forbade severing ties and relieving those who sever ties from sin. It informed them that severing ties and abandoning them are by God’s permission. Their poet, Samak the Jew, said about this: Did we not inherit the wise Book during the time of Moses and did we not turn away? You are shepherds of lean sheep in the plains of Tihama and Al-Akhif. You see the care we provide for you in every age that is unfair to you Oh witnesses, stop injustice and abhorrent logic. Perhaps the nights and the passage of time will show us who is just and fair. By killing the Nadir and expelling them and hamstringing the Nakhir and not picking it Hassan bin Thabit answered him: He lost a group of people who supported the Quraysh, but they had no supporter in their own town. They brought the Book and then neglected it, and they are blind to the Torah. You disbelieved in the Qur’an and refused to believe what the warner said. The fire in Bouira was so widespread that it was easy for the leaders of Bani Luay Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib answered him: May God perpetuate this act and burn its regions with fire. You will know which of us is better and which of our lands will be better If the palm trees were riders, they would say, You have no place to stay. So move on. Second: The departure of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was in Rabi` al-Awwal of the fourth year of the Hijra. They fortified themselves in fortresses, and he ordered the cutting down and burning of palm trees. At that time, the prohibition of alcohol was revealed. Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul and the hypocrites who were with him sent a message to Banu Nadir: We are with you, and if you are fought, we will fight with you, and if you are expelled, we will go out with you. They were deceived by that, but when the truth came, they abandoned them, surrendered them, and threw themselves into their hands. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) asked to spare their blood and deport them, on the condition that they would be entitled to whatever their camels carried of their wealth except weapons. They carried that to Khaybar, and some of them went to Ash-Sham. Among those who went to Khaybar were their leaders, such as Huyayy bin Akhtal, Salam bin Abi Al-Haqiq, and Kinanah bin Ar-Rabi`, and Khaybar surrendered to them. Third: It was proven in Sahih Muslim and other books on the authority of Ibn Umar that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cut down the palm trees of Banu Nadir and burned them. Hassan said about this: The fire in Bouira was so widespread that it was easy for the leaders of Bani Luay And in that regard the verse was revealed: What you cut down of palm trees People differed regarding destroying the enemy’s house, burning it, and cutting off its fruits. There are two opinions: The first is that it is permissible, as stated in Al-Mudawwana. The second is that if the Muslims know that it is theirs, they do not do it, but if they despair of it, they do it. Malik stated this in Al-Wadiha. The followers of Al-Shafi’i and Ibn Al-Arabi argue about this. The first opinion is correct. The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) knew that the palm trees of Banu Nadir were his, but he cut them down and burned them to spite them and weaken them so that they would leave. Destroying some of the wealth for the benefit of the rest is permissible according to Islamic law and is intended according to reason. Fourth - Al-Mawardi said: This verse is evidence that every ijtihadist will have a share. Al-Kaya al-Tabari said the same, saying: Even if ijtihad was considered excessive in such a case when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was among them, there is no doubt that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw that and remained silent, so they received the ruling from his confirmation. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is false, because the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was with them, and there is no ijtihad in the presence of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Rather, it indicates the ijtihad of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in matters that were not revealed to him, taking into account the generality of harming the disbelievers, and giving permission to everyone to do what would lead to their invasion and destruction, as God the Almighty says: And to disgrace the wicked. Fifth - There is a difference of opinion regarding what the soft date is, with ten opinions: The first: It is the entire palm tree except the old one, as stated by Az-Zuhri, Malik, Saeed bin Jubair, Ikrimah and Al-Khalil. It is narrated from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Al-Hasan: It is the entire palm tree, and they did not exclude Ajwa or others. It is also narrated from Ibn Abbas: It is a type of palm tree. It is narrated from Ath-Thawri: It is the most noble of palm trees. It is narrated from Abu Ubaidah: It is all types of dates except Ajwa and Barni. Jaafar bin Muhammad said: It is Ajwa specifically. It is mentioned that Al-Ateeq and Ajwa were with Noah, peace be upon him, in the ark. Al-Ateeq is the male. Ajwa is the origin of all females, and that is why it was difficult for the Jews to cut it down. Al-Mawardi narrated it. It is also said that it is a type of palm tree whose dates are called Al-Lawn color, its dates are the best of dates, and they are very yellow, the stone can be seen from the outside and the molars are absent in it. They prefer the young palm tree from it to the young palm tree. It is also said that it is the palm tree that is close to the ground. Al-Akhfash recited: The dove made me sad when it sang of the separation of the beloved from above It was said: The soft seedling is softer than the palm tree. From this comes the poet’s saying: They planted its softness in a certain channel, then surrounded the palm trees with thickets. It was said: All soft trees are soft due to their softness in life. Dhu al-Rummah said: The path of fears is soft and the dew of the night is trickling in his feathers And the tenth saying - that it is the date palm, said Al-Asma’i. He said: The people of Medina say that tables are not puffed until colors are present, meaning date palms. Ibn Al-Arabi said: What Al-Zuhri and Malik said is correct for two reasons: First - that they know their country and its trees. Second - that the derivation is wrong, and the linguists correct it, because the weight of the word laina is lawnhu, and it became weak according to their roots and turned into layna so it is lawn. So if the letter ha is added, its first letter is broken, like barak Al-sadr with a fatha on the ba and barakah with a kasra on it because of the letter ha. And it was said that layna is originally lawna, but the waw became a ya because of the kasra of the letter before it. The plural of layna is layn. And it was said: layyan. Imru’ Al-Qais said, describing the neck of his horse: A story like the crushing of soft wood, in which the misguided one set the price on fire Al-Akhfash said: It was named Layna because of its color, not because of softness. Al-Mahdawi said: There is a difference of opinion about its derivation. Some say it is from color and its root is lawna. Others say its root is Layna from laana yaleen. Abdullah read Ma qata’tum min Layna wa la tarkatum quma’a ‘ala asuluha, meaning standing on its stalks. Al-A’mash read Ma qata’tum min Layna or tarkatumuha quma’a ‘ala asuluha, meaning you did not cut it. It was read Qawma’ according to its root. There are two interpretations: One of them is that it is the plural of asl, karhan and rahn. The second is that the damma is sufficient instead of the waw. It was read Qayman according to its root, going with the word ma. By the permission of God means by His command. And to disgrace the wicked meaning to humiliate the disbelieving Jews through Him, His prophet, and His books.
59:6: The Almighty says: And what God bestowed upon His Messenger from them. This verse and the ones that follow it until His saying, severe in penalty, contain ten issues: First - The Almighty’s saying: And what God has bestowed meaning what God Almighty returned to His Messenger from the wealth of Banu Nadir. And what you urged upon means you placed upon it. Ijaf means Ijaf in traveling, which is speeding up. It is said: The horse rushed if it hurried, and I urged it means I moved it and followed it. From this is the saying of Tamim ibn Muqbil: The white camels are polished by the polishing of the knees sometimes when the lions are tired And the camels, the singular of which is rahah. He says: You did not travel far to it, nor did you encounter them in war or hardship, but it was only two miles from Madinah, Al-Farra’ said: So they walked to it and did not ride horses or camels, except for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who rode a camel, and it was said a donkey with a bridle of palm fiber, so he conquered it peacefully and expelled them and took their money. The Muslims asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to divide it for them, so this verse was revealed: And whatever God bestowed on His Messenger from them, you did not urge him to fight over it Al-Bukhari and Muslim. So he made the money of Banu Nadir specifically for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to put wherever he wanted, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided it among the Muhajireen. Al-Waqidi said, and Ibn Wahb narrated it from Malik: He did not give anything from it to the Ansar, except to three needy men, among them Abu Dujana Samak ibn Kharshah, Sahl ibn Hunaif, and Al-Harith ibn As-Simmah. It was said that he only gave it to two men, Sahl and Abu Dujana. It is said: Saad bin Muadh was given the sword of Ibn Abi Al-Haqiq, and it was a sword that was famous among them. No one from Banu Nadir converted to Islam except two men: Sufyan bin Umair and Saad bin Wahb. They converted to Islam with their wealth and kept it safe. In Sahih Muslim, it is narrated on the authority of Umar who said: The wealth of Banu Nadir was among what God had bestowed upon His Messengers, for which the Muslims had not fought with horses or camels. It was specifically for the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so he would spend it on his family for a year, and whatever remained he would put into mounts and weapons as equipment in the cause of God. “Al-Abbas said to Umar may God be pleased with them both: ‘Judge between me and this lying, sinful, treacherous traitor meaning Ali (may God be pleased with him) regarding the wealth of Banu Nadir that God bestowed upon His Messenger.’ Umar said: ‘Do you both know that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘We do not bequeath what we leave behind as charity?’ They said: ‘Yes.’ Umar said: ‘God, the Almighty, had singled out His Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with something in particular and did not single out anyone else with it. He said: ‘Whatever God has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns belongs to God and to the Messenger’ - I do not know whether he recited the verse before it - so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) divided the wealth of Banu Nadir among you, and by God, he did not keep it for himself from you nor did he take it without your permission until this wealth remained. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would take from it a year’s expenses, then he would make what remained equal to the wealth of…’” "The entire hadith was narrated by Muslim. It was said: When Banu Nadir left their homes and their hopes, the Muslims asked to have a share of them like spoils of war. God, the Most High, made it clear that it was booty. Some fighting had already taken place, as they were besieged for days, and they fought and were killed. Then they reached a peace agreement for evacuation. There was no actual fighting, rather the beginnings of the fighting and the siege took place. God reserved that wealth for His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. Mujahid said: God, the Most High, informed them and reminded them that He only aided His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and aided them without a troop or equipment. But God gives His messengers power over whom He wills, meaning among His enemies. This shows that that wealth was specifically for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and not for his companions. Second: The Almighty’s saying: What God has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns. Ibn Abbas said: “It refers to Qurayzah and An-Nadir, both of whom are in Madinah, and Fadak, which is three days’ drive from Madinah and Khaybar. God also gave the villages of Uraynah and Yanbu’ to His Messenger.” He explained that in that wealth which He allocated to Ar-Rawul (peace be upon him) there are two shares for other than the Messenger, considering that He is treating His servants well. Scholars have discussed this verse and the one before it, whether their meanings are the same or different from the verse in Al-Anfal. Some scholars said: The Almighty’s saying, What God has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns, has been abrogated by what is in Surat Al-Anfal, which states that one-fifth is for whoever was named, and the four-fifths is for whoever fought over it. This is the saying of Yazij ibn Ruman, Qatadah, and others. A similar statement was narrated from Malik, who said: “It is only spoils taken by peace, without the use of horses or camels, so it is spoils for whoever God has named over it. The first is for the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in particular, if he took something from him, then the rest is for the interests of the Muslims.” Muammar said: The first is for the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The second is the jizya and kharaj for the categories mentioned therein. The third is the spoils of war in Surat al-Anfal for the conquerors. Some people, including al-Shafi’i, said: The meaning of the two verses is the same, i.e. whatever wealth the disbelievers obtained without fighting was divided into five shares, four of which were for the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The remaining five were divided into five shares: a share for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) as well, a share for the relatives - who are Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib - because they refused to give charity, so they were given a right to the spoils of war, a share for orphans, a share for the poor, and a share for the wayfarer. After the death of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), what was of the spoils of war for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is spent, according to Al-Shafi’i’s opinion, on the mujahideen lying in wait to fight on the frontiers, because they are the ones who take the place of the Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and build bridges. The most important is given priority, and this is in four-fifths of the spoils of war. As for the share that he has from the fifth of the spoils of war and booty, it is for the interests of the Muslims after his death (peace and blessings of God be upon him), without dispute. As Ali, peace and blessings be upon him, said: I have nothing of your spoils except one-fifth, and one-fifth is returned to you. This has already been discussed in Surat Al-Anfal. Likewise, what he left behind in wealth is not inherited, but rather it is charity that is spent on the interests of the Muslims, as he, peace be upon him, said: We do not inherit; what we leave is charity. It was said that the spoils of war belonged to his Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, based on the Almighty’s saying: What God has bestowed upon His Messenger, so He added it to himself, but he did not keep wealth, rather he took as much as his family needed and spent the rest on the interests of the Muslims. Judge Abu Bakr ibn Al-Arabi said: There is no doubt that they are three meanings in three verses. As for the first verse, it is His saying: It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering. Then God, the Most High, said: And what God has bestowed upon His Messenger from them, meaning from the People of the Scripture. Umar said: It was specifically for the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, meaning Bani Ad-Dhir and what was like it. So this is one verse with a united meaning. The second verse - the Almighty’s saying: Whatever God has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns belongs to God and to the Messenger. This is a new statement, different from the first, for a different beneficiary. The third verse is called the verse of spoils, and there is no doubt that it has a different meaning with a second entitlement for another beneficiary. However, the first and second verses share the fact that each includes something that God has bestowed upon His Messenger. The first verse requires that it was obtained without fighting, and the verse of spoils requires that it was obtained by fighting. The third verse, which is His statement, What God has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns, is devoid of any mention of whether it was obtained by fighting or not, so the dispute arose from here. A group said that it is attached to the first, and it refers to all the money of peace treaties and the like. A group said: It is attached to the second verse, which is the verse of Al-Anfal. Those who said that it is attached to the verse of Al-Anfal differed over whether it was abrogated - as mentioned above - or is it decisive? Attaching it to the testimony of God with the one before it is more appropriate, because it renews the benefit and meaning. It is known that interpreting the letter of the verse, let alone the verse, to mean a renewed benefit rather than a repeated benefit. Ibn Wahb narrated from Malik, regarding the verse of God the Almighty: {And you did not urge against it any horses or camels}, regarding Banu An-Nadir, there was no fifth among them and no horses or camels were urged against it. It was purely for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so he divided it between the Muhajireen and three of the Ansar, as mentioned above. His statement, {And what God bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns}, is Qurayzah, and Qurayzah and the Trench occurred on the same day. Ibn Al-Arabi said: Malik’s statement that the second verse is about Banu Qurayzah indicates that its meaning goes back to the verse of Al-Anfal, and abrogation is attached to it. This is stronger than the statement of the rulings. We only choose what we have divided and explained that the second verse has a new meaning according to what we have indicated. And God knows best. I said: What he chose. It has been said that Surat Al-Hashr was revealed after Anfal, so it is possible that the earlier one abrogates the later one. Ibn Abi Najih said: Money is of three types: spoils of war, booty, or charity. There is not a single dirham of it except that God has made its place clear. This is more likely. Third: The wealth in which the Imams and governors have a role is of three types: that which is taken from the Muslims in order to purify them, such as charity and zakat. Second: Spoils of war, which is the wealth of the infidels that the Muslims obtain through war, coercion, and domination. Third: Fay', which is the wealth of the infidels that the Muslims take spontaneously and freely without fighting or aggression, such as peace treaties, the jizya, the land tax, and the tithes taken from the merchants of the infidels. An example of this is if the polytheists flee and leave their wealth, or if one of them dies in the land of Islam and leaves no heirs. As for charity, its disbursement is to the poor, the needy, and those who collect it, according to what God the Most High has mentioned, and this has been mentioned previously in Bara'ah. As for the spoils of war, they were in the hands of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) during the early days of Islam, and he could do with them as he wished, as He said in Surat al-Anfal 8:Say, ‘The spoils belong to God and to the Messenger.’ This was then abrogated by the statement of God the Most High: And know that whatever you obtain of spoils… (al-Anfal 8:41) It has already been explained in Al-Afal. As for the spoils of war, their division and the division of the fifth are the same. According to Malik, the matter in both is up to the Imam. If he sees fit to keep them for calamities that befall the Muslims, he does so. If he sees fit to divide them or divide one of them, he divides it all among the people, making it equal for their Arabs and their clients. He starts with the poor, men and women, until they become wealthy. Then the relatives of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) are given their share of the spoils according to what the Imam sees fit, and there is no known limit for it. There is disagreement about giving to the rich among them, but most people agree that it is their right. Malik said: It is not to be given to anyone except their poor, because it is made for them a substitute for charity. Al-Shafi’i said: Any wealth of the disbelievers that was obtained without fighting was divided during the time of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) into twenty-five shares: twenty for the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to do with as he wished, and the fifth is divided according to what the fifth of the spoils of war is divided according to. Abu Ja`far Ahmad ibn al-Dawudi said: This is a statement that no one we know of has preceded him in. Rather, it was purely for him, as is proven in the Sahih on the authority of `Umar, explaining the verse. If this were the case, then his statement, Purely for you, not for the believers (al-Ahzab 33:50) would indicate that it is permissible to give it to someone else, and that his statement, Purely for the Day of Resurrection (al-A`raf 7:32) would allow others to share it with them. The statement of al-Shafi`i has already been fully discussed on this, and praise be to God. The school of thought of al-Shafi`i may God be pleased with him is that the way of one-fifth of the spoils of war is the way of one-fifth of the booty, and that four-fifths of it were for the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), and after him they are for the interests of the Muslims. He also said another statement: that after him they are specifically for those who are waiting to fight after him, as mentioned previously. Fourth: Our scholars said that all the wealth is to be distributed in the land where it was collected, and it is not to be transferred from the land where it was collected until they become wealthy, then it is transferred to the closest relative, unless they are in a land other than the one where it was collected, in which case it is transferred to the needy wherever they are, as ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him did in the years of the ashes, which lasted five or six years. It was also said that it was two years. It was also said that it was a year in which the plague and famine were severe. If what we feared does not happen and the Imam sees fit to endow the spoils, he should endow them for calamities inflicted on the Muslims. From it, he should give to those who are self-sufficient, starting with those whose fathers are poor. The spoils of war are permissible for the rich. People are treated equally in their distribution, except that they are given preference to those in need and poverty. Preference in it is based on need. Creditors are given from it to pay off their debts. Prizes and gifts are given from it if that is a hope. Judges, rulers and those who benefit the Muslims are provided for. The most deserving of a share of it are those who benefit the Muslims the most. Whoever takes something from the spoils of war in the registry must fight if he fights. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: So that there will not be a state. The general reading is with the letter ya. Dawlah is in the accusative case, meaning so that the spoils will not be a state. Abu Ja’far, Al-A’raj, Hisham - on the authority of Ibn Amir - and Abu Haywah read it with the letter ta of dawlah in the nominative case, meaning so that a state will not occur. So fa-kana is complete. Dawlah is in the nominative case as the subject of kana and has no predicate. It is also possible for it to be incomplete and its predicate is among the rich among you. If it is complete, then his saying: among the rich among you is a description of dawlah. The general reading is dawlah with the letter d in the damma. Al-Salami and Abu Haywah read it in the accusative case. Isa bin Amr, Yunus, and Al-Asma’i said: They are two dialects with one meaning. Abu Amr bin Al-Ala’ said: Dawlah with the letter fatha is victory in war and other things, and it is the verbal noun. With the letter d in the damma, it is the name of the thing that is circulated of money. Abu Ubaidah said the same: Dawlah is the name of the thing that is circulated. Dawlah is the verb. The meaning of the verse is: We did this regarding this booty so that the leaders, the rich, and the powerful would not divide it among themselves without the poor and weak. This is because when the people of the Age of Ignorance took spoils of war, the leader would take a quarter of it for himself, which is the fourth. Then he would choose from it, after the fourth, whatever he wanted. And their poet said about it: You have the square and the waste He says that it should not be used as it was used in the pre-Islamic era. So God made this for His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to distribute in the places he was commanded to, where there was no fifth. So when a fifth came, it was distributed among all the Muslims. Sixth: The Almighty said: And whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and what he has forbidden you - refrain from. Whatever he has given you of spoils of war, take it, and whatever he has forbidden you of taking and misappropriation, refrain from it. This was said by Al-Hasan and others. Al-Sadri said: Whatever he has given you of spoils of war, accept it, and whatever he has prevented you from, do not seek it. Ibn Jurayj said: Whatever he has given you of obedience, do it, and whatever he has forbidden you of disobedience to Me, avoid it. Al-Mawardi said: It was said that it is carried on the generality of all his commands and prohibitions; he does not command except what is good and does not forbid except what is corruption. I say: This is the meaning of the foul that preceded it. So there are three opinions. Seventh: Al-Mahdawi said: The Almighty’s saying: And whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and what he has forbidden you - refrain from. This necessitates that everything the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded is a command from God Almighty. And even though the verse is about spoils of war, all of his commands and prohibitions, may God bless him and grant him peace, are included in it. Al-Hakam bin Umair - who was a companion of the Prophet - said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: This Qur’an is difficult and hard, tough for those who abandon it, easy for those who follow it and seek it. My hadith is difficult and hard, and it is the ruling. Whoever holds fast to my hadith and memorizes it will be saved with the Qur’an. Whoever neglects the Qur’an and my hadith will lose this world and the Hereafter. You have been commanded to take my saying, to be careful with two matters, and to follow my Sunnah. Whoever is satisfied with my saying has been satisfied with the Qur’an, and whoever mocks my saying has mocked the Qur’an. God the Most High said: And whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and what he has forbidden you - refrain from. Eighth: Abdur-Rahman bin Zaid said: Ibn Masoud met a man in ihram who was wearing his clothes and said to him: Take these off. The man said: Will you recite to me a verse from the Book of God? He said: Yes, And whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and what he has forbidden you - refrain from. Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Harun Al-Firyabi said: I heard Al-Shafi’i may God be pleased with him say: Ask me whatever you wish and I will tell you from the Book of God and the Sunnah of your Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). I said to him: What do you say - may God guide you - about a person in ihram killing a wasp? He said: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. God Almighty said: And whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and what he has forbidden you - refrain from. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us from Uyaynah from Abd al-Malik ibn Umair from Rib’i ibn Harash from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Follow the example of those who come after me, Abu Bakr and Umar. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us from Mis’ar from Kadam from Qays ibn Muslim from Tariq ibn Shihab from Umar ibn al-Khattab - may God be pleased with him - that he ordered the killing of a wasp during ihram, and he explained that they should follow Umar in this, and that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that they should follow his example, and that God Almighty ordered that what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, says should be accepted. So the permissibility of killing it is derived from the Qur’an and the Sunnah. This meaning has already been mentioned in the words of Ikrimah when he was asked about the mothers of children, and he said: They are free in Surat al-Nisa’ when God Almighty says: Obey God and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you (al-Nisa’: 14). 59] In Sahih Muslim and others, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has cursed the tattooers and those who get tattooed, the pluckers and file their teeth for the sake of beauty, and those who change God’s creation. report of that reached a woman from Banu Asad called Umm Ya`qub, so she came and said: I have heard that you cursed such and such! He said: Why should I not curse those who were cursed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it is in God’s Book? She said: I have read what is between the covers and I did not find in it what you say. He said: If you had read it, you would have found it! Haven’t you read: And whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and what he has forbidden you - refrain from? She said: Yes. He said: Indeed, he has forbidden it. The hadith. This has been discussed in full in An-Nisa’. Ninth - The Almighty’s saying: And whatever the Messenger has given you - take it. Even if it comes in the form of giving, which is handing over, then its meaning is a command, as is proven by the Almighty’s saying: And whatever he has forbidden you - refrain from. So He contrasted it with a prohibition, and a prohibition can only be contrasted with a command. The evidence for understanding that is what we mentioned before, along with: His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: If I command you to do something, then do as much of it as you can, and if I forbid you from something, then avoid it. Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed about the leaders of the Muslims. They said about the wealth of the polytheists that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, had seized: “O Messenger of God, take your share and a quarter, and leave us the rest. This is how we used to act in the pre-Islamic era.” And they recited to him: You have the square ones, the clear ones, your rule, the active ones, and the seasons. Then God Almighty revealed this verse. Tenth: The Almighty says: And fear God, meaning the punishment of God, which is severe for those who disobey Him. It was also said: Fear God in His commands and prohibitions, and do not waste them. Indeed, God is severe in penalty for those who disobey what He has commanded.
59:8: That is, the spoils of war are for the poor emigrants. It was also said: So that it will not be a circulating share among the rich, but rather for the poor. It was also said that this is an explanation of His statement: And for the near of kin, the orphans, the needy, and the traveler. (al-Hashr 59:7) So when they were mentioned in their categories, the money was given to them because they were poor, and the emigrants, who had been expelled from their homes, were the most deserving of it. It was also said: But God gives His messengers power over whom He wills, for the poor emigrants, so that the money will not be a circulating share among the rich of this world. It was also said: God is severe in punishment of the emigrants, that is, He is severe in punishment of the disbelievers because of the poor emigrants and for their sake. And included in these are those who were mentioned previously in the saying of God the Almighty: And for relatives and orphans. It was said: It is a conjunction to what has gone before, and the conjunction and was not used, like you say: This money is for Zaid, for Bakr, for so-and-so, for so-and-so. The emigrants here: those who emigrated to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, out of love for him and in support of him. Qatada said: These emigrants are those who left their homes, wealth, families, and homelands out of love for God and His Messenger, to the extent that a man among them would tie a stone over his stomach to support his back from hunger, and a man would make a hole in the winter that he had nothing as a blanket other than it. Abd al-Rahman ibn Uzzi and Sa`d ibn Jubayr said: There were people among the muhāriyyah, for one of them was a slave, a wife, a house, and a camel, on which he would perform Hajj and fight, so God attributed them to the poor and gave them a share in the zakat. The meaning of were driven out of their homes is that the infidels of Mecca drove them out, meaning they were forced to leave, and they were one hundred men. Seeking “A favor from God” meaning It was narrated that Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him delivered a sermon in Jabiyah and said: Whoever wants to ask about the inheritance laws, let him go to Zayd ibn Thabit. Whoever wants to ask about jurisprudence, let him go to Muadh ibn Jabal. Whoever wants to ask about wealth, let him come to me, for God the Almighty has made me his treasurer and distributor. I will start with the wives of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and give them, then the emigrants and the first ones. I and my companions were expelled from Mecca from our homes and our wealth.
59:9: It contains eleven issues: First - The Almighty’s statement: And those who were established in the home and in faith before them. There is no dispute that those who were established in the home are the Ansar who settled in Madinah before the emigrants. Before them is a relative clause of tabawa and the meaning is: And those who were established in the home before the emigrants and pledged faith and were sincere in it because faith is not a place to be established, like His statement, the Almighty: So decide your plan, you and your associates.
