(Yunus 10:71) meaning, and call upon your associates. Abu Ali, Al-Zamakhshari, and others mentioned this. It is similar to His statement: I fed her straw and cold water. It is permissible to interpret it with the omission of the ḍāf, as if he said: They were established in the home, and faith was not difficult. It is permissible to interpret it with what is indicated by tawa’u, as if he said: They adhered to the home and adhered to faith and did not leave them. It is permissible for the establishment of faith to be in the manner of a proverb, as you say: Then establish a close relationship with the Banu so-and-so. And to assume authority means to be able and stable. He does not mean that the Ansar believed before the Muhajireen, but rather he meant that they believed before the Prophet’s migration, may God bless him and grant him peace. Second: There is also a difference of opinion as to whether this verse is cut off from what precedes it or is connected. Their interpretation is that it is connected to His statement: for the poor emigrants, and that the verses in Al-Hashr are all connected to each other. If they had contemplated that and been fair, there would have been reasons contrary to what they have gone to, because God Almighty says: “It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering. You did not think they would be expelled” to His statement: the wicked. So He informed about Banu Nadir and Banu Qaynuqa. Then He said: “And what God gave to His Messenger from them - you did not urge against it any horses or camels. But God gives power to His messengers over whom He wills.” So He informed that that was for the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, because he did not urge against it when they were alone. And what they had presented of fighting and cutting down their trees, they had turned back from it and that matter was settled, then he said: What God has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns - it belongs to God and to the Messenger and to the near relatives and the orphans and the needy and the traveler This statement is not connected to the first. And likewise, and those who were established in the home and in the faith is the beginning of a statement in praise of the Ansar and commendation of them, for they handed over that booty to the Muhajireen, and it is as if the booty was for the poor Muhajireen, and the Ansar loved them and did not envy them for what was clear to them from the booty. And likewise, and those who came after them is the beginning of the statement, and the report says, Our Lord, forgive us. Ismail bin Ishaq said: His statement, and those who were established in the home and and those who came is connected to what came before and that they are partners in the booty, meaning this money is for the Muhajireen and those who were established in the home. Malik ibn Aws said: Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him recited this verse: Zakat is only for the poor, and he said: Are these the ones? He recited: And know that whatever you obtain of spoils, a fifth of it is for God (al-Anfal 8:41) and he said: This is for these. Then he recited: And what God has bestowed upon His Messenger - until he reached - for the poor emigrants, “and those who were established in the home and in faith,” and those who came after them, then he said: If I live, a shepherd will come to him while he is in the garden of Himyar and he has his share of it and his forehead will not sweat over it. It was said: He called the Muhajireen and the Ansar and consulted them about what God had revealed to him, and he said to them: Establish the matter and ponder it, then come to me. So he thought that night and it became clear to him that these verses in Surat Al-Hashra, and he recited: What God has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns - to His saying - for the poor Muhajireen. Then when he reached His saying: Those are the truthful, he said: It is not only for these. And he recited His saying: And those who came after them - to His saying - Kind and Merciful. Then he said: There is no one left from the people of Islam who has not entered into that. And God knows best. Third: Malik narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam from his father that Umar said: “Had it not been for the one who comes from the last of the people, he would have divided every town he conquered, just as the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) divided Khaybar.” In the widely circulated narrations from many chains of narration, it is stated that Umar left the blacks of Iraq and Egypt and whatever spoils he had conquered, so that they would be given to the fighters and provisions for the army and children. Az-Zubayr, Bilal and more than one of the Companions wanted him to divide what he had conquered, but they disliked that and there was disagreement about what he did. Some said: He pleased the people of the army, so whoever was satisfied with him leaving his share without a price in order to keep it for the Muslims was few, and whoever refused, he gave him an price for his share. Whoever said: He only kept the land after the people had pleased him, considered his action like the action of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), because he divided Khaybar, because his buying it and leaving whoever left willingly was like dividing it. It was also said: He left it without giving anything to the people of the armies. It was said that he interpreted in this regard the words of God Almighty: For the poor emigrants - to say - Our Lord, You are indeed Kind and Merciful as mentioned above. And God knows best. Fourth: The scholars differed regarding the division of the property. Malik said: The Imam has the right to endow it for the benefit of the Muslims. Abu Hanifa said: The Imam has the choice to divide it or make it an endowment for the benefit of the Muslims. Al-Shafi’i said: The Imam does not have the right to withhold it from them without their consent, but rather to divide it among them like all other property. Whoever is willing to give up his right to the Imam to make it an endowment for them, then he has the right. Whoever is not willing, then he has more right to his property. Umar may God be pleased with him was pleased with the souls of the conquerors and desired it from them. I said: Understand this, so his statement: And those who came after them is cut off from what preceded it, and they were urged to pray for the first ones and praise them. Fifth: Ibn Wahb said: I heard Malik mention the superiority of Madinah over other cities. He said: Madinah was established through faith and migration, while other cities were conquered by the sword. Then he recited: And those who were established in the city and in faith before them love those who emigrated to them [al-Masjid al-Haram] We have already discussed this and the prayer in the two mosques: the Sacred Mosque and the Mosque of Madinah, so there is no point in repeating it. Sixth - The Almighty said: And they find not in their hearts any need for what they have been given. Meaning, they do not envy the Muhajireen for what they have been given of spoils of war and other things. This is what people said. There is an estimation of the deletion of two complements, meaning the need of those who have lost what they have been given. And everything that a person finds in his heart that he needs to remove is a need. The Muhajireen were in the homes of the Ansar: When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, seized the wealth of Banu Nadir, he called the Ansar and thanked them for what they had done for the Muhajireen by giving them shelter in their homes and sharing in their wealth. Then he said: “If you like, I will divide what God has bestowed upon me from Banu Nadir between you and them, and the Muhajireen will remain as they are, living in your homes and with your wealth. Or if you like, I will give it to them and they will leave without you.” Sa`id ibn `Ubadah and Sa`id ibn Mu`adh said, Rather, we will divide it among the Muhajireen, and they will remain in our homes as they were. The Ansar called out, We are satisfied and we submit, O Messenger of God. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said, O God, have mercy on the Ansar and the sons of the Ansar. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) gave to the Muhajireen and did not give anything to the Ansar except the three we mentioned. It is possible that what he meant by and they do not find in their hearts any need for what they have been given is if it is little, but rather they are content with it and are satisfied. They were in this state when the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was alive in this world, and then they were in this state after his death (peace and blessings be upon him) with worldly rulings. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) warned them and said: You will see his trace after me, so be patient until you meet me at the Cistern. Seventh: The Almighty’s saying: And they give others preference over themselves, even though they are in need. In Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Abu Hurairah: A man [from the Ansar] had a guest spend the night with him, and he had nothing but his own food and the food of his children. So he said to his wife: Put the children to sleep, put out the lamp, and bring whatever you have to the guest. Then this verse was revealed: And they give preference over themselves, even though they were in need. He said: This is a good and authentic hadith. Muslim also narrated it. And he narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: A man came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: I am exhausted. He sent word to one of his wives, and she said: By Him who sent you with the truth, I have nothing with me except water. Then he sent word to another, and she said the same, until they all said the same: No, by Him who sent you with the truth, I have nothing with me except water. He said: Who will host this man tonight, may God have mercy on him? A man from the Ansar stood up and said: I will, O Messenger of God. He took him to his tent and said to his wife: Do you have anything? She said: No, except food for my children. He said: “Provide them with something. When our guest comes in, extinguish the lamp and make him think that we are eating, but when he reaches out to eat, get up and go to the lamp until you extinguish it.” They sat down and the guest ate. When morning came, he went to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and he said: God, the Almighty, is amazed at what you have done. "And in a narration on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: A man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to be his guest, but he did not have anything to host him. So he said: Is there no man who will host this man, may God have mercy on him? So a man from the Ansar called Abu Talha got up and went with him to his tent..., and he narrated the hadith in a similar manner to the one before it, and mentioned in it the revelation of the verse. Al-Mahdawi mentioned on the authority of Abu Hurairah that this was revealed about Thabit ibn Qays and a man from the Ansar - Thabit stayed with him - called Abu al-Mutawakkil. Abu al-Mutawakkil had nothing with him except his own food and the food of his children, so he said to his wife: Put out the lamp and put the children to sleep, and he presented what he had with him to his guest. And likewise al-Nahhas mentioned that Abu Hurairah said: It was revealed about a man from the Ansar - called Abu al-Mutawakkil - Thabit ibn Qays was his guest, and he had nothing with him except his own food and the food of his children, so he said to his wife: Put out the lamp and put the children to sleep, so the verse was revealed: "And they give preference over themselves, even though they were in privation - until His saying - It is those who are the successful." And it was said: That The one who did that was Abu Talha. Al-Qushayri mentioned Abu Nasr Abd al-Rahim ibn Abd al-Karim: Ibn Umar said: A man from among the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was given a sheep’s head as a gift, so he said: My brother so-and-so and his family are more in need of this than us. So he sent it to them. One kept sending it to another until it had been passed around seven houses, until it returned to those houses, and then the verse and they give others preference over themselves was revealed. Al-Tha’labi mentioned it on the authority of Anas, who said: A man from among the companions was given a sheep’s head as a gift, and he was poor, so he sent it to his neighbor, and it was passed around seven houses, then it returned to the first house, and then the verse and they give others preference over themselves was revealed. Ibn Abbas said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the Ansar on the day of Banu Nadir: “If you wish, I will divide some of your homes and wealth among the Muhajirun and you will share this booty with them. Or if you wish, your homes and wealth will be yours, and we will not divide any of the booty among you.” The Ansar said: Rather, we will divide some of our homes and wealth among our brothers and give them preference over the booty. Then the verse and give them preference over themselves was revealed. The first is more correct. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Anas: That a man used to give the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) date palms from his land until the Qurayzah and Nadir were conquered by him, after which he began to return to him what he had given him. Muslim’s wording: Az-Zuhri said on the authority of Anas ibn Malik: When the Muhajirun came from Makkah to Madinah, they did not have anything in their hands, and the Ansar were the owners of the land and property, so the Ansar divided the land with them on the condition that they would give them half of the fruits of their wealth every year and that they would suffice them in work and provision. Anas ibn Malik’s mother was called Umm Sulaym, and she was the mother of Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah, who was Anas’s brother on his mother’s side. Anas’ mother had given the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) a bunch of dates of hers, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) gave it to her, Umm Ayman, his freed slave, the mother of Usamah ibn Zayd. Ibn Shihab said: Anas ibn Malik informed me that when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) finished fighting the people of Khaybar and returned to Madinah, the Muhajirun returned to the Ansar the gifts they had given them of their fruits. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned her to Umm Udhaq, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave Umm Ayman their place in his garden. Also narrated by Muslim. Eighth - Altruism: It is giving precedence to others over oneself and one’s worldly interests, and a desire for religious interests. This stems from strong faith, affirmation of love, and patience in the face of hardship. It is said: I gave him such-and-such, meaning I singled him out for it and preferred him over it. The object of altruism is omitted, meaning they give them precedence over themselves with their wealth and homes, not out of desire, but rather because they need them, as explained above. In the Muwatta’ of Malik: It reached him on the authority of Aisha, the wife of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), that a poor man asked her while she was fasting and there was nothing in her house except a loaf of bread. She said to a female slave of hers: Give it to him. She said: Do you have nothing to break your fast with? She said: Give it to him. She said: So I did. She said: “When evening came, a family or a person gave us what was usually given to us: a sheep and its shroud. Aisha called me and said: “Eat some of this, for this is better than your loaf of bread.” Our scholars said: This is from the profitable wealth and the pure deed with God, the Most High, He makes from it what He wills, and that does not diminish what he has saved for himself. Whoever gives up something for the sake of God will not find its loss. Aisha may God be pleased with her in her action is among those whom God praised for giving others precedence over themselves despite their poverty, and whoever does that has been protected from his own greed and has succeeded with no loss after that. The meaning of a sheep and its shroud is that the Arabs - or some of the Arabs or some of their leaders - used this as part of their food. They would come to a sheep or a lamb and, after skinning it, cover it all with wheat dough and shroud it with it, then hang it in the oven, and nothing would come out of its skin except in that shroud. This was part of the good food according to them. An-Nasa'i narrated on the authority of Nafi' that Ibn 'Umar was sick and desired grapes, so he bought a bunch of grapes for a dirham. A poor man came and asked for it, so the Prophet said, "Give it to me." A man went back and bought it for a dirham, then brought it to Ibn 'Umar. A poor man came and asked for it, so the Prophet said, "Give it to me." A man went back and bought it for a dirham, then brought it to him, but the beggar wanted to return it, but he refused. Had Ibn 'Umar known that it was the bunch, he would not have tasted it, because what came out for God does not return to it. Ibn al-Mubarak mentioned that Muhammad ibn Mutraf told us, that Abu Hazim told us, on the authority of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'id ibn Yarbu', on the authority of Malik al-Dar, that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him took four hundred dinars, put them in a purse, and then said to the boy, "Go with it to Abu 'Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah, then wait in the house for a while until you see what he does with it. So the boy took it to him and said, The Commander of the Faithful says to you, 'Use this for some of your needs.' He said, 'May God connect him and have mercy on him.' He said, 'Come, girl, take these seven to so-and-so, and these five to so-and-so, so that I may deliver them.'" The boy went back to Umar who delayed him and found that he had prepared the same amount for Muadh ibn Jabal. He said, "Take this to Muadh ibn Jabal and wait in the house for a while until you see what he does. So he went with it to him and said, The Commander of the Faithful says to you, 'Use this for some of your needs.' He said, 'May God have mercy on him and connect him.' He said, 'Girl, go to the house of so-and-so with such-and-such and the house of so-and-so with such-and-such.' Muadh's wife looked in and said, 'And we, by God, are poor, so give us some.' There was nothing left in the rag except two dinars that he had brought to her. The boy went back to Umar and told him. Umar was pleased and said, They are brothers, one from the other. And something similar was narrated from Aisha may God be pleased with her about Muawiyah giving her ten thousand, and Al-Munkadir had entered upon her. If it is said: There are authentic narrations prohibiting giving in charity all that one owns, it is said: This was only disliked for someone who could not be trusted to be patient in poverty, and he feared that he would be exposed to begging if he lost what would benefit him. As for the Ansar, whom God praised for giving alms to themselves, they were not of this characteristic, rather they were as God the Most High said: And the patient in poverty and hardship and during battle (Al-Baqarah 2:177). And giving alms was better for them than withholding. And withholding is better for someone who is not patient and is exposed to begging than giving alms. “It was narrated that a man came to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) with something the size of an egg made of gold, and he said: This is charity. He threw it away and said: “One of you should bring everything he owns and give it in charity, then sit and beg from people.” And God knows best. Ninth: Giving one’s life is more important than giving one’s money, even if it comes back to one’s life. A popular proverb says: Generosity is the ultimate in generosity. One of the interesting Sufi expressions about the definition of love is: It is self-sacrifice. Don’t you see that when the wife of Al-Aziz became intense in her love for Joseph, peace be upon him, she preferred him over herself and said: I tried to seduce him. And the best generosity with one’s self is generosity in protecting the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. In the Sahih: Abu Talha shielded the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the day of Uhud. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was looking up to see the people. Abu Talha said to him: Do not look up, O Messenger of God! Do not let them hit you! My throat is before your throat! And the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) shielded himself with his hand and it failed. Hudhayfah al-Adawi said: “On the day of Yarmouk, I went looking for my cousin - and I had some water with me - and I saw a man saying, ‘Ah! Ah!’ My cousin gestured to me to go to him, and it was Hisham ibn al-‘As. I said, ‘Shall I give you a drink?’ He gestured yes. Then I heard another say, ‘Ah! Ah!’ Hisham gestured to me to go, so I went to him, and he was already dead.” Abu Yazid al-Bistami said: “No one has ever defeated me more than a young man from Balkh! A pilgrim came to us and said to me, ‘O Abu Yazid, what is the limit of asceticism according to you?’ I said, ‘If we find it, we eat. If we lose it, we are patient.’ He said, ‘This is how the dogs of Balkh are according to us.’ I said, ‘What is the limit of asceticism according to you?’ He said, ‘If we lose it, we are grateful, and if we find it, we give preference.’ Dhu al-Nun al-Misri was asked, ‘What is the limit of one whose chest is open?’ He said, ‘Three: distributing what is collected, abandoning the pursuit of what is lost, and giving preference when it comes to sustenance.’ It was narrated from Abu al-Hasan al-Antaki that more than thirty men gathered around him.” In a village of Rayy, they had a few loaves of bread that would not satisfy all of them, so they broke the loaves, put out the lamp, and sat down to eat. When he took it out, the food was still the same, so he did not eat anything from it, preferring its owner to himself. Tenth: - The Almighty’s saying: Even if they were in privation. Poverty is the need that disturbs the situation. Its origin is from the word ikhtisas, which means to be alone in a matter. Poverty is to be alone in need, meaning if they were in poverty and need. And from this is the saying of the poet: As for spring, if it is scarce, the sick will live in it and the poor will become rich. Eleventh - The Almighty said: And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who will be the successful. Stinginess and miserliness are the same. It is said: A stingy man is between stinginess, miserliness, and stinginess. Amr ibn Kulthum said: You see the miserly person if you command him to do so because of his wealth in it, he is humiliated Some linguists have described the miser as worse than the stingy. In As-Sahah: Stinginess is miserliness combined with greed. You say: shahhat with a kasra tashah. Shahhat also and tashah. A stingy man, stingy people and stingy people. What is meant by the verse is stinginess with zakat and what is not obligatory, such as maintaining family ties, hosting, and the like. So, he is neither stingy nor miserly who spends on that and holds back from himself. And whoever is generous with himself and does not spend on the zakat and acts of worship that we mentioned has not been protected from the stinginess of his soul. Al-Aswad narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud that a man came to him and said: I fear that I have been ruined. He said: What is that? He said: I heard God the Almighty say: And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who will be the successful. And I am a stingy man who can hardly give anything. Ibn Masoud said: This is not the greed that God mentioned in the Quran. Rather, the greed that God mentioned in the Quran is that you consume your brother’s wealth unjustly. Rather, that is miserliness, and miserliness is an evil thing. So he may God be pleased with him differentiated between miserliness and stinginess. Tawus said: Stinginess is for a person to be miserly with what he has in his hand, and miserliness is for him to be miserly with what people have. He should have what they have, whether lawful or unlawful. He should not be satisfied. Ibn Jubayr: Miserliness is withholding zakat and hoarding what is unlawful. Ibn Uyaynah: Miserliness is injustice. Al-Layth: Abandoning the obligatory duties and violating the prohibitions. Ibn Abbas: Whoever follows his desires and does not accept faith, that is the miser. Ibn Zayd: Whoever does not take something for something God has forbidden him, and miserliness does not lead him to withhold something from something God has commanded him, then God has protected him from the greed of his own soul. Anas said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He who pays zakat, entertains guests, and gives in times of calamity is free from miserliness. And on his authority: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to supplicate: O God, I seek refuge in You from the greed of my soul, its extravagance, and its whisperings. Abu Al-Hayaj Al-Asadi said: “I saw a man during the circumambulation supplicating: ‘O God, protect me from the greed of my soul.’ He did not increase anything, so I said to him: ‘What?’ He said: ‘If I protect myself from the greed of my soul, I will not steal, I will not commit adultery, and I will not do any of that.’” Then the man was Abd Al-Rahman bin Awf. I said: This is indicated by the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Beware of injustice, for injustice is darkness on the Day of Resurrection. And beware of greed, for greed destroyed those who came before you. It led them to shed each other’s blood and violate their sacred things.” We have already explained this at the end of Surah Al Imran. Khosrow said to his companions: What is most harmful to the son of Adam? They said: Poverty. Khosrow said: Greed is more harmful than poverty, because when a poor person has something, he is satisfied, while the miser and the miser, when he has something, will never be satisfied.
59:10: First: The Almighty said: And those who came after them meaning the followers and those who entered Islam until the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Layla said: People are divided into three levels: the Muhajireen, those who settled in the home and the faith, and those who came after them. So strive not to leave these levels. Some of them said: Be a sun, and if you cannot, then be a moon, and if you cannot, then be a shining star, and if you cannot, then be a small planet, and do not stop in your light. The meaning of this is: Be a Muhajireen. If you cannot, or you say: I cannot find any, then be an Ansar. If you cannot find any, then do as they did, and if you cannot, then love them and seek forgiveness for them as God has commanded you. Mus'ab ibn Sa'id narrated that he said: People are divided into three levels. Two levels have passed and one remains, so the best thing for you is to be in this level that remains. On the authority of Ja'far bin Muhammad bin Ali, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather Ali bin Al-Hussein may God be pleased with him, that a man came to him and said: O son of the daughter of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), what do you say about Uthman? He said to him: O brother, you are from a people about whom God said: For the poor emigrants (al-Baqarah 2:17). He said: No! He said: By God, if you are not from the people of the verse, then you are from a people about whom God said: And those who have established themselves in the home and in faith (al-Baqarah 2:17). He said: No! He said: By God, if you are not from the people of the third verse, then you will be expelled from Islam! It is the verse in which God the Almighty says: And those who came after them say, ‘Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith’ (al-Baqarah 2:17). It was said that Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Hasan may God be pleased with them narrated on the authority of his father that some people from Iraq came to him and cursed Abu Bakr and Umar may God be pleased with them and then Uthman may God be pleased with him and they cursed many times. He said to them: Are you from the first emigrants? They said: No. He said: Are you from those who established themselves in the home and in faith before them? They said, No. He said, You have disavowed these two groups! I bear witness that you are not among those about whom God Almighty said, And those who came after them say, 'Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith and put not in our hearts [any] resentment toward those who have believed. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful.'" Arise, God will do to you and do!! An-Nahhas mentioned it. Second: This verse is evidence of the obligation of loving the Companions, because He gave those who came after them a share of the spoils of war as long as they continued to love them, befriend them, and seek forgiveness for them. Whoever curses them or one of them or believes evil in him will have no right to the spoils of war. This was narrated from Malik and others. Malik said: Whoever hates one of the Companions of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him), or has rancor in his heart toward them, has no right to the spoils of war of the Muslims. Then he recited: And those who came after them verse. Third: This verse indicates that the correct opinion of the scholars is to divide the movable property and keep the real estate and land for all Muslims, as ‘Umar may God be pleased with him did, unless the governor exerts his own effort and implements an order, and his work in it goes ahead due to the people’s disagreement over it. This verse is decisive for that, because God the Most High informed us about the spoils of war and made it for three groups: the Muhajireen, the Ansar - and they are well known - And those who came after them say, ‘Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith.’ So it is general for all the Tabi’een and those who come after them until the Day of Judgment. “And in the authentic hadith: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out to the graveyard and said, “Peace be upon you, abode of the believers. And we, God willing, will join you. I wish that I could see our brothers.” They said, O Messenger of God, are we not your brothers? He said, Rather, you are my companions, and our brothers are those who have not yet come, and I will be their leader at the Cistern. Thus, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) explained that your brothers are those who come after them, not as As-Suddi and Al-Kalbi said, that they are those who migrated after that. Al-Hasan also said, And those who came after them means those who went to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in Madinah after the migration had stopped. Fourth: The Almighty’s statement: They say is in the accusative case as a state, meaning saying, Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith. There are two interpretations: The first is that they were commanded to seek forgiveness for those who came before this nation from the believers of the People of the Book. Aisha may God be pleased with her said: So they were commanded to seek forgiveness for them, but they reviled them. The second is that they were commanded to seek forgiveness for the first to come from among the Muhajireen and the Ansar. Ibn Abbas said: God the Almighty commanded us to seek forgiveness for the Companions of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and He knew that they would be tested. Aisha said: You were commanded to seek forgiveness for the Companions of Muhammad, but you reviled them. I heard your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, This nation will not end until its last one curses its first one. Ibn Umar said, “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, ‘If you see those who abuse my companions, then say, ‘May God curse your polytheists.’” Al-Awwam ibn Hawshab said, “I met the early generations of this nation when they used to say, ‘Mention the good qualities of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so that hearts may be united around them.’ Do not mention the disputes that occurred between them, lest people become bold towards them.” Al-Sha’bi said, “The Jews and Christians have one advantage over the Rafidah Shia in one characteristic. The Jews were asked, ‘Who are the best people of your religion?’ They said, ‘The companions of Moses.’ The Christians were asked, ‘Who are the best people of your religion?’ They said, ‘The companions of Jesus.’ The Rafidah were asked, ‘Who are the worst people of your religion?’ They said, ‘The companions of Muhammad.’ They were commanded to seek forgiveness for them, but they abused them. So the sword is drawn against them until the Day of Resurrection. No banner will stand for them, no foothold will be firm, and no word will unite them. Whenever they kindle the fire of war, God extinguishes it with the sword of their blood and the refutation of their argument.” May God protect us and you from the misleading horrors. And do not put in our hearts any hatred toward those who have believed meaning hatred and envy. Our Lord, You are indeed Kind and Merciful.
59:11: One is amazed at the Jews' deception about the victory promised to them by the hypocrites, knowing that they neither believe nor have a book. Among the hypocrites were Abdullah bin Ubayy ibn Salul, Abdullah Nabtal, Rifa'ah ibn Zayd, and it was said: Rifa'ah ibn Tabut, and Aws ibn Qayzi. They were among the Ansar, but they were hypocrites and said to the Jews of Qurazah and Nadir, If you are expelled, we will go out with you. It was said that this is from what Banu Nadir said to Qurazah. And his statement, And we will never obey anyone concerning you, means Muhammad, peace be upon him; we will not obey him in fighting you. This is evidence of the truth of Muhammad's prophethood from the perspective of knowledge of the unseen, because they were expelled but did not leave, and they were fought but did not support them, as God the Most High said, And God bears witness that they are liars, meaning in their words and actions.
59:12: The Almighty says: "If they are expelled, they will not go out with them. And if they are fought, they will not aid them. And if they aid them, they will turn their backs." That is, defeated. Then they will not be aided. It has been said that the meaning of will not aid them is willingly. "And if they aid them is unwillingly, they will turn their backs. It has also been said that the meaning of will not aid them is they will not continue to aid them." This is based on the fact that the two pronouns are identical. It has also been said that they are different, and the meaning is that if the Jews are expelled, the hypocrites will not go out with them, and if they are fought, they will not aid them. "And if they aid them means if the Jews aid the hypocrites, they will turn their backs. It has been said that If they are expelled, they will not go out with them" means that God knows that they will not go out if they are expelled. "And if they are fought, they will not aid them" means that God knows that about them. Then he said: They will turn their backs. So he informed about what he had informed would not happen. How would it have been if it had happened? It is like the Almighty’s saying: And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden. It was said: The meaning of And if they aided them is: And if We willed that they aid them, We would make that attractive to them. They will turn their backs.
59:13: God Almighty says: O Muslims, you are more fearful and dreadful of God in their hearts meaning the hearts of Banu Nadir. It was also said: in the hearts of the hypocrites. It is possible that it refers to both groups, meaning they fear you more than they fear their Lord. That is because they are a people who do not understand meaning they do not understand the extent of God’s greatness and power.
59:14: The Almighty said: They will not fight you all meaning the Jews except within fortified towns meaning behind walls and houses, which they think will protect them from you or from behind walls meaning from behind walls which they hide behind out of cowardice and fear. The reading of jadar is in the plural, and this is the preferred reading of Abu Ubaidah and Abu Hatim, because it makes the Almighty say: in fortified towns which is a plural. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaisin, and Abu Amr read jidar in the singular because singular replaces the plural. It was narrated from some of the Meccans jadar with a fatha on the jim and a sukoon on the dal, which is a dialect for jidar. It is possible that it means their palm trees and trees. It is said: ajdar an-nakhal palm tree when its tops appear at the beginning of spring. Jidar is a plant, the singular of which is jidar. The reading of jadar with a damma on the jim and a sukoon on the dal is the plural of jidar. It is permissible for the alif to be in the singular, like the alif of kitab, and in the plural, like the alif of zaraf. The same applies to a she-camel called hajan and two she-camels called hajan, because you say in the dual: hajanan, so the singular and plural forms are ambiguous in pronunciation but different in meaning, as Ibn Jinni said. God the Almighty says: {Their violence is severe among themselves} meaning their enmity towards one another. Mujahid said: {Their violence is severe among themselves} meaning in speech and threats that we will do such and such. Al-Suddi said: What is meant is the difference in their hearts to the point that they do not agree on one matter. It was also said: {Their violence is severe among themselves} meaning that if they do not encounter an enemy, they attribute to themselves severity and violence, but when they encounter an enemy, they are defeated. {You think they are united, but their hearts are diverse} meaning the Jews and the hypocrites, as Mujahid said. And it also means the hypocrites. Ath-Thawri said: They are the polytheists and the People of the Book. Qatadah said: {You think they are united} meaning united on one matter and opinion. {But their hearts are diverse} separated. So the people of falsehood have different opinions, different testimonies, different desires, and they are united in their enmity towards the people of truth. Mujahid also said: He meant that the hypocrites’ religion is different from the religion of the Jews, and this is to strengthen the souls of the believers against them. The poet said: I complain to God about a broken intention that is different today and was united yesterday. In Ibn Masoud’s reading, and their hearts are more scattered means more divided, that is, more different. That is because they are a people who do not reason, meaning that this dispersion and disbelief is because they have no reason to understand God’s command.
59:15: Ibn Abbas said: It means Qaynuqa', God gave them power over them before Banu Nadir. Qatadah said: It means Banu Nadir, God gave them power over them before Qurayzah. Mujahid said: It means the infidels of Quraysh on the day of Badr. It was said: It is general for everyone who was retaliated against for his disbelief before Banu Nadir from Noah to Muhammad, peace be upon him. The meaning of and the retribution is the recompense for their disbelief. Whoever says: It refers to Banu Qurayzah, makes the retribution of their affair their punishment based on the judgment of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, who ruled that the fighters should be killed and the children taken captive. This is the opinion of Ad-Dahhak. Whoever says that it refers to Banu Nadir, says: the retribution of their affair means expulsion and banishment. There were two years between Nadir and Qurayzah. The Battle of Badr took place six months before the Battle of Banu Nadir, which is why he said: Nearby. Some people said: The Battle of Banu Nadir took place after the Battle of Uhud. And for them is a painful punishment in the Hereafter.
59:16: The Almighty said: Like Satan when he said to man, ‘Disbelieve.’ This is a parable of the hypocrites and the Jews in their cowardice and failure to fulfill their duty to support them. The conjunction was omitted, and he did not say: Like Satan, because the omission of the conjunction is common, as in saying: You are wise, “You are generous,” You are knowledgeable. It was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The man to whom Satan said, Disbelieve, was a monk who had left a woman with him who had been afflicted with a disease, so that he could pray for her. Satan made it attractive to him, so he had intercourse with her and she became pregnant. Then he killed her for fear that he would be disgraced. Satan guided her people to her location, so they came and brought the monk down to kill him. Satan came and promised him that if he prostrated to him, he would save him from them. So he prostrated to him, and Satan disavowed him, so he surrendered him. This was mentioned by Qadi Ismail and Ali ibn al-Madini on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah on the authority of Umar ibn Dinar on the authority of Urwah ibn Amir on the authority of Ubayd ibn Rafa’ah az-Zarqi on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. His story was mentioned in full by Ibn Abbas and Wahb ibn Munabbih, but their wording is different. Ibn Abbas said, regarding the verse, like Satan,: There was a monk during the period called Barsisa, who worshipped in his monastery for seventy years, during which he did not disobey God for a moment. He exhausted Satan, so Satan gathered the rebellious devils and said, Can I not find among you someone who can suffice me in the matter of Barsisa? Al-Abyad said, while he was The companion of the prophets is the one who intended to go to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the form of Gabriel to whisper to him in the form of revelation. Gabriel came and entered between them, then pushed him with his hand until he fell to the farthest reaches of India. This is what God Almighty said: Possessor of strength, secure in the presence of the Lord of the Throne (al-Takwir 81:20). He said, I will suffice you against him. So he set out, dressed in the garb of monks, and shaved the middle of his head until he came to the monastery of Barsisa. He called out to him, but he did not answer him. He did not stop praying except once every ten days, and he did not break his fast except once every ten days. He continued praying for ten, twenty, or more days. When Al-Abyad saw that he did not answer him, he turned to worship at the beginning of his monastery. When Barsisa turned from his prayer, he saw Al-Abyad standing and praying in the good manner of a monk. He regretted not answering him, and said: What is your need? He said: That I be with you, so that I may learn from your manners, and acquire from your knowledge, and that we may meet in worship. He said: I am busy and do not care about you. Then he turned to his prayer, and Al-Abyad also turned to prayer. When Barsisa saw the intensity of his diligence and worship, he said to him: What is your need? He said: Give me permission so that I may come up to you. So he gave him permission. Al-Abyad stayed with him for a year, not breaking his fast except once every forty days, and not ending his prayer except every forty days, and sometimes he extended it to eighty. When Barsisa saw his diligence, his soul declined. Then Al-Abyad said: I have supplications with which God heals the sick, the afflicted, and the insane. So he taught them to him. Then he came to Satan and said: By God, I have destroyed the man. Then he approached a man and strangled him. Then he said to his family - who had taken the form of a human -: Your companion has madness, so may I cure him? They said: Yes. He said: I am not able to control his madness, but take him to Barsisa, for he has the Greatest Name of God, by which if He is asked, He gives, and if He is called upon, He answers. So they came to him and he supplicated with those supplications, and Satan left him. Then the white man did that to the people and directed them to Barsisa and they were cured. So he went to a slave girl from the daughters of kings among three brothers. Their father had been a king, but he died and made his brother his successor. Her uncle had been a king among the children of Israel. He tortured her and strangled her. Then he came to them in the guise of a physician to treat her and said, "Her devil is rebellious and unbearable. But take her to Barsisa and leave her with him. When her devil comes, he will pray for her and she will be cured." They said, He does not respond to us to this. He said, Build a cell on the side of his cell and place her in it, and say, 'She is a trust with you, so be patient with her.' They asked him to do that but he refused. So they built a cell and placed the slave girl in it. When he finished his prayer, he saw the slave girl and her beauty and he despaired of it. Then the devil came to her and strangled her. He finished his prayer and prayed for her and the devil left her. Then he went back to his prayer and the devil came to her and strangled her. He would uncover her and expose her to Barsisa, then Satan came to him and said: Woe to you! He had intercourse with her, for you have never found anyone like her, and then she repented. He kept on doing this until she became pregnant and her pregnancy was revealed. Satan said to him: Woe to you! You have been disgraced. Would you like to kill her and then repent so that you will not be disgraced? If they come to you and ask you, say that her devil came to her and took her away. So Barsisa killed her and buried her at night. Satan took the hem of her garment until only a piece of dirt remained sticking out of her, and Barsisa went back to his prayer. Then Satan came to her brothers in a dream and said: Barsisa did such and such to your sister, killed her and buried them both on such and such a mountain. They were astonished by that and said to Barsisa: Who is our sister? He said: Her devil took her away. They believed him and left. Then Satan came to them in a dream and said: She is buried in such and such a place, and the edge of her cloak is sticking out of the dirt. So they went and found her, and they demolished his cell, took him down, strangled him, and carried him to the king, where he confessed to it. The king ordered him to be killed. When he was crucified, Satan said: Do you recognize me? He said: No, by God! Satan said: I am your companion who taught you the supplications. Did you not fear God? Were you not ashamed while you were the most worshipped of the Children of Israel? Then your deed was not enough for you until you disgraced yourself, confessed to it, and disgraced those like you among the people! If you die in this state, no one of your peers will succeed after you. He said: What should I do? He said: Obey me in one thing and I will save you from them and I will take control of their eyes. He said: How is that? He said: Prostrate to me once. The king said: I will do that, so he prostrated to him instead of God. He said: O Barsisa, this is what I have shown you. The consequence of your affair was that you disbelieved in your Lord. I am innocent of you. I fear God, the Lord of the worlds. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: There was a worshipper among the Children of Israel, and he was one of the most devout people of his time. There were three brothers in his time who had a sister, and she was a virgin. They had no other sister. An expedition set out against the three of them, and they did not know with whom they should leave their sister, nor with whom they could feel safe, nor with whom they could place her. They agreed to leave her with a slave of the Children of Israel, and he had confidence in themselves. They came to him and asked him to leave her with him, so that she would be under his protection and care until they returned from their campaign, but he refused and sought refuge in God from them and from their sister. He said: They kept at him until he made them greedy. He said: Place her in a house opposite my monastery. So they placed her in that house, then they left her. She remained in the care of that worshipper for a while. Food would be brought down to her from his monastery, and he would place it at the door of the monastery, then he would close the door and go up to his monastery. Then he would order her to leave her house and take from her house what he had placed for her of food. Satan was gracious to him and he continued to encourage him to do good, and he made it difficult for him that the girl would leave her house during the day, and he would fear that someone would see her and he would hang her. He said: So he remained like that for a while, then Satan came to him and encouraged him to do good and gain reward, and said to him: If you were to walk to her with her food and place it in her house, your reward would be greater. He said: So he kept on at him until he walked to her with her food and placed it in her house. He said: So he remained like that for a while, then Satan came and encouraged him to do good and urged him to do it, and said: If you were to talk to her and converse with her so that she would find comfort in your conversation, for she has become very lonely. He said: So he kept on at him until he talked to her for a while, looking down on her from the top of his cell. He said: Then Satan came to him after that and said: If you were to go down to her and sit at the door of your cell and talk to her, and she would sit at the door of her house and talk to you, that would be more comfortable for her. He kept at him until he brought him down and sat him at the door of his cell to talk to her, and the slave girl came out of her house. They stayed talking for a while. Then Satan came to him and encouraged him to do good and to receive a good reward for what he would do to her. He said, If you were to leave the door of your cell and sit near the door of her house, that would be more pleasant for her. He kept at him until he did. They stayed at him for a while. Then Satan came to him and encouraged him to do good and to receive a good reward for what he would do to her. He said to him, If you were to come near the door of her house and talk to her, but she did not come out of her house, so he did. He would come down from his cell and sit at the door of her house and talk to her. They stayed like that for a while. Then Satan came to him and said, If you were to enter the house and talk to her and not let her show her face to anyone, that would be better for you. He kept at him until he entered the house. He talked to her all day, and in the evening he would go up to his cell. He said: Then Satan came to him after that, and he continued to adorn her for him until he struck the worshipper on her thigh and kissed her. Satan kept making her look good in his eyes and tempted him until he fell upon her and she became pregnant, and she bore him a boy. Then Satan came to him and said: What do you think if the brothers of this slave girl came and she had given birth to you? What would you do? Would you be safe from being disgraced or they disgracing you? Go to her son, slaughter him, and bury him, for she will conceal from you what you did to her for fear that her brothers will find out what you did to her. So he did. Then Satan said to him: Do you think she would conceal from her brothers what you did to her and the killing of her son? Take her, slaughter her, and bury her with her son. He kept on at her until he slaughtered her and threw her into the pit with her son. He closed a huge rock over her, leveled the dirt over it, and went up to his monastery to worship in it. He remained like that as long as God willed him to remain, until her brothers returned from the conquest. They came to him and asked him about her. He shed the report of her death to them and asked for mercy for her. He wept for them and said: She was the best of women, and this is her grave, so look at it. Her brothers came to the grave and wept over her grave and asked for mercy for her. They stayed at her grave for a few days and then returned to their families. When night fell upon them and they went to bed, Satan came to them in the form of a traveler. He began with the eldest of them and asked him about their sister, peace be upon her. Satan informed him of the words of the worshipper, her death, and his mercy upon her, and how he showed them the location of her grave. Satan denied him and said, "You did not believe the story of your sister. Indeed, your sister became pregnant and she bore him a boy. He slaughtered him and her with him, frightening you. He threw her into a pit he had dug behind the door where she had been, on the right of whoever entered. So speak and enter the house where she had been, on the right of whoever entered, for you will find her all there, as I have told you." He said, "The middle one came in his dream and told him the same thing. Then he came to the youngest of them and told him the same thing. When the people awoke, they awoke amazed at what each of them had seen. They turned to one another, each saying, 'I have seen something strange.' So they told each other what they had seen. The eldest of them said, 'This is a dream, nothing. Let us go and leave this one.'" The youngest of them said, I will not go until I reach that place and look into it. So they all set out until they entered the house where their sister was. They opened the door and searched for the place he had described to them in their dream. They found their sister and her son slaughtered in the pit, just as they had been told. They questioned the worshipper, and he confirmed what Satan had said about what he had done to them. They summoned their king against them, and he came down from his cell. They brought him forward to be crucified. When they had made him stand on the cross, Satan came to him and said, "You know that I am your companion who tempted you with the woman until she became pregnant and you slaughtered her and her son. If you obey me today and disbelieve in God who created you, I will deliver you from what you are in." So the worshipper disbelieved in God, and when he disbelieved, Satan left him alone with his companions, and they crucified him. He said, "It was about him that this verse was revealed: 'The example of Satan when he says to man, "Disbelieve. But when he disbelieved, he says, Indeed, I am disassociated from you. Indeed, I fear God, Lord of the worlds.' - until His saying - The recompense of the wrongdoers." Ibn Abbas said: God made this example of the hypocrites with the Jews. God the Almighty commanded His Prophet (peace be upon him) to expel Banu Nadir from Medina. The hypocrites sent them a message saying: “Do not leave your homes. If they fight you, we will be with you, and if they expel you, we will be with you.” So they fought the Prophet (peace be upon him), but the hypocrites let them down and disowned them, just as Satan disowned the worshipper Barsisa. After that, the monks would only walk in piety and secrecy. The wicked and immoral people coveted the rabbis, so they accused them of slander and ugly things, until the case of the monk Jareeh. God exonerated him, and after that the monks expanded and became visible to the people. It was said: The meaning is that the hypocrites, in their treachery towards Banu Nadir, is like Satan when he said to the infidels of Quraysh 106:No one can overcome you today from among mankind, and indeed, I am your protector. (al-Anfal 8:48) Mujahid said: Here, by ‘humans’, refers to all people in Satan’s deception of them. The meaning of the Almighty’s saying: When he said to man, ‘Disbelieve,’ is that he led him astray until he said, I am a disbeliever. Satan’s saying, Indeed, I fear God, Lord of the worlds, is not literal; rather, it is to disavow man. It is an emphasis on the Almighty’s saying, Indeed, I am innocent of you. Nafi’, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr opened the ya’ of inna with the fat-ha. The rest left it sukun. So the outcome of them both meaning the outcome of Satan and that man was that they would both be in the Fire, abiding eternally therein is an accusative in the state of the dual. The dual is apparent from those who made the verse specific to the monk and Satan. Whoever makes it in the genus, the meaning is: And the outcome of the two groups or categories was in the accusative case as the predicate of was. The noun is that they would both be in the Fire. Al-Hasan read so the outcome of them in the nominative case, which is the opposite of that. Al-A’mash read abiding therein in the nominative case, which is contrary to the written form. Its nominative case is as the predicate of that, and the circumstance is omitted.
59:18: The Almighty says: O you who have believed, fear God in His commands and prohibitions, performing His obligations and avoiding His disobedience. And let a soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow meaning the Day of Resurrection. The Arabs use the word tomorrow as a metaphor for the future. It has been said that mentioning tomorrow is an indication that the Hour is near, as the poet said: Tomorrow is near for those who look Al-Hasan and Qatada said: The Hour is so near that it is like tomorrow. There is no doubt that everything that is coming is near, and death is inevitable. The meaning of what you have put forth means good or evil. And fear God He repeated this repeatedly, like saying: Hurry, hurry, throw, throw. It was said that the first type of piety is repentance for past sins, and the second type is avoiding disobedience in the future. Indeed, God is Acquainted with what you do Saeed bin Jubair said: meaning what will happen from you. And God knows best.
59:19: The Almighty said: And do not be like those who forgot God meaning abandoned His command So He made them forget themselves so that they could not do good for them, as stated by Ibn Hayyan. It was also said: They forgot the right of God, so He made them forget the right of themselves, as stated by Sufyan. It was also said: They forgot God by abandoning thanking and glorifying Him. So He made them forget themselves by the punishment so that they could not remember one another, as related by Ibn 'Isa. Sahl ibn 'Abdullah said: They forgot God when they committed sins, So He made them forget themselves when they repented. God attributed the action to Himself in causing them to forget if that was because of His commands and prohibitions that they abandoned. It was also said that its meaning is that He found them abandoning His commands and prohibitions, like you would say: I praised the man if you found him praiseworthy. It was also said: They forgot God in times of ease, So He made them forget themselves in times of hardship. Those are the wicked. Ibn Jubayr said: The disobedient. Ibn Zayd said: Liars. The root of transgression is to go out, meaning those who went out of obedience to God.
59:20: The Almighty says: The companions of the Fire are not equal to the companions of Paradise meaning in merit and rank. The companions of Paradise are the successful ones meaning the ones brought near and honored. It was also said: those saved from the Fire. The meaning of this verse has already been discussed in Surat Al-Ma'idah when God says: Say, 'The wicked are not equal to the good' (al-Ma’idah 5:100). And in Surat As-Sajdah when God says: Is he who is a believer like he who is a disobedient? They are not equal (al-Sajdah 32:18). And in Surat Sad: Or should We treat those who believe and do righteous deeds like corrupters in the land, or should We treat the righteous like the wicked? (Sad: 28). So there is no point in repeating it, and praise be to God.
59:21: The Almighty said: If We had sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled. This refers to contemplating the admonitions of the Qur'an. He explained that there is no excuse for neglecting to ponder, because if this Qur'an were addressed to the mountains, despite their innate intelligence, they would have been moved by its admonition, and you would have seen them, despite their solidity and sturdiness, humbled and cracked, meaning cracked out of fear of God. The humble is the one who is submissive. The cracked is the one who is cracked. It was also said: humbled before God for what He has charged them with of obedience. Cracked out of fear of God that they disobey Him and He would punish them. It was also said that it is a metaphor for the disbeliever. God the Almighty says: {And these examples We present to the people} meaning, if this Qur’an were sent down upon a mountain, it would humble itself at His promise and crack at His threat. But you, who are oppressed by its miraculous nature, do not desire His promise nor are you in awe of His threat! It was also said that the address is to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), saying: Yes, O Muhammad, We sent down this Qur’an upon a mountain because it would have been firm and cracked by its sending down upon it. But We have sent it down to you and made you firm for it. So this is an expression of gratitude to Him for making it firm when mountains cannot be firm for it. It was also said that it is addressed to the Ummah, and that if God the Almighty were to warn the mountains with this Qur’an, they would have cracked out of fear of God. Man is less strong but more steadfast, so he stands up to it if he obeys, and is able to turn it back if he disobeys, because he is promised reward and warned against punishment.
59:22: The Almighty said: He is God, other than whom there is no deity, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. Ibn Abbas said: Knower of the secret and the open. It was also said: What was and what will be. Sahl said: Knower of the Hereafter and this world. It was also said: The unseen is what the servants do not know or witness. And the witnessed is what they know and witness. He is the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. It was mentioned above.
59:23: The Almighty's saying: He is God, other than whom there is no god, the Sovereign, the Holy meaning the One who descends from every shortcoming, and the Pure from every fault. Al-Quds with a fat-ha is a bucket in the dialect of the people of Hijaz, because it is used for purification. And from this comes the word qadus, which is one of the vessels used to draw water from a well with a bucket. Sibawayh used to say: Quddus and Subuh, with the first letter fat-ha. Abu Hatim narrated on the authority of Yaqub that he heard an eloquent Bedouin known as Abu al-Dinar at Al-Kisa'i's house who read al-Quddus with the first letter fat-ha. Tha'lab said: Every noun on the pattern fa'ul has a fat-ha on the first letter, like safood, kulubb, tanour, samur, and shabut, except for al-Subuh and al-Quddus, which are more common with a damma, and they may also have a fat-ha. The same applies to al-Duruh with a damma, which may also have a fat-ha. As-Salam means the one who is free from faults. Ibn al-Arabi said: The scholars, may God have mercy on them, agreed that the meaning of our saying about God, “Peace,” is the relation, meaning the possessor of safety. Then they differed in translating the relation into three opinions: The first - its meaning is the one who is safe from every defect and innocent of every deficiency. The second - He is the possessor of peace, meaning the one who greets his servants in Paradise, as He said: “Peace, a word from a Lord, Most Merciful” (Ya-Sin 36:58). The third - its meaning is the one from whose injustice creation is safe. I said: This is the saying of Al-Khattabi, and based on it and what preceded it, it is an adjective of an action. And based on the fact that it is free from faults and shortcomings, it is an adjective of the essence. It was said: Peace means the one who submits to His servants. The believer means the one who believes in His messengers by showing them His miracles, and the one who believes in the believers what He promised them of reward, and the one who believes in the disbelievers what He threatened them with of punishment. It was said: The believer is the one who makes His allies feel secure from His punishment, and makes His servants feel secure from His tyranny. It is said: He made him feel secure from security, which is the opposite of fear, as God Almighty said: And made them feel secure from fear (Quraysh 106:4), so he is a believer. An-Nabigha said: The faithful birds are touched by the riders of Mecca between Ghayl and Sind. Mujahid said: The believer is the one who unified himself by saying: God bears witness that there is no god but He (Al Imran 3:18). Ibn Abbas said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, the people of monotheism will be taken out of the Fire. The first to be taken out will be the one whose name matches the name of a prophet, until when no one remains in it whose name matches the name of a prophet, God will say to those who remain: You are the Muslims and I am Al-Salam, and you are the believers and I am the believer, so He will take them out of the Fire by the blessing of these two names. Al-Muhaymin, Al-Mighty: We have already discussed Al-Muhaymin in Al-Ma’idah and Al-Mighty in more than one place. Al-Jabbar: Ibn Abbas said: He is the Magnificent. The might of God is His greatness. According to this statement, it is an attribute of the Essence, from their saying: a mighty palm tree. Imru’ al-Qais said: Sumuq Jabbar Athith, its branches are high and its canes are made of red dates It means the palm tree that missed the hand. So this name indicates the greatness of God and His sanctification from being affected by shortcomings and the characteristics of the event. It was said: It is from the word jabr which means to repair. It is said: I repaired the great and he repaired it, meaning you repaired it after it was broken. It is a fa’al from jabr if you repaired the break and enriched the poor. Al-Farra’ said: It is from ajbarahu to do something, meaning he subdued him. He said: I did not hear a fa’al from af’al except in jabar and dirak from idraka. It was said: The tyrant is the one whose power is unbearable. Al-Mutakabbir is the one who is arrogant with his lordship, so there is nothing like him. It was said: The arrogant is above all evil, the one who is too proud to speak or criticize what is not befitting of him. The origin of arrogance and pride is abstinence and lack of discipline. Humaid ibn Thawr said: She forgave as a young camel forgives, so she became proud of the tough, yet she was submissive. Pride in the attributes of God is praiseworthy, and in the attributes of created beings it is blameworthy. In the Sahih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, as narrated from his Lord, the Blessed and Exalted, that He said: “Pride is My cloak and greatness is My garment. Whoever disputes with Me over either of them, I will break him and then throw him into the Fire.” It was said that al-Mutakabbir means the exalted. It was also said that it means the great, because He is too exalted to be arrogant. It may also be said: Tazalam means he oppressed, “Tashattam” means he cursed, and istiqara means he settled. Likewise, al-Mutakabbir means the great. It is not like how a creature is described by the verb tafa’ala when it is attributed to something that is not from it. Then He purified Himself and said: Glory be to God, meaning purifying His Majesty and Greatness from what they associate with Him.
59:24: The Almighty says: He is God, the Creator, the Inventor, the Fashioner. “The Creator” here is the Determiner. The Inventor is the Willer, the Inventor. The Fashioner is the Fashioner of images and their Compiler in different forms. Fashioning is ordered to creation and origination and is subordinate to them. The meaning of becoming is planning and shaping. God created man in the wombs of their mothers three creations: He made him a clot, then a lump of flesh, then He made him an image, which is the shaping by which he comes into an image and form by which he is known and distinguished from others by its feature. So blessed be God, the best of creators. Al-Nabigha said: The Creator, the Maker, the Fashioner, creates water in the wombs until it becomes blood. Some people have interpreted creation to mean formation, but this is not the case. Rather, becoming is the last, and the meaning is the first, and creation is between them. From this is the saying of the Truth: And when you created from clay, in the form of a bird (al-Ma’idah 5:110). Zuhair said: You create what you created, while some people create and then do not create. He says: You estimate what you estimate and then you fulfill it, that is, you carry it out according to your estimate, while others estimate what they cannot complete and what they want, either because of their inability to imagine their estimate or their inability to fulfill their goal. We have already discussed all of this in the book Al-Ansi in explaining the Most Beautiful Names of God. All praise is due to God. It is narrated on the authority of Hatib ibn Abi Balta’ah that he read Al-Bari’ Al-Musawwir with a fat-ha on the waw and a nasb on the ra’, meaning He who creates the fashioner, that is, He distinguishes what He forms with varying forms. Al-Zamakhshari mentioned it. “To Him belong the best names. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth exalts Him. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.” This has been discussed previously. Abu Hurairah said: I asked my close friend Abu Al-Qasim, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), about the Greatest Name of God. He said, O Abu Hurairah, recite the end of Surah Al-Hashr and recite it often. So I repeated it to him and he repeated it to me, so I repeated it to him and he repeated it to me. Jabir ibn Zayd said: The Greatest Name of God is God because of the location of this verse. On the authority of Anas ibn Malik: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever recites Surat al-Hashr, God will forgive him his past and future sins. And on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever recites the final verses of Surat al-Hashr during the night or day, and God takes his soul during that night or that day, God has made Paradise obligatory for him.
60:1: Al-Mumtahanah with a kasra on the ha means the tested one. The verb was added to it metaphorically, just as Surah Bara’ah and Al-Fadihah were named after it, because it revealed the faults of the hypocrites. Whoever says about this Surah Al-Mumtahanah with a fatha on the ha then he has added it to the woman about whom it was revealed, and she is Umm Kulthum bint Uqbah ibn Abi Mu’ayt. God Almighty said: “So test them. God knows best about their faith,” the verse. She is the wife of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, and she bore him Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Rahman. The Almighty said: O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies. The verb takhada has two objects, which are your enemy as allies. The word enemy is a verb from ada, like forgiving from forgiving. Because it has the weight of a verbal noun, it is applied to the plural as it is applied to the singular. There are seven issues in this verse: First: The Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as your friends. The Imams narrated, and the wording is from Muslim, “On the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent us, Al-Zubayr, and Al-Miqdad, and said: Go to Rawdat Khakh, for there is a woman there with a letter, so take it from her. So we set off, our horses racing, and there we came to the woman, and we said: Bring out the letter. She said: I do not have a letter. We said: Either bring out the letter or throw away the clothes. So she took it out of her tie, and we brought it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in it was: From Hatib bin Abi Balta’ah to some of the polytheists of Mecca, informing them of some of the affairs of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Hatib, what is this? He said: Do not be hasty with me, O Messenger of God, for I was a man attached to the Quraysh. Sufyan said: He was an ally of them, but he was not one of them, and among those who were with you were the emigrants who had relatives with whom they protected their families, so I wanted to…” “If I missed that from the lineage among them, that I would take a hand among them with which they would redeem my kinship, and I did not do it out of disbelief or apostasy from my religion, nor satisfaction with disbelief after Islam, then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He is truthful. Then Umar said: Let me, O Messenger of God, strike off the head of this hypocrite. He said: He witnessed Badr, and how do you know? Perhaps God looked at the people of Badr and said: Do what you want, for I have forgiven you. Then God Almighty revealed: “O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies.” It was said that the woman’s name was Sarah, from the clients of Quraysh, and it was in the letter: As for what follows, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has headed towards you with an army like the night, moving like a torrent, and I swear by God that if he had not marched towards you except alone, God would have given him victory over you and fulfilled his promise to you, for God is his Guardian and Supporter. Some of the commentators mentioned it, and Al-Qushayri and Al-Tha’labi mentioned: “Hatib bin Abi Balta’ah was a man from the people of Yemen, and he had an alliance in Mecca with Banu Asad bin Abd Al-Uzza, the people of Al-Zubayr bin Al-Awwam, It was said: He was an ally of Al-Zubayr ibn Al-Awwam, so Sarah, the slave girl of Abu Amr ibn Saifi ibn Hisham ibn Abd Manaf, came from Mecca to Medina while the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was preparing to conquer Mecca. It was said: This was during the time of Al-Hudaybah, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to her: Have you come as a migrant, O Sarah? She said: No. He said: Have you come as a Muslim? She said: No. He said: So what brought you? She said: You were my family, my clients, my origin, and my clan, and the clients have gone - meaning they were killed on the day of Badr - and I was in dire need, so I came to you so that you would give me some and clothe me. He, peace be upon him, said: So where are you compared to the youth of the people of Mecca? She was a singer. He said: Nothing was asked of me after the Battle of Badr. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, urged Banu Abd Al-Muttalib and Banu Al-Muttalib to give her some, so they clothed her, gave her some, and carried her. She went out to Mecca, and Hatib came to her and said: I will give you ten dinars and a cloak on condition that you deliver this letter to the people of Mecca. He wrote in the letter: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wants you, so be on your guard. Sarah went out and Gabriel came down and informed the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) of that. He sent Ali, Az-Zubayr and Abu Marthad Al-Ghanawi. In another narration: Ali, Az-Zubayr and Al-Miqdad. In another narration: He sent Ali and Ammar ibn Yasir. In another narration: Ali, Ammar, Umar, Az-Zubayr, Talhah, Al-Miqdad and Abu Marthad. They were all horsemen. He said to them: Go until you reach Rawdat Khakh, for there is a rebellious woman there and with her is a letter from Hatib to the polytheists. Take it from her and let her go. If she does not give it to you, strike off her head. They caught up with her in that place and said to her: Where is the letter? She swore that she did not have a letter with her. They searched her belongings but did not find any letter with her. They intended to return, but Ali said: By God, we have not lied, nor have we lied! He drew his sword and said: “Take out the letter, or by God I will unsheathe you and cut off your head.” When she saw the seriousness, she took it out from her forelock, and in another narration, from her room. They released her and returned with the letter to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He sent to Hatib and said: Do you recognize the letter? He said: Yes. He mentioned the hadith in a similar manner to the one mentioned above. It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, granted security to all the people on the day of the conquest except for four, one of whom was she. Second: The Surah is the origin of the prohibition of befriending infidels, and this has been mentioned in more than one place. And among these is the saying of God Almighty: Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies rather than the believers (Al Imran 3:28), O you who have believed, do not take as intimates those other than yourselves (Al Imran 3:118), O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies (Al Ma’idah: 51), and there are many like it. It was mentioned that Hatib heard O you who have believed and fainted from joy at the address of faith. Third: The Almighty’s statement: You throw affection to them means outwardly, because Hatib’s heart was sound, as evidenced by the fact that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: As for your companion, he has spoken the truth. This is a clear statement of the soundness of his heart and the sincerity of his belief. The ba in affection is redundant, as you say: I read the surah and I read the surah, and I conveyed to him what was in my heart and what was in my heart. It is permissible for it to be fixed, with the object of you throw affection to them being omitted, meaning you throw report of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to them because of the affection between you and them. Likewise, you whisper affection to them means because of affection. Al-Farra’ said: You throw affection to them is related to friends, and the inclusion of the ba in affection and its exclusion are the same. It is permissible for it to be related to do not take as a state of its pronoun, and to friends as a description of it. It is permissible for it to be a new sentence. The meaning of you throw affection to them is that you inform them of the secrets of the Muslims and advise them. Al-Zajjaj said the same.
