Fourth: If someone frequently looks into the faults of Muslims, warns them about them, and informs their enemy of their report, he is not considered an unbeliever if his action is for a worldly purpose and his belief in that is sound, as Hatib did when he intended to seize the hand and did not intend to apostatize from the religion. Fifth: If we say that he is not an unbeliever because of that, then is he to be killed as a prescribed punishment for that or not? People differed on this. Malik, Ibn al-Qasim, and Ashhab said: The imam should make his own judgment on that. Abd al-Malik said: If it was his habit to kill, then he is a spy. Malik said: The spy is to be killed, and this is the correct view, because he harms the Muslims and seeks to spread corruption on earth. Perhaps Ibn al-Majishun only repeated this because Hatib was caught at the beginning of his action, and God knows best. Sixth: If the spy is an infidel, Al-Awza’i said: It would be a breach of his covenant. Asbagh said: The military spy is to be killed, and the Muslim spy and the dhimmi are to be punished unless they cooperate in Islam, in which case they are to be killed. It was narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him: “A spy of the polytheists named Furat ibn Hayyan was brought to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he ordered that he be killed. He cried out: O group of Ansar, should I be killed while I bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God! So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that he be released, then he said: There are among you those who have accepted his faith, among them Furat ibn Hayyan.” His saying: And they disbelieved is a state, either from do not take or from you meet meaning do not take them as allies or befriend them, and this is their state. Al-Jahdary read when it came to you meaning they disbelieved because of what came to you of the truth. Seventh: The Almighty’s statement: They expel the Messenger is a new statement as an explanation of their disbelief and their obstinacy, or a condition of they disbelieved. “And you, lest you believe in God, your Lord” is an explanation of they expel. The meaning is that they expel the Messenger and expel you from Mecca because you believe in God, that is, because of your belief in God. Ibn Abbas said: Hatib was among those who went out with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: There is an inversion in the statement, and the meaning is: Do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies if you went out striving in My cause. It was said: There is an ellipsis in the statement, and the meaning is: If you went out striving in My cause and seeking My pleasure, then do not show them affection. It was said: If you went out striving in My cause and seeking My pleasure is a condition and its answer is presented. The meaning is: If you go out to fight in My cause, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies. The word fighting and seeking are in the accusative case because they are objects of the verb. His statement, You secretly go to them with affection is a substitute for you receive and clarifies it. Verbs are substituted for verbs, as God Almighty said, “And whoever does that will meet a sin. Doubled for him will be the punishment.” Sibawayh recited: When you come to visit us in our homes, you will find abundant firewood and a blazing fire. It was said: It is on the assumption that you are showing them affection, so it is a new beginning, and all of this is a rebuke to Hatib, and it indicates his virtue, his honor, his advice to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the sincerity of his faith, for rebuke is only from one who loves his beloved, as he said: I blame the affection of a friend if he dislikes me and avoids me If the reproach is gone, there is no friendship, and friendship remains as long as the reproach remains The meaning of with affection is with advice in the book to them. The ba is either redundant as we mentioned, or it is fixed and not redundant. God the Almighty said: And I know what you conceal you concealed and what you declare you made public. The ba in bima is redundant. It is said: I knew such-and-such and I knew such-and-such. It was also said: I know better than anyone what you conceal and what you make public, so min kullu was omitted, just as it is said: So-and-so is more knowledgeable and better than someone else. Ibn Abbas said: I know better what you concealed in your hearts and what you made public with your tongues of acknowledgment and monotheism. And whoever among you does it meaning whoever among you whispers to them and writes to them has certainly strayed from the right path meaning he has missed the right path.
60:2: The Almighty said: If they encounter you means they meet you and come across you. From this comes the word muthaqafah, meaning seeking to catch you by surprise in combat and the like. It was also said: if they encounter you means they will overcome you and gain power over you. They will be enemies to you and will stretch out their hands and tongues against you with evil meaning their hands with beating and killing, and their tongues with cursing. They wish that you would disbelieve in Muhammad, so do not advise them, for they will not advise you.
60:3: The Almighty’s saying: Your wombs will not benefit you. When Hatib apologized by saying that he had children and wombs between them, the Almighty Lord explained that family and children will not benefit you at all on the Day of Resurrection if you disobey because of that. He will judge between you. He will admit the believers into Paradise and admit the disbelievers into Hell. There are seven readings for yufasil: Asim read yufasil with a fatha on the ya’ and a kasra on the sad, and with a light pronunciation. Hamza and al-Kisa’i read it with a shaddah except that it is for the one who did not name the agent. Talha and al-Nakha’i read it with a kasra on the sad, and with a shaddah. It was narrated from Alqamah likewise with a light noon. Qatada and Abu Haywah read yufasil with a damma on the ya’ and a kasra on the sad, and with a light pronunciation from afdal. The rest read yufasil with a damma on the ya’ and a light fa’ and a fatha on the sad, and with a passive verb. Abu Ubaid chose this. Whoever read it with a light pronunciation is because of His saying: And He is better. “The separators” (al-An’am 6:57), and His statement: The Day of Separation (Al-Naba’: 17). Whoever emphasized it, it is because that is clearer in the case of a verb that is frequently repeated and iterated. Whoever used it without naming its agent, it is because the agent is known. Whoever used it with a named agent, it refers the pronoun back to God Almighty. Whoever reads it with the letter nun then it is for emphasis, And God is Seeing of what you do.
60:4: The Almighty said: "Indeed, in Abraham you have a good example to follow." When God Almighty forbade befriending the infidels, He mentioned the story of Abraham, peace be upon him, and that part of his conduct was to disavow the infidels, meaning follow his example and complete it, except for his seeking forgiveness for his father. An example is that which is followed, like a role model and an example. It is said: He is your example, meaning like you and you are like him. Asim read (aswa) with a damma on the hamza, two dialects. And those with him means the companions of Abraham from the believers. Ibn Zayd said: They are the prophets when they said to their people the infidels Indeed, we are innocent of you and of what you worship other than God meaning the idols. Bara’ is the plural of bari’, like sharīk and sharīk, ẓarif and ẓarifā’. The reading of the general public is on the weight of fa’ala’. Isa ibn ‘Umar and Ibn Abi Ishaq read (bara’) with a kasra on the ba’ on the weight of fa’al, like qasīr and qaṣār, and tawīl and tawwāl, and ẓarif And it is permissible to leave the hamza until you say: barra, and you add a tanween, and (bara’) was read as a description of the source, and (bara’) was read as a replacement for the damma from the kasra, like khal and rabab, and the verse is a text in the order to follow the example of Abraham, peace be upon him, in his actions, and that corrects that the law of those before us is a law for us in what God and His Messenger have informed, We disbelieved in you meaning in what you believed in of idols. And it was said: meaning in your actions, and we denied them and denied them that you are on the truth, And there appeared between us and you enmity and hatred forever meaning this is our way with you as long as you are on your disbelief, until you believe in God alone then the enmity turns into friendship except for the saying of Abraham to his father, “I will surely ask forgiveness for you so do not follow his example in asking forgiveness and ask forgiveness for the polytheists, for it was from a promise from him to him, said Qatadah and Mujahid and others, and it was said that the meaning of the exception is that Abraham abandoned and distanced them except in asking forgiveness for his father, then he explained His excuse is in Surat At-Tawbah. This is evidence of the superiority of our Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, over all other prophets, because when we were commanded to follow his example, we were commanded in an absolute manner in the words of God Almighty: And whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and what he has forbidden you - refrain from (al-Hashr 59:7). And when we were commanded to follow Abraham, peace be upon him, He made an exception for some of his actions. It was said that it is a disjunctive exception, meaning that Abraham’s saying to his father, I will surely ask forgiveness for you, only happened because he thought that he had become Muslim, but when it became clear to him that he had not become Muslim, he disowned him. Based on this, it is permissible to ask forgiveness for someone who thinks that he has become Muslim, and you did not find such an assumption, so you did not befriend them. And I have no power for you against God at all This is from the words of Abraham, peace be upon him, to his father, meaning I cannot ward off from you anything of God’s punishment if you associate partners with Him. Our Lord, in You we have put our trust This is from the supplication of Abraham, peace be upon him, and his companions. It was said that he taught the believers to say this, meaning disavow the disbelievers and put your trust in God and say: And to You we have turned back. "We have relied and to you we have returned meaning we have returned and to you is the destination" you will return in the hereafter.
60:5: Our Lord, do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve. That is, do not make us prevail so that they think they are right and are tempted by that. It was also said: Do not give them power over us so that they tempt us and torment us. "And forgive us, our Lord. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise."
60:6: God Almighty says: There has certainly been for you in them meaning in Abraham and the prophets and saints who were with him, an excellent pattern meaning in disavowing the disbelievers. It was said that it was repeated for emphasis, and it was said that the second was revealed after the first by a period of time, and there are many repetitions in the Qur’an in this manner. And whoever turns away meaning from Islam and accepting these sermons, then indeed, God is the Free of need meaning He did not worship them because of His need for them, the Praiseworthy in Himself and His attributes.
60:7: When this verse was revealed, the Muslims were hostile to their polytheist relatives. God knew the severity of the Muslims’ anxiety over this, so He revealed: Perhaps God will establish affection between you and those among you with whom you have been at enmity. This means that the disbeliever will convert to Islam. Some of them converted to Islam after the conquest of Mecca, and the Muslims mingled with them, such as Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, Al-Harith ibn Hisham, Suhayl ibn Amr, and Hakim ibn Hizam. It was said that the affection was the marriage of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Umm Habibah, the daughter of Abu Sufyan. At that time, Abu Sufyan’s temper softened, and his resolve in the enmity relaxed. Ibn Abbas said: She was married to Abdullah ibn Jahsh, and she and her husband were among the emigrants to Abyssinia. As for her husband, he converted to Christianity and asked her to follow him in his religion, but she refused and remained patient in her religion. Her husband died as a Christian, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent to the Negus and proposed to her. The Negus said to his companions: Who among you has the right to her? They said: Khalid ibn Sa`id ibn al-`As. He said: Then marry her to your Prophet. So he did, and the Negus gave her a dowry of four hundred dinars from his own money. It was also said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) proposed to her and sent her to him. Abu Sufyan, who was a polytheist, said when he heard that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had married his daughter: That stallion will not have his nose cut off. Yaqda` with the non-voweled dal, it is said: This is a stallion whose nose will not be cut off, meaning he will not have his nose cut off. This is if he is noble.
60:8: The Almighty’s saying: God does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion. There are three issues in this: First: This verse is a dispensation from God Almighty regarding the relationship with those who did not fight or oppose the believers. Ibn Zayd said: This was in the beginning of Islam when the truce was made and the command to fight was abandoned, then it was abrogated. Qatada said: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9:5). It was said: This ruling was for a reason, which was the peace treaty. When the peace treaty was abolished with the conquest of Mecca, the ruling was abrogated and the form remained and is recited. It was said: It is specific to the allies of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to those between whom and him there was a covenant that he did not break. This was said by Al-Hasan. Al-Kalbi: They are Khuza'ah and Banu al-Harith ibn Abd Manaf. Abu Salih said the same, and he said: They are Khuza'ah. Mujahid said: It is specific to those who believed but did not emigrate. It was said: He meant by it women and children because they are among those who do not fight, so God permitted being good to them. Some of the commentators narrated it. Most of the people of interpretation said: It is decisive and they provided evidence: “Asma' bint Abi Bakr asked the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Should she visit her mother when she came to her as a polytheist? He said: Yes.” Narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim. It was said that the verse was revealed about it, and Aamer bin Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr narrated on the authority of his father, that Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq divorced his wife who had been killed in the pre-Islamic period, and she was the mother of Asma bint Abi Bakr. She came to them during the period in which there was a truce between the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the infidels of Quraysh, and she presented Asma bint Abi Bakr Al-Siddiq with an earring and some things, but she was reluctant to accept them until she came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that to him, so God Almighty revealed: God does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion. This report was mentioned by Al-Mawardi and others, and Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi included it in his Musnad. The second: The Almighty’s saying: that you be righteous toward them (that) is in the accusative case as a substitute for (those), meaning that God does not forbid you from being righteous toward those who did not fight you, and they are Khuza’ah, who made a peace treaty with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that they would not fight him or aid anyone against him, so he ordered that they be righteous toward them and that they be fulfilled until their appointed time, as narrated by Al-Farra’, and that you be just toward them meaning that you give them a share of your wealth as a form of connection, and he does not mean by it justice, for justice is obligatory for those who fight and for those who do not fight, as Ibn Al-Arabi said. Third: Judge Abu Bakr said in his book, Al-Ahkam: “Some of those who are tied to it have used it as evidence that a Muslim son is obligated to provide for his infidel father. This is a great mistake, because permission for something or not prohibiting it does not indicate its obligation, but rather it gives you permission in particular. We have explained that Ismail bin Ishaq Al-Qadi had a dhimmi come to him and he honoured him, so those present took issue with him about that, so he recited this verse to them.”
60:9: The Almighty says: God only forbids you from those who fight you because of religion meaning those who strive against you for religion, and expel you from your homes and they are the rebellious people of Mecca, and aid meaning those who aided in expelling you, and they are the polytheists of Mecca, from taking them as allies (that) is in the accusative case as a substitute, as mentioned previously in (that you be righteous toward them), and whoever takes them as allies meaning takes them as allies, supporters, and loved ones, then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
60:10: The Almighty said: O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants, examine them. There are sixteen issues in this: First: The Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, when believing women come to you, when He commanded the Muslims to abandon the friendship of polytheists, this required the Muslims to emigrate from the lands of polytheism to the lands of Islam, and marriage was one of the most important reasons for friendship, so He explained the rulings on the emigration of women. Ibn Abbas said: The peace treaty with the polytheists of Quraysh took place in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah, on the condition that whoever came to him from the people of Mecca would be returned to them. Sa’idah bint Al-Harith Al-Aslamiyah came after the treaty was completed, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was still at Al-Hudaybiyyah. Her husband came, and he was an unbeliever, Saifi bin Al-Rahib, or it was said, Musafir Al-Makhzumi. He said: O Muhammad, return my wife to me, for you stipulated that! This clay of the Book had not yet dried, so God Almighty revealed this verse. It was said: “Umm Kulthum bint Uqbah ibn Abi Mu’ayt came, and her family came asking the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to return her. It was said: She ran away from her husband Amr ibn al-‘As, and with her were her two brothers, ‘Ammarah and al-Walid. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned her two brothers and imprisoned her. They said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Return her according to the condition. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The condition was for men, not for women, so God Almighty revealed this verse.” And on the authority of ‘Urwah, he said: Among the conditions that Suhayl ibn ‘Amr stipulated for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of al-Hudaybiyah was: No one from us should come to you, even if he is of your religion, except that you return him to us, until God Almighty revealed what He revealed regarding the believing women. This indicates that the condition regarding the return of women was abrogated by that. It was said: The one who came, Umaimah bint Bishr, was with Thabit ibn al-Shamrakh, so she ran away from him while he was a disbeliever at that time. So Sahl ibn Hunayf married her, and she bore him ‘Abdullah. Zayd ibn Habib said this. Al-Mawardi: Umaimah bint Bishr was married to Thabit bin Al-Shamrakh. Al-Mahdawi said: Ibn Wahb narrated on the authority of Khalid that this verse was revealed about Umaimah bint Bishr from Banu Amr bin Awf, and she was the command of Hassan bin Al-Dahdah. After her migration, Sahl bin Hanif married her. Muqatil said that she was Sa’idah, the wife of Saifi bin Al-Rahib, a polytheist from the people of Mecca. Most of the scholars said that she was Umm Kulthum bint Uqba. Second: The scholars differed as to whether women were included in the truce contract verbally or generally. A group of them said: The condition of returning them was explicitly stated in the truce contract, so God abrogated their return from the contract and forbade it, and the men remained as they were. This indicates that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, could exert his own judgment in rulings, but God did not allow him to be wrong. A group of the scholars said: Their return was not stipulated in the contract verbally, but rather the contract was made general in returning those who converted to Islam, so the apparent generality included them along with the men. God the Most High explained their exclusion from its generality, and differentiated between them and men for two reasons: First, that they have private parts and are forbidden to them, and second, that they are more tender-hearted and quicker to change than them. As for those of them who remain in their polytheism, they are returned to them. Third: The Almighty’s saying: Then test them. It was said that if one of them wanted to harm her husband, she said: “I will migrate to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.” Therefore, may God bless him and grant him peace, he ordered that they be tested. There are three opinions about what he tested them with: First: Ibn Abbas said: The test was that she would swear by God that she did not leave because of hatred for her husband, nor desire from one land to another, nor seeking worldly gain, nor love for any man among us, but rather out of love for God and His Messenger. So if she swore by God that there is no god but Him on that, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would give her husband her dowry and what he spent on her and would not return her. That is what God Almighty said: “But if you ascertain that they are believers, do not return them to the disbelievers. They are not lawful for the disbelievers, nor are they lawful for them.” Second: The ordeal was to testify that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. This was also said by Ibn Abbas. Third: With what He explained in the Surah after the words of God Almighty: O Prophet, when believing women come to you, Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was not tested except by the verse in which God said: When believing women come to you to pledge allegiance to you, narrated by Muammar on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Urwa Aisha. Al-Tirmidhi included it and said: This is a good and authentic hadith. Fourth: Most scholars are of the opinion that this abrogates what the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had covenanted with the Quraysh, that he would return to them whoever came to him as a Muslim. He abrogated that with regard to women. This is a view of which abrogation of the Sunnah by the Qur’an was taken. Some scholars said: It was abrogated with regard to men and women. It is not permissible for the imam to make a truce with the enemy on the condition that he returns to them whoever came to him as a Muslim, because it is permissible for a Muslim to stay in a land of polytheism. This is the view of the Kufians, and concluding a peace treaty on that basis is permissible according to Malik. The Kufians have cited as evidence for what they have said with regard to that the hadith of Ismail ibn Abi Khalid on the authority of Qays ibn Abi Hazim, “On the authority of Khalid ibn al-Walid: that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent him to a people from Khatham, and they held fast to prostration, so he killed them. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) paid them half the blood money, and said: I am innocent of every Muslim who stayed with a polytheist in the land of war, the fire of which cannot be seen.” They said: This abrogates the return of Muslims to the polytheists, since the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had absolved whoever stayed with them in the land of war. The view of Malik and al-Shafi’i is that this The ruling is not abrogated. Al-Shafi’i said: No one has the right to this contract except the Caliph or a man he orders, because he is in charge of all the money. So whoever concludes this contract other than the Caliph, it is rejected. Fifth: The Almighty’s statement: God knows best about their faith, meaning this is a test for you, and God knows best about their faith, because He is the One who takes care of secrets. And if you ascertain them to be believers, meaning by what is apparent of faith. It was said that if you ascertain them to be believers before the test, “then do not return them to the disbelievers. They are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them,” meaning God has not made it lawful for a believing woman to marry a disbeliever, nor for a believing man to marry a polytheist. This is the clearest evidence that what made a Muslim woman’s separation from her husband was her conversion to Islam, not her abandonment. Abu Hanifa said: What separated them was the difference between the two abodes. There is an allusion to this in the Maliki school of thought, or rather an expression, and the first is correct, because God Almighty said: They are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them. So He made it clear that the reason for the lack of permissibility is Islam and not the difference in the abode, and God knows best. Abu Omar said: There is no difference between the two abodes, neither in the Book nor in the Sunnah nor in analogy, but rather the consideration in that is the two religions, so the ruling is based on their difference and their meeting, not on the abode, and God is the source of help. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: And give them what they spent. God Almighty commanded that if a Muslim woman keeps her, her husband should return what he spent. This is from fulfilling the covenant, because when he was prevented from his family due to the sanctity of Islam, he commanded that the money be returned to him so that they would not suffer loss from both sides: the wife and the money. Seventh: There is no penalty unless the infidel husband demands it. If he comes and demands it, we prevent her and we pay. If she died before the husband came, we do not pay the dowry, as the prevention did not happen. If the specified amount was wine or pork, we do not pay anything, because it has no value. Al-Shafi’i has two opinions on this verse: One of them is that this is abrogated. Al-Shafi’i said: If a free woman from the people of the truce comes to us, a Muslim, emigrating from the land of war to the imam in the land of Islam or in the land of war, then whoever requests her from a guardian other than her husband, he is prevented from her without compensation. If her husband requests her for himself or someone else through his agency, then there are two opinions: One of them is that compensation is given, and the opinion is what God Almighty said. Another opinion is that the polytheist husband whose wife came as a Muslim is not given the honor, because the condition of the imam was to return the women. The condition, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was not to return the women. It was a condition of the condition of returning the women, and it was abrogated, and there is no compensation for it, because the abrogated condition is invalid and there is no compensation for invalidity. Eighth: God Almighty has commanded that what they spent be returned to their wives, and that the one addressed by this Imam should implement what is in his possession from the public treasury that has no designated expenditure. Muqatil said: The dowry that marries her from the Muslims should be returned, and if no Muslim marries her, then her unbelieving husband has nothing. Qatada said: The ruling on returning the dowry is only for women of the people of the covenant, but as for those who have no covenant between them and the Muslims, the dowry should not be returned to them, and the matter is as he said. Ninth: The Almighty’s saying: And there is no blame upon you if you marry them, meaning if they convert to Islam and their waiting period has ended, because it has been proven that marrying a polytheist woman or a woman in her waiting period is forbidden. If she converts to Islam before consummation, the marriage is valid immediately and she is permitted to marry. Tenth: The Almighty’s saying: If you have given them their due compensation, permits marrying her on the condition of a dowry, because Islam differentiated between her and her infidel husband. Eleventh: The Almighty’s saying: And do not hold on to the bonds of disbelieving women. The general reading is with a light emphasis on the word holding, which is the choice of Abu Ubaid, based on the Almighty’s saying: Then keep them in kindness. Al-Hasan, Abu Al-Aaliyah, and Abu Amr read And do not hold on with the accusative of the ta’, meaning do not hold on. The word ’asm is the plural of ’asma, which is what he holds on to. What is meant by ’asma here is marriage. He says: Whoever has a disbelieving wife in Mecca should not take her into account, for she is not his wife, for her bondsmanship has been severed due to the difference between the two abodes. And from Al-Nakha’i: She is a Muslim woman who joins the abode of war and becomes a disbeliever. The disbelievers used to marry Muslim women and the Muslims used to marry polytheistic women, then that was abrogated in this verse, so Umar ibn Al-Khattab then divorced his two wives in Mecca who were polytheists: Quraibah bint Abi Umayyah, whom Mu’awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan married while they were still polytheists in Mecca, and Umm Kulthum bint Amr Al-Khuza’iyah, the mother of Abdullah ibn Al-Mughira, whom Abu Jahm ibn Hudhafah married while they were still Their polytheism. When Umar took over the caliphate, Abu Sufyan said to Muawiyah: Divorce your relative so that Umar does not see his spoils in your house. Muawiyah refused. Talhah ibn Abdullah had Arwa bint Rabi’ah ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib, but Islam separated them. Then, in Islam, Khalid ibn Sa’d ibn al-’As married her. She was one of the infidel women who fled to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) imprisoned her and married her to Khalid. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) married his daughter Zaynab - who was a disbeliever - to Abu al-’As ibn al-Rabi’. Then she embraced Islam and her husband embraced Islam after her. Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Ibn Jurayj from a man from Ibn Shihab who said: Zaynab, the daughter of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), embraced Islam and migrated after the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in the first migration. Her husband, Abu al-’As ibn al-Rabi’, Abd al-’Uzza, was a polytheist in Mecca. The hadith says that she embraced Islam after her. Al-Sha’bi said the same. Al-Sha'bi said: Zaynab, the daughter of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), was the wife of Abu al-'As bint al-Rabi'. She converted to Islam and then joined the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Then her husband came to Madinah and she felt safe with him. He converted to Islam and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) returned her to him. Abu Dawud narrated from 'Ikrimah from Ibn 'Abbas: Based on the first marriage, and nothing new happened. Muhammad ibn 'Umar said in his hadith: After six years. Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali said: She should count for two years. Abu 'Umar said: "If this is correct, then there are two possibilities: Either she did not menstruate until her husband converted to Islam, or the command in this case was abrogated by the statement of God, the Almighty: "And their husbands have better right to take them back during that period." (Al-Baqarah 2:228) meaning during their waiting period. There is no disagreement among the scholars that it refers to the waiting period. Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri may God have mercy on him said regarding this story of Zaynab: "It happened before the laws of sharee'ah were revealed." Qatadah said: "This happened before Surat al-Bara'ah was revealed about the severance of treaties between them and the polytheists." And God knows best. Twelfth: The Almighty said: By the protection of the disbelieving women. What is meant by disbelieving women here are idol worshippers whom it is not permissible to marry. It is specific to disbelieving women from outside the People of the Book. It was said that it is general, and that the women of the People of the Book are excluded from it. If the verse was taken to mean the apparent meaning, then a disbeliever would not be permissible at all. According to the first opinion, if a pagan or Zoroastrian converts to Islam and his wife does not, then they should be separated. This is the opinion of some scholars. It is important to say that she should wait until her waiting period is complete. What he said about if Islam is offered to her and she does not convert to Islam - Malik ibn Anas. This is the opinion of Al-Hasan, Tawus, Mujahid, Ata’, Ikrimah, Qatadah and Al-Hakam. They argued with the verse: And do not hold on to the marriage bonds of disbelieving women. Az-Zuhri said: She should wait for her waiting period. This is the opinion of Ash-Shafi’i and Ahmad. They argued with the fact that Abu Sufyan ibn Harb converted to Islam before his wife Hind bint Utbah. He converted to Islam in Marr Adh-Dhahran, then he returned to Makkah while Hind was there, remaining a disbeliever. She grabbed his beard and said: Kill the misguided old man. Then she converted to Islam a few days after him, and they remained married because her waiting period had not expired. They said: The same applies to Hakim ibn Hizam, who converted to Islam before his wife, then she converted to Islam after him, so she remained married. Al-Shafi'i said: "There is no proof for those who cite the words of God the Almighty: And do not hold on to the marriage bonds of disbelieving women, because Muslim women are forbidden to disbelievers, just as disbelieving women, idolaters, and Jewish women are not permissible for Muslims, as God the Almighty says: They are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them. Then the Sunnah clarifies that what God meant by this statement is that they are not lawful for one another unless the other one converts to Islam during the waiting period. As for the Kufians, namely Sufyan, Abu Hanifa, and his companions, they said regarding disbelieving dhimmis: If the woman converts to Islam, Islam is offered to the husband; he must convert, otherwise they are separated. They said: If they are at war with each other, she is his wife until she has had three menstrual periods if they are both in the land of war or in the land of Islam. If one of them is in the land of Islam and the other is in the land of war, the marriage bond between them is severed, so they consider the land, but it is of no consequence. This has been mentioned previously. Thirteenth: This difference is only with regard to the woman who has been consummated with. If she has not been consummated with, then we do not know of any difference of opinion about the severance of the marriage bond between them, as there is no waiting period for her. This is what Malik says about a woman who apostatizes while her husband is Muslim: the marriage bond between them is severance. His proof is And do not hold on to the marriage bond of disbelieving women. This is the opinion of Al-Hasan Al-Basri and Al-Hasan bin Salih. The doctrine of Al-Shafi’i and Ahmad is that he waits for her to complete her waiting period. Fourteenth: If both spouses are Christians and the wife converts to Islam, there is also a difference of opinion regarding this. The doctrine of Malik, Ahmad and al-Shafi’i is to wait until the waiting period is complete. This is the opinion of Mujahid. Similarly, if a pagan converts his wife to Islam, if he converts to Islam during her waiting period, he has more right to her, just as Safwan ibn Umayya and Karmah ibn Abi Jahl had more right to their wives when they converted to Islam during their waiting periods, according to the hadith of Ibn Shihab, which Malik mentioned in al-Muwatta’. Ibn Shihab said: There was about a month between Safwan’s conversion to Islam and his wife’s conversion to Islam. Ibn Shihab said: We have not been informed that a woman migrated to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) while her husband was a disbeliever residing in a land of war, except that her migration caused separation between them, unless her husband migrated before her waiting period was over. Some scholars say: The marriage contract between them is annulled. Yazid ibn Alqamah said: My grandfather converted to Islam, but my grandmother did not, so Umar, may God be pleased with him, separated them. This is the opinion of Tawus. And a group other than him, including Ata’, Al-Hasan, and Ikrimah, said: There is no way to resolve the issue except through a marriage proposal. Fifth: The Almighty said: And ask what you have spent, and let them ask what they have spent. The commentators said: If a Muslim woman went as apostates to the unbelievers among the people of a treaty, it would be said to the unbeliever: Give her dowry. And it would be said to the Muslims if a Muslim woman who had emigrated came to them: Give her dowry to the unbelievers. This was fair and just between the two cases. This was the ruling of God specifically for that time in that particular case by the consensus of the ummah, as stated by Ibn al-Arabi. Sixteenth: The Almighty’s saying: That is the judgment of God, meaning what was mentioned in this verse. He will judge between you, and God is Knowing and Wise, was mentioned in more than one place.
60:11: It has three issues: First: The Almighty said: And if any of your wives escape you. In al-Naba 78:The Muslims said: We are satisfied with what God has judged, and they wrote to the polytheists, but they stopped, so this verse was revealed: And if any of your wives escape you to the disbelievers, and you retaliate, then give those whose wives have gone away the equivalent of what they spent. Az-Zuhri narrated on the authority of Urwah on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: God, the Almighty, has judged between you, and He, the Almighty, said: And ask what you have spent, and let them ask what they have spent. So the Muslims wrote to them: God, the Almighty, has judged between us that if a woman from us comes to you, you should send us her dowry, and if a woman from you comes to us, we will send you her dowry. So they wrote to them: As for us, you do not know of anything with us for you, so if we have something with you, then send it. So God, the Almighty, revealed: And if any of your wives escape you to the disbelievers, and you retaliate, then give those whose wives have gone away the equivalent of what they spent. Ibn Abbas said about the verse {That is the judgment of God, which He judges between you}, meaning between the Muslims and the infidels from among the people of Mecca who have a treaty, they shall be returned to each other. Az-Zuhri said: Were it not for the treaty, the women would have been kept back, even if they were returned to them in full. Qatadah and Mujahid said: They were only commanded to give those whose wives God has taken away, like what they spent from the spoils of war. They said: This applies to those with whom we have a treaty, but there is no treaty between us. They said: The meaning of {then you punished} is: you took revenge. {Then give those whose wives have taken away, like what they spent}, meaning the zakat. So it is general and applies to all infidels. Qatadah also said: And if any of your wives go to the infidels with whom you have a treaty, then give those whose wives have taken away, like what they lost. Then this was abrogated in Surat Bara’ah. Az-Zuhri said: This was cut off in the year of the Conquest. Sufyan ath-Thawri said: It is not implemented today. Some people said: It is still the established rule, as narrated by al-Qushayri. The second: The Almighty’s saying: So you punished The general reading is So you punished. Alqamah, An-Nakha’i, and Hamid Al-A’raj read So you punished with a shaddah. Mujahid read So you punished and said: You did as they did to you. Az-Zuhri said: So you punished with a light alif and changed. Masruq and Shaqiq bin Salamah read So you punished with a kasrah on the qaf and a light light one. He said: You gained booty. All of them are languages with the same meaning. It is said like aqab and aqab and aqab and aqaba and taqaba and itaqaba and takab if you gained booty. Al-Qutbi said: So you punished and fought “mu’aqibeen” meaning fight after fight. Ibn Bahr said: That is, you punished the apostate by killing her, so her husband gets her dowry from the spoils of the Muslims. Third: The Almighty said: {Then give those whose wives have gone away the equivalent of what they spent.} Ibn Abbas said: He means: If a believing woman joins the infidels of Mecca, and there is no treaty between you and them, and she has a Muslim husband before you, and you capture spoils, then give this Muslim husband his dowry from the spoils before it is divided into fifths. Az-Zuhri said: It is to be given from the spoils of war. And from him: It is to be given from the dowry of those who join us. It was said: That is, if they refuse to pay the dowry of this woman who has gone away to them, then abandon the treaty with them until you capture it, then take it from them. Al-A'mash said: It has been abrogated. Ata' said: Rather, its ruling remains in effect. All of this has been mentioned previously. Al-Qushayri: The verse was revealed about Umm Al-Hakam bint Abi Sufyan. She apostatized and left her husband, Ayyad ibn Ghanam Al-Qurashi. No other woman from Quraysh apostatized and then returned to Islam. Al-Tha'labi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: There are six women who renounced Islam and joined the polytheists from among the believing emigrant women: Umm Al-Hakam bint Abi Sufyan, who was married to Ayyad ibn Abi Shaddad Al-Fihri. Fatima bint Abi Umayya ibn Al-Mughira, the sister of Umm Salamah, who was married to Umar ibn Al-Khattab. When Umar emigrated, she refused and apostatized. Baru' bint Uqba, who was married to Shammas ibn Uthman. Abda bint Abd Al-Uzza, who was married to Hisham ibn Al-As. Umm Kulthum bint Jarwal, who was married to Umar ibn Al-Khattab. And Shahba bint Ghailan. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) gave them the dowries of their women from the spoils of war. And fear God Beware of transgressing what you have been commanded to do.
60:12: It contains eight issues: First: The Almighty said: O Prophet, when believing women come to you to pledge allegiance to you. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, conquered Mecca, the women of Mecca came to pledge allegiance to him, so he ordered them to take an oath that they would not associate partners with God. In Sahih Muslim: On the authority of Aisha, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, she said: When the believing women migrated to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, they were tested by the words of God Almighty: O Prophet, when the believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you that they will not associate anything with God and will not steal and will not commit adultery and will not kill to the end of the verse. Aisha said: Whoever among the believing women acknowledged this has acknowledged the test. And when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, acknowledged this by their words, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would say to them: Go, for I have given you my pledge. By God, the hand of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, never touched the hand of a woman, except that he gave them his pledge of allegiance verbally. Aisha said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, never took a pledge from the women, and when he took a pledge from them, he would say to them: I have given you your pledge verbally.” It was narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave the women their pledge of allegiance while there was a garment in front of him and in front of them, and he used to stipulate conditions for them. It was said: When he finished the men’s pledge of allegiance, he sat on Al-Safa with Umar below him, and he began to stipulate conditions for the women to pledge allegiance, and Umar Umm Atiyyah said: When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to Medina, he gathered the women of the Ansar in a house, then he sent Umar ibn al-Khattab to us. He stood up and greeted them, and they returned his greetings. He said: I am the messenger of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to you, that you will not associate anything with God. They said: Yes. He extended his hand from outside the house, and we extended our hands from inside the house. Then he said: O God, bear witness. Amr ibn Shu`ayb narrated on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, that when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) pledged allegiance to the women, he called for a cup of water, dipped his hand in it, and then ordered the women to dip their hands in it. Second: It was narrated: When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: On the condition that they do not associate anything with God, Hind bint Utbah said, while veiled, fearing that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would recognize her for what she had done to Hamza on the day of UHud 11:By God, you are demanding from us something that I have never seen you demand from men. Men had taken the oath of allegiance at that time only to Islam and jihad. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: And they should not steal. Hind said: Abu Sufyan is a stingy man, and I take from his wealth what we say. Abu Sufyan said: It is lawful for you. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) laughed and recognized her. He said: Are you Hind? She said: God has pardoned what has passed. Then he said: And they should not commit adultery. Hind said: And a free woman should not commit adultery! Then he said: And they should not kill their children, meaning they should not bury the girls buried alive or cause miscarriages. Hind said: We raised them when they were young and killed them when they were adults on the day of Badr, so you and they are more knowledgeable. Muqatil narrated that she said: We raised them when they were young and killed them when they were adults, but you and they are more knowledgeable. Umar ibn al-Khattab laughed until he lay down. Hanzala bin Abi Sufyan, her firstborn, was killed on the day of Badr. Then he said: And let them not bring forth a slander they have invented between their hands and their feet, nor disobey you in what is right. It was said that the meaning of between their hands is their tongues through backbiting. The meaning of between their feet is their private parts. It was also said that what was between their hands was kissing or touching, and what was between their feet was sexual intercourse. It was also said that the meaning is that they should not attribute to their men a child from someone other than them. This is the opinion of the majority. A woman would pick up a child and attribute it to her husband, saying, This is my child from you. This was a form of slander and fabrication. It was also said that what was between her hands and her feet is a metaphor for the child, because her womb in which she carries the child is between her hands, and her private parts from which she gives birth are between her legs. This is general in referring to giving birth to a child and attributing it to the husband, even though adultery was previously prohibited. It was narrated that when Hind heard that, she said: By God, slander is an ugly matter. You only command what is most righteous and of noble character! Then He said: And they shall not disobey you in what is right. Qatada said: “They shall not wail. And no woman among them shall be alone except with a mahram.” Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, Muhammad ibn al-Sa’ib, and Zayd ibn Aslam said: It means that they shall not scratch their faces, tear their garments, leave wailing, dishevel their hair, or speak to men except with a mahram. Umm Atiyah narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And they do not disobey you in what is right. He said: It is wailing. Mus`ab ibn Nuh said: “I met an old woman who pledged allegiance to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she told me about him, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his saying, ‘And they will not disobey you in what is right.’ He said: Nuh.” And in Sahih Muslim: On the authority of Umm Atiyyah, when this verse was revealed: They pledge allegiance to you that they will not associate anything with God - until His Most High’s saying: And they will not disobey you in what is right, he said: It included wailing. She said: So I said, O Messenger of God, except for the family of so-and-so, for they made me happy in the pre-Islamic era, so I must make them happy. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Except for the family of so-and-so. It was narrated on her authority that she said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) took a pledge from us that we would not wail, and no woman among us fulfilled it except five: Umm Sulaym, Umm al-Ala’, Ibn Sabra, the wife of Muadh, or the daughter of Abu Sabra, and the wife of Muadh. It was said: What is known here is obedience to God and His Messenger, as Maymun ibn Mihran said. Bakr ibn Abdullah al-Muzani said: They should not disobey you in every matter in which they are right. Al-Kalbi said: It is general in what is known that God the Almighty and His Messenger have commanded. It was narrated that Hind said at that time: We did not sit in this gathering of ours with the intention of disobeying you in anything. Third: God the Almighty and His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, mentioned various characteristics in the description of the pledge of allegiance, in which he clearly stated the pillars of prohibition in religion, but did not mention the pillars of command. They are also six: testimony, prayer, zakat, fasting, Hajj, and ritual bathing after sexual impurity. This is because prohibition is constant in all times and in all circumstances, so drawing attention to the condition of permanence is more emphatic. It was said that many women committed these prohibitions and their noble lineage did not prevent them from doing so, so they were mentioned specifically for this reason. And similar things. His saying, peace and blessings be upon him, to the delegation of Abd al-Qays, He forbade you from gourds, wheat, molasses, and pitch. So he alerted them to abandon the sin of drinking alcohol, not all other sins, because it was their desire and habit, and if a person abandons his desire for sins, it will be easy for him to abandon all other sins in which there is no desire. Fourth: When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said about the pledge of allegiance: And they shall not steal, Hind said: O Messenger of God, Abu Sufyan is a poor man, so is there any blame upon me if I take what is sufficient for me and my children? He said: No, except in a reasonable manner. Hind feared that she would limit herself to what he gave her and waste it, or that she would take more than that and thus be a thief who was constantly violating the pledge of allegiance mentioned. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to her: No, meaning that there is no blame upon you for what you take in a reasonable manner, meaning without going beyond what is necessary. Ibn al-Arabi said: This only applies to what is not stored from her in a veil and is not secured with a lock, because if the wife violates it and takes from it, she is a thief who disobeys him and her hand is cut off. Fifth: “Ubadah ibn al-Samit said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) took from us as he took from women: “Do not associate anything with God, do not steal, do not commit adultery, do not kill your children, do not bite each other, and do not disobey in what is right that He has commanded you.” The meaning of bite is bewitchment. And bite is magic. That is why Ibn Bahr and others said about the words of God the Almighty: And do not bring forth any slander, that it refers to sorcery. Ad-Dahhak said: This is a prohibition against slander, meaning that neither a man nor a woman should bite them. By slander means by magic. And God knows best. They fabricate it between their hands and feet, nor… The majority are of the opinion that the meaning of by slander is a child they fabricate between their hands is what you took as a foundling. “And their feet” is what you gave birth to from adultery. This has been mentioned previously. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: And they will not disobey you in what is right. In Bukhari, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the Almighty’s saying: And they will not disobey you in what is right, he said: It is a condition that God has stipulated for women. There is a difference of opinion regarding its meaning, as we have mentioned. The correct view is that it is general in all that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) commanded and forbade, so it includes wailing, tearing clothes, cutting hair, being alone with a non-mahram, and other things. All of these are major sins and from the actions of the Jahiliyyah. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Malik al-Ash’ari: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “These mourners will be placed on the Day of Resurrection in two rows, one on the right and one on the left, barking like dogs bark in a sleep that lasts for fifty thousand years. Then they will be ordered to the Fire.” It was narrated on the authority of ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him that he heard a woman who was mourning, so he went to her and hit her with a whip until her veil fell off her head. It was said: O Commander of the Faithful, a woman, a woman! Her veil has fallen off. He said: She has no sanctity. Jami’ah al-Tha’labi may God have mercy on him transmitted it. As for specifying his statement: in what is right despite the strength of his statement: nor will they disobey You, there are two opinions on this: The first is that it is an explanation of the meaning to support it, as God the Almighty said: He said, ‘My Lord, judge with truth’ (al-Anbiya’: 112) because if he had said judgement, it would have been sufficient. The second is that what is right was stipulated in the pledge of allegiance to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) so that it would be a warning that someone else is more deserving of that, more binding, more binding, and more obligatory for him, and eliminates confusion. Seventh: Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Ubadah bin Al-Samit, who said: We were with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and he said: Will you pledge allegiance to me that you will not associate anything with God, nor commit adultery, nor steal? He recited the verse of An-Nisa. Sufyan’s version of the verse is more correct: “And whoever among you fulfills it, his reward is upon God. And whoever commits any of that and is punished, it is an expiation for him. And whoever commits any of that and God conceals it, it is up to God. If He wills, He will punish him, and if He wills, He will forgive him thereof.” “And in the two Sahihs, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: I witnessed the prayer on the day of Eid al-Fitr with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman, and all of them were praying it before the sermon. They were delivering the sermon, and the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came down and it was as if I could see him when the men sat with his hand, then he came and led them away until he came to the women with Bilal and said: “O Prophet, when the believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you that they will not associate anything with God, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill their children, nor bring forth a slander they have invented between their hands and feet” - until he finished the entire verse. Then when he finished he said: Are you on that? Then only one woman said, and no one else answered him: Yes, O Messenger of God. Al-Hasan did not know who she was. He said: So give them in charity. He spread out his garment and they began to throw the bracelets and rings into a thin garment. Bukhari’s wording. Eighth: Al-Mahdawi said: The Muslims agreed unanimously that the Imam should not stipulate this upon them, and the command to do so is recommended, not obligatory. Some of the people of insight said: If a trial is needed because of the distance between the houses, then it is incumbent upon the Imam of the Muslims to establish the trial.
60:13: God the Almighty says: O you who have believed, do not take as allies those with whom God has become angry. They mean the Jews. This is because some poor Muslims used to tell the Jews report of the believers and maintain close contact with them, thus afflicting them with their wrath. So they were forbidden from doing so. They have despaired of the Hereafter. They mean the Jews, as stated by Ibn Zayd. It was also said that they are the hypocrites. Al-Hasan said that they are the Jews and Christians. Ibn Mas'ud said that it means that they have abandoned working for the Hereafter and preferred this world. It was also said that it means that they have despaired of the reward of the Hereafter, as stated by Mujahid. The meaning of as the disbelievers have despaired is the living ones from the disbelievers. of the inhabitants of the graves that they will return to them, as stated by Al-Hasan and Qatadah. Ibn 'Arafah said that they are the ones who said: And nothing destroys us except time (Al-Jathiya 45:24). Mujahid said that it means that the disbelievers in the graves have despaired of returning to this world. It was said: God the Almighty concluded the Surah with what it began with about abandoning friendship with the disbelievers, and this is addressed to Hatib bin Abi Balta’ah and others. Ibn Abbas said: {O you who have believed, do not take as allies} meaning do not befriend them and do not advise them. God the Almighty referred back with His length and favor to Hatib bin Abi Balta’ah. He meant that the disbelievers of Quraysh had despaired of the good of the Hereafter just as the disbelievers who were buried had despaired of any portion that they would have from God’s mercy in the Hereafter. Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza said about God the Almighty’s statement: {They have despaired of the Hereafter just as the disbelievers have despaired of the inhabitants of the graves} He said: Whoever dies from the disbelievers has despaired of the good. And God knows best.
61:1: It is Medinan according to everyone, as mentioned by Al-Mawardi. It was also said that it is Meccan, as mentioned by Al-Nahhas on the authority of Ibn Abbas. It has fourteen verses. “Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth exalts God. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.”
61:2: It contains five issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? Al-Darimi Abu Muhammad narrated in his Musnad: Muhammad bin Katheer told us, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Salam, who said: We sat fleeing from the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so we talked and said: If we knew which deeds are most beloved to God, we would do them. Then God revealed: “Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth exalts God, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise. O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?” until he finished it. Abdullah said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited it to us until he finished it. Abu Salamah said: Ibn Salam recited it to us. Yahya said: Abu Salamah recited it to us, and Yahya recited it to us, and Al-Awza’i recited it to us, and Muhammad recited it to us. Ibn Abbas said: Abdullah ibn Rawahah said: If we knew which deeds are most beloved to God, we would do them. When Jihad was revealed, they hated it. The believers said, O Messenger of God, if we knew which deeds are most beloved to God, we would hasten to them. Then this verse was revealed: Shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment? They remained for a while saying, If we knew what it was, we would buy it with our wealth, our lives, and our families. Then God guided them to it by saying: You believe in God and His Messenger and strive in the cause of God with your wealth and your lives. Then they were tested on the Day of Uhud and fled, so this verse was revealed to reproach them for not fulfilling their commitment. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: When God informed His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) of the reward of the martyrs of Badr, the Companions said, O God, bear witness! If we encounter fighting, we will do our utmost in it. So they fled on the Day of Uhud, so God reproached them for that. Qatada and Ad-Dahhak said, This verse was revealed about a people who used to say, 'We have striven and fought hard,' but they did not. Suhaib said: “A man had harmed the Muslims on the day of Badr and caused them great suffering, so I killed him. A man said: ‘O father of God, I killed so-and-so.’ The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was pleased with that. ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab and ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf said: ‘O Suhaib, did you not tell the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that you killed so-and-so? So-and-so claimed to have killed him.’ So he told him and he said: ‘Is that so, O Abu Yahya?’ He said: ‘Yes, by God, O Messenger of God.’ So the verse was revealed about the one who claimed to have killed him.” Ibn Zayd said: “It was revealed about the hypocrites. They used to say to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions: ‘If you go out and fight, we will go out with you and fight.’ But when they went out, they turned back and stayed behind.” Al-Haniya: This verse requires everyone who commits himself to an act of obedience to fulfill it. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Musa, that he sent to the reciters of the people of Basra, and three hundred men who had recited the Qur’an had entered upon him. He said, You are the best of the people of Basra and their reciters, so recite it and do not let the time be long for you, lest you harden your hearts as the hearts of those before you hardened. We used to recite a surah which we likened in length and severity to Bara’ah, but I forgot it, except that I memorized from it: If the son of Adam had two valleys full of wealth, he would desire a third, and nothing fills the belly of the son of Adam except dust. We used to recite a surah which we likened to one of the Mus-Bisahis, but I forgot it, except that I memorized from it: O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? This is established in the religion in wording and meaning in this surah. As for His statement, A testimony around your necks, about which you will be asked on the Day of Resurrection, its meaning is established in the religion, for whoever commits himself to something, it is binding upon him. Shara'an. And the vow is divided into two types: One of them is the vow, which is divided into two types: A vow of devotion that is initiated, such as saying: I owe God prayer, fasting, charity, and the like of devotion. This must be fulfilled by consensus. A vow of permissibility is one that is conditional upon desire, such as saying: If my absent one returns, then I must give charity, or one that is conditional upon fear, such as saying: If God suffices me from the evil of such-and-such, then I must give charity. The scholars differed concerning it. Malik and Abu Hanifa said: He must fulfill it. Al-Shafi'i said in one of his opinions: He is not obligated to fulfill it. The general meaning of the verse is evidence for us because in its absolute form it includes the responsibility of one who says something that he will not do, regardless of whether it is absolute or conditional. His companions said: A vow is only for what the intention of it is to draw near to God, which is of the same type as devotion. Although this is of the same type as devotion, it is not intended as a devotion, but rather the intention is to prevent oneself from doing or proceeding with an action. We say: The legal devotions are hardships and burdens, even if they are devotions. This is the effort of committing to this act of worship with difficulty in order to bring benefit or ward off harm. Thus, it does not go beyond the prescribed norms of obligation and does not depart from the intention of drawing closer to God. Ibn al-Arabi said: If what is said is a promise, then it is likely to be conditional upon a reason, such as saying: If you marry, I will help you with a dinar, or if you buy what you need, I will give you such and such. This is necessary according to the consensus of the jurists. If it is simply a promise, then it is said that it is conditional upon its connection. They connected it to the reason of the verse, as it is narrated that they used to say: If we knew which deeds are best or most beloved to God, we would do them. So God revealed this verse. It is an acceptable hadith. It was narrated from Mujahid that when Abdullah ibn Rawahah heard it, he said: I will continue to be imprisoned in the cause of God until I am killed. What is correct in my view is that a promise must be fulfilled in all cases except for an excuse. I said: Malik said: As for the waiting period, such as if a man asks someone to give him a gift and he says yes, then he changes his mind not to do it, I do not think that is binding on him. Ibn al-Qasim said: If someone makes a promise to creditors and says, I call you to witness that I have given them a gift that he will pay you back, then this is binding on him. As for him saying, Yes, I will do it, then he changes his mind, I do not think that is binding on him. I said: That is, he is not to be punished for that. As for good morals and good chivalry, then yes. God Almighty praised the one who is true to his promise and fulfills his vow, saying: And those who fulfill their covenant when they have made it (al-Baqarah 2:177), and God Almighty said: “And mention in the Book, Ishmael. Indeed, he was true to his promise” (Maryam 19:54), and his finger has already been mentioned. Third: Al-Nakha’i said: Three verses prevented me from narrating to the al-Nas 114:Do you enjoin righteousness upon people and forget yourselves? (al-Baqarah 2:44), And I do not want to go against you in that which I forbid you. (Hud 11:88), O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? Abu Na’im Al-Hafiz narrated from the hadith of Malik bin Dinar on the authority of Thamamah that Anas bin Malik said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “On the Night Journey, I came upon a people whose lips were being cut with scissors of fire. Every time they were cut, they would dry up. I said: ‘Who are these, O Gabriel?’ He said: ‘These are the orators of your nation who say but do not act, who recite the Book of God but do not act.’” It was narrated from one of the early Muslims that it was said to him: ‘Tell us,’ and he remained silent. Then it was said to him: ‘Tell us,’ and he said: ‘Do you think I would say what I do not do and thus hasten the wrath of God?!’ Fourth: The Almighty’s statement: Why do you say what you do not do? is a question of denial and rebuke, meaning that a person says about himself something good that he does not do. As for what is in the past, it would be a lie, and as for what is in the future, it would be a failure, and both are reprehensible. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah’s interpretation of the Almighty’s statement: Why do you say what you do not do? means why do you say something that is not up to you, so you do not know whether you will do it or not. Based on this, the statement is to be taken at its apparent meaning in denying the statement.
61:3: His saying, the Most High: It is most hateful to God that you say what you do not do. This may be used as evidence for the obligation of fulfilling one's duty in cases of obstinacy and anger, according to one of the two opinions of Al-Shafi'i. And it is in the subject and what precedes it is the predicate, as if he said: Your saying what you do not do is reprehensible. It is also possible for it to be the predicate of a deleted subject. Al-Kisa'i said: That is in the nominative case, because kabar fa'ala is like ba'isa mana akhuka your brother is a bad man. And ma'ta is in the accusative case as a differentiator, meaning it is most hateful for them to say what they do not do. It was also said: it is a state. Maqt and maqta are two verbal nouns, it is said: a man is hated and hated if people do not like him.
61:4: There are three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, God loves those who fight in His cause in rows. That is, they stand in rows, and the object is implied, meaning they stand in rows. As if they were a solid structure. Al-Farra’ said: Strongly joined together. Al-Bard said: Thaw comes from rasasat al-banaa which means to join together and bring them close together until they become like a single piece. It was also said that it comes from says, which is the joining of teeth, making them stick to each other. Raas means to stick together, and from this comes the word wa-tarasawu fi-saff. The meaning of the verse is: He loves the one who perseveres in jihad in the cause of God and sticks to his place like the firmness of a building. Sa’d ibn Jubayr said: This is a teaching from God to the believers on how to behave when fighting their enemy. Second: Some interpreters have used this as evidence that combat on foot is better than combat on horseback, because horsemen do not line up in this manner. Al-Mahdawi: This is not correct, given what has been said about the superiority of the horseman in wages and spoils. And horsemen are not excluded from the meaning of the verse, because its meaning is steadfastness. Third: It is not permissible to leave the ranks except for a need that arises, or in response to a message sent by the Imam, or for a benefit that appears in the situation, such as an opportunity that can be seized, and there is no disagreement about this. As for leaving the ranks to duel, there is a difference of opinion on two opinions: First: That there is nothing wrong with that as it is to terrorize the enemy, seek martyrdom, and incite people to fight. Our companions said: No one should come forward seeking that, because it is ostentation and a departure from what God has forbidden, which is meeting the enemy. A duel only applies if the disbeliever requests it, as it was in the wars of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the Day of Badr and in the Battle of Khaybar, and this is what the early generations followed. This has been fully discussed in Surat Al-Baqarah when God says: And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction (Al-Baqarah 2:195).
61:5: God Almighty says: And when Moses said to his people, when he mentioned the matter of jihad, he explained that Moses and Jesus were commanded to follow monotheism and fought in the way of God, and that punishment was imposed on those who opposed them: that is, mention this story to your people, O Muhammad. God the Almighty says: O my people, why do you harm me? That was when they attacked him with a stick, as mentioned at the end of Surat Al-Ahzab. Among the harm is what was mentioned in the story of Qarun: that he sent a woman to accuse Moses of immorality. Among the harm is their saying: Make for us a god as they have gods (Al-A’raf 7:138). Their saying: Then go, you and your Lord, and fight (Al-Ma’idah 5:24). And their saying: You killed Aaron. This was mentioned before. And you know that I am the Messenger of God to you. The Messenger is respected and glorified. The preposition qad was used before ya’lamoon for emphasis, as if he was saying: And you know with certainty that you have no doubt about it. “So when they deviated” means they turned away from the truth. God caused their hearts to deviate means He turned them away from guidance. It was also said: So when they deviated from obedience, God caused their hearts to deviate from guidance. It was said: So when they deviated from faith, God made their hearts deviate from reward. It was also said: That is, when they abandoned what they were commanded to do of respecting the Messenger, peace be upon him, and obeying the Lord, God created misguidance in their hearts as punishment for their actions.
61:6: God the Almighty says: And when Jesus, the son of Mary, said, meaning, mention to them this story as well. He said, O Children of Israel, and did not say, O my people, as Moses said, because he was not related to them, and they would be his mouth. Indeed, I am the Messenger of God to you, meaning the Gospel. Confirming what came before me of the Torah, because the Torah contains my description, and that I have not brought you anything that contradicts the Torah, so that you would be frightened away from me. And bringing good tidings of a Messenger, confirming. Bringing good tidings is in the accusative case as a state, and the world in it has the meaning of sending. To you is the connection of the Messenger. After me will come, whose name is Ahmad. Nafi', Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr read after me with a fat-ha on the ya'. This is the reading of As-Sulami, Zur ibn Hubaish, and Abu Bakr from Asim. Abu Hatim chose it because it is a noun, like the kaf in ba'dak and the ta' in qumat. The rest use the sukun. And after me, his name is Ahmad, deleting the Ya from the pronunciation. Ahmad is the name of our Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). It is a proper noun derived from an adjective, not from a verb. This adjective, not the verb, is used to indicate preference. The meaning of Ahmad is Ahmad, the one who praises his Lord. All the prophets (peace and blessings of God be upon them) praise God, and our prophet Ahmad is the one who praises the most. As for Muhammad, it is also derived from an adjective, and it has the meaning of praiseworthy, but it has the meaning of exaggeration and repetition. So Muhammad is the one who was praised time and time again. Just as al-Mukram is derived from al-Karm generosity time and time again. The same applies to al-Mamdooh the praised, and so on. So the name Muhammad is in accordance with its meaning, and God named him before he named himself. This is a sign of his prophethood, if his name is true to him, for he is praised in this world for the knowledge and wisdom to which he guided and the benefit he gained. And he is praised in the Hereafter through intercession. The meaning of praise was repeated as the wording requires. Then he was not Muhammad until he was Ahmad. He praised his Lord, so He informed him and honored him. Therefore, the name Ahmad came before the name which is Muhammad, so Jesus, peace be upon him, mentioned it and said: His name is Ahmad. And Moses, peace be upon him, mentioned him when his Lord said to him: This is the nation of Ahmad, so he said: O God, make me from the nation of Ahmad. So he mentioned Ahmad before he mentioned Muhammad, because his praise of his Lord was before the praise of the people for him. So when he was found and was sent, he was actually Muhammad. And likewise in intercession, he praises his Lord with the praises that He opens for him, so he is the most praised of people to his Lord, then he intercedes and is praised for his intercession. It was narrated that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: My name in the Torah is Al-Ahad because I will protect my nation from the Fire, and my name in the Psalms is Al-Mahi, through me God wiped out the idol worshippers, and my name in the Gospel is Ahmad, and my name in the Qur’an is Muhammad because I am praised by the people of the heavens and the earth. In the Sahih: I have five names: I am Muhammad and Ahmad, and I am Al-Mahi through whom God wipes out disbelief, and I am Al-Hashir at whose feet the people will be gathered, and I am the Last. And it was mentioned before. So when he came to them with clear proofs, it was said Jesus, and it was said Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. They said, This is obvious magic. Al-Kaswani and Hamza read it as sahir ta’ata for the man. It was narrated that it is the reading of Ibn Masoud. The rest said sahir ta’ata for what the Messenger brought.
61:7: The Almighty said: And who is more unjust meaning no one is more unjust than he who invents a lie against God This has been mentioned in more than one place. And he is called to Islam This is an expression of amazement at someone who disbelieved in Jesus and Muhammad after the miracles that appeared to them. Talhah ibn Musarraf read it while he is called with a fatha on the ya’ and the dal and with a shaddah on the ayn, meaning he is related equally. And God does not guide the wrongdoing people meaning whoever is in His judgment that he will be sealed with misguidance.
61:8: The Almighty said: They want to extinguish the light of God with their mouths. Extinguishment is quenching. They are both used for fire, and for similar things such as light and appearance. Extinguishment and quenching differ in one respect. Extinguishment is used for both little and much, while quenching is used for much, not little. So it is said: I put out the lamp, but you do not say I put out the lamp. There are five sayings regarding the light of God here: The first is that it is the Qur’an, meaning to invalidate and deny it with words. This was said by Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd. The second is that it is Islam, meaning to repel it with words. This was said by Al-Suddi. The third is that it is Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, meaning to destroy him with rumours. This was said by Al-Dahhak. Fourth - God's proofs and evidence, they want to invalidate them by their denial and disbelief, said Ibn Bahr.
