Fifth - It is a proverb, meaning that whoever wanted to extinguish the light of the sun with his mouth would find it impossible and unavoidable, so too whoever wanted to invalidate the truth, narrated by Ibn Issa. The reason for the revelation of this verse is what was narrated by Ata' on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The revelation was delayed forty days for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, so Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf said: O group of Jews, rejoice! God has extinguished the light of Muhammad in what was revealed to him, and his command was not completed, so the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, was saddened, so God revealed this verse and the revelation continued after it, all of which was narrated by al-Mawardi, may God have mercy on him. And God will perfect His light meaning by making it appear in the horizons. Ibn Kathir, Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, and Hafs on the authority of Asim read And God will perfect His light with the intention of separation, as in the Almighty's statement: Every soul will taste death (Al Imran 3:185). The rest read perfecting His light because it is in the future, so it worked. Even though the disbelievers dislike it from all other categories.
61:9: The Almighty said: It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance meaning Muhammad with the truth and right guidance. That He may make it prevail over all religions meaning with arguments. To prevail means to be victorious in battle. To prevail does not mean that no other religion will remain, but rather that the people of Islam will be superior and victorious. To make manifest means that no religion will remain but Islam at the end of time. Mujahid said: That will be when Jesus descends and there will be no religion on earth but Islam. Abu Hurairah said: And the religion of truth that He may make it prevail over all religions with the emergence of Jesus. At that time, no disbeliever will remain but will become Muslim. In Sahih Muslim, it was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The son of Mary will descend as a just judge. He will break the cross, the pigs will be abolished, the jizyah will be abolished, the camels will be left alone so that no one will run after them, and animosity, hatred, and envy will be eliminated. He will call for money but no one will accept it.” It was said: To make it manifest, meaning to inform Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, of all religions, so that he will be knowledgeable about them and aware of the ways in which they are false, and of what has been distorted and changed in them. On religion means religions, because religion is a verbal noun that expresses a plural.
61:10: It contains five issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a trade? Muqatil said: It was revealed about Uthman ibn Maz’un, and that is because he said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: "If you give me permission, I will divorce Khawlah, become a nun, become a eunuch, and forbid meat. I will never sleep at night or break my fast during the day!" The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, "Indeed, my Sunnah is marriage, and there is no monasticism in Islam. The monasticism of my nation is jihad in the way of God, and the eunuchism of my nation is fasting. Do not forbid the good things which God has made lawful for you. It is my Sunnah to sleep and stand, break my fast and fast. So whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me." Uthman said, By God, O Prophet of God, I have given birth to which trade is most beloved to God, so trade in it. Then this verse was revealed. It was also said, For you, meaning, I will guide you. And serious trade is important. God the Most High said, Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties. (al-Tawbah 9:111) This is addressed to all believers. It was also said, to the People of the Book. Second: The Almighty’s saying, It will save you, meaning it will deliver you, from a painful torment, meaning one that is hurtful. It has been mentioned before, and the general reading is It will save you, with a sukoon on the nun, from saving. Al-Hasan, Ibn Amir, and Abu Haywah read it with a shaddah from saving.
61:11: Then he explained the trade, which is the issue: - Third: He said: You believe in God and His Messenger and strive in the cause of God with your wealth and your lives. He mentioned wealth first because it is what spending begins with. That meaning this action is better for you than your wealth and your lives if you only knew. And you believe, according to Al-Mubarrad and Al-Zajjaj, means you have believed.
61:12: Therefore, Yahujjaru lakum came in the jussive mood as a response to the command. In Abdullah's recitation, they said, Believe in God. Al-Farra' said, Yahujjaru lakum is the response to the question, and this is either correct if it is understood according to the meaning, that is, You believe in God and strive is an apposition to His statement, Shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment? It is as if he did not know what the transaction was, so it was explained by faith and jihad, and they are both in meaning. So it is as if he said, Do you believe in God and strive, He will forgive you. Al-Zamakhshari said, "The basis of Al-Farra's statement is that the object of the indication is the transaction, and the transaction is explained by faith and jihad. It is as if it was said, "Do you trade with faith and jihad, He will forgive you? Al-Mahdawi said, If you did not understand this interpretation, the question does not become relevant, because the interpretation becomes, If you guide, He will forgive you, and forgiveness is only described by speech and faith, not by indication." Al-Zajjaj said: It is not if He guides them to what benefits them that He forgives them. Rather, He forgives them if they believe and strive. Zayd ibn Ali read you believe and you strive with the omission of the imperative lam, like his saying: Muhammad, sacrifice yourself every soul if you fear something, take care He wanted to redeem. Some of them were forced to say: May God forgive you. It is better to leave the assimilating, because the letter Ra is a strong, repeated letter, so it is not good to assimilate it with the letter Lam, because the stronger letter is not assimilated with the weaker letter. Fourth: The Almighty said: And good dwellings. Abu Al-Hasan Al-Ajurri narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: I asked Imran bin Al-Hisn and Abu Hurairah about the interpretation of this verse: And good dwellings. They said: It is omitted by someone who knows. We asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about it, and he said: A palace of pearls in Paradise, in which are seventy houses of red rubies. In each house are seventy houses of new green tiles. In each house are seventy beds. On each bed are seventy mattresses of every color. On each mattress are seventy women from the houris. In each house are seventy tables. On each table are seventy types of food. In each house are seventy male and female servants. So God, the Blessed and Exalted, gives the believer sustenance in a single morning to whoever can handle all of that. In the Gardens of Eden means residence. That is the great attainment means great and lasting happiness. The root of attainment is achieving what one desires.
61:13: Fifth: The Almighty said: And another which you love. Al-Farra' and Al-Akhfash said: Another is conjoined with trade, so it is in the accusative case. It was also said: It is in the nominative case, meaning, And for you is another characteristic and another trade which you love. "Victory from God," meaning, it is a victory from God. So, victory in this case is an interpretation of "and another." It was also said: "It is in the nominative case as a substitute for another, meaning, And for you is victory from God. "And a near victory," meaning, spoils in this world. It was also said: "The conquest of Mecca." Ibn Abbas said: He means the conquest of Persia and Rome. "And give good tidings to the believers," of God's pleasure with them.
61:14: He emphasized the matter of Jihad, meaning, be the disciples of your Prophet, so that God may make you victorious over those who oppose you, just as He made the disciples of Jesus victorious over those who opposed them. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Nafi' read Ansar God with the nunation. They said: Because its meaning is, stand firm and be helpers of God with the sword against his enemies. The rest of the people of Basra, Kufa, and Ash-Sham read Ansar God without the nunation, and they deleted the lam of addition from the name of God. Abu Ubaid chose it because he said: We are the supporters of God, and they did not add the nunation, and its meaning is, be supporters of the religion of God. Then it was said: There is an omission in the speech, meaning, tell them, O Muhammad, be supporters of God. It was also said: It is the beginning of a direct address from God, meaning, be supporters as the companions of Jesus did, so they were, by the praise of God, supporters and disciples. The disciples are the special ones of the messengers. Muammar said, It was by the praise of God, meaning they supported him, and they were seventy men, and they were the ones who pledged allegiance to him on the night of Aqaba. It was also said that they were from Quraysh. Qatada named them: Abu Bakr, Umar, Ali, Talhah, Az-Zubayr, Sa’d ibn Malik Abu Ubaidah - whose name was Amir - Uthman ibn Maz’un, and Hamza ibn Abdul Muttalib. He did not mention Sa’id, so let them be mistaken. He mentioned Ja’far ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with them all. As Jesus, son of Mary, said to the disciples, and they were his chosen ones, twelve men, and their names have been mentioned in Al Imran, and they were the first of the Children of Israel to believe in him, as Ibn Abbas said. Muqatil said, “God said to Jesus, ‘When you enter the city, go to the river by which the plasterers are and ask them for support.’ So Jesus came to them and said, ‘Who are my supporters for God?’ They said, ‘We will support you.’ So they believed in him and supported him.” The meaning of who are my supporters to God is who are my supporters with God, just as you say, the flock to the flock are camels, meaning with the flock. It was also said, Where are my supporters in what brings one closer to God? This was mentioned previously in Al Imran. So a party of the Children of Israel believed and a party disbelieved. The two groups in the time of Jesus split up after he was raised to heaven, as was explained previously in Al Imran. So We supported those who believed against their enemy, those who disbelieved in Jesus. And they became dominant, meaning victorious. Ibn Abbas said, God supported those who believed in the time of Jesus by making Muhammad prevail over the religion of the disbelievers. Mujahid said, They were supported in their time against those who disbelieved in Jesus. It was also said, “We have now supported the Muslims against the two misguided sects: those who said, ‘He was God, then He was raised,’ and those who said, ‘He was the son of God, then God raised him up to Himself,’ because Jesus, son of Mary, did not fight anyone and there was no fighting in the religion of his companions after him.” Zayd ibn Ali and Qatada said: And they became dominant victorious by argument and bet, because they said, as was narrated: Do you not know that Jesus used to sleep, and God does not sleep? And that Jesus used to eat, and God does not eat! It was said: This verse was revealed about the messengers of Jesus, peace be upon him. Ibn Ishaq said: “Those whom Jesus sent from the disciples and followers were: Peter and Paul to Rome; Andrew and Muthanna to the land whose people eat people; Thomas to the land of Babylon in the land of the East; Philip to Carthage, which is Africa; John to Daqus, the village of the people of Al-Kahq; James to Jerusalem, which is Jerusalem; Ibn Talma to Al-Arrabiya, which is the land of Al-Hijaz; Simeon to the land of the Berbers; and Judea and Bardas to Alexandria and its environs.” So God supported them with argument. And they became dominant means high, from the saying: I appeared on the wall meaning I ascended it. God Almighty knows best what is right, and to Him is the return and final destination.
62:1: Medinan according to everyone, and it consists of eleven verses. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The best day the sun has risen upon is Friday. On it, Adam was created, on it he entered Paradise, and on it he was expelled from it. The Hour will not come except on a Friday.” And on his authority, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We are the last but the first on the Day of Resurrection, and we are the first to enter Paradise. However, they were given the Scripture before us, and we were given it after them, and they differed, so God guided us to the truth regarding which they differed. This is the day regarding which they differed, and God has guided us to it.” He said: “It is Friday. Today is for us, tomorrow is for the Jews, and the day after tomorrow is for the Christians.” This has been discussed previously. Abu Al-Aaliyah and Nasr bin Asim read it as the Holy King, the Almighty, the Wise. All of them are in the nominative case, meaning He is the King.
62:2: God Almighty said: It is He who sent among the unlettered people a Messenger from themselves. Ibn Abbas said: The unlettered people are all Arabs, those who wrote among them and those who did not, because they were not people of the Book. It was said: The illiterate are those who do not write. This was also the case with Quraysh. Mansur narrated on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: The illiterate are those who read but do not write. This has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. A Messenger from among them means Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. There is no tribe among the Arabs except that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has relatives among them who gave birth to him. Ibn Ishaq said: Except for the tribe of Taghlib, for God Almighty purified His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from them because of their Christianity, so He did not allow them to have children with him. He was illiterate, did not read from a book and did not learn, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Mawardi said: If it is said: What is the aspect of gratitude in sending an illiterate prophet? The answer is threefold: First, because he agrees with what the prophets had given glad tidings of. Second, because his situation was similar to their situation, so he was closer to agreeing with them. Third, so that there would be no suspicion of him regarding his teaching of the books he had read and the wisdom he recited. I said: All of this is evidence of his miracle and the truth of his prophethood. God the Almighty says: {He recites to them His verses} meaning the Qur’an, {and purifies them} meaning, He makes them pure of heart through faith, as stated by Ibn Abbas. It was also said: He cleanses them from the filth of disbelief and sins, as stated by Ibn Jurayj and Muqatil. Al-Suddi said: He takes the zakat from their wealth, {and teaches them the Book} meaning the Qur’an, {and wisdom} meaning the Sunnah, as stated by Al-Hasan. Ibn Abbas said: The Book is writing with a pen, because writing became widespread among the Arabs through the Sharia when they were ordered to restrict it with writing. Malik ibn Anas said: Wisdom is understanding the religion. This has been discussed previously in Surat Al-Baqarah. {And if they were before}, {Where before him and before He sent to them?}, {in manifest error} meaning, in deviation from the truth.
62:3: His Almighty saying: and others among them is in apposition to the illiterate, meaning He was sent among the illiterate and He was sent among others among them. It is also permissible for it to be in the accusative case by being in apposition to the ha and mim in He teaches them and purifies them, meaning He teaches them and teaches others among the believers, because when teaching is consistent with the end of time, then all of it is attributed to its beginning, so it is as if He is the one who took charge of everything that was found of it. when they have not yet joined them, meaning they were not in their time and will be revived after them. Al-Ibn Umar and Sa'id ibn Jubayr: they are the non-Arabs. In Sahih Al-Bukhari and Muslim, it is narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah who said: We were sitting with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) when Surah Al-Jumu’ah was revealed to him. When he recited, And others among them who have not yet joined them, a man said, Who are these, O Messenger of God? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not respond to him until he asked him once, twice, or thrice. He said, And among us is Salman Al-Farsi. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) placed his hand on Salman and said, If faith were at the Pleiades, men from among these would attain it. In another narration, If the religion were at the Pleiades, a man from Persia—or he said—from the sons of Persia would take it and carry it until it reached them. This is the wording of Muslim. Ikrimah said: They are the Followers. Mujahid said: They are all people, meaning those after the Arabs among whom Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was sent. Ibn Zayd and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said the same. They said: They are those who entered Islam after the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) until the Day of Resurrection. Sahl ibn Sa’d al-Sa’idi narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Indeed, in the loins of my nation are men and women who will enter Paradise without being brought to account - then he recited - ‘and others among them who have not yet joined them.’ The first statement is more authentic. It was narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “I saw myself watering black sheep, then I followed them with white sheep, the first of which was O Abu Bakr. He said: O Messenger of God, as for the black sheep, they are the Arabs, and as for the white sheep, they are the Persians who will follow you after the Arabs. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: This is how the angel (i.e. Gabriel) began it.” Narrated by Ibn Abi Layla on the authority of a man from the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), namely Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him.
62:4: God Almighty says: That is the bounty of God which He bestows upon whom He wills, and God is the possessor of great bounty. Ibn Abbas said: When the Persians were joined to the Quraysh. It was also said: It means Islam, the grace of God which He gives to whom He wills, as said by Al-Kalbi. It was also said: It means revelation and prophethood, as said by Muqatil. A fourth statement is that it means money spent in obedience, which is the meaning of what Abu Salih said. Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, that the poor emigrants came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said, The wealthy have taken the highest ranks and eternal bliss. He asked, What is that? They said, They pray as we pray, they fast as we fast, they give charity but we do not give charity, they free slaves but we do not free slaves. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, Shall I not teach you something by which you will remind those who came before you and outdo those who come after you, and no one will be better than you except the one who does as you do? They said, Yes, O Messenger of God. He said, You should glorify God, magnify God, and praise God thirty-three times after every prayer. Abu Salih said, “The poor emigrants returned to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said, ‘Our wealthy brothers heard what we did and did the same.’ The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, “That is the bounty of God which He bestows upon whom He wills.” A fifth statement is that it was the people’s submission to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), their entry into his religion, and their support for him. And God knows best.”
62:5: He gave an example of the Jews when they abandoned working according to the Torah and did not believe in Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him. They carried the Torah meaning they were charged with working according to it, according to Ibn Abbas. Al-Jurjani said: It is from the word carrier meaning guarantee, meaning they guaranteed the rulings of the Torah. Like a donkey carrying books is the plural of book, which is a large book, because it reveals the meaning when it is read. Maymun ibn Mihran said: A donkey does not know whether it is on its back or a basket, and this is how the Jews are. In this, God is a warning to those who carry the book to learn its meanings and what is in it, lest they be subjected to the same blame that befell these people. The poet said: Travel songs, they have no knowledge of the best of them except as the knowledge of camels By God, a camel does not know whether it will go out with its load or not. Yahya bin Yaman said: One of them writes the hadith but does not understand or contemplate it. If one of them is asked about a matter, he sits as if he is a writer. The poet said: The narrators are ignorant of what they have been carrying, like camels carrying a camel. Neither the camels that carry the deposit benefit him nor the camels that carry the deposit benefit him Munther bin Al-Baluti, may God have mercy on him, said well: Caw as you wish and you will find supporters, and travel a lot and you will find a donkey. He carries what I have placed on my table, he carries it like a donkey He carries his books and does not know if what is in them is right or wrong. If they are asked, they say, “This is what we narrated. We did not lie or transgress.” Their elders become small when digging because they are ignorant. Then they did not carry it out means they did not act upon it. He likened them - while the Torah was in their hands and they did not act upon it - to a donkey carrying a book but it has nothing but the weight of the load without benefit. Carried is in the accusative case as a state, meaning carrying. It is also permissible for it to be in the genitive case as a description, because a donkey is like a mean person. He said: And the mean one ordered me to curse him How evil is the example of the people is the example that We have given them, so the complement was omitted. And God does not guide the wrongdoing people meaning those who knew in advance that they would be disbelievers.
62:6: When the Jews claimed virtue and said, We are the children of God and His beloved (al-Ma’idah 5:18), God Almighty said, If you claim that you are allies of God to the exclusion of the people, then the allies have honor with God. Then wish for death, if you should be truthful, so that you may become what the allies of God become.
62:7: And they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have put forth meaning, what they have put forth in denying Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. If they had wished for it, they would have died, and that would invalidate their statement and their claim of guardianship. In a hadith: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said when this verse was revealed: ‘By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, if they had wished for death, not a Jew would have remained on its deck but that he would have died.’” This is information about the unseen and a miracle for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The meaning of this verse has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah, in His statement: “Say: ‘If the home of the Hereafter with God is exclusively for you, to the exclusion of the people, then wish for death, if you should be truthful.’” (al-Baqarah 2:94)
62:8: Al-Zajjaj said: It is not said: If Zaid is gone, then go. Here he said: For he will meet you, because it has the meaning of that of condition and consequence, meaning if you flee from him, then he will meet you. This is an exaggeration to indicate that fleeing from him is of no use. Zuhair said: Whoever fears the causes of death will be overtaken by it, even if he seeks the causes of heaven with a ladder. I said: It is permissible to complete the speech when he says: That from which you flee, then he begins, for he will meet you. And Tarafa said: Death is enough to be a preacher to those for whom death has been decreed. Remember death and beware of mentioning it. Indeed, in death there is a lesson for the wise. Everything will die in a place or on a journey And fates are around him, watching him, but caution cannot save him from death
62:9: It contains thirteen issues: First: O you who have believed, when the call to prayer is made on the day of Jumu’ah, Abdullah ibn Az-Zubayr, Al-A’mash and others read Al-Jumu’ah with a sukoon on the meem for emphasis. These are two dialects. Their plural is jammu’ and jumma’. Al-Farra’ said: It is said Jumu’ah with a sukoon on the meem, Jumu’ah with a damma on the meem, and Jumu’ah with a fatha on the meem, so it is an attribute of the day, meaning a gathering of people. Just as it is said: a laughter for the one who laughs. Ibn Abbas said: The Qur’an was revealed with emphasis and emphasis, so read it as Jumu’ah meaning with a damma on the meem. Al-Farra’ and Abu Ubaid said: The emphasis is better and better, like ghurfah a room and ghurf, tarfa a room and hujr a room and hujr a room. The fatha on the meem is the language of Banu Uqayl. It was said that it is the language of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). On the authority of Salman: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It was called Jumu’ah because God gathered the creation of Adam in it. It was also said: Because God Almighty completed the creation of everything in it, so the creatures gathered in it. It was also said: So that groups would gather in it. It was also said: So that people would gather in it for prayer. And min means in, meaning in a day, like the Almighty’s saying: Show me what they have created on the earth (Fatir 35:40), meaning on the earth. Second: Abu Salamah said: The first one who said: As for after that, Ka’b bin Lu’ayy was the first to name Friday Friday. Friday was called Al-‘Uruba. It was said that the first one to name it Friday Al-Ansar. Ibn Sirin said: The people of Madinah gathered before the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to Madinah, and before the word Friday was revealed, and they were the ones who named it Friday. That is because they said: The Jews have a day in which they gather, every seven days, which is Saturday. And the Christians have a similar day, which is Sunday. So come, let us gather so that we can make a day for ourselves to remember God, pray on it and remember – or something like that – so they said: Saturday is for the Jews, and Sunday is for the Christians, so make it the Day of Al-‘Uruba. So they gathered to As’ad bin Zura Abu Umamah, may God be pleased with him, so he led them in two rak’ahs of prayer that day and reminded them, so they named it Friday when they gathered. As’ad slaughtered a sheep for them, and they ate dinner and lunch from it because of their small number. This was the first Friday in Islam. I said: It was narrated that they were twelve men, as will be mentioned later. It was mentioned in this narration that the one who gathered them and led the prayer was As`ad ibn Zurarah, and likewise in the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka`b ibn Malik, on the authority of his father Ka`b, as will be mentioned later. Al-Bayhaqi said: We narrated on the authority of Musa ibn `Uqbah, on the authority of Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, that Mus`ab ibn `Umair was the first to gather the Friday prayers in Madinah for the Muslims before the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) arrived there. Al-Bayhaqi said: It is possible that Mus`ab gathered them with the help of As`ad ibn Zurarah, so Ka`b was added to him. And God knows best. As for the first Friday prayer that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) held with his companions, the biographers and historians said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) arrived as an emigrant and descended upon Quba, to the Banu Amr ibn Awf, on Monday, twelfth night of the month of Rabi` al-Awwal, when the sun was at its highest. And from that year history is counted. He stayed in Quba until Thursday and established their mosque. Then he went out on Friday to Madinah, and the Friday prayer caught up with him with the Banu Salim ibn Awf in the valley of theirs, where the people had built a mosque. So he led them in the prayer and delivered the sermon. This was the first sermon he delivered in Medina, in which he said: “Praise be to God. I praise Him, seek His aid, ask His forgiveness, and ask His guidance. I believe in Him and do not disbelieve in Him, and I am hostile to those who disbelieve in Him. I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, without partner. I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. He sent him with guidance, the religion of truth, light, admonition, and wisdom after a period of time in which there were no messengers, little knowledge, misguidance among the people, a shortening of time, the approach of the Hour, and a nearness of the appointed time. Whoever obeys God and His Messenger has indeed been guided. Whoever disobeys God and His Messenger has indeed gone astray, neglected, and strayed far astray. I advise you to fear God, for the best advice a Muslim can give to another Muslim is to urge him toward the Hereafter and to command him to fear God. Beware of what God Himself has warned you about, for fear of God for the one who acts upon it out of fear and awe of his Lord is a true aid to whatever you seek in the Hereafter. Whoever puts things right between him and his Lord in secret And the public, if done for the sake of God only, will be remembered for him in this life and a store for what comes after death, when a person will need what he has sent forth. And whatever was other than that, he would wish that there was a great distance between it and it. “And God warns you of Himself, and God is Kind to His servants.” (Al Imran 3:30) He is the One Who has fulfilled His word and fulfilled His promise, without breaking it or causing humiliation. For He, the Most High, says: The word will not be changed with Me, and I am not unjust to the servants. So fear God in your life for this life and the next, in secret and in public, for Whoever fears God - He will remove from him his misdeeds and make great for him his reward. And whoever fears God has certainly attained a great attainment. And fearing God means avoiding His hatred, His punishment, and His wrath. And fearing God whitens faces, pleases the Lord, and raises one’s status. Take your share and do not be careless with regard to God, for He has taught you His Book and made His way clear to you, that He may know those who are truthful and know the liars. So do good as God has been good to you, and be hostile to His enemies, and strive in God’s cause with the striving due to Him. He has chosen you and named you Muslims. So he who perishes will perish by clear evidence, and he who lives will live by clear evidence. And there is no power and no say of God except with God. So remember God often, and work for what comes after death, for he who makes his relationship with God sound, God will suffice him against what is between him and the people. That is because God decrees over the people, but they do not decree over Him, and He possesses over the people, but they do not possess over Him. God is Great, and there is no power and no strength except with God, the Most High, the Almighty. The first Friday prayer after that was held in a village called Jawathi in Bahrain. It was said that the first person to call it Friday was Ka’b ibn Lu’ay ibn Ghalib, because the Quraysh gathered there with Ka’b, as mentioned above. And God knows best. Third: God addressed the believers on Friday, not the unbelievers, to honor and glorify them. He said: O you who have believed. Then He singled them out for the call, even though it was included in the general meaning of His statement: And when you call to prayer, to indicate its obligation and emphasis. Some scholars said: The fact that the prayer is Friday here is known by consensus, not from the wording itself. Ibn al-Arabi said: I believe it is known from the wording itself with a point, which is his statement: of Friday, and that is useful because the call that is specific to that day is the call to that prayer. As for other prayers, it is general and includes all other days. If it was not intended to be the call to Friday, there would be no meaning or benefit to specifying it for it and adding it to it. Fourth: The ruling on the call to prayer has been fully discussed in Surah Al-Ma’idah. The call to prayer during the time of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was as it is for all other prayers. One call to prayer would be made when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sat on the pulpit. Abu Bakr, Umar, and Ali used to do the same in Kufa. Then Uthman added a third call to prayer on the pulpit from his house called Al-Zawra’ when the people in Medina had increased in number. When they heard it, they would come. When Uthman sat on the pulpit, the muezzin of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would call to prayer. Then Uthman would deliver the sermon. This was narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Ishaq from Al-Zuhri from Al-Sa’ib ibn Zayd, who said: "The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) had only one muezzin. When he went out, he called the adhan and when he dismounted, he called the iqama. Abu Bakr and Umar were like that. When Uthman took over and the number of people increased, he added a third call to prayer from a house in the marketplace called al-Zawra'. When he went out, he called the adhan and when he dismounted, he called the iqama." Al-Bukhari transmitted it through different chains of narration with the same meaning. In some of them, it says that the third call to prayer on Friday was ordered by Uthman ibn Affan when the number of people in the mosque increased. The two adhans on Friday were when the imam sits. Al-Marudi said: As for the first call to prayer, it was an innovation. Uthman ibn Affan performed it so that the people would prepare to attend the sermon when the city expanded and its population increased. Umar may God be pleased with him had ordered that the call to prayer be made in the marketplace before the mosque so that people would get up from their transactions. When they gathered, the call to prayer would be made in the mosque. Uthman may God be pleased with him made it two calls to prayer in the mosque. This was stated by Ibn al-Arabi. In the authentic hadith, it says that the call to prayer was one during the time of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), but when Uthman came, he added the third call to prayer to al-Zawra'. He called it the third in the hadith because he added it to the iqama. As he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Between every two calls to prayer there is a prayer for whoever wishes, meaning the call to prayer and the iqamah. People think that this is a prayer, so they made three muezzins, which was a delusion. Then they gathered them together at one time, which was a delusion upon a delusion. I saw them calling to prayer in Madinat al-Salam after the call to prayer from the minaret, in front of the imam under the pulpit in a group, just as they used to do with us in previous countries. All of that is an innovation. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying, So hasten to the remembrance of God. There are three opinions regarding the meaning of striving here: The first is intention. Al-Hasan said: By God, it is not striving on foot, but rather striving with the heart and intention. The second is that it is action, like the Almighty’s saying, And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it with the necessary effort while he is a believer (al-Isra’ 17:19), and His saying, Indeed, your striving is diverse (al-Layl 92:4), and His saying, And that man can have nothing but what he strives for (al-Najm 53:39). This is the opinion of the majority. Zuhair said: People came after them to catch up with them. He also said: He sought revenge once after he had shed blood between the clan. So strive to go to the remembrance of God, and occupy yourself with its causes, such as washing, purification, and turning to Him. Third: What is meant by it is walking. This is a virtue, not a condition. In Sahih Al-Bukhari, it is narrated that Abu ‘Eesa ibn Jabr - whose name was ‘Abdur-Rahman and he was one of the senior Companions - walked to the Friday prayer on foot and said: “I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: ‘Whoever’s feet become dusty in the cause of God, God will forbid him from the Fire.’” Fourthly, its apparent meaning may be understood as running and strenuous activity. Ibn al-‘Arabi said: This is what the most knowledgeable Companions and early jurists rejected. ‘Umar recited it as “they set out to the remembrance of God, fleeing by running and guiding, which indicates the apparent meaning. Ibn Mas‘ud recited it in the same way and said: “If you had recited ‘so hasten,’ I would have hastened until my cloak fell off.” Ibn Shihab recited: So proceed to the remembrance of God, following that path. All of this is an interpretation from them, not a recitation of the revealed Quran. It is permissible to recite the Quran with tafsir when interpreting it. Abu Bakr al-Anbari said: Those who disagreed with the verses of the Qur’an used as evidence the readings of Umar and Ibn Mas’ud. Kharshah ibn al-Har said: Umar, may God be pleased with him, saw me with a piece of verses in which was: So proceed to the remembrance of God. Umar said to me: Who taught you this? I said: My father. He said: My father is the best of us at reciting the abrogated verses. Then Umar recited: So proceed to the remembrance of God. Idris told us, Khalaf told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of al-Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Kharshah, and he mentioned it. Muhammad ibn Yahya told us, Muhammad ibn Qat told us, except that he proceeded to the remembrance of God. Idris told us, he said, Khalaf told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, that Abdullah ibn Masoud recited, Proceed to the remembrance of God, and said, If it were ‘seek,’ I would have sought until my cloak fell off. Abu Bakr said, “He argued against him by saying that the nation agreed on ‘seek,’ based on the narration of that from God, Lord of the Worlds, and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace.” As for Abdullah ibn Masoud, it is not authentically reported from him, seek, because the chain of transmission is not connected. Ibrahim al-Nakha’i did not hear anything from Abdullah ibn Masoud, but rather seek was reported from Umar, may God be pleased with him. So if someone is alone in narrating something that contradicts the verse and the group, that is due to forgetfulness on his part. The Arabs agree that seek means to go forward, but it is not without seriousness and shrinking. Zuhair said: He sought to avenge the anger of Ibn Murrah after the bloodshed between the tribe had been shed. By striving, he meant to go with diligence and effort, and he did not mean to run and speed up his steps. Al-Farra and Abu Ubaidah said: The meaning of the one striving in the verse is to go. Al-Farra used as evidence their saying: He strives in the lands seeking God’s bounty, meaning he goes with diligence and effort. Abu Ubaidah used as evidence the saying of the poet: I strive for the sake of Bani Malik, every man strives for his own sake Is it possible to pursue this verse except through the method of proceeding with contraction? It is impossible that this meaning would have been hidden from Ibn Masoud, despite his eloquence and mastery of Arabic. I said: What indicates that what is meant here is not the enemy: He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: When the prayer is called, do not come running, but come to it with tranquility. Al-Hasan said: By God, it is not by striving on foot, and they were forbidden to come to prayer except with tranquility and dignity, but with the heart, intention, and humility. Qatada said: Striving means to strive with your heart and your actions. This is good, as it combines the three opinions. There are hadiths mentioned in the books of hadith about bathing for Friday, using perfume, and adorning oneself with clothing. Sixth: The Almighty’s statement, O you who have believed, is addressed to those who are accountable by consensus. Excluded from this are the sick, the chronically ill, travelers, slaves, women with evidence, the blind, and the elderly who cannot walk without a guide, according to Abu Hanifa. Abu al-Zubayr narrated on the authority of Jabir: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Whoever believes in God and the Last Day must perform the Friday prayer on Friday, unless he is sick, traveling, a woman, a child, or a slave. But whoever is content with amusement or business, God will be content with him, and God is Free of need and Praiseworthy.’ This was reported by Al-Daraquti. Our scholars may God have mercy on them said: ‘No one who is obliged to attend the Friday prayer should miss it except for an excuse that prevents him from attending it, such as an illness that prevents him from attending it, or fear of worsening of the illness, or fear of the ruler’s injustice towards him in money or body without ruling that he is justly entitled to it. Heavy rain with mud is an excuse if it does not stop. Malik did not consider it an excuse for him, as Al-Mahdawi narrated. And if someone misses it because of a close friend of his who is approaching death, and there is no one with him to take care of his affairs, hoping that he will be able to do so, Ibn ‘Umar did that. Whoever misses it without an excuse and prays before the imam must repeat it, and there is no consolation for praying before him. By missing it even though he was able to do so, he is disobeying God by his action.’” Seventh: The Almighty’s statement: When the call to prayer is made, applies only to those who are close by and can hear the call. As for those who live far away and cannot hear the call, they are not included in this address. There is a difference of opinion regarding who attends Friday prayer, whether near or far. Ibn ‘Umar, Abu Hurayrah, and Anas said: Friday prayer is obligatory for those in a city within a distance of six miles. Rabi’ah said: Four miles. Malik and Al-Layth said: Three miles. Al-Shafi’i said: The consideration for hearing the call to prayer is that the caller should be loud, the voices should be quiet, the wind should be still, and the caller should be standing at the surah of the city. In the Sahih, it is narrated on the authority of ‘Aishah: “People used to come to the Friday prayer from their homes and the upper reaches, and they would come in the dust, and the dust would cover them, and the wind would come out of them. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: If you had washed, this would have been your fault!” Our scholars said: If the sound is loud and the people are calm and quiet, then the furthest distance from hearing the sound is three miles. The upper reaches of Madinah are four to three miles. Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Ishaq said: Friday prayer is obligatory for whoever hears the call to prayer. Ad-Daraquti narrated from the hadith of Amr ibn Shuaib, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Friday prayer is only obligatory for the one who hears the call to prayer. Abu Hanifa and his companions said: It is obligatory for the one who is in the city, whether he hears the call to prayer or not. It is not obligatory for the one who is outside the city even if he hears the call to prayer. He was even asked: Is Friday prayer obligatory for the people of Zubarah - between which and Kufa there is a riverbed -? He said: No. It was also narrated from Rabi’ah: It is obligatory for the one who hears the call to prayer and leaves his house on foot and catches the prayer. It was narrated from Al-Zuhri: It is obligatory for him if he hears the call to prayer. Eighth: The Almighty’s saying: When the call is made for the prayer on the day of Jumu’ah, then proceed to the remembrance of God. This is evidence that Jumu’ah is not obligatory except with the call, and the call can only be made after the time for the prayer has begun. The evidence for this is the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him): When the time for prayer is present, give the call to prayer, then pronounce the iqama, and let the eldest of you lead you in prayer. This was said to Malik ibn al-Huwayrith and his companion. In Sahih al-Bukhari, it is narrated from Anas ibn Malik that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) used to pray Jumu’ah when the sun had declined. It has been narrated from Abu al-Siddiq and Ahmad ibn Hanbal that it is prayed before noon. Ahmad relied on the hadith of Salamah ibn al-Akwa’ in this regard: “We used to pray with the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) then we would leave, and the walls did not cast any shadow.” The hadith of Salamah is interpreted as referring to praying early. It was narrated by Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik, on the authority of Ya`la ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Iyas ibn al-Akwa`, on the authority of his father. And Wakee` narrated on the authority of Ya`la, on the authority of Iyas, on the authority of his father, who said: “We used to gather with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) when the sun had set and then returned, following the shade.” This is the view of the majority of the later and earlier generations, and is based on analogy with the noon prayer. The hadith of Ibn `Umar and Sahl is evidence that they used to arrive very early for the Friday prayer, either at dawn or before it, and they would not attend it until after the prayer had ended. Malik was of the view that arriving early for the Friday prayer should only be a little after noon. He interpreted: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever goes in the first hour, it is as if he has sacrificed a sacrificial animal… The entire hadith. That it was in one hour. All other scholars interpreted it to refer to the twelve hours of the day, whether equal or different according to the waxing and waning of the day. Ibn al-Arabi: It is more authentic, based on the hadith of Ibn Umar may God be pleased with them both: They did not take a nap or eat lunch except after Friday prayers because of the many people who came early to it. Ninth: God Almighty has made Friday prayer obligatory for every Muslim, in response to those who say: It is a communal obligation. This was reported from some Shafi’is. It was reported from Malik, who was not sure: It is a Sunnah. The majority of the Ummah and the Imams believe that it is an individual obligation, based on the statement of God Almighty: When the call is made for the prayer on the day of Jumu’ah, then proceed to the remembrance of God and leave business. It was proven that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Let some people cease neglecting Friday prayers, or God will seal their hearts and they will be among the heedless. This is a clear proof of the obligation of Friday prayer and its obligation. In Sunan Ibn Majah, it was reported on the authority of Abu al-Ja’d al-Damri - who was a companion of the Prophet - who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Whoever misses Friday prayer three times out of negligence, God will seal his heart.’” Its chain of transmission is authentic. Jabir ibn Abdullah said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever misses Friday prayer three times without necessity, God will seal his heart. Ibn al-Arabi: It has been proven that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Going to Friday prayers is obligatory for every Muslim. Tenth: God has made it obligatory to go to Friday prayer absolutely, without any condition. The condition of ablution has been established in the Qur’an and Sunnah for all prayers, as God Almighty says: When you rise to prayer, wash your faces (al-Ma’idah 5:6). The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God does not accept any prayer without purification. A group went astray and said: The Friday ritual bath is obligatory. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is false, because al-Nasa’i and Abu Dawud narrated in their Sunans: "The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: 'Whoever performs ablution on Friday, that is good and beneficial. Whoever performs ghusl, ghusl is better.'" In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: "The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: 'Whoever performs ablution on Friday and does it well, then goes to the Friday prayer and listens attentively, God will forgive him for what happened between that Friday and the next, plus three days. Whoever touches pebbles has engaged in idle talk.'" This is explicit. In Al-Muwatta', it is stated: A man entered on Friday while 'Umar ibn Al-Khattab was delivering the sermon... - the hadith - until he said: "I did nothing more than perform ablution. 'Umar said: 'And ablution too? You know that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to command ghusl. 'Umar commanded ghusl and did not command him to return." This indicates that it is to be interpreted as recommended. It was not possible, when he was engaged in the obligation - which is attending and listening to the sermon - to return to the Sunnah, and that was in the presence of the most eminent Companions and senior emigrants around 'Umar, and in the mosque of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Eleventh: Friday prayer is not waived because it falls on a holiday, contrary to Ahmad ibn Hanbal who said: If a holiday and a Friday prayer coincide, the obligation of Friday prayer is waived, because the holiday comes before it and people are busy with it instead of it. He based this on what was narrated that Uthman gave permission on a holiday for the people of the upper classes to stay away from Friday prayer. The statement of one of the companions is not valid if it is contradicted and he is not joined in congregation for it. The command to strive is valid on the day of Eid as it is on all other days. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Nu’man ibn Bashir, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to recite on the two Eids and on al-Jumuah 62:Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High and Has there come to you the report of the overwhelming event? He said: If the Eid and Friday fall on the same day, he would also recite them in the two prayers. Narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Majah. Twelfth: The Almighty said: To the remembrance of God, meaning prayer. It was also said: The sermon and exhortations, as stated by Saeed bin Jubair. Ibn Al-Arabi said: The correct view is that it is obligatory in all of them, and the beginning of it is the sermon. Our scholars said the same, except for Abdul Malik bin Al-Majushun, who considered it a Sunnah. The evidence for its obligation is that it prohibits selling, and were it not obligatory, it would not have prohibited it, because what is recommended does not prohibit what is permissible. If we say that what is meant by remembrance is prayer, then he says: A sermon from the prayer. The servant remembers God through his actions, just as he glorifies God through his actions. Al-Zamakhshari said: If you say: How can the remembrance of God be interpreted as a sermon when it includes other things? I say: Whatever is mentioned of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and praising him and his rightly-guided caliphs and the pious believers, and exhortation and reminder, then it is considered remembrance of God. As for everything other than that, such as mentioning the oppressors and their titles, praising them and praying for them - and they are more deserving of the opposite - then it is from the remembrance of Satan, and it is from the remembrance of God in stages. Thirteenth: The Almighty’s statement: And leave off trading is from what God the Almighty forbade during the Friday prayer, and He forbade it during that time for those who are obligated to perform it. Trading is not devoid of buying, so He sufficed with mentioning one of them, like His statement: Garments to protect you from the heat and garments to protect you from your violence (al-Nahl 16:81). He specified trading because it is what most market owners are busy with. And whoever is not obligated to attend Friday prayers is not forbidden from buying and selling. There are two opinions regarding the time of prohibition: 1- It is from after noon until it is over. This was stated by Ad-Dahhak, Al-Hasan and Ata'. 2- It is from the time of the call to prayer until the time of prayer. This was stated by Al-Shafi'i. Malik's school of thought is that selling should be abandoned when the call to prayer is made, and any sale that took place during that time should be annulled. However, manumission, marriage, divorce and other transactions should not be annulled, because people do not usually engage in them as they engage in selling. They said: The same applies to partnerships, livestock and charity, which are rarely annulled. Ibn Al-Arabi said: The correct view is that they should all be annulled, because selling is only prohibited because of engaging in it. So every contract that distracts from the agreed upon contract is religiously forbidden and annulled as a deterrent. Al-Mahdawi said: Some scholars are of the view that selling is permissible during the aforementioned time, and they interpreted the prohibition as recommended, and they based their evidence on the words of God the Almighty: That is better for you. I said: This is the Shafi'i school of thought: the sale is concluded and not annulled. Al-Zamakhshari said in his interpretation: The majority of scholars are of the opinion that this does not invalidate the sale. They said: Because the sale was not forbidden in and of itself, but because it involves forgetting what is obligatory. It is like praying on usurped land or clothing, or performing ablution with usurped water. Some people say that it is invalid. I said: The correct view is that it is corrupt and invalid. Because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Every action that is not in accordance with our command is rejected. That is, it is rejected. And God knows best.
62:10: The Almighty's statement: And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land. This is a command of permission, like His statement: And when you have completed your ihram, then hunt (al-Ma’idah 5:2). He is saying: When you have finished the prayer, disperse within the land for trade and to seek your needs. And seek from the bounty of God, meaning from His provisions. When 'Irak ibn Malik prayed the Friday prayer, he would leave and stand at the door of the mosque and say: O God, I have answered Your call, performed Your obligatory prayer, and dispersed as You commanded me, so provide for me from Your bounty, for You are the best of providers. Ja'far ibn Muhammad said regarding the Almighty's statement: And seek from the bounty of God, it refers to working on the Sabbath. Al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab reported: Seeking knowledge. It was also said: It refers to voluntary prayer. Ibn 'Abbas reported: They did not believe in seeking anything from this world; it only referred to visiting the sick, attending funerals, and visiting one's brother for the sake of God. God the Almighty says: And remember God often meaning, by obedience and speaking, and by thanking Him for the blessings He has bestowed upon you in order to perform the obligatory duties. That you may be successful so that you may be successful. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: “Dhikr is obedience to God the Almighty. So whoever obeys God has remembered Him, and whoever does not obey Him is not remembering Him, even if he glorifies God often.” This has already been mentioned with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet in Surat Al-Baqarah.
62:11: It contains seventeen issues: First: The Almighty said: And when they see a trade or amusement, they disperse to it. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was delivering the sermon while standing on Friday, and a caravan came from Syria, so the people dispersed to it until there were only twelve men left - in one narration, I was among them - so this verse was revealed about al-Jumuah 62:And when they see a trade or amusement, they disperse to it and leave you standing. In another narration: Among them were Abu Bakr and Umar, may God be pleased with them. Al-Kalbi and others mentioned: The one who brought it was Dihya ibn Khalifah al-Kalbi from Syria during a time of famine and high prices, and he had with him everything the people needed of wheat, flour, and other things. He dismounted at Ahjar al-Zayt and beat the drum to announce his arrival to the people, so the people went out except for twelve men. It was also said: eleven men. Al-Kalbi said: They were delivering the Friday sermon, so they dispersed to it, and eight men remained with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Tha’labi omitted it from Ibn Abbas, and Al-Daraqutni mentioned it from… Hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah: “While the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was leading us on Friday prayers, a caravan carrying food approached and stopped at Al-Baqi’a. They turned towards it and dispersed, leaving the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with him, except for forty men, including me.” He said: “And God, the Almighty, revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: ‘And when they see a transaction or amusement, they disperse to it and leave you standing.’” Ad-Daraqutni said: “No one in this chain of narration has mentioned more than forty men, other than Ali ibn Asim, on the authority of Hisayn. His companions disagreed with him and said: ‘No one remained with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) except twelve men.’ It was narrated from him (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he said: ‘By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if they were to go out all together, God would set the valley on fire around them.’” Az-Zamakhshari mentioned it: “The names of the twelve men were narrated in a mursal hadith, and it was narrated by Asad ibn Amr, the father of Asad ibn Musa ibn Asad. It states that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not remain with him except Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Talhah, Az-Zubayr, Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas, Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf, Abu Ubaidah ibn Al-Jarrah, Sa’id ibn Zayd, Bilal, and Abdullah ibn Mas’ud in one of the two narrations. In the other narration, Ammar ibn Yasir.” I said: He did not mention Jabir, and Muslim mentioned that he was among them, and al-Daraqutni as well. So they are thirteen. If Abdullah ibn Mas`ud was among them, then they are fourteen. Abu Dawud mentioned in his Marasil the reason why they allowed themselves to leave the sermon, and they were worthy of their virtue not to do so, so he said: Mahmud ibn Khalid told us, al-Walid told us, Abu Mu`ad Bakr ibn Maruf told me that he heard Muqatil ibn Hayyan say: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to pray the Friday prayer before the sermon, just like the two Eid prayers, until it was a Friday and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was delivering the Friday sermon. He had already prayed the Friday prayer and a man entered and said: ‘Duhaya ibn Khulayqah al-Kalbi has come with a trade mission.’ Whenever Duhayqah came, his family would meet him with tambourines. So the people went out and thought that there was nothing wrong with not delivering the sermon. Then God, the Almighty, revealed: ‘And when they see a trade or amusement, they disperse to it.’ So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) brought forward the Friday sermon and delayed the prayer. No one would go out for a nosebleed or minor illness after the prohibition until he asked permission from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He would point to him with his finger next to his thumb, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would give him permission and then point to him with his hand. Some of the hypocrites found the sermon and sitting in the mosque difficult, and whenever a Muslim man asked permission, the hypocrites would stand beside him, hiding behind him until he came out. Then God, the Almighty, revealed: ‘God knows those among you who sneak away secretly.’” (al-Nur 24:24) Al-Suhayli said: Even if this report is not transmitted from an authentic source, the good opinion of the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) requires that it be correct. Qatada said: We have been informed that they did it three times, each time for a caravan that had come from Ash-Sham, and each time it happened on a Friday. It was said that their going out because of the arrival of Dihya Al-Kalbi with his trade and their looking at the caravan of dates was a useless pastime, except that there would have been no sin in it if it had occurred in a different way. However, when it was connected to turning away from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and swooping down on his presence, he became harsh and arrogant, and what was revealed in the Qur’an and his slander in the name of pastime was revealed about him. It was said: “On the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Everything that a man plays with is futile except shooting with his bow.” The hadith has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Anfal, so praise be to God. Jabir ibn Abdullah said: When the slave girls were getting married, they would play flutes and drums, and they would disperse to them, so this was revealed. The metaphor was attributed to trade because it is more important. Talhah ibn Musarraf recited: And when they saw trade and amusement, they dispersed to it. It was said: We are satisfied with what we have and you are satisfied with what you have, but the opinion differs It was said: The best thing in Arabic is for the man to mention the other of the two names. Second: The scholars differed regarding the number required for the Friday prayer. Al-Hasan said: The Friday prayer is valid with two people. Al-Layth and Abu Yusuf said: It is valid with three people. Sufyan Al-Thawri and Abu Hanifa said: Four people. Rabia said: Twelve people. Al-Najjad mentioned Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Sulaiman, who said: Abu Khalid Yazid bin Al-Haitham bin Tahman Al-Daqqaq told us, Subh bin Dinar told us, Al-Ma’afi bin Imran told us, Ma’qil bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Mus’ab bin Umair, that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, sent him to Madinah, and that he stayed in the house of Sa’d bin Mu’adh, and he gathered them, and they were twelve men, and he slaughtered a sheep for them that day. Al-Shafi’i said: With forty men. Abu Ishaq al-Shirazi said in The Book of At-Tanbih ‘ala Madhhab al-Imam al-Shafi’i: “In every village that has forty sane, adult, free, resident men who do not leave it in summer or winter, and who are present from the beginning of the sermon until the Friday prayer is established, then Friday prayer is obligatory for them.” Ahmad and Ishaq tended towards this opinion and did not stipulate these conditions. Malik said: If there is a village that has a market and a mosque, then Friday prayer is obligatory for them. Abu Hanifa said: Friday prayer is not obligatory for the people of the cities and villages, and it is not permissible for them to hold it there. He stipulated for the obligation of Friday prayer and its convening: a mosque, a dominant ruler, an existing market, and a flowing river. He cited as evidence the hadith of Ali: There is no Friday prayer or Tashreeq prayer except in a city that has a mosque and companions to help them. This is mentioned in the hadith of Ibn Abbas, who said: The first Friday prayer after Friday prayer in the mosque of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was in a village in Bahrain called Jawatha. Imam Al-Shafi’i’s evidence in the Forty Hadith is the hadith of Jabir Al-Madkoor, which was included by Al-Daraqutni. In Sunan Ibn Majah and Al-Daraqutni also, and Dalā’il Al-Nubuwwah by Al-Bayhaqi, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Ka’b bin Malik, who said: I was leading my father when he lost his sight. When I took him to the Friday prayer and he heard the call to prayer, he prayed for Ibn Umamah and asked forgiveness for him. He said: He stayed for such a period of time, and he did not hear the call to prayer except that he did that. So I said to him: O Aya, what is your asking forgiveness for Abu Umamah every time you heard the call to prayer for Friday? He said: O my son, he was the first to gather in Madinah in a place in the Harrat Bani Bayada called Naqi’ Al-Khadimat. I said: How many were you that day? He said: Forty men. Jabir bin Abdullah said: It has been the Sunnah that every three should have an Imam, and every forty or more should have a Friday prayer, the morning prayer, and the evening prayer, and that is because they are a group. Narrated by Al-Daraqutni. Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Salman Al-Najjad narrated: It was read to Abd Abdul Malik bin Muhammad Al-Raqqashi and I was listening. Raja bin Salamah told me, he said: My father told us, he said: Rawh bin Ghutayf Al-Thaqafi told us, he said: Al-Zuhri told me, on the authority of Abu Salamah, he said: I said to Abu Hurairah, on how many men is Friday prayer obligatory? He said: When the report of Husayn reached the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) gathered them. It was recited to Abdul Malik bin Muhammad and I was listening. He said: Raja’ bin Salamah told us, ‘Ibad bin ‘Ibad al-Mahfali told us, on the authority of Ja’far bin al-Zubayr, on the authority of al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Friday prayer is obligatory for fifty men, but it is not obligatory for those less than that.’” Ibn al-Mundhir said: ‘Umar bin ‘Abdul ‘Aziz wrote: In any village in which fifty men gather, let them pray Friday prayer. Al-Zuhri narrated on the authority of Umm ‘Abdullah al-Dawsariyyah, who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Friday prayer is obligatory for every village, even if there are only four in it.’” By villages, he means cities. This is not authentic from al-Zuhri. In another narration, Friday prayer and the cloak are obligatory for the people of every village, even if there are only three, with their fourth being their imam. It is not authentic that al-Zuhri heard it from al-Hudusariyyah. This ruling is abandoned. Third: The Friday prayer is valid without the permission of the imam or his presence. Abu Hanifa said: It is a condition for an imam or a caliph. Our evidence is that Walid bin Uqba, the governor of Kufa, was slow one day, so Ibn Masoud led the people in prayer without his permission. It was narrated that Ali led the Friday prayer on the day Uthman was besieged, but it was not narrated that he asked his permission. It was narrated that when Saeed bin Al-As, the governor of Medina, left Medina, Abu Musa led the people in the Friday prayer without asking permission. Malik said: God has obligations on earth, and He does not neglect them, whether he has a governor or not. Fourth: Our scholars said: One of the conditions for performing it is a roofed mosque. Ibn al-Arabi said: I do not know the reason for that. I said: Its meaning is the Almighty’s saying: And purify My House for those who perform Tawaf, and His saying: In houses which God has permitted to be raised (al-Nur 24:36). The true meaning of a house is that it has walls and a roof. This is the custom, and God knows best. Fifth: The Almighty’s statement: and they left you standing is a condition for the preacher to stand on the pulpit when delivering the sermon. Alqamah said: Abdullah was asked: Did the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) deliver the sermon standing or sitting? He said: Do you not read and they left you standing? In Sahih Muslim: On the authority of Ka’b ibn ‘Ujrah that he entered the mosque and ‘Abdur-Rahman ibn Umm al-Hakam was delivering the sermon sitting, so he said: Look at this wicked man, delivering the sermon while sitting! God the Almighty said: And when they see a transaction or amusement, they disperse to it and leave you standing. It was narrated from Jabir that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to deliver the sermon standing, then they would sit down, then he would stand and deliver the sermon. Whoever told you that he delivered the sermon while sitting has lied, for by God I prayed more than two thousand prayers with him.” The majority of jurists and leading scholars agree on this. Abu Hanifa said: Standing is not a condition for it. It is narrated that the first to deliver the sermon while sitting was Mu’awiyah. Uthman delivered the sermon while standing until he grew weak, then he delivered the sermon while sitting. It was said: Yes, Muawiyah delivered the sermon while sitting because of his age. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to deliver the sermon while standing, then sit, then stand up and would not speak while sitting. Narrated by Jabir ibn Samurah. Narrated by Ibn Umar in the book of Bukhari. Sixth: The sermon is a condition for the Friday prayer to be valid, and it is not valid without it. This is the opinion of the majority of scholars. Al-Hasan said: It is recommended. Ibn Al-Majishun said the same: It is a Sunnah, not an obligation. Saeed bin Jubair said: It is like the two rak’ahs of the Dhuhr prayer, so if someone omits it and prays the Friday prayer, then he has left out the two rak’ahs of the Dhuhr prayer. The evidence for its obligation is the statement of God the Almighty: and they left you standing. This is blameworthy, and what is obligatory is that whose omission is blameworthy according to Islamic law. The Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) did not pray it without a sermon. Seventh: He delivers the sermon leaning on a bow or a stick. In Sunan Ibn Majah, it says: Hisham bin Ammar told us, Abd al-Rahman bin Saeed bin Ammar bin Saad told us, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivered the sermon during war, he delivered the sermon while leaning on a bow, and when he delivered the sermon on Friday, he delivered the sermon while leaning on a stick. Eighth: He should say the salutation of peace when he ascends the pulpit to the people, according to Al-Shafi’i and others. Malik did not hold this view. Ibn Majah narrated from the hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ascended the pulpit, he would say the salutation of peace. Ninth: If someone delivers a sermon without being in a state of ritual purity for all or part of the sermon, he has sinned according to Malik, and he does not have to repeat it if he prays in a state of ritual purity. Al-Shafi’i has two opinions regarding the requirement of ritual purity. He stipulated it in the new sermon but did not stipulate it in the old one. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifa. Tenth: The minimum that should be done in the sermon is to praise God and send blessings upon His Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), to recommend fear of God, and to recite a verse from the Quran. In the second sermon, four rak’ahs are obligatory, just like in the first, except that instead of reciting a verse in the first, a supplication is obligatory, as stated by most of the jurists. Abu Hanifa said that if he limited himself to praising God, glorifying God, or extolling God, it would suffice. Uthman may God be pleased with him ascended the pulpit and said: Praise be to God, but he hesitated and said: Abu Bakr and Umar were preparing to speak for this occasion, and you are more in need of an imam who does things than an imam who speaks things, and the sermons will come to you. Then he came down and prayed. This was done in the presence of the Companions, and no one denounced him. Abu Yusuf and Muhammad said: What is obligatory is what is included in the name of a sermon. This is the opinion of Al-Shafi’i. Abu Umar ibn Abd Al-Barr said: It is the most correct of what has been said about that. Eleventh: In Sahih Muslim: “On the authority of Ya`la ibn Umayya that he heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, reciting on the pulpit, ‘And they will call out, “O Malik!” (al-Zukhruf 43:77)” It was narrated on the authority of Umrah bint Abd al-Rahman on the authority of Umrah’s sister who said: “I did not learn ‘Qaf, by the Glorious Qur’an’ except from the mouth of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on Fridays while he was reciting it on the pulpit every Friday.” And it was mentioned in the beginning of Qaf. In the reports of Abu Dawud, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, he said: “The beginning of the sermon of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was: ‘Praise be to God. We praise Him, seek His aid, and ask His forgiveness, and we seek refuge in Him from the evils of our own souls. Whomsoever God guides, none can misguide him, and whomsoever He misguides, none can guide him. We bear witness that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, and He sent him with the truth as a bearer of good tidings and a warner before the Hour. Whoever obeys God and His Messenger has been guided, and whoever disobeys them has gone astray.’ We ask God, our Lord, to make us among those who obey Him and His Messenger, follow what pleases Him, and avoid His wrath, for we are only through Him and for Him.’ And on his authority, he said: ‘It has reached us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say when he delivered a sermon: ‘Everything that is coming is near, and what is coming is not far off. God does not hasten for the sake of anyone’s haste, nor does He delay for the sake of people’s affairs. What God wills, not what people will. God wills a thing and people will a thing. What God wills will be, even if people dislike it.’” What God brings near cannot be far away, and what God makes far away cannot be brought near. Nothing happens except by the permission of God, the Almighty and Majestic. Jabir said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would deliver the sermon on Friday and say, after praising God and sending blessings upon His prophets: “O people, you have landmarks, so reach your landmarks. You have an end, so reach your end. The believing servant is between two fears: a term that has passed and he does not know what God will decide for it, and a term that remains and he does not know what God will do with it. So let the servant take from himself for himself, from his worldly life for his afterlife, from his youth before old age, and from life before death. By the One in whose hand is my soul, there is no place after death for whom repentance is sought, and after this world there is no home but Paradise or Hellfire. I say this and I ask God’s forgiveness for myself and you.” The sermon he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) gave on the first Friday upon his arrival in Medina has already been mentioned. Twelfth: Silence during the sermon is obligatory for whoever hears it, and it is a Sunnah obligation. The Sunnah is for both those who hear and those who do not to be silent, and they are equal, God willing, in this regard. Whoever speaks in this case is acting idle, and his prayer is not invalidated by that. In the Sahih, it is narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah: “The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘If you say to your companion, “Be quiet while the imam is delivering the sermon,” then you have spoken idle words.’” Al-Zamakhshari said: And if the one who is listening says to his companion, “Shh, then you have spoken idle words. Wouldn’t the preacher who goes to extremes in this be acting idle? We seek refuge in God from the strangeness of Islam and the misery of days.” Thirteenth: The people should face the Imam when he ascends the pulpit, as Abu Dawud narrated in a mursal form, “On the authority of Abaan bin Abdullah, who said: I was with Adi bin Thabit on Friday, and when the Imam came out - or he said he ascended the pulpit - he faced him and said: This is how the Companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) did and acted with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him).” Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Adi bin Thabit, on the authority of his father, and he added to the chain of transmission: On the authority of his father, who said: “When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) stood on the pulpit, his Companions would face him.” Ibn Majah said: I hope it is connected. I said: Abu Naim Al-Hafiz narrated that Muhammad bin Muammar told us that Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Najiyah told us that Ubadah bin Ya’qub told us that Muhammad bin Al-Fadl Al-Khurasani told us on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Ibrahim on the authority of Alqamah on the authority of Abdullah who said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood on the pulpit, we would face him. Muhammad bin Al-Fadl bin Atiyah was the only one to narrate it on the authority of Mansur. Fourteenth: The one who enters the mosque while the imam is delivering the sermon should not bow, according to Malik, may God have mercy on him. This is also the opinion of Ibn Shihab, may God have mercy on him, and others. In Al-Muwatta’, he says: The imam’s exit interrupts the prayer, and his speech interrupts the speech. This is a mursal hadith.
