In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Jabir, it is narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If one of you comes to a Friday feast while the imam is delivering the sermon, let him bow two rak’ahs and make them brief. This is explicitly stated regarding bowing. Al-Shafi’i and others say the same. Fifteenth: [And] Ibn Awn mentioned on the authority of Ibn Sirin who said: They used to hate sleeping while the imam was delivering the sermon and they would say harsh words about it. Ibn Awn said: Then he met me after that and said: Do you know what they say? They say their example is like that of a raiding party that failed. Then he said: Do you know what they failed at? They did not gain anything. And on the authority of Samurah ibn Jundub: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If one of you becomes miserable, let him move to the seat of his companion and let his companion move to his seat. Sixteenth: We mention in it the virtues of beer and its obligation that we did not mention before. The Imams narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah may God be pleased with him that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) mentioned Friday and said: There is an hour in it when a Muslim slave asks God for something while he is praying, but He gives it to him. And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Musa, he said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: It is the period between the time when the imam sits down until the prayer is over. And it was narrated on the authority of Anas that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was delayed on us one day, and when he came out, we said: You were delayed! He said: “That is because Gabriel came to me in the form of a white mirror with a black dot on it. I said: What is this, O Gabriel? He said: This Friday has good for you and your nation, and the Jews and Christians wanted it but missed it, but God guided you to it.” I said: O Gabriel, what is this black dot? He said: “This is my illness on Friday. No Muslim slave asks God for something good in it, but He gives it to him, or stores up something like it for him on the Day of Resurrection, or turns away something like it from him. It is the best of days with God, and the people of Paradise call it the Day of More.” And he mentioned the hadith. Ibn Al-Mubarak and Yahya bin Salam said: Al-Mas’udi narrated to us on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr on the authority of Abu Ubaidah bin Abdullah bin Utbah on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud who said: “Race towards Paradise, for God, the Blessed and Exalted, appears to the people of Paradise every Friday on a white camphor hill, and they will be close to Him - Ibn Al-Mubarak said - according to the degree of their hastening to the Friday prayer in this world.” Yahya bin Salam said: Like their hastening to the Friday prayer in this world. He added: A miracle will occur to them that they had never seen before. Yahya said: “I heard someone other than Al-Mas’udi add to it: It is the statement of God, the Most High: ‘And with Us is more.’” (Qaf: 35) I said: His statement, on a dune, means the people of Paradise. That is, while they are on a dune, as Al-Hasan narrated, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The people of Paradise will look at their Lord. Every Friday, I will be on a dune of camphor, the ends of which cannot be seen. There is a flowing river in it, both sides of which are filled with musk. There will be girls on it reciting the Qur’an in the most beautiful voices that the first and the last have ever heard. When they return to their homes, each man will take the hand of whomever he wishes of them. Then they will pass over bridges of pearls to their homes. Were it not that God guides them to their homes, they would not have been guided to them because of what God does for them every Friday.” Yahya ibn Salam mentioned this. Anas said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: On the night of my Isra’, I saw beneath the Throne seventy cities, each city seventy times the size of your cities, filled with angels glorifying and sanctifying God, and saying in their glorification: O God, forgive those who witness Friday prayer, O God, forgive those who bathe on Friday. This was mentioned by al-Tha’labi. Judge al-Shariq Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Ibrahim al-Hashemi al-Issawi, from the descendants of Isa ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, narrated with a sahih chain of narration: On the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash’ari: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty will resurrect the days on the Day of Resurrection in their original state, and He will resurrect Friday radiant and luminous, its people surrounding it like a bride being given to its noble one, shining for them as they walk in its light, their colors as white as snow, and their fragrance shining like musk, wading through the mountains of camphor, and the two heavy burdens will look at them in amazement as they do not pass through. They will enter Paradise, and no one will mix with them except the muezzins and seekers of reward. In Sunan Ibn Majah, “On the authority of Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Friday to Friday is an expiation for what comes between them, as long as major sins are not committed.’” Narrated by Muslim with the same meaning. On the authority of Aws Al-Thaqafi, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever performs ablution on Friday, bathes, comes early, walks and does not ride, draws close to the imam, listens and does not engage in idle talk, will have for every step the reward of a year of fasting and standing in prayer.” On the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivered a sermon and said: “O people, repent to God before you die. Hasten to do righteous deeds before you become preoccupied. Establish the relationship between you and your Lord by remembering Him often and giving charity in secret and in public. You will be provided for, aided and rewarded. Know that God has enjoined Friday prayer upon you in this place of mine, in this month of mine, in this year of mine, until the Day of Resurrection. Whoever abandons it during my lifetime or after my death and has a just or unjust imam, out of disdain for it or denial of it, God will not bring his family together nor bless his affairs. There is no prayer for him, no zakat for him, no Hajj for him, no fasting for him, and no righteousness for him until he repents. Whoever repents, God will accept his repentance.” No woman should lead a man in prayer, no Bedouin should lead an immigrant in prayer, and no wicked person should lead a believer in prayer unless he is overpowered by a ruler whose sword or whip he fears.” Maymun ibn Abi Shaybah said: I went to the Friday prayer with Al-Hajjaj, so I prepared to go. Then I said: Where should I go and pray behind this wicked man? I hesitated once: Should I go, and once: Don’t go. Then I made up my mind to go, then a caller called to me from the side of the house: O you who believe, when the call is made for the prayer on Friday, then hasten to the remembrance of God and leave business. Seventeenth: The Almighty said: Say, ‘What is with God is better than amusement and trade.’ There are two interpretations: One of them is that what God has of reward for your deeds is better than the pleasure of your amusement and the benefit of your trade. The second is that what God has of your provision which He has apportioned to you is better than what you have obtained from your amusement and trade. Abu Raja’ Al-Attardi recited: “Say, ‘What is with God is better than amusement and trade for those who believe. And God is the Best of Providers.’” That is, He is the Best of providers and provides, so seek from Him and seek help through His obedience to attain what He has of good in this world and the hereafter.
63:1: Surat Al-Munafiqun is a city according to everyone, and it has eleven verses. In the name of God, the most gracious, the most merciful. If the hypocrites come to you, they say, ‘We bear witness that you are the Messenger of God.’ Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Zaid bin Arqam, who said: I was with my uncle and I heard Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salum saying, Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse. He said, If we return to Madinah, the more honorable will surely expel therefrom the more lowly. I mentioned that to my uncle, and my uncle mentioned it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent for Abdullah ibn Ubayy and his companions, and they fabricated what they said. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, believed them and disbelieved me. I was overcome by a worry the like of which had never befallen me, so I sat in my house. Then God, the Exalted, revealed: When the hypocrites come to you - to His saying - They are the ones who say, ‘Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God’ - to His saying - “they will surely expel therefrom the more honorable the more lowly. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent for me and then said, God has confirmed your statement. At-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan saheeh hadith. In At-Tirmidhi, on the authority of Zayd ibn Arqam, he said: We went on an expedition with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and there were some Bedouins with us. We used to go to the water tank and the Bedouins would beat us to it. The Bedouin would beat his companions to the water tank and fill it with stones, placing a mat on it until his companions came. A man from the Ansar came to a Bedouin and let the reins of his camel loose so that she could drink, but he refused to let go. He grabbed a stone and the water subsided. The Bedouin picked up a piece of wood and struck the Ansar on the head, wounding him. Then Abdullah ibn Ubayy, the leader of the hypocrites, who was one of his companions, went and informed him. Abdullah ibn Ubayy became angry and said, “Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) until they disperse from around him” - meaning the Bedouins - and they used to attend the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) for food. Abdullah said, When they disperse from Muhammad, then bring food to Muhammad so that he and those with him can eat. Then he said to his companions, If you return them to Madinah, the more honorable will expel therefrom the more humble. Zayd said: I was riding behind my uncle and I heard Abdullah bin Ubayy, so I informed my uncle. He went and informed the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent for him, but he swore and denied it. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) believed him and called me a liar. My uncle came to me and said: I did not want the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to hate you and call you a liar. I was afflicted by their audacity in a way that no one else had ever been. While I was traveling with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on a journey, my head was heavy with worry, when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to me, stroked my ear, and smiled in my face. I would not have liked to have eternal life because of it. Then Abu Bakr caught up with me and said: What did the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say to you? I said: He did not say anything except that he stroked my ear and smiled in my face. He said: Be of good cheer! Then Umar caught up with me and I said to him the same as I had said to Abu Bakr. When we woke up, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) recited Surat Al-Munafiqun. Abu Isa said: This is a good and authentic hadith. Hudhayfah ibn Al-Yaman was asked about the hypocrite, and he said: He is the one who describes Islam but does not practice it. Today, it is worse than they were during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, because they used to conceal it, but today they reveal it. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Hurairah: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The signs of a hypocrite are three: when he speaks, he lies; when he promises, he breaks his promise; and when he is entrusted, he betrays.” On the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “There are four characteristics, whoever has them is a pure hypocrite, and whoever has one of them has one characteristic of hypocrisy until he gives it up: when he is entrusted, he betrays; when he speaks, he lies; when he makes a promise, he breaks it; and when he disputes, he behaves immorally.” The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) stated that whoever has these characteristics is a hypocrite, and his statements are true. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan that this hadith was mentioned to him and he said: The children of Jacob spoke and lied, they made promises and broke them, they entrusted themselves and betrayed their trust. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said this as a warning to the Muslims, warning them against getting used to these characteristics, fearing that they might lead them to hypocrisy. This does not mean that whoever exhibits these traits unintentionally or habitually is a hypocrite. This has been fully discussed in Surat Bara’ah, and praise be to God. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When a believer speaks, he is truthful. When he promises, he fulfills. When he is entrusted, he fulfills.” Meaning: The perfect believer is truthful when he speaks. And God knows best. God the Almighty said: They said, ‘We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of God.’ It was said that the meaning of we bear witness is we swear. So the oath was expressed by the word testimony, because both the oath and the testimony are confirmations of an unseen matter. From this is the saying of Qays ibn Dharih: I testify before God that I love her, so this is for her with me, and what she has is for me It is possible that this can be taken literally, that they testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), as an acknowledgment of their oaths and a denial of hypocrisy from themselves, and this is more likely. And God knows that you are indeed His Messenger, as they said with their tongues. And God bears witness that the hypocrites are liars, meaning in what they declared of their testimony and oaths with their tongues. Al-Farra’ said: And God bears witness that the hypocrites are liars, in their pronouns. So the denial refers to the pronouns. This indicates that faith is the belief of the heart, and that true speech is the speech of the heart. Whoever says something and believes otherwise is a liar. This meaning has been fully explained at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah. It has also been said that God called them liars in their oaths, as He says, They swear by God that they are of you, but they are not of you.
63:2: God Almighty says: “They have taken their oaths as a cover and have averted [people] from the way of God. Indeed, evil is that which they have been doing.” There are three issues: The first: The Almighty’s statement, They have taken their oaths as a shield, meaning a screen. It does not refer to His statement, We bear witness that you are the Messenger of God, but rather it refers to the reason for the verse that was revealed to him, according to what Al-Bukhari and Al-Tirmidhi mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abi Talib, that he swore what he said and what he said. Al-Dahhal said: He means their oath by God. They are from you. It was said: What is meant by their oaths is what the Lord told us about them in Surat Bara’ah when He said: They swear by God that they did not say it. Second: If someone says, I swear by God, or I bear witness by God, or I vow by God, or I swear by God, or I bear witness by God, or I vow by God, or I swear by God, and says in all of that, By God, then there is no disagreement that it is an oath. Similarly, according to Malik and his companions, if he says, I swear, or I bear witness, or I vow, and does not say, By God, if he means By God. But if he does not mean By God, then it is not an oath. Al-Kiya reported it from Al-Shafi’i. Al-Shafi’i said, If he says, ‘I bear witness by God,’ and intends an oath, then it is an oath. Abu Hanifah and his companions said, “If he says, ‘I bear witness by God, such and such was the case,’ then it is an oath. But if he says, “I bear witness that such and such was the case,” without intending it, then it is an oath, based on this verse, because God mentioned testimony among them, then He said, They took their oaths as a shield. According to Al-Shafi’i, this is not an oath, even if he intended an oath, because God’s statement, They took their oaths as a shield, does not refer to His statement, They said, ‘We bear witness,’ but rather it refers to what is stated in Bara’ah from God’s statement, They swear by God that they did not say. Third: The Almighty’s statement: So they averted men from the way of God means they turned away, which is from the root word sudd turning away. Or they turned the believers away from implementing God’s ruling over them of killing, captivity, and seizing wealth, which is from saddr. Or they prevented people from jihad by staying behind and letting others follow their example. It was also said: They prevented the Jews and polytheists from entering Islam by saying, “Here we are, disbelievers in them. If Muhammad were truly God, He would have known this from us, and He would have made us an example.” So God made it clear that their condition was not hidden from Him, but His ruling is that whoever shows faith, He applies to him outwardly the ruling of faith. Indeed, evil were what they did meaning evil were their evil deeds - their hypocrisy, false oaths, and their truthfulness about the way of God.
63:3: God Almighty says: That is because they believed and then disbelieved, so their hearts were sealed, so they do not understand. This is a notification from God Almighty that the hypocrite is a disbeliever. That is, they acknowledged it with their tongues but disbelieved in their hearts. It was also said that the verse was revealed about a people who believed then apostatized. So He sealed their hearts means He sealed them with disbelief. So they do not understand faith or good. Zayd ibn Ali recited So God sealed their hearts.
63:4: God Almighty says: “And when you see them, their bodies impress you. And if they speak, you listen to their speech. They are as if they were wooden props propped up. They think that every shout is against them. They are the enemy, so beware of them. May God destroy them. How are they deluded?” His statement, And when you see them, their bodies impress you, meaning their forms and appearances. And if they speak, you listen to their speech, meaning Abdullah ibn Ubayy. Ibn Abbas said: Abdullah ibn Ubayy was handsome, well-built, and had a smooth tongue. When he spoke, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard his speech. God described him as having a perfect appearance and excellent eloquence. Al-Kalbi said: What is meant are Ibn Ubayy, Jad ibn Qays, and Mu’tab ibn Qushayr. They had bodies, appearances, and eloquence. In Sahih Muslim: And His statement, As if they were propped up pieces of wood, means: They were men of the most beautiful kind, as if they were propped up pieces of wood. He likened them to pieces of wood propped up against a wall, they neither hear nor understand, ghosts without souls and bodies without dreams. It was said that he likened them to pieces of wood that have decayed and are propped up by something else, and it is not known what is inside them. Fanbul, Abu Amr, and Al-Kisa’i read khashab with a sukoon on the sheen. This is the reading of Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib and the choice of Abu ‘Ubayd, because its singular is khashbah. As you say: badana badan and badan badan, and in the language there is no fa’ala that has the plural of fa’l fa’l. And its heaviness requires that you say: badan badan, so you read wa-al-badan wa-al-badan. Al-Yazidi mentioned that it is the plural of khashba’, like the Almighty’s saying: And gardens of thick clouds and one of them is ghalba’ garden. The rest read it with emphasis and this is the narration of Al-Bazzi from Ibn Kathir and Ayyash from Abu Amr, and most of the narrations are from Asim. Abu Hatim chose it, as if it is the plural of khashba’ and khashba’, like thamarah fruits and thamarah fruits and thamarah. If you wish, you can pluralize khashba’ as khashba’ as they say: badana badan and badan and badan. It has been narrated from Ibn Al-Musayyab that the kha’ and shin are opened in khashba’. Sibawayh said: khashba wooden and khashba’, like badana badan and badan. He said: And similar to it without the ha’ are asad lion and asad lion, wathan wicken and wathan. And khashba’ is read as plural of plural, khashba wooden and khashba’ and khashba’, like thamarah fruits and thamarah fruits. The root word is Isnad which means I inclined to something. I inclined is used to express abundance, meaning they relied on oaths to spare their blood. God the Almighty says: They think that every shout against them is the enemy. That is, every person who shouts against them is the enemy. So they are the enemy is the second object, although there is no pronoun in the sentence. He describes them as cowardly and weak. Muqatil and Al-Suddi said: That is, a crier calls out in the army that an animal has escaped or a lost animal has been reported, and they think that they are the ones meant, because of the fear in their hearts. As the poet Al-Akhtal said: You still consider everything after them to be horses charging at them and men It was said: “They think that every shout is against them. They are the enemy.” The pronoun in it does not need what follows, and its meaning is: They think that every shout is against them, that they have been warned about them and known of their hypocrisy, because suspicion brings fear. Then God resumed addressing His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: They are the enemy. This is the meaning of Ad-Dahhak’s statement. It was also said: They think that every shout they hear in the mosque is against them, and that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, has ordered their killing. They are always fearful that God will send down a command concerning them that will permit their blood to be shed and their veils to be torn. In this sense, the poet said: If she were a bird, I would have imprisoned her, poisoned, calling for slaves and sinners. A clan of Banu Yarbu'. Then God described them, saying: They are the enemy, so beware of them. Narrated by Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim. His statement, So beware of them, has two meanings: The first is: Beware of trusting what they say or leaning toward their speech. The second is: Beware of their leaning toward your enemies and their abandoning your companions. May God fight them means may God curse them, as stated by Ibn Abbas and Abu Malik. It is a word of blame and rebuke. The Arabs sometimes say, May God fight him, how he feels! They put it in the place of amazement. It was also said that the meaning of May God fight them is that He put them in the place of the one who fought him, a conquering enemy, because God Almighty conquers every stubborn person. Narrated by Ibn 'Ees. How they lie means they lie, as Ibn Abbas said. Qatada said: It means they deviate from the truth. Al-Hasan: It means they are diverted from the right path. It was also said that it means how their minds could go astray from this when the evidence is clear. It is from the word ifk which means diversion. And ani means how, and it has been mentioned before.
63:5: God the Almighty said: And when it is said to them, ‘Come, that the Messenger of God may ask forgiveness for you,’ When the Quran was revealed about them, their clans went to them and said, You have been disgraced by hypocrisy, so repent to the Messenger of God from hypocrisy and ask him to ask forgiveness for you. They turned their heads in mockery and disdain, as Ibn Abbas said. It was narrated from him that Abdullah ibn Ubayy used to take a stand regarding every cause that encouraged obedience to God and His Messenger, and it was said to him, “What good will that do you while the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) is angry with you? Go to him so he may ask forgiveness for you.” He refused and said, I will not go to him. The reason for the revelation of these verses. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) raided Banu al-Mustaliq at a watering place called al-Marisi' in the direction of Qudayd towards the coast. A hired servant of Umar's called Jahjah and an ally of Abdullah ibn Ubayy called Sinan rushed towards a watering place in al-Mushall. Jahjah shouted for the Muhajirun and Sinan shouted for the Ansar. Jahjah slapped Sinan, and Abdullah ibn Ubayy said, "Light a fire, they did it!" By God, our situation and their situation are as the first one said: "Fatten your dog and it will eat you." By God, if we return to Madinah, the most humiliated one - meaning Ubayy - will surely come out, meaning Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him). Then he said to his people, "Refrain from this man's food and do not spend on those who are with him until they disperse and leave him. Zayd ibn Arqam - who was one of Abdullah's relatives - said, By God, you are the humiliated one among your people, while Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) is honored by the Most Merciful and protected by the Muslims. By God, I will never love you after what you have said. Abdullah said, Shut up, I was just joking." Zaid informed the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) of what he had said, and he swore by God that he had neither done nor said it. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) excused him. Zaid said: “I felt this in myself, but the people did not like me. So Surat Al-Munafiqun was revealed confirming Zaid’s statement and denial of Abdullah. It was said to Abdullah: ‘Severe verses have been revealed concerning you, so go to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) so that he may ask for forgiveness for you.’ He nodded his head, and the verses were revealed.” [Narrated by Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and At-Tirmidhi with a similar meaning. The beginning of the Surah has already been mentioned.] It was also said: He asks forgiveness for you means that he will repent to you from hypocrisy, because repentance is asking for forgiveness. "I saw them turning away while they were arrogant." That is, they turned away from the Messenger, arrogant about believing. Nafi` read lawwa with a light pronunciation. The rest stressed it, and Abu Ubaid chose it and said: It is a verb of the group of Al-Nahhas. He made a mistake in this, because it was revealed about Abdullah bin Ubayy when he was told: Come, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, will ask forgiveness for you. He shook his head in mockery. If it is said: How do I report it with the action of the group? It is said to him: The Arabs do this when it is about a person. Sibawaba recited to Hassan: You thought that what you did could be hidden, while among us there is a Messenger who has the revelation and who brings it forth. Hassan Ibn Al-Abairaq was approached about something he had stolen in Mecca. His case is well-known. It may be permissible to tell about him and about the one who did what he did. It was said: Ibn Abi said when he turned his head, You ordered me to believe or to give only the zakat of my money. I have been given, so all that remains is for me to prostrate to Muhammad!
63:6: The Almighty says: It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them. This means that all of that is the same; your asking forgiveness will not benefit them at all, as God will not forgive them. Similar to this is: It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe. "It is the same for us whether you admonish them or are not among the admonishers." This has already been mentioned. "Indeed, God does not guide the defiantly disobedient people." This means that whoever God knows will die as a defiantly disobedient person.
63:7: God Almighty says: “They are the ones who say, ‘Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse.’ And to God belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth, but the hypocrites do not understand.” We mentioned the reason for revelation above. Ibn Abi said: Do not spend on those who are with Muhammad until they disperse, until they leave him. So God, the Exalted, informed them that the treasures of the heavens and the earth belong to Him, and He spends as He wishes. A man said to Hatim al-Asamm: Where do you eat from? He said: To God belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth. Al-Junayd said: The treasures of the heavens are the unseen, and the treasures of the earth are the hearts, for He is the Knower of the unseen and the Changer of hearts. It is as if al-Shalabi is saying: To God belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth, so where will you go? But the hypocrites do not understand, that when He wants something, He makes it easy.
63:8: God Almighty says: They say, ‘If we return to Medina, the more honorable will surely expel therefrom the more humble.’ But honor belongs to God and to His Messenger and to the believers, but the hypocrites do not know. The speaker is Ibn Abi, as mentioned above. It was said that when he said: The more honorable will expel the more humble from it. He returned to Madinah and did not stay for more than a few days until he died. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) asked forgiveness for him and dressed him in his shirt. Then this verse was revealed: God will never forgive them. All of this has been fully explained in Surah Bara’ah. It was narrated that Abdullah bin Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul said to his father: “By the One besides whom there is no god, you will not enter Madinah until you say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is the most arrogant and I am the most humiliated.” He said: They thought that honor lies in the abundance of wealth and followers, but God made it clear that honor, pleasure and power belong to God.
63:9: God Almighty says: “O you who have believed, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of God. And whoever does that - then it is those who are the losers.” Warning the believers of the behavior of the hypocrites, that is, do not be preoccupied with your wealth as the hypocrites did when they said - out of miserliness with their wealth -: Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God. From the remembrance of God meaning from Hajj and Zakat. It was also said: From reading the Quran. It was also said: From constantly remembering God. It was also said: From the five daily prayers, as Ad-Dahhak said. Al-Hasan said: All the obligatory prayers, as if he said: From obeying God. It was also said: This is addressed to the hypocrites, that is, you have believed in words, so believe in your heart. And whoever does that meaning whoever is preoccupied with wealth and children from obeying his Lord, then it is those who are the losers.
63:10: It contains four issues: First: His statement, Spend from what We have provided for you before death comes to any of you, indicates the obligation to pay zakat promptly, and it is not permissible to delay it at all. The same applies to all other acts of worship when their time is specified. Second: The Almighty said: He will say, ‘My Lord, if only You would delay me for a short term so I could give charity and be among the righteous.’ He asked to return to this world so that he could do righteous deeds. At-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak ibn Muzahim on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Whoever has wealth sufficient to perform Hajj to the House of his Lord or on which Zakat is due, but he does not do so, may ask to return upon death. A man said: O Ibn Abbas, fear God, only the disbelievers asked to return. He said: I will recite to you the Quran about that. He said: What necessitates Zakat? He said: If one’s wealth reaches two hundred or more. He said: What necessitates Hajj? He said: Provisions and rest. I said: Al-Halimi Abu Abdullah Al-Hussein bin Al-Hassan mentioned it in the book Minhaaj Al-Din with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said: And Ibn Abbas said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever has enough money to perform Hajj… He then mentioned the hadith. Its wording was previously mentioned in Al Imran. Third: Ibn al-Arabi said: Ibn Abbas took the generality of the verse to mean obligatory spending specifically without any transmission. As for its interpretation as zakat, it is all correct in general and its estimate is two hundred. As for the statement about Hajj, there is a problem with it, because if we say that Hajj is to be delayed, then in the case of disobedience in death before the disagreement among scholars, then the verse does not apply to this. If we say that Hajj is to be performed immediately, then the verse is correct in general, because whoever is required to perform Hajj and does not perform it will meet with God what he would wish he had returned to perform it. Ibn Abbas’s statement has no bearing on it, because returning and the Eid are not included in the issues of ijtihad or disagreement, but rather they are included in what is agreed upon. The correct view is that it includes obligatory spending, however it is disposed of, by consensus or by the text of the Qur’an, because what is other than that does not reach the implementation of the threat. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: Lawla means why not, so it is a question. It was also said: There is no connection, so the statement has the meaning of a wish. So, we can more accurately answer the wish with fa. And I was in apposition to I believe and this is the reading of Abu Amr, Ibn Muhaisin and Mujahid. The rest read it in the jussive mood as an apposition to the position of fa, because if it were not for fa, it would have been in the jussive mood, meaning I believe. Similar to it is the verse: He whom God sends astray, there is no guide for him, and He leaves them for those who are in the jussive mood. Ibn Abbas said: This verse is more difficult for the people of monotheism, because no one who has goodness with God in the hereafter would wish to return to this world or to be delayed in it.
63:11: I said: Except for the martyr, for he wishes to return until he is killed, because of the honor he sees. And God is Aware of what you do of good and evil. The general reading is with the ta’ as addressing the speaker. Abu Bakr, on the authority of Asim and As-Salami, read with the ya’ as reporting someone who died and said this statement. The Surah has been completed, thanks be to God and with His help.
64:1: A city according to the majority. Ad-Dahhak said: It was in Mecca. Al-Kalbi said: It is both Meccan and Medinan. It has eighteen verses. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, Surah At-Taghabun was revealed in Mecca, except for some verses at the end, which were revealed in Medina about Awf ibn Malik Al-Ashja’i. He complained to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the coldness of his family and children, so God, the Almighty, revealed: O you who have believed, indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them until the end of the Surah. On the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No child is born except that on the temples of his head are written five verses from the opening of Surat Al-Ghabin. In the name of God, the most gracious, the most merciful “Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth exalts God. His is the kingdom and His is the praise. And He is over all things competent.” Advance in more than one place.
64:2: God Almighty says: “It is He who created you, and among you are disbelievers and among you are believers. And God is Seeing of what you do.” Ibn Abbas said: God created believers and unbelievers among Adam, and He will return them on the Day of Resurrection as believers and unbelievers. Abu Saeed Al-Khudri narrated that he said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) delivered a sermon to us one evening and mentioned something that would happen, saying: “People are born into different classes. A man is born a believer, lives as a believer and dies a believer. A man is born a disbeliever, lives as a disbeliever and dies a disbeliever. A man is born a believer, lives as a believer and dies a disbeliever. A man is born a disbeliever, lives as a disbeliever and dies a believer.” Ibn Mas`ud said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God created Pharaoh in his mother’s womb as an unbeliever, and He created John, son of Zechariah, in his mother’s womb as a believer. And in the Sahih from the hadith of Ibn Masoud: “And one of you may do the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is only a cubit or a fathom between him and it, then what has been written will overtake him and he will do the deeds of the people of the Fire and enter it. And one of you may do the deeds of the people of the Fire until there is only a cubit or a fathom between him and it, then what has been written will overtake him and he will do the deeds of the people of Paradise and enter it.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Al-Tirmidhi, but it does not mention the cubit. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa’d Al-Sa’idi: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “A man may do what appears to people as the deeds of the people of Paradise, but he is one of the people of Hellfire. A man may do what appears to people as the deeds of the people of Hellfire, but he is one of the people of Paradise.” Our scholars said: The meaning is that Eternal Knowledge is attached to everything known, so what is known happens and disbelief is intended. It was said that something was omitted in the statement: Among you is a believer, and among you is a disbeliever, and among you is a sinner. This was omitted because the statement indicates this, as al-Hasan said. Others said: There is no omission in it, because the purpose is to mention both sides. A group of scholars said: God created creation, then they disbelieved and believed. They said: The completion of the statement is He is the One who created you. Then He described them, saying: Among you is a disbeliever, and among you is a believer. They cited as evidence the statement of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him): Every child is born in a state of fitrah natural disposition, but his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Zoroastrian. Hadith. And we have already discussed the Romans in detail. Ad-Dahhak said: “Some of you are disbelievers in secret but believers in public, like the hypocrite. Some of you are believers in secret but disbelievers in public, like Ammar and his family.” Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah said: Some of you are disbelievers in God but believers in the stars, and some of you are believers in God but disbelievers in the stars, meaning in the matter of lights. Az-Zajjaj said – and this is the best of the sayings, and the one that the imams and the majority of the ummah agree upon – “God created the disbeliever, and his disbelief is an action and an acquisition, even though God is the Creator of disbelief. And He created the believer, and his faith is an action and an acquisition, even though God is the Creator of faith. And the disbeliever disbelieves and chooses disbelief after God created him, because God, the Most High, has decreed that for him and knows about him. It is not permissible for either of them to exist other than what He has decreed for him and knows about him, because the existence of something contrary to what is decreed is inability, and the existence of something contrary to what is known is ignorance, and neither is befitting of God, the Most High. In this there is freedom from compulsion and predestination, as the poet said: O you who look into religion, the matter is neither fate nor compensation. Silan said: A Bedouin came to Basra and was asked: What do you say about predestination? He said: It is a matter about which suspicions have gone too far, and about which those who differ have differed. So it is necessary that we refer whatever is unclear to us about its ruling to what we previously knew about it.
64:3: God Almighty says: He created the heavens and the earth in truth and formed you and perfected your forms, and to Him is the final destination. God the Almighty said: He created the heavens and the earth in truth. This has been mentioned in more than one place, meaning He created them truly, certainly, without doubt. It has also been said that the preposition ba has the same meaning as the preposition lam, meaning He created them for the sake of truth, which is to reward those who do evil for what they have done and to reward those who do good with good. And He shaped you and perfected your forms means Adam, peace be upon him. He created him with His own hand as an honor to him, said Muqatil. The second: all creation. The meaning of sculpting has already been mentioned, that it is planning and shaping. If it is said: How did He perfect their forms? It is said: He made them the best of their forms. It is said: He made them the best of all animals and the most beautiful in form, as evidence that man does not wish for his form to be different from what he sees of other forms. Part of the beauty of His form is that He created him upright, not bent over, as God the Almighty said: Indeed, We created man in the best of stature, as will be explained, God willing. And to Him is the final destination, meaning the return, so He rewards each one according to his deeds.
64:4: God Almighty says: “He knows what is in the heavens and the earth, and He knows what you conceal and what you declare. And God is Knowing of that within the breasts.” It has been mentioned in more than one place. He is the Knower of the unseen and the seen, nothing is hidden from Him.
64:5: God Almighty says: Has there not come to you the report of those who disbelieved before? They tasted the consequences of their deed, and for them is a painful punishment. The address is to the Quraysh. Didn't you hear the report of the disbelievers of the past nations? So they tasted the consequences of their deed meaning they were punished. And for them in the Hereafter is a painful punishment meaning a place of return. This has been mentioned previously.
64:6: God Almighty says: “That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, but they said, ‘Shall human beings guide us?’ So they disbelieved and turned away, and God was free of need. And God is free of need and Praiseworthy.” God the Almighty says: {That} meaning this punishment is for them because they disbelieved in the messengers who came to them. {With clear proofs} meaning with clear evidence. {They said, Is it a human being who guides us?} They denied that the Messenger was a human being. {Abshar} was raised as a subject. It was also said that it is with an implied verb, and the plural means human beings. This is why He said: {They guide us} and did not say: {He guides us}. The singular may also have the meaning of the plural, so it is a generic noun. The singular of human beings does not have a singular in the verbal sense. The plural may also have the meaning of the singular, as in His statement: {This is not a human being}. {So they disbelieved} meaning in this statement, because they said it out of belittlement and did not know that God sends whomever He wills to His servants. It was also said that they disbelieved in the messengers and turned away from the proof, and turned away from faith and admonition. {And God is independent of} meaning His authority, so is independent of the obedience of His servants, as stated by Muqatil. It was also said that God is independent of any further additions that call to right guidance and lead to righteousness by what He showed them of proof and made clear to them.
64:7: God Almighty says: “Those who disbelieve claim that they will never be resurrected. Say, ‘Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected, then you will surely be informed of what you did. And that, for God, is easy.’” God the Almighty says: Those who disbelieve claim that they will never be resurrected. That is, they assumed. To assume is to say something based on conjecture. Shuraih said: Everything has a nickname, and the nickname of lying is they assumed. It was said that it was revealed about Al-Aas ibn Wa’il as-Sahmi and Khabbab, as was explained at the end of Surah Maryam. It includes every disbeliever. Say, O Muhammad, Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected. That is, you will come out of your graves alive. Then you will surely be informed. “What you did” that is, your deeds. And that, for God, is easy, as repeating is easier than starting over.
64:8: God Almighty says: “So believe in God and His Messenger and the light which We have sent down. And God is Acquainted with what you do.” God Almighty said: So believe in God and His Messenger. He commanded them to believe after He made them aware of the coming of the Hour. And the light which We have sent down, which is the Qur’an, is a light that guides people from the darkness of misguidance. And God is Acquainted with what you do.
64:9: God Almighty says: “The Day He will assemble you for the Day of Assembly. That will be the Day of Mutual Loss. And whoever believes in God and does righteousness - He will remove from him his misdeeds and admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. That is the great attainment.” There are three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: The Day He will gather you for the Day of Assembly. The agent in the Day you will surely be informed or the Knower because of the meaning of threat in it, as if he said: And God will punish you on the Day He will gather you. Or by implying remember and ghubn means deficiency. It is said: ghabbanahu if something is taken from him without its value. The common people read it as ya’a with ya’, because the Almighty said: And God is Knowing of what you do, so He informed. And because the name of God was mentioned first. Nasr, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Al-Jahdary, Yaqoub, and Salam read it with a noon, considering the statement: And the light which We have sent down. The Day of Assembly: The day when God will assemble the first and the last, mankind and the jinn, the people of the heavens and the people of the earth. It was said: It is the day when God will assemble every servant and his deeds. It was said: Because He will assemble the oppressor and the oppressed on that day. It was said: Because He will assemble every prophet and his nation on that day. It was said: Because He will assemble the reward of the people of obedience and the punishment of the people of disobedience on that day. That is the Day of Mutual Loss, meaning the Day of Resurrection. He said: I do not expect to live in a house of separation, but rather I expect comfort on the Day of Loss. The Day of Resurrection is called the Day of Loss Al-Taghabun because on that day the people of Paradise will be defrauded by the people of Hellfire. That is, the people of Paradise will take Paradise and the people of Hellfire will take Hellfire in exchange. Thus, the defrauding occurred because of their exchange of good for evil, good for bad, and bliss for torment. It is said, You defrauded someone if you sold or bought something from him, so the loss was his and you were victorious. The same applies to the people of Paradise and the people of Hellfire, as will be explained. It is also said, You defrauded the garment or You cheated it if it was too long for you and you took some of it. This is also a loss. What is defrauded is the loss of one’s family and their status in Paradise. On that day, the loss of every disbeliever due to abandoning faith will be made clear, and so will the loss of every believer due to their shortcomings in doing good and wasting their days. Al-Zajjaj said, And the one whose status is higher in Paradise will be defrauded by the one whose status is lower than his. Second: If it is said: What kind of transaction took place between them that would cause fraud? It is said: It is the representation of fraud in buying and selling, as God the Almighty said: Those are the ones who have purchased error in exchange for guidance. And when He mentioned that the disbelievers purchased error in exchange for guidance and did not profit from their trade but rather lost, He also mentioned that they were fraudulent, and that is because the people of Paradise purchased the Hereafter by abandoning this world, and the people of Hell purchased this world by abandoning the Hereafter. This is a type of exchange, both broadly and metaphorically. God the Almighty has divided creation into two groups: a group for Paradise and a group for Hell. And the dwellings of all are assigned in Paradise and Hell. For a servant to be forsaken may precede him - as we have explained in this surah and others - and he may be among the people of Hellfire. Thus, the one who is guided will be in the place of the forsaken, and the place of the one who is guided will be in Hellfire because of the forsaken. Thus, an exchange has taken place, and so there has been loss. Examples are used to explain the rules of language and the Qur’an. All of this is collected from the publication of the narrations and they have been mentioned separately in this book. This exchange may be mentioned through inheritance, as we have explained in Indeed, the believers have succeeded. And God knows best. And loss may take place on a day other than that day, as will be explained later. But what he meant is loss for which there is no remedy. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: It has come to our attention that loss is of three types: A man who acquired knowledge, then neglected it and did not act upon it, thus becoming miserable because of it; a man who acquired wealth in ways that he was asked about, but was stingy with it, and was negligent in obeying his Lord because of it, and did not do any good with it; and he left it to an heir who would not be held accountable for it, so that he acted upon it out of obedience to his Lord. A man had a slave who obeyed his Lord and was happy, but his master disobeyed his Lord and was miserable. It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: On the Day of Resurrection, God the Almighty will place a man and a woman before Him, and He will say to them, What will you say? The man will say, “O Lord, You made her maintenance obligatory upon me, but I spent it unfairly, both lawfully and unlawfully. These opponents are demanding that, and I have nothing left to pay.” The woman will say, “O Lord, what could I possibly say? I earned it unlawfully, ate it lawfully, and disobeyed You in pleasing You, and I was not pleased with that for him. So far from him and crushed.” God the Almighty will say, You have spoken the truth. Then she will be commanded to enter Paradise, and she will look at him from the levels of Paradise and say, “We have cheated you, we have cheated you. We are happy with what you suffered.” That is the Day of Loss. Third: Ibn al-Arabi said: Our scholars used the verse: That is the Day of Mutual Loss as evidence that it is not permissible to cheat in worldly transactions, because God, the Most High, specified the Day of Resurrection for the crime of cheating, saying: In a sale, it is returned if it exceeds one-third. The people of Baghdad preferred this view and presented evidence for it with various aspects, including the statement of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) to Hubban ibn Munqidh: When you make a sale, say, ‘No deception,’ and you have the option to choose three times. This has a long consideration which we have explained in the issues of disagreement. The gist of it is that fraud in this world is forbidden by consensus in the ruling of religion, as it is a type of deception forbidden by the Sharia in every religion, but a small amount of it cannot be guarded against by anyone, so it has been applied in sales, as if we were to protect it by rejecting it, no sale would ever be valid, because it is not free from it, until if It was a lot that could be guarded against, so it was obligatory to respond to it. The difference between a little and a lot is a well-known principle in the Sharia. Our scholars set a third for this limit, as they saw it in a will and other things. The meaning of the verse according to this is: That is the Day of Loss, which is absolutely permissible without detail, or that is the Day of Loss that can never be made up for, because worldly loss can be made up for in two ways: either by returning it in some cases, or by a profit in another sale and another commodity. As for the one who loses Paradise, he will never attain it. Some Sufi scholars have said: God has decreed loss upon all of creation, so no one meets his Lord except as a loser, because he cannot complete his work until he obtains the full reward. And in the hadith: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No one meets God except in a state of sleep, whether he has done wrong or not done well, or in a state of sleep, whether he has done good or not done better. God Almighty says: And whoever believes in God and does righteousness - He will remove from him his misdeeds and admit him to Gardens. Nafi’ and Ibn ‘Amir read them with a nun in both, while the rest read them with a ya.
64:10: God Almighty says: And those who disbelieve and deny Our verses - those are the companions of the Fire, abiding eternally therein, and wretched is the destination. God Almighty says: And those who disbelieved and denied Our verses meaning the Qur’an they are the companions of the Fire, abiding eternally therein, and wretched is the destination. When He mentioned what is for the believers, He mentioned what is for the disbelievers, as mentioned previously in more than one place.
64:11: The Almighty says: No disaster strikes except by God's permission meaning by His will and decree. Al-Farra' said: He means except by God's command. It was also said: except by God's knowledge. It was also said: The reason for its revelation was that the disbelievers said: If what the Muslims are doing was true, God would have protected them from disasters in this world. So God the Almighty made it clear that whatever disaster befalls a person, wealth, word or deed, causes concern or necessitates a punishment, sooner or later, God and His decree know. God Almighty says: And whoever believes in God meaning he believes and knows that no calamity befalls him except by God’s permission. He guides his heart to patience and contentment. It was said: It makes him steadfast in faith. Abu Uthman Al-Jizi said: Whoever's faith is sound, God guides his heart to follow the Sunnah. It was also said: And whoever believes in God, He guides his heart when afflicted, so he says: Indeed we belong to God and to Him we shall return, said Ibn Jubayr. Ibn Abdus said: It is that God places certainty in his heart so that he knows that what befell him could not have missed him, and that what missed him could not have befallen him. Al-Kalbi said: When he is tested, he is patient, when he is blessed, he is grateful, and when he is wronged, he forgives. It was also said: He guides his heart to attain reward in Paradise. The common reading is yahid with a fatha on the ya' and a kasra on the dal, because the name of God is mentioned first. As-Sulami and Qatadah read yahid qalbihu with a damma on the ya' and a fatha on the dal, indicating a passive verb and raising the ba' because it is a verb with no named agent. Talhah ibn Musarraf and Al-A'raj read nahd with a noon to emphasize his heart in the accusative case. Ikrimah read yuḍāḍa qalbihu with a silent hamza and raising the ba', meaning he calms down and is reassured. Malik ibn Dinar read it similarly, except that he softened the hamza. And God is Knowing of all things. The submission of one who submits and surrenders to His command, nor the dislike of one who dislikes it, is not hidden from Him.
64:12: That is, make the calamities easy for yourselves, and be engrossed in obeying God, and act in accordance with His Book, and obey the Messenger in acting in accordance with his Sunnah. If you turn away from obedience, then the Messenger has no duty except to convey.
64:13: God, there is no god but Him meaning there is no god but Him, and no creator but Him, so put your trust in Him.
64:14: It contains five issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them. Ibn Abbas said: This verse was revealed in Medina about Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja’i. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) complained about the coldness of his family and children, so it was revealed. An-Nahhas mentioned it. At-Tabari narrated it on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar, who said: The entirety of Surat At-Taghabun was revealed in Mecca except for these verses: It was revealed about Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja’i. He had a family and children, and whenever he wanted to go out for a military expedition, they would weep for him and show compassion to him, saying: To whom are you leaving us? He would take compassion and stay. So the entire verse was revealed in Medina about Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja’i. The rest of the verses to the end of the Surah are in Medina. Al-Tirmidhi narrated: On the authority of Ibn Abbas - and a man asked him about this verse - he said: These are men from Mecca who converted to Islam and wanted to come to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, but your wives and children refused to let them come to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. When they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, they saw that the people had understood the religion and they intended to punish them, so God Almighty revealed the verse. This is a good and authentic hadith. Second: Judge Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi said: This clarifies the nature of enmity, for the enemy does not lie in wait as an enemy in and of himself, but rather he is an enemy through his actions. So if the husband or child does the action of the enemy, then he is an enemy, and there is no action uglier than standing between the servant and obedience. In Sahih al-Bukhari, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah: On the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, he said: “Indeed, Satan sat for Adam on the path of faith and said to him, ‘Will you believe and abandon your religion and the religion of your fathers?’ He opposed him and believed. Then he sat for him on the path of emigration and said to him, ‘Will you emigrate and leave your wealth and your family?’ He opposed him and emigrated. Then he sat for him on the path of jihad and said, ‘Will you engage in jihad, killing yourself, marrying your women, and dividing your wealth?’ He opposed him and fought jihad and was killed, so it is incumbent upon God to admit him to Paradise.” Satan's presence is of two types: One of them is through whispering. The second is by forcing him to do what he wants from his wife, children and companions. God the Almighty said: And We appointed for them companions who made attractive to them what was before them and what was behind them. In the wisdom of Jesus, peace be upon him: Whoever takes a wife, wealth and children will be a slave to the world. In the authentic hadith, there is a statement of a lower status than that of the slave: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Cursed is the slave of the dirham, cursed is the slave of the fine silk, cursed is the slave of the velvet, cursed and upside down, and if he is tested, let him not puff up. There is no greater baseness than the worship of the dinar and the dirham, and no ambition is more base than the ambition that is raised by wearing a new garment. Third: Just as a man can have his wife and son as enemies, so too can a woman have her husband and child as enemies in this exact sense. The generality of His statement, of your wives, includes both males and females, as they are both included in every verse. And God knows best. Fourth: The Almighty's statement, So beware of them, means beware of yourselves. Beingware of oneself can be of two types: either due to bodily harm or religious harm. Bodily harm relates to this world, while religious harm relates to the afterlife. So, God, the Almighty, warns His servant against this and cautions him against it. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: But if you pardon and overlook and forgive - then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. At-Tabari narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding the Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them. He said: “A man wanted to go to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his family would say to him: ‘Where are you going and leaving us?’ He said: When he converted to Islam and was guided, he said: ‘I will surely go back to those who forbade this matter, and I will do this and that.’ So God, the Almighty, revealed: “But if you pardon and overlook and forgive - then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.” Mujahid said regarding the Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them. He said: They were not enemies to them in this world, but their love for them led them to take from them what is forbidden, so they gave it to them. The verse is general and applies to every sin that a person commits because of family and children. A specific reason does not prevent a general ruling.
64:15: The Almighty said: Your wealth and your children are but a trial meaning a trial and a test that will push you to earn what is forbidden and prevent the right of God Almighty, so do not give them in disobedience to God. In a hadith: A man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and it will be said, 'His children have eaten his good deeds.' Some of the early Muslims said that children are the worms of acts of obedience. Al-Qutbi said: A trial means infatuation. It is said that a man is tempted by a woman, meaning he is infatuated with her. It is also said that a trial is a test. From this is the saying of the poet: He has tempted people in their religion and left Ibn Affan with a long history of evil. Ibn Mas'ud said: "Let none of you say: 'O God, protect me from temptation,' for none of you returns to his wealth, family, or children except that he is encompassed by temptation. Rather, let him say: 'O God, I seek refuge in You from the misleading temptations.'" Al-Hasan said about the verse: Indeed, among your wives al-Baqarah 2:176: He included min for partiality because not all of them are enemies. He did not mention min in the verse: Your wealth and your children are but a trial, because they are not free from temptation and the heart being inflamed by them. Al-Tirmidhi and others narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Buraydah on the authority of his father who said: "I saw the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) delivering a sermon, and al-Hasan and al-Husayn (peace be upon them) came, wearing red shirts, walking and stumbling. He carried them and placed them in front of him, then said: 'God has spoken the truth. Your wealth and children are but a trial.' I looked at these two boys walking and stumbling, and I could not wait until I cut short my speech and picked them up. Then he began his sermon." And God has with Him a great reward meaning Paradise, for it is the ultimate goal, and there is no reward greater than it according to the commentators. In the two Sahihs - and the wording is from Bukhari - on the authority of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "God will say to the people of Paradise, and they will say: Here I am, our Lord, and at Your pleasure. He will say: Are you satisfied? They will say: Why should we not be satisfied when You have given us what You have not given to any of Your creation? He will say: Except that I will give you better than that. They will say: O Lord, what is better than that? He will say: I will bestow My pleasure upon you, and I will never be displeased with you after that." This has already been mentioned. There is no doubt that contentment is the ultimate goal. The Sufis chanted in confirmation of this: God tested His creation with it, so Hell and Paradise are in His grasp. His abandonment is greater than his fire, and his connection is better than his paradise.
64:16: God Almighty says: So fear God as much as you are able, and listen and obey, and spend [in charity] for the good of your souls. There are five issues: First: A group of interpreters said that this verse abrogates the Almighty’s saying: Fear God as He should be feared (Al Imran 3:102). Among them are Qatada, Al Rabi’ bin Anas, Al Suddī, and Ibn Zayd. At-Tabari mentioned: Yunus bin Abdul-A'la told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said about the verse: O you who have believed, fear God as He should be feared, he said: A severe matter came, they said: Who knows the extent of this or can reach it? When God knew that it had become severe for them, He abrogated it from them and brought this other verse, saying: So fear God as much as you are able. It was said: It is a definitive verse with no abrogation in it. Ibn Abbas said: The verse: Fear God as He should be feared, it was not abrogated, but the right to fear Him is to strive for God as He should be striven for, and not to be deterred by the blame of a blamer in God's cause, and to stand up for God with justice even if it is against yourselves, your fathers, and your children. This has been mentioned before. Second: If it is said: If this verse is definitive and not abrogated, then what is the point of His statement in Surat al-Taghabun 64:So fear God as much as you are able, and how is it possible to combine the command to fear God as He should be feared with the command to fear Him as much as we are able? The command to fear Him as He should be feared is an obligation of the Qur’an without specificity or connection to a condition, while the command to fear Him as much as we are able is a command to fear Him connected to a condition. It is said to him: His statement: So fear God as much as you are able is separate from what is indicated by His statement: Fear God as He should be feared. Rather, what He meant by His statement: So fear God as much as you are able is that you should fear God, O people, and be mindful of what He has made a trial for you regarding your wealth and children, lest their trial reach them and turn you away from what God has obligated you to do, which is to emigrate from the land of disbelief to the land of Islam, so you abandon emigration as much as you are able, meaning while you are able to emigrate. This is because God, the Most High, has excused those who are unable to emigrate by abandoning it, as He, the Most High, says: Indeed, those whom the angels take while they are wronging themselves - until His saying - It is those whom God may pardon (An-Nisa’: 99). So He informed that He has pardoned those who are unable to find a plan or a way by residing in the land of polytheism. Likewise, the meaning of His saying: So fear God as much as you are able in emigrating from the land of polytheism to the land of Islam is that you leave it with the temptation of your wealth and children. What indicates the correctness of this is that His saying: So fear God as much as you are able follows His saying: O you who have believed, indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them. There is no disagreement among the early scholars of Quranic interpretation that these verses were revealed because of a group of disbelieving people who delayed migrating from the land of polytheism to the land of Islam because their children discouraged them from doing so, as mentioned above. This is all the opinion of al-Tabari. It was said: So fear God as much as you are able in what they volunteered of voluntary acts or charity. When the verse So fear God as He should be feared was revealed, the people were hard pressed and stood until their heels became swollen and their foreheads became ulcerated. Then God revealed to them an alleviation: So fear God as much as you are able, thus abrogating the first verse, as Ibn Jubayr said. Al-Marudi said: It is possible, if this transmission is not proven, that the one who is forced to commit a sin is not held accountable for it because he is unable to avoid it. Third: The Almighty said: And listen and obey. That is, listen to what you are admonished with and obey what you are commanded and forbidden. Muqatil said: Hear means pay attention to what is revealed to you from the Book of God, which is the basic principle of listening. And obey His Messenger in what he commands you or forbids you. Qatada said: “Based on them, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was pledged allegiance to hearing and obedience.” It was said: And listen means accept what you hear, and it is expressed by listening because this is its benefit. I said: Al-Hajjaj misinterpreted this verse when he recited it and limited it to Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, the trustee of God and His successor. There is no dualism in it. By God, if I were to order a man to leave through one door of the mosque and he left through another, his blood would be permissible for me. He lied in his interpretation! Yes, it is for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, first, then for those in authority after him. His evidence is: Obey God, obey the Messenger, and those in authority among you. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: And spend. It was said: It refers to zakat, as Ibn Abbas said. It was also said: It refers to spending on transportation. Ad-Dahhak said: It refers to spending on jihad. Al-Hasan said: It refers to a man’s spending on himself. Ibn Al-Arabi said: A speaker attributed this to his saying: for yourselves, and it was hidden from him that the voluntary and obligatory spending in charity is a man’s spending on himself. God the Almighty said: If you do good, you do good for yourselves, and if you do evil, you do it to them. (al-Isra’ 17:7). And everything a man does of good is only for himself, and the correct view is that it is general. It was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that a man said to him: I have a dinar. He said: Spend it on…” Yourself. He said: I have another? He said: Spend it on your family. He said: I have another? He said: Spend it on your father. He said: I have another? He said: Give it in charity. So he started with himself, family and children and made the charity after that. And this is the basis of the Sharia. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: better for yourselves. According to Sibawayh, better is an object with an implied verb, indicated by spend. It is as if he said: Give in spending what is best for yourselves, or send forward what is best for yourselves. According to Al-Kisa’i and Al-Farra’, it is an adjective for a deleted source, meaning spend a spending that is best for yourselves. According to Abu Ubaidah, it is the predicate of an implied verb to be, meaning it will be better for you. Whoever makes good money, it is an object with spend. God Almighty says: And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who will be the successful. This has been discussed previously. Likewise, If you lend God a good loan, He will multiply it for you. This was also discussed in Surat Al-Baqarah and Surat Al-Hadid.
64:17: And He will forgive you, and God is Most Appreciative and Forbearing. The meaning of gratitude is mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. The patient: the one who is not hasty.
64:18: The Almighty says: Knower of the unseen and the witnessed meaning what is absent and present. He is the Exalted meaning the Victorious, the Dominant. It is one of the attributes of actions, and from this is His statement, the Almighty: The revelation of the Book is from God, the Exalted in Might, the Wise (al-Zumar 39:1). That is, from God, the Dominant, the Perfect, Creator of all things. Al-Khattabi said: It may also mean the preciousness of measure, and it is said from it:عزya'izz with a kasra on the 'ayn, so it includes the meaning of the Exalted, on this basis that nothing is equal to Him and that He has no equal. And God knows best. The Wise in managing His creation. Al-Anbari said: The Wise is the Perfect in the creation of all things, changed from mafa'il to fa'il. From this is His statement, the Almighty: "Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the Wise Book" (Yunus 10:10). Its meaning is the perfect, so it was changed from mafa'il to fa'il. And God knows best.
65:1: Surah At-Talaq It is a civil surah according to everyone. It has eleven or twelve verses. There are fourteen issues: The first: The Almighty’s statement: O Prophet, when you divorce women is addressed to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he was addressed in the collective phrase to show respect and glorification. In Sunan Ibn Majah, it is narrated on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) divorced Hafsah may God be pleased with her and then took her back.” Qatada narrated on the authority of Anas who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) divorced Hafsah may God be pleased with her and she went to her people, so God revealed to him: “O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for their waiting period.” It was said to him: Take her back, for she is a woman who prays and fasts, and she is one of your wives in Paradise. This was mentioned by al-Mawardi, al-Qushayri and al-Tha’labi. Al-Qushayri added: And regarding her going out to her people, the Almighty’s statement was revealed: Do not turn them out of their houses. Al-Kalbi said: The reason for the revelation of this verse was the anger of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) with Hafsah, when he confided in her a secret and she revealed it to Aishah, so he divorced her once, and so the verse was revealed. Al-Suddi said: It was revealed about Abdullah ibn Umar, who divorced his wife once while she was menstruating. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) ordered him to take her back and then keep her until she had finished menstruating and then became pure. Then if he wanted to divorce her, he should divorce her when she was pure, before having intercourse with her. This is the waiting period during which God the Almighty commanded that women be divorced. It has been said that men did the same as Abdullah ibn Umar, among them Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, Amr ibn Saeed ibn al-As, and Utbah ibn Ghazwan, and so the verse was revealed about them. Ibn al-Arabi said: Although all of this is not correct, the first opinion is more appropriate. The most correct view is that it is an explanation of a new law. It has also been said that it is addressed to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), but what is meant is his Ummah. He differentiated between the two verbal forms, present and absent, and this is an eloquent language, as He said: Until, when you were in the ships and they sailed with them with a good wind (Yunus 10:22). Its meaning is: O Prophet, tell them: When you divorce women, divorce them during their waiting period. This is what they say: The address is to him alone, and the meaning is to him and to the believers. If God intended the believers to be addressed, He would be gentle with them by saying: O Prophet. If the address is to him in both wording and meaning, He would say: O Messenger. I said: The correctness of this statement is indicated by the revelation of the waiting period for Asma bint Yazid ibn al-Sakan al-Ansariyya. In the book of Abu Dawud, she states that she was divorced during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a divorced woman did not have a waiting period. So when Asma was divorced, God Almighty revealed the waiting period for divorce, and she was the first for whom the waiting period for divorce was revealed. It was said that what was meant by it was a call from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, out of respect, then he began by saying: When you divorce women, like the saying of God Almighty: O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone alters [to other than God], and divining arrows… (al-Ma’idah 5:90). So He mentioned the believers in the sense of giving them precedence and honor, then He opened by saying: Intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone alters [to other than God], and divining arrows… (al-Ma’idah 5:90). Second: Al-Tha’labi narrated from the hadith of Ibn Umar that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: The most hated of permissible things to God is divorce. It was narrated from Ali that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Marry and do not divorce, for divorce shakes the Throne. It was narrated from Abu Musa that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Do not divorce women except out of suspicion, for God does not like those who indulge in sexual intercourse or are indulged in sexual intercourse. It was narrated from Anas that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: No one swears by divorce or is made to swear by it except a hypocrite. Al-Tha’labi may God have mercy on him narrated all of it in his book. Al-Daraqutni narrated that Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Ali al-Dawlabi and Ya’qub ibn Ibrahim told us that al-Hasan ibn Arfa told us that Ismail ibn Ayyash told us on the authority of Humayd ibn Malik al-Lakhmi on the authority of Makhul on the authority of Mu’adh ibn Jabal that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said to me: O Mu’adh, God has not created anything on the face of the earth more beloved to Him than freeing slaves, nor has He created anything on the face of the earth more hated than divorce. So if a man says to his slave, You are free, God willing, then he is free and there is no exception for him.
