And if a man says to his wife, You are divorced, God willing, then he has the right to make an exception and there is no divorce against him.” Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Ali told us: Humayd ibn al-Rabi’ told us: Yazid ibn Harun told us: Ismail ibn Ayyash told us with a similar chain of transmission. Humayd said: Yazid said to me, You have pleased me, you have pleased me! Now it has become a hadith. Uthman ibn Ahmad al-Daqqaq told us: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Sunayn told us: Umar ibn Ibrahim ibn Khalid told us: Humayd ibn Malik al-Lakhmi told us: Makhul told us, on the authority of Malik ibn Yakhamir, on the authority of Mu’adh ibn Jabal, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “God has not permitted anything more hateful to Him than divorce. So whoever divorces and makes an exception may have his two-fold divorce.” Ibn al-Mundhir said: They differed about the exception in divorce and emancipation. A group said: That is unjust. We have narrated this statement from Tawus. Hammad al-Kufi, al-Shafi’i, Abu Thawr and the People of Opinion said the same. And Exceptions may be made in divorce, according to Malik and Al-Awza'i. This is also the view of Qatada, especially regarding divorce. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: I agree with the first opinion. Third: Al-Daraqutni narrated from the hadith of Abd al-Razzaq, who said: My uncle Wahb ibn Nafi’ told me that he heard Ikrimah narrating from Ibn Abbas, who said: Divorce has four aspects: two are permissible and two are forbidden. As for the permissible, the permissible is for him to divorce her while she is pure and has not had intercourse with her, or to divorce her while she is pregnant and it is clear that she is pregnant. As for the forbidden, it is for him to divorce her while she is menstruating, or to divorce her while he has had intercourse with her, and she does not know whether the womb has carried a child or not. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: So divorce them during their waiting period. In the book of Abu Dawud, on the authority of Asma’ bint Yazid bin al-Sakn al-Ansariyya, she was divorced during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the divorced woman did not have a waiting period. So God Almighty revealed when Asma’ was divorced the waiting period for divorce, so she was the first for whom the waiting period for divorce was revealed, as mentioned above. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: for their waiting period implies that they are the ones with whom the husbands have consummated the marriage, because those with whom the husbands have not been consummated are excluded by the Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, then you have no waiting period to count for them (al-Ahzab 33:49). Sixth: If a man divorces his wife during a period of purity i.e., during which he has not had intercourse with her, his divorce is valid and he has followed the Sunnah. If he divorces her while she is menstruating, his divorce is valid but he has missed the Sunnah. Saeed ibn al-Musayyab said in another narration: Divorce does not take place during menstruation because it is against the Sunnah. This is the view of the Shiites. In the two Sahihs - and the wording is from al-Daraqutni - it is narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar who said: I divorced my wife while she was menstruating. Umar mentioned that to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) became angry and said: “Let him take her back and then keep her until she menstruates again, other than the one in which he divorced her. If he decides to divorce her, then he should divorce her while she is pure from her menstruation and before having intercourse with her, and that is the divorce for the waiting period as God has commanded.” Abdullah ibn Umar divorced her once, so it was counted as one divorce, and Abdullah ibn Umar took her back as the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) commanded him. In a narration on the authority of Ibn Umar, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: It is only one. This is a clear text. It refutes what the Shiites say. Seventh: On the authority of Abdullah ibn Masoud, who said: The Sunnah divorce is that he divorces her once during each menstrual period. If it is the last of that, then that is the waiting period that God has commanded. It was narrated by Ad-Daraqutni from Al-A’mash from Abu Ishaq from Abu Al-Ahwas from Abdullah. Our scholars said: The Sunnah divorce is that which meets seven conditions: that he divorces her once while she is menstruating, that she is pure and has not been touched during that period of purity, that it is not preceded by a divorce during her menstruation, or followed by another divorce during a period of purity that follows it, and that it is devoid of compensation. These seven conditions are from the hadith of Ibn Umar mentioned above. Ash-Shafi’i said: The Sunnah divorce is that he divorces her once during each period of purity specifically. If he divorces her three times during a period of purity, that is not an innovation. Abu Hanifa said: The Sunnah divorce is that he divorces her once during each period of purity. Ash-Sha’bi said: It is permissible for a man to divorce her during a period of purity in which he has had intercourse with her. Our scholars said: He divorces her once during a period of purity in which he has not had intercourse, that it is not followed by a divorce during her waiting period, and that the period of purity does not follow a menstrual period in which the divorce occurred. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Order him to take her back, then to keep her until she is pure, then menstruates, then becomes pure, then if he wishes, he may keep her, or if he wishes, he may divorce her. This is the waiting period during which God has commanded women to be divorced.” Imam al-Shafi’i relied on the apparent meaning of the verse: Divorce them for their prescribed waiting period. This is general for every divorce, whether one, two, or more. God, the Exalted, only considered the time in this verse and did not consider the number. The same applies to the hadith of Ibn ‘Umar, because the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) taught him the time, not the number. Ibn al-‘Arabi said: This is an omission of the authentic hadith, because he said: Order him to take her back, and this eliminates the three divorces. In the hadith, he said: What if he divorced her three times? He said: She is forbidden to you and separated from you because of disobedience. Abu Hanifah said: The apparent meaning of the verse indicates that the three divorces and the one divorce are the same. This is the view of al-Shafi’i, were it not for his statement after that: You do not know; perhaps God will bring about something new after that. This invalidates the inclusion of the three divorces under the verse. This is what most scholars have said, and it is unique from them. As for Malik, the general meaning of the verse was not hidden from him, as they said, but the hadith explained it as we said. As for Al-Sha’bi’s statement that it is permissible to divorce her during a period of purity in which he had intercourse with her, the hadith of Ibn ‘Umar refutes it in its text and meaning. We have already presented its text, and its meaning is that if divorce of a menstruating woman is prohibited because it is not considered valid, then the period of purity in which intercourse has taken place is more deserving of prohibition, because it cancels the waiting period due to the absence of the womb being occupied and the menstruation that follows it. I said: Al-Shafi’i provided evidence for the triple divorce with one word based on what Al-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Salamah bin Abi bin Abd Al-Rahman on the authority of his father that Abd Al-Rahman bin Awf divorced his wife Tamadhar bint Al-Asbagh Al-Kalbiyyah, who was the mother of Abi Salamah, three times with one word. It has not been reported to us that any of his companions... He criticized that. He said: Salamah bin Abi Salamah told us on the authority of his father that Hafs bin Al-Mughira divorced his wife Fatimah bint Qais three times in one word during the time of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) divorced her. We have not been informed that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) criticized that. He also cited as evidence the hadith of Uwaimir Al-Ajlani, who said: O Messenger of God, she is divorced three times. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not denounce him. Our scholars have separated from this in the best possible way. Its explanation is in another place. We have mentioned it in the book Al-Muqtabas min Sharh Muwatta Malik bin Anas. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and a group of the Tabi’in said that whoever goes against the Sunnah in divorce and pronounces it during a menstrual period or three times, it does not count as such, and they likened him to someone who is entrusted with divorce according to the Sunnah but goes against it. Eighth: Al-Jurjani said: The lam in His statement, for their waiting period means in, like His statement, the Most High, It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering (al-Hashr 59:2), meaning at the beginning of the gathering. So His statement, for their waiting period means during their waiting period, meaning at the appropriate time for their waiting period. There is consensus that divorce during menstruation is forbidden and during purity is permitted. This is evidence that the menstrual period is purity. This has been discussed previously in Surat Al-Baqarah. If it is said: The meaning of divorce them during their waiting period is before their waiting period, or before their waiting period. This is the reading of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, as Ibn Umar said in Sahih Muslim and others. Before the waiting period is the end of the purity until the menstrual period is the menstruation, it is said to him: This is the clear evidence of Malik and those who say the same, that the menstrual periods are the purities. If it were as al-Hanafi and those who follow him said, then it would have been necessary to say that whoever divorces at the beginning of the menstrual period is not divorced before the menstruation, because the menstruation has not yet begun. Also, the onset of menstruation occurs with the onset of menstruation, and the end of the period of purity does not occur. If the onset of menstruation were the opposite, then the fasting person would be breaking his fast before sunset, as night comes at the end of the day before the end of the day. Then, if he divorces at the end of the period of purity, it is considered a menstrual period. Some menstrual periods are called menstrual periods, as God the Almighty says: The Hajj is in well-known months (Al-Baqarah 2:197), meaning Shawwal, Dhul-Qadah, and some of Dhul-Hijjah, as God the Almighty says: But whoever hastens [to do so] within two days, there is no sin upon him (Al-Baqarah 2:203). He departs on some of the second day. All of this has been discussed in detail in Al-Baqarah. Ninth: The Almighty’s statement: And count the waiting period. This means regarding a woman who has been consummated with, because there is no waiting period for a woman who has been consummated with, and he has the right to take her back after less than three days before the end of the waiting period, and after that he is like someone who has been engaged. And she is not permissible for him after three days except after another husband. Tenth: The Almighty’s saying: And count the waiting period means observe it, that is, observe the time in which the divorce occurred, until the stipulated period, which is three menstrual periods, is over. The Almighty’s saying: Divorced women shall wait, concerning themselves, three menstrual periods (al-Baqarah 2:228) makes it permissible for husbands to remarry. This indicates that the waiting period is the period of purity and not menstruation. This is confirmed and explained by the Prophet’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recitation of before their waiting period and before a thing as part of it linguistically and literally, unlike its reception, which is something else. Eleventh: Who is addressed by the command to count? There are three opinions: First, they are the husbands. Second, they are the wives. Third, they are the Muslims. Ibn al-Arabi: The correct view is that those addressed by this wording are the husbands, because all the pronouns in talaqtum you have divorced, mathu you have counted, and do not expel them are all in a single system that refers to the husbands. However, the wives are included in it, and the husband is included. He counts in order to take them back, spend on them or cut them off, live with them or leave them, and maintain his lineage or cut them off. All of these are matters that he has in common with the woman, and the woman is unique in other matters. Likewise, the judge needs to count the waiting period in order to issue a fatwa on it and to settle disputes in the event of a dispute. These are the benefits of the commanded count. Twelfth: The Almighty said: And fear God, your Lord. That is, do not disobey Him. Do not turn them out of their houses. That is, the husband does not have the right to turn her out of the marital home as long as she is in her waiting period. She is not permitted to leave either due to the husband’s right except for a clear necessity. If she leaves, she will be sinful, but the waiting period will not be interrupted. The revocable divorce and the irrevocable divorce are the same in this regard. This is to protect the man’s semen. This is the meaning of attributing houses to them, like the Almighty’s saying: And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of God and wisdom [Al-Ahzab 33], and His saying: And abide in your houses [Al-Ahzab 33]. This is an attribution of residence, not an attribution of ownership. His saying: Do not turn them out implies that it is a right over the husbands. His saying: and they should not leave implies that it is a right over the wives. In the Sahih Hadith: “On the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, he said: I divorced my aunt and I wanted to harvest her palm trees, but a man warned her not to go out. So she came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Yes, harvest your palm trees, for perhaps you will give in charity or do something good.” Narrated by Muslim. In this Hadith is evidence for Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Ibn Hanbal, and Al-Layth in their opinion: The woman in her waiting period may go out during the day to take care of her needs, but she must stay in her home at night. According to Malik, it is the same whether it is revocable or irrevocable. Al-Shafi’i said regarding a revocable al-Talaq 65:She does not go out during the day or at night. Only a woman who has been irrevocably divorced may go out during the day. Abu Hanifa said: This is the woman whose husband has died. As for a divorced woman, she does not go out during the day or at night. The hadith refutes him. In the two Sahihs: Abu Hafs ibn ‘Amr went out with ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib to the oath. He sent to his wife Fatimah bint Qays a divorce that remained from her divorce, and ordered Al-Harith ibn Hisham and ‘Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi’ah to provide her with maintenance. They said to her, By God, you are not entitled to maintenance unless you are pregnant. She came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and told him what they had said. He said, You are not entitled to maintenance. She asked his permission to move and he gave her permission. She said, Where, O Messenger of God? He said, To Ibn Umm Maktum. He was blind and she would place her clothes with him but he would not see her. When her waiting period was over, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) married her to Usamah ibn Zayd. Then Marwan sent Qubaysah ibn Dhu'ayb to her asking her about the hadith, so she narrated it to him. Marwan said: We have not heard this hadith except from a woman. We will adhere to the principle of infallibility that we found people following. When Fatima heard Marwan's words, she said: "Between me and you is the Qur'an. God the Almighty says: 'Do not turn them out of their houses' (al-Quran 2:17)." She said: "This is for one who has the right to take them back. What happens after three divorces? How can you say that she is not entitled to maintenance if she is not pregnant? What do you think?" Wording by Muslim. He explained that the verse prohibiting expulsion and exit only applies to a woman who has been divorced with a revocable divorce. Fatima also argued that the verse that followed it prohibited a woman who had been divorced with a revocable divorce from going out, because her ex-husband might have an opinion about taking her back as long as she was in her waiting period, so it was as if she was under the husband's control at all times. As for the irrevocable divorce, he has no right to any of that, so it is permissible for her to go out if she needs to, or if she fears that her house might be exposed, as the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) permitted her to do. So he ordered her and she left. In Al-Bukhari, it is narrated on the authority of Aisha that she was in a wild place and it was easy for her, so the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) gave her permission. All of this refutes the statement of Al-Kufi. In the hadith of Fatimah: that her husband sent her a divorce that remained from her divorce, so it is evidence for Malik and against Al-Shafi’i. It is more authentic than the hadith of Salamah ibn Abi Salamah on the authority of his father that Hafs ibn Al-Mughira divorced his wife three times in one word, as mentioned above. Thirteenth: The Almighty said: Unless they commit a clear indecency. Ibn Abbas, Ibn Omar, Al-Hasan, Al-Sha'bi and Mujahid said that it is adultery, so she is expelled and the prescribed punishment is carried out on her. Also from Ibn Abbas and Al-Shafi'i: It is indecency towards her in-laws, so it is permissible for them to expel her. It was narrated from Sa'id bin Al-Musayyab that he said about Fatimah: That woman was able to overpower her in-laws with her tongue, so the Prophet (peace be upon him) ordered her to move. In the book of Abu Dawud, Sa'id said: That woman tempted the people. She was a follower of Sunnah, so she was put in the hands of the blind Ibn Umm Maktum. Ikrimah said: In the Mushaf of Abu Dawud: Unless he commits a clear indecency towards you. This is strengthened by the fact that Muhammad bin Ibrahim bin Al-Harith narrated from Aisha that she said to Fatimah bint Qais: Fear God, for you know why I was expelled. Also from Ibn Abbas: Indecency is every sin such as adultery, theft and indecency towards one's family. This is the preferred opinion of Al-Tabari. Also from Ibn Omar and Al-Suddi: Indecency is her leaving her house during her waiting period. The verse means: Unless they commit a clear immorality by leaving their homes without right. That is, if she leaves, she is a sinner. Qatada said: Immorality is rebellion, meaning that he divorces her for rebellion and she leaves his home. Ibn al-Arabi said: “As for those who say that it means going out for adultery, there is no basis for them, because that going out means killing and execution, and that is not exempted from what is permissible or forbidden.” As for those who say that it means obscenity, this is explained in the hadith of Fatima bint Qays. As for those who say that it means every sin, they are mistaken, because backbiting and similar sins do not permit expulsion or going out. As for those who say that it means going out without right, this is correct. The meaning of the statement: Do not turn them out of their homes, and they should not go out according to the law, except in transgression. Fourteenth: The Almighty said: And these are the limits set by God. That is, these are the rulings that He has made clear to His servants. He has forbidden transgression from them. Whoever transgresses them has wronged himself and brought himself to the point of destruction. You do not know, perhaps God will bring about after that something new. The thing that God will bring about is that He will turn his heart from some of it to loving her, from aversion to her to desire for her, and from the determination to divorce to regretting it, so he will take her back. All the commentators said: What is meant by the command here is the desire to take her back. The meaning of this statement is: urging people to divorce once and forbidding three times, because if he divorces three times, he will harm himself when he regrets the separation and desires to take her back, so he will not find a way to take her back. Muqatil said: After that, that is, after one or two divorces, a command, that is, taking her back, without disagreement.
65:2: The Almighty's statement: And when they have reached their term means they are close to the end of their waiting period, as in His statement: And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term, then keep them (al-Baqarah 2:231) meaning they are close to the end of the term. Then keep them according to acceptable terms means taking them back according to acceptable terms, i.e., with the desire not to cause harm by taking them back by prolonging her waiting period, as mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah. Or part from them according to acceptable terms meaning leave them until their waiting period is over and they are free to control themselves. In His statement: And when they have reached their term there is what requires that the woman's statement be accepted regarding the end of her waiting period if she claims that, as we explained in Surat Al-Baqarah when He says: And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs (al-Baqarah 2:228). God's statement: And bring to witness two just men among you. There are six issues: First: God's statement: And bring to witness is a command to bring to witness the divorce. It was also said: the taking back of the wife. What appears to be the case is the taking back of the wife, not the divorce. If he takes the wife back without bringing to witness, then there are two opinions among the jurists regarding the validity of the taking back. It was also said that the meaning is: Bring to witness both the taking back and the separation. This bringing to witness is recommended according to Abu Hanifa, like His statement: And bring to witness when you make a sale. (Al-Baqarah 2:282). According to Al-Shafi'i, it is obligatory in the taking back and recommended in the separation. The benefit of bringing to witness is that there is no denial between them, that he is not accused of keeping her, and that one of them does not die and the other claims the marriage to inherit. Second: Most scholars recommend having witnesses to take her back. If a person has intercourse, kisses, or touches her with the intention of taking her back, and speaks about taking her back, then it is considered a return according to Malik. If he did not intend that, then it is not considered a return. Abu Hanifa and his companions said: If he kisses, kisses, or touches her with lust, then it is a return. They said: Looking at the vagina is a return. Al-Shafi’i and Abu Thawr said: If he speaks about taking her back, then it is a return. It has been said: His intercourse is a return in any case, whether he intended it or not. This was narrated from a group of Malik’s companions. Al-Layth also held the same opinion. Malik used to say: If he had intercourse without intending to take her back, then it is an invalid intercourse, and he should not have intercourse with her again until he has purified her from his corrupted semen. He has the right to take her back during the remainder of the first waiting period, but he does not have the right to take her back during this period of purification. Third: Ahmad ibn Hanbal required witnesses for taking a wife back, according to one of his two opinions, and al-Shafi'i did the same based on the apparent meaning of the matter. Malik, Abu Hanifa, Ahmad, and al-Shafi'i, according to the other opinion, said that taking a wife back does not require acceptance, so it does not require witnesses like other rights, especially the solution of zihar by expiation. Ibn al-Arabi said: The followers of al-Shafi'i based the requirement of witnesses for taking a wife back on the fact that it is not valid to say: I took her back yesterday and I am witnessing today the acknowledgment of taking her back. One of the conditions for taking a wife back is having witnesses, so it is not valid without that. This is invalid and is based on the fact that having witnesses for taking a wife back is an act of worship. We do not accept this, nor for marriage, by saying that it is a matter of documentation. This applies to acknowledgment as it applies to contractual agreements. Fourth: If a man claims, after the waiting period has expired, that he took his wife back during the waiting period, then if she believes him, it is permissible, but if she denies it, she must swear an oath. If he presents evidence that he took her back during the waiting period and she did not know about it, her ignorance of it does not harm him, and she remains his wife. If she had married but he did not consummate the marriage with her, and then the first man presents evidence that he took her back, then there are two narrations from Malik on this matter: One of them is that the first man has more right to her. The other is that the second man has more right to her. If the second man consummated the marriage with her, then the first man has no right to her. Fifth: The Almighty’s statement: From among you, just men. Al-Hasan said: From among the Muslims. Qatada reported: From among your free men. This requires that testimony regarding taking a divorce be limited to males and not females, because just men is a male. Therefore, our scholars said: Women have no role in anything except wealth. This was mentioned previously in Surat Al-Baqarah. Sixth: The Almighty’s statement: And establish the testimony for God meaning, draw closer to God by establishing testimony in the proper manner, if the evidence is required of it, without alteration or change. The meaning of this has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah, when God Almighty says: And I establish the testimony (al-Baqarah 2:282). God Almighty says: This is what he admonishes with. That is, he is pleased with it. Whoever believes in God and the Last Day. As for the non-believer, he will not benefit from these admonitions. God Almighty says: And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out. It was narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asked about someone who divorced three times or a thousand times, does he have a way out? So he recited it. Ibn Abbas, Ash-Sha’bi and Ad-Dahhak said: This is specifically about divorce, meaning that whoever divorces as God has commanded him will have a way out by taking her back during the waiting period, and he will be like one of those who propose marriage after the waiting period. It was also narrated from Ibn Abbas: He will make for him a way out that will save him from every distress in this world and the hereafter. It was said: The way out is for God to make him content with what He has provided him, as Ali ibn Salih said. Al-Kalbi said: And whoever fears God by being patient in times of calamity. He will make for him a way out from the Fire to Paradise. Al-Hasan said: A way out from what God has forbidden. Abu Alia: A way out of every hardship. Al-Rabi’ bin Khaitham: He will make for him a way out from everything that is difficult for people. Al-Hussein bin Al-Fadl: And whoever fears God in performing the obligatory duties, He will make for him a way out from the punishment.
65:3: And He will provide him with reward from where he does not expect meaning He will bless him in what He has given him. Sahl ibn Abdullah said: And whoever fears God in following the Sunnah, He will make for him a way out from the punishment of the people of innovation, and He will provide him with Paradise from where he does not expect. It was also said: And whoever fears God in providing for himself by severing ties with others, He will make for him a way out with sufficiency. Omar ibn Uthman al-Sadfi said: And whoever fears God and adheres to His limits and avoids His disobedience, He will take him from what is forbidden to what is permissible, from hardship to ease, and from Hell to Paradise. And He will provide for him from where he does not expect from where he does not hope. Ibn Uyaynah said: It is the blessing in sustenance. Abu al-Sa'id al-Khudri said: And whoever disavows his power and strength by turning to God, He will make for him a way out from what He has charged him with by helping him. Ibn Mas'ud and Masruq interpreted the verse in a general way. Abu Dharr said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “I know a verse which, if people were to adhere to it, it would suffice them. He recited: ‘And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out * And will provide for him from where he does not expect.’ He kept repeating it. Ibn Abbas said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited: ‘And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out * And will provide for him from where he does not expect.’ He said: A way out from the doubts of this world, from the pangs of death, and from the hardships of the Day of Resurrection.’ Most of the commentators said, as al-Tha’labi mentioned, that it was revealed about Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja’i. Al-Kalbi narrated on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja’i came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, my son has been captured by the enemy and the mother is distressed. Jabir ibn Abdullah narrated: It was revealed about Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja’i. The polytheists captured one of his sons called Salim. He came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and complained to him of his poverty and said: The enemy has captured my son and the mother is distressed, so what do you command me? He (peace be upon him) said: Fear God and be patient, and I command you and her to say frequently, 'There is no power or strength except with God.' So he returned to his house and said to his wife, "The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) commanded me and you to say frequently, 'There is no power or strength except with God.' She said, 'Yes, that is what we were commanded to do.' They kept saying that, and the enemy forgot about his son, so he drove their sheep and brought them to his father, which were four thousand sheep. Then the verse was revealed, and the Prophet (peace be upon him) gave those sheep to him." In another narration, he came and had captured camels from the enemy, and he was poor. Al-Kalbi said: He captured fifty camels. In another narration: So his son escaped from captivity and rode a she-camel belonging to the people. On his way, he passed by some of their herds and drove them away. Muqatil said: He captured sheep and goods, so he asked the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Is it permissible for me to eat what my son has brought? He said: Yes. Then this verse was revealed: “And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out * And will provide for him from where he does not expect.” Al-Hasan narrated on the authority of Imran ibn al-Husayn that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Whoever devotes himself to God, God will suffice him from every burden and provide for him from where he does not expect. But whoever devotes himself to the world, God will leave him to it.” Al-Zajjaj said: That is, if he fears God and prefers what is lawful and is patient with his family, God will open up for him if he is in difficulty and provide for him from where he does not expect. On the authority of Ibn Abbas: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever frequently seeks forgiveness, God will provide for him a way out of every distress and a way out of every worry, and will provide for him from where he does not expect. God the Almighty said: {And whoever relies upon God - then He is sufficient for him} meaning, whoever entrusts his affair to Him, He will suffice him in whatever concerns him. It was said: meaning, whoever fears God, avoids sins, and relies on Him, then he will have sufficiency in what He gives him in the Hereafter of reward. He did not mean this worldly life, because the one who relies on Him may be afflicted or killed in this world. {Indeed, God will accomplish His purpose} Masruq said: meaning, He will judge the one who relies on Him and the one who does not, except that whoever relies on Him, He will expiate his misdeeds and grant him a great reward. The common reading is baghā with a nunation. Amrūh with the accusative case. Asim read baghā with the addition and omitted the nunation for the sake of lightness. Al-Mufaddal read baghā with the meaning of his statement: God has made is the predicate of in and baligh is the state. Dawud ibn Abi Hind read baligh his affair with the tanween and raising the ra. Al-Farra' said: It means that He accomplished what He intended. God has set for everything a [decreed] extent meaning that for everything, whether hardship or ease, there is an end to which it will reach. It was also said that it is an estimate. Al-Suddi said: It is the amount of time and waiting period for menstruation. Abdullah ibn Rafi' said: When the verse, And whoever relies upon God - then He is sufficient for him was revealed, the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: So if we rely on Him, we release what we had and do not protect it. So the verse, Indeed, God will accomplish His purpose was revealed concerning you and upon you. Al-Rabi' ibn Khaitham said: God Almighty has decreed for Himself that whoever relies on Him, He will suffice him, whoever believes in Him, He will guide him, whoever lends to Him, He will reward him, whoever trusts in Him, He will save him, and whoever calls upon Him, He will answer him. Confirmation of this is in the Book of God: And whoever believes in God - He will guide his heart; And whoever relies upon God - then He is sufficient for him; If you lend to God a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you; al-Taghabun 64:17 And whoever holds fast to God has certainly been guided to a straight path. Al Imran 3:101. “And when My servants ask you, [O Muhammad], concerning Me - indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me.” al-Baqarah 2:186.
65:4: God Almighty says: And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you are in doubt, their period is three months. There are seven issues in it: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation. When He explained the matter of divorce and taking back the woman who menstruates, and they had already known the waiting period of women who have menstrual periods, He explained to them in this surah the waiting period of one who does not see blood. Abu Uthman Omar bin Salim said: When the waiting period of women was revealed in Surat Al-Baqarah regarding the divorced woman and the woman whose husband died, Ubayy bin Kaab said: O Messenger of God, some people say that there are still women who are not mentioned in anything: young children and pregnant women. So, this verse: and those who have despaired of marriage was revealed. Muqatil said: When the verse: Divorced women shall wait concerning themselves three menstrual periods was mentioned, Khallad bin An-Nu’man said: O Messenger of God, what is the waiting period of one who has not menstruated, one whose menstruation has stopped, and one who is pregnant? So, this verse: and those of your women who have despaired of menstruation was revealed, meaning a marriage contract has been concluded. It was said that Muadh bin Jabal asked about the waiting period of an older woman who has despaired of menstruation, so this verse was revealed. And God knows best. Mujahid said: The verse was revealed regarding a woman with irregular bleeding who does not know whether it is menstrual blood or a disease. Second: The Almighty’s statement: If you are in doubt means you are suspicious, and it was said that you are certain. It is one of the opposites, it can be doubt and certainty like suspicion. Al-Tabari preferred that Al-Mughni be: If you are in doubt, so you do not know the ruling regarding them. Al-Zajjaj said: If you are in doubt about her menstruation and her menstruation has stopped and she is one of those who menstruate like her. Al-Qushayri said: There is a problem with this, because if we are in doubt whether she has reached menopause, we do not say her waiting period is three months. What is considered regarding the age of menopause is in His statement: The longest period of a woman in the world, and in another statement: Most of the women of the woman’s clan. Mujahid said: His statement If you are in doubt is for those being addressed, meaning if you do not know how long the waiting period of the one who has passed through menopause and the one who has not menstruated is this. It was said: The meaning is if you are in doubt as to whether the blood that appears from her is due to old age, or from the usual menstruation, or from istihadah, then the waiting period is three months. Ikrimah and Qatadah said: Among the doubts is the woman with istihadah who does not menstruate regularly, menstruating repeatedly in one or two months and once in three months. It was said that it is connected to the beginning of the surah. The meaning is: Do not turn them out of their homes if you are in doubt about the expiration of their waiting period. This is the most correct statement. Third: A woman who has doubts about her waiting period may not marry until she is clear of her doubt, and she may not leave the waiting period except when the doubt is removed. It has been said about a woman who has doubts and is relieved by her menses, and she does not know what is causing them, that she should wait one year from the day her husband divorced her, of which nine months are for purification and three months for waiting. If he divorces her and she menstruates once or twice, and then the menses are removed without despairing, she should wait nine months, then three months from the day she purifies from her menses, then she is permissible for marriage. This was the opinion of Al-Shafi’i in Iraq. Based on this opinion, a free woman whose husband has died and who has been purified after nine months should wait four months and ten days, and a slave woman should wait two months and five nights after the nine months. Al-Shafi’i also narrated that her menstrual cycles remain as they were until she reaches the age of menopause. This is the opinion of Al-Nakha’i, Al-Thawri and others. Abu ‘Ubaid narrated it from the people of Iraq. If the woman is young - which is the fourth issue - then she should be asked to see whether she is pregnant or not. If her pregnancy is evident, then her term is for delivery. If there is no clear evidence, Malik said: The waiting period of a woman whose menstruation stopped while she was young is one year. Ahmad and Ishaq said the same, and it was narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him and others. The people of Iraq believe that her waiting period is three menstrual periods after she had menstruated once in her life, even if she lived for twenty years, unless she reaches an age at which she despairs of menstruation, in which case her waiting period after menopause is three months. He said: Al-Tha'labi: This is the most correct view of the Shafi'i school of thought, and it is the view of the majority of scholars. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Saud and his companions. Al-Kiya said: This is the truth, because God Almighty has set the waiting period for a woman in despair to be three months, while a woman in doubt is not in despair. Fifth: As for the woman whose menstruation is delayed due to illness, Malik, Ibn al-Qasim, and Abdullah ibn Asbagh said: She observes a waiting period of nine months, then three. Ashhab said: She is like a breastfeeding woman after weaning, whether by menstruation or by a year. Hubban ibn Munqidh divorced his wife while she was breastfeeding, and she remained without menstruating for a year because of the breastfeeding. Then Hubban fell ill and feared that she would inherit from him, so he took her case to Uthman, who was with Ali and Zaid. They said: We think she should inherit from him, because she is neither among the elderly nor among the minors. Then Hubban died, so she inherited from him and observed the waiting period of death. Sixth: If her period is delayed for a reason other than sickness or breastfeeding, she should wait for a year without menstruation, nine months then three, as we have mentioned. She is then permissible as long as she does not suspect pregnancy. If she is suspicious of pregnancy, she should stay for four, five, or seven years, according to the different narrations from our scholars. The well-known view is five years. If she goes beyond that, she is permissible. Ashhab said: She is never permissible until the suspicion is removed. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is correct, because if it is permissible for the child to remain in her womb for five years, then it is permissible for it to remain for ten years or more. A similar narration was narrated from Malik. Seventh: As for the woman whose menstruation was unknown due to istihaadah, there are three opinions: Ibn al-Musayyab said: She waits for one year. This is the opinion of al-Layth. Al-Layth said: The waiting period of a divorced woman and a woman whose husband has died if she is suffering from istihaadah is one year. This is the well-known opinion of our scholars, whether she knows whether her menstrual blood is from her regular bleeding. If she experiences istihadah non-menstrual bleeding, whether she can distinguish between that and the end of her period, her waiting period in all cases according to Malik in his book Tahsil al-Madhhab is one year, including nine months for purification and three for waiting periods. Al-Shafi’i said in one of his opinions: Her waiting period is three months. This is the opinion of a group of the Tabi’un and the later Qurutiyyun. Ibn al-Arabi said: It is the correct opinion in my opinion. Abu ‘Umar said: If the bleeding of a woman with istihadah is separated and she knows whether her period is coming or going, she must observe a waiting period of three menstrual periods. This is more correct in terms of opinion and more established by analogy and tradition. God the Almighty said, And for those who have not menstruated - meaning the young girl - their waiting period is three months, so He implied the report. Her waiting period is in months because there is no menstruation during her waiting period. God the Almighty made the rulings based on customs, so she observes her waiting period by months. So if she sees blood during a time when it is possible for women, she switches to blood because the original principle exists. And if the original principle exists, then the substitute has no ruling. This is similar to the case with an elderly woman who observes her waiting period by blood, then her customs change to months. This is agreed upon. God the Almighty said: And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth. There are two issues in this: The first: God the Almighty’s statement: And for those who are pregnant, their term is giving birth. Even though this is apparently referring to a divorced woman because it is in apposition to her and the sentence refers back to her, the same applies to a woman whose husband has died, due to the general meaning of the verse and the hadith of Subai’ah. We have already discussed this in detail in Surat Al-Baqarah. Second: If a woman gives birth to a clot or a lump of flesh, it becomes permissible. Al-Shafi’i and Abu Hanifa said: It is not permissible except for what results in a child. This has been discussed previously in Surat Al-Baqarah and Surat Ar-Ra’d. Praise be to God. God the Almighty says: And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out. Ad-Dahhak said: That is, whoever fears God in divorce according to the Sunnah, He will make his way out easily. Muqatil said: And whoever fears God in avoiding His disobedience, He will make his way out easy by enabling him to obey God.
65:5: That is the command of God meaning that the rulings mentioned are the command of God that He revealed to you and made clear to you. And whoever fears God meaning acts in obedience to Him. He will remove from him his misdeeds from prayer to prayer, from Friday to Friday. And will make great for him his reward meaning in the Hereafter.
65:6: There are four issues: First: The statement of God the Almighty: Lodge them where you dwell, according to your means. Ashhab said on the authority of Malik: He leaves her if he divorces her and leaves her in the house, because God the Almighty says: Lodge them. If he had been with her, he would not have said Lodge them. Ibn Nafi' said: Malik said regarding the statement of God the Almighty: Lodge them where you dwell, meaning divorced women whose husbands have separated and they cannot take them back, and the husband is not pregnant, so she is entitled to housing, but she is not entitled to maintenance or clothing, because he has been divorced from him. They do not inherit from each other, and he does not have the right to take her back. If she is pregnant, she is entitled to maintenance, clothing, and housing until her waiting period expires. As for those who have not separated, they are their wives and they inherit from each other, and they do not leave unless their husbands give them permission so long as they are in their waiting period. They were not commanded to provide them with housing because that is obligatory for their husbands along with their maintenance and clothing, whether they are pregnant or not. God has commanded that women who have divorced their husbands be given housing and maintenance. God the Almighty says: And if they are pregnant, then spend on them until they give birth. Thus, God the Almighty has made housing and maintenance for pregnant women who have divorced their husbands. Ibn al-Arabi said: The explanation and clarification of this is that when God the Almighty mentioned housing, He made it general for every divorce, but when He mentioned maintenance, He restricted it to pregnancy. This indicates that a woman who has been irrevocably divorced is not entitled to maintenance. This is a serious issue, and we have paved the way for it in the Qur’an, Sunnah and meaning in the issues of disagreement. This is its source from the Qur’an. I said: The scholars differed regarding the woman who has been divorced three times, and they have three opinions. The school of Malik and Al-Shafi’i is that she is entitled to housing but not maintenance. The school of Abu Hanifa and his companions is that she is entitled to housing and maintenance. The school of Ahmad, Ishaq and Abu Al-Thawr is that she is not entitled to maintenance or housing, based on the hadith of Fatimah bint Qays, who said: “I entered upon the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and my husband was with me. I said: ‘My husband has divorced me, and this makes me feel that I am not entitled to housing or maintenance?’ He said: ‘Rather, housing and maintenance are yours.’ He said: ‘Her husband divorced her three times.’ The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Housing and maintenance are only the responsibility of the one who has the right to take her back.’ When I arrived in Kufa, Al-Aswad bin Yazid called me to ask me about that, and the companions of Abdullah say: ‘She is entitled to housing and maintenance.’” Narrated by Al-Daraqutni. Muslim narrated on her authority: Her husband divorced her during the time of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he had provided her with less than her maintenance. When she saw that, she said: By God, I will inform the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), for if I have maintenance, I will take what is best for me, and if I have no maintenance, I will not take anything. She said: So I mentioned that to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he said: You have no maintenance or housing. Ad-Darqunti narrated on the authority of Al-Aswad that he said: When Umar heard what Fatimah bint Qays had said, We do not accept the opinion of a woman regarding Muslims. He used to give a woman who had been divorced three times the right to housing and maintenance. Ash-Sha’bi said: Al-Aswad bin Yazid met me and said: O Shu’bi, fear God and retract the hadith of Fatimah bint Qays, for Umar used to give her housing and maintenance. I said: “I will not retract something that Fatimah bint Qays told me on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him).” I said: How good this is. Qatada and Ibn Abi Layla said: There is no housing except for the woman who has been divorced by revocable divorce, based on the statement of God the Almighty: You do not know; perhaps God will bring about after that something new. And His statement: Lodge them refers to what came before it, which is the woman who has been divorced by revocable divorce. And God knows best. And because housing is subordinate to maintenance and is similar to it, since maintenance is not due to the woman who has been divorced by revocable divorce, she is not entitled to housing. Abu Hanifa’s argument that maintenance is due to the woman who has been divorced by revocable divorce is based on the statement of God the Almighty: And do not harm them in order to make things difficult for them. And he left out one of the greatest harms. Umar's denial of Fatima's statement clarifies this. Because she was observing her waiting period and was entitled to housing following a divorce, she was entitled to maintenance like a revocable divorce. Because she was imprisoned by him due to his right, she was entitled to maintenance like a wife. Malik's evidence is the Almighty's statement: And if they are pregnant verse, as explained above. It has been said that God, the Almighty, mentioned the revocable divorcee and her rulings at the beginning of the verse until His statement: two just men among you, then after that He mentioned a ruling that applies to all divorcees, such as counting the months and other things. This is general for every divorcee, so the rulings that come after that apply to every divorcee. Second: The Almighty’s saying: From your means meaning from your abundance. It is said: I found in wealth, I found, I found, I found, I found, I found, I found, I found, I found, I found, I found, I found, I found, I found, I found, I found. Al-Wajd means: richness and ability. The common people read it with a damma on the waw. Al-A’raj and Al-Zuhri read it with a fatha, and Ya’qub with a kasra. All of them are languages regarding it. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And do not harm them in order to make things difficult for them. Mujahid said: In housing Muqatil said: In maintenance, and this is the opinion of Abu Hanifa. And on the authority of Abu Ad-Dahha: It is that he divorces her, and when two days remain of her waiting period, he takes her back and then divorces her. Fourth: The Almighty said: And if they are pregnant, then spend on them until they give birth. There is no disagreement among the scholars regarding the obligation of maintenance and housing for a pregnant woman who has been divorced three times or less until she gives birth. As for the pregnant woman whose husband has died, Ali, Ibn Umar, Ibn Mas`ud, Shuraih, An-Nakha`i, Ash-Sha`bi, Hammad, Ibn Abi Layla, Sufyan, and Ad-Dahhak said: She should be spent on from all the wealth until she gives birth. Ibn Abbas, Ibn Az-Zubayr, Jabir ibn Abdullah, Malik, Ash-Shafi`i, Abu Hanifah, and their companions said: She should not be spent on except from her share. This has been explained in Surah Al-Baqarah. God the Almighty said: Then if they breastfeed for you There are four issues: First: God the Almighty said: Then if they breastfeed for you - meaning the divorced women - your children from them, then the fathers are required to pay them for breastfeeding them. A man may hire his wife to breastfeed, just as he may hire a foreigner. However, according to Abu Hanifa and his companions, hiring a woman is not permissible if the child is from them, unless the child is born. However, according to Al-Shafi'i, it is permissible. Breastfeeding has been fully discussed in Al-Baqarah and An-Nisa, and praise be to God. Second: The Almighty said: And consult one another in what is right. This is addressed to husbands and wives, meaning, let some of you accept from others what is ordered of good and beautiful things. A good thing among them is breastfeeding the child without payment. A good thing among them is providing him with payment for the breastfeeding. It was said: Consult one another about breastfeeding the child in a right way so that no harm befalls the child. It was said: It is clothing and a blanket. It was said: Its meaning is that a mother should not be harmed by her child, nor a child by his child. Third: The Almighty said: {And if you both disagree} meaning the payment for breastfeeding, and the husband refuses to give the mother her breastfeeding and the mother refuses to breastfeed him, then he has no right to compel her, but he should hire a wet nurse other than his mother. It was also said that its meaning is: If you are in difficulty and quarrel, then he should hire someone other than her to breastfeed his child. It is a statement in the sense of a command. Ad-Dahhak said: If the mother refuses to breastfeed, then he should hire another woman for his child. If he does not accept, then his mother should be forced to breastfeed for a fee. Scholars have differed regarding who is obligated to breastfeed the father, and there are three opinions: Our scholars said: Breastfeeding the child is the responsibility of the wife as long as the marriage continues, except for her honor and position, in which case the father must breastfeed him on that day from his own wealth. The second - Abu Hanifa said: It is not obligatory on the mother under any circumstances. The third - It is obligatory on her in every case. Fourth: If he divorces her, she is not obligated to breastfeed him unless he is not receptive to the breast of anyone else, in which case she is obligated to breastfeed him. If they disagree over the wage, and she calls for a wage equal to hers and the father refuses, except as a voluntary act, then the mother is more entitled to a wage equal to hers if the father cannot find a volunteer. If the father calls for a wage equal to hers and the mother refuses, seeking excess, then the father is more entitled to it. If the father is unable to pay her wage, she is compulsorily forced to breastfeed her child.
65:7: There are four issues: First: The Almighty's saying: Let him spend meaning that the husband should spend on his wife and young child according to his ability, so that he can be generous to them if he is wealthy. And if the person is poor, then it is according to that. The maintenance is estimated according to the condition of the one who is spending and the need of the one who is being spent on, based on his own effort and the normal course of life. The mufti looks at the amount of the need of the one being spent on, then he looks at the condition of the one who is spending on him. If the condition is bearable, he approves it. If his condition does not meet the need of the one who is being spent on, he returns it to the amount he can bear. Imam al-Shafi'i may God be pleased with him and his companions said: Maintenance is determined and specified, and neither the ruler nor the mufti has the right to exert effort in this regard. Its estimation is based on the condition of the husband alone, whether he is wealthy or poor, and her condition and sufficiency are not taken into account. They said: The daughter of the caliph is entitled to what the daughter of the guard is entitled to. If the husband is well-off, then he is required to give two mudds. If he is average, then one and a half mudds. If he is poor, then one mudd. They provided evidence with the verse: Let the one with an abundance spend from his abundance (al-Baqarah 2:17). So He made the husband the criterion in terms of wealth and poverty, not her. And because the ruler or anyone else cannot know what is considered to be her sufficiency, it leads to litigation, because the husband claims that she is seeking more than she is able to, and she claims that what she is seeking is sufficient for her, so We made it a specific amount to cut off the litigation. The basis for this, according to them, is the verse: Let the one with an abundance spend from his abundance (al-Baqarah 2:233), as we mentioned, and His statement: The wealthy shall bear his capacity, and the poor his capacity. The answer is that this verse does not indicate more than a difference between the maintenance of the rich and the poor, and that it differs according to the wealth or poverty of the husband. This is accepted. As for not taking the wife's condition into consideration in its entirety, then this is not in it. God the Most High said: And the father of the child shall bear their food and clothing, according to what is equitable. (al-Baqarah 2:233) This requires that what is equitable be attached to both of them, because He did not specify in that regard either of them. It is not known that the sufficiency of a rich woman is like the maintenance of a poor woman. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said to Hind: Take what is sufficient for you and your children in a reasonable manner. He referred her to what is sufficient when he knew that Abu Sufyan was well-off and that it was obligatory for him to request it. He did not tell her that her sufficiency is not taken into account and that what is due to you is something that is set. Rather, he referred her to what he knew of her sufficiency and did not make it conditional on a known amount. Then what they mentioned of a limitation needs to be established, and the verse does not require it. Second: It was narrated that Umar may God be pleased with him imposed one hundred dirhams for a newborn, and Uthman imposed fifty dirhams for him. Ibn al-Arabi: It is possible that this difference was due to the different years or to the circumstances of fate in setting prices for food and clothing. Muhammad ibn Hilal al-Muzani narrated: My father and grandmother told me that she used to visit Uthman and he missed her, so he said to his family: Why don’t I see so-and-so? His wife said: O Commander of the Faithful, she gave birth last night. So he sent her fifty dirhams and his brother Sanbalaniyyah. Then he said: This is your son’s stipend and this is his clothing. When a year passes, we will raise it to one hundred. Ali may God be pleased with him brought a rejected child and he imposed one hundred for him. Ibn al-Arabi said: This stipulation before weaning is something that scholars differed about. Some of them saw it as recommended because it is included in the ruling of the verse, and some of them saw it as obligatory because of the new need and the increase in his expenses, and I say the same. However, its amount differs according to his condition after birth and his condition at weaning. Sufyan ibn Wahb narrated that Umar took the mudd in one hand and the qist in the other and said: I have imposed on you, for every Muslim soul, a mudd of wheat, a qist of vinegar, and a qist of oil every month. Another narrator added: “We have given you provisions and provided for you every month. Whoever reduces them, God will do such and such to him.” So he supplicated against him. Abu Darda’ said: “How many righteous and guided traditions did Umar may God be pleased with him establish for the nation of Muhammad (blessings and peace of God be upon him)!” The mudd and the qist are two Syrian measures for food and condiments, and they have been measured according to another custom. The mudd is measured to the measure. The qist is measured to the measure, but our estimation for it is two-quarters for food and two-eighths for condiments. As for clothing, it is according to the customary amount: a shirt and trousers for a meal in the winter, and a cloak, a loincloth, and a mat. This is the basic principle, and it may be increased according to circumstances and custom. Third: This verse is the basis for the obligation of spending on the child on the father and not the mother, contrary to what Muhammad ibn al-Mawaz said: It is on both parents according to the proportion of the inheritance. Ibn al-Arabi said: Perhaps Muhammad meant that it is on the mother in the absence of the father. In al-Bukhari: On the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): “A woman will say to you, ‘Spend on me or else divorce me.’ A slave will say to you, ‘Spend on me and employ me.’ And your son will say, ‘Spend on me.’ To whom do you speak? The Qur’an and Sunnah have complemented each other and come together in one law.” Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. That is, He does not charge the poor as He charges the rich. God will bring about, after hardship, ease. That is, after distress, wealth, and after hardship, ease.
65:8: The Almighty says: And how many a town When He mentioned the rulings, He mentioned and warned against disobeying the command, and He mentioned the emancipation of a people and the punishment that would befall them. The discussion of how many has already been mentioned in Al Imran, and praise be to God. It rebelled against the command of its Lord means it was protected, meaning the town and what is meant is its people. So We called it to account with a severe account meaning We rewarded it with punishment in this world, and punished it with a terrible punishment in the Hereafter. It was said: There is an inversion in the speech, so We punished it with a terrible punishment in this world with hunger, famine, sword, sinking, transformation and all other calamities, and We called it to account with a severe account in the Hereafter. Nakar means the reprehensible. It is read with a light and heavy vowel, and this has already been mentioned in Surat Al Kahf.
65:9: So she tasted the evil consequences of her deed meaning the consequence of her disbelief and the consequence of her deed was loss meaning destruction in this world as we mentioned, and in the Hereafter in Hell. The past tense was used as in the Almighty's saying: And the companions of Paradise will call out to the companions of the Fire (al-A’raf 7:44) and similar to that, because what is awaited from the promise and threat of God is actually cast down, and what is to come to pass is as if it has already happened.
65:10: God has prepared for them a severe punishment. He explained that loss and that it is the punishment of Hell in the Hereafter. So fear God, O you of understanding. That is, intellects. Those who have believed is a substitute for those of understanding, or a description of them, that is, O you of understanding who have believed in God, fear God who sent down the Qur'an to you. That is, fear Him, know that obeying Him is obligatory, and refrain from disobeying Him. A Messenger has already been mentioned. Al-Zajjaj said: The sending down of the reminder is evidence of the omission of sent, that is, He sent down a Qur'an to you and sent a Messenger. It was also said that the meaning is that God has sent down to you that He mentioned a Messenger. His mention of the Messenger would be His saying: Muhammad is the Messenger of God. (al-Fath 48:29) It is permissible for Messenger to be a substitute for remembrance, on the condition that messenger means message, or on the condition that it is in its category and is carried by the meaning, as if he said: God has revealed to you a reminder, a Messenger, so it is from the category of substituting something for something, and it is that. It is permissible for the word rasūl to be in the accusative case as an inducement, as if he said: Seek a messenger. It was said that the mention here means honor, like the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, We have sent down to you a Book in which is your remembrance (Al-Anbiya’: 10), and His saying: And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people (al-Zukhruf 43:44). Then He explained this honor by saying: a messenger. Most of the scholars agree that what is meant by the messenger here is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Kalbi said: It is Gabriel, so they are both revealed.
65:11: He recites to you the verses of God is an adjective for the Messenger. The verses of God are the Qur'an. The general reading is with a fat-ha on the ya', meaning God made it clear. Ibn 'Amir, Hafs, Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i read it with a kasra, meaning He makes clear to you the rulings you need. The first reading is that of Ibn 'Abbas and the choice of Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim, based on the statement of God, the Most High: We have made the verses clear to you (Al Imran 3:118). That He may bring forth those who have believed and done righteous deeds (al-Talaq 65:11) meaning those who have been foreordained in God's knowledge. From darkness meaning those who disbelieve. Into the light meaning guidance and faith. Ibn 'Abbas said: It was revealed about the believers among the People of the Book. He attributed bringing forth to the Messenger because faith is attained from him through his obedience. God Almighty says: And whoever believes in God and does righteousness - He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow. Nafi’ and Ibn ‘Amir read it with a nun, while the others read it with a ya. “God has given him good provision” means that God has made Paradise abundant for him.
65:12: The Almighty's saying: God is He Who created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them indicates the perfection of His power and that He has the power to resurrect and hold people accountable. There is no dispute that the heavens are seven, one above the other. This is indicated by the hadith of the Night Journey and others. Then He said: And of the earth the like of them meaning seven. There are two different opinions regarding them: The first - and this is the opinion of the majority - is that they are seven earths, one above the other, between each earth a distance like that between one heaven and the next, and in each earth are inhabitants of God's creation. Ad-Dahhak said: And of the earth the like of them meaning seven earths, but they are layered over one another without any separation, unlike the heavens. The first is more correct because the hadiths indicate it in At-Tirmidhi, An-Nasa'i and others. This has been explained previously in Surat Al-Baqarah. Abu Nu`aym narrated: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Hubaysh narrated to us: Ismail ibn Ishaq al-Sarraj narrated to us, H and Abu Muhammad ibn Hibban narrated to us: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Najiyah narrated to us: Suwayd ibn Sa`id narrated to us: Hafs ibn Maysarah narrated to us from Musa ibn `Uqbah from `Ata` ibn Abi Marwan from his father that Ka`b swore to him by He who split the sea for Moses that Suhayb told him that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, never saw a town he wanted to enter except that he said when he saw it: “O God, Lord of the seven heavens and what they shade, Lord of the seven earths and what they carry, Lord of the devils and what they lead astray, Lord of the winds and what they scatter, we ask You for the good of this town and the good of its people, and we seek refuge in You from its evil, the evil of its people, and the evil of what is in it.” Abu Nu`aym said: This is an authentic hadith from the hadith of Musa ibn `Uqbah, who is the only one to narrate it from `Ata`. He narrated from Ibn Abi al-Zinad and others. In Sahih Muslim, it is narrated on the authority of Sa'id ibn Zayd who said: "I heard the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: 'Whoever takes a handspan of land unjustly will have it hung around his neck on the Day of Resurrection from seven earths.'" A similar hadith is narrated by Aisha, and clearer than both of them is the hadith of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: No one takes a handspan of land unjustly except that God will hang him around the neck to the seven earths on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Mawardi said: "Considering that they are seven earths, one above the other, the supplication of the people of Islam is specific to the people of the upper earth, and does not apply to those on the other earths, even if there are those among them who possess reason and are distinguished by their nature." Concerning their seeing the evening sky and deriving light from it, there are two opinions: One of them is that they see the sky from every side of their land and derive light from it. This is the opinion of those who consider the earth to be flat. The second opinion is that they do not see the sky, and that God Almighty created light for them from which they derive light. This is the opinion of those who consider the earth to be like a sphere. There is a third opinion concerning this verse, narrated by Al-Kalbi on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that it is seven flat earths, not one above the other, separated by seas, and all of them are shaded by the sky." Therefore, if no one on earth has access to another land, the call of Islam is limited to the people on earth. If some of them have access to another land, it is possible that the call of Islam will be binding on them when it is possible to reach them, because the separation of the seas, if it is possible to traverse them, does not prevent the obligation of what is general in its ruling. It is possible that the call of Islam will not be binding on them, because if it were binding on them, the text would have been transmitted, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would have been commanded to do it. God knows best what He has kept to Himself and what is correct regarding what is unclear to His creation. Then He said, The Command descends between them. Mujahid said, The Command descends from the seven heavens to the seven earths. Al-Hasan said, Between every two heavens there is an earth and a Command. The Command here is revelation, according to Muqatil and others. Based on this, His statement, between them, refers to what is between this highest earth, which is the lowest, and the seventh heaven, which is the highest. It was also said that the Command is divine decree and predestination, and this is the opinion of the majority. Based on this, what is meant by God’s statement, between them, refers to what is between the lowest earth, which is the farthest, and the seventh heaven, which is the highest. It was said: The command descends between them with the life of some and the death of others, the wealth of a people and the poverty of others. It was also said: It is the wondrous planning He arranges in them, so He sends down rain and plants and brings forth night and day, summer and winter, and creates animals in all their different types and forms, moving them from one state to another. Ibn Kaysan said: This is according to the scope and breadth of the language, just as death is called the command of God, and the wind and clouds and the like. So that you may know that God is over all things competent means that He who has power over this great kingdom is even more competent over what is between them of His creation, and He is able to forgive and take revenge, even if all of that is equal in His power and ability. And that God has encompassed all things in knowledge so nothing is outside His knowledge and power. The word knowledge is in the accusative case as a confirmed source, because to encompass means to know. It was also said: It means that God encompasses with a comprehensive knowledge. The surah ends with praise to God and His help.
66:1: Surah At-Tahrim It is a Medinan surah according to everyone, and it has twelve verses. It is called Surat Al-Nabi. God the Almighty said: O Prophet! Why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you? It is proven in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to stay with Zainab bin Jahsh and drink honey at her place. She said: “Hafsa and I conspired that whichever of us the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) entered upon should say: ‘I detect a strong odor from you! Have you eaten maghāfir?’ So he entered upon one of them and she said that to him. He said: ‘Did you drink honey at Zainab bin Jahsh’s place? I will never do it again.’” Then this verse was revealed: Why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you - until His saying - if you both repent for Aisha and Hafsa. And when the Prophet confided a statement to one of his wives for His saying: Rather, I drank honey. It was also narrated from her that she said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) loved sweets and honey. When he had prayed the ‘Asr prayer, he would go around to his wives and approach them. He entered upon Hafsah and stayed with her longer than usual.” I asked about that and was told: A woman from her tribe gave her a gift of a bowl of honey, so she gave the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) a drink of it. I said: By God, we will find a plan for him. I mentioned that to Sawdah and said: When he enters upon you and approaches you, say to him: O Messenger of God, have you eaten maghāfir a type of sweet nectar? He will say: No, so say to him: What is this smell? - and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was very upset when he smelled a smell - he will say to you: Hafsah gave me a drink of honey. So say to him: I sat with the honeycomb of the ‘Arfat tree. I will say that to him, and you say it, O Safiyyah. So when he entered upon Sawdah - she said: Sawdah says: By God, there is no god but Him, I almost started with what you said to me, while he was at the door, fearing you.” When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came near, she said: O Messenger of God, have you eaten Maghafir? He said: No. She said: What is this smell? He said: Hafsah gave me a drink of honey. She said: The bees of the Arfaat tree have stung it. When he came to me, I said the same to him. Then he went to Safiyyah, and she said the same. When he came to Hafsah, she said: O Messenger of God, shall I not give you some to drink? He said: I need it. She said: “Sawdah says: ‘Glory be to God!’ By God, we have forbidden it.” She said: I told her to be quiet. In this narration, the one at whose house he drank the honey was Hafsah. In the first narration, it was Zaynab. Ibn Abi Malekah narrated from Ibn Abbas that he drank it at Sawdah’s house. It was also said that it was Umm Salamah. Asbat narrated it from As-Suddi. Ata’ ibn Abi Muslim also said the same. Ibn al-Arabi said: All of this is ignorance or imagined without knowledge. The rest of his wives said, out of envy and jealousy, to the one who drank it at her house: We smell the smell of Maghafir from you. Al-Maghāfīr: a herb or gum with a changeable smell, it has a sweetness, the singular of which is maghfur, and jarast: ate. Al-Arfat: a plant that has a smell like the smell of wine. The Prophet (peace be upon him) liked to have a good smell or find it, and he disliked a bad smell for the sake of talking to the king. This is one opinion. Another opinion is that he meant the woman who offered herself to the Prophet (peace be upon him), but he did not accept her because of his wives, Ibn Abbas and Ikrimah said. The woman was Umm Sharik. A third opinion is that the one he forbade was Maria the Copt, who had been given to him as a gift by Al-Muqawqis, the king of Alexandria. Ibn Ishaq said: She is from the district of Ansana, from a town called Hafn, so he had intercourse with her in the house of Hafsa. Al-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas on the authority of Umar who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered with his concubine, Mariyah, into Hafsa’s house. Hafsa found him with her - and Hafsa had gone away to her father’s house - and said to him: ‘You are letting her into my house! You did this to me among your other wives only because I am insignificant to you.’ He said to her: ‘Do not mention this to Aisha, for she is forbidden to you if you approach her.’ Hafsa said: ‘How can she be forbidden to you when she is your slave girl?’ So he swore to her that he would not approach her. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Do not mention it to anyone.’ She mentioned it to Aisha, and he swore that he would not enter upon his wives for a month. So he kept away from them for twenty-nine nights, and then God, the Almighty, revealed: ‘You forbid what God has made lawful for you, seeking…’” Second: The most correct of these sayings is the first one. And the weakest and the middle one. Ibn al-Arabi said: As for its weakness in the chain of transmission, it is due to the lack of trustworthiness of its narrators. As for its weakness in its meaning, it is because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) rejected a gift, which did not mean it was forbidden, because the one who rejected a gift did not make it forbidden for him. The true prohibition only comes after it had been made permissible. As for the one who narrated that he prohibited Maria the Copt, his chain of transmission is better and closer to the meaning, but it was not recorded in Sahih. It was narrated as a mursal. Ibn Wahb narrated from Malik from Zayd ibn Aslam who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prohibited Umm Ibrahim and said: ‘You are forbidden to me, by God, I will not come to you.’ So God, the Almighty, revealed regarding that: ‘O Prophet, why do you prohibit what God has made lawful for you?’” Ibn al-Qasim narrated something similar from him. Ashhab narrated from Malik who said: “I argued with ‘Umar about something with a woman from the Ansar, and he shuddered at that and said: ‘Women are not like this!’ She said: ‘Yes, and the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to argue with him.” So he took his garment, went out to Hafsa and said to her: Are you arguing with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him)? I said: Yes, and if I had known that you disliked it, I would not have done it.
