When Umar heard that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had abandoned his wives, he said: In the dust of Hafsa’s nose. What is correct is that it was in the honey and that he drank it at Zainab’s house, and Aisha and Hafsa conspired against him over it, so what happened happened and he swore not to drink it and kept it a secret. The verse was revealed regarding all of them. Third: God's statement, did not forbid. If the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade it and did not break his oath, then this is not considered an oath according to us. A man's statement, This is forbidden to me, does not forbid anything, except for his wife. Abu Hanifa said: If the word is general, it applies to food and drink, not clothing, and it is an oath that requires expiation. Zufar said: It is an oath in everything, even in movement and being. The opponent relied on the fact that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade honey, so expiation is required for it. God the Almighty said, God has prescribed for you the expiation of your oaths, and He called it an oath. Our evidence is the statement of God the Almighty: O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things which God has made lawful to you and do not transgress. (al-Ma’idah 5:87), and His statement, Say, 'Have you considered what God has sent down to you of provision and then you made some of it lawful and some unlawful?' Say, 'Has God permitted you, or do you invent a lie about God?' (Yunus 10:59). God condemned the one who forbids what is lawful and did not require expiation. Al-Zajjaj said: No one has the right to forbid what God has permitted. He did not give His Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) the right to forbid anything except what God forbade him. So whoever says to his wife or female slave, You are forbidden to me, without intending divorce or zihar, then this statement requires expiation for an oath. If he addresses a group of wives and female slaves with these words, then he must offer one expiation. If he forbids himself food or something else, then he is not required to offer expiation for that according to Al-Shafi’i and Malik. However, expiation is required for that according to Abu Mas’ud, Al-Thawri, and Abu Hanifa. Fourth: Scholars differed regarding a man who says to his wife, You are forbidden to me. There are eighteen opinions: One of them: He does not have to do anything. This was the opinion of Ash-Sha’bi, Masruq, Rabi’ah, Abu Salamah, and Asbagh. According to them, it is like forbidding water and food. God the Almighty said, O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you. (al-Ma’idah 5:87). Marital relations are among the good things and among what God has permitted. God the Almighty said, And do not say about what your tongues put forth falsely, “This is lawful and this is unlawful. (al-Nahl 16:116). Whatever God has not prohibited, no one has the right to prohibit, nor to make it unlawful by its prohibition. It is not proven that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said, What God has permitted is unlawful to me. Rather, he refrained from Maria because of an oath he had made, which was, By God, I will not approach her after today. So it was said to him, Why did you forbid what God has made lawful to you? meaning, he did not refrain from it because of the oath. Meaning, he went ahead and disbelieved. The second: It is an oath that must be expiated. This was stated by Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, Umar ibn al-Khattab, Abdullah ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas, Aisha may God be pleased with them, and al-Awza’i, and it is what the verse implies. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: If a man forbids his wife to him, then it is an oath that must be expiated. Ibn Abbas said: You have in the Messenger of God an excellent example to follow, meaning that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade his female slave, so God the Almighty said: Why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you - until His saying - God has already prescribed for you a way to expiate your oaths, so he expiated for his oath and made what was forbidden an oath. Narrated by al-Daraqutni. Third: It requires expiation and is not an oath. This was stated by Ibn Mas`ud and Ibn Abbas in one of his two narrations, and by Al-Shafi`i in one of his two opinions. This opinion is questionable. The verse refutes it as follows. Fourth: It is a form of Zihar, and there is expiation for Zihar, as stated by Uthman, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and Ishaq. Fifth: If he intended to pronounce Zihar while intending that she was forbidden, just as his mother’s back was forbidden, then it was Zihar. If he intended to make her specific property absolutely forbidden to him without divorce, then he must pay expiation for an oath. If he did not intend anything, then he must pay expiation for an oath. This was stated by Al-Shafi’i. Sixth: It is a revocable divorce, as stated by Omar bin Al-Khattab, Al-Zuhri, Abdul Aziz bin Abi Salamah, and Ibn Al-Majishun. Seventh: It is an irrevocable divorce. This was stated by Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman and Zayd ibn Thabit. It was also narrated by Ibn Khuwayz Mandad on the authority of Malik. The eighth: It is three divorces, as stated by Ali bin Abi Talib, Zaid bin Thabit, and Abu Hurairah. Ninth: It is three for a woman who has been penetrated, and he intends it for a woman who has not been penetrated. This was said by Al-Hasan and Ali bin Zaid Al-Hakam, and it is the well-known Maliki school of thought. And he lived with her: It is three, and he does not intend it in any case or place, even if he did not enter, said Abdul Malik in Al-Mabsut, and Ibn Abi Laila said the same. Eleventh: It is for the one with whom he has not consummated the marriage once, and for the one with whom he has consummated the marriage three times. This was stated by Abu Mus`ab and Muhammad ibn `Abd al-Hakam. Twelfth: If he intended divorce or zihar, then what he intended will be as he intended. If he intended divorce, then one divorce is irrevocable unless he intended three. If he intended two divorces, then one divorce is permissible. If he did not intend anything, then it is an oath and the man is free from his wife. This was stated by Abu Hanifa and his companions. Zufar said something similar, except that he said, If he intended two divorces, we oblige him. Thirteenth: The intention of Zihar will not benefit him, but rather it will be a divorce, said Ibn Al-Qasim. Fourteenth: Yahya bin Omar said: It is considered a divorce. If he takes her back, he is not permitted to have intercourse with her until he pays the expiation for Zihar. Fifteenth: If he intended divorce, then he may do as many times as he wanted. But if he intended only one divorce, then it is revocable. This is the opinion of Al-Shafi’i may God be pleased with him. A similar opinion was narrated from Abu Bakr, Umar, and others among the Companions and Followers. Sixteenth: If he intended three, then three, and if one, then one. If he intended an oath, then it is an oath. If he did not intend anything, then nothing is due on him. This is the opinion of Sufyan. Al-Awza’i and Abu Thawr said something similar, except that they said: If he did not intend anything, then it is one. Seventeenth: He has his intention and it cannot be less than one, as stated by Abu Shahab. And if he does not intend anything, then it is nothing, as stated by Ibn al-Arabi. And I saw from Saeed bin Jubair, which is: Eighteenth: He must free a slave even if he does not make it a form of Zihar. I do not know of any justification for this, and it is not far-fetched in my opinion. I said: Al-Daraqutni mentioned it in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and he said: Al-Husayn bin Ismail told us, he said: Muhammad bin Mansour told us, he said: Rawh told us, he said: Sufyan Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that a man came to him and said: I have made my wife forbidden to me. He said: You have lied! It is not forbidden to you. Then he recited: O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you? The most severe expiation is upon you: freeing a slave. A group of the people of interpretation said: When this verse was revealed, he expiated for his oath by freeing a slave, and he returned to Maria, Zayd bin Aslam and others said. Fifth: Our scholars said: The reason for the difference of opinion on this matter is that there is no reliable text or authentic apparent meaning on this issue in the Book of God or in the Sunnah of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Therefore, scholars have argued over it. Those who adhere to the original innocence said: There is no ruling, so nothing is required of it. As for those who say it is an oath, they said: God called it an oath. As for those who say: Atonement is required for it, but it is not an oath, they based their opinion on one of two matters: First, they assumed that God the Most High had made atonement obligatory for it, even if it is not an oath. Second, according to them, the meaning of an oath is prohibition, so atonement is applied to the meaning. As for those who say it is a revocable divorce, they interpret the wording according to its lesser meaning, and a revocable divorce is also prohibited in intercourse, so the wording is interpreted accordingly. This is binding on Malik, because he said: A revocable divorce is prohibited in intercourse. The same applies to those who say it is three, so they interpret it according to its greater meaning, which is the three divorces. As for those who say it is zihar, this is because it is the least degree of prohibition, as it is a prohibition that does not raise the degrees of marriage. As for those who said: It is an irrevocable divorce, they based their decision on the fact that a revocable divorce does not forbid the divorced woman, and that an irrevocable divorce forbids her. As for the statement of Yahya ibn Umar, he took precautions by making it a divorce, and when he took her back, he took precautions by requiring expiation. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is not valid because it combines opposites, as zihar and divorce cannot be combined in the meaning of one word, so there is no point in taking precautions in what cannot be combined in evidence. As for those who said: He should intend it with the one with whom he did not consummate the marriage, because one pronouncement makes her distinct and forbids her by law and unanimously agreed upon. Similarly, those who did not rule on the basis of their intention said: One pronouncement is sufficient before consummation in forbidding the wife by consensus, so it is sufficient by adopting the agreed upon minimum. As for those who said: It is three pronouncements with both, they took the greater ruling, if he had stated the three, it would have been as valid with the one with whom he did not consummate the marriage as it was with the one with whom he consummated the marriage. The meaning should be the same, which is forbidding. And God knows best. And all of this applies to the wife. As for the female slave, none of that is required of her, unless he intends it as emancipation according to Malik. The majority of scholars are of the view that he must offer expiation for breaking an oath. Ibn al-Arabi said: The correct view is that it is one divorce, because if he had mentioned divorce, the minimum would be one, unless he pronounces it more than once. Similarly, if it is a prohibition, the minimum would be unless it is restricted to a greater number, such as if he says: You are forbidden to me except after marriage. This clearly indicates what is intended. I said: Most of the commentators agree that the verse was revealed about Hafsah when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was alone in her house with his slave girl. This was mentioned by al-Tha’labi. Based on this, it is as if he said: What you forbade yourself is not forbidden to you, but you must make expiation for an oath. This also applies to the prohibition of honey and the slave girl. It is as if he said: What you forbade is not forbidden to you, but you added an oath to the prohibition, so make expiation for the oath. This is correct, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade it and then swore, as al-Daraqutni mentioned. Al-Bukhari mentioned its meaning in the story of honey on the authority of Ubayd ibn Umair on the authority of Aisha, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to drink honey at Zainab bint Jahsh’s house and stay with her. Hafsa and I conspired that whichever of us he entered upon should say: ‘Did you eat maghāfir? I smell the odor of maghāfir on you!’ He said: ‘No, but I drank honey and I will not do it again, and I swore not to tell anyone about that. ’ Seeking to please his wives,’ meaning by his saying: ‘And I will not do it again’ in the sense of prohibition. And by his saying: ‘I swore’, that is, by God, as evidenced by the fact that God, the Most High, sent down to him a rebuke for that and directed him to expiate the oath by His saying: ‘O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you? ’ He meant the forbidden honey by His saying: ‘I will not do it again. ’ ‘Seeking the pleasure of your wives. ’ That is, you do that seeking their pleasure. ’And God is Forgiving and Merciful. ’ Forgiving when He requires rebuke, Merciful, He removes blame. It has been said that this was a sin.” Of the minor sins. The correct view is that it is a reproach for neglecting the first, and that he did not commit any minor or major sins.
66:2: There are three issues: First: The Almighty's statement: God has prescribed for you the expiation of your oaths. The expiation of an oath is its expiation. That is, if you wish to make permissible what was sworn to, which is His statement in Surat al-Ma’idah 5:Then its expiation is the feeding of ten poor people. (al-Ma’idah 5:89). From this we conclude that whoever forbids something of food or drink, it is not forbidden according to him, because the expiation is for an oath, not for the prohibition, as we have explained. Abu Hanifa considers it an oath in everything, and considers the intended benefit of what is forbidden. So, if he forbids food, he has sworn to eat it, or his mother, he has sworn to have intercourse with her, or his wife, he has sworn to divorce her if he had no intention of doing so. If he intended to pronounce Zihar, then it is a Zihar, and if he intended to divorce, then it is an irrevocable divorce. The same applies if he intended two or three. If he says, I intended to lie, it is a debt between him and God Almighty. He does not owe a court to invalidate the oath. If he says: Everything permissible to him is forbidden, then he is liable for food and drink if he did not intend it that way. Otherwise, he is liable for what he intended. Al-Shafi'i does not consider it an oath, but rather a reason for expiation for women only. If he intended divorce, then it is revocable in his view, as explained above. If he swears that he will not eat it, he has broken his oath and must fulfill his obligation by offering expiation. Second: If he forbids his female slave or wife, then he must make expiation for an oath, as in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: If a man forbids his wife, then it is an oath for which he must make expiation. And he said: Indeed in the Messenger of God you have an excellent example to follow. Third: It was said that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) atoned for his oath. Al-Hasan said: He did not atoned because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had forgiven him for his past and future sins. The expiation for an oath in this Surah was only commanded to the Ummah, but the first is more correct, and that what is meant by that is the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Then the Ummah follows his example in that. We have already mentioned from Zayd ibn Aslam that he (peace be upon him) atoned by freeing a slave. And from Muqatil that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) freed a slave in order to forbid Mariyah. And God knows best. It was said: That is, God has made permissible for you the right hand to possess, so He explained in His statement, There is no blame upon the Prophet for what God has made obligatory for him (al-Ahzab 33:38), that is, in what He has made permissible for him regarding permissible women. That is, He made permissible for you the right hand to possess, so Mariyah was not forbidden to you even though God had made her permissible for you. It was said: The permissibility of an oath is the exception, that is, God has made the exception for you that which removes an oath. Then, according to some people, it is permissible to make an exception from oaths whenever he wishes, even if he is permissible for a period. According to most scholars, it is not permissible except when connected, so it is as if he said: Make an exception after this regarding what you swear. And the dissolution of an oath is its dissolution by expiation, and the original is tahlila, but it was assimilated. And taf’ila is from the verbal nouns of fa’ala, like naming and recommending. So, the dissolution is the dissolution of an oath. So, the oath is a contract and expiation is a solution. And it was said: the dissolution is expiation, meaning that it makes permissible for the one who swears what he has forbidden for himself, meaning if he expiates, he becomes as if he has not made it permissible. And God is your Master is your Guardian and Supporter by removing the prohibition on what you forbid for yourselves, and by granting you permission to dissolution your oaths by expiation and by rewarding you for what you give in expiation.
66:3: God the Almighty said: And when the Prophet confided a statement to one of his wives. That is, remember when the Prophet confided a statement to Hafsa, meaning that he forbade Maria to himself and kept it a secret from her. Al-Kalbi said: He confided in her that your father and Aisha’s father would be the successors over my nation after me. Ibn Abbas said the same. He said: He confided the matter of the caliphate after him to Hafsa, and she mentioned it to him. Al-Daraqutni narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Al-Kalbi on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of God the Almighty: And when the Prophet confided a statement to one of his wives, he said: “Hafsah informed the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from Umm Ibrahim, so he said: ‘Do not inform Aisha.’ He also said to her: ‘Your father and her father will rule or will be separated after me, so do not inform Aisha.’” Hafsah went and informed Aisha, and God revealed it to him. He recognized some of it and ignored some of it. He said: He ignored his statement: ‘Your father and her father will be separated after me.’ The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) disliked for that to be spread among the people. So when she informed him of it means that Aisha informed him of it because of the reconciliation that had existed between them, and they were both supporting each other against the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). And God revealed it to him means that God informed him that she had informed him of it. Talhah ibn Musarraf read So when he informed, and they are two languages: anba’ and naba’. The meaning of He knew some of it and ignored some of it is that Hafsa knew some of what was revealed to him, that she had told Aisha what he had forbidden her to tell her, and he ignored some of it out of generosity, as al-Suddi said. Al-Hasan said: No generous person has ever fully understood the meaning of the verse: He recognized some of it and ignored some. Muqatil said: Meaning, he informed her of some of what she said to Aisha, which is the hadith of his concubine, but he did not inform her of some of it, which is the statement of Hafsa to Aisha: Abu Bakr and Umar will rule later. The common people read upon him with a shaddah, and its meaning is what we have mentioned. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim preferred this, as indicated by the statement of God: And ignored some, meaning he did not inform her of it. If it was with a shaddah, he would have said the opposite and denied some. Ali, Talha bin Musarraf, Abu Abd al-Rahman as-Sulami, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Kalbi, al-Kisa’i, and al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Bakr, read he recognized with a shaddah. Ata’ said: When Abu Abd al-Rahman as-Sulami read it to a man, he would stone him with stones. Al-Farra’ said: The interpretation of God’s statement: He recognized some of it with a shaddah means he became angry and punished him. It is like saying to someone who wronged you: I will not let you know what you did, meaning I will punish you for it. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) rewarded her by divorcing her once. Umar said, “If there had been any good in the family of Al-Khattab, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) would not have divorced her.” Gabriel then ordered him to take her back and intercede on her behalf. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) kept away from his wives for a month and sat in the drinking place of Maria, the mother of Ibrahim, until the verse of prohibition was revealed, as mentioned above. It was also said that he then divorced her until Gabriel said to him, Do not divorce her, for she fasts and prays regularly, and she is one of your wives in Paradise. But he did not divorce her. When he informed her of it, meaning he informed Hafsa of what God had revealed to him, she said, ‘Who told you this, O Messenger of God, about me?’ She thought that Aisha had told him, so he (peace and blessings be upon him) said, The All-Knowing, All-Aware informed me, meaning the One from whom nothing is hidden. This is a substitute for the two objects of anba’ and naba’, the first of which is transitive to an object, and the second of which is transitive to one object, because if naba’ and anba’ do not precede the subject and predicate, it is permissible to suffice with one object and two objects. But if they precede the subject and predicate, each one of them is transitive to three objects, and it is not permissible to limit oneself to the two without the third, because the third is the predicate of the subject in the original, so it is not limited to less than it, just as it is not limited to the subject without the predicate.
66:4: The Almighty's statement: If you both repent to God refers to Hafsah and Aishah, and He urged them to repent for their inclination towards disliking the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). Your hearts have indeed turned away means they have deviated and deviated from the truth. That is, they loved what the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) disliked, namely avoiding his concubine and avoiding honey. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) loved honey and women. Ibn Zayd said that their hearts were inclined because they were pleased that he was kept away from the mother of his concubine, and what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) disliked pleased them. It was also said: Your hearts have indeed turned away from repentance. He said: Your hearts have indeed turned away, and did not say: Your two hearts have indeed turned away. It is the custom of the Arabs when they mention two things from two people to pluralize them because it is not difficult. This meaning was previously mentioned in Al-Ma'idah in the statement of God (peace and blessings be upon him): Then cut off their hands (Al-Ma'idah 5:38). It was also said: whenever the addition is established in a dual form, the plural form is more appropriate because it is more possible and lighter. His statement, For your hearts have been corrupted, is not a consequence of the condition, because this corruption had already occurred, so the answer to the condition has been omitted because it was known. That is, if you repent, it would be better for you both, because your hearts have been corrupted. God the Almighty said: {And if they both conspire against him} meaning, you conspire and cooperate against the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) by disobeying and harming him. In Sahih Muslim, it is narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: I spent a year wanting to ask Umar ibn al-Khattab about a verse, but I was unable to ask him out of awe of him, until he went out for Hajj, so I went with him. When he returned, we were part of the way there, and he turned to the arak tree for some need, so I stopped until he finished, then I walked with him and said: O Commander of the Faithful, who were the two wives who conspired against the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him)? He said: Those were Hafsah and Aishah. I said to him: By God, I have wanted to ask you about this for a year, but I could not out of awe of you. He said: Do not do that. Whatever you think someone has knowledge of, ask me about it, and if I know it, I will inform you... And he mentioned the hadith. {For God is his Guardian} meaning his Guardian and Supporter, so their conspiring against him will not harm him. And Gabriel and the righteous believers. Ikrimah and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Abu Bakr and Umar, because they were the fathers of Aisha and Hafsa, and they were his helpers against them. It was also said: The righteous believers are Ali, may God be pleased with him. It was also said: The best of the believers. Salih is a generic name, as in the saying of God the Almighty: By time, indeed, mankind is in loss. (Al-'Asr: 1-2) This was said by Al-Tabari. It was also said: The righteous believers are the prophets, as was said by Al-Ala' ibn Ziyadah, Qatadah, and Sufyan. Ibn Zayd said: They are the angels. Al-Suddi said: They are the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was also said: And the righteous believers is not the singular form, but rather the righteous believers, so he added the righteous to the believers, and wrote without a waw on the form because the singular and plural forms are the same in it. There are also things in the Qur'an in which the ruling on the form varies but not the placement of the script. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, told me: “When the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, withdrew from his wives, I entered the mosque and saw people poking stones at him and saying: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, divorced his wives - and that was before they were commanded to wear the hijab.” Omar said: I said, I will know that day. He said, “So I went to Aisha and said, ‘O daughter of Abu Bakr, has your status reached such that you harm the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him)?’ I said, ‘What do you have to do with me, O son of Al-Khattab? Mind your own fault!’ He said, “So I went to Hafsa bint Omar and said to her, ‘O Hafsa, has your status reached such that you harm the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him)?’ By God, I know that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) does not love you, and were it not for me, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) would have divorced you.’ She cried bitterly. So I said to her, ‘Where is the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him)?’ She said, ‘He is in his closet in the living room.’ So I went in and saw Rabah, the servant of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), sitting on the lintel of the living room, dangling his legs over a wooden stump, which is a tree trunk that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) used to climb up and down. I called, ‘O Rabah, ask permission for me to see the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him).’ Rabah looked at the room and then at me but did not say anything.” Then I said: O Rabah, ask permission for me to see the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Rabah looked at the room, then at me, but did not say anything. Then I raised my voice and said: O Rabah, ask permission for me to see the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), for I think that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) thought that I came because of Hafsa. By God, if the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) orders me to strike her neck, I will strike her neck. I raised my voice, and he motioned to me to lower it. I entered upon the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and he was lying on a mat. I sat down, and he pulled his lower garment down over him, and he was not wearing anything else. The mat had left marks on his side. I looked into the Messenger of God’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) treasury and saw a handful of barley, about a sa’, and the same amount of dates in a corner of the room. I saw a fistful of barley, about a sa’, and a similar amount of dates in a corner of the room. I woke up, hanging up - he said - and my eyes filled with tears. He said: What makes you cry, O son of Al-Khattab? I said: O Prophet of God, why should I not cry while this mat has left marks on your side, and this is your closet and I see nothing in it except what I see! And that one is short and Khosrau is among the fruits and rivers, and you are the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and His chosen one, and this is your closet! He said: O son of Al-Khattab, are you not satisfied that we have the Hereafter and they have this world? I said: Yes. He said: When I entered, I saw anger on his face and said: O Messenger of God, what is difficult for you regarding women? If you divorce them, then God is with you and His angels and Gabriel and Michael and I and Abu Bakr and the believers are with you. And I rarely spoke - and I praise God - except that I hoped that God, the Almighty, would confirm what I said and revealed this verse, the verse of choice: Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you. “And if they both conspire against him, then indeed, God is his Protector, and [so will] Gabriel and the righteous believers and the angels after that, [will be] your helpers.” Aisha bin Abi Bakr and Hafsa used to conspire against the other wives of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). I said: O Messenger of God, have you divorced them? He said: No. I said: O Messenger of God, I entered the mosque and the Muslims were kicking themselves with pebbles saying: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) has divorced his wives. Should I go down and tell them that you have not divorced them? He said: Yes, if you wish. I kept talking to him until the anger disappeared from his face and he grimaced and smiled, and he had the most handsome smile of people. Then the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came down and I went down. I went down holding onto the tree trunk, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came down as if he was walking on the ground, not touching it with his hand. I said: O Messenger of God, I was only in the room for twenty-nine days. He said: The month is twenty-nine days. So I stood at the door of the mosque and called out at the top of my voice: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) has not divorced his wives. And this verse was revealed: “And when there comes to them information about security or fear, they broadcast it. But if they had referred it back to the Messenger or to those in authority among them, then those among them who can extract information from it would have known about it.” (An-Nisa’: 83). So I was the one who extracted that information, and God revealed the verse of choice. God's statement, and Gabriel has various meanings that were mentioned previously in Surat Al-Baqarah. It is also possible that it is in apposition to his Master Mawla, and the meaning is: God is his Master and Gabriel is his Master. So, one should not stop at his Master but stop at Gabriel, and and the righteous believers would be the subject and and the angels would be in apposition to it. Backup is the predicate, and it has the meaning of plural. The righteous believers are Abu Bakr, as stated by Al-Musayyab ibn Sharik. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Umar. Ikrimah said: Abu Bakr and Umar. Shaqiq narrated from Abdullah: "On the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) regarding God's statement, 'Indeed, God is his Master and Gabriel and the righteous believers,' he said: The righteous believers are Abu Bakr and Umar." It was also said: It is Ali. Asma' bint Umays said: "I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: "And the righteous believers is Ali ibn Abi Talib. Other statements were made regarding what was previously mentioned. It is possible that and Gabriel is the subject, and what follows it is in apposition to it. The predicate is backup, and it also has the meaning of plural. So, one should stop at his Master. It is possible that and Gabriel and the righteous believers is in apposition to his master, so it stops at the believers, and and the angels after that are a support is a subject and predicate. The meaning of support is helpers. It means supporters, like the Almighty’s saying: And excellent are those as companions (An-Nisa’: 69). Abu Ali said: The word fa’il is used to indicate abundance, like the Almighty’s saying: “And no close friend will ask about a close friend. They will see them” (al-Ma’arij 70:10). It was said that the support from them was to control the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in spending, and for this reason he swore off from them for a month and kept away from them. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, he said: “Abu Bakr entered seeking permission to see the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and found the people sitting at his door, and he had not given permission to any of them. He said: So he gave permission to Abu Bakr and he entered. Then Umar came and sought permission and he was given permission. He found the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sitting surrounded by his wives, silent and gloomy. He said: I will say something that will make the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) laugh. He said: O Messenger of God, if you saw the daughter of Kharijah asking me for maintenance. So I went to her and slapped her on the neck. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) laughed and said: They are around me as you see, asking me for maintenance. So Abu Bakr went to Aisha and slapped her on the neck, and Umar went to Hafsa and slapped her on the neck, both of them saying: You are asking the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) for something he does not have! They said: By God, we will never ask the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) for anything he does not have. Then he kept away from them for a month or twenty-nine.” Then this verse was revealed to him: O Prophet, tell your wives - until he reached - For the good among you is a great reward. We have already mentioned it in Surat Al-Ahzab.
66:5: The Almighty's saying: Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you women, It has been mentioned in Sahih that this verse was revealed on the tongue of Umar may God be pleased with him. Then it was said: Every perhaps in the Quran is obligatory, except for this. It was also said: It is obligatory, but God, the Almighty, made it conditional, which is divorce, and He did not divorce them. That He will substitute for him wives better than you, because if you had been better than them, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would not have divorced you. As-Suddi said its meaning. It was also said: This is a promise from God, the Almighty, to His Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him), that if he divorced them in this world, He would marry him to better women in this world and cause them to ejaculate. God knew that he would not divorce them, but He informed of His power, that if he divorced them, He would substitute for him wives better than them, to frighten them. It is like the Almighty's saying: But if you turn away, He will replace you with another people, which is an explanation of the power and a frightening for them, not that there is anyone in existence better than the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). God the Almighty says: Muslims meaning sincere, as said by Saeed bin Jubair. It was also said that it means submitting to the command of God the Almighty and the command of His Messenger. Believers believing in what they were commanded and forbidden to do. Qanitan obedient. And qanut means obedience. It has been mentioned before. Ta’ibat meaning from their sins, as said by Al-Suddi. It was also said that they returned to the command of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, leaving what they fight against themselves. Abidat meaning they worship God the Almighty a lot. Ibn Abbas said: Every act of worship in the Quran is monotheism. Sa’ihat meaning correct, as said by Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan and Ibn Jubair. Zayd bin Aslam, his son Abd Al-Rahman and Yaman said: Emigrants. Zayd said: There is no travel in the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, except emigration. And no travel is roaming the earth. Al-Farra’, Al-Qutbi and others said: The fasting person is called a traveler because the traveler has no provisions with him, and only he who finds food eats. It was said: They are going in the obedience of God the Almighty, from the word saha when it gives. It was mentioned in Surah Bara’ah, and praise be to God. Thybaat and abkaran meaning some of them are thaybaan and some are virgins. It was said: The thayba is called thaybaan because she returns to her husband if he stays with her, or someone else if he leaves her. It was said: Because she is fixed in her parents’ house. This is more correct, because not every thaybaan returns to a husband. As for the virgin, she is the chaste woman. She was called bukr because she is in the first state in which she was created. Al-Kalbi said: By thaybaan he meant someone like Asiya, the wife of Pharaoh, and by bukr he meant someone like Mary, the daughter of Imran. I said: This only applies to the opinion of those who said: The exchange is a promise from God to His Prophet that if he divorced them in this world, He would marry him to someone better than them in the Hereafter. And God knows best.
66:6: There is only one issue - the command to protect oneself and one's family from the Fire. Ad-Dahhak said: Its meaning is protect yourselves and your families, so protect themselves from the Fire. Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Protect yourselves and command your families to remember God and supplicate so that God may protect them through you. Ali may God be pleased with him, Qatadah, and Mujahid said: Protect yourselves with your actions and protect your families with your advice. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is correct, and the understanding that it gives is the conjunction that requires sharing between the conjoined and the conjoined to it in the meaning of the verb, like his saying: I fed her straw and cold water And as he said: I saw your husband in the battlefield, carrying a sword and a spear. A man should reform himself through obedience and reform his family as a shepherd reforms his flock. In the authentic hadith, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Each of you is a shepherd and each of you is responsible for his flock. The ruler over the people is a shepherd and is responsible for them. A man is a shepherd over his family and is responsible for them.” Al-Hasan expressed this in this verse by saying: He commands them and forbids them. Some scholars said that when God said, Protect yourselves, it includes children because children are part of him. It also includes children in His statement, And there is no blame upon you if you eat from your houses (An-Nur 24:61). They did not mention them individually like all other relatives. He teaches him what is permissible and what is forbidden, and keeps him away from sins and wrongdoings, and other rulings. He, peace be upon him, said: The right of the child over the father is that he should give him a good name, teach him how to write, and marry him off when he reaches maturity. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: Nothing a father can give his son is better than good manners. Umar ibn Shuaib narrated on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him): Command your children to pray when they are seven, and beat them if they do not pray when they are ten, and separate them in their beds. This was narrated by a group of hadith scholars. This is the wording of Abu Dawud. It was also narrated on the authority of Samurah ibn Jundub who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Command the boy to pray when he reaches the age of seven, and beat him if he does not pray when he reaches the age of ten. He also informs his family of the time of prayer, the obligation of fasting, and the obligation of breaking the fast when it is obligatory, based on the narration of the crescent moon. It was narrated on the authority of Muslim: “When the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) performed the witr prayer, he would say: ‘Get up and perform the witr prayer, Aisha.’” It was also narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “May God have mercy on a man who gets up at night to pray, then wakes his family up. If they do not get up, he sprinkles water on their face. May God have mercy on a woman who gets up at night to pray and wakes her husband up. If he does not get up, she sprinkles water on his face.” And from this is his saying, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him: Wake up the women of the chamber. This is included in the general meaning of the saying of God the Almighty: And cooperate in righteousness and piety. (al-Ma’idah 5:2) Al-Qushayri mentioned that when this verse was revealed, ‘Umar may God be pleased with him said: O Messenger of God, we purify ourselves, but what about our families? He said: You forbid them from what He forbade you and command them to do what God has commanded. Muqatil said: That is a duty upon him regarding himself, his children, his family, his male and female slaves. Al-Kiya said: It is upon us to teach our children and families religion and goodness, and the indispensable good manners they need. This is the saying of God the Almighty: And enjoin prayer upon your family and be constant therein. (Ta-Ha: 132) Similar to the saying of God the Almighty to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): And warn your nearest relatives. And in the hadith: And command them to pray when they are seven years old. Its fuel is men and stones. This is mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. Over it are angels, harsh and severe. That is, the guardian angels are harsh-hearted and show no mercy when asked for mercy. They were created from wrath, and they are made to love punishing people just as eating food and drinking is made beloved to the children of Adam. Strong means strong in body. It was also said: harsh in speech and severe in action. It was also said: harsh in taking the people of Hell and severe with them. It is said that someone is harsh with someone, meaning he is strong against him and tortures him with various types of torture. It was also said: harsh means the size of their bodies, and severe means strength. Ibn Abbas said: The distance between the shoulders of one of them is a year's journey, and the strength of one of them is such that he can strike with a whip and push seventy thousand people into the depths of Hell with that strike. Ibn Wahb said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd narrated to us that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said about the keepers of Hell: The distance between the shoulders of one of you is like the distance between the east and the west. God the Almighty says: They do not disobey God in what He commands them. That is, they do not disobey Him in His command, whether by adding or subtracting from it. And they do what they are commanded. That is, at the appointed time, neither delaying nor advancing it. It was also said that their pleasure is in obeying God’s command, just as the joy of the people of Paradise in being in Paradise was mentioned after the Mu’tazila. They believe that it is impossible to be tasked tomorrow. The belief of the people of truth is well known that God tasks the servant today and tomorrow, and the task is not denied with regard to the angels. And God can do whatever He wills.
66:7: The Almighty says: O you who have disbelieved, make no excuses this Day, for your excuses will be of no use. This prohibition is to achieve despair. You will only be recompensed for what you used to do in this world. Similar to this is: So on that Day, no excuse will benefit those who did wrong, nor will they be asked to repent. (al-Rum 30:57). This has already been mentioned.
66:8: God the Almighty says: O you who have believed, repent to God with sincere repentance. There are two issues in this: The first: God the Almighty's saying: O you who have believed, repent to God is a command to repent, and it is obligatory for everyone in all circumstances and at all times. Its explanation and discussion have been presented in An-Nisa' and other verses. Sincere repentance The scholars and masters of hearts have differed in their expressions regarding sincere repentance, and there are twenty-three opinions. It was said: It is that after which there is no return, just as milk does not return to the udder. This was narrated on the authority of Umar ibn Mas'ud, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may God be pleased with them. Mu'adh traced it back to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. Qatadah said: Sincere is the honest and sincere one. It was also said: It is the pure one. It is said: He sincerely said: He was sincere, meaning he was sincere in his speech to him. Al-Hasan said: Sincere means he hates the sin that he loved and seeks forgiveness for it when he remembers it. It was also said: It is that which he does not trust will be accepted and he is afraid of it. It was also said: It is that for which there is no need for repentance. Al-Kalbi said: Sincere repentance is regret in the heart, seeking forgiveness with the tongue, ceasing to sin, and being reassured that one will not return to it. He said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: It is the accepted repentance, and it is not accepted unless three conditions are met: fear that it will not be accepted, hope that it will be accepted, and persistence in acts of obedience. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: A repentance with which you sincerely advise yourselves. Al-Qurazi said: It includes four things: seeking forgiveness with the tongue, desisting with the body, intending to refrain from returning to sin, and avoiding bad friends. Sufyan al-Thawri said: The signs of sincere repentance are four: fewness, illness, humiliation, and alienation. Al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad said: It is that the sin is between his eyes, as if he is looking at it. Similar to it is narrated by Ibn al-Sammak: That you place the sin for which you felt shame before God before your eyes and prepare for what awaits you. Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: It is that the earth becomes narrow for you despite its vastness, and your soul becomes narrow for you, like the three who were left behind. Abu Bakr Al-Wasiti said: It is repentance not for the loss of compensation, because whoever commits a sin in this world for his own comfort and then repents seeking his comfort in the hereafter, his repentance is for the sake of preserving himself, not God. Abu Bakr Al-Daqqaq Al-Misri said: Sincere repentance is restoring injustices, making amends to opponents, and constantly performing acts of obedience. Ruwaym said: It is to have a face for God and not a back, just as you were a back to Him when you sinned. Dhu Al-Nun said: There are three signs of sincere repentance: little speech, little food, and little sleep. Shaqiq said: It is that its owner frequently blames himself and does not refrain from regret, so that he may escape its harms with safety. Sari Al-Saqti said: Sincere repentance is not valid except with sincere advice from himself and the believers, because whoever accompanies his repentance loves for people to be like him. Al-Junayd said: Sincere repentance is to forget the sin and never mention it, because whoever has sincere repentance becomes a lover of God, and whoever loves God forgets everything besides God. Dhu Al-Adhanin said: It is when its owner has tears streaming down his cheeks and a heart that is stubborn and free from sins. Fath Al-Mawsili said: Its signs are three: opposing desires, crying a lot, and enduring hunger and thirst. Sahl bin Abdullah Al-Tustari said: It is repentance for Ahl Al-Sunnah wal-Jama’ah, because there is no repentance for the innovator, as evidenced by the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): God has prevented every innovator from repenting. And Hudhayfah said: It is enough evil for a man to repent from a sin and then return to it. The root of sincere repentance is from purity. It is said: This is sincere honey when it is purified from wax. It is also said that it is derived from nasaha, which means sewing. There are two ways to take it from it: First, because it is a repentance that has perfected and secured his obedience, just as a tailor perfects and secures a garment with his sewing. Second, because it has gathered his children and the friends of God and attached him to them, just as a tailor gathers a garment and sticks some parts together. The general reading is nasooh with a fatha on the noon, as a description of repentance, like a patient woman, meaning a repentance that is sincere and sincere. Al-Hasan, Kharijah, and Abu Bakr on the authority of Asim read it with a damma, and its interpretation according to this reading is: a sincere repentance for yourselves. It was said: it is permissible for it to be nasooh, the plural of nasih, or it can be a verbal noun, it is said: nasaha nasiha and nasuhan. Fa’ala and fa’ul may agree in verbal nouns, like adh-dahab and adh-dhub. Al-Mubarrad said: he meant a sincere repentance, it is said: I advised sincerely, nasiha and nasuhan. Second: Concerning the things for which one repents and how to repent from them. The scholars said: The sin for which one repents is either a right owed to God or to other human beings. If it is a right owed to God, such as neglecting a prayer, then repentance is not valid unless one adds regret to making up for what one has missed. The same applies if it involves neglecting to fast or neglecting to pay zakat. If it involves unjust killing, then one can obtain retaliation if it is due and required. If it is slander that warrants the prescribed punishment, then one should offer one's back to be flogged if required. If one is pardoned, then regret and a resolve to sincerely refrain from committing the crime are sufficient. Similarly, if one is pardoned for murder in exchange for money, then one must pay it back if one has the means. God the Almighty says: But if anyone is pardoned by his brother in exchange for money, then there should be a just settlement and payment to him with good conduct. (al-Baqarah 2:178) If it is one of the prescribed punishments of God, whatever it may be, then if one repents to God the Almighty with true regret, then the penalty is dropped from him. God the Almighty has stipulated that the punishment for those who wage war is dropped if they repent before being overpowered, as explained above. The same applies to drinkers, thieves, and adulterers: if they reform and repent, and this is known about them, and then they are brought before the Imam, he should not impose the punishment on them. If they are brought before him and say, We repent, they should not be left alone, and in this case they are like those who wage war if they are defeated. This is the Shafi'i school of thought. If the sin is one of oppression against people, then repentance is not valid unless it is returned to its perpetrator and he abandons it—whether the perpetrator is known to him or not—if he is able to do so. If he is not able, then he should resolve to repay it if he is able, as soon as possible. If he has harmed a Muslim, and that person is unaware of it or does not know where it came from, then he should remove that harm from him, then he should ask him to pardon him and seek forgiveness for him. If he pardons him, then the sin is dropped. If he sends someone to ask for this, and the oppressed person pardons his oppressor—whether he knows him personally or not—then that is valid. If a man wrongs another man by frightening him unjustly, or distressing him, or slapping him unjustly, or whipping him with a whip and causing him pain, and then the man comes to him seeking forgiveness, regretting what he did and intending not to do it again, and he continues to humble himself before him until he is content and forgives him, then that sin is dropped from him. The same applies if he insulted him with an unlawful act. God Almighty says: Perhaps your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds. “Perhaps” from God is obligatory. This is the meaning of the Prophet’s saying, He who repents from sin is like one who has no sin. And that is in the nominative case as the subject of perhaps. God the Almighty says: And admit you is in apposition to He will disbelieve. Ibn Abi Ubla read And admit you in the subjunctive mood, in apposition to the position of He may disbelieve. It is as if it was said: Repent, and He will require the expiation of your misdeeds, and He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow. The Day when God will not disgrace the Prophet is the agent in The Day: He will admit you or an implied verb, and the meaning of reward here is he will punish, meaning He will not punish him nor those who believed with him. Their light proceeds before them and on their right was mentioned previously in Surat Al-Hadid. They will say, Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us. Indeed, You are over all things competent." Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and others said: This is the supplication of the believers when God extinguished the light of the hypocrites, as was mentioned previously in Surat Al-Hadid.
66:9: The Almighty's saying: O Prophet, strive hard against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh upon them. This contains one issue - which is being harsh with regard to the religion of God. So He commanded him to strive against the disbelievers with the sword, good exhortation, and calling to God. And against the hypocrites with harshness and establishing proof, and to inform them of their condition in the Hereafter, and that they have no light by which to cross the Sirat with the believers. Al-Hasan said: That is, strive against them by implementing the prescribed punishments on them, because they were committing acts that warranted the prescribed punishments, and the prescribed punishments were implemented against them. And their refuge is Hell refers to both types. And wretched is the destination means the place of return.
66:10: God the Almighty set forth this parable to warn that no one can avail a relative or a close friend in the Hereafter if religion separates them. The name of Noah's wife was Walihah, and the name of Lot's wife was Wa'lah, said by Muqatil. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her: Gabriel came down to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and informed him that Noah's wife was Waghlah and Lot's wife's name was Wa'lah. But they betrayed them Ikrimah and Ad-Dahhak said: By disbelief. Sulayman ibn Ruqayyah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Noah's wife used to tell the people that he was crazy. And Lot's wife used to tell about his guests. And he the Prophet narrated: No prophet's wife ever betrayed him. This is the consensus of the commentators, as mentioned by Al-Qushayri. Their betrayal was in religion, and they were polytheists. It was also said that they were hypocrites. It was also said that their betrayal was gossiping: if God revealed something to them, they would divulge it to the polytheists, said Ad-Dahhak. It was said: Whenever a guest visited Lot's wife, she would smoke to let her people know that a guest had visited him, because they were accustomed to having intercourse with men. But they could not avail them at all against God meaning, Noah and Lot, despite their honor with God, did not ward off any of God's punishment from their wives - because they disobeyed, as a reminder that punishment is warded off by obedience, not by intercession. It was said: The disbelievers of Mecca mocked and said: Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, will intercede for us. God, the Most High, explained that his intercession would not benefit the disbelievers of Mecca, even if they were relatives, just as the intercession of Noah for his wife and the intercession of Lot for his wife would not benefit them, despite their closeness to them due to their disbelief. It was said to them: Enter the Fire with those who enter in the Hereafter, as is said to the disbelievers of Mecca and others. Then it was said: It is permissible for Noah's wife to be a substitute for His saying: for example, assuming the addition is omitted, meaning God set an example like Noah's wife. It is also permissible for them to be objects.
66:11: God the Almighty says: "And God presents an example to those who believe: the wife of Pharaoh." Her name was Asiyah bint Muzahim. Yahya ibn Salam said: His statement, God presents an example to those who disbelieve is an example that God presented to warn Aisha and Hafsa against disobedience when they conspired against the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Then He presented to them an example of the wife of Pharaoh and Mary, the daughter of Imran, to encourage them to adhere to obedience and steadfastness in religion. It was said: This is an exhortation to the believers to be patient in times of hardship, meaning do not be weaker in patience in times of hardship than the wife of Pharaoh when she endured Pharaoh's harm. Asiyah believed in Moses, and it was said that she was Moses' aunt who believed in him. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: Pharaoh found out about his wife's faith, so he went out to the crowd and said to them: What do you know about Asiyah bint Muzahim? They praised her. He said to them: She worships a god other than me. They said to him: Kill her. So he nailed pegs to her and strengthened her hands and feet, and she said, My Lord, build for me, near You, a house in Paradise. This coincided with the arrival of Pharaoh, and she laughed when she saw her house in Paradise. Pharaoh said, Aren't you amazed at her madness? We are tormenting her while she laughs. So he took her soul. Salman al-Farsi said, as narrated by Abu Uthman al-Nahdi: She was tormented by the sun, and when the heat of the sun harmed her, the angels shaded her with their wings. It was also said that he nailed her hands and feet to the sun and placed a millstone on her back, and God made her rise until she saw her place in Paradise. It was also said that when she said, My Lord, build for me, near You, a house in Paradise, she saw her house in Paradise being built. It was also said that it was made of pearls, according to al-Hasan. When she said, And save me, God saved her in the most honorable way, raising her to Paradise, where she eats, drinks, and enjoys. The meaning of from Pharaoh and his deeds refers to deeds of disbelief. It was also said that it refers to his knowledge of his torment, injustice, and gloating. Ibn Abbas said: It refers to sexual intercourse. And save me from the wrongdoing people. Al-Kalbi said: The people of Egypt. Muqatil: The Copts. Al-Hasan and Ibn Kaysan said: God saved her in the most honorable way and raised her to Paradise, where she eats and drinks.
66:12: God the Almighty says: And Mary, the daughter of Imran meaning, remember Mary. It was said that it is in apposition to the wife of Pharaoh. The meaning is: God sets forth an example of Mary, the daughter of Imran, and her patience in the face of the Jews' harm. Who guarded her chastity meaning from indecencies. The commentators said that what is meant by chastity here is the outer garment, because He said: Then We breathed into it of Our spirit and Gabriel, peace be upon him, only breathed into her outer garment and did not breathe into her vagina. According to Abu's reading, it is Then We breathed into her outer garment of Our spirit. Every tear in a garment is called an outer garment, and from this is the saying of God the Almighty: And she had no privations (Qaf: 6). It is possible that she guarded her chastity and the spirit was breathed into her outer garment. The meaning of Then We breathed is that We sent Gabriel, and he breathed into her outer garment of Our spirit meaning a spirit from Our spirits, which is the spirit of Jesus. This has been fully explained at the end of Surat An-Nisa', and praise be to God. And she believed in the words of her Lord is the general reading and sadaqqa with emphasis. Humayd and al-Amawi read sadaqqa with emphasis. In the words of her Lord is Gabriel's saying to her: I am only the Messenger of your Lord Maryam 19:19. Muqatil said: By the words he means Jesus and that he is a prophet and Jesus is the Word of God. This has been mentioned before. Al-Hasan and Abu al-Aaliyah read it with the word of her Lord and His Book. Abu Amr and Hafs from Asim read it with his books as a plural. From Abu Raja' with his books with a stressed ta'. The rest read it with his book as a sublime ta'. The book is intended to refer to the genus, so it has the meaning of every book that God revealed. And she was of the devout meaning of the obedient. It was also said: of those who pray between sunset and night prayers. He did not say of the devout because he meant and she was of the devout people. It is possible that this refers to her household, for they were obedient to God. On the authority of Muadh ibn Jabal may God be pleased with him, “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Khadija when she was dying: ‘Do you hate what has befallen you, while God has put good in hate? So when you visit your co-wives, greet them from me: Mary, daughter of Imran, Asiyah, daughter of Muzahim, and Kalima - or he said Hakima - daughter of Imran, the sister of Moses, son of Imran.’ She said: ‘May you be blessed with prosperity and children, O Messenger of God.’” Qatada narrated on the authority of Anas that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “From among the women of the world, four have kept you back: Mary, daughter of Imran, Khadija, daughter of Khuwaylid, Fatimah, daughter of Imran, and Asiyah, the wife of Pharaoh, daughter of Muzahim.” This has been discussed in detail in Al Imran, and praise be to God.
67:1: It was revealed in Mecca according to everyone. It is called Al-Waqiyah and Al-Munjiyyah. It has thirty verses. At-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: “A man from the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) pitched his tent over a grave, not realizing that it was a grave. Then, there was a grave of a man who was reciting Surat Al-Mulk until he completed it. He came to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and said: ‘O Messenger of God, I pitched my tent over a grave, not realizing that it was a grave, and then there was a grave of a man who was reciting Surat Al-Mulk until he completed it.’ The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: ‘It is the protector, the savior, it saves him from the punishment of the grave.’” He said: It is a hasan ghareeb hadith. It was also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: I wish that ‘Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion’ would be in the heart of every believer. Narrated by Al-Tha’labi. Abu Hurairah said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “There is a surah from the Book of God, which is only thirty verses, that will intercede for a man until it brings him out of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection and admits him to Paradise. It is Surat Al-Mulk.” At-Tirmidhi narrated it with the same meaning, and he said about it: It is a hasan hadith. Ibn Masoud said: When the deceased is placed in his grave, he will be approached from his feet and told: You have no right to him, for he used to stand and recite Surah Al-Mulk on his feet. Then he will be approached from his head and his tongue will say: You have no right to him, for he used to recite Surah Al-Mulk for me. Whoever recites it in one night will have done so much and in a better way. It was narrated that whoever recites it every night will not be harmed by trials. Tabarak is a verbal noun derived from barakah blessing. It has already been mentioned. Al-Hasan said: Taqadda sanctified. It has also been said that it lasts, meaning it is eternal, without beginning or end to its existence. In whose hand is the dominion means the dominion of the heavens and the earth in this world and the hereafter. Ibn Abbas said: In whose hand is the dominion, He honors whom He wills and humiliates whom He wills, He gives life and causes death, He enriches and impoverishes, He gives and withholds. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: His is the dominion of prophethood, by which He honors those who follow Him and humiliates those who oppose Him. And He is over all things competent of bestowing favors and vengeance.
67:2: There are two issues: The first: The Almighty's statement: Who created death and life. It was said that the meaning is that He created you for death and life, meaning for death in this world and life in the hereafter. He mentioned death before life because death is a form of subjugation, just as He mentioned daughters before sons, saying: He grants to whom He wills female children (al-Shura 42:49). It was also said that He mentioned it before because it was mentioned earlier, because things in the beginning were subject to the ruling of death, such as a drop of dust and the like. Qatada said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to say: God humiliated the children of Adam with death and made this world a place of life, then a place of death, and He made the hereafter a place of reward, then a place of eternity. Abu Ad-Darda' reported that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "Were it not for three things, the son of Adam would not bow his head: poverty, sickness, and death, and despite that, he will be rewarded." The second issue: Death and Life. Death was mentioned before life because the most powerful person who calls to action is he who sets his death before his eyes. It was mentioned before because it is more important in relation to the purpose for which the verse is presented. The scholars said: Death is not mere nonexistence, nor annihilation, nor diversion. Rather, it is the severing of the connection of the soul to the body and its separation, a barrier between them, a change of state, and a transition from one abode to another. Life is the opposite of that. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Al-Kalbi, and Muqatil that death and life are two bodies. He made death in the form of a ram that does not pass by anything or smell its scent without dying. He created life in the form of a female mare called Bilqaa - which is the one Gabriel and the prophets, peace be upon them, used to ride - its stride is as far as the eye can see. It is taller than a donkey and smaller than a mule. It does not pass by anything with its scent without it coming to life, and it does not step on anything without it coming to life. It is the one from whose trace the Samaritan took and threw it on the calf, and it came to life. Al-Tha’labi and Al-Qushayri narrated this from Ibn Abbas. Al-Mawardi narrated the same meaning from Muqatil and Al-Kalbi. I said: In the Qur’an, Say, ‘The Angel of Death who is set over you will take you’ (Surah al-Sajdah 32:11), And if you could but see when the angels take the souls of those who disbelieve (Surah Anfal: 50), then Our messengers will take them (Surah al-An’am 6:61), then He said, God takes the souls at the time of their death (Surah al-Zumar 39:42). So the intermediaries are honored angels, may God’s blessings be upon them. And He, glory be to Him, is the One who truly takes life. Death is represented by the ram in the Hereafter, which will be slaughtered on the Bridge, according to what was reported in the authentic hadith. What was mentioned from Ibn Abbas needs an authentic hadith to eliminate the excuse. And God knows best. Muqatil also said: He created death, meaning the sperm, the clot, and the lump of flesh, and He created life, meaning He created a human being and breathed the soul into him, so he became a human being. I said: This is a good statement, indicated by the statement of God the Almighty: {That He may test you which of you is best in deed}. This was discussed previously in Surat Al-Kahf. Al-Suddi said about the statement of God the Almighty: {He who created death and life to test you which of you is best in deed}, meaning that you are most mindful of death and best prepared for it, and most fearful and cautious of it. Ibn Umar said: “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited ‘Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion’ until he reached ‘which of you is best in deed’ and he said: ‘He who is most devout in refraining from the prohibitions of God and hastened to obey God.’” It was said that the meaning of ‘That He may test you which of you is best in deed – and He is the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving’ is to treat you as one who tests, that is, to test the servant with the death of someone dear to him to demonstrate his patience, and with life to demonstrate his gratitude. It was also said that God created death for resurrection and reward, and created life for testing. The lam in ‘that He may test you’ relates to the creation of life, not to the creation of death, as mentioned by Al-Zajjaj. Al-Farra and Al-Zajjaj also said: “The affliction did not fall on ‘any’ because between ‘balawa’ and ‘any’ there is an implied verb, as you say: ‘I tested you to see which of you is most obedient.’ Similar to this is the statement of God Almighty: ‘Ask them which of them will be responsible for that’ (Al-Qalam 68:40) meaning ask them then see which of them. ‘Any of you’ raised the subject and ‘better’ is its predicate. The meaning is: To test you and know which of you is best in deed. ‘And He is the Exalted in Might’ in taking revenge on those who disobey Him. ‘The Forgiving’ for those who repent.
67:3: The Almighty said: Who created seven heavens in layers meaning, one above the other, and the edges of them are joined together. This is also narrated from Ibn Abbas. In layers is an adjective for seven, so it is a description with a verbal noun. It was also said: a verbal noun meaning matching, meaning He created seven heavens and layered them in layers or matching. Or on the basis of they were layered layer by layer. Sibawayh said: He put layers in the accusative case because it is a second object. I said: So, creation means making and forming. Tabaq is the plural of tabaq, like camel and camels. It was also said that it is the plural of tabaqa. Abaan ibn Taghlib said: I heard some Bedouin criticizing a man, saying: His evil is tabaq, and his good is not lasting. It is permissible outside the Qur’an to say seven heavens tabaq, in the accusative case as an adjective for heavens. Similar to it is and seven green ears of corn (Yusuf 12:43). What do you see in the creation of the Most Gracious any inconsistency? The reading of Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i is from tafawat - without an alif - with a shaddah. This is the reading of Ibn Mas’ud and his companions. The rest are from tafawat with an alif. They are two dialects, like ta’ahudh and ta’ahhum, tadhammul and tahammul, tazahar and tadhafar, tasaagr and taghdir, tadhdhab and tadha’d, tafarad and taba’d, all with the same meaning. Abu Ubaid chose tafawat and cited as evidence a hadith from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr: The likes of me are missed by him in his daughters! An-Nahhas: This is a matter that is rejected by Abu Ubaid because tafawat is a variation with them. And tafawat in the verse is more similar. It is also said that something differs. It is said: the matter differed if it varied and was sold, meaning some of it missed the other. Don't you see that before it is the saying of the Almighty: Who created seven heavens in layers The meaning is: You do not see in the creation of the Most Gracious any crookedness, contradiction, or discrepancy - rather, it is straight and even, indicating its Creator - even if His forms and attributes differ. It is also said that what is meant is the heavens in particular, meaning you do not see any defect in the creation of the heavens. Its origin is from the word fawt, which means that something misses something else, so a defect occurs due to its lack of evenness. This is indicated by the saying of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him: from to separate. Abu Ubaidah said: It is said: Fawtawt means it was missed. Then He commanded that they look at His creation to consider it and reflect on His power, so He said: Then return your gaze - do you see any flaw? Meaning: Return your gaze to the sky. It is also said: Turn your gaze to the sky. It is also said: Strive by looking at the sky. The meanings are similar. He said: Return with the letter fa and there is no verb mentioned before it, because He said: what you see. The meaning is: Look, then look again. Do you see any cracks? Qatada said. Cracks are: the cracks, according to Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak. Qatada said: from a hole. As-Suddi said: from holes. Ibn Abbas said: from weakness. Its root is from the cracking and splitting, which means clefting. The poet said: He built for you, without pillars, a sky and adorned it, but what is in it is a crack. Another said: I split the heart and then poured your love into it, so why is the break complete? He penetrated where no drink, no drunkenness, and no pleasure reached.
67:4: The Almighty's saying: Then return your sight twice. The word twice is in the place of the verbal noun because it means two returns, meaning one time after another. The reason for ordering one to look twice is because if a person looks at something once, he will not see its fault unless he looks at it a second time. So the Almighty informed us that if he looks at the sky twice, he will not see any fault in it, but rather will be perplexed by looking at it. This is the meaning of the Almighty's saying: The sight will return to you humbled, meaning humbled, submissive, and distant from seeing any of that. It is said: Khasa'at al-Qalb meaning I drove it away and made it fly away. The dog was also said to have been driven away by himself, and it is transitive and intransitive. The dog was also said to have been driven away by his sight, meaning it became stricken. From this is the Almighty's saying: The sight will return to you humbled. Ibn Abbas said: The humiliated is the one who did not see what he desired. "And he is exhausted" means he has reached the peak of exhaustion. It has the meaning of an active participle, from "hasur" which means exhaustion. It may be an object of the verb to hold back after something, which is the meaning of Ibn Abbas’s statement. And from this is the poet’s statement: Whoever extends an eye beyond its limit, Khasan’s eye will turn back from him, holding back. It is said: He has lost his sight, meaning his sight has become dull and cut off due to a long period of time or something similar. He is also blind and lost. He said: I looked at her from Al-Muhassab in Mina, and he looked back, disappointed. Another one said, describing a camel: The sight of the two eyes is broken He put half of it in the adverbial case, meaning something like it. Another said: And the horses are disheveled, their steeds still sad, leaving their young ones on the road. It was said: He is the regretful one. And from this is the poet’s saying: Today I am not doing anything except, O daughter of the slave girl, I have gone away with regret What is meant by two balls here is abundance. The evidence for that is: The sight will return to you humbled and tired. This is evidence of the abundance of sight.
67:5: God the Almighty says: And We have certainly adorned the nearest heaven with lamps The plural of misbah is lamp. The planets are called lamps because of their illumination. And We made them shooting stars means We made them meteors, so the complement was omitted. The evidence for this is except for one who snatches a snatch, and he is pursued by a piercing meteor (al-Saffat 37:10). Based on this, the lamps do not disappear and are not stoned. It was said that the pronoun refers to the lamps, given that the shooting stars are among the most precious of the planets, and the planet itself does not fall, but rather something separates from it and is stoned without diminishing its light or image. Abu Ali said this in response to someone who asked: How can it be an adornment when it is shooting stars that do not last? Al-Mahdawi said: This is based on the fact that stealing is from the position of the planets. The first interpretation is that stealing is from passion, which is below the position of the planets. Al-Qushayri said: An example of what Abu Ali said is that we can say: It is an adornment before the devils are stoned with it. And rajum is the plural of rajm, which is a verbal noun from which that which is stoned is named. Qatada said: God created the stars for three purposes: as adornment for the sky, missiles to ward off the devils, and as signs to guide people on land, at sea, and at times. Whoever interprets them otherwise has undertaken what he has no knowledge of, and has transgressed and been unjust. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: By God, no one on earth has a star in the sky, but they take divination as a path and the stars as a cause. And We have prepared for them the punishment of the Blazing Fire means We have prepared for the devils the most severe burning. It is said: The fire was stoked, so it is raging and a blazing fire, like murdered and killed.
67:6: God Almighty says: When they are thrown into it, they will hear its deep breathing while it is…
67:7: The Almighty said: When they are thrown into it meaning the disbelievers. They will hear its roaring meaning a sound. Ibn Abbas said: The roaring is from their Hell when the disbelievers are thrown into it. It roars at them like a barley spit, then it exhales a sigh such that no one remains except in fear.
