It was said: The roaring is from the disbelievers when they are thrown into the Fire, said Ata'. The roaring is in the chests, and the exhalation is in the throat. This was mentioned in Surat Hud. And it is boiling meaning boiling, and from this is the saying of Hassan: You left your destiny with nothing in it, and the destiny of the people is a protector that wins Mujahid said: You will win over them as a little seed wins over a lot of water. Ibn Abbas said: You will boil them in the cauldron, and this is from the intensity of the flame of the fire due to the intensity of anger, just as you say so-and-so wins out of anger.
67:8: The Almighty says: It almost bursts into tears with rage meaning it bursts into pieces and separates parts from each other, as said by Saeed bin Jubair. Ibn Abbas, Ad-Dahhak, and Ibn Zayd said: it disperses. And from rage is the intense rage against the enemies of God Almighty. And it was said: from rage from boiling. The root of tamayuz is tamayuz. Whenever a company is thrown into it meaning a group of disbelievers. Its keepers will ask them by way of rebuke and reprimand. Did there not come to you a warner? meaning a messenger in this world who will warn them of this day so that you may beware.
67:9: They said, 'Yes, a warner has come to us.'" He warned us and frightened us. "But we denied and said, 'God has not sent down anything.'" That is, your tongues. "You are, O group of messengers, nothing but great error." They admitted to denying the messengers - then they admitted their ignorance.
67:10: They will say while they are in the Fire: If only we had listened to the warnings - meaning the messengers - they brought or understood from them. Ibn Abbas said: If only we had heard the guidance or attached it, or if only we had heard the hearing of one who gives and thinks, or understood the mind of one who distinguishes and considers. This indicates that the disbeliever has not been given any mind, and this has already been explained in At-Tur, and praise be to God. We would not have been among the companions of the Blaze means we would not have been among the people of the Fire. Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri reported that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The wicked will regret it on the Day of Resurrection and say, 'If only we had listened or understood, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze.' God, the Most High, said, 'So they acknowledged their sin.'" That is, their denial of the messengers. Sin here has the meaning of plural because it has the meaning of action. It is said: The people's gift went out meaning, I gave them.
67:11: Fashaqan to the companions of the Blaze meaning far away from God's mercy. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Abu Salih said: It is a valley in Hell called Al-Sahaq. Al-Kisa'i and Abu Ja'far read it with a damma on the ha', and it was narrated from Ali. The rest read it with a sukoon on it, and they are two dialects like saht poaching and ra'b terror. Al-Zajjaj: It is an accusative of the source, meaning may God crush them, a crushing, meaning may He distance them far away. Imru' al-Qais said: He roams the outskirts of the country, heading west, and the morning wind crushes him completely. Abu Ali said: The analogy is based on Isaac, so the source came with the deletion, as it was said: And if you perish, then that was my destiny, meaning my destiny. It was also said: The Almighty’s saying: You are only in great error is from the words of the keepers of Hell to its people.
67:12: The Almighty's statement: Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen is similar to the statement: Whoever fears the Most Merciful unseen Qaf: 33, which has already been discussed. That is, they fear God and fear His punishment, which is unseen, and it is the punishment on the Day of Resurrection. For them is forgiveness for their sins and a great reward, which is Paradise.
67:13: The Almighty said: And conceal your speech or declare it aloud. The wording is a command but what is meant by it is information, meaning that if you conceal your speech concerning Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, or you declare it aloud, then He is All-Knowing of that within the breasts meaning what is in the hearts of good and evil. Ibn Abbas said: This was revealed concerning the polytheists who used to speak ill of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and Gabriel, peace be upon him, would inform him. Some of them said to each other: Confide in what you say so that the Lord of Muhammad does not hear. So this verse was revealed: And conceal your speech or declare it aloud. Meaning: Confide in what you say concerning Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. It was also said: In all other sayings. Or declare it aloud, they announced it. He is All-Knowing of that within the breasts means what is in the breasts, just as a woman's child is called when it is a fetus in her womb.
67:14: Then he said: Does He not know who created? meaning does He not know the secret from who created the secret? He says, I created the secret in the heart, so will I not know what is in the hearts of His servants? The scholars of semantics said: If you wish, you can make Min a name for the Creator, the Most High, and the meaning is that the Creator does not know His creation. Or you can make it a name for the creation, and the meaning is: Does God not know who created? The Creator must be All-Knowing of what He created and what He will create. Ibn al-Musayyab said: While a man was standing at night among many trees and the wind was blowing, it occurred to him: Do you think God knows what falls from these leaves? Then a loud voice was called from the side of the thicket: Does He not know who created, while He is the Subtle, the All-Aware! Professor Abu Ishaq al-Isfarayini said: Among the names of the attributes of the Essence are those that indicate knowledge, among them is Al-Aleem, which means generalizing all information. Among them is Al-Abeed, which is specific to knowing what will happen before it happens. Among them is Al-Hakim, which is specific to knowing the subtleties of descriptions. Among them is Al-Shaheed, which is specific to knowing the absent and the present, and their meaning is that nothing is hidden from Him. Among them is Al-Hafiz, which is distinguished by not forgetting. Among them is Al-Muhsin, which is distinguished by not being distracted from knowledge by abundance, such as the light of day, the intensity of the wind, and the falling of leaves. He knows about the parts of the movements in each leaf. How could He not know, when He is the One who creates! He said: Does He not know who created, while He is the Subtle, the Acquainted?
67:15: God the Almighty says: It is He who made the earth submissive to you meaning easy for you to settle on. Submissive is the one who submits to you, and the source is humility which is softness and submission. That is, He did not make the earth such that walking on it is difficult or wrong. It was also said: That is, He made it firm so that it would not move with its people, and if it were flat and symmetrical, it would not have been submissive to us. It was also said: It indicated the ability to plant and cultivate, dig springs and rivers, and dig wells. Walk in its paths is an order of permission, and in it is a display of gratitude. It was also said: It is report of the form of a command, meaning so that you may walk in its edges and regions, hills and mountains. Ibn Abbas, Qatadah, and Bashir ibn Ka'b said: In its paths is in its mountains. It was narrated that Bashir ibn Ka'b had a concubine, so he said to her: If you tell me what the paths of the earth are, then you will be free. She said: Its paths are its mountains. So she became free. So he wanted to marry her, so he asked Abu Darda’, who said: Leave that which makes you tired for that which does not make you tired. Mujahid: On its edges. And also from him: On its roads and paths. Al-Suddi and Al-Hasan said it. Al-Kalbi said: On its sides. And the shoulders of a man: his two sides. The root of the shoulder is the side, and from it is the shoulder of a man. And the wind is the Nakba’. And someone was turned away from someone. So he says: Walk wherever you want, for I have made it submissive to you and will not resist. Qatada narrated from Abu Al-Jild: The earth is twenty-four thousand farsakhs, so the blacks have twelve thousand, the Romans have eight thousand, the Persians have three thousand, and the Arabs have a thousand. And eat of His provision meaning from what He has made lawful for you, said Al-Hasan. It was said: From what I have given you. And to Him is the resurrection The reference. And it was said: Its meaning is that He who created the heaven with no inequality in it, and the earth is submissive, Able to resurrect you.
67:16: Ibn Abbas said: Are you the punishment of He who is in the heaven if you disobey Him? It was also said that the meaning is: Are you the one whose power, authority, throne, and kingdom are in the heaven? He specified the heavens even though His kingdom is general, to indicate that the God whose power is implemented is in the heavens, not the one they glorify on earth. It was also said that it is a reference to the angels. It was also said that it refers to Gabriel, who is the angel assigned with the punishment. I said: It is possible that the meaning is: Are you the Creator of those in the heavens, so that He may cause the earth to swallow you up, as He caused it to swallow up Qarun? Then it will sway means it will go and come. Sway means to sway with coming and going. The poet said: Shoot, aim for the hearts, and you will not see any blood flowing except that it runs in the belts. Plural of hayzum, which is the middle of the chest. If a person is swallowed up by the earth and the earth rotates around him, then he is al-Mawr. The scholars said: You feel safe from above the sky, like His statement: So travel freely through the earth (al-Tawbah 9:2), meaning above it, not by touch or position, but by force and management. It was said: It means you feel safe from above the sky, like His statement: And I will surely crucify you on the trunks of palm trees (Ta-Ha: 71), meaning on it. It means that he is its manager and owner, as one says: So-and-so is over Iraq and Hijaz, meaning its governor and prince. The narrations on this subject are many, authentic, and widespread, pointing to loftiness, and none can deny them except an atheist or an ignorant stubborn person. What is meant by them is to revere Him and to sanctify Him from what is base and below. He is described as lofty and great, not by places, directions, and boundaries, because these are attributes of bodies. The hands are raised to the sky in supplication because the sky is the place where revelation descends, the place where rain descends, the place of holiness, the place of the purified angels, and to it the deeds of the servants are raised, and above it is His throne and His Paradise, just as God made the Kaaba the Qiblah for supplication and prayer. And because He created places although He has no need of them, and He existed in eternity before the creation of place and time, and He has no place or time. And He is now as He was. Qanbal read from Ibn Kathir al-Nashur and wa-amintum by changing the first hamza to a waw and softening the second. The Kufians, Basrans, and the people of Syria, except for Abu ‘Umar and Hisham, read it by softening the two hamzas, and the rest softened it. All of it has been mentioned above.
67:17: The Almighty says: Or do you feel secure that He who is in the heaven will not send upon you a storm of stones? That is, stones from women, as He sent them upon the people of Lot and the companions of the elephant. It was also said: a wind with stones and gravel. It was also said: a cloud with stones. Then you will know how my warner is. That is, my warning. It was also said: the warner means the warner. Meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then you will know his truthfulness and the consequence of their denial.
67:18: The Almighty says: And those before them denied meaning the disbelieving nations, such as the people of Noah, Aad, Thamud, the people of Lot, the people of Madyan, the people of Ar-Rass, and the people of Pharaoh. How was my denial? meaning my denial, as has been mentioned previously. Warsh included the ya' in nadhiri and nakiri in the connected form. Ya'qub included it in both cases. The rest omitted it in accordance with the Qur'an.
67:19: The Almighty said: Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading out their wings? That is, just as He has made the earth subservient to man, He has made the air subservient to birds. Spreading out their wings means spreading out their wings in the air when flying, because when they spread them out, they line up their legs in a row. And they fold in means they strike their sides with them. Abu Ja`far said: An-Nahhas: When a bird spreads its wings, it is said: Saf, and when it closes them so that its side touches it, it is said: Qabd, because it holds them together. Abu Kharash said: The night takes the initiative, for it is a refuge that urges the wing to expand and contract. It was said: And He closes their wings after spreading them when they stop flying. It is conjoined with the word saffat in conjunction with the present tense and the active participle, just as the active participle is conjoined with the present tense in the poet’s saying: He began to live in it with a severe temper, intending to roam its markets unjustly. No one holds them back means no one holds the birds in the air while they fly except God Almighty. He is All-Seeing of all things.
67:20: The Almighty said: Is this he who is your army? Ibn Abbas said: A party and protection for you to aid you other than the Most Gracious so that he repels from you what He intends for you if you disobey Him. The word army is singular, and that is why He said: This he who is your army which is a question of denial, meaning that you have no army to repel from you the punishment of God other than the Most Gracious meaning other than the Most Gracious. The disbelievers are only in delusion from the devils, who attack them with the idea that there is no punishment or reckoning.
67:21: God Almighty says: Is this He who provides for you? meaning, He gives you the benefits of this world. It was also said: The rain is from your gods. If He withholds means God Almighty's provision. Rather, they persisted, meaning they persisted and persisted. In insolence of tyranny and aversion from the truth.
67:22: God the Almighty said: Is he who walks prone on his face? God has set forth an example for the believer and the disbeliever, prone, meaning with his head bowed, not looking in front of him, to his right, or to his left. He is not safe from stumbling and falling on his face. Like someone who walks upright and straight, looking in front of him, to his right, and to his left. Ibn Abbas said: This is in this world. It is possible that he means the blind man who cannot find his way, so he stumbles and keeps falling on his face. He is not like the healthy, sighted man who walks on the right path. Qatada said: He is the disbeliever who was prone to disobeying God in this world, so God will gather him on the Day of Resurrection on his face. Ibn Abbas and Al-Kalbi said: Abu Jahl is sufficient for the one who walks prone on his face, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is sufficient for the one who walks prone. It was also said Abu Bakr. It was also said Hamzah. It was also said Ammar ibn Yasir, as was said by Ikrimah. It was said: It is general for the unbeliever and the believer, meaning that the unbeliever does not know whether he is on the highest truth or falsehood. Meaning, is this unbeliever guided or the Muslim who walks upright and upright, sees the path and is on the straight path which is Islam. It is said: The man fell on his face, in what is not transitive with the letter alif. But if it is transitive, it is said: May God throw him down on his face, without the letter alif.
67:23: The Almighty says: Say, ‘It is He who created you.’ He ordered His Prophet to inform them of the ugliness of their polytheism, even though they acknowledged that God created them. And He gave you hearing and sight and hearts. He means hearts. Little do you give thanks. That is, you do not give thanks for these blessings, and you do not believe in the Oneness of God Almighty. You say, I rarely do such-and-such, meaning I do not do it.
67:24: God Almighty says: Say, ‘It is He who has dispersed you throughout the earth.’ That is, He created you on the earth, as Ibn Abbas said. It was also said: He spread you out and dispersed you across it, as Ibn Shajarah said. And to Him you will be gathered, until He rewards each one according to his deeds.
67:25: And they say, 'When will this promise come to pass, if you should be truthful?' That is, when will the Day of Resurrection come to pass! And when will this punishment that you promise us come to pass? This is a mockery from them. It has been mentioned before.
67:26: God Almighty says: Say, 'Knowledge is only with God.' That is, O Muhammad, knowledge of the time of the Hour is with God, and no one else knows it. Similar to this is: Say, 'Knowledge thereof is only with my Lord.' (al-A’raf 7:187). And I am only a clear warner. That is, one who frightens and teaches you.
67:27: God the Almighty says: And when they saw it approaching is a verbal noun meaning close, Mujahid said. Al-Hasan: clearly. Most commentators agree that when they saw it, it means the punishment, which is the punishment of the Hereafter. Mujahid said: It means the punishment of Badr. It was also said: It means they saw what they were promised of gathering close to them. This is indicated by you will be gathered. Ibn Abbas said: When they saw their evil deeds close by. The faces of those who disbelieved will be made evil means evil was done to them. Al-Zajjaj said: Evil was evident therein, meaning that punishment upset them and a mark of their disbelief appeared on their faces, as God the Almighty said: The Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black Al-Imran 3:106. Nafi', Ibn Muhays, Ibn 'Amir, and Al-Kisa'i read sa'it with a damma. The rest read it without a kasra to make it lighter. Whoever reads with a damma observed the original. Al-Farra' said: You call upon [you], you supplicate [you], from supplication, and this is the opinion of most scholars, meaning you wish and ask. Ibn Abbas said: You lie, and its interpretation is: This is what you used to call upon falsehoods and hadiths for, as stated by Al-Zajjaj. The reading of the common people is you call upon with a shaddah, and its interpretation is what we mentioned. Qatadah, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Ad-Dahhak, and Ya'qub read you call upon with a light ta' sufficiency. Qatadah said: It is their saying: Our Lord, hasten for us our portion (Surah Sad: 16). Ad-Dahhak said: It is their saying: O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky (Surah al-Anfal 8:32). Abu Al-Abbas said: You call upon [you], you are hastening [you]. It is said: I called upon such and such if you asked for it, and I made a supplication from it. An-Nahhas said: You call upon [you] and you call upon one meaning, just as they say: he was able and he was able to, and he was able and he was able, except that in Ifta'ala the meaning of one thing after another, and the verb is used with little and much.
67:28: God the Almighty said: Say, 'Have you considered, if God should destroy me' meaning, say to them, O Muhammad - meaning the polytheists of Mecca, who were wishing for the death of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him), as God the Almighty said: Or do they say, 'He is a poet; we await for him a misfortune of time'? (al-Tur 52:30) - Have you considered, if we die or You have mercy on us and You delay our appointed times, then who can protect you from the punishment of God? So you have no need to await us or to hasten the Hour. Ibn Muhays, Al-Musayyibi, Shabih, Al-A'mash, and Hamzah sukunized the ya' in ahlakany while the rest opened it. All of them opened the ya' in wa man ma'i except the people of Kufa, who sukunized it. Hafs opened it like the rest.
67:29: The Almighty said: "Say: He is the Most Gracious. We have believed in Him, and upon Him we have relied, and you will know." Al-Kisa'i read it with a ya' as a statement, and narrated it from Ali. The rest read it with a ta' as an address. And it is a threat to them. It is said: I did not delay the object of aman and brought forward the object of tawakkalna. It is said: Because amanna occurred, it is an allusion to the disbelievers when it came after mentioning them. It is as if it was said: We believed and did not disbelieve as you disbelieved. Then He said: And upon Him we have relied, specifically, we did not rely on what you rely on of your men and your wealth, as Al-Zamakhshari said.
67:30: God the Almighty says: Say, 'Have you considered, O people of Quraysh, if your water were to become sunken in?' That is, if it were to sink into the ground and buckets could not reach it. Their water came from two wells: the Well of Zamzam and the Well of Maymun. Who would bring you flowing water? That is, flowing, as stated by Qatada and Ad-Dahhak. They will have to say, None can bring it to us except God. So say to them, Why do you associate with Him one who is not able to bring it to you? It is said, The water sank means it became erect. Ghor means deep and is described by a verbal noun for emphasis, just as you say, a man of justice and contentment. This has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Kahf, and the meaning has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Mu'minun. Praise be to God. Ibn Abbas said, with flowing water means apparent and visible, so it is a passive participle. It was also said that it is from the meaning of water meaning abundant, so in this case it is a passive participle. Ibn Abbas also said that the meaning is, Who would bring you fresh water? And God knows best.
68:1: The Almighty said: Nun and the Pen The second nun was assimilated into the waw in its spelling by Abu Bakr, Al-Mufaddal, Hibbah, Warsh, Ibn Muhays, Ibn Amir, Al-Kisa'i, and Ya'qub. The rest recited it with the izhar. Isa ibn Umar recited it with the fatha, as if he implied a verb. Ibn Abbas, Nasr, and Ibn Abi Ishaq recited it with the kasra, implying the oath letter. Harun and Muhammad ibn Al-Sameeq recited it with the damma, as a construction. There is disagreement over its interpretation. Muawiyah ibn Qurrah narrated on the authority of his father, tracing it back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), that he said: Nun is a tablet of light. Thabit al-Bunani narrated that Nun is the inkwell. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said the same. Al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated that Malik ibn Anas told us on the authority of Sumayy, the freed slave of Abu Bakr, on the authority of Abu Salih al-Samman, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: The first person God created was the pen. Then He created the nun and the ni, the inkwell. This is in the words of God the Most High: ‘Nun and the pen.’ Then He said: ‘I write.’ He said: ‘And what should I write?’ He said: ‘Whatever was and whatever will be until the Day of Resurrection of deeds, life span, provision, or influence.’ So the pen wrote with what will be until the Day of Resurrection.’ He said: ‘Then it was sealed, and the pen is not a pen that speaks and will not speak until the Day of Resurrection.’ Then He created the intellect, and the Almighty said: ‘I have not created a creation more pleasing to Me than you. By My Might and Majesty, I will perfect you among those I love and make you less numerous among those I hate.’ Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘The people who are most perfect in intellect are those who are most obedient to God and most devoting themselves to His obedience.’” Mujahid said: Nun is the fish beneath the seventh earth. He said: And the pen with which the remembrance was written. Likewise, Muqatil, Marra Al-Hamadhani, Ata Al-Khurasani, Al-Suddi and Al-Kalbi said: The Nun is the whale on which the earths are. Abu Dhibyan narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The first thing that God created was the Pen, and it wrote with what would be. Then He raised the water vapor and created the sky from it. Then He created the Nun and spread the earth on its back, so the earth shook and was fixed with the mountains, and indeed the mountains boast above the earth. Then Ibn Abbas recited Nun and the Pen the verse. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: Its name is Bahamut. The rajaz poet said: Why do I see you all silent, when God created the dumb? Abu Al-Yaqzan and Al-Waqidi said: Lyuthan. Ka’b said: Luthuthan. He said: Bilhamuthan. Ka’b said: “Iblis penetrated the whale on whose back the earths were, and whispered in its heart, saying: ‘Do you know what is on your back, O Luthathan, of beasts, trees, earths, and other things? If you vomit them out, I will throw them all on your back.’” So, Liyuthan wanted to do that, but God sent a beast to him, which entered his nostril and reached his brain. The whale cried out to God, the Almighty, to prevent it, but God granted it permission and it came out. Ka’b said: “By God, he looks at it and it looks at him. If he thinks of doing something to do that, he will be as strong as before.” Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Nun is the last letter of the letters of Ar-Rahman. He said: Alif-Lam-Ra, Ha-Mim, and Nun. Ar-Rahman is disjointed.” Ibn Zayd said: It is an oath by which God swore. Ibn Kaysan said: It is the opening of the Surah. It was said: It is the name of the Surah. Ata’ and Abu Al-Aaliyah said: It is the opening of the names Nasir, Nur, and Nasir. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: God swore by His victory for the believers, and it is true. Its explanation is the saying of God the Almighty: And it was incumbent upon Us to support the believers (al-Rum 30:47). Ja'far al-Sadiq said: It is a river from the rivers of Paradise called Nun. It was said: It is the well-known letter of the alphabet, because if it were otherwise, it would be inflected. This is the choice of al-Qushayri Abu Nasr Abd al-Rahim in his interpretation. He said: Because Nun is a letter that is not inflected, so if it were a complete word, it would be inflected as the Pen is inflected. Therefore, it is a letter of the alphabet as in the rest of the keys to the Surahs. Based on this, it was said: It is the name of the Surah, meaning this is Surah Nun. Then he said: And the Pen. He swore by the Pen because of what is in it of eloquence like the tongue, and it applies to every pen with which those in the heavens and those on the earth write. From this is the saying of Abu al-Fath al-Busti: If heroes swore one day by their sword and promised it what would bring them glory and honor The pen of the book is sufficient for honor and elevation throughout time. God swore by the pen. Poets have many verses about the pen's preference over the sword, the most important of which we have mentioned. Ibn Abbas said: This is an oath by the pen that God created, and He commanded it to write down everything that will happen until the Day of Resurrection. He said: It is a pen of light, as long as the distance between heaven and earth. It is said that God created the pen, then He looked at it and it split in two and said: Run. He said: O Lord, what will I be run over? He said: What will happen until the Day of Resurrection? So it ran on the Preserved Tablet. Al-Walid ibn Ubadah ibn al-Samit said: My father advised me upon his death, saying: O my son, fear God, and know that you will not fear God and will not attain knowledge until you believe in God alone and in predestination, both good and bad. I heard the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: The first thing God created was the pen, and He said to it: Write. It said: O Lord, what should I write? He said: Write the predestination. So the pen ran at that moment with everything that was and everything that will happen until eternity. Ibn Abbas said: The first thing God created was the pen, and He commanded it to write everything that will happen. Among what it wrote was: Perish the hands of Abu Lahab Al-Masad 76:1. Qatada said: The pen is a blessing from God Almighty to His servants. Another said: God created the first pen and wrote what would be in the remembrance and placed it with Him above His throne. Then He created the second pen to write with it on the earth, as will be explained in Surat Read in the name of your Lord (al-Alaq 96:1). God the Almighty said: And what they write down meaning what they write down. He means the angels who write down the deeds of the children of Adam, as Ibn Abbas said. It was also said: And what they write down means the people and what they understand from it. Ibn Abbas said: The meaning of what they write down is what they know. And what is a relative pronoun or a verbal noun, meaning and their written down or their writing down, and what is meant by it is everyone who writes down or the guardians, according to the disagreement.
68:2: You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman. This is the answer to the oath, which is a negation. The polytheists used to say to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that he was a madman, possessed by a devil. This is what they said: O you to whom the message has been sent down, indeed, you are mad. (al-Hijr 15:6) So God, the Most High, revealed in response to them and as a refutation of their statement, You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman. That is, by the mercy of your Lord. The grace here means mercy. It is possible secondly - that the grace here is an oath, and its interpretation is: you and your Lord are not mad, because the waw and the ba are among the letters of the oath. It was said that it is like you say: you are not mad, and praise be to God. It was said: its meaning is you are not mad, and the grace is to your Lord, like their saying: Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You, meaning and praise be to God. And from this is the saying of Labid: I was isolated in this world, my clan was lost, and a neighbor left me in Arbad, Nafi’ That is, it is Arbad. Al-Nabigha said: They were not deprived of good food, and their mother was full of daughters of remembrance. That is, he is a genius. The preposition bi'ma't Rabbik in bi'nimat Rabbik is related to madman in the negative, just as it is related to ghāfi'l in the positive. As in your saying: You, by the grace of your Lord, are heedless. Its position is in the accusative case as a state, as if he said: You are not mad, and that has been bestowed upon you.
68:3: And indeed, for you is a reward meaning a recompense for the burdens of prophethood that you have borne. Unbroken meaning not cut off or diminished. It is said: You cut the rope if you cut it. And a rope is manin if it is not strong. The poet said: A grim-faced, greedy woman whose food is not manin" That is, it is not cut off. Mujahid said: Unappreciated means calculated. Al-Hasan: Unappreciated means not clouded by favor. Ad-Dahhak: A reward without work. It was also said: Unmeasured, which is a favor, because the reward is measured and the favor is not measured. Al-Mawardi mentioned this, and it is the meaning of Mujahid’s statement.
68:4: There are two issues: The first: The Almighty's saying, And indeed, you are of a great moral character. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: Of a great moral character, a great religion among the religions, there is no religion more beloved to God Almighty nor more pleasing to Him than it. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Aisha: His moral character was the Qur'an. Ali may God be pleased with him and Atiyah said: It is the etiquette of the Qur'an. It was also said: It was his kindness to his nation and his honoring them. Qatada said: It is what he obeyed of God's commands and refrained from what God forbade. It was also said: That is, you are of a noble nature. Al-Mawardi: This is the apparent meaning. The true meaning of morality in the language is: What a person takes of his own morals is called morality, because it becomes like nature in him. As for what he is naturally endowed with of morality, it is the word khaym with a kasra: disposition and nature, it has no singular form from the same word. Wakhim: is the name of a mountain. So, morality is the artificial nature. And khaym is the instinctive nature. Al-A'sha made this clear in his poetry when he said: If the curious person is stingy with his master and his habits are clouded by bad morals That is, morals returned to their nature. I said: What you mentioned about Aisha in Sahih Muslim is the most correct of the sayings. She was also asked about his character, peace be upon him, so she recited, Indeed, the believers have succeeded up to ten verses, and she said: No one had better character than the Messenger of God, peace be upon him. No one from the Companions or from his family called upon him except that he said, At your service, and that is why he had the greatest share. Al-Junayd said: His character was called great because he had no concern other than God Almighty. It was said: His character was called great because he combined noble morals, as indicated by his saying, peace be upon him: God sent me to perfect noble morals. It was also said: Because he complied with God Almighty’s discipline of him in His saying: Adopt forgiveness, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant. al-A’raf 7:199. It was narrated that he, peace be upon him, said: “My Lord taught me good manners when He said: ‘Adopt forgiveness, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant’ (al-A’raf 7:199). When I accepted that from Him, He said: ‘And indeed, you are of a great moral character.’” Second: Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abu Dharr that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Fear God wherever you may be, and follow up a bad deed with a good one which will erase it, and treat people with good character. He said: A good and authentic hadith. Abu Ad-Darda’ narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Nothing will be heavier in the scale of a believer on the Day of Resurrection than good character. God hates the vulgar and obscene person.” He said: A good and authentic hadith. He also said: “I heard the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) say: ‘Nothing will be placed on the scale heavier than good character. The one who has good character will attain the status of the one who prays and fasts.’” He said: A strange hadith from this chain of transmission. Ibn Hurairah said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was asked: What most causes people to enter Paradise? He said: Fear of God. He was asked: What most causes people to enter Hell? He said: The mouth and the private parts. He said: This is a strange and authentic hadith. Abdullah ibn Mubarak described good character and said: It is a smiling face, doing good deeds, and refraining from harming others. On the authority of Jabir: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The most beloved of you to me and the closest to me in assembly on the Day of Resurrection will be the best of you in character.’ He said: ‘And the most hateful of you to me and the farthest from me in assembly on the Day of Resurrection will be the chatterers, the boasters, and the arrogant.’ They said: ‘O Messenger of God, we know the chatterers and the boasters, but who are the arrogant?’ He said: There is a hadith on this topic on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, and this is a hasan gharib hadith from this chain of transmission.
68:5: God Almighty says: Then you will see, and they will see. Ibn Abbas said: It means you will know, and they will know, on the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: You will see, and they will see, on the Day of Resurrection when truth and falsehood will be distinguished.
68:6: Which of you is afflicted? The ba is redundant, meaning you will see and they will see which of you is afflicted. That is, the one afflicted by madness, as God Almighty says: It produces oil (al-Mu’minun 23:20) and The servants of God will drink from it (al-Insan 76:6). This is the opinion of Qatada, Abu Ubaid, and Al-Akhfash. The rajaz poet said: We are the Banu Ja'dah, the owners of the falaj. We strike with the sword and hope for relief. It was said: The letter Baa is an extra letter, and the meaning is: Which of you is afflicted? meaning the trial. It is a verbal noun in the form of Maf’ul, and its meaning is trials, as they said: So-and-so has neither flogging nor reason, meaning intellect nor endurance. Al-Hasan, Al-Dahhak, and Ibn Abbas said the same. Al-Ra’i said: Even if they left no flesh for his bones, nor any understanding for his heart. Meaning rationally. It was said: There is an estimation of an omitted complement in the speech, and the meaning is: Which of you is the temptation of the tempted? Al-Farra’ said: The preposition ba means in, meaning you will be patient and they will be patient, whichever of the two groups is the madman, the group of believers that you are in or the more lax group. The tempted is the madman who has been tempted by Satan. It was said: The one who is tempted is the one who is tormented. And from the saying of the Arabs: He tempted the gold with fire if he heated it. And from this is the saying of the Almighty: The Day they will be tempted by the Fire (al-Dhariyat 51:13), meaning they will be tormented. Most of the Surah was revealed about Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira and Abu Jahl. It was said that the one who was tempted was the devil, because he was tempted in his religion. They used to say: He has a devil in him, and they meant this madman, so God the Most High said: And they will know tomorrow which of them is the madman, meaning the devil who is possessed by madness and confusion of mind.
68:7: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way. That is, God is the most knowing of who has deviated from His religion. And He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided. That is, those who are on the right path. So He will reward everyone tomorrow according to His knowledge.
68:8: God Almighty says: So do not obey the deniers. He forbade him from siding with the polytheists. They used to call him to take responsibility for them so that they would desist. God made it clear that siding with them is disbelief. He said: {And had We not strengthened you, you would have almost inclined to them a little.} It was also said: meaning, do not obey those who deny what I have called you to of their evil religion. This was revealed about the polytheists of Quraysh when they called him to the religion of God.
68:9: God Almighty said: They wish you would compromise so they would compromise. Ibn Abbas, Atiyyah, Ad-Dahhak, and As-Suddi said: They wish you would disbelieve so they would persist in their disbelief. Ibn Abbas also said: They wish you would make things easy for them so they would make things easy for you. Al-Farra’ and Al-Kalbi said: If you were lenient so they would be lenient with you. Adhan means being gentle with someone who should not be gentle, as stated by Al-Farra’. Mujahid said: The meaning is they wish you would incline towards them and abandon the truth so they would flatter you. Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: They wish you would lie so they would lie. Qatadah said: They wish you would abandon this matter so they would go with you. Al-Hasan said: They wish you would be accommodating to them regarding your religion so they would be accommodating to you regarding their religion. He also said: They wish you would reject some of your commands so they would reject some of their commands. Zayd ibn Salim said: If you were hypocritical and ostentatious so they would be hypocritical and ostentatious. It was also said: They wish you would be weak so they would be weak, as stated by Abu Ja’far. It was also said: They wish you would be accommodating regarding your religion so they would be accommodating regarding their religions, as stated by Al-Qutbi. On his authority: They asked him to worship their gods for a period and they to worship his god for a period. So these are twelve sayings. Ibn al-Arabi: The commentators mentioned about ten sayings, all of which are claims based on language and meaning. Examples of them are their sayings: They wish you would lie so they would lie, and They wish you would disbelieve so they would disbelieve. I said: All of them, God willing, are correct according to the language and meaning, because flattery means: gentleness and flattery. It was also said: to flatter the enemy and to be nice to him. It was also said: to approach one another in speech and to soften one’s words. The poet said: Some cheats are more decisive in matters that befall you than flattering enemies. Al-Mufaddal said: Hypocrisy and neglecting to offer sincere advice. According to this interpretation, it is blameworthy, but according to the first interpretation, it is not blameworthy, and none of these things exist. Al-Mubarrad said: It is said that he was treacherous in his religion and he was treacherous in his affair, meaning he betrayed it and showed something other than what he intended. Some people said: I was treacherous in the sense of I showed off, and I was treacherous in the sense of I deceived, as stated by Al-Jawhari. He said: They are treacherous, so he presented it as an object of conjunction. If he had used it as an answer to the prohibition, he would have said they are treacherous. Rather, he meant: If they wished that you did, then they would do as you did, an object of conjunction with no reward or recompense, but it is only an example and an analogy.
68:10: It means Al-Akhns ibn Shuraik, according to Al-Sha'bi, Al-Suddi and Ibn Ishaq. It was also said that it means Al-Aswad ibn Abd Yaghuth, or Abd Al-Rahman ibn Al-Aswad, as said by Mujahid. It was also said that it means Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira, who offered the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) money and swore to give it to him if he would renounce his religion, as said by Muqatil. Ibn Abbas said that it means Abu Jahl ibn Hisham. Al-Hallaf means someone who swears a lot. Al-Muhin means someone who is weak-hearted, according to Mujahid. Ibn Abbas: The liar. The liar is humiliated. It was said: The one who does a lot of evil, said Al-Hasan and Qatadah. Al-Kalbi said: The humiliated is the proud and weak. It was said: Its meaning is the insignificant in the sight of God. Ibn Shajarah said: It is the humiliated. Al-Rummani: The humiliated and lowly for doing a lot of ugly things. It is a fa’il from humiliation meaning fewness. Here it is fewness in opinion and discrimination. Or it is fa’il with the meaning of maf’il, and the meaning is humiliated.
68:11: Hammaz Ibn Zayd said: The one who backbites people with his hand and hits them. And the backbiter with the tongue. Al-Hasan said: He is the one who backbites a side in the gathering, like the saying of God the Almighty: Hammazah Al-Hamzah:1. It was said that the slanderer is the one who mentions people to their faces. And the backbiter is the one who mentions them in their absence, as Abu Al-Aaliyah, Ata bin Abi Rabah, and Al-Hasan also said. Muqatil said against this statement: The slanderer is the one who backbites in backbiting. And the backbiter is the one who backbites to someone's face. And Marra said: They are the same. And he is the slanderer who attacks a person in his absence. And something similar was narrated by Ibn Abbas and Qatadah. The poet said: Treat me kindly if you meet me with a lie, and if I am stupid, then you are the backbiter and slanderer. Walking around with gossip means spreading gossip among people to cause discord between them. It is said: Nam yanmum nama wa namimman wa namiman, meaning he walks around and strives to cause corruption. In Sahih Muslim: On the authority of Hudhayfah that he heard that a man was spreading gossip, so Hudhayfah said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: A gossiper will not enter Paradise. And the poet said: A master is like an ant's house, he has no good for his master except his striving to spread gossip. Al-Farra’ said: They are two languages. It was also said: Namiyyah is the plural of Namimah.
68:12: Preventer of good meaning money is not spent on it. Ibn Abbas said: He prevents his children and his clan from Islam. Al-Hasan said: He tells them, Whoever among you enters the religion of Muhammad, I will never benefit him in anything. "Transgressor" means oppressing people, exceeding the limit, and doing wrong. "Atheem means sinful, and its meaning is Athum", so it is a fa'il with the meaning of fa'ul.
68:13: He became a stubborn, wicked person. The stubborn person is someone who is harsh and severe in his disbelief. Al-Kalbi and Al-Farraa said: He is someone who argues harshly based on falsehood. It was also said that he is someone who makes people suffer and drags them into imprisonment or punishment. It is derived from the word 'atal' which means dragging, and from it is the saying of God Almighty: Seize him and smite him (al-Dukhan 44:47). In As-Sahah: I pulled a man violently, I pulled him violently. And a man with a broken collar said, describing a horse: We pull him violently, but we do not pull him violently. Ibn Al-Sikkit said: Atlah and Atnah, with both Lam and Noon. Al-Atl means the rough and coarse. Al-Atl also means: the thick spear, and a man is Atl with the Kasra between Al-Atl, meaning he is quick to evil. It is said: I will not move from my place. Ubaid bin Umair said: Al-Atl is the gluttonous, the drunkard, the strong, the powerful, he is placed on the scales and does not weigh a barley grain, the king pushes seventy thousand of those into Hell in one go. Ali bin Abi Talib and Al-Hasan said: Al-Atl is the obscene and ill-tempered. Muammar said: He is the obscene and mean. The poet said: I sent a mean man, who was neither helpful nor generous. In Sahih Muslim. On the authority of Haritha ibn Wahb, “I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘Shall I not tell you about the people of Paradise?’ They said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘Every weak, oppressed person who, if he swears an oath by God, God will fulfill it. Shall I not tell you about the people of Hell?’ They said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘Every violent, arrogant, cowardly person.’” In another narration on his authority: Every violent, arrogant, cowardly person. It was said that it means someone who has a lot of flesh and swaggers in his gait. Al-Mawardi mentioned on the authority of Shahr ibn Khawshab on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanam, and it was narrated by Ibn Mas’ud: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No one will enter Paradise who is violent, nor a violent, cowardly person, nor a violent, cowardly person. A man said: What is a violent person, what is a cowardly person, and what is a violent, cowardly person? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The violent person is the one who gathers and withholds. The violent person is the one who is coarse, harsh, broad-chested, healthy, gluttonous, drinker of food, and oppressor of people.” Al-Tha'labi mentioned it on the authority of Shaddad ibn Aws: The one who is rude, the one who is harsh, and the one who is violent and wicked will not enter Paradise. I heard these things from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. I said: What is rude? He said: The one who is violent and wicked. I said: What is violent and wicked? He said: The one who is broad-shouldered, well-mannered, gluttonous, drunk, oppressive, and unjust. I said: This interpretation of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) regarding the ‘atal is superior to the statements of the commentators. In the book of Abu Dawud, in the interpretation of the jawaz, it is stated that it is the harsh word. He mentioned it from the hadith of Haritha ibn Wahb Al-Khuza’i, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The jawaaz and the ja’zari will not enter Paradise. He said: The jawaz is the harsh word. So there are two interpretations of it with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, as we mentioned first. It has been said that it refers to the harsh-hearted. And on the authority of Zayn ibn Aslam, regarding the verse: And then he became harsh and fornicating, he said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “The heavens weep over a man whose body God made healthy, whose belly was spacious, and to whom God gave some of this world, yet he was unjust to the people. That is the harsh and fornicating old man. And it weeps over the fornicating old man so that the earth can hardly bear him.” The fornicator is the one who sticks to the people, according to Ibn Abbas and others. The poet said: A bastard whom men have called an increase, just as the legs have been increased in place of the leather. It was also narrated from Ibn Abbas: He was a man from Quraysh who had a tail like a sheep’s tail. Ibn Jubayr narrated from him: He is the one who is known for his evil as a sheep is known by its tail. Ikrimah said: He is the mean person who is known for his meanness as a sheep is known by its tail. It was said: He is the one who is known for his daughter. It was also narrated from Ibn Abbas: And from him: He is the oppressor. So these are six sayings. Mujahid said: He was a liar who had six fingers on his hand, on each thumb he had an extra finger. It was also narrated from him, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, and Ikrimah: He is the offspring of fornication who is elevated in lineage among the people. Al-Walid was an adopted child among Quraysh, not of their kind. His father claimed him eighteen years after his birth. The poet said: A bastard who doesn't know who his father is, a wicked mother, of lowly lineage Hassan said: You are a bastard who has set his sights on the Hashemites, just as a single cup has set its sights on a rider. I said: This is the same as the first statement. And on the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him: It is the one that has no basis, and the meaning is the same. It was narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The child of fornication will not enter Paradise, nor his child, nor his child’s child. Abdullah ibn Umar said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The children of fornication will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection in the form of monkeys and pigs. Maymunah said: “I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: ‘My nation will continue to be fine as long as the children of fornication do not become widespread among them. But if the children of fornication become widespread among them, God will soon afflict them all with punishment.’” Ikrimah said: If the children of fornication become numerous, there will be a drought. I said: As for the first and second hadith, I do not think they have a sound chain of transmission. As for the hadith of Maymunah and what Ikrimah said, it is in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Zaynab bint Jahsh, the wife of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out one day, frightened, his face red, saying, ‘There is no god but God. Woe to the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near. Today a hole has been opened in the barrier of Gog and Magog like this,’ and he made a circle with his thumb and the one next to it. I said, ‘O Messenger of God, will we be destroyed even though there are righteous people among us?’ He said, ‘Yes, when evil increases.’” Narrated by al-Bukhari. The increase in evil means the emergence of adultery and illegitimate children, as is how the scholars interpreted it. Ikrimah’s statement about the drought is an explanation of what will cause destruction. This requires verification, and he is more knowledgeable about where he said it. Most of the commentators agree that this was revealed about al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, who used to feed the people of Mina hais for three days, and he would call out, ‘No one should light a fire under a pot, no one should smoke from a foreleg, and whoever wants hais should come to al-Walid ibn al-Mughira. He would spend twenty thousand or more in a single Hajj, and would not give a single dirham to a poor person. It was said: He was a preventer of good. And about him was revealed the verse: And woe to the polytheists “who do not give zakat” (Fussilat 41:7). Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: It was revealed about Al-Akhnas ibn Shuraiq, because he was an ally attached to the Banu Zuhrah, and that is why he was called Zaneem. Ibn Abbas said: This verse is a description, so he was not recognized until he was killed, then he was recognized. He had a Zaneem around his neck by which he was recognized. Marra Al-Hamdani said: He only claimed him after eighteen years.
68:14: God the Almighty says: If he was a man of wealth and children Abu Ja'far, Ibn Amir, Abu Haywah, Al-Mughira and Al-A'raj read an kana with one extended hamza as a question. Al-Mufaddal, Abu Bakr and Hamzah read a'an kana with two definite hamzas. The rest read with one hamza as a statement. Whoever reads with an extended hamza or with two definite hamzas, then it is a question and the intended meaning is a rebuke. He should stop at zanim and begin with an kana with the meaning of because he was a man of wealth and children that you obey him. It is permissible to interpret it as: "Because he was a man of wealth and children, he says when Our verses are recited to him: Legends of the ancients!!" It is also permissible to interpret it as: Because he was a man of wealth and children, he disbelieves and is arrogant. This is indicated by the previous statement, so it becomes like what is mentioned after the question. Whoever reads an kana without a question, then it is an object for which the operator is an implied verb, and the interpretation is: he disbelieves because he was a man of wealth and children.
68:15: This verb is indicated by the following: When Our verses are recited to him, he says, 'Legends of the ancients.' Neither 'that' nor 'said' operate on the verb 'if' because what comes after 'if' does not operate on what comes before it, because 'if' is added to the clauses that follow it, and the complement does not operate on what comes before the complement. 'Qal' is the answer to the condition and does not operate on what comes before the condition, since the rule for the operator is that it comes before the complement, and the rule for the answer is that it comes after the condition, so it becomes presented or delayed in the state. It is possible that the meaning is 'do not obey him' because he was wealthy and numerous. Ibn al-Anbari said: Whoever reads without a question mark would not have stopped at 'zanim' because the meaning is 'was' and 'that he was', so 'an' is related to what comes before it. Someone else said: It is possible that it is related to his saying 'walked with pleasure' and the meaning is 'walked with gossip' because he was wealthy and children. Abu 'Ali permitted it to be related to 'atal'. 'Legends of the ancients' are their falsehoods, nonsense, and fables. This has been mentioned previously.
68:16: God Almighty said: We will brand him on the snout. There are two issues: The first: The Almighty’s statement: We will brand him. Ibn Abbas said: The meaning of We will brand him is that we will smash him with the sword. He said: The one about whom this verse was revealed was branded with the sword on the Day of Badr, and it remained branded until he died. Qatada said: We will brand him on the Day of Resurrection with a mark on his nose by which he will be known. It is said: I branded him, a mark, or a mark if a mark or cauterization has been left on him. God the Almighty said: The Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black (Al Imran 3:106). This is an apparent sign. God the Almighty said: And We will gather the criminals, that Day, blue (Ta-Ha: 102). This is another apparent sign. This verse indicates a third sign, which is the branding of the nose with fire. This is similar to His statement: The criminals will be known by their mark (al-Rahman 55:41). This was said by Al-Kalbi and others. Abu Al-Aaliyah and Mujahid said: We will brand him on the snout means on his nose, and We will blacken his face in the Hereafter, so he will be known by the blackness of his face. The snout is the nose of a human being. Among wild beasts, it is the location of the lip. The snouts of a people are their leaders. Al-Farra’ said: Even though the brand has been specifically used to describe the trunk, it is also used to mean the face, because some things are used to express the whole. Al-Tabari said: We will make his matter clear and distinct so that they will recognize him and it will not be hidden from them, just as the brand is not hidden from the trunks. It was said: The meaning is that we will brand him with shame and disgrace until he is like someone who has been branded on his nose. Al-Qutbi said: The Arabs say about a man who has been ascribed an ugly, lasting bad mark: He has been branded with the brand of evil, meaning that a disgrace has stuck to him that will not leave him, just as the mark cannot be erased. Jarir said: When I put my name on Al-Farazdaq and on Al-Baith, I cut off Al-Akhtal's nose. He meant it as satire. He said: All of this was revealed about Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira. We do not know that God Almighty has ever mentioned someone’s faults as much as he did, and has attached to them a disgrace that will not leave him in this world and the next, like a brand on the nose. It was said: It is what God afflicted him with in this world in himself, his wealth and his family of evil, humiliation and disgrace, Ibn Bahr said. He cited as evidence the words of Al-A’sha: Leave it and what does it benefit you? Turn to something else in your poetry and play with the nose of whoever you are and your name. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: The meaning is that we will punish him for drinking alcohol. Khartoum is for alcohol, and its plural is kharatheem. The poet said: You spend your day having fun and enjoying yourself, while at night you drink from the hoses. The rajaz poet said: A red-haired, strong-willed, and strong-willed woman Another said: Abu Hazer, whoever commits adultery will be known for his adultery, and whoever drinks from the hose will become intoxicated. Second: Ibn Al-Arabi said: Branding the face of the sinner was ancient among people, to the extent that it was narrated - as mentioned above - that when the Jews neglected stoning the adulterer, they compensated by beating and blackening the face, and this is a false fabrication. Among the correct branding on the face is what the scholars saw of blackening the face of a false witness, as a sign of the ugliness of the sin and to punish someone who was honored by speaking the truth but has become humiliated by the sin. The greatest humiliation is the humiliation of the face. Likewise, disdaining him in obeying God was a reason for eternal good and prohibiting him from entering the Fire, as God the Most High has forbidden the Fire to consume the traces of prostration from the son of Adam, according to what was proven in the Sahih.
68:17: First: The Almighty says: Indeed, We tested them meaning the people of Mecca. Testing is a trial. The meaning is that we gave them wealth so that they would be grateful, not so that they would be arrogant. When they became arrogant and opposed Muhammad (peace be upon him), we tested them with hunger and famine, just as we tested the people of Paradise, the report of which is well-known among them. This was in the land of Yemen, near them, several farsakhs from Sana'a - or it was said two farsakhs - and it belonged to a man who fulfilled God's right in it. When he died, it went to his sons, so they prevented the people from its goodness and were miserly with God's right in it, so God destroyed it from a place where they were unable to prevent what befell it. Al-Kalbi said: There were two farsakhs between them and Sana'a, and God tested them by burning their Paradise. It was said: It is a garden in Dhauran, and Dhauran is a farsakh from Sana'a. The people of this garden were stingy after the ascension of Jesus (peace be upon him) - and they were misers - so they would find dates at night for the sake of the poor. They wanted to harvest its crops and said: No poor person shall enter it upon you today. So they went to it in the morning and found that it had been uprooted and had become like a barren land, meaning like the night. The day is also called barren land. If he meant night, then its location would not be black. It is as if they found its location mud. If barren land was during the day, then it would mean the disappearance of the trees and crops and the purity of the land from them. It was Al-Ta'if that Gabriel (peace be upon him) circled around and uprooted it. It is said that he circled around the Ka'ba and then placed it where the city of Al-Ta'if is today, and that is why it was named Al-Ta'if. There is no other town in the Hijaz that has trees, grapes, and water except for it. Al-Bakri said in Al-Mu'jam: It was named Al-Ta'if because a man from the Sadaf tribe called Al-Damun built a wall and said: I have built you a barren land around your town, so it was named Al-Ta'if. And God knows best. Second: Some scholars said: Whoever harvests a crop that produces fruit must share it with those who are present. This is the meaning of the verse: And give its due on the day of its harvest (al-An’am 6:141). Some of them said: And upon him is leaving what the harvesters have taken. Some worshippers used to seek their sustenance from this. It was narrated that harvesting at night was forbidden. It was said: It is due to the kindness that is cut off from the poor in that. Those who said this interpreted the verse in Surat Nun and Surat Al-Qalam. It was said: It was only forbidden for fear of snakes and the vermin of the earth. I said: The first is more correct, and the second is good. We only said the first is more correct because the punishment was due to what they wanted to prevent the poor from eating, as God the Almighty mentioned. Asbat narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi who said: There were people in Yemen, and their father was a righteous man. When his crops were ripe, the poor would come to him, but he did not prevent them from entering them and eating from them and taking provisions. When he died, his sons said to one another: Why should we give our money to these poor people? Come, let us enter early and collect some of it before the poor know. They did not except him. So they set off, some of them saying to one another quietly: No poor person should enter it upon you today. This is what God the Almighty said: {When they swore} meaning they swore among themselves, {that they would harvest it in the morning} meaning that they would harvest it in the morning before the poor came out. They did not except him, meaning they did not say, God willing. Ibn Abbas said: That garden was two farsakhs from Sana'a. It was planted by a righteous man who had three sons. The poor had everything that the sickle could not reach from the vineyard. When it was thrown on the rug, everything that fell from the rug also belonged to the poor. When they harvested their crops, everything that the sickle could not reach also belonged to the poor. When they harvested their crops, everything that the sickle could not reach also belonged to the poor. When they threshed everything that was scattered, their father used to give charity from it to the poor. During their father's lifetime, he lived on that for the orphans, widows, and the poor. When their father died, they did what God mentioned about them. They said: Wealth is little and children are many. So they disagreed among themselves that they would go out early in the morning before the people leave, then harvest some of it so that the poor would not be recognized. His statement, When they swore, means they swore to harvest it, to cut down their palm trees when morning came in the middle of the night so that the poor would not notice them. And harvesting is cutting. It is said: The abundant rain has been harvested from the palm tree. And the palm tree was harvested means the time for harvesting it had come. Like I ride the horse and harvest the crops, meaning it is time to ride it and harvest it
68:18: And they do not make an exception meaning they did not say, God willing. It was said that the meaning of And they do not make an exception is they do not make an exception for the right of the poor, as said by Ikrimah. So they came to it at night and saw Paradise blackened and a tour guide from your Lord had visited it while they were asleep. It was said that the tour guide was Gabriel, peace be upon him, as mentioned above. Ibn Abbas said: A command from your Lord. Qatada said: A punishment from your Lord. Ibn Jurayj said: A neck of fire emerging from the valley of Hell. And the tour guide only occurs at night, said Al-Farra'. Third: I said: This verse is evidence that resolve is something for which a person will be held accountable, because they resolved to do something and were punished before they did it. Similar to this verse is the Almighty’s statement: And they did not persist in what they did (Al Imran 3:135).
68:19: A company from your Lord swept over them while they were asleep.
68:20: The Almighty said: So it became like a barren field meaning like a dark night, according to Ibn Abbas, Al-Farra’ and others. The poet said: Your dark night is long, but it does not give birth to a dark morning. That is, it was burned and became like a black night. And also from Ibn Abbas: Like black ash. He said: Al-Sareem is black ash in the language of Khuzaymah. Al-Thawri: Like harvested crops. Al-Sareem means the one whose contents were cut off. Al-Hasan said: The good was cut off from it, meaning it was cut off, so Al-Sareem is also a passive participle. Al-Muwarij said: That is, like the sand that has been cut off from most of the sand. It is said: Sareema and Sareem, so the sand does not grow anything useful. Al-Akhfash said: That is, like the morning that has passed from the night. Al-Mubarrad said: That is, like the day, so there is nothing in it. Shammar said: Al-Sareem is the night and Al-Sareem is the day, that is, this is cut off from that and that from this. It was said: The night is called Sareem because it cuts off from action with its darkness, and for this reason Fa’il has the meaning of Fa’il. Al-Qushayri said: There is a problem with this, because the day is called Sareem and it is not cut off from action.
68:21: They called out to each other in the morning.
68:22: Go forth to your tillage, if you should be determined to harvest and reap. Qatada said: Harvesting your crops. Al-Kalbi said: There were no crops or palm trees in their garden. Mujahid said: Their tillage was grapes, and they did not say, God willing. Abu Salih said: Their exception was their saying, Glory be to God, our Lord.
68:23: The Almighty says: So they set out, speaking in low voices. That is, they whispered, that is, they kept their speech secret so that no one would know about them. This was stated by Ata' and Qatadah. It is derived from the verb khafa to be still which means to be quiet and not clear. As Duraid ibn al-Summah said: I did not perish in vain, nor did I die in humiliation. Everyone has a bad opinion of me. It was said that they hid themselves from people so that they would not be seen. Their father would inform the poor and needy so that they would be present at harvest time.
68:24: That no poor person shall enter it upon you today.
68:25: And they went forth with determination and ability meaning with intent and ability in themselves and they thought that they had achieved their goal. Ibn Abbas and others said the same meaning. Harad means intention. Harad yahrid with kasra means hardan means intention. You say: haradatt haradak, meaning I intended your intention. And from this the rajaz poet said: A torrent came from God, rushing with the rush of the enchanted paradise. An-Nahhas recited: A torrent has come, by the command of God, rushing like the rush of a flooded paradise. Al-Mubarrad said: Al-Mughalla is the one with the yield. Another said: Al-Mughalla is the one in which water runs through its roots, i.e. in its roots. From this, it is said: Taghalaltu with Al-Ghaliya. From this, it is said: Taghalitat, replacing the Lam with a Ya. Whoever says Taghalaqtat means, according to him, I made it a covering. Qatada and Mujahid said: On hardness, i.e. on seriousness. Al-Hasan: On need and poverty. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Qutaibi said: On hardness on prevention, from their saying: Haradat Al-Ibil Haradan, i.e. their milk has decreased. Al-Harood is one of the camels with few milks. Haradat Al-Sana’ah means its rain and goodness have decreased. Al-Suddi and Sufyan said: On hardness on anger. And hardness is anger. Abu Nasr Ahmad bin Hatim, the companion of Al-Asma’i, said: It is lightened, and he recited poetry: If the horses came to drink, filled with anger and resentment Ibn Al-Sikkit said: It may be moved, so you say from it: ُهِرkasraهُِانhardan, so it is ُهِرandهُِانhardan. And from it it was said: ُسُهِرharad and ُهوارُهو. And it was said: on ُهِرalone, on ُهِرon his own. It is said: هِعوُانُيهِرُهِرhe moved away from his people and settled down alone and did not mix with them. Abu Zaid said: A ُهِرman from aهِرُاءharda people. And ُهِر ُهِعوُيهِرhe left his people and turned away from them. And a ُهِرa star means isolated from the stars. Al-Asma’i said: A ُهِرman means unique and solitary. He said: The one who moves away is the one who is alone in the language of Hudhayl. And he recited for Abu Dhu’ayb: As if he is a moving star in the sky. Abu ‘Umar narrated it with a jim and explained it as: singular. He said: It is Suhayl. Al-Azhari said: ُهِرis the name of their village. Al-Suddi: the name of their paradise, and there are two dialects for it: ُهِرand ُهِر. The common people read it with sukun. Abu Al-‘Aliyah and Ibn Al-Sumaiq read it with fathah, and they are two dialects. The meaning of capable is that they have determined their matter and built upon it, said Al-Farra’. Qatada said: Capable of their Paradise in their own eyes. Al-Sha’bi said: Capable means over the poor. It was also said that its meaning is from existence, meaning they were prevented while they were able to find it.
68:26: God the Almighty said: And when they saw it, they said, 'Indeed, we are astray.' That is, when they saw it burnt, with nothing in it, and it had become like a black night, looking at it like ashes, they denied it and doubted it. And some of them said to one another, Indeed, we are astray, meaning, we have lost our way to our Paradise, as Qatada said. It was also said: That is, we are astray from the right path in our setting out with the intention of preventing the poor, and for that reason we were punished.
68:27: Rather, we are deprived, meaning we were deprived of our Paradise because of what we did. Asbat narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Beware of sins. A servant may commit a sin and thereby be deprived of a provision that was provided for him." Then he recited: And a visit from your Lord swept over it and the two verses."
68:28: God the Almighty says: Their middle one said, meaning the best, most just, and most intelligent of them. Did I not tell you, 'Why do you not glorify God?' That is, why do you not make an exception? Their exclusion was glorification, as stated by Mujahid and others. This indicates that this middle one ordered them to make an exception, but they did not obey him. Abu Salih said: Their exclusion was Glory be to God. So he said to them: Why do you not glorify God? That is, say Glory be to God and thank Him for what He has given you? An-Nahhas said: The root of glorification is to sanctify God, the Almighty, the Majestic. Mujahid put glorification in place of Insha God, because the meaning is to sanctify God, the Almighty, from having anything happen except by His will. It was also said: Why do you not ask His forgiveness for your actions and repent to Him for the evil of your intentions? So the middle one said to them when they decided to do that and reminded them of His vengeance on the criminals.
68:29: They said, 'Glory be to our Lord.' They admitted their sin and declared God free from being unjust in what He did. Ibn Abbas said about their saying, Glory be to our Lord, that it means we seek forgiveness from God for our sin. Indeed, we were unjust to ourselves in withholding food from the poor.
68:30: So some of them turned to others, blaming each other, meaning that one blamed the other for the division and preventing the poor, and said: Rather, you have made us drink with this.
68:31: "They said, 'Woe to us! We were indeed transgressors.'" That is, disobedient by denying the rights of the poor and failing to make exceptions. Ibn Kaysan said: We were transgressors in our duty to God and did not thank Him for His blessings as our fathers had been before.
68:32: Perhaps our Lord will give us in exchange something better than it. They made a contract and said, If God gives us in exchange something better than it, we will do as our fathers did. So they supplicated to God and beseeched Him, so God gave them in exchange something better than their night. He ordered Gabriel to uproot that burnt garden and place it in Zaghar, in the land of Ash-Sham, and to take a garden from Ash-Sham and replace it. Ibn Mas'ud said, The people were sincere, and God knew their sincerity, so He gave them in exchange something called Al-Hayawan, in which there were grapes, from which a mule could carry a single cluster. Al-Yamani Abu Khalid said, I entered that garden and saw every cluster of grapes like a standing black man. Al-Hasan said, "The saying of the people of Paradise, 'Indeed, we are yearning for our Lord,' I do not know whether that was faith from them, or something similar to what happens to the polytheists when they are afflicted with hardship, which makes it difficult to determine whether they are believers." Qatada was asked about the people of Paradise: Are they more like the people of Paradise or the people of Hellfire? He said: You have made me tired. Most say: They repented and were sincere, narrated by Al-Qushayri. The general reading is yubaddalna with a light pronunciation. The people of Medina, Abu Omar, read it with a heavy pronunciation, and they are two dialects. It was said: Al-tabadul means changing something or changing its state, and the essence of something is established. Al-Ibdallal means raising something and putting another in its place. This has been discussed in Surat An-Nisa’.”
68:33: The Almighty says: Such is the punishment meaning the punishment of this world and the loss of wealth. It was narrated from Ibn Zayd. It was said that this is an admonition to the people of Mecca to return to God when He afflicted them with drought due to the supplication of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), meaning as We did to them, We will do to those who transgressed Our limits in this world. And the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew. Ibn Abbas said: This is an example of the people of Mecca when they went out to Badr and swore to kill Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions, and to return to Mecca so that they could circumambulate the House and drink wine, and have female singers play on their heads. But God disappointed them and they were captured, killed, and defeated, just like the people of this Paradise when they went out intending to harvest and were disappointed. Then it was said that the right that the poor people of Paradise denied them may have been obligatory upon them, or it may have been voluntary, but the former is more apparent, and God knows best. It was also said that the Surah is Meccan, after interpreting the verse to refer to the drought that afflicted the people of Mecca and to the Battle of Badr.
68:34: The Almighty's saying: Indeed, for the righteous, with their Lord are gardens of pleasure. This has been discussed previously, meaning that for the righteous in the Hereafter there are gardens in which there is nothing but pure pleasure, untainted by anything that spoils it as is the case with the gardens of this world. The leaders of Quraysh saw their abundant share of this world and the small share of the Muslims in it, so when they heard talk of the Hereafter and what God had promised the believers, they said: If it is more true that we will be resurrected, as Muhammad and those with him claim, then our condition and their condition would not be except like it is in this world. Otherwise, they would not have surpassed us or preferred us, and the most they would do is to be equal to us.
68:35: He said: Shall We then treat the Muslims like the criminals? That is, like the disbelievers. Ibn Abbas and others said: The disbelievers of Mecca said: We will be given better in the Hereafter than what you are given. So the verse Shall We then treat the Muslims like the criminals? was revealed.
68:36: Then he rebuked them and said: What is the matter with you? How do you judge? This crooked judgment. The matter of punishment was entrusted to you so that you could judge it as you wished. You have the same good as the Muslims.
68:37: Or do you have a book in which you study? That is, do you have a book in which you find the obedient and the disobedient?
68:38: Indeed, for you therein is that which you choose you choose and desire. The meaning is: that you have with the fatha but it is kasra due to the introduction of the lam. You say I knew that you were rational with the fatha, and I knew that you were rational with the kasra. So the operator in indeed, for you therein is that which you choose is you study in the meaning. And the lam prevented the opening of in and it was said: The speech was completed when he said: you study then he began and said indeed, for you therein is that which you choose meaning that in this book you have then what you choose, meaning that it is not for you. The pronoun in indeed, for it the first and second refers back to the book. Then he increased the rebuke.
68:39: Or do you have oaths? meaning covenants and pacts. Upon Us is decisive is emphatic, and decisive is with God the Most High. That is, do you have covenants with God the Most High that you have secured that He will admit you into Paradise? Indeed, you will have that which you judge. The word in was broken because the lam was included in the predicate. It is from the connection of oaths, and the position is accusative, but it was broken because of the lam. You say: I swore that you will have such-and-such. It was said that the discussion ended with the Almighty's saying: Until the Day of Resurrection, then He said: Indeed, you will have that which you judge. So, that is, the matter is not like that.
