Ibn Hormuz read Ayn lakum fihi lama atkhayaruna, ayn lakum lama juhkum with the question in both of them. Al-Hasan al-Basri read baligha in the accusative as a state, either from the pronoun in lakum because it is a predicate of faith, so it contains a pronoun from it. Or from the pronoun in Upon Us if you are able to judge us describing the oaths, not connected to the oaths themselves, because it contains a pronoun from it, as it would be if it was a predicate of it. It is possible that it is a state of oaths even if it is indefinite, just as they used the accusative case of haqq as a state of enjoyment in the Almighty’s saying: Enjoyment in a just manner is a duty upon the righteous (al-Baqarah 2:124). The general public read balighah in the nominative case as an attribute of oaths.
68:40: God the Almighty said: Ask them which of them is responsible for that. That is, O Muhammad, ask these slanderers which of them is responsible for what was mentioned above. That is, that they will have the same good as the Muslims. The leader is the guarantor and the guarantor, as stated by Ibn Abbas and Qatadah. Ibn Kaysan said: The leader here is the one who stands up with the argument and the claim. Al-Hasan said: The leader is the Messenger. Or have they partners? That is, the ha and the mim are connectives. Partners means witnesses. Then let them produce their partners to testify to what they claim.
68:41: If they are truthful in their claim. It was also said: that is, let them bring their partners if they are able to, so it is a command that means to compel.
68:42: The Almighty's saying: The Day the shin shall be laid bare. It is possible that the agent in the Day is they shall come meaning, they shall bring their partners on the Day the shin shall be laid bare so that the partners may intercede for them. It is also possible for it to be in the accusative case with an implied verb, meaning, mention the Day the shin shall be laid bare, so one stops at truthful and does not stop at the first estimation. The word the Day we uncover was read with a noon. Ibn Abbas read the Day we uncover the shin as a construction named after the doer, meaning, we uncover the severity or the Resurrection from its shin, like their saying: the war rolled up its shin. The poet said: A war boy, if war bites him, he bites it, and if war rolls up its leg, he rolls it up. The rajaz poet said: She has uncovered her leg, so tighten it. I have found war with you, so pull it. Another said: I was amazed at myself, at my compassion, and at the birds’ flight from their nests. In a year that has revealed its red leg, revealing the flesh from its sweat Another said: She revealed her leg to them and the evil became clear It was also narrated from Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan and Abu Al-Aaliyah that we uncover with a taa’ that is not the name of the agent. This reading goes back to the meaning of uncover, as if he said: The Day the Resurrection will uncover severity. It was read on the Day of Resurrection with a damma on the taa’ and a kasra on the sheen, from the root akshaf, which means to uncover. And from this: a man uncovers, so he is uncovered, if his upper lip is turned up. Ibn Al-Mubarak said: Usamah bin Zaid informed us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse: The Day the shin will be uncovered, he said: From distress and severity. Ibn Jurayj informed us, from Mujahid, who said: The severity of the matter and its seriousness. Mujahid said: Ibn Abbas said: It is the most intense hour on the Day of Resurrection. Abu Ubaidah said: When the war or the matter intensifies, it is said: The matter has been uncovered from its shin. The origin of this is that whoever falls into something that requires seriousness rolls up his shin, so the shin and uncovering it were borrowed to refer to severity. It was also said: The shin of something is its origin by which it is sustained, like the shin of a tree and the shin of a human being. That is, the Day the origin of the matter will be uncovered, so the truths of matters and their origins will be revealed. It was also said: The shin of Hell will be uncovered. It was said: From the leg of the throne. It was also said: He means the time of approaching death and the weakness of the body, that is, the sick person uncovers his leg to see his weakness, and the muezzin calls him to prayer, but he is unable to stand and go out. As for what was narrated that God uncovers His leg, then He, the Almighty, is above the limbs and hatred, and that He uncovers and covers. Its meaning is that He reveals the greatness of His affair. It was also said: He reveals His light, the Almighty, the Almighty. Abu Musa narrated: On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his saying, the Most High, about the shin, he said: A great light will be uncovered before which they will fall down in prostration. Abu al-Layth al-Samarqandi said in his interpretation: Al-Khalil bin Ahmad told us, he said: Ibn Mani’ told us, he said: Hudbah told us, he said: Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Ammarah al-Qurashi, on the authority of Abu Burdah, on the authority of Abu Musa, he said: My father told me, he said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: When the Day of Resurrection comes, what they used to worship in this world will be shown to every people. Every people will go to what they used to worship, and the people of monotheism will remain. It will be said to them, ‘What are you waiting for?’ They will say, ‘We have a Lord whom we used to worship in this world and we did not see Him.’ He said, ‘And you will recognize Him when you see Him.’ They will say, ‘Yes.’ It will be said, ‘How can you recognize Him when you have not seen Him?’ They will say, ‘He has no equal.’ Then the veil will be uncovered for them and they will look at God Almighty and fall down in prostration before Him. And there will remain people whose backs will be like the hooves of cows. They will look at God Almighty and want to prostrate but will not be able to. This is what God Almighty said: “On the Day the shin will be uncovered and they will call out, To prostrate, but they are unable to. Then God the Almighty will say, “My servants, raise your heads, for I have replaced every man among you with a man from the Jews and Christians in the Fire.” Abu Burdah said: “I narrated this hadith to Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, and he said, ‘By God, there is no god but Him, has your father narrated this hadith to you?’ So he swore three oaths to him. Umar said, ‘I have not heard a hadith from the people of monotheism that is more beloved to me than this.’” Qais ibn al-Sakn said: “Abdullah ibn Mas’ud narrated to Umar ibn al-Khattab, and he said, ‘When the Day of Resurrection comes, the people will stand before the Lord of the Worlds for forty years, their eyes fixed on the sky, barefoot, naked, and bridled with sweat. God will not speak to them or look at them for forty years. Then a caller will call out, ‘O people, is it not just from your Lord, who created you, shaped you, caused you to die, and gave you life, then you worshipped other than Him, that He should appoint every people to what they appointed?’ They said, ‘Yes.’” He said: “Then every people will be returned to what they used to worship besides God, and they will follow it until it throws them into the Fire. Then the Muslims and the hypocrites will remain, and it will be said to them: ‘Will you not go, for the people have gone?’ They will say: ‘Until our Lord comes to us.’ It will be said to them: ‘Do you recognize Him?’ They will say: ‘If he confesses to us, we will recognize Him.’ He said: “Then at that time He will uncover His shin and appear to them, and those who used to worship Him sincerely will fall down in prostration, and the hypocrites will remain, unable to do so, as if there were skewers on their backs. He will take them to the Fire, and these will enter Paradise. This is what God the Most High said: ‘And they are invited to prostrate, but they are unable.’”
68:43: Their eyes will be humbled meaning submissive and humble, and the accusative is in the state of humiliation will overwhelm them meaning that the believers will raise their heads and their faces will be whiter than snow. The faces of the hypocrites and disbelievers will turn black until they become blacker than tar. I said: The meaning of the hadith of Abu Musa and Ibn Masoud is confirmed in Sahih Muslim from the hadith of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri and others. God the Almighty says: And they were called to prostrate meaning in this world. while they were safe meaning healthy and sound. Ibrahim At-Taymi said: That is, they were called with the call to prayer and the call to stand, but they refused. Saeed ibn Jubayr said: They used to hear “Hayya ‘ala al-Falah but they did not respond.” Ka’b Al-Ahbar said: By God, this verse was only revealed about those who stayed away from congregational prayers. It was also said: That is, regarding the obligation imposed on them by the Shari’ah, and the meanings are similar. The obligation of congregational prayer was discussed in Surat Al-Baqarah. Ar-Rabi’ ibn Khaitham had paralyzed and he used to help two men to get to the mosque. It was said: O Abu Yazid, if you prayed in your house, you would have been excused. He said: Whoever hears “Hayya ‘ala al-Falah should respond, even if he has to crawl.” It was said to Saeed ibn Al-Musayyab: Tariq wants to kill you, so hide. He said: So that God cannot overpower me? It was said to him: Sit in your house. He said: I hear “Hayya ‘ala al-Falah, but I will not respond!”
68:44: The Almighty said: So leave me meaning leave me. And whoever denies is an object with it or is conjoined with the first person pronoun. With this hadith meaning the Qur'an, as al-Suddi said. It was also said: on the Day of Resurrection. This is a consolation for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, meaning I will reward them and take revenge on them. Then He said: We will gradually seize them from where they do not know meaning We will seize them unawares, so they were punished on the day of Badr. Sufyan al-Thawri said: We will bestow blessings upon them and make them forget to be grateful. Al-Hasan said: How many are lured by being treated kindly, how many are tempted by being praised, and how many are deceived by being covered up for. Abu Ruq said: Every time they commit a sin, We will renew a blessing for them and make them forget to seek forgiveness. Ibn Abbas said: We will plot against them. It was also said: It means that We will seize them gradually and not surprise them. In a hadith. A man from the Children of Israel said, O Lord, how often have I disobeyed You and You do not punish me. So God revealed to the prophet of their time, Say to him, ‘How many punishments have I against you and you do not perceive?’ The dullness of your eyes and the hardness of your heart are a temptation from Me and a punishment if it were suspended. Temptation means abandoning treatment. Transferring from one state to another is like gradualism. From this it is said, ‘degree,’ which is a station after a station. So-and-so tempted so-and-so, meaning he extracted a little of what he had. It is said, ‘degree to such-and-such,’ and he tempted him with one meaning, meaning he brought him closer to him gradually, so he was gradual.
68:45: And I will grant them respite means I will give them time and extend their period. Mulāḥa means a period of time. And God granted him respite, meaning He extended it for him. Al-Mulwān means the night and the day. It was also said: And I will grant them respite meaning I will not hasten their death, and the meaning is the same. This has been explained previously in Al-A'raf. Indeed, My plan is firm meaning My punishment is strong and severe, so no one can escape Me.
68:46: God Almighty says: Or do you ask them for a reward, so they are burdened with debt? The discussion returns to what was mentioned earlier in the Almighty's statement: Or do they have partners? That is, do you seek from them a reward for what you are calling them to of faith in God? They are burdened by the penalty of that, given the difficulty it takes to spend money. That is, there is no cost to them; rather, by following you, they will seize control of the earth's treasures and attain the gardens of bliss.
68:47: God Almighty says: Or do they have knowledge of the unseen? That is, knowledge of what is hidden from them. So they write. It was also said: Is the revelation sent down to them based on what they say? Ibn Abbas reported: The unseen here is the Preserved Tablet, so they write what is in it and dispute with you about it, and they write that they are better than you and that they will not be punished. It was also said: They write means they rule for yourselves as they wish.
68:49: The Almighty says: Had it not been that a blessing from his Lord had overtaken him The general reading is tadarakkahu. Ibn Hurmuz and Al-Hasan read tadarakkahu with a shaddah on the dal. It is a present tense verb whose ta' was assimilated into the dal. It is based on the narration of the situation, as if he said: Had it not been that a blessing had overtaken him. Ibn Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud said: tadarakkahu, which is contrary to the established ruling. Tadarakkahu is a past tense masculine verb that has been interpreted to mean blessing, because the feminine of blessing is not real. Tadarakkahu is pronounced as such. There is disagreement over the meaning of blessing here, because it is prophethood, as Ad-Dahhak said. It was also said that it is his worship that preceded, as Abu Jubayr said. It was also said that it is his call "There is no god but You, glory be to You. Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers," as Ibn Zayd said. It was also said that the blessing of God upon him was his being brought out of the belly of the whale, as Ibn Bahr said. It was also said that it means mercy from his Lord, so He had mercy on him and accepted his repentance. He was cast out into the open, and he was blameworthy. That is, he was cast out blameworthy, but he was cast out sick and not blameworthy. The meaning of blameworthy according to Ibn Abbas is: blameworthy. Bakr ibn Abdullah said: guilty. It was also said: blameworthy is far from all good. The open space is the vast, open land in which there are no mountains or trees to provide cover. It was also said: Had it not been for God's grace upon him, he would have remained in the belly of the whale until the Day of Resurrection, then he would have been cast out into the open space of the Resurrection, blameworthy. This is indicated by the words of God the Almighty: And had he not been of those who glorify God "He would have remained inside its belly until the Day they are resurrected" (Saffat: 144).
68:50: And made him among the righteous. Ibn Abbas said: God returned the revelation to him, and interceded for him in himself and for his people, and accepted his repentance, and made him among the righteous by sending him to one hundred thousand or more.
68:51: The Almighty says: "And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip" inna is the lightened form of the heavy one. "They would almost make you slip means they would stumbling upon you with their eyes" He informed us of the intensity of their hostility towards the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and they wanted to cast the evil eye on him. Some people from Quraysh looked at him and said: We have never seen anyone like him or his arguments. It was also said that the evil eye was among Banu Asad, to the extent that a fat cow or a fat she-camel would pass by one of you and he would examine it and say: "O girl, take the bucket and the dirham and bring us the meat of this she-camel." It would not move until it fell down to die and was slaughtered. Al-Kalbi said: There was an Arab man who would not eat anything for two or three days, then he would lift the side of the tent and camels or sheep would pass by him and he would say: "I have never seen camels or sheep more beautiful than these!" They would not go far before a group of them would fall down and perish. The infidels asked this man to cast the evil eye on the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he agreed. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by, he recited: Your people used to think you were a master, but I think you were a certain master. So God protected His Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), and the verse: And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip was revealed. Al-Mawardi mentioned something similar to this, and that when one of the Arabs wanted to harm someone - meaning his life or his wealth - he would starve himself for three days, then he would threaten himself and his wealth and say: By God, I have never seen anyone stronger, braver, more numerous, or more handsome than him. He would then harm him with his evil eye, and he and his wealth would perish. So God revealed this verse. Al-Qushayri said: “This is questionable, because harm by the evil eye only occurs with approval and admiration, not with hatred and loathing. That is why He said: “And they say, ‘He is mad,’” meaning they would attribute you to a madman if they saw you reciting the Quran. I said: The statements of the commentators and linguists indicate what we have mentioned, and that what they meant by looking at him is killing him. Disliking something does not prevent enmity from being afflicted by the evil eye until it is destroyed. Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masoud, Al-A'mash, Abu Wa'il and Mujahid read "li-yazahiqunaka meaning to destroy you. This is a reading according to the interpretation, from zahaqat anfshu and azhaqahu." The people of Medina read it with a fatha on the ya'. The rest read it with a damma. They are two dialects with the same meaning. It is said: "zalaqahu yazlaquhu and azlaqahu yazlaquhu izlaqan" if they moved him away and sent him far away. "Zalaqa ra'shu yazlaquhu zilaqan" if they shaved his head. Similarly, "azlaqahu and zalaquhu tazliqan" are also used. A man who is "zalaq and zamlaq - like hudbad - and zamalek and zamlaq" - with a shaddah on the meem - is the one who ejaculates before intercourse, as reported by Al-Jawhari and others. The meaning of the word is moving away and removing, and that does not happen in the case of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) except by his destruction and death. Al-Harawi said: He meant that they may attack you with their eyes and remove you from the position in which God has established you, out of enmity towards you. Ibn Abbas said: They may rescue you with their sight. It is said: An arrow slipped and pierced if it penetrated, and this is the opinion of Mujahid. That is, they may pierce you with the intensity of their gaze. Al-Kalbi said: They may overpower you. Also from him, as-Suddi and Saeed ibn Jubayr said: They may divert you from what you are doing in conveying the message. Al-Awfi said: They may shoot you. Al-Mu’ajj said: They may remove you. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl and Al-Akhfash said: They may tempt you. Abdul-Aziz ibn Yahya said: They may look at you askance with intense stare. Ibn Zayd said: They may touch you. Ja’far Al-Sadiq said: They may eat you. Al-Hasan and Ibn Kaysan said: They may kill you. This is like saying: He overpowered me with his glance, and killed me with his eye. The poet said: The eyes of the sled throw you with their end and the arrows of the archer leave you Another said: They borrow when they meet in a council, because the footsteps slip. It was also said that the meaning is that they look at you with hostility until they almost make you fall. All of this goes back to what we mentioned, and that the comprehensive meaning is: they afflict you with the evil eye. And God knows best.
68:52: God Almighty says: And it is only a reminder to the worlds. The Qur’an is only a reminder to the worlds. It was also said that Muhammad is only a reminder to the worlds by which they are reminded. It was also said that its meaning is honor, meaning the Qur’an. As God Almighty said: And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is also an honor to the worlds. They were honored by following him and believing in him, may God bless him and grant him peace.
69:1: Surah Al-Haqqah is Meccan according to everyone. It has fifty-one verses. Abu Al-Zaharia narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever recites eleven verses of Surat Al-Haqqah will be protected from the trial of the Antichrist. And whoever recites them will have a light on the Day of Resurrection from the top of his head to his feet.” In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. God the Almighty says: The Inevitable * What is the Inevitable? He means the Day of Resurrection. It was called this because matters will be established in it, as At-Tabari said. It is as if he made it from the root word night of a sleeper. It was also said that it was called this because it will be without doubt. It was also said that it was called this because it is certain for the people of Paradise, and certain for the people of Hell. It was also said that it was called this because in it every person will be truly rewarded for his deeds. Al-Azhari said: It is said that he overcame him and defeated him, meaning he overcame him and overcame him. So the Day of Resurrection is this Inevitable because it will establish every false opponent in the religion of God, meaning every disputant. In As-Sahah: And he overcame him means he argued with him and each of them claimed the truth, so if he overcame him, his right was claimed. And it is said about a man who argues about small matters: He is a stubborn, stubborn person. And it is said: He has neither right nor right in it, meaning a dispute. And the joining of the dispute. And enforcing: a dispute. Al-Haqqah, Al-Haqqah, and Al-Haqq are three languages with the same meaning. Al-Kisa’i and Al-Muraj said: The Inevitable Day is the Day of Truth. The Arabs say: When he knew the Inevitable from me, he fled. The first Inevitable is raised by the subject, and the predicate is the second subject and its predicate, which is what is the Inevitable.
69:2: What is the Inevitable? because it means what is it. The word is an interrogative, meaning to glorify and magnify his status, as you say: Zaid, what Zaid! to glorify his status.
69:3: And what will make you know what the Inevitable is? is also a question, meaning, what will make you know what that Day is? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) knew about the Resurrection, but the description. So it was said, to emphasize its importance: And what will make you know what it is? As if you do not know it since you have not witnessed it. Yahya ibn Salam said: I have been informed that everything in the Qur'an is And what will make you know, meaning it has made it known and taught it. And everything in which it says And what will make you know is something that he did not know. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: Everything in which it says And what will make you know means it has informed about it, and everything in which it says And what will make you know means it has not informed about it.
69:4: God Almighty said: Thamud and Aad denied the terrible calamity. Mention of those who deny the Resurrection. The Qari'ah is the Resurrection, and it was named thus because it strikes people with its terrors. It is said: the calamities of time struck them, meaning its terrors and hardships. We seek refuge in God from the calamities of so-and-so, his stings, and the stings of his tongue, the plural of Qari'ah, which is a hurtful word. The Qari'ah of the Qur'an: the verses that a person recites when frightened by jinn or humans, such as the Throne Verse, as if it strikes the devil. It was said: The Qari'ah is taken from the word qara'ah, which refers to the elevation of some people and the debasement of others, as stated by Al-Mubarrad. It was also said: He meant by the Qari'ah the torment that befell them in this world, and their prophet would frighten them with that so they would deny him. And Thamud and the people of Salih, and their homes were in Al-Hijr between Ash-Sham and Al-Hijaz. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: It is Wadi Al-Qura, and they were Arabs. As for 'Ad, they were the people of Hud, and their homes were in Al-Ahqaf. Al-Ahqaf is the sand dunes between Oman, Hadhramaut, and all of Yemen, and they were Arabs with good manners and simplicity, mentioned by Muhammad ibn Ishaq. It has been presented.
69:5: God Almighty said: As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the oppressor. It contains an implied meaning, that is, by the overwhelming action. Qatada said: That is, by the overwhelming shout, that is, exceeding the limit, that is, the limit of shouts of terror. As He said: Indeed, We sent upon them a single shout, and at once they were like dry stubble (al-Qamar 54:31). And tyranny means exceeding the limit. From this, Indeed, when the water overflowed (al-Haqqah 69:11), that is, it exceeded the limit. Al-Kalbi said: By the overwhelming thunderbolt. Mujahid said: By sins. Al-Hasan said: By tyranny, so it is a verbal noun like the lie, the consequence, and the well-being. That is, they were destroyed by their tyranny and disbelief. It was said: The tyrant hamstrung the she-camel, as Ibn Zayd said. That is, they were destroyed by what their tyrant did in hamstringing the she-camel. It was only one person, but they all perished because they were satisfied with his action and complied with him. He was called a tyrant, just as one says: So-and-so is a narrator of poetry, a shrewd person, a scholar, and a genealogist.
69:6: God the Almighty said: And as for 'Aad, they were destroyed by a furious wind meaning a cold one that pierces with its coldness like the burning of fire. It is derived from sar which means cold, as Ad-Dahhak said. It was also said that it refers to a loud sound. Mujahid said: a very poisonous wind. Overpowering means it rebelled against its storehouses and did not obey them, and they could not bear it because of the severity of its blowing. It became angry for the sake of God's anger. It was also said that it rebelled against 'Aad and subdued them. Sufyan al-Thawri narrated on the authority of Musa ibn al-Musayyab on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘God did not send a breeze except by measure, nor a drop of water except by measure, except on the Day of ‘Aad and the Day of Noah. For the water on the Day of Noah overflowed the storehouses, and they had no way to reach it.’ Then he recited: ‘Indeed, when the water overflowed, We carried you in the floating ship.’ (al-Haqqah 69:11) And the wind on the Day of ‘Aad overcame the storehouses, and they had no way to reach it. Then he recited: ‘by a furious, violent wind.’”
69:7: He subjected it to them meaning He sent it down to them in the middle. Subjugation means using something with power. Seven nights and eight days in succession meaning consecutively, without slackening or interruption, according to Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masoud and others. Al-Farra' said: Al-Hasoom means succession, from the root word hasam which means to cauterize the patient, because he cauterizes with an iron and then continues doing that to him. Abdul Aziz bin Zararah Al-Kalabi said: A time has separated them, in which years of decisiveness have followed one another. Al-Mubarrad said: It is from the saying he hasamt something if you cut it off from something else. It was also said: Hassam means extermination. The sword is called Husam because it stops the enemy from what he wants to achieve in his enmity. The poet said: Hussam, if you stand up supported by him, it is enough to return from him. The beginning is not a support. Meaning: It has decisively cut them off, that is, it has cut them off and eliminated them. It is the cutter with the torment of extermination. Abu Zaid said: It has decisively cut them off and left not a single one of them. It is also reported that it has decisively cut off the nights and days until it has completely covered them, because it begins with sunrise on the first day and ends with sunset on the last day. Al-Layth said: Al-Hasum is the ominous. It is said: These are the nights of Al-Hasum, meaning it cuts off good from its people, and this is what is stated in Al-Sahah. Ikrimah and Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: They are ominous, the evidence for which is the statement of God the Almighty: {in days of ill omen} Fussilat 41:16 Atiyyah Al-Awfi: Hasuman means it has cut off good from its people. There is disagreement about its beginning, some said: Wednesday morning, said Al-Suddi. It is said: Friday morning, said Al-Rabi’ bin Anas. It is said: Wednesday morning, said Yahya bin Salam Wahb bin Munabbih. Wahb said: These days are what the Arabs call the days of the old woman, with strong cold and wind. The first of them was on Wednesday, and the last of them was on Wednesday. They were named after the old woman because an old woman from Aad entered a flock and the wind followed her and killed her on the eighth day. It was said: They were called the days of the old woman because they fell in the last part of winter. It is in March, one of the Syriac months. It has famous names, and the poet Ibn Ahmar said about it: Winter broke in seven days, and we were stricken with grief during the month. When her days have passed and she has gone, like a sun and a sapphire with the fur And by order and his brother, the conference and the reason and the extinguisher of the coals Winter has gone away quickly, and the sun has come to you, blazing from the sky. And Hasuman is in the accusative case as a state. It was also said that it is in the verbal noun. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, He cast them out, hasuman, meaning He banished them, and it is a confirmed verbal noun. It may also be an object for it, meaning He subjected it to them for this period of time for the purpose of extermination, meaning to cut them off and uproot them. It may also be the plural of hasim. Al-Suddi read Hasuman with a fat-ha, as a state of the wind, meaning He subjected it to them, uprooting it. God the Almighty says: You will see the people therein meaning in those nights and days. Struck down is the plural of sarī’, meaning dead. It was also said: In it, meaning in the wind. As if they were trunks meaning roots. Empty palm trees meaning worn out, as Abu Tufayl said. It was also said: empty of the hollows, nothing in them. Palm trees are both masculine and feminine. God the Almighty said in another place: As if they were trunks of palm trees hollowed out (al-Qamar 54:20). It is possible that they were likened to palm trees that were struck down from their roots, which is a description of the enormity of their bodies. It is also possible that what is meant by it is the roots and not the trunks, meaning that the wind cut them down until they became like the hollow roots of palm trees. That is, the wind would enter their stomachs and strike them down like a palm tree with an empty cavity. Ibn Shajarah said: The wind would enter their mouths and bring out what was in their stomachs of stuffing from their backsides, so they became like empty palm trees. Yahya ibn Salam said, He said, ‘empty’ because their bodies were empty of their souls, like empty palm trees. It is possible that the meaning is that they were like the trunks of palm trees empty of their roots in the ground, as God Almighty said, Those are their houses, empty (al-Naml 27:52), meaning ruined and without inhabitants. It is possible that empty means worn out, as we mentioned, because when it decays, its interior becomes empty. So, after they perish, they were likened to empty palm trees.
69:8: God Almighty says: Do you see any remnant of them? Any remaining groups or remaining soul. It was said: from remnant. It was said: from survival. Fa’ilah with the meaning of a verbal noun, like consequence and well-being. It is permissible for it to be a noun, meaning do you find anyone remaining for them? Ibn Jurayj said: They were alive for seven nights and eight days in the torment of God from the wind, then when they reached the evening on the eighth day they died, so the wind carried them and threw them into the sea. This is what God the Almighty said: Then do you see any remaining for them? And His Almighty said: So in the morning nothing could be seen except their dwellings. al-Ahqaf 46:25.
69:9: God the Almighty says: And there came Pharaoh and those before him. Umar and Al-Kisa'i read it with a kasra on the qaf and a fatha on the ba', meaning those with him and those who followed him from his soldiers. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose this based on the reading of Abdullah, Ubayy and those with him. Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari read it with a fatha on the qaf and a sukoon on the ba', meaning those who came before him from the past generations and nations. And the overturned means the people of the towns of Lot. The general reading is with an alif. Al-Hasan and Al-Jahdary read it with the singular form. Qatada said: The towns of the people of Lot were called overturned because they were overturned, i.e., they were turned upside down. Al-Tabari reported on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka'b Al-Qurazi who said: Five towns: Sab'ah, Sa'rah, Amrah, Duma, and Sodom, which is the largest town. By the sinful act means by the sinful act, which is disobedience and disbelief. Mujahid said: By the sins that they used to commit. Al-Jurjani said: meaning a great mistake, so the mistake is a source.
69:10: The Almighty said: But they disobeyed the Messenger of their Lord. Al-Kalbi said: It is Moses. It was also said: It is Lot because that is closer. It was also said: He meant Moses and Lot, peace be upon them, as the Almighty said: Then say, 'Indeed, we are messengers of the Lord of the worlds.' (Ash-Shu'ara': 16). It was also said: Messenger means message. The message may be expressed by the word messenger. The poet said: The informers lied. I did not tell them my secret, nor did I send them a messenger. So He seized them with a severe seizure, meaning a high seizure, in addition to the seizures and punishment of the nations. Usury is derived from this word when someone takes more in gold and silver than he gave. It is said: The thing increased and multiplied. Mujahid said: severe, as if he meant an increase in severity.
69:11: The Almighty says: When the water overflowed meaning it rose high. Ali may God be pleased with him said: It overflowed its angelic keepers out of anger for his Lord, so they were unable to hold it back. Qatadah said: It increased over everything by fifteen cubits. Ibn Abbas said: The water overflowed during the time of Noah and its keepers became so numerous that they did not know how much had come out. Not a single drop of water descends before or after it except by a known measure, except on that day. This was mentioned as being lifted up at the beginning of the Surah. The purpose of the stories of these nations and the mention of the punishment that befell them is to deter this nation from following their example in disobeying the Messenger. Then He bestowed upon them a favor by making them the descendants of those who were saved from drowning, by saying: We carried you meaning We carried your fathers while you were in their loins. In the moving ship means in the moving ships. And those carried in the moving ship are Noah and his children, and everyone on the face of the earth is from the descendants of those.
69:12: That We may make it a reminder for you refers to the Ark of Noah, peace be upon him. God made it a reminder and an admonition for this nation until its first inhabitants reached it, according to Qatada. Ibn Jurayj said: Its planks were on Mount Judi. The meaning is: Those planks were left for you so that you may remember what happened to the people of Noah, and how God saved your forefathers. How many ships perished and turned to dust, nothing remaining of them. It was also said: That We may make that action of drowning the people of Noah and saving those who believed with him an admonition for you. For this reason God the Almighty said: And a hearing ear will receive it meaning that an ear that retains what came from God will memorize it and hear it. The Ark cannot be described as such. Al-Zajjaj said: It is said, I memorized such and such, meaning I memorized it in my soul, I memorized it. I memorized knowledge, and I memorized what I said, all mean the same thing. And I stored the goods in the vessel. Al-Zajjaj said: It is said of everything that you have memorized other than in your heart: I have retained it with an alif, and when you have memorized it in your heart, you have memorized it without an alif. Talhah, Hamid, and Al-A’raj read wa’tihiyya with a sukoon on the ‘ayn. Similar to the words of God the Almighty: And a listening ear retains it, “Indeed in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart” (Qaf: 37). Qatada said: The listening ear is an ear that understands from God the Almighty and benefits from what it hears from the Book of God the Almighty. Makhul narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said when this verse was revealed: I asked my Lord to make it the ear of Ali. Makhul said: “Ali may God be pleased with him used to say: I never heard anything from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and forgot it without memorizing it.” Al-Mawardi mentioned this. Al-Hasan narrated something similar, and Al-Tha’labi mentioned it: “When the verse: “And a listening ear retains it,” was revealed, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I asked my Lord to make it your ear, O Ali. Ali said: By God, I have not forgotten anything after that, and it was not for me to forget. Abu Barzah Al-Aslami said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Ali: ‘O Ali, God has commanded me to listen to you and not to turn you away, and to teach you and to understand, and it is God’s right that you understand.’”
69:13: God Almighty says: Then when the Trumpet is blown with a single blast. Ibn Abbas said: It is the first blast of the Hour, and no one will remain who has not died. It is permissible to make blow masculine because the feminine of blow is not real. It was said: This blow is the last. He said: One blow meaning it cannot be repeated. Al-Akhfash said: The verb falls on the blow since there was no raised noun before it, so it was said: a blow. It is permissible to make blow accusative as a verbal noun. Abu Al-Samal read it this way. Or it can be said: It is limited to reporting the action, as you say: he struck a striking. Al-Zajjaj said: In the trumpet, it takes the place of what the agent is not named.
69:14: The Almighty's saying: And the earth and the mountains were lifted up. The general reading is with a soft m, meaning they were lifted up from their places. Fadakta means they were crumbled and broken. A single crushing The only accusative case for Fadakta is the accusative case because the pronoun in Dakta is in the accusative case. Al-Farra' said: He did not say Fadakkan because he made all the mountains as one sentence, and the earth as one sentence. Similar to it is: That the heavens and the earth were joined together (Al-Anbiya': 30) and He did not say Kun. This crushing is like an earthquake, as God Almighty said: When the earth is shaken with its [final] earthquake (al-Zalzalah 99:1). It was also said: Fadakta means they were spread out once, and from this comes the camel's hump when it spreads out on its back. This has been discussed in Surat Al-A'raf. Abdul Hamid read on the authority of Ibn Amir, And the earth and the mountains were lifted up with a shaddah, attributing the action to the second object. It is as if it was originally Our power or one of Our angels carried the earth and the mountains, then the action was attributed to the second object and was constructed for it. If the first object had been used, the action would have been attributed to it, so it is as if he said: Our power carried the earth. It is also permissible to construct it for the second object by way of inversion, so it is said: The earth carried the angel, like you say: Zaid dressed the cloak, and I dressed the cloak for Zaid.
69:15: God Almighty says: Then on that Day the Event will occur, meaning the Resurrection will take place.
69:16: And the sky was split means it cracked and split. It was said that it was split because of the descent of the angels in it, as evidenced by the words of God Almighty: And the Day the heaven will be split with clouds and the angels will be sent down in succession (al-Furqan 25:25), which has been mentioned before. So on that Day it will be frail means weak. It is said: It is a building that is weak and fragile, so it is weak if it is very weak. It is also said: Frail speech, meaning weak. It was said: It becomes, after its hardness, like wool in its frailty, and that is because of the descent of the angels, as we mentioned. It was also said: Because of the terror of the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: Frail means torn, as Ibn Shajarah said. It is taken from their saying: It is a water skin when it is torn. Among their proverbs: Leave him who has no water to drink and who spills his water in the desert Anyone who is weak-minded cannot protect himself.
69:17: And the angels means the angels, a name for the species. On its edges means on its extremities when it splits, because the sky is their place, according to Ibn Abbas. Al-Mawardi: Perhaps this is the saying of Mujahid and Qatadah. Al-Tha'labi narrated it from Al-Dahhak, who said: On its edges, from what has not split. He means that the sky is the place of the angels, and when it splits, they will be at its edges. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The meaning is that the angels are on the edges of the world, meaning they descend to the earth and guard its edges. It was also said: When the sky becomes pieces, the angels will stand on those pieces that are not cracked within themselves. It was also said: When people see Hell, it will startle them, and they will call out like camels call out, and they will not come to any part of the earth except that they will see its angels and return from whence they came. It was also said: On its edges await what they are commanded to do with the people of Hell, such as driving to it, and with the people of Paradise, such as greetings and honor. All of this goes back to the meaning of Ibn Jubayr’s statement. It is indicated by the verse: And He sends down the angels in successive descents (al-Furqan 25:25) and the Almighty’s statement: O company of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth (Al-Rahman: 33) as we explained there. And the regions and directions in the language of Hudhayl, the singular of which is rajān, shortened, and its dual is rajwān, like ‘asā and ‘aswān. The poet said: So don't let the hope throw me out that I am the least of the people who cares about my place This is said for the letter of the well and the grave. God the Almighty says: And eight will bear the Throne of your Lord above them that Day. Ibn Abbas said: Eight rows of angels, and no one knows their number except God. Ibn Zayd said: They are eight angels. Al-Hasan reported: God knows best how many there are, eight or eight thousand. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The bearers of the Throne today are four, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, God Almighty will support them with four more, making them eight. This was mentioned by al-Tha’labi. Al-Mawardi narrated it on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Four bear it today, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be eight. Al-Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib said: They are eight angels in the form of mountain goats. This was narrated by the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) in the hadith: “Each angel has four faces: the face of a man, the face of a lion, the face of a bull, and the face of an eagle. Each face asks God for sustenance for that species.” When he recited before the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the words of Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt: Saturn and Taurus under his right foot, the eagle under the other, and a lion as an observatory. And the sun rises every last night, red, its color turning rosy She does not send them her messengers except to punish or to flog. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He spoke the truth. It is reported in the hadith that above the seventh heaven are eight angels, or a height between their hooves and knees, like the distance between one heaven and the next, and above their backs is the Throne. Al-Qushayri mentioned it and Al-Tirmidhi included it from the hadith of Al-Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib. It was mentioned in full in Surat Al-Baqarah. Al-Tha’labi mentioned something similar and the same wording. In a hadith attributed to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): The bearers of the Throne are eight angels in the form of mountain goats, and between their hooves and knees is the journey of a swift bird of seventy years. In Al-Kalbi’s interpretation: Eight parts out of nine angels, which would take too long to mention. The first was narrated by Al-Tha’labi and the second by Al-Qushayri. Al-Mardawi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Eight parts out of nine, and they are the Cherubim. The meaning is that the Throne descends. Then, the attribution of the Throne to God is like the attribution of a house, and a house is not for dwelling, so that is the Throne. The meaning of above them is above their heads. Al-Suddi said: The Throne is borne by the angels who bear it above them, and none bears the Throne except God. It was also said: above them means that the bearers of the Throne are above the angels who are in the heavens on all sides. It was also said: above them means above the people of the Resurrection.
69:18: The Almighty says: On that Day you will be exposed meaning before God. The evidence for this is: And they will be exposed before your Lord in rows (al-Kahf 18:48). This is not an exposure by which He knows what He does not know. Rather, it means the reckoning and the determination of their deeds for recompense. Al-Hasan narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "People will be exposed on the Day of Resurrection three times. As for the second of them, they will be arguing and making excuses. As for the third, at that time the scrolls will fly into the hands, and He will take hold of his right hand and his left." Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi. He said: It is not authentic that Al-Hasan did not hear it from Abu Hurairah. Nothing of you will be hidden means that He knows everything of your deeds. So hidden in this sense means something they used to hide from their deeds, as Ibn Shajarah said. It was also said: No person will be hidden from Him, meaning that no person will remain who will not be held accountable. Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Al-As said: The believer will not be hidden from the disbeliever, nor the righteous from the wicked. It was said: Do not cover your private parts. As the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: People will be gathered barefoot and naked. The Kufians, except for Asim, read it with a ya because the feminine of khafiya is not real, as in the verse of God the Almighty: And the shriek seized those who did wrong Hud 11:67. Abu Ubaid chose this because it separated the verb from the feminine noun, preposition and genitive. The rest read it with a ta because the feminine of khafiya is not real.
69:19: God the Almighty says: But as for he who is given his record in his right hand, Giving the record in the right hand is evidence of salvation. Ibn Abbas said: The first of this nation to be given his record in his right hand is Umar ibn al-Khattab, and it has rays like the rays of the sun. It was said to him: Where is Abu Bakr? He said: Never, never!! The angels escorted him to Paradise. Al-Tha'labi mentioned it. We have also mentioned it with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, on the authority of Zayd ibn Thabit, with its wording and meaning in Kitab al-Tadhkira. Praise be to God. He will say, 'Here, read my record.' That is, he says that out of confidence in Islam and joy at his salvation, because the right hand among the Arabs is a sign of joy, and the left hand is a sign of sorrow. The poet said: Tell me, have you placed me in your hands so I can be happy, or have you placed me in your left hand? Meaning: Ha'um, come, said Ibn Zayd. Muqatil said: Come. It was said: Take, and from this is the predicate in usury except for Ha' and Ha', meaning each one says to his companion: Take. Ibn Al-Sikkit and Al-Kisa'i said: The Arabs say Ha' ya rajul iqra, and for two people Ha'umma ya rajulan, and Ha'um ya rijal, and for a woman Ha' with a kasra on the hamza and Ha'umma and Ha'amen. The original is Ha'akum but the hamza was made prominent from the Kaf, said Al-Qatibi. It was said that Ha'um is a word that was coined to answer a caller when in a state of excitement or joy. It was narrated: “A Bedouin called out to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in a loud voice, so the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) answered him Ha'um, lengthening his voice.” The two books are in the accusative case with Ha'um according to the Kufians, and with Qara'u according to the Basrans because it is the closest of the two operators. The original is kitabi my book, so the ha' was inserted to show the fat-ha of the ya'. The ha' was for stopping, and the same is true for its sisters: hisabihi hisabihi, malihi my sultanihi, and in al-qari'ah what is it?. The general reading is with the ha' in them both when stopping and connected, because they are written in the Mushaf with the ha' so it is not omitted. Abu Ubaid chose to deliberately stop on them to conform to the language in adding the ha' in the pause and to conform to the script. Ibn Muhaisin, Mujahid, Hamid, and Ya'qub read by deleting the ha' in connection and keeping it when stopping in them, they are plural. Hamza agreed with them in malihi and sultanihi, and mahihi in al-qari'ah. The total number of these letters is seven. Abu Hatim chose the reading of Ya'qub and those with him, following the language. Whoever reads them with the ha' in connection with the intention of stopping.
69:20: I thought means I was certain and knew, from Ibn Abbas and others. It was said: It means I thought that God would punish me for my bad deeds, but He favored me with His forgiveness and did not punish me for them. Ad-Dahhak said: Every thought in the Qur'an from a believer is certainty. And from a disbeliever, it is doubt. Mujahid said: Thought of the Hereafter is certainty, and thought of this world is doubt. Al-Hasan said about this verse: The believer has good thoughts about his Lord, so he does good deeds, and the hypocrite has bad thoughts about his Lord, so he does bad deeds. That I will meet my account means in the Hereafter. I did not deny the resurrection, meaning that he was only saved by his fear of the Day of Reckoning, because he was certain that God would hold him accountable, so he worked for the Hereafter.
69:21: He is in a life of contentment meaning in a life that he is satisfied with, with nothing disliked in it, meaning a life that he is satisfied with. Abu Ubaid and Al-Farra' said: Satisfied means satisfied, like you say: gushing water, meaning gushing. It was also said: of contentment, meaning that its owner is satisfied with it. Like the son of and the date, meaning the owner of milk and dates. In the Sahih: On the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, They will live and never die, be healthy and never get sick, be comfortable and never see misery, and be young and never grow old.
69:22: In a high paradise meaning great in the souls.
69:23: Its fruits are within easy reach meaning easily accessible, even those standing, sitting, and lying down can reach it, as will be explained in Surat Al-Insan. Al-Qatuf is the plural of qatf with a kasra on the qaf, which refers to the fruits that are picked. Al-Qatf with a fatha is the verbal noun. Al-Qataf with a fatha and a kasra is the time of picking.
69:24: Eat and drink, that is, they will be told. Enjoyably, without any turbidity or bitterness. For what you have put forth, the righteous deeds you have done. In the days gone by, that is, in this world. And He said: Eat after His statement, for he will be in a pleasant life.
69:25: Because of his statement: But as for he who has been given and whoever includes the meaning of the plural. Ad-Dahhak stated that this verse was revealed about Abu Salamah Abdullah ibn Abd al-Asad al-Makhzumi, and this was also said by Muqatil. The verse that follows it is about his brother Al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Asad, according to Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak as well, and this was also said by Al-Tha'labi. This man and his brother were the reason for the revelation of these verses. The meaning includes all the people of misery and the people of happiness, as indicated by the Almighty’s saying: Eat and drink. It has been said that what is meant by this is everyone who is followed in good and evil. So if a man is a leader in goodness, calling to it, ordering it, and many people follow him in it, he will be called by his name and his father’s name, and he will advance. When he approaches, a white book will be brought out for him with white writing, inside of which are his sins and outside of which are his good deeds. He will begin with the bad deeds and read them, feeling pity, his face will turn pale, and his color will change. When he reaches the end of the book, he will find in it these are your sins, and you have been forgiven, so he will rejoice greatly. Then he will turn over his book and read his good deeds, but his joy will only increase. When he reaches the end of the book, he will find in it these are your good deeds, and they will be doubled for you. His face will turn white, a crown will be brought and placed on his head, he will be dressed in two garments, and every joint of his body will be adorned, and he will grow sixty cubits tall, which is the height of Adam, peace be upon him. It will be said to him: Go to your companions and inform them and give them good report that each one of them will have something like this. Then, when he has turned away, he will say, “Here, read my record. Indeed, I thought that I would meet my account.” God the Most High said, He will be in a pleasant life, meaning one that is pleasing to me, in a lofty garden, in the heavens, with its fruits and clusters, close at hand, brought near to them. Then he will say to his companions, Do you know me? They will say, “Honor has overwhelmed you. Who are you?” He will say, “I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so, giving each man good tidings like this. Eat and drink at ease for what you put forth in the past days,” meaning what you sent forth in the days of this world. If a man is a leader in evil, calling to it and ordering it, and many people follow him in it, his name and his father’s name will be called out, and he will go to his reckoning. A black book will be brought out for him with black writing on the inside, and on the outside, the bad deeds. He will start with the good deeds and read them, thinking that he will be saved. When he reaches the end of the book, he will find in it, These are your good deeds that have been returned to you. His face will darken, sadness will overcome him, and he will despair of goodness. Then he will turn over his book and read his bad deeds, but his face will only become blacker. When he reaches the end of the book, he will find in it, These are your bad deeds that have been doubled for you. That is, his torment will be doubled. This does not mean that what he does not do will be increased upon him. He said, “So the Fire will be made great, his eyes will turn blue, his face will turn black, and he will be covered with garments of tar. It will be said to him, ‘Go to your companions and tell them that each one of them has the same.’ So he will go away saying, ‘Oh, I wish I had not been given my book.’”
69:26: I did not know what my account was.
69:27: I wish she was the judge. He wishes for death.
69:28: God Almighty says: My wealth will not avail me.
69:29: My authority has been lost to me. Ibn Abbas's interpretation: My proof has been lost to me. This is the opinion of Mujahid, Ikrimah, As-Suddi, and Ad-Dahhak. Ibn Zayd said: It means my authority in this world, which is kingship. This man was obeyed by his companions.
69:30: God Almighty said: Seize him and chain him. It was said: One hundred thousand angels will rush to him and then gather their hands around his neck. This is what God Almighty said: And chain him, meaning bind him with shackles.
69:31: Then make him burn in Hell meaning make him burn in Hell
69:32: Then by a chain seventy cubits long. God knows which cubit, said Al-Hasan. Ibn Abbas said: Seventy cubits by the king's cubit. Nawf said: Each cubit is seventy cubits, and each cubit is the farthest distance between you and Mecca. And it was in the spacious Kufa. Muqatil said: If a link of it were placed on the top of a mountain, it would melt like lead melts. Ka'b said: A link of the chain of which God Almighty said its length is seventy cubits - that a link of it - is like all the iron in the world. Then pass it through. Sufyan said: We have been informed that it enters his anus until it exits his mouth. Muqatil said the same. The meaning is then pass a chain through him. It was also said: It enters his neck through it and he is dragged by it. It was reported that it enters his anus and exits his nostrils. In another report: It enters his mouth and exits his anus. Then his companions call out, Do you recognize me? They say, No, but we may see in you some shame. So who are you? Then he calls out to his companions, So-and-so, son of so-and-so, every one of you has something like this. I said: This interpretation is the most correct of what has been said about this verse. It is indicated by the Almighty’s statement: The Day We will call every people with their leader (al-Isra’ 17:71). There is a hadith of Abu Hurayrah with a similar meaning on this topic, narrated by Al-Tirmidhi. We have already mentioned it in Surah Subhan, so reflect on it there.
69:33: He did not believe in God Almighty.
69:34: And he does not encourage feeding the poor meaning feeding others, just as giving is used in place of giving. The poet said: After death, you will deny me and after your hundred gifts He wanted after giving you. So he explained that he was punished for not feeding and for ordering miserliness, just as he was punished for the cause of disbelief. And urging: incitement and exhortation. The root of food is to be in the accusative case with the implied source. Food is an expression for the eye, and it was added to the poor person because of the connection between them. And whoever does food as he does feeding, then the position of the poor person is in the accusative case. The meaning is on the feeder feeding the poor person, so the subject was deleted and the source was added to the object.
69:35: The Almighty's saying: So he has no close friend here today is the predicate of not His saying: for him and the predicate is not. His saying: here is not because the meaning becomes: there is no food here except from the two washes, and that is not correct, because there is food other than it. Here is related to what is in for him from the meaning of the verb. And the close friend here is the relative. That is, I have no relative who would pity him and defend him. It is taken from the word hameem which is hot water, as if he is the friend for whom he pities and whose heart burns.
69:36: And the two ghusls are two verbs from washing, so it is as if it is washed from their manners, and it is the pus of the people of Hell that flows from their wounds and private parts, according to Ibn Abbas. Ad-Dahhak and Ar-Rabi' ibn Anas said: It is a tree that the people of Hell eat. And the ghusl with the kasra: is what the head is washed with, such as marshmallow and others. And Al-Akhfash: And from it is the ghusl, and it is what is washed from the flesh and blood of the people of Hell. And the ya and the noon were added to it as they were added to Afrin. Qatada said: It is the worst and most hideous food. Ibn Zayd: It is not known what it is, nor Zaqqum. And he said in another place: {And they will have no food except from Dharee'} (Al-Ghashiyah 84:6) Dharee' may be from the two ghusls. And it was said: There is an inversion in the speech, and the meaning is that he has no close friend here today except from Ghasl, and it is hot water. And no food means they will have no food from which they can benefit.
69:37: None shall eat it except the sinners meaning the guilty ones. Ibn Abbas said: It means the polytheists. It was read al-khaatiyyun by replacing the hamza with a ya', and al-khaatiyun by dropping it. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas: What are the sinners? We all sin. Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali narrated from him: What are the sinners? They are the sinners. And what is soap? They are the righteous ones. It is possible that it is meant to refer to those who transgress from the truth to falsehood and overstep the limits of God Almighty.
69:38: God the Almighty said: So I swear by what you see * and what you do not see. The meaning is I swear by all things, what you see and what you do not see. There is no connection. It was also said that it is a refutation of what came before, meaning that the matter is not as the polytheists say. Muqatil said that the reason for that is that Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira said: Muhammad is a magician. Abu Jahl said: He is a poet. Uqba said: He is a soothsayer. So God the Almighty said: So I swear, meaning I swear. It was also said that no here is a negation of the oath, meaning that there is no need for an oath in this case because the truth is clear in that regard. Based on this, its answer is like the answer to an oath.
69:39: God the Almighty said: So I swear by what you see * and what you do not see. The meaning is I swear by all things, what you see and what you do not see. There is no connection. It was also said that it is a refutation of what came before, meaning that the matter is not as the polytheists say. Muqatil said that the reason for that is that Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira said: Muhammad is a magician. Abu Jahl said: He is a poet. Uqba said: He is a soothsayer. So God the Almighty said: So I swear, meaning I swear. It was also said that no here is a negation of the oath, meaning that there is no need for an oath in this case because the truth is clear in that regard. Based on this, its answer is like the answer to an oath.
69:40: Indeed, it is the word of a noble Messenger. "It meaning the Qur'an, is the word of a noble Messenger" meaning Gabriel, as stated by Al-Hasan, Al-Kalbi and Muqatil. The evidence for this is: "Indeed, it is the word of a noble Messenger, * Possessor of power and secure in the presence of the Lord of the Throne." al-Takwir 81:19. Al-Kalbi and Al-Qutbi also said: The Messenger here is Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him, because God says: "And it is not the word of a poet." The Qur'an is not the word of the Messenger, peace and blessings of God be upon him, rather it is the word of God, the Almighty, and the word is attributed to the Messenger because he is the one who recites it, conveys it and acts upon it, like our saying: This is the statement of Malik.
69:41: God Almighty says: A revelation from the Lord of the worlds. The Almighty says: A revelation meaning it is a revelation. From the Lord of the worlds is in apposition to His statement: Indeed, it is the word of a noble Messenger, meaning it is the word of a noble Messenger, and it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds.
69:42: The Almighty says: And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings. “He said” means he had made up his own mind and had said something on his own. And if he had fabricated against Us is read in the passive form.
69:43: God Almighty says: A revelation from the Lord of the worlds. The Almighty says: A revelation meaning it is a revelation. From the Lord of the worlds is in apposition to His statement: Indeed, it is the word of a noble Messenger, meaning it is the word of a noble Messenger, and it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds.
69:44: The Almighty says: And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings. “He said” means he had made up his own mind and had said something on his own. And if he had fabricated against Us is read in the passive form.
69:45: We would have seized him by the right hand meaning by force and power, i.e. We would have seized him by force. Min is an additional relative clause. Power and power are expressed by the word right hand because the power of everything is in its right hand, said Al-Qutbi. This is the meaning of the statement of Ibn Abbas and Mujahid. Similar to this is the statement of Al-Shamakh: If you see her raised to glory, you will receive her godmother on the right hand By force. Araba is the name of a man from the Ansar tribe of the Aws. Another said: When I saw the sun shining, I took what I needed from it with my right hand. Al-Suddi and Al-Hakam said: With an oath, with truth. He said: Araba received it with an oath. That is, by right. Al-Hasan said: We would have cut off his right hand. It was also said that the meaning is that we would have seized his right hand from action, as Naftawayh said. Abu Ja`far al-Tabari said: This statement was made to express humiliation, as people usually do when they take the hand of someone they are punishing. Just as a ruler says to someone they want to humiliate: Take his hands. That is, we would have ordered him to be taken by the hand and would have gone to extremes in his punishment.
69:46: The Almighty says: And indeed, it is a reminder for the righteous. The Almighty says: And indeed meaning the Qur'an is a reminder for the righteous meaning for those who fear God. Similar to it is: In it is guidance for the righteous (al-Baqarah 2:2) as we explained at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah. It was also said that what is meant is Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, meaning that he is a reminder, mercy, and salvation.
69:47: The Almighty’s saying: There is not one of you who can prevent Him is a negative and singular in the sense of plural, so that is its description with the plural, meaning there is not one of you who can prevent Him, like the Almighty’s saying: We make no distinction between any of His messengers (al-Baqarah 2:285). This is plural, because between only applies to two or more. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Spoils of war were not lawful for any of the black-headed people before you. Its wording is the same but its meaning is plural. Min is redundant. Hijz means prevention. Hajzeen may be an adjective for Ahad in the same sense as we mentioned, so it would be in the genitive case. The predicate is minkum and it may be in the accusative case as the predicate, and minkum is canceled, and it would be related to Hajzeen. The separation by it does not prevent the predicate from being in the accusative case in this, just as the separation by it did not prevent the predicate from being in the accusative case in Indeed, Zayd is desirous of you.
69:48: The Almighty says: And indeed, it is a reminder for the righteous. The Almighty says: And indeed meaning the Qur'an is a reminder for the righteous meaning for those who fear God. Similar to it is: In it is guidance for the righteous (al-Baqarah 2:2) as we explained at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah. It was also said that what is meant is Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, meaning that he is a reminder, mercy, and salvation.
69:49: God Almighty said: And indeed, We know that among you are deniers. Al-Rabi’ said: By the Qur’an.
69:50: And indeed, it is a regret means denial. Regret is remorse. It was said: meaning, the Qur'an will be a regret for the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection when they see the reward of those who believed in it. It was also said: it is their regret in this world when they were not able to oppose it when they were challenged to produce a surah like it. That is, it is a regret. It is a verbal noun meaning regret, so it is permissible to make it masculine. Ibn Abbas said: it is like your saying: the very essence of certainty and pure certainty. If certainty was an adjective, it would not be permissible to add it to it, just as you do not say: this is a charming man. It was said: it is an addition to itself due to the difference in the two words.
69:51: And it is the certain truth means that the Noble Qur'an is a revelation from God Almighty, so it is the certain truth. It was also said: meaning it is the certain truth so that it will be a regret for them on the Day of Resurrection.
69:52: So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great. That is, praise your Lord, as Ibn Abbas said. It was also said that it means sanctify God from evil and shortcomings.
70:1: Surat Al-Ma'arij, which is Meccan by consensus. It has forty-four verses. God the Almighty says: A questioner asked about a punishment to come true. Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read it as: A questioner asked about a punishment to come true. Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read it as: A questioner asked without a hamza. The rest read it with a hamza. Whoever adds a hamza, it is the question. The letter ba may be redundant, or it may mean about. Asking means supplication, meaning that a supplicant supplicated for a punishment, according to Ibn 'Abbas and others. It is said: He supplicated for woe upon so-and-so, and He supplicated for punishment upon him. It is also said: I called Zayd, meaning I sought to bring him. That is, a seeker sought a punishment for the disbelievers, which will inevitably befall them on the Day of Resurrection. Based on this, the letter ba is redundant, like God's statement: It will grow with oil Al-Mu'minun 33:20 and His statement: And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree Maryam 19:25. It is an emphasis. That is, a questioner asked about a punishment to come true. For the disbelievers means upon the disbelievers. He is Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith when he said: O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment (al-Anfal 8:32). So his question was revealed, and he and Uqbah ibn Abi Mu’ayt were killed patiently on the day of Badr. No one else was killed patiently, as Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said. It was said that the questioner here was Al-Harith ibn Al-Nu’man Al-Fihri. That is because when he heard the words of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about Ali may God be pleased with him: Whoever I am his master, he rode his camel and came until he knelt down in Al-Abtah and then said: O Muhammad, you commanded us on the authority of God to bear witness that there is no god but God and that you are the Messenger of God, so we accepted it from you. And to pray five times a day, so we accepted it from you. And to pay zakat on our wealth, so we accepted it from you. And to fast the month of Ramadan every year, so we accepted it from you. And to perform Hajj, so we accepted it from you. But you were not satisfied with this until you preferred your cousin over us! Is this something from you or from God? The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: By God, besides Whom there is no god, it is only from God. Al-Harith turned away saying: O God, if what Muhammad says is true, then rain down stones upon us from the sky or bring us a painful punishment. By God, he had not reached his she-camel when God threw a stone at him, and it struck his head and exited through his anus, killing him. Then the verse, A questioner asked about a punishment that is to come to pass was revealed. It was said that the questioner here is Abu Jahl, who is the killer, as stated by al-Rabi’. It was also said that it was the words of a group of the infidels of Quraysh. It was also said that it was Noah, peace be upon him, who asked for the punishment upon the infidels. It was also said that it was the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), meaning that he prayed for punishment and asked that God inflict it upon the infidels, and it will inevitably happen to them. The speech continued to the verse, So be patient with beautiful patience, meaning do not be impatient, for it is near. If the preposition ba has the meaning of about - which is the opinion of Qatadah - then it is as if a questioner asked about the punishment, who will it befall or when it will befall. God, the Most High, says, So ask about it one who is well-informed Al-Furqan 25:59, meaning ask about it. Alqamah said: If you ask me about women, I am an expert in women’s diseases. That is, about women. It is said: We went out to ask about so-and-so and so-and-so. The meaning is they asked about who will be punished and for whom, so God said: For the disbelievers. Abu Ali and others said: If it is from the question, then its origin is transitive to two objects, and it is permissible to limit it to one of them. If it is limited to one of them, it is permissible for it to be transitive to it with a preposition, so the meaning would be that a questioner asked the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, or the Muslims about a punishment or about a punishment. Whoever reads it without a hamza has two interpretations: The first is that it is a dialect for the question and it is the dialect of Quraysh, the Arabs say: he asked, he asks, musal, naal, yanal, and khafa, yakhaf. The second is that it is from the flow, and this is supported by the reading of Ibn Abbas, sala, sayl. Abdur-Rahman ibn Zayd said: A valley of the valleys of Hell flowed and it is called sa’il, and this is the saying of Zayd ibn Thabit. Al-Tha’labi said: The first is better, like the saying of al-A’sha in lightening the hamza: She asked me for divorce when she saw that I had become weak, and that you had come to me with something strange. In As-Sahah: Al-Akhfash said: It is said, We went out to ask about so-and-so and so-and-so. The hamza may be softened and it is said, He asked, and he said: And the exhausted one asked for pleasure from his echoes, but he did not seek help, and the winds of death surrounded him. Al-Marheq: The one who was caught in order to be killed. Al-Asdah with the dammah: A small shirt worn under the garment. Al-Mahdawi: Whoever reads sal may have lightened the hamza by adding an alif to it, which is a substitution not according to analogy. It is also possible that the alif was changed from a waw according to the language of those who said: salta asal, like khafat akhaf, I feared. Al-Nahhas: Sibawayh narrated salta asal, like khafat akhaf, meaning I asked. And he recited: Hudhayl asked the Messenger of God an obscene thing. Hudhayl went astray because of what they asked, but they did not do it right. It is said: They are arguing. Al-Mahdawi: It is possible that it is replaced by a Ya, from Salā yasīl. And Sa’il is a valley in Jahannam, so the hamza of Sa’il according to the first opinion is original, and according to the second it is a replacement for a Wāw, and according to the third it is a replacement for a Ya. Al-Qushayri: Wasā’il is hamzated, because if it is from Sa’ala with a Hamzah then it is hamzated, and if it is without a Hamzah it is also hamzated. The defect was not by deletion for fear of confusion, so it was by changing it to a Hamzah, and you can soften the Hamzah so that it is in between. Waqi’ means it will befall the disbelievers, it is clear that it is from God, the Possessor of the Ascending Stairways. Al-Hasan said: God the Most High revealed: A questioner asked about a punishment to come true, so he said: For whom is it? He said: For the disbelievers, so the Lam in the disbelievers is related to Waqi’. Al-Farra’ said: The meaning is with a punishment to befall the disbelievers, so Waqi’ is an attribute of the torment, and the Lam entered for the torment not for Waqi’, meaning this punishment for the disbelievers in the Hereafter will not be warded off by anyone. It was said that the Lam means upon, and the meaning is: it will befall upon. It was narrated that this is also the case in Abu’s reading. It was also said that it means about, meaning that there is no one who can defend the disbelievers from God.
70:2: God Almighty says: For the disbelievers there is no repeller.
70:3: That is, that punishment is from God, the Possessor of the Ascending Stairways, meaning the Possessor of the lofty ranks, virtues, and blessings, as said by Ibn Abbas and Qatadah. The Ascending Stairways are the levels of His blessings upon creation. It was also said: the Possessor of greatness and sublimity. Mujahid said: They are the Ascending Stairways of Heaven. It was also said: They are the Ascending Stairways of the Angels, because the Angels ascend to Heaven, and He described Himself with that. It was also said: the Ascending Stairways are the chambers, meaning that He is the Possessor of chambers, meaning He has made chambers for His friends in Paradise. Abdullah read the Ascending Stairways with the letter Ya. It is said: Ma'raj, Mi'raj, Ma'arij, and Ma'arij, like miftah and keys. The Ascending Stairways are the degrees, and from it is the verse: And Ascending Stairways upon which they ascend Az-Zukhruf 33.
70:4: The angels and the Spirit ascend (Al-Ma'arij: 4) meaning they ascend the ascents that God has made for them. Ibn Mas'ud and his companions, as-Sulami and al-Kisa'i read it with a ya' to indicate the plural, and because God says: Mention the angels but do not feminize them. The rest read it with a ta' to indicate the plural. The Spirit is Gabriel, peace be upon him, as Ibn Abbas said. The evidence for this is the statement of God the Almighty: The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down (Al-Shu'ara': 193). It was also said that he is another angel of great creation. Abu Salih said that he was created from God's creation in the form of people, but he is not people. Qubaysah ibn Dhu'ayb said that it is the spirit of the dead when he is taken. To Him means to the place where their residence is, which is in the heavens, because it is the place of His righteousness and honor. It was also said that it is like the statement of Abraham: Indeed, I am going to my Lord (al-Saffat 37:99). Meaning, to the place that He commanded me to go to. It was also said that to Him means to His throne. On a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years. Wahb, Al-Kalbi, and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: meaning the angels ascended to the place that inspired them in a time that, if others had ascended, would have been fifty thousand years. Wahb also said: The distance between the lowest part of the earth and the Throne is a journey of fifty thousand years. This is the opinion of Mujahid. He combined this verse with the statement, On a Day the extent of which is a thousand years 32:5 in Surat As-Sajdah. He said, On a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years.
