From the end of His command from the lowest part of the earth to the end of His command above the heavens is fifty thousand years. And the statement of God in Al-Sajdah 32:5: On a Day the extent of which is a thousand years 32:5. By this he means the descent of the command from the lowest heaven to the earth, and from the earth to the heaven in one day, so that is the extent of a thousand years, because the distance between the heaven and the earth is a journey of five hundred years. Mujahid also reported, as well as Al-Hakam and Ikrimah: It is the duration of the life of the world from the beginning of its creation until the end of what remains: fifty thousand years. No one knows how much has passed and how much remains except God, the Almighty. It was said: What is meant is the Day of Resurrection, meaning the length of the judgment therein if a created being were to assume it would be fifty thousand years. This was also said by Ikrimah, Al-Kalbi, and Muhammad ibn Ka'b. God the Almighty says, And I will finish it in an hour. Al-Hasan said: It is the Day of Resurrection, but the Day of Resurrection has no end. What is meant is mentioning their standing for the reckoning, which is in fifty thousand years of the years of this world. Then at that time the people of both abodes will settle in both abodes. Yaman said: It is the Day of Resurrection, in which there are fifty places, each place is a thousand years. Ibn Abbas said: It is the Day of Resurrection, which God made for the disbelievers the length of fifty thousand years, then they will enter the Fire to settle. I said: This statement is the best that has been said about the verse, God willing, as an alternative to what Qasim bin Asba’ narrated from the hadith of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: On a day the length of which is fifty thousand years. I said: How long is that! The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, it will be made easier for the believer to the point that it will be easier for him than the obligatory prayers he prayed in this world. An-Nahhas provided evidence for the validity of this statement with what Suhayl narrated from his father from Abu Hurayrah: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “There is no man who does not pay the zakat of his wealth except that a dragon of fire will be made with it to brand his forehead, back, and sides on a day the length of which is fifty thousand years until God judges between the people.” He said: This indicates that it is the Day of Resurrection. Ibrahim At-Taymi said: That day is not decreed for the believer except the length of time between Dhuhr and Asr. This meaning was narrated from the hadith of Muadh, from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: “God will hold you to account for the time between the two prayers. That is why He called Himself Swift in account and the Swiftest of accountants.” Al-Mawardi mentioned this. It was also said that the free time will be for half a day, as God the Almighty said: The companions of Paradise, that Day, will be the best settlement and the best place to rest [Al-Furqan 24]. This is according to the understanding of creation, otherwise no matter would distract Him from another. Just as He provides for them in such and such an hour, He will hold them to account in an instant. God the Almighty said: He did not create you and resurrect you except as a single soul [Luqman 28]. It was also narrated from Ibn Abbas that he was asked about this verse and about God the Almighty’s saying: In a Day the measure of which is a thousand years (Al-Sajdah 32:5). He said: God the Almighty has named these days, and He knows best how they will be, and I hate to say about them what I do not know. It was also said that the meaning of mentioning fifty thousand years is a metaphor, and it defines the length of the Resurrection period in the gathering place, and the hardships that people will face on that day.” The Arabs describe the days of hardship as long, and the days of joy as short. The poet said: And the day the spear's shadow became shorter, the blood of the wineskin fell on us and the flowers sang. It was said: There is an inversion in the speech, and the meaning is: A questioner asked about a punishment that would befall the disbelievers, which God has no averter for, on a day the length of which is fifty thousand years, to which the angels and the Spirit ascend. This statement is the meaning of what we have chosen, and God is the Grantor of success.
70:5: The Almighty said: So be patient with beautiful patience meaning, in the face of the harm done to your people. Beautiful patience is that in which there is no impatience or complaint to anyone but God. It was also said that it means that the one afflicted with the calamity is among the people and does not leave anyone behind. The meanings are close. Ibn Zayd said that it was abrogated by the verse of the sword.
70:6: They see it far away means that the people of Mecca see the torment of Hell far away, i.e. not existing.
70:7: And We see it as near because whatever is coming is near. Al-A'mash said: They see the resurrection as far away because they do not believe in it, as if they consider it impossible. Just as you say to someone you are debating: This is far away and cannot happen! It was also said: They see this day as far away and We see it, meaning we know it, because seeing is related to something that exists. It is like saying: Al-Shafi'i sees such and such in this matter.
70:8: The Almighty's saying: The Day the sky will be like molten copper. The agent in The Day will occur is the punishment will befall them on the Day. It was also said: We will see them or they will see them or it is a substitute for near. And molten copper is the filth and turbidity of oil, according to Ibn Abbas and others. Ibn Masoud said: What was melted of lead, copper and silver. Mujahid said: Like molten copper, like pus from blood and blood. The discussion of this has already been mentioned in Surat Ad-Dukhan and Surat Al-Kahf.
70:9: And the mountains will be like wool meaning like dyed wool. Wool is not called wool unless it is dyed. Al-Hasan said: And the mountains will be like wool which is red wool, and it is the weakest wool. From this is the saying of Zuhair: As if the crumbs of covenant in every house they settled in, the love of death was not destroyed Crumbs: pieces. And the wool is red, singular: uhna. It was said: uhna is the wool of many colors, so the mountains were likened to it in their changing colors. The meaning is: they soften after hardship, and disperse after gathering. It was said: the first thing that the mountains change is that they become scattered sand, then fluffy uhna, then scattered dust.
70:10: And no intimate friend will ask a close friend meaning about his own affairs, because every person will be preoccupied with himself, as Qatada said. As God the Almighty said: Every man among them, that Day, will have enough to make him indifferent to himself (Abasa 80:37). It was also said: No intimate friend will be asked about a close friend, so the preposition was omitted and the verb was connected. The general reading is yas'al with a fatha on the ya'. Shaibah and Al-Bazzi read it on the authority of Asim wa la yas'al with a damma on what the agent is not named, meaning no intimate friend will be asked about his intimate friend, nor a relative about his relative, rather every person will be asked about his deeds. Similar to this is: Every soul will be held in pledge for what it has earned (al-Muddaththir 74:38).
70:11: God the Almighty says: They will see them meaning they will see them. There is no creature on the Day of Resurrection that will not be in the sight of its companion, whether jinn or human. A man will see his father, brother, relatives, or clan, but will not ask him or speak to him, because they will be preoccupied with themselves. Ibn Abbas said: They will recognize each other for an hour, then they will not recognize each other after that hour. In some reports, it is stated that the people of the Day of Resurrection will flee from acquaintances for fear of injustice. Ibn Abbas also said: They will see them means they will see each other, get to know each other, then flee from each other. The pronoun in They will see them in this case refers to the disbelievers, and the mim refers to the relatives. Mujahid said: The meaning is that God will see the believers and the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection. The pronoun in They will see them refers to the believers, and the h and the mim refer to the disbelievers. Ibn Zayd said: The meaning is that God will see the disbelievers in the Fire who led them astray in this world. The pronoun in They will see them refers to the followers, and the h and the mim refer to the followed. It was said: The oppressed sees his oppressor and the murdered sees his murderer. It was also said: They see them, referring to the angels, meaning they know the conditions of the people and guide each group to what is appropriate for them. The discussion ended with His statement: they see them. Then He said: The criminal would wish, meaning the disbeliever wishes, “that he could ransom himself from the torment of Hell with the most precious of his relatives in this world, but he would not be able to. Then He mentioned them and said: “with his children, his wife, his brother, and his clan,” meaning his tribe. who shelters him supports him, as Mujahid and Ibn Zayd said. Malik said: his mother who raises him. Al-Mawardi narrated it and Ashab transmitted it from him. Abu Ubaidah said: A clan is less than a tribe. Tha’lab said: they are his closest fathers. Al-Mubarrad said: A clan is a part of the body, and it is less than a tribe. A man’s family is called his clan as a likeness to some of him. The discussion of the tribe and others has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Hujurat. Here is a question: If he is imprisoned for his clan or makes a will for them, then whoever claims generality applies it to the clan, and whoever claims specificity applies it to the fathers, the nearest and the nearest. The first is more pronounced. And God knows best. The meaning is: you shelter him, embrace him, and protect him from fear if he has any.
70:12: God Almighty says: and his wife and his brother.
70:13: The Almighty said, And his clan that sheltered him.
70:14: And all those on earth meaning, He would like to ransom him with them, and then save him meaning, that ransom would free him. So this omission is necessary, like His statement, And indeed, it is an abomination Al-An'am 6:121, meaning, and that eating it is an abomination. It was said: The criminal would like requires an answer with fa, like His statement, And they would like you to compromise so they would compromise Al-Qalam 6:9. The answer in this verse is then He will save him because it is one of the conjunctions, meaning the criminal would like to ransom himself, so the ransom will save him.
70:15: God the Almighty says: No indeed, it is a Blazing Fire. "No" has been said before in a speech and that it can mean truly, or it can mean no. Here it has both meanings. If it means truly, then the entire statement will save him. If it means no, then the entire statement will be against it, meaning that ransoming oneself will not save him from God's punishment. Then He said: "It is a Blazing Fire," meaning it is Hell, meaning you will find shade in its fires, like God the Almighty's saying: "So I have warned you of a blazing Fire." (al-Layl 92:14) The derivation of "laza is from talathi. The fire is its ignition, and talatha" means its inflaming. It was said that its origin was "lazath, meaning as long as its torment continues, but one of the two tha's accepted an alif, so laza" remained. It was said that it is the second level of the levels of Hell. It is a definite feminine noun and is not declined.
70:16: نزعة للشواءAbu Ja'far, Shaibah, Nafi', and Asim, according to the narration of Abu Bakr, Al-A'mash, Abu Amr, Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i, read Naza'a in the nominative case. Abu Amr narrated from Asim that Naza'a was in the accusative case. Whoever raises the word has five options: First, make Laza'a the predicate of in and raise Naza'a by implying she. From this option, it is appropriate to stop at Laza'a. The second option is that Laza'a and Naza'a are predicates of in. Just as you say, Indeed, he created a quarrel. The third option is that Naza'a is a substitute for Laza'a and Laza'a is the predicate of in. The fourth option is that Laza'a is a substitute for the noun of in and Naza'a is the predicate of in. The fifth option is that the pronoun in inha is for the story, Laza'a is the subject, Naza'a is the predicate of the subject, and the sentence is the predicate of in. The meaning is that the story and the predicate of Laza'a are for the complaint. Whoever places Naza'a in the accusative case, it is appropriate to stop at Laza'a and place Naza'a in the accusative case, separating from Laza'a if it is an indefinite noun connected to a definite noun. It is permissible to put it in the accusative case as a confirmed state, as He said: And it is the truth, confirming (al-Baqarah 2:91). It is also permissible to put it in the accusative case to mean that it is blazing, tearing it out, that is, in the state of tearing it out. The factor in it is what the speech indicates of the meaning of blazing, and it is permissible for it to be a state, as it is a state for those who deny its report. It is also permissible to put it in the accusative case as a definite state, as you say: I passed by Zayd the wise and virtuous. So these are five ways of putting it in the accusative case as well. And shawa is the plural of shawwat, which is the scalp. Al-A’sha said: A murdered woman said: What is wrong with him that his hair has turned gray? Another said: If the incidents had given you a gift, then the head would have been torn by its sharp edges. Al-Qateer: Gray hair. In Al-Sahah: al-Shura 42:The plural of Shawah, which is the scalp. Shawa: The hands, feet, and head of humans, and everything that is not a target. It is said: He shot him and wounded him, if he did not hit the target. Al-Hudhali said: There are words that have no basis in truth, if they slip from the tongue they will escape. He says: There is a saying that does not roast, but kills. Al-A'sha said: The murdered woman said: His money has turned his hair white. Abu Ubaid said: Abu Al-Khattab Al-Akhfash recited it to Abu Amr bin Al-Ala’ and he said to him: You’ve made a mistake! It is rather its narat, meaning its sides. Abu Al-Khattab was silent and then said to us: Rather, it is a mistake; it is its shawa. The shawa of a horse is its legs, because it is said: Abal Al-Shay, and this does not refer to the head, because they described horses as having flowing cheeks and a delicate face. Shawwa is the dregs of wealth. Shawwa is the insignificant and easy thing. Thabit Al-Bunani and Al-Hasan said: Naz’at Al-Shawa meaning for the noble qualities of his face. Abu Al-Aliya said: for the beauties of his face. Qatadah said: for the noble qualities of his creation and extremities. Ad-Dahhak said: It separates the flesh and skin from the bone until nothing is left of it. Al-Kisa’i said: They are the joints. Some of the imams said: They are the legs and skin. Imru’ Al-Qais said: Salim Al-Shazi, Abel Al-Shawa, Shanj Al-Nisa, has veils that supervise the omen Abu Saleh said: The tips of the hands and feet. The poet said: If you looked, you would recognize her pride and her eyes, but you would not recognize her shame. It means its ends. Al-Hasan also said: The grilled part is the head.
70:17: She calls whoever turned back and turned away meaning, she calls to the blazing fire whoever turned away in this world from obeying God and turned away from faith. Her call is to say: To me, O polytheist, to me, O disbeliever. Ibn Abbas said: She calls the disbelievers and hypocrites by their names in an eloquent tongue: To me, O disbeliever, to me, O hypocrite, then she picks them up as a bird picks up grain. Tha'lab said: She calls, meaning she destroys. The Arabs say: God has called you. Al-Khalil said: It is not like the supplication, Come, but her calling them enables her to torment them. It was said: The caller is the keepers of Hell, and their call was attributed to her. It was also said that it is a metaphor, meaning that the fate of whoever turned back and turned away is to her, so it is as if she is the one calling them. Similar to it is the saying of the poet: And We have certainly descended into the two valleys, one by one, and the companion calls to it, the one who is deaf and dumb. Al-Adheedh Al-Abkam: The fly. It does not call, but its buzzing alerts people to it, so it calls them to it. I said: The first statement is the truth, according to what was previously explained in the verses of the Qur’an and the authentic hadiths. Al-Qushayri: And the call of a blazing fire to create life in it when it calls, and the extraordinary things to come tomorrow are many.
70:18: And he gathered and stored meaning he gathered the money and put it in a container and withheld from it the right of God Almighty, so it was a gathering and a collection. Al-Hakam said: Abdullah bin Ukaim would not tie his purse and would say, "I heard God say: 'And he gathered and stored'."
70:19: God the Almighty said: Indeed, man was created impatient meaning the disbeliever, according to Ad-Dahhak. In the language, hal'a means extreme greed, the worst and most obscene impatience. Qatada, Mujahid and others said the same. The word hal'a with a kasra means to panic, so it is hal'u and halu'u, on the basis of exaggeration. The meaning is that he does not have patience with good or evil until he does what is not appropriate with them. Ikrimah: He is the impatient. Ad-Dahhak: He is the one who is never satisfied. The one who withholds money: He who, when he gains money, withholds from it what is due to God the Almighty. Ibn Kaysan said: God created man to love what pleases and pleases Him, and to flee from what dislikes and angers Him. Then God commanded him to spend what he loves and to be patient with what he dislikes. Abu Ubaidah said: The impatient one is the one who, when good befalls him, does not thank, and when harm befalls him, does not have patience. Tha'lab said this. Tha'lab also said: God has explained the impatient one, and it is the one who, when evil befalls him, shows intense impatience, and when good befalls him, he is miserly with it and people withhold it from him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The worst thing a servant can be given is greed and cowardice. The Arabs say, A she-camel is fast and light, when she walks quickly. He said: The cries of a fox, if you turn away from it, it will be embarrassing, if you stand on it, it will be frightening. Al-Dha'lab and Al-Dha'labah: the fast female camel. Ja'zu'an and Manu'u' are two adjectives for Halwa'. It is intended to be presented before 'idha'. It is also said that it is the predicate of an implied 'kan'.
70:20: God Almighty says: When evil touches him, he is impatient.
70:21: God Almighty says: And when good touches him, he withholds it.
70:22: The Almighty's statement: Except those who pray indicates that what preceded it was about the disbelievers. So, human is a generic noun, as evidenced by the exception that follows it, like His statement: Indeed, mankind is in loss, * Except for those who have believed (Al-'Asr: 2-3). An-Nakha'i said: What is meant by those who pray are those who perform the prescribed prayers. Ibn Mas'ud said: Those who pray them on time, as abandoning them is disbelief. It was also said: They are the Companions. It was also said: They are the believers in general, for excessive worry overcomes their trust in their Lord and their certainty.
70:23: Those who are constant in their prayers meaning at their appointed times. Uqbah ibn Amir said: They are those who, when they pray, do not turn right or left. Constant means still, and from this he forbade urinating in still water. Ibn Jurayj and Al-Hasan said: They are those who perform many voluntary prayers.
70:24: And those in whose wealth there is a known right refers to the obligatory zakat, as stated by Qatada and Ibn Sirin. Mujahid said: other than zakat. Ali ibn Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: maintaining kinship ties and bearing all. The first is more correct because it describes the right as known, while other than zakat is not known, but rather it is according to the need, and that can be little or much.
70:25: For the needy and the deprived is presented in the chapter on atoms.
70:26: And those who believe in the Day of Judgment meaning the Day of Recompense, which is the Day of Resurrection. This has been discussed in Surat Al-Fatihah.
70:27: And those who are fearful of the punishment of their Lord meaning afraid.
70:28: Indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not safe. Ibn Abbas said: For those who associate others with God or deny His prophets. It was also said: No one feels safe from it, rather, it is obligatory for everyone to oppose it and fear it.
70:29: It was mentioned in Surah: Indeed, the believers have succeeded. (Surah al-Mu’minun 23:1)
70:30: God Almighty says: Except from their wives or those their right hands possess, for indeed, they will not be blamed.
70:31: God Almighty says: But whoever seeks beyond that, then it is those who are the transgressors.
70:32: And those who are faithful to their trusts and their covenants. This also came before.
70:33: And those who uphold their testimonies against whoever it is against, near or far, they uphold it before the ruler and do not conceal it or change it. Testimony and its rulings have already been discussed in Surat Al-Baqarah. Ibn Abbas said: By their testimonies that God is One, with no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. It was read as their trustworthiness based on monotheism. This is also the reading of Ibn Kathir and Ibn Muhaisin. Trust is a generic noun, so it includes trusts in religion, for religious laws are trusts that God has entrusted to His servants. It also includes people's trusts from deposits, and all of this has already been fully discussed in Surat An-Nisa. Abbas Al-Duri, on the authority of Abu Amr and Ya'qub, read by their testimony in the plural. The rest by their testimony in the singular, because it is conveyed on behalf of the plural. The verbal noun can be singular even if it is added to a plural, like the Almighty's saying: Indeed, the most disagreeable of sounds is the braying of donkeys Luqman 4:19. Al-Farra’ said: “The evidence that it is ‘with their testimonies’ is unified, as God Almighty says: ‘And establish the testimony for God’” (al-Talaq 65:65).
70:34: And those who maintain their prayers Qatada said: their ablution, bowing, and prostration. Ibn Jurayj said: voluntary. This has been mentioned in Surat Al-Mu'minun. So, constancy is the opposite of constancy. Their constancy in them means that they maintain their performance, not neglecting them or being distracted from them by any distractions. Their constancy in them means that they take care to perform ablution perfectly and perform its prescribed times, perform its pillars, fulfill its Sunnahs and etiquette, and protect it from being rendered null by approaching sin. So, constancy refers to the prayers themselves, and constancy refers to their conditions.
70:35: They will be in gardens, honoured. That is, God will honour them there with various honours.
70:36: The Almighty said: Then why are those who disbelieved before you hastening? Al-Akhfash said: Hastening. He said: In Mecca, its people, and I saw them rushing to him to hear Meaning: Why do they rush to you and sit around you without knowing what you are ordering them to do? It was also said: What is wrong with them that they are so quick to deny you? It was also said: What is wrong with those who disbelieve that they rush to hear from you to criticize you and mock you? Atiyyah said: Rushing and turning away. Al-Kalbi: Looking at you in amazement. Qatada said: Intentionally. The meanings are close, meaning what is wrong with them that they rush to you, stretching out their necks, constantly looking at you. This is from the gaze of the enemy. It is in the accusative case as a state. It was revealed about a group of mocking hypocrites who were attending him - peace be upon him - but they did not believe in him. And before you means towards you.
70:37: On the right and on the left meaning on the right and left of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in circles and groups. Al-'Azin means groups in separate groups, as Abu Ubaidah said. And from this is the hadith of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “He went out to his companions and saw them in circles, so he said: What is the matter with you that I see you in groups? Do you not line up as the angels line up before their Lord?” They said: How do the angels line up before their Lord? He said: They complete the first rows and stand close together in the row. Narrated by Muslim and others. And the poet said: You see us with him, while the night is dark at his gates, in groups of strong ones.” That is, scattered. Al-Ra’i said: Caliph of the Most Gracious, my clan has come to you with its leaders, our condolences. That is, scattered. Another said: As if the skulls, from their falling, were like hyenas, swaying our various mourners. That is, scattered. Another said: When we came to the grave of the deceased, we scattered its pebbles in separate pieces. Al-Kumait said: We and Jandal Bagh left the battalions of Jandal, which we had been defeated in. Antara said: And a horn that I left to the one who is in charge of it, the bird, like a strong nerve One of them is ‘Azzain, plural with waw and noon to replace what was deleted from it. Its origin is ‘Azzah, but it became weak as sanah was weak for those who made its origin sanah. It was said that its origin is ‘Izwa, from ‘azzah ya’zuhu if he added it to someone else. So each one of the groups is added to the other, and what was deleted from it is the waw. In Al-Sahah: And the ‘Izza is a group of people, and the ha’ is a replacement for the ya’, and the plural is ‘azza - on fa’l - and ‘Azzun and ‘Azzun also with damma, and they did not say ‘Izzat as they said thabaat. Al-Asma’i said: It is said in the house ‘Azzun, meaning types of people. And ‘on the right and on the left’ is related to ‘mahta’in’ and it is permissible for it to be related to ‘Azzin’ like you say: I took it from Zaid.
70:38: Does every one of them aspire to enter a Garden of Delight? The commentators said: The polytheists used to gather around the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and listen to his speech, but they would lie about him and accuse him of lying, and they would mock his companions and say: If these people enter Paradise, we will surely enter it before them, and if they are given anything from it, we will be given more than it. So the verse: Does every one of them aspire to enter a Garden of Delight was revealed. It was also said: The mockers were five men. Al-Hasan, Talhah ibn Musarraf, and Al-A'raj read it as to enter with a fat-ha on the ya' and a damma on the kha', as the named subject. Al-Mufaddal narrated it from Asim. The rest read it as a passive verb. No means they will not enter it.
70:39: Then he began by saying: Indeed, We created them from that which they know, meaning that they know that they were created from a sperm-drop, then from a clot, then from a lump of flesh, as the rest of their kind were created. So they have no merit that would merit Paradise, but rather it is merited through faith, righteous deeds, and the mercy of God the Most High. It was said: They used to mock the poor Muslims and act arrogantly towards them. So he said: Indeed, We created them from that which they know, of filth, so this arrogance is not appropriate for them. Qatada said about this verse: O son of Adam, you were created from filth, so fear God. It was narrated that Mutraf bin Abdullah bin Ash-Shakheer saw Al-Muhallab bin Ai Sufra burning perfume on the edge of a silk garment and a piece of silk, so he said to him: O Abdullah, what is this gait that God hates?! He said to him: Do you recognize me? He said: Yes, at first you were a small speck of dust, at the end of you you will be a filthy corpse, and in between you carry filth. So Al-Muhallab moved on and abandoned his gait. Mahmoud Al-Warraq composed the following poem: I was amazed by someone who admires his image, even though he was originally a drop of sperm. And tomorrow, after his good image, he will become a filthy corpse in the grave. And he, in his confusion and pride, carries filth between his two garments. Another said: Is there any honor in the son of Adam other than the head, while he is struck with five kinds of dirt? A runny nose, stinky ears, a closed eye, and a burning mouth O son of dust and the one who eats dust, tomorrow you will be short, for you will be eaten and drunk. It was said: Its meaning is because of what they do, which is the command and prohibition, reward and punishment. Like the saying of the poet Al-A'sha: Have you decided to invent something from the family of Layla and have you strayed far from the one who loves you? For Laila.
70:40: The Almighty said: So I swear meaning I swear. And there is no connection. By the Lord of the Easts and the Wests refers to the places where the sun rises and sets. We have already discussed them. Abu Haywah, Ibn Muhaisin, and Hamid read By the Lord of the East and the West in the singular form. Indeed, We are Able "to replace them with better ones" meaning: We are able to destroy them and take them away. And to bring someone better than them in terms of choice, obedience, and wealth. "And We will not be outdone" meaning nothing escapes Us, and nothing we want is beyond Our power.
70:41: God Almighty says: That We may replace them with better ones, and We will not be outdone.
70:42: God Almighty says: So leave them to indulge in idle talk and play until they meet the Day they are promised. That is, leave them to indulge in their falsehood and play in their worldly life, as a threat. And occupy yourself with what you have been commanded to do and do not let their polytheism be too much for you, for they will have a Day when they will meet what they were promised. Ibn Muhaisin, Mujahid, and Hamid recited: until they meet the Day they were promised. This verse was abrogated by the verse of the sword.
70:44: The Almighty says: Their eyes will be humbled meaning submissive and submissive, not raising them to what they expect of God's punishment. Humiliation will overwhelm them Al-Ma'arij: meaning disgrace will overwhelm them. Qatada said: It is the blackening of faces. Rahaq means overwhelm, and from it is the word rahaquhu in the broken form yuhraquhu rahaqan meaning it overwhelms him, and from it is the saying of God the Almighty: And neither darkness nor humiliation will overwhelm their faces Yunus 10:26. That is the Day which they were promised meaning they were promised in this world that they would be punished on it. The report was presented in the past tense because what God promised him will inevitably happen.
71:1: Surah Nuh is Meccan, and it has twenty-eight verses. God the Almighty said: Indeed, We sent Noah to his people, [saying], ‘Warn your people before there comes to them a painful punishment.’ It was previously stated in Al-A’raf that Noah, peace be upon him, was the first messenger sent. Qatadah narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The first messenger sent was Noah, and he was sent to all the people of the earth. Therefore, when they disbelieved, God drowned all the people of the earth. He is Noah, son of Lamech, son of Methuselah, son of Enoch, who is Idris, son of Jared, son of Mahalalel, son of Enosh, son of Cainan, son of Seth, son of Adam, peace be upon him. Wahb said: They are all believers. He was sent to his people when he was one year old. Ibn Abbas said: Forty years. Abdullah ibn Shaddad said: He was sent when he was three hundred and fifty years old. This was previously stated in Surat An-Nakboot. Praise be to God. Warn your people means: warn your people. The position of an is in the accusative case, dropping the preposition. It was also said that its position is in the genitive case due to its strong service with an. It is possible that an has the meaning of the explanatory particle, so it has no syntactic position, because sending has the meaning of a command, so there is no need to omit the baa. The reading of Abdullah without an means We said to him, warn your people. The meaning of warning has already been mentioned at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah. before there comes to them a painful punishment Ibn Abbas said: It means the punishment of the Fire in the Hereafter. Al-Kalbi said: It is what descended upon them of the flood. It was also said: That is, warn them of the painful punishment in general if they do not believe. So he used to call his people and warn them, but he did not see anyone responding from them. They used to beat him until he fainted, so he would say: My Lord, forgive my people, for they do not know. This has already been mentioned in full in Surat Al-Ankaboot. Praise be to God.
71:2: God Almighty says: He said, ‘O my people, indeed I am to you a warner.’ That is, one who frightens. Clear, that is, one who reveals in your language that you know.
71:3: Worship God and fear Him. The explanation is based on what was mentioned previously in that I warn. Worship means to make Him One. And fear Him means to be afraid. And obey means in what I command you, for I am the Messenger of God to you.
71:4: He will forgive you some of your sins. The verb to forgive is in the subjunctive mood as a response to a command. Min is an extra relative clause. The meaning of this statement is He will forgive you your sins, as al-Suddi said. It was also said that it is not correct for it to be extra, because min does not add an obligation. Rather, it is used here to indicate a partial meaning, which is some of the sins, which are not related to the rights of human beings. It was also said that it is to clarify the genus. This is far-fetched, as no genus appropriate to it has preceded. Zayd ibn Aslam said: The meaning is that He will deliver you from your sins. Ibn Shajarah said: The meaning is that He will forgive you from your sins whatever you seek forgiveness for. And He will delay you for a specified term. Ibn Abbas said: That is, He will extend your lives. The meaning is that God had decreed before creating them that if they believed, He would bless their lives, and if they did not believe, they would be hastened with punishment. Muqatil said: He will delay you until the end of your lives in good health, so He will not punish you with famine or anything else. So the meaning according to this is that He will delay you from punishments and hardships until your lives. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, He delays you from the punishment so that you die a death other than that of those who are uprooted by punishment. Based on this, it was said: “A specified term with you that you know. He will not cause you to die by drowning, burning, or killing.” Al-Farra’ mentioned it. According to the first opinion, a specified term is with God. Indeed, when the term of God comes, it is not delayed. That is, when death comes, it is not delayed, whether by punishment or otherwise. And the term was attributed to Him, glory be to Him, because He is the One who established it. And it may be attributed to the people, like His statement, So when their term comes (al-Nahl 16:61) because it is set for them. If means if, meaning if you knew. Al-Hasan said: Its meaning is, If you knew, you would have known that when the term of God comes to you, it will not be delayed.
71:5: God Almighty says: He said, ‘My Lord, I have called upon my people night and day,’ meaning secretly and openly. It was also said: I continued to call upon God.
71:6: My supplication only increased their flight meaning their distancing from faith. The common reading is with a fat-ha on the ya' of du'a'i while the Kufians, Ya'qub, and al-Duri read it with a sukun on the ya' from Abu Amr.
71:7: The Almighty says: And whenever I called them meaning to the cause of forgiveness, which is belief in You and obedience to You, they put their fingers in their ears so they would not hear My call, and covered their faces with them meaning they covered them with their garments so they would not see Him. Ibn Abbas said: They put their garments over their heads so they would not hear His words. So covering their faces with their garments was to further block the ears so they would not hear, or to disguise themselves until He was silent, or so that He would know that they were turning away from Him. It was said: It is a metaphor for enmity. It is said: So-and-so dressed in enmity for me. And they persisted meaning in disbelief and did not repent. And they were arrogant about accepting the truth, because they said: Shall we believe in you while the lowest have followed you? (Ash-Shu’ara’: 111). Arrogance is an expression of glorification.
71:8: The Almighty said: Then I called them openly meaning I called them openly. It is in the accusative case with their call, as a verbal noun, because calling is one of the two types of equipment, so it is in the accusative case of squatting with sitting, because it is one of the types of sitting, or because he meant by their call that I called them openly. It is permissible for it to be an attribute of the verbal noun called, meaning a call openly, meaning openly. And it is in the accusative case as a verbal noun in the place of a state, meaning I called them openly with the call to them.
71:9: Then I declared to them and spoke to them secretly. That is, I left no stone unturned. Mujahid said: The meaning of declared is I shouted and spoke to them secretly, by praying for some of them from others. It was also said: And spoke to them secretly means I came to them in their homes. All of this from Noah, peace be upon him, is an exaggeration in praying for them and a gentleness in the summoning. The Haramiyun and Abu Amr opened the ya of I declared to them while the rest kept it silent.
71:10: First: The Almighty said: Then I said, 'Seek forgiveness of your Lord.' That is, ask Him for forgiveness for your past sins with sincere faith. He is Oft-Forgiving. This is an encouragement from Him to repent. Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman narrated on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he said: Seeking forgiveness erases sins. Al-Fudayl said: The servant says, I seek forgiveness from God, and its interpretation is, He has pardoned me.
71:11: Second: The Almighty’s saying: He sends down upon you abundant rain meaning He sends down water from the sky, so there is an omission in it. It was said: The sky is the rain, meaning He sends down rain. The poet said: If the sky falls on the land of a people, they will take care of it, even if they are angry. And abundant rain. And he who sends abundant rain is certain in response to an order. Muqatil said: When they denied Noah for a long time, God withheld rain from them and made the wombs of their women barren for forty years, so their livestock and crops perished. So they went to Noah, peace be upon him, and sought his help. He said: Seek forgiveness of your Lord, for He is ever Forgiving, meaning He remains so for those who turn to Him. Then he said, encouraging faith: He will send down upon you abundant rain.
71:12: And He will provide you with wealth and children and provide for you gardens and provide for you rivers. Qatada said: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, knew that they were greedy for this world, so he said: Come to the obedience of God, for in the obedience of God is the attainment of this world and the Hereafter. Third: In this verse and the one in Hud there is evidence that seeking forgiveness brings down provision and rain. Al-Sha’bi said: “Umar went out to seek rain, but he did nothing more than seek forgiveness until he returned. They were given rain, and they said, ‘We did not see you ask for rain.’ He said, ‘You have asked for rain with the angels of the sky by which rain is sent down.’ Then he recited: ‘Seek forgiveness of your Lord. Indeed, He is ever Forgiving. He will send [rain from] the sky upon you in showers.’” Al-Awza’i said: The people went out to seek rain, and Bilal ibn Sa’d stood up among them, praised and glorified God, then said, ‘O God, we have heard You say, “There is no blame upon the doers of good (al-Tawbah 9:91), and we have admitted to our wrongdoing. Is Your forgiveness except for the likes of us? O God, forgive us, have mercy on us, and give us rain!’ So he raised his hands, and they raised their hands, and they were given rain. Ibn Subaih said: A man complained to Al-Hasan about drought, so he said to him, Seek forgiveness from God. Another complained to him about poverty, so he said to him, Seek forgiveness from God. Another said to him, Pray to God to grant me a son, so he said to him, Seek forgiveness from God. Another man complained to him about the dryness of his garden, so he said to him: Seek forgiveness from God. We asked him about that. He said: “I did not say anything of my own. The manner of seeking forgiveness has already been mentioned in Surat Al Imran, and that it is done out of sincerity and abstaining from sins. This is the basis for prayers being answered.”
71:13: God the Almighty says: What is the matter with you that you do not have awe of God? It was said that hope here means fear, that is, why do you not fear God's greatness and power to punish any of you? That is, what excuse do you have for not fearing God? Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu al-'Aliyah, and Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: What is the matter with you that you do not return to God for reward and do not fear His punishment? Sa'id ibn Jubayr said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: What is the matter with you that you do not fear God's punishment and hope for reward from Him? Al-Walibi and Al-Awfi said on his authority: What is the matter with you that you do not know God's greatness? Ibn Abbas and Mujahid also said: What is the matter with you that you do not see God's greatness? Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak narrated: What is the matter with you that you do not care about God's greatness? Qutrub said: This is a Hijazi dialect. Hudhayl, Khuza'ah, and Mudar say: I did not hope lam arj (I did not care). Dignity means greatness. Reverence means glorification. Qatada said: Why do you not hope for the outcome of God? As if the meaning is: Why do you not hope for the outcome of faith in God? Ibn Kaysan said: In worshipping God and obeying Him, that He may reward you for your reverence with good. Ibn Zayd said: Why do you not perform obedience to God? Al-Hasan said: Why do you not recognize God’s right and thank Him for His blessings? It was also said: Why do you not worship God alone? Because whoever glorifies Him has worshipped Him alone. It was also said: “Reverence is steadfastness for God the Almighty, and from this is His statement: “And abide in your houses” (al-Ahzab 33:33) meaning, Be steadfast. Its meaning is: Why do you not affirm the Oneness of God the Almighty and that He is your God, you have no other god but Him? Ibn Bahr said:
71:14: And He has created you in stages meaning He made for you within yourselves a sign that points to His Oneness. Ibn Abbas said: Stages means a sperm-drop, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, meaning stage after stage until creation is complete, as mentioned in Surat Al-Mu'minun. Stage in the language means time, meaning whoever does this and is able to do it is more deserving of your reverence. It was also said: Stages: children, then youth, then old and weak, then strong. It was also said: Stages, meaning types: healthy and sick, sighted and blind, rich and poor. It was also said: Stages are their differences in morals and actions.
71:15: The Almighty says: Have you not seen how God created seven heavens in layers? He mentioned to them another proof, meaning, do you not know that the One who has power over this is the One who should be worshipped! The meaning of layers, one above the other, is that each heaven is layered over the other like domes, as stated by Ibn Abbas and Al-Suddi. Al-Hasan said: God created seven heavens in layers upon seven earths, between each earth and another earth, and one heaven after another is creation and command. His statement: Have you not seen? It is in the sense of informing, not witnessing, as you say: Did you not see me how I did such-and-such to so-and-so? And layers is in the accusative case as a verbal noun, meaning matching layers. Or it is a state meaning the essence of layers, so He deleted the essence and made layers in its place.
71:16: And He made the moon a light therein meaning in the lowest heaven, as one says: Banu Tamim came to me and I came to Banu Tamim, meaning some of them, as stated by Al-Akhfash. Ibn Kaysan said: If it is in one of them, then it is among them. Qutrub said: In them means with them, as stated by Al-Kalbi. Meaning, He created the sun and lifespan along with the creation of the heavens and the earth. The majority of linguists said about the statement of Imru' Al-Qais: And will someone whose last period was thirty months enjoy three conditions? In the sense of with. An-Nahhas: I asked Abu al-Hasan ibn Kaysan about this verse and he said: The grammarians’ answer is that if He put it in one of them, then He has put it in them, as you say: Give me the marked clothes even if I only marked one of them. Another answer is: It is narrated that the face of al-Umar is towards the sky, and if it is inside it then it is connected to the heavens. The meaning of light is for the people of the earth, as al-Suddi said. Ata’ said: A light for the people of the sky and the earth. Ibn Abbas and Ibn Amr said: His face shines for the people of the earth and his back shines for the people of the sky. And He made the sun a lamp means a lamp for the people of the earth so that they can manage their livelihoods. Concerning its illumination of the people of the sky, there are the first two opinions, as al-Mawardi narrated. Al-Qushayri narrated from Ibn Abbas that the face of the sun is towards the heavens and its back is on the earth. It was also said: The opposite. It was said to Abdullah ibn Amr: Why is it that the sun sometimes meets us and is cold for us at other times? He said: In the summer it is in the fourth heaven, and in the winter it is in the seventh heaven near the Throne of the Most Merciful. If it were in the lowest heaven, nothing would have stood up to it.
71:17: The Almighty's saying: And God caused you to grow from the earth as plants means that He created Adam, peace be upon him, from the surface of the whole earth, as Ibn Jurayj said. This was explained in Surat Al-An'am and Surat Al-Baqarah. Khalid bin Ma'dan said: He created man from clay, for hearts are only suitable in winter. And plant is a verbal noun based on a source other than the verbal noun, because its verbal noun is to grow, so the noun, which is plant, was made in the position of the verbal noun. This was explained in Surat Al-Imran and others. It was said: It is a verbal noun based on the meaning, because the meaning of to grow is that He made you grow as plants, as Al-Khalil and Al-Zajjaj said. It was said: That is, He caused plants to grow for you from the earth. So plant according to this is in the accusative case as an explicit verbal noun. The first is more evident. Ibn Jurayj said: He caused them to grow in the earth in largeness after smallness and in height after shortness.
71:18: Then He will return you into it and bring you out a [final] emergence. "Then He will return you into it" means when you die by being buried. "And bring you out a [final] emergence" by being resurrected for the Day of Resurrection.
71:19: God Almighty says: And God has made the earth a carpet for you meaning spread out.
71:20: That you may take therein wide paths. Paths: roads. Fajaj is the plural of faj, which is a wide road, as Al-Farra' said. It was also said that faj is the path between two mountains. This was mentioned previously in Surat Al-Anbiya and Surat Al-Hajj.
71:21: God Almighty said: Noah said, ‘My Lord, indeed they have disobeyed me and followed one whose wealth and children only increase him in loss.’ He complained to God Almighty about them, that they disobeyed him and did not follow him in what he commanded them, out of faith. The commentators said: He remained among them for a thousand years minus fifty, calling them to disbelief and disobedience. Ibn Abbas said: Noah, peace be upon him, hoped for sons after fathers, so that they would be given son after son until they reached seven centuries. Then he called down curses upon them after despairing of them, and he lived for sixty years after the flood until people became numerous and widespread. Al-Hasan said: The people of Noah used to plant twice a month, as narrated by Al-Mawardi. And they followed he whose wealth and children only increased him in loss means their leaders and rich people whose disbelief, wealth and children only increased them in misguidance in this world and destruction in the hereafter. The people of Medina, Ash-Sham and Asim read his son with a fat-ha on the waw and the lam. The rest read his son with a damma on the waw and a sukoon on the lam, which is a language for son. It is also permissible for it to be a plural for son, like the ark which is both singular and plural. This has been mentioned previously.
71:22: God Almighty says: And they plotted a great plot. Meaning: great and immense. It is said: great and grand and grand, like amazing and amazing and amazing with the same meaning, and the same is true for tall and tall and tall. It is said: a handsome man and handsome men, and beautiful and beauty, and readers for the reader, and whiteness for the whiteness. Ibn al-Sikkit recited: White hunts hearts and seizes the hearts of Muslims with beauty Another said: A man's good character makes him a youth of generosity, not of radiance. Al-Mubarrad said: Kabārān with emphasis for emphasis. Ibn Muhaisin, Hamid, and Mujahid read it as Kabārān with emphasis. There is a difference of opinion about their plot: What was it? Some say: It was their incitement of their predecessors to kill Noah. Others say: It was their strengthening of the people with what they were given of this world and children, until the weak said: If they were not on the truth, they would not have been given these blessings. Al-Kalbi said: It is what they attributed to God of a wife and children. Others say: Their plot was their disbelief. Muqatil said: It is the saying of their elders to their followers: Do not abandon your gods, and do not abandon Wadd, Suwa’, Yaghuth, Ya’uq, and Nasr.
71:23: God Almighty said: And they said, ‘Do not abandon your gods, and do not abandon Wadd, Suwa’, Yaghuth, Ya’uq, and Nasr.’ Ibn Abbas and others said: They are idols and pictures that the people of Noah used to worship, then the Arabs worshipped them. This is the opinion of the majority. It was said that they belonged to the Arabs and no one else worshipped them. They were the largest and most important idols to them, and that is why they specifically mentioned them after the verse: {Do not abandon your gods}. The Arabs said to their children and their al-Nas 114:Do not abandon Wadd, nor Suwa’, nor Yaghuth, Ya’uq, nor Nasr. Then the mention returned after that to the people of Noah. According to the first opinion, the entire speech is directed to the people of Noah. Urwah ibn al-Zubayr and others said: Adam (peace be upon him) complained while his sons were with him: Wadd, Suwa’, Yaghuth, Ya’uq, and Nasr. Wadd was the eldest of them and the most dutiful to him. Muhammad ibn Ka’b said: Adam (peace be upon him) had five sons: Wadd, Suwa’, Yaghuth, Ya’uq, and Nasr. They were worshippers, but none of them made them sad because of him. Then Satan said: I will make for you someone like him, if you look at him you will remember him. They said: Do it. So they cast him in the mosque of brass and lead. Then another died, and they cast him in it until they all died, and they cast them in it. Things decreased as they decrease today until, after a while, they abandoned the worship of God Almighty. Then Satan said to them: Why do you worship nothing? They said: What is far-fetched? He said: Your gods and the gods of your fathers. Do you not see them in your place of prayer? So they worshipped them instead of God until God sent Noah, and they said: Do not abandon your gods, nor abandon Wadd or Suwa' (al-Anfal 2:17). Muhammad ibn Ka'b and Muhammad ibn Qays also said: Rather, they were a righteous people between Adam and Noah, and they had followers who followed their example. When they died, Satan made it seem attractive to them to draw images of themselves to remind them of their efforts and to amuse themselves by looking at them, so he drew images of them. When they died and others came, they said: Would that we knew! What did our fathers do with this image? Then Satan came to them and said: Your fathers used to worship it, so it would have mercy on them and send them rain. They worshipped them, and idol worship began at that time. I said: In this sense, what was mentioned in Sahih Muslim from the hadith of Aisha was explained: Umm Habibah and Umm Salamah mentioned a church they had seen in Abyssinia called Mariyah, in which there were pictures of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: When there was a righteous man among them and he died, they would build a place of worship over his grave and make pictures, and those are the pictures. They are the worst of creation in the sight of God on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Tha’labi narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: These idols are the names of righteous men from the people of Noah. When they perished, Satan inspired their people to set up idols in the gatherings where they used to sit and name them after them so that they would remember them. They did so, but they were not worshipped until those men perished and knowledge was abolished, then they were worshipped instead of God. It was also mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Noah, peace be upon him, was guarding the body of Adam, peace be upon him, on a mountain in India, preventing the unbelievers from circumambulating his grave. Satan said to them: These people boast to you and claim that they are the sons of Adam without you. It is only a body, and I will make for you one like it for you to circumambulate around it. So he made for them these five idols and made them worship them. When the days of the flood came, mud, dirt and water buried them, and they remained buried until Satan brought them out to the polytheists of Arabia. Al-Mawardi said: As for Wadd, he was the first idol worshipped. It was named Wadd because of their love for him. After the people of Noah, it belonged to Kalb in Dumat al-Jandal. According to Ibn Abbas, Ata’ and Muqatil, their poet said about him: Welcome, my friend, for it is not permissible for us to indulge in women, and the religion has determined As for Suwa’, he was from Hudhayl on the sea coast, according to what they say. As for Yaghuth, he belonged to Ghataif of Murad in Al-Jawf of Saba, according to Qatada. Al-Mahdawi said: It belonged to Murad, then to Ghatafan. Al-Tha'labi said: A'la and An'am - and they are from Tayy - and the people of Jarash of Madhhij took Yaghuth and went with him to Murad and worshipped him for a period. Then Banu Najiyah wanted to take him from A'la and An'am, so they fled with him to Al-Hussain, the brother of Banu Al-Harith bin Ka'b of Khuza'ah. Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi said: I saw Yaghuth, and he was made of lead. They used to carry him on a white camel, and they would walk with him without disturbing him until he knelt down. When he knelt down, they would dismount and say: He has approved your home, and they would see a building on it and camp around it. As for Ya'uq, he was for Hamdan in Balkha', according to Ikrimah, Qatadah, and Ata'. Al-Mawardi mentioned him, and Al-Tha'labi said: As for Ya'uq, he was for Kahlan of Saba, then his sons inherited him, the oldest after the oldest, until he reached Hamdan. Malik bin Numat Al-Hamadhani said about him: God blesses in this world and heals but does not heal, He hinders but does not feather As for Nasr, it belonged to Dhu al-Kila’ of Himyar, according to the saying of Qatada and similarly from Muqatil. Al-Waqidi said: Wadd was in the form of a man, Suwa’ in the form of a woman, Yaghuth in the form of a lion, Ya’uq in the form of a horse, and Nasr in the form of an eagle from the birds. And God knows best. Nafi’ read Do not abandon Wadd with a damma on the waw. The rest read it with a fatha. Al-Layth said: Wadd with a fatha on the waw was an idol that belonged to a people who migrated, and Wadd with a damma was an idol of Quraysh, and ‘Amr ibn Wadd was named after it. In Al-Sahah: Wadd with a fatha is waid in the language of the people of Najd, as if they made the ta’ sukun and assimilated it into the dal. Wadd in the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: Show affection when you are generous and hide it when you are upset Ibn Duraid said: It is the name of a mountain. Wadd was an idol that belonged to the people of Noah, peace be upon him, then it belonged to Kalb and was in Dumat al-Jandal, and from it they named it Abd Wudd. And he said: Do not abandon your gods, then he said: And do not abandon Wadd or Suwa’, the verse. He mentioned it specifically because of the saying of God the Almighty: And when We took a covenant from the prophets and from you and from Noah. al-Ahzab 33:7. And they had certainly led many astray. This is from the saying of Noah, meaning their leaders had led many astray among their followers, so it is in apposition to his saying: And they plotted a great plot. It was said that the idols led many astray, meaning many were led astray because of them. Similar to the saying of Abraham: My Lord, indeed they have led many astray among the people, so he described them with what one can reason, because the disbelievers believed that about them.
71:24: And do not increase the wrongdoers except in error meaning torment, as Ibn Bahr said. He cited as evidence the words of God Almighty: Indeed, the criminals are in error and madness (al-Qamar 54:47). It was also said: Except loss. It was also said: Except a trial of wealth and children. This is possible.
71:25: The Almighty's saying: Because of their sins they were drowned "ma is an emphatic conjunction, and the meaning is from their sins." Al-Farra' said: The meaning is "because of their sins, so ma" conveyed this meaning. He said: "And what indicates recompense. Abu Amr's reading of khatayahum is in the broken plural, the singular being khatiya. The original plural was khatayy on the basis of fa'a'il, but when the two hamzas met, the second was changed to a ya because it was preceded by a kasra, then it became independent and the plural is heavy, and it is still defective, so the ya was changed to an alif, then the first hamza was changed to a ya because of its kha, which built the two alifs. The rest of the readings of khatayahum" are in the sound plural. Abu Amr said: A people who disbelieved for a thousand years and had nothing but sins, meaning that the sins are more than the sins. Some people said: "khatayyat and khatiyat" are one, two plurals used for many and few, and they provided evidence for that by the Almighty's saying: "The Words of God have not been exhausted" (Luqman 31:27). And the poet said: Our eyelids shine at noon, and our swords drip with the blood of salvation. Their sins are read by changing the hamza to a ya and assimilate it. Al-Jahdary, Amr ibn Ubayd, Al-A’mash, Abu Haywah, and Ashhab Al-Uqayli said that their sin was against monotheism, but what is meant is polytheism. So they entered the Fire means after they were drowned. Al-Qushayri said: This indicates the torment of the grave. Those who deny it say: They became deserving of entering the Fire, or their places in the Fire were shown to them, as God the Almighty said: The Fire they are exposed to morning and afternoon (Ghafir 40:46). It was said: They referred to what is in the hadith of His statement: The sea is fire within fire. Abu Rawq narrated from Al-Dahhak regarding His statement: They were drowned “So they entered the Fire” that he said: It means they were tormented with fire in this world along with drowning in this world in one state. They were drowning on one side and burning in the water on the other side. Al-Tha’labi mentioned it, saying: Abu Al-Qasim Al-Habibi recited to us, saying: Abu Sa’id Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rumaih recited to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Al-Anbari recited to me: Creation is a community that is in phases and separates, and events are arts with phases. Do not be surprised by opposites that come together, for God brings together water and fire. "And they found no helpers for themselves besides God" meaning no one to protect them from the punishment.
71:26: God Almighty said: And Noah said, ‘My Lord, do not leave upon the earth a single inhabitant of the disbelievers.’ These are four issues: First: He invoked curses upon them when he despaired of them following him. Qatada said: He invoked curses upon them after God revealed to him: None of your people will believe except those who have already believed Hud:36. So God answered his invocation and drowned his nation. This is like the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): O God, Revealer of the Book, Swift in account and Defeater of the confederates, defeat them and shake them. It was said: The reason for his invocation was that a man from his people was carrying a small child on his shoulder. He passed by Noah and said: Beware of this, for he will lead you astray. Noah said: O my father, put me down. So he put him down and threw him, wounding him. At that moment, Noah became angry and invoked curses upon them. Muhammad ibn Ka’b, Muqatil, Ar-Rabi’, Atiyah and Ibn Zayd said: He only said this when God brought forth every believer from their loins and the wombs of their women. He made the wombs of women and the loins of men barren seventy years before the punishment. It was also said: Forty years. Qatada said: There was no child among them at the time of the punishment. Al-Hasan and Abu Al-Aaliyah said: If God had destroyed their children with them, it would have been a punishment from God to them and justice towards them. However, God destroyed their children and offspring without punishment, then He destroyed them with punishment, as evidenced by the words of God Almighty: And the people of Noah, when they denied the messengers, We drowned them (al-Furqan 25:37). Second: Ibn Al-Arabi said: Noah supplicated against all the disbelievers, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) supplicated against those who formed parties against the believers and incited them against them. This was the basis for supplicating against the disbelievers in general. As for a specific disbeliever whose end is unknown, then one should not supplicate against him, because his wealth is unknown to us, while perhaps his happy end is known to God. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) specifically supplicated against Utbah, Shaibah, and their companions, because he knew their wealth and what had been revealed to him about their condition. And God knows best. I said: This issue has already been discussed in Surat Al-Baqarah, praise be to God. Third: Ibn al-Arabi said: If it is said, Why did Noah make his supplication against his people a reason for his stopping asking God to intercede for creation in the Hereafter? We say, “People have said two views on that: One of them is that that supplication arose out of anger and harshness, while intercession comes from contentment and tenderness, so he feared that he would be rebuked and it would be said, ‘You supplicated against the disbelievers yesterday and you intercede for them today.’” The second is that he supplicated in anger without explicit text or permission to do so, so he feared being caught up in it on the Day of Resurrection, just as Moses, peace be upon him, said, Indeed, I killed a soul I was not commanded to kill. He said, And this is what I say. I said: Even if he was not commanded to supplicate explicitly, he was told: None of your people will believe except those who have already believed (Hud 11:36). So he knew their consequences, so he supplicated for their destruction. Our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, also prayed against Shaibah, Utbah, and their peers, saying: May God deal with them, for I know their consequences. Based on this, it also means a command to pray. And God knows best.
71:27: Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: “Dwellings. If You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and will not give birth except to wicked disbelievers.” That is, whoever inhabits a dwelling, as Al-Suddi said. Its root is diwar on the pattern fa’aal from dar yadawar, so the waw was changed to a ya’ and one of them was assimilated into the other. Like qiyam, its root is qiywam. If it was fa’al, it would have been dawar. Al-Qutbi said: Its root is from dar, meaning someone who resides in a house. It is said: there is no one in the house diyar, meaning anyone. It is also said: diyar is the owner of the house.
71:28: God the Almighty says: My Lord, forgive me and my parents. He supplicated for himself and his parents, and they were believers. They were Lamech bin Methuselah and Shamkha bint Enosh, mentioned by Al-Qushayri and Al-Tha'labi. Al-Mawardi mentioned his mother's name, Manjal. Saeed bin Jubair said: By his parents, he meant his father and grandfather. Saeed bin Jubair read my parents with a kasra on the dal for the singular. Al-Kalbi said: Between him and Adam there were ten fathers, all of them believers. Ibn Abbas said: No father of Noah disbelieved between him and Adam, peace be upon them. And whoever enters my house as a believer meaning my mosque and my place of prayer, praying and believing in God. Only those who believed among the prophets would enter the houses of the prophets, so he made the mosque a reason for supplication for forgiveness. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "The angels send blessings upon one of you as long as he remains in the place where he prayed, as long as he does not speak during it. They say: O God, forgive him, O God, have mercy on him." The hadith has been mentioned before. This is the saying of Ibn Abbas: My house is my mosque. Al-Tha’labi narrated it and Ad-Dahhak said it. Ibn Abbas also said: And for whoever enters my religion. House means religion. Al-Qushayri narrated it and Juwaybir said it. Ibn Abbas also said: It means my friend who enters my house. Al-Mawardi narrated it. It was also said: He meant my house. It was also said: My ship. And for the believing men and believing women is general until the Day of Resurrection. Ad-Dahhak said it. Al-Kalbi said: From the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was also said: From his people, but the first is more apparent. And do not increase the wrongdoers meaning the disbelievers. Except in destruction except in ruin. So it is general for every disbeliever and polytheist. It was also said: He meant the polytheists of his people. Tabār means ruin. It was also said: loss, as As-Suddi narrated it. From this is the saying of God Almighty: Indeed, these will perish that which they are in. (al-A’raf 7:139). It was also said: Tabar means destruction, but the meaning is the same. And God knows best about that. He is the One who guides to what is correct. By the grace of God, the eighteenth part of Al-Qurtubi’s interpretation has been completed. It will be followed, God willing, by the nineteenth part, which begins with Surat Al-Jinn.
72:1: Meccan according to everyone. It has twenty-eight verses. First - The Almighty’s saying: Say, ‘It has been revealed to me,’ meaning, say, O Muhammad, to your nation, God has revealed to me through the tongue of Gabriel, that he listened to a group of jinn, and that he, peace be upon him, did not know about it before it was revealed to him. This is what Ibn Abbas and others said, as will come. Ibn Abi Ubla read ahya according to the original; it is said: it was revealed to him and he was revealed, so the waw was changed to a hamza. And from this is the saying of the Almighty: And when the messengers are gathered (al-Mursalat 77:11). It is from the absolute change that it is permissible in every waw that has a guaranteed letter. Al-Mazini also used it in the broken form, such as ishah, isadah, and returning his brother9 and the like. Second: There is disagreement as to whether the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw them or not. The apparent meaning of the Qur’an indicates that he did not see them, as God Almighty says: Listen, and He also says: And when We directed to you a company of the jinn, listening to the Qur’an (al-Ahqaf 46:29). In Sahih Muslim and Al-Tirmidhi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited to the jinn, but he did not see them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out with a group of his companions, intending to go to the market of ‘Ukaz. The devils were prevented from receiving report from heaven, and meteors were sent down upon them. The devils returned to their people and said: What is the matter with you? They said: We were prevented from receiving report from heaven, and meteors were sent down upon us! They said: That is not something that has happened. Travel to the east and west of the earth, and see what is it that has prevented us from receiving report from heaven? So they set out, traveling to the east and west of the earth. The group that had gone towards Tihamah passed by at Nakhl, intending to go to the market of ‘Ukaz, and he was leading his companions in the dawn prayer. When they heard the Qur’an, they listened to it and said: This is what has prevented us from receiving report from heaven. So they returned to their people and said: O our people, we have heard an amazing Qur’an. It guides to the right path, so we believe in it and we will not associate anyone with our Lord.” Then God Almighty revealed to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. “Say, ‘It has been revealed to me that a group of jinn listened. ’” Narrated by al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The jinn said to their people, When Abdullah stood up to call upon Him, they almost crowded around him. He said: When they saw him praying and his companions praying with him and prostrating with him, he said: They were amazed at the obedience of his companions to him. They said to their people, When Abdullah stood up to call upon Him, they almost crowded around him. He said: This is a good and authentic hadith. In this hadith is evidence that the Prophet, peace be upon him, did not see the jinn, but they were present and heard his recitation. It also indicates that the jinn were with the devils when they spied on the report because of the devils when they were shot with meteors. Those who were shot with meteors were also from the jinn, and they were called devils, as He said: Devils among mankind and jinn (al-An`am 6:122). For the devil is every rebel and one who goes against the obedience of God. In al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: “The jinn used to ascend to the heavens to listen to the revelation. When they heard a word, they would add nine to it. As for the word, it would be true, but as for what They increased it, so it would be false. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was sent as a leader, they were denied their seats. They mentioned that to Satan, and stars had not been shot before that. Satan said to them: This matter is nothing but something that has happened on earth! So he sent his soldiers and they found the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) standing praying in Bin Jabaleen - I think he said in Mecca - so they went to him and informed him. He said: This is the event that has happened on earth. He said: This is a good and authentic hadith. This hadith indicates that the jinn threw stones just as the devils threw stones. In Al-Suddi’s narration: “When they threw stones, they came to Satan and informed him of what had happened to them. He said: Bring me a handful of dirt from every land so I can smell it. So they came to him and he smelled it. He said: Your companion is in Mecca. So he sent a group of jinn. It was said: There were seven of them. It was said: Nine of them, including Zuba’ah.” And “Aasim narrated from Zur who said: The group of Zuba’ah and his companions came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Al-Thamali said: “I have been informed that they are from Banu Shaysban, and they are the most numerous of the jinn, and the most powerful, and they are the majority of the soldiers of Satan.” Asim also narrated from Zur: “They were seven men: three from Harran and four from Nasibin.” Juwaybir narrated from Ad-Dahhak: They were nine from Nasibin a village in Yemen other than the one in Iraq. It was said that the jinn who came to Mecca were the jinn of Nasibin, and those who came to him at Nakhl were the jinn of Nineveh. This was explained in Surat Al-Ahqaf. Ikrimah said: “The surah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to recite was ‘Read in the name of your Lord’ (al-Alaq 96:1). The names of the group of jinn were mentioned in Surat Al-Ahqaf, so there is no point in repeating that.” It was said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw the jinn on the night of the jinn, and this is more reliable. Amer Al-Sha’bi narrated: “I asked Alqamah, ‘Did Ibn Mas’ud witness the night of the jinn with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace?’ Alqamah said: ‘I asked Ibn Mas’ud, “Did any of you witness the night of the jinn with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace?” He said: ‘No, but we were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, one night and we missed him. We looked for him in the valleys and ravines, and we said, ‘He was carried away or killed.’ We spent the worst night ever spent by a people. When morning came, he came from the direction of Hira’. We said, ‘O Messenger of God! We missed you and looked for you but did not find you.’ We spent the worst night ever spent by a people.’ He said: ‘A caller from the jinn came to me, so I went with him and recited the Qur’an to them.’ He set off with us and showed us their traces and the traces of their fires. They asked him for provisions, and they were from the jinn of the peninsula. He said: ‘You have everything. ’” A bone mentioned in the name of God falls into your hands and is more abundant in meat, and every dung is fodder for your animals. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Do not use them for istinja cleaning oneself with them, for they are the food of your jinn brothers. Ibn al-Arabi said: Ibn Mas`ud knew better than Ibn `Abbas that he heard it, and a report is not like seeing it. It has been said that the jinn came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) twice: one time in Mecca, which is what Ibn Mas`ud mentioned, and the second time in Nakhlah, which is what Ibn `Abbas mentioned. Al-Bayhaqi said: What `Abdullah ibn `Abbas related is when the jinn first heard the recitation of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and knew of his condition. At that time, he did not recite to them and did not see them, as he related. Then the caller of the jinn came to him again, so he went with him and recited the Qur’an to them, as `Abdullah ibn Mas`ud related. Al-Bayhaqi said: The authentic hadiths indicate that Ibn Masoud was not with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the night of the jinn. Rather, he walked with him when he set out with him and others, showing him the traces of the jinn and the traces of their fires. He said: It has been narrated from more than one source that he was with him that night, and this meaning has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Ahqaf. Praise be to God. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I have been ordered to recite the Qur’an to the jinn, so who will go with me? They were silent. Then he said it a second time. Then Abdullah ibn Mas’ud said: I will go with you, O Messenger of God. So he set off until he came to al-Hujun at the ravine of Abu Dub. He drew a line and said: “Do not cross it.” Then he went to al-Hujun and people like partridges descended upon him, dragging stones with their feet, walking and drumming their tambourines as women drum their tambourines, until he became invisible and I could not see him. So I stood up and he motioned to me with his hand to sit. So he recited the Qur’an and he did not stop. His voice rose, and they stuck to the ground until I could not see them. When he turned to me, he said: Did you want to come to me? I said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: “That was not for you. These jinn came to listen to the Qur’an, then they returned to their people as warners. They asked me for provisions, so I provided them with bones and dung. So none of you should perfume himself with bones or dung.” Ikrimah said: They were twelve thousand from the island of Mosul. In another narration: “He set off with me, peace be upon him, until we came to the mosque which is by the wall of Awf. He drew a line for me, and a group of them came to him. Our companions said: They were like Zutt men and their faces were Makkawi. They said: Who are you? He said: I am the Prophet of God. They said: Who will testify to that for you? He said: This tree. What do you testify to?” It said: I testify that you are the Messenger of God. Then it returned as it came, dragging stones in its roots, rattling until it returned to what it was.” Then it was narrated: “When he, peace be upon him, finished, he placed his head on the lap of Ibn Masoud and slept, then he woke up and said: Do you have ablution? He said: No, except that I have with me a vessel containing wine. He said: Is it anything but dates and water, so perform ablution with it.” Third: We have already discussed water in Surah Al-Hijr and what is used for cleansing oneself in Surah Bara’ah, so there is no point in repeating it. Fourth: Scholars differed regarding the origin of the jinn. Ismail narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri: The jinn are the offspring of Satan, and mankind is the offspring of Adam. Among these are believers and disbelievers, and they share in reward and punishment. Whoever among these is a believer is a friend of God, and whoever among these is a disbeliever is a devil.
