Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The jinn are the offspring of the jinn and are not devils, and they believe. Among them are believers and disbelievers. The devils are the offspring of Satan and do not die except with Satan. They differed regarding the believing jinn entering Paradise, based on their origin. Those who claim that they are from the jinn and not from the offspring of Satan said: They enter Paradise by their faith. Those who say that they are from the offspring of Satan have two opinions: The first - which is the opinion of Al-Hasan - is that they will enter it. The second - which is the narration of Mujahid - is that they will not enter it even if they are turned away from the Fire. Al-Mawardi narrated it. In Surah Ar-Rahman, when God Almighty says: No man or jinn has touched them before them (al-Rahman 55:56), it is stated that they will enter it. Fifth - Al-Bayhaqi said in his narration: “And they asked him for provisions and they were from the jinn of the peninsula, so he said: ‘For you are all bones,’” which is evidence that they eat and are fed. A group of infidel doctors and philosophers denied the jinn and said: They are simple and their food is not permissible, daring and slandering God. The Qur’an and Sunnah refute them. There is nothing among the created beings that is simple, compound, and dual. Rather, the One is the One, glory be to Him, and everything else is compound, and there is nothing among the created beings that is disposed of in its state. It is not impossible that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw them in their forms as he sees the angels. Most of what we imagine them to be in the form of snakes is in Al-Muwatta’: “A man who had recently gotten married asked permission from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) at noon to return to his family... the hadith, and in it: And there was a huge snake curled up on the bed, so he threw his spear at it and strangled it.” And he mentioned the hadith. And in the Sahih, it is narrated that he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “These houses have inhabitants, so if you see one of them, then forbid it for three days. If it goes away, well and good, otherwise kill it, for he is a disbeliever.” And he said, Go and bury your companion. This meaning and the explanation of forbidding them have already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. Some people have said that this is specific to Madinah, based on the statement in the Sahih: In Madinah there are jinn who have become Muslims. This is a statement specific to it, so its ruling applies to it. We say: This indicates that other houses are like it, because the sanctity of Madinah was not mentioned as a reason, so that ruling would be specific to it. Rather, it was mentioned as a reason for Islam, and this is general and applies to other houses. Don’t you see his statement in the hadith, informing us about the jinn he encountered: And they were from the jinn of the Arabian Peninsula. This is clear and supported by his statement: And he forbade the inhabitants of the houses, and this is general. This has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah, so there is no point in repeating it. God the Almighty said: They said, ‘Indeed, we have heard a Qur’an of wondrous excellence.’ That is, in the eloquence of its speech. It was also said: Wonderful in the eloquence of its sermons. It was also said: Wonderful in the greatness of its blessings. It was also said: A mighty Qur’an, the like of which cannot be found. It was also said: They mean great.
72:2: The Almighty says, guides to the right path meaning to the right path in matters. It was also said: to knowing God, and guides is in the position of an attribute, meaning a guide. So we believed in it meaning we were guided by it and believed that it is from God. And we will not associate with our Lord anyone meaning we will not return to Satan nor will we obey him, because he is the one who sent them to bring him the report, then the jinn were pelted with meteors. It was also said that we will not take another god with God, because He is the One who is unique in Lordship. In this, the believers are amazed at the polytheists of Quraysh going beyond what the jinn had grasped by contemplating the Qur'an. The Almighty says, A group of jinn listened meaning they listened to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and they knew that what he vomited was the word of God. He did not mention the listeners because the situation indicates that. The group is a group. Al-Khalil said: between three and ten. Isa Al-Thaqafi read, guides to the right path with a fat-ha on the ra' and the shin.
72:3: The Almighty’s saying: And that He, the Most High, is the Lord of our Lord. Alqamah, Yahya, Al-A’mash, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, Ibn ‘Amir, Khalaf, Hafs, and As-Sulami used to put an in the accusative case throughout the Surah in twelve places, which are: And that He, the Most High, is the Lord of our Lord, “And that he used to say,” And we thought, “And that there were men,” And that they thought, “And that we touched the sky,” And that we used to sit, “And that we did not know,” And that among us are the righteous, “And that we thought that we would never cause failure to God on earth,” And when we heard the guidance, “And among us are the Muslims,” in apposition to His saying: That a group listened, “That he listened” can only be opened with a fat-ha, because it is in the position of an active participle was revealed and what follows it is in apposition to it. It was said: It is based on the ha’ in (We believed in him), meaning that (He, the Most High, is the grandfather of our Lord), and this is permissible, as it is an implied noun in the genitive case due to the abundance of the preposition with (an). It was said: The meaning is, we believe that he is the grandfather of our Lord. The rest read it all with kasra, which is correct, and Abu Ubaidah and Abu Hatim chose it in apposition to his statement, (They said, Indeed, we have heard because it is all from the speech of the jinn. As for Ja’far and Shaibah, they opened three places, which are in the statement of God Almighty: (And that He, the Most High, is the grandfather of our Lord), (And that he used to say), (And that there were men), they said: Because it is from the revelation, and they opened the rest because it is from the speech of the jinn. As for the statement of God Almighty, (And that when Abdullah stood up), they all opened it except Nafi’, Shaibah, Zar bin Hubaish, Abu Bakr, and al-Mufaddal from Asim, for they only opened it with kasra. There is no disagreement about opening the hamza in that a group of the jinn listened, “if they were upright,” and that the mosques are for God, and that they have conveyed. Likewise, there is no disagreement about breaking what comes after the word, such as the Almighty’s saying: They said, ‘Indeed, we have heard,’ and Say, ‘I only call upon my Lord’ (al-Jinn 72:20) and Say, ‘I do not know,’ and Say, ‘I do not control,’ (al-Jinn 72:21). Likewise, there is no disagreement about breaking what comes after the fa’ of the condition, such as the Almighty’s saying: For him is the fire of Hell (al-Jinn 72:23) and For he will walk before him because it is a place of beginning. God the Almighty said: And that He, the Most High, is the Lord of our Lord. In the language, Jadd means greatness and majesty. Anas said: When a man memorized Surah Al-Baqarah and Surah Al-Imran, he would become ‘Jadd’ in our eyes, meaning great and majestic. So the meaning of the Lord of our Lord is His greatness and majesty, as stated by Ikrimah, Mujahid, and Qatadah. From this, luck is called Jadd, and a man who is Jadd means lucky. In the hadith: And the wealth of one who is wealthy will not benefit from you. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Khalil said: meaning the wealthy, wealth from you, only obedience will benefit him. Ibn Abbas said: Your ability. Ad-Dahhak: His action. Al-Qurazi and Ad-Dahhak also said: His favors and blessings upon His creation. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Khafash said: His kingdom and authority. Al-Suddi said: His command. Saeed bin Jubair said: And that He, the Most High, is the grandfather of our Lord, meaning, Exalted is our Lord. It was said that they meant by that the grandfather who is the father of the father, and this is from the words of the jinn. Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Hussein and his son Ja’far Al-Sadiq and Al-Rabi’ said: God, the Most High, has no grandfather. The jinn only said it out of ignorance, so they were not held accountable for it. Al-Qushayri said: “It is permissible to use the word grandfather in reference to God, the Most High, because if it were not permissible, the Qur’an would not have mentioned it. However, it is an ambiguous word, so avoiding it is better.” Ikrimah’s reading jad is based on the letter jim: the opposite of joking. Abu Haywah and Muhammad bin Al-Samiq’ read it this way. It is also narrated from Ibn al-Sameeq and Abu al-Ashhab: (Jadd Rabbana) which means usefulness and benefit. Ikrimah also read (Jadd) with tanween Rabbana in the nominative case as if it is nominative, with (Ta’ala) and (Jadd) in the accusative case as a specification. Ikrimah also read (Jadd) with tanween and nominative case as (Rabbana) in the nominative case as if: Ta’ala, Jad, Jad, Rabbana, so the second Jad is a substitute for the first and was deleted and the complement to it was used in its place. The meaning of the verse: And that our Lord is too exalted to take a wife and a son to take comfort in them and to need them, and the Lord is exalted above rivals and equals.
72:4: God the Almighty said: And that our foolish one used to say an outrage against God. The ha' in (innahu) is for the command or the speech, and in (kana) it is its subject, and what follows it is the predicate. It is possible that (kana) is redundant. The foolish one here is Iblis according to Mujahid, Ibn Jurayj, and Qatadah. Abu Burdah bin Abi Musa narrated it on the authority of his father on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: The polytheists from the jinn. Qatadah said: The foolish one of the jinn disobeyed him just as the foolish one of mankind disobeyed him. Excessiveness and excess are: exaggeration in disbelief. Abu Malik said: It is injustice. Al-Kalbi said: It is lying. Its origin is distance, so it is used to express injustice because of its distance from justice, and to express lying because of its distance from truthfulness. The poet said: In any case, they ruled over you and went too far, and that is only when the trouble comes to you
72:5: God the Almighty says: And we thought meaning we thought that mankind and the jinn would never tell a lie about God so we believed them in that God has a wife and a son, until we heard the Quran and saw the truth through it. Ya'qub, Al-Jahdary and Ibn Ishaq read that you would never tell. It was said: The mention of the jinn was cut off here so God the Almighty said: And that there were men among mankind so whoever opens it and makes it from the saying of the jinn returns it to the saying of the jinn returns it to His saying: (that he listened), and whoever breaks it makes it the subject of the saying of God the Almighty. What is meant by it is what a man used to do when he went down to a valley, he would say: I seek refuge in the master of this valley from the evil of the foolish people of his people, so he would spend the night in his neighborhood until morning, as Al-Hasan, Ibn Zayd and others said. Muqatil said: The first to seek refuge with the jinn were a group of people from Yemen, then from the Hanifa, then it spread among the Arabs, but when Islam came, they sought refuge with God and abandoned them.
72:6: And Kurdam bin Abi Al-Saib said: I went out with my father to Madinah as soon as the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) mentioned it. He took us to a shepherd to spend the night. When it was midnight, a wolf came and carried off a lamb from the sheep. The shepherd said: O Aamer of the valley, I am your neighbor. Then a crier called: O Sarhan, release him. The lamb came running. God the Almighty revealed to His Messenger in Makkah: And that there were men among mankind who sought refuge with men among the jinn, but they increased them in burden. That is, the jinn increased mankind in burden, meaning sin and guilt, as said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatadah. In Arabic, rahq means sin and incest, and a man is rahq if he is like that. From this is the saying of God the Almighty: And humiliation will overwhelm them. (Yunus 10:27) Al-A’sha said: Nothing benefits me without seeing her. Will my pain be cured unless it is afflicted with exhaustion? Meaning a sin. The increase was attributed to the jinn since they were the cause of it. Mujahid also said: (So they increased them) meaning that mankind increased the jinn in transgression with this seeking of refuge, until the jinn said: We are the masters of mankind and the jinn. Qatadah also said, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Al-Rabi’ and Ibn Zayd: This increased mankind’s fear and dread of the jinn. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: Disbelief. And there is no denial that seeking refuge with the jinn rather than with God is disbelief and polytheism. It was said: The word men is not used to refer to the jinn, so the meaning is: There were men from among mankind who sought refuge from the evil of the jinn with men from among mankind. A man from among mankind would say, for example: I seek refuge with Hudhayfah ibn Badr from the jinn of this valley. Al-Qushayri said: This is arbitrary, since it is not far-fetched to use the word men to refer to the jinn.
72:7: God the Almighty says: And that they thought, just as you thought, that God would not resurrect anyone. This is from God's statement to mankind, meaning that the jinn thought that God would not resurrect the creation as you thought. Al-Kalbi: The meaning is: The jinn thought, just as mankind thought, that God would not send a messenger to His creation to establish proof against them. And every confirmation of the proof against Quraysh, meaning that if these jinn believe in Muhammad, then you are more deserving of that.
72:8: The Almighty said: And We touched the heaven This is from the words of the jinn, meaning we sought report of it as is our custom, and found it "filled with stern guards" meaning guardians, meaning the angels. Guards is the plural of guard, "and meteors" is the plural of meteor, and it is the swooping of the stars that burn them from eavesdropping. This has been discussed in Surat Al-Hijr and Surat As-Saffat. The verb "was found can be transitive with two objects, the first being the ha and the alif, and was filled" is in the position of the second object. It can also be transitive with one object, and "was filled is in the position of a state with the omission of qad". The verb "guards is in the accusative case as a direct object with was filled". The verb "severe" is an adjective describing guards, meaning it was filled with stern angels. And the word harsh is used in the sense of harass, which is as it is said: The righteous predecessors meaning the righteous. The plural of salaf is aslaf and the plural of hars is ahras. He said: I passed the guards and the horrors of the group It is possible that guard is a verbal noun meaning I guarded with great guarding.
72:9: God the Almighty said: "And we used to sit therein in stations to listen. But whoever listens now will find a burning star lying in wait for him." (From there) means from the sky, and (stations) are places one sits in to listen to report from the sky, meaning that the rebellious jinn used to do that to listen to report from the sky from the angels so that they could deliver it to the priests, as was explained above. So God the Almighty guarded it when He sent His Messenger with burning meteors. So the jinn said at that time: But whoever listens now will find a burning star lying in wait for him. Meaning by the meteor: the burning planet, and this was explained above. It is said that the falling of the planets did not occur until after the mission of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and it is one of his signs. The early generations differed as to whether the devils used to throw stones before the mission, or was that something that happened after the mission of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him)? Al-Kalbi and some people said: The heavens were not guarded during the period between Jesus and Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon them both: five hundred years, but rather it was for the sake of the mission of the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. Then when Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, was sent, they were prevented from all the heavens, and they were guarded by angels and meteors. I said: It was narrated by Atiyah Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and Al-Bayhaqi mentioned it. Abdullah bin Amr said: When the day came in which the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was given prophecy, the devils were prevented and were pelted with meteors. Abdul Malik bin Sabur said: The sky was not guarded during the period between Jesus and Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon them both). When Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was sent, the sky was guarded, and the devils were pelted with meteors, and they were prevented from approaching the sky. Nafi’ bin Jubayr said: During the period, the devils could hear but were not pelted, but when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was sent, they were pelted with meteors. A similar narration was narrated by Ubayy bin Ka’b, who said: No star was pelted from the time Jesus was taken up until the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was given prophecy and was pelted with it. It was said: That was before the mission, but it increased with the mission of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) as a warning of his condition, and this is the meaning of the Almighty’s saying: (filled), meaning its guards were increased. Aws bin Hajar, who was pre-Islamic, said: Then he pounced like a lion, followed by a storm that would make you think it was a ton of rain. This is the opinion of the majority. Al-Jahiz rejected this verse and said: Every poem narrated about it is fabricated, and that the shooting did not occur before the mission. The opinion about the shooting is more correct, because God Almighty said: So we found it filled with stern guards and meteors. This is a report about the jinn, that the guards of the sky were increased until it was filled with them and with them. And when it was narrated from Ibn Abbas, he said: "While the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was sitting with a group of his companions, a star was thrown at him. He said, 'What did you use to say about such a thing during the Age of Ignorance?' They said, 'We used to say, 'A great person dies or a great person is born.' The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, 'It is not thrown for the death or life of anyone, but when our Lord, glory be to Him, decrees a matter in the heaven, the bearers of the Throne glorify God, then the inhabitants of every heaven glorify God, until the glorification reaches this heaven. The inhabitants of the heaven ask the bearers of the Throne what your Lord has said, and they inform them, and the inhabitants of every heaven inform them, until the report reaches this heaven. Then the jinn are snatched away and they throw stones. Whatever they bring is true, but they add to it.'" This indicates that stoning was practiced before the Prophet's mission. Al-Zuhri narrated something similar on the authority of Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib on the authority of Ibn Abbas. At the end of it, al-Zuhri was asked, 'Was stoning practiced during the Age of Ignorance?' He said, 'Yes.'" I said: What do you think of His statement, the Most High: {And we used to sit therein in stations to listen. But whoever listens now will find a flaming fire lying in wait for him?} He said: It became more severe and intensified when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was sent. Al-Qutbi said something similar. Ibn Qutaybah said: It was, but the guarding intensified after the mission. Before that, they used to seek eavesdropping and throwing stones at people in some circumstances, but when Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was sent, that was completely prohibited. This was explained previously in Surah As-Saffat when He said: {And they are pelted from every side, driven away, and for them is a lasting punishment.} (al-Saffat 37:9) Al-Hafiz said: If someone were to say: How can the jinn be exposed to burning themselves because of hearing report, after it has become known to them? The answer is: God, the Most High, makes them forget that until the ordeal becomes great, just as Satan forgets at all times that he will not submit, and that God, the Most High, said to him: {And indeed, upon you is the curse until the Day of Judgment.} (al-Hijr 15:35) And were it not for this, the obligation would not have been fulfilled. And the watch: it was said from the angels, meaning and a watch from the angels. And the watch: the guardian of something and the plural is watches, and in other places it is permissible for it to be a plural like guards, and the singular: watcher. And it was said: the watch is the meteor, meaning a meteor that has been watched for it, to be stoned with it, so it is a verb with the meaning of a passive participle like hitting and shaking.
72:10: The Almighty said, We do not know whether evil is intended for those on the earth meaning these guards who guarded the heavens or whether their Lord intends for them right guidance meaning good. Ibn Zayd said: Iblis said, We do not know whether God intended by this prevention to send a punishment upon the people of the earth or to send a messenger to them. It was also said that it was from what the jinn said among themselves before they heard the recitation of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). That is, we do not know whether evil is intended for those on the earth by sending Muhammad to them, for they will deny him and perish because of his denial, just as others among the nations who denied him perished. Or whether He intended for them to be guided. Evil and right guidance, according to this, are disbelief and belief. Based on this, they had knowledge of the mission of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and when they heard his recitation, they knew that they were prevented from the heavens as a guard for the revelation. It was said: No, rather this is what their people said after they turned to them as vows, meaning when they believed, they feared that many of the people of the earth would not believe, so they said: We do not know whether the people of the earth will disbelieve in what we believe in or believe?
72:11: The Almighty said: And among us are the righteous and among us are less than that. This is from the words of the jinn, meaning some of them said to each other when they called their companions to believe in Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, And before listening to the Quran, among us were the righteous and among us were the disbelievers. It was said: And among us are less than that, meaning less than the righteous in righteousness, and this is more similar to interpreting it as belief and polytheism. We were different ways, meaning different groups, as al-Suddi said. Ad-Dahhak: different religions. Qatadah: divergent desires, and from this is the saying of the poet: The Constrictor, the Expander, the Guide by His obedience in the trial of people, when their desires are severe Meaning: Not all the jinn were disbelievers, rather they were different: some were disbelievers, some were righteous believers, and some were believers who were not righteous. Al-Musayyab said: We were Muslims, Jews, Christians, and Zoroastrians. Al-Suddi said about the verse {different ways}: Among the jinn are those like you, Qadariyyah, Murji’ah, Khawarij, Rafidah, Shi’ah, and Sunnis. Some people said: That is, after listening to the Qur’an, we are different: some of us are believers and some of us are disbelievers, that is, some of us are righteous, and some of us are believers who did not reach the peak of righteousness. The first is better because there were some among the jinn who believed in Moses and Jesus, and God has informed us that they said: {Indeed, we have heard a Book revealed after Moses, confirming what was before it} (Al-Ahqaf 25:30). This indicates that some of them believed in the Torah, and this was an exaggeration from them in calling those they called to faith. Also, there is no point in their saying: We are now divided into believers and disbelievers. Methods: the plural of method, which is a man’s school of thought, meaning we were different groups. It is said: a people have methods, meaning they follow different schools of thought. And qaddad: a type of method, which is an emphasis on it, its singular is qaddah. It is said: for every path qaddah, and its origin is from qad as-siyur, which means to cut it. Labid said, mourning his brother Arbad: The eye did not reach its full capacity on the night when the horses were like thorns. Another said: And I said, and Zaid was bareheaded, on the day when Amr’s horses turned away Al-Qad with a kasra: a strap made of untanned leather. It is said: it has neither a qad nor a qahf. Al-Qad: a vessel made of leather, and qahf: made of wood.
72:12: The Almighty’s saying: And we thought that we would never escape God on earth. The word thought here means knowledge and certainty, which is the opposite of the word thought in the Almighty’s saying: And we thought that you would never say (al-Jinn 72:5), and that they thought (al-Jinn 72:7), meaning we knew through deduction and contemplated the signs of God: We are in His grasp and power, we will not escape Him by fleeing or anything else. Fleeing is a verbal noun in the place of a circumstantial noun, meaning fleeing.
72:13: The Almighty said: And when we heard the guidance meaning the Qur'an we believed in it and in God, and we believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his message. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent to mankind and the jinn. Al-Hasan said: God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to mankind and the jinn, and He never sent a messenger from the jinn, nor from the people of the desert, nor from women. This is due to the Almighty's saying: And We did not send before you, [O Muhammad], except men to whom We revealed, from the people of the towns. (Yusuf 12:109) This meaning has already been mentioned. And in the Sahih: And I have been sent to the red and the black, meaning mankind and the jinn. So whoever believes in his Lord will not fear loss or oppression. Ibn Abbas said: He will not fear that his good deeds will be diminished or his bad deeds will be increased, because loss means decrease, and oppression means aggression and committing sins. Al-A’sha said: Nothing benefits me without seeing her. Will my pain be cured unless it is afflicted with exhaustion? Al-Wāmiq: The lover. He loved him, he loved him, so he is Wāmiq. This is a saying that God the Almighty related about the jinn, due to the strength of their faith and the soundness of their Islam. The common reading is (fa la yakhāf) in the nominative case, assuming that he does not fear. Al-A’mash, Yahya, and Ibrahim read (fa layakhf) in the subjunctive mood as a response to the condition and the cancellation of the fa’.
72:14: The Almighty said: And among us are Muslims and among us are the unjust. That is, after listening to the Qur'an, we differ. Some of us have become Muslims and some of us have disbelieved. Al-Qasit is the unjust, because he has cursed the truth. Al-Muqsit is the just, because he is just to the truth. It is said: Qasta, meaning he was unjust, and Aqsat means if he is just. The poet said: They are the people who killed Ibn Hind by force, Amras, and they oppressed Al-Nu'man God Almighty says: And whoever submits - those have sought the right path. That is, they have sought the path of truth and followed it, including seeking the direction of the Qiblah.
72:15: The Almighty says: But as for the unjust, meaning those who deviate from the path of truth and faith, they will be fuel for Hellfire, meaning fuel. And His statement, they will be, means in the knowledge of God Almighty.
72:16: The Almighty’s saying: And if they were to remain steadfast upon the way This is from the saying of God the Most High. That is, if these disbelievers had believed, We would have provided them with plenty in this world and expanded their provision. This is interpreted as revelation, that is, it was revealed to me that if they were to remain steadfast. Ibn Bahr said: Everything in this surah that has a broken, heavy in is a narration of the words of the jinn who listened to the Qur’an, so they returned to their people as warners. Everything in it that has a fatha, light an is a revelation to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn al-Anbari said: Whoever breaks the letters and opens and if they were to remain steadfast implies a complete oath, the interpretation of which is: By God, if they were to remain steadfast upon the way, just as one says in speech: By God, if I stand, I will stand, and by God, if I stand, I will stand. The poet said: By God, if you were free, you would not be free, nor would you be a free man. Whoever opens the letter before the lightened letter, he arranges it - I mean the light one - on (It was revealed to me that), (and that if they were to be steadfast) or on (we believed in it) and that if they were to be steadfast. It is permissible for whoever breaks all the letters to the lightened (that), to connect the lightened letter to (It was revealed to me) or to (we believed in it), and he dispenses with the oath oath. The general reading is with the kasra of the waw of (law) due to the meeting of two quiescent letters. Ibn Waththab and Al-A’mash read with the damma of the waw. And abundant water means abundant, and the rain had been withheld from them for seven years. It is said: the eye ghadqat taghdagh, so it is ghadqa, if its water is abundant. It was said: What is meant is all of creation, meaning if they were to be steadfast on the path, the path of truth, faith and guidance and were believers and obedient. We would have given them abundant water, meaning abundant.
72:17: The Almighty says, To test them therein meaning, to test their gratitude for those blessings. Omar said about this verse: Wherever there is water, there is wealth, and wherever there is wealth, there is temptation. The meaning of We would have given them drink is to provide them with plenty in this world. Abundant water is an example of this, because all goodness and provision come from rain, so it was used in its place, like the Almighty's saying: And if only the people of the cities had believed and feared God, We would have opened upon them blessings from the heaven and the earth (al-A’raf 7:96) and His saying: And if only they had established the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to them from their Lord, they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet (al-Ma’idah 5:66) meaning from rain. And God knows best. Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab, Ata` ibn Abi Rabah, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, Muqatil, Atiyyah, Ubaid ibn `Umair and al-Hasan said: By God, the Companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) were obedient and listening. Then the treasures of Chosroes, Caesar, Muqawqis and Negus were opened to them, and they were tempted by them. They attacked their leader and killed him, meaning `Uthman ibn `Affan. Al-Kalbi and others said: And if they had remained steadfast in the path of disbelief that they were upon, and they were all disbelievers, We would have expanded their provisions as a deception and lure them, until they were tempted by them, so We would have punished them with them in this world and the Hereafter. This is a statement made by al-Rabi` ibn Anas, Zayd ibn Asl and his son, al-Kalbi, al-Thamali, Yaman ibn Ri`ab, Ibn Kaysan and Abu Majlaz. They based their evidence on the verse: But when they forgot that by which they had been reminded, We opened to them the gates of every [good] thing (al-An`am 6:44). And the Almighty said: And had it not been that mankind would have become one community, We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful roofs of silver for their houses (al-Zukhruf 43:33), and the first is more likely, because the method is defined by the definite article, so it is more obligatory that his method be the method of guidance, and because righteousness can only be with guidance. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What I fear most for you is what God brings forth for you from the flowers of this world. They said: And what are the flowers of this world? He said: The blessings of the earth... And he mentioned the hadith. And he, peace be upon him, said: “By God, I do not fear poverty for you. Rather, I fear that the world will be made easy for you as it was made easy for those before you, and you will compete for it as they competed for it, and it will destroy you as it destroyed them.” God the Almighty said: {And whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord} meaning the Qur’an, as stated by Ibn Zayd. There are two interpretations regarding his turning away from it: One is about acceptance, if it is said that it is for the disbelievers. The second is about action, if it is said that it is for the believers. It was said: (And whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord) meaning does not thank Him for His blessings, He will lead him into a grievous punishment. The Kufians and Ayyash from Abu Amr read (yuslikuhu) with a ya’, and Abu Ubaidi and Abu Hatim preferred it, because the name of God was mentioned first, so he said: (And whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord) the rest of them (will lead him) with a noon. It was narrated from Muslim ibn Jundub with a damma on the noon and a kasra on the lam. Talhah and Al-A’raj read it this way, and they are two dialects. Salkahu and Aslahu mean the same, meaning We will make him enter. A grievous punishment meaning a very difficult one. Ibn Abbas said: It is a mountain in Hell. Al-Khudri said: Whenever they put their hands on it, it melts. Ibn Abbas said: The meaning is difficulty from the punishment. It is known in the language that ascension means hardship. You say: The matter ascends me: if it is difficult for you. From this is the saying of Omar: Nothing ascends me as the marriage sermon ascends me, meaning it is not difficult for me. And torment ascended means severe. Ascension is the source of ascension. It is said: He ascended ascending and ascending. So it is used to describe torment because the tormented one ascends, meaning it rises above him and overcomes him so that he cannot bear it. Abu Ubaidah said: Ascension is a source, meaning torment that has ascension, and walking in ascension is difficult. And ascension is the difficult obstacle. And Ikrimah said: It is A smooth rock in Hell that one is commanded to climb. When one reaches the top, he is forced to descend into Hell. Al-Kalbi said: Al-Walid ibn al-Mughira is commanded to climb a mountain in Hell made of smooth rock. He is pulled by those in front of him with chains and hit by whips from behind him until he reaches the top. He does not reach the top in forty years. When he reaches the top, he is forced to descend to the bottom. Then he is commanded to climb it again. This is his habit forever, and it is the saying of God Almighty: I will surely burden him with a mighty climb (al-Muddaththir 74:17).
72:18: God Almighty says: And the mosques are for God, so do not invoke anyone with God. There are six issues: First - The Almighty’s saying: And that the mosques are for God an with the fat-ha. It was said: It refers back to the Almighty’s saying: “Say: It has been revealed to me” meaning: Say: It has been revealed to me that the mosques are for God. Al-Khalil said: Meaning, because the mosques are for God. What is meant is the houses that the people of different religions build for worship. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: The jinn said: How can we come to the mosques and witness the prayer with you while we are far away from you? So the verse: And that the mosques are for God was revealed, meaning they were built for the remembrance of God and His obedience. Al-Hasan said: What is meant by it is all places, because the entire earth is a mosque for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He says: (Wherever you are, pray, for wherever you pray is a mosque. In Sahih Muslim: (And the earth has been made for me a place of prostration and purification). Saeed ibn al-Musayyab and Talq ibn Habib said: What is meant by mosques are the limbs on which the servant prostrates, which are the feet, knees, hands, and face. He says: These limbs God has bestowed upon you, so do not prostrate on them and do not humiliate them to anyone other than their Creator.” In Sahih Muslim: “On the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “I was commanded to prostrate on seven bones: the forehead” - and he pointed to his nose - the hands, the knees, and the tips of the feet. Al-Abbas said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When the servant prostrates, seven limbs prostrate with him. It was said: The mosques are the prayers, meaning that prostration is for God. Al-Hasan also said this. If you consider the mosques to be places, then the singular is masjid with a kasra on the jim, and it is also said with a fatha, as narrated by al-Farra’. If you make them limbs, then the singular is masjid mosque, with a fatha on the jim. It has also been said that it is the plural of masjid, which is prostration. It is also said: I prostrated myself in prostration and in masjid, just as you say: I struck the ground with a darban strike and a mudarban strike with a fatha, meaning I walked in search of a livelihood. Ibn Abbas said: The mosques here are Mecca, which is the Qiblah, and Mecca was called mosques because everyone prostrates towards it. The first statement is the most evident of these statements, God willing, and it is narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God have mercy on him. Second: The Almighty’s saying: To God is an addition of honor and respect. Then He specifically mentioned the Ancient House, saying: And purify My House (al-Hajj 22:26). And he, peace be upon him, said: A prayer in this mosque of mine is better than a thousand prayers in any other mosque, except the Sacred Mosque. Ibn al-Arabi said: It has been narrated through an acceptable chain of transmission that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: (One prayer in this mosque of mine is better than a thousand prayers in any other mosque, except the Sacred Mosque, for one prayer in it is better than a hundred prayers in this mosque of mine.) If this were true, it would be a clear text. I said: It is correct to transmit justice from justice according to what we explained in Surah Ibrahim. Third: Although mosques belong to God in terms of ownership and honor, they may be attributed to someone else as a definite noun, so it may be said: the mosque of so-and-so. In the authentic hadith: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, raced horses that had been trained from Al-Hafiya and continued them to Thaniyat Al-Wada’. He also raced horses that had not been trained from Al-Thaniyyah to the mosque of Banu Zuraiq.” This addition is by virtue of the locality, as if it were in their qibla, or it may be by way of their being endowed. There is no disagreement among the ummah regarding the endowment of mosques, bridges, and graveyards, although they differed regarding the endowment of other things. Fourth: Although mosques are for God and only God is mentioned in them, it is permissible to divide wealth in them. It is permissible to give charity in them as a share between the poor and everyone who comes to eat. It is permissible to imprison a debtor in them, chain up a prisoner, sleep in them, house the sick in them, open the door to a neighbor, and recite poetry in them if it is free of falsehood. All of this has been explained in Surah Bara’ah, Surah An-Nur, and others. Fifth - The Almighty’s saying, So do not invoke anyone with God. This is a rebuke to the polytheists for their supplication to God other than Him in the Sacred Mosque. Mujahid said: When the Jews and Christians entered their churches and synagogues, they associated others with God. So God commanded His Prophet and the believers to make their supplication sincere to God when they entered all the mosques. He said: So do not associate therein any idol or anything else that is worshipped. It was also said that the meaning is: Set apart the mosques for the remembrance of God, and do not take them as a place of mockery, trade, gatherings, or roads, and do not assign any share in them to anyone other than God. In the Sahih: (Whoever seeks something lost in the mosque, say, May God not return it to you, for mosques were not built for this purpose.” And sufficient rulings on mosques have been mentioned in Surat An-Nur, and praise be to God. Sixth: Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: When he entered the mosque, he would put his right foot forward and say, The mosques are for God, so do not invoke anyone with God. “O God, I am Your servant and Your visitor, and every visitor has a right over him, and You are the best to whom one may visit, so I ask You by Your mercy to free my neck from the Fire.” When he left the mosque, he would put his left foot forward and say, “O God, pour goodness upon me abundantly and do not take away from me the good things which You have given me ever. Do not make my livelihood a struggle, and grant me on earth means” meaning wealth.
72:19: The Almighty said: And when the servant of God stood up to call upon Him The fat-ha is permissible, meaning God revealed to him that. The kasra is permissible as a new sentence. The servant of God here refers to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, when he was praying in Batn Nakhl and reciting the Quran, as mentioned at the beginning of the surah. Calling upon Him means worshipping Him. Ibn Jurayj said: Calling Him means he stood up to them, calling to God Almighty. They were about to flock to him in droves Az-Zubayr ibn Al-Awwam said: They are the jinn when they listened to the Quran. It was also said: They were about to ride it out of eagerness, as Ad-Dahhat said. Ibn Abbas said: Desiring to hear the remembrance. Bard narrated on the authority of Makhul: The jinn pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, on this night, and they were seventy thousand, and they finished pledging allegiance to him at the break of dawn. Ibn Abbas also said: This is from the words of the jinn when they returned to their people and informed them of what they had seen of the obedience of the Prophet's companions, peace and blessings be upon him, and their following him in bowing and prostrating. It was said: The meaning is that the polytheists almost rode each other, out of spite for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Ibn Zayd said: It means, When the servant of God Muhammad stood up with the call, mankind and jinn gathered around this matter to extinguish it, but God refused except to support him and complete his light. Al-Tabari chose the meaning to be: The Arabs almost gathered around the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and conspired to extinguish the light that he brought. Mujahid said: His statement (labdan) means groups, and it is from the verb talabad to gather something on something, meaning to gather, and from it comes the word labd which is spread out due to the accumulation of its wool, and everything that you stick tightly together, you have stuck it together, and the plural of labdah is labd like qirbah and qirbah. The hair on the back of a lion is called labdah and its plural is labd. Zuhair said: The lion has a weapon, a sling, and his claws are not trimmed. A large number of locusts are called: Labd. There are four languages and readings for it: Fatha on the Ba and Kasra on the Lam, which is the reading of the common people. Damma on the Lam and Fatha on the Ba, which is the reading of Mujahid ibn Muhaisin and Hisham from the people of Ash-Sham, the singular of which is Labdah. With Damma on the Lam and the Ba, which is the reading of Abu Haywah, Muhammad ibn al-Samiqi’, Abu al-Ashhab al-Uqayli and al-Jahdary as well, the singular of which is Labd, like Raqi’ and Ruka’, and Sajid and Sujud. It is said: Labd with Damma on the Lam and Fatha on the Ba is something permanent, and from it Luqman’s eagle was called Labd for its permanence and permanence. Al-Nabigha said: He who has been unfair to Labed has been unfair to her Al-Qushayri: It was read (labda) with a damma on the lam and the ba, and it is the plural of labid, which is the small jawlaq. In As-Sahah: And the Almighty’s saying I have destroyed wealth in abundance (Labadan: 6) meaning gathered. It is also said: People are labd, meaning gathered together, and labd is also the one who does not travel or leave his home. The poet said: From a generous man who still has a lot of money that tires the body of the poor And he narrates: Al-Labad. Abu Ubaid said: It is more similar. Peas: good opinion. Someone is a pea-bearer: if he is one of those who undertake important matters. The poet said: If I occupy people's private parts, the paths are wide open. I rise with peas. Labd: The last of Luqman’s eagles. It is declined because it is not modified. The Arabs claim that Luqman was the one whom the ‘Ad tribe sent in their delegation to the Sacred Sanctuary to pray for rain. When they were killed, Luqman was given the choice between leaving seven brown antelopes on a rugged mountain, untouched by rain, or leaving seven eagles so that every time one eagle died, another would follow. He chose the eagles. The last eagle was called Labd, and poets mentioned it. Al-Nabigha said: It became empty and its people carried my sister who had betrayed me. Al-Lubaid: a small bag. It is said: I packed the water skin and put it in Labid’s bag. Labid: is the name of a poet from Banu Amir.
72:20: The Almighty said: Say, ‘I only call upon my Lord’ meaning the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I only call upon my Lord “and I do not associate anyone with Him.” This is how most of the reciters read said as a statement. Hamzah and Asim read Say as a command. The reason for its revelation was that the infidels of Quraysh said to him: You have come with a grave matter and you have been hostile to all of the people, so turn away from this and we will protect you. So it was revealed. The Almighty said: Say, ‘I do not possess for you any harm or any benefit.’
72:21: The Almighty said: Say, ‘Indeed, I have no power to cause you harm or to bring you any good.’ That is, I am not able to ward off harm from you, nor bring you any good. It was also said: I have no power to cause you harm, that is, disbelief, nor to bring you any good, that is, guidance, that is, I am only responsible for conveying the message. It was also said: Damage means torment, and guidance means bliss. It is the same as the first. It was also said: Harm means death, and guidance means life.
72:22: The Almighty said: Say, ‘No one can protect me from God.’ That is, no one can avert His punishment from me if I ask him to protect me. This is because they said, Leave what you are calling to and we will protect you. Abu al-Jawza’ narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud who said: I set out with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the night of the jinn until they reached Al-Hujun. He drew a line against me, then he advanced towards them and they crowded around him. Their chief, whose name was Wardan, said: I will drive them away from you. He said: No one can protect me from God. Al-Mawardi mentioned this. He said: It has two possible meanings. One is that no one will protect me while God protects me. The second is that no one will protect me from what God has decreed for me. And I will not find besides Him a refuge, meaning a place of refuge in Him, as Qatada said. And from him: a supporter and a protector. Al-Suddi: a talisman. Al-Kalbi: an entrance into the earth like a gorge. It was also said: a protector but not a protector. It was also said: a way of life but not a path. Ibn Shajarah narrated it and the meaning is the same, and from it is the saying of the poet: Oh, the anguish of my soul and the anguish that is useless to me, and there is no escape from God’s decree
72:23: The Almighty's statement, Except for a message from God and His messages, for in it is safety and salvation, as stated by Al-Hasan. Qatada said, Except for a message from God, so that is what I possess by God's grace, as for disbelief and faith, I do not possess them. Based on this, it is referred back to the statement of God, the Almighty, Say, 'Indeed, I have no power over you to harm or to bring you to righteousness,' meaning, I have no power over you except that I convey to you. It was said that it is an isolated exception from His statement, I have no power over you to harm or to bring you to righteousness, meaning, except that I convey to you, i.e., I convey to you what I was sent with, as stated by Al-Farra'. Al-Zajjaj said, It is in the accusative case as a substitute for His statement, (Asking for refuge), meaning, And I will not find any refuge besides Him," except that I convey what comes to me from God and His messages, i.e., from His messages that He commanded me to convey. Or, unless I convey from God and act according to His message, so I hold myself accountable for what I command others to do. It was said that it is a source, and la means lam, and in is for the condition. The meaning is that I will not find a refuge other than Him: that is, if I do not convey the messages of my Lord fully. God the Almighty said: "And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger" in monotheism and worship. "For him is the fire of Hell. The word in was broken because what comes after the fa" of the condition is a place of beginning, and it has been mentioned before. "Abiding therein forever" is in the accusative case as a state. The word "abiding therein" is plural because the meaning is for everyone who does that. So it was made singular first because of the word "whoever" then the state was plural. The word "abiding therein" is plural because the meaning is for everyone who does that. So it was made singular first because of the word "whoever" then the meaning was plural. His statement "forever" is evidence that disobedience here is polytheism. It was said that it refers to sins other than polytheism, and the meaning of "abiding therein forever" is unless I forgive or intercession reaches them, inevitably if they depart from this world in faith, then forgiveness reaches them. This meaning has been explained previously in Surah An-Nisa and elsewhere.
72:24: The Almighty says, Until, when they see what they are promised. “Until” here is the subject, meaning, Until, when they see what they are promised of the torment of the Hereafter, or what they are promised of the torment of this world, which is the killing at Badr. Then they will know then who is weaker in helpers - them or the believers. And fewer in number is conjoined.
72:25: The Almighty said: Say, 'I do not know whether that which you are promised is near.' Meaning the establishment of the Hour. It was also said: The torment of this world, meaning I do not know. So (in) means (what) or (no), meaning no one knows the time of the torment and the establishment of the Hour except God, so it is unseen and I do not know of it except what God knows. And (what) in His statement: (what they are promised): it is permissible for it to be with the verb as a verbal noun, or it is permissible for it to mean that which estimates the pronoun. Or will my Lord grant him a term? meaning an end and a deadline. The general public read it with a sukoon on the ya’ of rabbi, and the two imams and Abu Amr read it with a fatha.
72:26: The Almighty’s saying: He knows the unseen, and He reveals His secret to no one. There are two issues in this: First: The Almighty’s saying: Knower of the unseen. “Knower” is a nominative attribute of His saying: My Lord. It was said: That is, He is Knower of the unseen, and the unseen is that which is hidden from the servants. This was explained at the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah 2:And He does not disclose His unseen to anyone, for He discloses to whomever He wills of His unseen, because the messengers are supported by miracles, including informing about some of the unseen. In the revelation: And I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses. (Al Imran 3:49)
72:27: The Almighty said: Except whomever He chooses of messengers. Ibn Jubayr said: Except whomever He chooses of messengers refers to Gabriel, peace be upon him. This is far-fetched, but the meaning should be: He does not reveal His secrets to anyone except whomever He chooses of prophethood, for He informs him of whatever He wills of His secrets, so that this would indicate his prophethood. Second: The scholars, may God have mercy on them, said: When God, the Almighty, praised Himself for knowledge of the unseen and kept it to Himself without His creation, this was evidence that no one knows the unseen except Him. Then He excepted the messengers He chose, so He entrusted them with whatever He wished of His unseen through revelation to them, and made it a miracle for them and a true proof of their prophethood. The astrologer and those who imitate him, who throw pebbles, look into books, and frighten birds, are not among the messengers He chose, informing them of whatever they wish of His unseen. Rather, they are disbelievers, slandered by their intuition, guesswork, and lies. One of the scholars said: I wonder what the astrologer would say about a ship in which a thousand people of different circumstances and ranks boarded, among them the king and the commoner, the learned and the ignorant, the rich and the poor, the old and the young, with their different ascendants, births, and star degrees, yet the judgment of drowning encompassed them all in one hour? If the astrologer, may God curse him, says: It was only the horoscope they were riding that drowned them, then according to that, this horoscope nullified the rulings of all those horoscopes, with their differences, at the time of the birth of each one of them, and what his particular horoscope required of him. So there is no guide at all in the work of births, nor is there any indication in them of the wretched or the blessed. And nothing remains except to defy the Noble Qur’an. And in it is making his blood permissible based on this astrology. And the poet did well when he said: The astrologer ruled that my birth horoscope predicts that I will die by drowning. Tell the dreamer, in the morning of the flood, was everyone born on the planet of drowning? It was said to the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him, when he wanted to meet the Khawarij: Will you meet them while the moon is in Scorpio? He may God be pleased with him replied: Then where is their moon? And that was at the end of the month. Look at this statement with which he answered, and how it exaggerates in refuting those who believe in astrology, and how it silences every ignorant person who investigates the laws of the stars. Musafir ibn Awf said to him: O Commander of the Faithful! Do not set out at this hour, but set out during the last three hours of the day. Ali may God be pleased with him said: Why? He said: “If you set out at this hour, you and your companions will be afflicted with a severe calamity and harm, but if you set out at the hour I have commanded you, you will be victorious and prevail and obtain what you sought.” Ali may God be pleased with him said: “Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had no astrologer, nor will we after him” - in a long speech in which he cited verses from the Quran - “Whoever believes you in this statement, I do not feel safe from him being like one who has taken a rival or an opponent besides God. O God, there is no omen except Your omen, and no good except Your good.” Then he said to the speaker: We deny you and oppose you and we will travel at the time you forbade us from. Then he turned to the people and said: O people, beware of learning the stars except for what guides you in the darkness of the land and the sea. The astrologer is like a magician, and the magician is like an unbeliever, and the unbeliever will be in the Fire. By God, if I hear that you look at the stars and act upon them, I will imprison you for as long as I live, and I will deprive you of my stipend. I have no power over you. Then he traveled at the time you forbade him from, and he met the people and killed them. This was the Battle of Nahrawan, which is proven in the Sahih of Muslim. Then he said: If we had traveled at the time you commanded us and were victorious and triumphant, someone would have said, ‘We traveled at the time the astrologer commanded. Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would not have had an astrologer, nor would we have anyone after him. God opened for us the lands of Chosroes and Caesar and all the lands.’ Then he said: O people! Put your trust in God and have faith in Him, for He is sufficient against anyone other than Him. Then He will make guards march before him and behind him meaning angels guarding him so that no devil can approach him, thus protecting the revelation from the eavesdropping of devils and from being thrown to soothsayers. Ad-Dahhak said: God never sent a prophet except that he had with him angels guarding him from the devils so that they would not take the form of an angel. So if a devil comes to him in the form of an angel, they say: This is a devil, so beware of him. And if an angel comes to him, they say: This is the messenger of your Lord. Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd said: Watchers means guardians who guard the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from in front of him and behind him from the jinn and devils. Qatadah and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: They are four guardian angels. Al-Farra' said: What is meant is Gabriel. When he would bring the message, angels would descend with him to guard him so that the jinn would not hear the revelation, so they would throw it to their soothsayers and they would get ahead of the messenger. As-Suddi said: Watchers means guardians who guard the revelation. So whatever came from God, they would say: It is from God, and whatever the devil threw, they would say: It is from Satan. And (Rasdan) is in the accusative case as a direct object. In Al-Sahah: They said arsadan. The observer of something is the one who watches it. It is said: he watched it, he watches it, watching and watching. Watching is anticipation and the observer is the nurse of the observer.
72:28: God the Almighty says: That he may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord, and He encompasses what is with them and has enumerated all things precisely. God the Almighty says: That he may know Qatada and Muqatil said: That is, so that Muhammad may know that the messengers before him had conveyed the message just as he had conveyed the message. There is an omission in this context related to the lam, meaning, We informed him of Our preservation of the revelation so that he may know that the messengers before him were in the same state as him in conveying the truth and honesty. It was also said: So that Muhammad may know that Gabriel and those with him had conveyed to him the message of his Lord, as Ibn Jubayr said. He said: The revelation was not sent down except with four angelic guardians with him, peace be upon them. It was also said: So that the messengers may know that the angels conveyed the messages of their Lord. It was also said: So that the messenger may know, whoever he was, that the messengers other than him had conveyed. It was also said: So that Satan may know that the messengers had conveyed the messages of their Lord, free from his confusion and the eavesdropping of his companions. Ibn Qutaybah said: That is, so that the jinn may know that the messengers had conveyed what was revealed to them and that they were not the ones who conveyed it by eavesdropping on them. Mujahid said: So that he who denied the messengers may know that the messengers had conveyed the messages of their Lord. The reading of the congregation is li-ya’lam with a fat-ha on the ya’, and its interpretation is as we have mentioned. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Hamid, and Ya’qub read it with a damma on the ya’ to li-ya’lam an-rasool that people may know that the messengers had conveyed. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, so that God may know that His messengers had conveyed His messages, with a fat-ha on the ya’, like His statement: And God has made evident those among you who strive hard and made evident those who are patient. (Al-Imran 3:142) The meaning is: So that God may make evident that with visible knowledge, as He taught it to the angels. Ibn Jubayr said: The meaning is: So that the messengers may know that their Lord has encompassed all that is with them in His knowledge, so that they may convey His messages. And He has counted all things in number means He has encompassed the number of all things, knows them, and knows them, so nothing of it is hidden from Him. And (count) is in the accusative case as a state, meaning He counted everything in the state of counting, or if you like, as a source, meaning He counted and counted everything by number, so it is the source of the deleted verb. So He, glory be to Him, is the Counter, the All-Encompassing, the All-Knowing, the Preserver of everything. We have explained all of this in the Most Sublime Book, in the explanation of the Most Beautiful Names of God. And praise be to God alone.
73:1: It has twenty-seven verses. All of them are Meccan according to Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata', and Jabir. Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: Except for two verses from it: And be patient over what they say and the one that follows it, as mentioned by Al-Marudi. Al-Tha’labi said: The Almighty’s statement: Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand near to the end of the surah, was revealed in Medina. There are eight issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: O you who is wrapped up. Al-Akhfash Saeed said: “The root of al-Muzzammil is al-Mutazzammil, so the ta’ was assimilated into the zay, and the same is true of al-Muddaththir. Abi bin Ka’b read it according to the original form al-Mutazzammil and al-Mutaddaththir, and Saeed said: “al-Muzzammil.” There are two opinions about the root of al-Muzzammil 73:One of them is that it is possible. It is said: Zamala of something if he carries it, and from it comes the word al-Zamilah because she carries cloth. The second is that al-Muzzammil is the one who is wrapped up. It is said: Tazammal and Tadathir with his garment if he covers himself. And he covers someone else if he covers him, and everything that is wrapped up has been wrapped up and covered. Imru’ al-Qais said: Big people in Bajad Muzamil Second: The Most High’s saying: O you who is wrapped up in a cloak. This is addressed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. There are three opinions on this: The first is the saying of Ikrimah: O you who is wrapped up in a cloak with regard to prophethood and the one committed to the message. Also from him: O you who is wrapped up in this matter, meaning he carried it and then slackened. The reading used to be O you who is wrapped up in a cloak, with a soft zay, a fatha on the meem, and a shaddah on the meem, deleting the direct object. The same is true of al-Muddaththir, and the meaning is the one who is wrapped up himself and the one who is wrapped up himself, or the one who was wrapped up by someone else. The second is O you who is wrapped up in a cloak with the Quran, said by Ibn Abbas. The third is the one wrapped up in his clothes, said by Qatada and others. Al-Nakha’i said: He was wrapped up in Aisha’s velvet, a cloak fourteen cubits long, half of it on me while I was sleeping, and the other half on the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was praying. By God, it was not silk, nor brocade, nor brocade, nor wool, its warp was hair, and its weft was fur. This was mentioned by al-Tha’labi. I said: This statement by Aisha indicates that the surah was revealed in Medina, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not recite it except in Medina. What was mentioned about it being revealed in Mecca is not correct. And God knows best. Ad-Dahhak said: He wrapped himself in his clothes for his sleep. O you who are wrapped in garments and O you who are wrapped in garments. It was said that this was at the beginning of what was revealed to him, for when he heard the words of the angel and looked at him, he was seized with trembling, so he went to his family and said: Cover me, wrap me up. Its meaning was narrated from Ibn Abbas. The sages said: He addressed him as the one wrapped up and the one wrapped up at the beginning, because he had not yet wrapped himself up for conveying the message. Ibn al-Arabi said: There is a difference of opinion regarding the interpretation of O you wrapped up one. Some of them took it literally, as it was said to him: O you who are wrapped up in your clothes or in your quilt, get up, said Ibrahim and Qatadah. Some of them took it metaphorically, as if it was said to him: O you who are wrapped up in prophethood, said Ikrimah. This interpretation is only permissible if the mim is open and stressed in the form of the passive participle whose agent is not named, but if it is in the form of the agent, then it is invalid. I said: We have already shown that it is based on the deletion of the object, and it has been read in this way, so its meaning is correct. He said: As for the one who said that it is the Qur’an’s receptacle, this is correct in its metaphor, but we have already mentioned that it is not needed. Third: Al-Suhayli said: Al-Muzzammil is not one of the names of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was not known by this name as some people have claimed and counted it among his names, peace be upon him. Rather, Al-Muzzammil is a name derived from his state when he was addressed, as is the case with Al-Muddaththir. Addressing him with this name has two benefits: One is to show kindness, for when the Arabs intend to show kindness to the person being addressed and avoid reproaching him, they name him with a name derived from his state, like the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Ali when he was angry with Fatimah, may God be pleased with them both, so he came to him while he was sleeping with dirt stuck to his side and said to him: (Get up, O Abu Turab), indicating to him that he was not reproaching him, and as a way of showing him kindness. Similarly, his saying, peace be upon him, to Hudhayfah: (Get up, O Noman) while he was asleep, as a way of showing him kindness and leaving off reproaching and reprimanding. So God Almighty’s saying to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: (O you who are wrapped in a blanket, get up) is a way of showing comfort and kindness, so that he feels that He is not reproaching him. The second benefit: To alert everyone who is wrapped up and sleeping at night to be aware of performing the night prayer and remembering God Almighty during it, because the noun derived from the verb is shared by everyone who performed that action and was characterized by that trait.
73:2: Fourth: The Almighty's saying: Stand at night The general reading is with a kasra on the meem due to the meeting of two sukoon letters. Abu Al-Samal read it with a damma on the meem following his damma on the qaf. He reported the fatha due to its lightness. Uthman bin Jinni said: The purpose of this movement is to convey it, escaping the meeting of two sukoon letters, so with whatever movement it is moved the purpose has been achieved. It is one of the intransitive verbs that are not transitive to an object. As for the adverbial of time and place, it is permissible in it, except that the adverbial of place is not transitive to it except by an intermediary. You do not say: I stood up in the house until you say I stood up in the middle of the house or outside the house. It has been said that (qūm) here means pray, it was expressed with it and used as a metaphor for it until it became a common usage. Fifth: (Night) The definition of night: from sunset to dawn. This was explained in Surah Al-Baqarah. There is disagreement over whether standing during it was obligatory and mandatory, or recommended and encouraged. Evidence strengthens the point that standing during it is not specific to a particular time. Also, the timing of this was reported by Aisha and others, as will be mentioned below. There is also disagreement over whether it was obligatory on the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) alone, or on him and the prophets who came before him, or on him and his nation? There are three opinions: The first is the opinion of Saeed bin Jubair, as the address was directed to him specifically. The second is the opinion of Ibn Abbas, who said: Standing at night was an obligation on the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the prophets who came before him. The third is the statement of Aisha and Ibn Abbas, which is also correct, as in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Zurarah bin Awfa: “Saad bin Hisham bin Amir wanted to fight in the way of God... the hadith, and in it: So I said to Aisha: Tell me about the night prayer of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him? She said: Do you not recite “O you wrapped in a garment.” I said: Yes! She said: God, the Almighty, made the night prayer obligatory at the beginning of this surah, so the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and his companions stood for a year, and God, the Almighty, held back its conclusion for twelve months in the heavens, until God, the Almighty, revealed at the end of the surah the alleviation, so the night prayer became voluntary after it was obligatory. And he mentioned the hadith.” And Waki’ and Ya’la said: Musa’ar narrated to us on the authority of Samak al-Hanafi, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas say: When the beginning of O you wrapped in a garment was revealed, they would stand for approximately the same amount of time as they stand in the month of Ramadan until the end of it was revealed, and there was a period of about a year between its beginning and its end. Sa`id ibn Jubayr said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions spent ten years performing the night prayers. Then, after ten years, the verse was revealed: Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] nearly two-thirds of the night, so God made things easier for them. Sixth: The Almighty’s statement: except a little is an exception from the night, meaning pray the entire night except for a little of it, because staying up all night continuously is not possible, so He excepted a little from it for the sake of bodily comfort. A little of something is less than half, so it was narrated on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih that he said: A little is less than a tenth or a sixth. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: A third.
73:3: God the Almighty said: Half of it or subtract from it a little. This was an alleviation since the time of standing was not limited, so people stood until their feet swelled. This was then abrogated by His statement: He knows that you will not be able to count it. Al-Akhfash said: Half of it means make it equitable. It is said: Give him a dirham, two or three, meaning: Or two or three dirhams. Al-Zajjaj said: Half of it is a substitute for the night, and except a little is an exception to half. The pronouns in of it and upon it refer to half. The meaning is: Stand for half of the night, or subtract from half a little to a third, or add a little to two-thirds. It is as if he said: Stand for two-thirds of the night, or half of it, or a third of it. It was also said: Half of it is a substitute for a little. And he had a choice between three things: Standing for half in full, or for less than half, or for more than half. It is as if the meaning of the statement is: Stand for the whole night except for half of it, or less than half of it, or more than half of it. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: ((God the Almighty descends to the lowest heaven every night when the first third of the night has passed, and says: I am the King, I am the King. Who is there who calls upon Me that I may answer him? Who is there who asks Me that I may give him? Who is there who seeks My forgiveness that I may forgive him? And he continues like this until dawn breaks)).” And something similar was narrated by Abu Hurairah and Abu Sa’id, both of them, and it indicates the encouragement of the one who spends two-thirds of the night. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: (When half the night - or two-thirds of it - has passed - God descends)... The hadith was narrated by two chains of narration on the authority of Abu Hurairah like this, although there is doubt. And it came in the book of al-Nasa’i on the authority of Abu Hurairah and Abu Sa’id, may God be pleased with them, they said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ((God the Almighty waits until the first half of the night has passed, then He orders a caller to say: Is there a supplicant that He may be answered? Is there a seeker of forgiveness that He may be forgiven? Is there a questioner that He may be given?))” Abu Muhammad Abdul Haqq authenticated it. This hadith, despite its authenticity, explains the meaning of the descent and that it occurs at half Night. Ibn Majah narrated from the hadith of Shihab, “On the authority of Abu Salamah and Abu Abdullah al-Aghar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ((Our Lord, blessed and exalted be He, descends every night when the last third of the night remains and says: Who asks Me that I may give him? Who calls upon Me that I may answer him? Who seeks My forgiveness that I may forgive him? Until dawn breaks.))” So they preferred to pray the last part of the night over the first part. Our scholars said: With this arrangement, the hadith and the Qur’an are arranged, as they both see from one lamp. In al-Muwatta’ and other books, it is narrated from the hadith of Ibn Abbas: I spent the night with my aunt Maymunah until midnight, or a little before or a little after, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, woke up. He went to a hanging water skin and performed a light ablution. And he mentioned the hadith. Seventh: The scholars differed regarding the abrogating factor of the command to perform the night prayer. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas and Aisha that the abrogating factor of the command to perform the night prayer is the statement of God the Almighty: Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] nearly two-thirds of the night (al-Muzzammil 73:20) to the end of the surah. It was also said that God the Almighty’s statement: He knows that you will not be able to enumerate it (al-Muzzammil 73:20). It was also narrated from Ibn Abbas that it was abrogated by the statement of God the Almighty: He knows that there will be among you ill (al-Muzzammil 73:20). It was also narrated from Aisha, Al-Shafi’i, Muqatil and Ibn Kaysan that it was abrogated by the five daily prayers. It was also said that the abrogating factor for that is the statement of God the Almighty: whatever is easy of it (al-Muzzammil 73:20). Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Salami said: When the verse, O you who are wrapped in a garment, was revealed, they stood up until their feet and legs were swollen. Then the words of God Almighty were revealed: So recite as much of it as is easy for you. Some scholars said: It is an obligation that was abrogated by an obligation that was imposed on the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, specifically because of its virtue, as God Almighty said: And during part of the night, pray with it as an additional prayer for you (al-Isra’ 17:79). I said: The first statement includes all of these statements. God Almighty said: And establish prayer, so included in it is the statement of those who said that what abrogated it were the five daily prayers. Al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin stated that the night prayer is obligatory for every Muslim, even if it is equivalent to milking a sheep. Al-Hasan also said regarding this verse: Praise be to God is a voluntary prayer after the obligatory prayer. This is correct, God willing, because of the encouragement and virtue of performing it in the Qur’an and Sunnah. On the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, she said: I used to make a mat for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to pray on at night. The people would hear about it, but when he saw them gathered together, he disliked it and feared that the night prayer would be prescribed for them. So he entered the house looking angry, and they began to clear their throats and spit. He went out to them and said: O people, take on as many deeds as you can bear, for God does not tire of reward until you tire of working, and the best work is that which is done consistently, even if it is little. Then the verse, O you who are wrapped up in a cloak, was revealed and prescribed for them. It was revealed as an obligatory prayer, to the point that one of them would tie a rope and cling to it. They remained for eight months, but God had mercy on them and revealed: Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] nearly two-thirds of the night, so God returned them to the obligatory prayer and exempted them from the night prayer except for what they did voluntarily. I said: This hadith of Aisha was mentioned by Al-Tha’labi, and its meaning is confirmed in Sahih until the saying: (And if you say), and the rest of it indicates that the saying of God the Almighty: {O you who are wrapped in a garment} was revealed in Madinah and that they remained for eight months in sin. It was mentioned earlier in Sahih Muslim: a year. Al-Mawardi reported a third opinion from her, which is sixteen months, and no other opinion was mentioned from her. He mentioned from Ibn Abbas that there was a year between the beginning of Al-Muzzammil and its end. He said: As for the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, it was obligatory upon him.
