And regarding its abrogation from him, there are two opinions: The first: That it was obligatory upon him until God the Almighty took him. The second: That it was abrogated from him as it was abrogated from his nation. And regarding the period of its obligation until it was abrogated, there are two opinions: The first: The period of obligation upon his nation in the two previous opinions, meaning the saying of Ibn Abbas was a year, and the saying of Aisha was sixteen months. The second: That it was ten years until it was lightened by abrogation as an increase in the obligation, to distinguish it by the action of the Messenger, as Ibn Jubayr said. I said: This is contrary to what Al-Tha'labi reported on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, as mentioned above, so reflect on it. This issue will be further explained at the end of the Surah, God willing.
73:4: Eighth - The Almighty said: And recite the Qur’an with measured recitation. That is, do not rush in reciting the Qur’an, but recite it slowly and clearly, while pondering the meanings. Ad-Dahhak said: Recite it letter by letter. Mujahid said: The people most beloved to God in recitation are the most intelligent about it. And measured recitation means arrangement, coordination, and good organization. From this comes the word rattal and rattal, with a kasra or fatha on the ‘ayn: if it is well-arranged. Its explanation was presented in the introduction to the book. “Al-Hasan narrated that the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, passed by a man who was reciting a verse and crying, so he said: ((Have you not heard the saying of God, the Almighty: “And recite the Qur’an with measured recitation,” this measured recitation. And Alqamah heard a man reciting beautifully and said: He has recited the Qur’an with measured recitation, may my father and mother be sacrificed for him. Abu Bakr ibn Tahir said: Ponder over the subtleties of its speech, and demand of yourself to fulfill its rulings, your heart to understand its meanings, and your secret to turn to it. And Abdullah ibn Amr narrated that he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The reciter of the Qur’an will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and will be stopped at the first step of Paradise and it will be said to him: ‘Read, ascend, and recite as you used to recite in the world, for your station will be at the last verse you recite.’” Narrated by Abu Dawud and mentioned earlier in the book. Anas narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would prolong his voice while reciting.
73:5: The Almighty's saying: Indeed, We will cast upon you a weighty word is connected to the obligation of standing in the night, meaning, We will cast upon you, by imposing the night prayer, a weighty word that is difficult to bear, because the night is for sleeping, and whoever is commanded to stand for most of it will not be able to do that except by a great effort on the soul and striving against Satan, so it is a heavy matter for the servant. It was said: We will reveal the Quran to you, and it is a weighty word that makes acting according to its laws difficult. Qatada said: Its obligations and limits are heavy, by God. Mujahid: Its lawful and unlawful. Al-Hasan: Acting according to it. Abu Al-Aliyah: Heavy with the promise and threat, and the lawful and unlawful. Muhammad ibn Ka'b: Heavy on the hypocrites. It was said: On the disbelievers, because it contains an argument against them, a clarification of their misguidance, a cursing of their gods, and an exposition of what the People of the Book have distorted. Al-Suddi: Heavy in the sense of generous, taken from their saying: So-and-so is heavy on me, meaning he is generous to me. Al-Farraa’: (Heavy) is firm, not light and vulgar, because it is the speech of our Lord. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: Heavy, and only a heart supported by success and a soul adorned with monotheism can bear it. Ibn Zayd said: By God, it is heavy and blessed, just as it was heavy in this world, it will be heavy on the scales on the Day of Resurrection. It was said: (Heavy) means firm, as heavy is firm in its place, and its meaning is that it is firm in its miracle, its miracle will never disappear. It was said: It is the Qur’an itself, as came in the hadith: “Whenever revelation came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was on his camel, it would place its forearms - meaning its chest - on the ground, and it would not be able to move until it was relieved.” In Al-Muwatta’ and elsewhere: “He, peace be upon him, was asked: How does revelation come to you? He said: ((Sometimes it comes to me like the ringing of a bell, and that is the hardest for me, then it leaves me while I have understood what it says. And sometimes the angel appears to me as a man and speaks to me, and I understand what he says.)) Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: I saw revelation coming down to him on an extremely cold day, then it leaves him and his forehead is dripping with sweat. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is more appropriate, because it is the truth, and it says: “And He has not placed upon you in religion any difficulty” (al-Hajj 22:78). (I was sent with the easy, tolerant religion.) It was said that the statement in this surah is: the statement There is no god but God, as the statement is light on the tongue but heavy on the scales. This was mentioned by Al-Qushayri.
73:6: The Almighty says: Indeed, the rising of the night The scholars said: The rising of the night means its times and hours, because its times arise first and foremost. It is said: the thing originated, originates: if it began and came one thing after another, so it is emerging. And God originated, so it originated. And from this the cloud originated if it began and God created it, with an active participle from the verb to originate, originates, so it is an emerging. And from this the Almighty says: Or he who grows up in adornment while, in dispute, is not clear? (al-Zukhruf 43:18) What is meant are the emerging hours of the night, so the description was sufficient instead of the noun, so the word hour was feminized, because every hour occurs. And it was said: the rising is a source meaning the false and lying night prayer, meaning that the rising of the night is more intense. And it was said: the rising of the night is the night prayer. Ibn Masoud The Abyssinians say: he grew up meaning he stood up. Perhaps he meant that the word is Arabic, but it is common and prevalent in the speech of the Abyssinians. Otherwise, there is nothing in the Qur'an that is not in the Arabic language. This has been fully explained in the introduction to the book. Second: In this verse, God Almighty has explained the superiority of night prayer over daytime prayer, and that increasing the night prayer by reciting as much as possible brings greater reward and brings more recompense. Scholars differed about what is meant by the beginning of the night. Ibn Amr and Anas ibn Malik said: It is what is between sunset and evening prayers, based on the fact that the word the beginning indicates the beginning, so it was more deserving of priority. From this is the saying of the poet: If it were not for the saying You are a young man, I would have said to myself, You are a young man Ali ibn al-Husayn used to pray between Maghrib and Isha’ and would say: This is the rising of the night. Ata’ and Ikrimah said: It is the beginning of the night. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others said: It is the entire night because it begins after the day. This is the view favoured by Malik ibn Anas. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is what the wording suggests and the language requires. Aisha, Ibn Abbas and Mujahid also said: The rising is standing at night after sleeping. Whoever stands at the beginning of the night before sleeping has not stood up as a rising. Yaman and Ibn Kaysan said: It is standing at the end of the night. Ibn Abbas said: Their prayer was at the beginning of the night because when a person sleeps, he does not know when he will wake up. In al-Sahah: The rising of the night is the first hours of the night. Al-Qutbi said: They are the hours of the night because they begin hour after hour. Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: It is what comes after the last Isha’ prayer until dawn. Al-Hasan also said: Whatever comes after Isha’ is a rising. It is also said: What comes after the Isha’ of acts of worship, as narrated by al-Jawhari. Third - The Almighty’s saying: It is more severe in constraint. Abu Al-Aaliyah, Abu Amr, Ibn Ishaq, Mujahid, Hamid, Ibn Muhaisin, Ibn Amir, Al-Mughirah, and Abu Haywah read: Wa-ta’ with a kasra on the waw, a fatha on the ta’, and a long vowel. Abu Ubaid chose this. The rest read: Wa-ta’ with a fatha on the waw, a sukoon on the ta’, and a shortened vowel. Abu Hatim chose this, from your saying: The burden of their sultan weighed heavily on the people. That is, the provisions they carried were heavy on them. From this is the saying of the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him: (O God, intensify Your punishment on Mudar) The meaning is that it is heavier on the worshipper than the daytime hours. This is because the night is a time for sleeping, bidding farewells and gatherings. So whoever is occupied with worship has endured great hardship. The verb madd is a noun meaning I agreed with him, meaning I agreed with him. Ibn Zayd said: I agreed with him on the matter means I agreed with him in agreement. So-and-so's name agrees with my name, and they agreed on it, meaning they agreed. The meaning is a stronger agreement between the heart, sight, hearing and tongue, due to the cessation of sounds and movements. This was said by Mujahid, Ibn Abi Malekah and others. Ibn Abbas said the same meaning, meaning that the hearing agrees with the heart. God the Almighty said: That they may comply with the number which God has forbidden (al-Tawbah 9:37), meaning that they may agree. It was also said that the meaning is a more comfortable place to conduct thought and reflection. And wata' is the opposite of cover. It was said: (more steadfast than the day, with a sukoon on the ta and a fatha on the waw, meaning more steadfast than the day, because at night a person is alone with what he is doing, so he is more steadfast in work and removes distractions and occupies the heart. And steadfastness is firmness, you say: I trod the ground with my feet. Al-Akhfash said: more steadfast in standing. Al-Farra’: He established recitation and standing. And from him: more steadfast in wati’an meaning more steadfast in work and more lasting for whoever wants to increase his worship, and the night is a time of leisure from being occupied with earning a living, so his worship is lasting and does not stop. Al-Kalbi said: more steadfast in wati’an meaning more energetic for the one who prays, because it is a time of rest. Ubadah said: (more energetic for the one who prays, lighter and more steadfast in recitation. Fourth - The Almighty said: And I stand upright in saying meaning, reading at night is more upright than during the day, meaning more upright and consistent in what is correct, because the sounds are quiet and the world is still, so the worshipper is not disturbed by what he is reading. Qatada and Mujahid said: meaning more correct in reading and more steadfast in speech, because it is the time for understanding. Abu Ali said: (I stand upright in saying) meaning more upright because the mind is at ease at night. It was also said: meaning more quickly the supplication is answered. Narrated by Ibn Shajarah. Ikrimah said: Worship at night is more energetic, more sincere, and more blessed. Zaid bin Aslam said: It is more likely to be understood in the Quran. Al-A'mash said: Anas bin Malik recited: (Indeed, the hours of the night are more effective for concurrence and more correct for saying), so it was said to him: (And I stand upright in saying), so he said: I stand up, correct, and prepare all the same. Abu Bakr al-Anbari said: Some of these deviants went so far as to say: Whoever recites a letter that matches the meaning of a letter of the Qur’an is correct, if it does not contradict the meaning and does not come with anything other than what God wanted and intended. They cited as evidence the statement of Anas. This is a statement that should not be taken into consideration and its speaker should not be paid attention to, because if he recited with words that differed from the words of the Qur’an, if their meanings were similar and included their generality, then it would be permissible to recite in place of Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds (al-Fatihah 1:2): Thanks to the Creator, King of the creation. The matter expands in this to the point that the wording of the entire Qur’an would be invalidated, and the one who recites it would be slandering God Almighty and lying about His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. They have no proof in the statement of Ibn Mas’ud: “The Qur’an was revealed in seven letters. It is rather like one of you saying: ‘Come, come, and approach.’” Because this hadith requires the authentic readings transmitted with authentic chains of transmission from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, if they differ, it requires that the authentic readings transmitted with authentic chains of transmission from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, if their wording differed and their meanings agreed, then that would be in them like a disagreement in come, “come,” and approach. As for what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, his companions, and those who followed them, may God be pleased with them, did not recite, then whoever included a letter of it in the Qur’an is a slanderer. He deviated from the correct path. Abu Bakr said: The hadith that they made their basis for misguidance is a hadith that is not authenticated from any of the people of knowledge, because it is based on the narration of Al-A'mash from Anas, so it is disconnected and not connected, so it cannot be taken into account, because Al-A'mash saw Anas but did not hear from him.
73:7: Fifth - The Almighty's saying: Indeed, for you during the day is much exertion. The general reading is with an unvoiced ha, meaning to manage your needs, coming and going, coming and going. And sabīh means running and turning, and from it comes the word sabeeh in the water, for turning over with its hands and feet. And a sabīh horse: is a fast-running horse. Imru’ al-Qays said: Wipe if the swimmers on the light have affected the dust with the kicked iron It was said: Sabh is free time, meaning that you have free time for your needs during the day. It was also said: You have free time during the day, meaning sleep, and tasabh is stretching out, mentioned by Al-Khalil. On the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ata’: A long sabh means a long time for your sleep and rest, so make the night a time for your worship. Al-Zajjaj said: If you miss something at night, then you have free time during the day to make up for it. Yahya bin Ya'mar and Abu Wa'il read sabkha with the voiced kha. Al-Mahdawi said: It means sleep, and it was narrated from the reciters with this reading. It was said: It means lightness, spaciousness, and rest. "From this is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Aisha when she cursed the thief of her cloak: (Do not lighten his sin with your curse)" meaning do not lighten his sin. The poet said: So worry will overwhelm you, and know that if the Most Gracious has decreed something, it will be. Al-Asma'i: It is said that May God relieve you of fever, meaning that He eased it. And the heat became lighter and lighter. Tasbikh is a deep sleep. Tasbikh is also the spreading and fluffing of cotton, linen, and wool. It is said to a woman: Sabkhi qutnak. Tasbikh of cotton is what is fluffed after fluffing, meaning it is rolled up for the woman to spin. A piece of it is a sabikh, and the same is true of wool and fur. Pieces of cotton are called sabaikh. Al-Akhtal said, describing hunters and dogs: So send them to scatter the dust as one scatters the fluffy cotton strings. Al-Tha'lab said: Fever is from the heat of Hell, so they made it submerge in water, meaning they made it submerge. Abu Amr said: Submerging means sleep and idleness. I said: Therefore, it is one of the opposites, and it means rosary, with the unvoiced ha.
73:8: God Almighty says: And remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him with a complete devotion. There are three evenings: First - The Almighty’s saying: And remember the name of your Lord meaning, call upon Him by His beautiful names, so that you will achieve a good outcome through prayer. It was also said: meaning, intend with your deeds to please your Lord. Sahl said: Recite In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful at the beginning of your prayer, so that the blessing of its recitation will connect you to your Lord and cut you off from everything else. It was also said: Remember the name of your Lord in His promise and threat, so that you will be diligent in obeying Him and refrain from disobeying Him. Al-Kalbi said: Pray to your Lord, meaning during the day. I said: This is good, because when he mentioned the night, he mentioned the day, since it is its counterpart, and God Almighty said: And it is He who made the night and the day in succession for whoever wishes to remember (al-Furqan 25:62), as mentioned above. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And devote yourself to Him with a complete devotion. Devotion means devoting yourself to the worship of God Almighty, meaning devote yourself to Him in your worship, and do not associate anyone with Him. It is said: batallat something, meaning you cut it off, and from this is their saying: He divorced her completely with batala. This is a complete charity, meaning irrevocable and cut off from its owner, meaning he cut off his ownership of her completely. From this is Maryam the Virgin, because of her devotion to God Almighty. And the monk is called devotional, because of his devotion to people and his isolation in worship. He said: It lights up the darkness at night like a beacon of a devout monk's evening The hadith forbids celibacy, which means seclusion from people and groups. It was said that its origin among the Arabs is isolation, as stated by Ibn Arafa. The first is stronger for what we have mentioned. It is said: How did he say celibacy, and not celibacy? It was said to him: Because the meaning of celibacy is seclusion of oneself, so it was brought with its meaning in order to observe the right separations. Third - It was mentioned in Al-Ma’idah in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you (al-Ma’idah 5:87) as a dislike for someone who has become celibate and cut himself off and taken the path of monasticism as sufficient. Ibn al-Arabi said: “But today, when people’s covenants have been shattered, their misfortunes have diminished, and the forbidden has taken over the spoils, isolation is better than mixing, and celibacy is better than marriage. However, the meaning of the verse is: cut yourself off from idols and artifacts and from the worship of other than God. Mujahid said the same: its meaning is: devote your worship to Him alone, and it does not mean celibacy. So celibacy is commanded in the Qur’an and forbidden in the Sunnah. The object of the command is not the object of the prohibition, so they do not contradict each other. Rather, he was sent to explain to the people what was revealed to them. So the celibacy that is commanded is: cutting yourself off from God with sincere worship, as God Almighty said: “And they were commanded only to worship God, devoting their religion to Him alone” (al-Bayyinah 98:5). The celibacy that is forbidden is following the path of the Christians in abandoning marriage and becoming a monk in monastic monasteries. However, in the face of the corruption of time, the best wealth of the Muslim is sheep that he follows to the mountain passes and the places where rain falls, fleeing with his religion from tribulations.”
73:9: The Almighty's saying: Lord of the East and the West The people of the Two Sanctuaries, Ibn Mahisan, Mujahid, Abu Amr, Ibn Abi Ishaq, and Hafs read (Lord) in the nominative case as the subject and the predicate is there is no god but He. It was also said that it was based on the omission of (He). The rest read (Lord) in the accusative case as an attribute of the Almighty Lord in His saying: And remember the name of your Lord (Lord of the East) and whoever knows that He is the Lord of the East and the West will be devoted to his work and hope in Him. Then take Him as a Disposer of affairs meaning one who takes care of your affairs. It was also said that He will be the guarantor of what He promised you.
73:10: The Almighty said: And be patient over what they say meaning the harm, insults, and mockery. Do not be alarmed by what they say, and do not refrain from calling upon them. And leave them with gracious leave meaning do not interfere with them, and do not be preoccupied with rewarding them, because that means abandoning calling upon God. This was before the command to fight, then after that the command to fight and kill them was given, so the verse about fighting abrogated what came before it about abandoning it, as stated by Qatada and others. Abu al-Darda' said: We smile in the faces of people and laugh at them, although our hearts may hate them or curse them.
73:11: The Almighty said: And leave Me and the deniers meaning, leave Me alone for their punishment. It was revealed about the leaders of Quraysh and the chieftains of Makkah who mocked. Muqatil said: It was revealed about those who were fed on the day of Badr and they were ten. They were mentioned earlier in (Al-Anfal). Yahya bin Salam said: They are Banu Al-Mughira. Saeed bin Jubair said: I was told that they were twelve men. Those of ease meaning those who have wealth, luxury and pleasure in this world. And their respite is a little meaning until the end of their lives. Aisha may God be pleased with her said: When this verse was revealed, it was only a short time until Badr happened. It was also said: And their respite is a little means until the end of this world.
73:12: The Almighty said: Indeed, with Us are shackles and a blazing Fire. Ankaal: chains. Narrated by Al-Hasan, Mujahid and others. Its singular is nakal, which is what prevents a person from moving. It was also said that it was called nakl because it is used to punish him. Al-Sha'bi said: Do you think that God Almighty placed shackles on the feet of the people of Hellfire lest they flee? No, by God! But if they want to rise up, it will lift them up. Al-Kalbi said: Ankaal: Ankaal: shackles, and the first is more well-known in the language, and from it is the saying of Al-Khansa: He called you, so you cut off his shackles, while before you they were not cut off. It was said: It is the type of severe punishment. Muqatil said: “It was reported that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: (God loves to punish after punishing) with the fat-ha, as stated by Al-Jawhari. It was said: What is “punishment”? He said: (A strong, experienced man, on a strong, experienced horse) mentioned by Al-Mawardi. He said: From this, the chain was called nakl due to its strength, as well as the shackles and every strong punishment that becomes intense. And Hell is the blazing fire.
73:13: The Almighty said: And food that chokes meaning, it is not palatable, it sticks to the throat, neither going down nor coming out, and it is the two ghusls, the zaqqum, and the dari'. Ibn Abbas said this and it was also narrated from him: It is a thorn that enters the throat, neither going down nor coming out. Al-Zajjaj said: It means their food is the dari', as he said: They will have no food except from the dari' (Al-Ghashiyah 80:6) and it is a thorn like the bramble. Mujahid said it is the zaqqum, as he said: Indeed, the tree of zaqqum, the food of the sinner (Al-Dukhan 44:43-44). The meaning is the same. Hamran ibn A'yan said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited, Indeed, with Us are shackles and a Hellfire, and and food that chokes, and he fell unconscious. Khalid ibn Hassan said: Al-Hasan spent the evening fasting with us, so I brought him food and recited this verse to him: Indeed, with Us are shackles and a Hellfire, * And food that chokes and a painful punishment. He said: Take away your food. The second time, I brought him food and recited this verse to him, and he said: Take it away. And the third time, his son went to Thabit al-Bunani, Yazid al-Dhabi, and Yahya al-Bakka’ and told them. They came to him and they did not stop until he drank a sip of barley flour. Ghassah is a lump, which is what gets stuck in the throat from a bone or other thing. The plural is ghuss. Ghass with the fat-ha is the source of your saying: I choked, man, you choke. So you are choked with food and branches, and I choked him, and the house was crowded with people, meaning it was full of them.
73:14: The Almighty said: The Day the earth and the mountains will shake meaning they will move and tremble with those on them. Day is in the accusative case as an adverbial phrase, meaning they will be punished and tormented The Day the earth will shake. It was also said that the preposition was removed, meaning this punishment will be on the Day the earth and the mountains will shake. And the mountains will become like heaps of sand meaning they will be. And the heap is the sand dune - Hassan said: Diyar Zainab was known for its books, like the script of revelation on soft paper. Al-Muhayyal: that which passes under the feet. Ad-Dahhak and Al-Kalbi said: Al-Muhayyal: is that which if you step on it with the foot, it slips from under you, and if you take its bottom, it flows. Ibn Abbas said: (Muhayyal) means liquid, scattered sand. Its origin is Mahyul and it is a passive participle from your saying: I poured the dust on it, Ahayla Hailan: if you poured it. It is said: Muhayyal and Muhayyul, and Makyil and Makywul, and Madyan and Madyun, and Mu’in and Mu’ayyun. The poet said: Your people used to think you were a master, but I think you are a master of the unknown. (Atikaloon or Tahiloon) They said: Nahil. He said: (Measure your food and it will be blessed for you) and ahlat al-daqiq is a dialect for halat, so it is muhaal and muhayil. The waw was deleted because the damma is heavy on the yaa, so it was deleted and it and the waw were sukun due to the meeting of two sukun letters.
73:15: God Almighty says: Indeed, We have sent to you a Messenger, meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him to the Quraysh just as We sent to Pharaoh a Messenger, which is Moses.
73:16: The Almighty said: But Pharaoh disobeyed the Messenger, meaning he denied him and did not believe in him. Muqatil said: Moses and Pharaoh were mentioned because the people of Mecca looked down on Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and belittled him because he was born among them, just as Pharaoh looked down on Moses because he raised him and he grew up among them, as God the Almighty said: Did We not raise you among us as a child? (al-Shu’ara 26:18) Al-Mahdawi said: The definite article al-definite was added to the Messenger because he was mentioned before. That is why "peace be upon you" was chosen at the beginning of the book and "peace be upon you" was chosen at the end. And a heavy and severe punishment means heavy, said Ibn Abbas and Mujahid. From this comes the word wabil meaning heavy, said Al-Akhfash. Al-Zajjaj said: It means heavy and thick. From this comes the word wabil for rain. It was also said destructive and the meaning is We punished him with a heavy punishment. He said: I ate your children like a lizard until I found the bitterness of the terrible pasture So-and-so ended up in such-and-such a situation: meaning he did not find the outcome good. Bad water: meaning unpleasant and not pleasurable. Bad pasture and bad and pleasurable food: if it is not pleasurable or enjoyable. Zuhair said: They fulfilled their desires among themselves, then they were sent to a ripe and abundant pasture. Al-Khansa' said: I ate a lot of food on the day when I met Malik's knights. Al-Wabil also means: a huge stick. He said: If I had its reins in my right hand and a bucket in my other hand to guard it And also the word mawbal with a kasra on the b, and mawbalah also means a bundle of firewood, and so is wabil, as Tarafa said. The wife of Sheikh Kalobele Yelande
73:17: The Almighty's saying: How can you guard yourself, if you disbelieve, against a Day that will turn the children gray-haired? This is a rebuke and a rebuke, meaning, how can you guard yourself from the punishment if you disbelieve. There is an inversion of the meaning, meaning, how can you guard yourself from a Day that will turn the children gray-haired if you disbelieve? This is how Abdullah and Atiyyah read the verses. Al-Hasan said: Which prayer will you guard yourself from the punishment? Which fasting will you guard yourself from the punishment? And there is an implied meaning, how can you guard yourself from the punishment of a Day? Qatada said: By God, he who disbelieves in God will not guard himself from that Day at all. And (a day) is the object of (you fear) according to this reading and is not an adverbial phrase. If disbelief is understood to mean denial, then the day is the object of (you disbelieve.)) Some of the commentators said: The completion stops at his saying: you disbelieved and the beginning (a day) goes to the fact that the day is the object of (makes) and the action is for God, the Almighty, and it is as if he said: God makes the children gray in a day. Ibn al-Anbari said: This is not suitable, because it is the day that does this from the severity of its horror. Al-Mahdawi: The pronoun in (makes) may be for God, the Almighty, and it is possible for it to be for the day. If it is for the day, it is suitable for it to be an attribute of it, and that is not suitable if the pronoun is for God, the Almighty, except with the estimation of deletion, as if he said: a day in which God makes the children gray. Ibn al-Anbari: Some of them made the day the object of (you disbelieved) and this is ugly, because if the day is connected to (you disbelieved), it needs an attribute, that is, you disbelieved in a day. If someone argues that the attribute has It is deleted and what follows it is placed in the accusative case. We argued against it with Abdullah’s reading: How will you guard against a Day? I said: This reading is not mutawatir, but rather it came as an explanation. If disbelief means denial, then (one day) is an explicit object without an adjective or its deletion, meaning how can you fear God and be in awe of Him if you deny the Day of Resurrection and the recompense? Abu al-Samal Qanab read (so how can you be pious) with a kasra on the noon as an addition. And the children are the young boys. Al-Suddi said: They are the children of fornication. It was also said: The children of the polytheists. The general is more correct, meaning the young ones will turn gray without growing old. That is when it is said: (O Adam, arise and send forth the people of Hellfire) as mentioned in the beginning of Surat al-Hajj. Al-Qushayri said: Then God will change the conditions and descriptions of the people of Paradise as He wills. It was also said: This is an example of the severity of that day, and it is a metaphor, because there will be no children on the Day of Resurrection. However, its meaning is that the awe of that day will be such that if there were a boy on it, his head would turn gray from awe. It is also said: This is the time of terror, before the trumpet is blown, and God knows best. Al-Zamakhshari: I came across in some books the story of a man who spent the night with black hair like a crow's chin, and woke up with a white head and beard like a white dove. He said: I saw the Resurrection, Paradise, and Hell in a dream, and I saw people being led in chains to the Fire. Because of the horror of that, I have become as you see. It is permissible to describe the day as long, and that children reach old age and gray hair in it.
73:18: The Almighty says: The sky will be split by it meaning cracked due to its severity. The meaning of (by it) is in it, meaning on that Day due to its horror. This is the best that has been said about it. It is said: heavily laden by it, which leads to it splitting due to its greatness upon them and their fear of it occurring, like the Almighty's saying: Its burdens are heavy upon the heavens and the earth (al-A’raf 7:187). It is also said: (by it) means for it, meaning for that Day. It is said: I did such and such by your honor and for your honor. The ba' and lam in: are close together in such a place. God the Almighty said: {And We will set up the just scales for the Day of Resurrection} (Al-Anbiya': 47) meaning on the Day of Resurrection. It is also said: (by it) means by the command, meaning the sky will be split by what will make children gray-haired. It is also said: split by God, meaning by His command. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala' said: He did not say split, because its metaphor is the ceiling. You say: This is the sky of the House. The poet said: If he raised the sky to a people, we would join the sky and the clouds. In the Qur’an: And We made the sky a protected ceiling (Al-Anbiya’: 32). Al-Farra’ said: The sky is masculine and feminine. Abu Ali said: It is from the same root as the spreading locusts and the green tree, and like their saying: a nursing woman, meaning one who breastfeeds, so it is based on the path of lineage. His promise meaning of the resurrection, the reckoning, and the reward was done, existing without doubt or defect. Muqatil said: His promise was that his religion would prevail over all religions.
73:19: The Almighty's saying: Indeed, this is a reminder meaning that this surah or verses is an admonition. It was also said: the verses of the Qur'an, as it is like a single surah. So whoever wills, let him take to his Lord meaning whoever wants to believe and take thereby to his Lord a way meaning a path to His pleasure and mercy, let him desire it, for it is possible for him, because He showed him the arguments and proofs. Then it was said: It was abrogated by the verse of the sword, and likewise the Almighty's saying: So whoever wills, let him remember Him (Abasa 80:12). Al-Tha'labi said: It is most likely that it was not abrogated.
73:20: The Almighty says: Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] This verse is an explanation of the Almighty's saying: "Stand [in prayer] during the night, except for a little. Half of it, or subtract a little from it, or add to it" as mentioned above. It abrogates the obligation of standing in prayer at night as mentioned above. Stand means you pray, and less means less. Ibn al-Samiq', Abu Haywah, and Hisham, on the authority of the people of Ash-Sham, read two-thirds with a sukoon on the lam. And half of it and a third in the accusative is the reading of the general public, in apposition to two-thirds, meaning: you stand for less than two-thirds of the night, or half of it, or a third of it. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose it, like the Almighty's saying: He knows that you will not enumerate it, so how can they stand for half of it or a third of it when they cannot enumerate it? Ibn Kathir and the Kufians read and half of it and a third of it in the accusative case in apposition to less, meaning: you stand for less than two-thirds of the night, and you stand for half of it and a third of it. Al-Farraa said: This is more likely to be correct, because he said less than two-thirds, then he mentioned the small amount itself, not less than the small amount. Al-Qushayri said: According to this reading, it is possible that they were getting a third or a half, because standing at that amount was too easy for them, and they would increase, and in the increase they would get the intended goal. As for two-thirds, standing was too difficult for them, so they would not get it, and they would decrease from it. It is possible that they were ordered to stand at midnight, and in the middle up to a third. It is possible that they were assigned half and decreased to a third, and the increase to two-thirds. Some of them fulfilled that, and some of them left it until it was abrogated from them. A group of people said: God only imposed a quarter on them, and they decreased from a quarter. This statement is arbitrary. Second - The Almighty's saying: And God determines the night and the day meaning He knows the proportions of the night and the day according to their reality, and you know through investigation and diligence that errors occur. He knows that you will never be able to enumerate it meaning that you will never be able to know the reality of that and perform it. It was also said: meaning that you will never be able to perform the night prayer. The first is more correct, because the night prayer was never obligatory in its entirety. Muqatil and others said: When the verse Stand [in prayer] during the night, except for a little * Half of it or subtract from it a little * Or add to it was revealed, it was difficult for them, and a man could not know when half of the night was from a third of it, so he would stand until morning for fear of making a mistake, so their feet would swell and their colors would fade, so God had mercy on them and made it easier for them, so God the Almighty said: He knows that you will never be able to enumerate it and that is a lightened form of heavy, meaning He knows that you will never be able to enumerate it, because if you add to it, it will be too heavy for you, and you will need to be tasked with something that is not obligatory, and if you subtract from it, it will be difficult for you. Third - The Almighty’s saying: Then He turned to you in forgiveness, meaning, He pardoned you. This indicates that they had abandoned some of what He had been commanded to do. It was also said: That is, He turned to you in forgiveness of the obligation of standing up when you were unable to do so. The root of repentance is return, as mentioned above, so the meaning is that He returned to you from being burdensome to light, and from difficulty to ease. They were commanded to guard their times by means of careful observation, so that careful observation was made easy for them. It was also said: The meaning of And God determines the night and the day is that He creates them in measured amounts, like His saying: And He created each thing and determined it with [precise] determination. (al-Furqan 25:2) Ibn Al-Arabi said: There is no ruling attached to the determination of creation, but rather God connects to it whatever He wills of the duties of obligation. Fourth - The Almighty’s statement: So recite whatever is easy for you of the Qur’an. There are two opinions: One of them is that what is meant is the recitation itself, so recite in what you pray at night whatever is easy for you. Al-Suddi said: One hundred verses. Al-Hasan said: Whoever recites one hundred verses at night will not need the Qur’an. Ka’b said: Whoever recites one hundred verses at night will be recorded among the devout. Sa’id said: Fifty verses. I said: Ka’b’s statement is more correct, because he, peace be upon him, said: ((Whoever recites ten verses will not be recorded among the heedless, and whoever recites one hundred verses will be recorded among the devout, and whoever recites one thousand verses will be recorded among the devout.)) Narrated by Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi in his Musnad from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr. We mentioned it in the introduction to the book, and praise be to God. The second statement: So recite as much of it as is easy for you means pray as much as is easy for you, and prayer is called the Qur’an, as God the Almighty says: And the Qur’an of dawn (al-Isra’ 17:78) meaning the dawn prayer. Ibn al-Arabi, and this is the most correct, because he spoke about the prayer, and the statement goes back to it. I said: The first is more correct, as it takes the address to mean the apparent meaning of the word, and the second statement is a metaphor, as it is a naming of something by some of its actions. Fifth - Some scholars said: The Almighty's statement: So recite what is easy for you thereof abrogated the night prayer and half of it, and the decrease from half and the increase from it. Then the statement of God, the Almighty, So recite what is easy for you thereof was interpreted in two ways: One is that it is a second obligation, because another obligation was removed by it. The other is that it is an abrogated obligation that was removed by something else, just as another was removed by it. This is due to the statement of God, the Almighty, "And during part of the night, pray with it as an additional prayer for you. Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a position of praise." (Al-Isra': 79). So the statement of God, the Almighty, And during part of the night, pray with it as an additional prayer for you was interpreted in two ways: we pray with something other than what was obligatory from what is easy for us. Al-Shafi'i said: So it was obligatory to seek evidence from the Sunnah for one of the two meanings, so we found the Sunnah of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, indicating that there are no obligatory prayers except five. Sixth - Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr said: The well-known opinion is that the abrogation of the night prayer was for the Ummah, and the obligation remained for the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). It was said: The prescribed amount was abrogated, and the original obligation remained, like the saying of God the Almighty: Then whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal (al-Baqarah 2:196). So sacrificial animal is necessary. Similarly, there was no alternative to the night prayer, but its amount was left to the choice of the worshipper. Based on this, some people said: The night prayer is necessary, but its amount was left to the choice of the worshipper. Based on this, some people said: The obligation of the night prayer with a little remains, and this is the view of Al-Hasan. Some people said: It was abrogated completely, so the night prayer is not obligatory at all, and this is the view of Al-Shafi’i. Perhaps the obligation that remained for the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is this, which is his standing, and its amount is left to his choice. If it is proven that standing is not an obligation, then the saying of God the Almighty: So recite what is easy of it means recite if that is easy for you, and pray if you wish. Some scholars have argued that abrogation in its entirety also applies to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), as the night prayer was not obligatory for him. His statement, as a voluntary prayer for you, is interpreted as a voluntary prayer. Whoever says that the amount was abrogated and the original obligation of the night prayer remained and was then abrogated, this second abrogation occurred with the clarification of the prayer times, like the statement of God the Almighty: Establish prayer at the decline of the sun (al-Isra’ 17:78) and His statement: So exalt God when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning (Al-Rum: 17), as in the report that the addition to the five prayers is voluntary. It was also said that abrogation occurred with the statement of God the Almighty: And during part of the night, pray with it as an additional prayer for you (Al-Rum: 17), and the address to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is for the Ummah, just as the obligation of prayer, even though the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was addressed with it in the statement of God the Almighty: O you who are wrapped in garments, arise during the night (al-Isra’ 17:78), was general for him and others. It has been said that God's obligation extended beyond the Hijra and was abrogated in Medina, based on the Almighty's saying: He knows that there will be among you those who are ill and others who travel throughout the land seeking from the bounty of God and others who fight in the cause of God. Fighting was made obligatory in Medina, so based on this explanation, the times were set in Mecca. Thus, the night prayer was abrogated by the Almighty's saying: And during part of the night, pray with it as an additional prayer for you. (Al-Isra': 79). Ibn Abbas said that when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came, God's saying: Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand abrogated the obligation of the night prayer. Seventh - The Almighty’s saying: He knows that there will be among you ill Al-Akhbar 2:17. The Almighty has made clear the lightening of the night prayer, as some people are ill, and it is difficult for them to pray at night, and it is difficult for them to miss the prayer. The traveler for business may not be able to stand the night prayer, and neither is the mujahid. So God made it light for everyone for the sake of these people. The an in an sakun is a lightened form of the heavy one, meaning He knew that it would happen. Eighth: In this verse, God equated the status of those who strive in jihad with those who earn lawful money to spend on themselves and their families, and to do good and show generosity. This was evidence that earning money is equivalent to jihad, because it combines it with jihad in the cause of God. Ibrahim narrated on the authority of Alqamah who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: ‘There is no one who brings food from a land and sells it at the current price, but his status with God will be like that of the martyrs.’ Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) recited: ‘And others travel throughout the land seeking God’s bounty, and others fight in the cause of God.’” Ibn Mas’ud said: Any man who brings something to a Muslim city, patiently and seeking reward from God, and sells it at the current price, will have the status of the martyrs with God. He recited: ‘Others travel throughout the land.’” Ibn ‘Umar said: “God has not created a death for me, and I would rather die in it after death in the cause of God than dying between the forks of my saddle, seeking God’s bounty while traveling through the land.” Tawus said: He who strives for the widow and the poor is like one who fights in the way of God. It was narrated from one of the early Muslims that he was in Wasit and equipped a ship of wheat for Basra. He wrote to his agent: Sell the food on the day you enter Basra, and do not delay it until the next day. He encountered a price increase, so the merchants said to the agent: If you delay it until the end of the day, you will earn double the profit. So he delayed it until the end of the day and earned double the profit. He wrote to his friend about that, and the owner of the food wrote back: Oh man! We were content with a small profit despite our sound faith, and a crime has been committed against us. When this letter reaches you, take the money and give it in charity to the poor of Basra. I wish I could escape from hoarding with enough to cover my needs, neither for me nor for myself. It is narrated that a boy from the people of Mecca used to frequent the mosque, and Ibn Umar missed him, so he walked to his house. His mother said: He is selling some food. He met him and said: O my son! What do you have to do with the food? Why not camels? Why not cows? Why not sheep? The owner of the food loves the store, and the owner of the livestock loves the rain. Ninth - The Almighty’s saying: So recite as much of it as is easy for you. That is, pray as much as you can. So God made obligatory the night prayer as much as is easy, then He abrogated that by making the five daily prayers obligatory as mentioned above. Ibn al-Arabi said: Some people said that the obligation of the night prayer is a Sunnah in two rak’ahs of this verse. This was stated by al-Bukhari and others. He created a chapter in which he mentioned the hadith: “The devil ties three knots at the back of the head of any one of you when he sleeps, striking each knot in its place: You have a long night ahead of you, so sleep. If he wakes up and remembers God, one knot is undone. If he performs ablution, another knot is undone. If he prays, all his knots are undone, and he wakes up energetic and in a good mood. Otherwise, he wakes up evil and lazy.” He also mentioned the hadith of Samurah ibn Jundub from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) regarding a dream. He said: As for the one whose head is smashed with a stone, he learns the Qur’an but rejects it and sleeps through the prescribed prayers. And the hadith of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: A man was mentioned in the presence of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) who slept all night. He said: That is a man in whose ears the devil has urinated. Ibn al-Arabi said: These hadiths require that the general meaning of prayer be interpreted as referring to the prescribed prayer, so the general meaning is interpreted as referring to the specific meaning because it is possible for it, and the claim of the one who specifies the night prayer is dropped. In Sahih Al-Bukhari, and the wording is from Al-Bukhari: Abdullah bin Amr said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: O Abdullah, do not be like so-and-so, who used to pray at night and then stopped praying at night. Had it been obligatory, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not have approved of it, nor would he have reported anything like this about him. Rather, he would have condemned it with the utmost condemnation. In Sahih Al-Bukhari, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar, he said: During the lifetime of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), if a man had a dream, he would tell it to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). I was a young, unmarried boy, and I used to sleep in the mosque during the time of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). I saw in my sleep as if two angels took me and went with me to the Fire. It was folded up like the folding of a well, and it had two horns, and in it were people whom I recognized. I began to say, I seek refuge in God from the Fire. He said, “We met another angel, and he said to me, ‘You are not afraid.’ So I told it to Hafsa, and Hafsa told it to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he said, ‘Abdullah is a good man, if only he would pray at night.’” After that, he would only sleep a little at night. If not praying at night was a sin, the angel would not have said to him, You are not afraid. And God knows best. Tenth - If it is proven that the night prayer is not obligatory, and that his statement, So recite whatever is easy for you of the Qur’an, “So recite whatever is easy for you of it” is understood to refer to the apparent meaning of recitation in prayer, then the scholars differed as to the amount that he is obligated to recite in prayer. Malik and Ash-Shafi’i said: Al-Fatihah is not permissible to deviate from it, nor is it permissible to limit oneself to part of it. Abu Hanifa estimated it as one verse, regardless of which Surah it is in the Qur’an. He also mentioned three verses, because it is the shortest Surah. Al-Mawardi mentioned the first opinion, and Ibn Al-Arabi mentioned the second. The correct opinion is that of Malik and Ash-Shafi’i, based on what we have explained regarding Surat Al-Fatihah, the beginning of the Book, and praise be to God. It was said that what is meant by it is reciting the Qur’an outside of prayer. Al-Mawardi said: Based on this, this command in general is understood as obligatory, or recommended, but not obligatory. This is the opinion of the majority, because if it were obligatory for him to recite, then he would have been obligated to memorize it. The second is that it is obligatory, so that by reading it one may understand its miraculous nature and the proofs of Tawhid and the sending of Messengers. If one reads it and knows its miraculous nature and what it contains, he is not obligated to memorize it, because memorizing the Quran is a recommended act of worship, not an obligatory one. There are five opinions regarding the extent to which this matter of reading includes: The first is that it is the entire Quran, because God Almighty made it easy for His servants, said Ad-Dahhak. The second is that it is a third of the Quran, narrated by Jubair. The third is that it is two hundred verses, said As-Suddi. The fourth is that it is one hundred verses, said Ibn Abbas. The fifth is that it is three verses, like the shortest Surah, said Abu Khalid Al-Kinani. Eleventh - The Almighty said: And establish prayer meaning the obligatory prayer, which is the five daily prayers. And give zakat the obligatory charity on your wealth, as stated by Ikrimah and Qatadah. Al-Harith Al-Ukli said: Zakat Al-Fitr because the zakat on wealth became obligatory after that. It was also said: Voluntary charity. It was also said: All good deeds. Ibn Abbas said: Obedience to God and sincerity towards Him. Twelfth - The Almighty said: Lend to God a good loan. A good loan is one intended solely for the sake of God, with pure money. This has been explained in Surah Al-Hadid. Zayd ibn Aslam said: A good loan is spending on one’s family. Umar ibn Al-Khattab said: It is spending in the way of God. Thirteenth: The Almighty said: And whatever good you send forth for yourselves, you will find it with God. It was narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab that he had made a hais dates with milk and a poor man came to him, so he took it and gave it to him. Some of them said: This poor man does not know what this is. Umar said: But the Lord of the poor man knows what it is. It is as if he interpreted “And whatever good you send forth for yourselves, you will find it with God. It is better” meaning than what you left behind and succeeded, and than stinginess and negligence. And greater in reward Abu Hurairah said: Paradise. It is possible that it means greater in reward, because He gives him ten times for a good deed. The accusative of better and greater is the second object of you will find it and it is a separation according to the Basrans, and a pillar according to the Kufians, and has no syntactic position. Reward is a specification. And seek forgiveness from God meaning ask Him for forgiveness for your sins. Indeed, God is Forgiving of what was before repentance. Merciful to you after it, as Saeed ibn Jubayr said. I have finished the Surah [and praise be to God].
74:1: It was revealed in Mecca according to everyone. It has fifty-six verses. There are six issues First - The Almighty’s saying: O you who is wrapped up in your garments, meaning O you who has wrapped yourself up in your garments, i.e. covered yourself with them and slept. The original form is al-Mutadaththir, but the ta’ was assimilated into the dal to make them similar. Abi recited al-Mutadaththir according to the original form. Muqatil said: Most of this surah is about Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira. "And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who was one of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he was narrating - he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said while narrating about the period of revelation - he said in his hadith: (While I was walking, I heard a voice from the sky, so I raised my head, and there was the angel who had come to me in Hira sitting on a chair between the sky and the earth) The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I came from him in fear, so I returned and said: Cover me, cover me, so they covered me, and God, the Most High, revealed: {O you wrapped in your cloak! Arise and warn! And your Lord glorify! And your garments purify! And uncleanliness avoid.} ((In another narration - before prayer was made obligatory - which are idols. He said: ((Then the revelation continued.)) At-Tirmidhi also included it and said: A good and authentic hadith. Muslim said: Zuhair ibn Harb narrated to us, he said: Al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, he said: Al-Awza’i narrated to us, he said: I heard Yahya say: I asked Abu Salamah: Which of the Qur’an was revealed first? He said: {O you wrapped in your cloak!} So I said: Or ( Read) He said: I asked Jabir ibn Abdullah which of the Qur’an was revealed first? He said: O you wrapped up in a cloak. I said: Or ‘Read.’ Jabir said: “I will tell you what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) told us. He said: “I stayed in Hira’ for a month, and when I had finished my stay, I dismounted and went into the valley. I was called and looked in front of me, behind me, to my right and to my left, but I did not see anyone. Then I was called again, but I did not see anyone. Then I was called again, and I raised my head and saw that he was on the Throne in the air - meaning Gabriel (peace and blessings of God be upon him). A violent tremor overcame me. I came to Khadija and said: ‘Cover me.’ So they covered me and poured water over me. Then God, the Almighty, revealed: ‘O you wrapped up in a cloak, arise and warn. And your Lord glorify. And your garments purify.’” Narrated by Al-Bukhari. He said in it: “So I came to Khadija and said: ‘Cover me.’ They poured cold water over me. Then the following was revealed: ‘O you wrapped up in a cloak, arise Ibn al-Arabi said: Some of the scholars said that something happened to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from Uqbah ibn Rabi’ah, so he returned home distressed, became anxious and lay down, so “O you wrapped up in your cloak” was revealed. This is false. Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr said: It was said that he heard the words of the infidels of Mecca, You are a magician, and he felt distressed and feverish because of that, so he wrapped himself in his clothes, and God the Most High said: Arise and warn, meaning do not think about what they say, and convey the message to them. It was said: Abu Lahab, Abu Sufyan, Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira, Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith, Umayya bin Khalaf, Al-As bin Wa’il and Mut’am bin Adi met and said: The Arab delegations have gathered during the days of Hajj, and they are asking about the matter of Muhammad, and you have differed in reporting him. Some say he is a madman, another says he is a soothsayer, and another says he is a poet. The Arabs know that all of these things cannot be combined in one man, so they named Muhammad with one name that they agree upon, and the Arabs call him by it. A man among them stood up and said: Poet. Al-Walid said: I heard the words of An-Abras, Umayya bin Abi Al-Salt, and what is similar to the words of Muhammad, the words of one of them. They said: Soothsayer. He said: The soothsayer speaks the truth and lies, but Muhammad never lied. Another stood up and said: A madman. He said: A madman strangles people, but Muhammad never strangled. Al-Walid went home, and they said: Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira has become an apostate. Abu Jahl entered upon him and said: What is the matter with you, O Abu Abd Shams? The Quraysh are gathering something to give you. They claim that you protested and became an apostate. Al-Walid said: I have no need for that, but I thought about Muhammad, so I said: What happens to a magician? It was said: He brings separation between a father and his son, between a brother and his brother, and between a woman and her husband. So I said: He is a magician. This spread among the people and they shouted: Muhammad is a magician. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) returned to his house sad and covered himself with a velvet blanket, and O you who are wrapped up in your cloak was revealed. Ikrimah said that the meaning of O you who are wrapped up in your cloak is the one wrapped up in prophethood and its burdens. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is a far-fetched metaphor, because he had not yet prophesied. And although it was the first verse of the Quran, he was not able to do it after it was the second to be revealed. Second - The Almighty’s saying: O you wrapped up in garments: This is a kind address from the Generous One to the Beloved, as He addressed him in his state and described him by his description. He did not say O Muhammad or O so-and-so, so that he would sense the gentleness and tenderness from his Lord, as mentioned previously in Surat Al-Muzzammil. Similar to it is “the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Ali when he slept in the mosque: (Get up, O Abu Turab), and he had gone out in anger on behalf of Fatimah, may God be pleased with her, so his cloak fell off and dust got on him,” narrated by Al-Muslim. Similar to it is “his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Hudhayfah on the night of the Trench: (Get up, O Noman),” which was mentioned previously.
74:2: Third - The Almighty's saying: Arise and warn, meaning frighten the people of Mecca and warn them of the punishment if they do not submit. It was said: The warning here is informing them of his prophethood, because it is the introduction to the message. It was also said: It is calling them to monotheism, because that is what it is intended for. Al-Farra' said: Arise and pray and command the prayer.
74:3: Fourth - The Almighty said: And your Lord, so glorify Him meaning your Master, your Owner and the One who set right your affairs, so glorify Him. He described Him as being greater than to have a wife or a son. In a hadith, they said: How do you begin your prayer? So the verse: And your Lord, so glorify Him was revealed, meaning He described Him as being greater. Ibn Al-Arabi said: Although this statement generally implies glorifying the prayer, what is meant by it is glorification, sanctification and sanctification, to remove rivals and idols besides Him, and do not take as a guardian other than Him, and do not worship other than Him, and do not see any action for anyone other than Him, and no blessing except from Him. It has been narrated that Abu Sufyan said on the day of UHud 11:Hubal is higher than this. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Say ‘God is higher and more glorious.’ This expression has become, according to Islamic law, the standard for glorifying all acts of worship, including the call to prayer, prayer, and remembrance, by saying: God is greater. This is also the standard for the Prophet’s, may God bless him and grant him peace, expressions in general terms, in several instances, including his saying: Its prohibition is glorification, and its permission is the taslim. Islamic law requires, according to its custom, what it requires by its generality, and among its instances are the times of declaring one’s intention to slaughter for God, to free Him from polytheism, to announce His name in the ritual, and to single out what He has legislated for the purpose of commanding the shedding of blood. I said: It was mentioned in the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah that this phrase Allahu Akbar is what is used in prayer, as transmitted from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And in the interpretation: When the words of God Almighty were revealed: And glorify your Lord, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up and said: God is Great, so Khadiha glorified God, and she knew that it was a revelation from God Almighty. Al-Qushayri mentioned this. Fifth - The letter fa in the Almighty’s saying: And glorify your Lord is used to mean a response to a conditional sentence, just as it is used in fa’andhir, meaning arise and warn, and arise and glorify your Lord, as stated by Az-Zajjaj. Ibn Az-Zajjaj said: Ibn Jinni said: It is like you saying Zaidan fa-stribe, meaning Zaidan, strike, so the fa is redundant.
74:4: Sixth - The Almighty's saying: And your clothing purify There are eight opinions on this: One of them is that what is meant by clothing is action. The second is the heart. The third is the soul. The fourth is the body. The fifth is the family. The sixth is character. The seventh is religion. The eighth is the clothing worn according to the apparent meaning. Whoever goes with the first opinion said: The interpretation of the verse is and your work, so improve, as said by Mujahid and Ibn Zayd. Mansour narrated on the authority of Abu Razin who said: He says and your work, so improve, he said: And if a man's work is bad, they say that so-and-so has bad clothes, and if his work is good, they say that so-and-so has clean clothes, and something similar was narrated by Al-Suddi. And from it is the saying of the poet: No, Amer bin Jahm went on Hajj wearing dark clothes. Including what was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: (A person will regret the two garments he died in) meaning his good and bad deeds, as mentioned by Al-Mawardi. Whoever adopted the second opinion said: The interpretation of the verse is and purify your heart, as stated by Ibn Abbas and Saeed bin Jubair, and its evidence is the statement of Imru’ al-Qais: So, remove my clothes from your clothes and let them slip away My heart is from your heart. Al-Mawardi said: They have two interpretations of this verse: The first means and your heart, so purify it from sin and transgressions, as stated by Ibn Abbas and Qatadah. The second means and your heart, so purify it from treachery, meaning do not betray, lest your clothes become filthy. This was narrated from Ibn Abbas, and he cited as evidence the words of Ghailan ibn Salamah Al-Thaqafi: By the grace of God, I do not wear the garment of an immoral person, nor do I cover myself with the garment of treachery. And whoever adopted the third opinion said: The interpretation of the verse is and purify yourself, meaning from sins. The Arabs use the word clothes to refer to the soul, as Ibn Abbas said. And from this is the saying of Antarah: I pierced his clothes with a long spear. The generous man is not forbidden to use spears. Imru' al-Qais said: So separate my clothes from your clothes and let them fall off He said: The clothes of the Banu Awf are pure and clean, and their faces are as white as the traveler's. Any soul of Bani Awf. And whoever goes with the fourth opinion said: The interpretation of the verse is and your body purify, meaning from apparent sins. And among what was narrated from the Arabs in referring to the body with clothes is the saying of Layla, and she mentioned camels: They threw her in light clothes, so you see no resemblance to her except to the frightened ostrich That is, they rode it and threw it themselves. Whoever goes with the fifth opinion said: The interpretation of the verse is And your family, purify them from sins through preaching and discipline. The Arabs call family a garment, clothing, and lower garment. God Almighty said: They are clothing for you and you are clothing for them. (al-Baqarah 2:187) Al-Mawardi: They have two interpretations of the verse: The first means And your women, purify, by choosing the chaste believing women. The second means enjoying them in the vagina but not the anus, during purity and not during menstruation. This was narrated by Ibn Bahr. Whoever goes with the sixth opinion said: The interpretation of the verse is And your creation is good. This was said by Al-Hasan and Al-Qurazi, because the creation of man includes his conditions as his clothes include himself. The poet said: Yahya is not to be blamed for bad character, Yahya is pure and free Any good morals. And whoever goes with the seventh opinion said: The interpretation of the verse is: And purify your religion. And in the two Sahihs, on his authority, peace be upon him, he said: (And I saw people wearing clothes, some of which reached the breasts and some less, and I saw Umar ibn al-Khattab wearing a lower garment that he was dragging) They said: O Messenger of God, what is the interpretation of that? He said: (Religion) Ibn Wahb narrated from Malik that he said: I do not like to read the Qur’an except in prayer and in the mosques, not on the road. God the Almighty said: And your garments purify Malik meant that he used religion as a metaphor for clothes. Abdullah ibn Nafi’ narrated from Abu Bakr ibn Abdul Aziz ibn Abdullah ibn Umar ibn al-Khattab from Malik ibn Anas regarding the words of God the Almighty: And your garments purify meaning do not wear them on treachery. From this is the saying of Abu Kabsha: The clothes of Banu Awf are pure and clean, and their faces are as white as the traveler's. Meaning by the purity of their clothes: their safety from filth, and meaning by the radiance of their faces is their purity from forbidden things, or their beauty in creation, or both, said Ibn al-Arabi. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: Do not wear your clothes out of falsehood, injustice, treachery, or sin, said Ikrimah. And from this is the saying of the poet: I blame a pilgrim in dark clothes. That is, he has defiled it with sins. Al-Nabigha said: The soft sandals are good. Their reservations are good. They live with basil on the day of the sabbath. And whoever goes to the eighth opinion said: What is meant by it are the clothes worn, so they have four aspects in its interpretation: The first of them - its meaning is and your clothes, so clean them, and from it is the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: The clothes of Bani Awf are pure and clean Second: “And your garments, roll them up and shorten them, for shortening the garments keeps them further from impurity. If they are laid flat on the ground, there is no guarantee that they will not be contaminated, as stated by Al-Zajjaj and Tawus. Third: “And your garments purify” from impurity with water, as stated by Muhammad ibn Sirin, Ibn Zayd and the jurists. Fourth: Do not wear your garments except from lawful earnings so that they will be purified from what is unlawful. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Do not let the garments that you wear come from impure earnings. Ibn Al-Arabi, mentioning some of what we have mentioned, said: It is not impossible to interpret the verse in general terms, both literally and figuratively. And if we interpret it to refer to the garments that are known to be pure, then it includes two meanings: First: shortening the hems, because if they are let down they become impure. For this reason, Umar ibn Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him said to a young boy from the Ansar when he saw his hem hanging down: Lift up your garment, for it is more pious, purer and more lasting. And the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: ((The garment of the believer should reach the middle of his shin. There is no blame upon him for what is between it and the ankles. But whatever is below that is in the Fire.)) The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made the limit for wearing the garment to the ankles and threatened what is below it with the Fire. So what about men who let their hems hang down and lengthen their garments, then they take pains to lift them up with their hands? This is a state of arrogance and a lead to conceit. The worst thing about it is that they disobey, become impure, and associate themselves with someone whom God has not placed anyone else with Him nor associated anyone else with Him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: (God does not look at the one who drags his garment out of arrogance) “And the wording of the Sahih is: (Whoever drags his garment out of pride, God will not look at him on the Day of Resurrection) Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God! One of my garments drags unless I take care of it? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: (I am not one of those who do that out of pride) So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prohibited it in general terms, but he excluded Abu Bakr. Thus, the lowly meant to treat the high among themselves, but that is not for them. The second meaning is to wash it from impurity, which is apparent from it, and its art is correct. Al-Mahdawi and some scholars have used it as evidence for the obligation of purity of the garment. Ibn Sirin and Ibn Zayd said: Do not pray except in clean garments. Al-Shafi’i used it as evidence for the obligation of purity of the garment. It is not obligatory according to Malik and the people of Medina, and the same applies to purity of the body. This is indicated by the consensus on the permissibility of praying with stones without washing. This statement has been fully discussed in Surah Bara’ah.
74:5: God the Almighty says: And avoid the abomination. Mujahid and Ikrimah said: He means idols. The evidence for this is the statement of God the Almighty: So avoid the abomination of idols (al-Hajj 22:30). This was said by Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd. Ibn Abbas also said: And avoid the sin, meaning leave it. Mughirah also narrated from Ibrahim Al-Nakha'i who said: Abomination is sin. Qatadah said: Abomination is Asaaf and Na'ilah, two idols that were near the Ka'bah. It was also said: Abomination is punishment, assuming the subject is omitted, meaning: And avoid the action of abomination, or the action that leads to punishment. The root of abomination is punishment. God the Almighty said: If You should remove the punishment from us, we will surely believe in you (al-A’raf 7:134) and He the Almighty said: So We sent upon them a punishment from the sky (al-A’raf 7:162). So the idols were called abomination because they lead to punishment. The common reading is rajz with a kasra on the ra'. Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Mujahid, Ibn Muhaisin, and Hafs on the authority of Asim read and the punishment with a damma on the ra’. They are two dialects like dhikr and dhikr. Abu Al-Aaliyah, Al-Rabi’, and Al-Kisa’i said: The rajz with a damma means the idol, and with a kasra means impurity and disobedience. Al-Kisa’i also said: With a damma means the idol and with a kasra means the torment. Al-Suddi said: The rajz with a fatha on the ra’ means the threat.
74:6: First - The Almighty's saying: And do not bestow a favor, expecting to receive more in return. This has eleven interpretations. First - Do not bestow a favor upon your Lord by bearing the burdens of prophethood, like someone who considers his bearing too much because of someone else. Second - Do not give a gift seeking to gain something better in return. This was stated by Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, and Qatadah. Ad-Dahhak said: God forbade the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) because he was commanded with the most noble of manners and the most sublime of character, and He permitted it for his ummah. This was also stated by Mujahid. Third - Also from Mujahid: Do not be too weak to expect to receive more in goodness, as you would say, A weak rope. The evidence for this is Ibn Mas'ud's reading: And do not bestow a favor, expecting to receive more in return. Fourth - Also from Mujahid and Ar-Rabi': Do not think your action is too great in your eyes, expecting to receive more in goodness, for it is from the blessings God has bestowed upon you. Ibn Kaysan said: Do not consider your action too great, for it is from God's blessings upon you. Fifth - Al-Hassan said: Do not bestow your deeds upon God, lest you think they are too much. Sixth - Do not bestow prophethood and the Quran upon people, lest you take a reward from them, lest you think it is too much. Seventh - Al-Qurazi said: Do not give your money out of favor. Eighth - Zaid bin Aslam said: If you are given a gift, give it to your Lord. Ninth - Do not say, I prayed but I was not answered. Tenth - Do not perform an act of obedience and seek its reward, but be patient until God is the One who rewards you for it. Eleventh - Do not do good to show off to people. Second - Although these sayings were intended, the most evident of them is the saying of Ibn Abbas: Do not give in order to take more money than you were given. It is said: I bestowed such-and-such on someone, meaning I gave him something. A gift is also called a manah, so it is as if he ordered that his gifts be from God, not in anticipation of a reward from creation for them, because she, peace be upon her, did not collect the world, and for this reason he said: (I have nothing of what God has bestowed upon you except one-fifth, and one-fifth is returned to you.) And whatever was left over from his family’s expenses was spent on the interests of the Muslims. For this reason, he was not inherited from, because he did not have the ability to save or acquire anything for himself. God Almighty protected him from desiring anything of this world. For this reason, charity was forbidden to him, but gifts were permitted to him, so he would accept them and adhere to them. He said: (If I were invited to a leg, I would respond, and if a forearm were given to me, I would accept it.) Ibn al-Arabi used to accept it as a Sunnah and did not consider it too much according to Islamic law. If he did not give a gift that the rich would consider too much, then it is more appropriate to avoid it, because it is a door to humiliation. Similarly, the statement of those who said that its meaning is do not give a gift expecting its reward, because waiting is related to greed, and that is within its scope by virtue of abstention. God Almighty said to him: {And do not strain your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to categories of them—the splendor of worldly life by which We test them. And the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting.} (Ta-Ha 20:131) This is permissible for all creation, because it is from the enjoyment of this world, and seeking Earning and multiplying through it. As for the one who said that he meant by it work, i.e. do not boast of your work to God, thinking it is too much, then this is correct, because if the son of Adam were to obey God throughout his life without slackening, he would not have been able to express some gratitude for God’s blessings. Third - The Almighty’s saying: And do not bestow favors. The general reading is showing the doubling. Abu Al-Samal Al-Adawi, Ashhab Al-Uqayli and Al-Hasan read (and do not bestow favors) with an open assimilated letter. (You ask for more): The general reading is in the nominative case and it is in the meaning of the state. You say: Zaid came running, meaning do not give something that is estimated to be taken in its place with something greater than it. Al-Hasan read it in the jussive mood as an answer to the prohibition, which is bad because it is not an answer. It is possible that it is a substitute for (be given favors) as if he said: Do not ask for more. Abu Hatim rejected it and said: Because favor is not asking for more, so it is substituted for it. It is possible that it was sukoon for lightening like ‘udhud. Or it is considered the state of stopping. Al-A’mash and Yahya read (you ask for more) in the accusative case, thinking the lam of ki, as if he said: Do not ask for favors in order to ask for more. It was said: It is with the omission of (that) like his saying: Oh you who deter, come to the battlefield This is supported by the reading of Ibn Masoud: (And do not bestow favor, lest you should ask for more) Al-Kisa’i said: If Al-Kisa’i said: If (that) is deleted, the word is raised and the meaning is the same.
