It is possible that the word man means enumerating the blessings of the one who has been bestowed, so we refer to the second opinion, and it is supported by the statement of God Almighty: {And do not invalidate your charities with reminders or injury} (al-Baqarah 2:264), and it may be intended in this verse. And God knows best.
74:7: The Almighty said: And for your Lord be patient meaning for your Master and Owner, be patient in performing His obligations and worshipping Him. Mujahid said: With what you have been harmed with. Ibn Zayd said: You have undertaken a great matter, fighting the Arabs and the Persians, so be patient with it for the sake of God. It was also said: Be patient under the resources of fate for the sake of God Almighty. It was also said: Be patient with the affliction, because He tests His friends and chosen ones. It was also said: With His commands and prohibitions. It was also said: With separation from family and homeland.
74:8: The Almighty said: And when the trumpet is blown when the trumpet is blown. The trumpet is a passive participle from the verb naqr, as if it refers to that which is usually struck in it to make a sound. Naqr in Arabic speech means the sound, and from this is the saying of Imru' al-Qais: Lower it by clicking on what you have raised and raise it with a side that is not hidden or downcast They say: We acknowledge the man’s name when he calls him specifically with his call. Mujahid and others said: It is like the shape of a trumpet, and he means the second blast. It was also said: The first, because it is the beginning of the general, tremendous intensity. We have already discussed this in detail in An-Naml and Al-An’am and in the book At-Tadhkirah. Praise be to God. Abu Hibban said: Our mother Zarara bin Awfa, when he reached When the trumpet is blown, he fell dead.
74:9: God Almighty says: That day will be a difficult day. That is, that day will be a difficult day.
74:10: The Almighty said: For the disbelievers it is not easy meaning it is not easy nor simple, because their knots will not be undone except by a knot stronger than it, unlike the believing monotheists who have sinned, for they will be undone by something lighter than it until they enter Paradise by the mercy of God the Almighty. And (that day) is accusative, meaning that that will be a difficult day that day. It was said: it is genitive, meaning that that will be on that day. It was said: it is permissible for it to be nominative, but it is built on the fat-ha because it is added to something that is not established.
74:11: The Almighty said: Leave Me and he whom I created alone. "Leave Me" means leave Me, and it is a word of threat and intimidation. "And he whom You created means leave Me and he whom I created alone, so alone" in this case is a case of the omitted object pronoun, meaning I created him alone, he had no wealth or children, then I gave him after that what I gave him. The commentators say that he is Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah Al-Makhzumi, even though people were created like him. He was specifically mentioned because he was known for his ingratitude and for harming the Messenger (peace be upon him), and he was called Al-Walid among his people. Ibn Abbas said: Al-Walid used to say: I am the only one, the son of the only one, I have no equal among the Arabs, and Abu Al-Mughirah has no equal, and he was called Al-Walid, so God the Almighty said: "Leave Me and he whom I created according to his claim, alone", not that God the Almighty confirmed that he was alone. Some people said: The Almighty’s saying: alone refers to the Almighty Lord in two meanings: One of them: Leave me alone with him, and I will reward you in taking revenge on him for every avenger. The second: I am the only one who created him and no one shared with me in him, so I will destroy him and I do not need a helper in his destruction. So, alone in this case is a state of the subject pronoun, which is the ta in I created. The first is the saying of Mujahid, meaning I created him alone in his mother’s womb, having no property or children, then I bestowed blessings upon him but he denied them. So, his saying alone in this case refers to the newborn, meaning he had nothing, so I possessed him. It was said: He intended by this to indicate to him that he will be resurrected alone, as he left behind someone alone. It was also said: The only one is the one whose father is not known, and the newborn was known to be an adopted child, as we mentioned in the Almighty’s saying: After that, he became an adulterer (al-Qalam 68:13), and this is also in the description of the newborn.
74:12: God the Almighty said: And granted him abundant wealth meaning I granted him and gave him abundant wealth, which is what Al-Walid had between Makkah and Taif of camels, laps, livestock, gardens, slaves and female slaves, this is what Ibn Abbas used to say. Mujahid said: The yield of a thousand dinars, said Saeed bin Jubair and Ibn Abbas also. Qatada said: Six thousand dinars. Muqatil: He had an orchard whose bounty never ceased, winter or summer. Umar may God be pleased with him said: And granted him abundant wealth the yield of month after month. An-Nu'man bin Salim: Land in which he cultivates. Al-Qushayri: It seems more apparent that it is a reference to that which his livelihood never ceases, but rather continues, such as crops, livestock and trade.
74:13: God the Almighty says: And sons as witnesses meaning present and never absent from him in any action. Mujahid and Qatadah said: They were ten. It was also said: Twelve, as said by As-Suddi and Ad-Dahhak. Ad-Dahhak said: Seven were born in Makkah and five were born in Taif. Saeed ibn Jubayr said: They were thirteen sons. Muqatil said: They were seven, all men, three of whom embraced Islam: Khalid, Hisham, and Al-Walid ibn Al-Walid. He said: Al-Walid's wealth and children continued to decrease after the revelation of this verse until he died. It was also said: Witnesses, meaning that whenever he was mentioned, they were mentioned with him, as said by Ibn Abbas. It was also said: Witnesses, meaning they had become like him in witnessing what he witnessed and performing what he performed. The first is the statement of As-Suddi, meaning present in Makkah and never departing from it.
74:14: The Almighty said: And I made his livelihood easy for him meaning I made his life easy for him, until he settled in his town, comfortable and at ease, and he could make up his own mind. The word preparation among the Arabs means preparation and readiness, and from this comes the word cradle of a child. Ibn Aba' said: And I made his livelihood easy for him meaning I made the space between Yemen and Syria wide for him, and Mujahid said the same. Mujahid also said in And I made his livelihood easy for him that it means some money on top of some, as a bed is made wide.
74:15: God the Almighty says: Then he desires that I should increase meaning, after all of this, Al-Walid desires that I should increase his wealth and children. No meaning that this will not happen while he is ungrateful for the blessings. Al-Hasan and others said: Then he desires that I should admit him into Paradise. Al-Walid used to say: If Muhammad is truthful, then Paradise was created only for me. God the Almighty said in response to him and as a refutation of him: No meaning, I will not increase him. He continued to see the decrease in his wealth and children until he died. The then in God the Almighty's saying: Then he desires is not the then which indicates sequence, but rather it expresses amazement. It is like His saying: "And He made darkness and light. Then those who disbelieve equate others with their Lord." (Al-An'am 6:1) This is like saying: I gave you, then you treat me unfairly, as if amazed by that. It was said: He desires that I should leave that in consequence. This is because he used to say: Muhammad is cut off, meaning he is cut off and his memory will cease with his death. He thought that his provision would not be cut off by his death. It was also said: Then he hoped that I would help him in his disbelief.
74:16: The Almighty said: No indeed! He was obstinate towards Our signs. "No indeed" is a break in the hope of what he was hoping for in addition, so it is connected to the first statement. It was said: "No indeed" means truly and is a beginning. "He meaning Al-Walid was obstinate towards Our signs" meaning he was obstinate towards the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what he brought. It is said: he was obstinate, so he is on my side, like someone who sits, so he is a sitter, said Mujahid. And when it is pronounced with a kasra, it means he contradicted and rejected the truth while he knows it, so he is obstinate and stubborn. The stubborn is the camel that deviates from the path and turns away from the intended path. The plural is when it is pronounced with a bow and bows. Abu Ubaidah recited the words of Al-Harithi: If you ride, put me in the middle, for I am old and cannot stand stubbornness. Abu Saleh said: Stubborn means distant. The poet said: I see us in a state where we are separated, and I intend to be away from each other. Separation is stubborn. Qatada: denying. Muqatil: turning away. Ibn Abbas: denying. It was said: It is the one who openly declares his aggression. Mujahid also said: Deviating from the truth, defying it, turning away from it. The meanings are all close. The Arabs say: with a man if he is stubborn and exceeds his ability. And the stubborn camel: is the one who does not mix with camels, it is from one side. And a stubborn man is that is why he used to be alone and not mix with people. And stubbornness comes from tyranny. A stubborn vein: if its blood does not stop, all of this is one analogy and it has been mentioned in Surah Ibrahim. The plural of stubborn is with, like a loaf of bread and a loaf of bread.
74:17: The Almighty said: I will tire him out meaning I will make him suffer. Ibn Abbas used to say: I will force him, and exhaustion in Arabic means that a person is forced to do something. Up: (("As-Sau'ud: A mountain of fire that one climbs for seventy autumns, then falls back into it forever.")) Narrated by Sa'id al-Khudri from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). At-Tirmidhi recorded it and said that it is a strange hadith. Atiyyah narrated from Abu Sa'id who said: It is a rock in Hell. When they place their hands on it, it melts, but when they lift it up, it returns. He said: He will reach the top in forty years, and he will be pulled by those in front of him with chains and struck by whips from behind, until when he reaches the top, he will be thrown to the bottom, and that will be his habit forever. This meaning was previously mentioned in Surah Say, 'It has been revealed.' In the interpretation: It is a smooth rock that he is tasked with climbing. When he reaches the top of it, there is a slope in Hell, and he will stand and fall for a thousand years before reaching the bottom of Hell. He will be burned seventy times each day, and then he will be recreated anew. Ibn Abbas said: The meaning is: I will burden him with hardship and torment in which he will have no relief. A similar statement was narrated by al-Hasan and Qatadah. It was said: His soul ascended to death, even if death did not follow him, to be tormented from within his body as he was tormented from outside.
74:18: God the Almighty says: He thought and estimated meaning Al-Walid thought about the matter of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the Quran. He estimated means he prepared the speech in his mind. The Arabs say: He prepared something if he made it ready. That is because when the verse "Ha Meem. * The revelation of the Book is from God, the Exalted in Might, the Knowing" was revealed to him until His saying: To Him is the final destination (Ghafir 40:1-3), Al-Walid heard him reciting it and said: By God, I have heard from him speech that is not from the speech of humans or jinn. It has a sweetness and a freshness, its upper part is fruitful and its lower part is abundant. It is high and nothing is higher than it. No human being says this. Then the Quraysh said: Al-Walid has become a fool so that you may fool all of the Quraysh. Al-Walid was called the flower of the Quraysh. Abu Jahl said: I will suffice you against him. So he went to him sad. He said to him: Why do I see you sad? He said to him: Why should I not be sad while the Quraysh are collecting money for you to support you in your old age and they claim that you have embellished Muhammad’s speech and you go to Ibn Abi Kabshah and Ibn Abi Quhafah to take from their leftover food. Al-Walid became angry and arrogant and said: I need to break Muhammad and his companion and you know the value of my wealth. I have no need of Al-Lat and Al-Uzza. You only claim that Muhammad is crazy. Have you ever seen him choke? They said: No, by God. He said: And you claim that he is a poet. Have you ever seen him recite poetry? They said: No, by God. He said: So you claim that he is a liar. Have you ever experienced him lying? They said: No, by God. He said: So you claim that he is a soothsayer. Have you ever seen him practice soothsaying? We have seen soothsayers perform rhyming prose and intonation. Have you ever seen him do the same? They said: No, by God. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was called the Truthful and Trustworthy because of his great truthfulness. The Quraysh said to Al-Walid: What is that? He thought to himself, then looked, then frowned, and said: He is nothing but a magician! Haven't you seen him separate a man from his family, his children, and his clients?! This is what God Almighty says: He thought - that is, about the matter of Muhammad and the Qur'an - and determined in himself what he could say about them.
74:19: The Almighty said: Then he killed meaning he cursed. Some of the people of interpretation said: Its meaning is that he subdued and overcame, and everything that is humiliated is killed. The poet said: Your eyes did not shed tears except to fire your arrows at the tenths of a murdered heart. Al-Zuhri said: It was tortured, and it is a type of supplication. How was it decreed? Some people said: How is an expression of amazement, as one says to a man whose actions you are amazed at: How did you do this? This is what He said: See how they set forth for you examples (al-Isra’ 17:48).
74:20: The Almighty says: Then he was killed meaning he was cursed with a curse after a curse. It was also said: he was killed with a type of punishment, then he was killed with another type of punishment. How it was decreed meaning in whatever way it was decreed.
74:21: God Almighty says: Then he looked at what would prevent or repel the truth.
74:22: The Almighty said: Then he frowned meaning he frowned at the faces of the believers. This is because when he forced the Quraysh to say what he forced them to say about Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, that he was a magician, he passed by a group of Muslims, and they invited him to Islam, so he frowned at them. It was said: He frowned and frowned at the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, when he invited him. Al-Abs, in the lightened form, is the source of ‘abasa, ya’basan, ‘absan, and ‘abusan: if he frowned. Al-Abs is what clings to the tails of camels from their dung and urine. Abu al-Najm said: As if on their tails were the horns of a deer from the frown of summer. And his face turned dark means his face became pale and his color changed. This was said by Qatada and Al-Suddi. From this is the saying of Bishr bin Abi: We woke up in the morning, and the Jafars came to Shahba, gathered together as a family. Another said: I was disturbed by her aversion and her turning away from my needs and her stubbornness. It was said: The appearance of a frown on the face after the conversation, and the appearance of pimples on the face before the conversation. Some people said: (Basr) means stopping, neither advancing nor delaying. They said: And this is what the people of Yemen say when a ship stops, neither coming nor going: The ship has stopped, and has become absar, meaning it has stopped and we have become absar. The Arabs say: A face that is basr between the pimples: if it has changed and become black.
74:23: The Almighty says: Then he turned away meaning he turned away and went to his family. And he was arrogant meaning he was too proud to believe. It was also said: he turned away from faith and was arrogant when he was called to it.
74:24: The Almighty said: He said, ‘This’ meaning, what is this that Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, brought is nothing but magic that is passed on’ meaning, he passes it on to others. Magic is deception. Its explanation was presented in Surah Al-Baqarah. Some people said: Magic is presenting falsehood in the guise of truth. Atharah is the source of your saying: I passed on the hadith, atharhu, if you mentioned it from someone else. From this it was said: a hadith that is passed on, meaning it is passed on by generations from generations. Imru’ al-Qais said: Even if it came to me from someone other than him, the wound of the tongue is like the wound of the hand I would have said what the hand of the support still leaves behind. He means: the end of time. Al-A'sha said: What you have argued about is clear to the listener and the one who follows it.
74:25: The Almighty said: This is nothing but the word of a human being. Meaning, this is nothing but the speech of created beings, with which hearts are deceived as they are deceived by magic. Al-Suddi said: They mean that it is the words of Abu Al-Yusr, a slave of Banu Al-Hadrami, who used to sit with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, so they attributed to him that he learned it from him. It was also said that he meant that he received it from the people of Babylon. It was also said that it was from Musaylimah. It was also said that it was from Adi Al-Hadrami the soothsayer. It was also said that he received it from those who had claimed prophethood before him, so he followed their example. Abu Saeed Al-Darir said: This is nothing but a matter of magic that is passed on, i.e., it is inherited.
74:26: The Almighty said: I will cast him into Hellfire meaning I will put him into Hellfire so that he may suffer its heat. It is called Saqar from the sun's saqaratuhu meaning it melted, seared, and scorched the majority of his face. It is not declined for the purpose of definition or reprimand. Ibn Abbas said: It is the sixth level of Hellfire. Abu Hurairah narrated: "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ((Moses asked his Lord, "O Lord, which of Your servants is the poorest?" He said: "The companion of Saqar")) Al-Tha'labi mentioned it.
74:27: The Almighty says: And what will make you know what Hellfire is? This is an exaggeration in describing it, meaning, And what will make you know what it is? It is a word of glorification.
74:28: The Almighty said: It leaves nothing and spares nothing meaning, It leaves nothing of them except a bone, flesh, or blood, without burning them. The wording was repeated for emphasis. It was also said: It leaves nothing of them, then they will be created anew, so It leaves nothing of them and spares nothing of them from being burned like this ever again. Mujahid said: It leaves nothing of them alive and spares nothing dead, it burns them every time they are renewed. Al-Suddi said: It leaves nothing of them alive and spares nothing of them from being dead.
74:29: The Almighty said: A glaring light upon mankind meaning changing, from lahahu if it changed him. The general reading is (lawahah) in the nominative case as an adjective for (Saqar), in His statement: And what will make you know what is Saqar? Atiyah Al-Awfi, Nasr bin Asim, and Isa bin Omar read (lawahah) in the accusative case as a specification, for the purpose of intimidation. Abu Razin said: Their faces will be scorched by a glare that will make them blacker than night, and Mujahid said the same. The Arabs say lahahu al-bard, al-har, al-sickness, and al-hazn: if it changed him, and from this is the saying of the poet: You say, What happened to you, traveler? My cousin, the hot winds have caught up with me. Another said: Hind was surprised when she saw me pale, saying, Something painted by the heavens. And Ru'bah ibn al-'Ajaj said: A board from him after a body and a stump, your lean waving is folded for the race It was said: The word lawh means intense thirst. It is said: Thirst became intense and changed him. The meaning is that it is thirsty for the people of Al-Bishr, meaning for its inhabitants. Al-Akhfash said this, and he recited: She split me on a board of water, a drink that God gave her, the generous ones, to drink. Meaning by lawh is intense thirst, and tah means thirst. Raham is the plural of rahmah kasra, which is a light rain, and warhamat is the cloud that brings raham. Ibn Abbas said: Lawahah means it appears to people from a distance of five hundred years. Al-Hasan and Ibn Kaysan said: Hell appears to them until they see it with their own eyes, similar to: And Hellfire will be brought forth to the deviators (Ash-Shu’ara’: 91). There are two interpretations regarding bashar: One of them is that it is the human beings of the people of Hell, as said by Al-Akhfash and the majority. The second is that it is the plural of bashara, which is the visible skin of a human being, as said by Mujahid and Qatadah. The plural of bashar is abshar, and this is according to the first interpretation. As for the interpretation of Ibn Abbas, it only applies to people, not skins, because it is from laha the word for shining, which means to flash.
74:30: The Almighty says: Nineteen over it meaning nineteen angels over Saqar will throw its people into it. Then it was said: Over the Fire as a whole are nineteen angels who are its keepers, Malik and eighteen angels. It is possible that the nineteen are captains, or it is possible that the nineteen angels are specific. This is what most commentators agree with. Al-Tha'labi said: This is not denied, because if one angel takes the souls of all creation, then it is more likely that there will be nineteen over the punishment of some creation. Ibn Jurayj said: "The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) described the keepers of Hell and said: ((Their eyes are like lightning, and their mouths are like rocks. They drag their hair. One of them has the strength of the two heavy burdens. One of them drives the nation with a mountain on his neck, so he throws them into the Fire, and the mountain is thrown over them.)) I said: Ibn Al-Mubarak said: Hammad bin Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Azraq bin Qais, on the authority of a man from Banu Tamim, who said: We were with Abu Al-Awwam, and he recited this verse: “And what will make you know what Hellfire is? It leaves nothing behind, nor spares. A scourge for humanity. Over it are nineteen.” He said: What is nineteen? Nineteen thousand angels, or nineteen angels? I said: No, rather nineteen angels. He said: How do you know that? I said: Because God, the Almighty, said: And We did not make their number except as a trial for those who disbelieve. He said: You are right. They are nineteen angels, in the hand of each of them is a hammer with two branches, and he strikes with one blow and with it seventy thousand are thrown into the Fire. Amr bin Dinar said: Each one of them pushes into Hell at one time more than Rabi’ah. Some Jews said to some of the companions of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: Does your Prophet know the number of the keepers of Hell? They said: We do not know until we ask our Prophet. A man came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Muhammad, your companions were defeated today. He said: And how were they defeated? He said: “The Jews asked them: ‘Does your Prophet know the number of the keepers of Hell?’ He said: ‘What did they say?’ He said: “They said: ‘We do not know until we ask our Prophet.’” He said: “Are people defeated when they are asked about something they do not know and they say: ‘We do not know until we ask our Prophet?’ But they asked their Prophet and said: ‘Show us God openly! Bring me the enemies of God! I will ask them about the soil of Paradise, which is the dirham.” So they came and said: O Abu al-Qasim, how many are the keepers of Hell? He said: This way and this way. One time ten and another time nine. They said: Yes. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to them: What is the soil of Paradise? They were silent for a while, then they said: Bread, O Abu al-Qasim? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Bread is made of dirham. Abu ‘Eesa said: This is a strange hadith. We only know it from this chain of narration from Mujalid from al-Sha’bi from Jabir. Ibn Wahb said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd told us: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said about the keepers of Hell: The distance between the shoulders of one of them is like the distance between the east and the west. Ibn Abbas said: The distance between the shoulders of one of them is a year’s journey, and the strength of one of them is to strike with a hammer and push seventy thousand people into the depths of Hell with that strike. I said: The correct thing, God willing, is that these nineteen are the leaders and captains, and as for their totality, the phrase is incapable of expressing it, as God Almighty said: And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him (al-Muddaththir 74:31). It has been proven in Sahih on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Hell will be brought forth on that Day with seventy thousand reins, and each rein will be pulled by seventy thousand angels. Ibn Abbas, Qatadah and Ad-Dahhak said: When the verse over it are nineteen was revealed, Abu Jahl said to the Quraysh 106:“May your mothers be bereaved of you! Listen to Ibn Abi Kabsha telling you that the keepers of Hell are nineteen, and you are the most numerous and brave, and every ten of you will be unable to strike a single one of them!” As-Suddi said: Abu Al-Ashd Asid ibn Kalda Al-Jumahi said: “Do not be frightened by the nineteen. I will push ten angels with my right shoulder and nine with my left shoulder, and then you will pass on to Paradise,” he said mockingly. In another narration: Al-Harith ibn Kalda said: I will suffice you for seventeen, and you suffice me for two. It was said that Abu Jahl said: Is every hundred of you unable to strike one of them, and then you will be brought out of the Fire?
74:31: The Almighty says: And We have not made the companions of the Fire except angels meaning, We did not make them men so that you would try to overcome them. It was said: He made them angels because they are different from the kind of tormented jinn and humans, so they are not affected by the same compassion and tenderness that affects those of a similar nature, nor do people find comfort in them. And because they are the most upright of God's creation with regard to the right of God and with anger for His sake, so their appeasement is assured. And because they are the most powerful of God's creation in strength and the strongest in strike. And We have not made their number except as trial meaning, an affliction. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas through more than one chain of transmission that he said: Misguidance for those who disbelieved, meaning Abu Jahl and his people. And it was said: Except as a punishment, as God the Almighty said: The Day they will be tested over the Fire * Taste your trial (al-Dhariyat 51:13-14) meaning, We made that the reason for their disbelief and the reason for the punishment. And in (nineteen) with a damma on the ha. On the authority of Anas bin Malik (nineteen) and on his authority also (nineteen) and on his authority also (nineteen) Al-Mahdawi mentioned it and said: Whoever reads (nineteen) sukun the ‘ayn due to the successive vowels. And whoever reads (nineteen) it is as if it is from overlapping, as if he wanted to connect and leave the structure, so he raised the feminine ha’, then returned to the structure and sukun. As for (nineteen) it is not known, and Abu Hatim rejected it. And likewise (nineteen) because it is based on (nineteen) and the waw is a substitute for the hamza and there is no basis for that according to grammarians. Al-Zamakhshari: It was read (nineteen) plural of ‘ashir, like yameen and ayman. God the Almighty says: {That those who were given the Scripture may be certain} meaning that those who were given the Torah and the Gospel may be certain that the number of the keepers of Hell is in agreement with what they have, as stated by Ibn Abbas, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, Mujahid and others. Then it is possible that He means those who believed among them, such as Abdullah ibn Salam. And it is possible that He means all of them. {And those who believe will increase in faith} because the more they believe in what is in the Book of God, the more they believe, and then their faith increases by their belief in the number of the keepers of Hell. {And let not those who were given the Scripture doubt} meaning those who were given the Scripture, {and the believers} meaning those who believed among the Companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, {nor will they have any doubts that the number of the keepers of Hell is nineteen. {And let those in whose hearts is disease say} meaning in their chests doubt and hypocrisy from the hypocrites of the people of Madinah, who predict the future after the migration, and there was no hypocrisy in Makkah, but rather it predicted it in Madinah. It was said: The meaning is, let the hypocrites who will astrologer in the future after the migration say. And the disbelievers meaning the Jews and Christians What did God intend by this as an example? meaning by the number of the keepers of Hell. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: The surah is Meccan and there was no hypocrisy in Mecca, so the illness in this verse is a matter of disagreement. And the disbelievers meaning the polytheists of the Arabs. The first opinion is held by most of the commentators. It is possible that what is intended by illness is doubt and suspicion, because the majority of the people of Mecca were doubters, and some of them were categorical about lying. The Almighty’s statement, informing us about them: What did God intend? meaning what did He intend (by this) the number that He mentioned recently, meaning this is not from the hadith. Al-Layth said: The parable is the hadith, and from it: The parable of Paradise which the righteous have been promised (Ar-Ra’d: 35) meaning its hadith and report about it. Likewise meaning like God’s misguidance of Abu Jahl and his companions who denied the keepers of Hell. God misguides meaning He humiliates and blinds whom He wills and guides meaning He directs whom He wills like the guidance of the companions of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. And it was said: Likewise God misguides from Paradise whom He wills and guides to it whom He wills. “And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him” meaning none knows the number of the angels of your Lord whom He created to torment the people of Hell. Except Him meaning except God, the Most High. This is an answer to Abu Jahl when he said: Muhammad has only nineteen soldiers! And “On the authority of Ibn Abbas: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was dividing the spoils of Hunayn when Gabriel came to him and sat with him. Then an angel came and said: Your Lord commands you to do such and such. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, feared that it might be a devil, so he said: “O Gabriel, do you recognize him?” He said: He is an angel, and I do not know all the angels of your Lord. Al-Awza’i said: Moses said: O Lord, who is in the heavens? He said: My angels. He said: How many of them are they, O Lord? He said: Twelve tribes. He said: How many of each tribe is there? He said: The number of the dust. Al-Tha’labi mentioned both of them. In Al-Tirmidhi: “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “The heavens groaned, and it has every right to groan. There is not a space in it the size of four fingers except that there is an angel prostrating his forehead to God.” The Almighty’s statement: And it is only a reminder to mankind, meaning the proofs, arguments, and the Qur’an. It was said: And it is only a reminder meaning a sermon for mankind, meaning for creation. It was said: The fire of this world is a reminder of the fire of the Hereafter. This was said by Al-Zajjaj. It was said: What is this number? “But a reminder to mankind,” meaning so that they may remember and know the perfection of God’s power, and that He does not need helpers and supporters. So the metaphor for this in the Almighty’s statement: And it is only a reminder to mankind, refers to the soldiers. Because it is the closest mentioned.
74:32: The Almighty said: No, by the moon. Al-Farra' said: (No) is a conjunction for the oath, the meaning being, and the moon. It was also said that the meaning is truly, and the moon. Therefore, one should not stop at these two meanings at (No,) and Al-Tabari permitted stopping at it, and made it a refutation of those who claimed that they were resisting the keepers of Hellfire, meaning that the matter is not as those who claim that they are resisting the keepers of Hellfire say.
74:33: Then He, the Almighty and Majestic, swore on that by the moon and what comes after it, and said: And the night when it departs, meaning it has gone away. And likewise (dabar). Nafi’, Hamza, and Hafs (idh adabar) and the rest read (idha) with an alif and (dabar) without an alif, and they are two languages with the same meaning. It is said: dabar and adabar, and likewise before the night and aqbal. And they said: yesterday the dabar and the mudabbar, Sakhr bin Amr bin Al-Sharid Al-Sulami said: We killed you while praising and worshipping God, and left behind you a time like yesterday. It is narrated as al-mudabbir and this is the opinion of al-Farra’ and al-Akhfash. Some linguists said: Dabar al-layl means it passed and adbara means it began to decline. Mujahid said: I asked Ibn Abbas about the verse: And the night when it departs al-Dajjal 19:20, so he was silent until it had departed, then he said: O Mujahid, this is when the night departs. Muhammad ibn al-Sumaiqa’ read and the night when it departs with two alifs, and it is also in the copy of Abdullah and Ubayy with two alifs. Qatrib said: Whoever reads dabar means approached, from the Arabs’ saying dabar so-and-so meaning he came from behind me. Abu Amr said: It is the language of Quraysh. Ibn Abbas said in a narration from him: The correct form is adbara meaning yadbar means yadbar on the back of a camel. Abu Ubaid chose idha adabar and said: He said because it is more in agreement with the letters that follow it.
74:34: Don't you see that he says: And the morning when it brightens, so how can one of them be (when) and the other (when) while there is no section in the Quran followed by (when). The meaning of (asfar) is: brightened. The common reading is (asfar) with an alif. Ibn al-Samiq' read: (travel). They are two languages. It is said: the travel of so-and-so's face and asfar: if it brightened. And in the hadith: (Pray at dawn, for it is greater for the reward) meaning pray the dawn prayer at dawn. It is said: prolong it until dawn: illumination. His face became beautiful, meaning it shone. The woman uncovered her face, so she is a traveler. It is possible that it is from the word travel, meaning to sweep, as the house is swept, meaning to sweep. From this comes the word ambassador: when the leaves of the tree fall and crumble. It is said: it is called ambassador because the wind sweeps it. And the sweeper: the broom.
74:35: The Almighty's saying: Indeed, it is one of the greatest is the answer to the oath, meaning that this fire is one of the greatest meaning one of the calamities. In the interpretation of Muqatil ((the greatest) is a name for the fire. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas (it is) meaning that their denial of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is one of the greatest meaning one of the major sins. It was said: meaning that the establishment of the Hour is one of the greatest. And the greatest: are the great punishments. The rajaz poet said: O son of Al-Mualla, one of the greatest calamities of the age and the deaf of others has descended The singular form of al-kabr is al-kabr like al-sughra and al-saghr, and al-azm and al-‘azm. The general public read li-ahadah which is a noun that is initially feminine and not built on the masculine, like ‘aqba and akhra, and its alif is a qata’ alif that does not go away in connection. Jarir bin Hazim narrated on the authority of Ibn Kathir innahu lahdi al-kabr without the hamza.
74:36: His Almighty saying: {A warner to mankind} He means the Fire, meaning that this described Fire is a warner to mankind so it is an accusative case as a state of the implied word in (it) as said by Al-Zajjaj. And it was mentioned because it means torment, or it means a warning in the sense of kinship, like their saying: a divorced and pure woman. Al-Khalil said: The warner is a verbal noun like Nakir, and that is why it is used to describe the feminine. Al-Hasan said: By God, I have not warned creation with anything more terrible than it. And it was said that what is meant by the warner is Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, meaning arise as a warner to mankind, meaning frightening them, so (a warner) is a state of (arrive) at the beginning of the Surah when He said: Arise and warn as said by Abu Ali Al-Farisi and Ibn Zayd, and it was narrated from Ibn Abbas but Al-Farra’ rejected it. Ibn Al-Anbari said: Some of the commentators said that its meaning is (O you wrapped up, arise as a warner to mankind). This is ugly because the conversation between them has been prolonged. It was said: It is from the attributes of God the Most High. Abu Muawiyah Al-Dharee’ narrated: Isma’il bin Samee’ narrated to us on the authority of Abu Razin, A warner to mankind, he said: God the Almighty says: Indeed, you have a warner from it, so fear it. And (a warner) in this case is in the accusative case as a state, meaning (And We have not made the companions of the Fire except angels) warning mankind of that. And it was said: It is a state of (He) in His statement, the Most High: And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him. And it was said: It is in the position of a verbal noun, as if He said: A warning to mankind. Al-Farra’ said: It is permissible for the warner to mean warning, meaning warn a warning, so it is like His statement, the Most High: And you will soon know how I warn (al-Mulk 67:17) meaning My warning, so on this basis it refers to the beginning of the surah, meaning Arise and warn, meaning warn. And it was said: It is in the accusative case with an implied verb. Ibn Abi Ubla read (warner) in the nominative case, with an implied verb. It was said: That is, the Qur’an is a warning to humanity, because it contains promises and threats.
74:37: The Almighty's saying: For whoever among you wills to go forward or to lag behind The lam is related to (warner) meaning a warner for whoever among you wills to go forward to goodness and obedience, or lag behind to evil and disobedience, similar to the verse: And We have certainly known those among you who go forward (al-Hijr 15:24) meaning in goodness, And We have certainly known those who lag behind (al-Hijr 15:24) from him. Al-Hasan said: This is a threat and a warning, even if it is presented in the form of a report report, like the Almighty's saying: So whoever wills - let him believe, and whoever wills - let him disbelieve (al-Kahf 18:29). Some of the people of interpretation said: Its meaning is for whoever God wills to go forward or to lag behind, so the will is connected to God, may He be glorified, and going forward means believing, and delaying means disbelief. Ibn Abbas used to say: This is a threat and notification that whoever goes forward to obedience and belief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, will be rewarded with an unending reward, and whoever lags behind in obedience and denies Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, will be punished with an unending punishment. Al-Saddī said: For whoever among you wishes to advance to the previously mentioned fire, or to delay it to Paradise.
74:38: The Almighty said: Every soul will be held in pledge for what it has earned. That is, pledged for its earnings, held accountable for its deeds, either to save it or to ruin it. And (pawn) is not the feminine of raheen in the Almighty's saying: Every soul will be held in pledge for what it has earned. (al-Tur 52:21) because of the feminine of nafs, because if the description was intended, it would have been said raheen, because fa'il has the meaning of maf'ul and is used in both masculine and feminine forms. Rather, it is a noun meaning pledge, like shatima meaning cursing, as if it was said: Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned, and from this comes the verse of enthusiasm: The one who is far from me is a hostage of a tomb of dust and stones. It is as if he said a pledge of a grave. The meaning is: Every soul is pledged to God for its earnings, and it will not be released.
74:39: God the Almighty says: Except the companions of the right hand for they will not be held in pledge for their sins. There is a difference of opinion about identifying them. Ibn Abbas said: The angels. Ali ibn Abi Talib: The children of Muslims who have not earned anything, so they will not be held in pledge for their earnings. Ad-Dahhak: Those for whom God has already bestowed goodness. Similar to that is narrated by Ibn Jurayj, who said: All of them. Muqatil also said: They are the companions of Paradise who were on Adam's right hand on the Day of the Covenant when God said to them: These are in Paradise, and I do not care. Al-Hasan and Ibn Kaysan said: They are the sincere Muslims who are not held in pledge, because they have fulfilled what was required of them. Abu Dhibyan narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: They are the Muslims. It was also said: Except the companions of truth and the people of faith. It was also said: They are those who are given their books in their right hands. Abu Ja'far al-Baqir said: We and our Shi'a are the companions of the right hand, and whoever hates us, the people of the house, they are the mortgaged ones. Al-Hakam said: They are those whom God chose to serve Him, so they are not included in the mortgage, because they are the servants of God and His chosen ones, and their earnings do not harm them. Al-Qasim said: Every soul is held accountable for what it has earned, whether good or evil, except for he who relies on grace and mercy, without earning or service. So whoever relies on earning is mortgaged, and whoever relies on grace is not held accountable for it.
74:40: God Almighty says: In gardens meaning in orchards they ask one another meaning they ask.
74:41: God Almighty says: About the criminals meaning the polytheists What brought you in meaning what brought you in.
74:42: The Almighty says: In Saqar as you say: I threaded the thread into such and such, meaning I put it into it. Al-Kalbi said: A man from the people of Paradise will ask a man from the people of Hell by name, and he will say to him: O so-and-so. In the reading of Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr: (O so-and-so, what brought you into Saqar)? And it was narrated from him that Umar ibn al-Khattab read: (O so-and-so, what brought you into Saqar), and this is a reading based on interpretation, not that it is a verse from the Quran as those who challenge the Quran have claimed. Abu Bakr ibn al-Anbari said this. It was said: The believers will ask the angels about their relatives, and the angels will ask the polytheists and they will say to them: What brought you into Saqar? Al-Farra' said: This strengthens the idea that the people of the right hand are the children, because they do not know about sins.
74:43: God Almighty says: They said, meaning the people of Hell, We were not among those who prayed, meaning the believers who pray.
74:44: God Almighty says: And we did not feed the poor meaning we did not give charity.
74:45: The Almighty said: And we used to engage in vain talk with the vain talkers. That is, we used to mingle with the people of falsehood in their falsehood. Ibn Zayd said: We used to engage in vain talk with the vain talkers about the matter of Muhammad, may God curse them. This is what they say about him - may God curse them - a soothsayer, a madman, a poet, or a magician. Al-Suddi said: That is, we used to lie with the liars. Qatada said: Whenever he went astray, we went astray with him. It was also said that it means: We were followers and were not led.
74:46: God Almighty says: And we used to deny the Day of Judgment meaning we did not believe in the Day of Resurrection, the Day of Recompense and Judgment.
74:47: The Almighty’s saying: Until the certainty comes to us means death came to us and descended upon us. From this is the Almighty’s saying: And worship your Lord until the certainty comes to you (al-Hajj 22:99).
74:48: The Almighty's statement: So what benefit will the intercession of intercessors benefit them? This is evidence of the validity of intercession for sinners, as some people who believed in monotheism were punished for their sins, then intercession was made for them, so God had mercy on them because of their belief in monotheism and intercession, so they were taken out of the Fire, and the disbelievers will have no intercessor to intercede for them. Abdullah ibn Mas'ud may God be pleased with him said: Your Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) will intercede as the fourth of four: Gabriel, then Abraham, then Moses or Jesus, then your Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), then the angels, then the prophets, then the truthful ones, then the martyrs. Some people will remain in Hell, and it will be said to them: What has brought you to Hellfire? They will say, We were not of those who prayed, and we did not feed the poor." Until His statement: "So what benefit will the intercession of intercessors benefit them?" Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: These are the ones who will remain in Hell, and we have mentioned its chain of transmission in the book "At-Tadhkira."
74:49: The Almighty said: So why do they turn away from the reminder? Meaning, why have the people of Mecca turned away and turned away from what you have brought? In the interpretation of Muqatil: Turning away from the Qur’an has two aspects: One of them is denial and rejection, and the other aspect is abandoning acting upon what is in it. (turning away) is in the accusative case as a state of the ha’ and the mim in (for them) and in the lam there is the meaning of a verb, so the accusative case of the state is in the meaning of a verb.
74:50: The Almighty said: As if they meaning as if these disbelievers, in their flight from Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, were frightened donkeys. Ibn Abbas said: He meant wild donkeys. Nafi’ and Ibn ‘Amir read it with a fatha on the fa’, meaning frightened and terrified. Abu ‘Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose this. The rest read it with a kasra, meaning frightened. It is said: nafarta and istanfarta have the same meaning, like ‘ajaat and istajaabat, and sakharah and istasakharah. Al-Farra’ recited: Hold your donkey, it is alerted to the traces of the red ones who have gone west
74:51: The Almighty said: Fara'at meaning it was frightened and fled from Qasoora meaning from the archers who shoot it. Some linguists said: Qasoora is the archer, and its plural is Qasoora. This is what Saeed bin Jubair, Ikrimah, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Kaysan said: Qasoora are the archers and hunters. It was narrated by Ata' on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Abu Dhibyan on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari. It was said: It is the lion, as Abu Hurairah and Ibn Abbas also said. Ibn Arafa: It is from Qasr, meaning subjugation, as it subjugates wild beasts, and wild donkeys flee from wild beasts. Abu Jamrah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: I do not know of the word Qasoora as a lion in the language of any of the Arabs, but it is a group of men. He said: So Qasoora is the plural of men, and he recited: Oh girl, be good to the best of her maternal uncles, the jinn and the cruel people. And on his authority: The people focused, meaning their senses and voices. And on his authority also: (Fled from Qasoora) meaning from the hunters’ ropes. And on his authority also: Qasoora in the Arabic language: the lion, and in the Abyssinian language: the archers, and in the Persian language: Sher, and in the Nabataean language: Ariya. And Ibn al-A’rabi said: Qasoora: the beginning of the night, meaning she fled from the darkness of the night. And Ikrimah also said it. And it was said: It is the first blackness of the night, and the last of the blackness of the night is not called Qasoora. And Zaid bin Aslam said: From strong men, and every strong one among the Arabs is Qasoora and Qasoor. And Labid bin Rabi’ah said: If we shout a shout in our hearts, the returning men will come to us
74:52: God the Almighty says: Rather, every man among them desires to be given spread out pages. That is, to be given open books. This is because Abu Jahl and a group of Quraysh said: "O Muhammad! Bring us books from the Lord of the Worlds in which is written: 'Indeed, I have sent Muhammad to you, may God bless him and grant him peace.'" Similar to this is: And we will never believe in your incantations until you bring down to us a book that we can read. (Al-Isra': 93) Ibn Abbas said: They were saying: If Muhammad is truthful, then every man among us should have a page in which is written his innocence and his safety from the Fire. Matar Al-Warraq said: They wanted to be given something without doing anything. Al-Kalbi said: The polytheists said: We have heard that a man from the Children of Israel would wake up with his sins and expiations written near his head, so bring us something similar. Mujahid said: They wanted to send down to every one of them a book in which is from God the Almighty: 'To so-and-so, son of so-and-so.'" It was also said that the meaning is that he should be mentioned with a good mention, so the pages were made the place of mention as a metaphor. They said: If a person's sins are recorded against him, why don't we see that?
74:53: The Almighty said: No meaning that will not happen. It was also said: True. The first is better because it is a response to their saying Rather, they do not fear the Hereafter meaning I will not give them what they wish for because they do not fear the Hereafter, being deceived by the world. Saeed bin Jubair read (spread out pages) with a sukoon on the ha and the noon. As for sukoon on the ha, it is a lightening, and as for the noon, it is anomalous. It is only said: Nashr the garment and similar, and it is not said ansharat. It is permissible to liken the page to the dead as if it were a dead body with its folding, so if it is spread out it is brought to life, so it came as ansharah God the dead just as he likened the revival of the dead to spreading out the garment, so it was said in it God spread out the dead, so it is a language for it.
74:54: God Almighty says: No! It is a reminder. That is, the Qur’an is truly a lesson.
74:55: God Almighty says: So whoever wills, let him remember it. That is, let him take heed from it.
74:56: God the Almighty says: And they will not remember meaning, nor will they be admonished except that God wills meaning, they are not able to take admonition and remember except by the will of God, that is for them. The general reading of yadhkirun is with a ya', and Abu Ubaid chose it, based on God the Almighty's saying: No! Rather, they do not fear the Hereafter. Nafi' and Ya'qub read it with a ta', and Abu Hatim chose it because it is more general, and they agreed to make it light. He is the One worthy of piety and forgiveness In At-Tirmidhi and Sunan Ibn Majah on the authority of Anas ibn Malik: "On the authority of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) that he said regarding this verse: "He is the One worthy of piety and forgiveness." He said: (God the Blessed and Exalted said, 'I am worthy of being pious, so whoever is pious to Me and does not associate any god with Me, then I am worthy of being forgiven.'"" Wording by At-Tirmidhi, who said about it: A hasan ghareeb hadith. In some interpretations: He is the One who forgives those who repent to Him from major sins, and He is also the One who forgives minor sins by avoiding major sins. Muhammad ibn Nasr said: I am worthy of My servant fearing Me, and if he does not, I am worthy of forgiving him and having mercy on him, and I am the Forgiving, the Most Merciful.
75:1: Meccan and it has thirty-nine verses. The Almighty said: I swear by the Day of Resurrection. It was said that la is a conjunction, and it is permissible for it to occur at the beginning of the surah, because the Qur’an is connected to each other, so it is considered as one statement. For this reason, something may be mentioned in one surah and its answer may come in another surah, like the Almighty’s saying: And they said, ‘O you to whom the message has been sent down, indeed you are mad.’ (al-Hijr 15:6) and its answer in another surah: You are not, by the favor of your Lord, mad. (al-Qalam 68:2) The meaning of the statement: I swear by the Day of Resurrection. Ibn ‘Abbaas, Ibn Jubayr, and Abu ‘Ubaidah said this, and similar to it is the saying of the poet: I remembered Laila and I was overcome with passion, and my heart almost couldn't break Abu Al-Layth Al-Samarqandi narrated: The commentators agreed that the meaning of la aqsam is I swear. They differed in the interpretation of la. Some of them said: la is an addition to the speech for the sake of embellishment, and the addition of la occurs in the speech of the Arabs, as he said in another verse: He said, ‘What prevented you from prostrating?’ (al-A’raf 7:12) meaning that you prostrated. Some of them said: la is a response to their speech when they denied the resurrection, so he said: The matter is not as you claimed. I said: This is what Al-Farra’ said. Al-Farra’ said: Many grammarians say that la is a conjunction, and it is not permissible to begin with a denial and then make it a conjunction, because if this were the case, no predicate containing a denial would be known from one without a denial. However, the Qur’an came in response to those who denied the Resurrection, Paradise, and Hellfire, so the oaths came in response to them in many of the speeches that are initiated by it and not initiated by it, and that is like their saying: No, by God, I will not do it. So la is a response to a statement that has already passed, and that is like your saying: No, by God, the Resurrection is true, as if you had lied to a people who denied it. And someone other than Al-Farra’ recited from Imru’ Al-Qais: No, by your father, daughter of Al-Ameri, do not let the people claim that I am a deserter. Ghuwayya bin Salma said: Unless you called in front of him with a possibility to make me sad, I don’t care about you Its benefit is to emphasize the oath in response. Al-Farra’ said: “He who does not pay attention to this aspect would read ‘la-aqsam’ without an alif, as if no emphasis had entered into ‘aqsam’, and this is correct, because the Arabs say: ‘la-aqsam bi-God’, and this is the reading of Al-Hasan, Ibn Kathir, Al-Zuhri, and Ibn Hurmuz, ‘bi-Yawm Al-Qiyamah’, meaning the day on which people will stand before their Lord, and God, the Almighty, can swear by whatever He wills.”
75:2: The Almighty's saying: And I swear by the self-reproaching soul. There is no disagreement about this among the reciters of the Quran, which is that God swore by the Day of Resurrection to magnify its status and did not swear by the self. According to Ibn Kathir's reading, He swore by the first and did not swear by the second. It was said: And I swear by the self-reproaching soul is another response and the beginning of an oath by the self-reproaching soul. Al-Tha'labi said: The correct view is that He swore by both of them. The meaning of by the self-reproaching soul is by the soul of the believer whom you never see except blaming himself, saying: What did I mean by such and such? You never see him except reproaching himself. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Hasan and others. Al-Hasan said: By God, it is the soul of the believer. The believer is never seen except blaming himself: What did I mean by my words? What did I mean by my eating? What did I mean by my inner conversation? And the wicked person does not hold himself to account. Mujahid said: It is the one who blames himself for what he has done and regrets it. He blames himself for the evil he did, and for the good he did not do more of it. It was also said: It is the self-blaming. It was also said: It is the one who blames himself for what he blames others for. So, according to these aspects, the blaming one means the one who blames, which is a praiseworthy attribute. Based on this, swearing by it is permissible and good. In some interpretations: It refers to Adam, peace be upon him, who was constantly blaming himself for his sin that led him to be expelled from Paradise. It was also said: The blaming one means the blameworthy one - also from Ibn Abbas - so it is a blameworthy attribute. This is the opinion of those who denied it being an oath, since the sinner has no danger to swear by, so it is often blameworthy. Al-Farra’ said: There is no soul of the disbeliever who blames himself and regrets in the hereafter what he neglected in the way of God. Al-Farra’ said: There is no soul, good or evil, except that it blames itself. The doer of good blames himself if he had increased in goodness, and the evildoer blames himself if he had not refrained from his evil.
75:3: God the Almighty says: Does man think that We will not assemble his bones? So that We will restore them as a new creation after they have become dust. Al-Zajjaj said: He swears by the Day of Resurrection and by the self-reproaching soul: He will surely assemble the bones for the resurrection. This is the answer to the oath. An-Nahhas said: The answer to the oath is omitted, i.e., you will surely be resurrected. This is indicated by God's statement: Does man think that We will not assemble his bones? for life and resurrection. Man here is the disbeliever who denies the resurrection. The verse was revealed about Adi ibn Rabi'ah. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Tell me about the Day of Resurrection. When will it be, and what will its conditions and circumstances be?" The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) informed him of that. He said: "If I saw that day, I would not believe you, O Muhammad, nor would I have faith in it. Or will God assemble the bones?!" For this reason the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) used to say: O God, protect me from my bad neighbor Adi ibn Rabi'ah and Al-Akhns ibn Shuraik. It was also said that it was revealed about the enemy of God, Abu Jahl, when he denied the resurrection after death. He mentioned the bones, but what is meant is the whole soul, because the bones are the mold of creation.
75:4: The Almighty said: Yes A good pause. Come, begin. Able. Sibawayh said: It means We gather them, able. So (able) is a state of the implied subject in the deleted verb, as we mentioned from the estimation. And it was said: The meaning is yes, We are able, able. Al-Farra' said: (Able) is in the accusative case as an exit from (gather), meaning We are able and strengthen (able) for more than that. And he also said: It is appropriate to put it in the accusative case for repetition, meaning (Yes), so let him think of us as able. And it was said: The implied (we were) means we were able in the beginning, and the polytheists acknowledged it. Ibn Abi Ubla and Ibn al-Sameeq read (Yes, we are able) with the interpretation that we are able. To level his fingertips Banan among the Arabs: the fingers, the singular of which is Bananah. Al-Nabigha said: With a dyed hair, his fingers seem to be almost knotted from tenderness Antara said: Death is at my fingertips if I touch the Hindu So He pointed out the rest of the limbs with the finger. Also, they are the smallest bones, so He mentioned them specifically for that reason. Al-Qutbi and Al-Zajjaj said: They claimed that God does not resurrect the dead and that He is not able to reunite the bones. God the Most High said: Yes, We are able to restore the joints despite their smallness, and bring them together until they are equal. And whoever is able to do this is even more able to reunite the large ones. Ibn Abbas and most of the commentators said: The meaning is: (to make his fingertips in order), meaning that We make the fingers of his hands and feet one thing like a camel’s hoof, or like a donkey’s hoof, or like a pig’s hoof, and he cannot do anything with them. But We separated his fingers so that he can do with them what he wants. Al-Hasan used to say: He gave you fingers so you extend them and close them, and if He had willed, He could have brought them together, and you would not have been able to protect yourself from the earth except with your two hands. It was said: That is, we are able to return man to the form of animals, so how about in the form he was in, as God Almighty said: And We are not to be outdone * In changing your likes and producing you in that which you do not know (al-Waqi’ah 56:16-60). I said: The first interpretation is more similar to the context of the verse. And God knows best.
75:5: The Almighty said: Rather, man wants to commit sin before him. Ibn Abbas said: meaning the disbeliever denies what is before him of resurrection and accountability. Abdur Rahman bin Zaid said the same, and his evidence is: He asks, 'When is the Day of Resurrection?' meaning he asks when it will be! In the form of denial and disbelief. So he is not satisfied with what he is in of disbelief, but he sins for what is before him. What indicates that sin is disbelief is what Al-Qutbi and others mentioned: That a Bedouin went to Umar bin Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him and complained to him about the hole and back of his camels, and asked him to carry him on another one, but he did not carry him, so the Bedouin said: I swear to God, Abu Hafs never touched her from the inside or the outside Forgive him, O God, if he was a sinner Meaning, if he lied about what I mentioned. And also from Ibn Abbas: He hastens to commit a sin and rushes to repent. And in some hadith he said: He says, I will repent, but he does not repent, so he has broken his promise and lied. This is the saying of Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Al-Suddi, and Saeed bin Jubayr. He says, I will repent, I will repent, until death comes to him in the worst of conditions. Ad-Dahhak said: It is hope, he says, I will live and gain from this world, but he does not remember death. And it was said: It means he intends to commit a sin forever, even if he will only live for a short time. So the ha in these sayings refers to the human being. And it was said: The ha refers to the Day of Resurrection. The meaning is, rather, the human being wants to disbelieve in the truth before the Day of Resurrection. And immorality is originally deviation from the truth.
75:6: God Almighty says: He asks, ‘When is the Day of Resurrection?’ That is, when is the Day of Resurrection?
75:7: The Almighty said: And when the sight is dazzled Nafi' and Aban on the authority of Asim read barq with a fatha on the ra', meaning: his sight flashes from the intensity of his staring, so you see him not blinking. Mujahid and others said: This is at the time of death. Al-Hasan said: This is on the Day of Resurrection. He said in it the meaning of the answer to what a person asked about is as if it is the Day of Resurrection when the sight is dazzled * and the moon is eclipsed. The rest read it with a kasra barq and its meaning is: he is confused and does not blink, said Abu Amr, Al-Zajjaj and others. Dhu Al-Rummah said: If Luqman the Wise had been exposed to water openly, his eyes would have flashed. Al-Farra and Al-Khalil: (Barq) with the kasra: to frighten, bewilder, and bewilder. The Arabs say to a bewildered and astonished person: it has flashed, so he is barq. Al-Farra recited: Be patient with yourself and do not neglect me. Heal the wounds and do not be afraid. That is, do not be alarmed by the many wounds you have. It was also said: Baraq yabraq with the fat-ha means he slitted his eyes and opened them. Abu Ubaidah said this, and he recited the words of Al-Kalabi: When Umair came to me seeking help, I gave him a red camel, and he was delighted. That is, he opened his eyes. It was said that the kasra and fatha of the raa are two languages that have the same meaning.
75:8: The Almighty said: And the moon was eclipsed meaning its light was lost. An eclipse in this world is when it clears, unlike the Hereafter, when its light does not return. It may also mean it disappeared, as in the Almighty's saying: So We caused the earth to swallow him and his dwelling place. (al-Qasas 28:81) Ibn Abi Ishaq, Isa, and Al-A'raj read: And the moon was eclipsed with a damma on the kha and a kasra on the seen, indicating and the gathering of the sun and the moon. Abu Hatim Muhammad ibn Idris said: If some of it disappears, then it is an eclipse, and if all of it disappears, then it is an eclipse.
75:9: The Almighty said: And He joined the sun and the moon meaning He joined them together when their light went away, so there is no light for the sun just as there is no light for the moon after its eclipse, as stated by Al-Farra' and Al-Zajjaj. Al-Farra' said: He did not say joined because the meaning is He joined them together. Abu Ubaidah said: It is based on the masculine predominance. Al-Kisa'i said: It is based on the meaning, as if he said the two lights. Al-Mubarrad: The feminine is not real. Ibn Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud said: He joined them together, meaning He joined them together when they rise from the west, black, round, dark, and entwined, as if they were two hamstrung oxen. The hadith with this meaning has already been mentioned at the end of Surat Al-An'am. In the reading of Abdullah: (And He joined the sun and the moon) Ata' ibn Yasar said: He will join them together on the Day of Resurrection, then they will be thrown into the sea, and they will be the Great Fire of God. Ali and Ibn Abbas said: They will be placed in the light of the veils. They may be gathered together in the fire of Hell, because they were worshipped instead of God. The fire will not be a torment for them because they are inanimate. Rather, this is done to them to increase the rebuke and regret of the disbelievers. In Musnad Abi Dawud al-Tayalisi, on the authority of Yazid al-Raqashi, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, tracing it back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: (The sun and the moon are two barren bulls in the Fire.) It was said that this combination means that they meet and do not separate, and they come close to people, and sweat overtakes them due to the intense heat, so the meaning is that their heat is combined on them. It was said that the sun and the moon are combined, so there is no alternation of night and day.
75:10: God Almighty says: On that Day man will say, ‘Where is the escape?’ That is, the son of Adam, and it is said: Abu Jahl, will say, meaning, where is the escape? The poet said: Where is the escape while the rams butt heads, and any ram that deviates from them will be disgraced? Al-Mawardi: It has two possible interpretations: One is Where is the escape from God, out of shyness before Him. The second is Where is the escape from Hellfire, out of caution from it. This statement from a human being has two possible interpretations: One is that it is from the disbeliever specifically when facing the Day of Resurrection, not the believer, because the believer has confidence in the glad tidings of his Lord. The second is that it is said by the believer and the disbeliever upon the Day of Resurrection, out of the horror of what they witnessed. The reading of the common people is (al-mafar) with a fatha on the fa, and Abu Ubaidah and Abu Hatim chose it because it is a verbal noun. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan and Qatadah read it with a kasra on the fa and a fatha on the meem. Al-Kisa’i said: They are two dialects like mudab and mudab, and musah and musah. Al-Zuhri narrated with a kasra on the meem and a fatha on the fa. Al-Mahdawi: from the fatha on the meem, the one to whom one flees. And from the kasra on the meem and a fatha on the fa, it refers to the person who flees well, so the meaning is where is the person who flees well and he will not be saved despite that. I said: And from it is the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: Cunning, fleeing, approaching, retreating together He wants to be good at attacking and retreating.
75:11: The Almighty said: No meaning there is no escape. So (No) is a response and it is from the saying of God the Almighty, then He explained this response and said: No burden meaning no refuge from the fire. Ibn Masoud used to say: No fortress. Al-Hasan used to say: No mountain. Ibn Abbas said: No refuge. Ibn Jubayr said: No escape and no protection. The meaning of all of that is the same. In the language, burden is: what one takes refuge in, such as a fortress, mountain, or other than them. The poet said: By my life, a young man has no burden of death or old age. Al-Suddi said: When they were frightened in this world, they would take refuge in the mountains. Then God said to them: No burden will protect you from Me on that day. Tarafa said: Bakr learned that we are superior in opinion and in the mind is a burden
75:12: The Almighty's saying: To your Lord, that Day, is the final destination. That is, the end, as Qatada said. Similar to it is: Indeed, to your Lord is the final destination. (al-Najm 53:42) Ibn Mas'ud said: To your Lord is the destination and the return. It was said: That is, the final destination in the Hereafter where God, the Almighty, will settle him, as He is the judge between them. It was also said: (No) is from what a person says to himself when he knows that he has no escape. He says to himself: No! No burden! To your Lord, that Day, is the final destination.
75:13: God the Almighty says: Man will be informed meaning, he will inform the son of Adam, whether he is righteous or wicked, of what he sent forth and what he left behind: meaning, what he sent forth of bad or good deeds, or what he left behind of a bad or good practice to be followed after him. This was said by Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masoud. Mansour narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: He will be informed of the beginning and end of his deeds. Al-Nakha'i said the same. Ibn Abbas also said: meaning, what he sent forth of disobedience and what he left behind of obedience. This is the opinion of Qatada. Ibn Zayd said: (What he sent forth) of his wealth for himself (and what he left behind) means what he left behind for the heirs. Ad-Dahhak said: He will be informed of what he sent forth of an obligation and what he left behind of an obligation. Al-Qushayri said: This information will be on the Day of Resurrection when deeds are weighed. It is permissible for it to be at death. I said: The first is more apparent, because Ibn Majah included it in his Sunan from the hadith of Al-Zuhri. Abu Abdullah Al-Aghar told me on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Among the deeds and good deeds that will continue to the believer after his death are knowledge that he taught and disseminated, a righteous child that he left behind, a copy of the Qur’an that he inherited, a mosque that he built, a house that he built for wayfarers, a canal that he made flow, or charity that he gave from his wealth while he was healthy and alive that will continue to him after his death.” Abu Nu’aym al-Hafiz included it with a similar meaning from the hadith of Qatadah on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are seven things for which the reward will continue to continue for the servant after his death while he is in his grave: someone who taught knowledge, made a canal flow, dug a well, planted a palm tree, built a mosque, bequeathed a copy of the Qur’an, or left behind a child who seeks forgiveness for him after his death.” His statement: after his death while he is in his grave clearly states that this will not happen at the time of death, but rather he will be informed of all of that when his deeds are weighed, even though he will be given the good report of that in his grave. This is also indicated by the words of God Almighty: And they will bear their own burdens and other burdens besides their own (al-Ankabut 29:13) and His words, the Most High: And of the burdens of those whom they misguide without knowledge (al-Nahl 16:25). This will only happen in the Hereafter after the deeds are weighed. And God knows best. In the Sahih: “Whoever establishes a good practice in Islam will have its reward and the reward of those who act upon it after him, without that diminishing their reward in the slightest. And whoever establishes a bad practice in Islam will bear its burden and the burden of those who act upon it after him, without that diminishing their burden in the slightest.”
75:14: The Almighty said: Rather, man is a witness against himself. Al-Akhfash said: He made it the witness, just as you say to a man, You are an argument against yourself. Ibn Abbas said: Baseer means a witness, and they are the witnesses of his limbs against him: his hands with what he strikes with, his feet with what he walks with, and his eyes with what he sees with. Insight is the witness. Al-Farra’ recited: As if the wise man had an eye that saw his seat or a view that he was watching He is so cautious that he thinks all people are afraid that his secrets will not be hidden from them. The evidence for this interpretation from the Qur’an is the statement of God the Almighty: The Day their tongues, their hands, and their feet will bear witness against them as to what they used to do. (al-Nur 24:24) The feminine form of insight is used because what is meant by man here is the limbs, because they bear witness against man’s soul. It is as if God said: Rather, the limbs are insight against man’s soul. Al-Qutbi and others said this meaning. Some people say: This ha in His statement insight is what the grammarians call the ha of emphasis, like the ha in their statements dahiya, “alamah,” and rawiya. This is the opinion of Abu Ubaid. It was said that what is meant by insight are the two scribes who write down what is good or bad from him, as indicated by His statement, even if he presents his excuses, about those who make excuses hidden. This is the opinion of Al-Suddi and Al-Dahhak. Some of the commentators said: The meaning is: Rather, against man is insight against himself, meaning a witness, so the preposition was omitted. It is possible that insight is an adjective for a feminine noun, and it would be: Rather, man is an insightful eye towards himself. Al-Farra’ recited: He had a keen eye for the wise Al-Hasan said about the Almighty’s saying: Rather, man is a witness against himself, meaning he is aware of the faults of others, but ignorant of his own faults.
75:15: The Almighty says: Even if he presents his excuses meaning even if he lowers his curtain. In the language of the people of Yemen, curtain means excuse, as Ad-Dahhak said. The poet said: But she was stingy with us for an hour and made excuses for it. Al-Zajjaj said: Al-Mu'adhir excuse means the curtain, and the singular is Mu'adhir excuse, meaning that if he lowers his curtain, wanting to hide his action, then his soul will be a witness against him. It was said: That is, if he apologized and said, I did not do anything, then there would be someone from himself who would testify against him from his limbs. So even if he apologized and argued on his own behalf, then he has a witness against him that belies his excuse. This was said by Mujahid, Qatadah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd, Abu al-'Aliyah, Ata', al-Farra', al-Suddi and Muqatil. Muqatil said: That is, if he presented an excuse or argument, it would not benefit him. Similar to the saying of God the Almighty: {The Day when no excuse will benefit the wrongdoers} (Ghafir 40:52) and His saying: {And they will not be permitted to make excuses} (al-Mursalat 77:36). So Al-Mu'adhir according to this is taken from the excuse. The poet said: And beware of the matter that if its resources expand, the sources will become narrow for you It is not good for a person to excuse himself when no one else can excuse him. A man apologized to Ibrahim Al-Nakha'i, who said to him: I excuse you without an apology, for excuses are tainted by lies. Ibn Abbas said: Even if he presented his excuses meaning if he stripped off his clothes. Al-Mawardi narrated it. I said: It is more apparent that it is presenting an argument and apologizing for the sin, and from this is the saying of Al-Nabigha: This is an excuse, but if it is not of any use, then its owner is a participant in misery. The evidence for this is the statement of God the Almighty about the disbelievers: By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists (al-An’am 6:23) and His statement about al-Munafiqun 63:The Day God will resurrect them all and they will swear to Him as they swear to you (Al-Mujadilah: 18). In the Sahih, it is stated that he says: O Lord, I have believed in You and in Your Book and in Your Messenger, and I have prayed and fasted and given charity, and he praises God as much as he can. This has been mentioned previously in Ha Meem As-Sajdah and others. Excuses and excuses: the plural of excuse, and it is said: I excused him for what he did, I excused him with an excuse and an excuse, and the noun is excuse and excuse. The poet said: I have set a limit and I have no excuse for the limited And also the excuse, which is like the knee and the sitting, Al-Nabigha said: If you excuse me, it was not of any use, for its owner has lost his way in the country. This verse includes five issues: First: Judge Abu Bakr Ibn Al-Arabi said that the Almighty’s statement: Rather, man is a witness against himself, even if he presents his excuses is evidence of the acceptance of a person’s admission of himself, because it is a testimony from him against it. God Almighty said: On the Day when their tongues, their hands, and their feet will bear witness against them as to what they used to do (al-Nur 24:24).
