There is no disagreement about it, because it is a report in a way that avoids accusation from him, because a wise person does not lie about himself - and this is the issue: Second - God Almighty said in His Noble Book: “And when God took a covenant from the prophets, ‘Whatever I give you of the Book and wisdom and then there comes to you a Messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him.’ He said, ‘Have you acknowledged and taken upon yourself My commitment?’ They said, ‘We acknowledge.’ He said, ‘Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses.’” (Al Imran 3:81) And God Almighty said: “And others have acknowledged their sins. They mixed a righteous deed with another evil.” (At Tawbah: 102) And it is found in many hadiths. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ((Go, Anas, to this man's wife. If she confesses, stone her.)) As for the admission of another person against another person regarding an heir or a debt, Malik said: The agreed upon principle among us is that if a man dies and has children, one of them says: My father admitted that so-and-so is his son. That lineage cannot be proven by the testimony of a person who has children. Then one of them says: My father admitted that so-and-so is his son. That lineage cannot be proven by the testimony of one person. The admission of the one who admitted is only valid regarding his share of his father's wealth. The one who testifies for him is given the amount of the debt that he receives from the wealth in his possession. Malik said: The explanation of that is that if a man dies and leaves two sons and six hundred dinars, then one of them testifies that his deceased father admitted that so-and-so is his son, then the one who testified for the one who is entitled to it is one hundred dinars, and that is half the inheritance of the one who is claimed if he is claimed. If the other confesses for him, he takes the other one hundred, thus his right is complete and his lineage is proven. It is also like a woman who acknowledges a debt owed by her father or husband and the heirs deny it. She must pay to the one to whom she acknowledged the amount of that debt that would be due to her if it were proven against all the heirs. If she is a woman and inherits an eighth, she must pay the creditor an eighth of his debt. If she is a daughter and inherits half, she must pay the creditor half of his debt. This is what is paid to the woman who acknowledged it. Third: A confession is only valid from a person who is legally responsible, but on the condition that he is not under guardianship, because guardianship nullifies his statement if it is for his own benefit. If it is for the benefit of someone else, such as a sick person, then it is null and void, and in some cases it is permissible. Its explanation is in the issues of jurisprudence. A person has two states in his confession: The first is at its beginning, and there is no disagreement about it as mentioned above. The second is at its end, which is like the vagueness of the confession, and it has many forms, the main ones are six: The first form: That he says to him, I have something. Al-Shafi’i said: If he explained it as a date or a piece of bread, it will be accepted from him. What our principles require is that it is not accepted except for what has a value, so if he explained it as such, it is accepted from him and he swears to it. The second form: That he explains this as wine or pork or something that is not considered wealth in the Sharia: It is not accepted by consensus even if the one to whom he confessed helps him. Third scenario: If he interprets it with something that is disputed, such as the hide of a dead animal, a thief, or a dog, then the judge shall rule against him in that regard according to what he deems appropriate in terms of rejection and approval. If he rejects it, then no judge shall rule against him in that regard according to what he deems appropriate in terms of rejection and approval. If he rejects it, then no other judge shall rule against him with anything because the ruling has already been executed by invalidating it. Some of the followers of al-Shafi’i said: Wine and pork are binding, but this is an invalid opinion. Abu Hanifa said: If someone says to him, I owe something, then his interpretation is not acceptable unless it is measured or weighed, because nothing is established in the conscience by itself except these two. This is weak, because anything else is established in the conscience if it is required by consensus. Fourth scenario: If he says to him, I have money, before interpreting it as something that is not usually considered money, such as one or two dirhams, unless there is a circumstantial evidence that would rule him to pay more than that. Fifth scenario: If he says to him, I have a lot or a great deal of money, al-Shafi’i said: It is acceptable if it is a grain. Abu Hanifa said: It is not acceptable except in the amount of the zakat threshold. Our scholars have given different opinions on this, including the minimum amount for theft, zakat, and blood money. In my opinion, the minimum amount is the minimum amount for theft, because a Muslim’s limbs are not exposed except for a large sum of money. This is what most of the Hanafis say. Whoever is surprised by the statement of Al-Layth ibn Sa’d, that it is not acceptable for less than seventy-two dirhams, will be surprised. He was asked, How do you say that? He said, Because God, the Most High, said, ‘God has already given you victory in many battlefields and on the day of Hunayn.’ (al-Tawbah 9:25), and his battles and raids were seventy-two. This is not correct, because he excluded Hunayn from them, and he should have said that it is acceptable for seventy-one. God, the Most High, said, Remember God with much remembrance (al-Ahzab 33:41), and He said, There is no good in much of their private conversation (An-Nisa’: 114), and He said, And curse them with a great curse (al-Ahzab 33:68). Sixth example: If he says to him: I have ten, or one hundred, or one thousand, then he can interpret it as he wishes and it will be accepted from him. If he says a thousand dirhams, or one hundred and a slave, or one hundred and fifty dirhams, then he interprets the vague thing and it will be accepted from him. This is what Al-Shafi’i said. Abu Hanifa said: If he links it to the vague number, whether measured or weighed, then it is an interpretation, like his saying: one hundred and fifty dirhams, because the dirham is an interpretation of fifty, and fifty is an interpretation of one hundred. Ibn Khairan Al-Istakhri, one of Al-Shafi’i’s followers, said: The dirham is not an interpretation of one hundred and fifty except for fifty specifically, and he can interpret one hundred as he wishes. Fourth Issue: The Almighty said: And even if he presents his excuses. This means that if he apologizes after confessing, it will not be accepted from him. The scholars differed regarding the one who recants after confessing to the prescribed punishments that are purely the right of God. The majority of them, including Al-Shafi’i and Abu Hanifa, said: His recantation is acceptable after confessing. Malik said this in one of his two opinions, and he said in the other opinion: It is not acceptable unless he mentions a valid reason for his recantation. The correct view is that it is permissible to recant absolutely, based on what the imams, including Al-Bukhari and Muslim, narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) rejected the one who admitted to adultery four times, turning away each time. When he testified against himself four times, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called him and said: Are you crying because of madness? He said: No. He said: Are you chaste? He said: Yes. In the hadith of Al-Bukhari, it says: Perhaps you kissed, winked, or looked. In An-Nasa'i and Abu Dawud: Until he said to him in the fifth time, Have you had intercourse with her? He said, Yes. He said, Until that disappeared from you in that from her. He said, Yes. He said, Just as the eyeliner disappears into the kohl container and the rope into the well. He said, Yes. He said, Do you know what adultery is? He said, “Yes. I came to her unlawfully, just as a man comes to his wife lawfully.” He said, Then what do you want from me? He said, I want you to purify me. He said, So he ordered that he be stoned. At-Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud said: When he felt the touch of the stones, he ran wild, and a man struck him with a camel’s jawbone, and the people struck him until he died. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, Why didn’t you leave him? Abu Dawud and An-Nasa'i said: To confirm the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), but not to leave the prescribed punishment. All of this is a way to return and a clear statement of its acceptance. In the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Perhaps you kissed or winked is an allusion to the statement of Malik: that his return is accepted if he mentions a reason. Fifth - This is regarding the free man who is the master of his own affairs. As for the slave, his confession is not devoid of one of two types: Either he confesses to what is in his hand and his conscience, if he confesses to what is on his body in a matter for which there is a punishment of murder or less, then that is executed against him. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: It is not accepted from him, because his body is absorbed by the right of the master, and in his confession the rights of the master in his body are destroyed. Our evidence is the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Whoever is affected by any of these filth, let him conceal himself with the concealment of God, for whoever reveals his side to us, we will carry out the prescribed punishment on him. The meaning is: The place of punishment is the original creation, which is the doll in the case of illiteracy, and the master has no right to it, but his right is to the description and consequence, which is the financial asset that accrues to him. Don’t you see that if he confesses to money, it is not accepted, so Abu Hanifa said: If he says I stole this commodity, his hand is not cut off and the one to whom he confessed takes it. Our scholars said: The commodity belongs to the master, and the slave is held accountable for its value if he is freed, because the slave’s property belongs to the master by consensus, so his statement about it and his acknowledgment of it are not accepted, especially since Abu Hanifa says: The slave does not own it. It is not valid for him to own it nor for him to own it. Although we say that it is valid for him to own it, everything in his hand belongs to his master by consensus according to both opinions. And God knows best.
75:16: The Almighty said: Move not your tongue with it to hasten it. In Al-Tirmidhi: "On the authority of Sa'id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the Qur'an was revealed to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, he would move his tongue with it, wanting to memorize it. Then God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed: "Move not your tongue with it to hasten it." He said: So he would move his lips with it." "And Sufyan moved his lips. Abu 'Isa said: This is a good and authentic hadith. And Muslim's wording is on the authority of Ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was struggling with the severity of the revelation. He would move his lips, so Ibn Abbas said to me: I move them as the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, used to move them. Sa'id said: I move them as Ibn Abbas used to move them. So he moved his lips, and then God, the Almighty, revealed: "Move not your tongue with it to hasten it."
75:17: God Almighty said: Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation. He said: Collect it in your chest and then recite it.
75:18: God the Almighty said: So when We have recited it, then follow its recitation. He said: So listen to it and be silent. Then it is upon us to recite it. So after that, Gabriel, peace be upon them both, would come to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he would listen. And when Gabriel, peace be upon him, departed, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would recite it as he had approved. This was also narrated by Al-Bukhari. Similar to this verse is God the Almighty's saying: And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you. (Ta-Ha: 114), which has already been mentioned. Amir Al-Sha'bi said: He would hasten to recite it when it was revealed to him out of his love for it and because it was sweet to his tongue. So he was forbidden from doing that until it was complete, because some of it is connected to others. It was said: Whenever the revelation came down to him, peace be upon him, he would move his tongue with the revelation for fear that he would forget it. So the verse was revealed: And do not hasten with the Qur’an before its revelation is completed to you (Ta-Ha: 114), and the verse was revealed: We will make you recite, and you will not forget (al-A’la 87:6), and the verse was revealed: Do not move your tongue with it. Ibn Abbas said: And His recitation means and its recitation to you. Recitation and the Qur’an, according to Al-Farra’, are two sources. Qatada said: So follow His recitation means follow His laws and rulings.
75:19: The Almighty says: Then it is for Us to make it clear. That is, to explain what it contains of limits, what is permissible, and what is forbidden. This was said by Qatada. It was also said: Then it is for Us to make clear what it contains of promises and threats and to fulfill them. It was also said: That is, it is for Us to make it clear with your tongue.
75:20: The Almighty said: No. Ibn Abbas said: meaning that Abu Jahl does not believe in the interpretation and explanation of the Qur’an. It was also said: meaning (No) they do not pray nor do they pay zakat, meaning the infidels of Mecca. Rather, you love meaning, rather, you infidels of Mecca love the immediate life meaning the worldly life and the life in it.
75:21: God the Almighty said: And you leave meaning you call upon the Hereafter and working for it. In some of the interpretations it is said: The Hereafter is Paradise. The people of Medina and the Kufians read (but you love) and (you leave) with a ta' in both of them as addressing, and Abu Ubaid chose it. He said: If it weren't for the dislike of the disagreement of these reciters, I would have read it with a ya', because the human being was mentioned before that. The rest read it with a ya' as report, and this is the choice of Abu Hatim. So whoever reads with a ya' responded to the Almighty's saying: {And the human being is informed} which means people. And whoever reads it with a ta', then he confronted them with a rebuke, because that is more eloquent in the intended meaning, similar to the verse: {Indeed, these love the immediate and leave behind them a heavy Day} (al-Insan 76:27).
75:22: The Almighty said: Some faces, that Day, will be radiant, looking at their Lord. The first is from freshness, which means beauty and grace, and the second is from looking, meaning the faces of the believers will be radiant, beautiful, and soft. It is said: May God freshen them, may He make them fresh, and radiant, which means radiance, life, and wealth. From this comes the hadith: May God freshen a man who hears my words and remembers them.
75:23: The Almighty says: Looking to her Lord (Looking to her Lord) to her Creator and Owner (looking) meaning looking at her Lord, this is the opinion of the majority of scholars. There is a hadith of Suhaib on this topic, narrated by Muslim, and it was mentioned in Yunus when God the Almighty says: For those who do good is the best [reward] and even more (Yunus 10:26). Ibn Umar used to say: The most honored of the people of Paradise in the sight of God is the one who looks at His face morning and evening, then he recited this verse: Some faces, that Day, will be radiant * Looking at their Lord (al-Qiyamah 75:22-23). Yazid Al-Nahwi narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: Looking at their Lord. Al-Hasan used to say: Their faces will be radiant and they will look at their Lord. It was said: The looking here is awaiting the reward they will have from God. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar and Mujahid. Ikrimah said: They are awaiting the command of their Lord. Al-Mawardi narrated it on the authority of Ibn Umar and Ikrimah as well, and it is not known except from Mujahid alone. They cited as evidence the words of God the Almighty: No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision. (al-An’am 6:103) This statement is very weak and goes beyond the apparent meaning of the verse and the hadiths. In Al-Tirmidhi, it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “The lowest in status of the people of Paradise will be he who looks at his gardens, wives, servants, and couches a distance of a thousand years’ journey. The most honored of them in the sight of God will be he who looks at His face morning and evening.” Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited: Some faces, that Day, will be radiant, looking at their Lord. He said: This is a strange hadith. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, but he did not attribute it to the Prophet. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Qays, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Two gardens of silver, their vessels and everything in them, and two gardens of gold, their vessels and everything in them. Nothing stands between the people and seeing their Lord, may He be glorified and exalted, except the cloak of majesty over His face in the Garden of Eden.” Jarir ibn Abdullah narrated: We were sitting with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he looked at the moon on the night of the full moon and said: “You will see your Lord clearly just as you see this moon. You will not be harmed in seeing Him. If you can avoid being overcome in prayer before sunrise and before sunset, then do so.” Then he recited: And glorify the praises of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting. (Qaf: 39) Agreed upon. It was also narrated by Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi, who said it is a good and authentic hadith. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Abu Razin al-Uqayli who said: I said, O Messenger of God, will all of us see our Lord? Ibn Muadh said: Alone with Him on the Day of Resurrection? He said: Yes, O Abu Razin. He said: What is the sign of that in His creation? He said: O Abu Razin, do not all of you see the moon? Ibn Muadh said: On the night of the full moon, alone with Him. We said: Yes. He said: Then God is greater. Ibn Muadh said: He said: It is only a creation of God’s creation - meaning the moon - so God is greater and greater. And in the book of al-Nasa’i on the authority of Suhaib who said: How about the veil so that they look at it? By God, God has not given them anything more beloved to them than looking, nor more soothing to their eyes. And in the interpretation of Abu Ishaq al-Tha’labi on the authority of [Abu] al-Zubayr on the authority of Jabir who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Our Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, will manifest Himself until they look at His face, and they will fall down before Him in prostration. He will say, ‘Raise your heads, for this is not a day of worship.’” Al-Tha’labi said: Mujahid’s statement that it means waiting for the reward from his Lord, and none of His creation will see him, is a flawed interpretation, because when the Arabs meant to wait by looking, they said ‘he looked at him,’ as God, the Almighty, said: Do they await anything but the Hour? (Az-Zukhruf 43:66), Do they await anything but its interpretation? (Al-A’raf 7:53), and They await nothing but a single blast? (Yasin 36:49). And if they meant to think and reflect, they said: I looked at him. But if looking is coupled with mentioning to and mentioning the face, then it can only mean seeing and gazing. Al-Azhari said: Mujahid’s statement, She is waiting for the reward of her Lord, is wrong, because it is not said, He looked at something in the sense of waiting. And the saying of the speaker, I looked at so-and-so is nothing but seeing with the eye. The Arabs say this, because they say, I looked at him, if they mean seeing with the eye. But if they mean waiting, they say, I looked at him. He said: If you both give me a moment of time, it will benefit me with Umm Jundub. When he wanted to wait, he said, You are waiting for me, and he did not say, You are waiting for me. And when they wanted to look at the eye, they said, I looked at him. He said: I looked at her and the stars were like monks' lamps lit for locks Another said: I look to you as a poor man looks to a rich man. That is, I look at you with humility, because the look of humility and submission is more tender to the heart of the one being asked. As for the evidence they offer from the saying of God the Almighty: {No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision} (Al-An`am: 103), this only applies to this world. We have already discussed this in its proper place. Atiyyah Al-`Awfi said: They look at God, their eyes cannot encompass them because of His greatness, but His sight encompasses them, as indicated by the verse: {No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision} (Al-An`am: 103). Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr said: It was said that (to) is one of the blessings: the blessing of repelling, and they are in Paradise, they do not await the averting of His punishment from them, and the one who awaits something has a miserable life, so the people of Paradise are not described with that. It was said that the look is attributed to the face, and it is like the saying of God the Almighty: {Beneath which rivers flow} (al-Baqarah 2:25), and water runs in the river, not the river. Then the face may be mentioned in the sense of the eye, as God the Almighty said: {Then cast it upon my father’s face; he will come seeing} (Yusuf 12:93), meaning upon his eyes. Then the heart of habit is not far from tomorrow, until it creates vision and looking at the face, and it is like the saying of the Almighty: Is he who walks on his face? (al-Mulk 67:22), “It was said: O Messenger of God! How do they walk in the Fire on their faces? He said: (He who made them walk on their feet is able to make them walk on their faces)”
75:24: The Almighty said: And faces that Day will be gloomy. Meaning, the faces of the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection will be gloomy, gloomy, and scowling. In As-Sahah: The stallion is the she-camel and he beats her without mating her. And the man's face will be basura, meaning it will be dark. It is said: he frowned basura. As-Suddi said: (Basira) means changed, and the meaning is the same.
75:25: The Almighty said: You think that He will do to her a great calamity meaning you are certain and know. Faqirah is a disaster and a great matter. It is said: Faqra broke him meaning he broke the vertebrae of his back. Mujahid and others said its meaning. Qatada said: Faqirah is evil. As-Suddi: destruction. Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd: entering the fire. The meanings are close. Its origin is the branding on the camel's nose with an iron or fire until it reaches the bone, as Al-Asma'i said. It is said: I broke the camel's nose if you cut it with an iron and then put a jagged string on the place of the cut, to tame and tame it. From this comes their saying: The faqirah has been done to him. An-Nabigha said: I have a grave that is still in front of me and an axe blow above my head
75:26: The Almighty’s saying: No! When it reaches the collarbones. (No!) is a deterrent and a warning, meaning it is unlikely that the disbeliever will believe in the Day of Resurrection. Then He resumed by saying: When it reaches the collarbones, meaning when the soul or spirit reaches the collarbones. He informed about something that was not mentioned before, because the one addressed knew about it, like the Almighty’s saying: Until it is hidden by the veil (Surah Sad: 32) and His saying: Then why, when it reaches the throat? (Surah al-Waqi’ah 56:83), which has already been mentioned. It was said that (No!) means truly, meaning truly the one being led to God (When it reaches the collarbones) meaning when it ascends to the collarbones. Ibn Abbas used to say: When the soul of the disbeliever reaches the collarbones. Collarbones are the plural of collarbone, which are the bones surrounding the hollow of the throat, which is the front of the throat from the top of the chest, the site of the rattle. Duraid ibn al-Summa said: And a great Lord defended them, and their souls reached the collarbones. Healing from death may be referred to as the soul reaching the collarbone, and the purpose is to remind them of the severity of the situation when death descends.
75:27: The Almighty’s statement: “And it was said: ‘Whosoever recites an incantation?’” There is a difference of opinion regarding it. Some say it is from the word ruqyah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, and others. Samak narrated on the authority of Ikrimah that he said: Whosoever recites an incantation, he will cure means heal. Maymun ibn Mihran narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Is there a doctor who will cure him? Abu Qilabah and Qatadah said the same. The poet said: Is there a protector for a young man from the daughters of time, or is there a healer from the death baths? This was done on the basis of exclusion and despair, meaning who can ascend from death? And from Ibn Abbas also and Abu Al-Juza that it is from raqa yarqa: if he ascends, and the meaning is: who ascends his soul to the heavens? The angels of mercy or the angels of torment? And it was said: The Angel of Death says: who ascends? That is, who ascends with this soul, because the soul of the disbeliever hates the angels being close to it, so the Angel of Death says: O so-and-so, ascend with it. Asim and some people pronounced the nun in the verse of God the Most High: whoever ascends and the lam in His statement: (but ran) lest it be likened to maraaq who is a broth seller, and baran in the double wheat. The correct view is to leave it pronounced, and the kasra of the qaf in whoever ascends and the fatha of the nun in (but ran) is sufficient to remove ambiguity. An example of what was mentioned: He intended to stop at (man) and (bal), so he pronounced them, as Al-Qushayri said.
75:28: God Almighty says: And he thought meaning the person was certain that it was parting meaning parting from the world, family, wealth and children, and that was when he saw the angels. And the poet said: A separation like no other, a separation in which all hope of meeting has been lost
75:29: The Almighty said: And the leg shall be entwined with the leg meaning, one severity shall be joined with another, the severity of the last day of this world with the severity of the first day of the Hereafter. This was stated by Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan and others. Al-Sha'bi and others said: The meaning is that the legs of a person shall be entwined at the time of death due to the severity of the anguish. Qatadah said: Have you not seen him, when he is on the verge of death, striking one leg against the other? Sa'id ibn Al-Musayyab and Al-Hasan also said: They are the legs of a person when they are entwined in the shroud. Zayd ibn Aslam said: The leg of the shroud is entwined with the leg of the dead person. Al-Hasan also said: His legs died and his legs dried up so that they could not support him, and he was carried on them like a sled. Al-Hasan said: The first statement is the best. Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn Abbas: And the leg shall be entwined with the leg He said: The last day of this world and the first day of the Hereafter, so one severity meets another, except for whom God has mercy, meaning the severity of the anguish of death with the severity of the horror of the Day of Resurrection.
75:30: The evidence for this is the Almighty's saying: To your Lord, that Day, is the driving. Mujahid said: One trial after another. He says: Hardships befell him one after the other. Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said: Two severe matters came together for him: People were preparing his body, and the angels were preparing his soul. The Arabs only mention the leg in times of great trials and tribulations, and from this is their saying: The world stood on one leg, and the war stood on another leg. The poet said: The war started against us This meaning was mentioned at the end of Surat Nun and the Pen. Some people said: The soul of the disbeliever is tormented when his soul departs. This is the first stage. Then after them comes the stage of resurrection and its hardships: To your Lord meaning to your Creator. On that Day meaning the Day of Resurrection. The drive meaning the return. In some commentaries it says: His angel who was preserving his evil deeds drives him. The drive is the verbal noun from saqā yasūq, like maqāl from qāla yaqūl.
75:31: God the Almighty says: And he neither believed nor prayed meaning Abu Jahl did not believe nor pray. It was said that this refers to the human being in the beginning of the surah, and it is a generic noun. The first is the saying of Ibn Abbas. That is, he did not believe in the message (nor pray) and supplicated to his Lord, and prayed for his Messenger. Qatada said: He neither believed in the Book of God, nor prayed to God. It was also said: He neither believed in his wealth, which was stored up for him with God, nor did he pray the prayers that God commanded him to do. It was also said: He neither believed in his heart nor did he act with his body. Al-Kisa'i said: (La) means lam, but it is paired with something else. The Arabs say: Neither Abdullah is outside nor so-and-so, and you do not say: I passed by a man who is not good, so that it can be said: nor is it general. God the Almighty's saying: And he did not storm the steep path (al-Balad 90:11) is not of this type, because its meaning is: Why did he not storm, meaning why did he not storm, so the interrogative alif was deleted. Al-Akhfash said: He did not believe, meaning he did not believe, like his saying: He did not storm, meaning he did not storm. He did not stipulate that it be followed by anything else. The Arabs say: He did not go, meaning he did not go. So the letter of negation negates the past just as it negates the future. From this is the saying of Zuhair: He neither showed it nor advanced it
75:32: God Almighty says: But he denied and turned away. That is, he denied the Qur’an and turned away from faith.
75:33: The Almighty said: Then he went to his family, swaggering meaning, swaggering, proud of that, as said by Mujahid and others. Mujahid: It refers to Abu Jahl. It was also said: (stretching) comes from mata, which means back, and the meaning is he twists his tuck. It was also said: its origin is yamtattu, which is stretching from laziness and sluggishness, so he is sluggish about calling to the truth, so the taa was replaced with a yaa out of dislike for doubling. Stretching indicates lack of concern, and it is stretching, as if he stretches his back and twists it from strutting. The stagnant water at the bottom of the basin, because it stretches, that is, it expands. In the hadith: (If my nation walks with swagger and the Persians and Romans serve them, their fighting will be among themselves) And swaggering means swaggering and extending the arms while walking.
75:34: The Almighty's saying: It is more fitting for you, then more fitting is a threat after a threat, and a warning after a warning, meaning it is a warning four times four, as it was narrated that it was revealed about Abu Jahl, who was ignorant of his Lord, and he said: He neither believed nor prayed, but he lied and turned away meaning he did not believe the Messenger of God, nor did he stand before Me and pray, but he lied about My Messenger, and turned away from praying before Me. So abandoning belief is a characteristic, and denial is a characteristic, and abandoning prayer is a characteristic, and turning away from God Almighty is a characteristic. So the warning came four times in response to abandoning the four characteristics. And God knows best. It should not be said that his saying Then he went to his family, strutting about is a fifth characteristic, for we say that this was his habit before denying and turning away, so he informed about it. This is clear in the statement of Qatada, as we will mention. It was said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, left the mosque one day, and Abu Jahl met him at the door of the mosque, which is next to the door of Banu Makhzum. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took him by the hand, shook him once or twice, then said: ‘I have more right to you, I have more right to you.’ Abu Jahl said to him: ‘Are you threatening me? By God, I am the most honorable and generous of the people of the valley.’ And he descended upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as he had said to Abu Jahl.” It is a word of threat. The poet said: First, then first, then first. Is there a milker who milks from a camel?
75:35: God Almighty says: It is better for you, then better, then better for you, then better. Qatada said: Abu Jahl ibn Hisham came swaggering, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took him by the hand and said: It is more fitting for you, then more fitting, then more fitting for you. He said: “Neither you nor your Lord can do anything to me. I am more honorable than the two mountains between them.” Then, on the day of Badr, he looked down upon the Muslims and said: God will never be worshipped after this day. So God struck his neck and killed him in the worst way. It was said that its meaning is: Woe to you. And from this is the saying of Al-Khansa’: I have thought of all my worries, so the first thing that is best for myself is the first thing for her I will carry myself on a machine, either on it or for it The machine: the state, and the machine: also the bed on which the dead is carried, and on this interpretation it was said: it is from the inverted, as if it was said: woe, then the last letter is the weak letter, and the meaning: woe to you alive, and woe to you dead, and woe to you on the Day of Resurrection, and woe to you on the day you enter the Fire, and this repetition is as he said: You are a shame, you are a man Woe to you, then woe, then woe. This statement is weak. It was said: Its meaning is that blaming you is more appropriate than abandoning it, but it is common in speech and was omitted. It was said: The meaning is that you are more appropriate and deserving of this punishment. Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya said: Al-Asma’i said: (more appropriate) in the speech of the Arabs means closeness. God the Most High said: O you who have believed, fight those adjacent to you of the disbelievers (al-Tawbah 9:123) meaning those close to you. Al-Asma’i recited: He should be loyal to him Any boat to have, and also sing It is better for someone who is upset to be sad That is, its owner has come close to grief. Abu al-Abbas Tha’lab used to approve of al-Asma’i’s saying: No one interprets like al-Asma’i. An-Nahhas said: The Arabs say it is better for you: you almost perished and then escaped, as if it means: it is better for you and it is better for you to perish. Al-Mahdawi said: It is not better for better than you and it is the predicate of a deleted subject, as if he said: the threat is better for him than for others, because Abu Zaid said: the first ones now: if they are threatened. The inclusion of the feminine marker is evidence that it is not like that. For you is the predicate of the first ones. The first ones was not declined because it became a name for the threat, so it became like a man named Ahmad. It was said: The repetition in it means I will stick to you for your first bad deed, then for the second, the third, and the fourth, as mentioned above.
75:36: God Almighty says: Does man think meaning does the son of Adam that he will be left neglected meaning that he will be left unattended, neither commanded nor forbidden, as stated by Ibn Zayd and Mujahid. From this comes the word sada meaning camels grazing without a shepherd. It was also said: Does he think that he will be left in his grave like this forever, never to be resurrected? And the poet said: I swear by God with the strongest oath that God has left nothing in vain.
75:37: The Almighty said: Was he not a drop of emitted semen? That is, from a drop of water that was emitted in the womb, that is, it was shed into it. That is why it was called semen because of the shedding of blood. It was mentioned before. Semen is a small amount of water. It is said, Nathafat al-Ma' when it drips. That is, was it not a small amount of water in the loins of the man and the collarbones of the woman? Hafs read min mani yumna with a ya', and this is the reading of Ibn Muhaisin, Mujahid, Ya'qub, and Ayyash on the authority of Abu Umar. Abu Ubaid chose it because of semen. The rest read it with a ta' because of the semen. Abu Hatim chose it.
75:38: The Almighty said: Then he was a clot meaning blood after the sperm, meaning that the Almighty arranged all of this according to the baseness of his status. Then He said: Then he created meaning he determined Then he proportioned meaning he proportioned him perfectly, and made him proportionate by placing the soul within him.
75:39: The Almighty said: Then He made from him meaning from the human being. It was also said: from semen. Then the two mates, the male and female meaning the man and the woman. This was used as evidence by those who view the hermaphrodite as permissible to abort. This has also been discussed in Surat An-Nisa', and we mentioned its ruling in the verse on inheritance, so there is no point in repeating it.
75:40: The Almighty says: Is He not able to do that? That is, is He not able to create this soul from a drop of water? Able to bring the dead to life? That is, to restore these bodies to their original state for resurrection after they have decayed. It was narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: When he recited it, he would say: Glory be to You, O God, indeed. Ibn Abbas said: “Whoever recites ‘Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High’ (al-A’la 87:1), whether he is an imam or otherwise, should say: ‘Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.’ And whoever recites ‘I swear by the Day of Resurrection’ to the end, whether he is an imam or otherwise, should say: ‘Glory be to You, O God, indeed.’” Al-Tha’labi mentioned it from the hadith of Abu Ishaq al-Sabi’i, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Abu Abbas: I have completed the surah, and praise be to God.
76:1: It was revealed in Mecca according to Ibn Abbas, Muqatil, and Al-Kalbi. The majority said it was revealed in Medina, and some said it was revealed in Mecca, from the words of God Almighty: Indeed, it is We who have sent down to you the Qur’an gradually, to the end of the Surah. What precedes it is Medinan. “Ibn Wahb said: Ibn Zayd told us: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would recite “Has there not been over man a period of time?” and it was revealed to him while a black man was with him who used to ask the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Umar ibn Al-Khattab said to him: Do not burden the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Leave him, Ibn Al-Khattab. He said: So this Surah was revealed to him while he was with him. When he recited it to him and reached the description of Paradise, he sighed and his soul left him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The soul of your companion or brother left him, longing for Paradise.” It was narrated from Ibn Umar with a different wording, and it will come. Al-Qushayri said that this Surah was revealed about Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, and the meaning of the wording is general, and this is the same for everything that is said to have been revealed for such and such a reason. God the Almighty said: Has there not been over man a period of time when he was not a thing worth mentioning? “Half” means has already been, as stated by Al-Kisa’i, Al-Fa’, and Abu Ubaidah. It has been narrated from Sibawayh that Half means has already been. Al-Farra’ said: Half can be a denial, or it can be a predicate, and this is from the predicate, because you say: Did I give you? You confirm that you gave him. Denial is to say: Is anyone capable of such a thing? It was also said: It is in the position of a question, and the meaning is: has come. The human being here is Adam, peace be upon him, as stated by Qatada, Al-Thawri, Ikrimah, and Al-Suddi. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas: A period of time, Ibn Abbas said in the narration of Abu Salih: Forty years passed him, before the soul was breathed into him, and he was lying between Mecca and Taif. It was also narrated from Ibn Abbas in the narration of Al-Dahhak that he was created from clay, and he remained for forty years, then from altered black mud for forty years, then from clay for forty years, and his creation was completed after one hundred and twenty years. Ibn Masoud added: He remained from dust for forty years, then his creation was completed after one hundred and sixty years, then the spirit was breathed into him. It was said: The time mentioned here is: its extent is not known? Also from Ibn Abbas, narrated by Al-Mawardi. He was not a thing mentioned. Ad-Dahhak said from Ibn Abbas: Neither in the heavens nor on the earth. It was said: That is, he was a body formed from dust and clay, neither mentioned nor recognized, nor its name nor its being known, then the spirit was breathed into him, so he became mentioned. This was said by Al-Farra’, Qatrib, and Tha’lab. Yahya bin Salam said: He was not a thing mentioned in creation, even though he was something mentioned with God. It was said: This mention does not mean informing, for the Lord’s informing about beings is eternal, rather this mention means danger, honor, and value. You say: So-and-so is mentioned, meaning he has honor and value. God the Almighty said: And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people (Az-Zukhruf 43:44), meaning a time came when man had no value with the caliph. Then when God informed the angels that He had made Adam a successor and entrusted him with the trust that the heavens, the earth and the mountains could not fulfill, his superiority over all was evident, so he became mentioned. Al-Qushayri said: In short, he was not mentioned to creation, even if he was mentioned to God. Muhammad ibn al-Jahm narrated from al-Farra’: (He was not a thing) he said: He was a thing but he was not mentioned. Some people said: The negation refers to the thing, meaning that a period of time had passed and Adam was not a thing worth mentioning in creation, because he was the last of the types of creation He created, and the non-existent is not a thing until a time comes for him. The meaning is: Time had passed for him and Adam was neither a thing nor a creation nor mentioned to any of creation. This is the meaning of the words of Qatadah and Muqatil: Qatadah said: Man was created recently. We do not know of any creation of God, the Most High, that came after man. Muqatil said: There is an inversion in the speech, and its interpretation is: Has there come a period of time in which he was not a thing worth mentioning? Because he was created after the creation of all animals, and no animal was created after him. It has been said: (The human being) in the Almighty’s saying: Has there not come upon man a period of time? He means the offspring of Adam, and that the period of time is nine months, the period of gestation of man in his mother’s womb. He was not a thing worth mentioning: since he was a clot and a lump of flesh, because in this state he is inanimate and has no life. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said when he recited this verse: If only it had ended so that we would not be tested. That is, if only the period of time that passed over Adam had not been a thing worth mentioning had ended thus, so that he would not give birth and his children would not be tested. Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, heard a man reciting: Has there not come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing worth mentioning? So he said: If only it had ended.
76:2: The Almighty says: Indeed, We created man meaning the son of Adam without dispute from a drop of semen meaning from a dripping water, which is semen, and every little water in a container is a drop of semen, like the words of Abdullah bin Rawahah, rebuking himself: Why do I see you hating heaven? Are you nothing but a drop of semen in a bag? Plural: Nutf and Nataf. Amshaj: mixtures. Singular: Mishj and Mishij, like Khadn and Khadayn. He said: Ru’yah. They throw out every hasty, sobbing thing that has not covered itself with skin into the blood of the mixed ones. It is said: He mixed this with this, meaning he blended it, so it is mamshūj and mashīj, like makhlūt and makhlīt. Al-Mubarrad said: The singular of amshāj is mashīj. It is said: mashj yamshūj if he mixes, and here it means the mixing of sperm with blood. Al-Shamakh said: Folded the entrails trembling for a time on the path of his humiliating lineage Al-Farra’ said: Amshaj is a mixture of the male and female semen, blood, and the clot. When something of this is mixed, it is said: Mashij as in Makhalith and Mamshawj as in Makhlut. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, who said: Amshaj is the redness in the whiteness, and the whiteness in the redness. This is a statement preferred by many linguists. Al-Hudhali said: As if the feathers and the upper two of them were unlike the blade, and it was controlled by a mixture It was also narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: The man’s semen, which is white and thick, mixes with the woman’s semen, which is yellow and thin, and a child is created from them. Whatever nerves, bones, and strength are from the man’s semen, and whatever flesh, blood, and hair are from the woman’s semen. This has been narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as mentioned by Al-Bazzar. It was narrated from Ibn Mas’ud that: Its mixtures are the veins of the lump of flesh. It was also narrated from him that: The man’s semen and the woman’s semen are of two colors. Mujahid said: The man’s sperm is white and red, and the woman’s sperm is green and yellow. Ibn Abbas said: He was created from colors. He was created from dust, then from the water of the vagina and uterus, which is a sperm, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, then bones, then flesh, and so on. Qatadah said: These are the stages of creation: [A stage of sperm, a stage of clot, a stage of lump of flesh, and a stage of bones] Then He covers the bones with flesh, as He says in Surah al-Mu’minun 23:And We have certainly created man from an extract of clay. (al-Mu’minun 23:12) Ibn Al-Sikkit said: Amshaj is the mixture because it is mixed from various types, and from it man was created with different natures. The scholars of semantics said: Amshaj is what is plural but has the meaning of singular, because it is an adjective for sperm, as one says: A pot of tenths and A garment of morals. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Ayyub Al-Ansari that he said: “A Jewish rabbi came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: Tell me about the man’s semen and the woman’s semen?” He said: “The man’s semen is white and the woman’s semen is yellow and thin. If the woman’s semen prevails, she becomes female, and if the man’s semen prevails, she becomes male.” The rabbi said: I bear witness that there is no god but God and that you are the Messenger of God. This statement has already been fully explained in Surah al-Baqarah 2:Nabltihi means We test him. It was also said: We decree the test for him, which is the trial. There are two aspects to what is tested: One of them is that we test him with good and evil, as Al-Kalbi said. The second is that we test his gratitude in prosperity and his patience in adversity, as Al-Hasan said. It was also said: Nabltihi means We task him. There are also two interpretations: 1- By action after creation, as stated by Muqatil. 2- By religion, so that he is commanded to obey and forbidden from sins. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: We will test him means We will change him from one creation to another, to test him with good and evil. Muhammad ibn al-Jahm narrated on the authority of al-Farra’ that he said: The meaning, and God knows best, is So We made him all-hearing and all-seeing to test him, and it is an introduction that means a delay. I said: Because the trial does not occur until after the completion of creation. And it was said, So We made him hearing and seeing, meaning that We gave him hearing with which to hear guidance, and sight with which to see guidance.
76:3: The Almighty's saying: Indeed, We showed him the way means We made clear to him and showed him the path of guidance and misguidance, good and evil by sending the messengers, so he either believed or disbelieved, like His saying: And We showed him the two ways (al-Balad 90:10). Mujahid said: meaning We showed him the path to misery and happiness. Ad-Dahhak, Abu Salih, and As-Suddi said: The way here is its emergence from the womb. It was also said: the benefits and harms that he is guided to by his nature and mind. Either grateful or ungrateful meaning whichever of the two he does, We have made it clear to him. The Kufians said: In here is a recompense and ma is redundant, meaning We made clear to him the path whether he is grateful or ungrateful. Al-Farra' chose this, but the Basrans did not accept it, since in is not used as a recompense for nouns unless a verb is implied after it. It was said: That is, We guided him to the right path, that is, We showed him the path of monotheism by establishing evidence for it, then if We created guidance for him, he was guided and believed, and if We let him down, he disbelieved. It is like saying: I have given you sincere advice, if you wish, then accept, and if you wish, then leave it, meaning if you wish, then the fa is deleted. And the same is true for either grateful and God knows best. And it is said: I guided him to the path, for the path, and to the path. This has been mentioned previously in Al-Fatihah and elsewhere. He combined the grateful and the ungrateful, but did not combine the thankful and the ungrateful, even though they both share the meaning of exaggeration, negating exaggeration in thanks and affirming it in disbelief, because thanking God the Most High does not lead to anything, so exaggeration is negated from it, but exaggeration is not negated from disbelief, so his thanks were few, due to the abundance of blessings upon him and his abundance of disbelief, even if it was little, despite the kindness towards him. Al-Mawardi narrated it.
76:4: The Almighty's saying: Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains and shackles and a Blaze. He explained the condition of the two groups, and that He worships rational beings and charges them and enables them to do what He commanded them. So whoever disbelieves will have the punishment, and whoever believes in the Oneness of God and is grateful will have the reward. The chains: the shackles in Hell, the length of each chain is seventy cubits, as mentioned in (Al-Haqqah). Nafi', Al-Kisa'i, and Abu Bakr from Asim and Hisham from Ibn Amir read (Salasil) with a tanween. The rest without a tanween. Qanbal, Ibn Kathir, and Hamzah stopped without an alif. The rest with an alif. As for the first (Qawarir), its types are Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Al-Kisa'i, and Abu Bakr from Asim, and the rest did not add a tanween. Ya'qub and Hamzah stopped without an alif. The rest with an alif. As for the second (Qawarir), its types are also Nafi', Al-Kisa'i, and Abu Bakr, and the rest did not add a tanween. So whoever reads it with an alif, and whoever does not add a tanween drops the alif, and Abu Ubaid chose the tanween in the three, and the pause with an alif following the script of the Mushaf. He said: I saw in the Mushaf of Uthman (ِالئ) with an alif and (قوارير) the first with an alif, and the second was written with an alif so I copied it and saw its effect there clearly. So whoever declined has four arguments: The first - that the plurals resembled the singular, so they were made plural like the singular, so they were made according to the rule of the singular and were declined. The second - that Al-Akhfash reported from the Arabs the decline of all that is not declined except for af’al mink, and Al-Kisa’i and Al-Farra’ said the same: It is according to the language of those who decline all nouns except for their saying huwa a’zarf mink, for they do not decline it. Ibn Al-Anbari recited in that the saying of Amr ibn Kulthum: As if our swords, both within us and with them, were blunt instruments in the hands of our players. Labid said: And the islands of Issar were called to their death by locks whose bodies were identical Labid also said: Kindness and generosity help in giving and generous, willing to earn the spoils of his desires So, the inflections of Mukhariq, Mughāliq, and Raghā’ib are not inflected. The third argument is to say that we put the nun on the first Qawārīr because it is the beginning of a verse, and the beginnings of verses came with the nun, like the saying of God the Almighty: mentioned “all-Hearing, all-Seeing.” We put the nun on the first to stop between the beginnings of verses, and the nun on the second to be adjacent to the first. The fourth argument is to follow the copies of the Qur’an, because they are all combined in the copies of Makkah, Madinah, and Kufa with the alif. Those who did not inflect it in definite or indefinite nouns have argued that what comes after the alif is three letters like your saying Qanadīl, Wadiḍānīr, and Manādīl, and what comes after the alif is two letters like the saying of God the Almighty: For monasteries would have been demolished (Al-Hajj 22:40) because after the alif is two letters. Likewise, His saying: And mosques in which the name of God is much remembered (Al-Hajj 22:40) and what comes after the alif is a doubled letter like Shawāb and Dābīl. Khalaf said: I heard Yahya bin Adam narrating on the authority of Ibn Idris who said: In the first copies of the Qur’an, the first letter is with an alif and the second without an alif. This is an argument for the school of thought of Hamza. Khalaf said: I saw in a Qur’an attributed to the reading of Ibn Masoud the first is with an alif and the second changes the alif. And what is more beautiful than you, no Arab says in his poetry or otherwise it is more beautiful than you with a tanween, because whoever takes the place of an addition does not combine a tanween and an addition in a letter, because they are two indicators of nouns and two indicators are not combined, said Al-Farra’ and others. God the Almighty said: And shackles is the plural of shackles with which their hands are shackled to their necks. It was narrated on the authority of Jubayr ibn Nufayr on the authority of Abu al-Darda’ who used to say: Raise these hands to God, the Most High, before they are shackled. Al-Hasan said: The shackles were not placed around the necks of the people of Hellfire because they outsmarted their Lord, the Most High, but rather as a form of humiliation. And a Blazing Fire was discussed previously.
76:5: God the Almighty says: Indeed, the righteous will drink from a cup. Al-Abrar are the people of truthfulness, the singular of which is Barr, who obeys the command of God the Almighty. It was said that Barr is the monotheist, and Al-Abrar is the plural of Barr like Shahid and Ashhad. It was also said that it is the plural of Barr like Nahr and Anhar. In As-Sahah: The plural of Barr is Al-Abrar, and the plural of Barr is Al-Barrarah. So-and-so is righteous to his Creator and obeys Him, and a mother is righteous towards her child. Ibn Umar narrated that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: (God the Almighty called them Al-Abrar because they were righteous to their fathers and children, just as your father has a right over you, so too does your child have a right over you.) Al-Hasan said: Righteousness is that which does not harm even the offspring. Qatadah said: The righteous are those who fulfill God's right and fulfill their vows. In the hadith: (The righteous are those who do not harm anyone.) They will drink from a cup meaning from a vessel containing a drink. Ibn Abbas said: He means wine. In the language, a cup is a vessel containing a drink. If there is no drink in it, it is not called a cup. Amr ibn Kulthum said: Umm Amr poured the cup for us, and the cup flowed to the right. Al-Asma’i said: It is said, He poured the gift from us, or It was a favor that we poured it from him, meaning he refrained, as Al-Jawhari said. Its mixture means he mixed it and mingled it. Hassan said: As if a woman from the house of Ras has a temperament of honey and water And from it is the body’s temperament, which is what mixes it of yellow bile and black bile, heat and cold. Camphor Ibn Abbas said: It is the name of a spring of water in Paradise, called the Spring of Camphor. That is, the water of this spring called Camphor mixes with it. Saeed said on the authority of Qatadah: It will be mixed with camphor for them and sealed with musk. Mujahid said the same. Ikrimah said: Its temperament is its taste. It was said: Camphor is in its smell, not its taste. It was said: He meant like camphor in its whiteness, pleasant scent and coolness, because camphor is not drunk, like the saying of God the Almighty: {Until, when He makes it a fire} (Al-Kahf 18:96), meaning like fire. Ibn Kaysan said: Perfumed with musk, camphor and ginger. Muqatil said: It is not the camphor of this world. Rather, God called what is with Him what is with you so that hearts may be guided to it. His statement: Its temperament was was is redundant, meaning from a cup mixed with camphor.
76:6: A spring from which the servants of God drink. Al-Farra' said: Kafur is the name of a spring of water in Paradise, so (a spring) is a substitute for camphor according to this. It was also said: a substitute for a cup according to the place. It was also said: it is a state of the implied in (its mixture). It was also said: it is accusative of praise, as when a man is mentioned, you say: the wise, intelligent one, meaning you mentioned the wise, intelligent one, so it is accusative of praise, as when a man is mentioned, you say: the wise, intelligent one, meaning you mentioned the wise, intelligent one, so it is accusative with the implied I mean. It was also said that they drink from a spring. Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is from a spring. It is also said: camphor and qafur. Camphor is also: the container for the date palm's pollen, and so is kufri, as Al-Asma'i said. As for Al-Ra'i's saying: The crossroads and the valleys are covered with a scent of reeds and camphor. The deer from which musk is made grazes on spikes of perfume, so He made it camphor. He drinks from it. Al-Farra’ said: He drinks from it and he drinks from it are the same in meaning, as if he drinks from it, quenches his thirst with it and soaks in it. He recited: They drank sea water, then the green waves rose up, and they groaned. He said: And the same applies to someone who speaks nicely, and speaks nicely. It was said: The meaning is he drinks it, and the ba’ is redundant. It was said: The ba’ is a substitute for from, meaning he drinks from it, as Al-Qutbi said. They make it gush forth abundantly. It is said that a man among them walks in his houses and ascends to his palaces, and in his hand is a stick with which he points to the water, and it flows with him wherever he goes in his dwellings at ground level, not in a ditch, and it follows him wherever he ascends to the highest of his palaces. This is the saying of God Almighty: “A spring from which the servants of God drink. They make it gush forth abundantly.” They lead it wherever they wish, and it follows them wherever they turn, and it turns with them. Abu Muqatil narrated on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Sa’d on the authority of Abu Sahl on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are four springs in Paradise. Two springs flow from beneath the Throne. One of them is the one God mentioned, ‘They make it gush forth abundantly,’ and the other is ginger. The other two are gushing forth from above the Throne. One of them is the one God mentioned, a spring in it called Salsabil, and the other is Tanseem.” Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim mentioned this in Nawader Al-Usul. He said: Tanseem is for those brought near specifically, as a drink for them, and camphor is for the righteous, as a drink for them. The righteous are mixed from Tanseem for their drink. As for ginger and Salsabil, For the righteous there is a mixture of it. This is what was mentioned in the revelation, and it was silent about mentioning who it is to drink. So whatever the righteous have a mixture of is for those brought near only, and whatever the righteous have a mixture of is for the rest of the people of Paradise. The righteous are the truthful, and those brought near are the truthful.
76:7: God the Almighty says: {They fulfill their vows and fear a Day whose evil will be widespread.} Meaning, they do not break their vows. Muammar said on the authority of Qatadah: {With what God has enjoined upon them of prayer, zakat, fasting, Hajj, Umrah, and other obligatory duties.} Mujahid and Ikrimah said: {They fulfill when they make a vow to God, the Exalted.} Al-Farra' and Al-Jurjani said: {There is an omission in the speech, meaning they used to fulfill their vows in this world.} The Arabs sometimes add the word kana once and omit it another time. The true meaning of a vow is an act of worship that a person obligated to perform, such that if he had not obligated it, it would not be binding on him. Al-Kalbi said: {They fulfill their vows.} Meaning, they complete their covenants, and the meaning is the same. God the Almighty said: {Then let them complete their rites and fulfill their vows.} (al-Hajj 22:29) Meaning, the rituals of the Hajj that they obligated themselves to perform when they entered ihram for Hajj. This supports Qatadah's statement. A vow includes a person's commitment to obey God's commands through faith. This was stated by Al-Qushayri. Ashab narrated on the authority of Malik that he said: They fulfill their vows refers to vows to free slaves, fast, and pray. Abu Bakr ibn Abd Al-Aziz narrated on his authority that Malik said: They fulfill their vows means an oath. God Almighty says: And they fear meaning they are wary of a Day meaning the Day of Resurrection. The evil of which will be widespread meaning high, devastating, and widespread. In the language, it means widespread. The Arabs say: The crack in the bottle or the glass spread and became elongated, meaning it extended. Al-A’sha said: And she appeared, and she had caused a rift in my heart, despite her distance, spreading It is said: The fire spread, if it spread. And the dawn spread, if the light spread. Hassan said: A fire broke out in Bouira, Bani Luay Qatada used to say: By God, the evil of that day spread until it filled the heavens and the earth. Muqatil said: Its evil spread throughout the heavens, so they split open, the stars scattered, the angels were terrified, and the mountains on the earth were blown away and the waters sank.
76:8: God the Almighty says: And they give food, in spite of their love for it. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: In spite of its scarcity, their love for it, and their desire for it. Ad-Darani said: In spite of the love of God. Al-Fudayl ibn Iyad said: In spite of the love of giving food. Whenever a beggar would come to Ar-Rabi' ibn Khathim, he would say: Feed him sugar, for Ar-Rabi' loves sugar. Miskin means one who is in need. Abu Salih narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: It is going around asking you about your wealth. And an orphan means one of the orphans of the Muslims. Mansour narrated from Al-Hasan, who said: An orphan used to attend Ibn Umar's meal, so one day he asked for his food and looked for the orphan but could not find him. He came after Ibn Umar had finished his meal but could not find any food, so the Prophet asked for barley porridge and honey and said: Take this, for by God, I have not been cheated. Al-Hasan and Ibn Umar said: By God, he was not cheated. And a prisoner means one who is taken prisoner and imprisoned. Abu Salih narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: A prisoner is one who is imprisoned. And this is what Saeed bin Jubair and Ata’ said: It is a Muslim who is imprisoned justly. And from Saeed bin Jubair, something similar was said by Qatada and Ibn Abbas. Qatada said: God has commanded that the prisoners be treated well, and their captives at that time were the polytheists, and your Muslim brother has more right to be fed. And Ikrimah said: The captive is the slave. And Abu Hamza al-Thamali said: The captive is the woman, as indicated by the words of the Prophet, peace be upon him: (Treat women well, for they are captives with you) meaning captives. Abu Saeed Al-Khudri said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited: {And they give food, in spite of love for it, to the poor, the orphan, and the captive} and said: (The poor is the needy, and the orphan who has no father, and the captive who is a slave, and the prisoner) Al-Tha’labi mentioned it. It was said that feeding the poor abrogated the verse on charity, and feeding the captive was abrogated by the verse on the sword, as said by Saeed bin Jubair. Another said: Rather, the ruling remains the same, and feeding the orphan and the poor is voluntary, and feeding the captive is for the sake of his life, unless the ruler makes a choice in it. Al-Mawardi: It is possible that what is meant by the captive is the one with a defective mind, because in captivity he is insane and insane, and capturing a polytheist is revenge that depends on the opinion of the ruler, and this is righteousness and kindness. Ata’ said: The captive is from the people of the Qiblah and others. I said: It seems that this statement is general and includes all statements, and feeding the polytheist prisoner is an act of devotion to God Almighty, except that it is voluntary charity, but not obligatory charity. And God knows best. The discussion of the poor, the orphan, and the prisoner and the derivation of that from the language has already been completed in Al-Baqarah, and praise be to God.
76:9: The Almighty says: {We feed you only for the sake of God} meaning they say with their tongues, and the orphan and the captive, {We feed you only} for the sake of God, may He be glorified, fearing His punishment and tasting His reward. {We desire from you no reward} meaning no recompense. {Nor thanks} meaning do not praise Us for that. Ibn Abbas said: That was their intentions in this world when they fed. Salim narrated from Mujahid who said: They did not speak about it, but God, may He be glorified, knew it from them and praised them for it, so that someone might desire it. Saeed bin Jubair said the same, and Al-Qushayri narrated it from him. It was said that this verse was revealed about Mut’im bin Warqa’ Al-Ansari who made a vow and fulfilled it. It was also said that it was revealed about those who took care of the prisoners of Badr, and they were seven of the Muhajireen: Abu Bakr, Umar, Ali, Al-Zubayr, Abd Al-Rahman bin Awf, Saad, and Abu Ubaidah, may God be pleased with them. Al-Mawardi mentioned this. Muqatil said: It was revealed about a man from the Ansar who fed a poor person, an orphan, and a captive in one day. Abu Hamza al-Thamali said: I heard that a man said, ‘O Messenger of God, feed me, for by God I am exhausted.’ He said, ‘By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I do not have anything to feed you, but you should ask.’ So a man from the Ansar came while he was having dinner with his wife and asked him, and told him what the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had said. The woman said, Feed him and give him something to drink. Then an orphan came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said, O Messenger of God, feed me, for I am exhausted. He said, I do not have anything to feed you, but I should ask. So the Ansari asked for food, and the woman said, Feed him and give him something to drink. So he fed him. Then a captive came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said, O Messenger of God, feed me, for I am exhausted. He said, By God, I do not have anything to feed you, but I should ask. So the Ansari came and asked, and the woman said, Feed him and give him something to drink. Then the verse was revealed: And they feed food, in spite of their love for it, to the poor, the orphan, and the captive. This was mentioned by al-Tha’labi. The commentators said: It was revealed about Ali and Fatima, may God be pleased with them, and a slave girl of theirs named Fadda. I said: The correct view is that it was revealed regarding all the righteous and those who do good deeds, so it is general. Al-Naqqash, Al-Tha’labi, Al-Qushayri, and more than one of the commentators mentioned a hadith about the story of Ali, Fatima, and their slave girl that is neither authentic nor proven. It was narrated by Layth on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas: In the words of God the Almighty: “They fulfill their vows and fear a Day whose evil will be widespread. And they give food, in spite of their love for it, to the poor, the orphan, and the captive.” He said: “Al-Hasan and Al-Hussain fell ill, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) visited them, and so did most of the Arabs. They said: O Abu Al-Hasan” - and Jabir Al-Ju’fi narrated it on the authority of Qanbar, the freed slave of Ali, who said: Al-Hasan and Al-Hussain fell ill until the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) visited them. Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him said: O Abu Al-Hasan - the hadith goes back to the hadith of Layth ibn Abi Sulaym - what if you vowed something on behalf of your two sons, and every vow that cannot be fulfilled is nothing. So he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: If my two sons recover, I will fast for three days in gratitude to God. A Nubian slave girl of theirs said: If my master recovers, I will fast for three days in gratitude to God. Fatimah said the same. In the hadith of Al-Ja'fi, Al-Hassan and Al-Hussein said: We are like that, so dress the two boys in good health, and the family of Muhammad does not have much or little. So Ali went to Shimon bin Hariya Al-Khaibari, who was a Jew, and borrowed from him three sa's of barley, which he brought and placed in the corner of the house. Fatima got a sa' and ground it and tested it. Ali prayed with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, then he came to the house and placed the food in front of him. In the hadith of Al-Ja'fi: The girl got a sa' of barley and baked five loaves of bread from it, one for each of them. When their first fast was over, he placed bread and coarse salt in their hands, when a poor man came to them and stood at the door and said: Peace be upon you, people of the household of Muhammad - in the hadith of Al-Ja'fi - I am a poor man from the poor people of the nation of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and by God I am hungry. Feed me and may God feed you from the tables of Paradise. Ali, may God be pleased with him, heard him and began to say: Fatima, the one with virtue and certainty, is the daughter of the best of all people. Don't you see the poor, miserable man standing at the door, yearning for him? He complains to God and submits. He complains to us, hungry and sad. Every person is held in pledge for his earnings, but the doer of good deeds will see his reward revealed. Our appointment is in the highest paradise, which God has forbidden to the miserly. The miser has a humiliating position that leads him to hellfire and prison. His drink is hot water and two washes. Whoever does good will rise up fat. He will enter heaven at any time Then Fatima, may God be pleased with her, began to say: I obey your orders, cousin. I have no meanness or baseness in me. I became a bread maker, I make food and I don't care about the time I hope that if I satisfy this hunger, I will catch up with the report and the group And enter heaven for me intercession So they fed him food, and they spent a day and a night without tasting anything except pure water. When it was the second day, she got a saa’ a measure of food, ground it, and baked it. Ali prayed with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), then he came to the house and placed the food in their hands. An orphan stood at the door and said: “Peace be upon you, O people of the household of Muhammad.” - in the hadith of al-Ja’fi - “I am a poor man from among the poor of the nation of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and by God I am hungry. Feed me, and God will feed you from the tables of Paradise.” Ali may God be pleased with him heard him and began to say: So they fed him food, and they spent a day and a night without tasting anything except pure water. On the second day, she got a saa’ measure of food, ground it, and tested it. Ali prayed with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Then he came to the house and placed the food in their hands. An orphan stood at the door and said: “Peace be upon you, O people of the household of Muhammad. I am an orphan from the children of the emigrants. My father was martyred on the day of Aqaba. Feed me, and God will feed you from the tables of Paradise.” Ali heard him and began to say: Fatima, daughter of the noble master, daughter of a prophet who is not a fornicator God has brought the orphan. Whoever shows mercy today will be merciful. And he who is healthy will enter Paradise, for eternity has been forbidden to the vile. Is it not permissible to take the straight path and slip into the fire and into hell? Drink pus and hot water Then Fatima, may God be pleased with her, began to say: I feed him today and I don't care, and I prefer God over my children They went hungry, and they are my cubs, the youngest of them is killed in the fighting Bakr Bilal kills by assassination, woe to the killer and his punishment The fire will throw him down into the depths, and he will be bound with chains and shackles in his hands. A cable that has become more heavy than the cables So they fed him food and stayed for two days and two nights without tasting anything except pure water. On the third day, she got the remaining sa’, ground it, and tested it. Ali prayed with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Then he came to the house and placed the food in their hands. Suddenly, a prisoner came and stood at the door and said: “Peace be upon you, O people of the household of Muhammad. You take us captive and chain us up without feeding us! Feed me, for I am Muhammad’s prisoner.” Ali heard him and began to say: Fatima, daughter of the Prophet Ahmed, daughter of the master prophet Masoud And God named him Muhammad, and God adorned him with a beautiful, graceful face. This is a prisoner of the guided prophet, burdened with a chain. Hunger has come to us, he who feeds himself today will find it tomorrow. With the One and Only God, whatever the sower sows, he will reap. Give it to him, no, don't make him sit Then Fatima, may God be pleased with her, began to say: There is not a saa' left of what came. My hand is gone with my arm. My sons, by God, are hungry. Oh God, do not leave them lost. Their father is a man of good character who does good deeds with innovation. I have long arms and a strong hand, and I have no mask on my head Except a mask woven from the fabric So they gave him food and stayed for three days and nights without tasting anything except pure water. When it was the fourth day, and God had fulfilled the vow, he took al-Hasan with his right hand and al-Husayn with his left hand, and approached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while they were trembling like chicks from severe hunger. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw them, he said: “O Abu al-Hasan, what I see in you is most distressing to me. Let us go to my daughter Fatima.” So they went to her while she was in her prayer niche, her belly stuck to her back, and her eyes sunken in from severe hunger. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw her and recognized the famine in her face, he wept and said: Oh God, help! The family of Muhammad are dying of hunger. Then Gabriel, peace be upon him, descended and said: “Peace be upon you. Your Lord sends you peace, O Muhammad. Take it in good health among your family.” He said: And what should I take, O Gabriel? So he recited to him: Has there not been over man a period of time? until His saying: And they give food, in spite of their love for it, to the poor, the orphan, and the captive. "We feed you only for the sake of God. We desire from you neither reward nor thanks." Al-Tirmidhi the wise Abu Abdullah said in Nawader Al-Awal: This is a fabricated and fabricated hadith, in which its speaker has gone to extremes to the point that it seems to the listeners. The one who is ignorant of this hadith bites his lips in longing not to be of this description, not knowing that the one who does this is blameworthy. God the Most High said in His revelation: "And they ask you, what they should spend. Say, 'The excess.'" (al-Baqarah 2:219) It is the excess that one has over one's own wealth and children. There are many reports from the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) that: "The best charity is that which one earns from surplus wealth. And start with yourself, then with those under your care." God has enjoined on spouses the maintenance of their families and children. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: It is enough of a sin for a man to neglect those he is responsible for providing for. Can a sane person think that Ali was ignorant of this matter to the point that he exhausted young boys, five or six years old, with hunger for three days and nights? Until they were starving, and their eyes filled with tears because of their empty stomachs, until the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) wept over the exhaustion they were under. Suppose he had preferred this questioner over himself, would he have been permitted to force his family to do that?! Such a thing only occurs to fools and ignorant people. God forbid that alert hearts would think such a thing of Ali.
