I wonder who memorized these verses every night from Ali and Fatima, and how each of them would answer his companion, until he conveyed it to these narrators?! This and similar stories are from the hadiths of the people in prisons, as I see. I have been informed that some people are imprisoned for eternity, and so they remain helpless. They write hadiths about evening gatherings and the like. Such hadiths are fabricated, and when they reach the scholars, they throw them out and falsify them. There is nothing that does not have a plague and a plot, and the plague and plot of religion are greater.
76:10: The Almighty said: Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day of gloom and distress. (Glooming) is an adjective of the Day, meaning a day when faces will frown due to its horror and severity, so the meaning is we fear a Day of gloom. Ibn Abbas said that the disbeliever will frown on that day until sweat will flow from him like tar. And according to Ibn Abbas: Glooming means narrow and gloom is tall. The poet said: Very sullen and frowning It was said: The severe Qamatarir. The Arabs say: A day of Qamatarir, Qamatar and Asib, with the same meaning. Al-Farra’ recited: Our cousins, do you remember our affliction upon you when it was a day of calamities? With the qaf being pronounced with a damma. And qamatar means intense. Al-Akhfash said: qamatir is the most intense of days and the longest of affliction. The poet said: Flee when the dust of war rises and the gloomy, cloudy day enters it. Al-Kisa’i said: It is said that today it rained and it became very cold, qamatarran and zamharran, and it is qamatarira and zamharir, and a rainy day if it is very difficult and intense. Al-Hudhali said: We have given them a rain of rain, and whoever encounters us that day will flee. Mujahed said: Frowning is in the lips, and frowning is in the forehead and eyebrows, so he made them among the characteristics of the face changed by the hardships of that day, and Ibn al-A’rabi recited: He goes hunting, comes back broken, it rains for an hour and then turns dark Abu Ubaidah said: It is said that a man is qamtarir, meaning he has a contracted eye socket. Al-Zajjaj said: It is said that the she-camel has aqmatar if she raises her tail, gathers her two eyes together, and puckers her nose. So he derived it from qatar and made the mim an extra letter. Asad ibn Na’isa said: And I fought wars every day, Basil Al-Shar, the morning star
76:11: The Almighty said: So God saved them meaning He warded off from them the evil of that Day meaning its violence, severity and torment and met them meaning He came to them and gave them when they met Him, meaning they saw Him, freshness meaning goodness and happiness meaning joy. Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: Freshness in their faces and happiness in their hearts. There are three aspects to freshness: The first is that it is whiteness and purity, said Al-Dahhak. The second is beauty and splendor, said Ibn Jubayr. The third is that it is the effect of a blessing, said Ibn Zayd.
76:12: God the Almighty says: And He will reward them for their patience with a garden and silk garments for poverty. Al-Qurazi said: for fasting. Ata' said: for hunger for three days, which are the days of the vow. It was also said: for their patience in obeying God, and their patience in disobeying God and doing what He has forbidden. The word ma is a verbal noun, and this is based on the fact that the verse was revealed for all the righteous and those who do good deeds. Ibn Umar narrated: "The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asked about patience, so he said: ((Patience is of four types: the first of which is patience at the first shock, patience in performing the obligatory duties, patience in avoiding what God has forbidden, and patience in calamities.)) "A garden and silk" means He will admit them to Paradise and dress them in silk. That is, it is called the silk of this world and the silk of the hereafter, and it contains whatever God the Almighty wills of bounty. It was mentioned earlier: Whoever wears silk in this world will not wear it in the hereafter, but rather the one who wears it will wear it in Paradise as a compensation for their confining themselves in this world to the clothing that God has forbidden.
76:13: The Almighty says: Reclining therein meaning in Paradise. The accusative of reclining is in the state of the ha' and the mim in He rewarded them and the operator is jaza and the operator is sabrū and the operator is sabara and the operator is sabara because patience was only in this world and reliance is in the hereafter. Al-Farra' said: If you wish, you can make reclining a dependent, as if he said He rewarded them with a Paradise "reclining therein. On couches" means the beds in the seating areas, as mentioned above. The Arabs have names that contain attributes: one of them is the couch, which is only found in a seating area on a bed. Another example is the "sajjil, which is a bucket filled with water, so when it turns yellow, it is not called a sajjil". Similarly, sins are not called sins until they are filled, and a cup is not called a cup until it is full of wine. Similarly, the plate on which a gift is given is a gift, so if it is empty, it is called a plate or a tray. Dhu al-Rummah said: Cheeks dried up from walking, as if they were touching the couches of mourners. That is, the beds on the couches. They will not see therein the sun that is, they will not see in Paradise an intense heat like the heat of the sun, nor freezing cold that is, nor excessive cold. Al-A’sha said: A soft, sweet child who has never seen the sun or cold On the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ((The fire complained to its Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, saying: O Lord, some parts of me consume others. So He made for it two breaths, one in the winter and one in the summer. So the severity of the cold you experience is from its freezing cold, and the severity of the heat you experience in the summer is from its poisonous winds.)) And “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: ((The air of Paradise is Sajsaj: neither hot nor cold)) Sajsaj is the extended shade as between sunrise and sunrise. Marra Al-Hamdani said: Zamharir is the cutting cold. Muqatil bin Hayyan said: It is something like the heads of needles that descends from the sky in extreme cold. Ibn Masoud said: It is a type of torment, and it is intense cold, so that when the people of Hell are thrown into it, they ask God to torment them in Hell for a thousand years, which is easier for them than the torment of Zamharir for one day. Abu Al-Najm said: Or I was a wind, I was a cold winter Tha’lab said: “Zamharir is the moon in the language of Tayy’. Their poet said: And the night is dark, and the cold has not yet blossomed It is narrated: “It did not appear,” meaning the moon did not rise. The meaning is that they will not see therein a sun like the sun of this world, nor a moon like the moon of this world, meaning that they are in constant light, with neither night nor day, because the light of the day is from the sun, and the light of the night is from the moon. This meaning has already been mentioned in Surah Maryam, when God the Almighty says: And they will have their provision therein, morning and evening. (Maryam 19:62) Ibn Abbas said: While the people of Paradise are in Paradise, when they see a light, they think it is a sun that has shone with that light on Paradise. They say: Our Lord said: They will see therein neither sun nor freezing cold. So what is this light? Ridwan says to them: This is neither sun nor moon, but this is Fatima and Ali laughing. So Paradise shone from the light of their laughter, and about them God the Almighty revealed: Has there not come upon man a period of time? And he recited: I am the master of a young man who has been sent to him. Has he come? That is Ali al-Murtada, the cousin of the Chosen One
76:14: The Almighty says: And their shades will be drawn low for them meaning the shade of the trees in Paradise is close to the righteous, so it is a shade for them to increase their bliss even if there is no sun or moon there, just as their combs are gold and silver even if there is no dirt or disheveled hair there. It is said that the height of the trees in Paradise is the length of one hundred years, so when a friend of God desires its fruit, it will be drawn low for him to take it. (Daniya) is in the accusative case as a state in apposition to reclining just as you say: In the house, Abdullah is reclining and the curtains are hanging down over him. It is also said that it is in the accusative case as an attribute of Paradise, meaning He rewarded them with a Paradise that is close at hand, so it is an attribute of an omitted description. It is also said that it is in the place of they will see therein neither sun nor freezing cold and they will see it close at hand. It is also said that it is in praise, meaning it is close at hand. Al-Farra' said this. (its shadows) The shadows are raised and close. If it was read with the raising of close, so that shadows would be the subject and close, the predicate would be permissible, and the sentence would be in the position of the state of the ha and the mim in (and He rewarded them), and it was read thus. In the reading of Abdullah (and close to them) because the verb came before. In the letter i.e. (and close) it is raised as a resumption. and made subservient to them meaning its fruits were enchanted its fruits “making subservient” meaning subservient, so the one standing, sitting, and lying down may reach it. Their hands are not turned away from it after that, nor are there thorns, as Qatadah said. Mujahid said: If someone stands, it rises for him, and if he sits, it hangs down over him, and if he lies down, it comes close to him so he may eat from it. And it was also narrated from him: The earth of Paradise is made of leaves, its soil is saffron, its fragrance is the most fragrant musk, the roots of its trees are gold and leaves, its branches are pearls, emeralds, and rubies, and whoever eats from it while lying down, it will not harm him. Ibn Abbas said: If he intends to take from its fruits, it hangs down to him so that he may take from it what he wants. And making the fruits easy to reach means facilitating their access. The fruits are the fruits, the singular is qatf with a kasra on the qaf, it was named thus because it is picked, just as janee was named janee because it is harvested. Tadhleelan is an emphasis on what was described of humiliation, like His saying: And We sent it down gradually (al-Isra’ 17:106), And God spoke to Moses directly (An-Nisa’: 164). Al-Mawardi: It is possible that making its fruits easy to reach means that they are brought out from their coverings and their stones are released to them. I said: And this is more, for Ibn al-Mubarak narrated, he said: Sufyan informed us, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The palm trees of Paradise: their trunks are green emerald, and their fronds are red gold, and their leaves are clothing for the people of Paradise, from them are their garments and their clothes, and their fruit is like jugs and buckets, whiter than milk, sweeter than honey, and softer than butter, and it has no stones. Abu Ja`far al-Nahhas said: It is said that the one who has been tamed is the one whom the water has tamed, meaning he has made it visible. It is also said that the one who is tamed is the one whom the slightest breeze of his blessings greets, and it is said that the one who is tamed and leveled, because the people of Hijaz say: He tamed your palm tree, meaning he made it level. It is also said that the one who is tamed and close to reach, from their saying: a tamed wall, meaning short. Abu Ja`far said: These sayings that we have narrated were mentioned by the people of knowledge of the language, and they said them in the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: And the leg is like a tamed watering can
76:15: The Almighty said: And there will be passed around among them vessels of silver and goblets of crystal meaning, servants will circulate among these righteous people when they want to drink with vessels of silver. Ibn Abbas said: There is nothing in this world that is in Paradise except the names, meaning what is in Paradise is more noble, higher and purer. Then the golden vessels were not denied, rather the meaning is that they will be given to drink in silver vessels, and they may be given to drink in golden vessels. The Almighty said: And there will be passed around among them dishes of gold and goblets (al-Zukhruf 43:71). It was said: By mentioning silver, He pointed out the gold, like His saying: Garments to protect you from the heat (al-Nahl 16:81) meaning and the cold, so by mentioning one of them, He pointed out the other. The cups are the large goblets that have no ears or handles, each of which is a cup. Adi said: Reclining, his doors are knocked on, and the servant seeks him with a cup It was mentioned in (pottery). They were crystals * crystals of silver meaning in the clarity of crystals and the whiteness of silver, so its clarity is the clarity of glass and it is made of silver. It was said that the soil of Paradise is made of silver, and the vessels are made from the soil of the earth from which they are made. Ibn Abbas mentioned this and said: There is nothing in Paradise but that you have been given something similar to it in this world, except for the crystals of silver. He said: If you took silver from the silver of this world and struck it until it became like the wing of a fly, you would not see water behind it, but the crystals of Paradise are like silver in the clarity of crystals. Measured it by measurement is the reading of the common people with a fat-ha on the qaf and the dal, meaning the cupbearers who circulate it to them measured it for them. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others said: They brought it according to the measure of their thirst, neither more nor less. Al-Kalbi said: That is more delicious and more appetizing, and the meaning is: The angels who circulate around them measured it. Ibn Abbas also said: Measure it to fill the palm of the hand, neither more nor less, so that it would not harm them with heaviness or excessive smallness. It was said: The drinkers determined for it the measures of themselves, according to what they desired and estimated. Ubayd ibn Umair, Al-Sha’bi and Ibn Sirin read (qadruhuwa) with a damma on the qaf and a kasra on the dal, meaning it was made for them according to their desire. Al-Mahdawi mentioned this reading on the authority of Ali and Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, and he said: Whoever reads (qadruhuwa) then he is returning to the meaning of the other reading, and it is as if the original was qadruhu alayhi so the accusative was deleted, and the meaning was qadruhu alayhi. Sibawayh recited: I swear that the love of Iraq will be consumed by time and that love will be consumed by the village of Sous He went on to say that the meaning is about the love of Iraq. It was said: This estimation is that the cups fly and scoop up the amount of the drinker's desire, and that is the saying of God Almighty: Measure it by measure meaning it does not exceed nor fall short of the quenching, so the cups were inspired to know the amount of the quenching of the desire so that they scoop up that amount. Al-Tirmidhi the wise mentioned this saying in (Nawader Al-Usul).
76:16: It has already been mentioned in ((pottery)). The Almighty said: They were crystals * Crystals of silver meaning in the clarity of crystals and the whiteness of silver, so its clarity is the clarity of glass and it is made of silver. It was said that the soil of Paradise is made of silver, and the vessels are made from the soil of the earth from which they are made. Ibn Abbas mentioned this and said: There is nothing in Paradise but that you have been given something similar to it in this world, except the crystals of silver. He said: If you took silver from the silver of this world and struck it until it became like the wing of a fly, you would not see water behind it, but the crystals of Paradise are like silver in the clarity of crystals. Measure it by measure is the reading of the common people with a fat-ha on the qaf and the dal, meaning the cupbearers who circulate it among them measured it for them. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others said: They brought it according to the measure of their thirst, neither more nor less. Al-Kalbi said: That is more delicious and more appetizing, and the meaning is: The angels who circulate among them measured it. It was also narrated from Ibn Abbas: They measured it to fill the palm of the hand, neither more nor less, so that it would not harm them with heaviness or excessive smallness. It was said: The drinkers measured it according to their own desires and expectations. Ubaid bin Umair, Al-Sha’bi and Ibn Sirin read qadruhu with a damma on the qaf and a kasra on the dal, meaning it was made for them according to their desires. Al-Mahdawi mentioned this reading on the authority of Ali and Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, and he said: Whoever reads qadruhu has returned to the meaning of the other reading, as if the original was qadruhu alayhi and the accusative was deleted, and the meaning was qadruhu alayhi. Sibawayh recited: I swear that the love of Iraq will be consumed by time and that love will be consumed by the village of Sous He went on to say that the meaning is about the love of Iraq. It was said: This estimation is that the cups fly and scoop up the amount of the drinker's desire, and that is the saying of God Almighty: Measure it by measure meaning it does not exceed nor fall short of the quenching, so the cups were inspired to know the amount of the quenching of the desire so that they scoop up that amount. Al-Tirmidhi the wise mentioned this saying in (Nawader Al-Usul).
76:17: The Almighty said: And they will be given to drink therein a cup meaning wine in a vessel. Its mixture will be of ginger (was) is a connection, meaning its mixture will be of ginger, or it was in the judgment of God ginger, and the Arabs used to enjoy drinks mixed with ginger for the pleasantness of its scent, because it stimulates the tongue and digests food, so they desired the bliss of the hereafter with what they believed to be the ultimate in bliss and goodness. Al-Musayyab ibn Als said, describing a woman's lips: As if the taste of ginger was in it when I tasted it and the sourness of wine It is narrated: Generosity. Another said: As if a ginger genie had spent the night in her mouth and was consulting her And similar to it is the saying of Al-A’sha: As if cloves and ginger were in her mouth and Arya was consulting her And similar to it is the saying of Al-A’sha: As if cloves and ginger were in her mouth and she was looking at me Mujahid said: Ginger is the name of the spring from which the drink of the righteous is mixed. Qatada said the same: Ginger is the name of the spring from which the close ones drink pure and which is mixed for the rest of the people of Paradise. It was said: It is a spring in Paradise in which the taste of ginger is found. It was also said: It has the meaning of a drink mixed with ginger. The meaning is as if there is ginger in it.
76:18: The Almighty said: A spring instead of a cup. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case by implying the verb they give to drink from a spring. It is also permissible for it to be in the accusative case by dropping the preposition, i.e. from ain, as mentioned previously in the Almighty's saying: A spring from which the servants of God will drink. "In it meaning in Paradise, it will be called Salsabil. Salsabil is the delicious drink, and it is a verb from the root salalah." The Arabs say: This is a smooth drink, and "salsal and salsal and salsabil" have the same meaning, i.e., pleasant in taste and delicious. In As-Sahah: The water flowed in the throat, and "salsal" means I poured it into it. Water that is smooth and salsal means easy to enter the throat due to its sweetness and clarity. Chains with the letter "damma" are similar. Az-Zajjaj said: Salsabil in the language is a name for something that is extremely smooth, so it is as if the spring was named according to its description. Mujahid said: Salsabil is the sharp edge of the stream that flows in their throats smoothly. Ibn Abbas said something similar: It is the sharp edge of the stream. Al-Mawardi mentioned it, and from it is the saying of Hassan bin Thabit, may God be pleased with him: They are watered with roses of geckos, and upon them is a papyrus that claps with pure nectar. Abu Al-Aaliyah and Muqatil said: It is called Salsabil because it flows for them in the roads and in their homes, springing from the base of the Throne from the Garden of Eden to the people of Paradise. Qatada said: A chain whose water flows wherever they wish. Something similar was narrated from Ikrimah. Al-Qaffal said: That is, this is a noble spring, so ask for a way to it. This was narrated from Ali, may God be pleased with him. His statement: (it is called) means that it is mentioned by the angels, the righteous, and the people of Paradise by this name. Salsabil was declined because it is the beginning of a verse, like the statement of God the Almighty: the suspicions (al-Ahzab 33:10) and the way (al-Ahzab 33:67).
76:19: The Almighty's statement: And there will circulate among them immortal youths. He explained who will circulate among them with vessels, meaning that they will be served by immortal youths, as they are lighter in service. Then He said: Immortal meaning they will remain as they are of youth, freshness and beauty, they will not grow old or change, and they will be of the same age throughout the ages. It was also said: Immortal means they will not die. It was also said: Walled and decorated, meaning they will be adorned, and immortality means adornment. This has been mentioned before. If you saw them, you would think they were scattered pearls. That is, you would think, because of their beauty, large numbers, and pure colors, that they were scattered pearls in the hall. Pearls, if scattered on a carpet, are more beautiful than those strung together. Al-Ma’mun reported that on the night that Buran, daughter of Al-Hasan ibn Sahl, was married to him, he was on a carpet woven of gold, and the women of the Caliph’s household had scattered pearls on it. He looked at them scattered on that carpet and was pleased with the sight. He said, “May Abu Nuwas be praised. It is as if he saw this when he said: As if its smallest and largest bubbles are pearl pebbles on a golden ground It was said: He compared them to scattered pearls because they are quick to serve, unlike the houris, whom he compared to hidden and stored pearls because they are not used to serving.
76:20: God the Almighty said: And when you look, you will see bliss and great dominion. (Then): is an adverb of place, meaning there in Paradise. The operator of (Then) is the same as (I saw), meaning if you see with your sight (Then). Al-Farra' said: There is an implied (Ma) in the speech, meaning if you see what is then, like God the Almighty's saying: {Indeed, what has been severed between you} (Al-An'am 6:94), meaning what is between you. Al-Zajjaj said: (Ma) is connected to (-then) according to what Al-Farra' mentioned, and it is not permissible to omit the relative pronoun and leave the connection, but (I saw) is transitive in meaning to (Then), and the meaning is: if you see with your sight (Then), and by (-then) he means Paradise, and Al-Farra' also mentioned this. Bliss: everything that one enjoys. The great dominion: the angels asking permission to enter upon them, as Al-Suddi and others said. Al-Kalbi said: It is that the Messenger comes from God with a blessing of clothing, food, drink and gifts to the friend of God while he is in his home, and he asks permission to enter, and that is the great kingdom. This was said by Muqatil ibn Sulayman. It was said: The great kingdom is the angels asking permission to enter, this was said by Al-Suddi and others. Al-Kalbi said: It is that the Messenger comes from God with a blessing of clothing, food, drink and gifts to the friend of God while he is in his home, and he asks permission to enter, and that is the great kingdom. This was said by Muqatil ibn Sulayman. It was said that the great king is that one of them has seventy guards, one guard after the other. While the friend of God is in pleasure and happiness, an angel from God asks permission to enter. God has sent him with a letter, a gift, and a present from the Lord of the Worlds, which that friend of God has never seen in Paradise. He says to the guard outside: Seek permission to enter upon the friend of God, for I have a letter and a gift from the Lord of the Worlds. This guard says to the one below him: This is a messenger from the Lord of the Worlds with a letter and a gift seeking permission to enter upon the friend of God. Likewise, until he reaches the guard next to the friend of God, who says to him: “O friend of God! This is a messenger from the Lord of the Worlds seeking permission to enter upon you. He has a letter and a present from the Lord of the Worlds. May he be given permission?” He says: Yes! So give him permission. The one below him says: Yes, O king, you have been given permission. He enters and greets him, saying: “Peace sends you its greetings. This is a gift, and this is a letter from the Lord of the Worlds to you.” And behold, it is written upon it: From the Ever-Living Who does not die, to the Ever-Living Who dies. So he opens it and there is in it: Peace be upon My servant and My Friend, My mercy and My blessings. O My Friend, is it not time for you to long to see your Lord? So longing overwhelms him, so he rides Buraq, and Buraq flies with him, longing to visit the Knower of the Unseen, and He gives him what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has never crossed the mind of man. Sufyan al-Thawri said: It has reached us that the Great King is the angels’ greeting of them, the evidence for which is the saying of God Almighty: “And the angels will enter upon them from every gate. Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured. And excellent is the final home.” (Ar-Ra’d: 23-24) It was said: The Great King is the creation of crowns on their heads as they would be on the head of a king. Al-Tirmidhi the Wise said: It means the King of Being, so when they want something, they say to it, Be. Abu Bakr Al-Warraq said: A king who is not followed by anyone will perish. And in the hadith on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The greatest king is the one whose lowest status is such that he can see in his kingdom a distance of two thousand years, seeing its farthest point as he can see its lowest point. He said: The best of them in status is the one who looks at his Lord, the Most High, twice a day. Glory be to the Bestower.
76:21: The Almighty said: Upon them will be green garments of fine silk and heavy brocade. Nafi', Hamzah and Ibn Muhaisin read (aalihim) with a silent ya', and Abu Ubaid chose it based on the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Wathab and others (aalihim) and the interpretation of Ibn Abbas: Have you not seen the man wearing better garments than these? Al-Farra': It is nominative as a subject and its predicate is (thin fine silk) and the active participle is intended to be plural. According to Al-Akhfash, it is permissible for it to be singular as an advanced active participle and (thiyaab) is raised by it and takes the place of the predicate, and the addition in it is in the estimation of separation because it was not specified, and it was started with because it was specified by the addition. The rest read (aalihim) in the accusative. Al-Farra' said: It is like you say above them, and the Arabs say: Your people are inside the house, so they put inside in the accusative case as a circumstance because it is a place. But it is in the accusative case as a state of two things: One of them is the ha and the mim in his saying: And there will circulate among them meaning over the righteous (two boys) high up the righteous will wear garments of fine silk, meaning he will circulate among them in this state, and the second is that it is a state of the boys, meaning When you see them, you would think them to be scattered pearls in the case of the garments being high up over their bodies. Abu Ali said: The factor in the state is either And He met them with radiance and joy or And He rewarded them for what they patiently endured He said: It is permissible for it to be an adverbial phrase, so it is declined. Al-Mahdawi: It is permissible for the active participle to be an adverbial phrase, like you say it is a corner of the house, and since high up means above, it is treated as such and made an adverbial phrase. Ibn Muhaisin, Ibn Kathir and Abu Bakr from Asim read (Khidr) in the accusative case as an attribute of fine silk, istabrak in the nominative case in accordance with the garments, and its meaning is high up among them will be garments of fine silk and isabrak. Ibn Amir, Abu Amr, and Ya'qub read Khidr in the nominative case as an adjective for the garments, and istabrak in the accusative case as an adjective for the silken garments. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose this because of its good meaning, because Khidr is the best adjective for garments, so it is in the nominative case. The best way to connect istabrak to sindas is by connecting one type to another, meaning: Their upper garments are green garments of silken garments and istabraq, meaning of these two types. Nafi' and Hafs both read it in the nominative case, so Khidr is an adjective for the garments, because they are both in the plural form, and istabraq, in apposition to the garments. Al-A'mash, Ibn Waththab, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa'i both read it in the accusative case, so his statement Khidr is an adjective for the silken garments, and sindas is a generic noun. Al-Akhfash permitted describing a generic noun in the plural because he thought it was ugly. You say: The yellow dinar and the white dirham destroyed the people, but this is unlikely in speech. The meaning according to this reading is: Their upper garments are green garments of silken garments and garments of istabraq. All of them declined the word istibrak except Ibn Muhaisin, who opened it and did not decline it, so he read wa-istibraq in the accusative case in the genitive case, to prevent decline, because it is foreign and may be made a name for this type of clothing. It was read wa-istibraq by connecting the hamza and opening it, on the basis that it is named after the word istaf`ala from al-bareeq, but this is not correct either, because it is an Arabized word whose Arabization is well-known, and its origin is istabrak. Sindas is a fine silken garment, and al-istibrak is the thickest of it, as mentioned above. God the Almighty says: And they will be adorned with is in apposition to and will go around. Bracelets of silver and in Surah Fatir 35:They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold (al-Hajj 22:23) and in Surah al-Hajj 22:They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, so it was said: The man's jewelry is silver and the woman's jewelry is gold. It was also said: Sometimes they wear gold and sometimes they wear silver. It was also said: Two bracelets of gold, two bracelets of silver, and two bracelets of pearls will be combined on one hand to gather for them the beauties of Paradise, as said by Saeed bin Al-Musayyab. It was also said: That is, each people will have what their souls incline toward. And their Lord will give them to drink a pure drink Ali may God be pleased with him said regarding God the Almighty's saying: And their Lord will give them to drink a pure drink He said: When the people of Paradise head towards Paradise, they will pass by a tree from beneath whose trunk two springs spring forth, and they will drink from one of them, and it will flow over them with the freshness of bliss, so their complexions will not change and their hair will never become disheveled. Then they will drink from the other water, and whatever is in their bellies will be expelled. Then the keepers of Paradise will meet them and say to them, "Peace be upon you. You have done well, so enter it to abide therein eternally." (al-Zumar 39:73) An-Nakha'i and Abu Qilabah said: If they drink it after eating, it will purify them, and what they have eaten and what they have drunk will ooze musk, and their bellies will shrink. Muqatil said: It is from a spring of water at the gate of Paradise, springing from the trunk of a tree. Whoever drinks from it, God will remove whatever rancor, deceit, and envy is in his heart, and whatever harm and filth is in his stomach. This is the meaning of what was narrated from Ali, except that it is in a statement that was explained in Surat Al-Furqan. Praise be to God. Tayyib Al-Jamal said: I prayed behind Sahl bin Abdullah at 'Atmah, and he recited, And their Lord will give them to drink a pure drink, and he began to move his lips and mouth as if he were sucking something. When he finished, he was asked, Are you drinking or reciting? He said, By God, if I did not enjoy it when reciting it as I enjoy it when drinking it, I would not have recited it.
76:22: The Almighty says: Indeed, this was a reward for you meaning, it will be said to them: This is only a reward for you. And your effort meaning your work was appreciated meaning from God, and His appreciation of the servant means accepting his obedience, praising him for it, and rewarding him. Saeed narrated on the authority of Qatadah who said: He forgave them their sin and appreciated their goodness. Mujahid said: Appreciated means accepted, and the meanings are close, for when He, Glory be to Him, accepts the deed, He thanks him, and when he thanks Him, He rewards him abundantly, for He, Glory be to Him, is the possessor of great bounty. “It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar: An Ethiopian man said: O Messenger of God! You have been favored over us with images, colors, and prophethood. Tell me, if I believe in what you believe in and do what you do, will I be with you in Paradise? He said: (Yes, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, verily the whiteness of lions in Paradise and its brightness can be seen from a distance of a thousand years.) Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ((Whoever says La ilaha illa God will have a covenant with God for it. And whoever says Subhan God wa al-Hamdulillah will have for it with God one hundred thousand good deeds and twenty-four thousand good deeds.)) The man said: How will we perish after that, O Messenger of God? He said: ((A man will come on the Day of Resurrection with a deed which, if he placed it on a mountain, would weigh it down. Then a blessing from God comes and it almost uses up all of it, unless God is kind in His mercy.)) He said: Then the verse was revealed: {Has there not been over man a period of time…} until His saying: {and a great kingdom.} The Ethiopian said: O Messenger of God! And my eyes will see what your eyes see in Paradise? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: (Yes.) So the Ethiopian wept until his soul departed. Omar said: I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, lowering him into his grave and saying: “This was your reward and your effort was appreciated.” We said: O Messenger of God, what is it? He said: “By the One in Whose hand is my soul, God stopped him and then said: O My servant, I will surely whiten your face and I will provide you with a place in Paradise wherever you wish.” Yes, the reward of the workers is good.
76:23: The Almighty's saying: Indeed, it is We who sent down to you the Qur'an gradually. You did not invent it, nor did you bring it from your own source, nor of your own accord, as the polytheists claim. The connection between this verse and the previous one is that when He, the Almighty, mentioned the various types of promise and threat, He explained that this book includes what people need, so it is not magic, divination, or poetry, and that it is the truth. Ibn Abbas said: The Qur'an was sent down in parts, verse by verse, and it was not sent down all at once, which is why He said: We sent it down. This has been explained in detail, and praise be to God.
76:24: The Almighty says: So be patient for the decision of your Lord meaning for the decree of your Lord. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Be patient with the harm of the polytheists, this is how I judged. Then it was abrogated by the verse on fighting. It was also said: Be patient with what He has decreed for you in terms of obedience, or await the decree of God when He has promised you that He will grant you victory over them, and do not be impatient, for it will inevitably happen. And do not obey among them a sinner or an ingrate meaning do not obey the ingrates. Muammar narrated on the authority of Qatadah who said: Abu Jahl said: If I see Muhammad praying, I will step on his neck. Then God the Almighty revealed: And do not obey among them a sinner or an ingrate. It is said that it was revealed about Utbah ibn Rabi'ah and Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira, who came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) offering him money and marriage on the condition that he would abandon mention of prophethood. So it was revealed about them: And do not obey among them a sinner or an ingrate. Muqatil said: The one who offered marriage was Utbah ibn Rabi’ah. He said: My daughters are among the most beautiful women of Quraysh, so I will marry you my daughter without a dowry and reconsider this matter. Al-Walid said: If you did what you did for money, then I will give you money until you are satisfied and reconsider this matter. So it was revealed. Then it was said: (or) in the words of God: sinner or ungrateful is more emphatic than and, because when and says: Do not obey Zaid and Amr, and he obeys one of them, he is not disobedient, because God ordered him not to obey the two. So when He says: And do not obey among them a sinner or an ungrateful person, then or indicates that each of them is worthy of being disobeyed, just as if you say: Do not oppose Al-Hasan or Ibn Sirin, or follow Al-Hasan or Ibn Sirin, then you have said: These two are worthy of being followed and each of them is worthy of being followed, as Al-Zajjaj said. Al-Farra’ said: (or) here is like not, as if he said: nor ungrateful. The poet said: I have never found a bereaved woman like you, nor have I found a hasty woman like you. Or an old man found his camel lost on the day the pilgrims met, so they rushed forward. He wanted but did not find a sheikh. It was also said: The sinner is the hypocrite, and the ungrateful is the unbeliever who shows disbelief, meaning do not obey a sinner or an ungrateful among them. This is close to what Al-Farra’ said.
76:25: The Almighty says: And remember the name of your Lord in the morning and the evening. That is, pray to your Lord at the beginning of the day and at the end of it. At the beginning of it is the dawn prayer and at the end of it is the noon and afternoon prayers.
76:26: The Almighty said: And during part of the night prostrate to Him meaning the Maghrib and Isha prayers. And glorify Him during a long night meaning voluntary prayers at night, as stated by Ibn Habib. Ibn Abbas and Sufyan said: Every glorification in the Qur'an is a prayer. It was also said: It is general remembrance, whether in prayer or otherwise. Ibn Zayd and others said: His statement: And glorify Him during a long night was abrogated by the five daily prayers. It was also said: It is recommended. It was also said: It is specific to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. A similar statement has been made in Surah Al-Muzzammil, and Ibn Habib's statement is good. The plural of aseel is asa'il and asl, like saying safa'in and safin, he said: And there is nothing better than it if the origin is close He said in Al-Asa’il, which is the plural of plural: By my life, you are the home whose people are most honored, and I sit in its shade in the evenings. This was fully discussed at the end of Al-A'raf. The word min was used with the adverbial phrase to indicate some, just as it was used with the object in the Almighty's saying: He will forgive you some of your sins (Nuh 71:4).
76:27: The Almighty's saying: Indeed, these people love the immediate is a rebuke and a rebuke, and what is meant is the people of Mecca. The worldly haste and they leave means they postpone behind them meaning before them a heavy Day meaning a difficult and severe one, as He said: It will be heavy upon the heavens and the earth (al-A’raf 7:187) meaning they abandon belief in the Day of Resurrection. It was also said that behind them means behind them, meaning they leave the Hereafter behind them, and they do not work for it. It was also said that it was revealed about the Jews because of what they concealed of the description of the Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the truth of his prophethood. Their love of the immediate means that they took bribes for what they concealed. It was also said that it meant the hypocrites, because they concealed disbelief and worldly pursuits. The verse is general. The heavy Day is the Day of Resurrection. It was called heavy because of its hardships and terrors, and it was also said that it is for the judgment on it among His servants.
76:28: The Almighty said: We created them meaning from clay. And strengthened their bonds meaning He created them, as stated by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, Muqatil and others. Bonding is creation. Abu Ubaid said: It is said that a horse is of strong bond, meaning creation. It is also said that God Almighty strengthened it if He strengthened its creation. Labid said: The face contributed to the intense captivity of the supervisor of the guard, the knitted one. Al-Akhtal said: From every shunner, he is very captivated by his easy-going leadership, you would think he is arrogant. Abu Hurairah, Al-Hasan and Al-Rabi’ said: We strengthened their joints and their ligaments to one another with veins and nerves. Mujahid said in the interpretation of Al-Usr: It is the anus, meaning when feces and urine come out, the place contracts. Ibn Zayd said: Strength. Ibn Ahmar said, describing a horse: He walks with strong jobs, his captivity is deaf, his hooves do not protect him from the grasshopper It is derived from the word Isar, which is the string used to tie up the saddlebags. It is said: I tied the saddlebags tightly, meaning, I tightened and tied them up. It is also said: How good is the string of his neck, meaning, He tightened and tied it up. From this comes their saying: Take it completely, if they wanted to say, It is all yours, as if they wanted to make it obsolete and tighten it, without opening it or reducing anything from it. From this comes the word asir, because he was satisfied with the asir. The speech was directed to thank them for the blessings they received when they faced them with disobedience. Meaning, I made your creation perfect and perfected it with strength, then you deny me. And when We willed, We could have substituted others like them with [an] exchange. Ibn Abbas said: He means, If We willed, We could have destroyed them and brought others more obedient to God than them. Also from him: We would have changed their good looks to the most hideous and ugliest. This is what Ad-Dahhak narrated from him. The first version was narrated from him by Abu Salih.
76:29: The Almighty says: Indeed, this meaning the Surah is a reminder meaning an admonition so whoever wills may take to his Lord a way meaning a path leading to His obedience and seeking His pleasure. It was also said: (a way) meaning a means. It was also said that it is a destination and a path to Paradise. The meaning is the same.
76:30: The Almighty says: And you do not will meaning obedience, righteousness, and choosing the path to God except that God wills. Thus He informs them that the matter is up to Him, not up to them, and that no one's will is carried out or preceded unless His will precedes it. Ibn Kathir and Abu Omar read (and you do not will) with a ya' as if it were a report from them. The rest read it with a ta' as if it were a speech to God, the Almighty. It was said that the first verse is interwoven with the second. What is more likely is that it is not an abrogation, but rather a clarification that this does not happen except by His will. Al-Farra' said: And you do not will except that God wills is an answer to His statement: So whoever wills may take to his Lord a way. Then He informed them that the matter is not up to them, so He said: (And you do not will) that way (except that God wills) for you. Indeed, God is ever Knowing of your deeds, Wise in His commands and prohibitions to you. This has been mentioned in more than one place.
76:31: The Almighty said: He admits whom He wills into His mercy meaning He admits him into Paradise, having mercy on him. And the wrongdoers meaning He punishes the wrongdoers. He put it in the accusative case because it is implied that He punishes. Al-Zajjaj said: He put the wrongdoers in the accusative case because it was preceded by an accusative, meaning He admits whom He wills into His mercy and punishes the wrongdoers, meaning the polytheists. And He prepared for them is an explanation of this implied word, as the poet said: I no longer carry a weapon nor do I own the camel's head if they flee I fear sin if I pass by it alone, and I fear the wind and the rain. Meaning, I fear the wolf. Al-Zajjaj said: The preferred form is the accusative, although the nominative is permissible. You say, I gave Zayd and Amr, I prepared for them righteousness. The accusative is preferred, meaning, I made Amr righteous, or I made Amr righteous. And His statement in Ha Meem * Ain Sin Qaf, “He admits whom He wills into His mercy, and so do the wrongdoers” (Ash-Shura 42:8) is raised because He did not mention after it a verb that would be subject to it in the accusative case, so it was not permissible to connect it to the accusative before it, so it was raised by the subject. Here, His statement, He has prepared for them a punishment indicates and He punishes, so the accusative is permissible. Abaan bin Othman read and the wrongdoers in the nominative case as the subject and the predicate is He has prepared for them. “A painful punishment,” meaning painful and agonizing. This was previously mentioned in Surah Al-Baqarah and others, and praise be to God. The Surah has been concluded.
77:1: It was revealed in Mecca according to Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata' and Jabir. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said that the exception for one verse is the verse in which God the Almighty says: {And when it is said to them, Bow down, they do not bow down.} It was revealed in Medina. Ibn Mas'ud said: "Al-Burj Al-Mursalat those sent forth in succession was revealed to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) one night while we were walking with him until we took refuge in a cave in Mina, and it was revealed. While we were receiving it from him, and his mouth was moist with it, a snake leapt out. We pounced on it to kill it, but it went away. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: (You have been protected from its evil as I have been protected from your evil.) It was narrated on the authority of Kurayb, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, who said: He recited Surah Al-Burj Al-Mursalat those sent forth in succession and Umm Al-Fadl, the wife of Al-Abbas, heard me and wept. She said: By God, my son, your recitation of this Surah reminded me of it. It is the last thing I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recite in the Maghrib prayer.} And God knows best. It has fifty verses. God the Almighty says: "And the messengers sent forth in gusts." The majority of commentators agree that the messengers are the winds. Masruq narrated on the authority of Abdullah who said: They are the angels sent with what is known of God's commands and prohibitions, report and revelation. This is the opinion of Abu Hurairah, Muqatil, Abu Salih and Al-Kalbi. It was also said: They are the prophets sent with "there is no god but God," as said by Ibn Abbas. Abu Salih said: They are the messengers sent with what they are known for of miracles. Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masoud narrated: They are the winds, as God the Almighty said: "And We sent the winds" (al-Hijr 15:22) and said: "And it is He who sends the winds" (al-A’raf 7:57). The meaning of "in gusts" is that they follow one another like the mane of a horse. The Arabs say: People are heading towards so-and-so in one mane," if they head towards him in large numbers. It is the accusative case in the state of and the messengers, meaning the winds that were sent forth in succession. It is permissible for it to be a verbal noun, meaning in succession. The accusative case may be based on the assumption of a preposition, as if he said: And the messengers sent forth in gusts, and what is meant are the angels or the angels and the messengers. It was said: It is possible that what is meant by Al-Mursalat are the clouds, because of what they contain of blessings and punishment, knowing what they were sent with and to whom they were sent. They are the deterrents and sermons. (And they are known) according to this interpretation are consecutive like the mane of a horse, said Ibn Masoud. It was said: running, said Al-Hasan, meaning in the hearts. It was said: known in the minds.
77:2: The Almighty said: And the winds that blow violently (al-Isra’ 17:69) It was said: The winds that blow violently are the angels assigned to the winds that blow them violently. It was also said: The angels blow violently with the soul of the disbeliever. It is said that he blew something violently, meaning he destroyed it and ruined it. A she-camel is violent, meaning it blows violently with its rider, so it moves as if it were a wind in speed. The war blew violently with the people, meaning it took them away. It was also said: It is possible that they refer to the destructive signs, such as earthquakes and eclipses.
77:3: The Almighty says: And the spreaders spreading The angels who are in charge of the clouds spreading them. And the clouds are said to be rain. This was narrated on the authority of Abu Salih, who also said: The rains, because they spread the plants, so spreading means reviving. It is said: God spread the dead and spread him, meaning He revived him. Al-Suddi narrated on his authority: They are the angels who spread the books of God the Almighty. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: He means what is spread from the books and the deeds of the children of Adam. Ad-Dahhak said: They are the scrolls spread to God with the deeds of the servants. Al-Rabi' said: It is the resurrection on which the souls are spread. He said: (And the spreaders) with the waw, because it is a new section.
77:4: God the Almighty says: And those who distinguish means the angels who descend to distinguish between truth and falsehood. This was stated by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, and Abu Salih. Ad-Dahhak narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: What the angels distinguish are the sustenance, provisions, and life spans. Ibn Abi Nujayh narrated from Mujahid, who said: The distinguishing winds separate the clouds and scatter them. Saeed narrated from Qatada, who said: And those who distinguish means the Criterion, in which God distinguished between truth and falsehood, the forbidden and the permissible. This was stated by Al-Hasan and Ibn Kaysan. It was also said: It means the messengers distinguished between what God commanded and what He forbade, or did they clarify that? It was also said: The rain clouds are likened to the farq she-camel, which is the pregnant she-camel that comes out and spreads out on the ground when she gives birth, and the she-camels are fawariq and farq. Perhaps they likened the cloud that separates from the clouds to this she-camel. Dhu Al-Rummah said: Or a rain cloud whose depths are clear, lightning flashes and darkness is a toad.
77:5: And those who convey the message are the angels by consensus, meaning they convey the books of God Almighty to the prophets, peace be upon them, as stated by Al-Mahdawi. And it was said: It is Gabriel and he was named after all of them, because he used to descend with them. And it was said: What is meant is the messengers who convey to their nations what God revealed to them, as stated by Qatrib. And Ibn Abbas read (And those who convey) with emphasis and a fatha on the qaf, and it is like the saying of God Almighty: And indeed, you receive the Qur'an (al-Naml 27:6).
77:6: The Almighty’s saying: An excuse or a warning: meaning, he received the revelation as an apology from God or a warning to His creation of His punishment, as Al-Farra’ said. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Salih, who said: It means the messengers excuse and warn. Saeed narrated on the authority of Qatada: (An excuse), he said: An excuse from God, the Most High, to His creation, and a warning to the believers, from which they benefit and take it. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: (An excuse), meaning what God, the Most High, presents of excuses or His warning, which is repentance. (Or a warning), warning His enemies. Abu Amr, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Hafs read: (Or a warning) By sukun al-dhal and all seven on sukun al-dhal (adhran and nadhran) with waw al-atif and they did not put alif between them. They are accusative as the agent for it, meaning for the excuses or the warning. It was said: on the object, it was said: on the substitute for (dhikr), meaning the ones who throw an excuse or a vow. Abu Ali said: It is permissible for al-udhhar and nadhr to be with the heavy emphasis on the plural of aadhhar and nadhhar. Abu Ali said: It is permissible for al-udhhar and nadhr to be with the heavy emphasis on the plural of aadhhar and nadhhar, like the saying of God the Almighty: This is a warner from the first warnings (al-Najm 53:56), so it is accusative as a state of throwing, meaning they throw the reminder in a state of excuse and warning. Or it is an object of (dhikr), meaning (the ones who throw), meaning they remember an excuse or a vow. Al-Mubarrad said: They are with the heavy emphasis, plural, and the singular is adheer and nadheer.
77:7: The Almighty says: You are only promised that which will surely come to pass. This is the answer to what preceded the oath, meaning that what you are promised regarding the matter of the Resurrection will come to pass and descend upon you.
77:8: Then he explained the time of its occurrence, saying: Then the stars will be extinguished, meaning their light will be gone and their radiance will be erased, like when a book is erased. It is said: Tamas means that something is obliterated and obliterated, so it is obliterated. The wind obliterates the soil, so the wind is obliterating, and the trace is obliterated, meaning obliterated.
77:9: The Almighty said: And when the heaven is split open meaning it is opened and split. From this is the Almighty’s saying: And the heaven is split open and becomes doors. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: It was split open for the folding.
77:10: The Almighty said: And when the mountains are blown away meaning they are all quickly taken away. It is said: I blew something away or I blew it away meaning I took it all quickly. Ibn Abbas and Al-Kalbi used to say: It was leveled to the ground. The Arabs say: A horse is nasawuf if its belt is delayed by its elbows. Bishr said: She tugged at the belt with her elbows. The she-camel blew the pasture: if she grazed it. Al-Mubarrad said: To blew means to pull it out from its place. A man might say to another man who is pulling his feet out of the ground: His feet were blown away. It was said: Blowing means scattering parts until the wind scatters them. And from this comes the word to blow food, because it is moved until the wind removes some of the straw in it.
77:11: God the Almighty says: And when the messengers are gathered meaning they are gathered for their time on the Day of Resurrection, and the appointed time is the appointed time for which the thing is postponed, so the meaning is: He made for them a time and a appointed time for the separation and judgment between them and the nations, as God the Almighty said: The Day God will assemble the messengers (al-Nisa 4:109). It was said: This is in this world, meaning the messengers will be gathered for their appointed time that was set for them to bring down the punishment on those who denied it, that the disbelievers will be given respite. Doubts will be dispelled on the Day of Resurrection. The first is better, because the appointed time is before the Day of Resurrection. Abu Ali said: That is, He made a time for the Day of Judgment and separation for them. It was also said: He gathered, promised, and postponed. It was also said: He gathered means he was sent for specific times according to what God knew and wanted. The hamza in he gathered is a substitute for the waw, as stated by Al-Farra' and Al-Zajjaj. Al-Farra’ said: “Every waw that has a damma and its damma is essential, it is permissible to replace it with a hamza. You say, ‘The people prayed one of us,’ meaning ‘we both prayed,’ and they say, ‘These are the faces of Hasan and the faces.’ This is because the waw has a damma. Substitution is not permissible in the verse, ‘And do not forget graciousness between you.’ (Al-Baqarah 2:237) because the damma is not essential. Abu ‘Amr Wahid, Al-Hasan, Nasr, and ‘Asim and Mujahid read (waqtat) with a waw and a shaddah on the qaf according to the original form. Abu ‘Umar said, (aqtat) is only read by those who say fi wujuh ajwa. Abu Ja’far, Shaiba, and Al-A’raj read (waqtat) with a waw and a shaddah on the qaf according to the original form. Abu ‘Amr said, (aqtat) is only read by those who say fi wujuh ajwa. Abu Ja’far, Shaiba, and Al-A’raj read (waqtat) with a waw and a shaddah on the qaf according to the original form. It is fa’lat from the word ‘waqt,’ and from it is (a book with fixed times.’ (An-Nisa’ 4:103). Also, Al-Hasan said, (waqtat) with two waws, and it is fa’ulat from the word ‘waqt,’ like ‘awuhadat. If the waw in these two readings had accepted an alif, it would have been permissible. Yahya, Ayoub, Khalid ibn Elias, and Salam read “aqtat” with a hamza and a light pronunciation, because it is written in the Qur’an with an alif.
77:12: God Almighty says: For what day have you postponed? That is, have you delayed, and this is to glorify that day, so it is a question about glorification.
77:13: God Almighty says: That is, ‘the Day of Judgment’ It has been postponed. Saeed narrated on the authority of Qatada who said: People will be judged on it according to their deeds, whether they will be in Heaven or Hell. And in the hadith: When people are gathered on the Day of Resurrection, they will stand for forty years with the sun on their heads, their eyes fixed on the sky, awaiting the decision.
77:14: God Almighty says: And what will make you know what the Day of Judgment is? He followed the word great with emphasis, meaning, And what will make you know what the Day of Judgment is?
77:15: The Almighty's saying: Woe, that Day, to the deniers. Meaning, torment and disgrace for those who denied God, His Messengers, His Books, and the Day of Judgment. This is a threat. He repeated it in this surah at every verse for those who denied, because He apportioned it among them according to the degree of their denial. For every denier of something there is a punishment in addition to his denial of something else. And perhaps a thing that he denied is a greater crime than denying something else, because it is more heinous in its denial and greater in its rejection of God. So he is apportioned from woe according to its degree and according to the appropriate recompense, which is His saying: An appropriate recompense. (An-Naba': 26) It was narrated on the authority of An-Nu'man ibn Bashir who said: Woe is a valley in Hell in which there are various types of torment. This was said by Ibn Abbas and others. Ibn Abbas said: When Hell is extinguished, a live coal is taken and thrown on it, and some of it consumes others. It was also narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Hell was shown to me, and I did not see in it a valley greater than woe. It was narrated that it is the collection of the pus and blood of the people of Hell, and that something only flows in the lowest parts of the earth and cracks. The servants of God knew in this world that the worst places in this world are those in which the waters of filth, dirt, and washing from carcasses and bath water have stagnated. So it was mentioned that this valley is the swamp of the pus of the people of disbelief and polytheism, so that those with reason may know that there is nothing dirtier than it, nor more putrid, nor more bitter, nor more black than it. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, described it with what it contains of torment, and that it is the greatest valley in Hell, so God Almighty mentioned it in His threat in this surah. God God
77:16: The Almighty’s saying: Did We not destroy the former peoples? He informed us about the destruction of the infidels from the past nations from Adam to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.God
77:17: God Almighty says: Then We will make the last ones follow them. That is, We will make the last ones follow the first ones.God
77:18: The Almighty says: Thus do We deal with the criminals meaning, just as We did to those who came before, We deal with the polytheists of Quraysh, either with the sword or with destruction. The general public read Then We will follow them in the nominative case as a new sentence, while Al-A'raj read We will follow them in the accusative case as an appositive to We will destroy the former ones, just as you would say: Did you not visit me and then I honored you. What is meant is that He destroyed people after people at different times of the messengers. Then He resumed by saying: Thus do We deal with the criminals, meaning those who will be destroyed later. It is possible that the sukoon is to lighten the word We will follow them due to the successive vowels. It was narrated from him that the sukoon is to lighten the word. In Ibn Mas'ud's reading, it is: Then We will follow them and the kaf of Likewise is in the accusative case, meaning, We will inflict a similar destruction on every polytheist. Then it was said that its meaning is to intimidate their destruction in this world as a consideration. It was also said that it is a notification of their punishment in the Hereafter.
77:19: God Almighty says: Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
77:20: The Almighty says: Did We not create you from a despised water? meaning, a weak and insignificant fluid, which is the sperm, as mentioned previously. This verse is the basis for those who say that the creation of the fetus is only from the man's sperm. This has been discussed previously.
77:21: The Almighty says: So We placed him in a secure place, meaning in a secure place, which is the womb.
77:22: God Almighty says: to a known term. Mujahid said: until we create him. It was also said: until the time of birth.
77:23: God the Almighty says: So We decreed. Nafi' and Al-Kisa'i read it with a shaddah. The rest read it without a shaddah, and they are two meanings. This was stated by Al-Kisa'i, Al-Farra' and Al-Qutbi. Al-Qutbi said: Qadrana means Qadrana with a shaddah: just as you say: I decreed such-and-such and I decreed it. From this is the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about the new moon: If it is obscured from you, then estimate for it meaning estimate its journey and stations. Muhammad bin Al-Jahm said on the authority of Al-Farra': (Fa-Qadrana) He said: And he mentioned the shaddah of Ali may God be pleased with him and the lightness of it: He said: It is not far-fetched that the meaning of the shaddah and the lightness is one and the same, because the Arabs say: death was decreed for him and he was decreed. God the Almighty said: We have decreed death among you (Al-Waqi'ah: 60) It was read with a shaddah and with a shaddah, and he decreed his provision and he was decreed. He said: Those who made it without a shaddah argued and said: If it were thus, then it would have been, so excellent are the determiners. Al-Farra’ said: The Arabs combine the two languages. God Almighty said: “So give the disbelievers respite. Give them respite for a while.” (Al-Tariq: 17) Al-A’sha said: You denied me, and the only incidents I mentioned were gray hair and baldness. It was narrated from Ikrimah, Then We decreed with a lightened form from al-qudra, and it is the test of Abu Ubaid, Abu Hatim and al-Kisa'i, based on his saying: Then what excellent are the Able ones. And whoever stresses it, it is from al-Qadeer, meaning, We decreed the wretched and the happy, then what excellent are the ones who are decreed. Narrated by Ibn Mas'ud from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. It was said that the meaning is, We decreed him to be short or tall. Something similar was narrated from Ibn Abbas: We decreed, made possible. Al-Mahdawi: This interpretation is more similar to the lightened reading. I say: It is correct, because Ikrimah is the one who read Then We decreed with a lightened form. He said: Its meaning is, We owned, then what excellent are the owners. Thus, the two words convey two different meanings, meaning, We decreed the time of birth and the states of the sperm in its transition from one state to another until it became a normal human being, or the wretched and the happy, or the tall and the short, all according to the stressing reading. It was said that they have one meaning, as we mentioned.
77:24: God Almighty says: Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
77:25: The Almighty said: Have We not made the earth a receptacle? That is, a container that contains the living on its surface and the dead in its belly. This indicates the obligation to cover and bury the dead, and to bury his hair and everything else that he removes from him. And his saying, peace be upon him: Cut your nails and bury your clippings) This has already been explained in (Al-Baqarah). It is said: kafa al-shay' akfatuhu: if you gather and compact it, and kuft means to gather and collect, and Sibawayh recited: Generous when the snakes retreat to their stones from the frost Abu Ubaid said: Kafata are containers. The Nakhi is called Kaft or Kafita because it contains and holds the milk. He said: Today you are alive above the earth, and tomorrow it will hold you in its palms. Al-Shaabi went out to a funeral procession, looked at the coward and said: These are the palms of the dead. Then he looked at the houses and said: These are the palms of the living. The second - It was narrated on the authority of Rabia about the grave robber, he said: His hand would be cut off. It was said to him: Why did you say that? He said: God the Almighty says: {Have We not made the earth a receptacle * For the living and the dead} [Al-Ma'idah]. So the earth is a place of protection. This has already been mentioned in Surah Al-Ma'idah. They used to call Baqi' al-Gharqad its receptacle, because it is a cemetery that contains the dead. So the earth contains the living in their homes and the dead in their graves. Also, the settling of people on the face of the earth, then lying on it, is their joining to it. It was said: They are receptacles for the living, meaning the burial of what comes out of a person of waste in the earth, since there is no joining in the presence of people on it, and joining indicates inclusion in all aspects. Al-Akhfash, Abu Ubaidah, and Mujahid said in one of his two opinions: The living and the dead return to the earth, meaning the earth is divided into the living, which is that which grows, and the dead, which is that which does not grow.
77:26: Al-Farra' said: The word 'living and dead' is in the accusative case because the 'sucking bowls' fall on it, meaning, 'Have We not made the earth into bowls for the living and the dead?' So if the letter 'nun' is added, it is in the accusative case, like the Almighty's saying: Or feeding on a day of famine * An orphan (al-Balad 90:14-15). It was also said: It is in the accusative case as a state of the earth, meaning of it in the plural. Al-Khalil said: Turning something over is to turn something over from its back to its front or its back to its back. It is said: The people turned back to their homes, meaning they returned. So the meaning of the 'sucking bowls' is that they move around on its back, return to it, and are buried in it.
77:27: The Almighty said: And We placed therein meaning on the earth firm, lofty mountains meaning the mountains, the fixed firm mountains, and the tall, lofty mountains, and from this it is said: he raised his nose with arrogance. He said: And We gave you to drink sweet water meaning and We made for you a drink. And the Euphrates is the fresh water that is drunk and from which the crops are watered. That is, We created the mountains and sent down for you a drink. And the Euphrates is the fresh water that is drunk and from which the crops are watered. That is, We created the mountains and sent down sweet water. These matters are more amazing than the resurrection. In some of the hadith, Abu Hurairah said: In the earth from Paradise are the Euphrates, the Tigris, and the Jordan River. And in Sahih Muslim: (Sihan, Ceyhan, the Nile and the Euphrates are all rivers of Paradise).
77:28: God Almighty says: Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
77:29: The Almighty says: Go to that which you used to deny. That is, the disbelievers will be told to go to that which you used to deny, of the torment, meaning the Fire, for you have seen it with your own eyes.
77:30: The Almighty said: Go to the shade meaning smoke with three branches meaning smoke that rises and then branches out into three branches. This is also the case with great smoke when it rises and branches out.
77:31: Then he described the shade, saying: No shade meaning it is not like the shade that protects from the heat of the sun. Nor does it protect against the flame meaning it does not ward off the flames of Hell at all. The flame is that which rises above the fire when it is blazing, from red, yellow, and green. It was said that the three branches are the thorny thorn, the thorn, the thorn, and the thorns, as said by Ad-Dahhak. It was also said that the flame, then the sparks, then the smoke, because these are three states, which are the ultimate descriptions of the fire when it is blazing and intense. It was also said that it is a neck that emerges from the fire and branches out into three branches. As for the light, it stops on the heads of the believers, as for the smoke, it stops on the heads of the hypocrites, and as for the pure flame, it stops on the heads of the disbelievers. It was also said that it is the canopy, which is a tongue of fire that surrounds them, then three branches branch out from it, shading them until their reckoning is finished and they go to the fire. It was said: It is the shade of hot water, as God Almighty said: In scorching wind and scalding water, and shade of scalding water, neither cool nor warm (al-Waqi’ah 56:42-44), as mentioned above. And in the hadith: “The sun will draw near to the heads of creation, and on that Day they will have no clothing or shrouds. The sun will surround them and take their breaths and the duration of that Day. Then God will save by His mercy whom He wills to the shade of His shade.” Then they will say, So God has been gracious to us and has saved us from the punishment of the scorching wind. (al-Tur 52:27) And it will be said to the deniers, Go to that which you used to deny of God’s punishment and chastisement. Go to a shade of three branches. So the friends of God, may He be glorified, will be in the shade of His Throne or wherever He wills in the shade until the reckoning is completed. Then each group will be commanded to its destination in Paradise or Hell.
77:32: The Almighty said: It throws out sparks like castles. Sparks: singular: sharrah. And shirar: singular: shararah, and it is what flies from the fire in every direction. Its origin is from shararat al-thawb, which means to spread out a garment in the sun to dry. And qasr is a tall building. The common reading is (like qasr) with a sukoon on the sad: meaning fortresses and cities in size, and it is one of the palaces. Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masoud said this. It is in the meaning of the plural by way of the genus. It was said: qasr is the plural of qasrah with a sukoon on the sad, like jamrah, jamr, dateh, and dates. And qasrah is the singular of a thick piece of firewood. And in Bukhari, on the authority of Ibn Abbas also: (throwing sparks like palaces) He said: We used to raise wood with a height of three cubits or less, and raise it for the winter, so we called it palace. Saeed bin Jubair and Al-Dahhak said: They are the roots of trees and large palm trees when they fall and are cut. It was also said: Their necks. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Hamid and Al-Salami read (like palace) with a fatha on the sad, meaning the necks of palm trees. The short neck, its plural is qasr and qasrat. Qatada said: The necks of camels. Saeed bin Jubair read it with a kasra on the qaf and a fatha on the sad, and it is also the plural of qasra like badra and badr and qasaa and qasaa and halqa and halqah, for the rings of iron. Abu Hatim said: Perhaps it is a language, as they said need and need. It was said: Palace is a mountain, so he likened the sparks to palaces in their dimensions, then he likened it in its color to the yellow camels, which are black camels, and the Arabs call the black camels yellow, the poet said: These are my horses from him and these are my riders, their young ones are as yellow as raisins That is, they are black. The black camels were called yellow because their blackness is tinged with a bit of yellow, just as the eggs of gazelles are called al-adham red skin because their whiteness is covered with a turbidity. And the sparks, when they fly and fall and contain some of the color of fire, are most similar to black camels because of the yellowness that tinges them. And in the poetry of Imran ibn Hattan al-Khawarij: She called them at the top of her voice and threw them like yellow camels stripped of their hair. Al-Tirmidhi weakened this statement, saying: This statement is impossible in the language, that something could be tainted by a small amount, and then all of it could be attributed to that taint. So it is surprising that someone would say this.
77:33: God Almighty said: Yellow camels, but we do not know anything like this in the language. Our view is that fire was created from light, so it is a blazing fire. When God created Hell, which is the place of fire, He filled that place with that fire and sent His power and wrath to it, so it became black from His power and increased in intensity, and became blacker than fire and blacker than everything else. So when the Day of Resurrection comes and Hell is brought to the place of standing, it will throw its sparks at the people of the place of standing, in anger for the wrath of God. The sparks are black because they are from black fire. So when the fire throws its sparks, it throws them at the enemies, so they are black from the blackness of the fire. That does not reach the monotheists, because they are in the canopy of mercy that surrounds them in the place of standing, and it is the cloud in which the Lord Almighty comes. But they witness that throwing, and when they witness it, God removes that power and wrath from them in their sight until they see it yellow, so that the monotheists know that they are in the mercy of God, not in His power and wrath. Ibn Abbas used to say: The yellow camels: the ropes of ships, some of which are gathered together until they are like the waists of men. Al-Bukhari disliked it. And he used to read it (jamalat) with a damma on the jim, and likewise Mujahid and Hamid read (jamalat) with a damma on the jim, and they are the thick ropes, and they are the qalus of the ship, i.e. its ropes. The singular of qalus is qalas. And it was also narrated from Ibn Abbas that it refers to pieces of copper. And the definite article in the thick rope is jamal with a shaddah on the m as mentioned previously in (Al-A’raf). (and jamalat) with a damma on the jim: the plural of jamalah with a kasra on the jim and a unified, as if it is the plural of camel, like hijr and hijra, and dhikr and dhikarah. Ya’qub ibn Abi Ishaq, Isa and Al-Jahdary read (jamalah) with a damma on the jim and a unified, and it refers to a huge thing gathered together. Hafs, Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read (jamalah) and the rest of the seven read (jamalat). Al-Farra’ said: It is possible for jamalat to be the plural of jamal, as one says: rajul and rajal and rajal. And it was said: he likened them to camels because of their fast walking. And it was said: because of their following one another. And qasr is the singular of qasr. And qasr al-dhalam means its mixing. It is said: I came to him in the evening, meaning in the evening, so it is common. He said: As if they were a palace of lamps, a monk with a scale, whose wilt was watered by a sharp blow. Question: This verse provides evidence for the permissibility of bringing firewood and charcoal even if they are not considered staple food, as they are a source of a person’s interests and a means of alleviating poverty. This necessitates considering that they should be acquired at a time other than when one needs them, so that they are cheaper and more readily available, just as the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to store up staple food at a time when it was widely available from his earnings and wealth, and everything else was carried on him. Ibn Abbas explained this by saying: We used to take a piece of wood and cut it into three cubits or more or less and store it for the winter. We used to call it a palace qasr. This is the most correct statement about this matter, and God knows best.
77:34: God Almighty says: Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
77:35: The Almighty says: This is a Day when they will not speak meaning they will not talk. Nor will they be permitted to make excuses meaning that the Day of Resurrection has specific times and locations, so this is one of the times when they will not speak, nor will they be permitted to make excuses or deny their sins. It was narrated on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas that Ibn Al-Azraq asked him about the Almighty's saying: This is a Day when they will not speak and You will not hear except a whisper (Ta-Ha: 108) and the Almighty said: And some of them will turn to others, questioning each other (Saffat: 27). So he said to him: God the Almighty says: And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of those which you count (al-Hajj 22:47), so each of these days has one of these colors.
