It was said: They will not utter a beneficial argument, and whoever utters something that does not benefit or help, it is as if he did not speak. Al-Hasan said: They will not utter an argument even though they used to speak. It was said: This is the time for their response: Be gone into it, disgraced and do not speak to me (Al-Mu’minun 23:108), as has been mentioned previously. Abu Uthman said: They were silenced by the sight of awe and shame for their sins. Al-Junayd said: What excuse is there for one who turns away from his benefactor, denies him, and is ungrateful for his favors and blessings? The word Day is in the nominative case, as is the general reading of the verse as a subject and predicate, meaning the angels will say: This is a Day on which they will not speak. It is also possible that His statement: Go forth is from the words of the angels, then God will say to His friends: This is a Day on which the disbelievers will not speak. The meaning of Day is the hour and the time. Yahya ibn Sultan narrated from Abu Bakr from Asim: This is a Day on which they will not speak in the accusative case, and it was narrated from Ibn Harmaz and others. So it is permissible for it to be in the accusative case because it is added to the verb and its position is in the nominative case. This is the view of the Kufians. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case, provided that the reference is to something other than Day. This is the view of the Basrans, because according to them it is only in the nominative case when it is added to a nominative case, and the verb here is declined.
77:36: The Almighty said: And they will not be given permission to make excuses. The fa is a coordinating letter, i.e., it is in apposition toيَقِلِلنpermission is given. This was permitted because the endings of sentences are with nun. If he had said: and they will make excuses, he would not have made the verses correct. He also said: They will not be decreed to die (Fatir 35:36) in the accusative case, and both are correct. Similar to it is: Who is it that would loan God a goodly loan so He may multiply it? (al-Hadid 57:11) in the accusative and nominative cases.
77:37: God Almighty says: Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
77:38: The Almighty says: This is the Day of Judgment. That is, they will be told, This is the day on which the creation will be judged, and the truth will be distinguished from falsehood. "We have gathered you and the former peoples." Ibn Abbas said: He gathered those who denied Muhammad and those who denied the prophets before him. Ad-Dahhak narrated it from him.
77:39: The Almighty said: If you have a plan meaning a trick to escape destruction, then plan meaning plan for yourselves and resist Me, but you will not succeed. It was also said: If you have a plan meaning you are able to fight (then plan against me) meaning fight me. This is how Ad-Dahhak narrated from Ibn Abbas. He said: He means you used to fight Muhammad and fight me in this world, so today fight me. It was also said: meaning you used to commit sins in this world, but now you are unable to do them or defend yourselves. It was also said that it is from the words of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so it is like the words of Hud 11:Then plot against me all together and do not give me respite (Hud 11:55)
77:40: God Almighty says: Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
77:41: The Almighty says: Indeed, the righteous will be among shades and springs. He informs us of what the righteous will become tomorrow. What is meant by shades are the shades of trees and the shades of palaces, the place of shade in the three branches. And in Surat Ya-Sin 36:They and their spouses will be in shades, reclining on couches. (Ya-Sin 36:56)
77:42: The Almighty says: And fruits of whatever they desire meaning whatever they wish for. The general reading is (shades). Al-A'raj, Al-Zuhri, and Talhah read (shades), the plural of shade, meaning in Paradise.
77:43: The Almighty says: Eat and drink meaning that it will be said to them tomorrow instead of what is said to the polytheists: If you have a plan, then plan. So (eat and drink) is in the accusative case of the pronoun (the righteous) in the circumstance which is (in the shade) meaning that they are settled (in the shade) and that is said to them.
77:44: God Almighty says: Thus do We reward the doers of good. That is, We reward those who did good by believing in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and by their deeds in this world.
77:45: God Almighty says: Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
77:46: The Almighty's statement: Eat and enjoy yourselves a little. This refers back to what was mentioned before regarding the righteous, and it is a threat and a warning. It is a condition for the deniers, meaning woe is certain for them when it is said to them: Eat and enjoy yourselves a little. "Indeed, you are criminals," meaning disbelievers. It was also said: You have acquired an action that will harm you in the Hereafter, from polytheism and sins.
77:47: God Almighty says: Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
77:48: The Almighty said: And when it is said to them, ‘Bow down,’ they do not bow down. That is, when it is said to these polytheists, Bow down, meaning pray, they do not bow down, meaning they do not pray, as stated by Mujahid. Muqatil said: “It was revealed about Thaqif. They refused to pray, so this was revealed about them.” Muqatil said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to them: Become Muslims, and ordered them to pray. They said: We should not bow down, for that is a disgrace to us. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: There is no good in a religion in which there is no bowing or prostration. It is mentioned that Malik may God have mercy on him entered the mosque after the afternoon prayer, and he was one of those who did not believe in bowing after the afternoon prayer. He sat down and did not bow, so a boy said to him: Old man, get up and bow. So he got up and bowed, and did not argue with him about what he saw as his doctrine. He was asked about that, and he said: I feared that I might be among those who, ‘And when it is said to them, “Bow down, they do not bow down.” Ibn Abbas said: This will only be said to them in the Hereafter when they are called to prostrate but they are unable to. Qatadah said: This is in this world. Ibn al-Arabi said: This verse is evidence of the obligation of bowing and its inclusion as a pillar of prayer, and there is consensus on it. Some people thought that this only occurs on the Day of Resurrection and is not in the worldly realm of obligation. Whoever prostrates for God will be able to prostrate, and whoever prostrates out of compassion for someone else, his back will become a single plate. It was also said: Is it true that if they are told to submit to the truth, they will not submit? This is general in its application to prayer and other matters. Prayer is only mentioned because it is the foundation of religious laws after monotheism. It has also been said that it is the command to believe because it is not valid without faith.
77:49: God Almighty says: Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
77:50: God the Almighty says: Then in what statement after it will they believe? That is, if they do not believe in the Quran, which is the miracle and evidence of the truthfulness of the Messenger, peace be upon him, then in what will they believe! And He repeated Woe, that Day, to the deniers to mean repeated intimidation and threat. It was said: It is not a repetition, because with each statement he meant something other than what he meant with the last, as if he mentioned something and said: Woe to him who denies this, then he mentioned something else and said: Woe to him who denies this, then he mentioned something else and said: Woe to him who denies this, then he mentioned something else and said: Woe to him who denies this. And so on until the end. The surah has been concluded, praise be to God.
78:1: Meccan and called Surat An-Naba. It has forty or forty-one verses. God the Almighty said: About what are they asking one another? "About what are they asking one another? About what is an interrogative word, and that is why the alif of ma" was dropped from it to distinguish the report from the question. The same is true for "fi-ma and mmam" when asking a question. The meaning is: "About what are they asking one another?" Al-Zajjaj said: The origin of "About is about what, so the nun was assimilated into the mim" because it shares the nasal sound. The pronoun in "yatas'alun" refers to Quraysh. Abu Salih narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: When the Qur'an was revealed, Quraysh used to sit and talk among themselves, some of them believing it and some disbelieving it, so "About what are they asking one another?" was revealed. It was also said that "About" means: "About what are the polytheists arguing and quarreling?"
78:2: His Almighty saying: About the great report meaning they ask about the great report. So about is not connected to they ask which is in the recitation, because it would have been necessary to enter the interrogative particle, so it would be about the great report like saying: How much is your wealth, thirty or forty? So it is necessary, based on what we mentioned, that it is not connected to they ask which is in the recitation, but rather it is connected to they ask which is another implied word. And that is good because they ask before, as Al-Mahdawi said. Some of the people of knowledge mentioned that the interrogative in His saying: about is repeated except that it is implied, as if he said: About what are they asking about? About the great report? Based on this, it is connected to the first verse. And the great report means the big report.
78:3: The Almighty said: in which they differ meaning they differ from one another, so one believes and another denies. Abu Saleh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: It is the Qur'an, and his evidence is his statement: "Say: It is an important report. * From it you are turning away" [p. 67-68]. So the Qur'an is report, information, and stories, and it is report of great importance. Saeed narrated on the authority of Qatada, who said: It is the resurrection after death, in which people are divided into two groups: one who believes and one who denies. It was also said: It is the matter of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: That is because the Jews asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about many things, so God Almighty informed him of their differences.
78:4: The Almighty's saying: No! They will surely know meaning they will know the outcome of the Qur'an, or they will know the al-Qiyamah 75:is it true or false. And (No!) is a response to their denial of the resurrection or their rejection of the Qur'an, so it is stopped at. It is possible for it to mean truly or (ala), so it begins with it. What appears most apparent is that their question was only about the resurrection. Some of our scholars said: What is indicated by the Almighty's saying (Indeed, the Day of Decision is a time appointed) indicates that they were asking about the resurrection.
78:5: God the Almighty says: Then both of them will come to know meaning, truly, they will come to know the truth of what Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) brought of the Quran and what he mentioned to them about the resurrection after death. Ad-Dahhak said: (By no means, they will come to know) meaning the disbelievers will come to know the consequences of their denial. (Then both of them will come to know) meaning the believers will come to know the consequences of their belief. It was also said that it is the opposite. Al-Hasan said: It is a threat after a threat. The common people read both of them with the letter ya as a predicate, because God the Almighty says: They ask one another and He says: They differ therein. Al-Hasan, Abu Al-Aaliyah, and Malik ibn Dinar read them with the letter ta in both of them.
78:6: The Almighty's saying: Have We not made the earth a resting place? He showed them His ability to resurrect, meaning that our ability to create these things is greater than our ability to bring them back. The resting place is the mattress. The Almighty said: Who made the earth a bed for you (al-Baqarah 2:22) and it was read as a cradle. Its meaning is that it is for them like a cradle for a child, which is what is made for him and he sleeps on it.
78:7: The Almighty says: And the mountains as pegs meaning that they should be stable and not tip over or tilt with their inhabitants.
78:8: The Almighty says: And We created you in pairs meaning in types: male and female. It was also said: in colors. It was also said: This includes every pair of ugly and beautiful, tall and short, so that conditions differ and consideration is taken, so the superior is thanked and the inferior is patient.
78:9: The Almighty says: And We have made your sleep a rest ja'alna means we made, and therefore it has two objects. Sabatan is the second object, meaning rest for your bodies. From this comes the Sabbath, meaning the day of rest. That is, before the Children of Israel: Rest on this day, and do not do anything on it. Ibn al-Anbari denied this and said: Rest is not called sabaat. It was also said: Its origin is stretching. It is said: A woman sabaat her hair, meaning she loosened it and let it hang down. Sabaat is like stretching. A man is masboot al-khalq, meaning stretched out. And if a man wants to rest, he stretches out, so rest is called sabt. It was also said: Its origin is cutting. It is said: He shaved his hair sabatan, meaning he cut it. It is as if when he sleeps, he is cut off from people and from work. Sabaat is similar to death, except that the soul does not leave him. It is also said: Sir sabaat, meaning easy and soft. The poet said: And the folded relatives, as for its day, it is Saturday and as for its night, it is a curse
78:10: The Almighty says: And We have made the night as a covering, meaning that its darkness covers you and envelops you. This was stated by Al-Tabari. Ibn Jubayr and Al-Suddi said: It means a place of rest for you.
78:11: The Almighty's saying: And We have made the day for livelihood contains an implied meaning, a time for livelihood, that is, used to seek livelihood, which is everything that one lives on, such as food, drink, and other things. So (-living) according to this is a noun of time, so the second would be the first. It is also permissible for it to be a verbal noun meaning living, assuming the noun is deleted.
78:12: The Almighty says: And We built above you seven strong heavens, meaning seven firm heavens, meaning well-created and solidly constructed.
78:13: The Almighty said: And We made a blazing lamp meaning a kindling, which is the sun. And made here means created, because it is transitive with one object. The blazing one is the one who has a glow, it is said, he glowed, he glowed, he glowed, and it glows. And when a jewel sparkles, it is said, it glows. Ibn Abbas said: Bright, illuminating, and glittering.
78:14: The Almighty said: And We sent down from the pressed clouds abundant water. Mujahid and Qatadah said: The pressed clouds are the winds. Ibn Abbas said the same. It is as if they squeeze the clouds. It was also narrated from Ibn Abbas: They are the clouds. Sufyan, Al-Rabi’, Abu Al-Aaliyah and Al-Dahhak said: Meaning the clouds that squeeze water but have not yet rained, like the pressed woman whose menstruation is approaching but she has not yet menstruated. Abu Al-Najm said: She walks slowly, her veil swaying, three times a year, or her hurricane is approaching. Another said: I was the victim of three men who were afraid of him, a young man and a young woman. Another said: And the one with the thorns is like a daisy, adorned by the passing of youth and the fragrant presses. The winds are called mu’asarat, it is said: the wind squeezed, squeezes a hurricane: if it stirred up the dust, which is the hurricane, and the clouds are also called mu’asarat because they rain. Qatada also said: The mu’asarat are the sky, An-Nakhas: These sayings are correct, the winds that bring rain are called mu’asarat, and the winds fertilize the clouds, so it rains, and the rain comes down from the wind on this basis and it is permissible for the sayings to be one, and the meaning would be and We sent down from those with winds the mu’asarat “plentiful water”. The most correct saying is that the mu’asarat are the clouds. This is what is known that rain is from them, and if it was with the mu’asarat then the wind would be more appropriate. In As-Sahah: The mu’asarat are the clouds that squeeze with rain. And the people squeezed means they rained, and from this some of them read (and in it they squeeze) and the ma’asar is the girl who first reached puberty and menstruated, it is said: she has squeezed as if she entered the age of her youth or reached it, the rajaz poet said: A slave girl in Safwan, her house is walking slowly, her veil falling It has been squeezed or its hurricane has approached Plural: Ma'asir. It is said: It is the one that is close to menstruation, because the hurricane in a girl is like adolescence in a boy. I heard it from Abu Al-Ghaut Al-A'rabi. Someone else said: The Ma'asir is the cloud that is about to rain. It is said that the crops ripened, so it is Majnun, meaning it is about to ripen. Likewise, the clouds when they are about to rain have been squeezed. Al-Mubarrad said: It is said that a cloud is squeezed, meaning it holds water, and something is squeezed out of it one by one. From this comes the word 'Asr, with a fat-ha, for the refuge that one takes refuge to, and 'Asra, with a damma, is also a refuge. This meaning has already been mentioned in Surah Yusuf. Praise be to God. Abu Zubayd said: A friend who cries for help but is not helped. And it was the time of the rescuer. And from it is the word ma’sr for a girl who is close to puberty, it is said that she is ma’sr because she is confined to the house, so the house becomes her asr. In the reading of Ibn Abbas and Ikrimah, And We sent down by the pressed places and what is in the copies of the Qur’an is from the pressed places. Abi bin Ka’b, Al-Hasan, Ibn Jubayr, Zaid bin Aslam and Muqatil bin Hayyan said: from the pressed places meaning from the heavens. Pour forth water means continuous rain, from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others. And it is said: I poured his blood, so I poured it in the verse. Al-Zajjaj said: meaning pouring, and it is transitive as if he pours himself, meaning he pours. Ubaid bin Al-Abrash said: His upper body swelled, then his lower body shook, and he became fed up with carrying the water. In a hadith of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), he was asked about an accepted Hajj, so he said: Al-Ajj and Al-Thajj. Al-Ajj means raising the voice in the Talbiyah, and Al-Thah means shedding blood and slaughtering sacrificial animals. Ibn Zayd said: A great deal of Thajaj. The meaning is the same.
78:15: God Almighty says: That We may bring forth thereby meaning with that water grain such as wheat, barley, and other things plants from the root, which is what animals eat of grass.
78:16: The Almighty said: And gardens meaning orchards entwined meaning intertwined with each other due to the spread of their branches. It has no singular form like awza’ and akhyaaf. It was said that the singular of al-alaf is laf with a kasra, and laf with a damma. Al-Kisa’i mentioned this, and he said: A paradise of luxury, lavish living and companions who are all fair and good Also on his authority and Abu Ubaidah: Lafif like Sharif and Ashraf. It was said: It is the plural of plural. Al-Kisa’i narrated it. It is said: Jannah Lafa’ and Nabt Laf, and the plural is Laf with a damma on the lam like Hamr, then the plural of Laf is Faf. Al-Zamakhshari: If it was said the plural of Mutalifah with the estimation of deleting the extra letters, it would be reasonable. It is said: A tree Lafa’ and a tree Laf and a woman Lafa’: meaning thick-legged and fleshy. It was said: The estimation: And We bring forth with it gardens wrapped around, so it was deleted because the speech indicates it. Then this wrapping is the joining, meaning that the trees in the orchards are close together, so the branches of every tree are close together because of their strength.
78:17: The Almighty says: Indeed, the Day of Separation is a time appointed. That is, a time, a gathering, and an appointment for the first and the last, for what God has promised of reward and recompense. It is called the Day of Separation because God Almighty will separate between His creation on that day.
78:18: The Almighty says: The Day the Trumpet is blown meaning for the Resurrection. Then you will come meaning to the place of presentation. In groups meaning in nations, each nation with its leader. It was also said: in groups and droves. The singular is: group. And the word day is in the accusative case instead of the first day. It was narrated from the hadith of Muadh ibn Jabal that I said: O Messenger of God! Have you seen the words of God the Almighty: The Day the Trumpet is blown, and you will come in multitudes. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O Muadh ibn Jabal, you have asked about a great matter. Then he lowered his eyes weeping, and then he said: “Ten groups of my nation will be gathered together in separate groups. God the Almighty has distinguished them from the groups of Muslims, and He has changed their forms. Some of them will be in the form of monkeys, some in the form of pigs, some with their legs upside down, and their faces will be dragged on them. Some of them will be blind and will wander about, some of them will be deaf and dumb and will not understand, some of them will chew their tongues, and they will be hanging down over their chests, and pus will flow from their mouths like saliva, and the people of the assembly will be disgusted by them. Some of them will have their hands and feet cut off, some of them will be crucified on trunks of fire, some of them will have a foul odor than carcasses, and some of them will be dressed in tar-covered garments that stick to their skin. As for the one in the form of monkeys, they will be eaten by the “People - meaning the gossipers - and as for those who are in the image of pigs, they are the people of unlawful and forbidden things and taxes. As for those who hang their heads and faces, they are the ones who consume usury. The blind are those who rule unjustly. The deaf and dumb are those who admire their own deeds. Those who chew their tongues are the scholars and storytellers whose words contradict their deeds. Those whose hands and feet are cut off are those who harm their neighbors. Those who are crucified on trunks of fire are those who bring people to power. Those who stink more than carrion are those who enjoy lusts and pleasures, and prevent God’s right from their wealth. Those who wear the long robes are the people of arrogance, pride and conceit.”
78:19: The Almighty said: And the heaven was opened, and it became gates meaning for the angels to descend, as He the Almighty said: And the Day the heaven will be split open with clouds and the angels will be sent down in [a] descent. (al-Furqan 25:25) It was also said: It was cut apart, so it was in pieces like gates, so the word gates is in the accusative case according to this interpretation by deleting the letter kaf. It was also said: The meaning is that it had gates, because they all become gates. It was also said: Its gates are its paths. It was also said: It will dissolve and scatter, until it has gates. It was also said: Every servant has two gates in the heaven: a gate for his deeds, and a gate for his provision, so when the Day of Resurrection comes, the gates will be opened. In the hadith of the Isra': “Then he ascended with us to the heaven, and Gabriel asked for the gate to be opened. It was said: Who are you? He said: Gabriel. It was said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. It was said: Has he been sent to? He said: He has been sent to. So it was opened for us.”
78:20: The Almighty says: And the mountains will be set in motion and will become a mirage. That is, they will be nothing, just as a mirage is: the one who sees it thinks it is water, but it is not. It was also said: set in motion means that they will be blown away from their roots. It was also said: they will be removed from their places.
78:21: God the Almighty says: Indeed, Hell is ever in ambush. Mif'al from rasad and rasd: everything is in front of you. Al-Hasan said: There is an ambush on the Fire, no one will enter Paradise until he passes over it. Whoever comes and crosses it will pass, and whoever does not come with a pass will be detained. Sufyan may God be pleased with him said: There are three qatars over it. It was also said that it is marsad with ambushes, meaning it ambushes whoever passes through it. Muqatil said: A prison. It was also said: A path and a passageway, so there is no way to Paradise until one crosses Hell. In As-Sahah: Al-marsad is the road. Al-Qushayri mentioned that al-marsad is the place where one ambushes the enemy, like a racecourse: the place where horses are trained. That is, it is prepared for them. Al-marsad means a place, so the angels ambush the disbelievers until they descend into Hell. Al-Mawardi mentioned on the authority of Abu Sinan that it means an ambush, rewarding them for their actions. In As-Sahah: The observer of something: the one who watches it. You say: he watched him, he watches him, watching, and watching. Watching means anticipation. The observatory is the place of observation. Al-Asma’i: I watched him, I prepared for him: I watched them and I prepared for him. Al-Kisa’i said the same. I said: Hell is prepared and waiting, a verbal noun from the root word rasad, which means to watch, meaning it is waiting for whoever comes. The word marsad is a verbal noun from the structures of exaggeration like mi’tar and mughyar, so it is as if Hell often awaits the disbelievers.
78:22: The Almighty’s saying: For the transgressors is a place of return instead of His saying: (an ambush), and the place of return is the reference, meaning a place to which they will return. It is said: he returned, a return, if he came back. Qatada said: a shelter and a home. What is meant by the transgressors is the one who transgressed in his religion through disbelief, or in his worldly life through injustice.
78:23: The Almighty’s saying: They will abide therein for ages meaning they will remain in the Fire as long as the ages last, and they will never end. For every time an age passes, another will come. Al-Haqab with two dammahs means time and the ages are ages. Al-Haqab with a kasrah means a year, and the plural is huqab. Mutammam ibn Nuwayrah al-Tamimi said: We were like my companions, Juthayma, for a long time until it was said that they would never split apart. When we parted, it was as if Malik and I had not spent a night together because of our long meeting. Al-Haqq with Dammah and Sukun: eighty years. It was also said: more than that or less, as will come, and the plural is Ahqab. The meaning in the verse is that they will remain in it for the epochs of the Hereafter that have no end. The word the Hereafter was omitted because the speech indicates it, since the speech mentions the Hereafter, which is like saying the days of the Hereafter, meaning days after days without end. Rather, it would have indicated the time period if He had said five epochs or ten epochs and the like. He mentioned the epochs because the epochs were the most distant thing to them, so He spoke according to what their imaginations lead them to and what they know, and it is a metaphor for eternity, meaning they will remain in it forever. It was also said that he mentioned the epochs and not the days, because epochs are more terrifying to the hearts, and more indicative of eternity. The meanings are close, and this eternity is for the polytheists. The verse can be interpreted to refer to the disobedient who will emerge from the Fire after epochs. It was said: The ages are the time for them to drink boiling water and pus-filled water, and when it ends, they will have another kind of punishment. For this reason, He said: “They will abide therein for ages. They will not taste therein any coolness or drink, except scalding water and pus-filled water.” Labtheen is an active participle of labath, and this is strengthened by the fact that the source of it is labath with a sukoon, like drinking. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read labtheen without an alif, and this is the choice of Abu Hatim and Abu Ubaid, and they are two dialects. It is said: a man is labith and labith, like tamaa and tamaa, and farah and farah. It is said: he is labath in such-and-such a place,” meaning that abiding has become his habit, so it is similar to what is inherent in humans, like hadar and faraq, because the root of fa’ala is only for what is inherent in something in most cases, and this is not the case with the active participle of labith. Al-Haqab: “Eighty years according to Ibn Omar, Ibn Muhaisin, and Abu Hurairah. A year is three hundred and sixty days, and a day is one thousand years of the days of this world,” said Ibn Abbas. Ibn Omar narrated this with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. Abu Hurairah said: A year is three hundred and sixty days, each day like the days of this world. Ibn Omar also said: Al-Haqab: forty years. Al-Suddi: seventy years. It was also said: It is a thousand months. Narrated by Abu Umamah with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Bashir ibn Ka’b: Three hundred years. Al-Hasan: None of you knows what the epochs are, but they said that they are one hundred epochs, and one epoch is seventy thousand years, and today is like a thousand years of what you count. And on the authority of Abu Umamah also, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: (One epoch is thirty thousand years), mentioned by Al-Mahdawi. The first is Al-Mawardi. Qatrib said: It is a long, unlimited time. And Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By God, no one who has entered the Fire will leave it until he has spent eons in it. An eon is eighty-odd years, and a year is three hundred and sixty days, and each day is a thousand years of those which you count. So let none of them rely on himself to leave the Fire.” Narrated by al-Tha’labi. Al-Qurazi said: The eons are forty-three eons, each eon is seventy autumns, each autumn is seven hundred years, each year is three hundred and sixty days, and each day is a thousand years. I said: These are conflicting statements, and the specification in the verse of eternity requires a chain of transmission that removes the excuse, and that is not proven from the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him. Rather, the meaning - and God knows best - is what we mentioned first, that is, abiding therein for ages and eras, whenever a time passes, another follows it, and an era follows another, thus forever and ever without interruption. Ibn Kaysan said: The meaning of abiding therein for ages has no limit, so it is as if He said forever. Ibn Zayd and Muqatil said: It was abrogated by the statement of God, the Most High, {So taste [the punishment], for We will not increase you except in torment.} Meaning that the number has been cut off, and eternity has been achieved.
78:24: God Almighty says: They will not taste therein meaning in the ages coolness or drink. Coolness means sleep, according to Abu Ubaidah and others. The poet said: If I wanted, I would forbid women other than you. If I wanted, I would not eat the food of a camel or a cloven-hoofed animal. It was said by Mujahid, Al-Suddi, Al-Kisa’i, Al-Fadl bin Khalid, and Abu Muadh Al-Nahwi, and they recited the words of Al-Kindi: Her sheets became cold on me, so the cold turned me away from her and from kissing her. It means sleep. The Arabs say: The cold prevented the cold, meaning: Sleep took away the cold. I said: The hadith came: “He (peace and blessings be upon him) was asked, ‘Is there sleep in Paradise?’ He said, ‘No, sleep is the brother of death, and there is no death in Paradise.’ So too is Hellfire.” God the Almighty said, ‘They will not be decreed to die’ (Fatir 35:36). Ibn Abbas said: ‘Cold’ means the cold of a drink.’ Also from him: ‘Cold’ means sleep, and a drink is water.’ Al-Zajjaj said: ‘They will not taste therein the coolness of the wind, nor shade, nor sleep.’ So he made the cold the cold of everything that has comfort, and this is a cold that benefits them. As for freezing cold, it is a cold that they are harmed by, but it does not benefit them, so they will have from it a punishment that God knows best. Al-Hasan, Ata’, and Ibn Zayd said: ‘Cold’ means spirit and comfort. The poet said: You cannot find shade from the cold of the morning, nor can you taste the shade of the evening. (They will not taste therein any coolness or drink) is a clause in the position of a state of the oppressors, or an attribute of the eras. The eras are a time adverb, and the factor in it is (remaining) or (remaining) with the transitive verb. God Almighty says: They will not taste therein meaning in the ages coolness or drink. Coolness means sleep, according to Abu Ubaidah and others. The poet said: If I wanted, I would forbid women other than you. If I wanted, I would not eat the food of a camel or a cloven-hoofed animal. It was said by Mujahid, Al-Suddi, Al-Kisa’i, Al-Fadl bin Khalid, and Abu Muadh Al-Nahwi, and they recited the words of Al-Kindi: Her sheets became cold on me, so the cold turned me away from her and from kissing her. It means sleep. The Arabs say: The cold prevented the cold, meaning: Sleep took away the cold. I said: The hadith came: “He (peace and blessings be upon him) was asked, ‘Is there sleep in Paradise?’ He said, ‘No, sleep is the brother of death, and there is no death in Paradise.’ So too is Hellfire.” God the Almighty said, ‘They will not be decreed to die’ (Fatir 35:36). Ibn Abbas said: ‘Cold’ means the cold of a drink.’ Also from him: ‘Cold’ means sleep, and a drink is water.’ Al-Zajjaj said: ‘They will not taste therein the coolness of the wind, nor shade, nor sleep.’ So he made the cold the cold of everything that has comfort, and this is a cold that benefits them. As for freezing cold, it is a cold that they are harmed by, but it does not benefit them, so they will have from it a punishment that God knows best. Al-Hasan, Ata’, and Ibn Zayd said: ‘Cold’ means spirit and comfort. The poet said: You cannot find shade from the cold of the morning, nor can you taste the shade of the evening. The eras are a time adverb, and the factor in it is (remaining) or (remaining) with the transitive verb.
78:25: The Almighty's saying: Except scalding water and ghassaq is an interrupted exception according to those who say that coldness refers to sleep, and those who say that it refers to coldness are substitutes for it. And the scalding water: is hot water, said Abu Ubaidah. Ibn Zayd said: The scalding water: is their tears, collected in basins and then given to them to drink. An-Nahhas said: The root of the scalding water: is hot water, and from it is derived the bath, and from it the fever, and from it and shade of those who swelter (Al-Waqi'ah: 42). Rather, the hot water, and from it are derived the bath, and from it the fever, and from it and shade of those who swelter (Al-Waqi'ah: 42) is intended to mean the extreme heat. And the ghassaq: is the pus and discharge of the people of Hell. It was also said the freezing cold. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read it with a shaddah on the seen, and the discussion of it has already been mentioned in Sad. The Almighty's saying: Except scalding water and ghassaq is an interrupted exception according to those who say that coldness refers to sleep, and those who say that it refers to coldness are substitutes for it. And the scalding water: is hot water, said Abu Ubaidah. Ibn Zayd said: The scalding water: is their tears, collected in basins and then given to them to drink. An-Nahhas said: The root of the scalding water: is hot water, and from it is derived the bath, and from it the fever, and from it and shade of those who swelter (Al-Waqi'ah: 42). Rather, the hot water, and from it are derived the bath, and from it the fever, and from it and shade of those who swelter (Al-Waqi'ah: 42) is intended to mean the extreme heat. And the ghassaq: is the pus and discharge of the people of Hell. It was also said the freezing cold. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read it with a shaddah on the seen, and the discussion of it has already been mentioned in Sad.
78:26: The Almighty says: A just reward meaning in accordance with their deeds. According to Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others, Wifaq means according just as qital means fighting. Jaz'a is in the accusative case as a verbal noun, meaning We rewarded them with a reward that matched their deeds, as stated by Al-Farra' and Al-Akhfash. Al-Farra' also said: It is the plural of wafaq, and wafaq and lafaq are one and the same. Muqatil said: The punishment matched the sin, so there is no sin greater than polytheism, and no punishment greater than the Fire. Al-Hasan and Ikrimah said: Their deeds were bad, so God brought them what would harm them.
78:27: The Almighty says: Indeed, they did not expect meaning they did not fear an account meaning an accounting for their deeds. It was also said that it means they did not expect the reward of an account. Al-Zajjaj: That is, they did not believe in the resurrection, so they hoped for their account.
78:28: And they denied Our signs completely meaning what the prophets brought. It was also said: what We sent down of books. The reading of the common people is (kadhdhban) with a shaddah on the dhal and a kasrah on the kaf, on the basis of qadhb, meaning they lied a great lie. Al-Farra' said: It is a broad Yemeni dialect, they say: I lied to him a liar, and I tore the shirt completely. Every verb in the form fa'al has a stressed fa'al in their language. Some of the Kalbis recited: It has been a long time since I have been away from my friend and from the need to satisfy her in terms of healing. Ali, may God be pleased with him, read kadhdhaban with a light stress on the letter, which is also a verbal noun. Abu Ali said: Both the light stress and the heavy stress are verbal nouns for lying, like the saying of Al-A’sha: I believed her and I disbelieved her, but a person is benefited by his liar. Abu al-Fath 48:They both came as a source of lying and lying together. Al-Zamakhshari: (liar) with a lightened form is a source of lying, as evidenced by his saying: I believed her and I disbelieved her, but a liar benefits a person. It is like His statement: And He caused you to grow from the earth a plant (Nuh 71:17) meaning and they denied Our signs, so would they have denied a liar? Or you make it the accusative with (-they denied), because it includes the meaning of they denied, because every denier of the truth is a liar, because if they are liars in the eyes of the Muslims, and the Muslims are liars in their eyes, then there is lying between them. Ibn Omar read (liar) with a damma on the kaf and a shaddah, plural of liar, as Abu Hatim said. Al-Zamakhshari made it the accusative in the state. And the liar may mean: one who is eloquent in lying, it is said: a lying man, like you say: good-looking and miserly, so he makes it an attribute of the source (they denied), meaning the lie of an excessively lying liar. In Al-Sahah: And the Almighty’s saying: And they denied Our signs with denial, which is one of the sources of the doubled form, because its source can be expressed as taf’il like la taklim, and as fa’al kadhdhab, and as ta’la like tawsiyah, and as maf’al, And We tore them apart, every one of them torn apart (Saba’: 19).
78:29: The Almighty says: And everything We have recorded in a book. (Everything) is accusative with an implied verb as a subject. (A book) is accusative as a verbal noun, because the meaning is We have recorded it. Abu al-Samal read (And everything) in the nominative case as a subject. (A book) is accusative as a verbal noun because the meaning of We have recorded it is We wrote it down, that is, We wrote it down. Then it was said that what was meant by it is knowledge, because what was written down was further from being forgotten. And it was said that it was We wrote it down in the Preserved Tablet for the angels to know it. And it was said that what was meant was what was written down for the servants of their deeds. So this is a writing that came from the angels assigned to the servants by the command of God the Almighty to them to write it down, the evidence for which is His Almighty saying: Verily, over you are keepers * Noble and recording. (al-Infitar 82:10-11) So taste [the punishment], for We will not increase you except in torment. Abu Barzah said: I asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the most difficult verse in the Qur’an?
78:30: He said: ((The Almighty’s saying: So taste [the punishment], for We will not increase you except in punishment)) meaning (Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins) and (Every time they are extinguished, We will increase their blazing fire).
78:31: The Almighty says: Indeed, for the righteous is attainment. He mentioned the reward of the one who fears disobeying the command of God. (Mafaz is a place of victory, salvation, and deliverance from what the people of Hell are in. That is why a desert, when its water is scarce, is called a wilderness, as a sign of optimism for deliverance from it.
78:32: The Almighty says: Gardens and vineyards. This is an interpretation of victory. It was also said: Indeed, for the righteous is attainment. Indeed, for the righteous are gardens, the plural of garden, which is a fenced orchard. It is said that he surrounded it, meaning he enclosed it. And vines: the plural of grape, meaning grape vines, but it was deleted.
78:33: The Almighty said: And full-breasted maidens of equal age. Kawa'ib: the plural of Ka'ib, which means full-breasted. It is said: the slave girl Ka'abat tak'uban, and she Ka'abat tak'ib tak'iban, and she sighed takhudan. Ad-Dahhak said: Like the full-breasted virgins. From this is the saying of Qays ibn Asim: How many noble horses we have had, and how many maidens who did not know what misery is Atrab: peers in age. The singular form is tarab in Surah Al-Waqi’ah.
78:34: The Almighty said: And an overflowing cup. Al-Hasan, Qatada, Ibn Zayd, and Ibn Abbas said: brimming full. It is said: I overflowed the cup, meaning I filled it. A full cup, meaning full. He said: O give me pure water from your cup, the cupbearer gave me to drink from it Khaddash bin Zuhair said: Amer came to us seeking the Quran, so we gave him a full cup. Saeed bin Jubair, Ikrimah, Mujahid and Ibn Abbas also said: successive, one after the other, and from this the stones were crushed, which means they are very sticky and they enter into one another, so successive is like intertwined. And also from Ikrimah and Zaid bin Aslam: clear, the poet said: You are dearer to my heart than a thirsty person is to a cup of wine. Saeed bin Jubair, Ikrimah, Mujahid and Ibn Abbas also said: successive, one after the other, and from this the stones were crushed, which means they are very sticky and they enter into one another, so successive is like intertwined. And also from Ikrimah and Zaid bin Aslam: clear, the poet said: You are dearer to my heart than a thirsty person is to a cup of wine. It is the plural of dahaq, which is two pieces of wood used to push the stem. What is meant by the cup is wine, so the estimation is: wine with dahaq, meaning squeezed and filtered, said Al-Qushayri. In As-Sahah: And I poured the water: meaning I emptied it forcefully. Abu Amr said: And dahaq - with the emphasis on the letter kasra - is a kind of torture. In Persian it is ashkanjah. Al-Mubarrad: And madhuq: the one who is tortured with all kinds of torture that have no relief in it. Ibn Al-A'rabi: I broke and cut something, and likewise dahaqatuhu, and he recited for Hajar bin Khalid: We crush some of the meat for sale and dew and some of it boils with the blame of its soaking And dahmaqtuhu with the addition of the m: the same. Al-Asma’i said: dahmaqah is the softness of food and its goodness and tenderness, and so is everything soft, and from it is the hadith of Umar: If I wanted him to dahmaq for me, I would have done it, but God criticized a people and said: You have exhausted your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them (al-Ahqaf 46:20).
78:35: God Almighty says: They will not hear therein any idle talk or falsehood. Idle talk means falsehood, which is what is omitted from speech and discarded, and from it is the hadith: If you say to your friend, ‘Listen on Friday while the imam is delivering the sermon,’ then you have spoken idle talk. This is because when the people of Paradise drink, their minds do not change, and they do not speak idle talk, unlike the people of this world. Nor a liar: mentioned above, meaning they do not lie to each other, nor do they hear lies. Al-Kisa’i read kadhdhaban with a lightened kadhdhaban from kadhdhabtu kadhdhaban, meaning they will not lie to each other in Paradise. It was said that they are two verbal nouns for denial, and they lightened them here because they are not restricted by a verb that would become a verbal noun for it. He emphasized his statement, And they denied Our verses as liars, because they denied restricts the verbal noun to the liar.
78:36: The Almighty’s saying: A reward from your Lord is in the accusative case as a verbal noun. Because the meaning is that He rewarded them for what was mentioned above, as His reward. Likewise, a gift because the meaning of gave them and rewarded them is one and the same. That is, He gave them a gift. A reckoning means a lot, as Qatada said. It is said: I thought so-and-so was generous meaning I gave him a lot of gifts until he said It is sufficient for me. He said: We follow the newborn of the neighborhood if he is hungry and we think he is not hungry Al-Qutbi said: We see that the origin of this is that he gives him until he says Hasbi enough for me. Al-Zajjaj said: Hisab means what is sufficient for them. Al-Akhfash said the same. It is said: I think that such and such means it is sufficient for me. Al-Kalbi said: He held them to account and gave them ten for the good deed. Mujahid said: Hisab for what they knew. So, Hisab means counting. That is, according to what is due to him in the promise of the Lord. He promised ten for the good deed, and He promised to a people seven hundred times, and He promised to a people a reward that has no end or measure, as the Almighty said: Only the patient will be given their reward in full, without account (al-Zumar 39:10). Abu Hashim read Ata’a hisab with a fat-ha on the ha’ and a shaddah on the seen, on the weight of fa’al meaning sufficiency. Al-Asma’i said: The Arabs say: Hasabat a man with a shaddah, if you honored him. And he recited the words of the poet: If a guest comes to him, he thinks he is a guest. Ibn Abbas read Hassan with the letter nun.
78:37: The Almighty's saying: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Most Gracious. Ibn Mas'ud, Nafi', Abu 'Amr, Ibn Kathir, Zaid from Ya'qub, and Al-Mufaddal from 'Aasim read: (Lord) in the nominative case as a new sentence, (the Most Gracious) is its predicate. Or it means: He is the Lord of the heavens, and (the Most Gracious) would be a second subject. Ibn 'Amir, Ya'qub, and Ibn Muhaisin both read it in the accusative case, as a description of His saying: {A reward from your Lord}, meaning a reward from your Lord, Lord of the heavens, the Most Gracious. Ibn 'Abbas, 'Aasim, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa'i read: (Lord of the heavens) in the accusative case as a description, (the Most Gracious) in the nominative case as a subject, meaning He is the Most Gracious. Abu Ubaid chose it and said: This is the most just. He lowered (Lord) because it is close to His statement, Who is your Lord? and so it is an attribute of Him. He raised (the Most Gracious) because it is far from Him, as a new sentence. Its predicate is they do not possess any speech from Him, meaning they do not possess the right to ask Him except for what He has given them permission to do. Al-Kisa’i said: they do not possess any speech from Him by intercession except with His permission. It was said: Address means speech, meaning they do not possess the right to address the Lord, glory be to Him, except with His permission. The evidence for this is: No soul speaks except by His permission (Hud 11:105). It was said: He meant the disbelievers (they do not possess any speech from Him), but as for the believers, they intercede. I said: After they are given permission, because God Almighty says: Who is he that can intercede with Him except by His permission? (al-Baqarah 2:255) and God Almighty says: On that Day, no intercession will benefit except for one to whom the Most Merciful has given permission and whose word He approves. (Ta-Ha 20:109)
78:39: The Almighty says: That is the true Day meaning the one that will happen and will occur. So whoever wills may take to his Lord a way of return meaning a return through righteous deeds, as if if he does good, He returns it to God the Almighty, and if he does evil, He counts it as part of it. This meaning is seen in the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him): And all good is in Your hands, and evil is not from You. Qatada said: A way of return) means a path.
78:40: The Almighty's statement: Indeed, We have warned you of an imminent torment: He is addressing the infidels of Quraysh and the polytheists of Arabia, because they said: We will not be resurrected. The torment is the torment of the Hereafter, and everything that is coming is imminent. God the Almighty said: On the Day they see it, it will be as if they had not remained [in the world] except for an afternoon or a morning thereof. (An-Nazi'at: 46) Al-Kalbi and others said its meaning. Qatadah said: The punishment of this world, because it is the nearer of the two torments. Muqatil said: It is the killing of Quraysh at Badr. What is more apparent is that it is the torment of the Hereafter, which is death and the Resurrection, because whoever dies, his Resurrection has taken place. If he is one of the people of Paradise, he will see his seat in Paradise, and if he is one of the people of Hell, he will see disgrace and humiliation. For this reason, God the Almighty said: The Day when a man will see what his hands have put forth. (An-Naba': 40) He explained the time of that torment, meaning We have warned you of an imminent torment on that Day, which is the Day when a man will see what his hands have put forth, meaning he will see it. It was said: He will see what he put forth, but to was omitted. The person here is the believer, according to Al-Hasan, meaning he finds work for himself. As for the disbeliever, he does not find work for himself, so he wishes he was dust. When God said, And the disbeliever says (An-Naba’: 40), we know that what is meant by the person is the believer. It was said that the person here is Ubayy ibn Khalaf and Uqbah ibn Abi Mu’ayt. And the disbeliever says is Abu Jahl. It was said that it is general and applies to every person who will see on that day the reward for what he earned. Muqatil said: The verse, The Day when a man will see what his hands have put forth was revealed about Abu Salamah ibn Abd Al-Asad. Al-Tha’labi said: I heard Abu Al-Qasim ibn Habib say: The disbeliever here is Iblis, because he criticized Adam by saying that he was created from dust, and boasted that he was created from fire. So when he sees on the Day of Resurrection what Adam and his children will have of reward, comfort, and mercy, and sees what hardship and torment he is in, he will wish that he was in Adam’s place, so he will say, Oh, I wish I were dust. He said: I saw it in some of the commentaries of Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr. It was said: That is, Iblis will stand up and say, I wish I had been created from dust and had not said, ‘I am better than Adam.’ It was narrated from Ibn Umar: “When the Day of Resurrection comes, the earth will be spread out like a hide, and the beasts, cattle, and wild animals will be gathered together. Then retribution will be established among the animals, until the one-horned sheep takes retribution from the horned sheep for butting it. When the retribution is completed among the animals, until the one-horned sheep takes retribution from the horned sheep for butting it. When the retribution is completed among the animals, it will be said to the one-horned sheep, ‘Become dust.’ At that point, the unbeliever will say, ‘I wish I were dust.’” And something similar was narrated from Abu Hurairah and Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-‘As, may God be pleased with them. We have mentioned it in the book Al-Tadhkira, on the conditions of the dead and the affairs of the Hereafter, with proper pronunciation, and praise be to God. Abu Ja`far Al-Nahhas mentioned: Mu`mar told us, he said, Ja`far bin Burqan Al-Jazari told me, on the authority of Yazid bin Al-Asamm, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: God Almighty will gather all of creation, from animals, birds, and humans, then it will be said to the animals and birds, Become dust. At that time, the disbeliever will say, I was not given my book. (al-Haqqah 69:25) Abu Al-Zinad said: When judgment is passed between the people, and the people of Paradise are ordered to go to Paradise, and the people of Hell are ordered to go to Hell, it will be said to the rest of the nations and the believing jinn, Return to dust. So they will return to dust, and at that time, the disbeliever will say when he sees them, Oh, I wish I were dust. Layth bin Abi Sulaym said: The believing jinn will return to dust. `Umar bin `Abd Al-`Aziz, Al-Zuhri, Al-Kalbi, and Mujahid said: The believers of Paradise are around Paradise in suburbs and open spaces, but they are not in it. This is more correct, and it has been mentioned in Surah Al-Rahman. This is a statement that they are responsible: they are rewarded and punished. They are like the children of Adam, and God knows best.
79:1: Meccan by consensus. It consists of forty-five or forty-six verses. God the Almighty says: {And those who pull out the souls by drowning}: God the Almighty swears by these things that He mentioned, that the Resurrection is true. And (those who pull out) are the angels who pull out the souls of the disbelievers. This was said by Ali may God be pleased with him, and the same was said by Ibn Mas`ud, Ibn Abbas, Masruq, and Mujahid: They are the angels who pull out the souls of the children of Adam. Ibn Mas`ud said: He means the souls of the disbelievers, which the Angel of Death pulls out from their bodies, from under every hair, from under the nails, and the roots of the feet, pulling them out like a skewer pulled out from wet wool, then he drowns them, that is, he returns them to their bodies, then he pulls them out. This is His action with the disbelievers. This was also said by Ibn Abbas. Sa`id ibn Jubayr said: Their souls were pulled out, then drowned, then burned, then thrown into the Fire. It was also said: The disbeliever sees himself drowning at the time of the pullout. Al-Suddi said: And (those who pull out) are the souls when they are drowned in the chests. Mujahid said: It is death pulling out the souls. Al-Hasan and Qatada: They are the stars that move from one horizon to another, i.e. they go, from their saying: he moved to it, meaning he went, or from their saying: the horses moved, meaning they ran. Gharaqan means that they sink, set, and rise from one horizon to another. This was said by Aba Ubaidah, Ibn Kaysan, and Al-Akhfash. It was said: The Nazi’at are the bows that move with arrows, this was said by Ata’ and Ikrimah. Gharaqan means ighraqan, and ighraqan of the nazi’ in the bow is to reach the end of the extension, until it ends at the blade. It is said: he drowned in the bow, meaning he completed its extension, and that is by ending at the heel at the blade that is wrapped around it. And ighraq means comprehensiveness. The inside eggshell is called gharaq’a. It was said: they are the archer raiders. I said: It is the same as the one before it, because when he swears by the bows, what is meant is those who pull them out to magnify them, and it is like the saying of the Most High: And the charging steeds, panting (al-Adiyat 100:1), and God knows best. What he meant by drowning is exaggeration in pulling, and this is permissible in all ways of interpreting it. It was said: It is the wild beast that pulls from the grass and is frightened. Yahya ibn Salam narrated it. The meaning of drowning is distancing in pulling.
79:2: God the Almighty says: {And the ones who are active with activity.} Ibn Abbas said: It means the angels who stimulate the soul of the believer, and seize it as the rope is stimulated from the hand of a camel when it is released from it. Al-Farra’ narrated this statement and then said: What I heard from the Arabs is that they say antasata as if it was stimulated from a rope. And tying it means nasataha, and the ribat is the natasata. And if you tie a rope to the hand of a camel, you have stimulated it, so you are active. And if you loosen it, you have stimulated it and you are invigorated. And Ibn Abbas also said: It is the souls of the believers at death, they are stimulated to leave, and that is because there is no believer who is about to die except that Paradise is presented to him before he dies, and he sees in it what God has prepared for him of his wives and family of the wide-eyed maidens, and they call him to it, and his soul is excited to leave and come to them. And he also said: It means the souls of the disbelievers and hypocrites are stimulated as the heel is stimulated, which is followed by an arrow. Al-Aqab with a sukoon: The nerve from which the strings are made. The singular is Aqaba. You say from it: the heel of an arrow, a cup, or a bow, Aqban: if you twist something from it around it. Al-Nashat active: to pull quickly. From this comes the word anshutah loop: a knot that is easy to untie if pulled, like a knot of a tie. Abu Zaid said: I tied the rope with a noose, I untied it, and I stretched the rope until it was untied. Al-Farra’ said: I loosened the rope, meaning I loosened it. And nashat means I tied the rope to his hands. Al-Layth said: I tied him with a noose and two nooses, meaning I bound him. And nashat al-‘Iqal means I stretched his noose and it was untied. He said: It is said nashat active in the sense of anshaat active, two languages with one meaning, and based on this the statement of Ibn Abbas mentioned first is correct. And it was also narrated from him: The active ones are the angels due to their activity, they go and come by the command of God wherever it is. And it was also narrated from him and from Ali may God be pleased with them both. They are the angels who stimulate the souls of the unbelievers, between the skin and the nails, until they extract them from their bodies, refreshed by distress and grief, as wool is refreshed by an iron skewer. It is from the root nashaṭ, meaning to pull. It is said: nashaṭa al-dulū anshaṭa with kasra, and ashaṭa with damma: meaning I pulled it out. Al-Asma’i said: A well of nashaṭ: meaning one with a shallow bottom, from which the bucket comes out with a single pull. A well of nashūt: he said: it is one from which the bucket does not come out until it is very refreshed. Mujahid said: it is death that stimulates the soul of man. Al-Suddi: they are the souls when they are stimulated from the feet. It was said: an-Nāzi‘āt are the hands of the invaders or themselves, they pull out the bows by drowning the arrows, and they are the ones that activate the shackles. Ikrimah and Ata’: they are the shackles that activate the arrows. Also narrated by Ata’, Qatadah, al-Hasan and al-Akhfash: they are the stars that are active from horizon to horizon: meaning they go. And this is also in al-Sahīh. (And an-Nāshiṭat nashṭan) means the stars from one constellation to another, like a bull that is active from one country to another. Worries make their owner active. Humayyan bin Quhafa said: My concerns have become the catalyst for my activities, sometimes in the Levant and sometimes in the Middle East. Abu Ubaidah and Ata’ also: The active ones: are the beasts when they move from one country to another, just as worries move a person from one country to another, and he recited the words of Humayan: My worries became....* home It was said: And those who pull out is for the disbelievers and those who act upon is for the believers. So the angels gently pull the soul of the believer, and the pulling out is a strong pull, and the act upon is a gentle pull. It was also said: They are both for the disbelievers and the two verses after them are for the believers when they depart from this world.
79:3: God the Almighty says: And those that swim, swimming. Ali may God be pleased with him said: They are the angels that swim with the souls of the believers. Al-Kalbi said: They are the angels who take the souls of the believers, like someone who swims in water, sometimes submerging and sometimes rising. They take them gently and easily, then leave them until they rest. Mujahid and Abu Saleh said: They are the angels who descend from the sky, hurrying to God's command, just as a noble horse is called a sabih when it runs quickly. Mujahid also said: The angels swim in their descent and ascent. He also said: The sabihah: Death swims in the souls of the children of Adam. It was said: They are the horses of the raiders. Antara said: Horses learn when they swim in the pools of death Imru' al-Qais said: Wipe if the swimmers on the sand raise dust with the kicked iron Qatada and Al-Hasan: They are the stars swimming in their orbits, and so are the sun and the moon. God the Almighty said: Each in an orbit floats (al-Anbiya 21:33). Ata’: They are the ships swimming in the water. Ibn Abbas: The swimming ones are the souls of the believers swimming in longing to meet God and His mercy when they depart.
79:4: God the Almighty says: And the foremost ones will outpace each other. Ali may God be pleased with him said: They are the angels who precede the devils in revelation to the prophets (peace be upon them). Masruq and Mujahid said the same. Mujahid also said: And any forerunners: They are the angels who precede the son of Adam in goodness and righteous deeds. It was also said: They precede the sons of Adam to righteous deeds and record them. Mujahid also said: Death precedes man. Muqatil: They are the angels who precede the souls of the believers to Paradise. Ibn Masoud: They are the souls of the believers who precede the angels who take them and have witnessed joy, longing to meet God the Almighty and His mercy. Al-Rabi' said something similar: They are the souls who precede in leaving at death. Qatada, Al-Hasan, and Muammar said: They are the stars that precede each other in walking. Ata': They are the horses that precede in jihad. It was said: It is possible that the forerunners are the souls that precede the bodies to Paradise or Hell, as Al-Mawardi said. Al-Jurjani said: He mentioned (the ones who precede) with the letter fa’ because it is derived from the one before it, meaning those who swim and are first. You say: He stood up and went, so this requires that standing be a reason for going. If you said: He stood up and went, then standing would not be a reason for going.
79:5: God the Almighty said: And those who manage the affairs of God Al-Qushayri said: They agreed that it refers to the angels. Al-Mawardi said: There are two opinions: One of them is the angels, as stated by the majority. The second opinion refers to the seven planets. Khalid ibn Ma'dan narrated it on the authority of Mu'adh ibn Jabal. There are two views regarding their management of affairs: One is the management of their rising and setting. The second is their management of the changing circumstances that God has decreed for them. Al-Qushayri also narrated this opinion in his Tafsir. God the Almighty linked much of the management of the affairs of the world to the movements of the stars, so management was attributed to them even though it is from God, just as a thing is named after what is adjacent to it. The intended meaning of the managers are the angels, so their management is their descent with what is lawful and unlawful and its details, as stated by Ibn Abbas, Qatadah, and others. It is up to God, the Most High, but when the angels descended with it, it was called that, as God, the Almighty, said: The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down (Ash-Shu’ara’: 193), Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and God, the Almighty, is the One who sent it down. Ata’ narrated from Ibn Abbas: Those who manage affairs: the angels are entrusted with managing the affairs of the earth in terms of winds, rain, and other things. Abdur-Rahman ibn Sabat said: The management of worldly affairs is down to four: Gabriel, Michael, the Angel of Death, whose name is Azza’il, and Israfil. Gabriel is entrusted with the winds and the armies, Michael is entrusted with rain and plants, the Angel of Death is entrusted with taking souls on land and sea, and Israfil descends with the matter, and none of the angels is closer than Israfil, between him and the Throne a distance of five hundred years. It was said: that is, they were entrusted with matters that God made known to them. From the beginning of the Surah until here, there is an oath by which God has sworn, and God has the right to swear by whatever He wishes of His creation, and we do not have that right except through Him, the Almighty. The answer to the oath is implied, as if he said: And the ones who pull out and such and such, you will be resurrected and you will be held accountable. It is implied so that the listeners will know the meaning, said Al-Farra’. This is indicated by the statement of God the Almighty: When we are decayed bones Don’t you see that it is like the answer to their al-Nas 114:When we are decayed bones? So He sufficed with saying: When we are decayed bones? Some people said: The oath was based on His statement: Indeed in that is a lesson for whoever fears. This is the preferred choice of Al-Tirmidhi ibn Ali. That is, in what you have narrated of the mention of the Day of Resurrection and the mention of Moses and Pharaoh is a lesson for whoever fears. But the oath was based on what is mentioned in the surah that is clearly and prominently mentioned, which is more appropriate and more established than bringing something that is not mentioned, according to what Ibn Al-Anbari said: This is ugly because the speech between them was long. It was said: The answer to the oath is Has there reached you the story of Moses? because the meaning has reached you.
79:6: The Almighty said: The Day the Earthquake shakes meaning the Day it shakes, so the lam was deleted. It was also said that there is an inversion of the verb to shake, and that the inversion is the Day the Earthquake shakes followed by the One Who Follows It and the One Who Snatches, drowning. Al-Sijistani said: It is possible that this is an inversion of the verb to shake, as if he said: Then they are upon the Watchful One and the One Who Snatches al-Sahira wa al-Nazi'at. Ibn al-Anbari said: This is a mistake, because the letter fa does not open a sentence, and the first is the correct view. It was also said that the oath was based on the fact that the hearts of the people of Hell will dry up and their eyes will be humbled, so the word the Day the Earthquake shakes was in the accusative case according to this meaning, but it was not used accordingly. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, trembling hearts on the Day it shakes. It was also said that it was in the accusative case due to the omission of remember. And shakes means disturbed. And the shaking means the disturbed. This is what Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said. He said: It is the earth, and the following instant. Mujahid said: The shaking is the earthquake.
79:7: The Almighty said: Then it will be followed by the subsequent blast - the shout. Also narrated from him, Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, and Qatadah: They are the two blasts, meaning the two trumpets. The first will kill everything, by God's permission, and the second will revive everything, by God's permission. "It was narrated in the hadith that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: (Between them are forty years)" Mujahid also said: The subsequent blast is when the sky splits open and the earth and mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing, and that is after the earthquake. It was said: (The trembling shakes the earth, and the subsequent blast is another earthquake that annihilates the earths). And God knows best. A sufficient explanation of the blowing of the trumpet has already been given at the end of An-Naml. The root of trembling is movement. God Almighty said: On the Day the earth shakes. Trembling here is not only from movement, but from their saying: The thunder trembled, trembling and shaking: meaning it made sound and movement apparent. From this the arajīf were named, due to the disturbance of sounds in them, and the people’s abundance in them. He said: O son of blame, you threaten me with rumours, while in rumours you find meanness and cowardice. On the authority of Abi bin Kaab: When a quarter of the night had passed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would stand up and say: “O people, remember God. The first earthquake has come, followed by the second. Death has come with what it contains.”
79:8: The Almighty said: The hearts on that Day will be trembling meaning fearful and anxious. This was said by Ibn Abbas and is agreed upon by the majority of the musafirs. Al-Suddi said: Moving from their places. Similar to when the hearts are at the throats. (Ghafir 40:18) Al-Mu'arraj said: A widespread trembling, running, not still. Al-Mubarrad said: Agitated. The meanings are close, and what is meant are the hearts of the unbelievers. It is said: The heart trembles or it flutters if it beats, just as it is said: It was forced or "it was struck... They changed after a long, painful breath And (hearts) is the subject and (trembling) is its description.
79:9: The Almighty’s statement: And their eyes will be humbled is its predicate, like His statement: And a believing slave is better than a polytheist (al-Baqarah 2:221). The meaning of humbled is broken and humiliated by the horror of what they see. Similar to it is: Their eyes will be humbled, humiliation will cover them (al-Qalam 68:43). The meaning is the eyes of their owners, so the complement was omitted.
79:10: The Almighty says: They say, ‘Shall we indeed be returned to the grave?’ That is, these deniers who deny the resurrection, when it is said to them that you will be resurrected, say, denying and amazed: Shall we indeed be returned after our death to the beginning of the matter, so that we may return alive as we were before death? It is like their saying, Shall we indeed be resurrected as a new creation? (al-Isra’ 17:49). It is said: So-and-so returned in his grave, or on his grave, meaning he returned from where he came, as said by Qatada. Ibn al-A’rabi recited: Excavating on baldness and gray hair, God forbid, is such foolishness and shame He says: Shall I return to what I was like in my youth of flirting and youth after I have grown old and gone bald! It is said: He returned on his hoof: meaning the path he came from. And their saying in the proverb: The money is at the hoof. Jacob said: meaning at the first word. And it is said: The people met and fought at the hoof. Meaning at the first time they met. And it was said: The hasty hoof, meaning shall we be returned to the world and become alive as we were? The poet said: I swear I will not forget you, so know that until people return to the grave It was said: Al-Hafir is the land in which their graves are dug, so it means the dug place, like the saying of God the Almighty: Gushing water (Al-Tariq: 6) and A pleasant life (al-Haqqah 69:21). The meaning is: Are we really going to be returned to our graves alive? This was said by Mujahid, Al-Khalil, and Al-Farra. It was also said: The land was called Al-Hafir because it is the resting place of hooves, just as the foot was called Ard land because it is on the ground. The meaning is: Are we really going to return to the earth after death so that we can walk on our feet? Ibn Zayd said: Al-Hafir is the Fire. He also read: That then is a losing return. Muqatil and Zayd ibn Aslam said: It is one of the names of Hell. Ibn Abbas said: Al-Hafir in Arabic speech means the world. Abu Haywah read: Al-Hofra without an alif, shortened from Al-Hafir. It was also said that Al-Hofra is the land that stinks with the bodies of its dead, from their saying: His teeth dug if dirt has covered it from the outside and inside. It is said: There are holes in his teeth, it has been dug, it is dug, like it is broken, it is broken, if its roots are corrupted. Banu Asad say: In his teeth with the movement. And it has been dug, like he was tired, it is the worse of the two languages, as stated in Al-Sahah.
79:11: The Almighty said: Will we then be decayed bones? That is, worn out and crumbled. It is said: the bone decayed with a kasra, meaning it wore out and crumbled, it is said: decayed bones. This is how the majority of the people of Medina, Mecca, Syria and Basra read it. Abu Ubaid chose it, because the traces that mention bones, we looked at them and saw decay, not decay. Abu Amr, his son Abdullah, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masoud, Ibn Az-Zubayr, Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr read (بَرة) with an alif, and Al-Farra', Al-Tabari and Abu Muadh Al-Nahwi chose it, because it agrees with the beginnings of the verses. In As-Sahah: The decaying bone is one that has gas entering and then exiting, and it has a decay. It is said: there is no decay in it, meaning there is no one in it. Ya'qub narrated it from Al-Bahili. Abu Amr Ibn Al-Ala' said: The decaying bone is the one that has not yet decayed, meaning it has not worn out and is bound to decay. It is also said: the decaying bone and the hollow one. It was said: They are two words with the same meaning. Likewise, the Arabs say: Nakra the thing is gnawed, so it is Nakra the gnawing and Nakhaar the gnawing, like their saying: Ta’ama greed, so it is Ta’ama greed, Ta’ama he is greedy, Hadhir he is cautious, “Bukhal sheer, Bukhal he is stingy, Fara he is generous, the poet said: The old man who was obese and crawling on a crooked path with nodules remained there. Awj: means legs. In some interpretations: Nakhra with an alif: worn out, and Nakhra: the wind gnaws at it, meaning it passes through it, the opposite of the first. He said: After I became rotten bones Some of them said: An-Nakhra is the one whose edges were eaten away and only the middle remained. An-Nakhra is the one that was completely rotten. Mujahid said: An-Nahra means ruined, as God the Almighty said: Bones and remains. An-Nakhra ar-Rih with Dammah means the severity of its blowing. An-Nakhra is also an-Nakhra, an example of the Hamza: the tip of the nose of a horse, donkey, or pig. It is said: He smashed his Nakhra, meaning his nose.
79:12: God the Almighty said: "They will say, 'That then is a losing return.'" That is, a failed return, false and invalid, that is, it is not depressing. This was said by Al-Hasan and others. Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: (Losing) for whoever denied it. It was also said: That is, it is a losing return. The meaning is that its people are losers, as it is said: a profitable trade, meaning that its owner profits. And nothing is more losing than a return that entails the destination of Hellfire. Qatada and Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: That is, if we return alive after death, we will be gathered in Hellfire. They only said this because they threatened us with Hellfire. And "karr" means returning. It is said: "karra, and karr" itself. It is transitive and intransitive. And "karra means the time, and the plural is karat".
79:13: The Almighty said: It will be only a single blast. The Almighty mentioned the ease of resurrection for him, saying: (It will be only a single blast.) Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A single blast.
79:14: The Almighty said: Then they meaning all of creation will be in the Saahirah meaning on the face of the earth, after they had been in its belly. Al-Farra’ said: It was given this name because animals sleep and stay awake in it. The Arabs call the desert and the face of the earth Saahirah, meaning one with wakefulness, because one stays awake in it out of fear of it, so he described it with a description of what is in it. Ibn Abbas and the commentators provided evidence for this with the words of Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt: And in it is the meat of a watchful woman and the sea, and what they say about it is permanent for them. And he said to his horse on the last day of Dhi Qar: The oldest argument is that it is bracelets, and do not be afraid of a rare man Your palace is the dust of the watchful one, then you return to the grave After I became rotten bones In Sahih. It is said: As-Sahour is the shade of the Saharah, which is the face of the earth. And from this is the saying of God Almighty: And then they are about to face As-Saharah, Abu Kabir Al-Hudhali said: They wear a nightgown, all of them dark and gloomy. It is said: Al-Sahour is like the cover of the moon that it enters when it is eclipsed. They recited the words of Umayyah ibn Abi Al-Salt: The moon and the sun are shining And they recited to another, describing a woman: It is as if it is a poisonous vein when struck, or a hole that came out of the belly of a Sahour. He wants the moon apartment. It was said: As-Sahira: is the white land. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A land of silver, God, the Most High, was never disobeyed over it. He created it at that time. It was said: A land that God renewed on the Day of Resurrection. It was said: As-Sahira is the name of the seventh land that God, the Most High, will bring and hold the creation accountable for it, and that will be when the land is replaced by another land. Al-Thawri said: As-Sahira: The land of Ash-Sham. Wahb ibn Munabbih: The mountain of Jerusalem. Uthman ibn Abi Al-Atika: It is the name of a specific place on the land in Ash-Sham, and it is the area between Mount Arija and Mount Hassan, God extends it as He wills. Qatada: It is Hell, meaning these disbelievers are in Hell. It was called As-Sahira because they will not sleep on it at that time. It was said: As-Sahira: means the desert on the edge of Hell, meaning they will stop at the land of Resurrection, and wakefulness will last then. It is said: Al-Sahira: the flat white land. It was named thus because the mirage flows in it, from their saying: a sleepy eye: running water, and its opposite: asleep. Al-Ash’ath bin Qais said: And I am awake, the mirage is shining, covering its regions. I came to it veiled. Or because its traveler does not sleep for fear of death.
