79:15: The Almighty said: Has there come to you the story of Moses? * When his Lord called to him in the sacred valley of Tuwa? That is, the story of Moses has come to you and reached you. This is a consolation for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. That is, Pharaoh was stronger than the disbelievers of your time, then we took him, and so are they. It was said that (Has) means (What), that is, what has not come to you, but I have informed you of it, for in it is a lesson for those who fear. The story of Moses and Pharaoh has come before in more than one place, but what is sufficient is sufficient.
79:16: There are three readings for (Tawa): Ibn Muhaisin, Ibn Amir, and the Kufians read (Tawa) with a tanween, and Abu Ubaid chose it due to the lightness of the name. The rest read it without a tanween, because it is modified like Umar and Qatham. Al-Farra’ said: Tawa is a valley between Madinah and Egypt. He said: It is modified from Taw, as Umar modified it from Amir. Al-Hasan and Ikrimah read (Tawa) with a kasra on the ta’, and it was narrated from Abu Amr, with the meaning of the sacred time after time, said Al-Zajjaj, and he recited: O censurers, the blame is not for its essence, for I have been folded from your hesitant error That is, he blamed me repeatedly. It was said: The damma and kasra of the taa are two dialects, and the discussion of this has already been mentioned in Ta-Ha.
79:17: The Almighty said: Go to Pharaoh meaning his Lord called him, but it was omitted because calling is a statement, so it was as if his Lord said to him, Go to Pharaoh. "He has transgressed" meaning he exceeded the limit in disobedience. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: Pharaoh was a barbarian from Hamdan. It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid, who said: He was from the people of Istakhr. It was also narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: He was from the people of Isfahan, and he was called Dhu Dhafar, and his height was four spans.
79:18: God Almighty said: Then say, ‘Would you like to be purified?’ That is, submit and be cleansed of sins. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Would you like to testify that there is no god but God?
79:19: God Almighty says: And I guide you to your Lord meaning I direct you to obey your Lord so you fear That is, you fear Him and are pious to Him. Nafi’ and Ibn Kathir read it with emphasis on the zay, assimilating the ta’ into the zay because its root is tatazakka. The rest read it with a light zay meaning you drop the ta’. Abu Amr said: Tazakka with emphasis means you give charity, and Tazakka means you can be pure and faithful. He only called Pharaoh to be pure and faithful. He said: This is why we chose to lighten it. Sakhr ibn Juwayriyah said: When God sent Moses to Pharaoh, He said to him: Go to Pharaoh until the verse And I will guide you to your Lord so that you may fear Him, but he would not do so. He said: O Lord, how can I go to him when you know that he will not do so? So God revealed to him: Go to what I have commanded you to do, for in the heaven there are twelve thousand angels seeking knowledge of destiny, but they have not attained it nor comprehended it.
79:20: The Almighty says: Then he showed him the greatest sign meaning the greatest mark, which is the miracle. It was also said: the staff. It was also said: the white hand shining like the sun. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The greatest sign, he said: the staff. Al-Hasan: his hand and staff. It was also said: the splitting of the sea. It was also said: the sign: a reference to all of his signs and miracles.
79:21: God Almighty says: So he lied meaning the Prophet of God, Moses, lied, and disobeyed meaning he disobeyed his Lord, the Almighty and Majestic.
79:22: The Almighty says: Then he turned away, running away meaning he turned away, turning away from faith. He turned away means he spread corruption on earth. It was also said: he worked to spite Moses. It was also said: He turned away, running away fleeing from the snake.
79:23: The Almighty says: So he gathered meaning he gathered his companions to prevent him from it. It was also said: he gathered his soldiers to fight and battle, and the magicians to oppose. It was also said: he gathered the people to attend. So he called meaning he said to them in a loud voice.
79:24: The Almighty said: I am your highest lord meaning you have no lord above me. It is narrated that Satan appeared to Pharaoh in the form of a human in the bathhouse in Egypt, but Pharaoh denied him, so Satan said to him: Woe to you! Don't you know me? He said: No. He said: How did you create me? Didn't you say I am your highest lord? Al-Tha'labi mentioned this in his book Al-Ara'is. Ata' said: He had made small idols for them and ordered them to worship them, so he said I am the lord of your idols. It was also said that he meant the leaders and masters; he is their lord, and those are the lords of the common folk. It was also said that there is an inversion in the speech, He called out and he was gathered, because the call comes before the gathering.
79:25: The Almighty said: So God seized him with the punishment of the Hereafter and the first meaning the punishment of His statement: I have not known of any god for you other than Me (al-Qasas 28:38) and His statement after that: (I am your Lord, the Most High) was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Ikrimah. And there were forty years between the two words, said Ibn Abbas. The meaning is: He gave him respite in the first, then He seized him in the Hereafter, and punished him with His two words. It was said: The punishment of the first is that He drowned him, and the punishment of the Hereafter is the punishment in the Hereafter. Qatada and others said this. Mujahid said: It is the punishment of the beginning of his life and the end. It was said: The Hereafter is His statement: (I am your Lord, the Most High) and the first is his denial of Moses. Also from Qatada. (punishment) is in the accusative case as a confirmed verbal noun according to Al-Zajjaj, because the meaning of God seized him is: God punished him, so He made punishment a source of its meaning, not of its wording. It was said: It is in the accusative case by removing the letter of description, meaning for the punishment. Nakal: is the name given to that which is made a deterrent to others, i.e. a punishment for them so that they may consider it. It is said: Nakal someone to someone: if he inflicted a severe punishment on him. The word comes from the word refusal, and from this comes the refusal to take an oath, and Nakal is the chain. This has been mentioned in Surat Al-Muzzammil. Praise be to God.
79:26: God Almighty says: Indeed in that is a lesson meaning a consideration and an admonition. For whoever fears meaning fears God Almighty.
79:27: The Almighty's statement: Are you more difficult to create? He means the people of Mecca, meaning that your creation after death is more difficult in your estimation, or the heaven. So whoever has power over the heaven is also able to restore it, as in the statement of the Almighty: The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind. (Ghafir 40:57) and His statement: Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them? (Ya-Sin 36:81) So the meaning of this statement is a rebuke and a rebuke. Then He described the heaven and said: He built it, meaning He raised it above you like a building. He raised its ceiling, meaning He raised its roof in the air. It is said: He raised something, meaning He raised it above you like a building.
79:28: The Almighty said: He raised its ceiling meaning he raised its roof in the air. It is said: He raised something in the air and He raised something means he ascended. Al-Farra’ said: Everything that carries something from a building or other things is a samak. A high building and a high hump are also called masmuk high. The masmukat heavy are the heavens. It is also said: Your name is in the clouds meaning ascend the degree. The Almighty says, Then He proportioned it meaning He created it in a level creation, with no irregularities, cracks, or fractures.
79:29: The Almighty said: And He covered its night meaning He made it dark. He covered the night and God covered it, like you say: the night became dark and God was dark. It is also said: He covered the night itself, and God covered it, just as it is said: the night became dark, and God made it dark. Darkness and twilight: darkness. A blind man is someone who is blind, or someone similar to him. He has been covered, and the woman is covered. It is said: a dark night, a dark night, and a dark desert that cannot be found. Al-A'sha said: And at night, the wilderness is covered by the sound of its birds, which comforts me. Al-A'sha also said: I hamstrung my camel for them, and I deceived them with my cowardice. Meaning, He overwhelmed them with their night, because it covered them with its darkness. He added the night to the sky because night occurs with the setting of the sun, and the sun is added to the sky. It is also said: the stars of the night, because they appear at night. And brought forth its daylight means He made its daylight, light, and sun prominent. He added the daylight to the sky just as he added the night to it, because in it is the cause of darkness and light, which is the setting and rising of the sun.
79:30: The Almighty says: And after that He spread out the earth meaning He extended it. This indicates that the earth comes after the sky. This has already been discussed at the beginning of (Al-Baqarah) when the Almighty says: "It is He who created for you all that is on the earth. Then He directed Himself to the heaven" (al-Baqarah 2:29) in full. The Arabs say: I spread something out, I spread it out. The ostrich's nest is called adhi because it is spread out on the face of the earth. Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt said: And He spread out the creation in it when He spread it out, so they are its inhabitants until the call is made. Al-Mubarrad recited: He rolled it out, and when he saw it settled on the water, he set mountains on it. It was said: He leveled it, and from this is the saying of Zaid bin Amr: I surrendered my face to the one to whom the earth surrendered, carrying heavy rocks. He rolled it out, and when it was level, He strengthened it with His hands and fixed mountains on it. On the authority of Ibn Abbas: God created the Kaaba and placed it on the water on four corners, a thousand years before He created the world, then the earth was spread out from under the House. Some scholars mentioned that (after) is in place of (with) as if he said: and the earth in addition to that He spread out, as God Almighty said: After that he became a wicked man (al-Qalam 68:13). And from this is their saying: You are foolish and after this you are ill-mannered. The poet said: I told her to leave me to you, for I am forbidden, and after that I am intelligent. That is, he is intelligent. It was said: After means before, like the Almighty’s saying: And We had already written in the Psalms after the remembrance (Al-Anbiya’: 105), meaning before the Criterion. Abu Khurash Al-Hudhali said: I thanked my God after Urwa, when Kharash left, and some evil is less than others. They claimed that Khurash escaped before Urwa. It was said: (Dahaa) he plowed and split it. Ibn Zayd said this. It was also said: Dahaa made it easy for sustenance. The meanings are close. The general reading is (and the earth) in the accusative case, meaning he spread the earth. Al-Hasan and Amr ibn Maymun read (and the earth) in the nominative case, as a starting point, because of the return of the ha’. It is said: Daha yadhuwa dahawa and Daha yadhha dahya, like their saying: taghā yaghā yaghtuw, and taghā yaghtaghā, and maha yamhu yamhi, and laha al-ud yalha yalhu, so whoever says yadhu says dahuwat, and whoever says yadhi says dahaytu.
79:31: The Almighty says: He brought forth from it meaning He brought forth from the earth its water meaning the gushing springs of water. And its pasture meaning the vegetation that is grazed. Al-Qutbi said: He indicated with two things everything that He brought forth from the earth as sustenance and provision for mankind from grass, trees, grain, dates, straw, firewood, clothing, fire, and salt, because fire comes from sticks and salt comes from water.
79:32: The Almighty's saying: And the mountains He has fixed firmly. The general reading is (and the mountains) in the accusative case, meaning and He fixed the mountains (He fixed them firmly) meaning: He fixed them in it as pegs for it. Al-Hasan, Amr ibn Maymun, Amr ibn Ubayd, and Nasr ibn Asim read (and the mountains) in the nominative case as the subject. It is said: Why is the conjunction not inserted before (He brought out)? It is said: It is a state with the omission of qad, like the Almighty's saying: {Their chests have become constricted} (al-Nisa 4:90).
79:33: The Almighty says: For your enjoyment meaning benefit for you. And for your livestock such as camels, cows, and sheep. For your enjoyment is in the accusative case as a source without the wording, because the meaning of He brought forth from it its water and its pasture is to enjoy thereby. It was also said: It is in the accusative case by dropping the letter of description, meaning that you may enjoy it as enjoyment.
79:34: The Almighty said: And when the Greatest Calamity comes meaning the greatest disaster, which is the second blast, which will be accompanied by the resurrection, as Ibn Abbas said in the narration of Al-Dahhak from him, and it is the saying of Al-Hasan. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas also and Al-Dahhak: It is the Resurrection, and it was called that because it covers everything, so it encompasses everything other than it due to the enormity of its terror, meaning it accepts it. And in their proverbs: The valley ran and weaned on the villages Al-Mubarrad: The catastrophe among the Arabs is an unstoppable calamity. I think it was derived from their saying: The horse tamed tamim when it ran exhaustedly, and the water tamed when it filled the entire river. Others: It is derived from the torrent tamed the pool, meaning it buried it. Tam means burying and rising. Al-Qasim bin Al-Walid Al-Hamadani said: The greatest catastrophe is when the people of Paradise are led to Paradise and the people of Hell to Hell. This is the meaning of Mujahid’s statement. Sufyan said: It is the hour when the people of Hell are handed over to the guards. That is, the catastrophe that has overwhelmed and become great. He said: Some love blinds and deafens, and so does hatred, which is more severe and deafening.
79:35: God Almighty says: The Day when man will remember what he strove for, meaning what good or evil he did.
79:36: The Almighty says, And Hellfire will come into view meaning, it will appear. For whoever sees Ibn Abbas said: It will be uncovered so that everyone with sight will see it blazing. It was also said that what is meant is the disbeliever because he is the one who sees Hellfire with all the types of torment in it. It was also said that the believer will see it to know the extent of the blessing, and the disbeliever will burn in the Hellfire. The answer to the phrase And when the disaster comes is omitted, meaning, when the disaster comes, the people of Hellfire will enter Hellfire and the people of Paradise will enter Paradise. Malik ibn Dinar read: And Hellfire will come into view Al-Baqarah 2:17. Ikrimah and others read: For whoever you see Al-Baqarah 2:17, meaning, for whoever you see Hellfire, or for whoever you see, O Muhammad. The addressee is to him, peace be upon him, and what is meant by it is the people.
79:37: The Almighty says: But as for him who transgressed * and preferred the life of this world meaning, he exceeded the limit in disobedience. It was said that this verse was revealed regarding An-Nadr and his son Al-Harith, and it is general for every disbeliever who prefers the life of this world over the Hereafter. It was narrated on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer who said: Whoever makes three types of food has transgressed.
79:38: And he preferred the life of this world. Juwaybir narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak that he said: Hudhayfah said: What I fear most for this nation is that they will prefer what they see over what they know. And it is narrated that he found in the books: God, the Most High, said: (No servant of Mine prefers his worldly life over his afterlife, except that I spread out his worries and his loss upon him, and then I do not care in which of them he perishes).
79:39: The Almighty says: Indeed, Hellfire will be his refuge. That is, his refuge. The alif and lam replace the ha.
79:40: The Almighty says: But as for he who feared the position of his Lord, meaning he was wary of his standing before his Lord. Al-Rabi' said: His standing will be on the Day of Judgment. Qatadah used to say: God, the Almighty, has a position that the believers fear. Mujahid said: It is his fear of God, the Almighty, in this world when he commits a sin, so he refrains. Similar to this is: And for he who feared the position of his Lord are two Gardens. (Al-Rahman: 46) And he restrained the soul from desire, meaning he restrained it from sins and forbidden acts. Sahl said: Abandoning desire is the key to Paradise, based on the Almighty's saying: But as for he who feared the position of his Lord and restrained the soul from desire, Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: You are in a time when desire leads the truth, and there will come a time when desire leads the truth, so we seek refuge in God from that time.
79:41: God Almighty says: Indeed, Paradise is the refuge meaning the home. The two verses were revealed about Mus'ab ibn 'Umair and his brother 'Amir ibn 'Umair. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: "As for the one who transgressed, he is the brother of Mus'ab bin Umair, who was taken prisoner on the day of Badr. The Ansar took him prisoner and said, 'Who are you?' He said, 'I am the brother of Mus'ab bin Umair.' So they did not tie him up tightly, but they honored him and accommodated him with them. When morning came, they told Mus'ab bin Umair his story: 'He is not my brother. Tie up your prisoner, for his mother is the richest and most ornamented of the people of al-Batha'.' So they tied him up until his mother sent for his ransom. 'As for he who feared standing before his Lord,' Mus'ab bin Umair protected the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with his own life on the day of Uhud when the people dispersed from him, until the arrows penetrated his body. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw him covered in his blood, he said, 'I seek reward from God for you.' He said to his companions: 'I saw him wearing two cloaks whose value you did not know, and the straps of his sandals were of gold.'" It was said that Mus'ab bin Umair killed his brother Amir on the day of Badr. It was also narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: This verse was revealed about two men: Abu Jahl bin Hisham Al-Makhzumi and Mus'ab bin Umair Al-Abdari. Al-Suddi said: This verse, But he who feared standing before his Lord, was revealed about Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq may God be pleased with him. Abu Bakr had a slave who used to bring him food, and he used to ask him where he got it from. One day they brought him food but he did not ask him and ate it. His slave said to him, Why don't you ask me today? He said, I forgot, so where did you get this food from? He said, I performed soothsaying for some people during the pre-Islamic era and they gave it to me. He vomited it up immediately and said, O Lord, whatever remains in his veins is what You have held back. Then this verse, But he who feared standing before his Lord, was revealed. Al-Kalbi said, It was revealed about someone who intended to commit a sin but was able to do so in private, but then abandoned it out of fear of God. A similar narration was narrated from Ibn Abbas. Meaning, someone who feared standing before God when committing a sin, so he refrained from it. And God knows best. God Almighty said: “They ask you about the Hour: when will it come?” Ibn Abbas said: The polytheists of Mecca asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when the Hour would be, mockingly, so God Almighty revealed the verse.
79:43: Urwah ibn al-Zubayr said regarding the Almighty’s statement: What do you have to do with its remembrance? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, kept asking about the Hour until this verse was revealed: To your Lord is its destination.
79:44: Until this verse was revealed: To your Lord is its terminus and the meaning of (its anchorage) is its standing. Al-Farra’ said: Its anchorage is its standing like the anchorage of a ship. Abu Ubaidah said: Meaning its terminus, and the anchorage of a ship is where it ends. This is the saying of Ibn Abbas. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas: When is its time? The meaning is close. The explanation of that has already been mentioned in (Al-A’raf). “And on the authority of Al-Hasan that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: (The Hour will not come except with anger that angers your Lord.) “. (What do you have to do with its remembrance?) That is, what do you have to do with the remembrance of the Day of Resurrection and the questioning about it, O Muhammad? You are not to ask about it. This is the meaning of what Al-Zuhri narrated on the authority of Urwah ibn Al-Zubayr, who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) kept asking about the Hour until the following verse was revealed: “What is the matter with you regarding its remembrance? To your Lord is its limit.” That is, the limit of its knowledge. So it is as if, when they kept at him, he asked God to inform him of that, but he was told: Do not ask, for you have nothing to do with that. It is possible that it was a denial of the polytheists’ questioning him, that is, what is the matter with you regarding that, that they ask you to explain it, and you are not among those who know it. Its meaning was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Remembrance means remembrance. To your Lord is its limit. That is, the limit of its knowledge, for no one else has knowledge of the Hour. It is like the Almighty’s saying: Say, ‘The knowledge thereof is only with my Lord.’ (al-A’raf 7:187) and His saying: Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour. (Luqman 31:34)
79:45: The Almighty says: You are only a warner of him who fears it. That is, one who is frightened. The warning is specific to those who fear, because they are the ones who benefit from it, if it is a warner for every accountable person. It is like His Almighty saying: You can only warn him who follows the message and fears the Most Merciful unseen. (Ya-Sin 36:11). The common reading of the word is warner with an addition without a tanween, seeking to lighten the meaning. Otherwise, its original form is tanween because it refers to the future, and it is not given a tanween in the past tense. Al-Farra' said: It is permissible to give a tanween or leave it, like His Almighty saying: delivering His command (al-Talaq 65:3) and delivering His command and weaken the plot of the disbelievers (al-Anfal 8:18) and weaken the plot of the disbelievers. The tanween is the original form, and Abu Ja'far, Shaiba, Al-A'raj, Ibn Muhaysin, Hamid, and Ayyash from Abu Amr read it with warner with a tanween, and it is in the accusative case, and the meaning is accusative, Only he who fears the Hour will benefit from your warning. Abu Ali said: It is permissible for the addition to be for the past tense, such as I struck Zayd yesterday, because he had already given the warning. The verse is a response to those who said: The conditions of the afterlife are not perceptible, but rather they are the comfort of the soul or its pain without sensation.
79:46: The Almighty said: It will be as if, on the Day they see it meaning the disbelievers see the Hour, they had not remained meaning in their worldly life, except for an evening meaning the length of an evening or its morning meaning or the length of the morning that follows that evening, and what is meant is the reduction of the duration of this worldly life, as the Almighty said: They had not remained except for an hour of a day (Yunus 10:45). Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It will be as if, on the Day they see it, they had not remained except for one day. And it was said: They had not remained in their graves except for an evening or its morning, and that is because they shortened the duration of their remaining in the graves because of what they witnessed of the horror. Al-Farra' said: The speaker says: Does the evening have a morning? The word duha refers to the beginning of the day, but duha is added to the evening, which is the day on which, according to the custom of the Arabs, they say: I will come to you in the morning or its evening, and I will come to you in the evening or its morning. So the evening means the end of the day, and the morning means the beginning of the day. He said: And some of the Banu Uqayl recited to me: We became full in her house, barren, and hostile to the ends of her day Crescent Eve or its secrets He meant: the eve of the crescent, or the secrets of the evening, so it is more intense than I will come to you in the morning or its evening.
80:1: Meccan according to everyone, and it has forty-one verses. There are six issues: The Almighty said: He frowned meaning he frowned at him. It is said: He frowned and He frowned and it has been mentioned before. And he turned away meaning he turned away from him.
80:2: God the Almighty said: If there came to him (If) is in the accusative case because it is the object of the verb, meaning because the blind man came to him, meaning the one who does not see with his eyes. The commentators unanimously narrated that the words of some of the nobles of Quraysh who were with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and he had hoped for their conversion to Islam, then Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum came, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not want Abdullah to interrupt him, so he turned away from him, and this verse was revealed about him. Malik said: Hisham ibn Urwah told him on the authority of Urwah that he said: (He frowned and turned away) was revealed about Ibn Umm Maktum, who came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and kept saying: O Muhammad, come closer to me, and with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was a man from the leading polytheists, so the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) kept turning away from him and turning to the other, and saying: (O so-and-so, do you see anything wrong with what I am saying?) He said: No, by the dolls, I do not see anything wrong with what you are saying, so God revealed (He frowned and turned away) Al-Tirmidhi took over the chain of transmission and said: “Saeed bin Yahya bin Saeed Al-Umawi told us, my father told me, he said: This is what we presented to Hisham bin Urwa on the authority of his father on the authority of Aisha, she said: He frowned and turned away was revealed about Ibn Umm Maktum, the blind man. He came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and began to say: O Messenger of God, guide me. But with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was a man from the leaders of the polytheists. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, began to turn away from him and turn to the other man, saying: Do you see anything wrong with what I am saying? He said: No, for this is what it was revealed about. He said: This is a strange hadith. The second verse is a rebuke from God to His Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) for his turning away from and neglecting Abdullah bin Umm Maktum. It is said: Amr bin Umm Maktum, and the name of Umm Maktum is Atikah bint Amir bin Makhzum. This Amr is the son of Qais bin Zaida bin Al-Asamm, and he is the maternal cousin of Khadija may God be pleased with her. He was distracted from him by one of the great polytheists, it is said that he was Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira. Ibn Al-Arabi said: The Malikis said that he was from our uncles, and his kunya was Abu Abd Shams. Qatada said: He is Umayya bin Khalaf, and from him: Ubayy bin Khalaf. Mujahid said: They were three: Utbah and Shaybah bin Rabiah, and Ubayy bin Khalaf. He was accompanied by the leaders of Quraish: Utbah and Shaybah bin Rabiah, Abu Jahl bin Hisham, Al-Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib, Umayya bin Khalaf, and Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira, calling them to Islam, hoping that others would convert to Islam because of them. Ibn al-Arabi said: As for the statement of our scholars that it was al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, others have said that it was Umayya ibn Khalaf and al-Abbas. All of this is false and based on the ignorance of the commentators who did not investigate the religion. This is because Umayya ibn Khalaf and al-Walid were in Mecca, and Ibn Umm Maktum was in Medina. He did not attend with them, nor did they attend with him. They died as unbelievers, one of them before the migration, and the other at Badr. Umayya never intended Medina, nor did he attend with him alone, nor with anyone else. Third - Ibn Umm Maktum came while the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was busy with the notables of Quraysh who were present, calling them to God the Almighty. His taste of Islam had become strong, and in their Islam was the conversion of those of their people who followed them. Then Ibn Umm Maktum came, who was blind, and said: “O Messenger of God, teach me from what God has taught you.” He kept calling him repeatedly, not realizing that he was busy with something else, until dislike appeared on the face of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) for interrupting him. He said to himself: These people say that his followers are only the blind, the common people, and the slaves. So he frowned and turned away from him. Then the verse was revealed. Ath-Thawri said: “After that, whenever the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw Ibn Umm Maktum, he would spread out his cloak for him and say: ‘Welcome to the one about whom my Lord has rebuked me.’” And he would say: Do you have a need? He appointed him as his deputy in Madinah during two battles that he participated in. Anas said: I saw him on the day of al-Qadisiyyah riding, wearing a coat of mail and carrying a black banner. Fourth - Our scholars said: What Ibn Umm Maktum did would have been ill-mannered if he had known that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was busy with other things and that he hoped for their conversion to Islam. However, God the Blessed and Exalted admonished him so that the hearts of the people of the Suffa would not be broken, or so that he would know that a poor believer is better than a rich one. Looking at a believer, even if he was poor, is more appropriate and worthy than the other matter, which is turning to the rich in the hope of their conversion to Islam, even though that is also a kind of benefit. Based on this, the words of God the Almighty: It is not for a prophet to have captives (al-Anfal 8:67) are understood, as mentioned above. It was said that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) only intended to win the man over, trusting in the faith that was in Ibn Umm Maktum’s heart, as he said: I keep ties with a man, but others are dearer to me than him, for fear that God might throw him on his face into the Fire. Fifth - Ibn Zayd said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, frowned at Ibn Umm Maktum and turned away from him because he had signaled to the one leading him to stop him, but Ibn Umm Maktum pushed him away and refused to speak to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, until he informed him. This was a kind of rudeness on his part. However, God revealed regarding him to his Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: He frowned and turned away, in the form of a statement about someone absent, to honor him. He did not say: I frowned and turned away.
80:3: Then he turned to him to face him to comfort him and said: And what do you know? meaning, he knows Perhaps he means Ibn Umm Maktum and the removal of the darkness of ignorance from him. It was said: The pronoun in Perhaps refers to the disbeliever, meaning that if you hope that he will be purified by Islam or remembered, then the reminder will bring him closer to accepting the truth. And what do you know that what you hope for will come to pass? Al-Hasan read ""Has the blind man come to him? with a long vowel for interrogation, so -أنis related to an omitted verb indicated byِقتس والطالى" frowning and turning away. The interpretation is: Has he come to him, he turned away from him and turned away? So one stops at this reading at "والطالى" and does not stop at it in the reading of the narration, which is the reading of the general public. Sixth - Similar to this verse in reproach is the Almighty’s statement in Surat al-An’am 6:And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening (al-An’am 6:52), and also His statement in Surat al-Kahf 18:And let not your eyes pass beyond them, desiring adornments of the worldly life (al-Kahf 18:28), and what is similar to it, and God knows best.
80:4: The Almighty’s saying, Or he remembers is admonished by what you say, and the reminder benefits him, meaning the admonition. The common reading of the word and benefits him is in the accusative case. This is the reading of As-Salami and Zar ibn Hubaysh, as an answer to perhaps, because it is not obligatory, like the Almighty’s saying: Perhaps I will reach the means (Ghafir 40:36) Then he said: Then look (al-Saffat 37:55).
80:5: God Almighty says: But he who is self-sufficient meaning he has wealth and riches.
80:6: The Almighty says: Then you attend to him meaning you expose yourself to him and listen to his words. Attending to him means listening. Al-Ra'i said: He confronted Wadah as if his forehead was a lamp in the night, and the bracelets were bent towards him. Its root is tatasaddud from sadd, which means what faces you and is in front of you. It is said: my house is saddad his house, meaning opposite it, accusative of circumstance. It is also said: from sadda, which means thirst. That is, you are exposed to it as a thirsty person is exposed to water. And musadadah means opposition. The common reading is (tasada) with a light stress, by dropping the second taa for the sake of lightness. Nafi’ and Ibn Muhaisin read it with a shaddah due to assimilation.
80:7: God Almighty says: And it is not your fault that he does not purify himself. That is, this unbeliever will not be guided or believe. You are only a messenger, and your fault is only to convey the message.
80:8: God Almighty says: But as for he who comes to you striving seeking knowledge for the sake of God.
80:9: God Almighty says: And he fears meaning he fears God.
80:10: The Almighty says: Then you are distracted from it meaning you turn your face away from it and are busy with something else. Its root is tatalaha being distracted from something, it is said: I was distracted from something meaning I was preoccupied with it. Tatalaha being distracted from it means to ignore it. Hayt I was distracted from it and tatalahay being distracted from it have the same meaning.
80:11: The Almighty says: No! It is a reminder. Kalla is a word of deterrence and admonition, meaning the matter is not as you do with both groups, meaning do not do the same after it: by turning to the rich, and turning away from the poor believer. What the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did was leave the first as mentioned above, and if it was interpreted as a minor sin, it would not be far-fetched, as stated by Al-Qushayri. Stopping at Kalla in this manner is permissible. It is also permissible to stop at talha and then begin Kalla with the meaning of truly. "It meaning the surah or verses of the Quran is a reminder" meaning an admonition and insight for creation.
80:12: The Almighty's statement: So whoever wills may remember it means take admonition from the Quran. Al-Jurjani said: (It) meaning the Quran, and the Quran is a reminder, except that since He made the Quran a reminder, He used the word reminder, and if He had mentioned it, it would have been permissible, as the Almighty said in another place: No indeed! It is a reminder (al-Muddaththir 74:54). What indicates that He meant the Quran is His statement: So whoever wills may remember it meaning he memorizes it and does not forget, and He mentioned the pronoun because reminder has the meaning of reminder and admonition. Ad-Dahhak narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the Almighty's statement: So whoever wills may remember it he said: Whoever God the Blessed and Exalted wills, He inspires.
80:13: Then he spoke about His Majesty, saying: In the scriptures is the plural of scripture, honored meaning with God, as al-Suddi said. At-Tabari said: honored in religion because of what is in it of knowledge and wisdom. It was also said: honored because it was sent down by the noble guardians, or because it was sent down from the Preserved Tablet. It was also said: honored because it was sent down from a noble one, because the honor of a book comes from the honor of its owner. It was also said that what is meant are the books of the prophets, the proof of which is: Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Abraham and Moses (al-A’la 87:18-19).
80:14: The Almighty said: Exalted of high status with God. It was also said: Exalted with Him, the Blessed and Exalted. It was also said: Exalted in the seventh heaven, as said by Yahya ibn Salam. At-Tabari: Exalted in mention and status. It was also said: Exalted from doubt and contradiction. Purified Al-Hasan said: From all filth. It was also said: Protected from being reached by the disbelievers. This is the meaning of Al-Suddi's statement. Al-Hasan also said: Purified from being sent down to the polytheists. It was also said: That is, the Qur'an was established for the angels in scrolls that they read, so it is honored, exalted, and purified.
80:15: The Almighty said: In the hands of scribes meaning the angels whom God made ambassadors between Him and His messengers. They are righteous and have not been defiled by disobedience. Abu Saleh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: It is a purifier that purifies whoever carries it. In the hands of scribes he said: scribes. Mujahid also said this. They are the honorable angels who record the deeds of the servants in the scrolls, which are books, the singular of which is: safir, like you say: katib and kataba. It is also said: safrat, meaning I wrote, and the book is the journey, and its plural is asfar. Al-Zajjaj said: The reason for calling a book a journey, with a kasra on the seen, and for a writer a safir, is that it means that he clarifies and explains something. It is said: the morning became bright, and a woman became safrat, if she uncovered her face. He said: And from this, she traveled between the people asfar safara: she reconciled between them. Al-Farra' said it, and he recited: I do not claim to be an ambassador among my people, nor do I walk deceitfully when I walk. The ambassador: the messenger and the reformer between people. The plural is ambassadors, like faqih and jurists. The copyists are called ambassadors in Hebrew. Qatada said: The scribes here are the furriers, because they read the books. Ibn Abbas also said the same. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: ((In the hands of scribes. Noble and pious)) They are the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn al-Arabi said: The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were scribes, noble and pious, but they are not meant by this verse, nor did they come close to those meant by it. Rather, it is a term specific to the angels when it is used generally, and no one else shares it with them, and no one else is included in its scope. It was narrated in Sahih on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ((The example of the one who recites the Qur’an and has memorized it is with the noble and pious scribes. The example of the one who recites it and studies it, finding it difficult, is twofold.)) Agreed upon, and the wording is from al-Bukhari.
80:16: The Almighty says: honorable meaning honorable to their Lord, as Al-Kalbi said. Al-Hasan: honorable from sins, so they raise themselves above them. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding (honorable), he said: they are honored to be with the son of Adam when he is alone with his wife, or when he defecates. It was also said: that is, they prefer the benefits of others over their own benefits. Barra is the plural of barr, like kafir unbeliever and kafirs unbelievers, sahir magicians and sahirs sorcerers, fajir wicked and fajirs wicked people. It is said: barr good and barr good if he is worthy of truthfulness, and from this, someone is barr good in his oath: meaning he is truthful, and someone is righteous to his Creator and obeys Him: meaning he obeys Him. So the meaning of (barra) is obedient to God, truthful to God in their deeds. In Surah Al-Waqi'ah, the Almighty says: ((Indeed, it is a noble Qur'an * In a protected Book * None shall touch it except the purified ones (Al-Waqi'ah: [77-79)). They are the honorable and righteous ones in this Surah.
80:17: The Almighty said: The killing of man - how ungrateful he is! Qal’at means cursing. It was also said: tormenting. And the ungrateful man. Al-A’mash narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: Whatever was in the Qur’an, The killing of man only meant the ungrateful man. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: It was revealed about Utbah bin Abi Lahab, who had believed. When By the Star was revealed, he apostatized and said: I believe in the entire Qur’an except for An-Najm. Then God, the Exalted, revealed about him: Killing man, meaning He cursed Utbah because he disbelieved in the Qur’an. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, invoked God against him, saying: O God, unleash Your dog, the lion of Ghadir against him. So he immediately set out to trade with him to Ash-Sham. When he reached Ghadir, he remembered the supplication of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he promised whoever was with him a thousand dinars if he lived in the morning. So they put him in the middle of the group, and they placed the provisions around him. While he was like that, the lion approached, and when he came close to the saddle, it pounced on him and tore him apart. His father had mourned him and wept and said: Muhammad never said anything but it happened. Abu Salih narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: How ungrateful he is! What thing do I disbelieve in? It was said that how expresses amazement, and the Arabs usually say when they are amazed by something: May God kill him, how good he is! May God disgrace him, how unjust he is. The meaning is: They were amazed at the ingratitude of man for all that we have mentioned after this. It was also said: How ungrateful he is to God and His blessings, despite his knowledge of the abundance of His kindness to him, also expressing amazement. Ibn Jurayj said: That is, how intense his disbelief is. It was also said: What is an interrogative, that is, what made him disbelieve? It is a question of rebuke. What can express amazement, or it can mean which, so it is an interrogative.
80:18: God Almighty says: From what did He create him? That is, from what did God create this unbeliever that he should be arrogant? That is, be amazed at His creation.
80:19: The Almighty says: From a sperm-drop meaning from a small, insignificant, inanimate water. He created him. So he did not make a mistake in himself?! Al-Hasan said: How can someone who came out of the urinary tract twice be arrogant? Then He proportioned him in his mother's womb. This is what Ad-Dahhak narrated from Ibn Abbas: meaning He proportioned his hands, feet, eyes, and the rest of his organs, and made him handsome and ugly, short and tall, miserable and happy. It was also said: Then He proportioned him means He made him proportioned, as He said: Have you disbelieved in He who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then proportioned you as a man? (al-Kahf 18:37) and He said: Who created you and proportioned you? (al-Infitar 82:7). It was also said: Then He proportioned him in stages, meaning from one state to another, sperm-drop then clot, until his creation was complete.
80:20: God the Almighty said: Then the way is made easy for him. Ibn Abbas said in the narration of Ata', Qatadah, As-Suddi and Muqatil: He made it easy for him to emerge from his mother's womb. Mujahid said: He made the path of good and evil easy for him, i.e. He made it clear to him. His evidence is: Indeed, We showed him the way (al-Insan 76:3) and We showed him the two paths (al-Balad 90:10). Al-Hasan, Ata' and Ibn Abbas also said it in the narration of Abu Salih from him. Mujahid also said: The path of misery and happiness. Ibn Zayd said: The path of Islam. Abu Bakr ibn Tahir said: He made easy for everyone what He created for him and decreed for him, his evidence is the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him): (Work, for everyone is facilitated for what he was created for).
80:21: The Almighty said: Then He caused him to die and buried him meaning He made a grave for him in which to be buried as an honor, and He did not make him one of those thrown on the face of the earth to be eaten by birds and wild animals, as Al-Farra' said. Abu Ubaidah said: He made a grave for him means He made a grave for him and ordered that he be buried. Abu Ubaidah said: When Umar ibn Hubayrah killed Salih ibn Abdur-Rahman, Banu Tamim said and entered upon him: We buried Salih, so he said: Take him here. He said: He made his grave and did not say his grave, because the one who buries someone is the one who buries with his own hand, as Al-A'sha said: If you lean a dead person on your throat, he will live and not be transferred to the grave. It is said: I buried the dead: if you buried him, May God bury him: meaning, He made him a place where he would be buried, and made a grave for him. The Arabs say: I cut off the camel’s tail, and May God cut it off, “I bit the bull’s horn,” and May God bite it, “I expelled so-and-so,” and May God expel him, meaning He made him an outcast.
80:22: The Almighty said: Then if He wills, He will resurrect him meaning He will bring him back to life after his death. The common reading is (ansharuhu) with an alif. Abu Haywah narrated on the authority of Nafi` and Shu`ayb ibn Abi Hamzah (shaa`a nasharuhu) without an alif, two eloquent expressions with the same meaning. It is said: God resurrected the dead and brought him forth. Al-A`sha said: Until people say from what they saw, Oh, how strange is the dead man who spreads the report.
80:23: God the Almighty says: No, he has not yet fulfilled what he was commanded to do. Mujahid and Qatadah said: He has not yet fulfilled means no one fulfills what he was commanded to do. Ibn Abbas used to say: He has not yet fulfilled what he was commanded to do He did not fulfill the covenant that he took from Adam's loins. Then it was said: No is a deterrent and a warning, meaning that the matter is not as the disbeliever says, for when the disbeliever is informed of the resurrection, he says: And if I am returned to my Lord, indeed, I will have with Him the best [reward] (Fussilat 41:50). Perhaps he says, I have fulfilled what I was commanded to do. So he said: No, he did not fulfill anything, rather he is a disbeliever in Me and in My Messenger. Al-Hasan said: Meaning, truly, he did not fulfill what he was commanded to do. The word ma in the phrase lama when is a pillar of speech, like the Almighty’s statement: Then, by mercy from God (Al Imran 3:159) and His statement: In a little while, they will surely become regretful (al-Mu’minun 23:40). Imam Ibn Fawrak said: meaning: No, God did not decree for this disbeliever what He commanded him to do regarding faith, but rather He commanded him with what He did not decree for him. Ibn al-Anbari said: Stopping at kala is ugly, but stopping at amrahu and ansharuhu is good, so kala in this sense means truly.
80:24: The Almighty says: So let man look at his food. When He, the Most High, mentioned the beginning of man's creation, He mentioned what was made easy of his provision, meaning, let him look at how God created his food. This looking is the looking of the heart with thought, meaning, let him reflect on how God created his food, which is the foundation of his life, and how He provided him with the means of livelihood, so that he may prepare with them for the Hereafter. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan and Mujahid that they said: (So let man look at his food), meaning at his entrance and exit. Ibn Abi Khaithama narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Sufyan Al-Kalabi that he said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said to me: O Dahhak, what is your food? I said: O Messenger of God! Meat and milk. He said: Then it becomes what? I said: What you know. He said: God has given an example of what the son of Adam brings forth for the world. Ubayy ibn Ka’b said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “The food of the son of Adam has been made an example of the world, even his scum and his salt. So look at what it becomes.” Abu al-Walid said: I asked Ibn Umar about a man who enters the toilet and looks at what comes out of it. He said: An angel comes to him and says: Look at what you were stingy with and what it has become.
80:25: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, We poured out the water in abundance. The general reading is (inna) with a kasra, as a resumption. The Kufians and Ruways on the authority of Ya’qub read (ana) with a fatha on the hamza, so (-ana) is in the accusative case as a translation of the food, so it is a substitute for it, as if he said: (So let man look at his food) to (ana we poured), so it is not good to stop at (his food) completely. It is said: The meaning of (ana) is where, except that it is a metaphor for the faces, and its interpretation is: from which face We poured the water. Al-Kumait said: Where and how can I cry with joy, without passion or doubt? (We poured down water in abundance): meaning rain and downpour.
80:26: The Almighty says: Then We split the earth open: meaning with plants.
80:27: God Almighty says: Then We caused to grow therein grain, meaning wheat, barley, sorghum, and everything else that is harvested and stored.
80:28: God the Almighty says: And grapes and reeds which is fodder and animal feed. Al-Hasan said: It is called thus because it is pruned, i.e. cut after appearing, time after time. Al-Qutbi and Tha'lab said: The people of Mecca call qat qadab. Ibn Abbas said: It is the fresh fruit because it is pruned from the palm tree, and because he mentioned grapes before it. He also said: It is alfalfa, which is fresh qat. Al-Khalil said: Al-Qadab is the fresh alfalfa. It was also said: with a seen, so when it dries it is qat. He said: Al-Qadab is a name given to what is pruned from the branches of the tree, to make arrows or bows from them. It is said: Qadaban, meaning everything that is pruned, like qat, leeks, and all other legumes that are cut so that their roots grow. In Al-Sahah: The qadbah and the fresh qadbah, which is asphalt in Persian, and the place where it grows is Maqsaba.
80:29: The Almighty says: And olives meaning the olive tree, and palm trees meaning palm trees.
80:30: The Almighty said: And gardens meaning orchards, the singular of which is garden. Al-Kalbi said: Everything that is surrounded by palm trees or trees is a garden, and whatever is not surrounded by is not a garden. Ghalba is its tree, it is said: a ghalba tree, and the lion is called: the most powerful, because it has a stiff neck and does not turn around except all at once. Al-Ajjaj said: I still twist my back and head on the day of separation until I became like most people A man who is most powerful among the powerful is called a man with a thick neck. The origin of the description of powerful is the necks, so it was used metaphorically. Amr ibn Ma’di Karib said: He walks with it, conquering the necks, as if they were two kohl-lined camels, full of majesty. Ghalbā’ garden: intertwined. Ghalb gardens. The grass became dense and intertwined. Ibn Abbas said: Ghalb is the plural of Aghlab and Ghalbā’, which are the thick ones. Also from him: the tall ones. Qatada and Ibn Zayd: Ghalb is the noble palm trees. Also from Ibn Zayd and Ikrimah: the large, medium-sized, and trunks. Mujahid: intertwined.
80:31: The Almighty said: And fruits meaning what people eat from the fruits of trees, such as figs, peaches, and others. And grass is what animals eat from the grass. Ibn Abbas and Al-Hasan said: Grass is everything that the earth produces, which people do not eat. What humans eat is the harvest, and from it the poet said in praise of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: He has an auspicious invitation, its fragrance is pleasant, and God causes the harvest and the father to grow. It was said: He was called Abu because he returns, that is, he takes refuge and resorts. The father and mother are two brothers. He said: Our trunk is Qais and Najd is our home, and our father is in it and the one who raised his head Ad-Dahhak said: Ab is everything that grows on the surface of the earth. Abu Razin said the same: It is the hyena. This is indicated by the statement of Ibn Abbas, who said: Ab is what the earth grows of what people and livestock eat. Also from Ibn Abbas and Ibn Abi Talha: Ab is the fresh fruits. Ad-Dahhak said: It is the fig specifically. This is also narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: The poet said: They have no pasture for livestock, and their father is able to do so. Al-Kalbi: It is every plant except fruit. It was said: Fruit is the fresh fruit, and Ab is the dry fruit. Ibrahim Al-Taymi said: Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq may God be pleased with him was asked about the interpretation of fruit Ab, so he said: Which sky will shade me, and which land will bear me if I say: In the Book of God is that which I do not know. Anas said: I heard Omar bin Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him recite this verse and then say: We have known everything, but what is Ab? Then he raised a stick that was in his hand and said: This, by God, is a stretch, and what is wrong with you, O son of Umm Omar, that you do not know what Ab is? Then he said: Follow what has been made clear to you from this Book, and leave what is not. It was narrated from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he said: (You were created from seven, and you were provided with sustenance from seven, so prostrate to God for seven). What He meant by His statement: (You were created from seven) is from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh (al-Hajj 22:5), and sustenance is from seven, and it is the statement of the Most High: {Then We caused to grow therein grain * and grapes” until His statement: and fruit, then He said: and herbage, which indicates that it is not a sustenance for the son of Adam, and that it is specific to animals. And God knows best.
80:32: The Almighty's statement: For your enjoyment is in the accusative case as a source of emphasis, because the growth of these things is a enjoyment for all living things. This is a metaphor for God's striking of resurrecting the dead from their graves, like the growth of crops after they have been buried, as has been explained in more than one place. It also includes gratitude to them for what He has bestowed upon them, and this has been mentioned in more than one place as well.
80:33: The Almighty’s saying: {And when the Deafening Blast comes} After mentioning the matter of livelihood, He mentioned the matter of the afterlife, so that they may provision themselves for it with righteous deeds, and with spending from what He has bestowed upon them. The Deafening Blast is the shout that will bring about the Resurrection, and it is the second blast. It will deafen the ears: that is, it will deafen them so that they will not hear anything except what is called for the living. Some of the commentators said: The ears will be attentive to it, from your saying: He listened to such-and-such: that is, he listened to it. And from this is the hadith: (There is no creature but that it is silent on Friday, fearing the Hour, except the jinn and mankind.) The poet said: The sun neither rises nor sets except He listens to the report as a singer listens to another singer. Some scholars said: This is taken as a matter of acceptance of the ancients. As for the language, the first statement is required. Al-Khalil said: The deafening sound is a shout that deafens the ears with its intense impact. The root of the word in the language is: a severe slap. It was said: It is taken from the word sahha with a stone: if it slaps. Al-Zajir said: My neighbor, would you like to fight like a whip? From this chapter is the saying of the Arabs: Their health is deafening and their night is the disaster, which is the calamity. Al-Tabari: I think it is from the word sakh which means to deafen someone. Ibn Al-Arabi said: The deafness that causes deafness, and it is in his ears, and this is from the wonders of eloquence, so much so that some of the young of age and young of time said: The mourner is deaf to you, even if he is the most hearing Another said: Their secret made me deaf during the days of their separation. Have you heard of a secret that causes deafness? By God, the shout of the Resurrection will deafen the ears of the world, but will hear the matters of the Hereafter.
80:34: God the Almighty says: {The Day a man will flee from his brother} meaning he will flee, that is, the Deafening Blast will come on this day when he will flee from his brother, that is, from befriending and speaking to his brother, because he will not have time for that, due to his being preoccupied with himself, as He says after that: {Each man, that Day, will have something to occupy him} meaning something that will distract him from others. It was said: He flees only out of caution from their demands of him, because of the consequences between them. It was also said: So that they do not see the hardship he is in. It was also said: Because of his work that they will not benefit him or avail him at all, as He said: {The Day when no protector will avail another at all} (al-Dukhan 44:41). Abdullah ibn Tahir Al-Abhari said: He flees from them because of their inability and lack of resourcefulness, to the One who has the power to remove those distresses and worries from him. If that had become apparent to him in this world, he would not have relied on anything except his Lord the Almighty.
80:35: God Almighty says: and his mother and his father.
80:36: The Almighty says: And his wife meaning his wife. And his children meaning his sons.
80:37: The Almighty said: For every man, that Day, will be sufficient for him. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, she heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised. I said: O Messenger of God! Will men and women all look at each other? He said: O Aisha, the matter is more serious than for them to look at each other. Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: They will be gathered barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised. A woman said: Will some of us see or look at the private parts of others? He said: O so-and-so, “Everyone among them that Day will have something to occupy him.” He said: A good and authentic hadith. The reading of the common people is with the voiced ghayn, meaning a state that distracts him from his relatives. Ibn Muhaisin and Hamid read ya’nihu with the fatha on the ya’ and an unvoiced ‘ayn, meaning his matter concerns him. Al-Qutbi said: ya’nihu means it turns him away and diverts him from his relatives. From this it is said: ’aan ‘anni wajhika meaning turn him away and divert him from the foolish person. Khafaf said: The war of Bani Malik will concern you about obscenity and ignorance in the assembly
80:38: The Almighty says, Some faces, that Day, will be radiant, meaning bright and luminous. You will know what victory and bliss they will have, and they will be the faces of the believers.
80:39: The Almighty says: Laughing meaning happy and joyful. Blessed meaning with what God has given her of honor. Ata’ Al-Khurasani said: Blessed from the length of time she has been covered in dust in the path of God, the Most High. Abu Nu’aym mentioned it. Ad-Dahhak: from the effects of ablution. Ibn Abbas: from standing in prayer at night, as narrated in the hadith: (Whoever prays a lot at night, his face will be beautiful during the day) It is said: The morning has dawned when it has become bright.
80:40: God Almighty says: And faces that Day will be covered with dust meaning dust and smoke.
80:41: The Almighty said: It will overwhelm it meaning it will be covered by a darkness meaning an eclipse and blackness. This is what Ibn Abbas said. And also from him: humiliation and severity. And qutr in the speech of the Arabs means dust, the plural of qutra, on the authority of Ay Ubaid, and Al Farazdaq recited: Crowned with the king's robe, followed by waves above which you can see the banners and flags In the hadith: When the animals turn to dust on the Day of Resurrection, that dust will be turned into the faces of the unbelievers. Zayd ibn Aslam said: Qatrah is what rises to the sky, and dust is what descends to the ground, and dust and dust are the same.
80:42: The Almighty's saying: Those are the disbelievers. The plural of disbeliever is al-fajr, which is the liar who slanders God the Almighty. It was also said: the immoral, it is said: he committed immorality, meaning he committed immorality, and fajr means he lied. Its root is: inclination, and al-fajr means the one who inclines. Its explanation and discussion have already passed.
81:1: It was revealed in Mecca according to all opinions. It has twenty-nine verses. In Al-Tirmidhi: On the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever would like to look at the Day of Resurrection as if he is seeing it with his own eyes, let him recite “When the sun is wrapped up,” When the sky is split open, and When the sky is split open.’ He said: This is a hasan gharib hadith. God the Almighty said: When the sun is wrapped up. Ibn Abbas said: Wrapping it up means entering it into the throne. Al-Hasan: Its light goes away. Qatada and Mujahid said it, and it was also narrated from Ibn Abbas. Saeed bin Jubair: It became uncovered. Abu Ubaidah: It was wrapped up like wrapping up a turban, it was destroyed and wiped out. Al-Rabi bin Khaitham said: (Kawrat) means he threw it, and from this: He wrapped it up so it fell down. I said: The root of takwir is to gather, taken from the verb kar turban on his head, meaning to wrap it, and gather it, so it is takwir and its light is erased, then it is thrown into the sea. And God knows best. And on the authority of Abu Salih: kuwarat means to fold it.
81:2: And when the stars are scattered meaning they fall and scatter. Abu Ubaidah said: They are scattered like an eagle when it is broken. Al-Ajjaj said, describing a falcon: I saw a space ruin and I was afraid the falcon would kill me if the falcon broke Abu Saleh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “On that Day, not a single star will remain in the sky except that it will fall to the earth, until the people of the seventh earth will be terrified by what it has suffered and what has befallen the highest,” meaning the earth. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: They will fall. That is because they are lanterns suspended between the sky and the earth by chains of light, and those chains are in the hands of angels of light. When the first blast comes, everyone on earth and in the heavens will die, and those stars will scatter and the chains will fall from the hands of the angels, because whoever was holding them has died. It is possible that their falling will erase their traces. The stars are called stars because of their appearance in the sky by their light. Ibn Abbas also said: They fell and changed, so they no longer had light because they moved from their places. The meanings are similar.
81:3: The Almighty's saying: And when the mountains are set in motion means they are uprooted from the earth and set in motion in the air. This is similar to His saying: And the Day We set the mountains in motion and you see the earth appearing as a barren plain (al-Kahf 18:47). It has been said that setting them in motion means they will change from being stones, and they will become a heap of sand, that is, liquid sand, and they will be like wool, and they will be scattered dust, and they will be a mirage, like a mirage that is nothing. And the earth will return to being a flat, smooth plain, and you will see no crookedness or unevenness in it. This has been mentioned before in more than one place, and praise be to God.
81:4: The Almighty said: And when the ten-month-old camels are idle meaning the pregnant camels that have their young in their bellies, one of which is 'Ashra', or the one that has been pregnant for ten months, then that is still her name until she gives birth, and after she gives birth also. It is the custom of the Arabs to give something by its previous name even if it has passed that, a man says to his horse when it has become sore: Bring my dowry, and bring my dowry near, naming it by its previous name, Antara said: Do not mention my dowry and what I have coveted, lest your skin be like the skin of a mangy person. He also said: She carried my dowry in her middle and carried it The she-camels were mentioned specifically because they are the most precious to the Arabs, and their owners will not neglect them except on the Day of Resurrection. This is by way of a metaphor, because on the Day of Resurrection there will not be a she-camel that is not ten years old. Rather, what was meant by it is a metaphor, that the horror of the Day of Resurrection will be such that if a man had a she-camel that he would neglect it and be preoccupied with himself. It was said that when they rise from their graves, and see each other, and see the water basins and the beasts gathered, and in them is their she-camels, which were the most precious of their wealth, they will not pay attention to them, and their affair will not concern them. The Arabs were addressed about the she-camels because most of their wealth and livelihood comes from camels. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They were neglected: their owners neglected them because they were preoccupied with themselves. Al-A’sha said: He is the giver of the hundred chosen ones, either in childbirth or as a tithe. Another said: You see a person abandoned if his wealth is little, while the house of the rich is given to him as a gift and visited. What good is the money of the visitor to the host if he sends him a sack and a tax? It is said: a ten-year-old she-camel, two ten-year-old she-camels, ten-year-old she-camels, and ten-year-old she-camels. They replace the feminine hamza with a waw. The she-camel became ten-year-old. It was also said: the ten-year-old is the cloud that is deprived of what it contains, which is water, so it does not rain. The Arabs liken the clouds to a pregnant woman. It was also said: the houses are deprived and not inhabited. It was also said: the land whose crops are deprived of ten-year-old crops is deprived and not planted. The first is more common, and most people agree with it.
81:5: God the Almighty said: And when the wild beasts are gathered together meaning gathered. Gathering means gathering. It was narrated from Al-Hasan, Qatadah and others. Ibn Abbas said: Their gathering means their death. It was narrated from him by Ikrimah. And the gathering of everything means death except for the jinn and mankind, for they will meet on the Day of Resurrection. It was also narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: Everything will be gathered, even the creeping things. Ibn Abbas said: The wild beasts will be gathered tomoral-Saff 61:meaning they will be gathered until retribution is taken from some of them against others, so retribution will be taken from the horned ones, then it will be said to them, Become dust, and they will die. This is more authentic than what Ikrimah narrated from him, and we have explained it in full in the book At-Tadhkirah, and part of it has passed in Surat Al-An'am. Meaning, if the wild beasts are in this state, then what will the children of Adam be like? It was said: What is meant by this is that despite their aversion to people today and their being scattered in the desert, they will join the people tomorrow because of the horrors of that day. Ubayy ibn Ka'b said this meaning.
81:6: God the Almighty says: And when the seas are set ablaze meaning they are filled with water. The Arabs say: I set the Cistern ablaze if you fill it, and it is set ablaze. Masjoor and sajir in the language mean full. Ar-Rabi' ibn Khaitham narrated: Sajarat means overflowed and filled. This was also said by Al-Kalbi, Muqatil, Al-Hasan, and Ad-Dahhak. Ibn Abi Zamanin said: Sajarat means filled, so some of it overflows into others, so they become one thing, and this is the meaning of what Al-Hasan said. It was also said: He sent its fresh water upon its salty water, and its salty water upon its fresh water, until it was filled. Ad-Dahhak and Mujahid narrated: Meaning it burst forth and became one sea. Al-Qushayri said: That is, God will lift the barrier mentioned in His statement: Between them is a barrier so neither of them transgresses (al-Rahman 55:20). So when that barrier is lifted, the waters of the seas will burst forth and cover the entire earth, and the seas will become one sea. It was said: It became a single sea of scalding water for the people of Hell. Also narrated by Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Ibn Hayyan: It dried up so that not a drop of its water remained. Al-Qushayri: It is from the verb sajartu tannu to heat the oven asjarruhu sajran to heat it up, and if ignition is directed at it, the moisture in it dries up, and the mountains move at that time, and the seas and the entire earth become a single carpet, by filling the place of the seas with the dust of the mountains. An-Nahhas said: The sayings may be in agreement, that it may be that the water dries up after it overflows, some of it into others, and turns into fire. I said: Then the mountains will move at that time, as Al-Qushayri mentioned, and God knows best. Ibn Zayd, Shimr, Atiyyah, Sufyan, Wahb, Ubayy, Ali ibn Abi Talib, and Ibn Abbas, in the narration of Al-Dahhak from him, said: It was lit and became fire. Ibn Abbas said: God will roll the sun, moon, and stars into the sea, then God will send upon them a violent wind that will blow it away until it becomes fire. And likewise in some of the hadith: God, the Most High, will command the sun, moon, and stars, and they will scatter into the sea, then God, the Most High, will send a violent wind that will ignite them into fire. That is the Great Fire of God, with which He will punish the disbelievers. Al-Qushayri said: It was said in interpretation of Ibn Abbas’ statement, It was lit that it was lit, that it may mean that Hell is in the depths of the seas, and now it is not lit due to the existence of this world, but when this world ends, it will be lit and all of it will become fire, and God will admit its people into it. And it may mean that there will be fire under the sea, then God will ignite the whole sea and it will become fire. And in the hadith: (The sea is fire within fire) Muawiyah bin Saeed said: The Roman Sea is in the middle of the earth, below it are wells filled with copper that will be kindled with fire on the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: The sun will be in the sea, so the sea will be fire, the sea of the sun. Then everything in these verses may have happened in this world before the Day of Resurrection and be among its signs, and it may be on the Day of Resurrection, and these verses will not happen on the Day of Resurrection. I said: It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr: One should not perform ablution with sea water because it is the bottom of Hell. Abi bin Kaab said: Six signs before the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:While the people are in their markets, the light of the sun is gone and the stars appear, so they are confused and astonished. While they are thus looking, the stars are scattered and falling. While they are thus, the mountains fall to the face of the earth, so it moves, shakes and burns, so it becomes scattered dust. Humans flee to the jinn and the jinn flee to the humans. The animals, wild animals, insects and birds mingled, and some of them swayed among others. This is what God Almighty said: And when the wild animals are gathered together. Then the jinn will say to the humans: We will bring you report. So they set out to the seas, and behold, it is a blazing fire. While they are thus, the earth cracks with a single crack to the seventh lowest earth and to the seventh highest heaven. While they are thus, a wind comes to them and kills them. It was said: The meaning of (Sajrat) is the redness of its water, until it becomes like blood, taken from their saying: Ain Sajra, meaning red. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr also read (Sajrat), describing its condition once. The rest read it with emphasis, describing its condition by repeating that from it time after time.
81:7: God Almighty said: And when souls are paired. Al-Nu’man bin Bashir said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said, And when souls are paired. He said, Every man will be paired with every people who used to do according to his deeds. Umar ibn al-Khattab said, The wicked will be paired with the wicked, and the righteous will be paired with the righteous. Ibn Abbas said, “That will be when people will be in three pairs: the foremost will be paired - meaning a class - the companions of the right will be paired, and the companions of the left will be paired.” It was also narrated from him that he said, The souls of the believers will be paired with the wide-eyed houris, and the disbeliever will be paired with the devils, and so will the hypocrites. It was also narrated from him that every type will be paired with its type of people from the people of Paradise and the people of Hellfire, so the prominent in obedience will be paired with its type, the average will be paired with its type, and the people of disobedience will be paired with its type. Pairing means pairing something with its type, and the meaning is: And when souls are paired with their type in Paradise and Hellfire. It was also said that every man will be paired with whoever he was obliged to rule or have authority over, as God the Almighty said, Gather together those who did wrong and their type 37:22, meaning their type. Ikrimah said: And when the souls are paired, the souls are paired with the bodies, i.e. they are returned to them. Al-Hasan said: Every person is linked to his own group: the Jews with the Jews, the Christians with the Christians, the Magians with the Magians, and everyone who worships something other than God is linked to one another, the hypocrites with the hypocrites, and the believers with the believers. It was said: The seducer is linked to the one who seduced him, whether Satan or human, on the basis of hatred and enmity, and the obedient is linked to the one who called him to obedience from the prophets and believers. It was said: The souls are linked to their deeds, so due to their specialization, they become like a marriage.
81:8: The Almighty said: And when the girl [who was] buried alive is asked, * For what sin was she killed? The buried alive girl is the one who was killed, and she is a female slave who is buried alive. She is called that because no dirt is thrown over her, which would burden her until she dies. From this is the Almighty’s saying: And their preservation does not burden Him (al-Baqarah 2:255), meaning it does not burden Him. Mutammam ibn Nuwayrah said: And a girl buried alive in a desert with her slave girl, blackened and not paved They used to bury their daughters alive for two reasons. One of them was that they said: The angels are the daughters of God, so they attributed the daughters to Him. The second was either for fear of poverty or captivity and enslavement. This meaning has been fully discussed in Surat An-Nahl, when God the Almighty says: Or bury him in the dust? (al-Nahl 16:59). The honorable among them refrained from this and prevented it, so much so that Al-Farazdaq boasted about it and said: And among us is he who prevented the giving of gifts, so he revived the giving of gifts, so he did not bury them alive. Meaning his grandfather Sa'sa'ah used to buy them from their fathers, then Islam came and revived seventy buried girls. Ibn Abbas said: When a woman in the pre-Islamic era became pregnant, she would dig a hole and give birth on her head. If she gave birth to a girl, she would throw her into the hole and cover her with dirt. If she gave birth to a boy, she would imprison him. From this is the saying of the rajaz poet: I named her when she was born and she dies and the grave is the guarantor of my time The dignified Zamit, and Zamit is an example of the corrupt or from Zamit, and so-and-so is the most dignified of people, meaning he is the most dignified of them, and how severe his devotion is, according to Al-Farra. Qatada said: In the Age of Ignorance, one of them would kill his daughter and feed his dog, so God rebuked them for that and threatened them with His saying: (And when the buried girl is asked).
81:9: Umar said regarding the verse, And when the girl [who was] buried alive is asked," he said: Qais bin Asim came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: O Messenger of God! I buried alive eight daughters who were my daughters during the pre-Islamic era. He said: (Then free a slave for each one of them.) He said: O Messenger of God, I am a camel owner. He said: (Then sacrifice a camel for each one of them if you wish.) And the verse, "was asked," is a question of rebuke to her killer, just as a child is asked when he hits him: Why were you hit? And what is your sin? Al-Hasan said: God wanted to rebuke her killer, because she was killed without a crime. Ibn Aslam said: For what sin was she hit? And they used to hit her. Some of the scholars mentioned regarding His statement, "was asked," that he said: It was demanded, as if he meant as one demands the blood of the murdered. He said: It is like His statement, "And the covenant of God will be questioned about" (al-Ahzab 33:15), meaning demanded.
