So it is as if she was demanded from them and they were asked, "Where are your children?!" Ad-Dahhak and Abu Ad-Dahha read on the authority of Jabir ibn Zayd and Abu Salih: And when the girl [who was] buried alive will be asked. So the girl will cling to her father and say: For what sin did you kill me?! So he will have no excuse. Ibn Abbas said this. He used to read: And when the girl [who was] buried alive will be asked. And this is how it is in Abu’s copy of the Qur’an. Ikrimah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: (The woman who kills her child will come on the Day of Resurrection with her child clinging to her breasts, covered in his blood, and he will say, O Lord, this is my mother, and this one killed me.) The first opinion is accepted by the majority, and is similar to the words of God the Almighty to Jesus: Did you say to the people? (al-Ma’idah 5:116) as a way of rebuking and reprimanding them. Likewise, the question of the buried girl is a rebuke to the one who buried her, and it is more eloquent than her question about her killing, because this is something that is not valid except for a sin. So, for what sin was that? If it becomes clear that she was not guilty, then the calamity will be greater and the proof will be established against her killer. And God knows best. It was also read with emphasis, and in it is clear evidence that the children of polytheists are not tortured, and that torture is not deserved except for a sin.
81:10: The Almighty said: And when the records are spread out meaning they are opened after they were folded, and what is meant are the records of deeds in which the angels wrote down the good and evil of their people, they are folded up with death and spread out on the Day of Resurrection, and every person will stand at his record and know what is in it, and he will say: What is this record that leaves out nothing small or great but that it has recorded it? (al-Kahf 18:49) And Marthad bin Wada'ah narrated that when the Day of Resurrection comes, the records will fly from under the Throne, and the record of the believer will fall into his hand in a high garden (al-Haqqah 69:22) until His saying: the days that have passed (al-Haqqah 69:24) and the record of the disbeliever will fall into his hand in scorching wind and scalding water until His saying: nor noble (Al-Waqi'ah: 42-44) And it was narrated on the authority of Umm Salamah, may God be pleased with her: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection barefoot and naked. I said: O Messenger of God! What about women? He said: People are busy, O Umm Salamah. I said: And what is their business? He said: Spreading out scrolls containing weights equal to the weight of an atom and weight of a mustard seed. It has already been mentioned in Surah Subhan that Abu Bakr said: Whatever you wish, then when you die you will be blessed, until when you are resurrected it will be spread out. Muqatil said: When a person dies, his scroll of deeds is folded up, and when the Day of Resurrection comes it will be spread out. It was narrated from Umar may God be pleased with him that when he would recite it he would say: To you the matter will be brought, O son of Adam. Nafi’, Ibn Amir, Asim, and Abu Amr recited Nashra published without a vowel, as Nashra once, to establish the proof. The rest read it with emphasis, with the repetition of the spreading, to exaggerate the rebuke of the sinner and to give glad tidings to the obedient. It was also said: because of the repetition of that by humans and the angels, the witnesses over him.
81:11: The Almighty said: And when the sky is scraped away: scraping means to tear off due to intense adhesion, so the sky is scraped as the skin is scraped off a ram or other animal, and scraping is a dialect for it. In Abdullah's reading: (And when the sky is scraped away), and scraped the camel scraping means you removed its skin, and you do not say you flayed it, because the Arabs do not say about a camel except I scraped it or I skinned it, and scraped means it went away, so the sky is removed from its place as a cover is removed from something. It was said: it is folded as God Almighty said: The Day We shall roll up the heaven like the rolling up of a scroll for books (al-Anbiya 21:104), so the meaning is as if it was pulled up and folded. And God knows best.
81:12: The Almighty said: And when Hellfire is set ablaze meaning it is lit and kindled for the disbelievers. And its heating was increased. It is said: the fire was set ablaze and I set it ablaze. The general reading is with a light stress on the blazing fire. Nafi', Ibn Dhakwan, and Ruways read it with a shaddah because it is lit time and time again. Qatada said: Its stoke is the wrath of God and the sins of the children of Adam. And in Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ((The Fire was lit for a thousand years until it turned red, then it was lit for a thousand years until it turned white, then it was lit for a thousand years until it turned black, so it is black and dark)) and it was narrated as an interrupted hadith.
81:13: God the Almighty says: And when Paradise is brought near meaning it draws near and is brought close to the righteous. Al-Hasan said: They draw near to it, not that it moves from its place. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd used to say: Beautified: brought near? Az-Zulfi in Arabic speech means being close. God the Almighty says: And Paradise is brought near for the righteous (Ash-Shu'ara': 90). So-and-so draws near means he draws near.
81:14: The Almighty said: A soul will know what it has brought forth meaning what it has done of good and evil. This is the answer to When the sun is wrapped up and what follows it. Omar, may God be pleased with him, said: This is why the hadith was included. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Omar, may God be pleased with them both, that they recited it, and when they reached: A soul will know what it has brought forth, they said: This is why the story was included. So the meaning according to this is: When the sun is wrapped up and these things happen, a soul will know what it has brought forth of its deeds. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Adi bin Hatim, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is not one of you but that God will speak to him while there is an interpreter between him and Him. He will look to his right and see only what he has sent forth, and he will look to his left and see only what he has sent forth before him, and the Fire will confront him. So whoever among you is able to protect himself from the Fire, even with half a date, let him do so.” Al-Hasan said: When the sun is wrapped up is an oath that falls on the statement: A soul will know what it has brought forth, just as it is said: When Zaid flees, Amr flees. The first statement is more correct. Ibn Zaid said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God, the Most High, When the sun is wrapped up to His statement, When Paradise is brought near, there are twelve characteristics: six in this world and six in the Hereafter. We have already explained the first six based on the statement of Ubayy ibn Ka’b.
81:15: The Almighty said: So I swear by the stars that recede meaning I swear, and la is redundant, as mentioned above. By the stars that recede * the moving stars are the five shining planets: Saturn, Jupiter, Mercury, Mars, and Venus, according to what the commentators have mentioned. And God knows best. It was narrated from Ali, may God be pleased with him. There are two views regarding singling them out from among the other stars: One of them is because they face the sun, as Bakr ibn Abdullah Al-Muzani said. The second is because they cut through the galaxy, as Ibn Abbas said. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: They are the stars that recede during the day and when they set. Ali, may God be pleased with him, said the same. He said: They are the stars that recede during the day and appear at night, and are swept away at the time of their setting, meaning they are hidden from sight and therefore cannot be seen. In As-Sahah: And al-Khans means all the planets, because they recede at sunset, or because they recede during the day. It is said: They are the moving stars among them, not the fixed ones. Al-Farraa said about the verse: {And Venus and Mercury}, because they retreat in their course, and sweep, that is, they hide as the gazelles sweep in the cave, which is the sweeper. It is said: It was named Khans because of its delay, because they are the wandering planets that return from it. Al-Khans is the nose being delayed from the face with a slight rise in the hare. The man is Akhns, the woman is Khansa, and all cows are Khans. It was narrated from Abdullah ibn Masoud regarding the verse: {So I swear by the one who retreats}: It is the wild cow. Hisham narrated from Zakariya from Abu Ishaq from Abu Maysarah Amr ibn Shurahbil who said: Abdullah ibn Masoud said to me: You are an Arab people, so what is Al-Khans? I said: It is the wild cow. He said: And I see that. Ibrahim and Jabir ibn Abdullah said the same. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas: God only swore by the wild cow. Narrated by Ikrimah who said: Al-Khans are cows and Al-Kanas are gazelles. They are Khans when they see a person, they cower, shrink back, and retreat and enter their dens. Al-Qushayri said: And it was said on this basis that Al-Khans comes from Khans in the nose, which is the backwardness of the rabbit and the shortness of the tibia, and the noses of cows and gazelles are Khans. And the most correct is to carry it on the stars, because the night and morning are mentioned after this, so mentioning the stars is more appropriate for that.
81:16: I said: God has the right to swear by whatever He wills of His creations, whether animal or inanimate, even if the wisdom behind that is not known. It was narrated from Ibn Masoud and Jabir ibn Abdullah, both of whom were companions, and Al-Nakha'i that it is: wild cows. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas and Saeed ibn Jubayr that it is gazelles. It was narrated from Al-Hajjaj ibn Mundhir that he asked Jabir ibn Zayd about the sweeping maidens, and he said: gazelles and cows. So it is not far-fetched that what was meant was the stars. It was also said that it is the angels, as narrated by Al-Mawardi. The sweeping is the unseen, taken from the sweeper, which is the sweeper of wild animals that hides in it. Aws ibn Hajar said: Have you not seen that God sends down His rain and the gazelles rub their flocks in the dens? Tarafa said: As if the lost sweepers were covering it and the frames of the cross under the cross of the supporter It was said: The word knoos means to take refuge in its places, which are the places where wild animals and gazelles take refuge. Al-A’sha said: When we came to the neighborhood, Anas was stunned as one stunned under a broom. It is said: The day rose and the gazelle rose from her lair, meaning she lifted her neck high. Imru’ al-Qais said: He had dinner for a while, then he set out, stirring up dust from his sleeping place and his sweeping place. Al-Kanas: plural of Kanis and Kanisa, and likewise Al-Khans is plural of Khanis and Khanasa. Al-Jawari: plural of Jariyah from the root word Jariyah.
81:17: The Almighty said: And the night when it covers with darkness. Al-Farra' said: The commentators agreed that the meaning of 'Asaas is to depart, as narrated by Al-Jawhari. Some of our companions said: It is from its beginning and it became dark, and so is the cloud when it approaches the earth. Al-Mahdawi. And the night when it covers with darkness means it departs with its darkness, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and others. It was also narrated on their authority, and on the authority of Al-Hasan and others: It approached with its darkness. Zayd ibn Aslam: ('Asaas) is gone. Al-Farra': The Arabs say 'Asaas and Sa'sa' if nothing remains of it except a little. Al-Khalil and others: The night covers with darkness if it approaches or departs. Al-Mubarrad: It is one of the opposites, and the two meanings return to one thing, which is the beginning of darkness at the beginning, and its departure at the end. Alqamah ibn Qurt said: Until the morning breathes its breath and the night departs from it and darkens Ru'bah said: Oh Hind, how quickly you can run after being a young man! This is Al-Farra’s argument. Imru’ Al-Qais said: Even if He willed, He would bring us near to Him, and we would have a place of refuge from His fire. This indicates closeness. Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: Asasa means dark. The poet said: Until, when their night is dark, they ride on the edge of darkness, dark-skinned. Al-Mawardi: The root of ‘ass is to be full, and from this the large cup is called ‘ass because it is full of what is in it. So it was used to refer to the approach of night because it begins to fill up, and it was used to refer to its decline because it ends in its filling up, and to its darkness because it is completely filled with it. As for the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: Pain on the old quarter of Asa'sa A place in the desert. Asas is also the name of a man. Al-Zajer said: And Asas is a good young man That is, you depend on it. The wolf is called al-‘asas, al-‘asas, and al-‘assas, because it patrols at night and seeks. And hedgehogs are called al-‘asas because they frequently go around at night. Abu ‘Amr said: Ta’asas is the smell, and he recited: Like the nostril of a wolf when it is greedy Spying also means hunting at night.
81:18: The Almighty said: And the morning when it breathes meaning it extends until it becomes a clear day. When the day increases, it is said: it breathes. The same is true of waves when they spurt water. The meaning of breathing is the breeze emerging from the atmosphere. It was also said: (when it breathes) meaning it splits and cracks. From this comes the word the bow breathes meaning it cracks.
81:19: The Almighty's saying: Indeed, it is the word of an honored Messenger. This is the answer to the oath. The honored Messenger is Gabriel, as stated by Al-Hasan, Qatada, and Ad-Dahhak. The meaning is (Indeed, it is the word of a Messenger) from God, (honored) to God. He attributed the speech to Gabriel, peace be upon him, then moved it from him by saying (a revelation from the Lord of the worlds) so that those who verify the truth may know that the speech belongs to God, the Almighty. And it was said: It is Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him.
81:20: The Almighty's saying: of strength: whoever Gabriel made him, his strength is evident. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Among his strength are the fortresses of the cities of the people of Lot, with the tips of his wings. With the Lord of the Throne meaning with God, may He be glorified and exalted. Stable meaning of status and position. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Salih, who said: He enters seventy tents without permission.
81:21: The Almighty said: Obedient then: meaning in the heavens. Ibn Abbas said: Among the obedience of the angels Gabriel, is that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on the Night Journey, Gabriel, peace be upon him, said to Ridwan, the keeper of Paradise: Open for him. So he opened, and he entered and saw what was in it. And he said to Malik, the keeper of Hell: Open for him Hell so he can look at it. So he obeyed him and it was opened for him. Trustworthy" means trustworthy with the revelation that he received. And whoever says that what is meant is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, then the meaning is (strong) to convey the message (obeyed) meaning whoever obeys God, may He be glorified and exalted, obeys him.
81:22: The Almighty’s saying: And your companion is not mad. Meaning that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Gabriel in the form he has with his Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, and he said: That is not up to me. The Lord, may His praise be exalted, said to him: He came to him and he had blocked the horizon. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked at him, he fell unconscious. The polytheists said: He is mad. So the verses Indeed, it is the word of a noble Messenger and And your companion is not mad were revealed. He only saw Gabriel in his form and was afraid of him, and something happened to him that his constitution could not bear, so he fell unconscious.
81:23: The Almighty says: And he certainly saw him on the clear horizon. That is, he saw Gabriel in his true form, with six hundred wings. On the clear horizon that is, at the rising of the sun from the east, because if this horizon is where the sun rises, then it is clear. That is, things are seen from its direction. It was said: The clear horizon is the regions of the sky and its sides, as the poet said. We have taken the horizons of the sky upon you, for us are its two moons and the rising stars. Al-Mawardi: Based on this, there are three sayings, the first of which is that he saw him in the eastern horizon of the sky, said by Sufyan. The second: in the western horizon of the sky, narrated by Ibn Shajarah. The third: that he was towards Ajyad, which is the east of Mecca, said by Mujahid. Al-Tha’labi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to Gabriel: I would like to see you in the form in which the sky is. He said: You will not be able to do that. He said: Yes. He said: Where would you like me to appear to you? He said: In Al-Abtah. He said: It is not suffice for me. He said: Then in Mina. He said: It is not suffice for me. He said: Then in Arafat. He said: That would be more likely to suffice for me. So he made an appointment with him, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out at that time. Suddenly, he saw him coming with a rustle and a clatter from the mountains of Arafat, filling the space between the east and the west, with his head in the sky and his feet on the earth. When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw him, he fell unconscious. Gabriel took his form and hugged him to his chest and said, “O Muhammad, do not be afraid. How would it be if you saw Israfil with his head under the Throne and his feet on the edges of the seventh earth, and the Throne on his shoulders? Sometimes he would become small in fear of God, until he became like a bird, and nothing would carry the Throne of your Lord except His Majesty.” It was said that Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw his Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, on the clear horizon. This is the meaning of the statement of Ibn Mas`ud. This has been discussed in detail in By the Star, so ponder it there. Regarding Al-Mubeen, there are two opinions: One of them is that it is an attribute of the horizon, as Al-Rabi` said. The second is that it is an attribute of the one who saw it. Mujahid said. (And he is not suspicious of the unseen) with the letter Ḍād, the reading of Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and al-Kisa’i, meaning of them, and suspicion is accusation. The poet said: By the Book of God, I did not abandon it out of hatred, but out of suspicion. Abu Ubaid chose it because they did not deem him stingy but they called him a liar, and because most of the Arabs say: He is not stingy with such and such, and they do not say: He is not on such and such, rather they say: You are not accused of this. The rest read it (badhanin) with a ḍād: meaning stingy, from Ḍanṭa bi-shay’ aḍan ḍanan, so he is stingy. Ibn Abi Najeh narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: He does not deprive you of what he knows, rather he teaches the creation the words of God and His rulings. And the poet said: I am generous with my secrets, and I am stingy with your secret from whoever asks me The unseen: the Qur’an and the report of the heavens. Then this is a description of Muhammad, peace be upon him. It was said: a description of Gabriel, peace be upon him. It was also said: weak. Narrated by Al-Farra and Al-Mubarrad. It is said: a man who is doubtful: meaning weak. And a well is doubtful: if it has little water. Al-A’sha said: What made the grandfather suspicious that he avoided the rainy well? Like the Euphrates, when it overflows, it throws reeds and skilled fish. Suspicions: A debt that one does not know whether the debtor will pay it back or not. From this is the hadith of Ali, peace be upon him, about a man who has a debt that is suspected. He said: It purifies him for what he has owed when he collects it, if he is truthful. Suspicions: A man of bad character, so it is a general term.
81:25: God Almighty said: And it is not meaning the Qur’an the word of a cursed devil meaning one who is cursed and outcast, as the Quraysh said. Ata’ said: Yazid refers to the white devil who used to come to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the form of Gabriel, wanting to tempt him.
81:26: The Almighty said: Then where are you going? Qatada said: So where are you going to deviate from this statement and from obeying it? This is what Muammar narrated from Qatada, meaning where are you going from My Book and My obedience. Al-Zajjaj said: Which way do you take is clearer than this way that I have shown you. It is said: Where are you going? And where are you going? Al-Farra’ narrated from the Arabs: Ash-Sham went, Iraq left, and the market set out: meaning to it. He said we heard it in these three letters, and some of Banu Uqayl recited: Hanifa shouted at us when she saw us, and what kind of land does shouting take? He wanted to know which land you are going to, so he omitted the word to. Al-Junayd said: The meaning of the verse is connected to another verse, which is the Almighty’s saying: And there is not a thing but that with Us are its depositories. (al-Hijr 15:21) The meaning is: Whichever path you take is clearer than the path that God has shown you. This is the meaning of Al-Zajjaj’s statement.
81:27: The Almighty says: It meaning the Qur’an is only a reminder to the worlds meaning an admonition and a warning. In means what. It was said: Muhammad is only a reminder.
81:28: The Almighty says: For whoever among you wills to go straight meaning follows the truth and adheres to it. Abu Hurairah and Sulayman ibn Musa said: When the verse For whoever among you wills to go straight was revealed, Abu Jahl said: The matter is up to us. If we wish, we will go straight, and if we wish, we will not go straight - and this is predestination, which is the head of the Qadarites - then the verse And you do not will except that God wills, Lord of the worlds was revealed.
81:29: God the Almighty says: And you do not will except that God wills, Lord of the worlds. This makes it clear that a servant does not do good except with God's help, and does not do evil except by His abandonment. Al-Hasan said: By God, the Arabs did not will Islam until God willed it for them. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: I read in eighty-seven books of what God revealed to the prophets: Whoever assigns any of the will to himself has disbelieved. And in the revelation: And even if We had sent down to them the angels and the dead had spoken to them and We had gathered together before them all things in front of them, they would not have believed unless God willed. (Al-An'am 6:111) And God the Almighty says: And it is not for a soul to believe except by God's permission. (Yunus 10:100) There is much of this, as well as the hadiths, and that God the Almighty guides through Islam and misguides through disbelief, as mentioned previously in more than one place. I have finished the Surah, and praise be to God.
82:1: Meccan according to everyone, and it has nineteen verses. God the Almighty said: When the heaven is cleft asunder meaning it is split by God’s command, for the angels to descend, like His statement: And the Day the heaven will be split asunder with clouds and the angels will be sent down in [gradual] descent (al-Furqan 25:25). It was also said: It was split open out of awe of God the Almighty. And to split means to slit. It is said: I split it, so it split open. And from this comes the word to split in a camel’s fang: it came out, so it is a fatir camel. And something is split open: it slits, and a sword has cracks in it. Antara said: My sword is like a chariot, and it is like my weapon, it does not fail or break. It has been mentioned in more than one place.
82:2: The Almighty said: And when the stars are scattered meaning they fall. They scatter something, they scatter it, and it is scattered. The noun is scattering. Scattering, with the letter damma, means what is scattered of something, and scattered pearls, doubled for abundance.
82:3: The Almighty said: And when the seas burst forth meaning, some of them burst forth into others, and they become one sea, as mentioned above. Al-Hasan said: burst forth means their water disappears and they dry up. This is because they are initially stagnant and gathered together, but when they burst forth, they disperse, and their water disappears. These things will occur before the Hour, as mentioned above in When the sun is wrapped up.
82:4: The Almighty said: And when the graves are scattered meaning they are turned over and what is in them of their inhabitants is taken out, alive. It is said: I scattered the goods meaning I turned them upside down. And I scattered the pool and dug it up" meaning I demolished it and made its bottom its top. A group of people, including Al-Farra', said: "It scattered" means it took out what was in its belly of gold and silver. This is one of the signs of the Hour: that the earth will bring out its gold and silver.
82:5: The Almighty's statement: A soul will know what it has put forward and left behind is like the verse: On that Day man will be informed of what he put forward and left behind (al-Qiyamah 75:13), which has been mentioned previously. This is the answer to the verse, When the heaven is split open, because it is an oath, according to Al-Hasan, which falls upon the Almighty's statement: A soul will know. He says: When these signs of the Hour appear, deeds will be sealed, and every soul will know what it has earned, and no deeds will benefit it after that. It was also said: That is, when these things occur, the Day of Resurrection will take place, and every soul will be held accountable for what it has done, and will be given its book in its right or left, and when it is read, it will remember all its deeds. It was also said: It is a statement, not an oath, and this is the correct view, God willing.
82:6: The Almighty's saying, O mankind, is addressed to those who deny the resurrection. Ibn Abbas said: The human being here is Al-Walid ibn Al-Ghayrah. Ikrimah said: Abi ibn Khalaf. It was also said that it was revealed about Abi Al-Ashd ibn Kalda Al-Jumahi. On the authority of Ibn Abbas also: (What deceived you concerning your Generous Lord?) meaning, what deceived you that you disbelieved? (In your Generous Lord) meaning, the One who overlooked you. Qatada said: His devil who had power over him deceived him. Al-Hasan: His evil devil deceived him. And it was said: His foolishness and ignorance. Al-Hasan narrated it on the authority of Omar, may God be pleased with him. “And Ghalib Al-Hanafi narrated that he said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited, “O man, what has deceived you concerning your Generous Lord?” He said: (Ignorance has deceived him.) And Salih bin Mismar said: It has reached us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited, (O man, what has deceived you concerning your Generous Lord?) He said: (His ignorance has deceived him.) Omar, may God be pleased with him, said: As God Almighty said, Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant. (al-Ahzab 33:72) And it was said: He was deceived by God’s forgiveness, since He did not punish him the first time. Ibrahim bin Al-Ash’ath said: It was said to Al-Fudayl bin Iyad: If God Almighty were to establish you on the Day of Resurrection between His hands, and he said to you: What has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous? (al-Infitar 82:6)? What were you saying? He said: I used to say that your lowered curtain deceived me, because the Generous is the curtain. Ibn Al-Sammak put it in verse and said: O sinner, are you not ashamed, I swear, to say the second time in private? Your Lord has deceived you by His respite and His concealment of your long misdeeds. Dhu al-Nun al-Misri said: How many are deceived under the veil without realizing it. Abu Bakr bin Tahir Al-Abhari recited: O you who are excessively arrogant and confused, and who are deceived by your long persistence God has given you hope, so confront Him and do not fear His disobedience. It was narrated on the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him that he called out to his servant several times but he did not respond. So he looked and saw him at the door. He said: Why did you not answer me? He said: Because I trust your patience and feel safe from your punishment. He appreciated his answer and set him free. Some people say: What deceived you? What tricked you and tempted you, until you neglected what was required of you? Ibn Masoud said: There is no one among you but that God will be alone with him on the Day of Resurrection and say to him: O son of Adam, what deceived you about Me? O son of Adam, what did you do with what you knew? O son of Adam, what did you answer the messengers?
82:7: The Almighty says: Who created you meaning He determined your creation from a drop of semen then proportioned you in your mother's womb, and made for you two hands, two feet, two eyes and the rest of your limbs then balanced you meaning He made you balanced and of sound creation, as one says: this is something balanced. This is the reading of the common people, and it is the preferred choice of Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim. Al-Farra' said: Abu Ubayd said: It is indicated by the Almighty's statement: Indeed, We created man in the best of stature (al-Tin 95:4). The Kufians, Asim, Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i, read: (then balanced you) with a lightened vowel, meaning He made you well and turned you into whatever form He wanted, either ugly, tall or short. Musa bin Ali bin Abi Rabah Al-Lakhmi said on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: When the sperm settles in the womb, God brings to it every lineage between it and Adam. Have you not read this verse: In whatever form He willed, He assembled you 2:17-18: (between you and Adam).
82:8: Ikrimah and Abu Salih said: In whatever form He wills, He will assemble you: If He wills, in the form of a human, or if He wills, in the form of a donkey, or if He wills, in the form of an ape, or if He wills, in the form of a pig. Makhul said: If He wills, a male, or a female. Mujahid said: (In whatever form) means in any resemblance to a father, mother, paternal uncle, maternal uncle, or others. (In) is connected to (He assembled you), and not to (Your justice), according to the reading of those who preferred to make it lighter, because you say I turned to such-and-such, but you do not say I turned to such-and-such. That is why Al-Farra' forbade making it lighter, because he considered (In) to be connected to (Your justice), and (What) may be a confirmatory conjunction, meaning, in whatever form He wills, He assembled you. It may also be a conditional, meaning, if He wills, He assembled you in a form other than that of a human, such as an ape, donkey, or pig. Thus (What) has the meaning of condition and consequence, meaning, in whatever form He wills, He assembled you.
82:9: The Almighty's saying: No! Rather, you deny the Judgment. It is possible that (No) means truly, and (No) is used to begin with it. It is also possible that it means (No), so that the meaning is that the matter is not as you say, that you are right in your worship of other than God. Evidence for this is the Almighty's saying: {What has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?} Al-Farra' also says: Nasir says the meaning: It is not as you were deceived by it. It was also said: That is, the matter is not as you say, that there is no resurrection. It was also said: It means deterrence and admonition. That is, do not be deceived by God's forbearance and generosity, so you abandon contemplating His signs. Ibn Al-Anbari: It is good to stop at (the Judgment) and at (your knees), but stopping at (No) is ugly. Rather, you deny O people of Mecca the Judgment meaning the Judgment, and (But) is to negate something that came before and to confirm something else. Their denial of the Resurrection was well-known, even if it was not mentioned in this Surah.
82:10: God Almighty says: And over you are guardians meaning angelic watchers.
82:11: The Almighty’s saying: Noble meaning Ali, like His saying: Noble and pious (Abasa 80:16). Here there are three issues: First: “It was narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: ((Honor the honorable scribes who do not leave you except in one of two situations: defecation or sexual intercourse. So when one of you bathes, let him cover himself with the weight of a wall or his camel, or let his brother cover himself.)) It was narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: The king remains away from the servant as long as his private parts are exposed. It was narrated: (If a servant enters the bathroom without a loincloth, his two angels will curse him.) Second: People differed about the disbelievers: Do they have guardians over them or not? Some of them said: No, because their matter is clear and their actions are the same. God the Most High said: “The criminals will be known by their mark” (al-Rahman 55:41). And it was said: Rather, they have guardians, because God the Most High said: “No! Rather, you deny the Judgment. And indeed, over you are keepers, * Noble and recording. * They know whatever you do.”
82:12: And He said: But he who is given his record in his left hand (al-Haqqah 69:25) And He said: But he who is given his record behind his back (al-Inshiqaq 84:10), so He informed that the disbelievers will have a record and guardians over them. If it is said: What does the one on his right write and have no good deeds? It is said to him: The one who writes on his left hand does so with the permission of his companion, and he is a witness to that even if he does not write. And God knows best. Third - Sufyan was asked: How do the angels know that a servant has intended to do a good or bad deed? He said: If the servant intends to do a good deed, they smell from him the scent of musk, and if he intends to do a bad deed, they smell from him the stench of foul odor. And in Qaf, when God says: Not a word does he utter but there is a watcher by him ever ready to record (Qaf: 18), there is further clarification of the meaning of this verse. The scholars disliked speaking during defecation or sexual intercourse, because the angel would separate from the servant at that time. And in the last Surah Al Imran, this was mentioned. And from Al Hasan: They know, nothing of your deeds is hidden from them. And it was said: They know what is apparent from you, not what you whisper to yourselves. And God knows best.
82:13: The Almighty says: Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss, and indeed, the wicked will be in Hellfire. This is a division like His saying: A group will be in Paradise and a group will be in the Blaze (al-Shura 42:7) and He said: “On that Day they will be separated. As for those who believed” (al-Rum 30:14-15) the two verses:
82:14: God Almighty says: And indeed, the wicked will be in Hellfire.
82:15: The Almighty says: They will burn in it meaning they will be struck by its flames and heat on the Day of Judgment meaning the Day of Recompense and Reckoning.
82:16: God Almighty says: And they will not be absent from it.
82:17: And he repeated mentioning it to magnify its status, like the Almighty’s saying: The Calamity * What is the Calamity * And what can make you know what is the Calamity? (al-Qari’ah 101:1-3) Ibn Abbas said, as narrated from him: Everything in the Qur’an that says: And what can make you know? has made it known, and everything that says: (And what can make you know) has been omitted from it.
82:18: God Almighty says: Then what will make you know what the Day of Judgment is?
82:19: The Almighty said: The Day when no soul will possess control Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read (Day) in the nominative case as a substitute for (The Day of Judgment) or in response to the first day, so it is an adjective and a description of (The Day of Judgment). It is permissible to raise it by implying he. The rest read it in the accusative case as it is in the nominative case except that it is accusative because it is an intransitive noun, as you say: I like the day Zaid rises. Al-Mubarrad recited: Which day of my death is it? The day that was not destined or the day that was destined? The second two days are in the accusative case, as a translation of the first two days, except that they are in the accusative case in wording, because they are added to something that is not pure. This is the choice of al-Farra’ and al-Zajjaj. Some people said: The second day is in the accusative case as a place, as if he said on a day when no soul possesses anything for another soul. It was said: It means: these things will be on a day, or on the meaning of they will be judged on a day, because debt indicates it, or by the implication of remember. And the command on that day belongs to God no one will dispute it with Him, as He said: “To whom belongs the dominion this Day? To God, the One, the Prevailing. Today every soul will be recompensed for what it has earned. No injustice today.” (Ghafir 40:16-17). The surah is complete, and praise be to God.
83:1: It was revealed in Mecca according to Ibn Mas'ud, Ad-Dahhak, and Muqatil, and in Medina according to Al-Hasan and Ikrimah. It has thirty-six verses. Muqatil said: It was the first surah revealed in Medina. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: It was revealed in Medina except for eight verses from the words Indeed, those who commit crimes to the end of it, which are Meccan. Al-Kalbi and Jabir ibn Zayd said: It was revealed between Mecca and Medina. The Almighty’s saying: Woe to those who give short measure. There are four issues in this: First - Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to Madinah, they were among the worst people in measuring. So God revealed: Woe to those who give short measure. After that, they improved their measuring. Al-Farra’ said: They are among the most faithful people in measuring until this day. Also on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: “It is the first Surah revealed to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) when he arrived in Madinah, and this was the case with them. When they bought, they would take full measure, but when they sold, they would cheat in the measure and weight. So when this Surah was revealed, they stopped, and they are among the most faithful people in measuring until this day.” Some people said: “It was revealed about a man known as Abu Juhayna, whose name was Amr. He had two measures; he would take one and give with the other.” This was said by Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him. Second - The Almighty's saying: Woe! meaning severe torment in the Hereafter. Ibn Abbas said: It is a valley in Hell in which the pus of the people of Hell flows. This is the meaning of the Almighty's saying: Woe to those who defraud! meaning those who reduce their measures and weights. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: Al-Mutaffif is the man who hires a measurer knowing that he will be unfair in his measure and so his sin is upon him. Others said: Defrauding is in measuring, weighing, ablution, prayer and speech. In Al-Muwatta', Malik said: Everything is called fulfillment and defrauding. It was narrated on the authority of Salim ibn Abi Al-Ja'd who said: Prayer is by measure, so whoever fulfills it and whoever defrauds, you know what God the Almighty said about that: (Woe to those who defraud). Third - The linguists said: Al-Mutaffif is taken from Al-Tafeef, which means little, and Al-Mutaffif is the one who deducts the right of his owner by reducing it from the right, in measure or weight. Al-Zajjaj said: The one who does this is called Mutaff, because hardly anyone steals from the measure or scale except something small and light, and it is taken from the tuff of something which is its side. And the tuffaf of the kasra and tuffafah with kasra and fatha: what filled his bags, and likewise the tuff of the kasra and tuffah, and in the hadith: ((You are all the children of Adam. The measure is too small, yet you do not fill it.)) It means that it is close to being filled but does not. The meaning is that some of you are close to others, so no one has superiority over another except in piety. Tatfaaf and tafaafa with dammah means what is above the measure. A vessel is tafaaf if it reaches the tafaaf filling. You say from it: I have filled it too much. Tatfeef means reducing the measure, which means not filling it to its sides. It is said: I poured the cup to its asbar, meaning to its top. And the statement of Ibn Umar when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) mentioned the racing of horses: I was a rider that day, so I outran the people until the horse passed me by the mosque of Bani Zuraiq, until it was almost level with the mosque. Meaning: it leapt with me. Fourth - al-Mutaffifin 83:He is the one who cheats in measure and weight, and does not fulfill what we have explained. Ibn Al-Qasim narrated on the authority of Malik that he recited Woe to those who cheat and said: Do not cheat and do not defraud, but send [the measure] and pour it on him abundantly, until when he has finished, send [the measure] with your hand and do not hold it back. Abdul Malik bin Al-Majishun said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade wiping the one who cheats, and said: The blessing is in his head.” He said: I was informed that Pharaoh’s measure was wiped with iron.
83:2: God the Almighty says: {Those who, when they take a measure from people, take in full} Al-Farra’ said: meaning from people. It is said: I took from you, meaning I took what was due from you. Al-Zajjaj said: meaning, when they take a measure from people, they take in full the measure from them. The meaning is: those who, when they take in full, take the excess, and when they give in full or weigh for someone else, they take less, so they are not pleased for people what they are pleased for themselves. Al-Tabari said: (upon) means with.
83:3: There are two issues God the Almighty said: {And when they measure or weigh for them, they lose out}. That is, they measure for them or weigh for them, so the lam was deleted, so the verb becomes transitive and accusative. Similar to it are: I advised you and I advised you, I ordered you to do it and I ordered you to do it, as stated by Al-Akhfash and Al-Farra’. Al-Farra’ said: I heard a Bedouin woman say: When the people come, we go to the merchant and he will measure us out the mudd and the mudd until the next season. This is from the speech of the people of Al-Hijaz and those of Qais who lived near them. Al-Zajjaj said: It is not permissible to stop at (كالوا) and (وزنوا) until you connect it to (هم) He said: Some people make it an emphasis and permit stopping at (كالوا) and (وزنوا), but the first is the preferred opinion, because it is one letter. This is the opinion of Al-Kisa’i. Abu Ubaid said: Isa bin Umar used to make it two letters, and stop at (كالوا) and (وزنوا) and begin with (هم يخسررون) He said: I think that the reading of Hamza is like that as well. Abu Ubaid said: It is preferred that they be one word for two reasons: One of them is the script, as they wrote them without an alif, and if they were disconnected they would have been (كالوا) and (وزناوا) with an alif, and the other is that it is said: I katalaka and wazanataka meaning I katalaka laka, and likewise I thanked you and advised you and the like. His statement: (يهصومرون) means they decrease, and the Arabs say: I lost the scale and I made it lose. And (هم) is in the accusative case, according to the reading of the general public, referring to the people, its meaning is (وذا َقالوا) the people (or weighed them, they lose) and there are two views on this: One of them is that what is meant is they katalaka lahu or weighed lahu, so the preposition was deleted and the verb was connected, as he said: I have given you the most beautiful and the most beautiful things, and I have forbidden you from the daughters of the hyenas. He wanted: I harvested for you. The other way is: to delete the noun and replace it with the noun to which it is added. The noun is the measured and weighed. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him: You, O Persians, are the ones who perished because of them: the measure and the scale. He specified the Persians because they used to combine the measure and the weight together, and they were separated in the two sacred mosques. The people of Mecca used to weigh, and the people of Medina used to measure. According to the second reading, (they) is in the nominative case as a subject, meaning that if they measure or weigh for people, they lose. It is not correct because the first one would be cancelled and has no predicate. It would only be correct if it was after it: And if they measure, they decrease, or if they weigh, they lose. Second - Ibn Abbas said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ((Five for five: No people broke the covenant except that God would give power to their enemy over them. No people ruled by other than what God revealed except that poverty would spread among them. No people committed immorality except that plague would spread among them. No people cheated in measure except that plants were withheld and famine would befall them. No people withheld zakat except that God would withhold rain from them.)) Abu Bakr al-Bazzar transmitted it with the same meaning, and Malik ibn Anas also transmitted it from the hadith of Ibn Umar. We mentioned it in the Book of Remembrance. Malik ibn Dinar said: I entered upon a neighbor of mine who had been approached by death, and he began to say: Two mountains of fire! Two mountains of fire! I said: What are you saying? Are you delirious? He said: O Abu Yahya, I had two measures, I measured with one of them and I measured with the other. So I stood up and started hitting one of them with the other until I broke them. He said: O Abu Yahya, every time I hit one of them with the other, its size increases. So he died from the pain. Ikrimah said: I bear witness that he is in the Fire. Al-Asma’i said: I heard a Bedouin woman say: Do not seek chivalry from anyone who His chivalry lies in the heads of the measures, not the tongues of the scales. This was narrated on the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him. Abd al-Khair said: Ali may God be pleased with him passed by a man who was weighing saffron and he had tipped the scales, so he tipped the scales over, then said: Fix the weight justly, then tip it as much as you wish. It was as if he ordered him to do it evenly first so that he would get used to it and prefer what was due over the weight. Nafi’ said: Ibn Umar would pass by a seller and say: Fear God and give full measure and weight justly, for on the Day of Resurrection, those who give short measure will be stopped until their bridles are halfway up to their ears. It was narrated that Abu Hurairah came to Madinah and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had left the house, so he recited in the first rak’ah Kaf Ha Ya Ain Sad and in the second rak’ah he recited Woe to those who give short measure. Abu Hurairah said: “So I would say in my prayer: Woe to the father of so-and-so, for he had two measures. When he measured, he measured fully and when he measured less.”
83:4: The Almighty's saying: Do they not think? is a denial and great astonishment at their state, in daring to commit fraud, as if fraud does not cross their minds, nor do they even guess that they will be resurrected and will be held accountable for what they do. Here, thinking means certainty, meaning do they not believe? If they were certain, they would not have been deficient in measure and weight. It was said that thinking means hesitation, meaning if they are not certain of the resurrection, why do they not think about it, so that they may reflect and research it, and take the more cautious approach.
83:5: God Almighty says: For a great day which is the Day of Resurrection.
83:6: The Almighty’s saying: The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the Worlds contains four issues: First: The agent in (Day) is an implied verb, indicated by (repudiants). The meaning is that they will be resurrected (On the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the Worlds). It is permissible for it to be a substitute for Day in (On the Great Day), and it is constructed. It was said: It is in the accusative case because it was added to something that is not established. It was said: It is accusative as an adverbial phrase, meaning on the Day. It is said: Stay until the Day when so-and-so comes out, so Day is accusative. If they add it to the noun, then they lower it and say: Stay until the Day when so-and-so comes out. It was said: There is an inversion in the speech, the meaning is: They will be resurrected on the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the Worlds for a Great Day. Second - On the authority of Abdul-Malik bin Marwan: That a Bedouin said to him: You have heard what God the Most High said about Al-Mutaffifin, meaning that this great threat that you heard about has been directed at Al-Mutaffifin, so what do you think of yourself when you are taking the Muslims’ money without measure or weight? In this denial and astonishment and the word of suspicion, and describing the Day as great, and the people standing in it in submission to God, and describing Himself as the Lord of the Worlds, there is a clear statement of the enormity of the sin, and the aggravation of the guilt in Al-Mutaffifin, and in what was in a similar situation of injustice, and the failure to establish justice, and to work towards equality and fairness, in every taking and giving, and even in every word and deed. Third - Ibn Omar read: Woe to those who give short measure, until he reached The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds, and he wept until he fell down and refused to recite what came after it. Then he said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds, on a day the length of which will be fifty thousand years. Some of them will have sweat reaching their ankles, some of them reaching their knees, some of them reaching their waists, some of them reaching their chests, and some of them reaching their ears, until one of them will disappear into his sweat as a frog disappears.” And some people narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: They will stand for the length of three hundred years. He said: And the duration of their obligatory prayers will be made easy for the believers. And it was narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: (They stand for a thousand years in the shade) and Malik narrated on the authority of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: (On the Day when people will stand before the Lord of the Worlds, one of them will stand in sweat up to the middle of his ears), and also on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: (He will stand for a hundred years).” And Abu Hurairah said that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Bashir al-Ghifari: (What will you do on a day when people will stand before the Lord of the Worlds for the duration of three hundred years, and no good will come to them, and no matter will be commanded?) Bashir said: The one sought for help is God. I said: We have mentioned it with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet - from the hadith of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: (It is made easy for the believer, to the point that it is lighter for him than the obligatory prayer he prayed in this world) - in (A questioner asked). And on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The value of their obligatory prayer is made easy for the believers. And it was said: That standing is like the sun’s decline for the believer, and the evidence for this in the Book is the saying of the Truth: Unquestionably, for the allies of God there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve (Yunus 10:62) Then He described them and said: Those who believed and were righteous (Yunus 10:63). May God make us among them by His grace, generosity and goodness. And from this, Amen. And it was said: What is meant by people is Gabriel, peace be upon him, who stands before the Lord of the Worlds, said Ibn Jubayr. And there is more to it, because of the narrations we have mentioned in that, and they are authentic and established. It is sufficient for you what is in Sahih Muslim, Bukhari and Tirmidhi from the hadith of Ibn Umar from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: (The Day when people stand before the Lord of the Worlds) He said: One of them stands in his sweat up to halfway to his ears. Then it was said: This standing is the day when they rise from their graves. And it was said that in the Hereafter there are rights of worship in this world. Yazid Al-Rishk said: They stand before him to judge. Fourth: Standing up for God, the Lord of the Worlds, glory be to Him, is insignificant in comparison to His greatness and right. As for people standing up for one another, people have differed concerning it. Some of them permit it and some of them forbid it. It has been narrated that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, stood up for Ja’far ibn Abi Talib and embraced him, and Talhah stood up for Ka’b ibn Malik on the day he repented. And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to the Ansar when Sa’d ibn Mu’adh came up to him: Stand up for your master. He also said: Whoever is pleased for people to stand up for him, let him take his seat in Hellfire. This depends on the person’s condition and intention. If he waits for that and believes it for himself, then it is forbidden. However, if it is done to show cheerfulness and to connect with others, then it is permissible, especially for reasons, such as returning from a journey and the like. Some of this was mentioned at the end of Surah Yusuf.
83:7: The Almighty says: No indeed! The record of the wicked is in Sijjin. Some of the people of Arabic knowledge said: No indeed is a deterrent and a warning, meaning that the matter is not as it is of cheating in measure and weight, or denying the Hereafter, so let them be deterred from that. It is a word of deterrence and warning. Then He began again and said: The record of the wicked. Al-Hasan said: No indeed means truly. Some people narrated from Ibn Abbas: No indeed means: Do you not believe? So based on this: The pause is (to the Lord of the worlds). In the interpretation of Muqatil: The deeds of the wicked. Some people narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: The souls of the wicked and their deeds are (in Sijjin). Ibn Abi Nujayj narrated from Mujahidah that he said: Sijjin is a rock under the seventh earth, which is turned over and the record of the wicked is placed under it. Similar to this was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Qatadah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Muqatil, and Ka'b. Ka'b said: Underneath it are the souls of the disbelievers under the cheek of Iblis. It was also narrated from Ka'b that he said: Sijjin is a black rock under the seventh earth, on which is written the name of every devil, and the souls of the unbelievers are thrown into it. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Sijjin is under the cheek of Iblis. Yahya ibn Salam said: A black stone under the earth, on which the souls of the unbelievers are written. Ata' al-Khurasani said: It is the seventh lowest earth, and in it is Iblis and his offspring. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: Death attends the unbeliever, and the messengers of God attend him, but they are unable, due to God's hatred for him and their hatred for him, to delay him or hasten him until his hour comes. When his hour comes, they take his soul and raise him to the angels of punishment, and they show him whatever evil God wills him to see. Then they descend with him to the seventh earth, which is Sijjin, and it is the last part of Iblis's dominion, and they record his book there. On the authority of Ka'b al-Ahbar, regarding this verse, he said: When the soul of the wicked person is taken, it ascends to the heaven, but the heaven refuses to accept it. Then it descends to the earth, but the earth refuses to accept it, so it enters seven earths, until it reaches Sijjin, which is the cheek of Satan. A parchment is brought out for it from under Sijjin's cheek, and it is numbered and placed under the cheek of Satan. Al-Hasan said: Sijjin is in the seventh earth. It was also said: It is a metaphor and an indication that God, the Most High, rejects their deeds that they thought would benefit them. Mujahid said: The meaning is that their deeds are under the seventh earth, from which nothing ascends. He said: Sijjin is a rock in the seventh earth. Abu Hurairah narrated that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: (Sijjin is an open pit in Hellfire) and he said in al-Falaq 113:(It is a covered pit) Anas said: It is a level in the lowest earth. Anas said that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: (Sijjin is at the bottom of the seventh earth). And Ikrimah said: “Prisoner: loss and misguidance, like what they say to someone whose status has fallen: he has slipped into the abyss. Abu Ubaidah, Al-Akhfash and Al-Zajjaj said: (in prison) is in confinement and severe constriction, a verbal noun from prison, as one says: corrupt and drunk. Ibn Muqbil said: And the company beat the whites of the suburb with a beating that the heroes communicated with the prisoner Meaning: Their book is in prison. This is made as evidence of their lowly status, or because it is permissible to turn away from it and banish it in place of reprimand and humiliation. It was said: Its origin is Sajjil, but the Lam was replaced with a Noon. This has been mentioned before. Zayd ibn Aslam said: Sajjil is in the lowest earth, and Sajjil is in the lowest heaven. Al-Qushayri said: Sajjil is a place in the lowest world, in which the book of these people is buried, so it does not appear, but rather remains in that place like a prisoner. This is evidence of the wickedness of their deeds, and how God despises them. For this reason He said about the Book of the righteous: (Those brought near will witness it)
83:8: God Almighty says, And what will make you know what is Sijjin? That is, this is not something you knew, O Muhammad, nor did your people.
83:9: Then he explained it to him, saying: A Book marked, meaning written like a number on a garment, that is not forgotten or erased. Qatada said: Marked means written, a number for them, humans, no one will be added to them and no one will be subtracted from them. Ad-Dahhak said: Marked means sealed, in the language of Himyar, and the root of number is writing. He said: I will number the pure water to you, far from you, if water has a number There is nothing in his saying: And what will make you know what Sijjin is? to indicate that the word Sijjin is not Arabic, just as there is nothing in his saying: The Calamity * What is the Calamity * And what will make you know what is the Calamity? Rather, it is an emphasis on the importance of Sijjin. We mentioned in the introduction to the book - praise be to God - that there is nothing in the Qur’an that is not Arabic.
83:10: God Almighty says: Woe, that Day, to the deniers. That is, severity and punishment on the Day of Resurrection for the deniers.
83:11: Then God Almighty explained their situation, saying: Those who deny the Day of Judgment, meaning the Day of Reckoning, Reward, and Separation between the servants.
83:12: And none denies it except every transgressor and sinner. That is, one who is wicked and permissible to deviate from the truth, who transgresses against creation in his dealings with them, and against himself, and who is sinful in abandoning the command of God. This was said about Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira, Abu Jahl, and their peers.
83:13: Because God Almighty said: When Our verses are recited to him, he says, ‘Legends of the ancients.’ The common reading is (tattala) with two ta’s, and the reading of Abu Haywah, Abu Samak, Ashhab al-Uqayli and al-Salma is (idha yatalat) with a ya’. Legends of the ancients: their stories and falsehoods that they wrote and embellished. The singular is legend and myth, and it has been mentioned previously.
83:14: The Almighty said: No! Rather, what they were earning has covered their hearts. (No) is a deterrent and a warning, meaning it is not the legends of the ancients. Al-Hasan said: Its true meaning is (has covered their hearts). It was also said in Al-Tirmidhi: On the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “When a servant commits a sin, a black spot is placed on his heart. If he desists, seeks forgiveness from God, and repents, his heart is polished. If he returns to it, it is increased until it covers his heart. This is the ‘ran’ that God mentioned in His Book: ‘Nay, but what they were earning has covered their hearts.’ He said: This is a good and authentic hadith.” And the commentators said the same: It is sin upon sin until the heart blackens. Mujahid said: It is a man who commits a sin, and the sin surrounds his heart, then he commits another sin, and the sin surrounds his heart, until sins cover his heart. Mujahid said: It is the verse in Surat al-Baqarah 2:‘Yes, whoever earns evil…’ (al-Baqarah 2:81) The verse. And something similar was narrated from Al-Farra’, who said: He says that their sins and transgressions have increased, and have surrounded their hearts, and that is the rust on them. It was also narrated from Mujahid who said: The heart is like a cave, and he raised his hand. So when a servant commits a sin, He contracted and closed his finger, and if he committed a sin, he contracted and closed another, until he closed all his fingers, until his heart was sealed. He said: They used to think that this was rust. Then he recited: No! Rather, what they were earning has rusted over their hearts. And something similar was narrated from Hudhayfah may God be pleased with him. Bakr ibn Abdullah said: When a servant sins, there is in his heart like the prick of a needle, then if he sins a second time, it becomes like that. Then if sins increase, the heart becomes like a sieve, it does not recognize good and no righteousness remains in it. We have already explained this meaning in Al-Baqarah with the authentic narrations from the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), so there is no point in repeating them. Abdul-Ghani ibn Saeed narrated from Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman from Ibn Jurayj from Ata’ from Ibn Abbas, and from Musa from Muqatil from al-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas something - God knows best if it is authentic. He said: It is the rust that is on the thighs, shins, and feet, and it is what is worn in war. He said: Others said: Raran is the thought that crosses a man’s heart. This is something whose veracity is not guaranteed. And God knows best. As for the majority of the people of interpretation, they are on what was mentioned before this. And the people of language are on the same opinion. It is said: Raran on his heart is his sin meaning it overcame. Abu Ubaidah said about His statement: (No! Rather, what they were earning has covered their hearts) meaning it has overcome. Abu Ubaid said: Everything that overpowers you and overcomes you has covered you, covered you, and covered you. And the poet said: How many sins have covered the heart of a wicked person, and then he repented from the sin that had covered and disappeared. The wine overcame his mind: that is, it overcame him. Drowsiness covered him: if it covered him. From this is the saying of Omar about Al-Asifa’ - Asifa’ Juhayna: So he became drunk. That is, the debts overcame him, and he was in debt. From this is the saying of Abu Zubaydah describing a man who drank until he became drunk and he said: Then when he saw him, the wine became tainted and he did not see him with piety. His saying: The wine has become rancid on him, means it has overwhelmed his mind and heart. Al-Amawi said: The people have become rancid, so they are emaciated: if their livestock have perished and become emaciated. This is from the matter that has befallen them that has overwhelmed them, so they cannot bear it. Abu Zaid said: It is said: The man has become rancid: if he has fallen into something that he cannot get out of, and cannot bear it. Abu Muadh Al-Nahwi said: Rain is when the heart is blackened by sins, and tab means that it is stamped on the heart, and this is more severe than rain, and iqfal is more severe than tabb. Al-Zajjaj said: Rain is like rust that covers the heart like a thin cloud. The same applies to ghayn, it is said: Ghayn ‘ala qalbi: it is covered. Ghayn is a tangled tree, the singular is ghayna, meaning green with many leaves and intertwined branches. Al-Farra’ said previously that it is the sin that surrounds the hearts. Al-Tha’labi mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Rain ‘ala qulubhum: meaning it covered them. This is the correct version of his hadith, God willing. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, Al-A'mash, Abu Bakr and Al-Mufaddal read Rana with imala because the fa' of the verb is the ra' and its 'ayn is the alif changed from the ya', so the imala is good for that reason. Whoever reads it with a fatha, it is according to the original, because the chapter of the fa' of the verb in the fa'l has a fatha, like kala and ba'a and the like. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose this, and Hafs stopped bal then begins Rana with a stop that makes the lam clear, not for silence.
83:15: God the Almighty says: No indeed! Indeed they meaning the disbelievers will be veiled from their Lord that Day meaning the Day of Resurrection. It was also said that No is a deterrent and warning, meaning it is not as they say, but rather they will be veiled from their Lord that Day. Al-Zajjaj said: In this verse is evidence that God the Almighty will be seen on the Day of Resurrection. Were it not for that, there would be no benefit in this verse, nor would the status of the disbelievers be diminished by being veiled. God the Almighty said: Some faces, that Day, will be radiant, looking at their Lord. (al-Qiyamah 75:22-23) Thus God the Almighty informed us that the believers will be looking at Him, and He informed us that the disbelievers will be veiled from Him. Malik ibn Anas said about this verse: When He veiled His enemies so that they did not see Him, He revealed Himself to His friends so that they saw Him. Al-Shafi'i said: When He veiled some people with wrath, it indicates that some people will see Him with pleasure. Then he said: By God, if Muhammad ibn Idris had not been certain that he would see his Lord in the afterlife, he would not have worshipped Him in this world. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: When He veiled them in this world from the light of His Oneness, He will veil them in the afterlife from seeing Him. Mujahid said about the verse: veiled: meaning, they are prevented from His honor and mercy. Qatada said: It means that God will not look at them with His mercy, nor will He purify them, and they will have a painful punishment. The majority are of the opinion that they are veiled from seeing Him, so they will not see Him.
83:16: The Almighty says: Then they will surely burn in Hellfire, meaning they will remain in it and will burn in it, never emerging from it. Whenever their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins. (An-Nisa’: 56) and Whenever they die down, We will increase their blazing fire. (al-Isra’ 17:97) It is said that Hellfire is the fourth gate of Hellfire.
83:17: God Almighty says: Then it will be said to them, meaning the keepers of Hell will say to them, This is what you used to deny, to God’s messengers in this world.
83:18: God the Almighty says: No indeed! The record of the righteous is in 'Illiyeen. (No indeed) means truly, and the pause is on (you are lying). It was said: meaning that the matter is not as they say nor as they thought, rather their record is in Sijjin, and the record of the believers is in 'Illiyeen. Muqatil said: No indeed, meaning they do not believe in the torment that they will be subjected to. Then He resumed and said: (The record of the righteous) is raised in 'Illiyeen according to their rank. Ibn Abbas said: meaning in Paradise. It was also narrated from him that he said: Their deeds are in the record of God in the heaven. Ad-Dahhak, Mujahid, and Qatadah said: meaning the seventh heaven in which are the souls of the believers. Ibn Al-Ajlah narrated from Ad-Dahhak that he said: It is the Lote Tree of the Limit, to which everything related to God's command ends and they do not go beyond it. They say: Lord! Your servant so-and-so, and He knows him better than they do. Then a book comes to him from God the Almighty sealed with a guarantee against the torment. That is what God the Almighty says: No indeed! The record of the righteous. On the authority of Ka'b al-Ahbar, who said: When the soul of the believer is taken, it ascends to the heavens, and the gates of heaven are opened for it, and the angels carry it with good tidings, then they go out with it until they reach the Throne, and a scroll is brought out for them from beneath the Throne, which is numbered, and salvation from the reckoning on the Day of Resurrection is sealed in it, and those brought near to God witness it. Qatada also said: (in 'Illiyyun) is above the seventh heaven at the right foot of the Throne. Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: 'Illiyyun is in the seventh heaven under the Throne. Ibn 'Abbas also said: It is a tablet of green emerald suspended from the Throne, and their deeds are written on it. Al-Farra' said: 'Illiyyun is height after height.' It was also said: 'Illiyyun is the highest of places.' It was also said that its meaning is height upon height multiplied, as if it has no limit, and that is why it was pluralized with the letters waw and noon. This is the meaning of al-Tabari. Al-Farra’ said: It is a noun used in the plural, but it has no singular form, like when you say: twenty and thirty. When the Arabs make a plural noun and it does not have a singular or dual form, they use the letter nun for the masculine and feminine. This is the meaning of what Al-Tabari said. Al-Zajjaj said: The declension of this noun is like the declension of the plural, like when you say: this is Qansroon, and I saw Qansroon. Yunus the grammarian said: Its singular is Ali and Aliya, just as they say for a room Aliya, because it is from the word ulu, so when they removed the ta from Aliya, they replaced it with the plural with the letter waw and the letter nun, like they say in ardeen. It was said: Aliyan is an attribute of the angels, for they are the highest assembly, like when one says: So-and-so is among the sons of so-and-so,” meaning he is among them and with them. What is in the report from the hadith of Ibn Umar is that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ((The people of ‘Illiyyin look at Paradise from such and such a place. When a man from the people of ‘Illiyyin looks out, Paradise looks out because of the light of his face. They say: What is this light? It is said: A man from the people of ‘Illiyyin, the righteous, the people of obedience and truthfulness, has looked out.)) And in another report: The people of Paradise will see the people of ‘Illiyyin as one sees a brilliant star on the horizon of the sky. This indicates that ‘Illiyyin is the name of a high place. Some people narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Illiyyin, that he said: He informed us that their deeds and souls are in the fourth heaven.
83:19: Then he said: And what will make you know what is 'Aliyun?' That is, what will make you know, O Muhammad, what is 'Aliyun?' This is to glorify and magnify his high status.
83:20: The Almighty says: A Book inscribed. It was said: A Book inscribed is not an explanation of Illiyeen, but the speech ended with His saying Illiyeen, then He began and said: A Book inscribed, meaning the book of the righteous is a book inscribed. For this reason, the number is reversed in the book of the wicked. Al-Qushayri said this. It was narrated that the angels ascend with the deeds of the servant, and they belittle them [and despise them]. Then, when they reach whatever God wishes of His authority, He reveals to them: You are the guardians over My servant, and I am the watcher of what is in his heart. He sincerely dedicated his deeds to Me, so place him in Illiyeen, for He has forgiven him. And the angels ascend with the deeds of the servant, and they leave him. Then, when they reach whatever God wishes, He reveals to them: You are the guardians over My servant, and I am the watcher of what is in his heart. He did not sincerely devote his deeds to Me, so place him in Sijjin.
83:21: The Almighty's statement: It is witnessed by those brought near meaning the deeds of the righteous are witnessed by the angels brought near to God from every heaven. Wahb and Ibn Ishaq said: The ones brought near here are Israfil, peace be upon him. So when the believer does a righteous deed, the angels ascend with the scroll and it has a light that shines in the heavens like the light of the sun on earth, until it reaches Israfil, who seals it and writes on it. So His statement: It is witnessed by those brought near means he witnesses their writing.
83:22: The Almighty says: Indeed, the righteous meaning the people of truthfulness and obedience. will be in bliss meaning comfort. The word bliss with the fat-ha means enjoyment. It is said: the blessing of God and na’ima so you enjoy yourself. A woman mun’ima and mun’ama have the same meaning. That is, the righteous will be in paradise enjoying themselves.
83:23: The Almighty said: On couches which are the beds in the bridal chambers they will look meaning at what God has prepared for them of honors, as stated by Ikrimah, Ibn Abbas, and Mujahid. Muqatil said: They will look at the people of Hellfire. “And on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): (They will look at their enemies in Hellfire)” mentioned by Al-Mahdawi. And it was said: On couches of His bounty, they will look at His face and His majesty.
83:24: The Almighty said: You will recognize in their faces the radiance of delight meaning its joy, freshness and light. It is said: the plant is fresh: if it blossoms and lights up. The common reading is (َقَقرقف) with a fatha on the ta’ and a kasra on the ra’ (نضرة) in the accusative case, meaning you will recognize, O Muhammad. Abu Ja`far ibn al-Qa`qa`, Ya`qub, Shaibah and Ibn Abi Ishaq read (َقَقرقف) with a damma on the ta’ and a fatha on the ra’, indicating the passive verb (نضرة) in the nominative case.
83:25: The Almighty said: They will be given to drink of pure wine meaning a drink in which there is no adulteration. This was said by Al-Akhfash and Al-Zajjaj. It was also said that nectar is pure wine. In As-Sahah: nectar is the cream of wine. The meaning is the same. Al-Khalil: the purest and best wine. Muqatil and others said: it is old, white wine, pure and bright, Hassan said: They are watered with roses of geckos, and upon them is a papyrus that claps with pure nectar. Another said: Is there no way to youth, and its remembrance is more desirable to me than pure nectar? God the Almighty says: Sealed, its seal is musk. Mujahid said: It is used to seal the last sip. It was also said that the meaning is that when they drink this nectar and what is in the cup is used up, it will be sealed with the seal of musk.
83:26: God the Almighty says: Its seal is musk. Ibn Mas'ud used to say: They will find its end taste of musk. Something similar was narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, who said: Its seal is its last taste. This is good because the nature of drinks is for turbidity to come at the end, so the drink of the people of Paradise was described by having the scent of musk at the end. Masruq narrated from Abdullah that he said: The sealed is the mixed. It was also said: Sealed means sealed and prevented from being touched by anyone until its seal is broken by the righteous. Ali, Alqamah, Shuqayq, al-Dahhak, Tawus, and al-Kisa'i read (his seal) with a fat-ha on the kha and the ta' and an alif between them. Alqamah said: Haven't you seen a woman say to the perfumer: Make his seal musk, meaning its end? The seal and the seal are close in meaning, except that the seal is the noun and the seal is the verbal noun, as al-Farra' said. In al-Sahah: The seal is the clay with which one seals. Mujahid and Ibn Zayd also said: He sealed his vessel with musk instead of clay. Al-Mahdawi narrated it. Al-Farazdaq said: I prefer to close the conclusion Al-A'sha said: The most prominent one is the one with the seal on it That is, it is sealed clay, like nafad meaning manfud and qabd meaning maqbud. Ibn al-Mubarak and Ibn Wahb mentioned - and the wording is from Ibn Wahb - on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas`ud regarding the words of God the Almighty: (its seal is musk): mixed, not with a ring that seals. Do you not see the saying of one of your women: If such and such is mixed with perfume, it is mixed with musk. He said: A white drink like silver with which they seal their last drinks. If a man from the people of this world were to put his hand into it and then take it out, no living being would remain without smelling its fragrance. Ubayy ibn Ka`b narrated: It was said: O Messenger of God, what is the sealed nectar? He said: Pools of wine. It was also said: Sealed in vessels, and it is not what runs in rivers. And God knows best. And in that - that is, and in what we have described of the matter of Paradise - let the competitors compete - that is, let the desirers desire. It is said: I was stingy with something and did not like it to come to me. It was said: The letter fa means to, meaning, to that, let those who work hasten to do so, similar to: For the likes of this, let the workers work (al-Saffat 37:61).
83:27: God the Almighty says: And its mixture meaning the mixture of that nectar is of Tasneem which is a drink poured upon them from above, and it is the most noble drink in Paradise.
