The root of tasneem in the language is to rise, so it is a spring of water that flows from high to low, and from this comes the hump of a camel due to its height on its body, and the same is true of the tasneem of graves. It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah who said: Tasneem is a spring in Paradise from which those brought near drink pure, and the cup of the companions of the right hand is mixed from it and it becomes pleasant. Ibn Abbas said about God the Almighty's saying: And its mixture is of Tasneem He said: This is from what God the Almighty said: And no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes. (Sajdah: 17) It was said: Tasneem is a spring that flows in the air by the power of God the Almighty, and it is poured into the vessels of the people of Paradise according to the amount of its water. When it is full, it holds the water, so not a drop of it falls on the ground, and they do not need to draw water from it, as Qatada said. Ibn Zayd said: We have been informed that it is a spring that flows from beneath the Throne. And so it is in the letters of Al-Hasan. We mentioned it in Surat Al-Insan.
83:28: The Almighty said: A spring from which the nearest of kin will drink meaning the people of the Garden of Eden will drink from it. They are the best of the people of Paradise, purely as such, and it is a mixture for others. A spring is in the accusative case as an expression of praise. Al-Zajjaj said: It is in the accusative case as a state of -َقْينقاbecause it is a direct object, like the Almighty's saying: Or feeding on a day of famine * An orphan (al-Balad 90:14). This is what Al-Farraa said, that it is in the accusative case due to Tasnim. Al-Akhfash says it is in the accusative case due to they will give them to drink meaning they will give them to drink from a spring or from a spring. Al-Mubarrad says it is in the implied case of I mean as an expression of praise.
83:29: The Almighty's saying: Indeed, those who committed crimes is a description of the souls of the unbelievers in this world with the believers, mocking them. What is meant are the leaders of Quraysh from the polytheists. Some people narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: They are Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah, Uqbah bin Abi Mu'ayt, Al-'As bin Wa'il, Al-Aswad bin Abd Yaghuth, Al-'As bin Hisham, Abu Jahl, Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith, and those were among those who believed from the companions of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, like Ammar, Khabbab, Suhayb, and Bilal, laughing in a mocking manner.
83:30: The Almighty said: And when they pass by them when they come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, they wink at each other: they wink at each other and point with their eyes. It was said: that is, they taunt them about Islam and criticize it. It is said: I winked at something with my hand. He said: If I winked at a people's channel, I would break their heels or make them sick. Aisha said: When the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) prostrated, he would nudge me, so I would pull my leg back. The hadith has already been mentioned in An-Nisa’. And I nudged him with my eye. It has also been said that nudge means to find fault. It is said that someone nudges him, meaning he finds fault with him. There is no nudge in someone, meaning a fault. Muqatil said: It was revealed about Ali ibn Abi Talib, who came to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) with a group of Muslims, and the hypocrites nudged them, laughed at them, and winked at each other.
83:31: God the Almighty said: And when they return meaning when they go back to their families, friends and relatives they return joking meaning admiring them. It was also said: admiring their disbelief, joking about the believers. Ibn Al-Qa'qa', Hafs, Al-A'raj and Al-Sulami read: (fakahin) without an alif. The rest read it with an alif. Al-Farra' said: they are two dialects like greed and greed and dharna, and hadhar, and it was mentioned previously in Surah Al-Dukhan and Al-Hamdulillah. It was also said that Al-Fakkah is the most arrogant and haughty person, and Al-Fakih is the soft and indulgent person.
83:32: God Almighty says: And when they see them, meaning when these infidels see the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, they say, ‘Indeed, these are astray,’ in their following of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
83:33: God Almighty says: And they were not sent over them as guardians for their deeds, entrusted with their affairs, and watching over them.
83:34: God Almighty says: So today meaning this day which is the Day of Resurrection those who believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, laugh at the disbelievers just as the disbelievers laughed at them in this world. Its counterpart is at the end of Surah Al-Mu’minun, which has been mentioned previously. Ibn al-Mubarak said: Muhammad ibn Bashar informed us on the authority of Qatada regarding the words of God Almighty: So today those who believe will laugh at the disbelievers. He said: It was mentioned to us that Ka’b used to say: There are windows between Paradise and Hell, and if a believer wanted to look at an enemy he had in this world, he would look out through some of the windows. God Almighty said in another verse: So he looked and saw him in the midst of Hellfire. (al-Saffat 37:55) He said: God Almighty said: God mocks at them. (al-Baqarah 2:15) He said: The people of Hell will be told while he is in Hell: Come out. So the gates of Hell will be opened for them. When they see them opened, they will rush towards them wanting to leave, and the believers will look at them on couches. When they reach the gates, they will be closed in front of them. That is His saying: God mocks at them. (al-Baqarah 2:15) And the believers will laugh at them when they are closed in front of them. That is His saying: So today those who believe will laugh at the disbelievers.
83:35: God Almighty says: Reclining on couches, observing.
83:36: God the Almighty says: "Residing on couches, observing. Is the reward of the disbelievers for what they used to do?" This was mentioned in the beginning of Surah Al-Baqarah. The meaning of (is the reward) is: Are the believers rewarded for their mockery in this world if that was done to them? It was said that it is related to (they are observing), meaning they are observing: Are the disbelievers rewarded? So the meaning of (is the reward) is to report and its position is accusative with (they are observing). It was said that it is a resumption with no syntactic position. It was said that it is an omission in the statement, and the meaning is, some of the believers say to some (is the reward of the disbelievers), meaning I am rewarded and compensated. It is from the root word thaba yathub, meaning it returned. So the reward is what returns to the servant in return for his work, and it is used for good and evil. I have concluded the Surah, and God knows best.
84:1: Meccan according to everyone, and it is twenty-five verses God the Almighty says: When the sky is split open meaning it is cracked and burst with clouds, and clouds are like white clouds. This is what Abu Saleh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. It was narrated on the authority of Ali (peace be upon him) who said: It will be split open from the galaxy. He said: The galaxy is the gate of the sky. This is one of the portents and signs of the Hour.
84:2: The Almighty says: And she listened to her Lord and was entitled to it. That is, she heard, and she was entitled to hear. Its meaning was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and others. Among these is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: God did not listen to anything as He did to a prophet who chanted the Qur'an. That is, God did not listen to anything. The poet said: Deaf when they hear good things mentioned to them, but when they hear bad things mentioned to them, they listen. That is, they heard. Qanab bin Umm Sahib said: If they give permission for a doubt, they fly away with it in joy, but they do not give permission for a righteous person. It was said: The meaning is that God made it obligatory for her to obey His command to split. Ad-Dahhak said: It was obligatory: it obeyed, and it was right for her to obey her Lord, because He created her. It is said: So-and-so has the right to do such-and-such. And the obedience of the heavens means that it does not refrain from what God wanted for it, and the creation of life in it is not far off until it obeys and responds. Qatada said: It was right for it to do that, and from this is the saying of Kathir: If it is a reproach, then welcome and she deserves our reproach. I said:
84:3: The Almighty said: And when the earth is extended meaning, it is spread out and its mountains are leveled. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: It will be extended like the extension of a hide because when hide is extended, every fold in it disappears and it extends and becomes level. Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masoud said: And it will be increased, and its width is such and such, because the creation will stand upon it for the judgment until no human being will have more than a place for his foot, because of the multitude of creation upon it. It was previously mentioned in Surah Ibrahim that the earth will be replaced by another earth, and it is the watchful one according to what Ibn Abbas said, as previously mentioned.
84:4: The Almighty said: And it cast out what was in it and became empty meaning it brought out its dead and became empty of them. Ibn Jubayr said: It cast out what was in its belly of the dead and became empty of those on its back of the living. It was also said that it cast out what was in its belly of its treasures and minerals and became empty of them. That is, its cavity was empty, so there was nothing in its belly. This indicates the enormity of the matter, just as a pregnant woman casts out what is in her belly during times of distress. It was also said: It became empty of what was on its back of its mountains and seas. It was also said: It cast out what it had entrusted and became empty of what it had preserved, because God Almighty entrusted to it His servants, both living and dead, and preserved in it His lands, agriculture and sustenance.
84:5: The Almighty says: And she gave permission to her Lord meaning to throw up her dead. And she had the right meaning she had the right to hear His command. There is a difference of opinion regarding the answer to when, as Al-Farra' said: She gave permission. The waw is redundant, as is the case with and threw down. Ibn Al-Anbari said: Some of the commentators said: The answer to when the sky is split is she gave permission. He claimed that the waw is inserted, but this is a mistake, because the Arabs do not insert the waw except with until - when like in the Almighty's saying: until when they came to it and its gates were opened (al-Zumar 39:73) and with when like in the Almighty's saying: So when they both submitted and he prostrated upon his forehead, * And We called to him (Saffat: 103) meaning We called to him and the waw is not inserted with anything other than these two. It was said: The answer is an implied fa' as if he said: when the sky is split, so O man, you are laboring. It was said: The answer to it is what is indicated by (and he will meet it) meaning if the sky is split open, man will meet his toil. It was said: There is an inversion of the meaning in it.
84:6: God the Almighty said: O mankind, indeed you are striving toward your Lord with exertion and will meet Him When the sky is split. Al-Mubarrad said this. Also from him: The answer is (But as for he who is given his record in his right hand), which is the opinion of Al-Kisa'i, meaning, if the sky is split, then he who is given his record in his right hand, his ruling is such-and-such. Abu Ja'far Al-Nahhas said: This is the most correct and best of what has been said about it. It was said: It means, Remember, 'When the sky is split. It was also said: The answer was omitted because those addressed knew it, meaning, if these things happen, those who deny the resurrection will know their misguidance and loss. It was also said: A question was asked about the time of the Resurrection, so it was said to them: When its signs appear, the Resurrection will take place, and you have seen the consequences of your denial of it. The Quran is like a single verse in that some parts indicate others. Al-Hasan said: His statement, When the sky is split is an oath. The majority disagree with his statement, that it is report and not an oath. God the Almighty says: {O man, indeed you are striving toward your Lord with exertion.} What is meant by man is the human race, O son of Adam. Saeed narrated on the authority of Qatadah: O son of Adam, your striving is weak, so whoever is able to make his striving in obedience to God, let him do so, and there is no power except with God. It was said: He is a helper. Muqatil said: He means Al-Aswad bin Abdul Asad. It was also said: He means Ubayy bin Khalaf. It was also said: He means all the disbelievers. O disbeliever, you are striving. Toiling in the speech of the Arabs means work and earning. Ibn Muqbil said: Life is nothing but two tarts, one of which I die, and the other I struggle to live. Another said: And the smile of every good life passed, and I continued to toil for life and work hard Any work. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: (Indeed, you are striving) meaning you will return (to your Lord with toil) meaning a return inevitably. Then you will meet Him meaning you will meet your Lord. It was also said: meeting your work. Al-Qatabi said (Indeed, you are striving) meaning you will work hard to earn your living until you meet your Lord. Meeting means encounter, meaning you will meet your Lord with your work. It was also said: meaning you will meet the book of your work, because the work has already been completed. For this reason, He said: But as for he who is given his book in his right hand.
84:7: God Almighty says: But as for he who is given his record in his right hand, meaning the believer, he will be brought to account with an easy reckoning, about which there is no discussion.
84:8: Thus, “It was narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the hadith of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: (Whoever is brought to account on the Day of Resurrection will be punished.) She said: I said, O Messenger of God, did God not say, “But as for he who is given his record in his right hand, he will be brought to account with an easy reckoning?” He said: ((That is not the reckoning, but rather the presentation. And whoever is questioned about the account on the Day of Resurrection will be punished.))” Narrated by Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and Al-Tirmidhi.
84:9: He said: A good and authentic hadith. And he will return to his family, rejoicing His wives in Paradise from among the houris (rejoicing) meaning happy and content. It is said that it was revealed about Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Asad, he was the first to migrate from Makkah to Madinah. It was also said: To his family whom he had in this world, to inform them of his salvation and safety. The first is the opinion of Qatada. That is, to his family whom God has prepared for him in Paradise.
84:10: The Almighty's saying: And as for he who is given his record behind his back, was revealed about Al-Aswad ibn Abd Al-Asad, the brother of Abu Salamah, as stated by Ibn Abbas. Then it is general for every believer and disbeliever. Ibn Abbas said: He extends his right hand to take his record, but an angel pulls him away, dislocates his right hand, and takes his record with his left hand from behind his back. Qatada and Muqatil said: He loosens the tablets of his chest and bones, then his hand enters and exits from his back, and he takes his record likewise.
84:11: God Almighty says: Then he will call for destruction, meaning for ruin, and he will say: Woe to me, oh my destruction.
84:12: The Almighty says: And will be roasted in a Blazing Fire meaning, he will enter the Fire until he is roasted in its heat. The two imams, Ibn Amir, and Al-Kisa'i read it (and will be roasted) with a damma on the ya', a fatha on the sad, and a shaddah on the lam, like the Almighty's statement: Then they will roast him in Hellfire (al-Haqqah 69:31) and His statement: And roasting in Hellfire (Al-Waqi'ah: 94). The rest read (and will be roasted) with a fatha on the ya' and a lightened vowel, an intransitive verb, like His statement: Except he who is to roast in Hellfire (al-Saffat 37:63) and His statement: Roasted in the Great Fire (Al-A'la: 12) and His statement: Then indeed, they will roast in Hellfire (al-Mutaffifin 83:16). A third reading was narrated by Abaan on the authority of Asim and Kharijah on the authority of Nafi’ and Ismail Al-Makki on the authority of Ibn Kathir: (yalla) with a damma on the ya’, a sukoon on the sad, and a fatha on the lam, lightened, as it was read (and they will pray) with a damma on the ya’, and likewise in (Al-Ghashiyah) it was also read: (yasalla naran) and they are two dialects of salla and asla, like his saying: ((and he sent down. and he sent down)).
84:13: God the Almighty said: Indeed, he was among his family, rejoicing. Ibn Zayd said: God described the people of Paradise as having fear, sadness, weeping, and compassion in this world, and then He followed that with bliss and happiness in the Hereafter. He recited God the Almighty's statement: "Indeed, we were before fearful among our families. But God was gracious to us and saved us from the punishment of the scorching wind." (al-Tur 52:26-27) He said: And He described the people of Hell as having joy in this world, laughter, and amusement therein. So He said: Indeed, he was among his family, rejoicing.
84:14: The Almighty says: Indeed, he thought that he would never return meaning that he would never return alive and be resurrected to be held accountable, then be rewarded or punished. It is said:ها یهورif he returns. Labid said: A person is like a meteor, whose light turns to ash after it has once been shining. Ikrimah and Dawud ibn Abi Hind said, Yahwar is an Ethiopian word, and it means to return. The two words may agree, as they are a derivative word, and from this comes the word Hawari bread, because it returns to whiteness. Ibn Abbas said: “I did not know what yahwar was until I heard a Bedouin woman calling to her daughter: “Hawri”, meaning return to me. In Arabic, Hawri means to return, and from this comes the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him): (O God, I seek refuge in You from loss after increase) meaning: from returning to deficiency after increase. The same is true for Hawr with the letter Damma. And in the proverb (Hawr in a shell) meaning deficiency within deficiency. It is said about a man whose affairs are being managed. The poet said: They hastened to chew lightly, so they increased, and the blame remains, and the people increased in houris. Al-Hoor is also the noun in the phrase: The mill ground but did not return anything, meaning it did not return any of the flour. Al-Hoor is also: destruction. The rajaz poet said: In a well, there is no secret houri or hair Abu Ubaidah said: Any well of Houris, and La is redundant. It was narrated after the universe and its meaning is the spread of the matter after its completion. Muammar was asked about the Houris after the universe, and he said: It is the Kunti. Abd al-Razzaq said to him: What is the Kunti? He said: A man is righteous then he turns into a bad man. Abu Amr said: It is said to a man when he grows old: Kunti, as if it is attributed to his saying: I was such and such in my youth. He said: I became a coward and I became a scum, and the worst traits of a person are to be a coward and to be a scum A man kneads: if he stands up leaning on the ground due to old age. Ibn al-A'rabi said: Al-Kunti is the one who says: I was young, and I was brave. Al-Kani is the one who says: I had money and I used to give away, and I had horses and I used to ride.
84:15: The Almighty said: Yes meaning the matter is not as he thought, but rather he will turn back to Us and return. Indeed, his Lord was All-Seeing of him before He created him, knowing that he would return to Him. And it was said: Yes, he will turn back and return. Then He resumed and said: Indeed, his Lord was All-Seeing of him from the day He created him until He resurrected him. And it was said: Knowing of what had gone before him of misery and happiness.
84:16: The Almighty said: So I swear not meaning I swear, and no is a connection. By the twilight meaning by the redness that appears at sunset until the final 'Isha' prayer comes. Ashhab, Abdullah ibn al-Hakam, Yahya ibn Yahya, and many others said on the authority of Malik: The twilight is the redness in the sunset. When the redness disappears, the time for the sunset prayer has ended and the 'Isha' prayer becomes obligatory. Ibn Wahb narrated that more than one person told me on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, Muadh ibn Jabal, Ubadah ibn al-Samit, Shaddad ibn Aws, and Abu Hurayrah: The twilight is the redness, and Malik ibn Anas said the same. Among the Companions mentioned by others besides Ibn Wahb are: Umar, Ibn Umar, Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, Anas, Abu Qatadah, Jabir ibn Abdullah, and Ibn al-Zubayr. Among the Followers: Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ibn al-Musayyab, Tawus, Abdullah ibn Dinar, and al-Zuhri. Among the jurists, al-Awza'i, Malik, al-Shafi'i, Abu Yusuf, Abu Thawr, Abu Ubaid, Ahmad, and Ishaq said the same. It was said: It is whiteness. This was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurairah, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, al-Awza’i, and Abu Hanifa in one of the two narrations from him. Asad ibn Amr narrated that he went back on it. It was narrated from Ibn Umar as well that it is whiteness, and the first choice is made because most of the Companions, Followers, and jurists agreed with it, and because the evidence of the speech of the Arabs, derivation, and the Sunnah testifies to it. Al-Farra’ said: I heard some Arabs say about a garment that had dye on it: It was as if it was twilight and it was red. This is evidence of redness. The poet said: And red in color as the red of twilight Another said: Rise up, boy, I mean, do not be confused by time with a cup filled with twilight The ochre is called twilight. In As-Sahah: twilight is the remaining sunlight and its redness at the beginning of the night until close to darkness. Al-Khalil said: twilight: the redness, from sunset to the time of the last evening prayer, when it goes away it is said: the twilight has disappeared. Then it was said: the origin of the word is from the softness of something, it is said: something is twilight, meaning it has no cohesion due to its softness. And he pitied him: meaning his heart softened towards him, and compassion: the noun from pity, which is the softness of the heart, and so is twilight, the poet said: She loves my life and I love her death out of compassion, and death is the most honorable fight for the sanctuary Twilight: the remaining sunlight and its redness, as if that thinness is from the sunlight. The wise men claimed that the whiteness never sets. Al-Khalil said: I climbed the lighthouse of Alexandria and watched the whiteness, and I saw it moving from horizon to horizon, but I did not see it set. Ibn Abi Uways said: I saw it continue until dawn. Our scholars said: Since its time was not specified, its consideration was dropped. In Sunan Abi Dawud, on the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Bashir, he said: I inform you of the time of the last ‘Isha’ prayer. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to pray it when the moon set on the third day. This is a specification, and the ruling is dependent on the first part of the name. It cannot be said: It will be invalidated for you at the first dawn, because the first dawn has no ruling regarding prayer or abstaining from food, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) explained the dawn by his words and actions, saying: (And the dawn is not that you say thus - and he raised his hand upwards - but the dawn is that you say thus and he stretched it out) Its explanation has already been mentioned in the verse on fasting in Surat Al-Baqarah, so there is no point in repeating it. Mujahid said: Al-Shafaq is the entire day. Do you not see it? He said: (And the night and what it covers). Ikrimah said: What remains of the day. Al-Shafaq is also: the bad of things. It is said: Ata’ Mushfaq, meaning he is small. Al-Kumait said: A king more arrogant than kings, his hands are milked by those who ask for them, and he is merciless
84:17: The Almighty's saying: And the night and what it wraps up meaning it gathers, joins and wraps up. Its origin is from the chapter of the Sultan and his anger. If he had not come out to the servants from the door of mercy, the servants would not have been able to control his coming. Rather, he came out from the door of mercy and joked with it. So the creation calmed down before him, then they were terrified and met and withdrew, and each returned to his home and settled therein in fear of him. This is the saying of the Almighty: And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day that you may rest therein (Al-Qasas 28:73) meaning by night and that you may seek of His bounty (Al-Qasas 28:73) meaning by day as mentioned above. So the night gathers and joins what was spread out during the day in its disposal. This is the meaning of the saying of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Muqatil and others. Dhabi' ibn al-Hariq al-Barjami said: For I and you, and my longing for you, are like one who holds water but whose fingers have not given it to drink. He says: He has nothing of that in his hand, just as there is nothing in the hand of the one who holds the water. So when the night covers the mountains, trees, seas, and earth and they gather for him, then he has poured them out. And wasq is to gather something together. You say: I poured it at the bottom of it a wasq. And from this, a lot of food that is gathered together is called wasq, which is sixty sa’. And food that is muwasq means gathered, and camels that are mustawsaqah means gathered together. Al-Zajir said: We have truly beautiful, well-mannered camels, if only they could find a driver. Akrima said: And what was driven means what was driven of something to where it is located. So, wasq means expelled. From this, it is said of the prey of camels, sheep, and donkeys: wasqa’a. The poet said: As the traces of the document are traced On the authority of Ibn Abbas: (And what was carried) meaning what was concealed and covered. And on his authority also: And what was carried, and everything that I carried I carried, and the Arabs say: I will not do it as long as my eyes carried the water, meaning I carried it. And the she-camel carried a wasqan: meaning it carried and closed its womb on the water, so it is a wasq she-camel, and wasq she-camels like na’im and niyam, and sahib and sahab. Bishr ibn Abi Khazim said: He kept urging them on until the tricks became clear from the wicked. And also musical instruments. And the camel was laden: he carried its load, and the palm tree was laden: its load increased. Yaman, Al-Dahhak, and Muqatil bin Sulaiman said: He carried from the darkness. Muqatil said: Or he carried from the stars. Al-Qushayri: The meaning of carried is to gather and collect, and the night covers everything with its darkness, so when it covers it, it has laden it. And this oath is an oath by all creatures, because the night includes them, like the saying of the Most High: So I swear by what you see * and what you do not see. Ibn Jubayr said: And what was laden means what was done in it, meaning the night prayers and seeking forgiveness in the early hours of the morning. The poet said: One day you see us righteous, and another time you see us like a greedy, corrupt person. Like a worker.
84:18: The Almighty said: And the moon when it is full meaning it is complete, gathered, and level. Al-Hasan said: It is full and level. Ibn Abbas: It is level. Qatada: It became round. Al-Farraa: Its being full and level on the nights of the full moon. It is a causative verb from the word wasq which means gathering. It is said: I watered it so it was filled, just as it is said: I connected it so it was connected. It is also said: So-and-so's matter is consistent, meaning it is gathered together and in good order. It is also said: Something is consistent if it is continuous.
84:19: The Almighty said: You will surely ascend from one stage to another. Abu Omar, Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Masruq, Abu Wa'il, Mujahid, Al-Nakha'i, Al-Sha'bi, Ibn Kathir, Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i read Latarakaban with a fat-ha on the ba', addressing the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, meaning, O Muhammad, you will surely ascend from one stage to another, as Ibn Abbas said. Al-Sha'bi: You will surely ascend, O Muhammad, from heaven to heaven, degree to degree, and rank to rank, in drawing near to God the Most High. Ibn Mas'ud: You will surely ascend the heaven from one state to another, meaning the states that God the Most High has described it with, such as splitting and folding, and being sometimes like molten metal and sometimes like its solid. And on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah: (layer after layer) he said: The heaven changes from one state to another. From being a sperm-drop, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, then alive and dead, rich and poor. So the address to the human mentioned in His saying, O man, indeed you are striving is a noun for the species, and its meaning is people. The rest read (you will surely ascend) with a damma on the ba', addressing people. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose this. He said: Because the meaning of the people is more similar to it than to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, because of what was mentioned before this verse: whoever is given his book in his right hand and whoever is given his book in his left. That is, you will experience one state after another of the hardships of the Day of Resurrection, or you will follow the example of those who came before you in denying and fabricating lies against the prophets. I said: And all of it is intended, and there are hadiths about that. Abu Naim al-Hafiz narrated on the authority of Ja`far ibn Muhammad ibn `Ali on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The son of Adam is in heedlessness of what God Almighty has created. God, there is no god but Him. When He wants to create him, He says to the angel: Write his provision, his legacy, and his lifespan, and write whether he is wretched or happy. Then that angel is taken away, and God sends another angel to guard him until he reaches maturity. Then God sends two angels to write down his good and bad deeds. When death comes to him, those two angels are taken away. Then the Angel of Death, peace be upon him, comes to him and takes his soul. When death comes to him, those two angels are taken away. Then the Angel of Death, peace be upon him, comes to him and takes his soul. When he enters his grave, he returns the soul to his body. Then the Angel of Death is taken away. Then the Angel of the grave comes to him and tests him. Then they are taken away. When the Hour comes, the Angel of Good and the Angel of Bad descend upon him, and they open a book tied around his neck. Then they attend with him, one as a driver and the other as a witness.” Then God Almighty said: You were certainly heedless of this, but We have removed your covering, and your sight today is sharp. (Qaf: 22) The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You will surely ascend from one level to another. He said: One state after another. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A great matter is before you, so seek help from God, the Almighty. This hadith includes the states that befall a person, from the time he is created until the time he is resurrected, and all of it is one hardship after another, life then death, then resurrection then recompense, and in each of these states there are hardships. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: (You will follow the ways of those who came before you, hand span by hand span, cubit by cubit, to the point that if they entered the hole of a lizard, you would enter it too.) They said: O Messenger of God, do you mean the Jews and Christians? He said: (Then who)? Narrated by Al-Bukhari. As for the sayings of the commentators, Ikrimah said: One state after another, a weaned child after a suckling child, and an old man after a young man. The poet said: Likewise, if a person's life is extended, he will be placed on a new stage after the next. On the authority of Makhul: Every twenty years you will find a situation that you were not experiencing before. Al-Hasan said: One situation after another, ease after hardship, and hardship after ease, wealth after poverty, and poverty after wealth, and health after sickness, after health. Saeed bin Jubair: One status after another, some people were humble in this world and were elevated in the hereafter, and some people were elevated in this world and were humbled in the hereafter. It was said: One status after another, and one level after another, because whoever is righteous will be called to righteousness above him, and whoever is corrupt will be called to corruption above him, because everything follows its form. Ibn Zayd: And you will surely move from the level of this world to the level of the Hereafter. Ibn Abbas said: Hardships and terrors: death, then resurrection, then presentation. The Arabs say to someone who has fallen into a severe matter: He has fallen into the daughters of a level, and one of the daughters of a level. And from this, the severe disaster is called: mother of a level, and one of the daughters of a level. And its origin is from snakes, as a snake is called mother of a level due to its transformation. And the level in the language: the state as we described. Al-Aqra’ bin Habis Al-Tamimi said: I am a man who has milked the best parts of time, and I have been led from one side to the next. This is the clearest evidence of the creation of the world and the proof of the Creator. The wise men said: He who is in one state today and in another state tomorrow should know that his management is up to someone other than Him. Abu Bakr al-Warraq was asked: What is the evidence that this world has a Creator? He said: The change of states, the inability of strength, the weakness of the pillars, the subjugation of intention, and the cancellation of resolve. It is said: A group of people and a group of locusts came to us, meaning a group. Al-Abbas said in praise of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Move from the cross to the womb if the world has passed away the plate has appeared Any century of people. It is the layers of the earth, meaning it filled it. The layer is also: a thin bone that separates the two vertebrae. It is said: a layer of the night has passed, and a layer of the day: meaning most of it. The layer: one of the layers, so it is common. It was read (La tarakaban) with a kasra on the ba, addressing the self and (li rakban) with a ya on the basis of li rakban al-insan. And (an tabaqan) is in the accusative case as an attribute of (-tabaqan), meaning a layer exceeding a layer. Or a state of the pronoun in (La tarakaban), a layer exceeding a layer, or exceeding or passing according to the reading.
84:20: The Almighty says: So why do they not believe? Meaning, what is preventing them from believing after the verses were made clear to them and the evidence was established? This is a question of denial. It was also said: It is amazement, meaning they were amazed at them for abandoning belief despite these verses.
84:21: God the Almighty said: And when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate meaning they do not pray. In the Sahih, it is narrated that Abu Hurairah recited When the heaven is split and prostrated in it. When he finished, he informed them that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prostrated in it. Malik said: It is not one of the obligatory prostrations, because the meaning is that they do not submit or obey in performing its obligations. Ibn al-Arabi said: The correct view is that it is from him, and it is the narration of the Medinans from him, and the Qur'an and Sunnah support it. Ibn al-Arabi said: When I led the people in prayer, I omitted reciting it, because if I prostrated, they would deny it, and if I omitted it, it would be a shortcoming on my part, so I avoided it unless I prayed alone. This is the fulfillment of the promise of the Truthful One that good should be evil and evil should be good. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Aisha: Were it not for the recent disbelief of your people, I would have demolished the House and restored it to the foundations of Abraham. Our Sheikh Abu Bakr al-Fihri used to raise his hands when bowing and when rising from it. This is the doctrine of Malik and al-Shafi’i, and it is done by the Shi’a. One day, he came to me in the guardhouse of Ibn al-Shawa in al-Thaghr the place where I teach during the noon prayer. He entered the mosque from the guardhouse mentioned above and went forward to the row. I was in the back, sitting on the sea windows, breathing the wind from the intense heat. With me in one row was Abu Thamanah, the chief and commander of the sea, with a group of his companions, waiting for the prayer and looking at the ships under the port. When the Sheikh raised his hands during bowing and when rising from it, Abu Thamanah and his companions said, Don’t you see how this easterner entered our mosque? Go to him, kill him, and throw him into the sea so that no one can see you. My heart leapt from my chest and I said, Glory be to God, this is al-Tartushi, the jurist of the time. They said to me, And why did he not raise his hands? I said, “That is what the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to do.” This is the doctrine of Malik, according to the narrations of the people of Medina from him. I tried to calm them down and keep them quiet until he finished his prayer. I went with him to the house from the guard. He saw the change in my face and disapproved of it. He asked me and I told him. He laughed and said, How can I be killed for following a Sunnah? I said to him, This is not permissible for you, for you are among people who, if you follow it, will rise up against you and perhaps your blood will be shed. He said, Leave this talk and do something else.
84:22: God Almighty says: Rather, those who disbelieve deny Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what he brought. Muqatil said: It was revealed about Banu Amr ibn Umair, who were four, two of whom converted to Islam. It was also said: It applies to all disbelievers.
84:23: The Almighty said: And God knows best what they conceal meaning what they conceal in their souls of disbelief. This is what Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Mujahid said: They conceal their actions. Ibn Zayd: They collect good and bad deeds, taken from the container that collects what is in it. It is said: I stored the provisions and goods: if you put them in the container. The poet said: Goodness is more lasting, even if it takes a long time, and evil hides the provisions you have stored. And he memorized it, meaning he preserved it. You say: I memorized the hadith, I memorized it, and a retentive ear. And it was mentioned before.
84:24: The Almighty says: Then give them tidings of a painful punishment meaning, painful in Hell, for their denial. In other words, make that like good tidings. Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds is an isolated exception, as if He said: But those who believe in the testimony that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and do righteous deeds, meaning, they fulfill the obligations imposed upon them.
84:25: The Almighty says: For them is a reward meaning a recompense uninterrupted meaning not diminished or cut off. It is said: Mannat al-Habl meaning you cut the rope. This has been mentioned before. Nafi’ ibn al-Azraq asked Ibn Abbas about his statement: For them is a reward uninterrupted and he said: Uninterrupted. He said: Do the Arabs know that? He said: Yes, Akhu Yashkur knew it when he said: You see their creation from the speed of the return, as if it were dust. Al-Mubarrad said: Al-Manin is the dust, because it cuts it behind it. And every weak person is Manin and Manmunoon. It was said: Not Manmunoon means that He does not bestow it upon them. Some scholars mentioned that His statement (Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds) is not an exception, but rather it has the meaning of the conjunction and, as if he said: And those who believe. The discussion of this has already passed in (Al-Baqarah), and praise be to God. Surah Al-Inshiqaq is complete.
85:1: Meccan by consensus. It has twenty-two verses. God the Almighty said: And the heaven with the mansions is an oath by which God the Almighty swore. There are four opinions regarding al-Buruj 85:First: With the stars, said Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Mujahid, and Ad-Dahhak. Second: Palaces, said Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, and Mujahid as well. Ikrimah said: They are palaces in the sky. Mujahid said: The mansions contain guards. Third: With good character, said Al-Minhal ibn Amr. Fourth: With the mansions, said Abu Ubaidah and Yahya ibn Salam. They are twelve mansions, which are the mansions of the planets, the sun, and the moon. The moon travels in each sign for two days and a third of a day, so that is twenty-eight days, then it disappears for two nights, and the sun travels in each sign for a month. They are: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces. In Arabic, al-Buruj means palaces. God the Almighty said: And if you were in lofty towers. (al-Nisa 4:78), as mentioned previously.
85:2: God Almighty says: And the promised day meaning the promised day. This is another category, namely the Day of Resurrection, with no difference of opinion among the interpreters. Ibn Abbas said: The people of heaven and earth were promised that they would meet on that day.
85:4: The Almighty says: He killed the companions of the trench meaning he was cursed. Ibn Abbas said: Everything in the Qur'an that says killed is a curse. This is the answer to the oath - according to Al-Farra' - and the lam is implied, like His statement: ((And by the sun and its brightness. Then he said, He has succeeded who purifies it): meaning he has succeeded. It was said: There is an inversion in it, meaning he killed the companions of the trench and the sky with its constellations, as Abu Hatim Al-Sijistani said. Ibn Al-Anbari said: This is a mistake, because it is not permissible for a speaker to say, By God, Zaid stood up, meaning By God, Zaid stood up. Some people said: The answer to the oath is Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is severe (Al-Buruj 74:12), and this is ugly, because the conversation between them has been prolonged. It was said: Indeed, those who were tried (Al-Buruj 74:10), and it was said: The answer to the oath is omitted, meaning By the sky with its constellations, you will be resurrected. This is the preferred opinion of Ibn Al-Anbari. The trench is the large, rectangular crack in the earth like a trench, and its plural is akhādīd. And from it comes the word khid for tear ducts, and mukhada because the cheek is placed on it. And it is said: A man’s face is rife if it has furrows from wounds. Tarafa said: A face as if the sun had covered it with its pure color, unblemished
85:5: The Almighty said: The Fire with Fuel (the Fire) instead of (the Trench) as a substitute for inclusion. And (the Fuel) with the opening of the waw is the reading of the general public, and it is firewood. Qatada, Abu Raja' and Nasr bin Asim read with the damma of the waw as a source, meaning the one with the burning and inflammation. It was said: the one with the fuel in people's bodies. Ashhab Al-Uqaili, Abu Al-Samal Al-Adawi and Ibn Al-Sameefa' read (the Fire with) with the nominative case in both of them, meaning the fire with the fuel burned them.
85:6: The Almighty said: When they were sitting on it meaning those who dug the trenches and sat on them, throwing the believers into them, and they were in Najran during the period between Jesus and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The narrators differed in their hadith. The meaning is close. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Suhaib: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: There was a king among those who came before you, and he had a magician. When the magician grew old, he said to the king, I have grown old, so send me a boy to whom I may teach magic. So the boy was sent to him to teach him. On his way, whenever he took a monk, he sat beside him and listened to his speech and was pleased with him. Whenever he came to the magician, he would pass by the monk and sit beside him. When he came to the magician, he would hit him. So the monk complained about that to the monk, who said, “When you fear the magician, say, ‘My family has detained me.’ And when you fear your family, say, ‘The magician has detained me.’ While he was like that, he came upon a huge beast that had detained the people. He said, “Today I will know whether the magician or the monk is better.” The monk took a stone and said, O God, if the monk’s affair is more beloved to You than the magician’s affair, then kill this beast so that the people may move on. So he threw it and killed it, and the people moved on. The monk came and told him, and the monk said to him, “My son, you are better than me today. What I see in your affair is that which has come to pass, and you will be tested. If you are tested, do not guide me.” The boy cured the blind and the lepers, and treated people of all kinds of ailments. A companion of the king who had gone blind heard of this, so he came to him with many gifts and said, All this is yours if you cure me. He said, “I do not cure anyone; only God cures. If you believe in God, I will call upon God, and He will cure you.” So he believed in God, and God cured him. Then he came to the king and sat beside him as he had always sat. The king said to him, Who restored your sight? He said, My Lord. He said, Do you have a lord other than me? He said, My Lord, and your Lord is God. So the king seized him and continued torturing him until he directed him to the boy. Then the boy was brought to him, and the king said to him, O my son, has your magic reached such a level that you can cure the blind and the leper, and you do such and such? He said, I do not cure anyone; only God cures. So the king seized him and continued torturing him until he directed him to the monk. Then the monk was brought to him, and it was said to him, Abandon your religion. But he refused, so he called for a saw and placed it in the parting of his head and split it in two. Then the king's companion was brought and it was said to him, Repent of your religion. He refused and refused again. So the king placed the saw in the parting of his head and split it in two. Then the boy was brought and it was said to him, Repent of your religion. He refused and refused again. So the king handed him over to a group of his companions and said, "Take him to such-and-such a mountain and climb it with him. When you reach the top of it, he must renounce his religion; otherwise, throw him down." So they took him and climbed the mountain. The boy said, O God, protect me from them however You wish. The mountain shook and they fell down. Then he came walking to the king. The king said, What happened to your companions? He said, God protected me from them. So the king handed him over to a group of his companions and said, "Go and carry him in a boat and take him to the middle of the sea. If he renounces his religion, well and good, otherwise throw him down." So they took him and he said, O God, protect me from them however You wish. The ship capsized and they drowned. Then he came walking to the king, and the king said to him, What happened to your companions? He said, May God suffice me against them. Then he said to the king, You will not kill me until you do what I command you. The king said, And what is that? He said, “Gather the people in one plain and crucify me on a tree-trunk. Then take an arrow from my quiver and place the arrow in the bow and say, ‘In the name of God, the Lord of the boy,’ then shoot me, for if you do that you will kill me.” So he gathered the people in one plain and crucified him on a tree-trunk, then shot him. The arrow hit his temple, so the king put his hand to his temple, where the arrow had been, and he died. The people said, We believe in the Lord of the boy! We believe in the Lord of the boy! We believe in the Lord of the boy! So the king was brought and it was said to him, Have you seen what you were afraid of? By God, your caution has come upon you, and the people have believed. So he ordered that a trench be dug into it - or it was said to him, Cram it - and they did so, until a woman came with her child, and she hesitated to fall into it, so the boy said to her: O slave girl, be patient, for you are following the truth. Narrated by al-Tirmidhi with the same meaning. And in it: And on the boy’s path was a monk in a monastery. Muammar said: I think that the people who kept the monasteries were Muslims at that time. And in it: “The beast that stopped the people was a lion, and the boy was buried - he said - and it is mentioned that he was taken out during the time of Umar ibn al-Khattab with his finger on his temple as he had placed it when he was killed.” And he said: A strange hadith. And al-Dahhak narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: There was a king in Najran, and among his subjects was a man who had a boy, so he sent him to a magician to teach him magic. The boy’s path was to a monk who was reading the Bible, and he was pleased with what he heard from the monk, so he entered the monk’s religion. One day he came and saw a huge snake blocking the people’s path, so he took a stone and said: In the name of God, Lord of the heavens and the earth. And between them, so he killed her. And he mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above. And that when the king shot him with the arrow and killed him, the people of the king’s kingdom said: There is no god but the god Abdullah bin Thamir, and that was the name of the boy. So the king became angry and ordered that trenches be dug, and wood and fire were gathered in them, and the people of his kingdom were presented to them. Whoever renounced monotheism was left alone, and whoever remained in his religion was thrown into the fire. A nursing mother was brought and it was said to her: Return from your religion or we will throw you and your child into the fire. He said: “She was afraid and wanted to return, but the nursing boy said to her: O my mother, remain steadfast in what you are doing, for it is only a secret.” So they threw her and her son. Abu Salih narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the fire rose from the trench and was forty cubits above the king and his companions and burned them. Ad-Dahhak said: They were a group of Christians who were forty cubits above the king and his companions, so it burned them. Ad-Dahhak said: They are a group of Christians who lived in Yemen forty years before the mission of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Yusuf ibn Shuraheel ibn Tubba’ al-Himyari took them, and they were more than eighty men. He dug a trench for them and burned them in it. Al-Mawardi narrated it, and al-Tha’labi narrated from him that the People of the Trench from the Children of Israel took men and women, dug trenches for them, then lit a fire in them, and then made the believers stand over them. They were asked: Will you disbelieve or will you be thrown into the fire? They claim that it was Daniel and his companions, and Atiyah al-Awfi said the same. Something similar was narrated from Ibn Abbas. Ali may God be pleased with him said: A king became drunk and had intercourse with his sister. He wanted to make that a law for his subjects, but they refused. She suggested to him that he deliver a sermon stating that God, the Almighty, has permitted marriage to sisters, but he refused. She suggested to him that he dig a trench for them and throw into it everyone who disobeyed him. He did so. It was said: And their remnants used to marry sisters, and they are the Magians, and they were people of the book. It was also narrated from Ali: The reason for the People of the Trench was that a prophet was sent by God to Abyssinia, and some people followed him, so their people dug a trench for them, and whoever followed the prophet was thrown into it. A woman with a baby son was brought to her and she was alarmed, so he said to her: O mother, go on and do not be alarmed. Ayoub said on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: Ayoub on the authority of Ikrimah said: The People of the Trench were killed, he said: They were from your people from Sijistan. Al-Kalbi said: They are the Christians of Najran, they captured a group of believers there, so they dug seven trenches for them, each trench forty cubits long and twelve cubits wide. Then they poured oil and firewood into it, then they showed them to it, and whoever refused they threw him into it. It was said: They were a group of Christians who were in Constantinople during the time of Constantine. Muqatil said: The People of the Trench were three, one in Najran, another in Syria, and another in Persia. The one in Syria was Antinianus the Roman, the one in Persia was Nebuchadnezzar, and the one in the land of the Arabs was Yusuf ibn Dhi Nuwas. God did not send down a Quran about the one in Persia in Syria, but He sent down a Quran about the one in Najran. Two Muslim men, one of them was in Tihamah and the other in Najran, one of them hired himself out, so he began to work and read the Bible. The daughter of the tenant read the light while reading the Bible, so she told her father and he converted to Islam. They numbered eighty-seven between men and women, after Jesus was taken up. Yusuf ibn Dhi Nuwas ibn Tubba al-Himyari dug a trench for them, lit a fire in it, and presented them with disbelief. Whoever refused to disbelieve, he threw him into the fire, and said: Whoever renounces the religion of Jesus shall not be thrown. A woman had a young son who did not speak, so she returned, and her son said to her: O mother, I see before you a fire that will not be extinguished. So they both threw themselves into the fire, and God put her and her son in Paradise. So seventy-seven people were thrown in one day. Ibn Ishaq said on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih: There was a man from the remnants of the followers of the religion of Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, called Qayyumun. He was a righteous, hardworking man, devout in this world, and his prayers were answered. He used to travel from one village to another, and he would never know a village without passing by it. He was a builder who worked with clay. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: The people of Najran were polytheists who worshipped idols, and there was a builder who worked with clay. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: The people of Najran were polytheists who worshipped idols. In one of its villages near Najran, there was a magician who taught magic to the boys of Najran. When Qaymun settled there, he built a tent between Najran and the village where the magician was. The people of Najran began to send their boys to that magician to teach them magic. Al-Thamir sent Abdullah ibn al-Thamir to him, and he was with the boys of Najran. When Abdullah passed by the owner of the tent, he was pleased with what he saw of his prayer and worship, so he would sit next to him and listen to him until he converted to Islam. He believed in the oneness of God and worshipped Him, and he began to ask him about the greatest name of God. Abu al-Thamir thought that his son would go to the magician as boys go. When Abdullah saw that the monk had been stingy with him in teaching him the Greatest Name of God, he took a cup and gathered them. Then he left no name of God that he knew but he wrote it in a cup. When he passed by the Greatest Name, he threw his cup into it. The cup jumped until it came out of it without harming it at all. He took it and went to its companion and informed him that he had learned the Greatest Name of God which he had concealed from him. The monk asked, What is it? He said, Such and such and such. The companion asked, How did you know it? The monk told him what he had done. The monk said, O son of my brother, you have found it, so be patient, for I do not think you will do so. Whenever Abdullah ibn Thamir entered Najran, he would not encounter anyone afflicted except that he would say, O Abdullah, will you affirm the Oneness of God and enter my religion, so that I may supplicate to God for you and He may punish you for the affliction you are in? He said: Yes. So he would declare God’s oneness and submit to Him, and he would supplicate to God for him and he would be cured, until there was no one in Najran who was afflicted with any harm except that he would come to him and follow him in his religion and supplicate for him and he would be cured. Then his status would be brought before their king, who summoned him and said: You have corrupted the people of my village for me, and you have opposed my religion and the religion of my fathers, so I will kill you. He said: You will not be able to do that. So he would send him to the high mountain, and he would be thrown off his head and he would fall to the ground with no harm done to him. And he would send him to the waters of Najran, seas in which nothing is thrown without perishing. He would be thrown into them and he would come out with no harm done to him. When he defeated him, Abdullah ibn Thamir said to him: By God, you will not be able to kill me until you declare God’s oneness and believe in what I believe in, for if you do that, you will have power over me and kill me. So God declared that king to be one and bore witness to his testimony. Then he struck him with a stick, causing a small wound, not a large one, and killed him. The king died on the spot. The people of Najran united on the religion of Abdullah ibn Thamir, and he followed what Jesus, son of Mary, brought of the Gospel and his rule. Then the same events befell the people of their religion, and from that was the origin of Christianity in Najran. Dhu Nuwas the Jew marched towards them with his soldiers from Himyar. He invited them to Judaism and gave them the choice between that or death. They chose death. So he dug a trench for them, burned it with fire, killed with the sword, and mutilated them until he killed twenty thousand of them. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Twelve thousand. Al-Kalbi said: The people of the trench were seventy thousand. Wahb said: Then when Aryat took control of Yemen, Dhu Nuwas fled, and he rode into the sea on his horse and drowned. He said that Ishaq said: This Dhu Nuwas’s name was Zur’ah ibn Taban As’ad Al-Himyari, and he was also called Yusuf, and he had braids of hair that were tangled, so he was called Dhu Nuwas. He did this to the people of Najran, and a man named Dos Dhu Tha’laban escaped from them, and he drove the Abyssinians to triumph over them, so they took over Yemen and Dhu Nuwas perished in the sea, having thrown himself into it, and about him Amr ibn Ma’di Karib says: You threaten me as if you were a shepherd with the most comfortable life or a sleepless one And there was before you a kingdom of comfort and a permanent kingdom among the people It is ancient, from the time of Ad, the great conqueror of tyranny and cruelty. Time has removed their kingdom, so it has become a transfer from one people to another. Dhu Ra'in: A king of the kings of Himyar. Ra'in was his fortress and he was a descendant of Al-Harith bin Amr bin Himyar bin Saba. Question: Our scholars said: God the Almighty informed the believers of this nation in this verse of the hardships that the monotheists before them faced, and He comforted them with that. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) told them the story of the boy so that they would be patient with the harm, pain, and hardships they faced, so that they would take as an example the example of such a boy in his patience, steadfastness in the truth, and his adherence to it, and his sacrifice of himself in the right to spread his call and bring people into the religion despite his young age and great patience. Likewise, the monk was patient in adhering to the truth until he was sawed. Likewise, many people, when they believed in God the Almighty and faith was firmly established in their hearts, were patient in being thrown into the fire and did not renounce their religion. Ibn al-Arabi: We believe that this has been abrogated, as explained previously in Surah An-Nahl. I said: It is not abrogated according to us, and patience with that is better for the one who has a strong soul and firm religion. God Almighty said, informing about Luqman 31:“O my son, establish prayer, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and be patient over what befalls you. Indeed, [all] that is of the matters [requiring] determination.” (Luqman 31:17) Abu Saeed Al-Khudri narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Indeed, among the greatest jihad is a word of justice in the presence of an unjust ruler. Al-Tirmidhi included it and said: A good, rare hadith. Ibn Sinjar Muhammad ibn Sinjar narrated on the authority of Umaimah, the freed slave of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “I was performing ablution for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when a man came to him and said: Advise me. He said: ‘Do not associate anything with God, even if you are cut into pieces or burned with fire....’” The hadith: Our scholars said: Many of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, were tested with killing, crucifixion, and severe torture, but they were patient and did not pay attention to any of that. The story of Asim, Khubayb, and their companions and what they encountered of wars, trials, killing, captivity, burning, and other things is sufficient for you. It has been mentioned in An-Nahl that this is a consensus of those who are strong in this regard, so reflect on it there. His Almighty’s saying: The companions of the trench were killed is a supplication for those infidels to be removed from the mercy of God Almighty. It was said that its meaning is to inform about the killing of those believers, that is, they were killed by fire and they were patient. It was also said that it is to inform about those wrongdoers, as it was narrated that God took the souls of those who were thrown into the trench before they reached the fire, and a fire came out of the trench and burned those who were sitting on it. It was said that the believers were saved, and the fire burned those who were sitting. This was mentioned by An-Nahhas. The meaning of on it is near it, and on means near. It was said that on it is on what is close to it from the edges of the trench, as he said: And the dew and the shaved head were on the fire The factor in (if) is (killed), meaning they were cursed at that time:
85:7: The Almighty said: And they are witnesses to what they do to the believers. That is, present: meaning the disbelievers. They were present to the believers in disbelief, and whoever refused, they threw him into the fire. In that, they were described as harsh and then as serious in that. It was said: (on) means with, that is, they are witnesses to what they do to the believers.
85:8: The Almighty said: And they did not resent them. Abu Haywah read (they resented) with a kasra, but the correct pronunciation is the fatha. The statement about it has already been mentioned in (Bara’ah): That is, the king and his companions did not resent those whom they burned: except that they believe that is, except that they believe: in God, the Almighty that is, the Victorious, the Invincible: the Praiseworthy that is, the Praised One in every situation.
85:9: The Almighty says: To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He has no partner or equal in them. And God is Witness over all things, meaning He knows the deeds of His creation; nothing is hidden from Him.
85:10: The Almighty says: Indeed, those who put the believing men and believing women to trial meaning burned them with fire. The Arabs say: So-and-so put the dirham or the dinar to trial, meaning he put it in a bellows to see its quality. A dinar is torn. The goldsmith is called fattan, as is Satan. Paper is called fatin, meaning burnt silver. A free woman is called fatin, meaning as if she burned her stones with fire, due to its blackness. Then they did not repent, meaning from the ugliness of their actions despite the signs and clear proofs that God revealed to this tyrannical, unjust king and his people through the boy. For them is the punishment of Hell for their disbelief. For them is the punishment of the burning in this world for burning the believers with fire. This was mentioned previously from Ibn Abbas. It was said: For them is the punishment of the burning, meaning that in the Hereafter they will have a punishment in addition to the punishment of their disbelief in what they burned the believers. It was said: For them is a punishment, and the punishment of Hell is the burning. Al-Hariq: is one of the names of Hell, like Al-Sa'ir. Hell has levels and types and has names. It is as if they are being tortured with the freezing cold in Hell, then they are being tortured with the torment of burning. The first is the torment of its cold, and the second is the torment of its sea.
85:11: God Almighty says: Indeed, those who have believed meaning those who believed in God, meaning they believed in Him and His messengers, and done righteous deeds - for them are gardens meaning orchards, beneath which rivers flow of water that is not stagnant, of milk whose taste never changes, of wine that is delicious to those who drink, and of rivers of pure honey. That is the great attainment meaning the immense one, to which no attainment is like.
85:12: The Almighty's statement: Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is severe means that He seizes the tyrants and oppressors, as He, the Most High, says: "And thus is the punishment of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are doing wrong. Indeed, His punishment is painful and severe" (Hud 11:102). This has been mentioned before. Al-Mubarrad said: Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is the answer to the oath. The meaning is: By the heaven with its constellations, indeed, the punishment of your Lord, and what is between them is an interruption confirming the oath. Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim also said in Nawader Al-Usul: The oath applies to what he mentioned as being severe:
85:13: The Almighty's statement: Indeed, it is He who initiates and repeats means creation - according to most scholars - He creates them in the beginning, then He repeats them at the resurrection. Ikrimah narrated that he said: The disbelievers were amazed at God, the Most High, giving life to the dead. Ibn Abbas said: He initiates for them the punishment of burning in this world, then He repeats it upon them in the hereafter. This is the preferred interpretation of Al-Tabari:
85:14: The Almighty said: And He is the Forgiving meaning the Concealer of the sins of His believing servants, He does not disgrace them with them. The Loving meaning the One who loves His friends. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: As one of you loves his brother with good tidings and love. And also on his authority (The Loving) meaning the One who is affectionate to His friends with forgiveness. Mujahid said: The Loving to His friends, fa'ul means fa'il. Ibn Zayd said: The Merciful. Al-Mubarrad narrated on the authority of Ismail bin Ishaq Al-Qadi: That the Loving is the one who has no children, and he recited the words of the poet: I ride in the fear, naked, docile, winged, friendly, and affectionate That is, she has no son to whom she could yearn. The meaning of the verse is: He forgives His servants, but He has no son for whom He could forgive them, so that He is generous in forgiving without reward. It was also said: Al-Wadud means Al-Mawdood, like Riding and Milking, meaning that His righteous servants love and adore Him.
85:15: The saying of God the Almighty: The Owner of the Glorious Throne The Kufians except for Asim read (the Glorious) in the accusative case, as an attribute of the throne. It was also said: for (your Lord), meaning that the punishment of your Glorious Lord is severe, and separation is possible because it is similar to an adjective in terms of emphasis. The rest read it in the nominative case as an attribute of (the Owner), which is God the Almighty. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose it because glory is the ultimate in generosity and favor, and God the Almighty is described with that, even though He described His throne as the Generous at the end of (the Believers). The Arabs say: In every tree is fire, and the date palm and the black cumin are glorified, meaning they are at their peak in it, to the point that one can borrow from them. The meaning of Owner of the Throne is: Owner of the kingdom and authority, as one says: So-and-so is on his royal throne, even if he is not on a throne. And it is said: His throne has been taken away, meaning his authority has gone. This was explained in Al-A’raf and especially in The Book of Al-Asna, in Explaining the Beautiful Names of God.
85:16: The Almighty says: He does what He wills meaning nothing He wills is impossible for Him. Al-Zamakhshari: (Fa'al) is the predicate of a deleted subject. It was said (Fa'al) because what He wills and does is extremely common. Al-Farra' said: It is raised for repetition and resumption, because it is a purely indefinite noun. Al-Tabari said: (Fa'al) is raised, and it is a purely indefinite noun, in imitation of the parsing of (Al-Ghafoor Al-Wadud). Abu Al-Safar said: Some of the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) entered upon Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him to visit him. They said: Shall we not bring you a doctor? He said: He has seen me! They said: What did he say to you? He said: I do what I want.
85:17: God Almighty says: Has there come to you the report of the armies? That is, O Muhammad, the report of the disbelieving crowds who denied their prophets has come to you, comforting and consoling him with that.
85:18: The Almighty said: Pharaoh and Thamud, and they are in the accusative case as a substitute for the soldiers. The meaning is: You have known what God did to them when they denied His prophets and messengers.
85:19: The Almighty says: Rather, those who disbelieve meaning those who do not believe in you. in denial of you, as was the habit of those before them. He only mentioned Pharaoh and Thamud because Thamud were in the land of the Arabs, and their story was well-known among them, even though they were among the earlier ones. The story of Pharaoh was well-known among the People of the Book and others, and he was among those who came later in destruction, so He used them to indicate others like them in destruction. And God knows best.
85:20: The Almighty says: And God is behind them encompassing them. That is, He is able to bring down upon them what He brought down upon Pharaoh. The one who is encompassed is like the one who is confined. It was also said: That is, God is all-knowing of them, so He will punish them.
85:21: The Almighty says: Rather, it is a glorious Qur'an meaning it is the ultimate in honor, generosity, and blessing. It explains what people need of religious and worldly rulings, unlike what the polytheists claimed. It was also said that glorious means uncreated.
85:22: The Almighty says: In a Preserved Tablet meaning written on a tablet. It is preserved by God Almighty from the reach of the devils. It was said: It is the Mother of the Book, and from it the Qur'an and the books were copied. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Tablet is made of red rubies, its top is tied to the Throne and its bottom is in the stone of an angel called Matariyun, his book is light, and his pen is light. God Almighty looks at it three hundred and sixty times every day, and there is not a single look in which He does what He wills. He raises the lowly and lowers the exalted, enriches the poor and impoverishes the rich, gives life and causes death, and does what He wills. There is no god but Him. Anas ibn Malik and Mujahid said: The Preserved Tablet mentioned by God Almighty is on the forehead of Israfil. Muqatil said: The Preserved Tablet is to the right of the Throne. It was said: The Preserved Tablet, which contains the various types of creation, their affairs, their appointed times, provisions, deeds, decrees that will be carried out regarding them, and the outcome of their affairs. It is the Mother of the Book. Ibn Abbas said: The first thing that God wrote in the Preserved Tablet was: “I am God, there is no god but Me. Muhammad is My Messenger. Whoever submits to My judgment, is patient in My trials, and is grateful for My blessings, I will write him down as a friend and send him with the truthful. Whoever does not submit to My judgment, is not patient in My trials, and is not grateful for My blessings, let him take a god other than Me.” Al-Hajjaj wrote to Muhammad ibn al-Hanafah may God be pleased with him threatening him. Ibn al-Hanafah wrote back to him: “It has reached me that God, the Exalted, glances at the Preserved Tablet three hundred and sixty times every day. He honors and humiliates, tests and pleases, and does what He wants. Perhaps one of these glances will distract you, making you busy with it and not free.” Some commentators said: The Tablet is something that is glanced at by the angels, so they read it. Ibn As-Samee' and Abu Haywah read the Glorious Qur'an as an addition, meaning the Qur'an of a Glorious Lord. Nafi' read in a Preserved Tablet in the nominative case as an attribute of the Qur'an, meaning it is a Glorious Qur'an preserved in a tablet. The rest read in the genitive case as an attribute of the Tablet. The reciters agree on the fat-ha on the lam of (lawh) except for what was narrated from Yahya bin Ya'mar, as it is the Qur'an (lawh) with a damma on the lam, meaning it appears, and it has light, loftiness, and honor. Az-Zamakhshari said: The tablet is the air, meaning the tablet in the seventh heaven in which the tablet is. In As-Sahah: Laha Al-Shai yalhuwahan, meaning it glimpsed. Walahat Al-Safar: changed it. Laha Lawhan and Lawahan: thirst, and the crown is the same. Al-Lawh: the shoulder, and every wide bone. Al-Lawh: that in which it is written. Al-Lawh with a damma: the air between the sky and the earth. Praise be to God.
86:1: Meccan, and it has seventeen verses. God the Almighty said: {And the heaven and the nightcomer} are of two types: (the heaven) is one type, and (the nightcomer) is a type. The nightcomer is the star. God the Almighty explained it in His saying: {And what will make you know what is the nightcomer? It is the piercing star.} There is a difference of opinion concerning it. Some say: It is Saturn, the planet in the seventh heaven. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan mentioned it in his interpretation, and he mentioned reports about it, God knows best their authenticity. Ibn Zayd said: It is the Pleiades. It was also narrated from him that it is Saturn, and al-Farra’ said the same. Ibn Abbas said: It is Capricorn. Al-Farra’ also narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib - may God be pleased with them both: (The piercing star): A star in the seventh heaven, no other star inhabits it. So when the stars take their places in the heaven, it descends and is with them, then it returns to its place in the seventh heaven. It is Saturn. So it is a nightcomer when it descends, and a nightcomer when it ascends. Al-Farra’ narrated: The bird pierces when it rises and goes up. Abu Salih narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was sitting with Abu Talib when a star fell and the earth was filled with light. Abu Talib was startled and said: What is this? He said: (This is a star that has been thrown, and it is a sign from the signs of God) Abu Talib was amazed, and the following verse was revealed: By the heaven and the nightcomer. It was also narrated from Ibn Abbas: (By the heaven and the nightcomer) He said: The heaven and what knocks in it. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas and Ata’: (The piercing): The one that the devils throw. Qatadah said: It is general for all stars, because it rises at night, and whoever comes to you at night is a nightcomer. He said: And you are like a pregnant woman who has been knocked on the door, and a nursing mother who has been distracted by a man of charms. He said: Didn't you see that whenever I came knocking, I found it fragrant, even if it wasn't fragrant? Al-Tariq: the star, a generic name, named thus because it knocks at night, and from it the hadith: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade a traveler from visiting his family at night, so that the absent woman could be groomed and the disheveled woman could comb her hair.” The Arabs call every person who comes at night a taker. It is said: So-and-so came at night. He came at night, knocking, knocking, so he is a taker. Ibn al-Rumi said: O you who sleep at night, happy with its beginning, incidents may knock at dawn Do not rejoice over a night that has a good beginning, for many a night that has a bad end will stoke the fire. In Al-Sahah: Al-Tariq is the star that is called the morning star. And from it is Hind’s saying: We, Tariq's daughters, walk on cushions That is, our father is like a shining star in honor. Al-Mawardi: The root of tariq is knocking, and the hammer is named after it. So, the one who intends to come at night is called tariq, because he needs to knock to arrive. Some people said: It could be during the day. The Arabs say, I came to you today twice, meaning twice. And from this is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: I seek refuge in You from the evil of the visitors of the night and the day, except for a visitor who knocks with good, O Most Merciful. Jarir said in Al-Turuq: Your path is a heart-hunter, and now is not the time for a visit, so come back in peace
86:2: Then he explained, saying: And what will make you know what is the Nightcomer? It is the piercing star. Piercing means shining. And from it is a piercing meteor (al-Saffat 37:10). It is said: thaqaba yathiqub thaqaba wa thaqaba: if it illuminates. And thaqaba is its light. And the Arabs say: thaqaba narak, meaning light it up.
