He said: Spread it among the people until it is consumed by a fire lit with holes. Holes: what you light a fire with from fine sticks. Mujahid said: The piercing: the glowing. Al-Qushayri: And most of them are of the opinion that the night-comer and the piercing are generic names intended to be general, as we mentioned from Mujahid. And what will make you know what the night-comer is? is to magnify the importance of this thing sworn by. Sufyan said: Everything in the Qur’an And what will make you know? He informed him of. And everything in which He said And what will make you know? He did not inform him of.
86:3: God Almighty says: The piercing star.
86:4: God Almighty says: Indeed, every soul has a guardian over it. Qatada said: Guardians who protect your livelihood, your deeds, and your life span. It was also narrated from him that he said: His companion who protects his deeds, whether good or evil. This is the answer to the oath. It was also said: The answer is (Indeed, He is Able to bring him back) according to the statement of Al-Tirmidhi, Muhammad bin Ali. And (in) is a lightened form of the heavy one, and (ma) is an emphasised one, meaning that every soul has a guardian over it. It was also said: The meaning is that every soul has a guardian over it: He protects it from harm, until He hands it over to destiny. Al-Farra’ said: The guardian is from God, He protects it until He hands it over to the destinies, and Al-Kalbi said the same. Abu Umamah said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “One hundred and sixty angels are assigned to the believer, protecting him from that which he cannot control. Of that, seven angels protect him from sight, just as a fly is protected from a bowl of honey. If a servant were to be entrusted with himself for the blink of an eye, the devils would snatch him away.” Ibn ‘Amir, ‘Asim, and Hamzah read lama with a shaddah on the mim, meaning, There is no soul but that it has a guardian. This is the dialect of Hudhayl. Their speaker would say, I adjure you when you stand up. The rest read it with a shaddah, as it is an additional, emphatic word, as we have mentioned. Similar to this verse is the statement of God Almighty: He has guardians before him and behind him, guarding him by the command of God. (Ar-Ra’d: 11), as mentioned above. It was said that the guardian is God Almighty, for if it were not for His protection, it would not have survived. It was also said that the guardian is his mind, guiding him to what is best for him and restraining him from what is harmful. I said: The mind and other things are intermediaries, and the protector in reality is God Almighty. God Almighty said: So God is the best protector (Yusuf 12:46), and He said: “Say: Who protects you by night and by day from the Most Merciful?” (al-Anbiya 21:42). And there is nothing like it.
86:5: The Almighty's saying: So let man consider meaning the son of Adam from what he was created? The connection to what came before it is the recommendation for man to consider the beginning of his affair and his first year, so that he may know that the One Who created him is able to restore him and reward him, so that he may work for the Day of Resurrection and Recompense, and not dictate to its guardian except what pleases him in the outcome of his affair. And from what was he created? Is a question, meaning from what thing was he created?
86:6: Then he said: Created - which is the answer to the question - from gushing water meaning from semen. Gushing means pouring water. I poured the water, I poured it, so it is gushing water, i.e. spurted, as they said: a hidden secret, meaning concealed, because it is from your saying: the water gushed, without naming the doer. It is not said: the water gushed. It is said: May God gushed his soul, if death is called upon him. Al-Farra' and Al-Akhfash said: (from gushing water) meaning poured into the womb. Al-Zajjaj: from gushing water. It is said: armored, knight, and arrows, meaning one with a horse, armor, and arrows. This is the view of Sibawaba. The gushing water is the one that gushed with its intense strength. He meant two waters: the man's water and the woman's water, because man was created from them, but he made them one water because of their mixing. On the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: (gushing) is sticky.
86:7: The Almighty says: It brings forth meaning this water from between the loins meaning the back. There are four languages for it: sulub, sulub - and they were read with both of them - and sulub with a fat-ha on the lam, and saliib with the weight of qalib, and from it the saying of al-Abbas: Transfer from cruciate to uterus And the collarbones: meaning the chest, singular: taraba, which is the place of the necklace on the chest. He said: Slender, white, not overflowing, her collarbones are polished like a chain The back of the man, and the collarbones of the woman. Ibn Abbas said: The collarbones are the place of the necklace. And from him: What is between her breasts, and Ikrimah said. And it was narrated from him: He means the collarbones of the woman: the hands, feet, and eyes, and Ad-Dahhak said the same. Saeed bin Jubair said: It is the neck. Mujahid: It is what is between the shoulders and the chest. And from him: The chest. And from him: The collarbones. And from Ibn Jubair from Ibn Abbas: The collarbones: Four ribs on this side. And Az-Zajjaj narrated: That the collarbones are four ribs on the right side of the chest, and four ribs on the left side of the chest. Muammar bin Abi Habeeba Al-Madani said: The collarbones are the juice of the heart, and from it the child is born. And the famous speech of the Arabs: That they are the bones of the chest and throat. And Durayd bin As-Summa said: If you turn back, we will seize you by your backs, and if you accept, we will seize you by your collarbones. Another said: It seemed as if the collarbones of her throat were burning embers of ghada tree in her forearm. Another said: And saffron on her collarbones, east of her neck and throat On the authority of Ikrimah: The collarbones: the chest, then he recited: A system of pearls on her collarbones Dhu al-Rummah said: The coldness of the brow is removed from the free collarbones That is, they split. It is also narrated as Darjan with a ha, meaning they threw. In Al-Sahah: Tarbiyah is the singular of tarabiyyah, which are the bones of the chest, between the collarbone and the thorax. The poet said: Her breasts are above the knees Al-Muthaqab Al-Abdi said: And gold is sharpened on a rug, the color of ivory, without any flaws. According to non-Jawhari: The thundwa for a man is like the breast for a woman. Al-Asma'i said: It is the implantation of the breast. Ibn al-Sikkit said: It is the flesh around the breast. If you add a damma to the first letter, you give it a hamza, and if you open it, you do not give it a hamza. In the interpretation: From the man's semen that comes out of his loins, he creates the bone and the nerves. And from the woman's semen that comes out of her ribs, the flesh and the blood. This was said by al-A'mash. It has been mentioned before. It was said: The man's semen descends from the brain, then gathers in the testicles. This does not contradict his statement: (from between the loins), because if it descends from the brain, then it passes between the loins and the ribs. Qatada said: The meaning is: It comes out from the man's loins and the woman's ribs. Al-Farra' narrated that something like this comes from the Arabs, and based on this, the meaning of from between the loins is: from the loins. Al-Hasan said: The meaning is: It comes out from the man's loins and the man's ribs, and from the woman's loins and the woman's ribs. Then we know that cleanliness is from all parts of the body, and that is why a man greatly resembles his parents. This is the wisdom in washing the entire body from the emission of semen. Also, the one who has frequent intercourse feels pain in his back and backbone, and that is only because his backbone is empty of what was retained of water. Ismail narrated on the authority of the people of Mecca: (It comes out from between the backbone) with a damma on the lam. It was narrated on the authority of Isa Al-Thaqafi. Al-Mahdawi narrated it and said: Whoever makes semen come out from between the man’s backbone and his ribs, the pronoun in (comes out) refers to the water. And whoever makes it from between the man’s backbone and the woman’s ribs, the pronoun refers to the human being. It was read (the backbone) with a fatha on the sad and the lam. There are four pronunciations for it: salab, sulub, sulub, and salab. Al-Ajjaj said: In the heart like the reins of the sad In praise of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Transfer from cruciate to uterus
86:8: The famous verses are well known. The Almighty says: Indeed, He is Able to return it meaning that God, the Most High, is Able to return it meaning to return the water to the urethra, is Able as Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak said. They also said that the meaning is: He is Able to return the water to the loins, and this was said by Ikrimah. Ad-Dahhak also said that the meaning is: He is Able to return the human being's water as it was. He also said that the meaning is: He is Able to return the human being from old age to youth, and from youth to old age. This is also the case with Al-Mahdawi. Al-Mawardi and Ath-Tha'labi say: to youth, and from youth to sperm. Ibn Zayd said: He is Able to hold back that water so that it does not come out. Ibn Abbas, Qatadah, Al-Hayyan, and Ikrimah also said: He is Able to return the human being after death. This is the preferred opinion of At-Tabari and Al-Tha'labi, and it is the stronger opinion, because of His statement: On the Day when secrets will be exposed.
86:9: God Almighty says: The Day when secrets will be exposed. Al-Mawardi said: It may mean that He will return him to this world after his resurrection in the Hereafter, because the disbelievers will ask God Almighty to return him therein. God Almighty says: The Day when secrets will be exposed. There are two issues: The first: The factor in (Day) - according to the opinion of those who made the meaning that He is able to resurrect man - is his saying: (Able), and (Return) does not apply to it because of what it contains of separation between the relative clause and the relative pronoun with the predicate of (If) and according to the other opinions in (He is Able to return him), the factor in (Day) is an implied verb, and (Able) does not apply to it, because what is meant in this world is to be tested meaning it is tried and examined. Abu al-Ghoul al-Tahawi said: Their bravery will not wear out, even if they wage war from time to time. It is narrated: (Tabala by their question). Whoever narrated it as (Tabala) - with a damma on the taa - made it from the test, and the bravery according to this narration is the dislike, as if he said: They do not know of any dislike in it. And (Tabala) is known. The rajaz poet said: Before today you used to despise me, but today you are humiliating and belittling me. That is, I know you and you know me. And whoever narrated it tabla - with the taa’ open - the meaning is: they do not weaken from war even if it is repeated against them time after time. This is because if difficult matters are repeated for a person, they weaken him and make him weak. And it was said: (tabala al-sara’ir): meaning their hidden things come out and become apparent, and it is everything that a person conceals of good or evil, and conceals of faith or disbelief, as al-Ahwas said: A secret will be revealed to her in the heart and entrails on the day when secrets will be revealed. Second: It was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: ((God Almighty entrusted His creation with four things: prayer, fasting, zakat, and ritual bathing. These are the secrets that God Almighty will test on the Day of Resurrection.)) Al-Mahdawi mentioned it. Ibn Omar said that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ((Three things, whoever maintains them is truly a friend of God, and whoever neglects them is truly an enemy of God: prayer, fasting, and ritual ablution after sexual impurity.)) Al-Tha’labi mentioned it. Al-Mawardi mentioned on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Trust is three: prayer, fasting, and sexual impurity. God, the Almighty, has entrusted the son of Adam with prayer. If he wishes, he can say, ‘I prayed,’ but he did not pray. God, the Almighty, has entrusted the son of Adam with fasting. If he wishes, he can say, ‘I fasted,’ but he did not fast. God, the Almighty, has entrusted the son of Adam with sexual impurity. If he wishes, he can say, ‘I performed ghusl,’ but he did not. Recite, if you wish, ‘The Day when secrets will be exposed.’” Al-Tha’labi mentioned it on the authority of ‘Ata’. Malik said in a narration by Ashab from him, and I asked him about the words of God, the Almighty, ‘The Day when secrets will be exposed.’ Has it reached you that ablution is one of the secrets? He said, “That has reached me from what people say, but as for a hadith that I have narrated, no. Prayer is one of the secrets, and fasting is one of the secrets. If he wishes, he can say, ‘I prayed,’ but he did not pray. Among the secrets are those in the hearts, for which God rewards His servants.” Ibn al-‘Arabi said: “Ibn Mas’ud said: A martyr is forgiven except for trust. Ablution is one of the secrets, prayer and zakat are one of the secrets, and a deposit is one of the secrets, and the worst of that is…” The deposit will appear to him in the form it was on the day it was taken, then he will be thrown with it into the depths of Hell and it will be said to him: Take it out. He will tire himself out and put it around his neck. When he hopes to take it out, it slips from him, and he will follow it, and he will be like that for all eternity. Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: It is part of trustworthiness that a woman is entrusted with her private parts. Ashhab said: Sufyan told me: In menstruation and pregnancy, if she says, I did not menstruate while I was pregnant, she is believed, as long as she does not do something that is known to be a lie. In the hadith: Ghusl after major ritual impurity is part of trustworthiness. Ibn Umar said: On the Day of Resurrection, God will reveal every hidden secret. It will be an adornment on faces and a thing on faces. God knows everything, but He reveals the signs of the angels and the believers.
86:10: The Almighty said: For him meaning man there is no strength meaning protection to prevent him. nor helper to support him from what has befallen him. On the authority of Ikrimah, For him there is no strength nor helper he said: These kings, they will have no strength nor helper on the Day of Resurrection. Sufyan said: Strength is the clan. And helper is the ally. It was said: For him there is no strength in his body. nor helper from other than Him to protect himself from God. This is the meaning of the statement of Qatada.
86:11: The Almighty said: And the sky full of paths meaning full of rain. It returns every year with rain after rain. This is what most commentators have said. Linguists say: path means rain. They recited a poem by Al-Mutanakhil describing a sword that he likened to water: White as a sediment, if it settles in a reveler it will be alone He sank his foot in the mud, wading and sinking in it, as Al-Jawhari said. Al-Khalil said: Ar-Ra’j is the rain itself, and Ar-Ra’j also means spring plants. It was said: That of Ar-Ra’j means benefit. Rain is also called Awb, just as it is called Raj’an. He said: The highest heaven, which is not sheltered by anything but the clouds, nor the valleys and the paths. Abdur Rahman ibn Zayd said: The sun, the moon, and the stars return to the sky; they rise in one direction and set in another. It was also said: The essence of the angels, because they return to it with the deeds of the servants. This is a category.
86:12: The Almighty's saying: And the earth with its fissures is another category, meaning it cracks open to reveal plants, trees, fruits, and rivers, similar to Then We split the earth with a fissure (Abasa 80:26)... the verse. And fissure means splitting, because it splits the earth, so it cracks because of it. It is as if he said: And the earth with its vegetation, because plants split the earth. Mujahid said: And the earth with its roads that pedestrians split. It was also said: It is the earth with its fields, because they split it. It was also said: It is the earth with the dead, because it splits open to reveal them for resurrection.
86:13: The Almighty's saying: Indeed, it is a decisive statement. This is how the oath was conceived. That is, the Qur'an distinguishes between truth and falsehood. We mentioned in the introduction to the book what Al-Harith narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘A book in which is report of what came before you and the judgment of what will come after you. It is the decisive word, and it is not a joke. Whoever abandons it among the tyrants, God will break him, and whoever seeks guidance elsewhere, God will establish him.’” It was also said that what is meant by the decisive word is what was mentioned previously of the threat in this surah, in the words of God the Most High: Indeed, He is Able to bring him back * On the Day when secrets will be exposed.
86:14: The Almighty says: And it is not a joke. That is, the Qur'an is not falsehood or play. Joking is the opposite of seriousness, and one jokes or jokes. Al-Kumait said: He finds us every day and we are weak
86:15: God Almighty says: They meaning the enemies of God are plotting a plot meaning they are plotting against Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions.
86:16: The Almighty says: And I will surely punish them meaning I will punish them for their plot. It was also said that it refers to what God inflicted upon them on the day of Badr of killing and capture. It was also said that God's plot is to lure them in from where they do not know. This meaning was previously mentioned at the beginning of (Al-Baqarah) when God the Almighty says: God mocks them (al-Baqarah 2:15). Complete.
86:17: The Almighty said: Then give the disbelievers respite meaning, give them time, and do not ask God to hasten their destruction, and be satisfied with what He plans for their affairs. Then it was abrogated by the verse of the sword: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9:5). Give them respite is an emphasis. Mahla and Amhal have the same meaning, like nazala and anzala. And Amhal means to give him respite, and the noun is respite. And istimhal means to wait. And tamahal in his affair means to be patient. And tamatmalan means to straighten up and stand up. Imtalal is also: calmness and sluggishness. It is said: Mahlaan, so-and-so, meaning gently and calmly. Slowly means soon, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Qatadah: a little. And the interpretation: Give them respite a little. Rawwad in Arabic speech is the diminutive of rud. And Abu Ubaid said the same. And he recited: Like a drunk walking on a road That is, slowly. The interpretation of (slowly) is: slowly, and the interpretation of slowly you is: give him time, because the kaf is only used if it means af`al and not otherwise, and the dal is moved due to the meeting of two quiescent letters, so it is in the accusative case of the masdar, and it is the diminutive of ma`murubih, because it is the diminutive of irwad, which is the source of aruwad yarud. It has four aspects: a noun for the verb, an adjective, a state, and a source. The noun is like your saying: slowly `Umar, meaning I give him time. The adjective is like your saying: they walked slowly. The state is like `Amr with the addition, like the saying of God the Almighty: So he struck the necks (Muhammad 47:4). Al-Jawhari said all of them: What is in the verse from these aspects is that it is an adjective for the source, meaning a slow delay. It is permissible for it to be for the state, meaning He gave them time without hastening the punishment for them. The surah is concluded.
87:1: Meccan according to the majority. Ad-Dahhak said Medinan. It has nineteen verses. The Almighty’s saying: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, means saying after it: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said this, as did a group of the Companions and Followers, as will come. And Ja’far ibn Muhammad narrated on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, who said: Indeed, the Almighty has an angel called Ezekiel, who has eighteen thousand wings, and between one wing and the next is a journey of five hundred years. A thought occurred to him: Can you see the entire throne? So God increased his wings like that, so he had thirty-six thousand wings, and between one wing and the next is a journey of five hundred years. Then God revealed to him: O king, fly. So he flew for twenty thousand years, but did not reach the top of one of the legs of the throne. Then God doubled his wings and strength and commanded him to fly. So he flew for another thirty thousand years, but still did not reach it. Then God revealed to him: O king, if you were to fly to blow the trumpet with your wings and strength, you would not reach the leg of My throne. The king said: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High. Then God Almighty revealed: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Make it part of your prostration. Al-Tha’labi mentioned this in his Book of Brides. Ibn Abbas and Al-Suddi said: The meaning of Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High is to glorify your Lord, the Most High. The name is a connection intended to glorify the one named, as Labid said: Until the year, then peace be upon you both It was said: Pure your Lord from evil and from what the atheists say about Him. Al-Tabari mentioned that the meaning is: Pure the name of your Lord from being named by anyone other than Him. It was also said: Pure the naming and remembrance of your Lord, that you mention Him only with humility and reverence, and that His remembrance be respected. They made the name mean naming, but it is better for the name to be the one named. Nafi’ narrated from Ibn Umar who said: Do not say ‘In the name of God,’ for the name of God is the Most High. Abu Salih narrated from Ibn Abbas: Pray by the command of your Lord, the Most High. He said: That is, say ‘Glory be to your Lord, the Most High.’ It was narrated from Ali may God be pleased with him, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, Ibn Az-Zubayr, Abu Musa, and Abdullah ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with them that when they began reciting this Surah, they would say: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High, in compliance with His command at the beginning. So it is preferable to follow their example in their recitation, not that Glory be to my Lord, the Most High is part of the Qur’an, as some of the deviants said. It was also said that in Abu’s recitation it is: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High. Ibn Umar used to recite it in the same way. In the hadith: “When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited it, he would say: ‘Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.’” Abu Bakr al-Anbari said: Muhammad ibn Shahriyar told me, he said: Husayn ibn al-Aswad told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad told us, he said: Isa ibn Umar told us, on the authority of his father, he said: Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) recited in prayer: ‘Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High,’ then he said: ‘Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.’ When the prayer ended, he was asked: ‘O Commander of the Faithful, are you adding this to the Qur’an?’ He said: ‘What is it?’ They said: ‘Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.’ He said: ‘No, we were only commanded to do something and I said it.’ On the authority of ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir al-Juhani, he said: When the verse Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Include it in your prostration. All of this indicates that the name is the named, because they did not say: Glory be to the name of my Lord, the Most High. It was said that the first one to say Glory be to my Lord, the Most High was Michael, peace be upon him. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Gabriel: ((O Gabriel, tell me of the reward of one who says: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High, in his prayer or outside of his prayer.)) He said: ((O Muhammad, there is no believing man or woman who says it in his prostration or outside of his prostration, except that it will be on his scale heavier than the Throne, the Footstool, and the mountains of the world. And God, the Most High, says: My servant has spoken the truth. I am above all things, and there is nothing above Me. Bear witness, O My angels, that I have forgiven him and admitted him to Paradise. So when he dies, Michael visits him every day. On the Day of Resurrection, he carries him on his wing and makes him stand before God, the Most High, and says: O Lord, allow me to intercede for him. He says: I have accepted your intercession for him, so take him to Paradise.)) Al-Hasan said: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, meaning pray to your Lord, the Most High. It was also said: Pray with the names of God, not as the polytheists pray by whistling and clapping. It was also said: Raise your voice in remembrance of your Lord. Jarir said: God made the faces of Taghlib ugly as the pilgrims glorified and magnified God.
87:2: The Almighty's saying: Who created and proportioned. The meaning of proportioning has already been mentioned in (Al-Infitar) and elsewhere. That is, He proportioned what He created, so there was no irregularity in His creation. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, He made his stature straight. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He made what He created good. Ad-Dahhak said: He created Adam and proportioned his creation. And it was said: He created in the loins of the fathers, and proportioned in the wombs of the mothers. And it was said: He created the bodies, so He proportioned the minds. And it was said: That is, He created the human being and prepared him for accountability.
87:3: The Almighty says: And He Who has decreed and guided. Ali may God be pleased with him, As-Salami, and Al-Kisa'i read has decreed with a light dal, while the others stressed it. They have the same meaning, that is, He has decreed and made each form fit its shape. has guided means He has directed. Mujahid said: He has decreed misery and happiness, and guided to right conduct and misguidance. And from him he said: He has guided mankind to happiness and misery, and He has guided livestock to their pastures. And it was said: He has decreed their sustenance and provisions, and He has guided them to their livelihood if they are humans, and to their pastures if they are wild. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas, As-Suddi, Muqatil, and Al-Kalbi regarding His statement: has guided, they said: He has made known to His creation how the male approaches the female, as He said in Ta-Ha: He gave each thing its form and nature, then guided it (Ta-Ha: 50), meaning the male to the female. Ata' said: He made for every creature what is good for it, and guided it to it. It was said: He created benefits in things, and guided man to the way to extract them from them. It was also said: (He decreed and guided): He decreed for each animal what is good for it, guided it to it, and showed it the way to benefit from it. It is said that when a thousand years pass a snake becomes blind, and God inspires it to wipe its eyes with fresh rhizome leaves to restore its sight. Perhaps it is in a wilderness between which and the countryside is a days’ journey, so it covers that distance despite its length and its blindness, until it attacks a rhizome tree in some orchards, and does not miss it. It rubs its eyes with it and its sight returns, by God’s permission. Guidance for man to what is unlimited of his interests and what is countless of his needs, in his food and medicine, and in the doors of his worldly life and religion. The inspirations of the beasts, birds and insects of the earth are a wide door and a vast expanse, which no describer can encompass. Glory be to my Lord, the Most High. Al-Suddi said: He decreed the period of the fetus in the womb to be nine months, or more or less, then He guided it to exit the womb. Al-Farraa said: It means that He decreed, so He guided and led astray. So He was satisfied with mentioning one of them, like the saying of the Most High: {garments to protect you from the heat} (al-Nahl 16:81). It is possible that it means that He called to faith, like the saying of the Most High: {And indeed, you guide to a straight path} (al-Shura 42:52). That is, you call, and He called everyone to faith. It was said: (So He guided) means He guided them with His actions to His Oneness, and that He is All-Knowing, All-Powerful. There is no disagreement that whoever stresses the dal in (decree) that it is from the decree, like the saying of the Most High: (al-Furqan 25:52). And whoever lightens it, it is possible that it is from the decree, and they are in one meaning. It is possible that it is from power and dominion, meaning the dominion of things, and He guides whomever He wills. I said: I heard some of my sheikhs say: He who created, proportioned, measured, and guided. This is an interpretation of the transcendence that befits the majesty of God Almighty over all of His creation.
87:4: The Almighty says: And He who brought forth pasture meaning the grass and green herbage. The poet said: Pasture may grow on the dung of the soil, yet the grudges of the soul remain as they were.
87:5: The Almighty said: And made it black stubble. Al-Ghathaa is what the flood throws up on the sides of the valley from grass, plants, and cloth. And the same is true of al-Ghathaa with emphasis. The plural is al-Aghthaa. Qatada said: Al-Ghathaa is a dry thing. And the grass and herbs are called when they are broken and dry: ghathaa and hishim. And the same is true of what is around the water from cloth, ghathaa, as he said: As if the mud of the fire in the morning from the torrent and the scum is a spinning wheel Linguists said: The valley became dry and sparse. And the same applies to water: if it is covered with foam and cloth that is not useful. And the ahwa: is black, meaning that the plant turns to hawwa from the intensity of greenness like black. And hawwa: blackness, Al-A’sha said: Lamia has honey on her lips, a moustache on her teeth, and a gum on her gums. In As-Sahah: And Al-Hawwa: is the darkness of the lip. It is said: a man who is ahwa, and a woman who is hawa, and she has become ahwa. And a camel is ahwa if its greenness is mixed with black and yellow. The diminutive of ahwa is ahyu, in the language of those who say asyud. Then it was said: It is permissible for (ahwa) to be a state of (the pasture), and the meaning would be: as if its greenness is tending towards black, and the estimate is: He brought out the pasture who is ahwa, so he made it stubble. It is said: the plants have become ahwa, as Al-Kisa’i narrated. He said: And Ghaith from Al-Wasmi, whose hills are covered with two layers of Shidham Salatan It is possible that (Ahwa) is an adjective for (Ghathaa). The meaning is: it became like this after it had been green. Abu Ubaidah said: He made it black from burning and old age, and fresh dates turn black when they dry. Abdurrahman bin Zaid said: The pasture came out green, then when it dried it turned black from burning, so it became Ghathaa, which the winds and floods carried away. It is a metaphor that God Almighty gave to the unbelievers, for the world to go away after its freshness.
87:6: The Almighty's saying: We will make you recite meaning the Qur'an, O Muhammad, and teach it to you and you will not forget meaning memorize it. This was narrated by Ibn Wahb from Malik. This is good report from God, the Most High. He gave him good report by giving him a clear sign, which is that Gabriel would recite to him what he would recite to him from the revelation, although he was illiterate and could neither read nor write, so he would memorize it and not forget it. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Nujayh from Mujahid, who said: He would remember for fear that he would forget, so it was said: I have sufficed you for that. Mujahid and Al-Kalbi said: When Gabriel would come down to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with revelation, he would not finish the end of the verse until the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had spoken the beginning, for fear that he would forget it. So the following was revealed: We will make you recite, and you will not forget. After that, something was revealed, and I have sufficed you for that. The exception to this is what Al-Farra’ said: Except what God wills. He does not will that you forget anything, as in His statement: They will abide therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills. (Hud 11:107) and He does not will. It is said in speech: I will give you everything you ask for, except what you wish, and except that I wish to prevent you, and the intention is that He will not prevent him from anything. So, according to this, it is the course of oaths, and an exception is made in it, and the intention of the one who takes an oath is complete. In the narration of Abu Salih from Ibn Abbas: He did not forget after the revelation of this verse until he died, Except what God wills. And from Sa’id from Qatadah, he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not forget anything, Except what God wills. And it was said: Except what God willed that he forget, then he remembered after that, and then he had forgotten, but he remembered and did not forget completely. It was narrated that he omitted a verse while reciting in prayer, and Abu thought that it had been abrogated, so he asked him, and he said: I forgot it. It was said: It is from forgetfulness, meaning except what God wills you to leave so that He may abrogate it. This is about abrogate actions, and the first is about abrogate recitation. Al-Far’ani said: The people of knowledge would frequent Al-Junayd’s gathering, and Ibn Kaysan the grammarian would also visit him. He was a distinguished man. One day he said: What do you say, O Abu Al-Qasim, about God’s statement: We will make you recite, and you will not forget? He quickly answered him - as if the question had been asked to him many times before: Do not forget to act upon it. Ibn Kaysan said: May God not defile your mouth! Someone like you acts according to his own opinion. His statement: So do not is for negation, not prohibition. It was said that it is for prohibition, and the letter ya was confirmed because the beginnings of the verses are based on that. The meaning is: Do not neglect its recitation and repetition, lest you forget it, except what God wills you to forget by raising its recitation for the sake of benefit. The first is the preferred opinion, because the exception from the prohibition is almost never anything but a known, temporary one. Also, the letter ya is confirmed in all copies of the Qur’an, and the reciters follow it. It was said: Its meaning is except what God wills to delay its revelation. It was also said: The meaning is He made it black scum, except what God wills the children of Adam and the animals to attain, for it does not become like that.
87:7: The Almighty says: Indeed, He knows what is declared meaning what is said and done openly. And what is hidden meaning what is secret. Ibn Abbas said: What is in your heart and soul. Muhammad ibn Hatim said: He knows what is declared and hidden in charity. It was also said: What is declared is what you have memorized of the Qur'an in your chest. And what is hidden is what has been abrogated from your chest.
87:8: And We will make it easy for you: is in apposition to We will make you recite. And His statement, Indeed, He knows what is declared and what is hidden is I'tirash. The meaning of for the ease is for the easy way, which is doing good. Ibn Abbas said: We will make it easy for you to do good. Ibn Mas'ud said: For the ease, meaning for Paradise. And it was said: We will make you adhere to the easy Sharia, which is the easy, tolerant Hanafi school. Ad-Dahhak said its meaning. And it was said: We will make the revelation easy for you so that you will memorize it and act upon it.
87:9: The Almighty said: Then remind meaning, admonish your people, O Muhammad, with the Qur'an. If the reminder benefits meaning, the sermon. Yunus narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: A reminder for the believer and an argument against the disbeliever. Ibn Abbas used to say: It benefits My allies, but not My enemies. Al-Jurjani said: Remembrance is obligatory even if it does not benefit. The meaning is: Then remind, whether the reminder benefits or not, so the word was omitted, as He said: Garments to protect you from the heat (al-Nahl 16:81). It was said that it is specific to specific people. It was also said that if means what, meaning, then mention what the reminder benefits, so if means what, not condition, because the reminder is beneficial in all cases, as Ibn Shajarah said. Some Arabists have said that in means when, meaning when it benefits, as in the Almighty’s saying: And you will be the highest if you are believers. (Al Imran 3:139) meaning when you were. He did not inform of their being higher until after their belief. It was also said that it means had.
87:10: The Almighty said: He who fears will be reminded, meaning he who is mindful of God and fears Him. Abu Saleh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: It was revealed about Ibn Umm Maktum. Al-Mawardi: He who hopes for Him may be mentioned, but the reminder of the fearful is more eloquent than the reminder of the hopeful, and that is why He connected it to fear rather than hope, even though it is connected to both fear and hope. It was said: That is, you generalized the reminder and the preaching, even though preaching only benefits the one who fears, but you will obtain the reward of supplication, as narrated by Al-Qushayri.
87:11: The Almighty says: And the most wretched avoids it. That is, he avoids the remembrance and keeps away from it. The most wretched means the wretched in the sight of God. It was also said that this verse was revealed about Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira and Utba ibn Rabi'ah.
87:12: The Almighty says: Who will be exposed to the Great Fire meaning the greatest, which is the lowest level of Hellfire, as stated by Al-Farra'. Al-Hasan reported: The greatest is the fire of Hell, and the smallest is the fire of this world, as stated by Yahya ibn Salam.
87:13: The Almighty says: Then he will neither die therein nor live. That is, he will neither die and find rest from the torment, nor will he live a life that will benefit him, as the poet said: Is there no soul that does not die, so that its suffering ends and it does not live a life that has any taste? The hadith of Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri has been mentioned in An-Nisa' and other books, and that when the monotheists among the believers enter Hell - which is the lesser fire according to Al-Farra' - they will burn in it and die, until intercession is granted for them. Narrated by Muslim. It has also been said that the people of misery vary in their misery, and this threat is for the most miserable, even if there is a miserable person who does not reach this level.
87:14: God Almighty says: He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself, * And remembers the name of his Lord and prays. There are three issues: First: The Almighty’s statement: He has certainly succeeded, meaning he has found abiding in Paradise, meaning he who purifies himself from polytheism through faith. This was stated by Ibn Abbas, Ata’, and Ikrimah. Al-Hasan and Al-Rabi’ said: He whose deeds are pure and growing. Muammar said on the authority of Qatadah: He has been purified, meaning, through righteous deeds. It was narrated from him on the authority of Ata’ and Abu Al-Aaliyah: It was revealed regarding Zakat Al-Fitr. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Sirin: He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord and prays, he said: He went out and prayed after he had performed the ritual prayer. Ikrimah said: A man would say, I present my Zakat before my prayer. Sufyan said: God the Almighty said: He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord and prays, and it was narrated on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri and Ibn Umar: That is in a charity better than it, and better than providing water to drink. Kathir ibn Abdullah narrated on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather: On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the words of God Almighty: He has succeeded who purifies himself, he said: Pays zakat al-fitr, “And mentioned the name of his Lord and prayed,” he said: The Eid prayer. Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak said: And mentioned the name of his Lord on the way to the place of prayer, and prayed the Eid prayer. It was said that what is meant by the verse is zakat on all wealth, as stated by Abu Al-Ahwas and Ata’. Ibn Jurayj narrated that he said: I said to Ata’: He has succeeded who purifies himself for the sake of breaking the fast? He said: It refers to all charity. It was said that it is zakat on deeds, not zakat on wealth, meaning that he purifies his deeds from ostentation and negligence, because it is more common to say about wealth: it is purified, not that it is to be purified. Jabir ibn Abdullah narrated that he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He has succeeded who purifies himself meaning he who bears witness that there is no god but God, rejects rivals to Him, and bears witness that I am the Messenger of God. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, purifies himself means: There is no god but God. Ata’ narrated from him that he said: It was revealed about Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him. He said: There was a hypocrite in Medina who had a leaning palm tree in the house of an Ansar man. When the wind blew, it caused the dates and fresh dates to fall onto the house of the Ansar, so he and his family would eat. The hypocrite argued with him and complained about that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent to the hypocrite, not knowing of his hypocrisy, and said: Your brother, the Ansari, mentioned that your fresh dates and fresh dates fall to the hypocrite, and he does not know of his hypocrisy. He said:
87:15: The Almighty says: And he mentioned the name of his Lord and prayed. That is, he mentioned his Lord. Ata' narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: He means mentioning his return and his standing before God, the Most High, so he worshipped Him and prayed to Him. It was also said that he mentioned the name of his Lord with the takbir at the beginning of the prayer, because it is not valid without mentioning Him. This is the saying: Allahu Akbar. This is used as evidence for the obligation of the opening takbir, and that it is not part of the prayer, because the prayer is conjoined with it. This provides evidence for those who say that opening with any of the names of God, the Almighty, is permissible. This is a controversial issue among the jurists. This has been discussed previously at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah. It was also said that they are the takbirs of Eid. Ad-Dahhak said: And he mentioned the name of his Lord on the path to the place of prayer and he prayed, meaning the Eid prayer. It was said: And he mentioned the name of his Lord, meaning that he remembers Him in his heart during his prayer, fearing His punishment and hoping for His reward, so that his fulfillment of it and his humility in it are in accordance with his fear and hope. It was also said: It is to begin the beginning of every surah with In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. So he prayed means he prayed and remembered. There is no difference between saying, You honored me and visited me, and saying, You visited me and honored me. Ibn Abbas said: This is in the obligatory prayer, which are the five daily prayers. It was also said: Supplication, meaning supplication to God for the needs of this world and the hereafter. It was also said: The Eid prayer, as said by Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, Ibn Umar and others. It has been mentioned previously. It was also said: It is to voluntarily pray after paying zakat, as said by Abu Al-Ahwas, and it is implied by the statement of Ata’. It was narrated from Abdullah who said: Whoever establishes prayer but does not pay zakat, then his prayer is not valid.
87:16: God Almighty says: But you prefer the life of this world. The general readingبالْاُر رونwith the letter ta’ confirms Abu’s readingبالي انُرمرون. Abu Amr and Nasr ibn Asim readبالْاُر رونwith the letter ya’ in the third person, meaning: Rather, the wretched ones prefer the life of this world. According to the first reading, the interpretation of By God, you prefer, O Muslims, is to take more of this world and to take more of the reward. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he read this verse and said: Do you know why we preferred the life of this world over the hereafter? Because this world was present and hastened for us its good things, its food and drink, its pleasures and delights, while the hereafter was hidden from us, so we took the immediate and left the deferred. Thabit narrated on the authority of Anas who said: We were with Abu Musa on a journey, and the people were talking and mentioning this world. Abu Musa said: O Anas, these people almost tear the leather with their tongues, so come, let us remember our Lord for a while. Then he said: O Anas, what is the delay of the people! What slowed them down? I said: This world, Satan, and desires. He said: No, but the world has been hastened and the Hereafter has been hidden. By God, if they had seen it, they would not have been just or deviated.
87:17: The Almighty says: And the Hereafter is better and more lasting. That is, the home of the Hereafter, meaning Paradise. Better means better. And more lasting means more lasting than this world. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The world in comparison to the Hereafter is like the way one of you puts his finger in the sea. So let him consider how much of the clay remains, for it would be necessary to prefer clay that remains over gold that perishes. He said: How can it be, when the Hereafter is made of gold that perishes, and the world is made of clay that perishes?”
87:18: The Almighty's saying: Indeed, this is in the former scriptures. Qatada and Ibn Zayd said: He means His saying: And the Hereafter is better and more lasting. They said: God, the Most High, wrote one after the other - as you hear - that the Hereafter is better and more lasting than this world. Al-Hasan said: Indeed, this is in the former scriptures He said: God, the Most High, wrote all of it. Al-Kalbi said: Indeed, this is in the former scriptures from His saying: He has certainly succeeded to the end of the surah, based on the hadith of Abu Dharr as follows. Ikrimah narrated from Ibn Abbas: Indeed, this is in the former scriptures He said: This surah. Al-Dahhak and Al-Muttalib said: This Qur'an is in the former scriptures, meaning the first books.
87:19: The Almighty’s statement: The scriptures of Abraham and Moses means the books revealed to them. It was not reported that these exact words are in those scriptures, but rather it is based on the meaning, that is, the meaning of these words is mentioned in those scriptures. “Al-Ajurri narrated from the hadith of Abu Dharr who said: I said, O Messenger of God, what were the scrolls of Abraham? He said, "They were all parables: 'O domineering, afflicted, and arrogant king, I did not send you to gather the world against itself, but I sent you to respond to the supplication of the oppressed, for I will not respond to it even if it came from the mouth of an unbeliever.' And there were parables in them: The wise person should have three hours: an hour in which to commune with his Lord, an hour in which to take account of himself, thinking about what God Almighty has done for him, and an hour in which to devote himself to his needs of food and drink. The wise person should not travel except for three things: provisions for the afterlife, improvement of his livelihood, and pleasure in something that is not forbidden. The wise person should be aware of his time, focused on his affairs, and guard his tongue. Whoever counts his words as part of his deeds will speak little except in what helps him." I said, O Messenger of God, what were the scrolls of Moses? He said: ((They were all lessons: I am amazed at the one who is certain of death, how he rejoices! I am amazed at the one who is certain of destiny, how he is troubled! I am amazed at the one who sees the world and its vicissitudes with its people, how he feels at ease with it! I am amazed at the one who is certain of the reckoning tomorrow, yet he does not work))! He said: I said, O Messenger of God, do we have in our hands anything of what was in the hands of Abraham and Moses, of what God revealed to you? He said: (Yes, read, O Abu Dharr, “Indeed, he has succeeded who purifies himself * And remembers the name of his Lord and prays * But you prefer the life of this world * While the Hereafter is better and more lasting * Indeed, this is in the former scriptures * The scriptures of Abraham and Moses”) and he mentioned the hadith.
88:1: It is Meccan according to everyone, and it has twenty-six verses. God the Almighty says: Has there come to you the report of the Overwhelming Event? Ha means has come to you, like His statement: Has there come upon man? (al-Insan 76:1), as Qatrib said. That is, O Muhammad, the report of the Overwhelming Event has come to you, meaning the Resurrection that will overwhelm creation with its terrors and horrors, as most of the commentators said. Sa’id ibn Jubayr and Muhammad ibn Ka’b said: Al-Ghashiyah means the Fire will overwhelm the faces of the disbelievers. Abu Salih narrated it from Ibn Abbas, and its evidence is the statement of God the Almighty: And the Fire will overwhelm their faces (Ibrahim 14:50). It was also said: it will overwhelm creation. It was also said: what is meant is the second Trumpet Blast for Resurrection, because it will overwhelm creation. It was also said: Al-Ghashiyah means the people of Hell will overwhelm it and plunge into it. It was also said: the meaning of Has there come to you is that this was not from your knowledge, nor from the knowledge of your people. Ibn Abbas said: it had not come to him before that, in the detail mentioned here. It was said: It was used as a question to his Messenger, and its meaning is: If the report of the overwhelming event has not reached you, then it has reached you, and this is the meaning of what Al-Kalbi said.
88:2: Ibn Abbas said: He had not heard their hadith, so he told him about them, and he said: The Almighty’s saying: Faces that Day meaning the Day of Resurrection. Humbled Sufyan said: meaning humbled by the torment. And everything that is humbled is still and humble. It is said: He was humble in his prayer meaning he humbled himself and lowered his head. And the voice was humbled: it was lowly. God the Most High said: And the voices will be hushed before the Most Merciful (Ta-Ha: 108). What is meant by faces are the people with faces. Qatada and Ibn Zayd said: Humbled means in the Fire. What is meant are the faces of all the disbelievers, said Yahya ibn Salam. It was said: He meant the faces of the Jews and Christians, said Ibn Abbas.
88:3: Then he said: Working and striving This is in this world, because the afterlife is not a place of work. So the meaning is: faces working and striving in this world humbled in the afterlife. The linguists said: It is said of a man when he is persistent in his walk: he has worked, he does work. And it is said of a cloud when it continues gently: he has worked, he does work. And this cloud is working. Al-Hudhali said: Until the night became exhausted and the work became dull and the night did not allow him to sleep Nasibah means tired. It is said:نقصصبin the kasraينصب نقصيببto become tired, and alsoنقصيببto become tired, and someone elseنقصي برُر. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: They are those who set themselves up in this world to disobey God Almighty, and to disbelieve, such as idol worshippers, and the disbelieving People of the Book, such as monks and others. God, the Most High, does not accept from them anything except what is sincere for Him. Saeed said on the authority of Qatadah:َقْيَقة نقصصبصة He said: She was arrogant in this world to obey God Almighty, so God made her work and set her up in Hell, by dragging heavy chains, carrying shackles, and standing barefoot and naked in the open spaces, on a day the length of which is fifty thousand years. Al-Hasan and Saeed bin Jubayr said: She did not work for God in this world, nor did she set herself up for Him, so He made her work and set her up in Hell. Al-Kalbi said: They will drag on their faces in Hell. It was narrated from him and others: They will be ordered to climb an iron mountain in Hell, and they will be tormented therein with the most severe torment, by being made to wear chains and shackles, and wading through the Fire as camels wade through mud, and climbing up a mountain of Fire, and descending down a slope from it, and other torments therein. Ibn Abbas said the same. Ibn Muhaisin, Isa, and Hamid recited it, and Ubaid narrated it from Shibl from Ibn Kathir Nasibah in the accusative case as a state. It was also said: as a blame. The rest in the nominative case as an adjective or with an implied subject, so one stops at Khasha’ih. Whoever makes the meaning in the Hereafter, it is permissible for it to be a predicate after a predicate of Faces, so one does not stop at Khasha’ih. It was also said: Working and working means working in this world, working in the Hereafter. Based on this, it is possible that faces on that Day will be working in this world, working in the Hereafter, and humbled. Ikrimah and As-Suddi said: They worked in this world with sins. Saeed bin Jubair and Zaid bin Aslam said: They are the monks who live in monasteries. Ibn Abbas also said the same. It was mentioned earlier in Al-Dahhak’s narration from him. It was narrated from Al-Hasan who said: When Omar bin Al-Khattab - may God be pleased with him - came to Ash-Sham, an old monk, wearing black, came to him. When Omar saw him, he wept. He said to him: Commander of the Faithful, what makes you weep? He said: This poor man sought something but did not obtain it, and hoped for something but missed it. - and he recited the words of God the Almighty - Some faces, that Day, will be humiliated, toiling and weary. Al-Kisa’i said: Taqahhal means shabby appearance, and a man who is Mutaqahhal means dry-skinned and in a bad condition, like Mutaqahhal. Abu Amr said: Taqahhal means complaining of need. And he recited: If you find him, beware Qahal: ingratitude. Qahal means to praise with ugly praise. A man is qahal if he does something that criticizes him and defiles himself. He is weak and falls, as Al-Jawhari said. And on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, that they are the people of Harura. Meaning the Khawarij whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned when he said: “You consider your prayers insignificant compared to their prayers, your fasting insignificant compared to their fasting, and your deeds insignificant compared to their deeds. They will leave the religion as an arrow leaves its target.” Hadith.
88:4: The Almighty says: It will be burned with a blazing Fire meaning it will be afflicted by its scorching heat and intense heat. Burning is very hot, meaning it has been lit and heated for a long time. From this comes the word fire with a kasra and the oven became very hot in them, meaning its heat became intense. Al-Kisa'i said: The sun became very hot and they heated it with the same meaning. Abu Amr, Abu Bakr and Ya'qub read tasalla with a damma on the ta'. The rest read it with a fatha. tasalla was read with a shaddah. This has already been discussed in the chapter on When the sky is split al-Inshiqaq 27:1. Al-Mawardi said: If it is said, what is the meaning of describing it as hot when it is always hot, and this is the least of its conditions, so what is the point of exaggeration with this imperfect description? It is said: There is a difference of opinion regarding what is meant by hot here in four ways: First: That what is meant by it is that it is constantly hot, not like the fire of this world whose heat stops when it is extinguished. Second: What is meant by this is that it is a constant fever, unlike the fire of this world whose fever ceases when it is extinguished. Second: What is meant by the fever is a fever from committing forbidden acts and violating sacred things, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Every king has a sanctuary, and God’s sanctuary is His prohibitions. Whoever grazes around a sanctuary is likely to fall into it.” Third: It protects itself from being touched or touched, just as a lion protects its den. Similar to this is the saying of Al-Nabigha: Wolves attack those who have no dogs and fear the attack of the protective lion. Fourth: It is a fierce rage and fury, exaggerating the intensity of revenge. It does not refer to a fever of crime or self, as one would say, So-and-so became furious, meaning he became furious and angry when wanting revenge. God Almighty clarified this meaning by saying, You almost burst into tears with rage (al-Mulk 67:8).
88:5: The Almighty said: They will be given to drink from a spring of water. Al-Ani: that which has finished its heat, from the word Ina’a, meaning delay. And from it: Anit and Adh-Dhaytu. And anaah ian, meaning he delayed it, held it back and slowed it down. And from this They will circulate between it and scalding water (al-Rahman 55:44). And in the commentaries from a boiling spring meaning its heat is extreme, so if a drop of it were to fall on the mountains of the world, it would melt. Al-Hasan said: Aaniyyah meaning its heat has reached its peak, Hell has been kindled over it since it was created, so they were driven to it thirsty in thirst. And on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid, he said: It has reached its peak, and it is time to drink from it.
88:6: The Almighty says: They will have no food except from Dharee' meaning the people of Hell. No food except from Dharee'. When He mentioned their drink, He also mentioned their food. Ikrimah and Mujahid said: Dharee' is a thorny plant that sticks to the ground. The Quraysh called it shabraq when it was fresh, but when it dried up, it became Dharee'. No animal or beast should approach it or graze it. It is a deadly poison, and it is the most vile and abhorrent of food, according to most of the commentators. However, Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: It is something that the sea throws up, called Dharee', from the sustenance of livestock, not people. If camels fall into it, they are not satisfied and die of weakness. The correct view is what the majority said: that it is a plant. Abu Dhu'ayb said: The sharq al-rayyan grazed until it withered and became weak, and its flaws became apparent. Al-Hudhali said, mentioning camels and their poor pasture: They were imprisoned in the defeat of the wrathful, and their hunchbacked, bloody-handed, and stubborn Al-Khalil said: Adh-Dhari’ is a green plant with a foul odor, which is thrown by the sea. Al-Walabi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It is a tree of fire, and if it were in this world, it would have burned the earth and everything on it. Saeed bin Jubair said: It is stones, and Ikrimah said the same. It is more apparent that it is a tree with thorns, as it is in this world. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: "(Adh-Dhari': something that is found in Hell, similar to a thorn, more bitter than aloe vera, more putrid than a carcass, and hotter than Hellfire. God named it Adh-Dhari'). Khalid ibn Ziyad said: I heard Al-Mutawakkil ibn Hamdan being asked about this verse, "They will have no food except from Adh-Dhari'." He said: I have been told that Adh-Dhari' is a tree from the fire of Hell, borne of pus and blood, more bitter than aloe vera, and that is their food. Al-Hasan said: It is some of the torment that God has hidden. Ibn Kaysan said: It is food before which they humiliate themselves and beseech God, seeking deliverance from it. It was named thus because the one who eats it beseeches God to be spared from it, due to its dislike and roughness. Abu Ja'far Al-Nahhas said: It may be derived from Adh-Dhari', which means humiliated, meaning humbled, meaning from a drink of humiliation that befalls him. Al-Hasan also said: It refers to Zaqqum. It was also said: It is a valley in Hell. And God knows best. God the Almighty said elsewhere: So there is for him this Day no hot water source here, nor any food except from boiling water Al-Haqqah 59:35-36. Here He said: except from thorny thorns, which is not thorny thorns. The way to combine them is that Hellfire has levels, so some of them will eat Zaqqum, and some of them will eat thorny thorns. Some of them will eat thorny thorns, some of them will drink scalding water, and some of them will drink pus. Al-Kalbi said: Thorny thorns are in a level where there is no other, and Zaqqum is in another level. It is possible to interpret the two verses in two ways, as He said: They will circulate between it and scalding water Al-Rahman 55:44. Al-Qutbi said: “It is possible that thorny thorns and the tree of Zaqqum are plants of Hell, or from a substance that Hellfire does not consume. The same applies to the chains and shackles of Hellfire, its scorpions and snakes. If they were as we know them, they would not have remained in Hellfire.” He said: “God has shown us what is absent with Him through what is present with us. So the names are consistent in their meaning, but the meanings are different.” And also what is in Paradise of its trees and furnishings. Al-Qushayri said: An example of what Al-Qutbi said is that you say: He who keeps the disbelievers in the Fire so that the torment may last for them, keeps the plants and the tree of Zaqqum in the Fire so that He may torment the disbelievers with them. Some of them claimed that the thorny thorn tree itself does not grow in the Fire, nor that they eat it. The thorny thorn is a food for livestock, not for people. And if camels fall into it, they will not be satisfied, and they will die of weakness. So he meant that these people eat what does not fill them up, and he gave the thorny thorn as an example, that they are tormented by hunger just as the thorny thorn is tormented by its strength. Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim said: This is a weak view from its people and a vile interpretation, as if it indicates that they were confused about the power of God Almighty, and that He who caused this plant to grow in this soil is able to grow it in the burning fire. He made for us in this world fire from the green tree, so the fire does not burn the tree, and the moisture of the water in the tree does not extinguish the fire. So God Almighty said: Who made for you fire from the green tree, and then, behold, you kindle from it (Ya-Sin 36:80) and as it was said when it was revealed: And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection on their faces (al-Isra’ 17:97). They said, O Messenger of God, how will they walk on their faces? He said, He who made them walk on their feet is able to make them walk on their faces. Only the weak-hearted would be confused by such a thing. Has He not informed us that Whenever their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins (An-Nisa’: 56), and that their garments will be of pitch (Ibrahim 14:50), and that Indeed, with Us are shackles (al-Muzzammil 73:12), meaning chains. And a Hellfire, and food that chokes (al-Muzzammil 73:12-13). It was said: With thorns. So the torment is only recited to them with these things.
88:7: The Almighty's statement: It neither fattens nor satisfies hunger means that the thorny plant does not fatten its eater. How can someone who eats thorns fatten? The commentators said: When this verse was revealed, the polytheists said: Our camels get fat on the thorny plant. So the verse: It neither fattens nor satisfies hunger was revealed. They lied, because camels only graze it when it is fresh, and when it dries they do not eat it. It was also said: They were confused and thought it was like any other beneficial plant, because the similarity is similar. But they found that it neither fattens nor satisfies hunger.
88:8: God Almighty says: On that Day, some faces will be radiant, meaning, full of blessings. These will be the faces of the believers, blessed by what they witnessed of the consequences of their actions and righteous deeds.
88:9: The Almighty says: For her effort meaning for the work she did in this world. Satisfied in the Hereafter when she is given Paradise for her work. And as a reward: satisfied with the reward of her effort. And it contains an implied waw. The meaning: And faces on that Day, to distinguish between them and the previous faces. And the faces refer to the souls.
88:10: The Almighty says: In a lofty Paradise meaning elevated, because it is above the heavens, as mentioned above. It was also said: of high status, because it contains everything that the soul desires and the eyes delight in. And they will abide therein eternally.
88:11: The Almighty says: You will not hear therein any idle talk, meaning any foul, unsatisfactory speech. He said: Idle talk, and idle talk, idle talk, and idle talk have the same meaning. He said: About idle talk and obscene speech Al-Farra' and Al-Akhfash said: That is, no idle word will be heard therein. There are six meanings for this: First: It means lies, slander, and disbelief in God Almighty, as stated by Ibn Abbas. Second: Neither falsehood nor sin, as stated by Qatadah. Third: It means cursing, as stated by Mujahid. Fourth: Disobedience, as stated by Al-Hasan. Fifth: No one who swears a false oath will be heard therein, as stated by Al-Farra'. Al-Kalbi said: No one who swears a righteous or wicked oath will be heard in Paradise. Sixth: No idle word will be heard in their speech, because the people of Paradise will only speak with wisdom and praise of God for the eternal bliss He has provided them with, as stated by Al-Farra'. This is the best of them because it includes everything mentioned. Abu Amr and Ibn Kathir readل يسمْمwith a ya' other than the named agent. Nafi' did the same, except with a damma ta' because laghiya is a feminine noun, so fa-t is the verb because it is feminine. Whoever reads it with a ya' does so because it comes between the noun and the prepositional phrase. The rest read it with an open laghiya as a text that attributes this to the faces, meaning that the faces are not heard as laghiya in it.
88:12: The Almighty says: Therein is a flowing spring meaning with gushing water and various types of delicious drinks on the face of the earth without a trench. It was mentioned in Surah Al-Insan that there are springs in it. So ‘ain means springs. And God knows best.
88:13: God Almighty says: Therein are raised couches: meaning high. It was narrated that its height was equal to the distance between the sky and the earth, so that the friend of God could see His kingdom around him.
88:14: The Almighty says: And cups placed meaning pitchers and vessels. A pitcher is one that has a handle and spout. A cup is a vessel that does not have a handle or spout. This has been mentioned previously in Surat Az-Zukhruf and elsewhere.
88:15: The Almighty said: And cushions meaning pillows, one is a namariqah. “Arrayed” meaning one next to the other. The poet said: We are running the cup between our drink and Abu Qaboos over the cushions Another said: Old men and young men with handsome faces on lined beds and cushions In Al-Sahah: Namraq and Namraqa: a small pillow. Also, Namraqa with a kasra is a language narrated by Yaqub. And they may have called the cushion that is over the saddle a Namraqa, according to Abu Ubaid.
88:16: The Almighty said: And carpets spread out: Abu Ubaidah said: Carpets are rugs. Ibn Abbas said: Carpets are the fine nap rugs, the singular of which is: zarbiyyah, and this was said by Al-Kalbi and Al-Farra'. And Al-Mabthoutha is: spread out, said by Qatada. It was also said: some of them on top of each other, said by Ikrimah. It was also said: many, said by Al-Farra'. It was also said: scattered in gatherings, said by Al-Qutbi. I said: This is more correct, as they are many and scattered. And from it is: And He spread therein every kind of creature (al-Baqarah 2:64). Abu Bakr Al-Anbari said: Ahmad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hussain bin Arfa told us, he said: Ammar bin Muhammad told us, he said: I prayed behind Mansur bin Al-Mu’tamir, and he recited: Has there come to you the report of the Overwhelming? And he recited in it: And carpets spread out: spread out therein, softly.
88:17: The Almighty's saying: Do they not look at the camels - how they are created? The commentators said: When God the Almighty mentioned the matter of the people of the two abodes, the disbelievers were amazed by that, so they lied and denied it. God then reminded them of His creation and power, and that He is capable of all things, just as He created the animals, the heavens, and the earth. Then He mentioned camels first, because they are numerous among the Arabs, and they had not seen elephants. So God, the Most High, reminded them of a great thing among His creation, which He has subdued for the young, leading it, making it kneel, making it rise, and carrying heavy loads on it while it is kneeling, so it rises its heavy load. This is not the case with any other animal. So He showed them a great thing among His creation, subservient to a young thing among His creation, guiding them with that to His Oneness and His great power. And it was narrated from one of the wise men that he spoke about the camel and its wondrous creation. It grew up in a land where there were no camels, so it thought and then said: It is likely that it will have long necks. And when He intended them to be ships of the land, He made them patient in enduring thirst, until their thirst rose to ten degrees and above. And He made them graze on everything that grows in the wilderness and deserts, which other animals do not graze. And it was said: When He mentioned the raised thrones, they said: How do we climb them? So God revealed this verse, and explained that camels kneel until they are loaded and then stand up, and likewise those thrones lower themselves and then rise. Qatada al-Tha’labi said its meaning: And it was said about camels here: the clouds, but I did not find a basis for that in the books of the Imams. I said: Al-As'ami has mentioned Abu Sa'id Abdul Malik bin Qurayb. Abu Amr said: Whoever reads it Do they not look at the camels - how they were created with a light pronunciation means the camel, because it is a quadruped; it kneels and loads are carried on it, while other quadrupeds are not carried except while standing. Whoever reads it with a heavy pronunciation and says al-ibil, means the clouds that carry water and rain. Al-Mawardi said: There are two views regarding camels: The first, which is the most obvious and famous, is that they are camels from the naghm. The second: that they are the clouds. If what is meant by them is the clouds, then it is because they contain signs indicating His power and the general benefits for all of His creation. If what is meant by them are camels from the blessings, then it is because camels are more comprehensive in benefits than other animals, because they are of four types: milking, riding, eating, and carrying loads. Camels combine these four characteristics, so the blessing in them is more general, and the manifestation of power in them is more complete. Al-Hasan said: God only mentioned them specifically because they eat date pits and dung, and produce milk. Al-Hasan was also asked about it and they said: The elephant is the greatest wonder. He said: The Arabs have long known the elephant. Moreover, it is a pig whose meat is not eaten, whose back is not ridden, and whose milk is not milked. Shuraih used to say: Let us go out to the garbage dump so that we can see how camels were created. Camels have no singular form in their own words, and they are feminine, because plural nouns that have no singular form in their words, if they are for non-humans, then the feminine is obligatory. If you make them diminutive, the letter ha’ is added to them, so you say abilah and ghanima, and the like. Sometimes they say for camels: ibl, with the ba’ silent for ease, and the plural is abal.
88:18: The Almighty says: And to the heaven, how it was raised. That is, it was raised above the earth without pillars. It was also said: it was raised, so nothing could reach it.
88:19: The Almighty says: And to the mountains, how they are fixed. That is, how they are fixed on the earth, so that they do not move. This is because when the earth was spread out, it moved, so He anchored it with mountains. As He said: And We placed on the earth firm mountains, lest it should move with them. (Al-Anbiya’: 31)
88:20: The Almighty said: And to the earth, how it was spread out meaning it was extended and spread out. Anas said: I prayed behind Ali, may God be pleased with him, and he recited how it was created and raised and lowered and spread out, with a damma on the ta's, he attributed the pronoun to God Almighty. Muhammad bin as-Sameefa' and Abu al-Aliyah used to recite it this way, and the object was omitted, and the meaning is I created it. And so are the rest of it. Al-Hasan, Abu Haywah, and Abu Raja' recited sataht with a shaddah on the ta' and a sukoon on the ta'. The group recited it this way, except that they lightened the ta'. Camels were mentioned first, and if something else had been mentioned first it would have been permissible. Al-Qushayri said: This is not something in which any wisdom is sought. It has been said: It is closer to people in the case of the Arabs, because of their abundance, and they are the most knowledgeable about them. Also: Camels have more facilities than other animals, as they are edible, their milk is drinkable, they are suitable for carrying and riding, covering long distances, enduring thirst, little fodder, and carrying large loads, and they constitute most of the Arabs’ wealth. They used to ride camels alone, isolated from people, and someone like this would contemplate what was present, so he might look at his mount, then look up to the sky, then down to the ground. So they were commanded to look at these things, as they are the clearest evidence of the Creator, the Chosen, the Able.
88:21: God Almighty says: So remind, for you are only a reminder. That is, preach to them, O Muhammad, and frighten them. For you are only a reminder. That is, a preacher.
88:22: The Almighty said: You have no control over them meaning you have power over them to kill them. Then the verse of the sword abrogated it. Harun al-A'war read with a fat-ha on the ta', and al-musaytirun. It is the language of Tamim. In As-Sahah: (Al-Musaytaar and Al-Musaytaar: the one who has power over something to supervise it, and take care of its affairs, and write down its work. Its origin is from the line, because the meaning of the line is not to exceed, so the book is lined, and the one who does it is lined and the one who does it is lined, it is said: I controlled us, and the Almighty said: You have no control over them. And his line means he wrestled.
88:23: The Almighty’s saying: Except for he who turns away and disbelieves. This is an isolated exception, meaning, but for he who turns away from preaching and reminding.
88:24: The Almighty says: Then God will punish him with the greatest punishment, which is Hell, the torment of which is eternal. He only said the greatest because they were punished in this world with hunger, famine, captivity, and killing. The evidence for this interpretation is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: (Except for he who turns away and disbelieves. For indeed, God will punish him). It was also said: It is a connected exception. The meaning is: You will not have power except for he who turns away and disbelieves. So you will have power over him through jihad, and God will punish him after that with the greatest punishment. So, there is no abrogation in the verse according to this estimation. It was narrated that a man who had apostatized was brought to Ali, so he asked him to repent for three days, but he did not return to Islam, so he struck off his head and recited: Then God will punish him with the greatest punishment. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah recited ala as an opening and a warning, like the saying of Imru' al-Qais: Is there not a day for you from them that is good? And who is on this for the condition and the answer.
88:25: The Almighty says: Then God will punish him. The subject after the fa is implied, and the meaning is: So God will punish him, because if the answer was intended by the verb after the fa, it would be: Except for he who turns away and disbelieves, God will punish him. Indeed, to Us is their return meaning their return after death. It is said: abba ya'ub meaning he returned. Ubayd said: Everyone who is absent will return, but the one absent from death will not return. Abu Jaafar readيْابهمwith a shaddah. Abu Hatim said: The shaddah is not permissible, if it were, something similar would have been permissible in fasting and standing in prayer. It was said: They are two meanings. Al-Zamakhshari: Abu Jaafar Al-Madani readيْابهمwith a shaddah, and the reason for that is that it is fi’aal, a source of ayyab, it was said from al-iyyab. Or that its root is iwaaban fa’al from awb, then it was said: iwaaban in duwan. Then he did what is based on the root of sayyid and the like.
88:26: God Almighty says: Then upon Us is their account.
89:1: Meccan and it has thirty verses. God the Almighty said: And the dawn He swore by the dawn. And ten nights * And the even and the odd * And the night when it departs five divisions. There is a difference of opinion about the dawn. Some people said that the dawn here is the emergence of darkness from the day of every day. This was stated by Ali, Ibn al-Zubayr, and Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them. It was also narrated from Ibn Abbas that it means the entire day, and he referred to it as the dawn because it is its beginning. Ibn Muhaisin said on the authority of Atiyyah on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It means the dawn of the day of Muharram. Qatada said something similar.
