He said: It is the dawn of the first day of Muharram. From it the Sunnah begins. It was also narrated from him: The dawn prayer. Ibn Jurayj narrated on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The dawn means the morning of the Day of Sacrifice, because God the Almighty has made a night of qibla for every day, except for the Day of Nahr, for which He did not make a night of qibla or a night after it, because the Day of Arafah has two nights: a night before it and a night after it. So whoever reaches the standing place one night after Arafah has reached the Hajj at the break of dawn, the dawn of the Day of Sacrifice. This is the statement of Mujahid. Akrima said: And the dawn He said: The break of dawn on the day of Jumu’ah. And on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi: And the dawn is the last days of the ten days, when it is due on the day of Jumu’ah.
89:2: Ad-Dahhak said: Fajr of Dhul-Hijjah, because God linked the days to it, saying: And ten nights, meaning ten nights of Dhul-Hijjah. This is what Mujahid, As-Suddi, and Al-Kalbi said about His statement: And ten nights, meaning ten nights of Dhul-Hijjah, and Ibn Abbas said the same. Masruq said: They are the ten that God mentioned in the story of Moses, peace be upon him. And We completed it with ten (al-A’raf 7:142), which are the best days of the year. Abu Al-Zubayr narrated on the authority of Jabir: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By the dawn and ten nights. He said: The ten nights of Al-Adha. So they are ten nights according to this statement, because the night of the Day of Sacrifice is included in it, as God has made it a place of standing for those who did not stand on the Day of Arafah. It was made indefinite and not definite because of its superiority over others. If it had been made definite, it would not have received the meaning of superiority that is in the indefinite form, so it was made indefinite among what he swore by, because of the superiority that is not for others. And God knows best. And from Ibn Abbas also: It is the first ten of Muharram, which is the tenth of the Day of Ashura. And from Ibn Abbas: And ten nights with the addition he means: and the nights of ten days.
89:3: God Almighty says: And the even and the odd. Shafa’ means two, and Witr means one. There is disagreement about this. It was narrated on the authority of Imran ibn al-Husayn on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: (And shafa` and witr: the prayer, from it shafa` and from it witr). And Jabir ibn Abdullah said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And the dawn * and ten nights. He said: It is the dawn, and the ten days of sacrifice, and the witr is the day of Arafah, and shafa` is the day of sacrifice. This is the saying of Ibn Abbas and Ikrimah. An-Nahhas chose it and said: The hadith of Abu al-Zubayr from Jabir is the one that is authentic from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it has a more authentic chain of transmission than the hadith of Imran ibn Husayn. The day of Arafah is witr because it is the ninth, and the day of sacrifice is shafa` because it is the tenth. And on the authority of Abu Ayyub, he said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was asked about the verse: and the even and the odd. He said: The even is the Day of Arafah and the Day of Sacrifice, and the odd is the night of the Day of Sacrifice. Mujahid and Ibn Abbas also said: The even is His creation. God the Almighty says: And We created you in pairs (An-Naba’: 8) and the odd is God the Almighty. Mujahid was asked: Have you narrated it from someone? He said: Yes, from Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him). Muhammad ibn Sirin, Masruq, Abu Salih and Qatadah said something similar. They said: The even is the creation. God the Almighty says: And of everything We have created pairs (al-Dhariyat 51:49): disbelief and faith, misery and happiness, guidance and misguidance, light and darkness, night and day, heat and cold, sun and moon, summer and winter, sky and earth, jinn and mankind. And the Witr: is God the Almighty, He said, may He be glorified: “Say, ‘He is God, the One. God, the Self-Sufficient.’” (al-Ikhla 112:1-2) and “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘God has ninety-nine names, and God is odd and loves odd numbers.’” And also on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The even prayer is the Fajr prayer and the Witr is the Maghrib prayer. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas and Abu Al-Aaliyah said: It is the Maghrib prayer, the even prayer is two rak’ahs, and the Witr is the third. Ibn Al-Zubayr said: The even prayer is the eleventh, twelfth, and thirteenth of Mina. God the Almighty said: “But whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him. And whoever delays, there is no sin upon him.” (al-Baqarah 2:203) Ad-Dahhak said: Ash-Shafa’ is the ten days of Dhul-Hijjah, and Al-Witr is the three days of Mina. This is the opinion of Ata’. It was also said that Ash-Shafa’ and Al-Witr are Adam and Eve, because Adam was alone, so he made an even number with his wife Hawass, so he became an even number after an odd number. Narrated by Ibn Abi Nujayh, and Al-Qushayri narrated it from Ibn Abbas. In another narration: Ash-Shafa’ is Adam and Eve, and Al-Witr is God. It was also said that Ash-Shafa’ and Al-Witr are creation, because they are both even and odd, so it is as if He swore by creation. God swears by His names and attributes because of His work, and He swears by His actions because of His power, as He says: And by Him who created the male and female (al-Layl 92:3). He swears by His actions, because of the wonders of His creation, as He says: And by the sun and its brightness (Ash-Shams: 1), And by the heaven and He who constructed it (Ash-Shams: 5), And by the heaven and the Nightcomer (al-Tariq 86:1). It was said: Ash-Shafa': the levels of Paradise, which are eight. And Ash-Witr: the levels of Hellfire, because they are seven. This is the saying of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Fadl, as if he swore by Paradise and Hellfire. It was also said: Ash-Shafa': Al-Safa and Al-Marwah, and Ash-Witr: the Ka'bah. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: Ash-Shafa': the days and nights, and Ash-Witr: the day after which there is no night, which is the Day of Resurrection. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: Ash-Witr is God, and He is Ash-Shafa' also, because God the Almighty said: There are not three who confer privately but He is the fourth of them (Al-Mujadilah: 7). Abu Bakr Al-Warraq said: Ash-Shafa': the contrast of the descriptions of created beings: glory and humiliation, power and weakness, strength and weakness, knowledge without ignorance, life and death, sight and blindness, hearing and deafness, speech and muteness. Al-Witr: The uniqueness of God’s attributes: Glory without humiliation, Power without weakness, Strength without weakness, Knowledge without ignorance, Life without death, Sight without blindness, Speech without dumbness, Hearing without deafness, and what is equivalent to them. Al-Hasan said: What is meant by Shaf’ and Witr is the whole number, because a number is never devoid of both, and it is an oath by calculation. It was also said: Al-Shaf’ is the mosque of Mecca and Medina, which are the two sacred mosques. Al-Witr is the mosque of Jerusalem. It was also said: Al-Shaf’ is the combination of Hajj and Umrah or the enjoyment of Umrah to Hajj. Al-Witr is the separation of it. It was also said: Al-Shaf’ is the combination of Hajj and Umrah, or the enjoyment of Umrah to Hajj. Al-Witr is the separation of it. It was also said: Al-Shaf’ is the animal, because it is male and female. Al-Witr is the inanimate. Al-Kisa’i, Hamzah, and Khalaf said Wa-Witr with a kasra over the waw. The rest said Wa-Witr with a fatha over the waw, and they are two languages with one meaning. In As-Sahah: Al-Witr with a kasra is the individual, and Al-Witr with a fatha over the waw is the hump. This is the language of the people of Alia. As for the language of the people of Hijaz, it is the opposite of them. As for Tamim, it is the kasra in both.
89:4: The Almighty said: And the night when it departs. This is a fifth oath. After swearing by the ten nights specifically, He swore by the night in general. The meaning of descends is that it departs in it, as one says: a sleeping night, and a fasting day. He said: You blamed us, O Umm Ghilan, in the night, and you slept, while the night of the mounts was not asleep. And from this is the saying of God the Almighty: Rather, [it is] the plotting of the night and the day (Saba’: 33). This is the opinion of most of the people of semantics, and it is the opinion of Al-Qutabi and Al-Akhfash. Most of the commentators said: The meaning of yasra is: he traveled and went. Qatada and Abu Al-Aaliyah said: he came and approached. It was narrated from Ibrahim: and the night when it departs he said: when it is equal. Ikrimah, Al-Kalbi, Mujahid and Muhammad bin Ka’b said regarding His statement: and al-Layl 92:it is the night of Muzdalifah in particular, because it is unique in that people gather to obey God. It was said: it is the Night of Decree, because mercy spreads in it, and it is unique in that it is unique in that it is rewarded more. It was said: he meant the whole night in general. I said: This is more apparent, as mentioned above. And God knows best. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaisin, and Ya`qub read yusri with the ya’ in both cases, according to the original rule, because it is not jazm, so the ya’ was kept in it. Nafi` and Abu `Amr read it with it in connection and with it being deleted when stopping. This was narrated from al-Kisa’i. Abu `Ubaid said: Al-Kisa’i once said with the ya’ in connection and with it being deleted when stopping, following the Qur’an. Then he returned to deleting the ya’ in both cases because it is the beginning of a verse. This is the reading of the people of Ash-Sham and Kufa, and the choice of Abu `Ubaid, following the script, because it occurs in the Qur’an without a ya’. Al-Khalil said: The ya’ is dropped from it by agreement at the beginning of verses. Al-Farra’ said: The Arabs sometimes delete the ya’ and are satisfied with the kasra of what precedes it. One of them recited: Enough, a hand that does not befit a generous dirham and another that gives blood with the sword It is said: So-and-so does not deserve a dirham of his generosity, meaning he does not hold it or stick to it. Al-Mu'arraj said: I asked Al-Akhfash about the reason for dropping the ya' from yusra. He said: I will answer you until you spend the night at my door for a year. So I spent the night at his door for a year. He said: The night does not move, but rather it moves into it, so it is diverted. And whatever you divert from its direction, you diminish its syntactic position. Do you not see the saying of God the Almighty: {And your mother was not unchaste} (Maryam 19:28), and He did not say boughyah because He diverted it from baghiyah. Al-Zamakhshari: The ya' of yusra is dropped in the dargah, as it is sufficient for it to have a kasrah. As for when stopping, it is dropped with the kasrah. All of these nouns are in the genitive case by the oath, and the answer is dropped, which is li'ya'adhban, indicated by the saying of God the Almighty: {Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with} - to His saying: {So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment} [Al-Fajr 13]. Ibn al-Anbari said: It is Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful (al-Fajr 89:14). Muqatil said: Hal here is in place of in, meaning: Indeed, in that is an oath for one with reason. So hal according to this is in place of the answer to the oath. It was said that it is in its category of interrogation, the meaning of which is confirmation, like you saying: Did I not bestow a favor upon you? if you had bestowed a favor. It was said that what is meant by that is emphasis on what He swore by and what He swore upon. The meaning is: Rather, in that is convincing for one with reason. The answer to this is: Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful. Or an omitted implied word.
89:5: The meaning of one with reason is one with intelligence and intellect. The poet said: How can you hope to repent? Only those young men who have a mind are expected to repent. This is what most of the commentators said, except that Abu Malik said: the one with a screen: the one who is concealed from people. Al-Hasan said: the one with a dream. Al-Farraa said: They all go back to one meaning: the one with a dream, the one with a mind, the one with a dream, and the one who conceals, all with the meaning of the mind. The root of the word hajar is: prevention. It is said of someone who controls himself and prevents himself: he is a man of a dream, and from it the stone was named, because it is prevented by its hardness. And from it is the rule of the ruler over someone, meaning he prevented him and controlled him from acting, and for this reason the room was named a room, because what is in it is prevented by it. Al-Farraa said: The Arabs say: he is a man of a dream: if he is dominant over himself, controlling it, as if he took from the one who forbade the man.
89:6: The Almighty said: Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with 'Aad? meaning your Owner and Creator. 'Aad is the reading of the common people 'Aad with the tanween, while Al-Hasan and Abu Al-Aaliyah read 'Aad Iram' with the genitive case. Whoever does not add the genitive case makes Iram his proper noun and does not decline it, because he made 'Aad the name of their father and 'Iram the name of the tribe, making it a substitute for him or an explanatory conjunction. Whoever reads it with the genitive case and does not decline it makes it the name of their mother or the name of their town. The meaning is: 'Aad, the people of Iram. Like His statement: And ask the town (Yusuf 12:82) and it is not declined - whether it is a tribe or a land - for the purpose of definiteness and femininity. The common people read Iram with a kasra on the hamza. Also from Al-Hasan 'Aad Iram with both fat-has, and 'Aad Iram' is read with a sukoon on the ra' for the sake of alleviation, as it is read with your paper. And 'Aad Iram, of the pillars' is read by adding Iram -to- of the pillars. And Iram is the flag. That is, the people of knowledge are far away. It was read Baad Iram of the pillars, meaning, God made the pillars into dust. Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, and Qatadah read Iram with a fat-ha on the hamza. Mujahid said: whoever reads with a fat-ha on the hamza likened them to the Aram, which are the flags, the singular of which is Iram. And in the speech there is an inversion, meaning, and the dawn and so on and so forth. Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful. Have you not seen? That is, has your knowledge not reached what your Lord did to Aad? And this vision is a vision of the heart, and the address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant is general. And the matter of Aad and Thamud was with them Famous, as they were in the land of the Arabs, and the Stone of Thamud exists today. And the matter of Pharaoh they heard from their neighbors from the People of the Book, and the report about it was widespread, and the land of Pharaoh was connected to the land of the Arabs. This meaning was mentioned previously in Surah Al-Buruj and others. By Ad means by the people of Ad. Shahr bin Hawshab narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah who said: If a man from the people of Ad were to make a door from stones, even if five hundred of this nation gathered around him, they would not be able to lift him, and one of them would put his foot in the ground and it would enter into it.
89:7: And Iram: It was said that he is Sam bin Noah, as said by Ibn Ishaq. Ata' narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas - and he also narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq - who said: Ad bin Iram. So, Iram, according to this, is the father of Ad, and Ad bin Iram bin Aws bin Sam bin Noah. According to the first opinion: It is the name of the grandfather of Ad. Ibn Ishaq said: Sam bin Noah had sons, among them Iram bin Sam and Arfakhshad bin Sam. So, from the sons of Iram bin Sam were the giants, the Pharaohs, the tyrants, the tyrannical kings and the disobedient. Mujahid said: Iram is a nation among the nations. It was also narrated from him: that the meaning of Iram is: the ancient, and Ibn Abi Nujayj narrated it. Mujahid also said that it means the strong. Qatada said: It is a tribe from Ad. It was said: They are two Ad. The first is Iram, as God the Almighty said: And that He destroyed the former Ad (al-Najm 53:50). The descendants of Aad bin Aws bin Iram bin Sam bin Noah were called: Aad, just as the Banu Hashim were called: Hashim. Then the first of them were called: Aad the First. And Iram is a name for them by their grandfather’s name. And for those who came after them: Aad the Last. Ibn al-Ruqayat said: An ancient glory built by the first of them who reached Ad and before him Irma Muammar said: Iram: To it gathered Ad and Thamud. It was said: Ad Iram, and Ad Thamud. The tribes were descended from Iram. Of the pillars * The like of which had not been created in the land. Ibn Abbas said in the narration of Ata’: A man among them was five hundred cubits tall, and the short one among them was three hundred cubits tall, according to his own cubit. It was also narrated from Ibn Abbas that the height of a man among them was seventy cubits. Ibn al-Arabi: It is false, because in the Sahih: God created Adam sixty cubits tall in the air, and creation has continued to decrease until now. Qatada claimed that the height of a man among them was twelve cubits. Abu Ubaidah said: Dhat al-Imad means tall. It is said: A man with pillars if he is tall. Something similar was narrated from Ibn Abbas and Mujahid. Qatada also said: They were pillars for their people. It was said: So-and-so is the leader and pillar of the people, meaning their master. He also said: They were called that because they used to move with their tents to seek refuge, and they were people of tents and pillars, seeking rain and seeking pasture, then they would return to their homes. It was said: Dhat al-Imad means buildings raised on pillars. They used to erect pillars and build palaces on them. Ibn Zayd said: Dhat al-Imad means the strength of the building with pillars. In Al-Sahah: Imad means tall buildings, masculine and feminine. Amr ibn Kulthum said: If the pillars of the neighborhood fall on the diapers, we will prevent those who follow us The singular is imaadah. So-and-so has tall pillars: if his house is a landmark for his visitors. Ahfad: the plural of hafidh with a fat-ha, which is the furnishings of the house if it is prepared to be carried, i.e. it falls on the furnishings. It is narrated, about ahfadah, meaning it fell off the camels that carry the dung of the house. Ad-Dahhak said: Dhat al-Imad has strength and intensity, taken from the strength of the columns, the evidence for this is the saying of God the Almighty: And they said, ‘Who is stronger than us in strength?’ (Fussilat 41:15). Aouf narrated from Khalid Ar-Rab’i: Iram, Dhat al-Imad, he said: It is Damascus. This is the saying of Ikrimah and Saeed Al-Maqburi. Ibn Wahb and Ashab narrated it from Malik. Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi said: It is Alexandria.
89:8: The Almighty says: The like of which has not been created in any land. The pronoun in the like of it refers to the tribe. That is, the like of the tribe has not been created in any land: strength and intensity, large bodies, and tall stature, according to Al-Hasan and others. In Abdullah's version: The like of which has not been created in any land. It was said: It refers to the city. The first is more apparent, and most agree with it, according to what we have mentioned. Whoever makes Iram a city has decreed an omission, the meaning: How did your Lord deal with the city of Ad, Iram, or after its companion Iram? And Iram, according to this, is a definite feminine. Ibn Al-Arabi chose it to be Damascus, because there is nothing like it in any land. Then he began to describe it with its abundant waters and bounties. Then he said: Alexandria is truly amazing, if it had nothing but the lighthouse, for it is built, outwardly and inwardly, on columns, but it has its equals, but Damascus has no equal. Ma'n narrated from Malik that a book was found in Alexandria, but he did not know what it was? Then he said: “I am Shaddad bin Aad, who raised the pillars. I built it when there was no gray hair or death.” Malik said: A hundred years would pass without them seeing a funeral. It was mentioned on the authority of Thawr bin Zaid that he said: “I am Shaddad bin Aad, and I raised the pillars. I am the one who strengthened the valley with my two arms. I am the one who stored a treasure seven cubits long, which none but the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, will extract.” It was narrated that Aad had two sons: Shaddad and Shadid. They ruled and conquered, then Shadid died, and the matter was given to Shaddad, so he ruled the world, and its kings submitted to him. He heard about Paradise, so he said: Build something like it. So he built Iram in some of the deserts of Aden, in three hundred years, and he lived nine hundred years. It is a great city, its palaces are made of gold and silver, and its pillars are made of emerald and ruby. It has various types of trees and flowing rivers. When it was completed, he marched towards it with the people of his kingdom. When he was a day and a night’s journey from it, God sent a shout upon them from the sky. So they perished. It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Qilabah that he went out in search of his camels, and he came across them, so he carried what he could of what was there. report of this reached Muawiyah, so he summoned him and told him the story. The latter sent to Ka’b and asked him. He said: It is Iram of the Pillars, and a man from the Muslims will enter it in your time, red-haired, blond, short, with a mole on his eyebrow and a mole on his heel. He will go out in search of his camels. Then he turned and saw Ibn Qilabah and said: By God, this is that man. It was said: Nothing was created like the buildings of Aad, which were known as pillars. So the metaphor is for pillars. And pillars, according to this, is the plural of pillars. It was also said that Iram means destruction. It is said: The sons of so-and-so were Iram, meaning they perished, and Ibn Abbas said the same. Ad-Dahhak read: Iram of the Pillars, meaning he destroyed them and turned them into dust.
89:9: The Almighty said: And Thamud who hewed out the rocks in the valley. Thamud: they are the people of Salih. Hewed out means they cut. And from this: So-and-so travels the lands, i.e. he traverses them. And the shirt's pocket was named so because it is pocket, i.e. he cut. The poet said: He had stayed with Ibn al-Zubayr in Mecca, so he wrote him sixty wasqs to take in Kufa. So he said: She went on her way, praising the Al-Zubayr family and not treating anyone equally. She carried sixty wasqs in her bag, she did not carry her minimum load nor the full amount I have never seen a camel before that carried sixty camels or traversed a country with it. Any cut. The commentators said: The first to carve mountains, images, and marble were Thamud. They built 1,700 cities, all of them from stone. And 2,700,000 houses and dwellings, all of them from stone. God the Almighty said: And they carved out of the mountains, houses, feeling secure. (al-Hijr 15:82). And for their sustenance, they extracted rocks, dug into the mountains, and made them homes for themselves. In the valley means in the valleys of the villages, as Muhammad ibn Ishaq said. “Abu Al-Ashab narrated on the authority of Abu Nadrah that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to the valley of Thamud during the Tabuk expedition, and he was on a blond horse, and he said: Hurry up, for you are in a cursed valley.” It was said: The valley is between mountains, and they used to dig in those mountains houses, houses, and pools. And every gap between mountains or hills that is a path for a stream or an outlet is a valley.
89:10: God the Almighty says: And Pharaoh, lord of the stakes meaning the soldiers, armies, multitudes and armies that strengthen his kingdom, as stated by Ibn Abbas. It was also said that he used to torture people with stakes, and tie them to them until they died, out of his tyranny and arrogance. This is what he did with his wife Asiya and his daughter's hairdresser, as mentioned above at the end of Surah At-Tahrim. Abdur-Rahman bin Zaid said: He had a rock that was raised with pulleys, then a person would be taken and iron stakes would be fixed for him, then that rock would be lowered upon him and it would crush him. Sufficient mention of his stakes has already been made in Surah Sad. Praise be to God.
89:11: The Almighty says: Those who transgressed in the land meaning Aad, Thamud, and Pharaoh transgressed meaning they rebelled, acted insolently, and exceeded the limits in injustice and aggression.
89:12: The Almighty's statement: And they increased therein corruption meaning the harm and injury. Those who transgressed The best interpretation of this is that it is in the accusative case as a censure. It is also permissible for it to be in the nominative case as: they are the ones who transgressed, or in the genitive case as a description of those mentioned: Aad, Thamud, and Pharaoh.
89:13: The Almighty said: So your Lord poured down upon them a scourge of punishment. That is, He poured down upon them and threw it down. It is said: He poured down a robe of rank upon someone, meaning he cast it down upon him. Al-Nabigha said: So God bestowed upon him the best of His creations, and He was his helper among the wilderness. A whip of torment means a portion of torment. It is also said: its severity, because the whip was, for them, the ultimate means of torment. The poet said: Have you not seen that God has made His religion manifest and poured upon the disbelievers a scourge of torment? Al-Farra’ said: It is a word that the Arabs say for every type of torture. The origin of that is that the whip is their torture with which they torture, so it was used for every torture, as it was for them the ultimate torture. It was said: Its meaning is a torture that mixes flesh and blood, from their saying: Satahu yastuhu swatan or i.e. he mixed it, so he is a say’it. So the whip is: mixing one thing with another, and from it the name al-musawat was given. Intermediation means mixing it, so he is a say’it, and it is often said: So-and-so whipped his affairs. He said: Its middle is ugly and its opinion is unsuccessful, so I am not able to level it with meanings Abu Zaid said: It is said that their wealth is mixed among them, meaning mixed together. Yaqub narrated it from him. Al-Zajjaj said: It means that He made their whip with which he struck them the punishment. It is said: He struck his animal with his whip, meaning he struck it with his whip. Amr ibn Ubayd narrated: When Al-Hasan recited this verse, he said: God has many whips, so he took them with one of them. Qatada said: Everything with which God punishes is a whip of punishment.
89:14: God Almighty says: Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful. That is, He monitors the deeds of every person until He rewards him for them. This was said by Al-Hasan and Ikrimah. It was also said: That is, on the path of the servants, no one misses Him. The watchtower and the watchtower: the road. This was mentioned in Surah Bara’ah. Praise be to God. Ad-Dahhak narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: “There are seven bridges over Hellfire. A person will be asked at the first bridge about faith. If he completes it, he will pass to the second bridge. Then he will be asked about prayer. If he completes it, he will pass to the third. Then he will be asked about zakat. If he completes it, he will pass to the fourth. Then he will be asked about fasting the month of Ramadan. If he completes it, he will pass to the fifth. Then he will be asked about Hajj and Umrah. If he completes them, he will pass to the sixth. Then he will be asked about maintaining kinship ties. If he completes them, people will be allowed to do the same to him, and he will be punished for it from the people. This is what God, the Almighty, said: “Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful.” Ath-Thawri said: ever watchful means that Hellfire has three bridges over it: a bridge over which is kinship ties, and a bridge over which he hears and sees. I said: This is a good statement. He hears their words and their private conversations, and sees their deeds and secrets, so He rewards each one according to his deeds. It was narrated from some of the Arabs that he was asked: Where is your Lord? He said: He is watching. It was narrated from Amr ibn Ubayd that he recited this Surah in the presence of Al-Mansur until he reached this verse, and he said: Indeed, your Lord is watching, O Abu Ja`far! Al-Zamakhshari said: This call made him think that he was one of the tyrants who had been threatened with that, so may God bless him. What a lion of a horse was he before him? He crushed the oppressors with his denial, and suppressed the people of whims and innovations with his arguments!
89:15: The Almighty said: As for man, meaning the disbeliever. Ibn Abbas said: He means Utbah ibn Rabi’ah and Abu Hudhayfah ibn al-Mughirah. It was also said: Umayyah ibn Khalaf. It was also said: Ubayy ibn Khalaf. When his Lord tests him, meaning He tests him and tries him with blessings. Ma: is an additional conjunction. He honors him with money. And blesses him with what He has given him. Then he says, ‘My Lord has honored me,’ so he rejoices in that and does not praise Him.
89:16: God the Almighty says: But when He tests him i.e., tests him with poverty and tries him, then He restricts i.e., restricts his provision to the extent of what is sufficient. He says, ‘My Lord has humiliated me’ i.e., He has treated me with disgrace. This is the description of the disbeliever who does not believe in the resurrection. For him, honor and disgrace are due to the abundance or scarcity of his share in this world. As for the believer, honor for him is that God honors him with His obedience and guidance, which leads to the share of the Hereafter, and if He gives him plenty in this world, he praises and thanks Him. I said: The two verses describe every disbeliever. Many Muslims think that what God has given them is due to their honor and virtue with God, and they may say out of ignorance: If I did not deserve this, God would not have given it to me. Similarly, if someone is miserly with someone, he thinks that it is because he is insignificant before God. The general reading is fa-qadar with a light dal. Ibn ‘Amir read it with a shaddah, and these are two dialects. The preferred reading is the light one, based on God’s statement: And whoever has restricted his provision (al-Talaq 65:7). Abu ‘Amr said: and (qadar) means being miserly. qadar with a shaddah means giving someone what is sufficient for him, and if that were done to him, he would not have said My Lord has humiliated him. The people of the Two Sanctuaries and Abu ‘Amr read rabbī with a fathah on the ya’ in both instances. The rest made it sukun. Al-Buzī, Ibn Muhaysin, and Ya’qub confirmed the ya’ in akramaan and ahanan in both instances, because it is a noun and should not be deleted. The Medinan scholars confirmed it in the continuous version but not in the pause version, following the Qur’an. Abu Amr chose to keep it in the connected recitation or delete it, because it is the beginning of a verse, and to delete it when stopping due to the script of the Qur’an. The rest chose to delete it, because it occurred in both places without a ya’, and the Sunnah is not to deviate from the script of the Qur’an, because that is the consensus of the Companions.
89:17: The Almighty's statement: No is a response, meaning that the matter is not as he thinks, for wealth is not due to His grace, and poverty is not due to His humiliation, but rather poverty and wealth are from My decree and judgment. Al-Farra' said: No in this instance means that the servant should not have been like this, but rather he should praise God the Almighty for wealth and poverty. And in the hadith: (God Almighty says: No, I do not honor those whom I have honored with an abundance of this world, nor do I humiliate those whom I have humiliated with a scarcity of it. Rather, I honor those whom I have honored with My obedience, and I humiliate those whom I have humiliated with My disobedience.) God the Almighty said: Rather, you do not honor the orphan This is a report about what they used to do of denying the orphan his inheritance, and consuming his wealth extravagantly and hastily before they grow up. Abu Amr and Ya'qub read they honor, they incite, they eat, and they love with the letter ya because the human being was mentioned before, and what is meant by it is the species, so it was expressed in the plural. The rest read it with the letter ta in the four verses, addressing and directing them, as if he said that to them as a rebuke and reprimand. He abandoned honoring the orphan by denying him his right, and consuming his wealth as we mentioned. Muqatil said: It was revealed about Qudamah ibn Maz'un who was an orphan under the care of Umayyah ibn Khalaf.
89:18: The Almighty said: And do not urge one another to feed the poor meaning, they should not order their families to feed a poor person when they come. The Kufians read and do not urge one another with a fat-ha on both ta's because the statement indicates this. This is the preferred choice of Abu Ubaid. It was narrated from hadh, which means urging.
89:19: God the Almighty said: And you devour the inheritance meaning the inheritance of orphans. Its root is warath from waratha, so they replaced the waw with a ta', as they said in tijajah, takhamah, taka'ah, taw'ada and the like. Aklan lama has already been said, meaning intensely, as al-Suddi said. It was said: lamma is to gather, from their saying: I ate the food lama if you ate it all, as al-Hasan and Abu Ubaidah said. The root of the lam in Arabic is to gather, it is said: I gathered the thing, I gathered it, and from this it is said: God gathered his scattered matters, meaning he gathered the scattered matters. Al-Nabigha said: I will not leave a brother who does not blame you for his disheveled hair. And from this is their saying: Your house is a gathering place, meaning it gathers people, raises them, and brings them together. Al-Marnaq al-Ta’i said, praising Alqamah ibn Saif: He loved me like a boy and I did not guide him to the Generous and Majestic Al-Layth said: Al-Lam means strong gathering, and from it comes a gathered stone and a gathered battalion. So the eater gathers the tharid, gathers it into mouthfuls and then eats it. Mujahid said: He eats it in small bites. Al-Hasan said: He eats his share and the share of others. Al-Hutay’ah said: If the blame is not followed by his Lord, then may the Most Merciful sanctify those mills. Meaning that they combine their own share with the share of others in their eating. Ibn Zayd said: It is that when he eats his money, he is touched by the money of others and eats it, without thinking whether he ate from the bad or the good. He said: The polytheists did not leave inheritance to women or children, rather they ate their inheritance with their inheritance, and their heritage with their heritage. It was said: They eat what the dead person accumulated through injustice and he knows that, so he diversifies in eating between what is forbidden and what is permissible. It is permissible to criticize the heir who got the money easily and leisurely, without breaking a sweat, so he spends it extravagantly and eats it generously, combining the desired foods, drinks and fruits, as the idle heirs do.
89:20: The Almighty said: And you love wealth with an overwhelming love meaning a lot, both its lawful and unlawful aspects. And a lot is a lot. It is said: The thing became very large, meaning it gathered and became plentiful. And from this comes the word a lot in a pool: if it gathered and became plentiful. And the poet said: If you forgive, O God, you forgive a lot, and which servant of yours is there without pain? Al-Jammah: the place where water collects. Al-Jumum: a well with abundant water. Al-Jumum with dammah: the source. It is said: the water has accumulated abundantly in the well and gathered, after what is in it has been drawn out.
89:21: God Almighty says: No! When the earth is pounded to powder. God the Almighty said: No! meaning, this is not how things should be. It is a response to their immersion in this world and their accumulation of it, for whoever does that will regret it on the Day when the earth is leveled, and regret will be of no use. Daka means breaking and crushing, and it has been mentioned before. That is, the earth was shaken and moved, one movement after another. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, it was shaken, and Fadak crushed some parts of it. Al-Mubarrad said: That is, it stuck together and its height was lost. It is said: a she-camel dakaa, meaning it has no hump, and the plural is dak. This has been mentioned in Surah Al-A’raf and Surah Al-Haqqah. They also say: Dakkah means demolished. He said: Did someone destroy a cave and it collapsed? Dakka Dakka means time after time, it was shaken and some parts broke each other, so everything on its back was broken. It was also said: its mountains and highlands were crushed until they were level. It was also said: it was crushed, meaning it was spread out, so its houses, palaces, mountains, and all its buildings were gone. And from this the word dukan was named, because it was spread out. Dakka means to flatten the high ground with carpets, and this is the meaning of the saying of Ibn Masoud and Ibn Abbas: the earth was stretched out like a hide.
89:22: The Almighty's saying: And your Lord has come meaning His command and His judgment, said Al-Hasan. It is a case of deleting the complement. It was also said: meaning the Lord came to them with great signs, and it is like His saying: Unless God comes to them in canopies of clouds (al-Baqarah 2:210) meaning in canopies. It was also said: He made the coming of the signs His coming, to magnify the importance of the signs. From this is His saying, the Almighty, in the hadith: O son of Adam, I was sick and you did not visit Me, I asked you for water and you did not give Me, I asked you for food and you did not feed Me. And it was said: And your Lord came meaning that doubts were removed that day, and knowledge became necessary, just as doubts and suspicions are removed when the thing about which one was doubted comes. The scholars of allusion said: His power became apparent and took control, and God, may He be praised, is not described as moving from one place to another, and how could He move and transition? He has no place or time, and time and age do not apply to Him, because in the application of time to something there is the loss of times, and whoever misses something is powerless. God Almighty says: And the angels meaning the angels. Row upon row meaning in rows.
89:23: The Almighty said: And Hell will be brought forth on that Day: Ibn Mas`ud and Muqatil said: Hell will be led by seventy thousand reins, each rein held by seventy thousand angels, roaring and sighing, until it is placed on the left of the Throne. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas`ud, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Hell will be brought forth on that Day, with seventy thousand reins, each rein held by seventy thousand angels, pulling it. Abu Sa`id al-Khudri said: When the verse, And Hell will be brought forth on that Day, was revealed, the color of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) changed, and it was evident on his face, until he became very angry with his companions. Then he said, Gabriel recited to me, ‘No! When the earth is pounded to powder—the verse—and Hell will be brought forth on that Day.’ Ali may God be pleased with him said: I said, O Messenger of God, how will it be brought forth? He said, “It will be brought forth, led by seventy thousand reins, each of which will be led by seventy thousand angels. It will scatter in a manner that, if left alone, would burn up the people of the assembly. Then Hell will appear to me and say, ‘What do you and I have to do with you, O Muhammad? God has forbidden your flesh to me.’” Then no one will remain except that he will say, Myself, myself! Except Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him), for he will say, My Lord, my nation! My Lord, my nation! God the Almighty says: On that Day man will remember meaning he will be admonished and repent. He is the disbeliever, or the one whose concern is mostly this world. And how will he be reminded? meaning how will he be admonished and repent when he neglected them in this world. It is also said: What is the benefit of the remembrance? So the omission of the complement must be understood, otherwise there is a contradiction between On that Day he will remember and How will he be reminded? Al-Zamakhshari said this.
89:24: God Almighty says: He will say, ‘Oh, I wish I had sent forth something for my life.’ That is, in my life. The lam means in. It was also said: that is, I did good deeds for my life, that is, for a life in which there is no death. It was also said: The life of the people of Hell is not pleasant, as if they have no life. So the meaning is: I wish I had done good deeds to be saved from Hell, so I would be among those who have a pleasant life.
89:25: The Almighty’s saying: On that Day no one will punish with His punishment meaning no one will punish like the punishment of God, and no one will be bound like His binding. The metaphor refers to God Almighty. This is the opinion of Ibn Abbas and Al-Hasan. Al-Kisa’i readل يقَيضصب(ل يقَيضصب)ل يقَيضصبwith a fat-ha on the dhal and the tha’, meaning no one will be punished in this world like the punishment of God the disbeliever on that Day.
89:26: And he is not bound as the disbeliever is bound. What is meant is Satan, because the evidence has established that he is the most severely punished of people, due to his crime, so the statement was made general because of the accompanying explanation. And it was said: It is Umayyah ibn Khalaf, who narrated his crime, so the statement was made general because of the accompanying explanation. And it was said: It is Umayyah ibn Khalaf, narrated by Al-Farraa. Meaning that no one is punished like the punishment of this specific disbeliever, and no one is bound with chains and shackles like his, due to his extreme disbelief and stubbornness. And it was said: That is, no one is punished in his place, so no ransom is taken from him. And punishment means binding. And from this is the saying of the poet After your hundred gifts It was said: No one who is not an unbeliever will be punished with the punishment of an unbeliever. Abu Ubaidah and Abu Hatim chose to open the dal and the tha. The ha would be the pronoun for the unbeliever, because it is well-known that no one will be punished with the punishment of God. Abu Qilabah narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) read the Qur’an with a fat-ha on the dhal and the tha’. It was narrated that Abu Amr returned to the Prophet’s (peace and blessings be upon him) reading. Abu Ali said: It is possible that the pronoun refers to the disbeliever according to the reading of the group, meaning that no one is tortured like this disbeliever, so the ha’ would refer to the disbeliever. What is meant by one are the angels who are in charge of torturing the people of Hell.
89:27: The Almighty's saying: {O reassured soul} After mentioning the state of the one whose concern is this world and who accuses God of making him rich or poor, He mentioned the state of the one whose soul is reassured by God, so he submits to His command and puts his trust in Him. It was said: It is from the words of the angels to the friends of God, the Almighty. The reassured soul is the calm and certain one, certain that God is its Lord, so it submits to that, as said by Mujahid and others. Ibn Abbas said: Meaning the one reassured by God's reward. And from him: the believing woman. Al-Hasan said: The believing woman with certainty. And from Mujahid also: The one satisfied with God's decree, the one who knows that what missed her could not have befallen her, and that what befell her could not have missed her. Muqatil said: The one who is secure from God's punishment. And in the version of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: {O secure and reassured soul}. And it was said: The one who acts with certainty in what God promised in His Book. Ibn Kaysan said: The reassured soul here: The sincere one. Ibn Ata’ said: The knowledgeable one is the one who cannot be patient without it for the blink of an eye. It was also said: The one who is reassured by the remembrance of God Almighty. Its explanation: Those who have believed and whose hearts are assured by the remembrance of God (Ar-Ra’d: 28). It was said: reassured by faith, believing in the resurrection and reward. Ibn Zayd said: reassured because it is given good report of Paradise at death, at the resurrection, and on the Day of Resurrection. Abdullah ibn Buraydah narrated on the authority of his father that he meant the soul of Hamzah. The correct view is that it is general and applies to every faithful, sincere, and obedient soul. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: When God Almighty wants to take the soul of His believing servant, the soul is reassured by God Almighty, and God is reassured by it. Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As said: When a believer dies, God sends two angels to him, and with them a gift from Paradise, and they say to it: Come out, O reassured soul, well-pleased and pleasing, and with God well-pleased with you. Come out to a spirit and fragrance, and a Lord who is pleased and not angry. So it comes out like the most fragrant scent of musk that anyone has smelled from his nose on the face of the earth. And he mentioned the hadith. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: A man recited in the presence of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, O reassured soul. Abu Bakr said, How beautiful this is, O Messenger of God! The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, The angel will say it to you, O Abu Bakr. Sa`id ibn Jubayr said: Ibn Abbas died in Taif, and a bird, the likes of which had never been seen before, came and entered his coffin, and was never seen coming out of it. When he was buried, this verse was recited on the edge of the grave - it is not known who recited it: O reassured soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing.
89:28: God Almighty says: Return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing. Ad-Dahhak narrated: It was revealed about Uthman ibn Affan may God be pleased with him when he stopped the well of Ruma. It was also said that it was revealed about Khubayb ibn Adi, whom the people of Mecca crucified and turned his face toward Medina, but God changed his face toward the Qiblah. And God knows best. The meaning of to your Lord is to your companion and your body. This was stated by Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, and Ata’. Al-Tabari also favored this view, and his evidence is the reading of Ibn Abbas so enter among My servant in the sense of monotheism, as God will command the souls to return to their bodies tomorrow. Ibn Mas’ud read it in the body of My servant. Al-Hasan said: Return to the reward and honor of your Lord. Abu Salih said: The meaning is: Return to God.
89:29: The Almighty's saying: Then enter among My servants meaning among the bodies of My servants, the evidence for this is the reading of Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masoud. Ibn Abbas said: This is the Day of Resurrection, and so did Ad-Dahhak. The majority of scholars agree that Paradise is the eternal home which is the dwelling place of the righteous, the home of the righteous and the report. The meaning of among My servants is among the righteous among My servants, as He said: We will surely admit them among the righteous (Al-Ankaboot 29:9). Al-Akhfash said: among My servants meaning among My party, and the meaning is the same, meaning join their ranks.
89:30: And enter My Paradise with them.
90:1: Meccan by consensus. It has twenty verses. The Almighty’s statement: I swear by this city may be that la is redundant, as mentioned previously in I swear by the Day of Resurrection (al-Qiyamah 75:1), as stated by Al-Akhfash. That is, I swear, because He said: and this city (al-Tin 95:3), so how can he deny swearing by it when he swore by it? The poet said: I remembered Laila, and I felt a deep sense of longing, and my heart almost broke. That is, it is interrupted, and the letter la is a connective, and from this is the saying of the Most High: What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you? (al-A’raf 7:12), as evidenced by the saying of the Most High in Sad: What prevented you from prostrating? (Sad: 75). Al-Hasan, Al-A’mash and Ibn Kathir read la-aqsam without an alif after the lam as confirmation. Al-Akhfash also permitted it to have the meaning of ala. It was said: It is not a negation of an oath, but rather it is like the Arabs saying: No, by God, I would not have done such-and-such in this city if you were not in it after leaving it. This was narrated by Makki. Ibn Abi Nujayh narrated it on the authority of Mujahid, who said: la is a response to them. This is the preferred opinion of Ibn Al-Arabi, because he said: As for those who said that it is a response, it is a statement that has no response, because the meaning is correct and the wording and intent are possible. It is a response to the words of those who denied the resurrection and then began the oath. Al-Qushayri said: His saying la is a response to what the person mentioned in this surah, who was deceived by the world, imagined. That is, the matter is not as he thinks, that no one will be able to do it. Then he began the oath. The city: is Mecca, they agreed on it. That is, I swear by the sacred city in which you are, for the honor you have bestowed upon me and my love for you. Al-Wasiti said: That is, we swear to you by this city which you have honored with your place in it while alive, and your blessing while dead, meaning Medina. The first is more correct, because the surah was revealed in Mecca by consensus.
90:2: The Almighty's statement: And you will be abiding in this city means in the future, like His statement: Indeed, you will die, and indeed, they will die (al-Ramzah: 30). Similar expressions are broad in the speech of the Arabs. You say to someone you promise honor and love: You are honored and loved. This is broad in the speech of God, because future conditions are like present and observable conditions. Sufficient for you is conclusive evidence that it refers to the future, and that interpreting it as a present is impossible: that the surah is agreed to be Meccan before the conquest. Mansur narrated from Mujahid: And you will be abiding meaning: Whatever you do in it, you are absolved. Ibn Abbas said the same: It was made permissible for him on the day of Mecca to kill whomever he wanted, so he killed Ibn Khatal, Muqays ibn Subabaah, and others. It was not permissible for anyone to kill anyone there after the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Al-Suddi narrated: You are absolved from killing whoever fought you. Abu Salih narrated from Ibn Abbas: It was made permissible for him for an hour of a day, then it was closed and forbidden until the Day of Resurrection, and that was on the day of the conquest of Mecca. It was proven that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: (God made Mecca sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth, so it is sacred until the Hour comes. It was not lawful for anyone before me, and it will not be lawful for anyone after me. It was only lawful for me for an hour of a day.) This hadith has been mentioned previously in Surah Al-Ma’idah. Ibn Zayd said: No one was lawful in it except the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was also said: And you are residing in it and it is your place. It was also said: And you are doing good in it, and I am pleased with you in it. The linguists mentioned that it is said: A man who is lawful and lawful and a place, a man who is forbidden and a place, and a man who is forbidden and forbidden. Qatada said: You are a resident in it: you are not sinful. It was also said: It is praise for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, meaning that you are not committing in this country what is forbidden for you to commit, knowing from you the right of this House, not like the polytheists who commit disbelief in God in it. Meaning, I swear by this venerated House whose sanctity you have known, so you are residing in it and respecting it, not committing in it what is forbidden for you. Shurahbil ibn Sa’d said: And you are a resident in this country meaning that they forbid Mecca from killing game in it. Or they support a tree with it, and then they consider it permissible to expel you and kill you.
90:3: God the Almighty says: And a father and what he begot. Mujahid, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, Al-Hasan, and Abu Salih said: And the father of Adam, peace be upon him. And what he begot means and what descended from his children. He swore by them because they are the most amazing creation of God the Almighty on the face of the earth, because of what they possess of clarity, speech, and management, and among them are the prophets and those who call to God the Almighty. It was also said: It is an oath by Adam and the righteous among his descendants. As for the unrighteous, they are as if they were cattle. It was also said: The father is Abraham. And what he begot are his descendants. As for the unrighteous, they are as if they were cattle. It was also said: The father is Abraham. And what he begot are his descendants. This was said by Abu Imran Al-Jawni. Then it is possible that He means all of his descendants. It is possible that He means the Muslims among his descendants. Al-Farra’ said: Ma is suitable for people, as in His statement: What is good for you (An-Nisa’ 4:3), and as in His statement: And He created the male and the female (Al-Layl 72:3), and He is the Creator of the male and the female. It was said: Ma with what follows it is in the position of a verbal noun, meaning and a parent and his childbirth, as in His statement: And the heaven and He who constructed it (Ash-Shams 48:5). Ikrimah and Sa’id Jubayr said: And a parent means the one for whom a child is born. And what was born means the barren woman who does not have children, and Ibn Abbas said the same. Ma according to this is a negation, and this is far-fetched, and it is not correct except by implying the relative pronoun, meaning and a parent and and what was born, and that is not permissible according to the Basrans. It was said: It is general for every parent and every child, as stated by Atiyyah Al-Awfi. Its meaning was also narrated from Ibn Abbas, and this is the test of Al-Tabari. Al-Mawardi said: It is possible that the parent is the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, since he was mentioned previously, and and what was born of his female slave, because of his statement, peace be upon him: I am to you in the position of a father, I teach you.” So he swore by him and his nation after he swore by his country, exaggerating the honor of him, peace be upon him.
90:4: God Almighty says: We have certainly created man into hardship. Here ends the section, and this is its answer. And God can swear by whatever He wills of His creations to glorify them, as mentioned above. And man here is the son of Adam. In hardship means in hardship and difficulty from struggling in this world. The root of the word kabd is hardship. And from it is the word takadum to clot of milk: it thickened, curdled and became intense. And from it is the word kabd liver, because it is blood that thickened and became intense. And it is said: I struggled with this matter: I endured its intensity. Labid said: Oh eye, why did you not cry for Arbad when we and our opponents rose up in grief? Ibn Abbas and Al-Hasan said: in hardship meaning in hardship and fatigue. It was also narrated from Ibn Abbas: in hardship from his pregnancy, birth, breastfeeding, teething, and other conditions. Ikrimah narrated from him that he said: upright in his mother’s womb. The liver means straightness and uprightness. This is a blessing upon him in creation. God, the Most High, did not create an animal in its mother’s womb except bent over on its face, except for the son of Adam, for he is upright, and this is the opinion of Al-Nakha’i, Mujahid, and others. Ibn Kaysan: upright with his head in his mother’s womb, then when God permits him to emerge from his mother’s womb, he turns his head to his mother’s feet. Al-Hasan said: he endures the calamities of this world and the hardships of the hereafter. It was also narrated from him: he endures gratitude for ease and endures patience in hardship, because he is never devoid of one of the two. It was narrated by Ibn Umar. Yaman said: God did not create a creation that endures what the son of Adam endures, and despite that, he is the weakest of creation. Our scholars said: The first thing he suffers is the cutting of his umbilical cord. Then, when he is swaddled and tied up, he suffers distress and fatigue. Then he suffers breastfeeding, and if he misses it, it will be lost. Then he suffers the growth of his teeth and the movement of his tongue. Then he suffers weaning, which is more severe than slapping. Then he suffers circumcision, pains and sorrows. Then he suffers the teacher and his kindness, the tutor and his policy, the professor and his prestige. Then he suffers the work of marriage and hastening it. Then he suffers the work of children, servants and soldiers. Then he suffers the work of houses and building palaces. Then old age and decrepitude, weakness of the knee and foot, in calamities whose number is many, and misfortunes whose mention would take too long, such as headaches, toothaches, conjunctivitis, grief of debt, toothaches and earaches. He suffers hardships in wealth and soul, such as beatings and imprisonment. Not a day goes by without him suffering hardship and difficulty. Then death comes after all of that. Then the questioning of the King, the pressure and darkness of the grave, then the resurrection and presentation to God, until he is settled, either in Paradise or Hell. God the Most High said: Indeed, We created man into toil. If it were up to him, he would not have chosen these hardships. This indicates that he has a Creator who planned him and decreed these conditions for him, so let him obey His command. Ibn Zayd said: The human being here is Adam. And His saying: in toil means in the middle of the sky. Al-Kalbi said: This was revealed about a man from the Banu Jumah, who was called Abu Al-Ashdayn. He used to take a leather skin and put it under his feet, saying: Whoever removes me from him will have such and such. But he would pull it ten times until it was torn apart, but his feet would not move. He was one of the enemies of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). And regarding him, the verse: Does he think that no one will have power over him? was revealed, meaning because of his strength. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. In Kabd means severe, meaning severe in character, and he was one of the strongest men of Quraysh. And so was Rukana bin Hashim ibn Abdul Muttalib, who was an example of bravery and severity. It was said: In a liver, meaning bold of heart, thick of liver, with a weak constitution and lowly substance. Ibn Ata’: In darkness and ignorance. Al-Tirmidhi: Neglecting what concerns him, preoccupied with what does not concern him.
90:5: God Almighty says: Does he think that no one will have power over him? That is, does the son of Adam think that God Almighty will not punish him?
90:6: God Almighty says: He says, ‘I have squandered’ meaning I have spent. A great deal of wealth meaning a great deal of it collected together.
90:7: God the Almighty said: Does he think meaning does he think that no one saw it meaning that no one witnessed it "? Rather, God the Almighty knew that about him, so he was lying in his statement: I destroyed it and he did not spend it. Abu Hurairah narrated that the servant will stand and be asked, "What did you do with the wealth that I provided you with? He will say, I spent it and gave it in zakat. It will be said, It is as if you only did that so that it would be said, 'He was generous,' and that was said. Then he will be ordered to the Fire." Sa'id narrated from Qatadah: You will be asked about your wealth: from where you gathered it and how you spent it? Ibn Abbas said: Abu al-Ashdayn used to say, "I spent a lot of wealth in enmity towards Muhammad," and he was lying about that. Muqatil said: This was revealed about al-Harith ibn Amir ibn Nawfal. He sinned and sought a fatwa from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who ordered him to make expiation. He said, "My wealth has been lost in expiations and expenses since I entered the religion of Muhammad." This statement of his could be a sign of his extravagance in what he spent, in which case it would be out of his transgression, or regret over it, in which case it would be out of his remorse. Abu Ja`far read mālā labadan with a shaddah on the ba’ and a fathah, on the plural of labad, like rak`i’ and rak`u, sājid and sujūd, shahīd and shahād, and the like. Mujahid and Hamīd read it with a damma on the ba’ and the lam, and a lightened one, the plural of labūd. The rest read it with a damma on the lam and a kasrah and a fathah on the ba’, and a lightened one. Hamīd read it with a damma on the ba’ and labdah, which means that which is matted, meaning abundance. This has already been discussed in Surah al-Jinn. It was narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to read ayḥisab with a damma on the seen in both cases. Al-Hasan said: He says, I have wasted a lot of money, so who will hold me accountable for it? Let me count it. Does he not know that God is able to hold him accountable, and that God, the Almighty, sees his deeds?
90:8: Then he enumerated His blessings upon him and said: Did We not give him two eyes with which he could see?
90:9: The Almighty said: And a tongue with which to speak. And two lips with which to cover a gap. The meaning is: We are able to resurrect him and count his deeds. Abu Hazim said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God Almighty said: ‘O son of Adam, if your tongue contests with you concerning that which I have forbidden you, I have aided you with two layers, so close your eyes. If your sight contests with you concerning that which I have forbidden you, I have aided you with two layers, so close your eyes. If your private parts contest with you concerning that which I have forbidden you, I have aided you with two layers, so close your eyes.’” The word lip is originally shafha, but the ha was dropped from it. Its diminutive is shafiha, and the plural is shafaha. It is also said shafahat and shafawwat, but the ha is more correct and the waw is more general, likening it to years. Al-Azhari said: This is said as a lip in connection and as a lip, with the ta and the ha. Qatada said: The blessings of God are apparent, and He makes you feel satisfied with them until you are grateful.
90:10: The Almighty says: And We showed him the two ways meaning the two paths: the way of good and the way of evil. That is, We made them clear to him through the messengers We sent. The way is the high road. This is the opinion of Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masoud, and others. Qatada narrated that he said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: “O people, they are only the two Najds: Najd al-Khair and Najd al-Shar. So why do you make Najd al-Shar more beloved to you than Najd al-Khair?” It was narrated on the authority of Ikrimah who said: The two Najds are the two breasts. This is the opinion of Saeed bin al-Musayyab and al-Dahhak, and it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ali, may God be pleased with them, because they are like the two paths for the life and livelihood of the child. So Najd means the height, and the plural is Najoud, and from it it was named Najd, for its height from the lowlands of Tihamah. So Najd: the two high paths. Imru’ al-Qais said: Two teams, one of them is from Batn Nakhal and the other is from Qat’a Najd Kabkab.
90:11: God the Almighty says: And why did he not storm the pass meaning, why did he not spend the money that he spent in enmity against Muhammad, why did he not spend it storming the pass and be safe! Storming means throwing oneself into something without deliberation. It is said: He threw himself into the matter meaning he threw himself into it without deliberation. A horse throws its rider into it face to face if he throws it. Throwing oneself into something means entering it without deliberation. Al-Qahmah with the letter ḍammah is a destructive event and a severe drought. It is said: The Bedouins were afflicted with al-Qahmah meaning they were afflicted with drought and entered the countryside. Al-Qahmah means the difficult parts of the road. Al-Farra' and Al-Zajjaj said: The word la is mentioned once, and the Arabs rarely use la alone with a past tense verb in such a situation, until they repeat it in another statement, like God the Almighty's saying: And neither did they believe, nor did they pray [Al-Qiyamah 31], And there is no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve (Al-Baqarah 2:62). Rather, they singled it out because the end of the speech indicates its meaning. It is possible that His statement, Then he was among those who believed, is in place of repetition, as if he said, He neither stormed the pass nor believed. It was said: It is in the manner of a supplication, like His statement, He neither escaped nor was safe. His statement, the Most High, And what will make you know what the pass is? Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: Everything in which He said, And what will make you know? He informed about it, and everything in which He said, And what will make you know? He did not inform about it. He said: The meaning of And did not storm the pass is that he did not storm the pass, like the statement of Zuhayr: He had turned his back on the woman he was hiding, but he neither showed her nor advanced her. That is, he did not show it or advance. This is what Al-Mubarrad and Abu Ali said: La means did not. Al-Bukhari mentioned it from Mujahid. That is, he did not cross the obstacle in this world, so there is no need to repeat it. Then he explained the obstacle and riding it, saying: freeing a slave and so on, thus explaining aspects of financial closeness. Ibn Zayd and a group of commentators said: The meaning of the statement is a question whose meaning is denial, meaning: Why did he not cross the obstacle, or why did he not cross the obstacle? He says: Why did he not spend his money in denial, meaning: Why did he not cross the obstacle, or why did he not cross the obstacle? He says: His money is in freeing slaves and feeding the hungry, so that he can cross the obstacle, so that it would be better for him than spending it in enmity against Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. Then it was said: Crossing the obstacle here is a metaphor, meaning, do the great matters bear in his spending his money in obedience to his Lord and belief in Him. This is only appropriate for the statement of one who interprets So let him not storm the obstacle as a supplication, meaning that he who does not spend his money on such and such will not be saved or safe. It was said that the enormity, weight, and severity of sins were likened to an obstacle. So if someone frees a slave and does righteous deeds, his example will be like someone who storms the obstacle, which are the sins whose ascent to the obstacle is seven thousand years, and whose descent is seven thousand years. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: It is a steep obstacle in Hellfire before the bridge, so storm it in obedience to God. Mujahid, Al-Dahhak, and Al-Kalbi said: It is the path that is struck over Hellfire like the edge of a sword, a journey of three thousand years, easy, ascending, and descending. Storming it for the believer is like the distance between the afternoon prayer and the evening prayer. It was also said: Storming it is the length of time it takes to pray the obligatory prayer. It was narrated from Abu Al-Darda' that he said: Behind us is an obstacle, the people are saved from it the lightest of them. It was also said that Hellfire itself is the obstacle. Abu Raja' narrated from Al-Hasan that he said: We have been informed that no Muslim frees a slave except that it will be his ransom from the Hellfire. On the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, he said: Whoever frees a slave, God the Almighty will free a limb of his for every limb of hers. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: Whoever frees a slave, God will free a limb of his for every limb of hers from the Fire, even his private parts with his private parts. In Tirmidhi, on the authority of Abu Umamah and other companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: “Any Muslim man who frees a Muslim man, his release from the Fire will be equivalent to every limb of his for every limb of his, and any Muslim woman who frees a Muslim woman, her release from the Fire will be equivalent to every limb of hers for every limb of hers.” He said: This is a good, authentic, rare hadith. It was said: The obstacle is a summary of the horror of the presentation. Qatadah and Ka’b said: It is a fire before the bridge. Al-Hasan said: By God, it is a very difficult obstacle: the struggle of man against his self, his desires, and his enemy, Satan. Some of them recited: I have been afflicted with four who shoot arrows at me and set traps for me. Satan, the world, my soul and desires. How can I hope to escape from them? Oh God, help me with forgiveness, for I have come to hope for no one but You for them.
90:12: God Almighty said: And what will make you know what the steep path is? There is an ellipsis in it, meaning, And what will make you realize what storming the pass is? This is to emphasize the importance of adhering to the religious command, and the address is to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), to teach him how to storm the pass. Al-Qushayri said: “And interpreting ‘the pass’ as referring to the pass of Hell is far-fetched, since no one in this world has stormed the pass of Hell, unless it is interpreted to mean, ‘Why not make himself capable of storming the pass of Hell tomorrow?’” Al-Bukhari preferred the statement of Mujahid: that he did not storm the pass in this world. Ibn al-Arabi said: “And he chose that because he said after that in the second verse: ‘And what will make you realize what is the ‘Aqaba’? Then in the third verse he said: ‘The freeing of a slave,’ and in the fourth verse: ‘Or feeding on a day of famine,’ then in the fifth verse he said: ‘An orphan near of kin,’ then in the sixth verse he said: ‘Or a needy person in dust.’ These deeds can only be done in this world. The meaning is: So he did not do in this world anything that would make it easy for him to cross the pass in the Hereafter.”
90:13: The Almighty said: Freeing a slave. Freeing her: releasing her from captivity. It was also said: from slavery. In the hadith: And freeing a slave is to help with its price from the hadith of Al-Bara', and it was mentioned before in Surat Al-Bara'ah. Freeing: is removing the shackles, and slavery is a shackle. The enslaved is called a slave, because in slavery he is like a captive tied around his neck. And its neck is called freeing the prisoner from captivity. Hassan said: How many prisoners we have freed without a price, and how many forelocks we were masters of Uqbah bin Amir Al-Juhani narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever frees a believing slave, it will be his ransom from the Fire. Al-Mawardi said: It is possible, secondly, that he meant freeing his slave and saving his soul by avoiding sins and performing acts of obedience. Goodness is not impossible from this interpretation, and it is more likely to be correct. Second: The Almighty’s statement: A slave. Asbagh said: A disbelieving slave with a price is better for emancipation than a believing slave with a small price, “based on the statement of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, when he was asked, ‘Which slave is best?’ He said: ‘The one with the highest price, and the most precious to its owners.’” Ibn al-Arabi said: “What is meant in this hadith is: from the Muslims, based on the statement of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: ‘Whoever emancipates a Muslim man’ and ‘Whoever emancipates a believing slave.’” What Asbagh mentioned is a coincidence, but rather he is looking at reducing wealth, and looking at the emancipation of the slave for worship and freeing him up for monotheism is more appropriate.” Third: Manumission and charity are among the best deeds. Abu Hanifa reported that manumission is better than charity. His two companions reported that charity is better. The verse is more indicative of Abu Hanifa’s view, as manumission is given precedence over charity. Al-Sha’bi reported that a man who has surplus money to spend on his relatives should spend it on a relative or free a slave. He said: A slave is better, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever God frees for each of its limbs a limb from the Fire.
90:14: The Almighty said: Or feeding on a day of famine meaning famine. Famine means panic. And the hungry person is the one who is hungry. Al-Hasan read or feeding on a day of famine with an alif in that. Abu Ubaidah recited: If you were a neighbor, O son of Qais bin Asim, you would not have spent the night full while your neighbor was hungry. Feeding people is a virtue, and it is better than famine, which is hunger. Al-Nakha’i said about the Almighty’s statement: Or feeding on a day of severe hunger, that he said: On a day when food is scarce. It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: One of the reasons for mercy is feeding a hungry Muslim.
90:15: The Almighty said: of close kinship meaning kinship. It is said: So-and-so is my kin and my close relative. This teaches you that charity given to relatives is better than charity given to non-relatives, just as charity given to an orphan who has no guardian is better than charity given to an orphan who can find someone to take care of him. Linguists say: He is called an orphan because of his weakness. It is said: A man becomes orphaned: if he is weak. They mentioned that an orphan among people is from the father's side, and among animals is from the mother's side. This has been fully discussed in Surah Al-Baqarah. Some linguists said: An orphan is one whose parents die. Qays ibn Al-Mulawwah said: I complain to God about the loss of Layla, just as an orphan complains to God about the loss of his parents.
90:16: God the Almighty said: Or a poor person covered with dust meaning he has nothing, as if he is stuck to the dust due to poverty, he has no shelter but the dust. Ibn Abbas said: He is the one thrown on the road, who has no home. Mujahid: He is the one who is not protected from the dust by clothing or anything else. Qatada said: He is the one with a family. Ikrimah: The indebted. Abu Sinan: The one with hardship. Ibn Jubayr: The one who has no one. Ikrimah narrated from Ibn Abbas: The one covered with dust is the one who is far from his homeland, meaning the stranger who is far from his homeland. Abu Hamid Al-Kharzanji said: Dust here: from tarīb, which is a severe condition. It is said tarāb: if he becomes poor. Al-Hudali said: Whenever a guest came to our land, we would shed the blood of our people in the soil of the country. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr and Al-Kisa’i read:فكاwith a fatha on the kaf, as a past tense verb.َر َقبيَقةin the accusative case because it is a direct object.او أطمصاء with a fatha on the hamza and a nasb on the meem, without an alif, as a past tense verb as well, because of the statement: Then he was among those who believed. This is more problematic withفكا و أطمصاء. The rest read:فكاin the nominative case, as a verbal noun forفكاكت.رقَقبةin the genitive case with the addition.او إطمصاءwith a kasra on the hamza and an alif and a dhamma on the meem and a tanween on it as a verbal noun as well. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose it because it is an explanation of the statement of God the Almighty: And what will make you know what the pass is? Then He informed him and said: FRAGARQABA * OR ITAAM meaning: storming the pass: FARAGAR QABA or ITAAM. Whoever reads it in the accusative case, it is based on the meaning, i.e., neither freeing a slave nor feeding on a day of great severity, so how can one cross the pass? Al-Hasan and Abu Raja’ read:ذا م سبغas an adjective forيوم. It is permissible to read the accusative as an attribute of the position of the preposition and the noun, because his saying: on the day is an adverbial phrase in the accusative position, so it is a description of it in meaning but not in wording.
90:17: The Almighty's statement: Then he was among those who believed means: He would not take the difficult path of freeing a slave, or feeding the poor on a day of famine, until he was among those who believed, that is, they were truthful, because the condition for the acceptance of acts of obedience is belief in God. Belief in God after spending is of no benefit, rather the act of obedience must be accompanied by faith. God Almighty said about al-Munafiqun 63:And nothing prevented their expenditures from being accepted from them except that they disbelieved in God and in His Messenger (al-Tawbah 9:54). Aisha said: O Messenger of God, during the pre-Islamic period, Ibn Jud’an maintained family ties, fed the poor, freed the captives, freed slaves, and carried camels on his back for the sake of God. Did that benefit him at all? He said: No, for he never said, ‘O my Lord, forgive me my sin on the Day of Judgment.’ It was also said: Then he was among those who believed, meaning he did these things while he was a believer, then he remained a believer until his death. Similar to the words of God the Almighty: And indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents, believes and does righteousness and then continues in guidance. (Ta-Ha: 82) It was also said that the meaning is, Then he was among those who believe that this is beneficial for them with God the Almighty. It was also said: He performed these acts of worship for the sake of God, then he believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Hakim ibn Hizam said after he converted to Islam: O Messenger of God, we used to perform acts of worship during the Age of Ignorance, so do we have any of them? He, peace be upon him, said: I have become Muslim in accordance with the good I did before.
